articles.title: Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration in Ventricular Arrhythmia Ablation: A New Paradigm From Procedure to a Program of Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation of ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be complex, requiring multidisciplinary expertise for safe and comprehensive patient management. We assessed the extent of perioperative multidisciplinary collaboration for VA ablations.
METHOD: We retrospectively identified 363 cases of VA ablation at an expert referral centre between 2017 and 2021. For these cases, extent of multidisciplinary involvement, PAINESD and MORTALITIES-VA scores, outcomes of ventricular tachycardia (VT) recurrence or premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden, cardiac transplantation and all-cause mortality were assessed.
RESULTS: Of the 363 cases of VA ablation, 185 (51.0%) were elective and 178 (49.0%) were emergent. Most cases required peri-procedural involvement by another specialist (in addition to a cardiac electrophysiologist) (n=231 [63.6%]), including an intensivist in 97 (26.7%), anaesthetist in 87 (24.0%), geneticist in 38 (10.5%), cardiothoracic surgeon in 32 (8.8%), a heart failure and transplant cardiologist in 24 (6.6%), and immunologist in 16 (4.4%). The median PAINESD score was 6.2 (interquartile range [IQR] 0-9), and the median MORTALITIES-VA score was 3.0 (IQR 0-9). Subgroups with higher PAINESD and MORALITIES-VA scores and requiring more specialists in their care were emergent VA ablations (median 8 vs 3 [p<0.001], median 7 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 2 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively), non-PVC ablations (median 6 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 4.5 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 1 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively), and patients with structural heart disease (median 8 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 6 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 1 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively). In PVC ablations the median reduction in PVC burden was 96.5%, and in non-PVC ablations the VT recurrence rate was 39.9%. In the follow-up period, cardiac transplantation was required by 2.9% of patients, and 12.5% of patients died.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing VA ablation require multidisciplinary involvement for optimal care, with multiple specialties involved in the peri-ablation period.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes following transplantation of tumourectomised kidneys: a 30-year experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To report the long-term oncological and graft outcomes of a 30-year single-centre experience with transplantation of carefully selected tumourectomised kidneys.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective single-centre cohort study was performed of all recipients who underwent kidney transplantation following ex vivo bench excision of electively or incidentally detected kidney tumours ≤3 cm between 1996 and 2026 at the Princess Alexandra Hospital (Brisbane, Australia). Recipient, donor, and tumour characteristics, perioperative outcomes, oncological outcomes, patient survival and graft survival were evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 64 recipients underwent kidney transplantation following ex vivo bench excision of a small kidney mass during the study period, with a median (interquartile range [IQR]) follow-up of 11.3 (6.9-15.8) years. The median (IQR) recipient age was 62.5 (54.7-68.6) years. Most donor tumours were small, organ-confined renal cell carcinomas (RCC) with negative surgical margins following bench excision. Three presumed tumour recurrences occurred during follow-up (5.0%), comprising one local recurrence at the previous tumour excision site and two presumed de novo allograft tumours, with no metastatic disease or cancer-specific mortality. At latest follow-up, 50 recipients had died, including 34 (68.0%) with a functioning graft. Estimated patient survival was 93.5%, 88.7% and 62.9% at 1, 5 and 10 years respectively, with acceptable long-term graft outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Transplantation of carefully selected tumourectomised kidneys provides long-term oncological safety and acceptable patient and graft outcomes. These findings support the continued consideration of tumourectomised kidneys from living and deceased donors as a safe and effective strategy to expand the donor pool, reduce organ discard and increase access to kidney transplantation.

articles.title: Interdisciplinary Collaboration as Key Factor for the Optimization of Advanced Heart Failure Treatment.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major global health problem, with outcomes in advanced stages continuing to be poor despite the development of medical therapy and interventional strategies. This report proposes the concept of Interdisciplinary Heart Failure Collaboration (IHFC), a structured framework designed to optimize patient outcomes through coordinated, cross-sectoral care, focusing on the management of advanced HF. The IHFC integrates a broad spectrum of healthcare professionals-including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, nurses, anesthesiologists, intensivists, psychologists, ventricular assist device (VAD) coordinators, and many others-to provide optimal care from outpatient diagnosis to post-discharge long-term management. The model consists of three core management phases: 1) pre-hospital management, which includes outpatient clinic visits, accurate diagnosis and timely referral; 2) intra-hospital management, comprising interventional and surgical treatment including durable VAD implantation and heart transplantation; 3) post-discharge management; post-interventional and post-operative care, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up, patient education and support for self-care. In addition, this report discusses current challenges in implementation, including the need for standardized protocols and effective communication among team members. Rather than replacing existing HF care systems, the IHFC provides a practical framework for integrating established multidisciplinary principles across the entire clinical trajectory of advanced HF and may be adapted to different healthcare settings.

articles.title: Comparison of Experimental Methods for Quantitative Evaluation of Vocal Fold Movement Including Glottic Closure With a Focus on Citric Acid-Induced Cough-Like Reflex in a Rat Model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In animal studies, quantitative assessment of vocal fold movement, including glottic closure, remains challenging. This study compared methods for quantitative assessment of vocal fold movement reflecting both glottic opening and closure.
METHODS: Four methods were evaluated under general anesthesia: quiet respiration in all rats, recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) electrical and epiglottic mucosal stimulation in three rats each, and intratracheal citric acid-induced cough-like reflex in seven control rats and seven rats with left RLN palsy. Left vocal fold and arytenoid movement angles were measured from endoscopic images when feasible.
RESULTS: During quiet respiration, inspiratory vocal fold abduction was observed. RLN stimulation induced incomplete adduction. Epiglottic stimulation elicited a glottic closure reflex, but stable endoscopic fixation was not achievable. Citric acid induced repetitive cough-like reflexes, enabling quantitative analysis in all rats. During quiet respiration, vocal fold movement angles did not differ between groups, whereas arytenoid movement angles were greater in controls than in RLN-palsy rats (4.69 ± 1.78° vs. 0.67 ± 0.22°, P < 0.001; Hodges-Lehmann difference, 4.00° [95% CI, 2.14-5.55°]). During the cough-like reflex, vocal fold and arytenoid movement angles were greater in controls (29.06 ± 2.77° vs. 0.33 ± 2.09° and 19.80 ± 2.12° vs. 0.48 ± 0.87°, respectively; both P < 0.001; Hodges-Lehmann differences, 28.42° [95% CI, 25.27-32.07°] and 19.59° [95% CI, 16.68-21.51°], respectively). In controls, both angles were greater during the cough-like reflex than during quiet respiration (both P = 0.016; matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation = 1.00 for both; Hodges-Lehmann differences, 28.49° [95% CI, 23.82-30.75°] and 15.25° [95% CI, 12.63-17.36°], respectively). No significant within-animal differences occurred in RLN-palsy rats.
CONCLUSION: Citric acid-induced cough-like reflex enables quantitative assessment of vocal fold movement, including glottic opening and closure, under general anesthesia and may provide additional information on vocal fold movement.

articles.title: Remimazolam for sedation in elderly patients undergoing gastrointestinal endoscopy: Protocol for a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is one of the most commonly performed procedures in older adults, who constitute an increasing proportion of the endoscopic population yet face a higher risk of sedation-related cardiorespiratory adverse events, delayed recovery, and postoperative neurocognitive disturbances. Remimazolam, an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine metabolised by tissue esterases independently of hepatic and renal function, is a candidate sedative of particular interest in this group. However, the extent and gaps of the available evidence specific to sedation with remimazolam in elderly patients undergoing GI endoscopy have not been systematically mapped.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically map the existing evidence on the use of remimazolam for procedural sedation in elderly patients (aged ≥65 years) undergoing GI endoscopy, characterising study design, reported outcomes, comparators, and dosing regimens, and identifying knowledge gaps.
METHODS: This scoping review will be conducted in accordance with the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and reported following the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). We will search PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science, and Scopus, together with the Chinese databases CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP (CQVIP), from 1 January 2015 to the search date-a start date that precedes the earliest published clinical reports of remimazolam. Google Scholar will be used as a supplementary source for grey literature and additional records. The search will be further supplemented by trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov, the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform[ICTRP], and the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry[ChiCTR]), citation chasing, and additional grey literature. Eligibility will be limited to reports published in English or Chinese, reflecting the substantial body of relevant Chinese-language literature. Two reviewers will independently screen records and extract data using a piloted extraction form. Results will be presented in tabular and diagrammatic form alongside a narrative synthesis and an evidence map.
EXPECTED RESULTS AND DISSEMINATION: This scoping review is expected to map the current extent, range, and nature of evidence on remimazolam for sedation in elderly patients undergoing gastrointestinal endoscopy, will map the volume, designs and outcomes of existing studies and, by visualising this evidence, identify gaps to inform trial design in this high-risk population. The findings will be disseminated through publication in a peer-reviewed journal and presentation at relevant academic conferences.

articles.title: Short-Term Outcomes Following Surgery for Brachial Plexus Disorders and Related Nerve Procedures: Impact of Diabetes in a National Cohort of 4,040 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brachial plexus disorders can be debilitating, yet national patterns in patient demographics, procedural complexity, and outcomes remain poorly defined. Diabetes mellitus, which is known to impair wound healing, may further worsen perioperative outcomes, but its impact across large cohorts undergoing brachial plexus surgery is still unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) from 2008 to 2024 identifying adult patients undergoing surgery for brachial plexus disorders (a heterogeneous, decompression-predominant population) using ICD and CPT codes. Demographics, comorbidities, operative details, and 30-day outcomes were characterized and compared across diabetic and nondiabetic patients. Multivariable logistic regression with Firth's penalized likelihood was performed to identify independent predictors of surgical complications (primary outcome) and of medical complications, reoperation, and readmission (secondary outcomes).
RESULTS: Among 4040 patients, the median age was 36 years (IQR 26 to 47), 55.0% were female, and most procedures were elective (96.5%). Nerve decompression was the most common procedure (85.3%), whereas complex reconstruction was infrequent (nerve transfers 4.8%, nerve grafting 4.0%), consistent with a broader, less trauma-predominant population than traditional reconstructive series. Diabetes was present in 174 patients (4.3%) and was associated with older age (median 51 vs. 35 y), higher body mass index, obesity (61.5% vs. 29.2%), hypertension (59.8% vs. 12.8%), renal failure (8.6% vs. 0.5%), and ASA class III status (59.8% vs. 18.4%). Operative time (median 143 min) and length of stay (median 2 d) did not differ by diabetes status. Diabetic patients had higher unadjusted rates of reoperation (7.5% vs. 2.7%, P<0.001), readmission (7.4% vs. 3.3%, P=0.01), surgical complications (5.2% vs. 1.4%, P<0.001), and medical complications (5.2% vs. 1.7%, P=0.003). After multivariable adjustment, diabetes remained independently associated with surgical complications (aOR 3.38, 95% CI: 1.44-7.27, P=0.007) and reoperation (aOR 2.64, 95% CI: 1.30-5.02, P=0.009), but not with medical complications or readmission.
CONCLUSIONS: Short-term complications after brachial plexus surgery are uncommon but influenced by comorbidity burden. Diabetes was independently associated with higher odds of surgical complications and reoperation. Diabetes and the broader comorbidity burden should be weighed in perioperative risk assessment and counseling for patients undergoing brachial plexus surgery.

articles.title: Early arthroplasty versus conversion arthroplasty after failed PFNA in elderly patients with unstable intertrochanteric fractures: a multicenter matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In our study, the clinical and functional outcomes of early arthroplasty versus late conversion arthroplasty approaches were compared in individuals over 75 years of age who underwent PFNA for complex intertrochanteric fractures but whose treatment failed.
METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 136 patients treated between January 2023 and March 2025. The cohort consisted of 62 patients who underwent conversion arthroplasty after failed PFNA fixation and 74 patients who received primary early arthroplasty. Demographic characteristics, surgical parameters, complications, and functional and rehabilitation outcomes were compared between groups.
RESULTS: Early arthroplasty was associated with significantly better six-month functional outcomes, including higher Parker mobility and Merle d'Aubigné scores. The early arthroplasty group also demonstrated shorter times to effective weight-bearing and recovery of walking distance. Perioperative transfusion requirements and systemic complication rates were higher in the PFNA conversion group. However, the time to recovery of unassisted gait did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: Conclusion In elderly patients over 75 years of age with unstable intertrochanteric fractures, early arthroplasty was associated with better short-term functional outcomes, earlier effective weight-bearing and recovery of walking distance, and fewer systemic complications than conversion arthroplasty following failed PFNA. However, these findings should be interpreted in the context of the retrospective design and the functional deterioration that occurred between initial PFNA and subsequent conversion surgery. Primary arthroplasty may be a reasonable option in carefully selected patients with fracture patterns, poor bone quality, or clinical characteristics associated with a high risk of fixation failure.

articles.title: miR-339-3p alleviates sevoflurane-induced cognitive impairment in aged rats and exerts neuroprotective effects in SH-SY5Y cells via targeting GRIN1.
articles.abstract: Sevoflurane (Sev) exposure is a major risk factor for cognitive impairment in elderly patients, and miRNAs play a key regulatory role in its pathogenesis; however, the role and mechanism of miR-339-3p remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of miR-339-3p on Sev-induced cognitive impairment and its targeted regulatory relationship with GRIN1. We established a Sev-induced cognitive impairment model in aged rats and a neuronal injury model in SH-SY5Y cells, detected the expression of miR-339-3p and GRIN1, examined the role of miR-339-3p on neuronal damage through functional assays, and validated the targeting relationship between the two using dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue experiments. Following Sev treatment, miR-339-3p was markedly downregulated while GRIN1 was upregulated. Overexpression of miR-339-3p improved cognitive function in rats and alleviated apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses in cells. In vitro assays confirmed that miR-339-3p directly targets the 3'UTR of GRIN1, and GRIN1 overexpression partially reversed its protective effects. These findings indicate that miR-339-3p alleviates Sev-induced cognitive impairment in aged rats, with in vitro mechanistic evidence supporting its action through direct targeting and downregulation of GRIN1, offering a potential molecular target that may inform future research on anesthesia-related cognitive decline, although its direct clinical applicability requires further validation.

articles.title: The efficacy of adding leg wrapping to prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of post-spinal hypotension in elective cesarean section: a prospective double-blinded randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Various pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods have been studied in the literature to reduce the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of adding bilateral lower-limb wrapping to a prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of hypotension in parturients receiving intrathecal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Parturients were divided into the following: norepinephrine group (N) (n = 84), and norepinephrine and leg wrapping group (NW) (n = 84). The 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion continued until 5 min after fetal delivery. The primary outcome was the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of maternal severe hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, post-delivery hypotension, and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: The final analysis included 168 patients. The incidence of hypotension in the NW group was lower than in the N group (7/84 [8.3%], 18/84 [21.4%], respectively) with P = 0.017, RR = 0.39, and CI: (0.17-0.88). According to the Kaplan-Meier curve with the log-rank test, the time to post-spinal maternal hypotension differed significantly (P = 0.016), with a restricted mean time of 21.1 min in the NW group and 19.7 min in the N group (hazard ratio = 2.82 for the N group vs. NW, 95%CI: (1.18-6.76). Furthermore, a repeated-measures analysis revealed significant group-by-time interactions for both heart rate (P = 0.003) and systolic blood pressure (P = 0.028), demonstrating superior longitudinal hemodynamic stability in the NW group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for secondary maternal and neonatal outcomes.
CONCLUSION: When added to a prophylactic 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion, leg wrapping decreased the incidence of postspinal maternal hypotension and enhanced hemodynamic stability over time during elective cesarean delivery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06496061; principal investigator: Mohamed Ahmed Hamed; date of registration: 11/07/2024; no protocol amendments or study changes after trial start).

articles.title: Textbook Outcome and Associated Factors After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy and CBD Exploration.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess perioperative textbook outcome (TO) achievement and factors associated with TO failure after single-stage surgery for concomitant gallbladder and common bile duct (CBD) stones.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 218 patients who underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) plus laparoscopic CBD exploration (LCBDE) between January 2024 and November 2025. TO required successful surgery and CBD stone clearance, no conversion to open surgery, clinical complications, bile leakage, residual stones, reoperation, postoperative endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), or perioperative mortality, and a postoperative length of stay (LOS) of ≤5 days. Logistic regression identified factors associated with TO failure. Model discrimination, fit, and multicollinearity were assessed.
RESULTS: Overall, 176 patients (80.7%) achieved TO and 42 (19.3%) did not. Eight patients (3.7%) experienced postoperative clinical complications. The achievement rate for LOS ≤5 days was 83.5%, making prolonged hospitalization the principal limitation to TO achievement. American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class III-IV was independently associated with TO failure (odds ratio [OR] = 2.741, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.145-6.559, P = .024). Each 1-mm increase in CBD diameter was associated with a 21.6% increase in the odds of TO nonachievement in the 4-variable model (OR = 1.216, 95% CI: 1.070-1.381, P = .003). The model had an area under the curve of 0.730 (95% CI: 0.638-0.823) and acceptable fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = .060), without substantial multicollinearity.
CONCLUSIONS: Single-stage LC + LCBDE achieved a perioperative TO rate of 80.7%. ASA class III-IV and greater CBD diameter were associated with TO nonachievement in the 4-variable model. These associations require cautious interpretation and confirmation in larger studies.

articles.title: Idiopathic Neonatal Ileocolic Intussusception Without a Pathological Lead Point Presenting as Intestinal Obstruction: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Neonatal intussusception is extremely uncommon, being responsible for 0.3% of all cases of intussusceptions and 3% of all neonatal intestinal obstruction. Due to its nonspecific nature, it may mimic necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and cause a delay in the diagnosis. Idiopathic intussusception in the term neonates is unusual as most have a pathological lead point. A case of a full-term male infant presenting on the third day of life with abdominal distension, bilious vomiting, and stools with mixed blood. Examination showed a non-tender mass in the right iliac fossa while the digital rectal examination revealed red currant jelly stool. Ultrasonography showed 23 × 18 × 44 mm target sign suggestive of intussusception. On emergency laparotomy, there was gangrenous ileocolic intussusception that extended from 15 cm proximally to the ileocecal junction to mid-sigmoid colon. Reduction by manual manipulation under general anesthesia through laparotomy was unsuccessful and so the gangrenous bowel was resected and a primary end-to-end ileosigmoid anastomosis done. Histopathology did not reveal a lead point while the gross examination of the specimen confirmed the diagnosis of intussusception. The enteral feeds were started on postoperative day (POD) five and discharged on POD 10. He was asymptomatic and growing well at 1 month follow-up and still asymptomatic, achieving all his milestones at 6 months of follow-up. Idiopathic ileocolic intussusception should always be included in the differential diagnosis of all neonatal intestinal obstructions.

articles.title: The Postoperative Analgesic Efficacy of Two Bupivacaine Concentrations for Combined Ilioinguinal and Iliohypogastric Nerve Block After Inguinal Hernia Repair Under Spinal Anesthesia: Prospective Double-Blinded, Randomized Research.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of two different concentrations of bupivacaine, specifically 0.25% and 0.5%, used for unilateral ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerve block (IINB) following open inguinal hernia repair (IHR) under spinal anesthesia.
METHODS: A total of 91 patients aged between 21 and 65 years old and scheduled for IHR under spinal anesthesia were included in the final analysis for this randomized double-blinded trial. They were randomly assigned to two groups: Group I (n = 45): IINB (10 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine and 2 mg dexamethasone) and Group II (n = 46): IINB (10 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine and 2 mg dexamethasone). The primary aim was the time to first opioid request after surgery, while secondary endpoints included the numerical rating scores (NRS), the total 24 h morphine consumption postsurgery, and adverse effects.
RESULTS: The time to the first opioid analgesic request was significantly prolonged in Group I (21 ± 3.04 h) as compared to Group II (12 ± 3.4 h), p < 0.001. The total 24-h postoperative morphine consumption was significantly lower in Group I (3 ± 1.5 mg) than in Group II (9 ± 1.7 mg); p > 0.001. The median postoperative NRS pain scores at rest and during mobility were significantly lower in Group I as compared to Group II at 12, 18, and 24 h after surgery, p < 0.001. Patient satisfaction scores were significantly higher in Group I [4 (3-4)] than in Group II [2 (1-3)], p > 0.001. No patients in either group experienced any adverse effect in terms of complications related to nerve block.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing elective unilateral open IHR under spinal anesthesia, ultrasound-guided IINB using 0.5% bupivacaine prolonged the time to first rescue opioid analgesia, and decreased the total 24 h opioid consumption after surgery as compared to 0.25% bupivacaine. Also, it decreased late pain scores and increased patient satisfaction, with no block-related adverse events were observed during the study follow-up period. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05687981.

articles.title: Safe Administration of Minimal-to-Moderate Procedural Sedation and Analgesia: Practical Recommendations From the Taiwan Society of Anesthesiologists.
articles.abstract: Procedural sedation exists on a dynamic continuum. Some patients may rapidly and unintentionally progress to deep sedation or general anesthesia. This study is to establish practical recommendations for enhancing patient safety during minimal-to-moderate procedural sedation and analgesia. The key recommendations are as follows: (1) Risk stratification: High-risk patients require careful evaluation and planning by anesthesiologists, particularly those with an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status ≥ III, obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, an anticipated difficult airway, severe cardiovascular disease, advanced age, or organ failure. (2) Pharmacological stewardship: Sedatives and analgesics should be administered incrementally and carefully titrated to clinical effect, with sufficient time between doses. Close vigilance is required when sedatives and opioids are co-administered because of additive respiratory depression. Given its narrow therapeutic window and the potential for rapid, unintended progression to deep sedation, propofol should be restricted to personnel trained in advanced airway rescue. (3) Continuous monitoring: Continuous assessment of consciousness, airway patency, ventilation, oxygenation, and cardiovascular status is essential. Pulse oximetry and cardiovascular monitoring should be routinely performed, while continuous waveform capnography is recommended during moderate sedation to facilitate early detection of hypoventilation or apnea. Personnel must be prepared to provide immediate airway and respiratory rescue when unintended deep sedation occurs. (4) Post-procedural recovery: Following the procedure, patients should undergo structured recovery assessment using validated criteria, including the Modified Aldrete Score and Post-Anesthetic Discharge Scoring System. These findings suggest that standardized risk assessment, careful drug titration, vigilant monitoring, immediate rescue capability, and structured recovery protocols are essential to minimize sedation-related complications and optimize patient safety.

articles.title: Navigating Severe Aortic Stenosis in Hip Fracture Surgery: Perioperative Management and Surgical Timing.
articles.abstract: Severe aortic stenosis presents a significant challenge in patients requiring urgent hip fracture surgery. Although aortic stenosis increases the risk of cardiovascular complications and mortality, delaying fixation may independently contribute to morbidity, functional decline, and mortality. This creates a dilemma regarding whether to proceed directly to surgery or delay fracture repair for aortic valve intervention. This review examines management of patients with severe aortic stenosis pending urgent hip fracture surgery, with emphasis on timing, preoperative evaluation, anesthetic selection, and hemodynamic management. Current evidence suggests that asymptomatic patients with preserved left ventricular systolic function and stable hemodynamics may often undergo timely fracture fixation with appropriate monitoring. In contrast, symptomatic patients, those with ventricular dysfunction or hemodynamic instability, and patients with particularly severe disease may require evaluation for valvular intervention. When intervention is indicated, transcatheter aortic valve replacement may offer a more rapid treatment in certain patients, while balloon aortic valvuloplasty may serve as a temporizing strategy. For patients proceeding directly to fracture fixation, preservation of preload, systemic vascular resistance, coronary perfusion, and sinus rhythm is essential. Current evidence does not establish a clear superiority of general versus neuraxial anesthesia, supporting individualized anesthetic planning and avoidance of abrupt hemodynamic changes. Ultimately, management should balance the risks of delaying fracture fixation against the risks of surgery through coordinated, multidisciplinary decision-making.

articles.title: Impact of perioperative physical exercise on postoperative pulmonary complications in patients undergoing cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) increase morbidity and hospital stay after cardiac surgery. Perioperative respiratory-focused exercise interventions, including inspiratory muscle training (IMT), incentive spirometry, and breathing exercises, may reduce PPCs, but the effects of these heterogeneous interventions in cardiac surgery patients remain uncertain.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using PRISMA guidelines and included 11 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating perioperative exercise or respiratory-focused interventions administered before and/or after cardiac surgery. The principal components of the interventions included IMT, incentive spirometry, deep breathing exercises, and surgical respiratory re-education exercises. The analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4, with Rayyan used to assist in the screening and selection of studies.
RESULTS: Perioperative exercise or respiratory-focused interventions significantly reduced selected pulmonary outcomes, including PPC grade ≥2 (RR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.33-0.67), pneumonia (RR = 0.56, 95% CI: 0.38-0.83), and atelectasis (RR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.24-0.64). No statistically significant effects were observed for pleural effusion, respiratory failure, hypoxemia episodes, or re-intubation. Mechanical ventilation duration (SMD = -0.70, 95% CI: -1.04 to -0.37), ICU length of stay (SMD = -1.09, 95% CI: -1.81 to -0.36; I 2 = 85%), and hospital length of stay (SMD = -0.70, 95% CI: -0.97 to -0.44; I 2 = 40%) showed reductions. MIP (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: -0.08 to 1.86; I 2 = 94%) and 6MWD (SMD = 0.13, 95% CI: -0.31 to 0.57; I 2 = 34%) did not demonstrate statistically significant improvement when analyzed as separate outcomes. Certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative respiratory-focused exercise interventions may reduce selected postoperative pulmonary complications and may improve some short-term recovery outcomes in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, substantial variation in intervention type, timing, and duration, together with risk of bias and heterogeneity for some outcomes, resulted in moderate to very low certainty of evidence and limits the generalizability of the findings. The available evidence remains insufficient to determine an optimal exercise protocol or to establish consistent improvements in respiratory muscle strength or functional exercise capacity.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261294365, identifier CRD420261294365.

articles.title: CT-based radiomics for interpretable outcome prediction after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prognostic assessment after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) mainly relies on clinical variables and computed tomography (CT) findings, but current models often lack biological interpretability. We developed and validated a clinical-radiomics prognostic model and subsequently performed exploratory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomic characterization of model-defined risk phenotypes.
METHODS: This multicenter cohort from the PROSAH-MPC registry included 879 patients across four hospitals. Patients from the primary center were split into training (n = 637) and internal validation (n = 160) cohorts, while patients from three other centers formed an external validation cohort (n = 82). Admission CT hemorrhagic lesions were automatically segmented using the validated BrainHemoAI platform, and radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics. Clinical, radiomics, and combined clinical-radiomics XGBoost models were developed and interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Risk scores from the clinical-radiomics model were applied to an independent prospective enrichment, gene setCSF​ proteomic cohort to define combined model-based high- and low-risk groups. Gene Ontology (GO)/ Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The combined model yielded AUCs of 0.892 and 0.820 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively. Risk reclassification analyses suggested that radiomic features may provide complementary prognostic information. SHAP identified radiomic heterogeneity and key clinical variables as major predictors. Meanwhile, exploratory CSF proteomic analysis identified candidate differentially expressed proteins and associated pathway signals that differed between groups defined by high and low combined clinical-radiomics risk scores.
CONCLUSIONS: This clinical-radiomics prognostic model enables accurate outcome prediction and provides exploratory biological insight into unfavorable recovery after aSAH, supporting refined risk stratification and potential targeted therapeutic development.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSAH-MPC. NCT05738083. Registered 16 November 2022 - Retrospectively registered, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05738083 .

articles.title: Factors associated with graft rejection after penetrating keratoplasty in mechanical corneal injury.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate factors associated with graft rejection after penetrating keratoplasty in patients with mechanical corneal injury and evaluate their predictive value.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 50 patients with mechanical corneal injury who underwent penetrating keratoplasty between 2019 and 2025. Clinical variables, including onset duration, preoperative treatment, and corneal pathological changes, were analyzed. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression, time-to-event analysis, stratified analysis, mediation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Prolonged onset duration and preoperative corneal ulceration were associated with an increased risk of postoperative graft rejection, whereas preoperative treatment was associated with a reduced risk. With increasing onset duration, corneal neovascularization and fibrosis increased, whereas corneal edema decreased. Mediation analysis showed that these associations were mainly driven by direct effects. Prediction models demonstrated good discriminatory performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged onset duration and preoperative corneal ulceration may be risk factors for postoperative graft rejection in patients with mechanical corneal injury undergoing corneal transplantation, whereas preoperative treatment may be protective. Therefore, early intervention and disease course control are of great importance for improving transplant prognosis. These findings may provide a reference for preoperative risk stratification and perioperative management.

articles.title: The human body as a multi-organ coupled homeostatic organism: the core mechanism of the super minimally invasive surgery paradigm.
articles.abstract: Super minimally invasive surgery (SMIS) has been proposed as a treatment paradigm in which minimally invasive care is evaluated not only by access-related trauma but also by treatment-induced biological disturbance and preservation of organ function. We hypothesize that, when disease-control adequacy is comparable, strategies associated with lower multidimensional homeostatic disturbance will be associated with faster functional recovery and better long-term organ- and patient-centered outcomes. We define an SMIS-concordant strategy by three conditions: adequate disease control; lower measurable treatment-induced disturbance than an appropriate comparator; and preservation or faster restoration of organ and systemic function. Homeostatic disturbance is operationalized as a multidomain construct that may include inflammatory/immune, neuroendocrine, metabolic/nutritional, organ-specific, barrier/microbiome/circadian, functional, and patient-reported domains. Because no validated universal score, weighting scheme, or threshold is available, we propose a comparative measurement matrix rather than a new composite index. The framework yields three falsifiable predictions: SMIS-concordant strategies should produce less early biological disturbance, support a faster return toward baseline, and provide prognostic information for long-term recovery beyond conventional perioperative measures. Early gastric cancer illustrates the approach: in guideline-eligible patients, endoscopic resection preserves the stomach and is associated with lower procedural burden and better quality of life, while preliminary proteomic data suggest less postoperative immune-inflammatory perturbation; gastrectomy remains indicated when curative criteria are not met. SMIS is therefore presented as an integrative treatment-decision framework that requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Cipepofol combined with esketamine for anesthetic management of patients with extensive severe burns: a retrospective case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with extensive severe burns are prone to both hypermetabolic tachycardia and anesthesia-induced hypotension, and their pain is often inadequately controlled with opioids alone. Cipepofol, a novel intravenous hypnotic structurally related to propofol, has shown greater hemodynamic stability than propofol, whereas esketamine provides analgesia and has indirect sympathomimetic activity. We evaluated the feasibility of a cipepofol-esketamine total intravenous anesthesia regimen in this high-risk population.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective case series included consecutive adults with extensive severe burns (total body surface area ≥50% or full-thickness burn ≥20%) undergoing debridement, escharectomy, or skin grafting. Patient characteristics, postoperative complications, and the Day 28/pre-discharge global analgesic assessment were summarized for seven patients. Hemodynamics, bispectral index values, and rescue analgesic use were summarized across 16 procedures, while paired cortisol concentrations were analyzed for 12 procedures. Acute pain data were limited to event-triggered numerical rating scale scores recorded at rescue.
RESULTS: Seven male patients (mean age, 45.0 ± 11.1 years; mean total body surface area burned, 73.4 ± 17.2%) underwent 16 procedures. Heart rate (HR) was lower after incision. At 90 min, among 10 contributing procedures, the mean within-procedure HR change was -22.8 beats/min (95% CI, -30.4 to -15.1), while the mean arterial pressure (MAP) change was -11.1 mmHg (95% CI, -23.0 to 0.9). Variable sample sizes and wide blood-pressure confidence intervals limited interpretation. Bispectral index values were between 40 and 60 for 65.3 ± 21.0% of valid maintenance time. Rescue analgesia was required after 6/16 procedures, with event-triggered pain scores of 4-6. The late global analgesic rating was excellent or good in all seven patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Cipepofol-esketamine-based multimodal total intravenous anesthesia was feasible in this small series. Prespecified hypotension was common and was managed with intermittent norepinephrine boluses without continuous infusion. The observed arterial pressure profile reflects both the anesthetic regimen and active vasopressor management. With four agents co-administered and no comparator, the contribution of individual agents cannot be isolated. These descriptive findings establish neither comparative safety nor acute analgesic efficacy and require prospective controlled evaluation.

articles.title: Locking plate fixation with cerclage augmentation and bone grafting for Vancouver B2 periprosthetic femoral fractures around cementless stems: a surgical option in elderly high-risk patients unsuitable for revision arthroplasty (mid-term outcomes).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the mid-term clinical and radiographic outcomes of open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) with a locking plate, cerclage wires, and bone grafting for Vancouver B2 periprosthetic femoral fractures (PFF) in elderly, high-risk patients who are unsuitable for revision arthroplasty after primary cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 28 elderly patients with Vancouver B2 PFFs treated with locking plate fixation and cerclage wiring. Patient demographics, operative parameters (time, blood loss), and hospital stay were recorded. Fracture healing time, Harris Hip Score (HHS), and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) were evaluated preoperatively and at the final follow-up, with VAS also assessed postoperatively. Complications were documented.
RESULTS: The mean follow-up was 63.86 months (range, 24-120). During the follow-up period, three patients died due to advanced age, and two patients were lost to follow-up because of changes in contact information or failure to attend scheduled visits. Mean operative time was 176.32 ± 20.46 min, and mean blood loss was 358.93 ± 188.59 mL. All fractures united, with a mean healing time of 3.89 months. HHS improved significantly from 43.93 preoperatively to 90.32 at final follow-up (P < 0.001), and VAS decreased from 4.11 ± 1.03 to 0.43 ± 0.50 (P < 0.001). Postoperative DVT occurred in 7 patients (mean onset: 7.71 ± 1.11 days), including one case progressing to pulmonary embolism requiring an inferior vena cava filter; all were successfully managed with rivaroxaban. Prosthesis subsidence was observed in 5 patients, of whom 3 remained stable and were monitored, while 2 with delayed union underwent revision with distally fixed cementless stems. No other complications (infection, nonunion, implant failure, loosening, or osteolysis) were observed in the remaining patients. Kaplan-Meier analysis, with revision as the endpoint, estimated a 5-year survival rate of 92.3% (95% CI, 73.8%∼97.9%).
CONCLUSION: For selected high-risk elderly patients with Vancouver B2 PFF who are unsuitable for revision arthroplasty, ORIF with locking plate, cerclage wires, and bone grafting appears to be a potentially viable treatment option. Its success depends on rigorous case selection and standardized perioperative management, and further long-term prospective studies are warranted to confirm its durability.

articles.title: The Fate of Status 6 Candidates on Waitlist for Heart Transplant: A Nationwide Analysis.
Ultrasound-Guided Assessment of Gastric Volumes in Paediatric Patients Receiving Five Percent Dextrose Water Versus Plain Water Preoperatively: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative fasting guidelines recommend clear fluids up to two hours before surgery to prevent prolonged fasting times and pulmonary aspiration. Gastric ultrasound is a safe, valid, non-invasive and readily available tool that can be used to look for the residual gastric volumes (GVs) and to confirm the fasting status in case of doubtful fasting period. The aim of this study was to evaluate ultrasound-guided assessment of GVs in children receiving either 5% dextrose water or plain water preoperatively, and to look for the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) and thirst.
METHODS: The study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee and registered with CTRI with trial number CTRI/2023/09/057732. This prospective, randomised, controlled study included 60 American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) I-II paediatric patients (5-12 years) undergoing elective surgery. Gastric antral cross-sectional area (CSA) and volumes were measured. Patients received 3 mL/kg of either 5% dextrose water (Group A) or plain water (Group B) two hours before surgery. The primary outcome was the measurement of GV at baseline and two hours. Ultrasound assessments were performed at baseline and two hours after fluid intake. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of PONV and thirst in the postoperative period.
RESULTS: The study found no significant differences in antral CSA or volume between the two groups at baseline and two hours. At baseline, CSA: t = -0.900, p=0.372, effect size (Cohen's d) = -0.232 (95% CI: -0.580 to 0.220); GV: t= -0.800, p=0.427, effect size (Cohen's d) = -0.207 (95% CI: -3.660 to 1.569). After two hours, CSA: t=0.579, p=0.565, effect size (Cohen's d) = 0.149 (95% CI: -0.268 to 0.486); GV: t = -0.561, p=0.577, effect size (Cohen's d) = -0.145 (95% CI: -3.396 to 1.910). PONV was absent in both groups, and the prevalence of thirst did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSION: Administering 5% dextrose water or plain water two hours preoperatively has similar effects on residual GVs in paediatric patients. The choice between the two fluids did not influence PONV or thirst significantly.

articles.title: Caprini Score-Guided Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Spine Instrumentation Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Mechanical vs. Pharmacomechanical Strategies Across Etiological Subgroups.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), is a major source of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing spine surgery. Although various risk factors for developing VTE have been identified, pharmacological prophylaxis is used selectively in spine surgery due to the risk of epidural hematoma. We report our institutional experience with VTE prophylaxis following spine instrumentation surgery across all surgical etiologies.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study of patients ≥18 years of age who underwent spine instrumentation surgery for degenerative, traumatic, or oncologic pathologies, and patients of all ages who underwent surgery for spinal deformity over a three-year period was performed. Caprini VTE risk score was used for individual risk stratification.
RESULTS: A total of 265 patients were included: degenerative (n=174, 65.7%), trauma (n=45, 17.0%), deformity (n=33, 12.5%), and tumor (n=13, 4.9%). The overall mean age was 46.1±17.5 years, and there were 133 male patients (50.2%). Significant differences existed across groups in age (Kruskal-Wallis H=97.4, p<0.001), index procedure characteristics, and VTE risk profiles. Mechanical prophylaxis alone was employed in 212 patients (80.0%), while 53 patients (20.0%) received combined pharmacomechanical prophylaxis. No patient (0%) in the mechanical-only group developed a perioperative VTE event or postoperative hematoma. One patient (1.9%) in the combined pharmacomechanical group developed a postoperative PE, arising in the context of a preoperative proximal DVT. Firth's penalized logistic regression identified polytrauma (OR 29.0, 95% CI 3.3-3835.0; p=0.001), Caprini score ≥7 (OR 8.8, 95% CI 3.8-20.9; p<0.001), and prior VTE history (OR 61.8, 95% CI 5.7-8406.4; p<0.001) as independent predictors of combined prophylaxis receipt.
CONCLUSION: Mechanical prophylaxis, implemented as part of a structured protocol that included sequential pneumatic compression devices and standardized postoperative care, was associated with low VTE risk following spine instrumentation surgery. Individualized risk stratification using validated tools such as the Caprini score, combined with selective pharmacomechanical prophylaxis in high-risk patients, may optimize outcomes in this population. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Management of severe valvular heart disease in patients with active cancer: a French multidisciplinary position paper.
articles.abstract: The co-existence of valvular heart disease (VHD) and active cancer presents a unique clinical challenge, necessitating an individualized multidisciplinary strategy to balance oncologic treatment urgency with cardiovascular risk. The indication, optimal timing, and modality of VHD intervention in patients with active cancer remain unclear, particularly given the risks of cancer treatment-related cardiac dysfunction, perioperative complications, delays in oncologic therapy, and the cancer prognosis. This multidisciplinary position paper aims to provide evidence-based suggestions on the management of severe VHD in active cancer patients, focusing on (i) risk stratification of VHD in cancer patients, including the impact of chemotherapies, targeted therapies, and non-cardiac surgery, (ii) indication and timing considerations for cardiac intervention to minimize oncologic treatment delays, and (iii) comparison of surgical vs percutaneous interventions, highlighting patient selection criteria. A conservative approach should be discussed insofar as it does not limit access to optimal oncology care. Percutaneous interventions should be favoured when feasible to minimize oncologic delays (<4 weeks), while surgical approaches remain essential in select cases with anatomical contraindications. Future research should focus on prospective studies.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

articles.title: Optimising glycaemic control in cardiac surgery: narrative review and author recommendations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Diabetes and peri-operative hyperglycaemia are associated with increased morbidity and mortality following cardiac surgery. Despite this, specific guidance on peri-operative glycaemic management during cardiac surgery is lacking in United Kingdom (UK) and Europe. This narrative review presents evidence-based author recommendations for glycaemic control during adult cardiac surgery for those with, and without diagnosed diabetes.
METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted using PubMed (1946-2025) and Embase (1974-2025), supplemented by Web of Science, Google Scholar, and thesis repositories. Studies reporting outcomes relating to diabetes status, HBA1C, and/or blood glucose were included.
RESULTS: Our recommendations include:- evaluating HbA1c in all patients referred for cardiac surgery, regardless of diabetes status; HbA1c target of 58 mmol/mol (7.5%) for patients with diabetes having elective cardiac surgery, maintenance of intra-operative blood glucose between 6-10 mmol/L (110-180 mg/dL) for all patients, and moderate rather than intensive peri-operative glycaemic control. We recommend patients with peri-operative hyperglycaemia be assessed by in-patient diabetes specialist team if available, and/or following discharge. All cardiac surgery hospitals in time, should aim to have a dedicated cardiac surgical diabetes working group, responsible for all cardiac surgery diabetes patients, and national outcome reporting.
CONCLUSIONS: Lack of consensus on peri-operative diabetes management for cardiac surgery exists in the UK and Europe. Our practical recommendations, including universal HbA1c screening and glycaemic control targets, seek to standardize peri-operative management, improve clinical outcomes, and improve outcome reporting for this expanding vulnerable patient group.

articles.title: Effect of megadose vitamin C in patients with sepsis: the CEMVIS randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous randomized trials of vitamin C in sepsis have reported conflicting findings, but whether the effect of vitamin C varies according to septic shock status remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the effect of megadose vitamin C in sepsis and explore whether treatment effect differed according to septic shock status.
METHODS: CEMVIS was a multicenter, randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted in four tertiary hospitals in China. Adults meeting Sepsis-3 criteria were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive intravenous vitamin C (12 g every 12 h for 4 days) or placebo using stratified randomization according to septic shock status. Patients were analyzed according to the modified intention-to-treat principle. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.
RESULTS: Between Feb 8, 2022, and Dec 25, 2024, 114 patients in the vitamin C group and 117 in the placebo group were included in the modified intention-to-treat population. 28-day mortality did not differ significantly between groups (35/114 [30.7%] vs 36/116 [31.0%]; odds ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.56-1.74; p = 0.97). No significant differences were observed in the duration of mechanical ventilation, vasopressor therapy, and renal replacement therapy, or in changes in SOFA scores over 96 hours. Prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant interaction according to septic shock status (P for interaction = 0.026), with the treatment effects on 28-day mortality numerically favoring vitamin C among patients without septic shock (15.4% vs 34%) and numerically favoring placebo among those with septic shock (38.7% vs 29%). Hypernatremia occurred more frequently in the vitamin C group (40/114 [35.1%] vs 24/117 [20.5%]; p = 0.02). Exploratory restricted cubic spline analyses showed that increasing lactate levels were associated with a progressive shift in treatment effect from potential benefit toward potential harm. Post hoc Bayesian analyses further provided probabilistic characterization of the potential treatment effect according to septic shock status.
CONCLUSIONS: The results of this trial do not support the routine use of megadose vitamin C to reduce 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis. Treatment effects may vary according to septic shock status.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov on 3 January 2022 (identifier: NCT05194189).

articles.title: Learning curve and hospital resource utilization of unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar decompression: a CUSUM analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) surgery has been increasingly adopted for lumbar degenerative diseases; however, its learning curve and impact on healthcare resource utilization remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted in 37 consecutive patients who underwent UBE lumbar decompression by a single surgeon. Operative time per level was evaluated using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis. Comparisons were performed between the earlier and later phases according to the CUSUM-derived transition point. Correlation, multivariable regression, and sensitivity analyses evaluated the relationships between operative efficiency, hospitalization parameters, and healthcare costs.
RESULTS: CUSUM analysis demonstrated an apparent transition in operative efficiency at Case 24. Operative time per level was significantly shorter in the later phase (144.8 ± 45.3 vs. 93.9 ± 25.9 min, p < 0.001), and multivariable regression confirmed that increasing surgical experience was independently associated with shorter operative time per level after adjustment for age, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, and number of operated levels. No statistically significant between-phase differences were observed in total length of stay, postoperative length of stay, total hospitalization cost, or DPC reimbursement. By contrast, adjusted multivariable analysis showed that increasing case number was independently associated with shorter total length of stay, but not postoperative length of stay. Cost structure analysis showed no significant between-phase differences in individual cost components. Sensitivity analyses using alternative CUSUM cutoffs yielded consistent results for the primary outcome. Hospitalization duration was strongly associated with total hospitalization cost (ρ = 0.914, p < 0.001) and DPC reimbursement (ρ = 0.892, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Operative efficiency improved progressively with increasing surgical experience in UBE lumbar decompression. However, no statistically significant between-phase differences were observed in hospitalization parameters or healthcare costs. Hospitalization duration showed the strongest association with healthcare expenditure, suggesting that perioperative management and discharge planning may influence healthcare resource utilization more than operative efficiency alone.

articles.title: Modified percutaneous vertebroplasty with bilateral cannulated screws and staged cement injection for stage I and II Kummell's disease: a mid-to-long term follow-up study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kummell's disease (KD) is a delayed post-traumatic vertebral osteonecrosis often complicated by intravertebral vacuum cleft (IVC), cement loosening, and progressive vertebral collapse after conventional percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) or kyphoplasty. This study introduces a modified PVP technique using bilateral cannulated screws and staged cement injection for stage I and II KD, and evaluates its safety, feasibility, and mid-to-long-term clinical and radiological outcomes.
METHODS: A total of 38 patients with stage I (n = 18) or stage II (n = 20) KD were retrospectively enrolled. All underwent a modified procedure under local anesthesia: bilateral pedicle placement of headless cannulated screws, transmidline cement delivery using a steerable cannula (Ascend™), and staged injection (high-viscosity cement followed by low-viscosity cement). Clinical outcomes were assessed by visual analogue scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Radiological outcomes included anterior vertebral height (AVH) and Cobb angle. Evaluations were performed preoperatively, at postoperative day 1, 6 months, 12 months, and at final follow-up (mean 17.2 months). Complications were recorded.
RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed postoperatively and maintained throughout follow-up. VAS decreased from 6.89 ± 0.87 preoperatively to 1.26 ± 0.61 at final follow-up (P < 0.001). ODI improved from 69.58 ± 9.24% to 17.89 ± 7.03% (P < 0.001). AVH and Cobb angle were both significantly restored at day 1 and remained stable without progressive kyphosis or height loss. Cement extravasation occurred in 15.8% and adjacent vertebral fracture in 5.3%. Stage I patients received larger cement volume than stage II (6.83 ± 1.17 vs. 5.78 ± 1.12 mL, P = 0.008), but final outcomes did not differ between groups (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The modified PVP combining bilateral cannulated screws, steerable cement delivery, and staged injection is safe and feasible for stage I and II KD. It provides sustained pain relief, functional improvement, and durable vertebral height and kyphosis correction, potentially preventing cement loosening and vertebral re-collapse.

articles.title: Frailty and Clinical Outcomes After Isolated Tricuspid Valve Surgery: Implications for Future Transcatheter Tricuspid Intervention Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is recognized as a determinant of outcomes following valvular interventions; however, data on its prevalence and prognostic impact in patients undergoing isolated tricuspid valve (TV) surgery remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the prevalence of frailty and its association with outcomes in patients undergoing isolated TV surgery.
METHODS: Among Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥65 years who underwent isolated TV surgery (2017-2023), frailty was assessed using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score and categorized as low (<5), intermediate (5-15), and high (>15). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 1 and 5 years. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital and 30-day mortality and prolonged hospitalization (≥10 days). Multivariable Cox models assessed associations between frailty and outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 8179 patients (mean age 76 ± 7 years, 58% female), 58%, 33%, and 9% were classified as low, intermediate, and high frailty risk. Increasing frailty was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, and prolonged hospitalization (all p < 0.001). One-year mortality was 12.2% (95% CI: 11.3-13.2), 25.8% (95% CI: 24.1-27.6), and 35.8% (95% CI: 32.4-39.5) across frailty groups, with similar gradients observed at 5 years (all p < 0.001). Beyond 1 year, mortality increased more steeply in intermediate- and high-frailty patients. After adjustment, intermediate (hazard ratio: 1.18 [95% CI: 1.04-1.33]) and high frailty (hazard ratio: 1.32 [95% CI: 1.11-1.57]) remained independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Among Medicare beneficiaries undergoing isolated TV surgery, frailty is common and independently associated with increased perioperative and long-term mortality. Routine frailty assessment may improve risk stratification and inform patient selection, with potential implications for clinical trial design.

articles.title: Contemporary transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) practice in Europe: insights from the second European TAVI pathway registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) continues to expand rapidly, with over 100 000 procedures now performed annually in Europe. This growth highlights the need to optimize patient selection and procedural workflows to ensure quality and cost-effective care.
AIMS: The Second European TAVI Pathway Study aimed to describe current TAVI practices across Europe and assess changes since the 2022 edition.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Between January and May 2025, TAVI operators from 42 European countries were invited to complete an online survey concerning their centre's current practice.Responses were received from 202 centres in 37 different countries, performing 44 089 TAVI procedures in 2024 (mean 218 per centre; interquartile range [IQR] 99-284). Dedicated Heart Valve Clinics are present in 54%, and supportive staff in 52%. Most centres (81%) use a Heart Team approach, with age thresholds for TAVI typically set at ≥75 (64%) or ≥80 (26%) years. On-site cardiac surgery is available in 96% of participating centres. Local anaesthesia alone (33%) or with conscious sedation (63%) is the most common for routine transfemoral TAVI. Secondary radial access (70%) and left ventricular wire pacing (59%) have increased from 48% and 43% in 2022, respectively. Early mobilization (≤8 hours) is routine in 63% of cases, and early discharge (≤2 days) rose from 43% in 2022 to 51% in 2024. However, the proportion of centres reporting waiting times >3 months increased from 19% to 26%.
CONCLUSION: Minimalist TAVI approaches are widely adopted across Europe, with increasing rates of early discharge. However, extended waiting times remain a significant challenge.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

articles.title: Clinical practical advice for anaesthetic management of adults with congenital heart disease undergoing non-cardiac surgery: A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Working Group on Adult Congenital Heart Disease, the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care, the European Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and the International Society of Adult Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients often require non-cardiac surgery (NCS) and the need of such interventions is growing as the population ages. The intricacies inherent to their distinct physiology pose ACHD patients at a higher risk of perioperative complications, perioperative mortality, longer length of stay, and higher hospital charges compared with the general population. While 2020 ESC guidelines comprehensively address most aspects of ACHD care, they do not cover this specific area. Furthermore, although risk assessment for non-cardiac surgery is included in the 2022 ESC Guidelines on Cardiovascular Assessment and Management of Patients Undergoing Non-Cardiac Surgery, the unique pathophysiology of ACHD patients necessitates tailored considerations. The aim of this clinical consensus statement is to address the specific situations and needs of ACHD patients undergoing NCS from a multidisciplinary and practical point of view and to describe the organization of care for this complex group of patients. A group of experienced professionals from 4 cardiology and anaesthesiology scientific societies [the ESC Working Group on ACHD, the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC), the European Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (EACTAIC), and the International Society of Adult Congenital Heart Disease (ISACHD)] have evaluated the available scientific data and reached expert consensus in areas of gaps in evidence.
articles.journal: Eur Heart J Valvular Struct Heart Dis

articles.title: Perioperative management of proximal femur fractures in patients on direct oral anticoagulants.
articles.abstract: Fractures of the proximal femur represent one of the most common urgent diagnoses in geriatric patients and are associated with significant short- and long-term mortality. With the growing number of very elderly and polymorbid patients, the proportion of individuals treated with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) is also increasing, which substantially influences perioperative decision-making. Delaying surgery beyond 24 hours is clearly associated with worse outcomes; therefore, it is essential to establish management strategies that prevent residual anticoagulant activity from being misinterpreted as a reason to postpone surgery. Available data indicate that routine coagulation tests (INR, aPTT) are not suitable for assessing the effect of DOACs and should not constitute a barrier to urgent surgical treatment. Clinical decision-making should be based primarily on the time since the last dose, renal function, and in unclear situations, on targeted laboratory assays. The pharmacokinetic properties of DOACs further support the fact that in most patients, surgery can be performed safely within a relatively short time frame without the need for routine reversal. Choice of anesthesia (regional versus general) does not significantly affect key clinical outcomes, including mortality or incidence of postoperative delirium. In DOAC users, however, neuraxial techniques face safety limitations and may prolong the time to surgery. General anesthesia supplemented with peripheral nerve blocks therefore represents a pragmatic strategy enabling early and safe surgical management. A major challenge in current practice remains the high variability of perioperative protocols. Implementation of a unified, algorithm-driven approach may reduce unnecessary delays, standardize clinical decision-making, and improve treatment outcomes in this rapidly growing patient population.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane Block in Adults with Severe Obesity Undergoing Laparoscopic Bariatric Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Bariatric surgery is a foremost treatment for obesity, but post-operative pain management can be complex. Port-site infiltration is used regularly, but many patients still require opioids, which may have risks with the population with obesity. The transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block has been proposed as an alternative, but current evidence is inconsistent. This meta-analysis compares the TAP block with port-site infiltration in bariatric surgery patients. Five studies with 706 patients were included (TAP = 307, control = 399). At 24 h, pain scores favored TAP (MD = -3.56; 95% CI: -5.96 to -1.16), but there was no significant difference at 6, 12, or 48 h. TAP block may provide better pain relief at 24 h, but further trials are needed.

articles.title: Prophylactic Intraoperative Norepinephrine Infusion during Major Noncardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and GRADE assessed Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prophylactic norepinephrine infusion has gained increasing attention to prevent intraoperative hypotension during major non-cardiac surgery, but its effect on haemodynamic stability, tissue perfusion, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through May 9, 2026 for randomised trials comparing prophylactic norepinephrine with standard reactive management. Outcomes included change in serum lactate, haemodynamic measures, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes, including complications and mortality. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed.
RESULTS: Eleven trials (1688 patients) were included. Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a lower rise in lactate (mean difference (MD) -0.13 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.01; P = 0.03; I²=67.2%), higher post-induction mean arterial pressure (MD 10.79 mmHg, 95% CI 5.53 to 16.04; P < 0.01; I²=95.3%), higher postoperative mean arterial pressure (MD 2.78 mmHg, 95% CI 0.63 to 4.92; P = 0.01; I²=69.8%). Prophylactic norepinephrine use was associated with lower crystalloid administration (MD-548.22 mL, 95% CI -1087.16 to -9.28, P = 0.05, I²=99%) although substantial heterogeneity and protocol-driven differences limit interpretation. Exploratory analyses suggested lower incidences of myocardial infarction (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-0.98), pneumonia (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.36-0.95), and 30 day-surgical site infection (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.97). No statistically significant differences were demonstrated for acute kidney injury, atelectasis, length of stay, or mortality. Certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. TSA indicated insufficient evidence to establish a definitive treatment effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a statistically significant but small reduction in intraoperative lactate rise, higher post-induction and post-operative mean arterial pressures. Postoperative complication findings remain exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered randomised trials.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD420261345140).

articles.title: An absent or weak cough doubles the odds of extubation failure after acute brain injury: an updated systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To update the evidence on neurological and respiratory predictors of extubation failure after acute brain injury and to compare the two families, as pre-specified.
METHODS: Five databases were searched through July 2026 for studies relating a predictor measured at or near extubation to extubation failure in ventilated adults with acute brain injury. Screening and extraction were done in duplicate; risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Adjusted estimates were pooled after harmonising outcome framing and predictor coding, restricting each pool to one scale and instrument, with random-effects (REML, Hartung-Knapp) and Bayesian hierarchical models. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: 98 studies (24 505 patients) yielded 415 predictor-outcome estimates; 194 carried a confidence interval, and 6 studies contributed to pooled adjusted estimates. Absent or weak cough was associated with failure (4 studies; OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.46-4.19; posterior median 2.55, 95% CrI 1.54-4.71, P(OR > 1) = 0.999; I² = 0%; moderate certainty), in line with the previous synthesis; in an illustrative projection at a 19% failure rate, about 30% versus 15%. Below-threshold motor GCS was associated with failure in two concordant studies (posterior median OR 5.99, 2.42-16.1; very low certainty). The pre-specified comparison between families could not be validly estimated from published data.
CONCLUSIONS: An absent or weak cough at extubation is the best-supported single bedside predictor of failure after acute brain injury and should be assessed with secretions, swallowing and consciousness. Fewer than one in ten eligible studies are poolable, mainly for remediable reporting reasons; a minimum reporting set is proposed.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261442541 (submitted 6 July 2026; registered 2 September 2026). Protocol v2.3 was prepared before the searches; the PROSPERO amendment and all deviations are listed in Supplementary Table S1.
REPORTING GUIDELINE: PRISMA 2020 [1].

articles.title: Prognostic performance of the Simplified Acute Physiology Score models II and 3 in critical care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of external validation studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic performance of the Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) models has not been thoroughly investigated. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed SAPS mortality prediction metrics across diverse intensive care unit (ICU) populations worldwide.
METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were queried for external validations of SAPS in ICU settings. The "CHARMS" and "PROBAST" tools were applied for data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment, respectively. C-statistics and observed-to-expected ratios were summarised using random-effects models. Heterogeneity sources were explored using meta-regression. Evidence certainty was evaluated using the "GRADE" approach. PROSPERO registration CRD42023446721.
RESULTS: Ninety studies (89 articles) were reviewed, totalling 565,994 ICU patients across 87 countries, and validating the SAPS II (n = 35), SAPS 3 global (n = 37), and/or SAPS 3 region-specific (n = 28) models. Endpoints were in-hospital (n = 70), in-ICU (n = 16), and/or 28/30-day mortality (n = 12). Nine studies performed recalibrations of SAPS II and 7 of SAPS 3. The meta-analyses provided high-certainty evidence of excellent discriminatory ability across all SAPS models in predicting in-hospital mortality, whereas data on unsatisfactory overall calibration were graded as low certainty. Successful recalibration was graded as high certainty for SAPS II and moderate certainty for SAPS 3. For ICU and 28/30-day mortality, the evidence was low to very low certainty for all SAPS models. Five decision curve analyses were conducted in three studies, all yielding positive net benefit across meaningful risk thresholds.
CONCLUSIONS: SAPS models remain reliable as mortality risk-ranking tools in critical care. With adequate sample sizes, local recalibrations and dynamic updating of in-hospital mortality predictions are essential to ensure clinical utility.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42023446721.

articles.title: Scoping review on dosing of anaesthetic and perioperative drugs in patients with obesity: which body weight for which molecule.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of obesity is rising. Patients with obesity are increasingly exposed to anaesthesia, critical care, and perioperative pharmacotherapy. Obesity alters drug pharmacokinetics in a non-linear, drug-specific manner, so that simply scaling doses to total body weight (TBW) exposes patients to overdose or underdose. A recurring clinical question is therefore: which body weight descriptor should be used for which molecule?
METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. We synthesized pharmacokinetic evidence, recent meta-analyses, and French and European guidelines on dose adjustment in adults with obesity for five drug classes of anaesthesia and critical care: hypnotics, opioids, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA), perioperative antibiotics, and non-opioid analgesics. We summarised the recommended dosing weight for each molecule in a table and a figure.
RESULTS: No single weight descriptor applies. Lipophilic induction agents (propofol), most opioids (alfentanil, fentanyl, sufentanil), and non-depolarising NMBA are best dosed on lean or ideal body weight, whereas succinylcholine, neuromuscular reversal, and aminoglycosides use total or adjusted body weight. Maintenance of hypnosis and pain management in the post-anaesthesia care unit are titrated to monitored effect. Cephalosporin-based antibiotic prophylaxis relies on fixed doses (e.g., cefazolin 2 g) up to high body mass index values due to their hydrophilic properties. Paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are given at standard doses and never scaled to TBW. Findings are consolidated in a single bedside reference table.
CONCLUSION: Dosing in obesity must be molecule-specific, guided by the relevant weight descriptor and by intraoperative monitoring rather than by TBW alone.

Esketamine Mitigates Perioperative Neurocognitive Impairment Through Attenuation of Blood-Brain Barrier Injury By Downregulating C3 Expression in Aged Mice.
articles.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are common complications in elderly patients, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a key contributing factor. This study investigated the effects of esketamine on postoperative cognitive function, BBB integrity, and complement component C3 (C3) expression in aged mice. Fifteen-month-old male C57BL/6 mice underwent laparotomy under sevoflurane anesthesia to establish a PND model. Animals were randomly assigned to five groups: control (CON), esketamine alone (ES), PND model (PND), PND with esketamine treatment (PND + ES), and PND with esketamine plus exogenous C3 (PND + ES + C3). Cognitive function was assessed using the Morris water maze and Y-maze tests.
