This association was directionally consistent in an exploratory analysis adjusted for international normalized ratio, bilirubin concentration, platelet count, heparin dose, and weight. Hemorrhage was not associated with aPTT < anti-Xa discordance. Neither pattern was associated with thrombosis. Discordance patterns varied by weight, bilirubin concentration, platelet count, heparin dose, and intensive care unit type.
CONCLUSIONS: Among adult ECMO patients receiving heparin, aPTT > anti-Xa discordance was associated with increased hemorrhage risk. Simultaneous aPTT and anti-Xa assessment may provide clinically meaningful information beyond either assay alone.

articles.title: Simulation-Based Training for the Anesthetic Management of Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices Undergoing Gastrointestinal Endoscopy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Improved survival among left ventricular assist device (LVAD) patients has increased the need for non-cardiac procedures. Given that gastrointestinal bleeding remains a major adverse event in LVAD patients, colonoscopies and endoscopies encompass many of the non-cardiac procedures performed in this population. Limited formal training on anesthetic management of LVAD patients can reduce provider confidence and preparedness. A prospective educational intervention study was developed in the form of a structured, simulation-based educational course, created to enhance expertise and improve provider confidence.
METHODS: The designed program combines an online module and four in-person simulation scenarios focused on anesthesia for endoscopy cases in LVAD patients, followed by evaluation of changes in knowledge, confidence, and simulation performance. Participants completed a pre-training knowledge test and a confidence survey prior to any intervention. Participants then completed pre-course training modules and performed Simulation 1, followed by a post-training knowledge test, and a confidence survey. They returned 4-8 months later for a knowledge retention test and confidence survey followed immediately by Simulation 2. Pre- and post-training scores were compared using t-tests for the total cohort and novice/experienced subgroups.
RESULTS: 44 participants enrolled; 41 completed all assessments. Passing rates of scenarios 1-4 increased from 48.8%, 82.9%, 36.6% and 48.8% to 97.6%, 100%, 80.05%, and 65.9% respectively between their initial and second attempt. Knowledge scores significantly improved after completion of Simulation 1 (p <0.001) but were not significantly different from post-Simulation 1 scores at Simulation 2 (p =0.60). Confidence scores increased from 2.0 ± 0.6 to 3.7 ± 0.6 after Simulation 1 (p <0.001). Confidence declined slightly before Simulation 2 (p <0.02) but remained higher than pre-Simulation 1 (p <0.001).
DISCUSSION: Simulation-based education significantly improved anesthesia providers' knowledge and confidence in managing LVAD patients. While some skill decay occurred over time, confidence and knowledge remained higher than baseline. This approach demonstrates promise for broader applications in anesthesia training.

articles.title: Ketamine versus Diazepam for Pediatric MRI Sedation in Northern Malawi: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in children requires adequate sedation to ensure procedural success. In resource-limited settings, sedative options are often restricted, and comparative data on ketamine and diazepam are scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and MRI completion rates of ketamine versus diazepam for pediatric sedation at a low-resource hospital in northern Malawi.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study including children aged 0-14 years who underwent MRI with ketamine (n = 20) or diazepam (n = 36) at Mzuzu Central Hospital between August 2025 and March 2026. Sedation success was defined as Ramsay Sedation Score 4-5 with stable vital signs and absence of movement during MRI. Primary outcomes were sedation onset time, sedation success rate, recovery time, adverse events, and MRI completion rates.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Ketamine was associated with a shorter sedation onset (mean 1.55±0.39 min vs 3.43±0.45 min, P < 0.01), higher sedation success rate(19 (95%)vs 24 (67%), P < 0.05), and longer recovery time (mean 58.64±7.14 min vs 43.10±5.04 min, P < 0.01) compared with diazepam. The incidence of adverse events was similar between the two groups, with no severe complications observed. First-pass MRI completion (19 (95%)vs 21 (58%), P < 0.01) and overall scan success rates (20(100%)vs 25(69%), P < 0.05) were higher in the ketamine group.
CONCLUSIONS: In this low-resource setting, ketamine provided faster, more reliable pediatric MRI sedation than diazepam, with higher procedural success and a favorable safety profile. Ketamine may be considered the preferred sedative for pediatric MRI in similar resource-limited hospitals, provided continuous monitoring and anesthetic oversight.

articles.title: A comparative cross-sectional study on the accuracy, readability, and understandability of AI-generated (ChatGPT and Google Gemini) versus traditional patient information sheets for labor epidural analgesia.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated tools are being studied in diverse areas of anesthesia. A labor analgesia (LA) patient information sheet (PIS) forms the foundation to include "a pain free delivery experience" in a parturient's obstetric plan. The present study was planned to compare and evaluate the accuracy, readability, and understandability of the two AI-generated PISs on labor epidural from ChatGPT and Google Gemini (GG) with the human-made, traditional PIS. Ten experts in the field of obstetric anesthesia evaluated the accuracy and completeness of each PIS on labor epidural, both the AI-generated versions, and the traditional PIS based on a Likert scale (from 1 to 10). The readability of each PIS was evaluated by the Flesch Reading Ease. The Patient Materials Education Assessment Tool analysis was performed by all experts for the three drafts. Descriptive statistics were used to calculate the mean scores for accuracy and completeness. A one-way ANOVA followed by post hoc comparisons using the Tukey test was performed to assess statistical differences between the drafts. Inter-rater reliability across the 10 raters was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient. A statistically significant mean difference for both accuracy and completeness was found on comparing the traditional PIS versus GG (P = 0.012). Readability ease and understandability were comparable between drafts. ChatGPT and GG were both more actionable than traditional PIS (P = 0.001). Google Gemini was more accurate, complete, and actionable than traditional PIS but at par with ChatGPT. AI-generated PISs must be reviewed and validated by clinical experts.

articles.title: In pursuit of seeking the ideal combination of fascial plane blocks for breast surgery - A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Despite fascial plane block emergence to the forefront in breast surgeries, individual fascial plane blocks have not lived up as sole analgesia techniques often needing reinforcements. The ideal regional anesthesia techniques involve block combination as an adjunct to general anesthesia often, rather than as a standalone breast block, which led to seek ideal combination of fascial plane blocks for breast surgery.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Studies published in the last decade involving a combination of fascial plane blocks for breast surgery were searched systematically in databases, involving appropriate MeSH terminologies, with inclusion of randomized control studies (RCTs), prospective case series (PCSs), and case reports (CRs). A combination of fascial plane block inclusions were prelaid and nomenclature clarifications put across prior to study initiation.
RESULTS: The review included 34 studies with 10 RCTs, 5 PCSs, and 15 CRs with an inclusion of 747 heterogeneous patients. The combinations involved peri-paravertebral blocks, antero-lateral chest wall blocks, and parasternal block combinations. Three embalmed fresh cadaveric studies and one study involving functional conduction imaging were included. Analgesic efficacy, opioid sparing effect, patient satisfaction, and block performance-related complications were evaluated. Risk of bias (RoB) evaluation was done with RoB2 and ROBINS-I, respectively, toward RCTs and case series. Cadaveric RCTs were evaluated by quality appraisal cadaveric studies and the RoB generic tool.
CONCLUSIONS: Decoding ideal combination needs standardized nomenclature. High thoracic level blocks hold promising future. Combination fascial plane blocks in the form of erector spinae-parasternal, Pectoralis I-serratus anterior plane, and pectoralis II-parasternal block combinations have emerged with favorable results.

articles.title: The 90% effective dose (ED 90) of 0.75% intrathecal ropivacaine for day-care surgery in patients undergoing lower abdominal, inguinal, and urological surgery: Estimation with the biased coin up-and-down sequential method.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The increasing demand for day-care surgeries highlights the necessity for efficient anesthesia techniques. While general anesthesia is often preferred to prevent prolonged motor blockades, spinal anesthesia offers notable advantages, such as enhanced pain management and fewer postoperative complications. Newer local anesthetics such as ropivacaine have renewed the interest in subarachnoid block due to shorter duration of motor blockade and improved safety profile. Our study aimed to determine the effective dosage of intrathecal ropivacaine for lower abdominal surgeries using the biased coin up-and-down method. Our goal was to find a dose that allowed patients to be discharged on the same day.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Forty male patients aged 18-60 years (American Society of Anesthesiologists 1 and 2), with heights between 150 and 160 cm, weighing 50-80 kg, participated in the study. Exclusion criteria included spinal abnormalities, infections, and an expected duration of surgery of more than 2 h. After obtaining informed consent, comprehensive preoperative assessment was conducted. In the operating room, standard monitoring protocols were established, and the first patient received 1.5 mL of 0.75% isobaric ropivacaine. Sensory and motor block levels were assessed, and subsequent doses were adjusted using the biased coin method, with dosage information kept confidential from both patients and surgeons.
RESULTS: The estimated 90% effective dose for 0.75% ropivacaine was 1.91 mL (95% confidence interval: 1.78-1.98 mL). Mean recovery times for sensory and motor functions were 186.4 min (52.07) and 39.2 min (16.68), respectively, with a mean time to meet post anesthesia care unit discharge criteria of 195.7 (41.87) min.
CONCLUSION: Intrathecal ropivacaine enabled rapid recovery, facilitating same-day discharge.

articles.title: Comparison of efficacy of ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group block with and without lateral cutaneous femoral nerve block for postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing fracture hip surgery: A randomized double-blind controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block provides effective analgesia for the anterior hip capsule but does not reliably cover the lateral cutaneous femoral nerve (LCFN). This limitation is important in hip fracture surgeries via lateral or posterolateral incisions, where pain from the lateral thigh remains inadequately controlled. Alternatives such as fascia iliaca or epidural blocks have drawbacks, highlighting the need for improved techniques. Combining PENG with LCFN block may provide more complete analgesia and reduce opioid-related adverse outcomes. This study aimed to compare PENG plus LCFN block with PENG alone in hip fracture surgery. The primary outcome was duration of analgesia; secondary outcomes included Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) scores over 24 hours, Ease of Spinal Positioning (EOSP), postoperative analgesic consumption, quadriceps weakness, and patient satisfaction.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This randomized controlled trial included 46 adult patients scheduled for elective unilateral hip fracture surgery under spinal anesthesia. Patients were randomly allocated to two groups: PE (n = 23) received PENG block, and PL (n = 23) received PENG with LCFN block prior to spinal positioning.
RESULTS: The duration of analgesia was significantly longer in group PL (18.26 ± 5.471 h) compared to group PE (14.96 ± 5.456 h; P = 0.029). NRS scores were significantly lower in group PL at 8 h (P = 0.005), 12 h (P = 0.027), and 24 h (P = 0.033). Additional analgesic requirement within 24 hours was also lower in group PL (P = 0.023). EOSP, Medical Research Council scores, and patient satisfaction were comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: Adding LCFN block to PENG block results in superior and longer-lasting analgesia in hip fracture surgery.

articles.title: Needle Arthroscopy Versus Conventional Arthroscopy for Medial Meniscus Repair: Faster Early Recovery Without Compromising Clinical Outcomes in a Prospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Needle arthroscopy (NA) may reduce surgical trauma compared with conventional arthroscopy (CA), but evidence regarding therapeutic meniscal repair remains limited.
PURPOSE: To compare pain, functional outcomes, and return to work after single-implant repair of selected short medial meniscus tears using NA versus CA.
STUDY DESIGN: Cohort study; Level of evidence, 2.
METHODS: A total of 108 patients with short, localized horizontal or flap medial meniscus tears, estimated intraoperatively at approximately 10 mm or less, were enrolled. Treatment selection followed patient preference (NA, n = 55; CA, n = 53). Two procedures planned as NA were converted to CA and analyzed according to the procedure completed. After 8 patients were lost to follow-up, 100 patients (50 per group) completed a 12-month follow-up. All repairs were performed by 1 surgeon using a single identical all-inside FiberStitch implant and a standardized rehabilitation protocol. Pain was assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS) and function using the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) preoperatively and at 2, 6, and 12 weeks and 6 and 12 months. Return to work was also recorded.
RESULTS: Pain and function improved significantly over time in both groups (P < .001). VAS scores were significantly lower after NA at 2, 6, and 12 weeks (all P < .001) and 6 months (P < .01), with no difference at 12 months. Early differences in KOOS Pain, Symptoms, and Activities of Daily Living favored NA but remained below published minimal clinically important difference thresholds for meniscal repair. Outcomes converged at later follow-up. Return to work was faster after NA (5 vs 7 weeks; P < .001). No reoperations or clinical failures occurred.
CONCLUSION: For selected short medial meniscus tears suitable for single-implant repair, NA was associated with less early postoperative pain and faster return to work than CA, while 12-month functional outcomes were similar.

articles.title: Effect of low-dose esketamine on quality of recovery after gynecologic laparoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although low-dose esketamine has shown analgesic benefits, its effect on the quality of recovery after gynecologic laparoscopy remains unclear.
METHODS: In this double-blind randomized controlled trial, 140 adults with ASA I-II and a BMI of 18.5-30 kg/m² undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopy (hysterectomy, myomectomy, or ovarian cystectomy) were randomly assigned to Group E (esketamine group) or Group C (control group). Patients in Group E received 0.25 mg/kg esketamine bolus after anesthesia induction followed by a continuous infusion of 0.1 mg/kg/h until 15 min before the end of surgery, whereas those in Group C received an equal volume of normal saline. The primary outcome was the total score on the Quality of Recovery-40 questionnaire (QoR-40) at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) scores at rest and during activity at 0, 6, 12, and 24 h postoperatively, tracheal extubation time, rescue analgesic consumption, and the incidences of nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and nightmares.
RESULTS: Group E had significantly higher global QoR-40 scores than Group C at 24 h postoperatively (adjusted mean difference 2.30, 95% CI 0.21 to 4.39; P = 0.034). Pain scores at rest and during activity were lower in Group E at 6 h (rest: mean (SD), 2.28 (1.69) vs. 3.01 (2.09), P = 0.025; activity: 3.03 (1.80) vs. 3.81 (2.08), P = 0.020) and 24 h (rest: 1.88 (1.30) vs. 2.29 (1.32), P = 0.045; activity: 2.56 (1.43) vs. 3.16 (1.60), P = 0.022), but were comparable between groups at 0 h and 12 h. The incidence of dizziness was significantly higher in Group E than in Group C during the PACU period (23.5% vs. 8.7%; risk difference (RD) 14.8%, 95% CI 2.8% to 26.9%; P = 0.033). However, this difference resolved by 24 h postoperatively (25.0% vs. 23.2%; P = 0.962), and no significant differences were observed in other secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose esketamine was associated with a statistically higher QoR-40 score, but the magnitude was below the Minimum Clinically Important Difference (MCID) and therefore may not represent a clinically meaningful improvement in gynecologic laparoscopy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trials Registry ( www.chictr.org.cn , registration number: ChiCTR2300072538, date of registration: 16/06/2023).

articles.title: Needs for preoperative anesthesia communication from the perspectives of older patients and their caregivers: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative anesthesia communication (PAC) is a crucial component of the anesthesia process. However, the specific PAC needs of older patients remain insufficiently understood, and age-related characteristics and cognitive differences further complicate their comprehension of anesthesia-related information. This study aims to systematically explore the current state of PAC awareness and unmet needs among older patients undergoing elective surgery and their family caregivers, with the goal of informing the optimization of PAC processes and improving communication quality.
METHODS: This study adopted a descriptive qualitative design. Purposeful sampling was used to recruit older patients (aged ≥ 65 years) and their family caregivers scheduled for elective surgery at a tertiary hospital between July and September 2025. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to explore their perceptions of the current PAC process and their unmet needs. Interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis, with coding supported by NVivo 12 version xx.
RESULTS: This study recruited 14 older patients and their family caregivers and identified key themes in PAC needs. Through thematic analysis, we identified four themes and nine subthemes, with anesthetic knowledge needs, communication preferences, decision-making needs, and psychosocial support needs as the themes. The subthemes expand upon the main themes. Participants expressed a need for both general information and personalized details tailored to older patients' health conditions. They also expressed a need for improved clinical decision-making, as well as deeper, more comprehensive needs including psychological support.
CONCLUSION: This study enhances understanding of the experience of older patients and family caregivers in the current PAC process and identifies their needs for personalized content, detailed communication, and adapted formats. It also clarifies the collaborative roles of patients, family caregivers and healthcare professionals in PAC, highlighting the importance of multi-party interaction in supporting information comprehension and decision-making. The findings provide a practical basis for optimizing the PAC process. Future work should develop tailored communication aids, such as question prompt lists for older patients, to improve engagement, reduce barriers, alleviate preoperative anxiety, and promote informed decision-making.

articles.title: The effect of a telephonic reminder on fasting duration in children undergoing computed tomography scan under sedation in a resource-limited setting - A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Prolonged preprocedural fasting remains common among children undergoing diagnostic imaging, particularly in low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings where communication challenges and high patient turnover can limit effective counseling. It can lead to increased patient discomfort, dehydration, and hypoglycemia. The aim of the study was to evaluate the effect of a telephonic reminder of fasting instructions to parents of children undergoing computed tomography (CT) scan under sedation on the proportion of children fasting for ≤6 hours.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted in children aged ≤13 years scheduled for a CT scan under sedation. Participants were randomized into two groups in a 1:2 (control: phone) ratio: parents in the control group received written and/or verbal fasting instructions, while those in the phone group additionally received a reminder of the same instructions via a telephonic call and text message one day before the scan. The primary outcome was the proportion of children with fasting duration ≤6 hours. The secondary outcomes included the feasibility of intervention, complications related to prolonged and inadequate fasting, and the proportion of children with delay or cancellation due to inadequate fasting.
RESULTS: A total of 161 children were included - 108 children in the phone group and 53 in the control group. The proportion of children with fasting duration ≤6 hours was higher in the phone group compared to that in the control group by both intention-to-treat analysis (primary analysis) (68.5% vs. 43.4%; P = 0.002) and as-treated analysis (79.5% vs 42.2%; P < 0.001). Delay or cancellation due to inadequate fasting was significantly more frequent in the control group (57% vs 25%; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A telephonic reminder reduced prolonged preprocedural fasting, improved periprocedural comfort, and decreased delays/cancellations in children undergoing CT scans.

articles.title: Erector spinae plane block versus fascia iliaca compartment block for postoperative analgesia in total hip arthroplasty: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is associated with significant postoperative pain, and while regional anesthesia techniques such as fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) and erector spinae plane block (ESPB) are employed to manage postoperative pain, their relative efficacy and safety have not been systematically established. This review aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ESPB and FICB for postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing THA.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, APA PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature were searched from inception to July 30, 2024. Two independent reviewers screened titles, abstracts, and full texts to include randomized trials comparing ESPB and FICB for postoperative analgesia in adult patients undergoing THA. Reference list screening and citation tracking of included studies ensured literature saturation. The primary outcome was 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption measured as morphine equivalents. The secondary outcomes were time to first rescue analgesic requirement, postoperative static and dynamic pain scores, and any block-related adverse effects. A prepiloted data extraction sheet, Risk of Bias 2 tool, GRADE approach, inverse variance meta-analysis, and I2 statistic were used for data extraction, risk of bias assessment, grading certainty of evidence, meta-analysis, and assessing outcome heterogeneity, respectively. Mean (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD) and relative risk (RR) or odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used for continuous and dichotomous outcomes, respectively.
RESULTS: Five studies randomized 280 patients undergoing THA under spinal anesthesia to receive either ultrasound (USG)-guided single shot ESPB (n = 140) or FICB (n = 140). A low to moderate level of evidence indicated no significant difference between ESPB and FICB with respect to 24-hour postoperative oral morphine milligram equivalent consumption (MD 1.23, 95% CI -3.55 to 6.01; P 0.62, I2 = 86%), pain scores at rest at 2 (SMD -0.22, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.21; P 0.31, I2 = 49%), 4 (SMD 0.09, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.58; P 0.70, I2 = 61%), and 24 hours (SMD 0.25, 95% CI -0.01 to 0.51; P 0.06, I2 = 0%) and on movement at 24 hours (SMD 0.14, 95% CI -0.30 to 0.58; P 0.52; I2 = 54%), time to first rescue analgesic requirement in hours (MD -0.77, 95% CI -4.07 to 2.53; P 0.65, I2 = 90%), and postoperative nausea vomiting (Peto's OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.10 to 2.56; P 0.41). A moderate level of evidence indicated ESPB to be associated with significantly earlier onset of ambulation and reduced quadriceps weakness compared to FICB (Peto's OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.42; P 0.0002, I2 = 0%). An NNTH of 4 (95% CI 2 to 7) indicated that one additional patient incurs quadriceps muscle weakness for every four patients receiving FICB rather than ESPB for THA.
CONCLUSIONS: There was no significant difference between ESPB and FICB for postoperative analgesia in terms of postoperative opioid consumption, pain scores, and time to first rescue analgesic requirement based on the current limited evidence, and either type of block can be used for postoperative analgesia in total hip arthroplasty. However, ESPB was associated with reduced quadriceps weakness and faster onset of ambulation as compared to FICB after THA, but the evidence comes from only two studies. Further well conducted and adequately powered randomized controlled trials comparing the two types of blocks are warranted.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD42024551027, dated 09 June 2024.

articles.title: The comparison of total intravenous anesthesia and inhalation anesthesia effects on postoperative recovery by quality of recovery (QoR-40) in septorhinoplasty: a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery is a multidimensional outcome that reflects patients' physical, psychological, and functional well-being after surgery. Although total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) and inhalational anesthesia are widely used for maintenance of general anesthesia, their effects on postoperative recovery quality remain controversial. This study aimed to compare the effects of propofol-based TIVA and sevoflurane-based inhalational anesthesia on postoperative recovery quality in patients undergoing elective septorhinoplasty.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center, assessor-blinded trial, 92 patients scheduled for elective septorhinoplasty under general anesthesia were randomly assigned to receive either propofol-based TIVA or sevoflurane-based inhalational anesthesia. The primary outcome was postoperative recovery quality assessed 24 h after surgery using the Quality of Recovery-40 questionnaire, including both the global score and its five dimensions: physical comfort, emotional state, physical independence, psychological support, and pain. Secondary outcomes included extubation time, recovery time, postoperative pain scores, rescue analgesic requirements, and postoperative nausea and vomiting.
RESULTS: A total of 89 patients completed the study (TIVA, n = 45; inhalational anesthesia, n = 44). Postoperative global Quality of Recovery-40 scores were comparable between the groups (187 [181-192] vs. 184.5 [158.8-192], p = 0.182). No significant differences were observed in any of the five recovery domains. Postoperative pain scores were significantly lower in the TIVA group (3 [1-3] vs. 3 [2-5], p = 0.034). However, rescue analgesic requirements, incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, extubation time, recovery time, and post-anesthesia care unit stay did not differ significantly between groups. Total remifentanil consumption was significantly higher in the TIVA group (p = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Propofol-based TIVA and sevoflurane-based inhalational anesthesia provided comparable postoperative recovery quality following elective septorhinoplasty. Although TIVA was associated with lower postoperative pain scores, this advantage did not result in improved overall recovery quality or other clinically relevant recovery outcomes. These findings suggest that anesthetic maintenance technique alone may have a limited impact on patient-perceived recovery when contemporary perioperative care protocols are applied.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06423313. Registered on May 17, 2024.

articles.title: Thoracoscopic rib fracture fixation versus conventional open rib fracture fixation: a comparative analysis of efficacy based on propensity score matching.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: With advances in minimally invasive techniques, complete video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for rib fixation has demonstrated promising benefits. However, its efficacy relative to conventional open surgery remains controversial. This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes between thoracoscopic and conventional open surgery in patients with multiple rib fractures.
METHODS: A total of 141 patients between January 2016 and January 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Based on the surgical approach, patients were categorized into a minimally invasive cohort (MG)-including the thoracoscopic fixation group (TG) and hybrid fixation group (HG) -and conventional surgery group (CG). Propensity score matching was performed to create balanced cohorts for comparing perioperative outcomes, including hospital stay, chest tube duration, mechanical ventilation duration, ICU stay, and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 33 matched pairs were identified between the MG and the CG. The MG had shorter hospital stay compared with the CG (18.42 ± 11.19 vs. 25.36 ± 15.46 days, P = 0.041), despite longer operative times (284.73 ± 123.83 vs. 214.70 ± 111.56 min, P = 0.019). For the HG and CG, 24 matched pairs were obtained. Patients in the HG also had shorter hospital stay (18.04 ± 11.96 vs. 26.67 ± 14.61 days, P = 0.030). The TG showed a trend toward shorter mechanical ventilation duration compared with the HG, but the difference did not reach statistical significance. The Thoracic Trauma Severity (TTS) score was identified as an independent risk factor for postoperative pulmonary infiltrative abnormalities during hospitalization (OR = 1.39; CI: 1.22-1.60; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive rib fracture fixation strategies (including complete thoracoscopic and hybrid approaches) are associated with shorter hospital stay compared with conventional open fixation. The hybrid approach achieves favorable clinical outcomes in patients with multi-site fractures, including shortened hospitalization. The TTS score was identified as a significant predictor of postoperative pulmonary infiltrative abnormalities, underscoring the importance of enhanced postoperative monitoring and targeted interventions in high-risk patients.

articles.title: The clinical efficacy of unilateral biportal endoscopic treatment for lumbar spinal stenosis with preservation of the ligamentum flavum: a comparative retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As a minimally invasive surgical approach for treating lumbar spinal stenosis, Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) is receiving significant attention from clinical practitioners. Conventional UBE surgery involves the removal of the ligamentum flavum, and to date, there is no research on UBE techniques that preserve the ligamentum flavum.
METHOD: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 100 patients with lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) who underwent UBE treatment from January 2022 to March 2024. The surgical techniques of decompression of the lumbar canal while preserving the ligamentum flavum using UBE technology were summarized. Patients were divided into two groups based on whether the ligamentum flavum was preserved during surgery: the preservation group with 40 patients, and the removal group with 60 patients. The intraoperative surgical time and blood loss of the two groups were compared, as well as perioperative Visual Analogue Pain Scores (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and complications such as dural tears and epidural hematoma. The difference in radiological decompression between the two groups was assessed using the cross-sectional area of the dural sac on lumbar MRI.
RESULTS: The ligamentum flavum preservation group had significantly shorter surgical time (mean difference: -16.34 min, P < 0.01) and less blood loss (mean difference: -28.13 ml, P < 0.01) compared to the ligamentum flavum removal group. There was no difference in the VAS scores and ODI scores between the two groups at 3 days and 6 months postoperatively. The postoperative dural sac cross-sectional area was 164.31 ± 26.35 mm² in the preservation group and 170.92 ± 27.68 mm² in the removal group, with no statistically significant difference between groups (mean difference: -6.61 mm², 95% CI: [-17.75 to 4.53], P = 0.24). Although this difference was not statistically significant, the similar absolute values suggest that both techniques achieved a comparable and substantial degree of radiological decompression. The incidence of postoperative complications was 1.92% in the ligamentum flavum preserved group and 5.77% in the ligamentum flavum removed group, which was not statistically significant (P = 0.61).
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective study, UBE with ligamentum flavum preservation was associated with reduced operative time and blood loss, with comparable clinical outcomes. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Optimal timing of endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography and laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the management of cholecystocholedocholithiasis: a multicenter retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To compare the clinical outcomes of ERCP combined with laparoscopic LC using both one-step and two-step approaches for the treatment of cholecystocholedocholithiasis, and to investigate the optimal timing for performing LC within two weeks after ERCP.
METHODS: The clinical data of 520 patients with cholecystocholedocholithiasis who were treated with ERCP and LC between January 2018 and December 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Those who underwent ERCP and LC simultaneously with a single anesthesia constituted the one-step group (n = 60), whereas those who had ERCP and LC in separate sessions were categorized as the two-step group (n = 460), patients in the one-step approach group and the two-step approach group were matched using 1:4 propensity score matching (PSM). After PSM, the one-step approach group comprised 58 cases, and the two-step approach group comprised 218 cases. The 460 patients in the two-step group were further divided into three subgroups: ≤24 h group (n = 186), 24-72 h group (n = 187), and 72 h-2w group (n = 87). We compared general patient information, preoperative laboratory indexes, imaging data, intraoperative conditions, and postoperative outcomes between the one-step and two-step groups, as well as among the three subgroups of the two-step method. An ordinal logistic regression model was used to evaluate the effect of ERCP-related complications occurring before LC on LC timing, and a sensitivity analysis was performed to validate the robustness of the findings.
FINDINGS: The one-step approach group exhibited significantly shorter hospital stays (7 vs. 9 days, P < 0.001) and lower hospital costs (29,703 vs. 33039rmb, P = 0.002) than the two-step approach group; The 72 h-2w group exhibited a longer length of stay (11vs.8vs.9days, P < 0.001), higher hospitalization costs (36810vs.32264vs.31556rmb, P < 0.001), a greater overall complication rate after ERCP (18.4%vs.5.9%vs.7.5%, P = 0.002), and an increased incidence of cholecystitis after ERCP (8%vs.0%vs.0%, P < 0.001) compared to the ≤ 24 h group and the 24-72 h group. Ordinal logistic regression identified ERCP‑related complications occurring before LC as an independent predictor of delayed LC (OR = 0.338, P = 0.001) ; sensitivity analysis excluding these patients showed consistent trends across groups.
CONCLUSIONS: One-step management of cholecystocholedocholithiasis results in a shorter hospitalization duration and reduced costs. In a two-step approach, LC should be performed within 72 h following ERCP.

articles.title: Transfusion-sparing anesthetic management and immediate extubation in pediatric liver transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood-sparing anesthesia and rapid recovery are central in pediatric liver transplantation (PLTx). The aim of this study was to describe the intraoperative anesthetic management adopted by a dedicated team.
METHODS: This is a retrospective study performed at IRCCS-ISMETT, a transplant center specialized in all solid organ transplantation. Main anesthetic strategies were restrictive crystalloid administration, multifactorial assessment for blood-products transfusion, and planned immediate extubation (IE). Pre-, intra-, and postoperative variables were extracted. Logistic regressions were applied to explore variables associated with PRBC transfusion and IE and subsequent multiple analyses on select variables.
RESULTS: Ninety-nine consecutive recipients (0-17 years) between January 2018 and July 2023 were reviewed (75% living-related). Median fluid rates were respectively 9, 14, and 9 ml/kg/h during the pre-anhepatic, anhepatic and neohepatic phases. 34% of recipients required no PRBC, and 77% received < 20 ml/kg. Plasma or platelets were administered to 17 children. IE succeeded in 89 patients (90%). Median hospital stay was 18 days. One-year graft and patient survival were 99%. Transfusion-free PLTx was associated with lower tolerated intraoperative hemoglobin and higher mean arterial pressure, greater weight, and lower preoperative international normalized ratio (INR) or pediatric end-stage liver disease score. IE was associated with no requirement for vasopressors, shorter surgical time, and lower lactate levels at the end of operation.
CONCLUSIONS: Blood-sparing anesthetic strategies and IE are feasible in PLTx within an experienced multidisciplinary program, and are associated with favorable early postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: Modified nasopharyngeal airway device facilitates nasal fiberoptic intubation for trainee anesthesiologists: a randomized clinical study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fiberoptic nasotracheal intubation is an essential skill for anesthesiologists. Trainee anesthesiologists often face challenges due to the complex anatomy of the nasopharynx and the risk of upper airway collapse after anesthesia administration, which can lead to confusion and difficulty in identifying the glottic opening. This study evaluated whether a modified nasopharyngeal airway (mNPA) device can assist less experienced operators in performing nasal fiberoptic intubation on anesthetized patients with non-difficult airway.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial analyzed 54 patients undergoing elective surgery with nasal intubation. The patients were then assigned to either the mNPA group (n = 28) or the conventional nasal fiberoptic intubation (cNFI) group (n = 26). In the mNPA group, a modified airway guided the flexible fiberoptic bronchoscope to the glottis, and the device was subsequently removed to facilitate intubation. Trainee anesthesiologists performed all intubations. The primary outcome was intubation time. The secondary outcomes included first-attempt success rate and bleeding complications.
RESULTS: The mNPA group had a significantly faster vocal cord visualization time (11.49 vs. 47.56 s, P < 0.001) and a shorter intubation time (56.25 vs. 107.02 s, P < 0.001) than the cNFI group. The mNPA group had a significantly higher first-attempt success rate (96.43% vs. 73.08%, P value = 0.038) and a significantly lower incidence of blood staining in the periglottic area (3.57% vs. 26.92%, P value = 0.022) than the cNFI group.
CONCLUSION: The mNPA significantly improved nasotracheal intubation time and success rates and reduced the number of attempts and bleeding complication rates for operators with limited experience in performing nasal fiberoptic intubation in non-difficult airway patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20230809006. Registered 9 August 2023.

articles.title: Prognostic nomogram predicts postoperative mortality in children with brain tumors in a multicentre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer-related death in children. Reliable tools for predicting postoperative mortality in children remain limited. The aim of the study is to develop and validate a clinically applicable prognostic nomogram.
METHODS: We developed and externally validated a prognostic nomogram using data from two prospective cohorts in South China. The model included 375 patients (internal cohort) and 224 patients (external validation). Multivariate Cox regression identified independent predictors, which were integrated into the nomogram to estimate 12-, 36-, and 60-month survival.
RESULTS: Here we show that five factors-age, World Health Organization classification, extent of resection, systemic immune-inflammation index, and Count of major neurological dysfunctions (muscle weakness, disorientation)-are independently associated with mortality. The model shows good discrimination with C-index values of 0.789 (training), 0.841 (test), and 0.789 (external). Area Under Curves at all timepoints exceed 0.80. Sensitivities and specificities ranged from 0.824-0.905 and 0.619-0.671, respectively. Calibration and clinical utility are satisfactory.
CONCLUSION: This nomogram enables individualized prediction of postoperative mortality in pediatric brain tumor patients, aiding surgical and perioperative decision-making.

articles.title: Effect of intraoperative jugular venous oximetry-based management on outcome in patients undergoing excision of intracranial meningiomas: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Continuous jugular venous oximetry using fiberoptic techniques can detect critical episodes of cerebral desaturation that may occur during excision of intracranial meningiomas where considerable blood loss and hemodynamic alterations occur. Thus, we planned this study to evaluate the neurological outcome of patients undergoing craniotomy for excision of meningiomas using intraoperative fiberoptic jugular venous oximetry versus the standard care. We hypothesized that intraoperative jugular venous oximetry monitoring in these patients will improve the patient outcome.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients (American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I and II) aged 18 to 60 years undergoing elective craniotomy for excision of intracranial meningioma were randomized to receive either jugular venous oxygenation-based intraoperative management or standard anesthesia management. Patient demographics, intraoperative vitals, and length of hospital stay were noted. Patients' neurological status was assessed telephonically at 1 month postoperatively using extended Glasgow outcome scale (GOSE).
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients were enrolled in this study. Demographics and intraoperative variables were comparable between two groups. There were five episodes of jugular venous oxygen desaturation in three (7.5%) of the study patients. None of the patients had jugular pressure more than 6 mm Hg at any time point of surgery, irrespective of position of the patient. The hemodynamic variables were comparable between the two groups. The mean lactate oxygen index was 0.002 in Group B. Both groups had no significant difference with respect to GOSE at 1 month. We did not observe any complications with respect to procedure and technique of placement of jugular venous catheter.
CONCLUSIONS: Results of this preliminary study suggest that the intraoperative management guided by continuous jugular venous oximetry is not superior to standard management for improving neurological outcome in patients undergoing excision of intracranial meningiomas. Further research is necessary to confirm these findings and explore its complete potential.

articles.title: Opioid-free anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative delirium incidence: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The use of opioids as anesthetic agents is associated with multiple adverse effects, such as delirium. Patients with postoperative delirium (POD) have a higher risk of mortality or major complications. Recently, a multimodal anesthetic technique known as opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) has been developed to minimize or eliminate the use of opioids during anesthesia, which is hypothesized to reduce the incidence of POD. This systematic review aims to compare OFA and opioid-based anesthesia (OBA) to the incidence of POD.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Literature searches were conducted electronically without time restrictions across six databases: PubMed, Cochrane Central Register for Controlled Trials, ProQuest, ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, and PMC Europe. Additional studies were obtained through electronic searches on Google. The inclusion criteria were human studies involving participants aged ≥18 years, interventions of OFA and OBA, and POD as an outcome. Study selection was performed using Rayyan QCRI, and risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I).
RESULTS: Six studies met the inclusion criteria; three randomized controlled trials (RCTs), two cohort studies, and one case-control study. Five studies demonstrated no significant difference in the incidence of POD between the OFA and OBA groups; one study reported no occurrence of POD in either group. Several factors influencing POD included advanced age, type and duration of surgery, and the pharmacological effects of anesthetic agents such as dexmedetomidine, lidocaine, midazolam, and regional analgesic agents.
CONCLUSION: OFA has not been shown to clearly reduce the incidence of POD. The occurrence of POD is multifactorial.

articles.title: Efficacy of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia in children undergoing magnetic resonance imaging: A prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pediatric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires deep sedation to ensure immobility and optimal image quality. Propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia is effective but may cause airway depression and hemodynamic instability at higher doses. Dexmedetomidine has minimal respiratory effects but may prolong sedation. This study evaluated whether a low-dose dexmedetomidine bolus combined with propofol shortens recovery time (primary outcome); improves hemodynamic stability; reduces airway events, induction time, and total propofol dose; and minimizes scan interruptions (secondary outcomes).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective, randomized controlled trial, children undergoing MRI were assigned to two groups. Group D+P received 0.5 µg/kg of dexmedetomidine over 2-3 minutes plus a 1 mg/kg bolus of propofol followed by infusion; Group P received propofol alone as bolus and infusion. Propofol infusion rate was adjusted to achieve a Ramsay Sedation Scale score of 5-6. Recovery time was analyzed using t test; scan interruptions were compared using Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: Group D+P had a shorter recovery time (19.4 ± 35 vs. 31.4 ± 36.1 min; P = 0.042) and faster induction (128.9 vs. 224.6 sec; P < 0.001). The propofol infusion rate was lower in Group D + P than in Group P (76.3 ± 65.6 vs 123 ± 45.5 µg/kg/min; P < 0.001). Additional boluses were more frequent in Group P (P = 0.003). Bradycardia occurred in significantly more children in Group D + P than in Group P (P = 0.008).
CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose dexmedetomidine as an adjunct to propofol for pediatric MRI sedation reduces recovery time, propofol requirement, and airway-related complications, while enabling faster induction and fewer scan interruptions with increased risk of bradycardia.

articles.title: Utility of programmed intermittent bolus infusion modality in peripheral nerve catheters for postoperative pain management - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Continuous peripheral nerve block catheters deliver prolonged anesthesia or analgesia during the perioperative period and have evolved into established practices. Recent advancements in regional anesthesia aim to improve patient outcomes by reducing morbidity. Despite the use of adjuvants, single injection pain management typically lasts only 16 to 24 hours. Alternatively, continuous infusion (CI) pumps may increase local anesthetic doses, raising the risk of toxicity and opioid use. The newly evaluated programmed intermittent bolus (PIB) pumps show promise for peripheral nerve blocks, yet a Cochrane Library search indicates a gap in research, with only handful of registered trials on this topic. This highlights the need for further investigation and subgroup analyses to strengthen evidence for this modality in pain management.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In accordance with the PROSPERO registry protocol for this review, we conducted a literature search to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the PIB pumps in peripheral nerves blocks for postoperative pain management. Our primary outcomes included pain scores, consumption of local anesthetics, morphine, and rescue analgesics, as well as any encountered side effects.
RESULTS: There were 25 published randomized controlled trials, meeting the inclusion criteria, comprising 1572 patients, directly comparing PIB and CI, and explaining all the comparatives with rare complications. Despite the ever growing quest to find the ideal postoperative pain management method, there is limited literature and it is insufficient to guide clinical practice. Our study underscores the utility of PIB.
CONCLUSION: PIB proves a better analgesic mode than CI.

articles.title: Confronting-View One-Window and Two-Port Robot-Assisted Thoracic Surgery for Anatomical Lung Resection: Surgical Technique and Initial Perioperative Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the surgical technique and evaluate the perioperative outcomes of confronting-view 1-window and 2-port robot-assisted thoracic surgery (CV-1W2P RATS) compared with conventional look-up-view multiport RATS (LU-MP RATS).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 109 patients who underwent CV-1W2P RATS and compared them with 100 patients who underwent LU-MP RATS. Perioperative outcomes and postoperative pain management were evaluated.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally similar between the groups. All 101 CV-1W2P RATS procedures without conversion to thoracotomy were completed using 3 incisions without CO2 insufflation. Operative time was similar, whereas console time was significantly shorter in the CV-1W2P RATS group. Conversion to thoracotomy occurred in 8 patients (7.3%) in the CV-1W2P RATS group but in none of the LU-MP RATS group. No significant differences were observed in blood loss, postoperative complications, chest tube duration, or postoperative hospital stay. Despite less frequent use of epidural analgesia, postoperative pain scores were similar, and significantly fewer patients in the CV-1W2P RATS group required additional analgesics at the first postoperative outpatient visit.
CONCLUSION: CV-1W2P RATS is a feasible reduced-port approach; however, conversion to thoracotomy occurred more frequently than with conventional LU-MP RATS during our initial experience. This difference should be considered when introducing the approach, particularly in technically demanding cases. Its confronting-view configuration, reduced chest wall invasiveness, improved bedside assistance, and avoidance of CO2 insufflation may provide additional clinical and educational advantages.

articles.title: Heart transplantation in complex clinical and social contexts: expanding indications, ethical boundaries, and clinical decision-making.
articles.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the definitive therapy for selected patients with stage D heart failure; however, current practice increasingly extends beyond traditional eligibility criteria. Progress in mechanical circulatory support, donor management, immunosuppressive therapies, and perioperative care has facilitated transplantation in patients with complex clinical profiles, including advanced age, obesity, chronic infections, prior malignancies, substance use disorders, and socioeconomic vulnerabilities. This review traces the evolution from strict contraindications to personalized risk assessment supported by multidisciplinary transplant teams and ethical oversight. The discussion encompasses clinical decision-making between HTx and left ventricular assist devices, incorporating INTERMACS profiles, end-organ function, frailty, psychosocial evaluation, donor availability, and waiting times. Emerging strategies to broaden the donor pool, such as donation after circulatory death, normothermic regional perfusion, and ex-vivo heart perfusion, are examined with respect to safety and clinical outcomes. Particular attention is paid to combined heart-kidney transplantation, management of recipients with chronic viral infections, and collaboration with cardio-oncology for patients with histories of cancer. Finally, the review addresses ethical considerations related to equity, organ allocation, and shared decision-making, as well as future directions including precision transplant medicine, artificial intelligence-based risk modeling, and evolving ethical frameworks aimed at enhancing outcomes amid persistent organ scarcity.

articles.title: Identification of Risk Factors for Nonadherence in Preoperative Patients Following Pharmacist Intervention: A Retrospective Study in Japan.
articles.abstract: Nonadherence to preoperative medication instructions can lead to surgical delays or cancellations. Some patients fail to follow medication instructions properly. This study aimed to identify risk factors for preoperative medication-related nonadherence in a Japanese cohort and to develop a practical risk scoring system. We conducted this single-center retrospective cohort study at St. Luke's International Hospital among adult patients who were scheduled for anesthesiologist-managed surgery and received preoperative medication instructions from pharmacists between June 2021 and May 2023. Nonadherence was defined as failure to follow instructions regarding the temporary discontinuation or continuation. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed using complete case data to identify independent risk factors for nonadherence. Candidate variables included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), number of regular medications, interval from pharmacist counseling to surgery, number of remaining teeth, American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status, and presence of a cohabiting partner. A risk scoring system was developed based on the regression coefficients. Of 8181 eligible patients, 6162 complete cases were analyzed. Medication-related nonadherence was observed in 350 patients. Multivariable analysis identified four independent risk factors for nonadherence: age ≥75 years (p < 0.001), an interval from pharmacist counseling to surgery of ≥30 d (p = 0.002), use of ≥5 regular medications (p = 0.013), and BMI >25 kg/m2 (p = 0.027). No significant interactions were observed between age group and process-related factors. The derived risk score showed modest discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.630. These factors may help identify patients who require reinforced preoperative medication counseling, thereby potentially supporting more targeted preoperative medication management.

articles.title: Mortality prediction at the tracheostomy decision point after liver transplantation: development and internal validation of a bedside risk score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver-transplant (LT) recipients requiring prolonged ventilation and considered for percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) have high short-term mortality, but LT-specific tools to support prognosis-aligned communication at this decision point are lacking. We developed and internally validated a simple PDT-day model and an integer Tracheostomy Decision-Point Risk Score (TRS) to estimate 90-day mortality from the PDT decision point in LT recipients undergoing PDT.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 83 adult LT recipients undergoing PDT between December 2010 and June 2024. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 90 days from the PDT decision point, operationalized as the day of PDT. The model estimates risk after the PDT decision point and not the causal effect of PDT. Logistic regression used routinely available PDT-day variables; internal validation used bootstrap shrinkage. Discrimination and calibration were assessed by AUC, Brier score, calibration-in-the-large, and calibration slope. Coefficients were converted to an integer TRS.
RESULTS: 90-day mortality was 62.7% (52/83). Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD; +5 points), age (+ 10 years), and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; +5 s) measured on the PDT day were independently associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratios 2.54 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.45-4.47], 1.97 [1.16-3.36], and 1.53 [1.02-2.28], respectively; all p ≤ 0.040). Discrimination was good (AUC 0.846; bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.829 [95% CI 0.74-0.93]) with favorable calibration (calibration-in-the-large - 0.01; slope 1.02). The TRS (+ 2 points per + 5 MELD, + 2 per + 10 years, + 1 per + 5 s aPTT) retained discrimination (AUC 0.831) and stratified observed 90-day mortality: 38% (14/37) low, 72% (13/18) intermediate, and 89% (25/28) high. 90-day survival differed across bands (global log-rank p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: For LT recipients who reach the PDT decision point and undergo PDT, the TRS provides internally validated 90-day mortality estimates that may support prognosis-informed multidisciplinary deliberation and bedside risk communication. It should be used only as one component of decision-making and does not estimate the causal effects of PDT, no-PDT strategies, or PDT timing. Use in prolonged-ICU LT recipients without PDT requires separate validation.

articles.title: Intraoperative bedside lung-ultrasound use to optimize positive end-expiratory pressure for elective robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated efficacy and safety of intraoperative individualized stepwise positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration guided by lung ultrasound (LUS) in reducing pulmonary atelectasis and complications in patients undergoing robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy or cystectomy (RARPC).
METHODS: This randomized trial included 88 patients undergoing elective RARPC. Patients were assigned to either standard ventilation (PEEP 4 cmH₂O; group C) or LUS-guided stepwise PEEP titration up to 12 cmH₂O (group R). Patients, outcome assessors, and the data analyst were blinded. The primary outcome was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, estimating the between-group difference in LUS score at 2 h after surgery.
RESULTS: Group R showed significantly lower total LUS scores at 2 h after surgery (adjusted difference: -1.68, 95%CI: -2.89 to -0.47; p = 0.007) compared to group C. Likewise, significantly lower LUS scores were observed in Group R from the end of surgery onward. PEEP titration progressively reduced post-pneumoperitoneum atelectasis rates from 50% to 9.1%, at a highest PEEP level of 12 cmH₂O. Dynamic lung compliance in group R was significantly greater at Top compared with the control group (58.93 ± 3.48 vs. 49.91 ± 5.74 mL/cmH₂O; p < 0.001). Heart rate, mean arterial pressure, oxygen saturation, and end-tidal CO₂ were comparable at all time points. Both groups were comparable for intraoperative hypotension and bradycardia.
CONCLUSION: Intraoperative LUS-guided individualized PEEP optimization significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative atelectasis and improved dynamic lung compliance without compromising hemodynamic stability in patients undergoing RARPC. Lung ultrasound offers a practical, effective, and non-invasive bedside tool for optimizing ventilation in high-risk surgical settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION AND PROTOCOL: This study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov in March 2024 (ID: NCT06307704). The trial protocol is available through the ClinicalTrials.gov registry at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06307704 .

articles.title: The effects of ephedrine, phenylephrine, and norepinephrine on pregnant human myometrial contractility: an ex vivo study✰.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The choice of vasopressor during Caesarean delivery to prevent maternal hypotension remains debated. This study aimed to determine the concentration-dependent effects of vasopressors on pregnant myometrium, with and without oxytocin.
METHODS: In this prospective ex vivo study, myometrial samples were obtained from full-term pregnant women during elective Caesarean delivery. Myometrial contractility to vasopressors was recorded in the absence/presence of oxytocin compared with controls. Concentration-response testing was done with ephedrine, phenylephrine, and norepinephrine. The primary outcome was the motility index (amplitude×frequency). Isolated primary myometrial cells were also used for calcium mobilisation assays.
RESULTS: Myometrial samples were obtained from 32 females. The mean motility index increased with ephedrine (+39.9%; 95% CI 20.6-62.5; P<0.001) and phenylephrine (+36.2%; 95% CI 19.3-55.4; P<0.001), but norepinephrine had no effect (+12.0%; 95% CI -0.7 to 26.1; P=0.066) compared with control. Similar changes in motility index were observed in the presence of oxytocin. Calcium mobilisation recordings on primary myometrial cells supported the contractility findings, with increases in intracellular calcium ions after ephedrine and phenylephrine, but not with norepinephrine compared with control.
CONCLUSIONS: Ephedrine and phenylephrine increased ex vivo human myometrial contractility, both independently and in combination with oxytocin, consistent with improving uterine tone during Caesarean delivery. Norepinephrine does not affect myometrial contractility, suggesting that it is safe to use before delivery.

articles.title: Association between early self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications after non-cardiac surgery: A secondary analysis of three prospective cohort studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine the overall postoperative outcome and success, it is important to assess the occurrence of postoperative complications as well as patients' perception of their health outcomes. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications.
METHODS: This secondary analysis included data from three prospective observational studies evaluating quality of recovery in patients undergoing elective non-cardiac surgery. Self-reported quality of recovery was assessed using the Quality of Recovery-15 questionnaire (QoR-15), which was completed by patients preoperatively and on the first postoperative day. Postoperative complications were recorded between surgery and hospital discharge according to the Clavien-Dindo classification (CDC) of surgical complications. Binary logistic regression models were used to assess the association between self-reported quality of recovery and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: A total of 1,151 patients were included in this secondary analysis. Of these, 361 (31.4%) experienced postoperative complications. The median difference between preoperative and postoperative QoR-15 sum scores was higher in patients with postoperative complications compared to patients without complications (34 [IQR: 15-51] vs. 22 [IQR: 7-41]; p < 0.001). We found a relevant association between a greater decline in QoR-15 scores from preoperative to first postoperative day and postoperative complications after adjusting for potential confounders (OR 1.18 [95% CI: 1.14;1.23], p < 0.001). The association with no or minor complications was stronger in heterogeneous populations with various types of surgical procedures than in patients with radical prostatectomy.
CONCLUSIONS: Early self-reported quality of recovery is associated with the occurrence of postoperative complications after elective non-cardiac surgery. Whether this association may aid in identifying patients at risk of developing postoperative complications warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins overlap with the hyperinflammatory phenotype in acute respiratory failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of acute respiratory failure (ARF) identifies patients with high mortality, but its underlying pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell injury in critical illness. We investigated whether plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins characterize the hyperinflammatory phenotype and whether they contribute to its association with mortality.
METHODS: We analyzed 285 emergency department patients with ARF and suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Inflammatory phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis using nine biomarkers and clinical indicators. A mitochondrial-protein score was calculated from 59 MitoCarta3.0-matched proteins, and mitochondrial clusters were derived by principal component analysis and k-means clustering. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.
RESULTS: Latent class analysis identified 185 hypoinflammatory (65%) and 100 hyperinflammatory (35%) patients, with a significant difference in 28-day mortality (14/185, 7.6% vs. 31/100, 31.0%; p < 0.001). The mitochondrial-protein score increased with the probability of hyperinflammation (ρ=0.46, p < 0.001). Forty-three of 59 mitochondrial-associated proteins were more abundant in the hyperinflammatory phenotype, with prominent differences in apoptosis regulation, oxidative stress, and oxidative phosphorylation proteins. In a mutually adjusted model, the hyperinflammatory phenotype remained associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR]=6.40, 95%CI:3.08-13.95; p < 0.001), whereas the mitochondrial-protein score was not (OR=0.83 per SD, 95%CI:0.58-1.17; p = 0.30). Mitochondrial clusters yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of ARF is characterized by increased plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins, linking inflammation with mitochondrial biology and cellular injury. This mitochondrial signature did not account for mortality independently of inflammatory phenotype, suggesting that it represents a biological component of the hyperinflammatory state.

articles.title: Effects of pneumoperitoneum pressure on perioperative atelectasis assessed using lung ultrasonography in patients undergoing robotic-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery: A prospective, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery commonly requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which promote perioperative atelectasis and may increase complication risk. We aimed to investigate the effect of low pneumoperitoneum pressure (LPP) on atelectasis following robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, surgeon- and assessor-blind, randomised controlled trial in women undergoing elective robot-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery. Participants were randomly allocated to the LPP (12 mmHg) or standard pneumoperitoneum pressure (SPP: 15 mmHg) group. Primary outcomes were modified lung ultrasound (mLUS) scores assessed after surgery and 30 min post-extubation. Secondary outcomes included incidence of atelectasis, percentage of desaturation in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU), lengths of PACU and hospital stay, surgeon satisfaction with the operative visual field, numeric rating scale pain score and modified clinical pulmonary infection score on postoperative day 1, and postoperative pulmonary complications 7 days postoperatively.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were enrolled (30 per group). The mLUSs were significantly lower in the LPP group versus the SPP group postoperatively (P < 0.001) and 30 min post-extubation (P < 0.001), particularly in the posterolateral lung region (P < 0.001). Compared with the SPP group, the LPP group experienced a 1.59-fold reduction in the risk of postoperative atelectasis 30 min post-extubation in the PACU (P = 0.004). Other secondary outcomes showed no significant intergroup differences.
CONCLUSIONS: A low pneumoperitoneum pressure during robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery reduced perioperative modified lung ultrasound scores and the incidence of early postoperative atelectasis. However, this imaging difference was not accompanied by significant improvements in oxygenation. Further studies powered for clinical pulmonary outcomes are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, https://www.chictr.org.cn/; ChiCTR 2400085515.

articles.title: Purinergic signaling in perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury: Pharmacological strategies for organ protection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) remains a significant cause of postoperative organ dysfunction and mortality after cardiac, vascular, transplant, and high-risk noncardiac surgery. Despite advances in anesthetic and surgical techniques, practical strategies to prevent IRI are limited. Growing evidence indicates that purinergic signaling, mediated by extracellular ATP, ADP, adenosine, and their receptors, centrally regulates inflammation, microvascular function, and tissue recovery during perioperative ischemia and reperfusion.
METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes preclinical, translational, and clinical evidence on purinergic mechanisms in perioperative IRI across major organ systems, including the heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, intestines, and brain, emphasizing pharmacological strategies and anesthetic interactions relevant to intraoperative and early postoperative management.
RESULTS: During ischemia and early reperfusion, extracellular ATP released from injured cells activates P2 receptors, promoting inflammasome activation, endothelial dysfunction, and microcirculatory injury. Subsequent hydrolysis of ATP by ectonucleotidases CD39 and CD73 generates adenosine, which activates P1 receptors (Adora1, Adora2a, Adora2b, and Adora3) to suppress inflammation, improve perfusion, and enhance tissue protection. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-dependent upregulation of CD73 and A2B transcriptionally amplifies this ATP-to-adenosine transition, and miRNAs post-transcriptionally modulate it. Pharmacological approaches targeting these pathways represent promising strategies for perioperative organ protection, whereas clinical evidence supporting anesthetic regimen selection for purinergic modulation remains insufficient. The efficacy of conditioning strategies, including ischemic preconditioning and remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC), remains controversial, with negative large-scale trials highlighting the translational gap between preclinical models and multimorbid surgical patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Purinergic signaling provides a unifying mechanistic framework for perioperative ischemia-reperfusion injury and represents a promising target for pharmacological organ protection. Prioritize pharmacological strategies that enhance adenosine generation, activate protective adenosine receptors, or inhibit ATP-P2X7-driven inflammation in perioperative clinical trials. Understanding how comorbidities and concomitant medications modulate purinergic pathways is essential for successful clinical translation.

articles.title: A Second Major Change in Jehovah's Witness Blood Transfusion Policy within 6 Months.
Effects of lowering inspired oxygen fraction during anesthesia emergence on immediate postoperative loss of lung aeration assessed by ultrasonography: a multicentre randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Controversy remains regarding the effect of inspired oxygen fraction (FIO2) on postoperative lung aeration. We sought to evaluate whether lowering FIO2 solely during emergence from anesthesia reduces immediate postoperative loss of lung aeration, assessed by lung ultrasonography.
METHODS: In this double-blind multicentre randomized controlled trial, we allocated 102 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrectomy to either a low- or high-FIO2 group (FIO2 = 0.5 vs 0.8 during emergence, respectively). The primary outcome was the lung ultrasonography score (LUS) measured in the postanesthesia care unit (PACU). Secondary outcomes were the Oxygen Reserve Index™ (ORi™) after extubation, atelectasis on chest radiography taken on postoperative day (POD) 2, and oxygen desaturation events in the PACU and within the first 48 postoperative hr.
RESULTS: The median [interquartile range (IQR)] LUS did not significantly differ between the two groups (low-FIO2 group, 3 [2-5] vs high-FIO2 group, 3 [2-6]; P = 0.48). The median [IQR] ORi values after extubation were 0.42 [0.10-0.74] and 0.52 [0.30-0.83] in the low- and high-FIO2 groups, respectively (adjusted P = 0.36). The incidence of atelectasis on chest radiography on POD 2 (low-FIO2 group, 57% vs high-FIO2 group, 49%; P = 0.43; adjusted P > 0.99) and other pulmonary complication rates were not different between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Lowering the FIO2 from 0.8 to 0.5 during the anesthesia emergence period alone did not reduce immediate postoperative LUS after laparoscopic gastrectomy. Routine reduction of the FIO2 < 0.8 during emergence solely for the purpose of preserving postoperative lung aeration may have limited clinical value in a relatively low-risk patient population.
STUDY REGISTRATION: CRIS.nih.go.kr (KCT0008594); first submitted 29 June 2023.

articles.title: Postoperative pulmonary function after video-assisted thoracic surgery using epidural analgesia or oral morphine for pain management: A secondary analysis of the SEAVATS randomised trial.
Anaphylactic Shock With Bovine Serum Albumin Tissue Adhesive (BioGlue) in Cardiac Surgery: Case Series of an Under-Recognised Phenomenon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Anaphylaxis during cardiac surgery is a rare but life-threatening condition in which a severe systemic allergic reaction occurs in response to a specific allergen. BioGlue is a haemostatic agent used in cardiac surgery, composed of 45% purified bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 10% glutaraldehyde. Its use has been associated with anaphylactic shock in rare but well-described cases, typically mediated through immunoglobulin E (IgE) cross-reactivity between feline albumin (Fel d 2) and BSA. We aimed to assess the link between the use of BioGlue in cardiac surgery and anaphylactic reactions, and to identify potential measures to mitigate this risk.
METHOD: This article presents a case series of three patients who developed anaphylactic shock during cardiac surgery following application of BioGlue at a single UK centre within a period of 3 years. A structured literature review was conducted to explore the incidence, potential mechanisms, and management strategies of anaphylactic reactions associated with BioGlue.
RESULTS: All three patients developed profound vasoplegia and bronchospasm during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) shortly after BioGlue application, with markedly elevated serum tryptase. Skin-prick testing confirmed hypersensitivity to the BSA component in all cases. Feline serum albumin (Fel d 2)-specific IgE was detected in all three patients; alpha-galactose sensitisation and overt dietary pork intolerance were absent.
CONCLUSIONS: We emphasise the need for vigilance regarding anaphylactic reactions during cardiac surgery involving BioGlue. Its use should be avoided in patients with known Cat-Pork syndrome. We propose a practical mitigation strategy-saline field washout after BioGlue application-to reduce antigen recirculation via the CPB circuit.

articles.title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).
CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence.
