Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

articles.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials.
AIMS: To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence.
CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

articles.title: Complex Type Split Cord Malformation: A Two-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Complex spinal dysraphism is the condition where multiple dysraphic pathologies are observed in the same patient. Complex type split cord malformation (SCM) is a compound dysraphic phenotype involving disruptions at multiple developmental stages, characterized by the co-occurrence of SCM and spina bifida aperta. This study aimed to understand the differences between complex SCMs from classical SCM cases in terms of embryological aspects, perioperative management, and follow-up.
METHODS: Patients with SCM associated with spina bifida aperta who were treated at Dicle University and Kocaeli University, Departments of Neurosurgery, between 2011 and 2025 were included in the study. Patient age (months), gender, presenting clinic, lesion localization, SCM type, number of affected vertebrae, neurological status, presence of tethered cord, presence of kyphoscoliosis, spina bifida aperta type, Chiari malformation, syringomyelia, presence of posterior fusion defect number of vertebrae with defect, hydrocephalus, accompanying intracranial pathologies, and additional anomalies were included in the study.
RESULTS: The study included 44 patients who underwent surgery for complex SCM. Of the patients, 81.8% were operated on during the neonatal period in the same session with spina bifida aperta surgery. Surgery was planned for 11.4% of patients for follow-up purposes and for 6.8% following detection of SCM on MRI performed due to gait disturbances. It was observed that 68.2% of patients were plegic/severely paretic, 22.7% had moderate paresis, and 9.1% had mild paresis/normally. Regarding the type of spina bifida aperta, 72.7% of patients had myelomeningocele, and 27.3% had myeloschisis. Type 1 SCM was detected in 79.5% of patients, type 2 SCM in 13.6%, and type 1.5 SCM in 6.8%. Additionally, 93.2% had tethered cord/thickened-fatty filum terminale, 90.9% had posterior fusion defects, 77.3% had hydrocephalus, 68.2% had kyphoscoliosis, 65.9% had Chiari malformation, 54.5% had syringomyelia, 45.5% had intracranial pathologies other than hydrocephalus, and 4.6% had lipoma.
CONCLUSION: Complex SCMs should not be viewed solely as a spinal pathology; they should be evaluated multidisciplinarily in the perioperative period in terms of anomalies accompanying spina bifida aperta. In these cases that are diagnosed at a younger age, the incidence of type 1 SCM increases, while the frequency of occurrence in the lumbar region decreases and increases in the thoracic region. Furthermore, it has been determined that additional anomalies accompanying spina bifida aperta occur more frequently with complex SCMs.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of older adults who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery for symptomatic Rathke cleft cysts.
articles.abstract: Rathke cleft cysts (RCCs) are benign cystic lesions in the sellar and suprasellar regions that are often asymptomatic but may cause symptoms due to the compression of adjacent structures. With the aging of population, the incidence of symptomatic RCCs in older adults is increasing. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, and follow-up between older and younger adult patients systematically. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for RCCs at a single center from 2011 to 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: nonelderly (18-59 years) and elderly (≥ 60 years). A total of 153 patients were analyzed, with 120 younger and 33 older adult patients. Older adults presented more frequently with dizziness and fatigue. The elderly group had a shorter operation time, whereas the other surgical outcomes were similar between the two groups. The incidences of perioperative diabetes insipidus and mortality during follow-up were significantly higher in the elderly group. The recurrence rate was also higher, but no significant difference was observed. In multivariable Fine-Gray competing risk analysis, older age (adjusted SHR: 3.99, 95% CI: 1.45-11.00, p = 0.007) and cyst location, including both suprasellar (adjusted SHR: 12.70, 95% CI: 1.39-115.00, p = 0.024) and sellar-suprasellar extension (adjusted SHR: 8.67, 95% CI: 1.09-68.70, p = 0.041; vs. sellar), were associated with recurrence, whereas preoperative hypopituitarism was not (adjusted SHR: 2.20, 95% CI: 0.76-6.36, p = 0.200). EES is safe and effective for elderly patients with symptomatic RCCs. Elderly patients often present with atypical symptoms, leading to a delayed diagnosis. RCCs seem to be more likely to recur in older patients than in younger adults; thus, more careful monitoring and longer follow-up period is needed on the older adults.

articles.title: SiLaC versus PEPSiT for pediatric pilonidal sinus disease: a monocentric retrospective cohort study (PILO-LASER).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence comparing minimally invasive approaches for pediatric pilonidal sinus disease (PSD) is limited. We aimed to compare the effectiveness of Sinus Laser-Assisted Closure (SiLaC) and Pediatric Endoscopic Pilonidal Sinus Treatment (PEPSiT), with particular emphasis on wound healing time and disease recurrence rate.
METHODS: A retrospective monocentric cohort study was conducted including patients aged under 18 years treated for PSD between January 2022 and December 2025. The primary outcome was wound healing time. Secondary outcomes included recurrence rate, postoperative complications and operative time.
RESULTS: Seventy-three patients were included: 21 underwent SiLaC and 52 underwent PEPSiT. Age, sex, height, weight and body mass index did not differ significantly between groups, whereas redo surgery was more frequent in the SiLaC group (6/21 vs. 3/52; p = 0.014). Median wound healing time was significantly shorter following SiLaC than PEPSiT (15 [IQR 15-22] vs. 55.5 [IQR 24.3-113.3] days; p < 0.001; Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the location shift - 38 days, 95% CI - 55 to - 14). Among the 69 patients with available data, recurrence was observed in 3/19 (15.8%) in the SiLaC group and 12/50 (24.0%) in the PEPSiT group (Fisher's exact test, p = 0.534; odds ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.15-2.39). Operative time was slightly shorter with SiLaC (18 vs. 22 min; p = 0.046), although the 95% CI of the location shift reached zero (- 4 min, 95% CI - 8 to 0). No Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complication occurred. Follow-up was shorter in the SiLaC group (2 vs. 5 months; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: SiLaC was associated with significantly shorter time to clinically documented wound healing. Recurrence findings should be interpreted as short-term observations; the study does not investigate long-term recurrence rates. SiLaC's compatibility with lateral positioning and local or locoregional anesthesia may facilitate perioperative and postoperative management. Prospective studies with longer follow-up are warranted to assess long-term efficacy, recurrence, recovery, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Characteristics and co-morbidities of pediatric patients requiring cholecystectomy.
articles.abstract: Cholelithiasis in children is an increasingly recognized condition, due to the rising prevalence of risk factors and advances in diagnostic techniques. This retrospective descriptive cohort analyzed the characteristics of patients who underwent surgery for cholelithiasis in two Italian centers. From 2013 to 2023, 53 pediatric patients were retrospectively analyzed. Data collected included surgical indications, predisposing factors, and perioperative management. When preoperative ultrasound detected stones in the common bile duct, Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) was performed, followed by Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (LC) after two months. Postoperative clinical and ultrasonographic follow-up was conducted at 6 months and 1 year. The primary indication for surgery was symptomatic cholelithiasis in 38 patients (71.7%), followed by acute cholecystitis in 11 (20.7%) and persistent cholelithiasis in 4 (7.6%). Predisposing factors included hematological disorders in 14 cases (26.4%), a positive family history in 25 (47.2%), exposure to lithogenic substances in 9 (17.0%), and obesity in 9 (17.0%). ERCP was performed in 7 patients. Postoperative complications included one case of biliary fistula and one case of post-cholecystectomy syndrome. At follow-up, all patients were asymptomatic except for two who reported nonspecific abdominal pain. The most common risk factors for pediatric cholelithiasis in our cohort were a positive family history, hematological disorders, and obesity. LC remains the standard surgical treatment in children, with the primary aim of preventing complications.

articles.title: Acupuncture for Perioperative Pain Management in Cesarean Section: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Focusing on Pain Subtypes and Heterogeneity Exploration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cesarean section (CS) is among the most common surgical procedures worldwide, yet postoperative pain management remains challenging, with opioid-related adverse effects constraining analgesic options in lactating women.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy of acupuncture and acupoint stimulation for perioperative pain management in CS, focusing on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)-classified pain subtypes and heterogeneity sources.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and CBM through January 15, 2025 (PROSPERO: CRD42023487558). Eligible studies were RCTs evaluating acupuncture for CS perioperative pain. Primary outcomes were 24-h and 48-h pain intensity and analgesic consumption. Fixed- or random-effects models were used according to the heterogeneity criteria described in the Methods. Heterogeneity was explored via meta-regression, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Forty-one RCTs (n = 4,823) were included. Acupuncture and acupoint stimulation significantly reduced 24-hour pain (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -2.63, 95% CI [-2.97, -2.28]; prediction interval [-4.80, -0.46]; I² = 94%) and 48-hour pain (MD = -2.06, 95% CI [-2.29, -1.82]; I² = 96%). Low-RoB sensitivity analysis yielded SMD = -1.42, suggesting unblinded designs inflate estimates. Combined modalities produced the largest effect (SMD = -2.75). GRADE certainty was low-to-moderate across outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Acupuncture and acupoint stimulation may reduce pain after cesarean section. Substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias and low-to-moderate certainty limit confidence in the magnitude and applicability of the pooled effects. Use as an adjunct in enhanced recovery pathways warrants evaluation in rigorously designed trials.

articles.title: Case Report: Manic Decompensation During the Second Trimester of Pregnancy Requiring Electroconvulsive Therapy.
articles.abstract: Manic episodes during pregnancy represent a significant clinical challenge due to risks for both the mother and fetus, as well as the limitations inherent to pharmacological treatment during gestation. Severe affective episodes-particularly those with manic symptoms-may lead to heightened maternal stress, impulsive behaviors, impaired self-care, and potential obstetric complications. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) constitutes a therapeutic alternative when pharmacotherapy is ineffective or contraindicated. We present the case of a 31-year-old pregnant woman with a history of an unspecified affective disorder within the bipolar spectrum, who developed an acute manic episode during the second trimester following withdrawal of lithium for conception planning. The patient required psychiatric hospitalization due to progressive psychomotor agitation, disinhibition, and insomnia. After multidisciplinary evaluation, nine ECT sessions were administered between 18 and 21 weeks of gestation, with standardized anesthetic management and close obstetric monitoring. No maternal or fetal complications were observed. The patient exhibited progressive clinical improvement, allowing stabilization and safe continuation of pregnancy. This case highlights the potential efficacy and relative safety of ECT in managing severe manic episodes during pregnancy when prompt maternal stabilization is required. It also underscores the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary care and individualized risk-benefit assessment.

articles.title: Association between prior epidural labour analgesia and increased incidence of hypotension after spinal anaesthesia for caesarean section: A retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: The administration of spinal anaesthesia after epidural labour analgesia may increase the risk of block failure or high spinal block, particularly when the intrathecal local anaesthetic dose is reduced. This retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study evaluated the feasibility of using a standard spinal dose in partients (i.e. women who are in labour) with epidural labour analgesia undergoing caesarean section. Women who underwent caesarean delivery between April 2016 and March 2020 were analysed. The primary outcome was the rate of conversion to general anaesthesia. After 161 patients had been matched in the epidural labour analgesia-to-spinal anaesthesia and spinal anaesthesia groups, general anaesthesia conversion rates were comparable (3.3% vs 2.5%, P = 0.544); all conversions resulted from block failure. However, the epidural labour analgesia-to-spinal anaesthesia group experienced significantly more frequent hypotension (55.9% vs 30.4%, P < 0.001) and required higher doses of ephedrine (mean 8.3, standard deviation 9.8 mg vs mean 5.9, standard deviation 11.1 mg, P = 0.036). Although epidural labour analgesia did not increase the rates of block failure or high spinal block when preventive strategies were utilised, it was associated with a higher incidence of hypotension and increased vasopressor requirements.

articles.title: Bioadhesive Hyaluronic Acid-Cellulose Hydrogels for Sustained BDNF Release to Mitigate Local Anesthetic Neurotoxicity and Enhance Peripheral Nerve Repair.
articles.abstract: Peripheral nerve block (PNB) is indispensable in regional anesthesia, yet local anesthetics such as lidocaine can provoke neurotoxicity, causing dorsal root ganglion injury and delayed nerve recovery. Although brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a potent neuroregenerative cue, its clinical value is limited by rapid degradation and poor local retention. Here, we report an injectable, bioadhesive hybrid covalent/dynamic hydrogel (DAHA-POMC) constructed from hyaluronic acid and cellulose for sustained BDNF delivery and peripheral nerve repair. The hydrogel exhibited rapid in situ gelation, favorable mechanics, elastic recovery, and controllable degradation, enabling prolonged retention of bioactive BDNF. In vitro, BDNF released from the DAHA-POMC hydrogel retained neurotrophic activity, and protected lidocaine-exposed dorsal root ganglion (DRG)-derived neuronal cells by improving viability, preserving mitochondrial membrane potential, reducing apoptosis, and promoting axonal outgrowth. Transcriptomic and protein analyses supported the involvement of ERK signaling in this neuroprotective effect. In vivo, in an intraneural lidocaine-associated sciatic nerve injury (SNI) model, the BDNF-loaded hydrogel significantly outperformed free BDNF, improving nerve conduction, remyelination, and gastrocnemius muscle preservation. Collectively, this work establishes DAHA-POMC as a multifunctional neuroregenerative platform that integrates localized BDNF delivery with regenerative tissue support, offering a potential post-injury treatment strategy for focal peripheral nerve injury associated with local-anesthetic exposure.

articles.title: Modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach for postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative analgesia after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy is challenging in patients with obesity because of opioid-related respiratory risks. We evaluated the incremental analgesic effect of adding ropivacaine to a bilateral modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial included 100 adults undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. Patients received bilateral ultrasound-guided modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach with 30 mL of 0.2% ropivacaine or placebo (30 mL of 0.9% saline) per side. Pain intensity was assessed for 24-hours using a 0-10 Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). Morphine consumption, postoperative recovery, 15-item Quality of Recovery (QoR-15) score, adverse effects, and interleukin-6 and interleukin-8 concentrations were also evaluated. Repeated outcomes were analyzed using linear or generalized linear mixed models.
RESULTS: Across 24-hours, the overall mean difference in pain at rest was -0.57-points (95% Confidence Interval [95% CI -1.21 to 0.08]; p = 0.085), with no group-by-time interaction (p = 0.836). Pain during movement was lower with ropivacaine (overall mean difference, -0.84-points; 95% CI -1.46 to -0.23; p = 0.008), without a significant group-by-time interaction (p = 0.078). Twenty-four-hour morphine consumption was 10 (7-14) versus 11 (5-19) mg (p = 0.473). The median QoR-15 score was 125 (116-132) versus 118 (110-124) (p = 0.042), whereas recovery-category distributions did not differ (p = 0.140). No overall group differences were observed for postoperative symptoms or interleukin-6 or interleukin-8.
CONCLUSION: Adding ropivacaine to bilateral modified thoracoabdominal nerve block through a perichondrial approach produced a modest reduction in pain during movement without reducing pain at rest or morphine consumption. The improvement in postoperative recovery was small.

articles.title: Intrathecal morphine with or without transversus abdominis plane block for major abdominal surgery: a retrospective exploratory cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether adding a Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block to Intrathecal Morphine (ITM) improves analgesia after open Major Abdominal Surgery (MAS) is unknown. In cesarean delivery, the combination provides no additional benefit, but MAS involves greater tissue trauma and a larger visceral pain component. We assessed the additive analgesic value of TAP block to ITM in MAS.
METHODS: In this retrospective exploratory cohort study, patients undergoing MAS at a single center who received at least one regional technique were categorized into three groups: ITM alone, TAP block alone, or both. Primary outcomes were maximum pain score and total opioid consumption during the first 24 postoperative hours. Multivariable regression adjusted for prespecified prognostic factors.
RESULTS: Of 271 patients analyzed (ITM, n = 105; TAP block, n = 122; both, n = 44), ITM was associated with significantly lower adjusted pain scores (β = -1.26; 95% CI: -2.19, -0.34; p = 0.003) and opioid consumption (β = -18.61; 95% CI: -26.76, -10.47; p < 0.001) at 0-24 hours compared with TAP block alone. Adding a TAP block to ITM was not associated with additional benefit, with no significant differences between the two groups in pain scores (β = -0.01; 95% CI: -1.14, 1.12; p = 0.98) or opioid consumption (β = 2.27; 95% CI: -7.67, 12.22; p = 0.582). These differences were most pronounced during the first 8 postoperative hours and equalized by 16-24 hours.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing MAS, adding a TAP block to ITM was not associated with additional analgesic benefit. ITM alone was associated with significantly lower pain scores and opioid consumption compared with TAP block.

articles.title: Sensitivity to Physical Activity Predicts Daily Physical Activity Levels in People with Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated whether Sensitivity to Physical Activity (SPA, a measure of changes in pain responses to standardized physical tasks) predicts self-report and objective physical activity levels in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain. We also examined whether SPA offers predictive value in activity levels beyond psychological factors and quantitative sensory testing (QST).
METHODS: Sixty-one participants with chronic MSK pain completed a standardized SPA lifting task, psychological questionnaires (Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Pain Catastrophizing Scale), and QST (pressure pain thresholds, temporal summation of pain). Participants wore an accelerometer for up to nine days to objectively measure physical activity. Self-reported activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the predictive value of SPA, psychological, and QST measures on physical activity outcomes.
RESULTS: SPA significantly predicted objectively measured daily physical activity levels, explaining unique variance in both average daily steps (ΔR²=11.6%, P=0.005) and time spent performing moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (ΔR²=6.1%, P=0.030), after controlling for age and pain levels. SPA was not associated with self-reported physical activity. Neither psychological factors nor QST measures significantly predicted objective or subjective activity levels.
DISCUSSION: Lifting-based SPA emerged as a unique predictor of real-world physical activity in individuals with chronic MSK pain, outperforming traditional psychological and sensory predictors. These findings support the potential of SPA as a biopsychosocial marker for physical inactivity and the importance of objective activity monitoring in rehabilitation planning.

articles.title: Effect of PEEP on Diaphragm Is Associated with Lung Recruitability in ARDS: A Physiological Study.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Cardiovascular physiology of respiratory support in acute cardiac critical illness: A hemodynamic guided approach.
articles.abstract: Respiratory support is traditionally regarded as a treatment for respiratory failure. However, interventions that modify pleural pressure, transpulmonary pressure, lung volume, or the work of breathing simultaneously influence venous return, ventricular loading conditions, pulmonary vascular resistance, ventricular interdependence, myocardial oxygen demand, cardiac output, and systemic perfusion. Consequently, similar respiratory interventions may produce different haemodynamic effects according to the predominant cardiovascular physiology. This narrative review examines heart-lung interactions during respiratory support in acute cardiac critical illness and proposes a physiology-based framework organized around three predominant haemodynamic phenotypes: left ventricular congestion/afterload excess, left ventricular low-output/cardiogenic shock, and right ventricular pressure overload/failure. Acute pulmonary embolism is considered an important aetiology of the latter phenotype rather than a separate haemodynamic category. We discuss how high-flow nasal oxygen, continuous positive airway pressure, bilevel non-invasive ventilation, and invasive mechanical ventilation modify cardiovascular physiology and how their effects may be anticipated and reassessed using clinical examination, systemic perfusion, haemodynamic monitoring, focused echocardiography, and lung ultrasound. These phenotypes are dynamic and may overlap or evolve during critical illness; therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as a conceptual bedside approach rather than a validated therapeutic algorithm. Respiratory support may consequently be considered a cardiovascular as well as a respiratory intervention, requiring repeated assessment of both respiratory benefit and haemodynamic cost.

articles.title: The SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol and Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS) for dynamic assessment of peripheral edema burden in critically ill patients: a prospective, longitudinal observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive fluid resuscitation may lead to pathologic fluid accumulation and increased mortality. Cumulative fluid balance (CFB) correlates poorly with outcomes. Ultrasonographic central congestion metrics (VExUS/Lung ultrasound) inherently overlook critical fluid shifts within the peripheral reservoir. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed the SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol for standardized, semi-quantitative assessment of peripheral edema burden.
METHODS: Ultrasonographic assessment was performed bilaterally across six core anatomical regions using the SUBCUT protocol on days 1, 3, and 7. Individual sites were graded semi-quantitatively using the Ultrasonographic Subcutaneous Edema Grade (USEG, 0-4), yielding the Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS, 0-48) as the cumulative sum across 12 evaluation sites. The primary endpoint was ICU mortality, evaluating the prognostic performance of Day 3 SWELS.
RESULTS: Among 111 patients analyzed (ICU mortality 23.4%; 26/111), baseline SWELS and CFB were similar between survivors and non-survivors. By Day 3, median SWELS surged in non-survivors (24 vs. 8; P < .001), yielding greater unadjusted, apparent discrimination than CFB (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.65). In competing-risk analysis, a 5-point increase in Day 3 SWELS was independently associated with ICU mortality (sHR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.22-1.86; P < .001). Incorporating Day 3 SWELS into a contemporaneous clinical base model (Age, Admission Sepsis, Day 3 SOFA) enhanced model fit and discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.043; P = .008).
CONCLUSIONS: The SUBCUT protocol provides a novel framework for assessing peripheral edema burden. At Day 3, its derivative, SWELS, demonstrates incremental prognostic association beyond contemporaneous organ dysfunction, offering an extravascular perspective for multi-compartment fluid mapping.

articles.title: Magnesium slips through the filter.
Health-care utilization, costs, and quality of life in patients with sepsis: Results from the SAGA trial in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet detailed patient-level data on long-term healthcare costs and quality of life (QoL) is mainly based on intensive care unit (ICU) survivors and relies on model-based projections for patients treated in general wards.
AIM: To assess direct and indirect healthcare costs and QoL during the first year after community-onset sepsis.
METHODS: Data were obtained from a cluster-randomized trial of patients hospitalized with sepsis of urological, abdominal or unknown origin in the Netherlands. Mean direct hospitalization costs were collected from hospital data. Additional healthcare utilization and productivity losses were obtained through structured questionnaires in a subset of patients followed for 12 months. We used inverse probability weighting to adjust for differences between the subset and full cohort. QALYs were estimated using the EQ-5D-5L at months 0 (then-test), 2, 6, and 12, and the SF-36 was administered at 12 months.
RESULTS: Among 472 patients, 91 (19%) required ICU admission. Mean direct hospitalization costs were €8858 (95% CI: 7988-9855) per patient: €6697 (95% CI: 6185-7251) for general ward-admitted patients and €18,155 (95% CI: 14,856-22,342) for ICU-admitted patients. Over 12 months, mean total costs per patient were €30,889 (95% CI: 22,485-43,105): €25,839 (95% CI: 19,089-35,845) for general ward-admitted patients and €41,769 (95% CI: 23,132-48,943) for ICU-admitted patients. The weighted mean QALY during follow-up was 0.62 (95% CI: 0.51-0.74) compared with 0.65 (95% CI: 0.54-0.75) before sepsis. SF-36 at 12 months showed the greatest limitations in general health, physical role functioning, and energy/fatigue.
CONCLUSION: Sepsis is followed by substantial healthcare and societal costs during the first year after admission, with a significant burden among patient treated in general wards. By providing Dutch patient-level cost and QoL data across ICU and non-ICU settings, this study enables improved economic evaluations and better-informed health policy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Union Clinical Trials Register (2021-001,840-83). Count = 296.

articles.title: Preoperative Serum Biomarkers Improve Prediction of Poor Postoperative Outcome After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Compared With Clinical Variables in Neonates.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Neonates undergoing surgery for congenital heart disease (CHD) are at risk for poor postoperative outcomes after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), including death, prolonged ICU stay, and ICU readmission. Current prognostic models rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical factors.
OBJECTIVES: To utilize machine learning methods to compare the predictive utility of preoperative blood biomarkers vs. clinical features alone for ICU-30, a validated composite outcome after neonatal CPB that includes postoperative 30-day morbidity and mortality.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prospective observational single-center cohort study of consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days undergoing CPB for CHD.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Plasma and clinical data were collected from consecutively enrolled neonates younger than 30 days immediately before CPB. Thirty-seven biomarkers were measured by individual or multiplex enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and tested for association with ICU-30, defined as 1) mortality within 30 days of CPB, 2) ICU stay longer than 30 days, or 3) ICU readmission within 30 days. Predictive performance of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and random forest (RF) models was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). For XGBoost, the top 20 features were identified based on model importance (gain).
RESULTS: Biomarkers were available for 144 neonates. Most were male (51%), White (64%), and non-Hispanic (75%). Most operations were Society of Thoracic Surgeons-European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery (STAT) category 3 (32%) or STAT category 5 (29%). ICU-30 occurred in 29 neonates (20%). Using combined clinical and biomarker data, XGBoost demonstrated moderate discrimination for ICU-30 (AUROC, 0.74), outperformed RF (AUROC, 0.72), and LASSO (AUROC, 0.70). Biomarkers alone performed better (AUROC, 0.72) than clinical data alone (AUROC, 0.67) with XGBoost. The top two features in the combined XGBoost model were neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) and trefoil factor 3 (TFF3). Using Shapley additive explanation to assess both predictive impact and directionality, the most influential features were NGAL, a disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13 (ADAMTS13), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among neonates with CHD requiring CPB, multibiomarker models improved prediction of poor postoperative outcome compared with clinical variables alone. The most informative model features included markers of renal injury/perfusion and gastrointestinal epithelial injury (NGAL and TFF3), as well as vascular injury and inflammation (ADAMTS13 and Ang-2). These findings support further investigation of biomarker-informed risk stratification and may provide insight into pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying adverse postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: How ICU Teams Can Engage With Healthcare Leaders to Transform the Practice of Critical Care Medicine Through ICU Liberation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The ICU liberation ABCDEF bundle is a quality improvement (QI) tool designed to optimize pain, sedation, and delirium management in critically ill patients, to facilitate ventilator weaning and early mobility in patients, and to increase patient and family engagement in care. Increasing bundle performance is associated with improved ICU patient outcomes and reduced healthcare costs. Support for bundle implementation and sustainability efforts by healthcare system leaders is the strongest determinant of bundle performance. This narrative review outlines strategies that ICU teams can use to secure the necessary executive support for their bundle implementation and sustainability efforts to improve their bundle performance.
DATA SOURCES: Medline and PubMed databases. Search terms included critical care, ICU liberation, ABCDEF bundle, ICU outcomes, QI, implementation, patient safety, healthcare leadership, and administrative harm.
STUDY SELECTION: Peer-reviewed clinical trials, systematic reviews, observational studies, and narrative reviews (English only, from January 1990 to June 2025) focusing on the clinical and economic impacts of the ICU liberation ABCDEF bundle and the role of healthcare leadership in improving bundle performance.
DATA EXTRACTION: Data were narratively aggregated without new statistical meta-analyses.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Leadership strategies that support bundle performance include: executive sponsors engaging with ICU teams, developing an executive pitch, making a compelling business case for bundle implementation, and aligning the bundle with healthcare system strategic initiatives. Healthcare leaders should prioritize patient safety, teamwork, and family engagement in the ICU and provide the necessary information technology and QI resources to support data-driven bundle performance efforts.
CONCLUSIONS: The ICU liberation ABCDEF bundle offers a synergistic, patient-centered framework to improve ICU patient care and outcomes and reduce healthcare costs for all ICU patients. Executive support for the bundle significantly improves bundle performance by ICU teams. ICU teams must partner with healthcare executives to get the necessary resources for their bundle implementation efforts.

articles.title: Stakeholders' Perceptions About Intraoperative Communication and Hand-Offs During Liver Transplant.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: After multidisciplinary discussion of a complication during orthotopic liver transplant at our institution, we sought to evaluate stakeholders' perceptions of cross-disciplinary communication and management of intraoperative hand-offs.
METHODS: Semistructured interviews were performed with operating room (OR) personnel who participate in liver transplants at our hospital (surgical technologists, anesthesiology, and surgery). Interview transcripts were coded using inductive and deductive analysis.
RESULTS: Participants identified role-specific critical time periods which mandated complete concentration and varying strategies to minimize interruptions during these times. Participants described several team characteristics and individual behaviors which influence safety, including paying attention, assisting others, documenting relevant information (such as time of organ out of ice and time of reperfusion), minimizing interruptions, cross-disciplinary communication, team member familiarity, and the microculture within the transplant OR. We identified role-specific variation in optimal timing of intraoperative hand-offs during liver transplant; however, participants were unanimous that hand-offs were inappropriate during warm ischemia and reperfusion as well as any periods of patient instability. Anesthesiology and surgery interviewees agreed that cross-disciplinary communication leading up to warm ischemia and reperfusion is critical to patient safety during this high-risk period.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings have informed a quality improvement project to optimize intraoperative communication during liver transplants at our institution.

articles.title: Robot-assisted pyelo-ureteral reconstruction for ureteral stricture in kidney transplant recipients: functional outcomes and perioperative morbidity from a bicentric cohort.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In kidney transplantation, urinary complications are the most common (occurring in 4-10% of cases), with ureteral strictures (US) and vesicoureteral reflux being the most prevalent. Initial management often involves emergency urinary diversions, which serve as long-term palliative solutions. Reconstruction via pyeloplasty or pyelo-native ureteral anastomosis is the gold standard technique following failure of endoscopic treatment. Whilst open surgery remains the standard approach, robot-assisted laparoscopy may reduce parietal trauma in these immunocompromised patients and optimise preservation of peri-ureteral tissues. However, data on this approach remain limited. The aim of our study was to evaluate the functional outcomes in intention to treat of this technique.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, two-centre study was conducted, including kidney transplant recipients who underwent urinary anastomosis reconstruction (pyelo-native ureteral anastomosis, uretero-ureteral anastomosis or uretero-vesicostomy) via robot-assisted laparoscopy between March 2018 and January 2026. The primary outcome measure was the absence of upper urinary diversion (endoureteral stent or nephrostomy) at one year, analysed in intention to treat. Secondary outcome measures included anatomical restoration, changes in serum creatinine levels and postoperative morbidity according to the Clavien-Dindo classification.
RESULTS: Twenty-four patients were included (mean age 54 years). Two procedures were terminated intraoperatively due to a complete pelvic retraction in the context of chronic graft rejection. Technical feasibility was 91.6% (22/24). Overall treatment success, defined as freedom from urinary diversion at one year in intention to treat, was 66.7% (14/21), and functional success among evaluable reconstructed patients was 77.8% (14/18). Functional outcomes appeared most favourable after pyelo-native ureteral anastomosis, although the small and heterogeneous subgroups preclude any conclusion of superiority. No significant change in serum creatinine was observed, although the small sample size precludes any conclusion of preserved graft function. Postoperative morbidity remained acceptable despite the high technical complexity.
CONCLUSION: These results suggest that robot-assisted laparoscopy is an effective minimally invasive alternative for urinary reconstruction following kidney transplantation. Functional outcomes of urinary reconstruction by pyelo-native ureteral anastomosis are encouraging, but the small effective size do not allow its superiority over the other reconstructive techniques to be established. This approach, which is particularly suitable for immunocompromised patients, nevertheless requires specialised surgical expertise and rigorous patient selection. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to confirm these encouraging results and to define its optimal indications.

articles.title: Modern Diagnostic Tools for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Management of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) constitutes a major component of urologic practice. With the rise of remote healthcare from the COVID-19 pandemic, there is a shift in BPH testing to improve accessibility for patients and providers. This study aims to review modern diagnostic tests available for BPH.
METHODS: A literature review was performed with keywords including benign prostatic hyperplasia, lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), bladder outlet obstruction, uroflow, urocuff, penile cuff test, digital therapy, mobile health apps, and remote diagnostic and monitoring tools. Inclusion criteria included studies assessing tools for the diagnostic and perioperative work-up of patients with BPH, those assessing flow parameters, and those published within the past 6 years (2020-2026).
RECENT FINDINGS: Multiple methods for remote BPH evaluation exist including questionnaires, remote uroflow, ambulatory urodynamics (UDS), and noninvasive pressure flow studies. Remote questionnaires aid in tracking BPH symptoms but often require technological literacy and are often not validated. Remote uroflow, such as sound-based uroflow and catheter free UDS, allows for multiple data points collected in a more familiar environment but is susceptible to variations in calibration. Ambulatory urodynamics, including Glean UDS, offers a catheter-free alternative to traditional methods. Non-invasive pressure flow studies offer novel ways to measure voiding pressures. Multiple remote and noninvasive tools are emerging in the field of BPH. These tests aim to reduce discomfort, embarrassment, and variability compared to traditional testing. Further studies should be performed to improve validation and standardization of these novel techniques.

articles.title: Treatment of Single-level Thoracolumbar Tuberculosis by Bilateral Percutaneous Endoscopic Debridement and Percutaneous Pedicle Screw Fixation: A Retrospective Cohort Study With 2-year Follow-up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the efficacy of bilateral percutaneous endoscopic debridement (BPED) with percutaneous pedicle screw fixation for single-level thoracolumbar tuberculosis with 2-year follow-up.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 62 patients with single-level thoracolumbar tuberculosis from January 2023 to December 2024. Of these, 32 underwent BPED with percutaneous pedicle screw fixation (BPED group), and 30 received open anterior debridement with posterior fixation (control group). Clinical outcomes (ie, visual analog scale [VAS], Oswestry Disability Index [ODI]) and radiographic parameters (ie, local kyphotic angle, fusion status) were assessed. Subgroup analyses stratified by lesion level (thoracic vs lumbar) were performed.
RESULTS: BPED showed shorter operative time (mean difference, 29.99 min, 95% CI: 19.45-40.53), less blood loss (mean difference, 468.64 mL, 95% CI: 445.21-492.07), shorter hospital stay (mean difference, 3.44 days, 95% CI: 2.52-4.36), and no transfusion requirement (vs 40% in controls) (all P < .001). All patients achieved solid fusion at 12 months. Local kyphotic angle improved significantly in both groups (P < .01), with no between-group difference (P > .05). VAS and ODI were lower in BPED group at 3 months (P < .05) but not at 12 or 24 months. Subgroup analyses by lesion level yielded consistent results.
CONCLUSION: BPED offers favorable perioperative outcomes and comparable short-term efficacy to that of open surgery for single-level thoracolumbar tuberculosis. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy History is Associated with Improved Postoperative Ambulatory Recovery in Postmenopausal Women with Hip Fragility Fractures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare changes in ambulatory status after hip fracture surgery in women with and without a history of systemic menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) use.
METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort.
SETTING: Single center academic Level 1 trauma center.
PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients were included if they were female, >=50, received surgery for OTA/AO 31-A (intertrochanteric/peritrochanteric), 31-B (femoral neck), and 32-A (subtrochanteric) fragility fractures from December 2022 to September 2025, and had minimum 3-month follow-up data.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Patients were categorized into "Ever User" and "Never User" groups based on MHT exposure documented in electronic records. Primary outcomes were postoperative ambulatory status, categorized using a six-level functional scale, and return to baseline ambulation, measured as a binary variable at 30 and 90 days postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day hospital readmission and six-month all-cause mortality. Comparisons of outcomes were made between cohorts following adjustment for age, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade, baseline ambulatory status, and dementia diagnosis.
RESULTS: Among 358 included female patients, Ever Users (n=80) and Never Users (n=278) demonstrated similar ages (mean:80.6, range:60-100 vs. mean:78.8, range:50-101; P=0.14) and baseline ambulatory independence (48.8% vs. 46.0%, P=0.76). At 30 days, cohorts demonstrated similar rates of return to baseline function (25.3% vs. 23.4%; P=0.85). At 90 days, Ever Users demonstrated higher rates of independent ambulation (17.5% vs. 9.1%; P=0.029) and return to baseline status (53.8% vs. 35.8%; P<0.01). Thirty-day readmissions were less common among Ever Users (3.8% vs. 16.5%; P=0.0026), while 90-day readmission (23.8% vs. 21.6%; P=0.80) and six-month mortality (13.8% vs. 14.7%; P=0.97) were similar between groups. After adjustment for age, ASA grade, baseline ambulatory status, and dementia, MHT history was independently associated with 90-day return to baseline status (aOR 2.7, 95% CI 1.6-4.6, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In women undergoing fragility hip fracture surgery, history of menopausal hormone therapy use was independently associated with improved return to baseline ambulation by 90 days postoperatively. These findings suggested prior menopausal hormone therapy exposure may confer functional benefits extending beyond fracture prevention.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III (Retrospective Cohort Study).

articles.title: A Retrospective Study of 62 Patients With Single-Level Cervical Spondylotic Radiculopathy and Outcomes From Posterior Cervical Endoscopic Surgery With and Without Robotic Guidance.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Conventional C‑arm fluoroscopy‑guided puncture positioning for posterior cervical endoscopic surgery is highly surgeon‑dependent, often requiring repeated adjustments and causing excessive radiation exposure. Robot‑assisted positioning can address these limitations. This single‑center retrospective study of 62 patients with single‑level cervical spondylotic radiculopathy (CSR) compared outcomes of posterior cervical endoscopic surgery with versus without robotic guidance. MATERIAL AND METHODS We retrospectively analyzed clinical data from 62 patients who underwent posterior cervical endoscopic surgery between January 2023 and July 2025. Patients were assigned to a robot‑assisted group (n=30, using robotic assistance with C‑arm fluoroscopy) or a conventional group (n=32, using C‑arm fluoroscopy alone). Perioperative indicators (operative duration, working-channel establishment time, V‑point exposure time, fluoroscopy sessions), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores, Neck Disability Index (NDI), disc height, cervical curvature, and complications were compared between the 2 groups. RESULTS Compared with the conventional group, the robot‑assisted group had significantly shorter operative duration (mean difference [MD]: 12.67 min, 95% CI: 0.12 to 25.22, P=0.048), working-channel establishment time (MD: 2.64 min, 95% CI: 1.62 to 3.65, P<0.001), V‑point exposure time (MD: 2.18 min, 95% CI: 1.54 to 2.81, P<0.001), and fewer fluoroscopic sessions (MD: 2.26, 95% CI: 1.17 to 3.36, P<0.001). Both groups showed significant postoperative improvements in VAS and NDI scores (all P<0.05). Complication rates were comparable between the 2 groups (conventional: 3.13% vs robot‑assisted: 3.33%; P>0.05). CONCLUSIONS Robot‑assisted puncture localization for posterior cervical endoscopic surgery in single‑level CSR can shorten the operative workflow, reduce fluoroscopic radiation exposure, and yield comparable short‑term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Prophylactic Inferior Vena Cava Filters in High-Risk Hip Fracture Patients: Clinical implications of an early retrieval strategy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).
METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.
PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients older than 50 years who sustained a low-energy hip fracture (AO/OTA 31A, B, and 32A) and underwent prophylactic IVC filter insertion before hip fracture surgery between 2005 and 2025 were included. Prophylactic IVC filter placement was selectively performed in patients with either objectively confirmed deep vein thrombosis on preoperative screening or absolute contraindications to mechanical and pharmacological venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Those who had multiple trauma at the time of injury, a clinical follow-up duration ≤6 months after surgery, or undergone IVC filter placement following a confirmed diagnosis of PTE based on pulmonary computed tomography or lung perfusion scanning were excluded.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was the rate of newly developed symptomatic PTE. Secondary outcomes included IVC filter-related complications, retrieval rates, and 30-day mortality.
RESULTS: One hundred fifty-six patients were included in the prophylactic IVC filter group (39 men 25.0%], 117 women [75.0%]; mean age, 75.8 ± 11.1 years; femoral neck [AO/OTA 31B], n = 71 [45.5%]; intertrochanteric [31A], n = 75 [48.1%]; subtrochanteric [AO/OTA 32A], n = 10 [6.4%];mean indwelling time, 9.1 days; retrieval rate, 88.5%). Among these patients, no cases of newly developed symptomatic PTE were observed (0%), whereas the incidence in the overall hip fracture cohort (n=4,568) was 0.44%. Filter-related complications occurred in 3.9% of patients (minor tilting, 2.6%; vessel adhesion, 1.3%), with no major mechanical failures such as migration or perforation. Although no thrombi were detected at insertion, 4.5% of the patients had trapped thrombi at the time of removal. The 30-day all-cause mortality rate was 1.3% (2/156) in the prophylactic IVC filter group, compared with 1.5% (67/4,568) in the overall hip fracture cohort. (p=0.845). Neither death in the prophylactic IVC filter group was attributed to PTE or an IVC filter-related complication.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study's selected extreme pulmonary thromboembolism risk cohort, including patients with CT-confirmed preoperative DVT, those clinically expected to undergo prolonged perioperative immobilization, or those with contraindications to prophylactic anticoagulation, such as GI bleeding, prophylactic inferior vena cava filter served as an effective and safe temporary bridge therapy rather than a routine prophylactic strategy.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III.

articles.title: Operative Strategies for Treating Tibial Plateau Fractures in Patients Aged 55 Years and Older: A Five-Year Comparison of Acute Total Knee Arthroplasty with Open Reduction and Internal Fixation, Conversion Total Knee Arthroplasty, and Total Knee Arthroplasty for Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare outcomes of acute total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for tibial plateau fracture in patients aged 55 years and older with matched patients undergoing open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF), conversion TKA after failed ORIF, and primary TKA for osteoarthritis.
METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching.
SETTING: Federated multi-institutional electronic health records database (TriNetX United States Collaborative Network).
PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients aged ≥55 years with tibial plateau fracture treated with acute TKA, ORIF, or conversion TKA after failed ORIF were identified. A separate cohort undergoing primary TKA for osteoarthritis without fracture history was identified as a non-traumatic comparator. The study period was restricted to January 1, 2005 through December 31, 2020 to ensure a minimum of five years of potential follow-up for all included patients.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was revision surgery at 5 years, defined as conversion to TKA after ORIF and as revision TKA after arthroplasty. Secondary outcomes were a composite "return to the operating room (OR)" outcome (selected major reoperations), periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), surgical site infection (SSI), aseptic loosening, manipulation under anesthesia (MUA), and periprosthetic fracture. Three 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons were performed (acute TKA versus ORIF; acute versus conversion TKA; acute TKA versus primary TKA for osteoarthritis), with risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) calculated. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age (55-70 years; ≥70 years).
RESULTS: After matching, 1,321 patients per cohort were compared in the primary acute TKA versus ORIF analysis. Mean age was 66.1 years in the acute TKA cohort and 66.6 years in the ORIF cohort (range, 55 to 90 in both), and 65.3% and 66.7%, respectively, were female. Acute TKA had higher 5-year revision rates than ORIF (7.0% versus 0.8%; RR 8.36, 95% CI 4.50-15.56; P < 0.001) and elevated PJI rates (6.2% versus 1.3%; RR 4.82, 95% CI 2.88-8.09; P < 0.001). Return to OR rates did not differ significantly between acute TKA and ORIF (25.6% versus 23.5%; RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.95-1.25; P = 0.21). Revision did not differ between acute and conversion TKA (9.0% versus 10.0%; RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.58-1.35; P = 0.589) but was higher after acute TKA than after primary TKA for osteoarthritis (7.4% versus 3.5%; RR 2.12, 95% CI 1.48-3.00; P < 0.001). Revision was higher after acute TKA than ORIF in patients aged 55-70 years (9.3% versus 1.7%; RR 5.41, 95% CI 2.80-10.48; P < 0.001) and was not reportable in those aged ≥70 years owing to small cell counts.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients aged 55 years and older, acute TKA for tibial plateau fracture was associated with higher risks of revision and complications compared with ORIF. Revision and complication rates after acute TKA were comparable with those after conversion TKA following failed ORIF but higher than those after primary TKA for osteoarthritis. Acute TKA should be reserved for patients at highest risk of ORIF failure requiring subsequent conversion to TKA.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Reconstructive Surgical Outcomes in War Trauma During the Sudan Current Conflict: A 491-Patient Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic injuries resulting from armed conflict are complex and require urgent and efficient reconstructive surgical care. In a resource-limited environment, such as the situation in Sudan during the ongoing armed conflict, delivery of such care is affected by the delayed presentation of patients with contaminated injuries and infrastructure destruction. Our study evaluates the patterns of conflict-related injuries, reconstructive surgical interventions, and postoperative outcomes during the current conflict in Sudan.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study from a major tertiary hospital in Sudan that included 491 patients who underwent reconstructive surgical interventions between October 2023 and December 2024. Data were collected from hospital records and operative logs.
RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 31.7 ± 10.5 years, with most patients aged 18-35 years. The main mechanisms of injury were shrapnel/explosive fragmentation (42.8%) and gunshot wounds (41.8%). Extremities were most commonly affected, particularly the hand (23.8%). Skin and soft tissue procedures were the most frequently performed (42.6%), while only 7.7% required flap reconstruction. General anesthesia was used in 64% of cases, and most procedures were performed within 90 minutes. The length of hospital stay was 5 days for the majority of patients (63.1%). Postoperative complications occurred in 25.5% of patients, with postoperative wound infection being the most common (14.3%). Significant associations with complications were observed for injury site (p < 0.001), flap type (p = 0.031), and length of hospital stay (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: Armed conflict-related injuries in Sudan primarily affect young adults and are mostly caused by High-energy trauma, including penetrating injuries. Due to severe resource constraints, most cases were managed with relatively simple reconstructive techniques and achieved acceptable short-term outcomes. The study's findings emphasize the importance of adaptable, mindful surgical strategies tailored to available resources and highlight the critical role of reconstructive surgery in conflict settings.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound of the upper airway for direct confirmation of correct endotracheal tube placement in paediatric patients: analysis of 110 cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care ultrasound of the upper airway can rapidly confirm the anatomical position of the endotracheal tube without the need for preliminary ventilation. However, evidence on specific sonographic signs in children remains limited.
METHODS: This prospective, single-centre, observational study included children undergoing elective ENT surgery under general anesthesia. The study assessed four predefined ultrasound signs of the upper airway: the snowstorm sign, the bullet sign, the tracheal dilatation sign, and the absence of the double-track sign. Bilateral lung sliding was also evaluated. Correct intubation was defined as quantitative capnography combined with bilateral chest auscultation. The sensitivity, positive and negative predictive values, and 95% confidence intervals were estimated for the individual signs, combinations of signs, and a cumulative ultrasound score.
RESULTS: A total of 104 children were included in the study, of whom 103 had correct tracheal intubation. The sensitivity was found to be 81.6% for the snowstorm sign, 75.7% for the tracheal dilatation sign, 53.4% for the bullet sign and 100% for both the absence of the double-track sign and bilateral lung sliding. At least one positive dynamic sign showed 85.4% sensitivity, while at least one positive static sign or a cumulative score of at least one both achieved 100% sensitivity. The positive predictive values were consistently high, reflecting the absence of false positives in a cohort with almost exclusively successful intubations.
CONCLUSIONS: Upper-airway point-of-care ultrasound appears feasible as an adjunct for confirming paediatric orotracheal intubation. Static signs were identified more consistently than some dynamic signs. Further studies including sufficient esophageal or misplaced intubations are needed to establish specificity and overall diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Current Status of Pain-Related Patient-Reported Outcomes and Perioperative Pain Management among 40,785 Patients: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: This study analyzed self-reported pain-related outcomes of 40,785 surgical patients from 125 centers collected by CAPOPS (China Acute Postoperative Pain Study) between September 2019 and August 2023, to characterize the current status of acute postoperative pain management protocols and pain prognoses in Chinese medical institutions. Every participant completed the International Pain Outcome Questionnaire on the first postoperative day. Patient self-reported pain outcomes were assessed across the domains of pain severity, interference with activities and emotional well-being, adverse events, and perception of care. Outcome differences across geographic regions, time periods, and surgical types were analyzed. Risk factors associated with severe pain (score ≥ 7 on a 0-10 scale) were also evaluated with logistic regression. Overall, 12.6% of patients reported severe pain. Compared with earlier CAPOPS datasets, the prevalence of severe pain decreased consistently across surgical specialties, procedure categories, and geographic regions. Although such improvements were observed, perioperative pain management remained suboptimal in certain subgroups, particularly obstetric patients. We noted growing adoption of intraoperative non-opioid analgesics, combined regional anesthesia techniques, postoperative patient-controlled analgesia, and greater patient participation in pain management decision-making. Multivariable regression analysis demonstrated that these practices were significantly associated with a reduced risk of severe postoperative pain.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Suprascapular Nerve Block Versus Intravenous Fentanyl for Analgesia in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department With Traumatic Scapular Fractures.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare the analgesic efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block with intravenous fentanyl in patients with traumatic scapular fractures.
METHODS: We conducted an open-label randomized controlled pilot trial in the emergency department (ED) of a Level I trauma center in North India. Adults with traumatic scapular fractures and Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale scores of 7 and higher, were randomly assigned to ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block or intravenous fentanyl (1 μg/kg). Pain scores were assessed at baseline and 30, 60, 120, 240, and 360 minutes. Secondary outcomes included rescue analgesia and adverse events.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were randomly assigned to the 2 groups. Median baseline pain score was 10 in both groups. Pain scores were consistently lower with suprascapular nerve block, with median scores of 3 (interquartile [IQR] 2 to 5) versus 7 (IQR 6 to 8) at 30 minutes. Between-group differences were 4 (95% confidence interval [CI], 3 to 4) at 30 and 60 minutes, 2 (95% CI, 2 to 2) at 120 and 240 minutes, and 1 (95% CI, 1 to 2) at 360 minutes. Rescue analgesia was less frequent with suprascapular nerve block (13% versus 79%; risk difference, -66% [95% CI, 47.5 to 85.2]). Drowsiness was more common with fentanyl (12 versus 2 participants); hypotension occurred in 1 fentanyl recipient and paresthesia in 1 suprascapular nerve block recipient.
CONCLUSION: In this pilot randomized trial, ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block provided greater and sustained pain relief, reduced rescue analgesia, and fewer systemic adverse effects than intravenous fentanyl in adults with traumatic scapular fractures. Larger multicenter trials are needed to confirm these findings and evaluate cumulative opioid use and longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Anesthetic Challenges during Endoscopic Ultrasound-guided Gastric Variceal Coiling in a Patient with Severe Cytopenia.
Preoperative Biliary Drainage for Pancreatobiliary Tumor.
articles.abstract: Obstructive jaundice from pancreatobiliary tumors causes bacterial translocation into the liver and systemic circulation, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, multiorgan failure, and malnutrition, thereby increasing perioperative risk. Preoperative biliary drainage (PBD) aims to reverse these effects and enable safer neoadjuvant therapy and surgery. However, whether the benefits of relieving obstructive jaundice outweigh the risks of procedure-related and perioperative infectious complications remains controversial. This narrative review provides a comprehensive overview of the indications, modalities, timing, and ongoing debates regarding PBD in patients with distal and hilar biliary malignancies. In general, indications for PBD include cholangitis, severe or progressive jaundice with organ dysfunction, the need to optimize liver function for neoadjuvant therapy, and anticipated prolonged preoperative delays. In patients undergoing major hepatectomy, future liver remnant protection warrants additional consideration. Endoscopic biliary drainage is generally preferred over percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (PTBD) because PTBD carries a potential oncological risk and causes patient discomfort. However, PTBD remains an alternative to endoscopic drainage or as a supplementary method to drain additional effective liver volume. Fully covered self-expandable metal stents offer superior patency during the preoperative period but may increase the risks of pancreatitis, cholecystitis, and local inflammation, potentially affecting surgical complexity. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biliary drainage shows promise but requires further validation of its safety profile and long-term oncologic outcomes. Given its distinct benefits and risks, PBD should be tailored to the patient's clinical status, treatment plan, and institutional expertise. Further studies are needed to evaluate the optimal timing of surgery, the ideal stent design, and the impact of each PBD modality on perioperative safety and long-term oncologic outcomes.

articles.title: Perioperative antiplatelet use is not associated with increased risk of mortality among older adults undergoing operative hip fracture repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess whether perioperative antiplatelet use increases mortality risk among older adults undergoing operative hip fracture repair.
DESIGN: Retrospective study.
SETTING: Level 1 trauma center.
PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: A total of 965 patients 65 years or older who underwent surgical fixation for hip fractures (OTA/OA 31A, 31B and 31C) between 2018 and 2023.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was mortality at 365 days after discharge. Secondary outcomes were mortality at 30 days and 90 days, length of stay (LOS) > 7 days, need for blood transfusion, and 30-day readmission.
STATISTICAL METHODS: Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between antiplatelet use and mortality. For secondary outcomes, a Firth penalized logistic regression model was used, correcting for potential confounders.
RESULTS: The use of antiplatelet medications perioperatively was not significantly associated with mortality at 365 days, with adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) of 1.17, 95% confidence interval (CI) [0.76, 1.79] or at 30 days and 90 days, with aHRs of 0.94, 95% CI [0.44, 2.00] and 1.03, 95% CI [0.54, 1.97], respectively. There was a higher odds of being readmitted within 30 days of hospital discharge and getting a transfusion, with adjusted odds ratios (aORs) of 1.83, 95% CI [1.12, 3.00] and 1.60, 95% CI [1.00, 2.56], respectively, whereas there was no significant association with length of stay greater than 7 days, with aOR of 0.84, 95% CI [0.56, 1.26].
CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that undergoing hip fracture repair while on antiplatelet medications does not appear to confer a higher risk of mortality but may be correlated to higher readmission or transfusion rates.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level III.

articles.title: World's First Carbon Dioxide Laser-assisted Submandibular Skin Incision in the Surgical Management of a Mandibular Fracture.
articles.abstract: The submandibular incision is conventionally raised with a scalpel blade or cautery to expose fractures of the mandibular body, angle, and ramus. We report a 34-year-old male who sustained a right parasymphysis fracture with a left coronoid-ramus fracture after a road traffic accident. Following initial stabilization with bridle wiring, he underwent open reduction and internal fixation under general anesthesia, during which the submandibular skin incision was raised using a carbon dioxide (CO2) laser instead of a scalpel or cautery. The laser incision achieved simultaneous cutting and coagulation, giving a visibly bloodless field, and the wound healed uneventfully with a fine, inconspicuous scar at two-week follow-up. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first documented uses of a CO2 laser for a submandibular skin incision in maxillofacial trauma surgery, illustrating a technique that may merit further evaluation for its hemostatic and cosmetic potential.

articles.title: Sealed with Age: A Rare Case of Labial Adhesion in a Postmenopausal Woman.
articles.abstract: Labial adhesion is a rare occurrence in postmenopausal women, although relatively common among prepubertal girls. The condition is typically associated with a hypoestrogenic state that leads to vulvovaginal atrophy and epithelial fragility. A 62-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with complaints of difficulty in micturition and vulvar discomfort for 3 months. She had no history of genital trauma, surgery, or infection. Local examination revealed complete fusion of the labia minora with a pinhole opening for urine passage. Routine investigations were normal. Adhesiolysis was performed under local anesthesia, followed by topical estrogen and antibiotic therapy. At a 2-month follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic with no recurrence. Postmenopausal labial adhesion is an uncommon and underdiagnosed condition. Estrogen deficiency leads to thinning and inflammation of the vulvar epithelium, predisposing to adhesion formation. Chronic irritation, infections, or poor hygiene can aggravate the process. Conservative management with topical estrogen is effective for mild cases, while surgical separation is indicated for dense adhesions. Preventive measures, including hygiene and continued estrogen application, are the key to avoiding recurrence. Labial adhesion should be considered in postmenopausal women presenting with urinary or vulvar complaints. Prompt recognition and appropriate management can ensure complete recovery and prevent recurrence.

articles.title: Number of Surgical Levels, Rather Than Frailty or JOA Score, Is Associated With Spine-Specific Complications After Adjustment for Surgical Region.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study.
OBJECTIVE: To identify independent predictors of SAVES-V2-graded complications after elective spine surgery, and whether frailty (mFI-5) and JOA score remain associated after adjusting for surgical region.
METHODS: A total of 691 adult patients undergoing elective spine surgery (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, or deformity; 2014-2024) were analyzed. The primary outcome was SAVES-V2 ≥3 complications (90 patients, 13.0%). Three multivariable models addressed hypertension/mFI-5 overlap (r=0.753): Model A (n687), Model B (hypertension excluded; n=687), and Model C (Model B plus region; n=635), designated primary as region improved fit (P=0.036). Surgical levels' functional form was assessed with a spline and clinically grouped categories.
RESULTS: Transient neurological deficit (n=41; C5 palsy, n=29) and surgical site infection requiring reoperation (n=19) were most frequent. A linear per-level specification was not well supported (P<0.001); risk rose through 4-6 levels and plateaued thereafter (OR 13.89 for 4-6 vs. 1 level; P<0.001). Surgical levels were independently associated with complications in Model C (OR 1.281/level) and Model B (OR 1.258/level; both P<0.001). After region adjustment, JOA score, age, male sex, and BMI were no longer significant (all P>0.1); lumbar carried lower risk than cervical (OR 0.408; P=0.014). The mFI-5 remained paradoxically protective (OR 0.720; P=0.034). Discrimination was poor for both mFI-5 (C=0.487) and JOA score (C=0.582; DeLong P=0.007), a secondary finding; Model C showed the best discrimination overall (C=0.731).
CONCLUSIONS: Number of surgical levels, not frailty or JOA score, remained the most robust predictor after region adjustment, though non-linear and not a comprehensive complexity measure. Both frailty and JOA showed limited discrimination, insufficient alone for perioperative risk stratification.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III (Surgery; Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine, 2009).

articles.title: Erratum: Analgesic Effect of a Thromboxane A2 Receptor Agonist on Multiple Pain Models in Mice.
Private Equity: Anesthesia in the Age of Consolidation.
Does Size Matter? PDPH Risk During DPE and CSE Labor Analgesia.
CT-guided trigeminal nerve block for refractory oncologic facial pain: Pain relief, and opioid-sparing effect in a retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Management of refractory facial pain in oncologic patients is challenging, particularly in the presence of distorted skull base anatomy and limited response to systemic analgesia. This study aimed to describe the clinical outcomes and technical feasibility of CT-guided trigeminal nerve block and to explore an exploratory multidimensional CCS for assessing treatment response.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included oncologic patients who underwent CT-guided trigeminal nerve block. Clinical outcomes were assessed using Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) scores at baseline, early (1-7 days), and late (30-45 days) follow-up. The CCS integrating pain intensity, opioid consumption, and patient-reported subjective improvement, was used to assess treatment response.
RESULTS: Sixteen procedures were performed in 12 patients. Pain intensity decreased significantly at early follow-up and remained lower than baseline at 30-45 days. Mean opioid consumption decreased by 48% at early follow-up and remained 39% below baseline. Early clinical improvement according to the CCS was observed in 62.5% of procedures, with sustained improvement at 30-45 days in 60%. Exploratory analyses suggested that treatment-related neuropathic pain may be associated with more durable response.
CONCLUSIONS: CT-guided trigeminal nerve block was associated with favorable clinical outcomes in patients with refractory oncologic facial pain, including rapid pain relief and reduced opioid consumption. CT guidance facilitated precise needle placement in patients with complex skull base anatomy, supporting its feasibility as an image-guided treatment option in carefully selected patients with limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Optimal Dose of Ciprofol for Anesthesia Induction in Older Hypertensive Patients with Elevated Baseline Systolic Blood Pressure: A Bayesian Phase 1/2 Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify the optimal ciprofol induction dose for older hypertensive patients with elevated baseline invasive systolic blood pressure (SBP ≥ 140 mmHg) using a Bayesian adaptive design.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center, seamless phase 1/2 trial enrolled 51 hypertensive patients aged 65-80 years with baseline invasive SBP ≥ 140 mmHg undergoing elective non-cardiac procedures. General anesthesia was induced with ciprofol (0.20-0.40 mg/kg), sufentanil (0.4 µg/kg), and rocuronium (1.0 mg/kg). Phase 1 used the Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) design to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) was defined as post-induction hypotension (PIH; mean arterial pressure [MAP] < 65 mmHg from induction to 3 minutes post-intubation). The target DLT probability was set at 45% to accommodate the high baseline hypotension risk in this cohort. Phase 2 adopted the Bayesian Optimal Phase 2 (BOP2) design to find the optimal biological dose (OBD), evaluating both efficacy (loss of consciousness within 2 minutes without rescue dosing) and safety.
RESULTS: Phase 1 (n = 30) identified the MTD at 0.35 mg/kg (posterior mean PIH incidence: 33%, 95% credible interval [CrI]: 11%-61%). Phase 2 (n = 21) selected 0.25 mg/kg (n = 12) as the OBD, achieving a high induction success rate (91%, 95% CrI: 71%-99%) alongside a lower PIH risk (25%, 95% CrI: 6%-52%). The peak MAP after endotracheal intubation was higher with 0.25 mg/kg than 0.35 mg/kg (126.1 ± 20.9 vs 97.8 ± 14.8 mmHg; Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Guided by the Bayesian algorithm, 0.25 mg/kg was identified as the protocol-selected OBD for older hypertensive patients with baseline invasive SBP ≥ 140 mmHg, balancing reliable anesthesia with acceptable hypotension risks. However, compared with 0.35 mg/kg, this lower dose less effectively blunts intubation-induced hypertensive surges and requires careful hemodynamic monitoring.

articles.title: Differential Effects of Sevoflurane and Propofol on Perioperative Glomerular Permselectivity During Cardiopulmonary Bypass: A Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Creatinine-defined acute kidney injury does not capture early, compartment-specific renal responses to cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Whether anesthetic choice modulates the charge and size selectivity of the glomerular filtration barrier (GFB) remains unknown.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial, 106 adults undergoing elective cardiac surgery with CPB were assigned 1:1 to sevoflurane-based anesthesia or propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia. The primary outcome was longitudinal urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR). Secondary outcomes included plasma heparan sulfate (HS), syndecan-1, clearance-derived charge and size selectivity indices, and postoperative acute kidney injury.
RESULTS: The UACR group-by-time interaction was significant (P = 0.001). Sevoflurane-to-propofol ratios were 0.785 (95% CI 0.714-0.863) 10 min after aortic unclamping, 0.826 (0.751-0.908) 1 h after surgery, and 0.779 (0.708-0.856) 24 h after surgery (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). Coordinated separation was also observed for HS (interaction P = 0.001), charge selectivity (P = 0.013), and size selectivity (P = 0.011). HS was associated with UACR and both selectivity indices.
