Postoperative acute kidney injury occurred in 13/53 (24.5%) participants receiving sevoflurane and 17/53 (32.1%) receiving propofol.
CONCLUSION: Sevoflurane attenuated a coordinated perioperative GFB phenotype characterized by albumin leakage, HS release, and deterioration of charge and size selectivity. Functionally resolved glomerular permselectivity may provide exploratory pharmacodynamic measures for studying renal effects of anesthetic regimens during CPB, but their measurement properties and clinical utility require further validation. Outcomes-powered trials are required to determine whether modulation of this early phenotype improves renal recovery.

articles.title: Perioperative hydrocortisone for modulating stress and inflammation after microvascular decompression for hemifacial spasm: a single-center, randomized, assessor-blinded, controlled trial protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular decompression (MVD) for hemifacial spasm triggers substantial perioperative stress and inflammatory responses that may contribute to early postoperative symptoms and potentially influence long-term surgical outcomes. Perioperative corticosteroids can modulate these responses, but their efficacy and safety in this specific neurosurgical population remain inadequately characterized. This trial aims to evaluate whether short-course perioperative hydrocortisone reduces early postoperative symptom burden and to explore its effects on biomarker dynamics and long-term efficacy.
METHODS: This single-center, randomized, assessor-blinded, controlled trial will enroll 100 patients aged 18-70 years undergoing elective MVD for primary hemifacial spasm. Participants will be allocated 1:1 to receive either intravenous hydrocortisone (100 mg at induction, then days 1-2) or matching placebo. Primary outcomes are mean postoperative headache intensity (visual analogue scale, days 1-3) and 72-h cumulative rescue opioid consumption (oral morphine milligram equivalents). Secondary outcomes include recovery parameters, postoperative symptoms, and inflammatory biomarkers (interleukin-6, C-reactive protein, S100B), with serum cortisol reported only as a descriptive drug exposure variable. Long-term hemifacial spasm control and quality of life at 6 months will be explored. Safety monitoring includes infection, hyperglycemia, and psychiatric symptoms through 30 days. Intention-to-treat analysis will use Bonferroni-adjusted α = 0.025 for primary outcomes.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The protocol has been approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the Second People's Hospital of Liaocheng (Approval Number: [2025] Ethical Review No. (090), date of approval: 31 December 2025). The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600117513) on 26 January 2026, and recruitment of the first participant has not yet commenced. All participants will provide written informed consent. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations regardless of findings.
CRITICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, ChiCTR2600117513.

articles.title: Quantified standardized individualized small craniotomy vs. conventional large craniotomy for cerebral herniation secondary to acute supratentorial epidural hematoma: a propensity score-matched study for emergency and battlefield trauma care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute supratentorial epidural hematoma (EDH) with uncal transtentorial herniation is a fatal emergency for civilian and battlefield trauma. Conventional large craniotomy causes excessive surgical damage inconsistent with damage control surgery (DCS). Current minimally invasive EDH approaches lack standardized bone window metrics, rarely enroll patients with definite brain herniation, and lack battlefield-adapted evidence. This 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) study compared perioperative trauma and long-term neurological outcomes between a stratified quantitative small craniotomy and traditional decompressive surgery.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included patients with isolated acute EDH and preoperative uncal herniation (2012-2018). Confounders such as age, admission GCS, hematoma volume and anisocoria were balanced via PSM. A five-step CT-guided quantified small craniotomy workflow with tiered 4.0-6.0 cm bone windows was applied. Primary outcomes were operative time and intraoperative blood loss; secondary outcomes covered reoperation risk, hematoma clearance, soft tissue complications, wound healing and 6-month GOS.
RESULTS: Twenty-two matched pairs (44 patients) were analyzed. Small craniotomy was associated with a 31.1% reduction in operative duration and 71.7% reduction in intraoperative blood loss (both p < 0.001). It lowered persistent scalp numbness and accelerated suture removal (both p < 0.05). No reoperations occurred in either group. No statistically significant intergroup differences in residual hematoma, clearance efficiency and 6-month neurological recovery were detected, although the cohort size limits our capacity to exclude small-to-moderate clinically meaningful differences. Subgroup exploratory analyses are reported in Supplementary Table S1.
CONCLUSION: CT-guided quantified individualized small craniotomy represents a DCS-compliant minimally-invasive surgical option for patients with herniated acute EDH in this selected cohort. No statistically significant between-group differences in hematoma evacuation efficacy or 6-month neurological functional recovery were detected, though our analysis is limited by modest sample size and cannot definitively rule-out small-to-moderate clinically meaningful differences between procedures. The procedure was associated with reduced surgical trauma metrics. This standardized rapid decompression protocol possesses hypothetical translational value for civilian emergency treatment and resource-limited casualty-care scenarios.

articles.title: Oliguria in critically ill patients: physiological or pathological?
articles.abstract: Urine output (UO) is a major clinical sign, available at the bedside for all patients, all over the world. Currently, oliguria is defined according to the KDIGO guidelines as a UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h over 6 h. The threshold was originally selected by expert consensus and has since been associated with adverse outcomes. However, the optimal cut-off remains uncertain and its bedside relevance is regularly challenged by clinicians. Observational studies have suggested that transient or mild oliguria may not consistently be associated with adverse outcomes. Indeed, mild oliguria may capture episodes of physiological water retention rather than pathological kidney injury with structural damage. However, oliguria remains one of the main triggers for fluid or diuretic administration in intensive care units. Improving the understanding of oliguria at the bedside and its influence on clinical decisions requires a thorough knowledge of the physiological mechanisms underlying urine formation and the pathophysiology of oliguria. In this review, we describe the process of urine formation and explain the different physiological and pathological mechanisms leading to oliguria. We further discuss how pathological and physiological oliguria can be differentiated at the bedside, highlighting the role of clinical tools, biomarkers and imaging techniques. Finally, we examine how this distinction may inform clinical decision making, and guide interventions.

articles.title: High-risk profile for perioperative diabetic ketoacidosis in patients undergoing femoral fracture surgery and prevention implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a severe metabolic complication, but data on perioperative DKA in patients undergoing femoral fracture surgery remain limited. This study aimed to identify risk factors and associated complications of perioperative DKA in this population using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS).
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed NIS data from 2016-2022. Patients with traumatic femoral fracture who underwent internal fixation were identified by ICD-10-CM/PCS codes. DKA was identified by ICD-10 codes E08.1, E09.1, E10.1, E11.1, and E13.1. Multivariable models examined demographic, hospital, comorbidity, and complication associations, with FDR correction.
RESULTS: Among 337,988 patients, 579 had perioperative DKA. Annual DKA proportions ranged from 0.128% to 0.219%, with an overall increasing trend (Cochran-Armitage p=0.00272). In the comorbidity-domain model, additional diabetes coding (OR=4.074, 95% CI 3.209-5.173) and fluid/electrolyte disorders (OR=3.695, 95% CI 2.982-4.580) were strongly associated with DKA and remained significant after FDR correction. DKA was also associated with sepsis, acute renal failure, shock, pressure ulcer, dialysis, intestinal obstruction, and acute myocardial infarction, as well as longer length of stay and higher hospitalization costs.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative DKA after femoral fracture surgery is uncommon but showed an increasing trend and was strongly associated with diabetes, fluid/electrolyte disorders, severe complications, and greater healthcare utilization. These findings support targeted metabolic monitoring in high-risk patients.

articles.title: A SHAP-interpretable nomogram for predicting postoperative pneumonia in elderly hip fracture patients with preoperative anemia: a single-center retrospective study with internal validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pneumonia is a frequent and serious complication in elderly patients undergoing surgery for hip fractures, particularly in those with preoperative anemia. Early identification of high-risk individuals is crucial for improving clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 339 elderly patients with hip fractures and preoperative anemia. A multivariable logistic regression model, incorporating variables selected via the Boruta algorithm, was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative pneumonia. A clinical nomogram was constructed to facilitate individualized risk stratification. The model's performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was utilized to interpret the model and quantify the contribution of each predictor.
RESULTS: Four variables were identified as independent predictors of postoperative pneumonia: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), preoperative planned intensive care unit (ICU) admission, preoperative serum albumin (ALB) levels, and preoperative non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use. The developed nomogram showed moderate discrimination, with an apparent AUC of 0.746 and a nested bootstrap-validated AUC of 0.751 (95% CI 0.691-0.808). The calibration plot demonstrated acceptable agreement, and DCA confirmed the model's clinical utility across a broad threshold probability range (0.13-0.87). SHAP analysis revealed that COPD and hypoalbuminemia were the most significant drivers of risk.
CONCLUSION: This study provides an internally validated nomogram for predicting postoperative pneumonia in elderly, anemic patients with hip fractures. By integrating clinical and laboratory data, this tool may support early risk stratification and inform the implementation of targeted perioperative preventive strategies for high-risk patients.

articles.title: Tönnis Grade 2 Osteoarthritis Is Associated With Widespread Muscle Volume Reduction in Symptomatic Hip Dysplasia.
articles.abstract: Hip dysplasia can alter periarticular muscle biomechanics, but the extent and distribution of muscle changes across the hip and thigh remain incompletely characterized. This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated 72 patients with unilateral symptomatic hip dysplasia and a pain-free contralateral hip who underwent eccentric rotational acetabular osteotomy. Preoperative computed tomography images were analyzed using an artificial intelligence-based three-dimensional segmentation system to quantify bilateral muscle volume and mean attenuation in 19 muscles or muscle regions, summarized into six functional groups. Total assessed muscle volume and overall muscle attenuation were lower on the symptomatic side. After false discovery rate correction, symptomatic-side reductions remained significant for quadriceps muscle volume and gluteus maximus mean CT attenuation among the six functional muscle groups. After adjustment for clinical and radiographic factors, Tönnis grade 2 osteoarthritis was associated with a 6.99-percentage-point greater symptomatic-side reduction in total assessed muscle volume compared with grades 0 and 1 and with greater volume reductions across all six functional groups. Tönnis grade 2 was not independently associated with overall muscle attenuation asymmetry, and acetabular morphology was not associated with either primary outcome. These findings suggest that, among patients with symptomatic hip dysplasia undergoing eccentric rotational acetabular osteotomy, more advanced osteoarthritis is associated with widespread muscle volume reduction. STATEMENT OF CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Recognition of widespread periarticular hip and thigh muscle involvement in patients with more advanced osteoarthritis may support more comprehensive preoperative muscle assessment and inform future studies of perioperative rehabilitation.

articles.title: Nerve Blocks.
articles.abstract: This article provides a clinical framework for implementing point-of-care blocks, distinguishing between precision-target and volume-dependent planar techniques for conditions like hip fractures and thoracic trauma. By focusing on sonographic anatomy, procedural ergonomics, and standardized safety protocols, the text outlines strategies to mitigate risks like Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity. Integrating New York School of Regional Anesthesia-standardized methodologies, the article emphasizes improving functional recovery through anatomy-driven, opioid-sparing interventions.

articles.title: General Considerations for Bedside Procedures.
articles.abstract: Bedside procedures remain a core part of internal medicine practice. Although each procedure has its own technical considerations, many of the principles that promote safe and effective performance are shared across procedures. Success depends on more than technical skill alone. Procedural success also depends on a systematic approach that includes careful preparation, thoughtful technical execution, and attentive postprocedural care. This article reviews principles relevant to nearly all bedside procedures performed by internists, including indications and contraindications, preprocedural evaluation, infection prevention, and sterile technique, local anesthesia, and periprocedural sedation.

articles.title: Effect of perineural dexamethasone as adjunct to ropivacaine in PENG block on postoperative pain, surgical stress, and opioid-sparing effect in paediatric hip surgeries - A prospective randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Paediatric hip reconstruction produces intense postoperative pain and stress, often requiring opioids. This study evaluated if adding perineural dexamethasone to ropivacaine prolongs pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block duration and modulates postoperative inflammatory stress.
METHODS: In a double-blind randomised trial, 65 children (1-5 years) undergoing hip reconstruction received ultrasound-guided PENG block with 0.2% ropivacaine 0.5 mL/kg plus 0.1 mg/kg dexamethasone (Group A, n = 33) or ropivacaine alone (Group B, n = 32). The primary outcome was time to first rescue analgesia. Secondary outcomes included Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) scores, opioid consumption, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), blood glucose, and adverse events over 48 hours.
RESULTS: The median time to first rescue analgesia was not reached in Group A within 48 hours, versus 10.0 hours [95% confidence interval (CI): 8.4 to 11.1] in Group B [hazard ratio (HR) 0.21; P < 0.001]. For children requiring rescue analgesia, the mean time was 15.14 hours in Group A versus 8.90 hours in Group B (mean difference 6.24 hours, 95% CI: 4.87 to 7.61; t (33) =9.24, P < 0.001). Fewer children in Group A required rescue opioids (33.3% versus 75.0%; P = 0.001), with lower 24-hour fentanyl consumption (P < 0.001). FLACC scores and postoperative rises in NLR and PLR from baseline were lower in Group A (all P < 0.001). Glucose levels and adverse events were comparable.
CONCLUSION: Perineural dexamethasone significantly prolongs PENG block analgesia, reduces opioid exposure, and attenuates postoperative increases in NLR and PLR in children undergoing hip reconstruction.

articles.title: Intrathecal hyperbaric versus isobaric bupivacaine for caesarean delivery: A meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Intrathecal bupivacaine facilitates caesarean delivery and is available in two forms: isobaric or hyperbaric with differing pharmacokinetic profiles. This meta-analysis primarily aimed to compare the incidence of hypotension (defined as a drop ≥20% from baseline systolic or mean arterial pressure) when used in caesarean delivery.
METHODS: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intrathecal isobaric and hyperbaric bupivacaine for caesarean delivery were identified from MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and Cochrane databases. Secondary outcomes included incidence of ephedrine use, nausea/vomiting, bradycardia, maximum block height, time to maximum block height, and offset of block. Jadad scores evaluated the trials' quality. RevMan statistical software® calculated the standardised mean difference with 95% confidence intervals for continuous variables. The Mantel-Haenszel test and a random effect model were used to calculate the odds ratio for dichotomous variables. Included articles were assessed for risk of bias and consistency with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation guidelines.
RESULTS: Nineteen articles with 1501 patients were analysed with 722 patients receiving isobaric bupivacaine versus 779 receiving hyperbaric bupivacaine. There was no significant difference in the rates of hypotension [odds ratio (OR) 1.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.63 to 2.46] or incidence of ephedrine use (OR 1.44, 95% CI 0.75 to 2.77). There was a faster onset of motor block with hyperbaric bupivacaine (standardised mean difference -0.46, 95% CI -0.86 to -0.05) but no other differences in secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Despite differences between isobaric and hyperbaric bupivacaine, neither caused a significantly higher incidence of hypotension. Both produce similar clinical profiles except for onset of motor block. High levels of heterogeneity between the studies indicate the need for focused RCTs on this topic.

articles.title: Modulation of mRNA expression of OXTR gene following the use of ultrasound-guided transversalis fascial plane block for prevention of chronic persistent postsurgical pain following caesarean delivery: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic persistent postsurgical pain (CPSP) after caesarean delivery may occur in up to 18% of patients. Transversalis fascia plane block (TFPB) provides effective analgesia after caesarean delivery. Oxytocin (OXT) may influence pain perception through its receptor (OXTR). This study evaluated modulation of OXTR gene expression following TFPB and its association with CPSP.
METHODS: This pilot subanalysis of a prospective, randomised study included American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-III patients scheduled for lower-segment caesarean delivery under subarachnoid block. Group C received wound infiltration, whereas Group T received bilateral TFPB. Blood samples were collected preoperatively and 14 weeks postoperatively to assess OXTR gene expression.
RESULTS: Sixty patients (30 per group) were analysed for OXTR gene expression. Cycle threshold (Ct) values were obtained for OXTR and GAPDH, a normaliser gene. The mean delta Ct (ΔCt) was calculated as the difference between their mean Ct values. At 14 weeks, ΔCt was - 1.61 [standard deviation (SD): 0.84] [95% confidence interval (CI): -1.92, -1.30] in Group C and - 2.41 (SD: 0.72) (95% CI: -2.68, -2.14) in Group T, mean difference 0.80 (95% CI: 0.40, 1.20; P = 0.001; df = 58). In Group T, ΔCt correlated positively with Numeric Rating Scale-Pain at 14 weeks (r = 0.622; 95% CI: 0.337, 0.802; P < 0.001; df = 28). Fold change in OXTR expression was greater in Group T.
CONCLUSION: TFPB was associated with upregulation of OXTR gene expression. Because ΔCt is inversely related to expression, its positive correlation with pain intensity indicates that lower OXTR expression is associated with greater pain intensity.

articles.title: Combined thoracic segmental spinal anaesthesia and erector spinae plane block with indwelling catheters for breast tumour surgery in selected high-risk patients: A case series.
articles.abstract: Breast tumour surgeries are conventionally performed under general anaesthesia (GA). However, in high-risk patients with significant comorbidities, GA may increase perioperative morbidity. Thoracic segmental spinal anaesthesia (TSSA) combined with erector spinae plane (ESP) block may provide effective surgical anaesthesia and prolonged postoperative analgesia. We present a case series of five female patients undergoing breast tumour surgeries under combined TSSA and ultrasound-guided ESP block with indwelling catheter placement. Procedures included modified radical mastectomy, breast-conserving surgery, lumpectomy, and mastectomy. TSSA was administered at the T4-T5 level using low-dose isobaric levobupivacaine, while ESP catheters were inserted under ultrasound guidance at the same thoracic level. Adequate surgical anaesthesia was achieved in all patients without need for conversion to GA. The combination of TSSA and ESP block with continuous catheter analgesia appears to be a feasible and effective regional anaesthesia technique for breast tumour surgery in selected high-risk patients.

articles.title: Regional anaesthesia techniques for cataract surgery in India: Practice patterns and compliance with guidelines - A survey study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Although cataract anaesthesia practice patterns have been surveyed in several countries, Indian data are lacking. This study aimed to determine preferred regional anaesthesia techniques for cataract surgery in India and evaluate adherence to existing guidelines.
METHODS: A structured 23-item cross-sectional online questionnaire covering current practices in pre-operative optimisation of the patient, regional anaesthesia techniques, and local anaesthetics/adjuvants administered was distributed electronically among cataract surgeons and ophthalmic anaesthesiologists in India.
RESULTS: Out of 597 responses, 49.7% were from private clinical practitioners, 32.7% from private institutions, and 17.6% from government hospitals. Peribulbar anaesthesia (34.2%) was the preferred choice, followed by topical anaesthesia (32.8%). Around 45% used injection adrenaline as an adjuvant, 20% used injection hyaluronidase >15 IU/mL, and 17% were unaware of the dosages administered. Pre-operative continuation of antiplatelets and anticoagulants was reported by 16.1% and 13.6% of respondents, respectively. A local anaesthetic combination of lignocaine + bupivacaine was preferred (56%), pre-operative fasting was advised for sedation by 31%, and pre-operative allergic skin test to hyaluronidase was performed by 22.8% respondents. Electrocardiogram and non-invasive blood pressure monitoring were used by 26% and 44% respondents, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Peribulbar followed by topical anaesthesia are the most preferred anaesthesia techniques for cataract surgery in India. Practices such as continuation of oral antiplatelets before cataract surgery, limiting doses of hyaluronidase <15 IU/mL, and minimising the use of adrenaline should be incorporated in guidelines for the Indian population. Use of newer local anaesthetics (ropivacaine/levobupivacaine) needs to be encouraged, and pulse oximetry should be made mandatory for all.

articles.title: Regional versus general anaesthesia and neutrophil extracellular traps in orthopaedic trauma surgery: A randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Anaesthetic drugs may modulate immunological responses and neutrophil functions. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are web-like chromatin structures released by activated neutrophils, comprising cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid (cfDNA), histones, and myeloperoxidase (MPO), and contribute to perioperative inflammation.
METHODS: Seventy patients aged 18-60 years, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-II, undergoing isolated pelvic-acetabular or femoral shaft fracture surgery were randomised to general anaesthesia (GA, n = 35) or regional anaesthesia (RA) (subarachnoid block + epidural; n = 35). Blood samples were collected pre-operatively (T1), intra-operatively (T2), immediately postoperatively (T3), and 24 hours postoperatively (T4). NETs, MPO, and cfDNA were quantified by flow cytometry; histone H3 was quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Patients were followed for 5 days for the development of systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS).
RESULTS: NET formation, measured as MPO-cfDNA co-localisation events, was significantly lower in the RA group at T3 and T4 compared with GA [median (interquartile range): 1.72 (1.12-4.1) vs 3.75 (2.8-7.1), P = 0.01; and 1.6 (0.91-4.3) vs 4.24 (3.02-7.8), P = 0.01, respectively]. MPO and histone H3 were also significantly lower in RA at T3 and T4 (P = 0.01). cfDNA was lower in RA at all time points but without statistical significance. SIRS incidence was significantly lower with RA than GA [7 (20%) vs 16 (45.71%), P = 0.02].
CONCLUSION: NET formation was significantly lower in the RA group at T3 and T4. A statistically significant correlation was observed between NETs and their key components (MPO and histone H3). A lower incidence of SIRS was observed in the RA group.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Prophylactic Vasopressors During Anesthetic Induction and Emergency Tracheal Intubation in Adults: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Hemodynamic instability is the most frequent serious complication of tracheal intubation in critically ill adults, and prophylactic vasopressors are increasingly used to prevent it. This systematic review assessed comparative evidence on adrenergic vasopressors given before or during anesthetic induction in adults, with emergency tracheal intubation analyzed as a clinically distinct subgroup. Applicability was examined according to clinical determinants of hemodynamic risk, with procedural location, including urgent radiology, considered as one contextual factor. No protocol was registered. Eligibility was broadened from a radiology-specific population to adult induction and emergency intubation in any setting after preliminary searching found no direct comparative studies. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched for studies published from August 2021 to 15 August 2026, with supplementary searching to 26 September 2026. Risk of bias was assessed with risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2) and Risk of Bias in Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and the narrative synthesis followed the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline. Of 341 database records, 205 were screened, and 67 full texts were assessed; 13 studies were included (eight randomized, five nonrandomized), one of which was published after the primary database search date. Two studies addressed emergency intubation and 11 addressed planned induction. In planned induction, point estimates mostly favored prophylaxis, but effect sizes ranged from large reductions in moderate hypotension to no difference in severe hypotension (mean arterial pressure below 55 mmHg) in the cardiac surgery trial. The two emergency intubation cohorts were observational and gave discordant results, and no study evaluated intubation for urgent radiology. Benefits for kidney injury and mortality were not shown, and pressure benefits were accompanied in some trials by hypertension or dose-related bradycardia. Prophylactic vasopressors can reduce induction-related hypotension in selected planned-induction populations, but evidence for emergency intubation is limited and conflicting. Emergency status, baseline shock and vasopressor requirement, cardiovascular reserve, and induction technique are more plausible determinants of benefit than procedural location. No universal agent, dose, or regimen can be recommended.

articles.title: Biomarkers Related to Sarcopenia and Physiological Reserve in Total Joint Arthroplasty and Other Clinical Populations.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a multidimensional syndrome reflecting impaired physiological reserve rather than isolated skeletal muscle loss. Although numerous circulating biomarkers have been associated with sarcopenia and adverse orthopaedic outcomes, their biological significance varies according to the underlying clinical context. This narrative review integrates current evidence on circulating biomarkers of sarcopenia and physiological reserve across elective total hip and knee arthroplasty, fragility hip fracture, community-dwelling older adults, and medically complex populations. The available evidence demonstrates that sarcopenic phenotypes differ substantially between these populations, with predominantly disuse-related muscle deterioration in elective arthroplasty, frailty-associated sarcopenia after hip fracture, and metabolically driven muscle loss in chronic systemic diseases. Nutritional (albumin, geriatric nutritional risk index), inflammatory (C-reactive protein (CRP), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, CRP-to-albumin ratio), metabolic (aspartate aminotransferase-to-alanine aminotransferase ratio, glucose-to-albumin ratio), endocrine (vitamin D, insulin-like growth factor-1), and emerging molecular biomarkers reflect complementary biological domains of physiological reserve rather than directly measuring skeletal muscle quantity or quality. Current evidence supports their greatest clinical value in perioperative risk stratification and identification of patients at increased risk of adverse postoperative outcomes, whereas the diagnosis of sarcopenia should continue to rely on established assessments of muscle strength, muscle quantity and/or quality, and physical performance. Integrating circulating biomarkers with established sarcopenia assessment may improve patient phenotyping, individualized perioperative optimization, and risk prediction, although methodological standardization and prospective multicenter validation are required before widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Perioperative Blood Management Strategies in Anemic Patients Undergoing Surgery: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Perioperative anemia is a common occurrence in patients undergoing surgery. The severity and cause of anemia can vary in different clinical settings. Anemia can complicate surgical patients and adversely affect the recovery of these individuals after surgery. Some of the causes of perioperative anemia include microcytic anemia and acute blood loss due to gastrointestinal bleeding or trauma. Other causes include hemodilution after fluid resuscitation and physiological changes in pregnancy. Managing anemia in surgical patients is an important aspect of perioperative care. In this narrative review, the causes of perioperative anemia, its consequences, and the effects of anemia on postoperative care were examined. Two independent reviewers conducted a literature search for studies related to perioperative anemia. The studies reviewed were published between March 27th, 1997, and April 14th, 2026. The literature search included the terms "perioperative anemia," "preoperative anemia," "postoperative anemia causes," and "anemia in elective surgeries." Perioperative anemia is a problem in both elective and emergency surgeries. It may remain a problem for patients during the postoperative period. Identifying and correcting the causes of anemia before surgery is an important part of clinical practice. However, several confounding factors may influence the development and persistence of anemia in surgical patients.

articles.title: Effects of Intravenous Dexamethasone on IL-6 Levels in Children Undergoing Cardiac Surgery With Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary bypass provokes a systemic inflammatory response in children, with interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels rising rapidly after bypass. Corticosteroids are frequently used to blunt this response, but paediatric evidence remains inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a single intravenous dose of dexamethasone reduces the post-bypass increase in plasma IL-6 and improves early postoperative outcomes in children undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
METHODS: This single-centre quasi-experimental study enrolled 46 children aged one month to 12 years undergoing elective repair of congenital heart disease between January 2025 and August 2025. Participants were purposively recruited and alternately allocated to intravenous dexamethasone (1 mg/kg, maximum 10 mg; n=23, 50.0%) or 2 mL normal saline (n=23, 50.0%) after induction of anaesthesia. Plasma IL-6 was measured before drug administration, two hours after cardiopulmonary bypass, and 24 hours after bypass. Haemodynamic variables, oxygen saturation, extubation time, and intensive care unit stay were recorded.
RESULTS: The median IL-6 increase from baseline to two hours was lower with dexamethasone than with saline (261.90 pg/mL, interquartile range: 195.0-824.0, versus 447.0 pg/mL, interquartile range: 261.70-1,230.20), but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.177). At 24 hours, the median change from baseline was 8.20 pg/mL in the dexamethasone group and 13.0 pg/mL in the saline group (p=0.350). Blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and extubation time were comparable. First-postoperative-day heart rate was higher with dexamethasone (143.63 ± 18.93 versus 117.76 ± 19.57 beats/min; p=0.001), and median intensive care unit stay was longer (120 versus 95.5 hours; p=0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of intravenous dexamethasone at 1 mg/kg, capped at 10 mg, did not significantly attenuate the IL-6 response after paediatric cardiopulmonary bypass. The higher heart rate and longer intensive care stay observed in the dexamethasone group should be treated as exploratory because allocation was nonrandom and perioperative complexity was not adjusted for.

articles.title: Technical innovation and clinical effects of single-port laparoscopy for pediatric indirect inguinal hernia using needle graspers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the technical innovation, feasibility and clinical efficacy of single-port laparoscopic high ligation of the hernia sac in pediatric indirect inguinal hernia using needle graspers.
METHODOLOGY: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 403 children with unilateral indirect inguinal hernia treated at Hebei Children's Hospital from January 2022 to December 2025. Based on the surgical technique used, these children were divided into the grasper group(n=198, who underwent trans umbilical single-port laparoscopic high ligation of the hernia sac using needle graspers) and the conventional group (n=205, who underwent conventional two-port laparoscopy) and the perioperative indicators, postoperative pain scores, incidence of complications, recurrence rates and cosmetic satisfaction were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: The operation time for the grasper group was slightly longer than that of the conventional group(P=0.001). However, the FLACC pain score at 24 hours postoperatively was significantly lower in the grasper group(P<0.001), with an earlier time to first ambulation (P<0.001). Meanwhile, there were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of intraoperative blood loss, length of hospital stays, incidence of complications, or recurrence rates (P>0.05). Additionally, the cosmetic satisfaction score in the grasper group was markedly higher than in the conventional group (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: The application of single-port laparoscopy for pediatric indirect inguinal hernia using needle graspers is safe and feasible. Despite the slightly longer operation time, it offers substantial advantages in mitigating postoperative pain, promoting early ambulation and improving cosmetic outcomes.

articles.title: Preoperative indication meetings optimise outcomes in elective urological surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES: Elective urological surgery involves risks beyond the technical aspects. Structured preoperative indication meetings provide a forum for comprehensive review, risk assessment, and patient-centred optimisation. Our objective was to evaluate the impact of structured preoperative indication meetings on surgical planning, modification patterns, and short-term perioperative outcomes in elective urology.
METHODOLOGY: A prospective observational study was conducted at a university hospital from June 2024 to May 2025. Adult patients (≥18 years) scheduled for elective urological procedures across various subspecialties were included. Weekly online preoperative meetings reviewed demographics, comorbidities and surgical plans etc. Modifications were classified as major or minor. Cases were monitored for 30 days postoperatively to assess complications, readmissions, etc. Multivariable logistic regression analyses identified factors predicting changes in surgical plans. Statistical significance set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Among 703 analysed cases, 147 (20.9%) underwent modifications after review. Older age (>50 years), male gender, comorbidities, history of addiction, anticoagulation therapy, higher ASA scores, and endoscopic procedures were linked to plan changes (p < 0.01). Major modifications accounted for 25.8%, while minor modifications made up 74.2%. Additional counselling (27.2%) and diagnostic imaging (17.3%) were the most common reasons for changes. Multivariable analysis identified male gender (OR 3.61), addiction (OR 5.53), ASA III (OR 3.34), anticoagulation (OR 4.52), and procedure type as independent predictors. Postoperative complications were low (1.8%), mostly minor, and there was no perioperative mortality.
CONCLUSION: Structured preoperative indication meetings improve surgical planning, patient selection, and perioperative preparedness, serving as a safety net for high-risk patients and supporting evidence-based, patient-centred urological care.

articles.title: Observation of the safety and efficacy of alfentanil and sufentanil in anesthesia for elderly patients undergoing colorectal surgery: A prospective randomized controlled study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This paper aims to explore the safety and efficacy of alfentanil in anesthesia for laparoscopic colorectal surgery.
METHODOLOGY: This study was designed as a prospective study at CR & WISCO General Hospital. Eighty elderly patients who underwent laparoscopic colorectal surgery between February 2023 and February 2025 were selected and randomly divided into an alfentanil group and a sufentanil group, with 40 patients in each group. The LIDCOrapid non-invasive hemodynamic monitor was used to record the heart rate (HR) and mean arterial pressure (MAP) of patients at five time points: pre-anesthesia baseline (T0), before tracheal intubation (T1), one minute after tracheal intubation (T2), three minutes after tracheal intubation (T3), and five minutes after tracheal intubation (T4). The incidence of intraoperative adverse reactions and the use of vasoactive drugs were recorded, and the recovery of patients after discontinuation of anesthetic drugs was compared.
RESULTS: Compared with the alfentanil group, the MAP levels and HR in the sufentanil group fluctuated more significantly at T1, T2, and T3 (P < 0.05). The incidence of hypotension and the use of ephedrine were higher in the sufentanil group than in the alfentanil group (P < 0.05). The eye-opening time, orientation recovery time, and time to discharge from the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) in the sufentanil group were longer than those in the alfentanil group (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Compared with sufentanil induction, alfentanil administration in laparoscopic colorectal surgery for elderly patients can more effectively reduce hemodynamic fluctuations, decrease the use of intraoperative active drugs, and ensure rapid awakening without increasing postoperative adverse reactions - that is, it provides a higher level of comfort.

articles.title: Pediatric Dermatologic Conditions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric skin conditions of the lower extremity present a diagnostic and management challenge, and this article offers the practitioner a systematic framework. It opens with practical guidance on performing cutaneous procedures in children-engaging the parent, minimizing pain and anxiety through topical anesthesia and distraction, and setting postoperative limits for optimal scar outcomes. It then surveys environmentally induced disorders, bites and stings, genodermatoses including the palmoplantar keratodermas, and bacterial, viral, and fungal infections. Eczematous conditions, psoriasis, nevi, pediatric melanoma, and nail disorders are each reviewed with attention to lower extremity presentation, common misdiagnoses, and current management strategies.

articles.title: Transfusion practices among children admitted to a South African PICU following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood products may be required in patients undergoing cardiac surgery; however, there is a paucity of data on blood transfusion guidelines in the perioperative and postoperative cardiac surgery period.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the prevalence of blood product transfusion, factors associated with transfusion and outcomes in patients who received blood products following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-centre observational study that consecutively recruited 126 children aged <18 years admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) following cardiac surgery between July 2017 and January 2018. Demographic, intraoperative and postoperative blood product transfusion data were extracted from patient records, entered into a standardised case record form and analysed using Statistica version 13 (StatSoft Inc, USA). Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.
RESULTS: Of the recruited children, 53% received blood products, with 30.9% receiving cryoprecipitate, 22.2% receiving packed red blood cells, 18.3% receiving albumin, 15.9% receiving fresh frozen plasma and 15.1% receiving platelet concentrates. Factors associated with the use of blood products included previous cardiac surgery, younger age, lower weight and prolonged coagulation parameters (p<0.05). Receiving blood products was associated with worse outcomes: a standardised mortality ratio of 3.1 v. 0 (p<0.0001), median (IQR) PICU length of stay of 5 (3 - 11) v. 2 (2 - 5) days (p<0.0001), and duration of mechanical ventilation of 47 (22 - 132) v. 20 (6 - 27) hours (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSION: There is a high prevalence of blood product use in children in the PICU following cardiac surgery, and this is associated with worse outcomes.
CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY: This is the first South African study to describe the use of all major blood product types, not only red blood cells, and their indications in children following paediatric cardiac surgery. It demonstrates a markedly different transfusion pattern from that reported in North American PICUs, with cryoprecipitate, rather than red blood cells, being the most frequently used product. Blood product use was common and was independently associated with worse outcomes, including longer PICU stays, prolonged ventilation and higher standardised mortality. These findings highlight the need for locally developed, evidence-based transfusion protocols to support blood product stewardship, particularly in resource-constrained settings that depend on voluntary blood donation.

articles.title: Lighting the Way: Joseph Cichon, Inaugural Emery N. Brown Award Recipient.
Surgery for Nonthymomatous Myasthenia Gravis.
articles.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by fluctuating muscle weakness due to impaired neuromuscular transmission, most commonly mediated by antibodies against the acetylcholine receptor. The thymus plays a central role in disease pathogenesis, and complete thymectomy including all thymic and mediastinal adipose tissue has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with nonthymomatous, antiacetylcholine receptor antibody positive generalized MG. Minimally invasive approaches, including video-assisted and robotic-assisted thymectomy, offer remission rates comparable to open surgery with reduced perioperative morbidity. Careful patient selection and perioperative disease optimization remain essential.

articles.title: Elevated electrical stimulation thresholds for sciatic nerve block in individuals with diabetic complications: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is associated with peripheral nerve structural alterations, potentially affecting nerve excitability. Electrical stimulation threshold is a key parameter for nerve localization during sciatic nerve block. This meta-analysis investigates the impact of diabetes mellitus and its complications on this threshold.
METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang Database, from their inception to November 10, 2025, for studies comparing electrical stimulation thresholds during sciatic nerve block between diabetic and non-diabetic subjects. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Newcastle‑Ottawa Scale (NOS). Data were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses were conducted by alternating effect models and sequentially excluding individual studies. Subgroup analyses were performed to explore potential sources of heterogeneity. In addition, trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to determine whether the sample size was sufficient and to assess statistical power. The quality of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
RESULTS: Six studies involving 486 participants were included, all of which were of high quality according to the NOS. The pooled analysis demonstrated a significantly higher stimulation threshold in diabetic participants compared to controls (mean difference [MD] = 0.57 mA, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.22-0.91, P = 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 94%). Sensitivity analyses, including alternating effect models and sequential exclusion of individual studies, confirmed the robustness of these findings. Subgroup analysis identified the presence of diabetic complications (peripheral neuropathy or diabetic foot) as a significant source of heterogeneity (P = 0.02), while geographic region and puncture site were not associated with heterogeneity (P > 0.05). TSA indicated that the evidence was robust, with sufficient statistical power to support the conclusion. The result was supported by low evidence.
CONCLUSION: Diabetic complications, particularly peripheral neuropathy or diabetic foot, are associated with elevated electrical stimulation thresholds for sciatic nerve block. This suggests that procedural parameters may need adjustment in this patient subgroup to ensure accurate nerve localization.

articles.title: Bacteriological profiling and antimicrobial resistance of combat-related infections: analysis of war wounds from Ukraine during 2024-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combat-related wound infections in the Russo-Ukrainian war pose high morbidity due to the prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) organisms. The aim of the study was to characterize pathogen distribution, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dynamics, and risk factors (evacuation and sampling timing) with the intent to develop a prognostic model for resistance in wounded military personnel.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 203 patients with ballistic injuries treated at a Role 3 military hospital (Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine) was performed. Microbiological sampling yielded 685 unique strains. Isolates were categorized by year (2024 vs. 2025), sampling timing (≤ 48 h vs. > 48 h), and evacuation interval (< 72 h vs. ≥ 72 h). Susceptibility testing followed EUCAST v.14-15. Bacteriological profiling was made for Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR), and Pan-drug-Resistant (PDR) microbes. Data was managed in WHONET Microbiology Laboratory Database Software (2025); statistical analyses used R and AMR packages. A supervised machine-learning workflow using a standard Random Forest algorithm was implemented to predict phenotypic resistance risk, with model performance evaluated by ROC-AUC analysis.
RESULTS: Gram-negative bacteria predominated, led by A. baumannii, K. pneumoniae, E. coli, and E. cloacae. Overall resistance rate was 51.2%. True patient-level carbapenem resistance was high in K. pneumoniae (imipenem 83.1%) and A. baumannii (imipenem 91.5%); colistin retained activity. Patient-corrected MDR prevalence significantly escalated from 72.9% in 2024 to 82.3% in 2025 (p = 0.022), confirming a deepening ecological resistance reservoir. Polymicrobial infections were common (93.6% of episodes), often including MDR/XDR pathogens. Resistance was highest in the early-evacuation/early-sampling (Groups 1, 73.6% MDR) and late-evacuation/late-sampling (Groups 4, 97.1% MDR) groups. Random Forest predicted resistance with an overall AUC = 0.718, demonstrating reliable performance specifically within high-volume cohorts (Groups 1 and 4).
CONCLUSIONS: Combat wounds demonstrate a severe burden of resistant Gram-negative pathogens with stationary chronological resistance plateaus linked to evacuation and sampling timelines. The rapid colonization kinetics observed during early transit continuum indicate that the institutional reservoir is pervasive across the evacuation network. The machine-learning model provides reliable automated risk stratification for high-volume echelons to optimize empirical selection, while early clinical management must prioritize aggressive surgical debridement and source control over premature antimicrobial escalation.

articles.title: Patient knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding postoperative patient-controlled analgesia: a cross-sectional study using structural equation modelling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative pain management is crucial for recovery, and Patient-Controlled Analgesia (PCA) provides an important self-administration method for pain relief. However, inadequate understanding can hinder its optimal use. Therefore, this study aimed to explore patients' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding postoperative PCA.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among postoperative patients using a self-designed KAP questionnaire through a non-random, non-probability convenience sampling method at one hospital from September 12, 2023 to December 25, 2023. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between knowledge, attitude, and practice.
RESULTS: The study enrolled 451 participants, averaging 48.76 ± 15.87 years in age, with 42.35% utilizing intravenous PCA. The knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 9.10 ± 3.87 (out of 24), 19.02 ± 3.96 (out of 30), and 29.95 ± 7.24 (out of 50), respectively. SEM revealed a direct positive influence of knowledge on practice (β = 0.538, P = 0.012) and a direct negative influence of knowledge on attitude (β = -0.355, P = 0.009), with no significant direct effect of attitude on practice.
CONCLUSION: Patients demonstrated insufficient knowledge, negative attitudes, and suboptimal practices regarding postoperative PCA. The negative knowledge-attitude correlation may be attributed to a phenomenon of blind optimism or the bliss of ignorance, where patients with lower knowledge exhibit more favorable, albeit ungrounded, attitudes toward PCA. Additionally, the failure of attitudes to influence practice highlights that favorable beliefs alone cannot drive behavioral change without skill-building and systemic support. Despite single-center and convenience sampling limitations, these findings underscore the need for nuanced interventions addressing both psychological complexities and practical barriers to PCA use.

articles.title: MRI-derived lumbosacral cerebrospinal fluid volume influences both the extent and persistence of spinal anesthesia: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Considerable interindividual variability exists in the spread and duration of spinal anesthesia despite standardized anesthetic techniques. Lumbosacral cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) volume has been proposed as an important anatomical determinant of neuraxial block characteristics. However, its influence on clinically relevant outcomes beyond peak sensory block level remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between MRI-derived lumbosacral CSF volume and spinal anesthesia characteristics in patients undergoing elective lower extremity orthopedic surgery.
METHODS: Thirty-nine patients undergoing elective lower extremity orthopedic surgery under spinal anesthesia were prospectively evaluated. Lumbosacral CSF volume was measured using semi-automated segmentation of three-dimensional T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) datasets. Correlations between CSF volume and spinal block characteristics were assessed using Pearson or Spearman correlation analyses, as appropriate. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of peak sensory block level.
RESULTS: The mean lumbosacral CSF volume was 12.60 ± 5.16 cm³. Lower CSF volumes were significantly associated with higher peak sensory block levels (ρ = -0.475, p = 0.002), longer sensory block duration (ρ = -0.455, p = 0.006), longer motor block duration (ρ = -0.445, p = 0.007), prolonged two-segment regression time (ρ = -0.343, p = 0.015), and higher sensory block levels at 5 min (ρ = -0.483, p = 0.004). Height demonstrated a moderate positive correlation with CSF volume (ρ = 0.529, p < 0.01). In multivariable regression analysis, lumbosacral CSF volume was identified as the only independent predictor of peak sensory block level (β = -0.563, p < 0.001), explaining 31.7% of the observed variability (R² = 0.317).
CONCLUSION: MRI-derived lumbosacral CSF volume influences both the extent and persistence of spinal anesthesia. Lower CSF volumes were associated with greater cephalad sensory spread, prolonged sensory and motor blockade, and delayed regression. Furthermore, lumbosacral CSF volume emerged as the only independent predictor of peak sensory block level in multivariable analysis. These findings suggest that lumbosacral CSF volume is an important anatomical determinant of spinal anesthesia behavior and may contribute to future individualized neuraxial anesthetic planning.

articles.title: Tailored strategies for vitamin C, D, iron, and carnitine in critical illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Micronutrients are essential cofactors for metabolic, immune, and cellular processes. Low plasma concentrations are frequent in ICU patients but poorly reflect tissue stores. Inflammation drives redistribution and utilisation, while disease, reduced intake, impaired absorption, dilution, and increased losses may contribute to true deficiency. Plasma values, therefore, cannot distinguish redistribution from deficiency, making individualised requirement estimation difficult. This narrative review focuses on four micronutrients of recent high interest, aiming to address some missing links in critical illness.
MAIN BODY: Current guidelines recommend routine provision of basal micronutrient requirements for all ICU patients, with additional monitoring and increased doses reserved for high-risk groups with losses. Plasma measurements, often the only available tool, should be interpreted alongside inflammatory markers, clinical context, and risk factors. Large RCTs of vitamin C have mainly yielded neutral or negative results, which may reflect unguided supplementation across heterogeneous populations without accounting for timing, duration, dosing strategies, and biochemical formulation variability; alternatively, vitamin C may simply be ineffective as an early intervention in critical illness. Available evidence from ICU vitamin D trials indicates signals of outcome benefit, but the evidence is heterogeneous and trial sizes are limited, preventing firm ICU-specific recommendations. Ongoing large trials are expected to clarify effects of high-dose strategies. Iron status spans a narrow therapeutic window: iron deficiency and anaemia are highly prevalent during and after ICU, yet iron overload and ferroptosis-related toxicity also contribute to organ dysfunction. Targeted, hepcidin-guided intravenous (I.V.) iron therapy appears promising to safely correct deficiency. Both carnitine deficiency and high blood levels are associated with worse outcomes in ICU patients. Risk factors for alterations in carnitine concentrations include CRRT, renal and hepatic dysfunction, valproate use, inflammation, and wound losses. Supplementation should be evaluated in a stepwise approach to detect potentially excessive levels in a dose-finding RCT.
CONCLUSION: New biomarkers and analytical approaches are needed to differentiate redistribution from deficiency, capturing dynamic changes over time. Future approaches should move beyond plasma measurements toward cellular and functional biomarkers that better reflect stores and biological activity. Given current limitations, testing should be selective to where results are expected to alter management, include CRP, and timing guided by underlying risk. Research should prioritise precision strategies with better biomarkers and longitudinal sampling to account for dynamic risk, needs, losses, and responses.

articles.title: Perioperative transient myoclonic state with asterixis in an elderly patient: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transient myoclonic state with asterixis (TMA) is characterized by repetitive, short-lived myoclonus without impaired consciousness disturbance. Herein, we report a case of an elderly man who developed TMA perioperatively.
CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 80 s who was independent in activities of daily living underwent lumbar laminectomy under general anesthesia. Post-operatively, he emerged from anesthesia without any issues including neurological symptoms. On the night of postoperative day (POD) 1, he remained conscious, but developed acute dysarthria, finger tremor, and involuntary tremulous movements involving the face, neck, tongue, and bilateral upper extremities. Routine laboratory investigations and brain magnetic resonance imaging showed no abnormalities. He was diagnosed with TMA and responded well to oral clonazepam.
CONCLUSIONS: TMA should be recognized in the differential diagnosis of acute onset involuntary movements, particularly in patients after general anesthesia. Increased awareness of this condition is important to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary interventions and ensure appropriate management.

articles.title: Advancing evidence quality and reproducibility in endoscopic transorbital approach in neurosurgery research: a systematic review and reporting guideline for enhanced comparability.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the quality of studies reporting clinical and surgical outcomes of meningiomas and trigeminal schwannomas treated with the endoscopic transorbital approach (ETOA), and to develop a Reporting Guideline to enhance reproducibility, data pooling and comparability.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science up to July 2025. We included studies reporting patients with meningiomas or trigeminal schwannomas that were treated with ETOA. Reporting quality was assessed across nine domains: (1) patient baseline characteristics; (2) imaging methods and tumor features; (3) definitions of pivotal concepts; (4) neurosurgical/interventional team characteristics; (5) anesthetic protocol; (6) surgical procedure details; (7) clinical and procedural outcomes, including adverse events; (8) retreatment details; and (9) funding and conflicts of interest. Additionally, baseline characteristics of the included studies were extracted to contextualize our analysis.
RESULTS: Thirteen observational studies comprising 310 patients (81.6% meningiomas, 18.4% trigeminal schwannomas) were included. Critical appraisal revealed consistent shortcomings across all nine domains, highlighting major gaps in the current literature. The main gaps included the lack of reporting previous comorbidities, tumor classification, clear definitions of perioperative complications, morbidity, and mortality, as well as anesthesia related details. Additional gaps included limited reporting on symptom duration, elective versus emergency status, intraoperative and postoperative complications - particularly hemorrhage, mortality, and its underlying causes. Based on these findings, we developed the Endoscopic Transorbital Approach Reporting Guideline, comprising 70 items across the nine domains, designed to standardize reporting of surgical and clinical outcomes.
CONCLUSION: This systematic review revealed substantial methodological and reporting deficiencies, which undermine the reliability of current evidence and constrain the advancement of knowledge in this field. The proposed Reporting Guideline provides a structured framework to address these shortcomings and to improve transparency, reproducibility, and comparability in future research, ultimately strengthening the evidence base and improving patient care.

articles.title: Association of preoperative sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use with postoperative delirium and long-term cognitive decline in older adults: a target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is an important postoperative neurocognitive complication associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes, particularly in older adults with type 2 diabetes. Current perioperative guidelines recommend withholding sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors 3-4 days before surgery to prevent euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis. We emulated a target trial to investigate whether recent preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with clinically coded postoperative delirium and subsequent cognitive diagnostic outcomes.
METHODS: Using the TriNetX global health research network, we identified adults aged ≥ 60 years with type 2 diabetes undergoing major operative procedures between January 2016 and December 2025. Applying a new-user design and 1:1 propensity score matching, we compared patients with recent preoperative prescriptions for SGLT2 inhibitors within 90 days preoperatively with matched non-users. The primary outcome was clinically coded postoperative delirium within 7 days. Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality and long-term coded cognitive diagnostic outcomes.
RESULTS: The matched cohort included 126,190 patients (63,095 per group). SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a lower risk of clinically coded postoperative delirium compared with non-use (3.98% vs. 4.53%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.83-0.92; P < .001). Exploratory surgical-category analyses suggested that the association was more pronounced in cardiovascular and respiratory procedures than in several other surgical categories, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Long-term follow-up (> 5 years) revealed lower risks of subsequent coded delirium and coded cognitive diagnostic outcomes among SGLT2 inhibitor users. Findings were consistent across several sensitivity analyses and were supported by negative control analyses, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower risks of postoperative delirium and long-term cognitive outcomes in older adults with type 2 diabetes undergoing surgery. These findings identify a clinically important perioperative neurocognitive signal in a population increasingly exposed to SGLT2 inhibitors. Because residual confounding, exposure misclassification, and outcome underascertainment cannot be excluded, prospective studies with adjudicated exposure, standardized delirium assessment, and perioperative safety monitoring are needed.

articles.title: Association between perioperative blood transfusion and 30-day complications in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Perioperative blood transfusion (PBT) is a common intervention in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. However, its association with postoperative complications remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PBT and 30-day complications in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted using the clinical database of a tertiary referral center for elderly patients (≥ 60 years) who underwent hip fracture surgery between December 1, 2021, and December 22, 2022. The primary outcome was the incidence of 30-day composite complications, including both major and minor complications following surgery. Multivariate logistic regression was used to assess the association between PBT and outcomes, and the adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were calculated.
RESULTS: Of the 1,156 included patients (64.8% female; median age 76 years), the 30-day composite complications rates were 36.6% (260 patients) in the PBT group and 23.6% (105 patients) in the non-transfusion group (P < 0.001). In multivariate models, an increased risk of 30-day composite complications in elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery was significantly associated with PBT (preoperative only: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.946; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.519-5.716; intraoperative or postoperative only: aOR, 2.499; 95% CI, 1.421-4.394; preoperative and intraoperative or postoperative: aOR, 2.436; 95% CI, 1.324-4.483) compared to patients without transfusions.
CONCLUSION: Among elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, PBT is observed to be associated with an increased risk of 30-day composite complications, and the timing of preoperative transfusion may represent a period of heightened risk.

articles.title: Admission body mass index categories and short-term mortality in critically ill adults: a retrospective cohort study using Asian-oriented cut points.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Admission body mass index (BMI) is routinely available in intensive care, but BMI-mortality associations are difficult to interpret because BMI may reflect adiposity, nutritional reserve, sarcopenia, fluid status, illness severity, and selection processes. We evaluated admission BMI category in relation to in-hospital mortality and intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in critically ill adults using Asian-oriented BMI cut points.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adult ICU admissions from 2018 to 2020. BMI was categorized using Asian-oriented cut points as < 18.5, 18.5-23.9, 24.0-26.9, and > = 27.0 kg/m². The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; ICU mortality was secondary. Multivariable logistic regression with patient-level cluster-robust standard errors adjusted for age, sex, APACHE II score, ICU type, admission source, and selected comorbidities. A conceptual directed acyclic graph was added to clarify the assumed covariate structure and to guide interpretation of the adjusted associations.
RESULTS: Among 16,692 ICU admissions, BMI was available for 11,923/16,692 (71.4%). Adjusted analyses included 11,450/11,923 admissions (96.0%) for in-hospital mortality and 11,379/11,923 admissions (95.4%) for ICU mortality. In-hospital mortality was 22.8% (314/1,376), 15.8% (747/4,729), 12.5% (352/2,806), and 9.4% (283/3,012) across increasing BMI categories. Compared with normal BMI, adjusted odds ratios for in-hospital mortality were 1.31 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.62; p = 0.011) for underweight, 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.95; p = 0.012) for overweight, and 0.61 (95% CI 0.50-0.74; p < 0.001) for obesity. Obesity was also associated with lower ICU mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.58-0.90; p = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Admission BMI category was associated with short-term mortality in this cohort. The findings should be interpreted as adjusted associations rather than evidence that higher BMI is causally protective. The substantial proportion of missing BMI data, uncertainty around anthropometric measurement, and residual confounding limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: Risk factors and a perioperative prediction model for postreperfusion syndrome in donation after circulatory death liver transplantation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postreperfusion syndrome (PRS) is a common and clinically important complication during liver transplantation. It is characterized by marked hemodynamic instability after graft reperfusion and has been associated with adverse perioperative outcomes. However, perioperative factors associated with PRS in donation after circulatory death (DCD) liver transplantation remain incompletely defined, and clinically applicable prediction tools are limited. This study aimed to identify perioperative factors associated with PRS, develop an internally validated prediction model, and explore the relationship between PRS and postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult recipients who underwent orthotopic liver transplantation using DCD grafts at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University between January 2016 and May 2025. PRS was defined as a decrease in mean arterial pressure of at least 30% from the prereperfusion baseline within 5 min after reperfusion, lasting for at least 1 min. Prespecified donor-, recipient-, and intraoperative variables were screened, and a limited number of clinically plausible candidate predictors were entered into multivariable logistic regression to reduce the risk of overfitting. A nomogram was constructed from the final model. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap internal validation. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression were used to explore the association between PRS and long-term outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 430 eligible recipients, 82 developed PRS, yielding an incidence of 19.1%. Multivariable analysis identified donor age ≥ 40 years (OR 3.54, 95% CI 1.65-7.59; P = 0.001), donor ALT ≥ 200 U/L (OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.66-9.46; P = 0.002), hepatic encephalopathy (OR 3.90, 95% CI 1.48-10.27; P = 0.006), severe thrombocytopenia (≤ 30 × 109/L) (OR 3.34, 95% CI 1.34-8.37; P = 0.010), and higher prereperfusion norepinephrine infusion rate (OR 1.12 per 0.1 µg/kg/min increase, 95% CI 1.01-1.24; P = 0.031) as independent factors associated with PRS. The model showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.736, 95% CI 0.668-0.804) and reasonable calibration; the optimism-corrected C-index after bootstrap validation was 0.64. Patients with PRS had greater intraoperative blood loss and transfusion requirements, higher postoperative NT-proBNP, serum creatinine, and bilirubin levels, longer ICU stay and mechanical ventilation duration, and higher rates of early allograft dysfunction and acute kidney injury (all P < 0.05). PRS was also associated with higher mortality in the overall cohort (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.08-2.23; P = 0.02). In subgroup analyses, this association was more evident in recipients with non-malignant liver disease than in those with hepatocellular carcinoma.
CONCLUSIONS: In DCD liver transplantation, older donor age, elevated donor ALT, hepatic encephalopathy, severe thrombocytopenia, and greater prereperfusion norepinephrine requirement were independently associated with PRS. The proposed model may serve as an internally developed perioperative risk-stratification tool, although further external validation is needed. PRS was associated with worse perioperative outcomes, and its relationship with long-term survival appeared to vary across recipient subgroups.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction model of transition from acute kidney injury to acute kidney disease after liver transplantation: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to acute kidney disease (AKD) is a frequent sequela after liver transplantation (LT), associated with increased short-term mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and increased likelihood of progression to chronic kidney disease. Early identification of high-risk patients remains a critical unmet need. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based model for early prediction of AKI-to-AKD transition after LT.
METHODS: Patients who underwent LT and developed postoperative AKI between January 2019 and December 2022 were enrolled as the development cohort (n = 359), randomly allocated into a training set and an internal validation set. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated to construct prediction models. All models were subsequently assessed in a temporal validation cohort in the same medical center (n = 104 from January 2024 to December 2025). The Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. An online risk calculator was developed based on the final model.
RESULTS: The incidence of postoperative AKD in the training set was 57.1%. AKD progression was associated with 8 predictors: postoperative day 7 blood urea nitrogen (BUN), preoperative serum creatinine (Scr), postoperative day 7 sodium, calcineurin inhibitor overexposure, imipenem/cilastatin use, amphotericin B use, sex, and cefoperazone/sulbactam use. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.805 in the internal validation cohort and 0.809 in the temporal validation cohort, with good calibration. SHAP analysis indicated that postoperative BUN, preoperative Scr, and postoperative sodium were the most influential predictors. Decision curve analysis demonstrated net clinical benefit.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and temporally validated an interpretable predictive model for AKI-to-AKD transition after LT, which can facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide individualized nephroprotective strategies.

articles.title: Quality of postoperative recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection as affected by transversus abdominis plane block combined with moderate neuromuscular blockade: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery quality in laparoscopic surgery may benefit from deep neuromuscular blockade, whereas the effects of combining transversus abdominis plane block (TAPB) with moderate neuromuscular blockade in this regard remain unreported. This work investigated whether moderate neuromuscular blockade differs from deep neuromuscular blockade in terms of postoperative recovery quality in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery with routine TAPB, to provide evidence-based support for optimizing perioperative neuromuscular blockade strategies.
METHODS: 110 patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery were randomized to moderate (train-of-four count 1-2) or deep (post-tetanic count 1-2) neuromuscular block, with both groups undergoing TAPB. The primary outcome was recovery quality assessed by the Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40) on postoperative day 1 (POD1).
RESULTS: No statistically significant between-group differences in mean POD1 QoR-40 scores were found (172.18 ± 6.78 vs. 172.51 ± 6.89; 95% CI - 2.91 to 2.26; P = 0.802), with no significant differences across the scale's five subdomains.
CONCLUSIONS: During TAPB application for laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection, no clinically meaningful differences in postoperative recovery quality were identified between moderate and deep neuromuscular blockade.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500103278, registered 27 May 2025.

articles.title: Back to bedside: reflections on how we diagnose neuropathic pain.
Comparison of gasping breaths induced by three commonly used volatile anesthetics in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies showed that administration of inhaled 2-MAC sevoflurane induces gasping in mice by activating a persistent sodium current in the brainstem, an effect blocked by riluzole. However, whether other commonly used volatile anesthetics elicit a similar gasping response in mice has not previously been investigated. This study compared respiratory responses to high doses of three volatile anesthetics.
METHODS: Seven spontaneously breathing adult mice each inhaled one of three anesthetics (sevoflurane, isoflurane, and desflurane) on separate days, and eventually inhaled all three anesthetics. Each anesthetic concentration was increased from 1 MAC to inhaled 2-MAC, while breathing patterns and suprahyoid muscle electromyographic activity (EMGSH) were measured. The effects of riluzole (18 mg/kg, i.p.) on gasping were also tested in five additional mice anesthetized with desflurane and/or isoflurane.
RESULTS: All three inhaled anesthetics altered the respiratory pattern from eupnea in 1 MAC to gasping in inhaled 2-MAC in seven mice. However, the time course of ventilation and EMGSH responses to volatile anesthetics at inhaled 2-MAC differed significantly among the three agents: desflurane had the strongest inhibitory effect on inspiratory and EMGSH activities, isoflurane had the weakest inhibitory effects and promoted stable gasping, and sevoflurane showed an intermediate effect. In addition, riluzole administration eliminated isoflurane- and desflurane-induced gasping in five mice.
CONCLUSION: All three anesthetics produced a similar gasping response at inhaled 2-MAC; however, the response's time course and the mechanism by which stable gasping was maintained depend heavily on the volatile anesthetic used.

articles.title: Perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation after initial burn surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early surgical intervention, including debridement and grafting, is crucial in acute burn injury management.
