Although early extubation in operating rooms (ORs) reduces intensive care unit length of stay and ventilator-associated complications, extubation feasibility following initial burn surgery remains uncertain. We investigated perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation (MV) after initial burn surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed patients with burns who underwent acute-phase debridement between 2018 and 2024. Patients requiring postoperative MV were compared with those extubated in ORs. Factors independently associated with postoperative MV were identified using multivariate logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: Among 418 patients, 75 required postoperative MV. Age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.03, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-1.06), percentage of total body surface area (%TBSA) burned (aOR = 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.12), preoperative intubation (aOR = 11.8, 95% CI 3.02-46.4), intraoperative fluid administration volume (ml/kg) (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and intraoperative maximum vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.10-1.26) were independently associated with postoperative MV continuation. This association between the intraoperative maximum VIS and postoperative MV continuation was maintained in the sensitivity analysis excluding preoperatively intubated patients (aOR = 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25).
CONCLUSION: Age, %TBSA burned, preoperative intubation, intraoperative fluid administration volume, and maximum intraoperative VIS were independently associated with postoperative continuation of MV after initial burn surgery. Maximum intraoperative VIS may provide additional information regarding the hemodynamic component of perioperative severity by quantifying the intensity of vasoactive and inotropic support required during surgery.

articles.title: Professionalism and leadership in obstetric anesthesia: from ethical practice to teamwork.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To examine how professionalism and leadership support safe, respectful obstetric anesthesia and clarify the contribution and limitations of the proposed Integrated Professionalism-Leadership Framework for Obstetric Anesthesia (IPL-OA).
RECENT FINDINGS: Professionalism increasingly encompasses organizational responsibilities alongside individual conduct. Obstetric anesthesia guidance emphasizes maternal autonomy, response to pain, and continuity of care. Teamwork and simulation literature supports communication and coordination, although evidence directly linking leadership interventions to improved maternal outcomes remains limited. Consensus recommendations, observational associations, and intervention findings, therefore, require different interpretations. IPL-OA connects six domains across clinician, team, unit, and institutional levels. Its proposed contribution is a specialty-specific mapping of ethical commitments to observable actions, enabling resources, accountable owners, and candidate measures. An illustrative pathway for inadequate neuraxial anesthesia during cesarean delivery demonstrates this mapping without presenting patient data or observed improvement.
SUMMARY: IPL-OA is an unvalidated implementation proposal that complements existing competency, high reliability, and clinical frameworks. Its evaluation should establish feasibility and measurement reliability before testing added benefit over existing care. Patient experience, equity, workforce conditions, and unintended effects should accompany clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Validation of weight-based formulae for estimating paediatric epidural depth.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accurate prediction of epidural depth in children enhances procedural success and safety in regional anaesthesia. Multiple weight-based formulae exist, yet comparative validation using both actual procedural and imaging data is limited. We aimed to evaluate and identify the most reliable formulae for estimating lumbar and thoracic epidural depth in paediatric patients using retrospective needle depth and prospective ultrasound measurements.
METHODS: Seven published formulae were applied to a retrospective cohort (n = 140) with recorded needle depth at 'loss of resistance' and a prospective cohort (n = 70) with ultrasound-measured posterior dura depth. Performance was assessed using goodness-of-fit statistics adjusted for age, mean absolute error (MAE), the proportions of estimates within ±0.5 cm and ±1.0 cm of the measured depth, and Bland-Altman agreement analyses.
RESULTS: For lumbar epidurals, Hasan's formula (Depth = 0.8 + 0.05 × weight in kg) demonstrated the best fit across both measurement methods, yielding a MAE of 0.16-0.26 cm, with 88.7%-95.7% of predictions within ±0.5 cm and up to 98.6% within ±1.0 cm. For thoracic epidurals, Wong's formula (Depth = 1.06 + 0.067 × weight in kg) showed the strongest correlation, with a MAE of 0.21-0.33 cm and up to 92.9% of estimates within ±0.5 cm.
CONCLUSION: These two formulae provide bedside estimates of dura depth in paediatric patients with clinically acceptable accuracy and may support pre-procedural planning, although their clinical impact on complication rates and procedure time requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Electroencephalography-derived spectral edge frequency 95 targets in toddlers under propofol anaesthesia✰.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proprietary processed EEG indices are less accurate in young children. We evaluated spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), a nonproprietary EEG index representing the frequency below which 95% of total EEG power resides, to establish target thresholds for varying anaesthetic depths during propofol anaesthesia in toddlers. Secondary objectives were to assess the relationship between SEF95 and plasma propofol concentration, and to evaluate airway reactivity during laryngoscopy.
METHODS: In this prospective study of toddlers aged 13 to 24 months, Dixon's up-and-down method and centred isotonic regression were used to determine the SEF95 targets for 50% (ED50) and 90% (ED90) probability of nonresponse to three clinical stimuli: pacifier placement (assessing consciousness), electrical nerve stimulation (nociception), and laryngoscopy (intubation readiness). Linear mixed-effects regression was used to analyse the association between plasma propofol concentration and SEF95.
RESULTS: Among 51 toddlers, SEF95 ED50 and ED90 targets (Hz) were 21.8 (90% CI 20.8-23.4) and 20.3 (19.1-20.7) Hz for pacifier placement, 12.0 (10.8-18.3) and 10.4 (8.7-11.3) Hz for electrical stimulation, and 10.3 (4.6-11.8) and 4.4 (1.5-5.4) Hz for laryngoscopy. Each 1 Hz increase in SEF95 corresponded to a 0.21 μg ml-1 decrease in plasma propofol (r=0.46, P<0.001), as described by the equation: plasma propofol concentration (μg ml-1)=5.80-0.21×SEF95 (Hz).
CONCLUSIONS: This study defined EEG SEF95 targets for loss of consciousness, response to noxious stimuli, and intubation readiness in toddlers aged 13 to 24 months. When combined with existing infant data, these age-specific SEF95 targets can optimise propofol titration and dosing accuracy during EEG-guided propofol anaesthesia in patients aged <2 yr.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT05701748. Registered 17 January 2023; PI: Ian Yuan.

articles.title: Sugammadex versus neostigmine in adults aged 60 years and older undergoing surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of postoperative recovery and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncertainty remains regarding the clinical advantages of sugammadex over neostigmine in older adults, particularly for recovery efficiency and postoperative outcomes.
AIM: To compare the effects of sugammadex versus neostigmine on postoperative recovery and clinical outcomes in adults aged 60 years and older undergoing surgery.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis included eight randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was postoperative residual neuromuscular blockade (PRNB). Secondary outcomes included post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, time to extubation, hypoxemia, pneumonia, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). Effect measures were risk ratio and mean difference.
RESULTS: A total of 851 participants were included, and 50.2% received sugammadex. Sugammadex was associated with a lower risk of PRNB (RR 0.34 [95% CI: 0.18; 0.64]; p < 0.001; I² = 54%), with moderate between-study heterogeneity; however, the 95% prediction interval (0.11; 1.03) included the null value. Sugammadex significantly reduced PACU length of stay (MD -8.84 [95% CI: -12.18; -5.51], p < 0.001, I2 = 0%), hospital length of stay (MD -1.12 [95% CI: -2.01; -0.24], p < 0.01, I2 = 16%), and hypoxemia (RR = 0.61 [95% CI: 0.38; 0.97]; p = 0.04, I2 = 0%). No statistically significant differences were observed for the remaining outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Sugammadex was associated with a lower risk of PRNB and shorter PACU stays compared with neostigmine. Although the primary analyses suggested reductions in hypoxemia and hospital length of stay, these associations were not statistically significant after the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. INTERNATIONAL PROSPECTIVE REGISTER OF SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS (PROSPERO): CRD420261376045.

articles.title: Empiric Antifungal Therapy in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Surgery for Severe Intra-Abdominal Infection: a Large Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-abdominal candidiasis is frequent in critically ill surgical patients and is associated with high mortality. Whether empiric antifungal therapy improves outcomes after surgery for intra-abdominal infection (IAI) in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center data warehouse-based cohort study of 1,061 adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) after surgery for IAI between 2018 and 2024. Patients who received systemic antifungal therapy within 24 hours after surgery were compared with those who did not. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were day-5 renal dysfunction, assessed by the renal SOFA component and the creatinine-based KDIGO stage, and the need for surgical reintervention. Adjusted analyses used propensity-score overlap weighting. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses used a Peritonitis Score ≥3, the identification of at least one organism in peritoneal samples, and a yeast-positive peritoneal sample.
RESULTS: Empiric antifungal therapy was initiated in 46.0% of patients. Peritoneal sampling was available in 957 patients (90.2%); 21.4% had no organism identified and 25.2% had a yeast-positive sample. In adjusted analyses, empiric therapy was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality (OR 1.53, 95% CI 0.83-2.78), lower day-5 renal SOFA score, lower KDIGO stage, or fewer reinterventions. Findings were consistent in patients with Peritonitis Score ≥3, with at least one identified organism, and with a yeast-positive sample. ICU and hospital stays were longer in treated patients after weighting.
CONCLUSIONS: Empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 24 hours after surgery for severe IAI was not associated with improved short-term outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NA.

articles.title: Monitoring of Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in the ICU: the MAVERIC pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous congestion is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of organ dysfunction during acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Although the Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) score is a promising bedside marker of systemic venous congestion, its dynamic evolution during CRRT remains unknown. We aimed to describe serial changes in VExUS during CRRT and explore their association with ultrafiltration intensity and fluid balance.
METHODS: MAVERIC was a prospective single-centre observational pilot study including adults undergoing CRRT for acute kidney injury. VExUS was assessed before CRRT initiation and after 24 and 48 hours. The primary objective was to describe temporal changes in VExUS using an alluvial plot. Patients were classified into three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution. Associations with net ultrafiltration (NUF) and cumulative fluid balance were explored.
RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were included. Overall, VExUS grades decreased significantly during the first 48 hours of CRRT (p = 0.0048). Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were identified: persistently low congestion (45%, n = 21), resolving congestion (32%, n = 15), and persistent or worsening congestion (23%, n = 11). Patients with resolving congestion had the highest NUF rates (1.35 [0.85-1.66] mL/kg/h) and the most negative cumulative fluid balance (-36.7 [-74.6 to -21.1] mL/kg), with significant differences across groups (p = 0.003 and p < 0.001, respectively). Patients with persistent or worsening congestion had lower NUF rates.
CONCLUSIONS: Serial VExUS assessment provides dynamic information on systemic venous congestion during CRRT. Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were associated with differences in net ultrafiltration and fluid balance. Serial VExUS monitoring may help identify patients with persistent or worsening congestion, raising the hypothesis that it could inform reassessment of decongestion strategies. Whether integrating serial VExUS assessment into individualised decongestive strategies improves renal outcomes should be evaluated in prospective interventional studies.

articles.title: Accuracy and Precision of Acceleromyography and Electromyography at the Adductor Pollicis Muscle in Restricted Thumb Movement Positions: An Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative neuromuscular monitoring commonly uses acceleromyography (AMG) or electromyography (EMG). Acceleromyography requires unrestricted thumb movement, whereas EMG is independent of thumb motion. We compared the accuracy and precision of AMG and EMG responses after patients' arms were immobilized during routine surgical positioning.
METHODS: Patients undergoing general anaesthesia without neuromuscular block were enrolled. EMG and AMG monitors were placed on contralateral arms, and both arms were tucked under surgical drapes. The monitors simultaneously recorded train-of-four ratio (TOFR) after ulnar nerve stimulation every minute. Accuracy was defined as TOFR variability from the expected baseline value (1.00), and precision as consistency of repeated measurements, quantified by the coefficient of repeatability (CR). Failed measurements were defined as the absence of valid quantitative TOFR values, displayed as "0" or "?". AMG TOFR values were normalized to patient-specific baseline TOFR measurements for secondary analyses.
RESULTS: Forty patients provided 3,733 TOFR measurements (1,879 EMG and 1,854 AMG). EMG was more accurate than AMG (mean EMG-AMG difference in absolute deviation from 1.0, -0.108; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.134 to -0.083; p < 0.001) and more precise, with a smaller CR (0.10 vs. 0.35; p < 0.001), including compared with normalized AMG (CR, 0.35). Device failure rate was lower with EMG than AMG (3.6% vs. 27.7%; p = 0.0003). Failures increased over time, particularly for AMG after approximately 45 minutes.
CONCLUSION: EMG provided more accurate and precise TOFR measurements than AMG, including normalized AMG, with fewer failures, supporting EMG-based monitoring when upper extremity mobility is restricted.
REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Database (Registration Number: NCT06805032, Principal investigator: J.R.R., date of registration January 28, 2025).

articles.title: Calm in Crisis: Lessons from My First Intraoperative Emergency.
Perioperative Right Heart Failure in Cardiac Surgery: Reply.
Rethinking the Responsible Adult Requirement after Ambulatory Anesthesia: Toward Risk-stratified Discharge.
articles.abstract: For decades, ambulatory anesthesia pathways have commonly required a "responsible adult" before discharge after sedation or anesthesia. In practice, this requirement may function as a binary eligibility criterion based on a patient's social circumstances. However, the empirical evidence evaluating discharge without an escort remains limited and derives largely from observational studies. This Focal Point argues that carefully selected low-risk patients should be studied within structured alternative discharge pathways that preserve safe transportation, communication, observation, and rescue capacity. Such pathways should not permit self-driving or unrestricted solo discharge. The aim is to determine whether postanesthesia safeguards can be matched more precisely to patient, anesthetic, procedural, recovery, transport, and postdischarge risk while preserving conventional adult support for patients whose clinical circumstances warrant it.

articles.title: I Told You So! Scientists Who Were Ridiculed, Exiled, and Imprisoned for Being Right.
Perioperative Right Heart Failure in Cardiac Surgery: Comment.
Advanced Heterotopic Pregnancy with Invasive Extrauterine Placentation.
Value of Magnetic Resonance Imaging before Cesarean Delivery in Klippel-Feil Syndrome.
Trends in Women Entering Anesthesiology and Other High-compensation Specialties Relative to the U.S. Doctor of Medicine Graduate Pipeline, 2010 to 2024.
Tegileridine versus Sufentanil for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting after Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind Superiority Trial.
Evaluating the analgesic effectiveness of erector spinae plane block for patients undergoing cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Sex, Smoking Status, and Long-Term Outcomes After Lung Cancer Resection: An STS General Thoracic Surgery Database Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of lung cancer in women is increasing, yet the effect of smoking history on survival remains uncertain.
METHODS: Adults who underwent resection for non-small cell lung cancer (2015-2024), from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons database, were grouped by sex and smoking status. Outcomes were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and Cox models.
RESULTS: In total, 145,103 patients were identified (current or former smoker women: 65,650 [45.2%]; current or former smoker men: 55,912 [38.5%]; never-smoker women: 16,902 [11.7%]; never-smoker men: 6,639 [4.6%]. Median age was 69 years. Never-smoker women were more likely to be Asian, have clinical stage I disease, and have adenocarcinoma; they also had the lowest rates of 30-day mortality and major morbidity. Current or former smoker men had the highest complications rates. These findings persisted after risk adjustment. Longitudinal mortality data were available for 59,756 patients (57%). Five-year survival was 79% for never-smoker women, 70% for never-smoker men, 71% for current or former smoker women, and 58% for current or former smoker men. Risk-adjusted survival was longer in women versus men and in never-smokers versus current or former smokers for both sexes. Compared with never-smoker women, all-cause mortality risk was higher in current or former smoker women (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]=1.18 [95% confidence interval {CI},1.11-1.26]), never-smoker men (aHR=1.44[95% CI,1.30-1.60]), and current or former smoker men (aHR=1.71 [95% CI,1.59-1.84]).
CONCLUSIONS: Never-smoker women had the lowest perioperative risk and superior long-term survival, highlighting sex and smoking status as independent determinants of outcomes after lung cancer resection.

articles.title: Vagus nerve stimulation in a patient with bilateral cochlear implants: potential device interactions and clinical considerations.
articles.abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is one of the standard treatments for drug-resistant epilepsy, and cochlear implants (CIs) are one of the standard treatments for profound sensorineural hearing loss. However, case reports combining both CIs and VNS devices are extremely rare, and there is limited knowledge regarding interference between these devices and their safety. We report the case of a 13-year-old boy with drug-resistant epilepsy associated with congenital cytomegalovirus infection, who had previously undergone bilateral cochlear implantation. He presented with multiple seizure types and multifocal epileptogenic discharges on long-term video-electroencephalography. Despite polytherapy, the seizures persisted and VNS was introduced. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, with no device interference between the CIs and VNS. This case demonstrates that patients with bilateral CIs can safely undergo VNS implantation with appropriate perioperative management and postoperative follow-up.

articles.title: Influence of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics on aseptic bone flap resorption: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aseptic bone flap resorption (ABFR) remains a common complication after autologous cranioplasty following decompressive craniectomy (DC), with reported prevalences varying widely-often reported between 10% and 30%-likely due to inconsistent follow-up. Data on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics in pathogenesis of ABFR are scarce. Aim of the present study was therefore to identify potential risk factors, with a particular focus on CSF drainage procedures.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent DC followed by autologous cranioplasty from 2015 to 2022. We collected demographics, clinical details, perioperative variables, and CSF interventions. Univariate and multivariate analyses identified associations, with subgroup focus on patients completing structured follow-up.
RESULTS: ABFR was diagnosed in 39/259 patients (15.1%), resulting in 38/101 (37.6%) in the 6-months follow-up cohort. Changes in CSF dynamics such as preoperative lumbar CSF drainage (p = 0.035) were identified as a risk factor, whereas ventriculoperitoneal shunt pressure adjustment was not associated with an increased risk of ABFR. After differentiation of the direction of adjustment, pressure reduction was not associated with ABFR. Especially preoperative lumbar CSF drainage remains an independent risk factor (p = 0.023) in multivariate analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Without structured imaging follow-up, ABFR rates are likely underestimated. CSF dynamic alterations beyond shunt presence alone may represent a relevant risk factor for ABFR. Our findings emphasize that primary alloplastic cranioplasty could be considered in at least a subgroup of patients.

articles.title: Surgical hyperlactataemia during resection of an intraventricular meningioma.
articles.abstract: We present the first documented case of intraoperative hyperlactataemia during a minimally invasive resection of an intraventricular meningioma. The phenomenon remains unstudied, which creates a significant gap in both neurosurgical knowledge and patient management during perioperative periods. This will therefore help neurosurgeons and anaesthesiologists to recognise intraoperative metabolic problems, which will lead to further research and the development of better methods to handle such situations.

articles.title: Does gabapentin affect the incidence of postoperative delirium in a dose dependent pattern?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway for Colorectal Surgery (CRS) emphasizes opioid-sparing analgesia to reduce ileus and length of stay (LOS). Our hospital adopted gabapentin as part of postoperative analgesia for CRS. We evaluated the association between perioperative gabapentin use and postoperative delirium (POD).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,165 encounters of patients ≥65 years undergoing elective CRS between 04/2015-06/2023. Encounters requiring critical care, LOS>3 months, or readmissions were excluded. Delirium was identified using chart review, ICD codes and/or new antipsychotic use. Multivariate logistic regression compared delirium rates among three groups: No Gabapentin (NG), low dose (LG) and high dose (HG). Models adjusted for age, race, ethnicity, gender, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), etc. Subgroup analyses investigated delirium by age, gender, CCI.
RESULTS: 1,027 individuals were studied: 20.5% NG, 70.8% LG, and 8.7% HG. NG Individuals were older (75.5±7.2) than LG (74.2±6.7) or HG (72.7±6.6), while CCI (6.6±3.8) was similar across groups. The NG group had more patients with dementia (NG 14.2% vs LG 9.5%, p=0.05 vs HG 11.2%). A higher incidence of POD was noted in NG (34.6%) when compared with LG (25.3%, 1.74(1.22-2.47), adj. p=0.002) as well as HG (23.6%, p=0.06). Prior gabapentin exposure did not significantly impact the incidence of postoperative delirium (OR 1.33 (0.86-2.05)) when the cohort was compared based on prior gabapentin exposure.
CONCLUSION: The use of low dose gabapentin postoperatively is associated with lower incidence of delirium compared to absence of gabapentin. However, the absence of gabapentin in our study is a reflection of baseline vulnerability for delirium. Prior exposure to gabapentin had no influence on incident POD. Future prospective trials are required to address the factors to be considered when determining the optimal dosing of gabapentin in older surgical adults.

articles.title: The effect of two different interventions applied during the transfer of children to the operating room for circumcision on fear, anxiety, comfort and pain levels: Randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of an animal-assisted intervention and kaleidoscope on the fear, anxiety, comfort, and pain levels of children while transferring them to the operating room for circumcision surgery.
METHODS: This randomised controlled trial with pretest-posttest design included 96 children aged 7-10 years who were scheduled for circumcision surgery at the urology and paediatric surgery departments of a State Hospital and met the inclusion criteria (animal-assisted intervention group = 31, kaleidoscope group = 32, control group = 33). The interventions were administered while transferring them to the operating room. Data were collected using five tools: a Child Information Form, the Children's Fear Scale, the Children's Anxiety Meter-State, the Comfort Behaviors Checklist, and the Wong Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance, dependent samples t-test, and Bonferroni post-hoc test.
RESULTS: The posttest mean scores of CFS, CAMS, and FACES were significantly lower in the animal-assisted intervention and kaleidoscope groups than in the control group, while posttest CBC mean scores were significantly higher (p < 0.05). Both interventions alleviated their fear, anxiety, and pain and improved their comfort during the transfer. The animal-assisted intervention was more effective than the kaleidoscope intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: These interventions should be integrated into standard nursing practice for paediatric surgery, particularly during operating room transfer.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Integrating AAI and kaleidoscope interventions into paediatric perioperative nursing care may promote child-friendly practices and improve children's surgical experiences.

articles.title: Beyond Factor Levels: A Narrative Review of Pregnancy Outcome and Bleeding Risk in Congenital Factor VII Deficiency.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCongenital factor VII (FVII) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive bleeding disorder with highly variable clinical expression. Pregnancy management is difficult because FVII activity may rise during gestation in heterozygous women, yet bleeding phenotype and peripartum outcomes correlate poorly with factor level.ObjectiveTo summarize published pregnancies in women with congenital FVII deficiency, clarify how FVII activity, bleeding history, delivery mode, hemostatic prophylaxis, and obstetric factors relate to maternal and neonatal outcomes, and review the reported efficacy and safety of available treatment options.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with descriptive synthesis of published pregnancy cases. PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched from database inception, covering publications available through May 2026. Case reports and case series describing pregnancy outcomes in women with confirmed or presumed congenital FVII deficiency were included. Data were extracted on demographics, genotype or zygosity where reported, FVII activity, bleeding history, delivery mode, anesthesia, prophylaxis, estimated blood loss, thrombotic events, and neonatal outcomes.Bleeding outcomes were standardized using the contemporary ACOG definition of primary PPH, while other clinically significant obstetric bleeding was recorded separately using intervention-based criteria.ResultsForty-five pregnancies from 30 published reports (1992-2026) across 17 countries were identified. Delivery was vaginal in 23 cases and by cesarean section in 20 cases; one case involved medical termination and one did not specify the delivery mode. Severe deficiency (FVII <10%) was present in 27 cases. Among the published cases with evaluable prophylaxis status, hemostatic prophylaxis was administered in 32 of 44 pregnancies (73%). Five of 45 published pregnancies (11%) met contemporary criteria for primary PPH. Five additional cases had other clinically significant primary or peripartum bleeding requiring therapeutic intervention but did not meet contemporary PPH criteria. One source-reported PPH case could not be classified because blood-loss volume and hypovolemia were insufficiently reported. Secondary PPH and clinically significant antepartum hemorrhage occurred in one case each. Most bleeding episodes with a documented etiology were attributable to obstetric or surgical causes, including uterine atony, genital tract laceration, or placental abruption with disseminated intravascular coagulation. However, one recent undiagnosed case developed refractory postpartum hemorrhage after common obstetric causes were excluded, underscoring that coagulopathy may still be contributory.These proportions are descriptive of the published cases and should not be interpreted as population-based estimates of incidence or risk.Four pregnancies were complicated by either confirmed primary PPH or other clinically significant peripartum bleeding despite prophylactic rFVIIa, whereas several pregnancies in women with severe deficiency were managed without prophylaxis and without hemorrhage. These descriptive findings cannot establish prophylactic effectiveness because treatment indications, obstetric risk, and dosing varied across reports.Thrombotic events or thrombotic history were reported in two women. No neonatal hemorrhage was reported among 43 live births.ConclusionsFVII activity alone appears to be an unreliable predictor of peripartum bleeding in the published cases. Management should be individualized according to bleeding phenotype, third-trimester FVII activity, obstetric risk, delivery route, anesthesia requirements, and thrombotic risk. Delivery planning should include timely access to tranexamic acid and appropriate factor replacement when clinically indicated. Postpartum VTE prophylaxis should be individualized according to bleeding stability, thrombotic risk factors, delivery route, and exposure to rFVIIa. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine prophylactic rFVIIa, although it may be considered on a case-by-case basis when the perceived bleeding risk is high. These conclusions are based on heterogeneous case reports and small case series and should be interpreted accordingly.

articles.title: Implementation of a spinal-induced hypotension management bundle for elective cesarean delivery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Spinal-induced hypotension (SIH) remains the most common complication associated with spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery and may compromise maternal hemodynamic stability and uteroplacental perfusion. Evidence supports prophylactic vasopressor therapy, serotonin receptor antagonists, and optimized fluid management; however, these strategies are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. This quality improvement (QI) project evaluated the effect of a standardized SIH management bundle (SIHMB) on maternal hemodynamic outcomes.
METHODS: A prospective QI initiative was conducted in the obstetric operating suites of an academic medical center with a Level II trauma facility. Adult parturients undergoing elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia were included. The intervention bundle consisted of intravenous ondansetron 8 mg administered 5 to 10 minutes prior to spinal anesthesia, crystalloid co-loading with 1 L of fluid during spinal placement, and prophylactic phenylephrine infusion initiated at 0.5 mcg/kg per minute. Data were collected during 12-week preimplementation and postimplementation periods. Primary outcomes included incidence and severity of hypotension. Secondary outcomes included rescue vasopressor use, antiemetic administration, and bundle adherence. This QI project was reported in accordance with the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines for reporting QI initiatives.
RESULTS: A total of 242 patients were included (103 preimplementation, 139 postimplementation). Implementation of the SIHMB significantly reduced the incidence of hypotension from 46% to 32% (P = .024). Mean lowest systolic and diastolic blood pressures increased significantly following implementation. Rescue vasopressor administration decreased from 72% to 49% (P < .001). Utilization of prophylactic phenylephrine infusion increased from 32% to 62%.
CONCLUSION: Implementation of a standardized hemodynamic management bundle significantly improved maternal hemodynamic stability during cesarean delivery. Standardizing prophylactic strategies for SIH may enhance obstetric anesthesia safety and reduce reliance on reactive vasopressor therapy.

articles.title: Maximum dose recommendations for local anesthetics: a scoping review.
Baseline frailty severity and survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive mechanical ventilation in patients with sepsis: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty has been associated with adverse outcomes during mechanical ventilation (MV). We evaluated the association between frailty severity, assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), and survival to intensive care unit (ICU) discharge without ongoing invasive MV.
METHODS: We analyzed adults with sepsis enrolled in the prospective, multicenter Korean Sepsis Alliance registry between September 2019 and December 2023 who received invasive MV on ICU day 1. Patients with CFS 9 were excluded. The primary outcome was survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive MV. Frailty was defined as CFS 5-8 versus CFS 1-4 and was examined across increasing CFS severity using categorical and restricted cubic spline analyses. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a participating-center random intercept was adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, ICU day 1 Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, and infection site.
RESULTS: Among 2,204 patients, 1,458 (66.2%) had CFS 5-8. The primary outcome was achieved by 1,120 patients (50.8%); crude rates were 52.9% in patients with CFS 1-4 and 49.7% in those with CFS 5-8 (P = 0.152). Frailty was associated with lower adjusted odds of the primary outcome (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.73; 95% CI 0.59-0.90). Compared with CFS 1-4, the estimate for CFS 5 was close to the null (OR, 1.08; 95% CI 0.78-1.49), while the odds were lower for CFS 6, 7, and 8 (ORs, 0.68, 0.73, and 0.59, respectively; global P < 0.001). In spline analysis, the adjusted probability of the primary outcome decreased from 58.6% at CFS 1 to 43.3% at CFS 8 (P overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.55). In pairwise analyses of ICU discharge status, frailty was associated with higher odds of survival with ongoing invasive MV versus survival without ongoing invasive MV (adjusted OR, 1.94; 95% CI 1.26-2.98); the corresponding estimate for ICU death versus survival without ongoing invasive MV was 1.22 (95% CI 0.97-1.53).
CONCLUSIONS: Among invasively ventilated patients with sepsis, baseline frailty was associated with lower adjusted odds of survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive MV. These findings support considering frailty severity when discussing recovery and care needs, but do not establish a treatment threshold or a causal effect of frailty.

articles.title: From evidence to bedside: A decade of critical care pharmacotherapy and implications for ICU training.
articles.abstract: Pharmacotherapy management is integral to the care of critically ill patients, yet decisions are frequently made in dynamic and uncertain conditions. Over the last decade, a series of large trials and shifts in understanding have reshaped how therapies are selected and applied in the intensive care unit (ICU), often challenging long-standing practices and refining established treatment strategies. This review examines influential studies and paradigm shifts across four major areas of ICU pharmacotherapy: respiratory failure and acute respiratory distress syndrome, infectious disease and antimicrobial therapy, hemodynamic management in sepsis and septic shock, and sedation and delirium. We highlight how emerging evidence led to pharmacotherapeutic evolution within each domain and identify common patterns across these domains supporting a movement toward individualized, context-dependent care and more deliberate use of pharmacologic therapies. For trainees, the last decade provides important lessons regarding application of pharmacotherapy in the ICU, including the need to integrate evidence interpretation with clinical judgement.

articles.title: Capillary refill time at the admission of trauma patients: A prospective, observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The early identification of tissue perfusion is a significant challenge in the management of severe trauma cases. Capillary refill time (CRT) is a simple clinical marker of peripheral perfusion. The objective of this study was to ascertain the correlation between CRT and serum lactate levels in patients with severe trauma.
METHODS: A prospective, single-center observational study was conducted in a 20-bed intensive care unit (ICU) of a level 1 trauma center between April 2025 and January 2026. Adult patients who were directly admitted to the ICU from the scene of the accident for severe trauma, as defined by an injury severity score above 15, were included in the study. The CRT and serum lactate were measured on admission to the ICU. The primary endpoint was the association between admission serum lactate and admission CRT ≥ 3 s (abnormal CRT). Secondary analyses included the correlation between CRT and serum lactate at admission and the association between CRT and duration of vasopressor exposure during the first 3 days. Multivariate linear regression was performed on logarithmically transformed serum lactate, adjusted for age, core body temperature, prehospital weight-adjusted fluid administration, prehospital use of norepinephrine and prehospital timing.
RESULTS: Of 627 patients screened, 196 were included in the analysis. The admission CRT was 2.4 [1.7-3.1] s with serum lactate level at 2.1 [1.3-3.4] mmol/L. Admission serum lactate did not differ significantly between the patients with abnormal CRT and those with normal CRT (2.6 [1.4-4.6] versus 1.9 [1.3-3.1] mmol/L; p = 0.07) while CRT and serum lactate levels were correlated (r = 0.33; p < 0.01). In multivariate analysis, continuous analysis of CRT was independently associated with serum lactate levels with a 15% increase in serum lactate per additional sec of CRT (95% CI 1.06-1.25; p < 0.01). Among patients with serum lactate >2 mmol/L, abnormal CRT was associated with longer vasopressor exposure at day 3 and increased ICU mortality.
CONCLUSION: Admission lactate did not differ significantly between normal and abnormal CRT groups. Exploratory subgroup findings suggest that CRT may complement serum lactate in characterizing patients with severe trauma.

articles.title: Applications and Current Landscape of Digital Health Technologies in the Continuity of Care for Liver Transplant Candidates and Recipients: Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplant candidates and recipients require continuous care throughout the transplant trajectory, including pretransplant prehabilitation and long-term posttransplant management. Conventional care models are constrained by time, distance, and limited health care resources and may therefore be insufficient to meet patients' needs across the continuum of care. Digital health technologies offer new approaches to remote care delivery and self-management support in liver transplantation.
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to map the technological modalities, intervention components, outcome measures, and implementation issues associated with digital health technologies used across the care continuum for adult liver transplant candidates and recipients and to identify gaps for future digital continuity-of-care research.
METHODS: Nine English- and Chinese-language databases-PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, the Cochrane CENTRAL, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, and SinoMed-were searched from inception through July 10, 2026. Original quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods studies involving adult liver transplant candidates or recipients and the use of digital health technologies for care beyond conventional in-person settings were eligible. The review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework, was refined using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews, and was reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines.
RESULTS: The search identified 7746 records, and 28 studies were included. Telehealth platforms or remote management systems were used in 24 studies, and remote education was included in 22 studies. From the 28 studies, 5 focused on pretransplant/candidacy, 9 focused on early posttransplant recovery, 4 focused on long-term survivorship, 8 were cross-stage/mixed, and 2 had unspecified posttransplant timing. No study focused only on the perioperative/inpatient-to-home transition stage. A total of 9 randomized intervention studies were identified. Among these studies, positive findings were more common for medication or treatment adherence, self-management, health behaviors, psychological outcomes, and selected health service outcomes. Results were less consistent for quality of life, physiological outcomes, and functional outcomes. From the 28 studies, 15 reported implementation-related outcomes. Reported barriers included limited device access, privacy concerns, limited uptake, and difficulties with sustained engagement.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence is concentrated in early posttransplant recovery. Evidence across transplant stages and outcome domains is uneven. Studies focused on the perioperative/inpatient-to-home transition stage are lacking. Future studies should use multicenter designs and standardized outcome measures; include longer follow-up; and evaluate implementation, equitable access, and costs.

articles.title: Early Inflammatory Biomarkers and Outcomes After Liver Transplantation: A pilot Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Early allograft dysfunction (EAD) and ischemic-type biliary lesions (ITBL) remain significant complications following liver transplantation, with limited understanding of their pathogenesis and opportunities for prevention. This exploratory pilot study investigated the associations of perioperative cytokine profiles with EAD, ITBL and other long-term complications.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 33 patients undergoing orthotopic liver transplantation between February and November 2023 were enrolled. Two patients required re-transplantation, resulting in 35 procedures analyzed. Blood samples were collected preoperatively, at 4 hours post-reperfusion, and on postoperative days 1, 4, 7, and 30±4. Cytokine profiles were analyzed using Luminex multiplex assays, and immune cell populations characterized by flow cytometry. The associations between these immunological measurements and clinical outcomes were systematically evaluated.
RESULTS: EAD developed in 57% (20/35) of transplantations. Interleukin-1α (IL-1α) levels at 4 hours after reperfusion were significantly elevated in EAD patients (median 9.6 vs 0.8 pg/mL, p=0.005) with an AUROC of 0.82. Additional pro-inflammatory mediators including Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor (MIF), IL-16, and IL-17 also showed significant associations with EAD development. The IL-1α/IL-1RA ratio was associated with subsequent ITBL development (AUROC 0.80). Hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) levels were elevated in patients with biliary complications. Chemokines Monocyte Chemoattractant Protein-1 (MCP-1) and Stromal Cell-Derived Factor-1α (SDF-1α) at POD1 were similarly associated with subsequent ITBL development. Last, patients with EAD showed reduced fractions of CD4+ T cells and regulatory T cells in blood samples.
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative IL-1α elevation was associated with subsequent EAD development following liver transplantation. MIF, IL-16, and IL-17 provide additional discriminatory power. The preoperative IL-1α/IL-1RA ratio and postoperative HGF, MCP-1, and SDF-1α levels were associated with ITBL development. These biomarkers may help identify patients at risk and warrant validation in larger cohorts to confirm these results and explore their potential to guide therapeutic interventions in the critical early post-transplant period.

articles.title: Can Outpatient Total Hip Arthroplasty Be Done at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary outpatient (same-day discharge) total hip arthroplasty (THA) has gained popularity, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Same-day discharge shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. In contrast, surgeon reimbursements continue to decline. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches associated with outpatient THAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center.
METHODS: At our institution, 1,970 outpatient primary THAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,813 unique patients. The mean age was 61 years, 56% were men, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 30, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.2, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.2 (range, 1 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after THA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed.
RESULTS: Rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.6, 1.5, and 0.9%, respectively. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 131 in 2019 to greater than 4,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (39%), followed by dislocation (14%) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) evaluation (12%; actual VTE incidence 0.3%). The most common reason for reoperation and revision was acute periprosthetic joint infection (PJI; incidence 0.7%). Increasing BMI was associated with risk of reoperations (odds ratio [OR] 1.1; P = 0.02), revisions (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), and PJI (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), but not with ER visits or dislocations. Increasing CCI was associated with risk of first-time ER visits (OR 1.2; P < 0.001) and dislocations (OR 1.3; P = 0.02). Increasing ASA score was associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.8; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Outpatient THA patients had a high rate of ER visits within 90 days postoperatively, with almost 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing BMI was associated with increased reoperation, revision, and PJI risk, while increasing CCI and ASA score increased ER visit risk, and increasing CCI increased dislocation risk. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches. As outpatient THA grows, surgeon compensation should be reevaluated given the heightened administrative burden.

articles.title: Bilateral Sinonasal Glomangiopericytoma Originating From the Posterior Nasal Septum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal glomangiopericytoma (GPC) is a rare perivascular tumor of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, accounting for <0.5% of sinonasal tumors. It typically presents with nonspecific symptoms such as nasal obstruction and epistaxis, and definitive diagnosis relies on histopathologic and immunohistochemical assessment.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old medically free male presented with a 7-month history of progressive left-predominant nasal obstruction, intermittent epistaxis, blood-stained purulent nasal discharge, and hyposmia. Endoscopic examination revealed a friable vascular mass arising bilaterally from the olfactory groove/posterior septal region. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral enhancing soft-tissue lesions centered along the posterior nasal septum, without skull base erosion, orbital involvement, or intracranial extension. Office-based biopsy confirmed sinonasal GPC.
MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOME: The patient underwent complete endoscopic tumor excision under general anesthesia with functional endoscopic sinus surgery, coblation-assisted resection of the septal attachment, bilateral middle turbinate resection, and superior septectomy. Frozen section confirmed GPC. The postoperative course was uneventful, with complete symptom resolution and no endoscopic evidence of residual or recurrent disease at 9-month follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights an uncommon bilateral presentation of sinonasal GPC arising from the posterior nasal septum. Complete endoscopic excision with careful identification of the tumor attachment can provide excellent clinical outcomes, although long-term endoscopic surveillance remains essential due to the risk of delayed recurrence.

articles.title: Beyond the Operating Room: Trends and Safety in Nonoperating Room and Office-Based Anesthesia.
Osteoporosis Treatment in Lumbar Fusion: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Perioperative pharmacologic bone-health optimization is increasingly recommended before lumbar fusion, but the supporting evidence may not apply to short-segment degenerative fusion. This scoping review mapped how well treatment recommendations are supported in that population.
RECENT FINDINGS: Of 1,842 records screened, 145 underwent full-text review and 54 met inclusion criteria. Most high-level evidence pooled degenerative disease with adult spinal deformity and osteoporotic vertebral fracture without construct-specific analysis. In short-segment degenerative fusion, small teriparatide studies reported lower screw loosening and higher or earlier union, whereas a 1,040-patient registry found no reduction in operative nonunion with preoperative bisphosphonates. High-quality short-segment data for romosozumab and abaloparatide were absent, and timing and duration were inconsistent. Recommendations are supported by biologic rationale but limited by population mismatch. Teriparatide has the strongest degenerative-specific signal; evidence for bisphosphonates and newer agents is insufficient. Future trials should isolate 1- to 2-level degenerative fusion and prioritize cage subsidence, screw loosening, fusion, and reoperation.

articles.title: Surgical management of spontaneous tendon rupture in rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spontaneous, non-traumatic rupture of the extensor or flexor tendons of the hand and wrist is an uncommon disabling complication of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Management is mainly surgical, and decisions must account for perioperative disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) and biologic therapy. The evidence remains fragmented, with no existing systematic synthesis specific to RA. This review aims to estimate re-rupture, functional recovery and complication rates after surgery and to examine prognostic factors and perioperative antirheumatic management in relation to these outcomes.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature Ultimate will be searched from inception, without language restrictions, supplemented by trial registries and backward and forward citation searching. Case series, cohort, case-control and randomised studies reporting surgical management of RA-related spontaneous hand or wrist tendon rupture will be included; single-patient case reports will be summarised narratively only. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool for comparative studies, the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for case series and the Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomised trials. Single-arm proportions will be pooled using a random-effects generalised linear mixed model, and comparative outcomes will be expressed as ORs or mean differences with 95% CIs, prioritising adjusted estimates. Pooling will follow prespecified clinical comparability criteria. Certainty of evidence will be rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval is not required, as this review involves only previously published data. Findings will be disseminated through publication in an open-access peer-reviewed journal, presentation at hand surgery and rheumatology meetings and a plain-language summary shared with RA patient organisations.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261477222.

articles.title: Audit of ASA status reporting in emergency laparotomy studies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to evaluate the compliance with reporting of American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status of patients in studies investigating postoperative mortality after emergency laparotomy.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. All studies investigating postoperative mortality as the primary outcome in patients undergoing non-trauma emergency laparotomy were included and analysed. Compliance with ASA status reporting was assessed and the potential predictors of poor compliance were evaluated using a multivariable binary logistic regression model.
RESULTS: In total, 81 studies were included. Compliance with ASA status reporting was 77.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 67.5-86.2). Multivariable binary logistic regression showed that compliance with ASA status reporting was not affected by year of publication (coefficient: -0.0199, p = 0.767), sample size of the study (coefficient: 0.0001, p = 0.995), the impact factor of the journal in which the study is published (coefficient: 0.1389, p = 0.334), the level of evidence provided by the study (coefficient: 0.3405, p = 0.594) or the risk of mortality reported by the study (coefficient: -1.6150, p = 0.656). There was no difference in the reported risk of postoperative mortality between studies that reported ASA status (13.1%, 95% CI 12.0-14.2%) and those that did not (13.1%, 95% CI 11.9-14.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: Reporting of the ASA status of patients in studies investigating postoperative mortality after emergency laparotomy is suboptimal. Authors, reviewers and editors should proactively ensure compliance with ASA status reporting in this setting.

articles.title: After-hours hip fracture surgery-influence on reoperation risk, mortality, and surgical complications: a cohort study of 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Previous studies have shown that timing of hip fracture surgery is important for outcomes. We aimed to determine whether hip fracture surgeries performed after regular working hours were associated with increased 1-year reoperation risk, 30-day mortality, or intraoperative complications.
METHODS: Data from 98,607 patients ≥ 65 years with hip fracture reported to the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Absolute risk estimates were calculated with Kaplan-Meier, and Cox regression models were used to estimate hazard rate rations (HRRs) for 1-year reoperation risk and 30-day mortality for surgeries performed in the evening (16:00-22:00) and nighttime (22:00-08:00) compared with daytime surgery (08:00-16:00). Analyses were adjusted for age groups, sex, the American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) physical status class, cognitive impairment, type of fracture, type of surgery, waiting time to surgery, and duration of surgery. Surgeons self-reported intraoperative complications to the registry.
RESULTS: 46,655 patients (47%) underwent daytime surgery, 40,916 (42%) evening surgery, and 11,036 (11%) nighttime surgery. The mean age was 83 years, 69% were females. Patients operated on during nighttime had overall shorter waiting time to surgery than the other groups. 1-year reoperation risk was 4.9% (n = 2,290) for daytime surgery, 5.2% (n = 2,151) for evening, and 6.0% (n = 673) for nighttime, with no statistically significant differences between the groups. Nighttime surgery was associated with a slightly lower 30-day mortality (7.8%, n = 870) compared with daytime surgery (9.6%, n = 4,494), HRR 0.91 (95% confidence interval 0.84-0.98). No statistically significant differences in intraoperative complications were observed across the 3 surgical time periods: daytime (2.9%), evening (2.9%), and nighttime (2.9%).
CONCLUSION: Evening and nighttime hip fracture surgery were not associated with increased risk for 1-year reoperation, 30-day mortality, or intraoperative complications compared with daytime surgery.

articles.title: Evolving Management of Hip Fracture Patients on Anticoagulant and Antiplatelet Medications: A 22-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate temporal trends in anticoagulant (AC) and antiplatelet (AP) use among patients undergoing operative treatment of hip fractures and to assess the association of antithrombotic regimen with time to surgery and postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Single North American Level I trauma center.
PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients aged 55 years or older who underwent operative treatment for a hip fracture (AO/OTA types 31-A, 31-B, and 31-C) between 2000 and 2022 while receiving anticoagulant and/or antiplatelet therapy at admission were included.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Temporal trends in antithrombotic prescribing, time to surgery, perioperative transfusion, readmission, 90-day medical and surgical postoperative complications, and 90-day mortality were assessed. The odds of warfarin versus direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) prescription were compared across study years, and time to surgery from admission and each outcome were compared across study years and across antithrombotic regimens (warfarin, DOAC, DOAC or warfarin plus antiplatelet, and antiplatelet alone).
RESULTS: 476 patients were included (mean age 81.2 years [range, 60-103]; 288 [60.4%] female). Anticoagulant therapy was used by 155 (32.7%) and antiplatelet therapy by 385 (80.7%); 64 (13.4%) received both. The odds of warfarin prescription relative to a DOAC decreased by an estimated 37% per year (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% CI 0.53-0.74; P<0.001). Time to surgery did not change significantly over the study period (-0.01 hours/year, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.02; P=0.4) and was not associated with antithrombotic regimen (-0.01, 95% CI: -0.04-0.01; P=0.3). Perioperative transfusion odds decreased 12% per year (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.93; P<0.001) and 1-year readmission odds decreased 46% per year (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.48-0.60; P<0.001), independent of medication class. Ninety-day (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.04; P=0.8) and 90-day mortality (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.54-1.14; P=0.2) did not change over time.
CONCLUSIONS: In this 22-year single-center cohort of hip-fracture patients receiving anticoagulant (AC) or antiplatelet (AP) therapy, antithrombotic regimen was not associated with time to surgery, 90-day complications, or mortality. Perioperative transfusion and 1-year readmission rates declined over the study period independent of medication class. These findings supported expedited operative management of hip fractures in patients receiving AC or AP therapy.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Perioperative medication optimisation: what to continue, what to stop and what to deprescribe.
articles.abstract: Polypharmacy is common in patients undergoing surgery. This reflects an increasingly older, frail surgical population prescribed medications for multiple long term conditions. Inappropriate management of pre-admission medications has patient safety implications; inappropriate continuation risks cancellations, whereas inappropriate cessation risks postoperative complications or withdrawal. Medications should be continued preoperatively unless the risk of bleeding, thrombosis, infection, anaesthetic interactions or impact of fasting outweighs the benefits of continuation. The evidence base underpinning this is continually evolving, with recent publications suggesting continuation of medications that would historically have been stopped. Perioperative medication optimisation, however, should go beyond simple continuation or cessation of medications. Polypharmacy is independently associated with postoperative complications, longer length of hospital stay and increased readmission. The preoperative period represents an opportunity to reduce these risks by utilising comprehensive geriatric assessment to holistically review patients, optimise long term conditions and deprescribe medications associated with an increased risk of postoperative harm.

articles.title: Perioperative Peripheral-Central Lipidomic Integration for Risk Stratification of Delayed Neurocognitive Recovery.
articles.abstract: Delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR) affects up to 54% of elderly surgical patients and accelerates dementia progression, yet its perioperative lipidomic profile remains poorly understood. We conducted a multicenter prospective observational cohort study at two tertiary academic medical centers in Shanghai, China (2021-2022) to characterize the perioperative serum lipidome, identify dNCR-associated lipid candidates, build a preoperative predictive model, and elucidate peripheral-central lipid dysregulation. Targeted lipidomics was performed preoperatively and on postoperative day 1 in patients aged ≥60 years (ASA I-III) undergoing elective general anesthesia, with cortical lipidomic validation in aged C57BL/6J mice. Among 141 screened patients, 110 were included; 42 (38.2%) developed dNCR within 30 days, defined by a ≥1-SD decline on standardized neuropsychological testing. We identified 38 preoperative and 58 perioperative dynamic lipid candidates. Ontology enrichment revealed C20:3 enrichment preoperatively and phospholipid-related terms, including negatively charged headgroups, perioperatively (both FDR <0.05). An integrated Lipid Score combined with total protein and blood glucose achieved an AUC of 0.817, outperforming clinical-only (0.734) and lipidomic-only (0.770) models. Perioperative changes in putatively annotated fatty-acid-associated signals correlated with cognitive changes. Several candidate lipids showed directionally concordant serum and cortical differences, notably elevated cortical TG 52:3 (14:0), which correlated with maze latency (P=0.033), while cortical putative FA 24:1 tended to decrease after surgery. These findings identify perioperative lipid alterations associated with dNCR and provide exploratory evidence of concordant peripheral and cortical lipid responses, highlighting lipid alterations potentially related to mitochondrial phospholipid homeostasis, sphingomyelin-ceramide balance, and free-fatty-acid availability.

articles.title: Neurological recovery and perioperative outcomes after surgery for degenerative cervical myelopathy in older versus younger patients: a propensity score-matched analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Older patients can benefit from surgery for degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), but age-related differences in neurological recovery, patient-reported function, and perioperative outcomes remain uncertain. We compared these outcomes between older (≥ 75 years) and younger patients.
METHODS: We analyzed a single-center registry of 1,016 patients who underwent surgery for DCM in 2009-2023 (85 older and 931 younger). Older patients were matched one-to-one to younger patients by exact matching on surgical approach and propensity-score matching on the preoperative Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) score, sex, comorbidity, and physical status (78 pairs). The primary outcome was achievement of the severity-specific JOA minimal clinically important difference (MCID) at 12 months. Longer-term recovery to 5 years was exploratory.
RESULTS: At 12 months, MCID achievement did not differ significantly between the matched groups (42.3% versus 46.2%; risk difference - 3.8% points, 95% CI - 19.1 to + 11.4; p = 0.74), nor did the recovery rate (p = 0.14). Matched patient-reported changes were nonsignificant, whereas exploratory adjusted full-cohort analyses showed smaller improvements in the Neck Disability Index (p = 0.004) and Short Form-12 physical component summary (p = 0.001) in older patients. Improvement persisted among assessed older patients, but longer-term comparisons were inconclusive owing to incomplete follow-up. Recorded perioperative complications affected 7.1% of older and 11.0% of younger patients. Inter-department transfer, nearly always for rehabilitation, was more frequent in older patients (15.2% versus 5.8%; p = 0.009), but not among matched patients with a recorded discharge disposition (12.7% versus 17.5%).
CONCLUSION: Approximately two in five matched older patients reached the adapted severity-specific MCID threshold, with no significant difference from younger patients, although equivalence was not established. Our findings suggest that advanced age alone should not preclude surgery for DCM, but comorbidity and perioperative medical and rehabilitation needs should guide selection and counseling.

articles.title: Laser interstitial thermal therapy in older patients with drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) is a minimally invasive treatment for focal drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). This study sought to examine the efficacy of LITT for a cohort of older adults with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE) and evaluate predictors of safety.
METHODS: We examined 24 patients aged ≥50 years, with 10/24 (42%) ≥60 years. Primary outcomes were Engel classification and reduction from baseline seizure frequency. We additionally reviewed post-ablation complications, hospital length of stay (LOS), neurocognitive and psychiatric worsening, and anti-seizure medication (ASM) reduction. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was calculated to assess its utility in prediction of postoperative complications.
RESULTS: 22/24 (92%) had ≥50% reduction in seizure frequency, and 17/24 (71%) had ≥90% reduction at last follow-up, with median follow-up of 5.2 years (range, 1.5-10.4 years). Engel Class I outcome was achieved in 19/24 (79%) of patients by 6 months post-ablation and maintained in 12/24 (50%) of patients by last follow-up. Immediate postoperative complications were mostly transient, though worse cognitive symptoms were reported in 5/24 (21%), and worse mood was reported in 3/24 (13%) at 6 months post-ablation. Higher CCI did not correlate with complications but was associated with prolonged LOS. ASM reduction occurred in half of patients.
SIGNIFICANCE: In our cohort, LITT offered favorable seizure and safety outcomes in an older population with focal DRE. Perioperative risk assessments such as the CCI may be useful in older patient selection for LITT.

articles.title: Postoperative Delirium After Pheochromocytoma Resection: An Exploratory Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative management of pheochromocytoma has traditionally focused on cardiovascular stability, while acute postoperative neurocognitive outcomes remain insufficiently documented. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence, associated clinical factors, and postoperative outcomes of probable postoperative delirium (POD) following pheochromocytoma resection in an exploratory single-center cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational cohort study of 30 consecutive adult patients who underwent adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma between January 2022 and May 2026, diagnosed preoperatively on clinical, biochemical, and radiological grounds and confirmed by postoperative histopathological examination. Probable POD was identified through retrospective medical record auditing combined with documented Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) evaluations performed throughout the ICU/PACU stay. We compared continuous variables using Student's t-test (with Welch's correction when appropriate) or Mann-Whitney U test and categorical data using Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of retrospectively identified probable POD was 33.3% (n = 10). Clinical phenotypes included psychomotor agitation (n = 6), hallucinations/confusion (n = 3), and hypoactive somnolence (n = 1). In unadjusted exploratory analyses, POD was significantly associated with older age (56.0 ± 9.3 vs. 47.4 ± 10.3 years, p = 0.034), open laparotomy (90.0% vs. 25.0%, p = 0.001), higher baseline ASA score (ASA III: 60.0% vs. 10.0%, p = 0.010), larger tumor size (44.9 ± 6.0 vs. 39.3 ± 7.5 mm, p = 0.048), and deeper postresection diastolic hypotension (nadir DBP: 55.7 ± 5.4 vs. 60.4 ± 3.7 mmHg, p = 0.027). Patients experiencing POD had a longer median ICU stay (2.5 vs. 1.0 days, p = 0.011). Total in-hospital mortality was 6.7% (n = 2), occurring exclusively in nondelirious patients experiencing refractory vasoplegic shock.
CONCLUSION: Probable POD occurred in one-third of patients following pheochromocytoma resection and was associated with open surgery, older age, tumor size, and postresection diastolic hypotension in exploratory unadjusted comparisons. Standardized prospective screening and targeted hemodynamic management warrant further investigation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: The Effect of Telemedicine-Based APAP Management on 24-Hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Telemedicine improves access to obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) care, but whether telemedicine-based auto-adjusting positive airway pressure (APAP) management is noninferior to in-person care for the 3-month change in 24-hour mean blood pressure (BP) remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether comprehensive telemedicine-based APAP management is noninferior to standard in-person care in reducing 24-hour mean BP in patients with OSA.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized non-inferiority trial, 344 participants with suspected OSA were randomized 1:1 to telemedicine-based (TM) or in-person (IP) management for 3 months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in 24-hour mean BP. The prespecified non-inferiority margin was 1.5 mmHg. Secondary outcomes included APAP adherence, patient-centered outcomes and metabolic parameters.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 344 randomized participants, 256 completed the 3-month follow-up (127 IP and 129 TM). The between-group difference (TM - IP) in the change in 24-hour mean BP was -0.59 mmHg (95% CI, -2.42 to 1.25) in the intention-to-treat analysis and -1.21 mmHg (95% CI, -3.24 to 0.81) in the completer analysis. Both upper confidence limits were below the prespecified 1.5-mmHg non-inferiority margin. No clear evidence of between-group differences was observed in APAP adherence, patient-reported outcomes, or metabolic measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Telemedicine-based APAP management was noninferior to in-person management for the 3-month change in 24-hour mean BP, using a prespecified margin of 1.5 mmHg. These findings support telemedicine as a potential alternative delivery model for blood pressure management in patients with OSA.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: On the Cover.
Learning curve analysis of artificial intelligence-assisted ultrasound for teaching popliteal fossa sciatic nerve block to novice anesthesiologists: a pilot randomized educational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted ultrasound may improve ultrasound-guided regional nerve blocks, but its effect on novice learning curves is unclear.
METHODS: In this pilot randomized educational study (June-August 2025), inexperienced anesthesiology residents from Shanghai General Hospital were assigned to AI-assisted or conventional training groups. The AI group used an ultrasound system with an AI module and received additional ethics and principles training, while the conventional group received standard training. Image acquisition and interpretation, debriefing time, trainee speaking time, and feedback were evaluated.
RESULTS: Twenty-one trainee anesthesiologists were recruited (AI, n = 10; conventional, n = 11). The group-level cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis identified an estimated turning point (TP) at approximately 12 attempts in the AI group. No comparable TP was identified within the 15-attempt training period in the conventional group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in participant-level phase-specific success rates (all P > 0.05). Compared with the conventional group, the AI group reported higher post-training feedback scores for training content (4.7 ± 0.5 vs. 3.6 ± 1.0, P = 0.0076), satisfaction (4.9 ± 0.3 vs. 3.5 ± 0.8, P < 0.0001), and confidence (5.0 ± 0.0 vs. 4.5 ± 0.7, P = 0.0216). Compared with the conventional group, the AI group also had a shorter participant-level mean debriefing time (7.33 ± 0.34 vs. 10.65 ± 0.61 min, P < 0.0001) and a greater proportion of trainee speaking time during debriefing (69.5% (65.70, 70.55) vs. 49.0% (46.70, 49.70), P < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted ultrasound training might enhance post-training feedback, increase satisfaction and confidence, and reduce debriefing time among inexperienced anesthesiology residents, suggesting its potential utility in the medical education of ultrasound.

articles.title: Treatment Selection for Frail Older Adults with Chronic Subdural Hematoma in the Era of Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization: A Clinical Review.
articles.abstract: Chronic subdural hematoma increasingly affects older patients who are frail, multimorbid, and dependent on long-term antithrombotic therapy. In this population, treatment selection is rarely a binary choice between observation and burr-hole drainage. Although burr-hole drainage remains essential for rapid decompression, recurrence, reoperation, perioperative bleeding, and the timing of antithrombotic resumption often determine the overall clinical outcome. Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) targets inflammation, angiogenesis, and blood supply to the outer membrane. It may help reduce recurrence, support treatment in surgically high-risk patients, and facilitate individualized antithrombotic management. This review synthesizes the contemporary pathophysiological understanding of chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), the evidence base for available treatment modalities, and peri-procedural antithrombotic strategies. This narrative review proposes a clinically oriented framework that prioritizes the need for rapid decompression, physiological reserve, recurrence risk, and antithrombotic requirements. These factors guide selection among conservative management, burr-hole drainage, standalone MMAE, and combined therapy. At present, MMAE is best viewed as a selective adjunctive or alternative strategy rather than a universal replacement for conventional treatment.

articles.title: Feasibility of a Multicomponent Protocol to Promote Dreaming during Surgical Anesthesia: Erratum.
Intraoperative direct oral anticoagulant removal during urgent CABG: A feasibility and hypothesis-generating interim report from the STAR registry.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Intraoperative direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) removal by a hemoadsorption device in patients undergoing urgent cardiac surgery may reduce perioperative bleeding complications. The international STAR Registry evaluates outcomes of antithrombotic removal (ATR) during urgent cardiac surgery (NCT05077124).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The STAR Registry is collecting data at 28 European centers where device use for ATR is standard of care in patients undergoing urgent cardiac surgery before completing guideline recommended drug washout. The current analysis includes 42 DOAC patients (mean age 71.5 ± 8.3 years; 88.1% male) who required urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG; EuroSCORE-II 7.4 ± 11.1%). Patients were on apixaban (52.4%), rivaroxaban (26.2%), edoxaban (14.3%), and dabigatran (7.1%); 50% were also on aspirin. CABG was performed at a median 25.5 h (IQR: 23.3-48.6) after last DOAC dose. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were 109.5 ± 38.8 and 67.6 ± 28.3 min. Primary endpoint was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) grade 4 bleeding which occurred in 2 patients (4.8%), both due to transfusion of ≥5 units of packed red blood cells. Mean 24-h chest tube drainage was 762 ± 296 ml, while no patient required reoperation for bleeding. No device-related adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: The present interim analysis of the STAR Registry provides hypothesis-generating observational data suggesting that intraoperative DOAC removal during urgent CABG before completion of drug washout may be associated with a reduced risk of severe bleeding. These findings require confirmation in adequately powered prospective randomized studies before definitive conclusions regarding efficacy and safety can be drawn.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Postoperative High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T Elevation After Thoracic Surgery: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine perioperative factors associated with postoperative high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) elevation after thoracic surgery.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study screened 588 consecutive records of patients who underwent thoracic surgery between June 2020 and June 2023, counting only the first eligible operation for each patient. After the exclusion of 128 records, all 460 eligible patients were included in the analysis. The outcome was defined as any hs-cTnT value ≥0.014 µg/L (14 ng/L) on postoperative day 1, 3, or 5.
