Eleven variables were entered simultaneously into a binary logistic regression model, with surgical method represented by indicator variables. Age was entered in years, and its odds ratio (OR) was expressed per 10-year increase; other continuous variables were analysed in their original units.
RESULTS: Postoperative hs-cTnT elevation occurred in 155 of 460 patients (33.7%). In the multivariable model, age (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.23-2.63), procedure type (wedge resection: OR 4.47, 95% CI 1.57-12.71; segmentectomy/lobectomy: OR 5.52, 95% CI 2.04-14.96; oesophageal surgery: OR 27.96, 95% CI 5.50-142.27; each compared with other thoracic procedures), operation duration (OR 1.53 per hour, 95% CI 1.21-1.93), preoperative creatinine (OR 1.021 per µmol/L, 95% CI 1.007-1.035), preoperative potassium (OR 3.59 per mmol/L, 95% CI 1.84-7.02), and pre-existing atrial fibrillation (OR 5.56, 95% CI 1.84-16.83) were associated with the outcome. Postoperative day-1 haemoglobin showed an inverse association that did not reach statistical significance (OR 0.972 per g/L, 95% CI 0.942-1.002; p = 0.069), and the inverse association with ejection fraction was also not significant (OR 0.905 per %, 95% CI 0.772-1.060; p = 0.216).
CONCLUSIONS: Older age, procedure type, longer operation duration, higher preoperative creatinine, higher preoperative potassium, and pre-existing atrial fibrillation were associated with postoperative hs-cTnT elevation after multivariable adjustment. These associations do not establish causality or constitute a validated prediction model; rather, they generate hypotheses for the prospective evaluation of postoperative monitoring strategies.

articles.title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition.
RESULTS: Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p < 0.001), as were length of stay (8 vs 5 days; p < 0.001), thromboembolic events (6.5% vs 1.8%; p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.

articles.title: Efficacy and Prognostic Analysis of Neuro-Navigation Robot-Assisted Puncture Drainage for Thalamic Hemorrhage: A Comparison With Neuro-Endoscopy and External Ventricular Drainage.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aims to compare the clinical efficacy of three surgical techniques-robot-assisted neuro-navigation, external ventricular drainage (EVD), and neuro-endoscopy-in evacuating intracranial hematomas in patients with thalamic hemorrhage.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 110 patients, divided into three groups based on the surgical method: robot group (n = 30), EVD group (n = 37), and neuro-endoscopy group (n = 43). Baseline characteristics, perioperative parameters, neurological function, inflammatory response, complications, and functional outcomes were compared and analyzed among the three patient groups.
RESULTS: Compared with the EVD and neuro-endoscopy groups, the robot group had shorter operative times (p < 0.001), higher hematoma clearance rates (p < 0.001), better postoperative neurological function (p < 0.05), a lower inflammatory response (p < 0.05), fewer complications (p < 0.05), and better functional outcomes (p < 0.05). Robot-assisted neuro-navigation-guided puncture drainage was associated with better clinical outcomes than EVD and neuro-endoscopy in this retrospective study.
CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted neuro-navigation-guided puncture drainage was associated with improved neurological recovery and short-term outcomes in patients with thalamic hemorrhage.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a LASSO-Based Prediction Model for Postoperative Bleeding Following Pediatric Tonsillectomy and Adenoidectomy.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Despite technological advancements, children undergoing adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation remain at risk for postoperative bleeding. This study aimed to construct a precise machine learning-based model to predict the risk of postoperative bleeding in this population.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study involving 306 pediatric patients who underwent the procedure between January 2023 and January 2025 was conducted. Clinical data, including demographic characteristics, preoperative laboratory findings, and surgical details, were collected and cleaned. The dataset was randomly divided into a training set (n = 244) and a validation set (n = 62) at an 8:2 ratio. A predictive model was developed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) cross-validation algorithm, and its performance was assessed in the validation cohort.
RESULTS: Among 306 children, 24 (7.8%) experienced postoperative bleeding. Univariate comparisons identified significant differences in 11 variables: age, height, weight, body mass index (BMI), disease duration, postoperative infection, dietary compliance, postoperative pain, lymphocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR) (all p < 0.05). At lambda.1se = 0.022, LASSO logistic regression retained four predictors: postoperative infection, dietary compliance, age, and postoperative pain. After 1000 bootstrap resamples, the out-of-bag area under the curve (AUC) was 0.935 (95% CI: 0.875-0.995), with a Brier score of 0.035, calibration intercept of 0.045, and calibration slope of 1.418. At the optimal probability cutoff of 0.114, sensitivity was 0.875, specificity was 0.936, and the Youden index was 0.811.
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative infection, dietary adherence, postoperative pain, and age are significant predictors of bleeding following pediatric adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation. The LASSO-based model provides a reliable tool for identifying high-risk patients and optimizing perioperative management.

articles.title: Ventilator-circuit configurations for noninvasive ventilation in infants with acute respiratory failure: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract: Patient-ventilator synchrony may differ across ventilator and circuit configurations during noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in infants. We compared an intentional-leak single-limb turbine configuration (SLC-turbine), a dual-limb turbine configuration with an active expiratory valve (DLC-turbine), and a dual-limb compressed-gas pediatric ICU configuration (DLC-PICU) in infants receiving NIV for acute respiratory failure METHODS: In this single-center randomized crossover physiological study, infants underwent three 30-minute NIV phases in randomized order with unchanged pressure support, PEEP, and FiO₂. Esophageal pressure was used to assess the asynchrony index (AI), individual asynchronies, and inspiratory effort. Primary and secondary endpoints were AI differences between DLC-PICU and SLC-turbine and between DLC-PICU and DLC-turbine, respectively RESULTS: Twenty infants entered stabilization, 13 were randomized, and 12 completed the protocol (age 10 [7-21] months; SpO₂/FiO₂ 185 [160-220]). AI differed across configurations: 8.6% [6.7-16.5] with SLC-turbine, 25.4% [16.3-35.0] with DLC-turbine, and 45.7% [30.5-63.8] with DLC-PICU (p=0.0023). AI was higher with DLC-PICU than with SLC-turbine (Hodges-Lehmann difference +32.0%, 95% CI +13.9 to +50.1; p=0.0015) and DLC-turbine (+18.4%, 95% CI +5.9 to +36.3; p=0.021). Auto-triggering showed the clearest configuration-dependent difference and was more frequent with DLC-PICU than with SLC-turbine (7.5 [0.6-11.4] vs 0 [0-2.5] events/min; difference +5.30 events/min; p=0.0039), without a significant difference between DLC-PICU and DLC-turbine. Ineffective efforts, double triggering, and premature cycling did not differ across configurations. All NIV configurations reduced inspiratory effort versus unassisted spontaneous breathing, with no significant differences among NIV configurations CONCLUSIONS: AI was lower with SLC-turbine and DLC-turbine than with DLC-PICU and lowest with SLC-turbine. Auto-triggering showed the clearest configuration-dependent difference. All configurations reduced inspiratory effort versus unassisted spontaneous breathing, without significant between-configuration differences. Because ventilator platform, circuit and expiratory architecture, and device-specific control functions differed, effects of individual components cannot be determined. These findings are specific to the ventilators and configurations evaluated. Further studies should determine whether these physiological differences translate into improved NIV tolerance or short- and long-term clinical outcomes TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04017780. Registered on 12 July 2019.

articles.title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated.
RESULTS: No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001); RM-ANOVA showed significant group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects for both AOFAS and VAS scores. DVT occurred in 3/41 (7.3%) patients in the intensive-pathway group and 8/43 (18.6%) in the routine-management group, and the difference was not statistically significant (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.08-1.41). These findings represent associations with the integrated bundle and cannot be attributed independently to preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, analgesia, mobilization, or follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

articles.title: Intraoperative active warming with or without active prewarming on maternal hypothermia in patients undergoing elective cesarean delivery with spinal anesthesia: A randomized controlled study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal hypothermia affects up to 60% of patients undergoing scheduled cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia and is associated with maternal and neonatal morbidity. Although intraoperative active warming is standard, the effect of preoperative warming to improve zero-flux core temperature remains unclear.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 78 women scheduled for cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia received intraoperative forced-air warming and warmed crystalloids. The active group received 20 min of preoperative forced-air warming. The primary outcome was zero-flux core maternal temperature on arrival to post-anesthesia care unit. Secondary maternal outcomes included intraoperative shivering and in post-anesthesia care unit, maternal hypothermia (core temperature < 36 °C), thermal comfort scores in post-anesthesia care unit, and neonatal temperature. The Mann-Whitney U test and the Chi-Square test were used for analysis.
RESULTS: Median with interquartile range [IQR] core temperature on arrival to post-anesthesia care unit did not differ between the active and control groups (36.6 °C [36.45-36.85] vs. 36.6 °C [36-36.75]; P = 0.99). Hypothermia incidence was 5.1% in the active group vs. 15.4% in the control group (P = 0.161). Shivering incidence was 10.3% in the active group vs. 28.2% in the control group (P = 0.06). Thermal comfort scores were significantly higher in the active warming group (52.05 ± 6.56 vs. 43.84 ± 10.91; P = 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: Adding 20 min of preoperative forced-air warming to active intraoperative warming did not significantly increase core temperature or reduce hypothermia upon arrival to post-anesthesia care unit. However, active pre-warming significantly improved maternal thermal comfort.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of robotic versus open catheterizable channels in a pediatric population - A 10 year retrospective review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recent literature has demonstrated the feasibility of robotic continent catheterizable channel creation as it offers reduced morbidity with equivalent clinical outcomes and complication rates compared to traditional open techniques. Our aim was to compare the peri-operative and post-operative outcomes of patients undergoing robotic versus open CCC creation at a single institution.
METHODS: A retrospective review was performed of patients with neurogenic bladders undergoing robotic or open catheterizable channel creation at a single institution between 2015 and 2024. Patient demographics were collected and intra-operative and post-operative outcomes were compared using Fischer's exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests where appropriate. Time to surgical revision as assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Univariable and multivariable analysis were performed to compare clinical outcomes between the robotic and open groups while controlling for potential confounding factors. A p-value of ≤0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 189 patients were identified, with a median follow up time of 4.0 years (IQR 1.8-6.8 years). The robotic group had a significantly higher 5-year surgical revision rate than the open group (61.7% [95%CI, 44.4%73.6%] vs 30.8% [95%CI, 20.6%-39.6%]; log rank test:χ2(1) = 23.63, p < 00.001). The robotic group had a threefold higher risk of surgical revision (adjusted HR 3.01, 95% CI 1.95-4.64; p < 0.001) on multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis. There was no significant difference in 30-day complication rates (32.8% vs 39.5%, p = 0.37) for robotic versus open channel creation. Patients who underwent a robotic channel creation had a significantly longer median operative time (340.0 vs 214.5 min, p = 0.007). The robotic cohort had significantly lower post-operative narcotic usage (0.4 vs 0.7 mg/kg morphine equivalents, p = 0.049), and shorter hospital stays even when excluding patients who underwent a concurrent augment or Monti creation (5.0 vs 7.0 days, p = 0.015). On multivariable linear regression analysis, robotic approach was associated with shorter hospital stay by 2.31 days (B = -2.31 [95%CI:-3.67 to -0.94], p = 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Robotic catheterizable channel creation in a pediatric population has similar short term complication rates but higher long term surgical revision rates compared to an open approach while offering the benefit of shorter hospital stays and reduced narcotic rates.

articles.title: Predicting Postoperative Pulmonary Complications After High-Altitude One-Lung Ventilation Surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to develop and validate a novel nomogram for predicting postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) in patients undergoing one-lung ventilation (OLV) thoracic surgery at high altitude.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Tibet Autonomous Region People's Hospital (Lhasa, China; altitude 3650 m). We enrolled 570 adult OLV cases under general anesthesia from January 2020 to July 2024; after excluding incomplete records, 492 patients were analyzed and split chronologically into a development set (n = 369) and a test set (n = 123). PPCs were defined as pneumonia, atelectasis, ARDS, respiratory failure, reintubation, or ventilator support for > 48 h within the first postoperative week. Predictors were selected via LASSO regression and entered into multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: PPCs occurred in 42.9% (211/492) of patients; this relatively high incidence likely reflects both the physiological challenges of the high-altitude setting and our modified inclusion of all radiographic atelectasis. PPCs were associated with longer hospital stays (median 16 vs. 11 days, p < 0.001). Among the 43 raw features, the following eight were finally incorporated into the logistic regression model: age, Tibetan ethnicity, body mass index, preoperative heart rate, comorbid pneumonia, ASA physical status, bronchial blocker use, and surgical duration. The nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.808 (95% CI: 0.764-0.853) and 0.732 (95% CI: 0.642-0.823) in development and test cohorts, respectively, outperforming the ARISCAT score (AUCs: 0.708 and 0.555; p < 0.01). The nomogram showed good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p > 0.05) and provided net benefit across risk thresholds of 12%-92% in the development set and 18%-74% in the test set.
CONCLUSIONS: This PPCs prediction tool for high-altitude OLV patients incorporates easily obtainable clinical variables and demonstrates strong discrimination and calibration. Further prospective external validation in independent populations is required before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Prognostic Role of Circulating Dipeptidyl Peptidase 3 in Critical Care and Perioperative Settings:A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Circulating dipeptidyl peptidase 3 (cDPP3) is an angiotensin II-degrading enzyme associated with increased mortality and hemodynamic deterioration in cardiogenic shock (CS). This scoping review aimed to systematically map the available evidence on cDPP3 as a prognostic biomarker in critical care and perioperative settings, including after cardiac surgery. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL from database inception through July 2026. Nineteen publications were selected for analysis, including 12 prospective observational studies, 5 ancillary analyses of prospective observational cohorts or randomized controlled trials, and 2 post hoc analyses. Fourteen studies evaluated nonsurgical conditions (worsening heart failure, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), CS, septic shock, cardiac arrest); 4 studies, enrolling 464 patients in total, evaluated perioperative populations; and 1 study included a mixed cohort of surgical and nonsurgical patients. Elevated cDPP3 levels were associated with short-term outcomes including prolonged vasopressor requirements, multiorgan dysfunction, prolonged intensive care unit stay, and mortality in patients with CS, septic shock, and post-cardiac surgery. Serial measurements showed that persistent cDPP3 elevation was generally associated with worse outcomes, while decreasing levels were associated with clinical improvement. Further research is needed to better understand the source and clearance of cDPP3, its prognostic role in different cardiovascular conditions, and its potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Postoperative Complications: Prevention and Management.
articles.abstract: Postoperative complications following pituitary neuroendocrine tumor surgery remain an important source of morbidity despite advances in surgical techniques and perioperative care. Endocrine and fluid-electrolyte disturbances, particularly arginine vasopressin deficiency and delayed hyponatremia, are the most common complications and major drivers of readmission. Structural complications such as hematoma, cerebrospinal fluid leak, and vascular injury are less frequent but carry a higher risk of morbidity. Risk factors include modifiable and nonmodifiable traits such as patient characteristics, tumor size and invasiveness, prior treatment, and intraoperative events. Early recognition through standardized monitoring of sodium balance, urine output, and cortisol levels enables perioperative care.

articles.title: PAIN moves to online-only publication: the end of our print era.
Subclavian Vein-to-Artery Distance in Supraclavicular Versus Infraclavicular Approaches: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the subclavian vein (SCV)-subclavian artery (SCA) distance between supraclavicular and infraclavicular views.
DESIGN: Prospective observational study.
SETTING: University tertiary hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Fifty-five adult patients undergoing general anesthesia.
INTERVENTIONS: None (SCV sonographic measurements were obtained under 4 conditions: neutral and arm-abducted positions, each in supraclavicular and infraclavicular views).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was the difference in SCV-SCA distance between supraclavicular and infraclavicular views under neutral positioning. Secondary outcomes were the SCV-SCA overlap index, clavicle shadowing index, and relative SCA position. In the neutral position, the SCV-SCA distance was significantly greater in the supraclavicular view than in the infraclavicular view (1.19 ± 0.75 cm v 0.16 ± 0.75 cm, p < 0.001), likely attributable to anterior scalene muscle interposition, observed in 78.2% of the supraclavicular views but none of the infraclavicular views. In the supraclavicular view, unlike in the infraclavicular view, arm abduction did not improve the SCV-SCA overlap index (p for interaction = 0.022) and significantly worsened the clavicle shadowing index (p for interaction < 0.001). In the neutral position, a posterocaudal SCA position was absent in all supraclavicular views, whereas 78.2% of infraclavicular views showed posterocranial or posterior SCA positions, in which the SCA was located posterior to the SCV.
CONCLUSIONS: The supraclavicular view provided a greater sonographic SCV-SCA distance than the infraclavicular view, with anterior scalene muscle interposition as a potential contributor, and showed a more favorable relative SCA position. Arm abduction, however, appeared disadvantageous for the supraclavicular approach.

articles.title: Milrinone versus Epinephrine in Cardiac Surgery: An Entropy-Balanced Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare clinical outcomes associated with milrinone and epinephrine use after cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, entropy-balanced cohort study.
SETTING: Intensive care unit (ICU) of a large tertiary academic hospital in the United States, 2001-2022.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients admitted to intensive care after cardiac surgery.
INTERVENTIONS: Initial treatment with milrinone or epinephrine within 48 hours of ICU admission, classified by the agent started first.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury, renal replacement therapy, ICU length of stay (LOS), hospital LOS, and time in postoperative organ dysfunction. Of 13,023 cardiac surgical patients, 1,310 (10%) received milrinone (312 [24%]) or epinephrine (998 [76%]) as the first agent. After entropy balancing, there was no evidence of a difference in 90-day mortality between milrinone and epinephrine groups (7.1% v 6.6%; risk ratio [RR], 1.1; 95% CI, 0.67-1.7). Milrinone was associated with longer ICU LOS (mean difference [MD], +1.8 days; 95% CI, 0.74-3.0), longer hospital LOS (MD, +1.2 days; 95% CI, 0.11-2.3), longer time in postoperative organ dysfunction (MD, +14 hours; 95% CI, 7.5-21), higher risk of acute kidney injury (73% v 61%; RR, 1.2; 95% CI, 1.1-1.3), and higher risk of renal replacement therapy (13% v 7.6%; RR, 1.7; 95% CI, 1.2-2.3).
CONCLUSION: In this entropy-balanced study, there was no evidence of a difference in 90-day mortality between milrinone and epinephrine. Milrinone was associated with more complications and longer LOS, though these findings remain hypothesis-generating and warrant a randomized trial.

articles.title: The compressed rescue window: Frailty and the pathways to postoperative mortality in older surgical patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty predicts postoperative mortality and may act through both increased complication risk and a reduced ability to survive complications. Clarifying their relative contributions may guide perioperative strategies.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Participant Use Files (2020-2024), including patients aged 65 years or older undergoing general/gastrointestinal, vascular, orthopedic, thoracic, or urologic surgery. Emergent and urgent procedures were excluded. Preoperative frailty was measured using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-adapted Risk Analysis Index and the 5-factor modified frailty index. A 4-way causal mediation decomposition (mediator: major complication) partitioned the frailty-mortality effect into complication-occurrence and rescue (direct) pathways. A multistate model assessed frailty as a modifier of the complication → death transition.
RESULTS: Thirty-day mortality was 1.9%, major complications occurred in 11.3%, and failure to rescue occurred in 12.2% of the patients with complications. Each 1-standard deviation increase in the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-adapted Risk Analysis Index was associated with higher mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 2.08; 95% confidence interval, 2.06-2.11). Most frailty-attributable excess mortality occurred through the rescue pathway (pooled 70% by National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-adapted Risk Analysis Index, 63% by 5-factor modified frailty index), ranging from 58% (vascular) to 77% (orthopedic) across specialties (heterogeneity, P < .001). Frailty accelerated the complication → death transition (National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-adapted Risk Analysis Index: hazard ratio, 1.37 per standard deviation; 95% confidence interval, 1.36-1.39); cumulative mortality reached 5% within 2 days in the most-frail quintile versus 13 days in the remainder, and failure to rescue increased from 3.9% to 19.8% across frailty quintiles.
CONCLUSION: In older surgical patients, frailty was associated with both increased complication occurrence and reduced survival after complications, the latter accounting for a larger proportion of excess mortality. These findings support preoperative optimization to improve physiologic reserve and frailty-informed postoperative surveillance to detect and treat complications within a limited rescue window.

articles.title: Prehabilitation in the surgical patient: current concepts and evolving strategies for perioperative optimization.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: More than two decades after its introduction, prehabilitation has evolved from a proof-of-concept strategy into an established component of perioperative care. This review summarizes recent evidence supporting prehabilitation, highlights emerging concepts that may expand its therapeutic scope, and discusses the transition from efficacy studies toward scalable, personalized, and implementation-focused models of care.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent evidence continues to support prehabilitation for improving functional capacity and postoperative recovery. However, effectiveness appears strongly influenced by adherence, frailty, sarcopenia, treatment exposure, and delivery context. Increasing emphasis on frailty, behavioral support, teleprehabilitation, wearable technologies, and patient-centered outcomes is reshaping the field. Digital health platforms are expanding access and facilitating large-scale implementation, while biological phenotyping, digital biomarkers, immune modulation, and the microbiome offer opportunities for greater personalization. Emerging implementation studies suggest that the key challenge is no longer demonstrating efficacy but achieving sustainable, equitable, and scalable effectiveness in routine practice.
SUMMARY: Prehabilitation is evolving beyond a strategy to improve fitness before surgery into a comprehensive approach aimed at enhancing resilience across the perioperative continuum. Future progress will depend on precision prehabilitation, using tiered delivery models, maximizing patient engagement, and integrating prehabilitation into longitudinal care pathways to close the effectiveness gap between research and real-world practice.

articles.title: Immediate Fixation of Peri-Trochanteric Fractures in Patients on Antithrombotic Therapy Does Not Lead to Increased Transfusion Requirements.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Geriatric patients with peritrochanteric fractures typically present with multiple medical comorbidities, many of which are treated with chronic antithrombotic therapy. Patients with these fractures frequently require perioperative blood product administration (PBPA). Unstable fracture patterns, general anesthesia, elderly age, and low preoperative hemoglobin levels contribute to the need for PBPA. The purpose of this study is to characterize risk factors for PBPA in patients with peritrochanteric fractures fixed with an intramedullary nail.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients who underwent short or intermediate intramedullary nailing for a peritrochanteric fracture between January 2012 and December 2022. Patient demographics, comorbidities, injury characteristics, perioperative chronic anticoagulation, PBPA, and 30-day complications were recorded. Categorical dependent variables were analyzed by χ2 and logistic regression. Multivariate analyses are reported with odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: 600 patients met inclusion criteria. PBPA was not associated with perioperative chronic antithrombotic use (OR = 0.59, CI [0.27 - 1.27]). Patients who received PBPA had a lower average hematocrit on admission than those who did not (34.3 vs 37.3, p <0.001). Decreased time between injury to surgical fixation reduced transfusion risk (OR = 0.90, [0.82 - 0.99]). (Female sex was associated with increased odds of PBPA (OR = 2.0, CI [1.05 - 3.8]). Lower hematocrit (OR = 0.90, [0.85 - 0.96], increased age at fracture (OR = 1.02, [1.00 - 1.04]), and longer hospital length of stay (OR = 1.06 per day, [1.01 - 1.12]) all increased the risk of requiring PBPA.
CONCLUSION: In patients with peritrochanteric hip fractures fixed with a short or intermediate intramedullary nailing, chronic antithrombotic therapy does not increase the risk of PBPA. OTA class A1 fracture pattern was an independent protective factor for PBPA, while increased age and decreased baseline hematocrit were risk factors for PBPA.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence - Driven Risk Stratification in Emergency Surgery: Development and Validation of the PROMETHEUS-AI Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency General Surgery is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity, and accurate perioperative risk stratification remains challenging. Artificial intelligence and machine learning may improve risk prediction by integrating multiple demographic, clinical, laboratory, and operative variables. This study aimed to develop and internally validate PROMETHEUS-AI, an artificial intelligence-driven framework for predicting postoperative complications in Emergency General Surgery.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center observational cohort study included 250 adult patients who underwent emergency surgery for acute appendicitis, acute cholecystitis, or non-oncological intestinal obstruction between 2020 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and operative variables were incorporated into Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models. Internal validation was performed using an 80:20 training-validation split. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).
RESULTS: Postoperative complications occurred in 48 patients (19.2%), while major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grade IIIa-V) occurred in 17 patients (6.8%). XGBoost demonstrated the highest predictive performance, with a ROC-AUC of 0.88, accuracy of 85.0%, sensitivity of 83.0%, specificity of 86.0%, precision of 81.0%, and an F1-score of 0.82. Random Forest achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.84, while Logistic Regression achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.78. SHAP analysis identified serum albumin, age, ASA physical status classification, C-reactive protein, serum lactate, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as the six highest-ranked predictors, followed by operative duration, hemodynamic instability, sepsis on admission, and Clinical Frailty Scale.
CONCLUSIONS: PROMETHEUS-AI demonstrated promising internally validated performance for postoperative complication risk stratification in Emergency General Surgery, with XGBoost showing the highest discrimination among the evaluated algorithms. These findings support the feasibility of explainable machine learning for perioperative risk assessment. However, given the retrospective single-center design, limited sample size, and absence of external validation, PROMETHEUS-AI should be regarded as an exploratory proof-of-concept model requiring prospective multicenter and external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Incidence and Predictors of Fetal Adverse Outcomes Among Cesarean Deliveries: A Retrospective Cohort Study in South Ethiopia Using Poisson Regression.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cesarean section (C/S) may be associated with adverse fetal outcomes. Evidence on intraoperative predictors remains limited. This study assessed the incidence and predictors of adverse fetal outcomes in South Ethiopia.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study reviewed records of 662 fetuses delivered by C/S. Data were analyzed using STATA. Poisson regression identified predictors of composite adverse fetal outcomes.
RESULTS: The incidence was 17.9 per 100 births (95% CI: 14.9-20.9). Predictors included emergency C/S (ARR=1.73, 95% CI: 1.16-2.57), maternal age >35 (ARR=2.7, 95% CI: 1.24-5.98), anesthesia type (ARR=1.83, 95% CI: 1.27-2.63), preterm birth (ARR=4.3, 95% CI: 1.73-10.63), MAP at 10 minutes (ARR=2.4, 95% CI: 1.48-3.9), incision to-delivery time >5 minutes (ARR=1.52, 95% CI: 1.15-2.01), and induction-to-delivery time >8 minutes (ARR=1.96, 95% CI: 1.44-2.72).
CONCLUSION: Adverse fetal outcomes were high, warranting improved ANC and reduced intraoperative delays.

articles.title: Safety and Complications of Carpal Tunnel Release in Patients Aged 90 and Older: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical practice increasingly observes elderly patients with carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) as life expectancy increases globally. This study aims to investigate the complication rate in patients aged 90 years and older to determine the safety of this procedure.
METHODS: This study retrospectively reviewed the charts of patients aged 90 years or older who underwent either open or endoscopic CTR between April 2014 and January 2024. Surgical and medical complications were evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 223 patients were studied, with a mean age of 92 ± 2 years and a median follow-up time of 2 weeks (range: 2-83 weeks). Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) was used in 123 patients (55%), and local anesthesia in 100 patients (45%). The overall complication rate was 10% (22 patients). Scar pain or tenderness was the most common minor complication, occurring in 9% (20 patients). No cases of infection, hematoma, complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS), or wound dehiscence were reported. There were no medical complications documented in the available records in the available records after either endoscopic or open CTR.
CONCLUSION: CTR appears to have a favorable early perioperative safety profile in patients aged 90 years and older, with a low observed incidence of major complications. Most reported postoperative events consisted of transient scar pain or tenderness. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to better characterize long-term outcomes and complication rates in this population.

articles.title: The Association Between Caregiver Support and Early Postoperative Outcomes after Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early postoperative recovery after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) shows considerable variability despite standardized surgical and rehabilitation protocols. Social support provided by caregivers may influence early pain control and functional recovery; however, its clinical impact has not been well quantified.
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between caregiver support and early postoperative pain and functional outcomes following primary unilateral TKA.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 86 patients who underwent primary unilateral TKA performed by a single surgeon at a single tertiary referral center. All patients received standardized spinal anesthesia without regional nerve blocks or patient-controlled analgesia. Caregiver-related variables included the number of caregivers during hospitalization and at home, caregiver proximity, cohabitation status, and caregiver participation in physiotherapy. Pain was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at postoperative 2 weeks and 3 months. Functional outcomes included independent ambulation, stair climbing ability, and knee range of motion. Spearman correlation analyses and multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses with HC3 robust standard errors were performed.
RESULTS: Mean VAS scores decreased from 3.67 ± 2.16 at 2 weeks to 2.00 ± 1.52 at 3 months postoperatively. A higher number of caregivers at home was independently associated with lower VAS scores at both time points and greater pain reduction over time (p < 0.05). A higher number of caregivers at home was also associated with a higher likelihood of stair climbing (OR = 15.44, p = 0.010). In contrast, a higher number of caregivers during hospitalization was associated with higher VAS scores at 2 weeks and a lower likelihood of stair climbing. Caregiver-related variables were not significantly associated with knee range of motion.
CONCLUSION: Greater caregiver support at home is associated with improved early postoperative pain control and functional independence following TKA. Caregiver availability in the home setting represents an important factor to consider in postoperative care planning.

articles.title: Nerve Blocks for Traumatic Injuries.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks are important for modern, opioid-sparing trauma care. Proficiency in select, high-yield blocks can provide rapid targeted analgesia and improve clinical outcomes. For example, in a patient with multiple rib fractures, performing an erector spinae or serratus anterior block can alleviate chest wall pain and improve respiratory function. Similarly, a fascia iliaca block in an elderly patient with a hip fracture minimizes pain while also reducing the risk of delirium. Safety requires precise needle visualization and proper anesthetic dosing. Standardizing workflows with dedicated carts and documentation templates promotes efficiency. This approach delivers effective pain managment while maintaining the speed and safety necessary in emergency settings.

articles.title: Re-use of Ambu aScope during exploration of the common bile duct for stones in low-resource settings- a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Various methods confirm stone clearance during surgical exploration of bile duct, but choledochoscopy is considered the most effective. However, choledochoscopes are expensive in context of low-resource settings. The Ambu aScope, a disposable flexible video-bronchoscope used in anesthesia, has been successfully tried as a cheaper alternative for CBD (Common Bile Duct) exploration in few limited studies but in those studies the aScope had not been re-used. In Nepal, where affordability is a concern, even the reuse of properly disinfected Ambu aScopes may be justifiable if proven safe. This study is probably the first of its kind to evaluate the reuse of the Ambu aScope for choledochoscopy.
METHODS: This study includes all patients with CBD stones who underwent CBD exploration for stone using Ambu aScope in Department of Surgery of BPKIHS, Dharan between January 2022 and December 2024.
RESULTS: Over the study period, a total of 75 cases of CBD exploration had been performed at our institute using Ambu aScope. These patients had a mean age of 55.21 ± 13.73 years (26-84 years) with female: male ration of 2.5:1. Choledocholithiasis was secondary to Gallbladder stone in majority (82.7% of cases) and was multiple with average size of the largest stone being 18.47 ± 3.26 mm. The approaches used for exploration of CBD were laparoscopic (in 21.3% cases) and open (in 78.7% cases). Using Ambu aScope, acceptable view of extrahepatic biliary tree with complete stone retrieval was achieved in 97.3% cases. No intraoperative complications related to the use of the Ambu aScope were encountered. Moreover, none of the patients developed cholangitis, an infectious complication that may be related to the reuse of the aScope.
CONCLUSION: Based on our experience, the Ambu aScope may serve as a practical and economical alternative to the conventional choledochoscope for CBD exploration, offering acceptable visualization of the extrahepatic biliary tree without evident reuse-related infectious complications. Further studies with larger cohorts are warranted to confirm these findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study has been registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07285447). After the ethical clearance from Institutional Review Committee (CODE- IRC/2994/025) and Research committee of BPKIHS, this study has been conducted.

articles.title: Lipidomics reveals phosphatidylserine (20:4/20:4) as a novel biomarker for delayed neurocognitive recovery in clinical and animal aging models.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The accumulation of various metabolic substances in elderly patients following surgery and anesthesia contributes to delayed neurocognitive recovery (dNCR). Progress in clinical diagnosis and therapeutic interventions is hindered by the lack of reliable biomarkers. This study aims to identify lipid markers that can predict dNCR during the perioperative management for elderly patients.
METHODS: A systematic lipidomics approach was employed to examine the impact of anesthesia and surgery on metabolism and to identify potential biomarkers for predicting and diagnosing dNCR. The study included 67 patients (25 with dNCR, 42 without). Blood samples were collected pre- and post-surgery for metabolite analysis. Differential metabolites were identified using stringent criteria (variable importance in projection [VIP] > 1, fold change [FC] > 1.5 or < 0.67, adjusted P-value < 0.05, area under the curve [AUC] > 0.75). In a mouse model, lipid metabolism alterations in the brain after anesthesia and surgery were analyzed in relation to cognitive dysfunction to identify blood biomarkers linked to dNCR.
RESULTS: Thirteen lipid molecules in preoperative blood samples showed significant associations with dNCR. Phosphatidylserine(PS) (20:4/20:4) levels in the prefrontal cortex of dNCR mice were markedly elevated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated strong correlations between pre- and postoperative PS (20:4/20:4) levels and dNCR. Logistic regression confirmed that preoperative PS (20:4/20:4) levels were significantly associated with postoperative dNCR risk.
CONCLUSION: Dynamic monitoring of PS (20:4/20:4) levels offers an early indicator of dNCR risk. However, whether lowering PS (20:4/20:4) levels would reduce dNCR incidence requires further mechanistic studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05105451, registered 2021-11-03).

articles.title: The effect of mandala coloring on perioperative psychological well-being, emotional self-efficacy and anxiety in gynecologic cancer patients: a randomized controlled study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women diagnosed with gynecologic cancer frequently experience heightened anxiety and psychological distress during the perioperative period. Mandala coloring, defined as the structured coloring of pre-drawn symmetrical circular patterns to promote focused attention and relaxation, is a brief art-based intervention increasingly used in oncology settings.
AIM: This randomized controlled study aimed to evaluate the effect of perioperative mandala coloring on psychological well-being, emotional self-efficacy, and state anxiety in women undergoing surgery for gynecologic cancer.
METHODS: The study was conducted between May and August 2025 in the inpatient Obstetrics and Gynecology ward of a state hospital in Türkiye. Eighty-four patients were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 42) or a control group (n = 42). The intervention group received two structured mandala coloring sessions on two consecutive preoperative days (35-50 min each). Outcome measures including the Psychological Well-Being Scale (PWBS), Emotional Self-Efficacy Scale (ESES), and State Anxiety Scale (SAS) were administered at baseline (T1), 1-3 h after the first session (T2), and 24 h after the second session (T3). For the control group, outcome assessments were conducted at baseline (T1), 1-3 h after baseline (T2), and 24 h after baseline (T3). Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA to examine group (intervention vs. control), time (T1-T3), and group × time interaction effects.
RESULTS: No significant between-group differences were observed at baseline (p > .05). Significant group × time interactions were observed for psychological well-being, emotional self-efficacy, and state anxiety (p < .001). Compared with controls, the intervention group demonstrated significantly greater increases in psychological well-being and emotional self-efficacy and greater reductions in anxiety at T2 and T3. Significant group × time interaction effects were observed for psychological well-being, emotional self-efficacy, and state anxiety (all p < .001). Compared with controls, the intervention group demonstrated greater increases in psychological well-being and emotional self-efficacy, along with greater reductions in anxiety across the perioperative period. Effect sizes were large (partial η² range: 0.80-0.85).
CONCLUSION: Brief perioperative mandala coloring significantly improved psychological well-being and emotional self-efficacy while reducing state anxiety in women with gynecologic cancer. Mandala coloring may serve as a feasible, low-cost supportive nursing intervention during the perioperative period.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07160062; registered September 6, 2025.

articles.title: Switching from controlled to assisted ventilation based on oxygenation thresholds and PEEP: a target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PaO2/FiO2-based dynamic treatment strategies can optimise the timing of switching from controlled to assisted ventilation.
DESIGN AND SETTING: Target trial emulation using the MIMIC-IV database v3.1 (2008-2022).
PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients on controlled invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ≥ 48 h with at least one PaO2/FiO2 <300 mmHg. A sensitivity analysis included patients ventilated for ≥ 24 h, excluding post-surgical patients.
INTERVENTIONS: We compared strategies defined by switching once PaO2/FiO2 exceeded predefined thresholds (150, 200, or 250 mmHg). Additionally, to account for possible PEEP-dependent effects, the thresholds were evaluated depending on the set PEEP (< 8 vs. ≥8 cmH2O), yielding nine strategies. Outcomes were 28-day restricted mean time lost (RMTL) to successful extubation (where a lower RMTL indicates a longer time to extubation) and mortality.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 1,635 patients, the strategy of delaying the switch until PaO2/FiO2 >250 mmHg showed a longer time to successful extubation compared to switching at > 150 mmHg or > 200 mmHg (RMTL 17.4 days [95% CI: 15.9-18.6] vs. 19.6 days [95% CI: 18.6-20.9] and 19.8 days [95% CI: 18.5-21.1], respectively). Exploratory PEEP-dependent analyses demonstrated the longest time to successful extubation with '>250 mmHg' for both low and high PEEP and the shortest with '>150 mmHg for low PEEP; >200 mmHg for high PEEP'. Among patients ventilated for ≥ 24 h, the 150 mmHg threshold was most favourable, irrespective of PEEP. No mortality differences were observed across strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: Switching as soon as PaO2/FiO2 >150 mmHg is generally favoured over delaying until > 250 mmHg. Patients requiring ≥ 48 h of controlled IMV with PEEP ≥ 8 cmH2O may potentially benefit from a slightly higher threshold (> 200 mmHg). Prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: Development and external validation of age-specific predictive models for sepsis in critically ill neonates and children using multidimensional hematological parameters: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units (NICU/PICU). Given the rapid clinical deterioration of these vulnerable populations, shifting from reactive diagnosis to proactive prediction of sepsis onset is crucial. Multidimensional hematological parameters may provide new insights for risk stratification. While routine complete blood count (CBC) is widely used, the predictive potential of high-dimensional hematological cell morphology features that extend beyond traditional CBC remains under-investigated in large-scale pediatric cohorts.
METHODS: This multicenter study utilized a large-scale dataset from the CALM2302 project, encompassing 17,066 critically ill neonates and children across 30 Chinese hospitals between October 2020 and October 2023. We developed population-specific CatBoost models for NICU and PICU to predict sepsis onset. To mitigate class imbalance, random undersampling was applied to the training sets. From a candidate pool of 1,924 parameters (37 routine CBC and 1,887 research features), optimized signatures of approximately 200 features were selected for each population. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) across internal and dual external validation cohorts. Furthermore, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was performed to ensure model interpretability and identify key biological predictors.
RESULTS: Among the total cohort, 10,347 infants were categorized into the NICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 7.48%), while 6,719 children formed the PICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 10.92%). CatBoost was identified as the optimal architecture after benchmarking nine machine learning algorithms. The population-specific simplified 18-variable models demonstrated robust performance. In the NICU cohort, the model achieved an internal AUC of 0.846 and external AUCs of 0.742 and 0.827. For the PICU cohort, corresponding AUCs were 0.803, 0.717, and 0.811. These simplified models maintained highly comparable discriminative power to the full models (range of AUC attenuation: 0.005-0.027). SHAP analysis identified 18 key predictive features for each cohort, with only two shared features between the two populations and the remaining being cohort-specific. Notably, most of these 18 features were research parameters rather than traditional blood counts indices. Furthermore, most of these features remained statistically significant in multivariable analyses after adjustment for age, sex, and study sites.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, we developed and validated simplified 18-variable models that accurately predict sepsis in both neonatal and pediatric populations. By capturing early hematological morphological alterations beyond traditional blood counts, these models offer a robust, interpretable, and clinically accessible solution for proactive sepsis management in intensive care units.

articles.title: A multimodal model integrating biomarkers, clinical features, and geriatric assessment to predict post-hip-fracture complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major postoperative complications in older adults with hip fracture vary widely among individuals. Reliable tools for identifying high-risk patients are lacking, especially multidimensional risk models combining clinical features, biomarkers and geriatric assessment. This study aimed to develop and validate a multidimensional predictive model for individualized risk stratification of major postoperative complications in older adults with hip fracture.
METHODS: A total of 342 older adults with hip fracture were retrospectively enrolled and split into training (n = 240) and validation (n = 102) sets at 7:3. Predictors were screened by univariate and LASSO regression. Three machine learning models were constructed and compared. Model performance was evaluated by ROC, calibration curves and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Seven independent factors were identified: modified Frailty Index-5, C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index, lymphocyte-to-calcium ratio, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index and Mini-Mental State Examination score. The random forest model achieved optimal AUC (training: 0.877; validation: 0.833), with good calibration and high clinical net benefit at 0.1-0.8 threshold.
CONCLUSION: A multimodal prediction model for postoperative complications in older adults with hip fracture was successfully established. It shows good discrimination, calibration and clinical utility, supporting early risk identification and perioperative strategy optimization.

articles.title: Pain-control strategies for blind office endometrial biopsy: a systematic review with inert-controlled meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blind office endometrial biopsy is common, but pain during sampling can limit acceptability. Prior reviews have often combined different procedures, comparators, and pain timepoints. We evaluated randomized evidence for pain-control strategies during blind outpatient or office-based endometrial biopsy or sampling.
METHODS: For the primary estimand, we restricted meta-analysis to randomized comparisons against placebo, saline, placebo gel, distilled water, or other inert controls, defined as controls without intended analgesic activity, that reported extractable intra-procedural pain scores on a 0-10 compatible scale. We searched PubMed, CENTRAL, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Wanfang, VIP, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP from inception to 9 May 2026, with update checks of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov on 12 June 2026. CNKI, SinoMed/CBM, and ChiCTR were checked supplementally. Random-effects mean differences were pooled. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE.
RESULTS: The PRISMA-counted searches identified 2632 records; 619 duplicates were removed and 2013 records were screened. Eight randomized trials involving 944 participants were included in the primary meta-analysis. Pain-control interventions lowered average pain during biopsy compared with inert controls (mean difference, -1.87 points; 95% confidence interval, -2.52 to -1.22; I-squared = 86.7%). REML and Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses remained directionally consistent, although the prediction interval crossed no effect. Excluding the single systemic COX-2 inhibitor trial left seven local-anesthetic trials and 864 participants with a similar direction of effect (mean difference, -2.10; 95% confidence interval, -2.71 to -1.48; I-squared = 83.7%). Evidence was driven mainly by local anesthetic trials. Harms were sparsely and inconsistently reported. Certainty was low for pain reduction and very low for safety.
CONCLUSIONS: Low-certainty randomized evidence suggests that tested pain-control strategies, mainly local anesthetic interventions, may reduce average intra-procedural pain during blind office endometrial biopsy with inert comparators, but heterogeneity is substantial and the optimal intervention class remains uncertain. These findings support patient-centered discussion of pain-control options but do not establish any specific agent or intervention class as standard care.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This systematic review was not prospectively registered.

articles.title: Analgesic efficacy of 0.75% ropivacaine versus 2% lidocaine after unilateral mandibular third molar extraction: a prospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This prospective observational cohort study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of 0.75% ropivacaine in unilateral mandibular third molar extraction and to compare its postoperative analgesic outcomes with those of 2% lidocaine.
METHODS: A total of 128 patients undergoing unilateral mandibular third molar extraction were prospectively enrolled. According to the local anesthetic administered during routine clinical practice, patients were categorized into two exposure cohorts: 2% lidocaine (China Otsuka, Tianjin, China) and 0.75% ropivacaine (Shijiazhuang No.4 Pharmaceutical, Shijiazhuang, China). All patients received inferior alveolar nerve block anesthesia with the designated agent, supplemented with local infiltration anesthesia using articaine (Primacaine, Mérignac, France). Postoperative assessments were conducted at 24 h and 7 days using standardized electronic questionnaires. Key measures included: (1) onset of postoperative pain (primary endpoint); (2) duration of lower lip numbness; (3) time to first analgesic intake; (4) 10 cm Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at 24 h and 7 days; (5) Postoperative Symptom Severity scale (PoSSe).
RESULTS: The cohort included 41 males and 82 females, with a mean age of 28.5 ± 7.61 (ranging: 17‒65 years). In ropivacaine group, the Median (Quartile) of postoperative pain onset, durations for lower lip numbness, and time to first analgesic intake were 9.00 (6.00, 11.00) hours, 8.00 (6.00, 9.00) hours, and 7.00 (6.00, 10.00) hours respectively, compared to 3.00 (3.00, 4.00) hours, 3.00 (2.25, 3.00) and 3.00 (2.00, 5.00) hours in lidocaine group. No significant difference was found in both VAS scores at 24 h (24hVAS) and 7 days (7dVAS). No significant difference was found in PoSSe. Only the 24hVAS showed a positive correlation with the Pell & Gregory II classification in both lidocaine group and ropivacaine group. The 7dVAS only showed a positive correlation with the Pell & Gregory II classification in lidocaine group, and the PoSSe only showed a positive correlation with the Pell & Gregory I classification in ropivacaine group (P < 0.05, r > 0).
CONCLUSIONS: The results demonstrate that 0.75% ropivacaine delays pain onset and analgesic consumption, which may offer an advantageous option for prolonged surgical procedures and early postoperative pain management. However, all patients received supplementary articaine infiltration, which may limit the interpretation of the true analgesic efficacy of the tested agents. Besides, it requires confirmation in randomized trials.

articles.title: Status epilepticus in mTORopathies: a systematic review of clinical features, management, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway plays a critical role in epileptogenesis; however, its involvement in human status epilepticus (SE) remains poorly understood. mTORopathies, genetic disorders defined by mutations that disrupt mTOR signaling, frequently manifest severe neurological complications, among which SE is particularly consequential.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science was conducted for studies on mTORopathies and SE. We analyzed the clinical presentation, treatment strategies, and outcomes of all cases.
RESULTS: Eight hundred ninety-seven records were initially identified, of which 31 were included in this review. SE may manifest in different mTORopathies. SE often presents early, recurs frequently, and can be catastrophic. Refractory SE (RSE) predominantly affects neonates and infants and frequently occurs in the context of MCD. SE can be terminated with multiple anti-seizure medications (ASMs), alone or in combination with mTOR inhibitors. However, managing RSE is challenging. Current treatment strategies include novel ASMs, anesthetics, mTOR inhibitors, the ketogenic diet, immunotherapy, epilepsy surgery, and neuromodulation. A multifaceted approach is preferred to achieve seizure control and to improve developmental outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: SE remains a significant clinical challenge in patients with mTORopathies. mTOR signaling may contribute to the pathogenesis of SE and could represent a potential therapeutic target. Further investigation in large cohort studies is needed to clarify the role of mTOR signaling in SE and to evaluate the effects of mTOR inhibitors and immunotherapies on outcomes in patients with SE/RSE.

articles.title: Suzetrigine Use in the Perioperative Period: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Effective perioperative pain management is central to anesthesia and enhanced recovery after surgery protocols. Opioids remain the mainstay for moderate-to-severe postoperative pain, but their adverse effects, including CNS depression and dependency, have driven the search for non-opioid alternatives. Suzetrigine, the first selective NaV1.8 inhibitor approved for moderate-to-severe acute pain in adults, offers a novel mechanism by selectively blocking nociceptive signaling in peripheral sensory neurons and is the first new class of analgesics in decades.
RECENT FINDINGS: Phase III trials in patients undergoing abdominoplasty and bunionectomy demonstrated that suzetrigine reduced postoperative pain versus placebo with a favorable safety profile. Efficacy was generally comparable to hydrocodone/acetaminophen, and its opioid-sparing profile makes it an attractive component of multimodal perioperative analgesia. This review summarizes suzetrigine's pharmacology and emerging role in perioperative pain management, emphasizing its integration into multimodal analgesic pathways, opioid-sparing potential, and directions for future study.

articles.title: Imaging Subphenotypes in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: From Characterization to Treatment-Effect Modification.
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is defined by clinical and radiographic criteria, yet patients differ in underlying biology, physiological impairment, and regional lung injury. Such heterogeneity may influence treatment response. Current ventilatory strategies, however, are generally guided by physiological targets without fully accounting for the biological, structural, and functional diversity of ARDS. Computed tomography, lung ultrasound, and electrical impedance tomography offer complementary information on lung morphology, aeration, and regional ventilation, while selected approaches may inform recruitability assessment. Nevertheless, evidence that imaging-defined subphenotypes identify patients who derive differential clinical benefit from specific interventions remains limited. This review examines the contribution of lung imaging to individualized respiratory management in ARDS, separating descriptive and prognostic findings from evidence of treatment-effect modification. Limitations of categorical classification and the dynamic nature of lung injury are discussed alongside the potential integration of imaging, physiological, biological, and clinical data. Such multimodal approaches remain investigational but may support evaluation of heterogeneous responses to positive end-expiratory pressure, prone positioning, and other supportive strategies. Before these approaches can guide treatment selection, standardized image acquisition, reproducible classification, longitudinal assessment, independent validation, and prospective demonstration of clinical benefit are required.

articles.title: Sugammadex Use In Severe Renal Dysfunction Despite Regulatory Recommendations: A Secondary Analysis Of The Prospective Multicentre DELPO Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: European product information does not recommend sugammadex in severe renal impairment, including dialysis, because renal elimination is markedly reduced. European data describing reversal practice in this population are limited.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether sugammadex was the predominant pharmacological reversal agent among patients in GFR categories G4-G5 or receiving dialysis.
METHODS: This secondary analysis of the prospective DELPO cohort included adults who received general anaesthesia, neuromuscular blockade, and pharmacological reversal with sugammadex or neostigmine at 43 Spanish hospitals. Patients were classified as being in GFR categories G1-G3 (eGFR ≥30 mL min-¹ 1.73 m-²) or GFR categories G4-G5 or receiving dialysis (eGFR <30 mL min-¹ 1.73 m-² or dialysis). Reversal-agent use was described overall and according to renal function.
RESULTS: The analysis included 1331 patients, of whom 35 were in GFR categories G4-G5 or receiving dialysis, including 20 receiving dialysis. Sugammadex was used in 1,278 of 1,331 patients overall (96.0%), in 1248 of 1,296 patients in GFR categories G1-G3 (96.3%), and in 30 of 35 patients in GFR categories G4-G5 or receiving dialysis (85.7%; 95% CI, 70.6-93.7%). Among the 20 patients receiving dialysis, sugammadex was administered to 16 (80.0%; 95% CI, 58.4-91.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in GFR categories G4-G5 or receiving dialysis who received pharmacological reversal, sugammadex was used in 85.7% (30/35), including 80.0% (16/20) of patients receiving dialysis, despite current European product information not recommending its use in this population.

articles.title: Quadratus lumborum versus transversus abdominis plane block for postoperative analgesia in laparoscopic colorectal surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective pain management after surgery is crucial for recovery following laparoscopic colorectal resection in enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programs. While the transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block is commonly used, it may not fully address visceral pain. The quadratus lumborum (QL) block might provide better coverage for both somatic and visceral pain due to its ability to spread to the thoracolumbar fascia and paravertebral space.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare the clinical outcomes of QL versus TAP blocks in laparoscopic colorectal surgery. The main outcome was total opioid use within 24 h. Secondary outcomes included early pain scores, time until the first rescue analgesic was needed, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), length of stay, surgical complications, and side effects related to the blocks.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic literature search using PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to 27 July 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing QL and TAP blocks. Two reviewers independently screened the studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. We calculated pooled estimates using a random-effects model and evaluated the reliability of the evidence on the basis of the grading of recommendations, assessment, development, and evaluation (GRADE) framework.
RESULTS: Four RCTs (n = 419) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with the TAP block, the QL block led to lower opioid use within 24 h (MD [mean difference] -8.92 mg morphine equivalents; 95% CI -11.57 to -6.28) and reduced pain scores both at rest MD -0.25 (-0.37 to -0.21) and during movement MD -0.40 [-0.52 to -0.29]. Operative time numerically favored the QL block, but the pooled difference was not statistically significant. The rates of PONV (OR 0.54; 95% CI 0.25-1.19) and dizziness (OR 0.60; 95% CI 0.22-1.63) were not significantly different between the two groups. The evidence was rated high for PONV and operative time, and moderate for opioid consumption, pain at rest, pain during movement, and dizziness, reflecting downgrades for imprecision and, for opioid consumption and pain during movement, substantial-to-high heterogeneity (I2 85% and 93%, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: In laparoscopic colorectal surgery, the QL block shows better opioid-sparing effects and lower pain scores at rest and during movement than the TAP block. Operative time numerically favored the QL block but did not differ significantly between groups. Importantly, it does not lead to more adverse effects. These findings suggest that the QL block may be a useful opioid-sparing option within ERAS-based perioperative care, although larger multicenter RCTs are needed before routine preference over the TAP block can be firmly recommended.

articles.title: Risk factors for surgical site infection in clean surgeries at a modern small animal teaching hospital-a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: There are various studies on potential risk factors for the development of a surgical site infection (SSI). None of them analyse the factors with a focus on the daily practice of a small animal teaching clinic, especially the studies on the influence of personnel in the operating room are sparse. Over a period of 7 months, 102 dogs and cats belonging to private owners that had undergone clean surgery were prospectively studied for the occurrence of an SSI and potential associated risk factors. Patients were followed up 30 or 90 days later, either through examinations at the clinic or via telephone interviews with the pet owners. An SSI occurred in a total of 12% of surgeries (12/102). Although no significant risk factors for SSI were identified, surgery duration was longer and perioperative body temperatures were lower than reported in previous literature. The high number of personnel present in the operating room and the differences in SSI risk between surgical categories warrant further investigation. Skin surgeries tended to have a higher SSI risk than orthopaedic and neurosurgical procedures.

articles.title: Use of transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage in the Nordic countries: A survey of incidences and indications.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical guidelines for cervical cerclage vary in terms of indications and patient management. In this study, we investigated the incidence, indications, surgical techniques, timing of placement, and peri- and postoperative care for both transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage use in the Nordic countries.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This study was a cross-sectional survey. An electronic questionnaire was developed and distributed via an electronic data capture system (REDCap) to an obstetrician from all birth units in Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden. The primary outcome was the reported incidence of transvaginal cerclage, both history- and ultrasound-indicated, and of transabdominal cerclage.
RESULTS: The estimated incidence per 100 000 births of history-indicated transvaginal cerclage was 231 in DK, 70 in FI, 140 in IS, 133 in NO, and 166 in SE. For ultrasound-indicated transvaginal cerclage, the estimated incidence per 100 000 births was 166 in DK, 21 in FI, 140 in IS, 17 in NO, and 59 in SE. For transabdominal cerclage, the estimated incidence was 63 in DK, 7 in FI, 28 in IS, 31 in NO, and 18 in SE.
CONCLUSIONS: There is substantial variation in the use of cervical cerclage between the Nordic countries. We advocate for a harmonized Nordic model of cerclage care to ensure equitable and consistent practice across countries, coupled with a Nordic research collaboration network that can drive knowledge generation and implementation across the region.

articles.title: An aptamer/hydrogel system for prolonged sustained drug delivery.
articles.abstract: Prolonged drug effect from a single-dose administration offers therapeutic advantages. To achieve that goal, we developed a hydrogel modified with an aptamer to a specific drug (Gel-Apt). This system, using both affinity- and diffusion-controlled mechanisms allowed increased duration of effect and decreased systemic toxicity. We demonstrate the efficacy of this system with tetrodotoxin (TTX), an ultrapotent local anesthetic, in rat sciatic nerve block. Gel-Apt loaded with TTX caused nerve block lasting 39 h. This system using both affinity-and diffusion-controlled mechanisms could be applicable to any drug for which there is a specific aptamer.

articles.title: What every intensivist should know about pharmacology.
Ultrasound-Guided Pudendal Nerve Block in Elderly Pelvic Organ Prolapse Surgery: Impact on Anesthetic Consumption and Postoperative Recovery-A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nerve block is often used for multimodal analgesia. Surgeries for pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in elderly patients are focused on the perineal area, where pudendal nerve block (PNB) can provide analgesia or anaesthesia. There are limited studies on PNB in POP surgery, mainly addressing postoperative pain relief. This prospective randomized controlled trial examined the impact of ultrasound-guided PNB on intraoperative medication and postoperative recovery in elderly POP surgery patients.
METHODS: Patients aged 60-70 undergoing total vaginal hysterectomy (with or without sacral fixation/colporrhaphy) under general anesthesia were randomized into two groups: PNB (pudendal nerve block) and NPNB (no pudendal nerve block). Anesthesia was induced with target-controlled infusions of remifentanil (3 ng/mL) and propofol (3 µg/mL). The study compared intraoperative anesthetic doses, hemodynamic changes, cardiovascular drug needs, wakefulness time, and post-op recovery quality between the groups.
RESULTS: 58 patients completed the study. The PNB group required significantly less remifentanil (386.6 ± 239.1 µg vs 563.1 ± 235.7 µg, p = 0.005) and propofol (645.5 ± 315.2 mg vs 804.2 ± 297.2 mg, p = 0.028) compared to the NPNB group. Intraoperative hemodynamics were more stable in the PNB group, with a reduced need for vasopressors. The PNB group also exhibited faster emergence, lower postoperative pain, and less oversedation,with a non-significant trend toward higher QoR-40 scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided PNB in elderly POP surgery patients reduced opioid and anesthetic doses, shortened awakening time, and produced clinically favourable improvements in postoperative recovery. Larger studies are needed to confirm these benefits for postoperative rehabilitation.

articles.title: Intraoperative Recognition and Management of Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Defibrillator Lead Dysfunction During Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation.
Body mass index and diaphragm dysfunction in critically ill adults: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diaphragm dysfunction (DD) may be present at ICU admission or be detected during subsequent critical care. Body mass index (BMI) influences respiratory loading and diaphragm morphology, yet it has usually been treated as a descriptive characteristic or adjustment variable rather than as the exposure of primary interest. We therefore examined the association between BMI and protocol-defined DD in critically ill adults.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 221 adult ICU patients between January and June 2023. BMI was analyzed primarily as a continuous exposure; World Health Organization BMI categories were examined as exploratory analyses.
