We evaluated whether out-of-hours cesarean delivery was independently associated with transfusion in a Romanian tertiary maternity unit operating under constrained resources. Methods: We conducted a retrospective unmatched case-control study of cesarean deliveries performed from 2023 to 2025. All eligible transfused women were included as cases; two non-transfused controls per case were randomly selected within each calendar year. Eligibility required preoperative hemoglobin ≥ 10 g/dL and normal coagulation. The primary exposure was out-of-hours surgery, and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal, obstetric, placental, and hematological factors. Results: The source population contained 6773 cesarean deliveries, with 608 transfusions (9.0%). The analytical sample comprised 401 cases and 802 controls. Out-of-hours procedures occurred in 64.1% of cases and 52.5% of controls (crude OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.26-2.07). After adjustment, out-of-hours delivery remained associated with transfusion (aOR 2.03, 95% CI 1.45-2.84). Placenta previa, suspected placenta accreta spectrum, and lower preoperative hemoglobin were the strongest clinical predictors. When postoperative/pre-transfusion hemoglobin was added, the out-of-hours association attenuated to an aOR of 1.02 (95% CI 0.63-1.65); sensitivity analyses remained consistent with the primary model. Conclusions: Out-of-hours cesarean delivery was associated with approximately two-fold higher transfusion odds after adjustment for the measured clinical factors. Because cesarean indication, urgency, and labor characteristics were not available, this association may partly reflect the different case mix and acuity of out-of-hours surgery rather than the working period itself. Attenuation after adjustment for post-exposure hemoglobin is compatible with, but does not establish greater perioperative blood loss. In high-cesarean, resource-constrained settings, standardized hemorrhage-risk identification and equivalent preparedness across duty periods warrant prospective evaluation in studies that also record indication and urgency.

articles.title: Osteopenia Is Associated with Inferior Survival After Deceased-Donor Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Background: Alterations in body composition have been linked to both perioperative and long-term outcomes that cause orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT). Nevertheless, the potential predictive role of recipient bone mineral density (BMD) in clinical outcomes following OLT remains uncertain. In this study, we aimed to explore the role of BMD as a prognostic factor in patients undergoing OLT after brain death donation, in the context of long-term outcome. Methods: A total of 480 patients who underwent OLT during the period from 2010 to 2023 at the University Hospital RWTH Aachen were included in the retrospective analysis. Preoperative computed tomography-based segmentation was used to measure BMD at the level of the 11th thoracic vertebra. Osteopenia was defined based previously described sex-specific cutoffs. Perioperative complications were assessed by Clavien-Dindo (CD) classification and comprehensive complication index (CCI). Survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and uni- and multivariable Cox regression. Results: In our cohort, osteopenia was highly prevalent (48%). Patients with osteopenia exhibited significantly inferior overall survival (log-rank p < 0.001, observed median follow-up 52 months [14-97] vs. 59 months [18-101]) and impaired graft survival (log-rank p = 0.037, observed median follow-up 50 months [13-97] vs. 52 months [14-96]). In our multivariable model, osteopenia was confirmed as an independent risk-factor for inferior overall survival (HR 1.602, 95% CI 1.113-2.306; p = 0.011) and inferior graft survival (HR 1.379, 95% CI 1.018-1.870; p = 0.038). Furthermore, patients suffering from osteopenia required more perioperative red blood cell units (8 [4-13] vs. 6 [3-10], p = 0.027). No significant differences in perioperative complications were observed between osteopenic and non-osteopenic patients. Conclusion: The presence of osteopenia may represent an easily assessable marker associated with long-term outcome in patients undergoing OLT after brain death donation, thus underlining the predictive significance of body composition in this context. Further research is warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Biliary Drainage and Complex Hepatobiliary Surgery in Biliary Tract Cancers: A Framework for Selective Centralization.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Biliary tract cancers (BTCs) are rare, heterogeneous malignancies that frequently present with biliary obstruction and require complex multidisciplinary care. Decisions regarding biliary drainage, future liver remnant (FLR) optimization, and major hepatobiliary surgery may influence perioperative risk and treatment eligibility. This narrative review evaluates the evidence supporting selective centralization and proposes a network-based framework that considers tumor subtype, procedural complexity, and access to care. Methods: The scope and principal topics were defined during the multidisciplinary COST Training School "Biliary Tract Cancers: Practical Approaches in Challenging Environments", held in Barcelona, Spain, on 20-21 March 2026. Members of the author group conducted topic-specific PubMed/MEDLINE searches within their areas of expertise. Guidelines, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant clinical studies were synthesized narratively. BTC-specific findings were distinguished from evidence derived from mixed populations. No formal risk-of-bias assessment or consensus voting process was undertaken. Results: Preoperative biliary drainage should be selective, with the indication, target, and modality determined by clinical status, biliary anatomy, treatment intent, and planned intervention. FLR assessment should integrate volume and function, particularly in patients with cholestasis or cholangitis. Evidence supporting augmentation strategies varies by technique and population. Observational studies associate higher procedural volumes with favorable outcomes, although patient selection and case-mix differences limit causal interpretation. Tumor-specific pathways distinguish perihilar, intrahepatic, and distal cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer. The proposed network combines expert-center coordination of complex interventions with regional care supported by shared protocols, defined responsibilities, escalation pathways, and outcome monitoring. Conclusions: Selective centralization offers an organizational approach to balancing specialist expertise with timely and equitable access. Prospective multicenter evaluation is needed to assess safety, treatment delays, access to curative therapy, patient-centered outcomes, and resource use before wider clinical or policy adoption.

articles.title: Mid-Term Clinical, Radiographic, and Safety Outcomes After Hemiarthroplasty with the CL TRAUMA Cemented Femoral Stem: A Post-Market Clinical Investigation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cemented femoral stems are a well-established treatment option for femoral neck fractures (FNFs) in elderly patients. This study evaluated mid-term clinical and radiographic outcomes and safety profile in patients undergoing hemiarthroplasty with the CL TRAUMA cemented femoral stem (LimaCorporate) for FNF. Methods: The single-center observational Post-Market Clinical Investigation identified 474 patients who underwent hip arthroplasty between 2017 and 2023. Of these, 54 (11.4%) who were alive, contactable, willing, and physically able to attend were included in the mid-term follow-up (FU) assessment. Perioperative, discharge, and 1-month FU data were collected retrospectively, while mid-term clinical and radiographic FU was performed prospectively after a minimum of 2 years. The primary endpoint was satisfactory status, defined as a Harris Hip Score (HHS) ≥ 80. Secondary endpoints included patient satisfaction assessed using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), radiographic outcomes, and documented serious adverse events (SAEs). Results: The 54 evaluated patients (54/474; 11.4% of the implanted population) included 49 females and 5 males, with a mean age at surgery of 77.1 ± 9.1 years and a mean FU of 4.4 ± 0.8 years. All patients underwent hemiarthroplasty for FNF. Mean HHS was 80.6 ± 16.9, with 33 patients (61.1%) achieving the primary endpoint. Mean VAS satisfaction was 76.4 ± 29.3. At mid-term FU, RLLs were observed in 38.9% of patients, predominantly of limited thickness. Distal stem migration was observed in one case (1.9%), and bone remodeling in three patients (5.6%). Eleven SAEs occurred in 10 patients (18.5%); three events were related and two possibly related to the surgical procedure, whereas none was considered related to the device. No femoral stem revisions were documented among the 54 evaluated patients during the available FU. Conclusions: Among the selected patients who survived and completed mid-term follow-up after bipolar hemiarthroplasty with the CL TRAUMA cemented femoral stem, satisfactory functional status and patient satisfaction were observed, together with generally stable stem-specific radiographic findings. No SAEs were considered related to the femoral stem, and no femoral stem revisions were documented. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and cannot be extrapolated to the entire implanted population.

articles.title: Perioperative and Long-Term Outcomes of Surgery in Patients Aged 80 Years or Older with Esophageal or Esophagogastric Junction Cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: With population aging, determining appropriate surgical indications for patients aged ≥80 years with esophageal or esophagogastric junction cancer has become increasingly important. This study compared perioperative and long-term outcomes between surgically treated patients aged ≥80 years and those aged <80 years.
METHODS: Patients who underwent surgery for esophageal or esophagogastric junction cancer between April 2009 and April 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Propensity score matching was performed using sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, tumor location, histological type, clinical stage, surgical procedure, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. After matching, 40 patients were included in each group. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, overall survival (OS), and disease-specific survival (DSS) were compared.
RESULTS: Operative time, blood loss, and postoperative hospital stay did not differ significantly between the groups. Patients aged ≥80 years had fewer dissected lymph nodes (26.0 vs. 48.5, p = 0.003) and a lower incidence of Clavien-Dindo grade ≥IIIa complications (17.5% vs. 40.0%, p = 0.047). The incidences of pneumonia, recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, and anastomotic leakage did not differ significantly. The 5-year OS was lower in patients aged ≥80 years (32.9% vs. 55.3%, p = 0.006; HR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.24-4.28), whereas 5-year DSS did not differ significantly (55.4% vs. 69.0%, p = 0.122; HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 0.84-4.12).
CONCLUSIONS: Surgery may be feasible in carefully selected patients aged ≥80 years. These findings do not establish a survival advantage over non-surgical treatment. Surgical eligibility should be based on overall condition, oncological factors, and anticipated surgical invasiveness rather than chronological age alone.

articles.title: When "Normal" Hemoglobin May Not Be Enough: Sex-Specific Anemia Thresholds and Outcomes in Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sex-specific anemia criteria classify women with hemoglobin (Hb) 12.0-12.9 g/dL as non-anemic. We assessed whether World Health Organization (WHO) criteria underrecognize red blood cell (RBC) transfusion risk compared with a uniform patient blood management (PBM) threshold of Hb <13.0 g/dL in elective open cardiac valve surgery (CVS). Methods: This nationwide retrospective cohort included adults undergoing elective open CVS in 40 Spanish centers (2016-2024), 32 of which reported preoperative Hb. Hb was modeled continuously and in three strata (<12.0, 12.0-12.9, ≥13.0 g/dL). The primary outcome was RBC transfusion; secondary outcomes were postoperative complications, length of stay, and in-hospital mortality within 30 days. Mixed-effects models adjusted for age, comorbidity burden, surgical complexity, valve position, year of surgery, and center. Results: Among 29,757 eligible patients, 20,017 had available Hb measurements; 9247 (46.2%) were women, including 2333 (25.2%) with Hb 12.0-12.9 g/dL. In this stratum, 68.0% of women and 52.7% of men received RBC transfusions. The adjusted between-sex probability difference was 15.1 percentage points (95% CI, 11.4-18.9; adjusted odds ratio, 1.85; 95% CI, 1.59-2.16). The categorical sex × Hb interaction was significant (p < 0.001), whereas the continuous interaction was not (p = 0.486). Sex did not significantly modify the Hb associations with complications or in-hospital mortality within 30 days. Conclusions: Women with Hb 12.0-12.9 g/dL had substantial transfusion risk despite being classified as non-anemic by the WHO criteria. Hb <13.0 g/dL may be a pragmatic sex-inclusive trigger for perioperative risk recognition and etiologic evaluation, not a proven therapeutic target.

articles.title: Beyond Neuromonitoring: Spinal Cord Perfusion, Autonomic Dysregulation, and Neurological Risk During Complex Spinal Deformity Correction.
articles.abstract: Background: Advances in spinal deformity surgery have expanded treatment options for pediatric and adolescent patients, but neurological complications remain among the most serious adverse events. Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) enables early detection of spinal cord dysfunction, while preservation of adequate spinal cord perfusion remains an important component of perioperative neurological protection. Objective: This narrative review examines current evidence regarding neurological protection during complex spinal deformity surgery, with emphasis on spinal cord perfusion, IONM interpretation, hemodynamic management, and the potential interaction between mechanical and autonomic factors. An illustrative case of recurrent IONM deterioration associated with profound hemodynamic instability is included. Methods: A narrative review of contemporary literature was conducted, focusing on spinal cord perfusion, mechanisms of neurological injury, IONM, perioperative blood pressure management, corrective strategies, and postoperative neurological surveillance. Pediatric deformity studies were prioritized, while adult and mixed-population studies were included when relevant mechanistic or technical information was provided. The clinical case was analyzed separately from the literature synthesis. Results: Current evidence supports maintaining adequate systemic perfusion and promptly evaluating reversible physiological and mechanical contributors when IONM deterioration occurs. Blood pressure augmentation may restore signals in a subset of patients, but IONM changes cannot be assumed to be purely ischemic, and improved perfusion may not overcome persistent mechanical compromise. In the illustrative case, recurrent IONM signal loss occurred during corrective maneuvers and was associated with profound hypotension and bradycardia during a subsequent correction attempt. Motor and somatosensory evoked potentials were comparable to baseline by the end of surgery after release of corrective forces, hemodynamic management, and vasopressor support; they had recovered to 50% of baseline immediately before correction was resumed. Because these interventions were performed concurrently, the relative contribution of mechanical release, improved systemic perfusion, and possible autonomic mechanisms could not be determined. Motor and sensory function remained intact postoperatively, although she later reported sweating and temperature asymmetry during follow-up. Conclusions: Neurological protection during complex spinal deformity correction requires an integrated perioperative approach combining individualized surgical strategy, multimodal IONM, hemodynamic optimization, and postoperative surveillance. When IONM deterioration occurs, mechanical, hemodynamic, anesthetic, and technical causes should be assessed concurrently. The presented case supports consideration of a possible autonomic contribution to severe intraoperative hemodynamic instability, but does not establish a specific autonomic syndrome or causal pathway.

articles.title: Gram-Negative Infections in Orthopedic Surgery: Current Challenges for Anesthesiologists and Intensive Care Physicians-A SANRA Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Background: Gram-negative bacterial infections represent an increasingly relevant challenge in orthopedic surgery, particularly in complex patients exposed to major trauma, revision procedures, prolonged hospitalization, previous antimicrobial therapy, and intensive care. Although Gram-positive organisms remain predominant in prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) and fracture-related infections (FRIs), the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative pathogens has important implications for perioperative management, antimicrobial prophylaxis, and treatment. Objective: This narrative review examines the epidemiology, pathogenesis, antimicrobial resistance, and management of Gram-negative orthopedic infections, with particular emphasis on issues relevant to anesthesiologists and intensive care physicians. Methods: A structured narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to July 2026, according to the principles of the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). Original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, consensus statements, and relevant narrative reviews addressing Gram-negative infections in orthopedic surgery were considered. Results: Gram-negative pathogens account for a minority of orthopedic infections but become increasingly relevant in complex PJIs, FRIs, open fractures, revision surgery, and patients with substantial healthcare exposure. Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii are among the principal pathogens involved. Their clinical relevance is amplified by biofilm formation and increasingly complex antimicrobial resistance mechanisms. Perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis should remain individualized in patients colonized or previously infected with MDR Gram-negative organisms, avoiding indiscriminate broad-spectrum prophylaxis. Once infection is established, management requires adequate microbiological sampling, surgical source control, and susceptibility-guided antimicrobial therapy. New β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations and cefiderocol have expanded therapeutic options against resistant Gram-negative pathogens; however, evidence specifically supporting cefiderocol for bone and joint infections remains limited. Conclusions: Gram-negative orthopedic infections represent an emerging challenge at the intersection of orthopedic surgery, infectious diseases, anesthesiology, and critical care. Early recognition of high-risk patients, individualized perioperative strategies, effective source control, resistance-guided antimicrobial therapy, and multidisciplinary management are essential.

articles.title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) in Cardiac Surgery: From Evidence to Precision Perioperative Medicine.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery is increasingly performed in older, frailer patients with multimorbidity, making postoperative recovery dependent not only on technical success but also on the quality of perioperative care. Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) programs address this challenge through coordinated preoperative optimization, attenuation of surgical stress, organ protection, opioid-sparing analgesia, early mobilization, and structured discharge. This narrative review critically appraises ERAS in cardiac surgery and organizes the evidence across the perioperative pathway. Available studies associate complete ERAS programs with modest reductions in intensive care and hospital length of stay and possible reductions in overall complications, but evidence certainty is limited by heterogeneous bundles, single-center designs, and predominance of observational studies. Component-level evidence is strongest or clinically most relevant for frailty assessment, Patient Blood Management, multimodal analgesia, oxygen delivery-guided perfusion, delirium prevention, and early mobilization, although universal thresholds and isolated technologies should be avoided. Successful implementation depends on multidisciplinary governance, explicit responsibilities, adherence measurement, audit, and patient-centered outcomes. Future development should retain a standardized core while allowing transparent adaptation to baseline risk and observed response. Precision perioperative approaches remain hypothesis-generating and require external validation, clinical impact evaluation, assessment of equity, and demonstration of cost-effectiveness before routine adoption.

articles.title: Development of a Complex Intervention for Perinatal Bladder Management Among Pregnant Women Based on the Medical Research Council Framework: A Development Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Postpartum urinary retention (PUR) is a common childbirth complication that may lead to bladder dysfunction and adverse maternal outcomes if not promptly identified and managed. Although existing guidelines address aspects of perinatal bladder care, a standardized, context-specific intervention is still lacking. This study aimed to develop a comprehensive perinatal bladder management intervention for pregnant women using the Medical Research Council (MRC) framework for complex interventions.
METHODS: This intervention development study was conducted in accordance with the development phase of the updated MRC framework. A multidisciplinary group was established, including experts in obstetrics, anesthesia, midwifery, nursing management, and evidence-based practice. The intervention was informed by a review of the physiological mechanisms underlying postpartum voiding dysfunction and a qualitative study guided by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), involving 16 women after vaginal delivery and 18 healthcare professionals. Evidence was identified and appraised from clinical guidelines, evidence summaries, systematic reviews, expert consensus statements, and randomized controlled trials. A two-round Delphi consultation with 18 experts was conducted to refine and validate the intervention framework.
RESULTS: Twelve evidence sources were included: four guidelines, three evidence summaries, three expert consensus documents, one systematic review, and one randomized controlled trial. Thirty-four evidence-based recommendations were synthesized across four domains: antenatal bladder management, intrapartum bladder management, postpartum bladder management, and management of urinary retention. Health education was integrated as a cross-cutting theme. After two Delphi rounds, the final intervention comprised four primary domains and 29 components. Both Delphi rounds achieved 100% response rates, with high expert authority coefficients (Cr = 0.956 and 0.972).
CONCLUSIONS: Using the MRC framework, this study developed a theory-informed and evidence-based perinatal bladder management intervention integrating evidence synthesis, clinical expertise, and stakeholder perspectives. The intervention provides a structured basis for future feasibility, implementation, and effectiveness evaluations. However, its clinical effectiveness, safety, feasibility, and external validity remain to be established.

articles.title: Thoracic and Abdominal Complications After Posterior Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: Evidence and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Background: Posterior spinal fusion (PSF) is an established treatment for progressive adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) requiring surgery. Thoracic and abdominal complications range from transient postoperative findings to uncommon emergencies. This narrative review examines their reported frequency, recognition, prevention, and management. Methods: Literature published between January 2000 and June 2026 was reviewed using PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar, supplemented by reference-list screening. AIS-specific evidence was prioritized. Reports involving other deformities or surgical approaches and general management guidelines were used as explicitly identified contextual evidence. No pooled incidence estimates were calculated. Results: Reported frequencies depended strongly on outcome definitions, imaging protocols, surgical approach, and follow-up. Two retrospective AIS studies detected pleural effusion in 71.0% and 76.3% of patients on computed tomography approximately one week after PSF; in the latter study, all effusions were asymptomatic and required no treatment. These findings should not be equated with clinically significant pulmonary complications. Postoperative ileus was reported in 13.2% of one 318-patient AIS cohort aged 10-20 years, whereas superior mesenteric artery syndrome, chylothorax, hemothorax, and implant-related vascular injury were supported largely by small series or case reports. Enhanced recovery pathways were consistently associated with shorter hospitalization, but evidence that they prevent individual rare complications was limited. Accurate instrumentation, appropriate blood conservation, individualized nutritional assessment, opioid-sparing analgesia, and symptom-directed investigation support perioperative care. Conclusions: Thoracic and abdominal complications after PSF for AIS require separate interpretation of radiographic findings, clinically diagnosed events, and events requiring intervention. Persistent vomiting, progressive abdominal distension, respiratory deterioration, unexplained anemia, or hemodynamic instability warrant prompt reassessment. Management should follow the suspected diagnosis, patient physiology, and relevant pediatric or multidisciplinary guidance.

articles.title: Nutrition and Frailty in the Older Adult: A Case-Based Approach to Assessment, Diagnosis, Intervention, Monitoring, and Evaluation in Preoperative Care.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Frailty is a multidimensional syndrome characterized by reduced physiologic reserve and increased vulnerability to adverse outcomes, including postoperative complications, functional decline, and mortality. Malnutrition frequently coexists with frailty and contributes to muscle loss, impaired function, and decreased resilience. This narrative review explores the relationship between frailty and malnutrition and highlights practical approaches to assessment and management in older adults undergoing surgery. Methods: A narrative review of the current literature on frailty, malnutrition, comprehensive geriatric assessment, and prehabilitation was conducted. A fictional case study of Mrs. Jones, a 71-year-old woman undergoing evaluation for colon cancer surgery, was used to illustrate evidence-based assessment and management strategies. Results: Frailty and malnutrition interact in a reciprocal cycle that increases surgical risk and worsens health outcomes. Early screening can identify modifiable deficits, including weight loss, inadequate nutritional intake, impaired physical performance, functional limitations, and social barriers. Comprehensive geriatric assessment facilitates evaluation of medical, nutritional, functional, cognitive, and psychosocial factors. Evidence supports multimodal prehabilitation that combines individualized nutrition interventions, adequate protein and energy intake, exercise, medication optimization, oral-health management, and social support to improve surgical readiness and recovery. Conclusions: Routine screening for frailty and malnutrition, followed by comprehensive geriatric assessment and interdisciplinary management, can help identify reversible risk factors and guide individualized care. Integrating nutrition-focused interventions within prehabilitation programs may improve perioperative outcomes while supporting the preservation of strength, function, independence, and quality of life in older adults.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Safety of Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Fine-Needle Biopsy (EUS-FNB) Under Conscious Sedation for Small Solid Pancreatic Lesions (<20 mm): A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The diagnostic evaluation of small (<20 mm) solid pancreatic lesions (SPLs) remains technically challenging, and most available EUS-FNB data derive from cohorts performed under deep sedation or heterogeneous sedation protocols. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance, feasibility, and safety of endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) performed under standard conscious sedation in consecutive eligible patients with SPLs < 20 mm. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database including 114 patients with SPLs < 20 mm who underwent EUS-FNB under conscious sedation between January 2021 and December 2024. Procedural characteristics, histologic adequacy, diagnostic accuracy, repeated procedures, and adverse events were collected. Index diagnostic accuracy was calculated on completed index procedures; procedures aborted because of intolerance were analyzed as sedation failures and included in the safety and cumulative analyses. Variables associated with tissue core adequacy were assessed in an exploratory univariate analysis. Results: The mean target lesion size was 14.2 ± 4.3 mm, and 31 lesions (27.2%) were sub-centimetric (<10 mm). A 22-gauge needle was used in 98.2% of cases, a Franseen-tip needle in 80.4%, and at least two passes were performed in 87.5%. Among the 112 completed index procedures, histologic adequacy was 93.8% (105/112, 95% CI 87.7-96.9) and diagnostic accuracy was 91.1% (102/112; 95% CI 84.3-95.1), increasing to a cumulative accuracy of 97.4% (111/114) after targeted repeat procedures. Index accuracy was 93.5% (29/31) for lesions < 10 mm and 90.1% (73/81) for lesions of 10-19 mm (p = 0.724). Counting the three repeat procedures performed with anesthesiology support as failures of the conscious sedation pathway, cumulative accuracy under conscious sedation alone was 94.7% (108/114). Sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV of the index EUS-FNB for malignancy were 92.5%, 100%, 100% and 73.1%, respectively. No severe intraprocedural adverse events occurred; two index procedures (1.8%) were aborted because of intolerance under conscious sedation and required anesthesiology support, and two mild, self-limiting cases of acute pancreatitis (1.8%) occurred after the procedure. In the exploratory analysis, performing at least two needle passes was the only variable associated with sample adequacy (p = 0.041), although this finding was based on only seven inadequate samples. Conclusions: EUS-FNB under conscious sedation appears feasible, with high diagnostic yield and a low rate of adverse events, in consecutive eligible patients with small SPLs, including sub-centimetric targets. These findings support a pragmatic real-life workflow based on careful patient selection, adequate monitoring, modern FNB needles, macroscopic core assessment, and consideration of at least two passes whenever feasible (a hypothesis-generating finding), with ROSE or anesthesiologist support reserved for selected unresolved or poorly tolerated cases. Prospective comparative studies are needed before concluding equivalence with propofol-based deep sedation or systematic anesthesiologist-directed care.

articles.title: Altered Sensory and Affective Inflammatory Pain Responding in the VPA Model of Autism Is Associated With Reduced IL1β-NLRP3 Expression in the ACC in Males but Not Females.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal valproic acid (VPA) exposure, a well-validated preclinical model of autism, is associated with altered sensory responding to noxious heat and mechanical stimuli. However, whether sensory and affective responding to inflammatory noxious stimuli are altered, and whether effects are sex-specific is unknown. Neuroimmune crosstalk in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) modulates sensory and affective dimensions of pain and may contribute to altered pain in autism.
METHODS: This study examined acute and chronic inflammatory pain responding following intraplantar formalin or complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) in male and female VPA-exposed rats, and associated gene changes in the ACC.
RESULTS: VPA-exposed male and female rats exhibited heat and mechanical hyposensitivity, with no change in responses to innocuous cold. Nociceptive responding in the formalin test was unaltered; however, following CFA administration, VPA-exposed rats displayed higher mechanical, but not cold, withdrawal thresholds compared with saline counterparts. VPA-exposed rats showed higher paw withdrawal latencies in the Hargreaves' test following CFA, with effects influenced by sex and time. VPA-exposed males exhibited reduced anxiety-like behavior in the open field test following CFA and reduced affective/aversive pain behavior in the PEAP test prior to and following CFA administration, effects not observed in females. In male VPA-exposed rats, CFA-induced mechanical hypersensitivity and aversive-like behavior were associated with reduced Il1b and Nlrp3 expression in the ACC.
CONCLUSION: These data demonstrate that prenatal VPA exposure alters nociceptive and chronic inflammatory pain responding and suggest that sex-specific neuroimmune alterations in the ACC may play a central role in these effects.
SIGNIFICANCE: Pain in autism is poorly understood and challenging to manage. This study shows sex-dependent changes in chronic inflammatory pain responding and associated alterations in neuroimmune gene expression in the ACC in an autism-relevant preclinical model. These findings highlight neuroimmune signalling as a potential contributor to atypical pain processing in autism and an important avenue for future translational pain research.

articles.title: Clinical and Inflammatory Outcomes Following Multimodal Anesthesia and On-Table Extubation in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Cardiac Surgery with (Partial) Sternotomy: A Secondary Analysis of RERACS Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) is a multimodal approach aiming for optimized postoperative outcomes. Regarding demographic change and the epidemiology of heart diseases, ERACS concepts with on-table extubation (OTE) might be a resource-aware solution needed to ensure adequate perioperative surgical care to an aging society. We investigated clinical outcomes and inflammatory effects of ERACS with multimodal anesthesia and OTE in patients >65 years undergoing elective cardiac surgery. Methods: This study is a secondary analysis of the RERACS study (Regensburg Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery). Sixty-four elderly RERACS patients were compared with a retrospective control group (age >65 years, n = 67) undergoing elective cardiac surgery via (partial) sternotomy. The RERACS concept consisted of shortened fasting periods, breathing training, opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia, OTE, patient-reported outcome measures and additional exploratory evaluation of Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TNF-alpha in this secondary analysis. The control group received standard care with extubation in the intensive care unit (ICU). Results: Unadjusted baseline analysis showed no significant differences between the two groups. Length of stay in ICU (ICU-LOS) and postoperative catecholamine weaning were significantly shorter in the RERACS group. RERACS patients showed significantly lower C-reactive-protein levels 24 h after surgery than control patients. In the RERACS group, postoperative low interleukin-6 levels were associated with postoperative complications like delirium or infection, but not with atrial fibrillation. Patient-reported outcome measures in the RERACS group showed high patient satisfaction, good pain compensation and low levels of postoperative nausea and vomiting but remarkable levels of sore throat/hoarseness, despite shorter ventilation time. Conclusions: Data support that ERACS with OTE is feasible in selected elderly patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery via (partial) sternotomy. No apparent increase in required postoperative respiratory support occurred compared to patients with conservative, prolonged mechanical ventilation. The RERACS program with multimodal anesthesia and OTE was associated with shorter ICU-LOS, earlier weaning from vasoactive support, and high patient satisfaction. Further studies are needed to evaluate immunomodulatory effects of ERACS measures and investigate the role of IL-6 levels as a marker for immunoparalysis in elderly cardiosurgical patients.

articles.title: An Integrated ERAS-PBM Pathway for Cardiac Surgery: Insights and Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Anemia is a common condition in cardiac surgery and is strongly associated with adverse outcomes, including higher transfusion requirements, increased morbidity, and prolonged hospital stay. Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) and Patient Blood Management (PBM) are both multimodal strategies designed to improve perioperative care. This study evaluates the impact of integrating ERAS and PBM with preoperative anemia management into a single standardized pathway in elective cardiac surgery. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, single-center before-after study at Lausanne University Hospital, comparing a pre-ERAS cohort (2019) with a prospective cohort managed under the ERAS-PBM pathway (May 2023-November 2024). The ERAS-PBM pathway included systematic preoperative anemia screening and treatment, reinforcement of adherence to existing restrictive transfusion thresholds, optimized blood conservation techniques, and standardized perioperative care bundles coordinated by a dedicated ERAS nurse. The primary outcome was the rate of red blood cell (RBC) transfusions during hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included overall transfusion rates, hemoglobin levels, complications, and length of stay. Results: A total of 391 patients were included (ERAS, n = 229; pre-ERAS, n = 162). RBC transfusion rates were significantly lower in the ERAS group (23.6% vs. 38.9%, p = 0.0012), with a reduction in the number of units per patient (p = 0.0005). Hemoglobin at admission was higher in the ERAS cohort (139.5 vs. 134 g/L, p = 0.0009). Overall complication rates decreased (46.3% vs. 66.7%, p < 0.0001), including major adverse cardiovascular events and pulmonary complications. Hospital stay was shorter (9 vs. 12 days, p < 0.0001), as was mechanical ventilation time (0 vs. 2.1 h, p < 0.0001). Anemic patients at admission were more transfused (39.3% vs. 18.6%, p = 0.002). Within the ERAS group, RBC transfusion was associated with higher rates of selected postoperative complications and longer ICU and hospital stays. In an exploratory multivariable logistic regression analysis, ERAS-PBM implementation was associated with lower odds of RBC transfusion during hospitalization (adjusted OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.36-0.98; p = 0.041). Conclusions: The integration of ERAS and PBM into a single multimodal pathway was associated with significant reductions in transfusion rates, complications, and length of stay in elective cardiac surgery. Anemia at admission and perioperative transfusion were associated with worse outcomes, emphasizing the importance of anemia management. Larger, multicenter prospective studies are warranted to confirm these results and to optimize anemia correction strategies, including earlier treatment of iron deficiency and outpatient erythropoietin use.

articles.title: Ageing and anaesthetic sensitivity: the role of inflammaging in the vulnerable surgical brain.
articles.abstract: Ageing surgical patients demonstrate increased vulnerability to anaesthetic agents, including heightened sensitivity, reduced drug requirements, and delayed emergence, and they are also at increased risk of postoperative complications such as delirium and haemodynamic instability. These phenomena are only partially understood and have traditionally been attributed to the global functional decline associated with ageing. However, emerging preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that inflammaging and related neuroimmune alterations, including peripheral macrophage activation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and immune-to-brain signalling, may also modulate anaesthetic response. This narrative review examines current evidence on anaesthetic sensitivity in older adults, the role of macrophage phenotypes in ageing, and the mechanisms by which neuroinflammation may alter neuronal excitability, synaptic function, and electroencephalographic markers of anaesthetic depth. It also reviews methodological approaches ranging from rodent models to biomarkers such as the cerebrospinal fluid to plasma albumin ratio and EEG-derived indices. Overall, the available literature supports a biologically plausible link between age-related immune dysregulation and altered anaesthetic sensitivity, while also suggesting that these same pathways may contribute to broader perioperative brain vulnerability, including postoperative delirium. Direct clinical evidence remains limited, however, and many mechanistic links continue to rely on extrapolation from preclinical models. Further integrative perioperative studies combining immunological profiling, neurophysiological monitoring, and pharmacodynamic modelling are needed to clarify how neuroimmune ageing influences anaesthetic brain sensitivity in older adults.

articles.title: Nonischemic and normothermic beating cardiac xenotransplantation.
articles.abstract: Cardiac xenotransplantation-the transplantation of a heart from one species to another- offers a clinically viable solution to the organ shortage problem. Despite significant advances in genetic engineering technologies and new immunosuppressive medications such as co-stimulatory blockade, bringing cardiac xenotransplantation to the clinic still has several challenges. Perioperative cardiac xenograft dysfunction is a major limitation to long-term xenograft survival and is attributed to the ischemia-reperfusion damage associated with the procurement and transplant of the porcine heart. This dysfunction can be reduced by utilizing commercial ex vivo perfusion devices which limit the cold ischemia time. Unfortunately, these devices still require an obligatory ischemic period during the initial arrest with cardioplegia and subsequent explanting of the organ, and then again during the implantation of the heart. These commercial devices also do not support smaller pediatric sized hearts, reducing the pool of recipients eligible for xenografts. We sought to establish a novel method of explanting and orthotopically implanting beating donor hearts from genetically modified pigs without any ischemia, while maintaining normothermic perfusion in a pig-to-nonhuman primate model. Eliminating cold and warm ischemia has never previously been achieved in cardiac xenotransplantation and has important implications for bringing it to the clinic, as well as broader translatability in allotransplantation. We performed a proof-of-concept experiment utilizing our novel technique in a non-survival model and then performed a successful experiment with nearly 8 weeks of survival of a single GGTA1 knockout pig heart. Our initial data suggest that utilization of a normothermic coronary perfusion circuit in cardiac xenotransplantation is feasible and safe and may be a plausible method towards achieving survival.

articles.title: Outcomes After Bilateral Native Nephrectomy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Contemporary Single-Centre NHS Cohort Study (2018-2024).
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Bilateral native nephrectomy (BNN) is undertaken selectively in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) to relieve symptoms or to create iliac fossa space for transplantation. Contemporary UK National Health Service outcome data are scarce. We describe indications, morbidity and mortality after open BNN at a UK tertiary transplant centre. Methods: This is a retrospective descriptive cohort study of 34 consecutive adults with ADPKD undergoing open BNN between August 2018 and September 2024, reported per STROBE, without a comparator group. Pre-specified primary outcomes were length of stay (LoS) and Clavien-Dindo (CD) ≥III complications. Exploratory analyses used regression on log(LoS), with a sensitivity analysis excluding one outlier, and Firth-penalised logistic regression. Results: Median age was 55 years (IQR 51-62); 29 patients (85.3%) were dialysis-dependent, and 5 (14.7%) had a functioning allograft. No procedure was concurrent with transplantation. The commonest indication was insufficient space for a kidney graft (21/34, 61.8%). Median LoS was 8 days (IQR 7-10). CD≥III complications occurred in 5/34 (14.7%; 95% CI 6.4-30.1%) and transfusion in 6/34 (17.6%); grade I-II complications were not systematically recorded. There were no in-hospital, 30-day or 90-day deaths. Over a median potential follow-up of 53 months, 15/34 (44.1%) underwent transplantation. Transfusion was associated with longer LoS (β = 0.58; p = 0.035), but not after excluding one outlier (p = 0.348), and was not significantly associated with CD≥III (OR 4.05; 95% CI 0.54-28.4). No invasive malignancy was found in 29 histopathology reports. Conclusions: In this small single-centre series, open BNN was performed mainly to enable transplantation, with no early mortality and a 14.7% CD≥III rate. These descriptive baseline data cannot establish benefit relative to unilateral or no nephrectomy.

articles.title: Analysis of causative factors and preventive strategies for traumatic orthopedic medical malpractice in Shanghai: a high-responsibility perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical malpractice is recognized as the most severe category of adverse medical events, characterized by illegality, negligent conduct, and resultant harm. Cases classified as high-responsibility-level malpractice impose substantial impacts on healthcare institutions and medical personnel. This study aims to identify negligence-related determinants contributing to such cases and to explore targeted preventive strategies designed to reduce the occurrence of high-responsibility-level medical malpractice.
METHODS: A total of 125 cases of traumatic orthopedic medical malpractice were retrieved from the Office of Medical Malpractice Handling under the Shanghai Municipal Health Commission. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 26.0. Descriptive data were presented as counts, frequencies, and percentages. Intergroup differences in negligence-related factors between high- and low-responsibility-level categories were evaluated using chi-square tests. Additionally, binary stepwise logistic regression analysis was performed to determine independent associations between specific negligence factors and high responsibility levels.
RESULTS: Traumatic orthopedic medical malpractice cases in Shanghai demonstrated several distinct characteristics, including a relatively low mortality rate (4.00%), a notably high disability rate (74.4%), a greater occurrence in secondary hospitals (60.00%), and increased involvement of attending physicians and associate chief physicians (76.80%). High-responsibility-level cases constituted 45.60% of all included cases. Chi-square analysis indicated that inappropriate surgical procedures and violations of clinical practice standards were significantly more prevalent in the high-responsibility-level group compared with the low-responsibility-level group (P < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis further revealed that inappropriate surgical procedures [odds ratio (OR) = 6.078], violations of clinical practice standards (OR=5.001), and missed or misdiagnoses (OR=2.872) were independently associated with elevated responsibility levels. Stratified regression analysis further indicated that violations of clinical practice standards represented the dominant negligence factor in secondary hospitals (OR=2.94), whereas inappropriate surgical procedures constituted the primary determinant in tertiary hospitals (OR=7.20).
CONCLUSIONS: Several preventive measures are recommended, including strengthening perioperative management, ensuring strict compliance with clinical diagnostic, therapeutic, and nursing protocols, standardizing imaging examinations and comprehensive physical assessments to reduce missed and misdiagnoses, enhancing physician-patient communication, standardizing medical record documentation, and reinforcing early postoperative rehabilitation strategies.

articles.title: Integrating quantitative biometrics and automated risk stratification for ophthalmic surgical triage.
articles.abstract: Ophthalmology generates extensive quantitative data from ocular biometry and imaging, yet these device-derived measurements are often separated from medical, social, and utilization data in the electronic health record (EHR). No validated ophthalmic tool currently integrates these streams for real-time, patient-specific perioperative decision support. This mini-review examines how automated EHR-based risk stratification and quantitative ocular biometrics could support perioperative decision-making. Across surgical specialties, cancellation models using demographic, comorbidity, socioeconomic, and appointment-related variables have achieved development areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.75-0.92 with a validation range of 0.70-0.74. When the bundle is paired with targeted care pathways, reduced same-day cancellations have been observed, although bundle designs prevent quantifying the independent contribution of the model. In cataract surgery, Epic's Health Composite Score independently predicts same-day cancellation but provides only limited discrimination, and does not predict operative or postoperative outcomes, which remain more closely associated with ocular complexity and surgeon-related factors. Cataract and glaucoma literature identifies additional candidate predictors of technical complexity, surgical outcomes, and access, including pupil and lens characteristics, axial length, anterior chamber anatomy, prior ocular surgery, angle dimensions, conjunctival imaging, frailty, and social vulnerability. We propose an EHR-integrated framework with endpoint- and procedure-specific models for surgical readiness, technical complexity, and adverse outcomes. Each output should be linked to a defined response, such as patient navigation, anesthesia review, case assignment, operative setting, equipment planning, or intensified postoperative follow-up. Prospective multicenter development should assess whether model-guided interventions improve access, efficiency, and outcomes.

articles.title: Molecular and Translational Anti-Inflammatory Strategies After Abdominal and Liver Surgery: From Immunonutrition to Cell-Based Therapies.
articles.abstract: Postoperative inflammation influences recovery after abdominal and liver surgery. This narrative review critically synthesizes clinical and translational evidence on inflammation-modulating strategies using a structured search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library for publications from 2015 to 2025. Case reports, pediatric studies, and publications lacking clinical or translational relevance were excluded. Immunonutrition and early enteral nutrition are the most established approaches, with benefits for postoperative recovery and infectious complications. Perioperative corticosteroids in liver resection and short-course antibiotics following adequate source control offer procedure- and indication-specific benefits. Emerging interventions, including microbiota modulation, N-acetylcysteine, activation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/heme oxygenase-1 signaling, and cell-based therapies, show biological promise but lack sufficient high-quality clinical evidence for routine implementation. Established strategies should be integrated into Enhanced Recovery After Surgery pathways according to patient risk and surgical context. Personalized management requires prospective validation of emerging therapies and candidate biomarkers, including interleukin-6, C-reactive protein, and heme oxygenase-1, with standardized assays and sampling schedules.

articles.title: Neuroprognostication in unconscious patients after cardiac arrest: considering the time course of prognostic markers.
articles.abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) is a major determinant of outcome after cardiac arrest (CA) and accounts for approximately two-thirds of deaths in patients who remain comatose after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), frequently following withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy (WLST) based on an anticipated poor neurological prognosis. Accurate neuroprognostication is therefore crucial to identify patients with potential for neurological recovery while avoiding premature pessimistic predictions. Current guidelines recommend a multimodal approach integrating clinical examination, electrophysiology, biomarkers, and neuroimaging. However, neuroprognostication is inherently time-dependent: HIBI is a dynamic process, and the prognostic value of individual markers evolves substantially during the hours and days following CA. Some markers may provide relevant prognostic information early after ROSC, whereas others achieve optimal accuracy only after 24-72 h or later, as brain injury evolves and confounding factors progressively resolve. Thus, both the selection of prognostic markers and the timing of their assessment are critical to optimize prognostic accuracy. This review summarizes the temporal evolution of the prognostic performance of clinical examination, electroencephalography, somatosensory evoked potentials, biomarkers of brain injury, and neuroimaging after CA, and discusses how their integration according to optimal assessment windows may improve multimodal neuroprognostication and reduce prognostic uncertainty.

articles.title: Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Endometrial Cancer: Experience from a Tertiary Referral Center in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Background: Sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping has become an established alternative to systematic lymphadenectomy for surgical staging in endometrial cancer. This study evaluated SLN mapping rates, anatomical distribution, factors associated with mapping failure, and perioperative outcomes in patients with early-stage endometrial cancer. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included patients with early-stage endometrial cancer who underwent SLN mapping during minimally invasive surgical staging between September 2022 and January 2025. Overall and bilateral SLN detection rates were calculated. Anatomical distribution of SLNs, factors associated with mapping failure (including a hemipelvis-level generalized estimating equation [GEE] analysis), and perioperative outcomes according to surgical approach were analyzed. Results: A total of 165 patients were included. The overall SLN detection rate was 96.4%, and bilateral mapping was achieved in 125 patients (75.8%). A total of 584 SLNs were removed, most commonly from the iliac basin. In the hemipelvis-level GEE analysis (330 hemipelves, 46 failures), ICG use (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.50, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-18.83) and, in a sensitivity model, conventional laparoscopy compared with robotic surgery (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.14-4.69) were associated with higher odds of mapping failure, whereas age and BMI were not. Operative time and intraoperative complication rates were comparable among laparoscopic, robotic-assisted, and vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) procedures. Postoperative complication rates and length of hospital stay differed significantly across surgical approaches (both p = 0.002); post hoc pairwise comparison of complication rates showed that the difference was driven mainly by conventional laparoscopy compared with robotic-assisted surgery, whereas the small vNOTES group (n = 8) did not differ significantly from either approach and does not permit conclusions on its comparative safety. Conclusions: SLN mapping demonstrated high overall detection rates and acceptable bilateral mapping success in early-stage endometrial cancer. These findings support the feasibility of SLN mapping as a minimally invasive staging strategy in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Five Multimodal AI Configurations Versus Anaesthesiologists for Pecto-Intercostal Block Classification in an Archived-Image Reader Study of a Prospective CABG Cohort.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We compared five general-purpose multimodal AI configurations with anaesthesiologists classifying sonographic pecto-intercostal fascial plane block spread. Methods: This archived-image reader study used a prospective cohort of 120 ASA III adults undergoing isolated coronary artery bypass grafting at one centre. In June 2026, five free AI configurations and three experts classified identical sets of 8-10 left-sided frames. Direct binary comparisons used each expert's labels in 115 block recipients; five no-block controls were separate. The senior expert reviewed expert labels before setting the final reference, precluding independent expert-AI accuracy comparison. Reference-conditioned balanced accuracy was defined as mean sensitivity and specificity. Results: Direct balanced agreement was 42.3-53.9% for four configurations and 55.4-64.9% for Kimi K2.6. AI asserted spread in 17/25 no-block classifications; all 20 human classifications indicated absence. Final-reference balanced accuracy was 76.9-91.9% for experts and 44.6-66.9% for AI, conditional on the expert-informed reference. Pain analyses were exploratory. Conclusions: Direct comparisons establish neither anatomical accuracy nor independent expert superiority. Limitations include one centre, operator and ultrasound system; selected frames; free access; no raw AI outputs, reproducible a priori power calculation or non-recruitment-day eligibility log.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Two-Point Transversus Abdominis Plane in Adult Horses: An Experimental Study Assessing Wall Sensitivity.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane blocks may provide somatic analgesia for equine abdominal procedures, but evidence in adult horses remains limited. This prospective, blinded, randomized, paired study evaluated the feasibility, sensory effects, and motor effects of a two-point transversus abdominis plane block in eight healthy, standing, unsedated mares. Each horse received lidocaine 2% (2 mg/kg in 0.1 mL/kg per injection site) on one side and saline on the contralateral side. Responses to standardized mechanical stimulation were assessed at 21 sensory evaluation points per side for 300 min. The block was completed successfully in all horses without visible discomfort or procedural complications. No desensitization occurred on saline-treated sides. Following lidocaine administration, sensory blockade began at a median of 10 min, peaked at 30 min, and lasted a median of 258 (233-260) minutes. Desensitization was significantly greater at the stifle and intermediate horizontal levels than at the coxal tuberosity level. Transient motor impairment occurred in seven of eight horses and was severe in two. The technique produced multi-metameric desensitization, predominantly in the ventrocaudal flank, but limited dorsal coverage and frequent motor impairment may restrict its clinical application. Further dose optimization and clinical safety and efficacy studies are warranted.

articles.title: Outcomes of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in critically ill patients with sickle cell disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) may be considered as rescue therapy in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD) presenting with life-threatening cardiorespiratory failure, particularly acute chest syndrome (ACS). However, outcomes of ECMO in this population remain poorly defined, especially in adult populations. We aimed to synthesize available evidence on mortality and complications associated with ECMO use in adult and pediatric populations with SCD.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting ECMO use in patients with confirmed SCD. MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from January 2000 to January 2025. Risk of bias for included studies was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions was performed to estimate pooled mortality. Exploratory study-level meta-regression was used to examine associations between mortality and prespecified moderators, including age group, ECMO modality, and ACS as the indication for ECMO.
RESULTS: Seven retrospective studies including 252 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled mortality estimate was 64.5% (95% CI, 39.3-86.0%), with heterogeneity across studies (I² = 80%). Mortality estimates appeared numerically higher in studies including predominantly adult populations, greater use of veno-arterial ECMO, and a higher proportion of patients with ACS at cannulation. Exploratory meta-regression suggested trends toward higher predicted mortality with increasing proportions of adult patients and ACS, and lower mortality with higher proportions of veno-venous ECMO. Reporting of ECMO-related complications was inconsistent, and hemolysis was systematically assessed in only one study.
DISCUSSION: ECMO use in patients with SCD is associated with high mortality, particularly in severe clinical contexts such as ACS. Substantial heterogeneity and methodological limitations preclude firm conclusions. These findings underscore the need for prospective, disease-specific registries to better define patient selection and management strategies.'

articles.title: Postoperative Delirium Across the Perioperative Pathway: A Structured Narrative Review of Clinical Maturity and Implementation Priorities.
articles.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a highly prevalent but frequently underrecognized complication that disproportionately affects frail and older surgical patients. This structured narrative review aims to synthesize contemporary evidence on adult postoperative delirium across the perioperative pathway and to classify major preventive and therapeutic strategies according to clinical maturity, target population, and implementation readiness. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and Web of Science Core Collection was performed, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, official ESAIC and ASA resources, reference-list screening, and selected seminal pre-2021 publications. Current evidence supports a multifactorial model in which baseline cognitive and physiological vulnerability interacts with inflammatory, pharmacological, hemodynamic, nociceptive, sleep-related, and environmental stressors. No single anesthetic technique, processed-EEG target, blood-pressure threshold, cerebral oximetry strategy, or pharmacological agent consistently prevents POD across surgical populations. Multicomponent non-pharmacological prevention has the most consistent support, whereas dexmedetomidine and other pharmacological approaches appear context-dependent, and biomarkers and metabolic targets remain investigational. Future progress will depend on standardized delirium ascertainment, better phenotyping, multimodal prediction and prevention strategies, and reliable implementation systems that identify vulnerability early and maintain effective preventive care across transitions.

articles.title: Early Changes in Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter Associated with Endotracheal Tube Versus Laryngeal Mask Airway in Children Undergoing Elective Surgery Under General Anesthesia: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Purpose: Ultrasonographic optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD) has been investigated as a noninvasive sonographic marker associated with intracranial pressure. This study aimed to compare the early change in ONSD after airway placement between children managed with an endotracheal tube (ETT) and those managed with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA). Methods: This single-center prospective, non-randomized observational study included 160 children stratified into age groups of 1-4 and 5-11 years, with 40 patients in each airway subgroup. Bilateral mean ONSD was measured before airway placement (T0), immediately after airway placement and initiation of mechanical ventilation (T1), and after airway removal but before full awakening (T2). The primary outcome was the between-device difference in the change in ONSD from T0 to T1. Repeated measurements were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model, with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. Results: The increase in bilateral mean ONSD from T0 to T1 was 0.269 mm greater in the ETT group than in the LMA group (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.131-0.408; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). The age-specific ETT-LMA difference in change was 0.293 mm in children aged 1-4 years (95% CI, 0.097-0.488; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0068) and 0.246 mm in those aged 5-11 years (95% CI, 0.050-0.442; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0137). The age group × airway device × time interaction was not significant (Holm-adjusted p = 0.743). In exploratory analyses, peak inspiratory and plateau pressures were higher in the ETT group in both age strata. Conclusions: In the early period after airway placement, ETT use was associated with a greater increase in bilateral mean ONSD than LMA use. Although the association was directionally consistent in both age strata, there was no evidence that the magnitude of the effect differed by age group. Because ONSD is not a direct measurement of intracranial pressure, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical intracranial hypertension or causality. The airway device was not randomized but was determined by surgical and clinical factors and the attending anesthesiologist's judgment, and the clinical significance of the 0.269 mm difference is uncertain.

articles.title: Perinatal Characteristics and Automated Auditory Brainstem Response Screening Outcomes in Newborns: A Retrospective Hospital-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Universal newborn hearing screening (UNHS) programs are essential for early detection of congenital hearing impairment. In community and secondary hospital settings, distinguishing true screening failures from protocol-driven risk referrals and tracking outpatient follow-up represent key operational challenges. Objective: To evaluate automated Auditory Brainstem Response (AABR) screening outcomes and explore their associations with delivery mode, anesthesia type, nationality, and selected perinatal characteristics in a retrospective newborn cohort. Secondary objectives were to describe protocol-driven risk referrals despite normal screening results and to assess incomplete screening due to loss to outpatient follow-up. Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study evaluated 406 consecutive singleton newborns undergoing universal AABR screening between 1 June 2024 and 31 May 2025 at a private secondary hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye. Screenings followed a multi-stage protocol using the MADSEN AccuScreen system (35 dB nHL click stimuli). Outcomes were classified into four mutually exclusive groups: (1) normal AABR without referral, (2) protocol-driven referral due to predefined hearing-loss risk factors despite a normal AABR, (3) final AABR refer (screening failure), and (4) incomplete screening/lost to outpatient follow-up. Primary exploratory analyses compared completed normal passes (n = 384) with final screen refers (n = 7) using exact tests. A post hoc sensitivity analysis was conducted treating all incomplete cases as screening refers (n = 22 vs. n = 384). Results: Among 406 singleton newborns, 343 (84.5%) passed AABR without referral, 41 (10.1%) passed AABR but were referred for audiological surveillance due to clinical risk factors, 7 (1.7%) had a final AABR refer result and were referred for diagnostic audiological evaluation, and 15 (3.7%) had an initial refer but defaulted before completing outpatient rescreening. In the primary analysis, lower gestational age showed a nominal association with a final AABR refer [median 37.0 weeks (IQR 36.5-38.0) vs. 38.0 weeks (IQR 38.0-39.0); p = 0.026]. In the sensitivity analysis incorporating all 15 incomplete cases (n = 22), this nominal association with lower gestational age was also observed [median 37.5 weeks vs. 38.0 weeks; p = 0.028]. Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission (p = 0.018) and predefined risk factors (p = 0.004) showed nominal univariate associations with screening refer; after Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons, only the predefined risk factor composite remained below 0.05. Sex, delivery mode (cesarean vs. vaginal), and anesthesia type were not significantly associated with screening outcome; however, given the small number of events (n = 7), these findings should be regarded as statistically inconclusive rather than definitive evidence of no effect. Among the 41 risk-referred infants, prolonged NICU hospitalization (>5 days) was the predominant referral criterion (n = 29, 70.7%). In the post hoc worst-case sensitivity analysis, general anesthesia compared with regional anesthesia (p = 0.014) and Syrian nationality compared with Turkish nationality (p = 0.008) showed nominal associations with the hypothetical expanded refer outcome, illustrating the sensitivity of these findings to incomplete follow-up. Conclusions: In this retrospective hospital-based cohort, only seven newborns had a final AABR refer result, limiting the precision of association estimates. Although lower gestational age and NICU admission showed nominal associations with final screening refer, only the predefined hearing-loss risk factor composite remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Fifteen newborns (3.7%) did not complete outpatient rescreening, identifying a measurable gap in follow-up documentation. These findings support improved screening-completion tracking and warrant validation in larger cohorts with confirmatory audiological outcomes.

articles.title: The "Heat-and-Cold" Strategy: Combining Intercostal Nerve Cryoablation for Analgesia After Uniportal VATS Pleurectomy and Hyperthermic Intrathoracic Chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: We report interesting images from a 54-year-old woman with recurrent B2 thymoma associated with myasthenia gravis, treated using a minimally invasive uniportal VATS pleurectomy combined with hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITHOC). Preoperative imaging identified two hypermetabolic pleural lesions. Complete resection was achieved, followed by cisplatin-based HITHOC. Postoperative pain was managed by a multimodal approach combining erector spinae plane block and intercostal nerve cryoablation, resulting in a VAS score of two on the first postoperative day, decreasing to zero subsequently, and with no opioid requirement to control pain. The patient experienced an uneventful recovery and rapid discharge. This case highlights the feasibility and safety, with favourable outcomes in this patient. Larger and comparative series are needed to confirm the potential advantages of combining minimally invasive surgery with advanced analgesic strategies in complex thoracic oncology.

articles.title: Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease and Kidney Transplantation: A Narrative Review of Pathophysiological Mechanisms, Implications for Nutritional Status, and Biotic Interventions.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a serious public health issue affecting 10% of the global population. CKD is associated with intestinal dysbiosis, characterized by a reduction in saccharolytic bacteria and an increase in proteolytic genera that produce uremic toxins. This may promote intestinal barrier impairment ("leaky gut" syndrome), chronic low-grade inflammation, and protein-energy wasting (PEW), although most of the supporting evidence is observational. Kidney transplantation (KT) improves survival but may not fully reverse dysbiosis. KT recipients are exposed to residual uremia, use of perioperative antibiotics, and chronic immunosuppressive regimens. Drugs such as mycophenolate mofetil can cause gastrointestinal toxicity and reduced intake due to diarrhea or enteropathy, whereas corticosteroids and calcineurin inhibitors induce hyperphagia, hypomagnesemia, and insulin resistance. These factors may lead to a spectrum of complications ranging from persistent PEW in the early post-transplant period to a higher prevalence of weight gain and obesity, sarcopenia, and post-transplant diabetes. Furthermore, the microbiota may modulate pharmacological responses; in experimental and small clinical studies, genera such as Faecalibacterium have been linked to alterations in the metabolism of tacrolimus, potentially altering its therapeutic levels and the risk of nephrotoxicity or rejection. Interventions using biotics (prebiotics, probiotics, and synbiotics) are emerging as a potential adjuvant strategy to restore eubiosis and mitigate PEW. In non-dialysis and dialysis CKD patients, some biotics have been reported to reduce uremic toxins and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α), although results are heterogeneous. However, there is no evidence available regarding its ability to improve nutritional status following a KT. Safety data are limited, although biotic interventions are generally considered safe. Future prospective studies are required to confirm their efficacy and immunological safety, as well as any possible association with infectious adverse events.

articles.title: Frailty Indices and Preoperative Clinical Factors for Predicting Myocardial Injury After Non-Cardiac Surgery (MINS) in High-Risk Geriatric Orthopedic Patients: A Machine-Learning Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS) is a common, often asymptomatic complication in geriatric orthopedic patients that increases postoperative mortality. The Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) may not adequately capture the age-related loss of the physiological reserve. We investigated whether frailty indices (mFI-5, mFI-11) improve machine-learning prediction of preoperative MINS risk, and compared an exploratory perioperative model with ASA and RCRI. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 656 patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent major orthopedic surgery with postoperative ICU monitoring and troponin surveillance were analyzed; MINS occurred in 82 (12.5%). The models were as follows: Model 1 (preoperative baseline), Model 2 (+mFI-5), Model 3 (+mFI-11), and an exploratory perioperative model, Model 4 (+intraoperative vasopressor use and postoperative mechanical ventilation). AUCs on a 30% hold-out set were compared with ASA/RCRI using the paired DeLong test, with Bonferroni adjustment across 15 comparisons. A sensitivity analysis with an identical classifier and predictor set isolated the contribution of the frailty indices. Results: Frailty indices did not provide significant incremental value: adding mFI-5 or mFI-11 changed the AUC only marginally (0.5744 to 0.5828 and 0.5881; all p > 0.5). Preoperative models (hold-out AUC 0.6005-0.6935) did not differ significantly from ASA or RCRI after Bonferroni correction. Model 4, incorporating intra- and postoperative variables, reached an AUC of 0.7584, significantly higher than ASA (adjusted p = 0.002) but not RCRI (adjusted p = 0.268). Conclusions: With the algorithm and predictor set held constant, no incremental value of frailty indices was demonstrable, and no model significantly outperformed RCRI after multiplicity correction. The numerically higher AUC of Model 3 versus Model 2 cannot be attributed to frailty indices, as the models differed in both predictors and algorithm. Power was limited; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Whether frailty indices improve prediction needs to be tested in external cohorts large enough to detect it.

articles.title: Unplanned Inpatient Admission After Intended Outpatient Total Extraperitoneal Inguinal Hernia Repair: Precautionary Monitoring or Clinically Relevant Morbidity?
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Unplanned inpatient admission after intended outpatient surgery is commonly regarded as failure of ambulatory management, although the clinical relevance of such admissions remains unclear. This study evaluated the causes, management, and short-term outcomes of unplanned inpatient admission after intended outpatient total extraperitoneal (TEP) inguinal hernia repair. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included all patients requiring unplanned inpatient admission after intended outpatient unilateral TEP repair between January 2022 and May 2025. Admission triggers, perioperative management, Clavien-Dindo complication severity, length of stay, need for invasive intervention, and 30-day outcomes were analyzed descriptively. Results: Among 153 intended outpatient TEP procedures, 45 patients (29.4%) required unplanned inpatient admission. The most frequent trigger was suspected intraoperative bleeding requiring observation (29/45, 64.4%), followed by technical or anatomical factors (6/45, 13.3%), cardiovascular events (4/45, 8.9%), other medical reasons (3/45, 6.7%), postoperative pain or nausea (2/45, 4.4%), and social or organizational reasons (1/45, 2.2%). Thirty-seven patients (82.2%) had no postoperative complication, six (13.3%) had Clavien-Dindo grade I-II complications, and two (4.4%) had grade III or higher complications requiring invasive intervention. Most patients were discharged on postoperative day 1 (35/45, 77.8%). No patient required blood transfusion, intensive care admission, or 30-day readmission. Conclusions: Unplanned inpatient admission occurred in 29.4% of intended outpatient TEP procedures, representing a relatively high admission rate for a planned outpatient pathway. Although most admissions were associated with precautionary monitoring rather than clinically relevant morbidity, invasive intervention was required in a small proportion of patients. The retrospective data do not allow individual admissions to be classified as avoidable; however, the findings suggest potential for pathway optimization through more standardized discharge assessment and formalized admission criteria. Prospective studies are required to determine whether such standardization can reduce unplanned inpatient stays while maintaining patient safety.

articles.title: Aldosterone-Mediated Atrial Remodeling and Atrial Fibrillation: Molecular Mechanisms, Translational Insights and Implications for Cardiac Surgery.
