MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Based on albumin levels at CKRT initiation and on day 7, patients were categorized into the persistent, resolved, new-onset, and no hypoalbuminemia groups. A composite of progression to end-stage kidney disease and all-cause mortality within 365 days was the primary outcome. The composite outcome occurred in 33.4% (363/1087) of the patients. The adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for the primary outcome was significantly higher in all groups when compared with the no hypoalbuminemia group (persistent: aOR, 2.64; 95% CI, 1.73-4.04; p < 0.001; resolved: aOR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.38-3.75; p < 0.001; new-onset: aOR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.06-2.68; p = 0.028). No hypoalbuminemia group was associated with the most favorable prognosis, whereas persistent hypoalbuminemia was associated with the worst outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: During CKRT, early albumin level changes are associated with long-term kidney failure and mortality risk. Persistent hypoalbuminemia predicts the worst outcomes. Even in patients without baseline hypoalbuminemia, early decline in albumin is associated with worse prognosis.
authors: LINking health medical records, biospecimens, and biosignals in Korean patients with Acute kidney injury consortium (LINKA) investigators

articles.title: Integrating a Host-Protein Bacterial/Viral Test into the Emergency Department Sepsis Alert Order Set Is Associated with Changes in Sepsis Category Distribution and Patient Management: A Pre/Postimplementation Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of implementing a host-protein bacterial/viral test in the emergency department (ED) sepsis alert order set.
DESIGN: Pre/postimplementation study. Host-protein testing was automatically ordered both pre- and postimplementation as part of the ED sepsis alert order set; test results were accessible to treating clinicians only postimplementation. The pre- (September 2024 to December 2024) to postimplementation (January 2025 to March 2025) transition also involved education on the host-protein test to ED clinicians. The primary outcome was patient classification into Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) sepsis categories (definite/probable vs. possible vs. unlikely sepsis).
SETTING: ED of an academic medical center.
PATIENTS: Adults who triggered the ED sepsis alert order set.
INTERVENTIONS: Host-protein bacterial/viral test (MeMed BV) automatically ordered in ED sepsis alert order set. Test result was only visible to clinicians postimplementation.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: There were 893 eligible patients; 505 patients in the preimplementation cohort and 388 in the postimplementation cohort. The distribution of SSC sepsis categories differed between pre- and postimplementation cohorts (χ2(2) = 8.73; p = 0.013). The difference was primarily driven by a larger proportion of patients classified as unlikely sepsis (from 32.5% to 41.1%; p = 0.009) and a smaller proportion classified as possible sepsis (from 18.4% to 13.2%; p = 0.043). Among unlikely sepsis patients, host-protein test implementation was associated with ordering fewer cefepime doses (from 3.3 to 2.2; p = 0.044) and a lower hospitalization rate (from 92.1% to 79.9%; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support an association between host-protein testing for patients triggering ED sepsis alerts and the distribution of possible vs. unlikely sepsis cases. Multicenter clinical utility studies are warranted.

articles.title: Dynamics of Mitochondrial Structure, Biogenesis and Function in Skeletal Muscle of Critically Ill Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To define the timing and phenotype of mitochondrial ultrastructural remodeling and electron transport chain (ETC) function in skeletal muscle during early critical illness.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a prospective observational study with serial muscle biopsies.
SETTING: Adult ICU.
PATIENTS: Thirty-three mechanically ventilated ICU patients (median age, 49 yr; 27% women) with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment greater than or equal to 9 on three consecutive days; skeletal muscle biopsies of the vastus lateralis muscle at ICU day 5 (n = 29) and day 15 (n = 22). Healthy subjects served as controls.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Vastus lateralis biopsies were analyzed by electron microscopy with stereology, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting, and spectrophotometric ETC enzyme assays (reported per tissue weight and normalized to citrate synthase [CS]). Intact mitochondrial profiles were reduced vs. controls (fold change vs. controls: day 5, 0.24 [0.18-0.34]; p = 0.039 and day 15, 0.20 [0.16-0.33]; p = 0.011) and disturbed profiles increased (day 5, 5.62 [3.20-7.17]; p < 0.001 and day 15, 5.20 [3.67-6.36]; p = 0.001), with reduced volume density of intact mitochondria (day 5, 0.33 [0.20-0.49]; p = 0.009 and day 15, 0.32 [0.21-0.50]; p = 0.005). Inner mitochondrial membrane surface-to-volume ratio was reduced at day 5 (0.69 [0.49-0.89]; p = 0.022) and remained unchanged at day 15. Complex III tissue activity was reduced at day 5 (85.6 [22.1-133.3] vs. 151.4 [100.5-205.0]; p = 0.015) and day 15 (50.5 [36.0-69.8]; p = 0.001), remaining reduced after CS normalization (day 5, 0.83 [0.34-1.49]; p = 0.040 and day 15, 0.87 [0.65-0.93]; p = 0.007). Complex IV activity remained reduced before and after CS normalization at both time points (all p < 0.001). CS activity declined by day 15 (56.3 [52.7-65.1] vs. 95.6 [80.1-133.0]; p = 0.001 and day 15 vs. day 5; p = 0.041). qRT-PCR and Western blot supported reduced ETC components and altered biogenesis signaling.
CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal muscle mitochondrial ultrastructure is altered by ICU day 5 and remains abnormal at day 15, with persistent complex III/IV dysfunction after CS normalization. These findings define an early sustained mitochondrial remodeling phenotype in skeletal muscle during critical illness.

articles.title: Language Concordance in Critical Care: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Language barriers are associated with differences in care delivery processes and outcomes in critical care settings, with differences despite language assistance services. Less is known about outcomes associated with language concordant care. Language concordance is a linguistic match between a patient's preferred language and the language used by their care team. We undertook a systematic review to examine the measurement and impact of language concordant care delivery during critical illness, inclusive of the critical care recovery period after hospitalization.
DATA SOURCES AND STUDY SELECTION: A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Embase, and Cochrane of English-language publications from database inception to March 3, 2026. Studies that investigated adults in critical care and post-ICU recovery clinic settings that included measurement of language concordance were included. Study quality was evaluated by the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Of 1,682 unique records identified, 11 were eligible for inclusion (128,181 total patients; mean [sd] age, 68.4 [17.9 yr]; 72,872 [56.9%] male and 55,082 [43.1%] female). Six studies assessed clinical decision-making. Reported outcomes included code status changes, family conferences, communication complexity, delirium, length of stay, mechanical ventilation, and mortality. Due to significant heterogeneity in study analyses and reported outcomes, data were not pooled for quantitative analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that language-concordant care may influence clinically meaningful processes of critical care, warranting interventional studies to guide care delivery recommendations.

articles.title: Liver transplant team involvement in level III and IV renal tumor thrombectomy: Perioperative and oncologic outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Resection of renal cell carcinoma with inferior vena cava (IVC) tumor thrombus above the hepatic veins requires extensive liver mobilization using techniques derived from liver transplantation. We assessed whether dedicated liver transplant team involvement in radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy for thrombi above the hepatic veins (level III and IV) was associated with perioperative and oncologic outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this unplanned, hypothesis-generating analysis of a single-center retrospective cohort (2018-2024), cases were classified by liver transplant team involvement, and intraoperative factors, 90-day outcomes, and survival were compared. Because liver transplant team involvement was adopted progressively, sensitivity analyses adjusting for year of surgery and restricted to the adoption period were performed.
RESULTS: Of 36 cases, 18 (50%) involved the liver transplant team. Intraoperative factors were similar. Liver transplant team involvement was associated with fewer major complications (Clavien grade ≥3: 11% vs. 50%, P = 0.03) and less hepatic dysfunction (0% vs. 39%, P = 0.01) within 90 days, with similar recurrence-free and overall survival. Adjusting for cardiac bypass, liver transplant team involvement was associated with lower odds of major complications (odds ratio [OR] 0.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.005-0.57) and hepatic dysfunction (OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.002-0.83). After adjustment for year of surgery, point estimates were similar but neither association remained statistically significant (OR 0.13, 95% CI 0.01-1.24; OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.001-1.22).
CONCLUSIONS: Liver transplant team involvement was associated with fewer major complications and less hepatic dysfunction. Although this association could not be reliably separated from calendar time, these findings warrant prospective, multi-institutional evaluation of liver transplant team involvement in high-level renal tumor thrombectomy.

articles.title: Anesthetic outcomes in robotic kidney transplantation: a retrospective cohort analysis.
articles.abstract: Kidney transplantation is the definitive treatment for end-stage renal disease. Within the last decade, robotic-assisted kidney transplants have emerged as a promising alternative to the traditional open approach, but the impact on postoperative pain is unclear. We conducted a propensity-matched retrospective study to investigate postoperative pain control between open and robotic kidney transplant in adults at the University of Illinois Hospital from September 2020 to September 2025. The primary outcome was opioid consumption within 30 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes included the highest pain score within 72 hours of surgery, intraoperative opioid consumption, length of stay, and total hospital length of stay. Of 1379 patients, significant differences in baseline characteristics were observed between the open (n = 1234) and robotic (n = 145) approaches for age, weight and BMI. Propensity matching resulted in 127 pairs with no significant difference in opioid consumption within 30 days of surgery, intraoperative milligram morphine equivalents, highest pain score in recovery within 72 hours, and length of stay. Robotic cases were longer with less blood loss and required a smaller volume of packed red blood cell transfusions. Multivariate linear regression of 30-day morphine equivalents demonstrated a reduction in patients who were immediately extubated following completion of surgery. Robotic transplants resulted in similar postoperative opioid consumption and pain scores to open transplants but were longer and less bloody. Prolonged intubation after surgery contributed to opioid use. Our results contradict prior literature, which has reported reduced pain and opioid use with robotic approaches.

articles.title: Therapeutic Judgment and Surgical Innovation in the Nineteenth-Century American South and Trans-Appalachian Frontier.
articles.abstract: The early history of American surgery is often told through breakthroughs that emerged in the trans-Appalachian frontier and antebellum South: Ephraim McDowell's ovariotomy in Danville, Kentucky (1809), Crawford Long's use of ether anesthesia in Jefferson, Georgia (1842), and J. Marion Sims's closure of vesicovaginal fistula in Montgomery, Alabama (1845-1849). The concentration of these advances outside institutional centers in Philadelphia, New York, and Boston that dominated American medicine raises a historical question: why did surgical innovation emerge from regions regarded by northeastern elites as a medical backwater? This paper argues that early American surgical innovation emerged within a professional culture organized around therapeutic judgment under uncertainty. In the antebellum South and frontier regions, weak organized supervision, sparse credentialing structures, practitioner autonomy, and dispersed medical authority created environments in which surgeons could act decisively before consensus existed. Successful outcomes, published case narratives, and accumulated reputation established operative legitimacy retrospectively. Southern surgical innovation thus developed as a distinct judgment-based system of medical authority, preceding the standardized methods of scientific validation that later characterized institutional medicine. McDowell and Long's innovations occurred far from academic institutions and the journals and mutual visits to urban hospitals on both sides of the Atlantic that transmitted medical knowledge. Sims publicized his revolutionary operation through mainstream publications and by transplanting his practice to New York, London, and continental Europe. Samuel Gross represented the transition to institutionalized transmission through textbooks, teaching, journals, and national professional organizations. Johns Hopkins Hospital subsequently transformed surgical legitimacy through laboratory science, residency training, asepsis, and institutional hierarchy. The story of surgery in the American South thus includes how its innovations were transmitted, validated, and reproduced.

articles.title: Equine castration in Sweden: a retrospective study of postoperative complications across field and hospital practices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This retrospective study describes and compares the surgical techniques and medical protocols used for castration of male horses in Swedish ambulatory practices (Field group) and in Swedish equine hospitals (Hospital group). Data on patient characteristics, perioperative medical protocols, surgical techniques and postoperative complications were collected as documented in patient records of both groups. Descriptive statistics, univariable and multivariable analyses were used to evaluate factors associated with postoperative complication.
RESULTS: The overall complication rate was 35% in the Field group and 13% in the Hospital group. This difference remained significant after adjusting for age and breed in a multivariable analysis (OR 4.5; CI 3.18-6.36). In the Field group 511/521 horses (98%) were castrated standing using sedation and local analgesia, incisions were left un-sutured in all horses (100%). The surgical technique was described in 230/521 records (44%), the open technique was used in 194/230 horses (84%) and the half-closed technique was used in 36/230 horses (16%). Complication and surgical site infection were associated with higher odds in horses that did not receive perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (OR 1.5; CI 1.01-2.36 and OR 1.7; CI 1.08-2.82 respectively). In the Hospital group, 554 stallions were castrated under general anaesthesia, and the incisions were sutured in 473/554 horses (85%). The closed technique was used in 503/554 horses (91%) and the half-closed was used in 51/554 (9%). Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis was administered to all horses in the Hospital group. Postoperative antimicrobial prophylaxis did not decrease the odds of surgical site infection in any of the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In Sweden, standing, open castration with un-sutured incisions was preferred in ambulatory practice, whereas a closed, sutured technique dominated in the hospitals. Field castration was associated with a substantially higher odds of postoperative complications, compared with hospital-based castrations performed under general anaesthesia. These findings provide locally relevant evidence to guide clinical decision-making and antimicrobial stewardship and may contribute to the ethical discussion regarding the use of standing castration when alternatives are feasible.

articles.title: Risk factors for postoperative hyponatremia after endoscopic endonasal surgery for nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative hyponatremia is a common complication after endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (Pit-NETs, also known as a pituitary adenoma), but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study evaluated its incidence, clinical course, and risk factors after EES for nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma/ Pit-NET.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 229 patients who underwent EES for nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas/ Pit-NETs between April 2014 and March 2024. Postoperative hyponatremia was defined as serum sodium < 135 mEq/L. Clinical, radiological, endocrine, and perioperative variables, including body mass index (BMI), tumor dimensions, and intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage graded using the Esposito classification, were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify risk factors.
RESULTS: Postoperative hyponatremia occurred in 36 patients (15.7%) at a mean of 6.6 ± 1.9 days after surgery. Fluid restriction alone achieved sodium normalization in 31 patients (86.1%). Univariate analysis identified lower BMI, Esposito grade 3 CSF leakage, and larger superior-inferior tumor diameter as significant risk factors. Multivariate analysis revealed that lower BMI (p = 0.021; odds ratio [OR] 0.873; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.778-0.979) and Esposito grade 3 (p = 0.049; OR, 3.251; 95% CI, 1.006-10.50) were independently associated with postoperative hyponatremia.
CONCLUSION: Lower BMI and Esposito grade 3 CSF leakage were independent risk factors for postoperative hyponatremia after EES for nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas/ Pit-NETs. These findings may help identify patients requiring careful postoperative sodium monitoring.

articles.title: How to Prevent Complications During Aquablation. Lessons Learned from a Prospective Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate perioperative complications following robotic water-jet ablation (Aquablation) for benign prostatic hyperplasia and to identify modifiable intraoperative technical factors associated with adverse events.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study included 628 consecutive patients who underwent Aquablation between March 2023 and December 2025. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, functional results, and delayed reinterventions were recorded prospectively. Adverse events were graded using the Clavien-Dindo classification. Technical factors associated with complications were analyzed using a structured review of intraoperative findings and postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: Mean age was 71.5 ± 8.2 years, and mean prostate volume was 89.1 ± 47.9 cm³. Functional outcomes improved significantly during follow-up: mean International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) decreased from 24.7 ± 6.0 to 6.8 ± 5.6 at 3 months (P < .001), with a durable benefit over time. Early complications were mostly low-grade. Bleeding-related events included transfusion in 52 patients (8.2%), clot retention in 19 (3.0%), endoscopic fulguration in 8 (1.3%), and angioembolization in 2 (0.3%). A temporal analysis demonstrated a marked reduction in transfusion rates following stepwise technical refinements, decreasing from approximately 8% in the initial phase to 1% in later cases. Urinary retention occurred in 32 patients (5.1%), of whom 4 (0.6%) required suprapubic catheter placement. Delayed reintervention was required in 34 patients (5.4%), most commonly transurethral resection of the prostate (4.6%). Intraoperative factors associated with complications included bladder-neck jet misalignment (bleeding), inadequate apical resection (retention), traumatic handpiece insertion (urethral complications), and overlapping distal resection planes causing delayed obstruction ("cross-healing").
CONCLUSIONS: Aquablation provides significant and durable symptom improvement with an acceptable safety profile in real-world practice. Outcomes appear highly reproducible, whereas many complications are related to modifiable technical factors. Optimization of surgical technique may improve procedural safety and long-term durability.
articles.journal: J Laparoendosc Adv Surg Tech A

articles.title: Evaluation of preoperative and perioperative characteristics in patients admitted to a postoperative intensive care unit: A prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission is commonly considered for patients perceived to be at increased risk of postoperative complications. This study aimed to describe the preoperative and perioperative characteristics of patients admitted to a postoperative ICU and to explore associations between routinely available clinical parameters, inflammatory biomarkers, and short-term outcomes. This prospective observational study included 126 adult patients admitted postoperatively to a tertiary reanimation ICU. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, ASA physical status, anesthesia type, laboratory parameters, postoperative organ support requirements, ICU length of stay, and mortality were recorded. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) were evaluated. Continuous and categorical variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and chi-square or Fisher exact test, as appropriate. The mean age was 67.3 ± 16.1 years, and 114 (90.5%) patients were classified as ASA III. Abdominal surgery was the most common surgical category (56, 44.4%). Mean NLR and CAR values were 6.17 ± 8.36 and 1.17 ± 2.52, respectively. Two patients died (1.6%; exact 95% CI, 0.2-5.6%). Mortality was not significantly associated with NLR (P = .310), CAR (P = .845), admission SpO2 (P = .084), or hemoglobin level (P = .907). ICU length of stay showed an exploratory association with mortality (P = .004); given that only 2 deaths occurred, this observation cannot establish a prognostic relationship. In this selected postoperative ICU cohort, preoperative and perioperative characteristics did not clearly distinguish patients according to short-term outcomes. Because there was no non-ICU comparator cohort and mortality events were very limited, the findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger multicenter studies are needed to evaluate whether these parameters can support postoperative ICU admission decisions.

articles.title: Preoperative glycaemic control and severity of sternal wound infections after cardiac surgery: association of elevated Hemoglobin A1c with deep versus superficial infections.
articles.abstract: Sternal wound infections (SWIs), including superficial sternal wound infection (SSWI) and deep sternal wound infection (DSWI), are complications after coronary artery bypass grafting and other cardiac surgeries. Elevated preoperative HbA1c, suggesting poor glycaemic control, impairs wound healing and may escalate postoperative risk. This study evaluates the association between preoperative HbA1c levels and the anatomical severity (superficial versus deep) of SWIs among patients who develop postoperative wound complications. A 24-month retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care cardiac surgery centre. Adult patients (≥18 years) going through elective or urgent isolated cardiac surgery with a preoperative HbA1c measured within 30 days were included. Using consecutive sampling, 133 patients who developed SWIs were identified. DSWI and SSWI were defined according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria, and logistic regression was employed to evaluate the association between HbA1c categories and the odds of presenting with DSWI rather than SSWI. Among 133 sternal infections, 69.9% were DSWI and 30.1% were SSWI. Diabetic-range HbA1c was common (62.4%) and was associated with a higher proportion of DSWI, occurring in 94% of diabetic-range patients versus 26.5% in normal and 37.5% in pre-diabetic groups χ2 = 61.357, P<0.001. Univariable logistic regression demonstrated that, among patients who developed a wound infection, those with a diabetic-range HbA1c had significantly higher odds of the infection involving deep tissues rather than remaining superficial (OR 36.40; 95% CI 12.59-105.18; P<0.001). Among patients who develop postoperative SWIs, an elevated preoperative HbA1c is strongly associated with deep rather than superficial infection involvement. While this case-only design cannot establish the absolute risk of infection development, preoperative HbA1c serves as a valuable indicator of potential anatomical severity within an infected cohort. Rather than mandating clinical delays, routine preoperative HbA1c assessment should be utilized as a non-invasive risk-stratification tool to identify patients who may benefit from closer perioperative metabolic optimization and extended postoperative surveillance.

articles.title: Outcomes and Trends in Pediatric Orthognathic Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compares risk factors, complication rates, and perioperative outcomes among pediatric patients undergoing Le Fort I osteotomy (LF1), mandibular osteotomy (MO), bimaxillary osteotomy (BMO), or Le Fort I with distraction osteogenesis (LF1+DO).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Pediatrics database from 2018 to 2023, including patients aged 5-18 years who underwent an orthognathic procedure. The primary outcome was unplanned readmission or reoperation. Secondary outcomes included total hospital length of stay, operative time, and blood loss.
RESULTS: A total of 1203 patients met inclusion criteria: LF1 (n = 651), BMO (n = 294), MO (n = 190), and LF1+DO (n = 68). BMO was associated with a significantly higher risk of readmission or reoperation compared with both LF1 (odds ratio = 4.84, P < 0.01) and MO (odds ratio = 2.10, P = 0.03). American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification of 3 or higher was independently linked to increased hospital length of stay (β = 6.3, P < 0.01) and longer operative times (β = 4.3, P < 0.01). BMO was associated with a longer hospital stay compared with LF1 (β = 2.2, P = 0.03). There was no significant difference in readmission and reoperation between LF1 and LF1+DO.
CONCLUSIONS: BMO was associated with the greatest surgical burden, whereas LF1+DO had a similar safety profile to LF1. In addition, higher ASA class predicted prolonged stays and operative times. Careful patient selection and multidisciplinary planning are essential to optimize pediatric orthognathic outcomes.

articles.title: Opioid-sparing Pain Management for Pediatric Alveolar Bone Grafting: Efficacy of the Bupivacaine-soaked Absorbable Sponge.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The iliac crest is the gold-standard donor site for alveolar bone grafting, yet donor-site pain often leads to increased opioid use and prolonged hospital stays. This study evaluates whether the adjunctive use of bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge in addition to subcutaneous local anesthesia infiltration provides improved postoperative pain management compared with local anesthetic alone.
METHODS: Medical records of consecutive patients who underwent alveolar bone grafting between January 2023 and September 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were grouped based on whether they received bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge with local anesthetic (sponge group, N = 28) or subcutaneous local anesthetic alone (no-sponge group, N = 38). The primary outcome measure was postoperative opioid consumption. Secondary outcomes included nonopioid analgesic use, hospital length of stay, and discharge opioid prescriptions.
RESULTS: Sixty-six patients with comparable baseline demographics were analyzed. Multivariable regression revealed significantly lower opioid consumption on postoperative day 0 in the sponge group compared with the no-sponge group (-0.14 mg/kg oral morphine equivalents; P = 0.04). Furthermore, all no-sponge group patients required supplemental nonopioid analgesics on postoperative day 0, compared with 82% of patients in the sponge group (P = 0.01). No significant differences were observed between groups in hospital length of stay, discharge opioid prescriptions, and opioid or nonopioid analgesic use beyond postoperative day 0.
CONCLUSIONS: The application of bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge at the iliac crest donor site is a simple, inexpensive, and effective method for enhancing immediate postoperative pain management in pediatric patients undergoing alveolar bone grafting compared with subcutaneous local anesthetic alone.

articles.title: Impact of antibiotic prophylaxis on the occurrence of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia in trauma patients (antiVAP): a propensity score-weighted, retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-course antibiotic prophylaxis has been associated with a reduced risk of early-onset ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) in selected populations, particularly patients with acute brain injury. However, its role in severely injured trauma patients remains controversial.
METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study, conducted in 15 French trauma centres, included severely injured adults who required mechanical ventilation initiated within 24 h of admission and continued for at least 48 h. Propensity score-based analyses assessed the association between early antibiotic prophylaxis (initiated within the first 24 h of management and continued for up to 72 h) and patient outcomes. The primary outcome was early-onset VAP; secondary outcomes included late-onset VAP, extrapulmonary infections, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU and hospital length of stay, and 30-day mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 1,321 trauma patients were included. Antibiotic prophylaxis was administered to 746 patients (56%), with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid used in more than 90% of cases. Early-onset VAP occurred in 240 of 746 patients (32%) who received antibiotic prophylaxis and in 195 of 575 (34%) who did not. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with early-onset VAP (weighted odds ratio [wOR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.22; p = 0.48). A cause-specific Cox model accounting for the competing risk of death before day 7 yielded similar results (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR] 0.87, 95% CI 0.71-1.07; p = 0.19). Antibiotic prophylaxis was not associated with improve of secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis in severely injured trauma patients was not associated with a reduced risk of early-onset VAP.
CLINICALTRIALS: Gov ID NCT07059039 - Registration date: July, 10th 2025.

articles.title: Multimodal Point-of-Care Ultrasound Indices and Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: An Exploratory Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CSA-AKI) remains a common and multifactorial complication. Conventional biomarkers such as Serum Creatinine (SCr) detect injury late. This study explored whether perioperative multimodal Doppler ultrasonography could identify early haemodynamic alterations associated with CSA-AKI.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre observational study, adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital underwent serial transthoracic echocardiography and renal Doppler ultrasonography at baseline, on postoperative day 1, and on day 4. Clinical and Doppler-derived parameters were compared between patients who developed CSA-AKI and those who did not. CSA-AKI was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Univariable logistic regression was performed.
RESULTS: Fifty-four patients were included; 21 (39%) developed CSA-AKI. CSA-AKI was associated with higher EuroSCORE II (OR 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.50), diabetes mellitus (OR 7.47, 95% CI 2.17-29.3), reduced baseline mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62-0.96), lower renal End-Diastolic Velocity (EDV) at baseline (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59-0.91) and Day 4 (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.89), and Day 1 elevated Central Venous Pressure (CVP) (OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.04-1.41). SCr increased, and eGFR declined in the CSA-AKI group by Day 4.
DISCUSSION: The study findings suggest that CSA-AKI was associated with a perioperative haemodynamic profile characterised by lower MAPSE and renal EDV and higher CVP. These unadjusted associations are consistent with impaired longitudinal ventricular function, reduced renal diastolic perfusion, and venous congestion, respectively, but they do not establish causality. Left-ventricular ejection fraction and Renal Resistive Index (RRI) were not statistically associated with CSA-AKI in this cohort. The findings support a hypothesis regarding possible haemodynamic contributors to CSA-AKI that requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.
CONCLUSION: CSA-AKI was associated with lower MAPSE, higher CVP, and reduced renal EDV in univariable analyses. In this observational study, reduced renal EDV may represent a potential haemodynamic marker warranting further investigation; however, no diagnostic threshold or clinical implication can be inferred from these data. Adequately powered prospective studies are required to validate this association and determine its potential clinical utility.

articles.title: A brain network framework for cognitive dysfunction in chronic pain.
Best Evidence Summary for Preoperative Pain Management in Elderly Patients with Hip Fracture.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative pain represents a major symptom among elderly patients with hip fracture; however, evidence-based guidance specifically addressing the preoperative phase has not been well synthesized. We aimed to systematically identify, evaluate, and synthesize the best available evidence for preoperative pain management in this patient population.
METHODS: Following the JBI evidence-summary methodology and PRISMA 2020 reporting principles, a systematic literature search was performed across the databases PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, CNKI, SinoMed (CBM), and Wanfang Data, as well as the guideline websites of NICE, AAOS, APTA, ESTES, ANZHFR, COA, JOA, KHS, UpToDate, and BMJ Best Practice, covering the period from database inception to 29 September 2026. Two reviewers independently conducted literature screening and assessed methodological quality utilizing the AGREE II instrument, the AMSTAR 2 checklist, and JBI appraisal tools. The identified evidence was subsequently graded according to the JBI pre-classification system (2014).
RESULTS: A total of eighteen documents were included, comprising four evidence summaries, four guidelines, one expert consensus, eight systematic reviews, and one clinical decision support resource. The evidence was organized into seven thematic categories: team training, assessment, intervention principles, pharmacological interventions, non-pharmacological interventions, selected complementary approaches, and health education, resulting in 30 best-evidence items.
CONCLUSIONS: This evidence summary provides 30 best-evidence items for preoperative pain management in elderly patients with hip fracture. The evidence supports cognitive-specific pain assessment, timely multimodal analgesia, regional analgesia where feasible, and selected non-pharmacological approaches. Recommendations for regional analgesia and for selected complementary approaches apply only where trained personnel, monitoring capacity, and local expertise are available.
REGISTRATION: Fudan University Center for Evidence-based Nursing (ES20258809).

articles.title: Impact of AI-assisted Sedation on Early Cognitive Function and Sleep Quality in the Elderly Undergoing GI Endoscopy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effect of ENDOANGLE-assisted sedation by the "ENDOANGLE" on early cognitive function and sleep quality in elderly patients after gastrointestinal endoscopy.
METHODS: A total of 180 patients (aged 65-80, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) I-III) scheduled for sedated endoscopy were randomly assigned to an ENDOANGLE-assisted group (AI group, n = 87) or a control group (C group, n = 85). We recorded procedural metrics (induction time, resuscitation time, directional force recovery, propofol dose), Ramsay scores, vital signs, and adverse events. Sleep quality was evaluated using the St. Mary's Hospital Sleep Questionnaire (SMH score) and actigraphy (Honor Band 6) at baseline (T0), on bowel preparation day (T1), post-procedure evening (T2), and 3 (T3) and 7 (T4) days post-procedure. Cognitive function was assessed with the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Verbal Fluency Test (VFT), Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Trail Making Tests A and B (TMT-A/B) before examination (T1), 30 minutes post-emergence (T2), and at 3 (T3) and 7 (T4) days postprocedure.
RESULTS: The resuscitation time and directional force recovery in the AI group were significantly shorter than those in the C group. The induction time and total amount of propofol administered during examinations were comparable between the two groups. There were no statistically significant differences in cognitive test scores across time points between the two groups; however, on the day of enema administration, SMH scores in both groups were significantly lower than baseline. However, at night, the AI group had significantly higher SMH scores compared to the C group. On the third and seventh days after surgery, there were no differences in SMH scores from baseline within each group or between the two groups, and the sleep monitoring results from the Honor Band were largely consistent with the SMH scoring system.
DISCUSSION: AI-assisted sedation with ENDOANGEL improved sleep quality on the procedure night in elderly patients but did not affect cognitive function or sleep at 3 and 7 days postoperatively. This early benefit may stem from optimized propofol titration, which reduces acute sleep disruption. The transient effect and unchanged cognition underscore the safety and limited duration of AI impact. Future research should explore mechanisms and whether early sleep improvement enhances overall recovery.
CONCLUSION: AI-assisted sedation showed no difference in early cognitive function compared to conventional sedation, despite both groups experiencing transient post-procedural cognitive changes. The ENDOANGEL system can improve sleep quality in elderly patients at night. However, it did not affect sleep quality on the third and seventh days after painless gastrointestinal endoscopy.

articles.title: Diagnostic agreement between the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition criteria and Subjective Global Assessment for preoperative malnutrition in adults undergoing elective surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Protein-energy malnutrition remains frequently unrecognised, under-reported, and undertreated in surgical populations despite being associated with a higher risk of postoperative complications. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic agreement between the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) operational criteria and the Subjective Global Assessment for identifying adults at risk of preoperative protein-energy malnutrition undergoing elective surgery. MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 5 May 2025. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across eight included studies (n=5834) in the definitions, cut-offs, and measurement methods for GLIM phenotypic and aetiologic criteria. In six noncardiac surgical studies (n=3999), pooled sensitivity and specificity were 76% (95% confidence interval [CI] 69-81%) and 88% (95% CI 77-94%), respectively, using a random-effects bivariate model (very low certainty of evidence). Overall diagnostic agreement was fair; thus, the GLIM criteria alone may be insufficient to make the diagnosis of malnutrition and to guide nutritional interventions without additional clinical or dietetic assessment.

articles.title: The impacts of ocular surface factors on refractive outcomes and visual quality in cataract surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Preoperative ocular surface abnormalities are increasingly recognized as critical modifiable factors influencing refractive and visual outcomes in cataract surgery. This review synthesizes high-level evidence on the impact of tear film instability, dry eye disease (DED), meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD), corneal epithelial lesions, and total corneal irregular astigmatism (TCIA) on postoperative outcomes.
RECENT FINDINGS: Shortened tear film break-up time (TBUT) independently causes refractive prediction error. Each 1-s TBUT increase raises the odds of target refraction nearly fivefold, with a ≥ 6-s clinical threshold. A two-week regimen combining artificial tears and eyelid hygiene reduces mean absolute error (MAE). Intense pulsed light combined with meibomian gland massage (IPL-MGX) or cryopreserved amniotic membrane transplantation improve ± 0.50 D accuracy. Tear film instability drives dynamic higher-order aberrations (HOAs) and fluctuating visual disturbances. Total corneal irregular astigmatism (TCIA) impairs patient-reported functional vision, even with precise postoperative refraction. Systematic preoperative screening, stratified interventions, adoption of TBUT ≥ 6 s as a biometric target, and 1-3 months of postoperative ocular surface management are essential.
SUMMARY: Individualized and stepwise perioperative strategies guided by TBUT and HOAs improve objective refractive accuracy, visual quality, and patient satisfaction. Future research should develop dynamic tear film assessment and integrate ocular surface parameters into next-generation intraocular lens (IOL) formulas.

articles.title: Safety of living liver donors with remnant liver volume below 30% after laparoscopic living donor hepatectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Donor safety is paramount in living-donor liver transplantation. A remnant liver volume (RLV) ≥ 30% is widely recommended, although supporting evidence remains limited. Given ongoing organ shortages, it is critical to determine whether excluding donors with marginally low RLVs is justified. The objective of this study was to evaluate the safety of living liver donors with RLV < 30% after laparoscopic right hemihepatectomy.
METHODS: Prospectively collected data were analysed from living liver donors who underwent purely laparoscopic right hemihepatectomy between January 2022 and December 2024. The primary endpoint was posthepatectomy liver failure (PHLF), defined according to the International Study Group of Liver Surgery criteria. Secondary outcomes included the achievement of textbook outcomes in liver surgery, postoperative liver function trends, complications (Clavien-Dindo classification), and length of hospital stay. Propensity score matching (1:3) was used to compare donors with RLV < 30% and ≥ 30%.
RESULTS: Among the 374 screened donors, 28 with RLV < 30% and 77 matched controls with RLV ≥ 30% were analysed. The mean RLV values were 28.3% and 35.7%, respectively. The incidence of PHLF was numerically higher in donors with RLV < 30%, but the difference was not statistically significant (9 of 28 (32%) versus 13 of 77 (17%); P = 0.203). Similarly, textbook outcomes in liver surgery achievement rates did not differ significantly between the two groups (24 of 28 (86%) versus 70 of 77 (91%); P = 0.430). Donors with RLV < 30% exhibited transiently higher bilirubin levels (P = 0.007) and earlier international normalized ratio peaks (P = 0.040) but values normalized during follow-up. No significant differences were found in other biochemical parameters, complications, or hospitalizations.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, RLV < 30% was not statistically associated with worse PHLF or composite perioperative safety outcomes. Although PHLF occurred more frequently in donors with RLV < 30%, most events were grade A and postoperative biochemical dysfunction resolved during follow-up. These findings suggest that, in carefully selected donors undergoing minimally invasive donor hepatectomy at experienced centres, an RLV < 30% may not necessarily represent a strict binary threshold, although caution is warranted given the limited sample size.

articles.title: Total Knee Arthroplasty as the Initial and Definitive Treatment for the Multiligament Injured Knee.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiligament knee injuries (MLKIs) are complex injury patterns that pose challenges for patients and surgeons alike. The objective of this study was to evaluate the clinical and functional perioperative outcomes of a cohort of patients with evidence of pre-existing knee osteoarthritic changes that underwent total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as the initial and definitive treatment for MLKI.
METHODS: Patients from 2 tertiary care centers that underwent TKA as primary treatment for their MLKI within 1 year from their initial time of injury were retrospectively identified for study inclusion. Range of motion, and Knee Society Scores were evaluated for all patients. Perioperative complications as well as TKA component types and degrees of implant constraint were also analyzed.
RESULTS: Twelve patients met study inclusion criteria. Mean follow-up time was 40 months (range 24 to 86 mos). Mean time from MLKI to TKA was 5 months (range 3 days to 11 months). Mean age was 61 years (range 51 to 78). Mean postoperative knee range of motion was 1-106 degrees at last follow-up. Knee Society Scores improved by an average of 129 points at last follow-up. Two patients required rotating hinge TKA components with all others requiring lesser degrees of implant constraint. There were no instances of postoperative knee instability and no patients required revision TKA surgery at last follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: TKA is a viable primary treatment option for MLKI in older patients with pre-existing multicompartmental knee osteoarthritis. In this patient population, TKA may allow for improved function and adequate stability of the multiligament injured knee.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective case series.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV.

articles.title: Transperineal Ultrasound Assessment of Fetal Head Descent and Successful Manual Rotation in Women Undergoing Labor With Neuraxial Analgesia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Manual rotation is commonly used to correct fetal head malrotation during labor. This study assessed the effectiveness of manual rotation under neuraxial analgesia and evaluated whether transperineal ultrasound (TUS)-derived parameters were associated with procedural success and could provide additional information when considering manual rotation.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 59 women with fetal rotational abnormalities during labor under neuraxial analgesia at a tertiary care center. Rotational abnormalities were defined as occiput posterior or occiput transverse positions with a midline angle (MLA) ≥ 45°, assessed 1 h after full cervical dilation. Manual rotation success was defined as correction to an MLA < 45°. Delivery, maternal, neonatal, and TUS-derived parameters were compared between successful and unsuccessful cases.
RESULTS: Manual rotation was successful in 44 of 59 cases (74.5%). The vaginal delivery rate was significantly higher in the successful group than in the unsuccessful group (90.9% vs. 46.7%, p < 0.001). No significant differences were noted in maternal or neonatal outcomes. Among TUS parameters, only the TUS-station was significantly associated with procedural success. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified a cutoff of 14.3 mm, above which the likelihood of successful rotation was 95.8%. In exploratory logistic regression models, TUS-station remained associated with successful manual rotation after adjustment for clinically relevant covariates.
CONCLUSIONS: Manual rotation performed under neuraxial analgesia was associated with a high-procedural success rate. A TUS-station ≥ 14.3 mm was associated with a high likelihood of successful manual rotation and may provide complementary information when considering the procedure, although further validation is required.

articles.title: Effects of remimazolam on postoperative delirium in adults undergoing general anesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Benzodiazepines have traditionally been associated with postoperative delirium (POD), but the effect of remimazolam on POD remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the incidence of POD and perioperative safety outcomes associated with remimazolam in adults undergoing general anesthesia. We searched databases from inception through April 27, 2025, and included randomized controlled trials and non-randomized studies comparing remimazolam with conventional anesthetic agents in adults undergoing general anesthesia. The primary outcome was POD incidence, and secondary outcomes comprised perioperative safety measures. We assessed the certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Seventeen studies involving 3,180 patients were included. POD incidence did not differ significantly between the remimazolam and control groups (risk ratio [RR], 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.71-1.09; I2 = 0%). Similarly, the incidence of intraoperative hypotension did not differ significantly between groups (RR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.56-1.06). Remimazolam was associated with lower incidences of vasopressor administration (RR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.41-0.93) and bradycardia (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.62-0.99). Time to eye opening and the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting did not differ significantly between groups. The certainty of evidence was very low for POD and low or moderate for secondary outcomes. POD incidence did not differ significantly between remimazolam and conventional anesthetic agents in adults undergoing general anesthesia. Some secondary outcomes suggested a potentially favorable hemodynamic profile; however, the evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Further trials using standardized POD assessment tools and prespecified hemodynamic endpoints are warranted.

articles.title: Cohort profile: The Mental Health, Resilience, and Immune System in Transplantation (MeRIT) cohort of living-donor transplant recipients and donors in Korea.
articles.abstract: The Mental Health, Resilience, and Immune System in Transplantation (MeRIT) cohort was established to investigate psychological health, biological responses, and clinical outcomes in living-donor transplant recipients and donors during the perioperative and early post-transplant periods. Recruitment began at Severance Hospital in Seoul, Korea, in November 2024 and is ongoing through December 2026. By July 23, 2026, 651 participants had enrolled: 187 kidney recipients, 106 liver recipients, 202 kidney donors, and 156 liver donors. Recipients are assessed at admission, before discharge, 1 month after discharge, and 6 months after surgery; donors are assessed at admission, before discharge, and 6 months after surgery. Core mental health outcomes, loneliness, and family functioning are assessed repeatedly in both groups, while resilience and other psychosocial characteristics are assessed at baseline. Recipients also undergo assessments of cognitive function, heart rate variability, and immune and inflammatory biomarkers, with wearable monitoring limited to kidney recipients. Clinical information is linked from electronic medical records. The MeRIT cohort enables research into psychological adaptation and its relationships with biological and clinical outcomes. Access to de-identified data or collaborative analyses may be considered after the MeRIT study team reviews research proposals and applicable institutional procedures are followed.

articles.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: clinical evidence and mechanistic perspectives.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are common neurological complications in older surgical patients and are associated with impaired recovery, loss of independence, and worse quality of life. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a non-invasive neuromodulatory intervention with plausible effects on inflammatory, autonomic, sleep, pain, and cognitive-network pathways.
METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review of direct perioperative randomized clinical evidence and, when outcomes were sufficiently comparable, an exploratory meta-analysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 5 August 2026. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Mechanistic and translational evidence was synthesized separately using a structured narrative approach.
RESULTS: Four randomized trials enrolled or randomized 480 participants, of whom 469 contributed to reported analyses. Two trials involving 220 participants assessed related but non-identical early postoperative cognitive-decline constructs: one used dNCR and the other investigator-defined traditional POCD. Both studies individually favored taVNS, and the individual study estimates were treated as the primary evidence. A post hoc exploratory cross-construct synthesis yielded an RR of 0.34 (95% CI 0.18-0.64). Because the contributing trials used non-equivalent cognitive definitions, stimulation regimens, and comparator conditions, this secondary pooled estimate should not be interpreted as representing either a single standardized cognitive outcome or the effect of a single standardized taVNS intervention. A separate multicenter trial reported postoperative delirium in 12.0% versus 25.3% of participants (risk ratio 0.47, 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.98), and another trial showed more favorable postoperative Montreal Cognitive Assessment trajectories. Beyond clinical outcomes, the broader mechanistic literature supports a multilevel neurophysiological rationale for taVNS, consistent with possible modulation of auricular vagal afferent-nucleus tractus solitarius signaling, locus coeruleus and autonomic regulation, inflammatory reflex pathways, splenic sympathetic-cholinergic immune modulation, blood-brain barrier/neurovascular unit protection, glial responses, sleep-arousal regulation, and cognitive-network plasticity. However, most mechanistic evidence remains derived from preclinical or non-perioperative studies, and no causal pathway linking target engagement to cognitive improvement has been established.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence suggests a promising but preliminary clinical signal for taVNS in perioperative neurocognitive disorders. However, certainty remains low to very low, and routine clinical implementation is not yet supported. Available adverse-event data are insufficient to establish perioperative safety or to exclude uncommon cardiovascular or autonomic adverse events. Standardized PND outcomes, credible sham conditions, optimized stimulation dose and timing, systematic adverse-event ascertainment, multimodal target-engagement biomarkers, and risk-enriched confirmatory trials are priorities for future development.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261468039, Identifier: CRD420261468039.

articles.title: Hemorrhagic complications following open surgical biopsy in pediatric liver tumors: 3 cases, a review of literature and a plea for image-guided core needle biopsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histopathological confirmation remains an important component of the diagnostic workup of pediatric liver tumors. Despite the growing consensus that image-guided core needle biopsy is the least traumatic strategy, open surgical biopsy or intraoperative tumor manipulation is still performed in a selected group of patients. The potential complications associated with surgical manipulation of pediatric liver tumors may be underappreciated in current diagnostic algorithms.
METHODS: Here, we report three consecutive cases of children referred to our tertiary pediatric liver center following severe hemorrhagic complications and requiring intensive care management after open surgical biopsy or manipulation. A narrative review of the literature regarding pediatric liver tumor biopsy was performed, focusing on indications, technical considerations, periinterventional management, and rescue management.
RESULTS: All three children developed severe hemorrhagic complications following open surgical biopsy or manipulation of a liver tumor. Complications included hemorrhage and coagulopathy, which required abdominal packing, temporary abdominal wall non-closure, mechanical ventilation and intensive care treatment, sequentially leading to referral to our pediatric liver center. One child developed hemorrhagic shock with acute liver and kidney failure and required high-urgency liver transplantation for hepatoblastoma. Final diagnoses were hepatoblastoma, hepatocellular neoplasm not otherwise specified (HCN-NOS) and malignant rhabdoid tumor of the liver.
CONCLUSION: Open surgical biopsy of pediatric liver tumors should not be regarded as a minor diagnostic procedure. If feasible, biopsy should be carefully planned in a multidisciplinary setting and performed as image-guided core needle biopsy with coaxial technique, controlled pediatric anesthesia and a predefined hemorrhage rescue pathway. Avoiding open biopsy whenever feasible may significantly improve patient safety.

articles.title: Association of multidisciplinary perioperative enhanced recovery pathways with perioperative outcomes in pediatric scoliosis correction surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary perioperative enhanced recovery pathways are increasingly utilized in pediatric scoliosis correction surgery, yet the robustness of their pooled outcome estimates compared to usual care remains inadequately characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the pathway-level associations of these protocols with both clinical and operational outcomes.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception through March 31, 2026. Eligible studies compared structured multidisciplinary pathways with usual care in pediatric scoliosis populations. Outcomes included postoperative complications, 30-day unplanned readmission, operative duration, and length of hospital stay. Outcome definitions and ascertainment were extracted as reported by the original studies, including the reported follow-up period and measurement reference point where available. Because postoperative complications could encompass clinically heterogeneous events and length of hospital stay could be influenced by institution-specific discharge criteria and measurement conventions, no post hoc uniform definition was imposed across studies; relevant differences in outcome ascertainment were considered when interpreting the pooled evidence. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and weighted mean differences (WMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were derived using random-effects models. Given the inherent methodological heterogeneity of real-world observational data, restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation with Knapp-Hartung adjustment was applied as a prespecified sensitivity analysis for outcomes demonstrating extreme statistical heterogeneity (I2 > 90%). DerSimonian-Laird was the primary analysis for all outcomes.
RESULTS: Twenty studies were included in the review, with different subsets contributing to each outcome-specific meta-analysis. Twelve studies (n = 1,874) revealed no statistically significant association with postoperative complications (OR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.43 to 1.31; I2 = 34.5%). Seven studies (n = 1,386) demonstrated no statistically significant association with 30-day readmissions (OR: 1.21; 95% CI: 0.73 to 2.02; I2 = 0.0%). While the primary DerSimonian-Laird analysis showed a significant reduction in operative duration (WMD: -26.05 min; 95% CI: -48.54 to -3.55), this finding became statistically non-significant under the more conservative REML with Knapp-Hartung adjustment (WMD: -22.46 min; 95% CI: -59.23 to 14.32; p = 0.197). In contrast, fifteen studies demonstrated a statistically significant but uncertain association with length of hospital stay (WMD: -1.75 days; 95% CI: -2.18 to -1.32; p < 0.001), which remained robust after conservative adjustment (p < 0.001). Extreme heterogeneity (I2 > 95%) was observed for all continuous outcomes, and significant publication bias was detected for length of hospital stay (Egger's test, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis provides a quantitative signal that multidisciplinary enhanced recovery pathways are associated with a reduced length of hospital stay, suggesting an improvement in perioperative discharge efficiency. However, the evidence for reduced operative duration is statistically fragile and inconclusive, and no statistically significant associations were found for complications or readmissions. The overall certainty of the evidence is very low due to the predominance of retrospective designs, extreme heterogeneity, and publication bias.

articles.title: Wide-awake local anaesthesia without routine tourniquet for cubital tunnel surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cubital tunnel surgery is performed under general or regional anaesthesia. Wide-awake local anaesthesia no tourniquet (WALANT) may reduce anaesthetic dependency, postoperative pain and resource use while permitting active assessment of ulnar nerve stability. We evaluated clinical outcomes, anaesthetic feasibility and reported complications.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidance (PROSPERO CRD420261407435), MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from inception to June 2026, with CENTRAL additionally searched in September 2026. Comparative and uncontrolled studies of decompression, medial epicondylectomy or anterior transposition under awake local infiltration without routine tourniquet inflation were included. Meta-analysis was undertaken where sufficiently comparable data were available.
RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 535 participants were included: 328 participants entered an eligible awake-local or intended-WALANT intervention arm and 207 received comparator anaesthesia. The 328 intervention-arm participants accounted for 330 procedures because two participants underwent bilateral surgery. Three non-randomised comparative studies involving 111 participants did not demonstrate clear evidence of a difference in patient-reported disability between awake local and comparator anaesthesia (standardised mean difference 0.13, 95% confidence interval -0.24 to 0.51; I2 = 0%). Revision or reoperation events were sparse and were not quantitatively pooled because follow-up duration, operative procedure and treatment pathways differed materially between studies. Individual studies reported lower early postoperative pain and shorter perioperative pathways. Supplemental infiltration was sometimes required, and seven of 40 patients in one intended-WALANT cohort ultimately received general anaesthesia, although the timing of pathway alteration was unclear. Reported adverse events were uncommon but inconsistently ascertained.
CONCLUSIONS: Awake local anaesthesia without routine tourniquet inflation appears feasible for selected patients. Available non-randomised comparative evidence has not demonstrated a clear difference in medium-term patient-reported function between awake-local and comparator anaesthetic pathways. Some studies reported lower early postoperative pain and shorter perioperative pathways, but these findings remain susceptible to confounding. Current evidence does not establish superior neurological recovery, lower revision risk or definitive safety.

articles.title: Predictive models for prolonged hospitalization following major hemorrhage: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This retrospective study aimed to identify the perioperative risk factors associated with prolonged hospital stays in patients undergoing hemostatic resuscitation for intraoperative massive bleeding.
METHODS: The retrospective analysis included clinical data from 119 patients who received intraoperative resuscitation for intraoperative massive hemorrhage. Patients were divided into two groups based on length of hospital stay, using the 3rd quartile as the cutoff (> 26 days vs. ≤ 26 days). The Mann-Whitney U test or independent samples t-test analyzed the influence of categorical variables on hospital stay. Chi-square test was used for count data, and continuous variables were analyzed using Spearman correlation. Risk factors prolonging hospitalization were identified and predictive models developed.
RESULTS: Multivariate analysis revealed that independent risk factors for prolonged hospitalization following major hemorrhage comprised unplanned reoperation (OR = 6.743, P = 0.008), admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) (OR = 9.294, P = 0.020), impaired renal function (OR = 11.554, P < 0.001), Postoperative pulmonary inflammation (OR = 4.696, P = 0.018) and body mass index (BMI) (OR = 10.030, P = 0.046). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the constructed predictive model was 0.908.
CONCLUSION: Our study identified potentially risk factors, like BMI and abnormal kidney function, prolonging hospitalization after intraoperative massive hemorrhage. The predictive model may aid in identifying high-risk patients needing aggressive management to minimize complications. However, it is imperative to conduct prospective, high-quality research in order to validate our findings in the future.

articles.title: Modified geriatric nutritional risk index as a prognostic indicator for patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma undergoing liver resection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The modified Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (mGNRI), which incorporates C-reactive protein (CRP) level and ideal body weight ratio, has been proposed as a prognostic indicator for survival in certain cancers. This study evaluated its association with outcomes in patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) undergoing hepatectomy.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 99 patients with ICC who underwent hepatectomy between April 2008 and August 2022. The optimal mGNRI cut-off (88.2) determined by receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, classified patients into low and high mGNRI groups.
RESULTS: Forty-five patients (45.5%) were in the low mGNRI group, and 54 (54.5%) were in the high mGNRI group. The low mGNRI group had a significantly lower body mass index (BMI) and hemoglobin and serum albumin levels, but higher CRP levels compared with the high mGNRI group. Recurrence-free survival (RFS; hazard ratio [HR]: 2.09, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.29-3.39, p = 0.003) and overall survival (OS; HR: 2.25, 95% CI: 1.32-3.83, p = 0.003) were both worse in the low mGNRI group than in the high mGNRI group. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that a low mGNRI was an independent prognostic factor for OS (HR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.03-3.37, p = 0.041). Postoperative dietary intake was significantly lower in the low vs. the high mGNRI group.
CONCLUSIONS: The mGNRI has a prognostic impact on patients with ICC after hepatectomy. Patients with a low mGNRI showed poorer survival and a lower postoperative oral energy adequacy ratio, highlighting the importance of perioperative nutritional assessment in this population.

articles.title: Association between the preoperative geriatric nutritional risk index and 90-day complications after open radical cystectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer requiring radical cystectomy is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity, particularly in elderly patients. This study evaluated the predictive capacity of the preoperative Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) for 90-day complications following open radical cystectomy with ileal conduit urinary diversion.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 80 consecutive patients who underwent open radical cystectomy and exclusively ileal conduit urinary diversion (100.0%) between November 2022 and December 2025. Preoperative GNRI was calculated from serum albumin and body weight metrics. Multivariable analysis was conducted using a 3-covariate Firth's penalized logistic regression model. An empirical threshold (GNRI < 94.5) derived from ROC analysis was evaluated alongside continuous GNRI scores.
RESULTS: The overall 90-day complication rate was 82.5% (66/80). Mean preoperative GNRI was 94.81 ± 7.24. The ROC-derived optimal cutoff for overall complications was GNRI < 94.5 (AUC = 0.628, Sensitivity: 71.2%, Specificity: 57.1%). While continuous GNRI was not an independent predictor of total complications in multivariable analysis (OR: 1.052 per 1-unit decrease, 95% CI: 0.948-1.168, p = 0.342), patients with GNRI < 94.5 exhibited significantly higher rates of specific severe morbidity subtypes, including infectious complications (67.7% vs. 34.7%, OR: 3.95, p = 0.004), gastrointestinal complications (74.2% vs. 36.7%, OR: 4.95, p = 0.001), and cardiovascular adverse events (25.8% vs. 4.1%, OR: 8.17, p = 0.005). Advanced pathological stage (≥pT3) remained the sole independent predictor of overall 90-day morbidity (OR: 4.187, p = 0.024).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative GNRI is not an independent predictor of overall 90-day post-cystectomy complications; however, lower GNRI values (<94.5) strongly correlate with organ-specific infectious, gastrointestinal, and cardiovascular morbidity. GNRI serves as a valuable, objective screening tool within Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways to trigger targeted perioperative prehabilitation and nutritional optimization.

articles.title: Beyond blood glucose targets: integrating glucose variability into acute glycemic care in French ICUs - a multicenter prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although hyperglycemia is a common adaptative response in hospitalized intensive care units (ICUs) patients, there are no recommendations regarding blood glucose management protocols. Consequently, practices differ between ICUs. We aimed to prospectively describe glucose management in French-speaking ICUs with the main objective to assess the impact of glucose management on glucose variability within the first 48 h of insulin infusion.
RESULTS: A total of 650 patients from 38 ICUs across France and Belgium were included with 649 patients analyzed. Management with tighter glucose targets did not result in an increase in Glycemic Lability Index (OR 0.79, 95% CI [0.51-1.21]; p = 0.28) but episodes of severe hypoglycemia were more frequent in tight blood glucose control group. Nurse workload did not impact glucose variability significantly. Deviations from the protocol were frequent in 24.9% of cases, independently to the blood glucose target used. Percentage spent in the target range was significantly higher in the liberal group (p < 0.01). ICU mortality rate was higher in patients who had at least one episode of hypoglycemia <3.9 mmol/L (p = 0.04), and lower in patients with at least one episode of hyperglycemia >11.1 mmol/L (p = 0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite heterogenous practices through French speaking ICUs, management with tight blood glucose targets did not significantly impact glucose variability but was associated with higher incidence of severe hypoglycemia.

articles.title: Direct anterior versus conventional approaches for hemiarthroplasty in femoral neck fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of functional outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Femoral neck fracture (FNF) in older adults is associated with morbidity and functional decline. The optimal surgical approach for hemiarthroplasty (HA) remains uncertain. The direct anterior approach (DAA), a muscle-sparing technique, may improve early recovery compared with conventional approaches. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared DAA with conventional approaches following HA for FNF.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched through December 2025 according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Comparative studies of DAA versus conventional approaches were included. The primary outcome was Harris Hip Score (HHS); secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, operative time, blood loss, transfusion, and hospital stay. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251270460).
RESULTS: Forty-two studies involving 7582 patients were included. Three studies contributed to early HHS analysis, showing no significant difference between approaches (MD, 1.38; 95% CI, -4.85 to 7.60; I2 = 77.2%). Similarly, three studies at mid-term follow-up showed no significant difference (MD, 1.04; 95% CI, -3.67 to 5.76; I2 = 67.8%). Only 1 study provided quantitatively evaluable long-term HHS data (MD, 0.70; 95% CI, -2.41 to 3.81). DAA was associated with lower postoperative pain (SMD, -0.38; 95% CI, -0.72 to -0.05; P = 0.02), lower blood loss (MD, -61.0 mL; 95% CI, -103.2 to -18.9 mL; P < 0.01), and shorter hospital stay (MD, -1.12 days; 95% CI, -1.78 to -0.46; P = 0.001). Operative time was longer with DAA (MD, 9.6 min; 95% CI, 6.2 to 13.0 min; P < 0.001), while transfusion requirements were comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: DAA was associated with modest perioperative benefits following HA for FNF. However, HHS analyses did not demonstrate statistically significant functional differences at early or mid-term follow-up, and long-term evidence was limited. Sustained functional superiority of DAA remains uncertain.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III (systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised and observational comparative studies).

articles.title: Effect of lung transplantation on biventricular function in pulmonary arterial hypertension: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) leads to progressive right ventricular (RV) failure and secondary left ventricular (LV) dysfunction due to chronic pressure overload and ventricular interdependence. Lung transplantation (LTx) is an established treatment for end-stage PAH, yet patterns of biventricular recovery and the role of veno-arterial perioperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) remain incompletely defined. A PubMed search identified studies published from 1990 to 2025 using MeSH terms related to lung transplantation, ventricular function, echocardiography, cardiac MRI, and ECMO. Prospective studies, retrospective analyses, and case series evaluating post-transplant cardiac function in PAH were included. A total of 13 studies were included. Across studies, LTx resulted in rapid and substantial RV reverse remodeling, with improvements in RV size, mass, systolic function, tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary pressures. This reduction in RV afterload was accompanied by progressive improvement of RV output. In contrast, LV recovery was more variable, possibly due to chronic underfilling and LV remodeling. Cardiac MRI and echocardiography demonstrated progressive biventricular structural and functional adaptation over time. Perioperative VA-ECMO may provide hemodynamic support during this transition by unloading the RV and maintaining perfusion while ventricular loading conditions rapidly change. Lung transplantation for PAH initiates transition from chronic RV pressure overload and LV underfilling to improved pulmonary vascular conditions and subsequent biventricular recovery. Further longitudinal studies are needed to identify predictors of maladaptive LV responses and determine which patients may benefit from prolonged perioperative VA-ECMO support.

articles.title: Serial Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio and Mortality in Culture-Positive Pediatric Postoperative Sepsis Following Congenital Heart Surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between serial neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) measurements and in-hospital mortality in children with culture-positive postoperative sepsis following congenital heart surgery.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: Tertiary pediatric cardiac surgical center.
PARTICIPANTS: Microbiologically confirmed postoperative sepsis developed in 237 of 2,458 children who underwent congenital heart surgery between 2018 and 2022. At the time of sepsis evaluation (T2), patients with infection-associated organ dysfunction and a Phoenix Sepsis Score ≥ 2 were classified as having postoperative sepsis and were eligible for inclusion. Eight patients with unavailable follow-up NLR data through day 14 were excluded, leaving 229 patients for analysis.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: NLR was measured preoperatively (T1), at sepsis diagnosis (T2), and on days 7 (T3) and 14 (T4). Among 229 patients, 66 (28.8%) died during hospitalization. NLR was significantly higher in nonsurvivors at T2, T3, and T4, with day 7 NLR showing the highest discriminatory performance for mortality (area under the curve, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.67-0.81). The Phoenix Sepsis Score showed a weak positive correlation with concurrent NLR at sepsis diagnosis (ρ = 0.252, p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each unit increase in NLR at T2 (odds ratio [OR], 1.06; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; p = 0.018) and T3 (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; p = 0.012) was independently associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Serial NLR measurements, particularly during the first week after sepsis diagnosis, were independently associated with in-hospital mortality and may provide complementary prognostic information in pediatric patients with postoperative sepsis after congenital heart surgery.

articles.title: Shoulder Dislocation Reduction Using Inhaled Nitrous Oxide in the Emergency Department: Retrospective Case Series.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inhaled nitrous oxide (iNO) offers rapid onset analgesia with a favorable safety profile yet remains underused for shoulder dislocation reductions in the emergency department (ED). The objective of this study was to evaluate the use and outcomes of iNO for shoulder reduction in the ED, including whether intravenous (IV) access was required, whether successful reduction could be accomplished without additional analgesic or sedative medications under procedural sedation, and the rate of adverse effects from iNO.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of shoulder dislocation reductions using iNO at two high-volume EDs over three years (2019-2022).
