Data collected included age, sex, indication, procedural success, IV placement, medications administered, and adverse events and was stored in a password-protected database. The primary endpoint was successful reduction with iNO as the primary procedural analgesic; secondary endpoint was occurrence of any adverse events.
RESULTS: Of 138 patients, 125 (90.6%; 95% CI, 0.84-0.95) achieved successful reduction with iNO alone without escalation to procedural sedation; 102 patients (74%) did not require IV access. Adverse events were rare (2/138 or 1.4% [95% CI, 0.02-0.05]): one patient experienced transient agitation (a known side effect of N-methyl-D-aspartate antagonism), and one had vomiting. Both were self-limited without hemodynamic changes.
CONCLUSION: This retrospective case series, the largest of its kind to date examining iNO for shoulder dislocation reduction, demonstrated a 90.6% success rate with minimal adverse events and reduced resource utilization compared to procedural sedation. These findings support further prospective investigation of iNO for shoulder dislocation as well as other orthopedic reductions and painful ED procedures.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Low-Dose Ketamine Infusion for Pain Management after Cardiac Surgery:A Single Center Pre-Post Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether the addition of continuous low-dose ketamine infusion to an enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocol reduces postoperative opioid consumption and improves pain control after cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, before-and-after cohort study with propensity score matching.
SETTING: University-affiliated tertiary care hospital cardiothoracic intensive care unit.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery and admitted postoperatively to the cardiothoracic intensive care unit between June 2023 and January 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients managed under an ERAS protocol without ketamine (control) were compared with patients managed under ERAS plus a continuous postoperative low-dose ketamine infusion (0.1-0.3 mg/kg/h).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was opioid consumption in morphine milligram equivalents (MME) from postoperative day (POD) 0-2. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, time to first analgesic, recovery metrics, length of stay, and adverse events. Of 548 screened patients, 244 were included after propensity matching (122 ketamine, 122 control). Ketamine was associated with lower cumulative opioid use through POD2 (30 vs 52.5 MME; p = 0.003), with reductions on POD0 and POD1. Time to first analgesic was longer (7.4 vs 4.5 h; p < 0.001), and maximum pain scores were lower across the first 48 hours (all p < 0.05). Intensive care unit length of stay was modestly longer, while hospital length of stay was shorter in the ketamine group. No hallucinations were observed, delirium rates were low, and urinary retention was significantly reduced (9.8% vs 34%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Within an ERAS pathway after cardiac surgery, low-dose ketamine infusion was associated with reduced opioid use and improved early postoperative pain control without increased central nervous system adverse events, supporting its role as a safe adjunct in postoperative analgesia.

articles.title: Stone Characteristics and Surgical Treatment Patterns Among Patients With Urolithiasis at a Brazilian Referral Hospital: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urolithiasis is a common and recurrent disorder that can cause obstruction, infection, renal impairment, repeated emergency care, and the need for surgical intervention. Real-world treatment patterns may help referral centers understand case mix and plan endourological resources.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the institutional surgical case mix of patients undergoing operative treatment for urolithiasis at a Brazilian nonprofit teaching hospital. Secondary exploratory analyses assessed the associations of stone location and stone size with the primary surgical procedure performed.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 624 unique patients aged 16 years or older who underwent rigid ureteroscopy, flexible ureterorenoscopy, or percutaneous nephrolithotomy between June 1 and December 31, 2025. Demographic, stone-related, operative, anesthetic, and ureteral stent variables were extracted from institutional records. Three secondary exploratory contingency analyses evaluated procedure versus stone location, procedure versus stone size, and stone location versus stone size using Pearson's chi-square tests; Cramer's V quantified effect size. Analyses involving missing stone size or location used complete cases.
RESULTS: Men accounted for 361 patients (57.9%), and mean age was 46.6 ± 13.8 years. Flexible ureterorenoscopy was the most frequent primary procedure (436; 69.9%), followed by rigid ureteroscopy (147; 23.6%) and percutaneous nephrolithotomy (41; 6.6%). Spinal anesthesia, alone or with sedation, was used in 559 patients (89.6%), and a double-J stent was used in 448 (71.8%). Procedure distribution varied markedly according to stone location (χ2(4) = 1108.77, p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.946; n = 619) and stone size (χ2(6) = 301.23, p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.505; n = 591). Stone size and location were also associated (χ2(6) = 323.63, p < 0.001; Cramer's V = 0.525; n = 588).
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical care was dominated by minimally invasive endourological procedures. Procedure distribution varied markedly according to stone location and size. These findings describe the operative case mix of a Brazilian referral hospital and may support service planning and future prospective quality studies.

articles.title: Low platelets, high stakes: pregnancy after a diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract: Many patients live with chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) during their reproductive years and may desire to become pregnant or may unexpectedly become pregnant. Although patients should be educated about potential risks to both the mother and child in such cases, a healthy pregnancy with good outcomes is still possible. In this review, we address topics spanning the pregnancy journey from preconception through the postdelivery period for patients with ITP. We recommend that reproductive plans be addressed proactively to allow for ITP treatment optimization for pregnancy. This may involve discontinuation of therapies with known fetal toxicity risks, such as fostamatinib, determining the timing of rituximab use or splenectomy, and adjusting for chronic therapies, such as thrombopoietin receptor agonists. The risk of bleeding with ITP is not higher during pregnancy, but thrombocytopenia often requires treatment to minimize delivery-related hemorrhagic risk or allow neuraxial anesthesia. Prednisone and IV immunoglobulin are effective for these purposes in most patients. There is evolving evidence to support the role of rituximab and romiplostim. We lack biomarkers to predict the severity of thrombocytopenia in both mothers and fetuses/neonates and to predict response to treatment. Similarly, there are limited data on patient-reported outcomes and mental health needs among patients who are pregnant and caring for their infant while managing their ITP. Care standardization and harmonization among different specialists for pregnant patients with ITP remains an unmet need.

articles.title: Comparison of the effects of normal saline versus Plasma-Lyte® on acid-base balance during living donor kidney transplantation surgery using goal-directed fluid therapy based on pulse pressure variation- a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Normal saline (NS) is commonly used during kidney transplantation but may cause hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis when administered in large volumes. Balanced crystalloids such as Plasma-Lyte® (PL) may attenuate these effects. We compared acid-base outcomes of NS versus PL when administered using pulse pressure variation (PPV)- guided goal-directed fluid therapy during living donor kidney transplantation (LDKT).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective randomised assessor-blinded trial, adult patients undergoing LDKT were allocated to receive intraoperative NS or PL. Fluid administration was titrated according to a predefined PPV-guided algorithm. Acid-base status was assessed using the Stewart physicochemical analysis. The primary endpoint was the difference in apparent strong ion difference (SIDa). Secondary outcome measurements included haemodynamics, electrolytes, lactate, serum creatinine trends, dialysis requirement, and graft function.
RESULTS: A total of 111 patients were analysed (NS, n = 55, PL, n = 56). Baseline characteristics and total intraoperative fluid volumes were comparable (1796 ± 337 vs 1903 ± 434 mL; p = 0.15). Apparent strong ion difference declined over time in both groups (time effect p < 0.001), but did not differ between groups (group effect p = 0.50; interaction p = 0.37). In the baseline-adjusted analysis (ANCOVA) of the primary endpoint, the adjusted between-group difference in SIDa at the end of surgery was 0.71 mmol/L (90% CI - 0.90 to + 2.32 mmol/L) against the pre-specified equivalence margin of ± 2 mmol/L; formal equivalence was not established, although no significant difference was detected (adjusted p = 0.46). Effective strong ion difference (SID e), strong ion gap (SIG), pH, serum potassium, and lactate were similar at all measured time points (p > 0.05). Early graft dysfunction (4.1% vs 7.4%; p = 0.472) and delayed graft function (3.6% vs 0%; p = 0.150) did not differ significantly; however, the trial was not powered for these exploratory outcomes. Postoperative creatinine trajectories did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSION: During LDKT, PPV-guided goal-directed fluid therapy produced no significant between-group difference in acid-base balance or early graft outcomes with NS and PL. Formal equivalence in the primary endpoint was not established; nonetheless, at the moderate volumes delivered, the findings suggest that haemodynamic strategy may influence perioperative acid-base status more than crystalloid choice.
CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION DETAILS: The study was prospectively registered in the Clinical Trials Registry of India (ctri.nic.in) Registration number: CTRI/2021/01/030227 Registered on 04/01/2021.

articles.title: A retrospective study of the clinical efficacy of arthroscopic double-row and single-row suture-bridge techniques for rotator cuff tears.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The comparative efficacy of single-row (SR) and double-row (DR) suture-bridge techniques in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair remains controversial, particularly with regard to optimal patient selection. This study aimed to compare the early clinical outcomes of the two techniques and, importantly, to perform subgroup analyses according to tear size to identify the patient populations most likely to benefit from the DR technique.
METHODS: A total of 144 patients were retrospectively assigned to the DR group (n = 73) or SR group (n = 71) according to the surgical technique used. Perioperative parameters, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, Constant-Murley scores (CMS), American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) scores, University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) shoulder scores, and range of motion (ROM) were compared between the two groups before surgery and at the final follow-up. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed 12 months postoperatively to assess the rotator cuff retear rate. Subgroup analyses were conducted after stratification into small-to-medium (SM) and large-to-massive (LM) tear groups.
RESULTS: Operative time and intraoperative blood loss were greater in the DR group than in the SR group, with statistically significant differences between the groups (P = 0.007). Postoperatively, functional scores and VAS scores improved significantly from baseline in both groups (P < 0.05). Compared with the SR group, the DR group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in VAS, CMS, UCLA, and ASES scores (all P < 0.001). Assessment of shoulder ROM and imaging outcomes also showed significantly greater improvements in the DR group than in the SR group (P < 0.05). Subgroup analysis revealed that the functional benefits of the DR technique were primarily attributable to patients with LM tears, in whom the improvements exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). In contrast, for patients with SM tears, the clinical relevance of the observed between-group differences was less definitive.
CONCLUSION: Arthroscopic double-row suture-bridge repair is associated with superior early functional recovery and a lower retear rate than the single-row technique. However, these benefits appear to be driven primarily by outcomes in patients with large-to-massive tears. For small-to-medium tears, the clinically meaningful advantage of the DR technique is less evident, suggesting that tear size may be an important determinant when selecting the surgical repair technique.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury and renal replacement therapy: a critical synthesis of metabolic derangements and nutritional implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects up to 50% of critically ill patients and is frequently complicated by severe metabolic derangements, requiring the initiation of replacement therapy (RRT) in 10-15% of cases. Despite substantial progress in the diagnosis of AKI and optimisation of RRT delivery, the nutritional management of these patients remains an underexplored area.
MAIN BODY: AKI is increasingly recognised as a systemic metabolic disorder extending beyond impaired renal clearance. Key metabolic alterations include mitochondrial dysfunction, dysregulated gluconeogenesis, increased proteolysis and altered amino acid metabolism, with accelerated nitrogen wasting. These abnormalities are further amplified by acute systemic stress states, including sepsis, systemic inflammation, trauma, burns, liver dysfunction and multiorgan failure. RRT introduces additional metabolic consequences through extracorporeal losses of amino acids and micronutrients. Conversely, citrate anticoagulation, glucose-containing dialysate, and lactate-buffered solutions represent sources of clinically relevant calories. Current nutritional recommendations are largely extrapolated from heterogeneous intensive care populations. Available evidence suggests that AKI primarily influences energy balance rather than energy expenditure, which appears broadly comparable to that of other critically ill populations. While evidence specific to AKI is limited, protein provision of approximately 1.2-1.3 g/kg/day is generally recommended during critical illness. However, higher intakes of up to 1.7-2.5 g/kg/day may be considered in patients receiving RRT to offset extracorporeal amino acid losses and increased protein catabolism. In this setting, emerging concepts such as metabolic tolerance and biomarker-guided metabolic phenotyping may facilitate individualised nutritional strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: AKI, particularly when requiring RRT, is associated with profound and dynamic metabolic disturbances that substantially influence energy and protein requirements, thereby making nutrition an integral component of organ support therapies. Future research should evaluate precision nutrition strategies that tailor nutritional support to the phase of critical illness, measured energy expenditure, metabolic tolerance, and RRT-related nutrient losses and gains. Such studies should prioritise patient-centred outcomes, including physical function and recovery, in addition to nutritional and metabolic endpoints.

articles.title: Increasing utilization of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and its association with venous thromboembolism following lung transplant.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common complication following lung transplantation, and perioperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) use has increased substantially over time. The relationship between ECMO exposure and early post-transplant VTE remains incompletely defined.
METHODS: A single center retrospective cohort study of adult lung transplants from 2010 to 2024 was performed. The primary outcome was the occurrence of a deep venous thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) within 14 days of transplant. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE during this time period and Cox proportional hazards models to evaluate the association between early VTE and survival.
RESULTS: Among the 1083 lung transplant recipients, 22% developed VTE within 14 days. The incidence of VTE increased over time (11% in 2010-2013 vs. 38% in 2022-2024, p<0.001), paralleling the increase in ECMO utilization as well as implementation of a screening protocol. In adjusted analysis, both preoperative (adjusted OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.45-5.52) and intraoperative/postoperative ECMO exposures (adjusted OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.52-3.29) were independently associated with VTE. Early VTE was not associated with mortality (adjusted HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.67-1.12).
CONCLUSIONS: Early VTE after lung transplantation is common and has increased over time alongside increasing ECMO utilization. Perioperative ECMO exposure is independently associated with VTE. The findings highlight the need for targeted VTE prevention and surveillance strategies in lung transplant patients receiving ECMO support.

articles.title: Reduced multimodal physiological signal complexity during neurointensive care is associated with delayed cerebral ischaemia and worse functional outcome in aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage: a single-centre retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autonomic dysfunction and reduced signal complexity (SC) may occur after aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) and reflect impaired physiological adaptability. However, the relationships with cerebral physiology, delayed cerebral ischaemia (DCI), and long-term functional outcome remain incompletely understood. This study explores heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and systemic and cerebral SC in aSAH patients during neurointensive care (NIC).
METHODS: This observational, single-centre cohort study included 690 aSAH patients with intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring during the first 10 days post-ictus, treated at Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden (2008-2024). HRV, BRS, and multiscale entropy derived SC of each of heart rate (HR), mean arterial pressure (MAP), ICP, ICP pulse amplitude (AMP), and cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) were analysed using high-frequency monitoring data. Associations with NIC physiology (ICP, CPP, pressure reactivity index [PRx]), DCI, and 12-month Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, two-variable outcome heatmaps, and Spearman's correlations. DCI was defined as new focal neurological deficits or declining consciousness after exclusion of other aetiologies.
RESULTS: In multivariable regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, radiological, and physiological predictors, reduced SC of each of HR, MAP, ICP, AMP, and CPP independently correlated with worse functional outcome, while reduced cerebral SC (of ICP, AMP, and CPP) the first 3 days post-ictus was independently associated with DCI. Reduced SC generally correlated with higher ICP, lower CPP, and higher PRx. Reduced SC combined with high ICP and PRx and low CPP was particularly associated with poor recovery in outcome heatmaps.
CONCLUSION: Reduced SC was independently associated with DCI and worse functional outcome after aSAH. SC may serve as a prognostic marker and a bedside indicator of DCI and vulnerability to secondary insults, with potential to guide more individualised NIC. Prospective, multi-centre studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Outcomes of heart transplantation with or without pre-transplant mechanical circulatory support: a single-center cohort study in Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart transplantation is considered the definitive treatment for patients with end-stage heart failure (HF). Many patients with end-stage HF progress to cardiogenic shock or severe low cardiac output states while on the waiting list and require mechanical circulatory support (MCS) as a bridge to transplantation. The primary endpoint of this study was to assess overall survival after heart transplantation according to pre-transplant MCS use. The secondary outcomes included postoperative complications, intensive care utilization, and perioperative transfusion requirements.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included recipients of heart transplantation. A total of 100 consecutive patients were categorized into three groups according to pre-transplant MCS use (ECMO, LVAD, and non-MCS groups). Follow-up was censored on February 28, 2026.
RESULTS: The mortality was significantly higher and the overall survival was significantly lower in the ECMO group than in the non-MCS group. Overall survival significantly differed among the three groups (log-rank P = 0.001), driven mainly by worse survival in the ECMO group than in the non-MCS group, whereas survival did not significantly differ between the ECMO and LVAD groups.
CONCLUSIONS: The ECMO group showed a significantly worse survival than the non-MCS group, whereas survival did not significantly differ between the ECMO and LVAD groups, which was likely attributed to the small sample size of the LVAD group. Postoperative continuous renal replacement therapy and other markers of organ dysfunction were more frequent in the ECMO group and likely reflected the greater severity of illness in these patients rather than the independent risk factors.

articles.title: Inhaled anesthetics and severe neurologic complications in individuals with Venezuelan maternal ancestry carrying the mitochondrial MT-ND4 m.11232 T > C variant: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Severe neurologic injury after uncomplicated general anesthesia in previously healthy patients is rare. Since 2021, reports from South America and later from North America and Europe have described catastrophic neurologic deterioration and death after routine general anesthesia in children and adults with Venezuelan maternal ancestry. A homoplasmic mitochondrial DNA variant, MT-ND4 m.11232 T > C (p.Leu158Pro), affecting complex I of the electron transport chain, has emerged as the leading candidate susceptibility factor. This systematic review identified, appraised, and synthesized available evidence linking inhaled anesthetics, in particular sevoflurane, with severe perioperative neurologic complications in carriers of this variant and in individuals with Venezuelan maternal ancestry. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261471143), with searches of major biomedical databases, gray literature, and variant databases. The evidence describes a consistent but incompletely characterized syndrome defined by maternal Venezuelan ancestry, apparent preoperative health, predominant sevoflurane exposure, delayed emergence, and severe basal ganglia injury with frequent death. In patient-derived fibroblasts and cybrids, sevoflurane markedly suppressed complex I-dependent respiration, whereas propofol did not. Incidence, penetrance, and agent-specific risk remain uncertain. Cautious perioperative strategies that avoid volatile anesthetics appear justified.

articles.title: Long- versus medium-chain triglycerides in lipid resuscitation therapy for local anesthetic systemic toxicity: Does the length matter? A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Intravenous lipid emulsion (ILE) is the recommended first-line treatment for local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST), particularly when cardiovascular compromise occurs. However, uncertainty persists regarding the optimal lipid formulation, specifically the comparative efficacy of ILEs containing 100% long-chain triglycerides (LCT) versus ILEs containing a 50/50 mixture of medium- and long-chain triglycerides (MCT/LCT), as well as ILEs with a 20% versus 30% lipid concentration. The primary aim of this narrative review was to compare the efficacy of 100% LCT-containing ILEs versus 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs by analyzing their respective mechanisms of action in experimental models of local anesthetic-induced cardiovascular toxicity, whereas the secondary objective was to compare ILEs with a 20% versus a 30% lipid concentration. The review also integrates the physiological rationale underlying lipid resuscitation and explores a mechanistically informed framework for interpreting formulation-specific effects of ILEs. A literature search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar was conducted from January 1998 through January 2026. Twenty experimental studies were identified-nine in vitro, one ex vivo, and ten in vivo-and qualitatively synthesized according to their principal mechanisms of action, including lipid shuttle, cardiotonic, vascular, and metabolic effects. The available experimental evidence suggests that 100% LCT-containing ILEs provide greater overall cardiovascular recovery than 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs, particularly through more effective lipid-shuttle activity and sustained myocardial protection. Conversely, 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs demonstrated greater vascular effects in several experimental models. Evidence comparing lipid concentrations was limited to 100% LCT-containing formulations and generally showed greater pharmacokinetic, hemodynamic, and survival effects with a 30% versus a 20% lipid concentration when administered at the same volume. The available evidence is derived exclusively from heterogeneous preclinical experimental models and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than practice-informing. Triglyceride composition and lipid concentration may influence distinct mechanisms contributing to cardiovascular recovery during LAST. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for exploring formulation-phenotype associations but do not establish formulation-specific treatment recommendations. Further experimental and translational studies are needed to determine whether these mechanistic findings translate into clinically meaningful benefits in patients with LAST.

articles.title: Poorly Controlled Hypertension Alters Coronary Microvascular Contractile Response to Endothelin-1 Before and After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic hypertension have worse outcomes following on-pump (cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass [CP/CPB]) cardiac surgery. Altered vasomotor function of the coronary microvasculature to ET-1 (endothelin-1) and other agonists may underlie these differences.
METHODS: Heart samples were collected from 85 patients undergoing CP/CPB enrolled in this observational study. Ex vivo coronary microvascular responses to ET-1, adenosine diphosphate, and sodium nitroprusside were assessed using video microscopy. Immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and multiomics approaches were also used.
RESULTS: Coronary microvascular contractile response to ET-1 in patients with uncontrolled hypertension was increased compared with the other 2 cohorts pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05 across ET-1 10-10 to 10-7 mmol/L). Adenosine diphosphate-induced coronary microvascular vasodilation was conversely decreased (P<0.05 for adenosine diphosphate 10-5 and 10-4 mmol/L). Post-CP/CPB microvascular responses to ET-1 and adenosine diphosphate were blunted overall (P<0.05). Antagonism of pro-vasoconstrictive endothelinA receptor diminished contractile response (P<0.05). Transcriptomics and proteomics showed wide regulation of pro-vasoconstrictive pathways. Regression showed that hypertension status and cardiac mass reliably approximated ET-1-induced coronary microvascular contraction (R2 0.95 pre-CP/CPB, R2 0.86 post-CP/CPB), which, in turn, estimated change in ejection fraction pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05). Patients with uncontrolled hypertension had -11% change in EF when compared with the other 2 groups pooled (P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Altered coronary microvascular vasomotor function in patients with uncontrolled hypertension may jeopardize myocardial perfusion. Hypertension status and cardiac mass may be used to prognosticate this physiology, which, in turn, estimates change in ejection fraction postoperatively. Perioperative endothelin receptor blockers may benefit patients with uncontrolled hypertension and thus warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization.
RESULTS: Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
CONCLUSIONS: EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Nurse-coordinated multidisciplinary prehabilitation for older adults with frailty undergoing elective transcatheter aortic valve replacement: protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Frailty assessment can identify older adults undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) who are at increased risk of disability and poor functional recovery despite procedural success. A nurse-coordinated, multidisciplinary prehabilitation model may integrate the physical, nutritional, educational and psychological components needed to address these vulnerabilities, but randomised evidence in this population remains limited.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This investigator-initiated, single-centre, assessor-blinded, parallel-group randomised controlled trial will enrol 96 adults aged 65–90 years with an Essential Frailty Toolset score of 3 or greater who are scheduled for elective TAVR. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to usual perioperative care alone or usual care plus a nurse-coordinated prehabilitation programme. The intervention combines supervised aerobic and functional exercise, respiratory training, individualised nutritional optimisation, structured education and psychological support from the day after admission until the day before TAVR. The primary outcomes are 6-minute walk distance within 48 hours before hospital discharge and health-related quality of life assessed using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level at 1 and 3 months after discharge. Secondary outcomes are hospital-associated disability and post-TAVR complications. Additional exploratory and process outcomes include anxiety and depressive symptoms, functional capacity at other time points, hospital costs, feasibility, adherence, acceptability and safety. The primary analysis will follow the intention-to-treat principle.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The Biomedical Ethics Review Committee of West China Hospital, Sichuan University, approved the protocol (approval no. 2025 Review (2324)). The trial was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on 22 May 2026 (ChiCTR2600125252). Results will be submitted to a peer-reviewed journal and presented at scientific conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2600125252.

articles.title: Early versus delayed surgery to prevent hemorrhagic transformation in patients with septic cerebral emboli from infective endocarditis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The optimal timing of cardiac surgery in patients with infective endocarditis and ischemic septic cerebral embolism remains uncertain, largely because of concern for perioperative hemorrhagic transformation. This study evaluates the association between surgical timing and outcomes in this population.
METHODS: Patients with infective endocarditis and preoperative septic cerebral emboli who underwent cardiac surgery were identified from an institutional database (1999-2025). After excluding those with preoperative cerebral hemorrhage, 240 patients with ischemic stroke were stratified by interval from stroke to surgery: early (≤7 days, n=109) versus delayed (8-30 days, n=131). Propensity score matching was used to balance baseline confounders. The primary outcome was postoperative hemorrhagic transformation; secondary outcomes included new postoperative stroke, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay, four-year survival assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis, and mortality assessed by Cox proportional hazards modeling.
RESULTS: Matching yielded 194 patients. Postoperative hemorrhagic transformation occurred in 10 of 194 (5.2%) patients and did not differ by timing (6.2% early vs. 4.1% delayed, p=0.73). New postoperative stroke occurred in 19 of 194 patients (9.8%) and was similar (10.3% early vs. 9.3% delayed, p>0.99), as was 30-day mortality (6.2% early vs. 10.3% delayed, p=0.42). Four-year survival did not differ by timing (68.0% early vs. 57.4% delayed, p=0.07), and there was no significant association between surgical timing and mortality (HR 0.67 [0.44-1.03]; p=0.07).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with infective endocarditis and ischemic stroke, early surgery (≤7 days) was not associated with increased rates of postoperative hemorrhagic transformation, new stroke, or 30-day or long-term mortality compared with delayed surgery.

articles.title: Risk factors associated with in-hospital mortality and a composite of major complications following paediatric congenital cardiac surgery: A systematic review protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 70% of patients born with congenital heart disease (CHD) require medical or surgical treatment in their first year of life. A reported 90-95% will survive to adulthood due to advances in paediatric cardiology, cardiac surgery and anaesthesia. These reported advances are still not available for over 90% of the children born with CHD in low-and middle-income countries (LMIC). The objectives of this study are to determine the pooled incidence of in-hospital all-cause mortality; identify risk factors associated with in-hospital all-cause mortality and a composite of major complications in paediatric patients undergoing congenital cardiac surgery; and to compare these risk factors between LMICs and high-income countries (HICs).
METHODS: A systematic review will be conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines; this has been registered with PROSPERO 2024 (CRD42024618297). The Population, Exposure and Outcome (PEO) framework will guide the search strategy. Eligible studies will include prospective and retrospective cohort studies, case-control studies, interventional studies and registry/database studies reporting risk factors for in-hospital all-cause mortality and/or major postoperative complications in paediatric patients (≤18 years) undergoing cardiac surgery for CHD. A comprehensive electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library and Web of Science will identify peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2000-2026. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data using a standardised data extraction form, and assess risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or ROBINS-I, as appropriate to study design. Where appropriate, we will perform random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled effect measures and 95% confidence intervals. Statistical heterogeneity will be assessed using the I² statistic, and results will otherwise be synthesised narratively. Where sufficient data are available, risk factors will be compared between LMICs and HICs.
DISCUSSION: In-hospital mortality and major complications following paediatric congenital cardiac surgery are associated with a combination of patient-, surgical- and perioperative risk factors. Identifying these facilitates early risk stratification and optimisation of modifiable risk factors to support targeted perioperative interventions and resource allocation, particularly in LMICs where evidence remains limited. A meta-analysis is not anticipated because of substantial heterogeneity in the study population.

articles.title: Underweight and obesity as outcome predictors after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the DOUBLE-CHOICE trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: An "obesity paradox" has been described after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), suggesting lower mortality in patients with higher body mass index (BMI) despite greater comorbidity. In contrast, underweight consistently predicts adverse outcomes. Whether these associations reflect a true biological effect or are primarily driven by residual confounding, frailty, and patient selection remains uncertain.
METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis included eligible patients from the randomized DOUBLE-CHOICE trial comparing two transcatheter heart valves and two anesthesia strategies (minimalist approach with local anesthesia only vs. standard care with conscious sedation). The primary endpoint was a 30-day composite of all-cause mortality, vascular and bleeding complications, infections requiring antibiotic therapy, and neurologic events. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, frailty, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and anesthesia strategy.
RESULTS: Among 752 patients (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, n = 192; BMI < 30 kg/m2, n = 560), obese patients had lower rates of the 30-day primary endpoint (15.2% vs. 27.6%; p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, obesity remained independently associated with lower risk (adjusted OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.002). In contrast, underweight (BMI < 20 kg/m2; n = 23) was associated with a higher incidence of the primary endpoint (55.0% vs. 23.4%; p = 0.003) and remained an independent predictor after adjustment (adjusted OR 3.74, 95% CI 1.30-9.52; p = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: In this randomized TAVI population, obesity was independently associated with favorable 30-day outcomes, whereas underweight identified a small but high-risk subgroup with substantially increased procedural risk. These findings identify underweight as a potential high-risk phenotype requiring further investigation in future studies incorporating more detailed measures of frailty and body composition.

articles.title: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography detection of a mobile echogenic structure at the left atriotomy suture line - A case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) provides real-time anatomical and functional assessment during cardiac surgery and may detect abnormalities that require surgical intervention.
CASE: An 80-year-old woman underwent minimally invasive left atrial myxoma excision combined with a maze procedure under general anesthesia. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, routine TEE revealed a small but highly mobile echogenic structure near the right superior pulmonary vein. The operating surgeon was notified, and external palpation localized the finding to the superior left atriotomy, consistent with a redundant atrial tissue flap protruding through the suture line. Reinforcing sutures were placed to incorporate the flap into the closure and eliminate its protrusion into the left atrium. Repeat TEE confirmed complete disappearance of the lesion. The patient recovered without embolic complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Careful post-bypass TEE examination, including systematic assessment of atriotomy closure sites, may identify potentially embolic mobile echogenic structures and guide surgical management, thereby contributing to perioperative patient safety.

articles.title: Microscope-Assisted Tubular Lumbar Discectomy vs Open Microdiscectomy: A Prospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a leading cause of radiculopathy and disability worldwide. Open microdiscectomy remains the criterion standard, but it requires paraspinal muscle stripping, which may delay recovery. Microscope-assisted tubular discectomy, which combines reusable tubular retractors with a standard operating microscope, is useful in resource-limited settings where endoscopic platforms are unavailable, yet prospective data from such settings are scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether microscope-assisted tubular discectomy is associated with a more favorable perioperative and early recovery profile, with no statistically significant difference in long-term clinical outcomes, compared with open microdiscectomy for single-level LDH.
METHODS: In this prospective comparative study, 150 patients with single-level LDH were enrolled at a tertiary care neurosurgical center (January 2020 to December 2024) and allocated on a nonrandomized basis, determined by operative list scheduling and surgeon availability, to tubular (n = 75) or open microdiscectomy (n = 75). After loss to follow-up, 71 and 72 patients, respectively, were analyzed. All procedures in both arms were performed or directly supervised by a single senior neurosurgeon. Primary outcomes were visual analog scale leg and back pain and Oswestry Disability Index at baseline, 2 weeks, and 3, 6, and 12 months. Secondary outcomes included operative time, blood loss, hospital stay, time to ambulation, and return to work among employed patients. Longitudinal primary outcomes were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models (patient as random intercept; group, time, and group by time as fixed effects). Multivariable regression was adjusted for baseline covariates, and a propensity-score-matched sensitivity analysis was performed to further address confounding from nonrandomized allocation.
RESULTS: Tubular discectomy was associated with shorter operative time (48.5 vs 72.3 minutes), less blood loss (32.4 vs 78.6 mL), shorter hospital stay (1.2 vs 1.8 days), earlier ambulation (0.8 vs 1.2 days), and faster return to work among employed patients (18.0 vs 28.0 days; n = 60 vs 57; all P < 0.001). Linear mixed-effects models showed significantly lower visual analog scale and Oswestry Disability Index scores in the tubular group at 2 weeks and at 3 and 6 months; between-group differences did not exceed established minimum clinically important difference thresholds, and the difference was not statistically significant at 12 months. Complication (11.3% vs 16.7%, P = 0.39) and recurrence rates were comparable; dural tears occurred in 9.9% vs 4.2% (P = 0.19). A propensity-score-matched sensitivity analysis (58 pairs) reproduced the direction and approximate magnitude of these findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Microscope-assisted tubular discectomy offered meaningful perioperative advantages and faster early recovery, with long-term outcomes not significantly different from open microdiscectomy at 12 months. Given the nonrandomized design and the observational nature of the comparison, these findings should be interpreted as evidence of a favorable perioperative profile rather than a demonstration of long-term superiority.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Microscope-assisted tubular discectomy using reusable retractors and a standard operating microscope is a safe and efficient alternative to open microdiscectomy, particularly in resource-constrained environments where endoscopic infrastructure is unavailable.

articles.title: Respiratory-compensated non-contrast vs breath-hold contrast-enhanced MR angiography in pediatric Fontan patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare a highly accelerated ECG-triggered and navigator-gated, non-contrast respiratory-compensated 3D magnetic resonance angiography with Dixon water-fat separation (NC-MRA) to respiratory-suspended non-ECG-triggered multiphase contrast-enhanced MRA (CE-MRA) in pediatric patients with partial or total cavopulmonary connection (PCPC/TCPC).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, between 02/2021 and 09/2023, 30 consecutive pediatric patients (mean age 3.6 ± 0.8 years) with PCPC or TCPC underwent 1.5 T cardiovascular MRI under deep sedation and mechanical ventilation. NC-MRA was acquired before contrast administration alongside standard CE-MRA. Two blinded readers independently evaluated image quality using a 5-point Likert scale and measured vascular diameters of predefined aortic segments, the Glenn anastomosis, Fontan conduit, and pulmonary arteries in consensus. Datasets were presented in randomized order. We used paired statistical testing for method comparison and Cohen's kappa to assess inter-rater agreement.
RESULTS: Mean NC-MRA acquisition time (5:55 ± 2:19 min) was comparable to that of multiphase CE-MRA (5:48 ± 3:03 min), including pre-contrast acquisition p = 0.54). Overall image quality was generally comparable between techniques for most vascular segments (NC-MRA median 5, IQR 5-5, CE-MRA median 5, IQR 4-5, p = 0.06-0.52). No significant differences were found in vascular diameter measurements across all segments (p = 0.06-0.59). Inter-reader agreement was at least substantial (κ > 0.65).
CONCLUSION: Respiratory-compensated NC-MRA at 1.5 T provides image quality and vascular diameter measurements comparable to CE-MRA in pediatric PCPC/TCPC patients. Eliminating breath-holds and contrast administration, the technique simplifies workflow, avoids mechanical ventilation, and improves patient safety in this vulnerable population.
KEY POINTS: Question Is a non-contrast, ECG-triggered, and navigator-gated 3D MRA sequence diagnostically equivalent to conventional breath-hold CE-MRA for vascular assessment in pediatric Fontan patients? Findings There were no significant differences in vascular diameters, and image quality was comparable between both sequences in most segments, showing substantial inter-rater agreement and diagnostic reliability. Clinical relevance Non-contrast, ECG-triggered, and navigator-gated MRA enables reliable vascular assessment in pediatric Fontan patients without gadolinium or breath-holds, reducing anesthesia requirements, improving safety, and simplifying workflow in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Risk prediction for neonatal resuscitation and intensive care admission after cesarean under general anesthesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates delivered by cesarean under general anesthesia (GA) may require resuscitation or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. This study aimed to develop and validate clinical prediction models for these outcomes.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included singleton cesarean deliveries under GA at four tertiary centers from January 2009 to August 2023. Patients were randomly split into development and validation cohorts (7:3). Candidate clinical and anesthesia-related variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, decision curve analysis, and risk stratification.
RESULTS: Among 1523 neonates, 1067 were assigned to the development cohort and 456 to the validation cohort. Neonatal resuscitation occurred in 212 neonates (13.9%), and NICU admission occurred in 482 (31.6%). The resuscitation model yielded development/validation AUCs of 0.834/0.682, versus 0.810/0.773 for NICU admission. Earlier gestational age was a major predictor of both outcomes, with anesthetic regimen, dexamethasone exposure, and gestational diabetes also contributing to risk estimation.
CONCLUSION: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related variables may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and NICU admission risk after cesarean under GA. These models may support neonatal team preparedness and delivery-room resource planning.
IMPACT: Routinely available perinatal and anesthesia-related data may help estimate neonatal resuscitation and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission risk after cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. This multicenter study focuses on neonates already exposed to general anesthesia rather than comparing anesthetic techniques. The models incorporate maternal, obstetric, fetal, and anesthesia-related variables, including the induction-to-delivery interval, for individualized pre-delivery risk estimation. The NICU admission model showed more consistent validation performance than the neonatal resuscitation model. These tools may support neonatal team notification, delivery-room readiness, and multidisciplinary planning in high-acuity cesarean deliveries.

articles.title: Volume Guarantee Versus Manual Tidal Volume Monitoring During High-Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation in Neonates: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The present study compared the effects of high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) with automated volume guarantee (HFOV-VG) versus careful manual high-frequency tidal volume (VThf) monitoring (HFOV-VM) on the incidences of hypo/hypercarbia in neonates.
METHODS: In this open-labeled, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 60 neonates failing conventional mechanical ventilation were allocated to receive HFOV-VG (n = 30) versus HFOV-VM (n = 30) as a rescue mode. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia at 1 h. Secondary outcomes were incidences of hypo/hypercarbia at 6/12/24/48 h and beyond, time-specific trends for partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO2), delivered VThf and mean airway pressure (MAP), cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) and regional cerebral oxygenation (CrSO2), duration of respiratory support, and incidences of in-hospital adverse events. Stata 18 was used for an intention-to-treat analysis.
RESULTS: The incidence of hypo- or hypercarbia at 1 h of intervention was 15/30 (50%) in the HFOV-VG and 13/30 (43%) in the HFOV-VM groups (p = 0.61). No differences were observed in the incidences of hypo- or hypercarbia anytime during HFOV. Time-specific pCO2, VThf, and MAP were similar. On regression analysis, the only significant predictor for pCO2 at 1 h was the baseline pCO2 level in both the groups. No difference was observed in ACA-CBF, CrSO2, duration of respiratory support, and in-hospital adverse events including mortality.
CONCLUSION: There was no difference in the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia with HFOV-VG versus HFOV-VM at 1 h and throughout the duration of ventilation with a similar rate of complications when used as a rescue therapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial registry of India, Registration no: CTRI/2024/09/073455, Registered prospectively on 05/09/2024, https://ctri.icmr.org.in/.

articles.title: Trends in medications for opioid use disorder before surgery by payer type, 2016-2021.
Things pain takes.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Risk of Pain-Related Medical Encounters Among Patients with Comorbid Type 2 Diabetes and Opioid Use Disorder: A Target Trial Emulation Study.
articles.abstract: While GLP-1 receptor agonists (RAs) are postulated to alleviate pain, limited data exist to support the drugs' benefits in reducing pain-related medical encounters, particularly in patients with opioid use disorder (OUD), who have a high prevalence of pain. This study aims to examine the associations of GLP-1 RAs use with risk of emergency department (ED) visits or hospitalizations for pain among patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes (T2D) and OUD. We conducted a retrospective cohort study design in a target trial emulation framework using Merative MarketScan claims data between 2016 and 2023. Participants included adults between 18 and 64 years of age with a diagnosis of T2D and OUD who initiated GLP-1 RA or other second-line antidiabetic medication. Key outcomes included counts of incident pain-related ED visits, hospitalizations, or a composite outcome of either medical encounter, with a primary or secondary diagnosis coded for pain. Of 5842 eligible patients, those with use of GLP-1 RAs (vs. second-line antidiabetic medications) had a lower adjusted incident rate of pain-related ED visits (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR]: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.69, 0.96, P=.01), pain-related hospitalizations (aIRR: 0.92; 95% CI: 0.68, 1.24, P=.56), although non-significant, and composite outcome of pain-related ED visit or hospitalization (aIRR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.72, 0.97, P=.02). Initiation of GLP-1 RA therapy compared with second-line antidiabetic medication was associated with reduced risk of the composite outcome of pain-related ED visits or hospitalizations, indicating potential benefit of GLP-1 RA use for reducing pain-related medical encounters. Perspective In this cohort study, use of GLP1-1 RAs vs second-line drugs for T2D was associated with a lower risk of pain-related ED visits or hospitalizations among adults with comorbid T2D and OUD. GLP-1 RAs may be repurposed as a non-opioid pharmacological treatment for pain in patients with OUD.

articles.title: Itch signal processing mechanisms and central sensitization in the spinal dorsal horn of atopic dermatitis model mice.
articles.abstract: Although significant progress has been made in understanding the spinal mechanisms of itch, the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying chronic itch remain poorly understood. Specifically, the direct neurophysiological alterations in central itch signal processing at the whole-animal level are largely unknown. To address this research gap, we employed an in vivo electrophysiological approach to investigate pathological neurophysiological changes in the spinal dorsal horn (SDH) of an atopic dermatitis model mouse (FADS mouse). In vivo extracellular recordings revealed spontaneous firing in the superficial layer in SDH of FADS mice that was absent in healthy controls. Spontaneous activity was abolished by CNQX, an α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR)/kainate receptor antagonist, but not by RC-3095, a gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR) antagonist, or by anantin, a natriuretic peptide receptor A (NPRA) antagonist. In vivo patch-clamp recordings further demonstrated increased spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents (sEPSCs) and decreased spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic currents (sIPSCs) in SDH neurons of FADS mice. Molecular analyses revealed increased mRNA expression of gastrin-releasing peptide (GRP) and the microglial marker Iba1. Taken together, these findings indicate that SDH neurons receive glutamate-mediated itch signals and suggest that changes in the excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance contribute to central sensitization under chronic itch conditions. To our knowledge, this is the first study to directly demonstrate alterations in E/I balance in a mouse model of chronic itch. PERSPECTIVE: This study found that glutamate acts as a key neurotransmitter and that alterations in E/I balance induce central sensitization in the spinal cord of an atopic dermatitis model. To our knowledge, this is the first study to directly demonstrate that changes in E/I balance induce central sensitization in a chronic itch model.

articles.title: Home-based transcranial direct current stimulation and exercise for pain in people with knee osteoarthritis: A mixed-methods pilot randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: This mixed-methods pilot trial evaluated the feasibility and patient perceptions of home-based transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with exercise for pain in people with knee osteoarthritis. Twenty-four participants were allocated to active or sham home-based tDCS plus exercise. Participants completed 10 tDCS sessions over two weeks and an eight-week exercise program, with laboratory assessments at baseline, week four, and week eight. Primary outcomes were recruitment, adherence, adverse events, attrition, and tolerability. Secondary outcomes included local pressure pain thresholds, pain, function, quality of life, and semi-structured interviews exploring intervention facilitators and barriers. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively and qualitative data using inductive thematic analysis. All prespecified feasibility and safety criteria were met. Adherence was high, with 88% of participants (21/24) completing at least 75% of tDCS sessions, and 75% (18/24) completing at least 75% of exercise sessions. No significant adverse events occurred. Mean (SD) pain intensity /100 decreased from 47.3 (25.6) to 28.3 (16.1) in the active group and from 46.4 (17.8) to 33.5 (16.7) in the sham group at week 8. A future trial would require 80 participants. Qualitative themes indicated that evidence of effectiveness was more important to engagement than financial cost, tDCS was viewed as an appealing alternative to pharmacological treatment, and initial device operation was a greater barrier than safety or home use. Home-based tDCS combined with exercise was feasible, acceptable, and well tolerated. These findings support a fully powered trial to determine whether this scalable intervention improves pain and function in people with knee osteoarthritis. PERSPECTIVE: This pilot trial indicates that home-based tDCS combined with exercise is feasible, acceptable, and well tolerated for knee osteoarthritis. Participants valued its convenience and non-pharmacological nature. These findings support a fully powered trial to determine whether this scalable approach improves pain and function and broadens access to care.

articles.title: Prognostic relevance of protein prescriptions based on adjusted body weight in critically ill overweight or obese patients - analysis of a large international database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ESPEN currently recommends using adjusted body weight (aBW) to guide protein prescriptions for critically ill overweight or obese patients. The prognostic relevance of this concept is unknown.
METHODS: We analyzed a subset of a large international point prevalence survey of nutritional practice in 785 intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Patients were included if they had been in the ICU for at least 96 h and had a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m². We modelled the association between early average protein intake (days 1-4 after ICU admission) and the cause-specific adjusted hazards of in-ICU death and ICU discharge alive within a competing risks framework. Intake was normalized to aBW, defined as ideal body weight plus 25% of the difference between actual and ideal body weight.
RESULTS: 9,068 patients were analyzed. There was no evidence of an association between early protein intake and ICU discharge alive. In contrast, very low protein intake (below approximately 0.45 g/kg aBW/day) was associated with a higher hazard of in-ICU death. Above this threshold, there was no clear evidence of a further association between protein intake and the hazard of in-ICU death. The strongest association was observed at 0 g/kg aBW/day (adjusted hazard rate 1.41 i.e. an estimated 38% higher risk, 95% confidence interval 1.17-1.69).
CONCLUSIONS: Early protein intake does not appear to be associated with time to ICU discharge among survivors. However, in critically ill patients with overweight or obesity, very low protein intake during the early acute phase may be associated with less favorable in-ICU outcomes.

articles.title: What is your diagnosis? A life-threatening complication in severe acute pancreatitis.

National Early Warning Score 2-Guided Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle Care for Adults With Suspected Sepsis in the Emergency Department: A Hybrid Type 1 Effectiveness-Implementation Stepped-Wedge Randomized Controlled Trial Pilot Study (NEWS-1 TRIPS).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To increase the uptake of the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle, we implemented a novel sepsis care model (National Early Warning Score [NEWS]-1 care), in which the Hour-1 Bundle is objectively triggered by a high NEWS-2 (≥ 5). We aimed to determine the feasibility of a full-scale type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation trial of this model.
DESIGN: A pilot type 1 hybrid trial, comprising a stepped-wedge cluster randomized controlled trial and mixed-methods implementation evaluation with staff focus group interviews and an anonymous survey guided by the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance framework.
SETTING: Four emergency departments in Hong Kong.
PATIENTS: Adult patients of 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of infection requiring hospitalization and a NEWS-2 greater than or equal to 5.
INTERVENTIONS: Implementation of the Hour-1 Bundle when NEWS-2 was greater than or equal to 5.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was the feasibility of a full-scale hybrid trial, evaluated based on 14 progression criteria. Preliminary clinical effectiveness and safety were assessed, alongside implementation barriers and facilitators. During the implementation phase, compliance with lactate, blood culture, and antibiotics increased significantly. All progression criteria were met, except for suboptimal overall bundle compliance (56.1%). Exploratory intention-to-treat analysis (standard care group, n = 102; NEWS-1 group, n = 98) showed no significant between-group difference in 30-day all-cause mortality (standard care group, 3.9%; NEWS-1 group, 9.2%; absolute risk difference, 5.3%; 95% CI -1.6% to 12.1%); in-hospital, 90-day all-cause, or sepsis-related mortality; need for mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, intensive care, or surgery; or ventilator-free days and adverse events. Implementation evaluation identified 15 barriers and 13 facilitators.
CONCLUSIONS: The effectiveness of NEWS-1 care remained uncertain, though adverse events were rare. A full-scale hybrid stepped-wedge trial is feasible but requires a much larger sample size. Real-world implementation barriers and facilitators should be considered in sepsis management guidelines.

articles.title: Global Prevalence of Obstetric Causes of Critical Illness in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence, risks, and outcomes of obstetric causes of critically ill pregnant women admitted to the ICU.
DATA SOURCES: We searched the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Ovid, and ScienceDirect databases up to May 15, 2026.
STUDY SELECTION: We included studies reporting primary data on critically ill pregnant and postpartum women (up to 48 d post-delivery) admitted to an ICU, with relevant obstetric risk factors and maternal outcomes.
DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the adapted Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects model with 95% CIs.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Of the 3,735 total records, 50 studies met the eligibility criteria, encompassing 7,756,232 women receiving obstetric care in tertiary hospitals across 20 countries, with 49,299 ICU admissions. Globally, 1.0% (95% CI, 0.8-1.3%) of pregnant and postpartum women experience critical illness and require admission to an ICU. The frequency varies according to the country's income levels, with the highest in low-income countries (4.1%) and the lowest in high-income countries (0.5%). Notably, 72.3% of ICU admissions were attributed to known obstetric causes, primarily obstetric hemorrhage (23.3%) and hypertension in pregnancy (26.9%). Nearly 33.3% of ICU patients required either respiratory or transfusion support, and the maternal mortality rate among ICU-admitted obstetric women was 8.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in 100 pregnancies require admission to intensive care due to critical illness, and nearly three-quarters of these admissions were due to direct obstetric causes, with high maternal morbidity and mortality. Obstetric hemorrhage and hypertensive disorders account for the majority of ICU admissions. Strengthening obstetric care in resource-limited settings through the expansion and optimization of intensive care services is essential for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes and reducing preventable morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Neurological Outcomes of Rhythm Transitions in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest With Initial Nonshockable Rhythms: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prognostic implications of rhythm transitions between asystole and pulseless electrical activity (PEA) in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with initial nonshockable rhythms.
DESIGN: Nationwide population-based observational study.
SETTING: Nationwide OHCA Registry of South Korea, managed by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency.
PATIENTS: Consecutive adult (≥ 18 yr old) OHCA patients with nonshockable rhythms from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2021.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Patients were categorized into four groups based on rhythm changes during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR): asystole-to-asystole (A-A), asystole-to-PEA (A-P), PEA-to-asystole (P-A), and PEA-to-PEA (P-P). The primary outcome was good neurologic outcome at hospital discharge, defined as a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1-2. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to adjust for measured confounding. In the primary IPTW model, weighted risks of good neurologic outcome were 0.101% in A-A, 0.231% in A-P, 0.384% in P-A, and 0.874% in P-P. Compared with A-A, the odds of good neurologic outcome were higher in A-P (odds ratio [OR], 2.28; 95% CI, 1.78-2.93; risk difference [RD], 0.130 percentage points), P-A (OR, 3.80; 95% CI, 3.01-4.80; RD, 0.283 percentage points), and P-P (OR, 8.70; 95% CI, 6.98-10.83; RD, 0.773 percentage points). Compared with A-P, P-A had higher odds of good neurologic outcome (OR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.39-1.99; RD, 0.153 percentage points).
CONCLUSIONS: Asystole conversion to PEA during CPR was associated with a better neurologic outcome than persistent asystole. Although transitioning from PEA to asystole was associated with lower odds of a good outcome compared with persistent PEA, it was associated with a better outcome than A-P transitions. Recognizing these patterns may provide prognostic context beyond a single rhythm assessment.

articles.title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review of In-Hospital and Post-Discharge Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis determines the incidence of new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) in critically ill patients, risks of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism, anticoagulation therapy, and the proportion diagnosed with AF post-discharge.
DATA SOURCES: A search of registered databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CINAHL) was performed from inception to April 20, 2026.
STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included critically ill patients (≥ 18 yr old) who developed NOAF during admission to general ICUs or high-dependency units. NOAF was defined as AF in patients without prior history of AF.
DATA EXTRACTION: Data were independently extracted from full-text versions of included studies by nonblinded reviewers.
DATA SYNTHESIS: A Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted on 54 studies (367,896 patients) with a random-effects model using R (Version 4.3.3). Pooled incidence of NOAF in critically ill patients was 10.6% (95% credible interval [CrI], 8.6-12.9%). Absolute risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism was 7.1% (95% CrI, 4.5-11.0%), changing to 6.9% (95% CrI, 4.2-11.6%) after age and sex adjustment. Evidence from six studies reports that critically ill patients with NOAF had 1.94 times (95% CrI, 1.23-3.29) higher relative risk of systemic thromboembolism post-discharge than patients without NOAF, rising to 2.01 (95% CrI, 1.54-2.80) with adjustment. Absolute and relative risk are evaluated with follow-up durations ranging from 1.5 months to 5 years, with variable anticoagulation exposure. Anticoagulation rates were low: 32.9% in-hospital (95% CrI, 14.6-57.9%) and 35.9% post-discharge (95% CrI, 19.7-55.9%). On follow-up, 23.9% (95% CrI, 13.9-38.5%) of critically ill patients with NOAF were subsequently diagnosed with AF.
CONCLUSIONS: Our review suggests that NOAF during critical illness is associated with significantly increased risk of post-discharge systemic thromboembolism and subsequent AF diagnosis. However, rates of anticoagulation initiation remain low, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and targeted strategies post-discharge.

articles.title: Structured Patient and Family-Centered Rounding in the ICU is Associated With Increased Family Confidence in Staff Compassion and Perceived Quality of Information Shared.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Determine whether inviting families to participate in structured, multidisciplinary rounding in the ICU can lead to improved quality of information shared and greater overall confidence in the care delivered to patients.
DESIGN: Pre- and postimplementation observational study based on surveys provided by the Society of Critical Care Medicine-Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute initiative.
SETTING: Academic teaching hospital with 21 medical (closed unit) and 25 surgical (open unit) ICU beds.
SUBJECTS: Family members and care providers of critically ill adults of 18 years and older.
INTERVENTIONS: Families and clinicians were surveyed before and after implementation of a quality initiative to promote greater patient and family-centeredness in daily ICU rounds, using a structured and scripted rounding template. Additional information was gathered regarding provider attitudes toward the incorporation of families in rounds.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In pre-and postintervention periods, 36 and 28 families were surveyed in the MICU, and 44 and 42 families were surveyed in the SICU, respectively. In pre-and postintervention periods, respectively, 53 and 48 clinicians were surveyed in the MICU, and 46 and 28 clinicians were surveyed in the SICU. Clinician perceptions improved favorably in the MICU, with statistically significant improvements falling under the category of family welcoming, presence, and participation in decision-making; less so in the SICU. Family perceptions improved in almost all parameters in the MICU, with statistical significance achieved in perceived interest in patient needs, control of agitation and pain, and consistency and honesty of information shared. Similar patterns were observed in the SICU but did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Structured, multi-disciplinary rounding with regular inclusion of family members and bedside nurses was associated with significantly greater family confidence in the quality and honesty of information shared, and an increase in perceived compassion in the care provided by ICU staff. Clinician perceptions regarding family inclusion on rounds were generally positive.

articles.title: The Impact of Hospital Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Volume and Its Distribution Across ICUs on Adult Patients' Outcomes: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Research from a prior era of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) found that higher hospital ECMO volume was associated with higher survival rates, but it did not examine whether distributing ECMO volume across multiple ICUs affected this relationship.
DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry.
SETTING: ECMO centers contributing to the registry.
PATIENTS: Adult patients required ECMO support from 2012 to 2023.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We analyzed adult patients from the ELSO registry (2012-2023), adjusting for hospital factors and case mix using multivariable hierarchical logistic regression. The main outcome was in-hospital mortality. Hospital experience was measured by the annual number of adult ECMO cases and total ECMO hours. Volume-outcome associations were modeled for all centers and by total adult ICUs per center. We included 115,849 adults on ECMO across 495 hospitals. Model estimates showed small decreases in mortality odds with higher annual case counts (odds ratio [OR], 0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99 per 10-case increase) and ECMO hours (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr increase). Hospitals with one ICU had a median of 10 cases (interquartile interval [IQI], 3-25 cases), while those with four or more ICUs had a median of 50 (IQI, 28-91). Adjusted mortality was higher in centers delivering ECMO across four+ ICUs compared with one ICU (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.06-1.31), the annual case model (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06-1.26), and the annual ECMO hours model. Higher volume was associated with a reduction in the odds of mortality for hospitals with four+ ICUs compared with those with one ICU (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.96-1.00 per 10 cases and OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.99-1.00 per 1000 hr).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher hospital ECMO volume is associated with reduced mortality. Hospitals with more adult ICUs that perform ECMO may experience higher mortality, which may be explained by increased patient complexity and is offset by the higher center volume. More research is needed to better understand the optimum design of ECMO centers.

articles.title: A Telemedicine Intervention for Spontaneous Awakening and Breathing Trials in Small and Large ICUs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of a tele-critical care (TCC) daily audit-and-feedback intervention on spontaneous awakening trial and spontaneous breathing trial protocol compliance.
DESIGN: Pre-post quality improvement study.
SETTING: Single health system composed of 14 hospitals in the Midwestern United States.
PATIENTS: A total of 8909 patients of 18 years or older receiving mechanical ventilation via endotracheal tube for more than 1 calendar day between October 01, 2022 and September 20, 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: Daily in the early afternoon, TCC nurses reviewed mechanically ventilated patients to determine whether a spontaneous awakening trial and spontaneous breathing trial had occurred. They contacted the bedside nurse if no trial had occurred and no weaning exclusion criteria were noted during a manual chart review.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The coprimary outcomes were the proportion of ventilator days during each ventilator episode with documentation of spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials. Linear mixed effects models were used to examine the effect of the intervention on each outcome stratified by ICU size (large ≥ 15 beds or small < 15 beds). Spontaneous awakening trial documentation improved over time throughout the entire period, but the rate of improvement increased significantly after the telemedicine intervention (preintervention slope: 0.2% increase per 30 d; 95% CI, -0.2% to 0.6% and postintervention slope: 1.4% increase per 30 d; 95% CI, 1.0% to 1.9%; p < 0.001 for intervention-time interaction). The telemedicine intervention was associated with a step increase in spontaneous breathing trial documentation in small ICUs (absolute increase, 12.8%; 95% CI, 8.7-16.9%) but not in large ICUs (absolute increase, -0.1%; 95% CI, -1.8% to 1.6%; p = 0.02 for intervention-ICU size interaction).
CONCLUSIONS: The telemedicine intervention was associated with increased spontaneous awakening trials and spontaneous breathing trials selectively in small ICUs. Telemedicine may have promoted practice standardization in small ICUs where exposure to ventilated patients was infrequent. Local ICU characteristics may impact the effectiveness of TCC interventions.

articles.title: Green-Lyte: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project to Optimize Electrolyte Replacement and Reduce Environmental Burden in ICUs at a Comprehensive Cancer Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrolyte replacement therapies are commonly prescribed in ICUs. However, studies have shown that electrolytes are frequently administered to patients with no clear clinical indications and, in most cases, the IV route is used. In this study, we evaluated the impact of a multidisciplinary quality improvement project, Green-Lyte, on electrolyte replacement and on the environmental burden.
METHODS: This was a quality improvement retrospective study conducted in the adult ICUs at a comprehensive cancer center comparing preimplementation (September 2024 to February 2025) and postimplementation (May 2025 to October 2025) phases of the Green-Lyte project. Green-Lyte consisted of defined criteria to guide both the indication and route of administration for potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus replacement, along with ongoing education and follow-up. Outcomes included the number of electrolyte prescriptions, concordance with Green-Lyte criteria for indication and route of administration, as well as the generated waste and estimated material-associated carbon footprint. Outcomes were standardized per 100 ICU patient-days.
RESULTS: Over the study period, a total of 603 IV and oral electrolyte replacement doses were prescribed in the pre-Green-Lyte phase, and 573 IV and oral electrolyte replacement doses were prescribed in the post-Green-Lyte phase. When adjusted per 100 ICU patient-days, 30.7 doses vs. 19.4 doses were dispensed in the pre- and postimplementation phases, respectively, representing a 36.9% reduction in prescribed electrolytes. Concordance with the Green-Lyte criteria for indication increased from 57.8% to 72.8%, representing a 26% relative improvement, whereas concordance with the criteria for route of administration increased from 22.5% to 45.9%, representing a 104% relative improvement. In addition, the generated waste and the estimated material-associated carbon footprint decreased by 61.8% and 63.2%, respectively.
