Motor block onset and time to maximum motor block did not differ significantly between the groups. Recovery-room pain scores were higher at several assessment time points in the opioid-dependent group, and 11/28 (39.3%) patients in this group required morphine, compared with 4/28 (14.3%) controls (P = 0.035). No significant differences were observed in overall patient satisfaction or adverse events. Hemodynamic measurements did not differ significantly at most time points; however, systolic blood pressure was higher at 25 minutes and heart rate was lower at 12 minutes after spinal anesthesia in the opioid-dependent group (both P = 0.039).
CONCLUSIONS: Opioid dependence was associated with shorter sensory and motor block durations, a longer sensory block onset time, and greater analgesic requirements in the early recovery room after spinal anesthesia with intrathecal ropivacaine. These findings suggest that opioid-dependent patients may benefit from individualized perioperative anesthetic and analgesic strategies to optimize pain management and potentially improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Anatomical Classification of Jejunal Vessels and Patterns of Venous Injury During Robot-Assisted Pancreaticoduodenectomy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Venous injury during mesojejunum dissection can cause significant bleeding during robot-assisted pancreaticoduodenectomy (RPD). This study aimed to classify proximal jejunal vessel anatomy according to its relationships with the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) and jejunal arteries and characterize the patterns and sites of venous injury.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 224 consecutive patients who underwent RPD between January 2018 and December 2024. Preoperative multidetector computed tomography with three-dimensional reconstruction was used to classify proximal jejunal venous anatomy into four types: proximal dorsal jejunal vein (PDJV) parallel, PDJV crossed, proximal left jejunal vein (PLJV), and Mixed type. Perioperative outcomes and jejunal venous injury or bleeding events were analyzed by anatomical type.
RESULTS: The PDJV parallel type was most common (44.6%), followed by the PDJV crossed (32.1%), PLJV (12.5%), and Mixed type (10.7%). Nine jejunal venous injury or bleeding events occurred: five in the PDJV parallel type, two in the PDJV crossed type, two in the PLJV type, and none in the Mixed type. In the PDJV parallel type, all five events involved the PDJV root or inferior pancreaticoduodenal vein and were unrelated to mesojejunum dissection. The two events during mesojejunum dissection occurred in the PDJV crossed type at points where jejunal veins crossed jejunal arteries. One patient required conversion to open surgery because of PDJV root injury during SMA dissection.
CONCLUSION: Jejunal venous anatomy showed four distinct patterns, with differing sites and circumstances of injury. The small number of events precludes conclusions about differences in overall injury risk among anatomical types. However, recognizing these anatomical relationships may help surgeons anticipate potential sites of venous injury during RPD.

articles.title: Topical 15% trichloroacetic acid versus silver nitrate cauterization in the management of idiopathic childhood epistaxis: a prospective randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The purpose of the study is to compare the outcomes of trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to silver nitrate chemical cauterization in managing pediatric epistaxis. In this prospective randomized assessor-blinded clinical trial, of 172 randomized patients, 157 pediatric patients with idiopathic anterior epistaxis were divided into 2 groups in a ratio 1:1, where group (A) was treated with silver nitrate 25% after local anesthesia application and group (B) was treated with 15% TCA locally applied to the bleeder. Patients were assessed upon recurrence, pain, and crusting at 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 12th week post-intervention. The incidence of epistaxis was not significantly different between the two groups. Pain was significantly greater in the TCA group (P = 0.008*). Nasal crusting was slightly greater in the TCA group, but the difference was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Although not widely utilized in the management of pediatric epistaxis, TCA is considered an effective chemical cautery agent for the management of childhood epistaxis, with results comparable to those of silver nitrate in terms of recurrence but was slightly worse in terms of pain after intervention.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Number NCT06836791, Date of registration 02/19/2025.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Epistaxis is a very distressing complaint in pediatric otorhinolaryngology. • One of the utilized modalities nowadays that proved efficacy in the management of epistaxis is the chemical cauterization of the prominent vessels in Little's area.
WHAT IS NEW: • This is the first study to compare the efficacy of silver nitrate to TCA in epistaxis treatment. • TCA is considered an effective chemical cautery agent for the management of childhood epistaxis, with results comparable to those of silver nitrate agent.

articles.title: Differential effects of prone positioning and PEEP on ventilation/perfusion distribution across inflammatory ARDS subphenotypes: a porcine experimental study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ARDS comprises distinct inflammatory subphenotypes, including hyper- and hypo-inflammatory forms. Whether these differ in ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) mismatch and response to ventilatory strategies remains unclear. Dual-energy CT enables regional assessment of aeration and perfusion. This experimental study aimed to compare V/Q mismatch between hyper- and hypo-inflammatory subphenotypes, and respective responses to PEEP and prone positioning.
METHODS: In 10 pigs, hypo-inflammatory ARDS was induced by lung lavage followed by injurious ventilation. Hyper-inflammatory ARDS was produced by i.v. endotoxin infusion and fluid loading. Pigs were randomised to hypo- or hyperinflammatory ARDS, with similar oxygenation impairment. Dual-energy CT scans were obtained at individualised low, optimal, and high PEEP settings, in supine and prone positions. V/Q was derived from regional gas and blood volume and classified as low (<0.5), normal, or high (>2). Linear mixed-effects models included injury group, PEEP, and posture as fixed effects, and subject as a random effect.
RESULTS: Hyper-inflammatory injury showed more severe V/Q mismatch than hypo-inflammatory injury (normal V/Q: 35% [sd=10] vs 51% [8] at low PEEP, supine position; P<0.01). Both PEEP optimisation and prone positioning improved V/Q. Prone positioning reduced high V/Q and dead space in hypo-inflammatory injury (group×posture interaction: F1,50=4.32, P=0.04), whereas PEEP reduced low V/Q and shunt in the supine position independent of ARDS subphenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: In porcine models of hyper- and hypo-inflammatory ARDS, hyper-inflammatory injury was associated with more severe V/Q mismatch despite similar oxygenation. Distinct responses to PEEP and prone positioning support a subphenotype-tailored approach to ventilatory management.

articles.title: Focused transesophageal echocardiography in cardiac arrest: promise, limits, and perspective.
Fellowship, research, and practice preferences: an updated survey of Canadian anesthesiology residents.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Canada faces mounting anesthesia workforce pressures, particularly in rural and smaller urban centres. Understanding residents' motivations regarding practice setting, research, and fellowship training is essential for workforce planning. We aimed to update a 2015 national survey to characterize current preferences and temporal shifts among Canadian anesthesiology residents.
METHODS: We conducted an anonymous, cross-sectional survey of residents in accredited Canadian anesthesiology programs (November-December 2024) using Research Electronic Data Capture. Items addressed demographics, practice setting, research experience and intentions, and fellowship plans. Selected responses were compared with 2015 survey items using Chi square tests and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals; all tests used an alpha of 0.05.
RESULTS: Ninety-four residents responded (12% response rate). Most preferred academic practice (63%), and half preferred to remain at their training institution (49%). Interest in rural practice was reported by 49%. Although research participation was common during medical school (94%) and residency (83%), only 18% intended to pursue research after residency. Approximately 63% intended to pursue fellowship training. Compared with the 2015 survey, there were significant increases in intention to remain at the same institution (from 35% to 50%; P = 0.02) and residency research participation (from 69% to 83%; P < 0.01), whereas intention to pursue research after residency declined (from 34% to 18%; P < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Canadian anesthesiology residents continue to favour academic practice and fellowship training, yet fewer plan to integrate research into future careers. These findings highlight opportunities for targeted mentorship, greater research autonomy, financial support, and expanded rural training pathways to align resident priorities with workforce needs.

articles.title: The need for research for predicting time to death after withdrawal of life-sustaining measures in children: ethical and practical considerations for end-of-life care.
Voluntariness of same-day versus advance consent in low-risk clinical research: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The solicitation of same-day consent for participation in clinical research is commonly prohibited by research ethics boards because of concerns about limited decision-making time and patient vulnerability. However, these concerns lack empirical support and restrict both research efforts and patient participation opportunities, particularly in medical specialties such as emergency medicine, critical care, and anesthesiology, in which clinicians and patients interact for the first time on the day of a procedure. We aimed to assess the voluntariness of research consent solicited on the day of surgery compared with consent obtained in advance.
METHODS: We performed a prospective, noninferiority randomized controlled trial examining the voluntariness of informed consent to participate in a low-risk clinical research trial at Women's College Hospital in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The trial design included active deception (invitation to participate in a fabricated research trial) to capture authentic measurements of participants' perceptions of any perceived coercion.
RESULTS: We randomized 114 patients scheduled to undergo anterior cruciate ligament repair for recruitment into a fabricated low-risk perioperative research trial at one of two time points: at a virtual preanesthesia clinic appointment in advance of the day of surgery, or on the day of surgery. Regardless of their decision, all participants received the (same) standard of care. Overall, 71/114 patients (62%) either consented to participate in the fabricated trial or declined participation but consented to a feedback session during which perceptions of coercion were assessed. Greater participation was observed among patients approached on the day of surgery (fabricated trial, 26/58 [45%]; feedback session only, 18/58 [31%]) than in advance (fabricated trial, 17/56 [30%]; feedback session only, 10/56 [18%]). Perceived coercion, measured using two validated psychometric instruments, did not differ between patients recruited on the day of surgery and those recruited in advance. A subset of patients in each group reported modest perceptions of undue influence, but regardless of recruitment time point, these patients demonstrated their agency to decline participation.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that restrictive same-day consent policies, when based on concerns regarding undue influence, may represent a structural barrier to participation in low-risk trials that lacks empirical justification.
STUDY REGISTRATIONS: 1) Open Science Framework ( 46twc ); first submitted 17 March 2023; 2) ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT07380035 ); first submitted 16 January 2026.

articles.title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery.
RESULTS: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.

articles.title: Perioperative dynamics of selenoproteins and risk of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) affects over 20% of patients and is associated with perioperative mortality and long-term renal impairment. Reliable early biomarkers remain limited. Selenoproteins, including glutathione peroxidases (GPX1, GPX3) and selenoprotein P (SEPP1), are critical for redox homeostasis, but their perioperative changes in CSA-AKI remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize selenoprotein dynamics and explore their association with renal function and CSA-AKI. In this prospective observational cohort study, 99 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery were enrolled, serum and urine samples were collected preoperatively and at 24/48 h postoperatively. SEPP1, GPX1, GPX3, and KIM-1 were measured. Mixed-effects, correlation, and logistic regression assessed selenoprotein dynamics and associations with CSA-AKI, with an exploratory model including age and preoperative SEPP1. Among 89 analyzed patients, 22 (24.7%) developed AKI. Univariable analyses showed that lower perioperative SEPP1 levels, attenuated urinary SEPP1 increases, and greater serum GPX1 decreases were associated with higher odds of CSA-AKI; older age, hypertension, and longer operation time were also associated with CSA-AKI. Postoperatively, serum SEPP1 declined markedly, remaining lower in AKI patients. Urinary SEPP1 increased significantly in non-AKI patients. Changes in GPX1 and GPX3 differed between AKI and non-AKI groups. Serum SEPP1 correlated positively with eGFR and inversely with creatinine and cystatin C. An exploratory model incorporating age and preoperative serum SEPP1 yielded an apparent AUC of 0.818. In summary, perioperative alterations in selenoproteins (GPX1, GPX3, SEPP1) are closely linked to CSA-AKI. Preoperative SEPP1 combined with clinical variables may enable early risk prediction and support timely intervention.

articles.title: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial.
SETTING: Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023.
PARTICIPANTS: 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.
RESULTS: 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2000039376.

articles.title: Impact of Mental Health Disorders on Pulmonary Resection: A Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Medicare Linked Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine the prevalence of comorbid mental health disorders (MHDs) and association with stage of diagnosis, extent of resection, and post-operative morbidity/mortality in patients undergoing operative intervention for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: Adults undergoing elective resection of stage I-III NSCLC were identified from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (July 2018-June 2024) and linked to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to determine long-term survival. Primary outcomes were stage at diagnosis, extent of resection, perioperative morbidity, and 5-year survival. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regressions estimated associations between MHDs on each outcome. Risk-adjusted survival was derived using multivariable frailty Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: Among 103,263 patients, 24.4% (n=25,163) had ≥1 MHD. Prevalence of MHDs increased from 16.8% in 2018 to 28.0% in 2024 (p<0.001). In risk-adjusted analysis, patients with an MHD were more likely to have clinical stage I disease (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.22) and to undergo sublobar resection (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). Perioperative mortality, morbidity, and length of stay were all significantly increased in patients with MHDs. In risk-adjusted analysis among Medicare linked patients, 5-year mortality was modestly but significantly greater among patients with MHDs (aHR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.18).
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of MHDs among patients undergoing NSCLC resection nearly doubled over 6 years and was associated with an ∼20% increase in morbidity and a reduction in adjusted 5-year survival. These findings underscore the need for targeted perioperative pathways and longitudinal support to mitigate adverse outcomes in this growing population.

articles.title: Emerging Multidimensional Technologies for Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major contributor to myocardial damage across diverse ischemic conditions and remains a particular challenge in cardiac surgery. Its development cannot be explained by a single pathway, but reflects a complex injury process triggered by ischemia and amplified during reperfusion. Recent advances in omics profiling, artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods, advanced imaging, and gene-regulatory technologies have provided new opportunities to investigate MIRI at molecular, cellular, spatial, and temporal levels. In this review, we examine how these approaches have advanced the understanding of key pathological processes in MIRI, including regulated cell death, oxidative stress, inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and brain-heart axis regulation. We also discuss their contributions to biomarker discovery, therapeutic target validation, myocardial injury assessment, and optimization of intervention strategies, while considering their implications for both mechanistic research and perioperative cardioprotection. Closer integration of these technological advances with clinically relevant questions may improve risk assessment and help guide more precise strategies for the prevention and treatment of MIRI.

articles.title: Neuronal injury and inflammatory protein signatures of postoperative delirium and cognitive decline in older adults-combining insights from post-surgical and memory clinic cohorts.
articles.abstract: Plasma proteomics may offer novel characterization of the longer-term inflammatory and neuronal injury alterations in older adults undergoing elective surgery, and their relations to delirium and cognitive decline. We leveraged plasma protein data from N = 616 participants across two longitudinal cohorts. Plasma proteomic profiling of 447 proteins related to inflammation and neuronal injury (Olink platform) was applied to perioperative samples (collected at baseline, postoperative day (POD)1, and POD30) from the primary Southeast-Asian surgical cohort (N = 88), followed-up for postoperative delirium. Secondary mechanistic verification of key proteins was performed within an independent Southeast-Asian memory-clinic cohort (N = 528) followed-up for 4 years with cognitive and neuroimaging assessments. In the surgical cohort, significant dysregulations were observed within 330 proteins on POD1 and 230 proteins on POD30-mapping to diverse biological processes. The protein profiles most dysregulated on POD1 related to systemic inflammation, while that on POD30 exhibited a broader profile reflecting neuronal injury (i.e., EN-RAGE, NEFL, PAEP). A twelve-protein time-course signature was concordantly altered in participants with postoperative delirium (N = 26, 30%). Secondary validation within the memory-clinic cohort further prioritized 6 of the 12 proteins associating with delirium, as additional biomarkers of brain atrophy, cerebral small vessel disease, and 4-year cognitive decline: NEFL, TNFRSF10B, PLA2G10, SLC39A14, TNFRSF10A, GGT5. Leveraging insights from surgical and memory clinic cohorts, we prioritized protein signatures exhibiting robust signals for (i) postoperative delirium, (ii) neuroimaging pathology, and (iii) 4-year cognitive decline. These proteins may represent mechanistic targets for optimizing cognitive health in older adults.

articles.title: Development and validation of an early prediction model for intestinal failure-associated liver disease after enterostomy for necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infants undergoing enterostomy for necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) are at high risk of intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD). Early identification of high-risk infants remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate an early prediction model for IFALD using routinely available perioperative variables.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective study included 388 infants who underwent enterostomy for NEC between November 2019 and November 2024. Clinical, nutritional, and laboratory variables were collected. Boruta and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used for feature selection. Logistic regression, LASSO regression, random forest, naïve Bayes, and partial least squares (PLS) models were compared using discrimination, classification metrics, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the final model.
RESULTS: Among 388 infants, 103 (26.5%) developed IFALD. The training cohort comprised 273 infants (73 IFALD and 200 non-IFALD), and the validation cohort comprised 115 infants (30 IFALD and 85 non-IFALD). Infants with IFALD had lower gestational age, lower birth weight, shorter residual bowel length, delayed enteral nutrition recovery, and longer parenteral nutrition (PN) dependence. The random forest model showed the best validation performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.805 (95% confidence interval, 0.719-0.891), sensitivity of 0.700, specificity of 0.765, and accuracy of 0.748. SHAP analysis identified birth weight, residual bowel length, age at admission, preoperative systemic immune-inflammation index, postoperative platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and central venous catheter infection as the most important predictors.
CONCLUSIONS: Infants with enterostomy after NEC surgery often need prolonged PN, which increases the risk of IFALD. This study built an early prediction model using routine perioperative data. The random forest model showed good discrimination and high sensitivity, and may help clinicians identify infants who need closer liver monitoring, careful PN management, and infection prevention.
IMPACT: 1. An early six-variable model predicts intestinal failure-associated liver disease after enterostomy for neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis. 2. The model uses birth weight, residual bowel length, age at admission, preoperative systemic immune-inflammation index, postoperative platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and early central venous catheter infection. 3. Random forest performed best among five evaluated models, with a validation area under the curve of 0.805. 4. This study adds a direct comparison of conventional and machine-learning approaches using routinely available perioperative variables in a comparatively large cohort. 5. After external validation, the model could support early risk stratification, closer liver monitoring, individualized parenteral nutrition management, and catheter-infection prevention.

articles.title: Does Montelukast Decrease Post-Adenotonsillectomy Pain in Children? A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of perioperative Montelukast as an analgesic for adenotonsillectomy.
METHODS: This was a randomized controlled double-blind trial. The trial enrolled 116 children between the age of 3-8 undergoing adenotonsillectomy with planned 23-h observation for sleep disordered breathing were randomized to receive either montelukast or placebo perioperatively. Outcome variables including postoperative opioid usage, FLACC pain scores, post-tonsillectomy hemorrhage rate (PTH), and number of postoperative contacts were examined.
RESULTS: One-hundred and thirteen patients received either montelukast or placebo, and 92 received a second dose of the same. There were no differences in demographics between groups. There were no significant differences in the proportion of patients requiring opioids in PACU (46% in control group vs. 45% in the montelukast group, p = 0.9) or the number of postoperative contacts between groups. There was no difference in PTH between groups (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Montelukast does not lead to lower rates of pain postoperatively compared to placebo in patients undergoing adenotonsillectomy for sleep disordered breathing and does not lower postoperative contacts with the medical system.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02793375 LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 2.

articles.title: Utilization of remimazolam during cesarean section for a parturient with prior birth trauma.
articles.abstract: The placement of neuraxial anesthesia, and cesarean section itself, can be a source of significant anxiety and discomfort. While anxiolysis may improve patient comfort, the use of benzodiazepines is often limited by concerns about maternal respiratory depression, neonatal sedation, and hypotonia. Remimazolam (ByFavo™ in the US) is a novel, ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine characterized by a rapid onset, predictable recovery, and favorable hemodynamic profile. As a category of medications, benzodiazepines do cross the placenta and may cause respiratory depression, hypotension, and sedation in neonates. However, the novel structure and rapid metabolism of remimazolam is responsible for its clinically decreased recovery time and makes it an ideal agent for procedural anxiolysis for obstetric procedures. Remimazolam was approved for procedural sedation in the US in 2020 for adult populations; however, its use in obstetric anesthesia remains off-label and largely underutilized due to limited safety data. Despite this, it has been described in case reports and explored for potential benefits such as the prevention of nausea and vomiting during cesarean delivery. This case illustrates a novel application of remimazolam in a sensitive population, highlighting its potential as a safe and effective agent for anxiolysis in the obstetric setting.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Sugammadex Versus Neostigmine for Neuromuscular Blockade Reversal in a Population of Neonatal Intensive Care Patients.
Safety and Effectiveness of Motherwort Injection for Hemostasis and Menstrual Regulation: Protocol for a Prospective, Observational, Multicenter Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motherwort injection (MI) is a traditional Chinese medicine injection widely used for hemostasis and menstrual regulation in obstetrics and gynecology. Although clinical trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated its effectiveness for specific indications, comprehensive real-world evidence (RWE) regarding its safety, effectiveness, and use patterns across diverse clinical settings remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of MI in routine clinical practice and to generate RWE to support its rational use in women receiving treatment for approved obstetric and gynecological indications.
METHODS: This prospective, observational, multicenter real-world registry study plans to enroll 20,000 patients receiving MI for approved obstetric and gynecological indications in routine clinical practice in China. Treatment decisions, including whether to use MI and the dose and duration of treatment, as well as the use of concomitant medications, are made independently by treating physicians. Safety outcomes include the occurrence, type, severity, and incidence of adverse events and adverse drug reactions (ADRs). Effectiveness outcomes are assessed according to the clinical indication and include perioperative bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage, postabortion bleeding and menstrual resumption, uterine involution, menstrual regulation, and treatment satisfaction. Descriptive statistics will be used to characterize patient characteristics, MI use, and safety and effectiveness outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses will examine heterogeneity across major clinical groups. An exploratory nested case-control analysis with 1:4 matching and conditional logistic regression will be used to investigate factors associated with the occurrence of ADRs.
RESULTS: This study has received funding and obtained ethics approval in March 2024 (approval P24003-PJ03). Participant recruitment began on March 31, 2026. By September 2026, a total of 774 participants had been enrolled and included in the study database. The protocol specifies a target sample size of 20,000 participants, with data collection, monitoring, and quality control being conducted according to standardized study procedures. Data analysis has not yet commenced, and the study findings are expected to be published in October 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: This study will provide large-scale RWE regarding the safety and effectiveness of MI in obstetric and gynecological practice. The findings are expected to support postmarketing safety surveillance, optimize clinical decision-making, and contribute to the evidence-based evaluation of traditional Chinese medicine injections.

articles.title: COMFORT trial protocol: a triple-blind randomized controlled trial of surgeon-administered TAP block during complex cesarean delivery.
articles.abstract: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT06925152.

articles.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Analgesia Protocol with TAP Block Reduces Postoperative Opioid Use in Bariatric Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perioperative opioid use after bariatric surgery carries substantial risk of opioid-related harm, and multimodal analgesia (MMA) protocols limit opioids while maintaining effective pain control. We evaluated whether adding an intraoperative laparoscopic transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block to an established MMA regimen reduces inpatient and outpatient opioid use, pain scores, and 30-day perioperative outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study at a high-volume MBSAQIP-accredited academic medical center of patients who underwent minimally invasive bariatric surgery from 2015 to 2024. Patients with concurrent ventral hernia repair, cholecystectomy, or preoperative opioid use were excluded. Two cohorts were compared: MMA alone (January 2015-June 2017) and MMA + TAP block (July 2017-December 2024). The primary outcome was inpatient morphine milligram equivalents (MME).
RESULTS: Of 2,660 patients (MMA alone, n = 618; MMA + TAP, n = 2,042), baseline characteristics were similar despite a small difference in procedure mix (p < 0.0001). The MMA + TAP cohort required fewer inpatient opioids (median MME 76 vs. 134, p < 0.0001) and had lower median inpatient pain scores (3 vs. 4, p < 0.0001). Opioid use at 12 months was lower with MMA + TAP (17% vs. 24%, p < 0.0001) and remained reduced at 36 months. Length of stay, readmissions, and emergency department visits were comparable.
CONCLUSION: A comprehensive multimodal pain regimen including laparoscopic TAP block reduced opioid use and pain scores without increasing 30-day emergency department visits or readmissions.

articles.title: Characterization of Urgent ICU Consultations in the Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Urgent ICU consultation is intended to elicit advice and consider ICU transfer. Our objective was to describe the nature and outcomes of ICU consultations across a global cohort.
DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of patients with one or more ICU consultations. A care episode was defined as consecutive urgent ICU consultations until an ICU admission or at least 2 weeks without an urgent ICU consultation. We describe consultation outcomes for the last care episode. Late escalations were defined by a Children's Resuscitation Intensity Scale score greater than 2.
SETTING: Twenty-one centers participating in the Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) cluster-randomized trial.
PATIENTS: There were 4288 urgent ICU consultations in 3625 care episodes for 3000 patients with a median (interquartile range) age of 25 months (5-99 mo).
INTERVENTIONS: In the parent EPOCH trial, hospitals were randomized to Bedside Pediatric Early Warning System or usual care; no intervention was assigned in this secondary analysis.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The outcomes of the 3000 last care episodes were in-consultation death in three (0.1%) and urgent ICU admission in 1477 (49.2%). Among 3000 first, 400 second, and 68 third consultations, the proportions of ICU admission were 42%, 44%, and 47%. The proportions of ICU admissions that were late escalation were similar across groups: 18% for first and second urgent ICU consultations, and 25% for third urgent ICU consultations. among patients having a second urgent ICU consultation, patients who had received resuscitation interventions in their first urgent ICU consultation (and remained on the ward) had more frequent resuscitation events (23.2% vs. 3.4%, p < 0.01) and had a similar frequency of late escalation (31.8% vs. 15.6%, p = 0.07) and ICU admission (51.1% vs. 43.1%, p = 0.40) compared with patients without resuscitation in their first urgent ICU consultation.
CONCLUSIONS: Urgent consultation to the ICU is common during pediatric hospitalization. Repeated ICU consultation was associated with a similar frequency of late escalation. Resuscitation measures were provided in one of 12 ICU consultations where patients were not admitted to ICU and were a risk factor for late escalation in subsequent consultations.
authors: Evaluation of Processes of Care and the Outcomes of Children in Hospital (EPOCH) Investigators

articles.title: Low Physical Activity and Reported Barriers Among Survivors of Critical Illness: A Mixed-Method Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine physical activity levels in survivors of critical illness across 6 months, and to understand the barriers and facilitators of physical activity.
DESIGN: Prospective, longitudinal, convergent mixed-methods study.
SETTING: Functional testing laboratory.
PATIENTS: Adults admitted to the ICU for at least 72 hours with acute respiratory failure or sepsis.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Patients wore an accelerometer starting at hospital discharge, at 3- and 6-month follow-up to quantify daily step counts. At 6 months, physical function and patient-reported outcomes were collected in-person, with a subset of participants completing semi-structured interviews. Eighty-two patients were enrolled, with 67 (82%) having physical activity data with median age of 60 years (interquartile range [IQR], 52-66 yr), 54% male, and ICU stay 9.0 days [IQR, 5.8-17.0 d]. The median daily steps were 1358 (IQR, 742-2799) in 50 patients at baseline, 2305 (IQR, 1081-3898) in 54 patients at 3 months, and 2826 (IQR, 1609-4781) in 44 patients at 6 months. Higher comorbidity burden and earlier measurement associated with lower step counts. At 6 months, patients walked a mean of 344 ± 169 meters on the 6-minute walk test and reported being sedentary a median of 300 min/days (150-480 min/d). Eleven participants completed interviews, yielding three themes: 1) "a marathon, not a sprint": the extended ICU recovery trajectory; 2) engagement in physical activity is highly regulated by personal context; 3) value-driven and motivation-informed physical activity decisions. Mixed-methods integration demonstrated that qualitative themes expanded upon quantitative findings to explain nonlinear recovery patterns, contextualizing persistent sedentary behavior, and revealing that motivational and behavioral gaps are not captured by accelerometry.
CONCLUSIONS: Survivors showed gradual improvement in daily steps over 6 months yet remained below recommended activity levels. Survivorship and attrition biases may lead to overestimation of step counts, further warranting larger studies. Integrating quantitative and qualitative data reveals modifiable contextual factors that may inform the design of pragmatic physical activity interventions.
authors: Trajectories of Recovery after ACutE and cRitical illness (TRACER) study group

articles.title: Evaluation of Sequential Organ Failure Assessment-2 Performance Across Demographic Subgroups: An External Validation Using MIMIC-IV.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the discrimination and calibration of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-2 score for ICU mortality across demographic subgroups defined by age, sex, race and ethnicity, primary language, and insurance status.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Single academic medical center in the northeastern United States (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, MA), using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV database (version 3.1), 2008-2022, a dataset external to the SOFA-2 development cohort.
PATIENTS: Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) with at least one ICU admission. The first ICU admission of the first qualifying hospitalization per patient was analyzed.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: First-day SOFA-2 scores were calculated from the worst values recorded during the first 24 hours of ICU admission across six organ systems, with ICU mortality as the primary outcome. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and calibration using intercept and slope, with subgroup differences in AUROC estimated by bootstrap resampling. Among 64,015 ICU patients (mean [sd] age, 64.6 [17.1] yr; 56.1% male; 66.1% White), overall AUROC was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.76-0.77). Discrimination declined significantly with age: AUROC, 0.85 (0.83-0.87) for ages 18-44 years vs. 0.72 (0.70-0.73) for ages 75 or older (ΔAUROC, -0.14 [95% CI, -0.16 to -0.11]), with systematic underprediction in older patients. Discrimination was significantly decreased among non-English speakers (ΔAUROC, -0.04) but did not differ across documented racial/ethnic groups. Patients with missing demographic information had markedly higher mortality than the overall cohort rate of 7.2% (14.1% for missing race/ethnicity; 23.1% for missing language).
CONCLUSIONS: SOFA-2 demonstrated good overall performance but with clinically meaningful variation across subgroups, particularly with age and language. Patients with missing demographic data experienced markedly higher mortality. These findings argue for routine equity evaluation as a complement to traditional validation of clinical prediction tools.

articles.title: The Effect of Guanfacine on Delirium in Surgical and Trauma ICU Patients: A Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of conducting a randomized controlled trial investigating guanfacine for ICU delirium, including assessment of recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, and data completeness, while estimating treatment effects to inform future trial design.
DESIGN: Single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial conducted from November 2020 to February 2023.
SETTING: Surgical and Trauma ICUs at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Hospital.
PATIENTS: One hundred critically ill adults with Confusion Assessment Method-ICU-confirmed delirium randomized 1:1 to guanfacine or placebo.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients received 2 mg guanfacine or matching placebo nightly for up to 14 days, or until ICU discharge or delirium resolution.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Primary feasibility outcomes included protocol adherence (target ≥ 90%), retention (target ≥ 80%), recruitment rate (target ≥ 2 patients/mo), and data completeness (target ≥ 95%). Most feasibility targets were achieved: protocol adherence was 100%, retention was 100%, and data completeness was 100%. Recruitment was significantly impacted by COVID-19 pandemic disruptions, achieving 0.9 patients/wk during active recruitment periods.For clinical outcomes, in unadjusted analyses, median delirium and coma-free days were higher with guanfacine than placebo (2 [interquartile range [IQR], 0-6] vs. 1 [IQR, 0-4]; p = 0.02); however, this association was not statistically significant after adjustment for prespecified baseline covariates. ICU and hospital length of stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ significantly between groups. No hemodynamic differences or safety concerns were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study successfully supports feasibility for a definitive trial, with excellent protocol adherence, adequate retention, and preliminary signals that warrant further evaluation. Although adjusted analyses were not statistically significant, the observed unadjusted difference in delirium and coma-free days and favorable safety profile support progression to a multicenter trial informed by these pilot estimates.

articles.title: Composite Endpoints in Critical Care Delirium Trials.
articles.abstract: Delirium is an abnormal mental status, commonly occurring among critically ill patients, in which a person's attention and awareness change acutely. Delirium is associated with negative outcomes, including death. Furthermore, a longer duration of delirium is associated with long-term cognitive impairment in survivors of critical illness. Hence, there is a need for novel interventions that reduce the duration of delirium; however, measuring and analyzing "duration of delirium" as an endpoint in randomized trials is challenging due to the episodic nature of delirium and the competing events of coma and death, which can bias analyses of duration of delirium. Given these challenges, delirium trials have adopted one of two composite endpoints: delirium- and coma-free days, defined as the number of days alive without delirium or coma for both survivors and nonsurvivors, and an alternative composite that ranks death as the worst state and orders days alive without delirium or coma among survivors. To date, these composite endpoints have not been rigorously evaluated. Hence, herein we use data from the Maximizing Efficacy of Targeted Sedation and Reducing Neurologic Dysfunction (MENDS) trial to motivate the use of composite endpoints in critical care delirium trials, discuss how to define the effect of treatment on each composite endpoint and their clinical interpretability, and present a method for visualizing how the treatment effects accrue over the course of follow-up. Based on these analyses, we provide practical recommendations for the use of composite endpoints in critical care delirium trials, which could be extended to other randomized trials that rely on similar composite endpoints.

articles.title: Normocapnia Versus Mild Hypercapnia During Lung Protective Ventilation in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This trial emulation aimed to answer the question: Among patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) who receive lung protective ventilation with low tidal volume, is normocapnia through an increase in respiratory rate associated with lower mortality than mild hypercapnia?
DESIGN: Target trial emulation.
SETTING: Hospitals of the ARDS Network and Prevention and Early Treatment of Acute Lung Injury (PETAL) Network.
PATIENTS: Patients with ARDS enrolled in seven ARDS Network and PETAL Network randomized controlled trials.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A target trial was emulated, assigning participants in a 1:1 ratio to normocapnia (target Paco2 35-45 mm Hg) or mild hypercapnia (target Paco2 50-55 mm Hg) for 4 days following the initiation of lung protective ventilation. The primary outcome was 90-day in-hospital mortality. Of 5367 potentially eligible subjects, 292 patients were assigned to normocapnia and 292 to mild hypercapnia. Separation in Paco2 values was preserved over the 4-day period of emulated intervention. Both groups had median pH greater than or equal to 7.33. Bicarbonate levels, driving pressure, tidal volume, and dead-space fraction did not differ clinically significantly between groups, while median respiratory rate was 33.0 breaths/min in the normocapnia vs. 28.0 breaths/min in the mild hypercapnia group (p < 0.001). Death within 90 days occurred in 84 of 292 patients (28.8%) in the normocapnia group and in 84 of 292 patients (28.8%) in the mild hypercapnia group (log-rank p = 0.842). This result persisted in subgroups such as older (≥ 65 yr) and obese (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m2) patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ARDS who received lung protective ventilation, normocapnia through an increase in respiratory rate was not associated with lower mortality than mild hypercapnia. As this finding is derived from a trial emulation, it should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for significant residual bias.

articles.title: Circulating Cell-Free Mitochondrial DNA, Delirium, and Long-Term Cognitive Impairment in Critically Ill Adults With Sepsis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: During sepsis, circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) is released and elevated due to cell injury, augments the immune response, and may contribute to organ dysfunction. Delirium is common and deleterious during sepsis, but little is known about the relationship between mitochondrial injury and delirium during sepsis. We sought therefore to examine associations between ccf-mtDNA and delirium and other clinical outcomes during sepsis.
DESIGN: Multicenter, prospective cohort study.
SETTING: Medical and surgical ICUs in university and community hospitals in Nashville, TN.
PATIENTS: Four hundred eighty patients with sepsis plus shock and/or acute respiratory failure.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We measured ccf-mtDNA in plasma collected on multiple days (study days 1, 3, and 5) during sepsis and assessed participants bid for delirium and coma using the validated Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU and Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale. We then assessed survivors' cognitive function 3 and 12 months after hospital discharge using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status. During sepsis, the adjusted odds of delirium were 7% lower for individuals at the 75th percentile of ccf-mtDNA compared with those at the 25th percentile (odds ratio [OR], 0.93; 95% CI, 0.86-0.99; p = 0.048). ccf-mtDNA was marginally associated with in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.99-1.20; p = 0.08), but was not associated with coma (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.90-1.05; p = 0.31) or 3-month (beta, 0.23; 95% CI, -1.58 to 2.05; p = 0.80) and 12-month (beta, -0.36; 95% CI, -2.13 to 1.42; p = 0.69) cognitive outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter, prospective cohort study, higher levels of ccf-mtDNA were associated with lower odds of delirium, a result that contradicted our hypothesis. This provocative finding should be interpreted cautiously until replicated and explained by future studies.

articles.title: Alarm Fatigue Across Critical Care Domains: Comparative Insights and Independent Predictors From a Cross-Sectional Multicenter Survey Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Alarm fatigue, the desensitization to excessive false alarms, threatens patient safety and staff performance across critical care domains. It is unclear whether alarm fatigue differs between hospital departments. This study compared alarm fatigue among staff in the ICU, cardiac telemetry ward (CTW), and operating room (OR), and, secondarily, identified its independent determinants.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional, multicenter survey study.
SETTING: ICUs, a CTW, and ORs.
PATIENTS: A total of 514 healthcare professionals working in the ICU, CTW, and OR.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Alarm fatigue was assessed using the Dutch-translated Charité Alarm Fatigue Questionnaire, which includes alarm stress and alarm coping subscales. Participants also rated their self-perceived alarm fatigue on a 1-10 scale and the percentage of perceived false alarms. Telemetry staff reported the highest self-perceived alarm fatigue (B = 0.65; 95% CI, 0.06-1.24; p = 0.032) and perceived false alarms (B = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.23-1.30; p = 0.005), while OR staff reported the lowest (B = -1.01; 95% CI, -1.59 to -0.43; p < 0.001). Second, physicians (B = -0.13; 95% CI, -0.25 to -0.01; p < 0.031) and less experienced staff (< 3 mo; B = -0.34; 95% CI, -0.68 to -0.01; p = 0.046) reported lower alarm fatigue.
CONCLUSIONS: Alarm fatigue varied significantly across departments and professions, being highest in telemetry staff and lowest among physicians and less experienced personnel. Targeted department-specific interventions and longitudinal research are necessary to mitigate alarm fatigue and enhance patient safety.

articles.title: Effective dose for successful insertion of a laryngeal mask and impact on discharge time of alfentanil combined with remimazolam besylate in ambulatory hysteroscopic surgery: study protocol for a single-centre, prospective, randomised, controlled clinical trial in China.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alfentanil, a μ-opioid receptor agonist, offers a rapid onset of action, quick recovery and stable haemodynamics, making it an ideal agent for ambulatory surgery anaesthesia. However, the optimal dosing regimen of alfentanil in combination with remimazolam besylate—a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine—for laryngeal mask airway (LMA) insertion has not yet been investigated. This study aims to assess the effective dose of alfentanil and whether alfentanil provides non-inferior discharge times and other relevant outcomes compared with remifentanil in patients undergoing ambulatory hysteroscopic surgery.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-centre, prospective, randomised controlled trial enrolling 160 patients undergoing hysteroscopic surgery. The study consists of two phases. In the first phase, the modified Dixon up-and-down method will be used to determine the median effective dose (ED₅₀) and 95% effective dose (ED₉₅) of alfentanil and remifentanil, each in combination with remimazolam, for successful LMA insertion. In the second phase, patients will be randomised to receive alfentanil or remifentanil and postoperative discharge time and recovery profiles will be compared between groups. The primary outcomes are the ED₅₀ and ED₉₅ for successful LMA insertion and the non-inferiority of discharge time in the alfentanil group compared with the remifentanil group. Secondary outcomes include induction-related safety, postoperative adverse events and the overall safety and efficacy of alfentanil for LMA-based general anaesthesia in ambulatory hysteroscopic surgery.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This randomised controlled trial was reviewed and approved by the Ethics Committee of the Guangzhou First People’s Hospital (Approval number: S-2023-219-01). The results will be published in peer-­reviewed journals.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2600121808.

articles.title: Perianaesthetic comfort in patients undergoing day-case biopsy surgery: A pilot feasibility study.
articles.abstract: Day-case biopsy surgery combines procedural stress with diagnostic uncertainty. This pilot feasibility study aimed to describe perianaesthetic comfort, identify associated factors, and assess the Perianaesthetic Comfort Scale (PCS) in this setting. A descriptive, cross-sectional census over one year in one Turkish university day-surgery unit recruited 46 of 50 eligible patients (92%). Mean age was 55.1 (SD 14.4) years; 60.9% were male. Mean total PCS score was 117.9 (SD 10.2; range 90-134; possible range 24-144). Scores were lower with chronic comorbidity (115.4, SD 10.5) than without (121.0, SD 9.1; U = 364, p = 0.025, r = 0.33, power 64%). No associations were found with age, gender, education, prior surgery, anaesthesia mode, fasting or anaesthesia duration, or pain. Internal consistency was low (Cronbach's alpha 0.65). These preliminary findings suggest chronic comorbidity may reduce perianaesthetic comfort; the PCS requires further psychometric evaluation before use in day-case biopsy populations.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of the Preoperative Pan-Immune-Inflammation Value for Adverse Outcomes After Hip Arthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) is an emerging systemic inflammatory biomarker, but its prognostic value in patients undergoing hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between preoperative PIV and postoperative adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included older adults who have femoral neck fractures undergoing hip arthroplasty between June 2024 and May 2026. Preoperative PIV was calculated from routine complete blood count parameters. Multivariable logistic regressions, receiver operating characteristic curve analyses, DeLong tests, restricted cubic spline analyses, and bootstrap validations were performed to evaluate the predictive value of PIV. Nomograms integrating PIV with clinical variables were developed.
RESULTS: Among 594 patients, 38 (6.4%) had postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission and 67 (11.3%) developed pulmonary infection. High PIV was independently associated with ICU admission (odds ratio [OR], 6.551; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.022 to 14.203; P < 0.001) and pulmonary infection (OR, 3.995; 95% CI, 2.202 to 7.248; P < 0.001). Preoperative PIV showed good discrimination for ICU admission (area under the curve [AUC], 0.860; 95% CI, 0.793 to 0.928) and moderate discrimination for pulmonary infection (AUC, 0.690; 95% CI, 0.612 to 0.768). Adding PIV to clinical models improved discrimination for ICU admission (AUC, 0.928) and pulmonary infection (AUC, 0.842).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative PIV is independently associated with postoperative ICU admission and pulmonary infection after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. As a simple and cost-effective biomarker, PIV may facilitate perioperative risk stratification and early identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: Real-world paediatric inflammatory bowel disease surgery: International variation in care and practice.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Paediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) surgery is delivered across heterogeneous settings, with limited paediatric-specific evidence guiding organisation of care, perioperative management, and operative strategy. We characterised contemporary international practice.
METHODS: An international cross-sectional centre-level survey was conducted within the Paediatric IBD Surgery Network. A 28-item questionnaire addressing organisation of care, perioperative management, procedural volumes, and surgical practice was distributed electronically. Analyses were descriptive and performed per question.
RESULTS: Twenty-six of 36 invited centres from 14 countries responded (72%). University or teaching hospitals represented 96% of centres, and paediatric surgeons accounted for 69% of respondents. Regular multidisciplinary team meetings were reported by 85%. Use of an enhanced recovery after surgery protocol, structured nutritional screening, and deferral of elective surgery for nutritional optimisation whenever feasible were reported by 50%, 54%, and 42% of centres, respectively. Medication withholding varied, from corticosteroids in 69% of centres to anti-tumour necrosis factor (anti-TNF) agents in 31% and individual newer biologic or small-molecule classes in 15-19%. Formal national centralisation was reported as recommended or mandatory by 42%. Median annual luminal Crohn's disease surgery volume per centre was two procedures (interquartile range [IQR] 1-5) in 2018, 2.5 (IQR 2-5) in 2022, and 2.5 (IQR 1-5) in 2024. Median annual ileal pouch-anal anastomosis volume in children with ulcerative colitis was 1 (IQR 0.1-3.5).
CONCLUSIONS: Considerable variation was observed in perioperative optimisation and medication management, integration of medical and surgical therapy, centralisation, and operative strategy. These findings provide a baseline for international benchmarking, consensus development, and prospective collaborative research.

articles.title: Intravenous Paracetamol for Perioperative Shivering Prophylaxis in Patients Undergoing Spinal Anesthesia: A Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative shivering (POS) is a common, distressing complication of spinal anesthesia (SA), but a standard prevention has not been identified. This study aimed to determine whether intravenous (IV) paracetamol prevents POS in patients undergoing surgery under SA.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind controlled trial, 92 patients scheduled for surgery under SA received IV paracetamol 15 mg/kg (n = 46) or an equal volume of saline (n = 46) over 15 min before SA. The primary outcome was the overall incidence of POS. The primary analysis was per-protocol (PP) (n = 86; paracetamol 42; control 44) after exclusion of 6 patients postrandomization. Post hoc best-case and worst-case sensitivity analyses including all 92 patients were also performed. Secondary outcomes included shivering score, shivering duration, rescue pethidine requirements, temperature changes, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Baseline and intraoperative characteristics were comparable between groups. In the PP analysis, POS incidence was lower with paracetamol than control (26.2% vs. 50.0%; p = 0.023). This was not robust to missing-data assumptions: the best-case analysis remained significant (23.9% vs. 52.2%; p = 0.005), but the worst-case analysis did not (32.6% vs. 47.8%; p = 0.137), and the fragility index was 2. Intraoperative shivering occurred in 4.8% vs. 22.7% (p = 0.016). Paracetamol also demonstrated lower highest shivering score (p = 0.039), shorter duration of shivering (p = 0.031), and less rescue pethidine use (p = 0.019). There were no statistically significant differences in temperature changes, hypothermia, or nausea and vomiting between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In the PP analysis, prophylactic IV paracetamol was associated with a lower incidence, severity, and duration of POS and a lower need for rescue pethidine use. However, the primary finding was not robust under worst-case assumptions (fragility index 2); larger confirmatory trials are warranted. Trial Registration: Thai Clinical Trials Registry: TCTR20210209004.

articles.title: Association Between Cytomegalovirus and Fibromyalgia: A Large-Scale Retrospective Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fibromyalgia is a chronic widespread pain disorder with incompletely understood pathogenesis. Viral infections have been proposed as potential triggers, but studies examining cytomegalovirus (CMV), a herpesvirus establishing lifelong latency, and fibromyalgia are scarce. We investigated the association between CMV infection and subsequent fibromyalgia.
METHODS: This retrospective matched case-control study used a database of over 370,000 individuals from 01/2003 to 12/2025. Cases were defined by at least two fibromyalgia diagnoses separated by ≥ 6 months. Up to five controls per case were matched on year of birth, sex, lookback period, and neighborhood socioeconomic status. Exposure was defined as a positive CMV IgM or IgG test, with a two-year washout period. Conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios adjusted for psychiatric disorders, sleep disorders, obesity, and smoking.
RESULTS: After exclusions, 1,811 cases were matched to 8,988 controls. Prior CMV exposure was documented in 50.7% of cases versus 45.6% of controls (P < 0.001). CMV infection was significantly associated with fibromyalgia (adjusted odds ratio 1.321; 95% CI 1.173-1.488; P < 0.001). The association persisted across stricter case definitions and alternative washout periods.
CONCLUSIONS: CMV infection is significantly associated with increased odds of fibromyalgia. Prospective studies are warranted to establish causality and underlying mechanisms.
