articles.title: Surgical Approaches and Extent of Resection for Non-myasthenic Thymic Epithelial Tumors:Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors are rare anterior mediastinal neoplasms that include thymoma, thymic carcinoma, and neuroendocrine tumors. Complete surgical resection remains the cornerstone of curative treatment;however, the optimal extent of thymectomy and surgical approach are still being debated. Advances in minimally invasive techniques, such as video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery and robot-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (RATS), have shifted practice away from traditional median sternotomy. Evidence consistently shows that complete resection is the most important prognostic factor across all subtypes. Regarding early-stage thymoma, multicenter and propensity score-matched studies showed that partial thymectomy may achieve similar oncologic outcomes to total thymectomy, with shorter hospital stays and reduced perioperative morbidity. Conversely, total thymectomy remains essential for thymic carcinoma or invasive disease. Minimally invasive approaches, particularly RATS, offer advantages including precise dissection in narrow mediastinal spaces, less blood loss, and faster recovery without compromising the margin status or long-term survival. Emerging data also suggest potential long-term immunological and oncologic consequences of total thymectomy in adults, underscoring the need for individualized surgical planning. Overall, current evidence supports tailoring the extent and approach of thymectomy according to the histological subtype, tumor stage, and patient factors, balancing oncologic radicality with the preservation of physiological thymic function. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 319-325, August, 2026.

articles.title: Chronic midazolam exposure disrupts allopregnanolone responses to surgical stress, leading to postoperative cognitive impairment in rats.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Long-term benzodiazepine use is a risk factor for postoperative delirium, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated whether chronic benzodiazepine exposure disrupts endogenous neurosteroid responses to surgical stress and thereby exacerbates postoperative neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction.
METHODS: Male rats received chronic midazolam administration (1 mg/kg/day) for 14 days and subsequently underwent intestinal manipulation surgery. Postoperative cognitive function was assessed using trace fear conditioning. Neuroinflammatory markers and endogenous allopregnanolone (ALLO) levels were measured in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. The effects of perioperative exogenous ALLO supplementation were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Chronic midazolam exposure did not impair cognitive performance;however, when combined with surgery, it reduced trace memory retention without affecting context memory. This impairment was accompanied by amplified increases in pro-inflammatory cytokines and suppression of the surgery-induced rise in endogenous ALLO. Perioperative administration of exogenous ALLO attenuated neuroinflammatory responses and restored trace memory performance, despite no sustained recovery of endogenous ALLO levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Chronic benzodiazepine exposure may impair endogenous ALLO responses to surgical stress, enhancing neuroinflammation and postoperative cognitive dysfunction. These findings suggest a neurosteroid mechanism linking long-term benzodiazepine exposure to postoperative brain vulnerability and highlight perioperative ALLO as a potential preventive strategy. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 373-381, August, 2026.

articles.title: Perioperative neurocognitive outcomes after robot-assisted pelvic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reported proportions, comparative risk and prognostic factors.
articles.abstract: Delirium and cognitive decline may complicate recovery after robot-assisted pelvic surgery, but their frequency and relationship to positioning remain uncertain. We assessed reported proportions, comparative surgical risk and prognostic factors. PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP were searched through 4 August 2026. Eligible adult robotic pelvic studies reported objective cognitive testing or delirium. Two reviewers performed original screening, extraction and question-specific bias appraisal. Post hoc logit random-effects meta-analyses summarized prospective cohorts using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals in R. Twenty-six reports represented 25 studies. Five cognitive cohorts (356 participants) yielded 29.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 20.2-39.8%); excluding Beck yielded 31.8% (20.7-45.4%). Three delirium cohorts (245 participants) yielded a descriptive model summary of 10.3% (2.2-37.0%). Individual delirium proportions were 8/82 (9.8%; exact 95% CI 4.3-18.3%), 4/80 (5.0%; 1.4-12.3%) and 14/83 (16.9%; 9.5-26.7%). The approximate 95% prediction interval from the delirium meta-analysis was very wide (<0.1-99.8%). The same-procedure prostatectomy comparison yielded an unadjusted risk ratio of 1.06 (0.73-1.55) for early cognitive decline. Comparative evidence was of low or very low certainty. Definitions, surveillance and selection limited interpretation; Trendelenburg-duration findings were inconsistent. These proportions describe selected study-defined outcomes. They do not establish attributable robotic or positioning risk, a safe exposure threshold, or benefit from horizontal breaks. Standardized prospective measurement is needed.

articles.title: Adolescent Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Can Be the First Clue to Multisystem Mitochondrial Disease.
articles.abstract: Up to 40% of children with mitochondrial disease develop hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) during their disease course, but HCM is almost never the first presenting manifestation. When it is, the underlying mitochondrial disorder is easily missed: the cardiomyopathy is managed in isolation, and extracardiac findings that emerge later may be dismissed as unrelated. We describe an adolescent whose severe HCM was the first major manifestation of clinicopathologically confirmed multisystem mitochondrial disease with a phenotype consistent with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. Her cardiomyopathy was managed in isolation for over a year before optic atrophy, primary ovarian insufficiency, osteopenia, and exercise intolerance were ultimately recognized as part of a single mitochondrial process. Endomyocardial and skeletal muscle biopsy confirmed mitochondrial pathology. The diagnosis directly changed management: cofactor supplementation was initiated, her visual acuity stabilized on idebenone, and perioperative planning for transplantation was adapted to prevent catabolic decompensation. Her cardiac disease progressed to heart failure requiring transplantation at age 16 years, but she remains clinically stable with preserved graft function more than 15 years later. This case challenges the assumption that mitochondrial disease should enter the differential only after neurologic dysfunction appears. General pediatricians, who see the whole child longitudinally, are uniquely positioned to recognize when dysfunction in other high-energy tissues points toward a unifying mitochondrial diagnosis in a child with cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma : an age- and sex-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The purpose of this study was to compare surgical techniques and postoperative outcomes in an age- and sex-matched cohort of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) for neck of femur fracture (#NOF) and for osteoarthritis (OA).
METHODS: A single-centre, consecutive series of patients at minimum one-year follow-up following THA for #NOF were compared with a 1:1 age- and sex-matched cohort of patients following THA for osteoarthritis from the same institution. The primary outcome measure was frequency of dislocation at one year postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included rates of all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term postoperatively. Cox regression compared medium-term outcomes between groups, accounting for unequal follow-up duration.
RESULTS: A total of 722 patients were included, with 361 in each group. BMI was greater in the OA group (28.9 kg/m2 vs 24.7 kg/m2; p < 0.001). Sex, age, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, and comorbidity profile did not differ between groups (p > 0.247). Overall, 151 patients (41.8%) in the #NOF group received dual-mobility implants, compared with eight (2.2%) in the OA group (p < 0.001). Femoral offset was similar between groups (42.6 mm and 42.7 mm, p = 0.892). Dislocation rates were greater in the #NOF group than the OA group at one-year (4.4% vs 1.1%; p = 0.011) and by final follow-up. The one-year rates of periprosthetic fracture, all-cause revision, and mortality were similar between groups (p > 0.340), although risk of mortality was greater by final follow-up after THA for #NOF (hazard ratio 1.577; p = 0.033).
CONCLUSION: Despite the more frequent use of dual-mobility implants in THA for #NOF than OA and the otherwise comparable patient demographics and implants used, the risk of early dislocation after THA for #NOF was four times greater than in an age- and sex-matched elective THA cohort. Early postoperative complication rates were otherwise comparable between the groups.

Patient-reported disability has insufficient clinical accuracy for predicting physical function in survivors of critical illness: a secondary analysis of a cluster-randomised trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-ICU care often misses patients unable to attend in-person clinic visits. Remote assessments of physical function might increase access to ICU aftercare. We investigated whether patient-reported disability predicts handgrip strength (HGS) and the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) distance with sufficient clinical accuracy.
METHODS: This secondary analysis of the stepped-wedge cluster-randomised Enhanced Recovery after Intensive Care trial included patients from 10 German ICU clusters who completed the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 plus either HGS, the 2MWT, or both, 6 months after ICU discharge. Relationships between WHODAS 2.0, HGS, and 2MWT were analysed using scatter plots, correlation coefficients, linear regressions, and Bland-Altman plots. Predictions of HGS and the 2MWT were compared with the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for both measures.
RESULTS: Of 1463 enrolled patients, 620 were analysed. The median WHODAS 2.0 sum score was 11 (Q1, Q3: 3, 22). The median HGS, expressed as a percentage of the expected value (%exp), was 70.6%exp (Q1, Q3: 54.4, 85.6), and the median 2MWT distance was 73.7%exp (Q1, Q3: 61.5, 85.8). The 2MWT was not completed by 59% of patients. Higher disability was moderately correlated with lower HGS (Spearman %exp: -0.41) and shorter 2MWT distance (Spearman %exp: -0.47). In multivariable regression models, the WHODAS 2.0 sum score predicted HGS in kg (β: -0.27 [95% CI: -0.33 to -0.22]; P<0.001) and 2MWT distance in m (β: -1.94 [95% CI: -2.37 to -1.51]; P<0.001), but the limits of agreement exceeded the MCIDs.
CONCLUSIONS: With increasing disability, HGS and 2MWT performance declined, although correlations were moderate and uncertainty of predictions exceeded MCIDs of both instruments. Remote WHODAS 2.0 assessments cannot replace in-person physical function testing.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03671447.

articles.title: Sugammadex versus Neostigmine-Glycopyrrolate for Reducing the Risk of Postoperative Urinary Retention in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Otolaryngologic Surgery: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative urinary retention (POUR) is a clinically important postoperative complication, particularly in patients at high risk for voiding dysfunction. Sugammadex reverses aminosteroid neuromuscular blockade without requiring concomitant antimuscarinic administration and may therefore reduce the risk of POUR compared with neostigmine-glycopyrrolate.
METHODS: In this prospective randomised trial, 124 adults at high risk for POUR undergoing elective otolaryngologic surgery were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive neostigmine-glycopyrrolate or sugammadex for neuromuscular block reversal. The primary outcome was confirmed POUR, defined as inability to void requiring urinary catheterisation with an ultrasound-confirmed bladder volume ≥400 mL. Secondary outcomes included postoperative nausea and vomiting, haemodynamic events, patient-reported thirst intensity, and hospital length of stay.
RESULTS: Confirmed POUR occurred in 12 of 62 patients (19.4%) in the neostigmine-glycopyrrolate group and in none of the 62 patients (0%) in the sugammadex group (risk difference, 19.4%; 95% CI, 9.5%-30.9%; P < 0.001; NNT = 6). Exploratory analysis showed that symptomatic urinary retention was also more frequent with neostigmine-glycopyrrolate than with sugammadex (40.3% vs. 4.8%; P < 0.001). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative nausea and vomiting, haemodynamic events, thirst intensity, or hospital length of stay; secondary-outcome comparisons were not powered to detect between-group differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients at high risk for POUR undergoing elective otolaryngologic surgery, sugammadex reduced the risk of confirmed POUR compared with neostigmine-glycopyrrolate. Comparisons of secondary outcomes were underpowered and should be interpreted cautiously.
REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06398899; principal investigator: Pei-Lin Lin; registered on 5 March 2024).

articles.title: Expertise by Design: Why Modern Training Requires Deliberate Cultivation.
Postoperative Digital Health Interventions After Non-Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recovery after non-cardiac surgery increasingly occurs at home, where clinical deterioration may go unrecognized. Digital health interventions may extend postoperative surveillance beyond discharge, but vary widely in components and clinician involvement. We evaluated their association with readmission and other outcomes.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to December 12, 2025, for prospective randomized and observational studies comparing digital health interventions with standard care in adults after non-cardiac surgery. Readmission was the primary outcome; all-cause and major complications, emergency room (ER) visits, length of stay (LOS), and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were secondary. Interventions were grouped by whether a clinician reviewed patient-submitted data and had the ability to take action (active clinician involvement). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and standardized mean differences (SMD). p values were adjusted for multiple comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg).
RESULTS: In 38 studies (30 randomized, 8 observational; 7,494 patients), digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions (17 studies, n=3,944; RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.99, adjusted p=0.045), ER visits (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.97), and major complications (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.94), but not all-cause complications (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79-1.08) or LOS (MD -0.04 days, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.18). Pain and anxiety were lower and functional status, quality-of-life, and satisfaction scores higher (absolute SMD 0.41-0.69). Readmission risk was lower with active clinician involvement (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.92) but not without it (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78-1.18; interaction p=0.029). Heterogeneity in interventions, cohorts, and outcomes was substantial (PROM I² 50-97%).
CONCLUSIONS: Digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions, ER visits, major complications, and better PROMs, but not fewer all-cause complications or shorter LOS. The readmission association was concentrated in studies with active clinician involvement. Heterogeneity was substantial and certainty of evidence low to very low.

articles.title: Quality of Recovery After Primary Breast Cancer Surgery: A Randomized, Two-Centre, Triple-Blinded Trial Comparing Erector Spinae Plane Block and Intravenous Lidocaine Infusion Within a Multimodal Analgesia Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The erector spinae plane block (ESPB) is widely used for primary breast cancer surgery (BCS), though its clinical benefits within optimized multimodal analgesia pathways remain uncertain. Intravenous lidocaine infusion (IVLI) offers a simple, reproducible alternative with potential systemic analgesic effects. This randomized, tripleblinded, placebo controlled, twocentre trial compared the quality of recovery after ESPB versus IVLI for BCS.
METHODS: Eighty adult patients undergoing primary BCS, with or without axillary dissection, were randomized to receive either ultrasoundguided ESPB (n=40) or intraoperative IVLI (n=40), in addition to a standardized multimodal analgesic protocol. The primary outcome was quality of recovery (QoR15) score at 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, adverse events, and rescue analgesia requirements.
RESULTS: Both interventions produced excellent postoperative recovery, with 24hour QoR15 scores approaching preoperative baselines with no significant difference between groups (mean (SD) 24-hour QoR score; ESPB vs. IVLI group, 137.7(17.9) vs. 136.3(8.8), p=0.61). Pain burden and analgesic requirements over the first 24 hours were similarly low, and no ESPB or lidocainerelated adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Within a standardized multimodal analgesic framework, postoperative recovery and analgesic outcomes did not differ significantly between IVLI and ESPB, suggesting that IVLI may offer a pragmatic alternative when regional anesthesia expertise is limited.

articles.title: Integration of different robotic platforms in a thoracic surgery program: perioperative outcomes and learning curves from a prospective clinical implementation study.
CABG in uncontrolled thyrotoxicosis complicated by thyroid storm: A case report.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery in patients with active thyrotoxicosis carries substantially increased perioperative risks. We report a case of urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in a 43-year-old man with severe biochemical thyrotoxicosis and critical left main coronary artery disease who presented with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. Urgent off-pump CABG was performed with intra-aortic balloon pump support. Within 48 hours of surgery, the patient developed a thyroid storm characterized by fever (40 °C), tachycardia (140-180 beats/min), encephalopathy, and jaundice. The condition was successfully treated with anti-thyroid drugs and intravenous hydrocortisone. The patient recovered fully and was euthyroid at follow-up. Early recognition and prompt multidrug treatment of postoperative thyroid storm are life-saving.

articles.title: Efficacy of pulsed radiofrequency combined with greater occipital nerve blockade in refractory chronic migraine.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveChronic migraine may be resistant to treatment and can impair an individual's quality of life. Greater occipital nerve blockade is a commonly used method for migraine management, whereas pulsed radiofrequency represents a promising neuromodulation technique. This study evaluated the clinical contribution of pulsed radiofrequency as an adjuvant therapy to greater occipital nerve blockade in refractory cases.MethodsThis retrospective study included 107 patients diagnosed with chronic migraine who did not respond to at least two prophylactic treatments. Patients were divided into two groups. Group A (n = 45) received four weekly sessions of ultrasound-guided greater occipital nerve blockade with 0.5% bupivacaine. Group B (n = 62) received the same greater occipital nerve blockade, with the addition of a 4-min pulsed radiofrequency application during the fourth session. Pain intensity, attack frequency, attack duration, and the number of days of analgesic use were recorded at baseline and at 1, 3, and 6 months.ResultsBoth groups exhibited significant improvement in all outcome measures compared with baseline at each follow-up (p < 0.001). At month 3, Group B had significantly lower visual analog scale scores (4.06 vs. 5.18; p = 0.039), attack frequency (4.24 vs. 5.09; p = 0.005), attack duration (13.55 vs. 19.76 h; p = 0.024), and days of analgesic use (5.20 vs. 6.56 days/month; p = 0.038) than Group A. At month 6, attack duration (14.10 vs. 22.73 h; p = 0.043) and days of analgesic use (5.43 vs. 7.98 days/month; p = 0.048) remained significantly lower in Group B.ConclusionBoth greater occipital nerve blockade and greater occipital nerve blockade + pulsed radiofrequency are effective and safe for the management of refractory chronic migraine. The addition of pulsed radiofrequency provided incremental clinical benefits in pain control and reduced analgesic use at 3 and 6 months, suggesting superior outcomes of the combined approach.

articles.title: Development and validation of a neonatal mouse brain stereotaxic injection platform for maintaining perioperative physiological homeostasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal mouse brain stereotaxic injection is an essential experimental technique for investigating neurodevelopmental regulation and neonatal neurological disorders. However, immature thermoregulation and limited anesthetic tolerance make neonatal mice highly susceptible to uncontrolled perioperative hypothermia and physiological instability, which compromise postoperative survival, increase experimental variability, and may confound disease modeling and the interpretation of intervention outcomes.
NEW METHOD: We developed an integrated digital temperature-controlled stereotaxic platform that combines non-invasive head fixation, inhalation anesthesia, and real-time closed-loop thermal regulation. The platform provides continuous perioperative thermal support to maintain physiological homeostasis and is compatible with a wide range of neonatal intracerebral injection applications.
RESULTS: The platform maintained stable perioperative body temperature, significantly improved postoperative survival, and reliably supported secondary intracerebral intervention after brain injury, ultra-early gene knockout, and microglial viral tracing in neonatal mice.
COMPARISON WITH EXISTING METHODS: Existing neonatal stereotaxic procedures rely on hypothermia-induced anesthesia, room-temperature surgery, or external warming methods such as warm-water systems and heating pads, which may provide insufficiently stable temperature control and require additional operational steps. In contrast, the present platform integrates stereotaxic injection and active temperature regulation, simplifying surgical procedures while enabling precise thermal management and maintaining intraoperative body temperature in neonatal mice.
CONCLUSIONS: By integrating physiological support with stereotaxic surgery, this platform provides a standardized, reliable, and reproducible approach for neonatal mouse intracerebral injection and facilitates advanced experimental manipulation in neonatal neuroscience research and disease modeling.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes in Stage 1 Palliated Infants Undergoing Noncardiac Procedures: A Comparison by Shunt Type.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interstage infants with single-ventricle (SV) physiology following Stage I palliation represent a high-risk population for noncardiac procedures requiring anesthesia. Data comparing perioperative outcomes by shunt type remain limited.
AIMS: Describe anesthetic management, perioperative complications, and postoperative outcomes in interstage SV infants undergoing noncardiac interventions and compare outcomes between right ventricle-to-pulmonary artery (Sano) and modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt (mBTTS) patients.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of interstage SV infants with Stage I palliation undergoing noncardiac surgery or nonsurgical procedures requiring anesthesia between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were stratified by shunt type.
RESULTS: A total of 208 noncardiac interventions in 120 interstage SV infants were analyzed; 136 (65.4%) encounters in 86 Sano patients and 72 (34.6%) encounters in 34 mBTTS patients. Compared with mBTTS infants, Sano patients underwent interventions at a younger age (57 [IQR 40-83] vs. 105 [59-278] days, p < 0.001) and lower weight (3.6 [3.0-4.1] vs. 4.8 [3.4-7.3] kg, p < 0.001). mBTTS procedures had higher rates of ventricular dysfunction (34.3% vs. 12.7%, p < 0.001), chromosomal abnormalities (63.9% vs. 19.1%, p < 0.001), gastrointestinal comorbidities (87.5% vs. 72.1%, p = 0.014), and hematologic comorbidities (41.7% vs. 22.8%, p = 0.006). Hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive support was the most common perioperative complication and occurred similarly between groups (31.9% mBTTS vs. 31.6% Sano, p = 0.962). There were no perioperative cardiac arrests. Rates of postoperative escalation of care (2.9%), reintubation (3.0% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999), readmission (16.2% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.999), and 30-day mortality (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999) were low and comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the high-risk physiology of interstage SV patients, perioperative outcomes were comparable between Sano and mBTTS cohorts. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not imply low procedural risk. Favorable outcomes likely reflect careful patient selection, multidisciplinary perioperative care, and specialized institutional expertise.

articles.title: Transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block versus standard analgesia for postoperative pain following open upper abdominal surgery through a midline incision: a protocol for a prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To determine whether bilateral ultrasound-guided subcostal transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block, added to standardized non-opioid multimodal analgesia, reduces early pain after open upper midline laparotomy.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial, 108 adults undergoing elective open upper abdominal surgery through a midline incision will be randomized 1:1 (stratified by procedure category) to TAP block (bupivacaine 0.25%, 30 mL per side, maximum 2.5 mg/kg) plus multimodal analgesia or multimodal analgesia alone. Outcome assessors and the statistician will be blinded; no sham block is used. The primary outcome is pain at rest on a 100-mm visual analog scale (VAS), averaged over 6, 12 and 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes include movement-evoked pain, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), consumption of each rescue analgesic, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), time to ambulation, time to first flatus and adverse events (actively monitored until 48 h after surgery or hospital discharge, whichever is later).
PLANNED ANALYSIS: The primary effect will be estimated by intention-to-treat using a mixed model for repeated measures, as the equally weighted mean between-group difference with 95% confidence interval.
CONCLUSION: This trial will quantify the incremental benefit of subcostal TAP block in a defined surgical population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (www.pactr.org) identifier is PACTR202608546707144.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Pan African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR; www.pactr.org), PACTR202608546707144, registered on 18 August 2026.

articles.title: Efficacy of Preoperative High-Power Diode Laser Irradiation in Reducing Local Anesthetic Volume: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Local anesthesia is fundamental in dental practice to ensure patient comfort and pain control during invasive procedures. This study evaluated whether preoperative high-power diode laser (HPDL) irradiation reduces the volume of local anesthetic required to achieve effective anesthesia during endodontic treatment of teeth with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis (SIP) without compromising clinical efficacy or patient comfort.
METHODS: Sixty patients (ASA I-II, aged 18-60 years) diagnosed with SIP in mandibular posterior teeth were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 30): Control Group (CG)- 1.8 mL 4% articaine with epinephrine, and Experimental Group (EG)- HPDL irradiation (810 nm; 1.2 W) at the puncture site prior to administering a volume of 0.9 mL. Primary outcomes were anesthetic success rate and onset latency. Pain intensity (VAS 0-10) was measured during needle insertion, coronal access, and instrumentation.
RESULTS: In the CG, mean VAS scores were 4.27 at puncture, 2.74 during coronal access, and 1.56 during instrumentation. Anesthetic success was achieved in 76.7% of CG, with 23.3% requiring supplemental anesthesia. The EG demonstrated a 100% anesthetic success rate with 0% requiring supplemental reinforcement (P< .05). Mean VAS scores in the EG were significantly lower: 2.33 at puncture, 1.50 during coronal access, and 0.20 during instrumentation. Profound anesthesia onset within 3 minutes was observed in 60% of EG compared to 40% in CG.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative HPDL irradiation effectively halves the required local anesthetic volume while maintaining 100% clinical efficacy and superior patient comfort during endodontic treatment of mandibular teeth with SIP.

articles.title: Continuous Regional Anesthesia: A Practical Review of Perineural and Fascial Plane Catheters, Clinical Evidence, and Troubleshooting.
articles.abstract: Continuous regional anesthesia (CRA) can extend postoperative analgesia beyond the duration of single-injection blocks and may reduce reliance on systemic opioids. The expanding use of perineural and fascial plane catheters has broadened the clinical applications of catheter-based regional analgesia across a wide range of surgical settings. However, successful CRA requires appropriate patient and catheter selection, accurate catheter placement, effective local anesthetic delivery, securement, monitoring, and timely recognition of catheter failure or complications. This review provides a practical overview of contemporary perineural and fascial plane catheter techniques and summarizes the available clinical evidence for their use in upper- and lower-limb, thoracic, cardiac, and abdominal surgery. Catheter-through-needle and catheter-over-needle systems, catheter tip configurations, pumps and delivery systems, and continuous, programmed intermittent, and patient-controlled infusion strategies are discussed. Practical aspects of ultrasound-guided catheter insertion, catheter-tip confirmation, fixation, and prevention of catheter migration are also reviewed. Current evidence suggests that continuous catheter techniques can improve postoperative analgesia and reduce opioid requirements in selected procedures, although the magnitude and consistency of benefit vary according to the surgical population, anatomical target, catheter technique, and comparator. Local anesthetic selection, concentration, infusion rate, cumulative dose, catheter location, and patient-specific risk factors should be considered to balance analgesic efficacy against motor impairment and local anesthetic systemic toxicity. Particular attention is required in patients with increased susceptibility to toxicity and when bilateral or multiple catheters are used. Catheter failure may result from inadequate dosing or spread, catheter malposition or migration, mechanical dysfunction, or pain outside the expected block distribution. A structured approach incorporating clinical assessment, catheter-site inspection, delivery-system evaluation, and ultrasound-guided assessment of injectate spread may identify reversible causes of inadequate analgesia. A stepwise troubleshooting algorithm is presented to guide catheter optimization, rescue interventions, replacement, or removal. In conclusion, effective CRA requires integration of appropriate catheter technology, individualized dosing, secure fixation, systematic monitoring, and structured troubleshooting.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients.
METHODS: This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%).
RESULTS: Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome.
CONCLUSION: Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

articles.title: Elevated Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Predicts Early Aggravation of Organ Dysfunction in Septic Patients in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), a simple marker of immune dysregulation, is associated with early organ dysfunction progression in emergency department (ED) patients with sepsis.
DESIGN: Exploratory secondary analysis of observational clustering cohort.
SETTING: Single-center ED.
PATIENTS/SUBJECTS: Among 999 patients with adjudicated infection, 364 fulfilled Sepsis-3 criteria for sepsis or septic shock and had available Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores at admission and 24 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Organ dysfunction trajectory was defined according to the evolution in SOFA score during the first 24 hours (ΔSOFA) and categorized as improving (ΔSOFA ≤ -2), stable (ΔSOFA -1 to +1), or worsening (ΔSOFA ≥ +2). Of the 364 patients, 135 (37%) were classified as improving, 187 (51%) as stable, and 42 (12%) as worsening. NLR differed significantly across trajectory groups, with median values of 12 (7-21), 12 (7-22), and 23 (10-37), respectively (p = 0.015). In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, lactate concentration, and baseline SOFA score, NLR remained independently associated with worsening organ dysfunction trajectory (odds ratio [OR] 5.55, 95% CI, 1.86-18.18; p = 0.003). Patients with worsening trajectories more frequently required ICU admission (26% vs. 5% vs. 4%; p < 0.001) and experienced higher 28-day mortality (36% vs 17% vs 17%; p = 0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: NLR was independently associated with early worsening of organ dysfunction in ED patients with sepsis. Beyond its prognostic value, NLR may provide complementary information to conventional severity assessment by reflecting immune dysregulation.

articles.title: Ketamine Vs. Etomidates and Cardiovascular Collapse During Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Secondary Analysis of the DEVICE and PREOXI Trials.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults is a high-risk procedure.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate associations of ketamine vs. etomidate with cardiovascular collapse and other peri-intubation outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Secondary analysis of individual-participant data from the DEVICE and PREOXI trials, treating induction medication as an observational exposure. The cohort included 2357 adults intubated in emergency departments or ICUs; 1822 received etomidate, 312 ketamine, and 223 other induction regimens.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was cardiovascular collapse, defined as new or increased vasopressor use, nadir systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg, or cardiac arrest between induction and 2 minutes after intubation. Secondary outcomes included severe hypoxemia (oxygen saturation < 80%) and procedural outcomes.
RESULTS: In weighted analyses, cardiovascular collapse occurred in 14.0% of etomidate recipients and 20.4% of ketamine recipients. In weighted, covariate-adjusted models, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.80; 95% CI, 1.24-2.62) and new or increased vasopressor use (aOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.02-2.23), nominally lower odds of severe hypoxemia (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.88), and shorter modeled time to successful intubation (hazard ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.02-1.33). The latter two associations were not significant after multiplicity adjustment. Estimates for systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg and cardiac arrest were too imprecise for reliable inference. Successful intubation on the first attempt and 28-day in-hospital mortality did not clearly differ between ketamine and etomidate.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Compared with etomidate, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse, primarily reflecting new or increased vasopressor use. Associations with severe hypoxemia and intubation time did not remain significant after multiplicity adjustment. Because induction medication was not randomized and residual confounding remains possible, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.

articles.title: General anesthesia or Procedural sedation and analgesia for laparoscopic sterilization; a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to compare postoperative recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic sterilization under procedural sedation and analgesia (PSA) and those receiving general anesthesia (GA).
DESIGN: Single-center, single-blinded randomized controlled trial SETTING: Gynaecological unit in a general teaching hospital PARTICIPANTS: Patients scheduled for a laparoscopic sterilization.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to either receive GA or PSA during their laparoscopic sterilization.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome measure was the recovery 24 hours postoperatively assessed using the Quality of Recovery 40 questionnaire (QoR-40). In addition, peri-operative data were measured including vital parameters, complications, conversions, the times of induction and surgery, total operating room time and total recovery room time. Usage of analgesics and the recovery index 10 (RI-10) were measured one week postoperatively. A sample size of 46 participants was calculated, with an expected difference of 10 points of the QoR-40 and an alpha of 0.05 and a beta of 80%.
RESULTS: The study comprised a total of 46 patients, 23 per arm. No significant difference was found in the main outcome; QoR-40 (PSA; 170, GA; 167 p=0.471) or in the RI-10. The total operating room time was eighteen minutes shorter in the PSA group compared to those receiving GA (43 vs 61 minutes; p=0.001). There was no difference in pain medication usage. There were no anesthesia related complications in either group.
CONCLUSION: This study observed no difference in recovery after 24 hours and 7 days between PSA en GA. However, the operation times were significantly shorter, making PSA more cost effective. We therefore conclude that PSA is a promising option in patients undergoing a laparoscopic sterilization, especially for low-risk patients. More research should be performed into the safety for higher-risk patients, and for the use of PSA for other minimally invasive gynaecological procedures.

articles.title: Patient-reported adequacy does not reliably reflect immediate recall of a postoperative instruction after carpal tunnel release: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative communication is commonly assessed through documentation and patient-reported adequacy, although these measures may not indicate whether clinically relevant instructions are recalled. This study addressed three questions: (1) does patient-reported adequacy reflect immediate recall of a key postoperative instruction after carpal tunnel release; (2) which patient- or process-related factors are associated with incorrect immediate recall; and (3) is incorrect immediate recall associated with early postoperative outcomes?
HYPOTHESIS: The proportion of patients reporting adequate information would exceed the proportion demonstrating correct immediate recall, and patient-reported adequacy would have limited ability to identify patients with incorrect recall.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective observational study included a pragmatic convenience sample of adults undergoing isolated ambulatory minimally invasive carpal tunnel release between January 2023 and March 2024. All patients followed a standardised surgical and anaesthetic pathway and received the same key postoperative instruction: use of the operated hand could begin immediately. Approximately 10 min later, before discharge explanations were provided, patients completed a study-specific digital questionnaire assessing perceived information adequacy, identification of the surgeon and anaesthetist, and immediate recall of the instruction. Associations with incorrect recall were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Postoperative pain, unexpected patient-initiated contacts, complications, sick-leave extension and supervised hand therapy were assessed exploratorily for up to 3 months.
RESULTS: Of 406 patients approached, 385 were analysed. Information provided during the surgical consultation was considered adequate by 381/385 patients (99.0%), whereas 326/385 (84.7%) correctly recalled the postoperative instruction, an absolute difference of 14.3 percentage points. Among patients reporting adequate information, 58/381 (15.2%) nevertheless had incorrect immediate recall. Correct identification of the anaesthetist was independently associated with lower odds of incorrect recall (adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.25-0.80; p = 0.007). Age, sex, surgeon identification and perceived clarity of postoperative recommendations were not independently associated with recall. No statistically significant differences in exploratory postoperative outcomes were detected according to recall status; event numbers were low.
DISCUSSION: Consistent with previous evidence of incomplete patient recall after perioperative information, patient-reported adequacy should not be considered a surrogate for immediate recall. Within this standardised ambulatory pathway, perceived adequacy and immediate recall represented distinct dimensions of perioperative communication. Brief objective recall assessment may complement existing quality indicators in ambulatory surgery and warrants evaluation in future intervention studies.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV; prospective observational study without a control group.

articles.title: Robotics in endoscopic spine surgery: a scoping review of clinical applications, workflow integration, and patient outcomes.
articles.abstract: Robotic and endoscopic technologies are increasingly being combined in spine surgery, yet the clinical literature remains fragmented across procedures, platforms, and robotic functions. We conducted a scoping review to map clinical applications of robot-assisted endoscopic spine surgery, describe how robotic systems are incorporated into endoscopic workflows, and summarize the technical, perioperative, and patient-centered outcomes reported to date. PubMed and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Human clinical reports were eligible when endoscopy constituted part of the operative visualization or working approach and a robotic system directly assisted the same spinal procedure. Study selection was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Of 374 records identified, 122 duplicates were removed and 252 records were screened. Sixty-six reports were sought, 13 were not retrieved, 53 full texts were assessed, and 24 studies were included. The evidence comprised 11 comparative studies, four uncontrolled clinical series, and nine case-based or technical clinical reports. Applications ranged from discectomy and decompression to interbody fusion, pars repair, infection, trauma, and thoracic or craniovertebral procedures. Robots were used for trajectory planning, localization, percutaneous access, guidewire or pedicle screw placement, drilling, endoscope stabilization, and interbody instrumentation. Comparative studies most often showed gains in fluoroscopy use, access efficiency, or instrumentation accuracy; patient-reported outcomes were usually similar between groups. Robotic-endoscopic integration is clinically feasible across an expanding range of spinal procedures, but its patient-level value remains incompletely defined.

articles.title: Endoscopist-directed propofol versus monitored anesthesia care in outpatient endoscopy: Quality and safety metrics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopist-directed propofol (EDP) is endorsed by multisociety guidelines for elective outpatient endoscopy in low-risk patients, yet formal credentialing pathways for EDP remain absent from some health systems. We report procedural quality and sedation safety metrics from comparing an initial EDP period with a subsequent monitored anesthesia care (MAC) period with the aim of generating the regional evidence base required to inform a national EDP credentialing framework.
METHODS: This is a retrospective before-after cohort study of 3,049 consecutive endoscopic procedures performed at a single consultant-led endoscopy unit. Two sequential periods were defined by the date on which an attending anesthesiologist joined the unit: EDP period (n = 1,037; propofol directed by the performing gastroenterologist) and MAC period (n = 2,012; propofol directed by the anesthesiologist). Neither period received concurrent benzodiazepine or opioid coadministration.
RESULTS: Procedure-type mix, sex (46.3% female in both), and age (median 41.5 vs 43.3 years; P = 0.08) were well balanced between periods. The MAC period was associated with higher median propofol doses (150 vs 140 mg; P < 0.001), but there was no difference in cecal intubation rate (99.7% EDP vs 99.1% MAC; P = 0.57), PDR (26.4% vs 23.7%; P = 0.35), or polypectomy rate (20.7% vs 17.9%; P = 0.28). Zero documented adverse events were recorded in the EDP period versus one documented adverse event in the MAC period ( P = 1.00). All metrics in both periods exceeded ASGE, ESGE, and SGA benchmarks.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center cohort, measured procedural-quality outcomes were similar during sequential EDP and MAC periods. Prospective multicenter studies with structured adverse-event capture should be performed.

articles.title: Reinke's Edema: From the Operating Theater to Office-Based Blue Laser Treatment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare voice-related quality of life and endoscopic outcomes in patients with Reinke's edema treated with an office-based 445-nm blue laser versus microlaryngoscopy under general anesthesia.
METHODS: Sixty-three patients underwent office-based laser (OBL) treatment and 40 patients underwent microlaryngoscopy under general anesthesia (GA) for Reinke's edema at a tertiary laryngological center between 2018 and 2025. Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10) scores and endoscopic grading were assessed before and after treatment. Within-group comparisons used the paired t-test and the Wilcoxon signed rank test; between-group comparisons used the Welch t-test.
RESULTS: In the OBL group, VHI-10 scores improved from 15.0 ± 8.8 to 2.0 ± 3.5 (p < 0.001), and 43 of 52 patients (82.7%) achieved complete regression of edema (grade 0). Mean operative time was 6.9 ± 3.1 min, significantly shorter than in the GA group (37.0 ± 17.1 min; p < 0.001). In the GA group, VHI-10 scores improved from 19.5 ± 10.7 to 5.1 ± 6.7 (p < 0.001), with complete regression in 16 of 20 evaluable patients (80.0%). Eleven OBL patients (21.2%) required retreatment (maximum three sessions). No adverse events were recorded.
CONCLUSIONS: Office-based 445-nm blue laser treatment was associated with significant improvements in voice-related quality of life and stroboscopic outcomes, together with significantly shorter operative time than microlaryngoscopy under general anesthesia. These findings support the use of office-based approaches in selected patients with Reinke's edema as a sound alternative to conventional treatment under general anesthesia.

articles.title: Assessing Visual Field in a Visually-Impaired California Sea Lion (Zalophus Californianus) Pre- and Post- Bilateral Cataract Surgery.
articles.abstract: Cataracts, a lens condition that causes clouding of the lens and the progressive obstruction of vision, are common among wild, stranded, and captive pinnipeds. The development of cataracts is attributed to nutritional deficiencies, trauma, age, inadequate access to shade, and/or genetic risk factors. However, despite the well-documented prevalence of ocular diseases in pinnipeds, there is a paucity of information regarding the efficacy of corrective surgery, which is notably complex due, in large part, to the administration of general anesthesia, requires comprehensive pre-surgical training and post-operative monitoring, and incurs a considerable cost to managed care facilities. In this study, the efficacy of the surgical intervention was assessed through visual field tests administered pre- and post-bilateral cataract removal surgery. The subject was a 20-year-old female California sea lion (Zalophus californianus) with advanced cataracts in both eyes, who was trained to orient towards various light sources to test visual response. Trials were conducted prior to surgical correction and following bilateral cataract removal surgery over a 12-month period. The rate of successful responses to light stimuli declined significantly prior to surgery and improved after surgery, indicating some degree of post-operative restoration of visual functioning. These data serve as a foundation for establishing the efficacy of corrective surgery in California sea lions with cataracts and can assist in decision-making regarding the need and potential outcomes of surgical intervention.

articles.title: Preoperative Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index Complements Vertebral Hounsfield Units for Osteoporosis-Related Risk Stratification After Lumbar Fusion Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Bone health optimization is increasingly emphasized in spinal surgery because poor bone health is associated with postoperative mechanical complications. Computed tomography-derived vertebral Hounsfield unit (HU) values primarily reflect local vertebral bone mineralization, which is a component of overall bone quality. In contrast, the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) may reflect systemic nutritional and physiological vulnerabilities. We hypothesized that combining HU and the GNRI would provide complementary risk information about mechanical complications after lumbar fusion surgery.
PURPOSE: To determine whether the preoperative GNRI provides additional risk stratification beyond vertebral HU values in predicting postoperative osteoporosis-related complications after lumbar fusion surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis.
STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: Retrospective multicenter cohort study.
PATIENT SAMPLE: A total of 150 patients who underwent short-segment lumbar fusion surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis and completed a minimum 5-year follow-up were included.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Postoperative osteoporosis-related complications included incident vertebral fractures, cage subsidence, or screw loosening. Individual complications were also analyzed. Longitudinal clinical outcomes included Japanese Orthopaedic Association and visual analog scale scores for low back and leg pain.
METHODS: Preoperative nutritional status was assessed using the GNRI, with low GNRI defined as <98. Vertebral bone quality was assessed using mean L1-L4 HU values on computed tomography, with low HU defined as ≤100. Multivariable logistic regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, and osteoporosis medication was performed, including subgroup analyses of patients with low HU. This study received no external funding, and the authors report no relevant financial relationships or conflicts of interest.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients had low GNRI scores. The low GNRI group had lower HU values and a higher incidence of postoperative osteoporosis-related complications than the high GNRI group. In multivariable analyses, a low GNRI was associated with screw loosening, whereas low HU was associated with incident vertebral fractures, screw loosening, and cage subsidence. Among patients with low HU, a low GNRI was associated with an increased risk of overall complications (odds ratio, 6.22; p = 0.018) and screw loosening (odds ratio, 5.85; p = 0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative GNRI complements vertebral HU values for risk stratification after lumbar fusion surgery. In patients with a low HU, a low GNRI identified a subgroup with a higher risk of osteoporosis-related complications, particularly screw loosening. The combined assessment of HU and the GNRI may support risk-adapted perioperative bone health optimization.

articles.title: Complications in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation: an analysis of the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Difficult tracheal intubation is associated with serious complications, including hypoxia, bradycardia and cardiac arrest. Neonates have increased physiologic vulnerability compared with older children, yet detailed data on management strategies and outcomes in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation remain limited. We hypothesised that clinicians have lower first-attempt tracheal intubation success and higher complication rates for neonates compared with older children with difficult tracheal intubation.
METHODS: We analysed the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry to determine tracheal intubation first attempt success and incidence of complications. We used logistic regression to identify variables associated with complications in neonates.
RESULTS: During the study period, 6283 paediatric difficult tracheal intubations were recorded, including 420 neonates. First attempt success was lower for neonates (139/420, 33.1%) than older children (2394/4683, 51.1%). Complications occurred more frequently in neonates (123/420, 29.3%) than older children (637/4683, 13.6%). Hypoxia occurred in 92/420 (21.9%) neonates and 269/4683 (5.7%) older children. Severe complications were more frequent in neonates vs. older children (12/420, 2.9% vs. 30/4683, 0.6%, respectively), with cardiac arrests occurring in 4/420 (1.0%) neonates and 11/4683 (0.2%) older children. Difficult mask ventilation occurred more frequently in neonates (60/420, 14.3%) than older children (353/4681, 7.5%). In neonates, increased number of tracheal intubation attempts (aOR 1.61 per attempt, 95%CI 1.30-2.00, p < 0.001) and difficult facemask ventilation (aOR 3.17, 95%CI 1.38-7.30, p = 0.007) were associated with complications. Anticipated difficulty with airway management had a protective effect (aOR 0.37, 95%CI 0.16-0.88, p = 0.025).
DISCUSSION: Neonates with difficult tracheal intubation experience a substantially higher rate of complications than older children. Early recognition of risk is critical in order to enable careful planning to minimise tracheal intubation attempts in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Cancer Microbiome and Metabolome: Ongoing Trials and Future Directions for the Surgical Oncologist.
articles.abstract: The role of the human microbiome in cancer development, progression, and response to therapy has moved from correlative curiosity to demonstrated impact on tumor biology. This represents a critical factor for surgical oncologists as they not only resect these tumors, but also direct perioperative antimicrobial exposure and increasingly co-manage neoadjuvant and surveillance pathways in which microbial state may predict and modify response. This review summarizes the basis for therapeutic modulation of the cancer microbiome and metabolome in a contemporary clinical-trial landscape across four broad strategies: additive (fecal microbiota transplantation, defined consortia, and live biotherapeutic products), subtractive (targeted antimicrobials), dietary and metabolome-directed interventions, and engineered or next-generation platforms. Particular attention is given to subtractive approaches in colon and rectal cancer and to the underexplored perioperative interface between the microbiome and surgical outcomes such as anastomotic leak. We outline the principal methodological and translational obstacles, including low-biomass contamination, causal inference, unintended antibiotic effects, and product standardization. Looking ahead, we propose roles for surgeons across the care continuum, from biospecimen stewardship and trial referral to integration of microbiome and circulating tumor DNA signals in surveillance.

articles.title: From Catheters to Wearables: Advanced Hemodynamic Monitoring and the Emerging Role of PPG-Based Devices.
articles.abstract: Advanced hemodynamic monitoring, including cardiac output (CO), stroke volume (SV), and systemic vascular resistance (SVR), is important for the management of cardiogenic shock, postoperative patients, and heart failure. Traditional approaches such as pulmonary artery catheterization (PAC) provide comprehensive hemodynamic assessment but are invasive, costly, and associated with procedure-related risks. This review summarizes established invasive and minimally invasive techniques alongside emerging noninvasive approaches, including pulse contour analysis, bioimpedance, pulse wave transit time, and photoplethysmography (PPG)-based systems. Particular emphasis is placed on PPG-based technologies, which combine pulse wave analysis, pulse wave transit time, and advanced signal processing to estimate blood pressure and flow-related parameters. As a representative case study, the clinical development and evaluation of the Biobeat BB-613WP wearable are described, including preclinical swine hemorrhagic shock models, intensive care and perioperative validation against invasive reference methods, and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring studies. Available evidence suggests that PPG-based wearables can achieve clinically acceptable agreement with invasive reference methods in selected populations while offering the potential for continuous, noninvasive, and ambulatory monitoring. However, the available evidence is limited by small sample sizes, single-center studies, controlled conditions, and limited independent validation. Further multicenter, outcome-oriented studies are required to establish the clinical role of PPG-based devices across diverse patient populations and stages of care.

articles.title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sacral fracture with spinopelvic dissociation (SPD) is a rare, high-energy injury associated with substantial mortality and morbidity. Surgical stabilization is technically challenging and has historically been associated with relatively high rates of construct failure. The present study describes and evaluates a novel minimally invasive spinopelvic diamond-shaped construct (The MIS-Diamond fixation), designed to improve rigid triangular stabilization while minimizing soft-tissue morbidity and facilitate the fracture reduction.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted including patients who underwent MIS-Diamond fixation for AO Type C3 sacral fractures at a single Level-I Trauma Center between January 2014 and December 2024, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, and radiological outcomes were systematically assessed. Fractures were classified according to the AO Spine Sacral Injury Classification System.
RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (mean age 39 years) were included. Surgery was performed at a median of 5 days post-injury, with a mean operative time of 115.8 min and mean estimated blood loss of 82.7 mL. No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a postoperative S1 motor impairment attributed to indirect radicular injury during reduction. Implant-related complications were recorded in 4 patients (12.5%), including one late-onset surgical site infection and three cases of asymptomatic iliac screw loosening. No soft tissue or wound healing complications were observed. Implant removal was successfully completed in 28 patients (87.5%) at 12 months postoperatively.
DISCUSSION: MIS-Diamond fixation demonstrated a favourable safety profile while enabling early postoperative mobilization. The incorporation of a 5.5 mm transverse iliac rod converts the classical triangular construct into a rigid box-like configuration, enhancing rotational stability and preventing coronal diastasis during vertical distraction. Limiting instrumentation to L4-L5 reduces the number of immobilized motion segments compared to previously described longer constructs, potentially mitigating long-term degenerative sequelae.
CONCLUSIONS: The MIS-Diamond fixation represents a safe and effective minimally invasive surgical option for SPD, providing reliable multiplanar stabilization with a low complication profile. Routine implant removal at 12 months is feasible and recommended to preserve motion segment function. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to further validate these findings.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture for Procedural Anesthesia: A Scoping Review of Stimulation Parameters and Anesthetic-Sparing Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological local anesthetics carry risks of systemic toxicity and hypersensitivity and do not attenuate the surgical stress response. Electroacupuncture (EA) has been proposed as an adjunct for procedural anesthesia, but the heterogeneous clinical evidence has not been systematically mapped.
METHODS: This scoping review was registered on the Open Science Framework and follows PRISMA-ScR. PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI and J-STAGE were searched from inception to April 8, 2026, without language restrictions. Eligible human studies used needle-based EA, alone or with pharmacological anesthesia, for procedural local or regional anesthesia, nerve block or local anesthetic dose reduction. Consistent with scoping review methodology, no formal critical appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine studies published between 1971 and 2025 were included: randomized controlled trials (59%), non-randomized and observational studies (36%) and case reports (5%), spanning minor soft-tissue, head and neck, anorectal and abdominal, and spinal and orthopedic procedures, mixed surgical series and experimental pain models. Of the 20 studies that quantified local anesthetic consumption, seven allowed calculation of reductions relative to controls (10%-86%), which were calculated on different dose bases and are not directly comparable. A small number of studies reported no requirement for supplemental local anesthetic or rescue medication. The dense-disperse 2/100 Hz waveform with a 20-30-minute pre-operative induction phase was the most frequently used protocol in trials published from 2012 onward.
CONCLUSION: This review maps potentially promising stimulation parameters but cannot establish the efficacy or clinical superiority of EA. The 2/100 Hz protocol with structured pre-operative induction should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating starting point for standardized trials, for which this evidence map provides a design framework. Kilohertz-frequency stimulation, studied only experimentally, is a hypothesis for future research.
SCOPING REVIEW REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework, DOI: https://osf.io/4n357 (registered April 28, 2026).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial number: not applicable.

articles.title: Beyond the Reach of Standard Prophylaxis: Mycoplasma hominis and Ureaplasma Spp. in Postoperative Urological, Andrological and Renal Transplant Infections.
articles.abstract: Genital mollicutes, namely Mycoplasma hominis, Ureaplasma urealyticum and Ureaplasma parvum, colonize the lower urogenital tract of a substantial minority of healthy adults yet are rarely considered in postoperative urological, andrological or renal transplant infection. This narrative review examines the diagnostic and prophylactic gap they create. Their lack of a cell wall makes Gram staining uninformative and confers intrinsic resistance to beta-lactams and glycopeptides. Routine microbiology also has limited sensitivity: Ureaplasma spp. generally require specialized culture or molecular detection, whereas M. hominis may grow slowly on enriched routine media but is easily overlooked. Reported disease ranges from sterile pyuria and graft pyelonephritis to perinephric or prostatic abscess, encrusting uropathy, recurrent struvite calculi and hyperammonemia syndrome. Commonly recommended perioperative agents provide little or no reliable activity against these organisms. Acquired resistance is strongly regional: among Ureaplasma isolates from North America and Germany, reported resistance to several key agents remains below 8%, whereas Vietnamese surveillance found ciprofloxacin resistance of 76.0% in U. urealyticum and 88.0% in M. hominis; doxycycline and josamycin retained greater activity but were not uniformly active. We propose five pragmatic clinical triggers, compartment-directed sampling and region-aware empiric management while emphasizing that these recommendations rest predominantly on case-level evidence. Prospective surgical studies are needed to define incidence, diagnostic thresholds and the role of screening.

articles.title: Controlled Hypothermic Storage and Time-Shifting in Lung Transplantation: A Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study compared lung transplant outcomes between cases using controlled hypothermic storage (CHS) donor lung transport with ischemic times > 6 h and those using cold static storage (CSS) transport with ischemic times < 6 h.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed lung transplantations performed at our center from September 15, 2014 to March 29, 2025, excluding ex vivo lung perfusion, single-lung, redo, and multi-organ cases. Perioperative outcomes were assessed using univariate, multivariable, survival, and propensity-matched analyses.
RESULTS: Among 770 recipients, 87 (11.3%) and 683 (88.7%) received lungs preserved using CHS and CSS, respectively. In the CHS group, ischemic times were significantly longer (median, 11.0 vs. 4.3 h, p < 0.001), and transport distances were greater (median, 750 vs. 219 nautical miles, p < 0.001). CHS was associated with higher rates of daytime transplantation (79% vs. 51%, p < 0.001) and delayed chest closure (22% vs. 13%, p = 0.023). Primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3) at 72 h was lower in the CHS group (13% vs. 26%, p = 0.019), and CHS was independently associated with a lower risk of PGD3 on multivariable analysis (aOR 0.38, 95% CI 0.17-0.83, p = 0.016). In a propensity-matched analysis, PGD3 at 72 h was lower in the CHS group, but the difference did not reach statistical significance (12% vs. 26%, p = 0.059). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated similar survival between groups (p = 0.53).
CONCLUSION: CHS enables the safe extension of ischemic time beyond conventional limits, facilitating broader geographic access and a shift toward increased daytime transplantation. Short-term outcomes were comparable to those of CSS, with a lower incidence of PDG3.

articles.title: Second-Stage Labor Duration and Risk of Postpartum Urinary Retention in Nulliparous Women With Epidural Analgesia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Postpartum urinary retention (PUR) is a clinically relevant complication after vaginal delivery; however, independent risk factors among nulliparous women receiving epidural analgesia remain unclear. To identify independent risk factors for PUR among nulliparous women undergoing vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of nulliparous women who underwent vaginal delivery at ≥ 37 weeks' gestation with epidural analgesia between January 2022 and June 2023 at our institution. PUR was defined as either absence of spontaneous voiding with no urge to void at 6 h postpartum, or diminished urge to void with a postvoid residual volume ≥ 150 mL measured by intermittent catheterization despite spontaneous voiding. Variables were compared between the PUR and non-PUR groups. Multivariable logistic regression was then performed with second-stage labor duration prespecified as the primary variable of interest. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Among 215 women, PUR occurred in 26 (12.1%). Second-stage labor duration was significantly longer in women with PUR than in those without (228 [151-275] min vs. 127 [70-210] min; p = 0.0005). In multivariable models adjusting separately for pre-pregnancy body mass index, neonatal birth weight, operative vaginal delivery, or duration of continuous epidural infusion, each 1-h increase in second-stage labor duration remained independently associated with PUR. ROC analysis demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC 0.71; 95% CI, 0.61-0.81), with an optimal cutoff of 215 min (sensitivity 61%, specificity 76%).
CONCLUSIONS: In nulliparous women undergoing vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia, second-stage labor duration is independently associated with PUR. It may serve as a pragmatic marker for targeted postpartum bladder surveillance.

articles.title: Large-Scale Brain Network Connectivity and Cognitive Performance in Chronic Pain During Aging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic pain and cognitive impairment are highly prevalent among older adults and represent major contributors to disability. Although chronic pain is associated with cognitive decline, the neural mechanisms underlying this relationship in older adults remain unclear. Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for prevention and intervention, as brain connectivity offers modifiable intervention targets. This study tested whether resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) within the default mode (DMN), frontoparietal (FPN), and salience (SN) networks relates to cognitive performance in older adults with chronic pain. We expected greater DMN and lower FPN connectivity and examined SN connectivity without a directional prediction.
METHODS: Fifty-six older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain (70.1 ± 5.81 years; 21 males), 57 pain-free older adults (70.02 ± 5.05 years; 21 males), and 60 younger adults (20.27 ± 2.1 years; 26 males) underwent neuropsychological assessments. A subset-30 older adults with chronic pain, 29 pain-free older adults, and 29 younger adults-underwent fMRI scanning.
RESULTS: Older adults with chronic pain performed worse than pain-free peers across verbal fluency, attention, memory, and executive function; after FDR correction, phonemic fluency and the WCST pattern remained significant. They also showed reduced FPN and increased DMN connectivity relative to younger adults (FDR; p < 0.05). Exploratory analyses linked greater DMN connectivity to poorer WCST performance within the chronic pain group (uncorrected ps < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the value of integrating cognitive and brain connectivity measures to characterize cognition in the context of chronic pain and aging, while motivating longitudinal research into relationships among pain, cognition, and network organization.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Older adults with chronic pain showed poorer executive performance than pain-free older adults. Among older adults with chronic pain, lower frontoparietal and greater default mode connectivity emerged only relative to younger adults; the older groups did not differ significantly. Exploratory analyses linked default mode connectivity with poorer executive performance within the chronic pain group. Together, these cognitive and connectivity findings motivate longitudinal studies examining how chronic pain, executive function, and brain network organization interact during aging.

articles.title: Inadequate neuraxial anesthesia during cesarean delivery: incidence and predictors in a large retrospective contemporary cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Spinal anesthesia is the preferred anesthetic technique for cesarean delivery because of its favorable maternal and neonatal safety profile. Despite its widespread use, inadequate neuraxial anesthesia remains an important clinical problem that may result in intraoperative pain, supplemental pain relief, or conversion to general anesthesia. Previous studies have shown inconsistent incidence rates and unreliable predictors of failed spinal anesthesia. This study aimed to determine the incidence of inadequate spinal anesthesia during cesarean delivery and to identify patient- and procedure-related factors associated with block inadequacy.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included all adult patients who underwent cesarean delivery under planned spinal anesthesia at a tertiary university hospital between January 2020 and January 2026. Inadequate spinal anesthesia was defined as the combination of partial and total failure of spinal block. Demographic, obstetric, anesthetic, and surgical variables were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of inadequate spinal anesthesia.
RESULTS: A total of 3,382 cesarean deliveries performed under spinal anesthesia were analyzed. Adequate spinal anesthesia was achieved in 3,216 patients (95.1%). Inadequate spinal anesthesia occurred in 166 patients (4.9%), including 135 partial failures (4.0%) and 31 total failures (0.9%). Increasing age and higher educational level were associated with lower odds of inadequate spinal anesthesia, whereas postpartum sterilization and surgical adhesions were independently associated with higher odds of inadequate spinal anesthesia.
CONCLUSIONS: Although spinal anesthesia provided effective surgical anesthesia in the vast majority of cesarean deliveries, inadequate neuraxial block remained clinically relevant. Both patient-related and surgical factors were associated with an increased risk of block inadequacy. Identification of high-risk patients may facilitate individualized anesthetic planning and improve maternal intraoperative experience.

articles.title: PC6 injection enhanced the preventive effect against postoperative nausea of granisetron compared with intravenous injection in gynecological laparoscopic patients: a randomized controlled study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate to severe postoperative nausea and vomiting significantly impedes recovery and is inadequately managed by current pharmacotherapy. This study investigates whether granisetron injection at the PC6 acupoint enhances prevention of postoperative moderate to severe postoperative nausea and vomiting compared to intravenous injection.
METHODS: 244 participants undergoing elective gynecologic endoscopic surgery under general anesthesia were randomly assigned to PC6 granisetron group, IV granisetron group, PC6 saline group and control group. All patients receive 5 mg dexamethasone during anesthesia induction. At the end of surgery, 2 mg granisetron was injected at the PC6 acupoint in PC6 granisetron group, 2 mg granisetron was injected intravenously in IV granisetron group, 2 ml saline was injected at the PC6 acupoint in PC6 saline group, no additional measures to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting in control group.
RESULTS: The incidence of moderate-to-severe postoperative nausea in PC6 granisetron group was significantly lower than that in IV granisetron group, PC6 saline group and control group within 24 h after surgery. (14.8% [9/61] vs. 32.8% [20/61]; RR = 0.45, [95% CI: 0.22, 0.91]; P = 0.02 (14.8% [9/61] vs. 29.5% [18/61]; RR = 0.50 [95% CI: 0.24, 1.02]; P = 0.058, (14.8% [9/61] vs. 43.9% [25/57]; RR = 0.34 [95% CI: 0.17, 0.66]; P < 0.01.) These differences started from 2 h after surgery. There was no adverse events about PC6 acupoint injection was found.
CONCLUSION: Granisetron injection at the PC6 acupoint enhances prevention of moderate-to-severe postoperative nausea within 24 h after surgery in patients undergoing elective gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered at http://www.chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2400085300).

articles.title: Comparison of unilateral biportal endoscopic decompression and percutaneous endoscopic lumbar decompression for single-segment degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis: a retrospective comparative study involving clinical efficacy and cost analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical efficacy and hospitalization medical cost associated with unilateral biportal endoscopic decompression (UBED) vs. percutaneous endoscopic lumbar decompression (PELD) for the treatment of single-segment degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis (DLSS).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 94 patients with single-segment DLSS, who received surgery between January 2023 and July 2025: 42 in UBED group and 52 in PELD group. Perioperative parameters, including intraoperative blood loss, fluoroscopy times, operative duration, time to postoperative ambulation, and length of hospital stay, were compared between groups. Additionally, patient-reported outcomes, namely, pain intensity (assessed using visual analog scale, VAS), functional disability (Oswestry disability index, ODI), and neurological function (Japanese Orthopaedic Association, JOA score), were evaluated preoperatively and at follow-up. Longitudinal between-group comparisons were performed using generalized estimating equations (GEE), with preoperative baseline scores as covariates and Bonferroni correction for post-hoc comparisons.
