Resting NRS at earlier time points (PACU arrival and 15 and 30 min) and at 2, 4, 6, and 12 h, movement NRS at all time points, 24-h tramadol consumption, rescue medication use, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) were secondary, exploratory outcomes.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Neither co-primary outcome differed significantly between groups: resting NRS at 24 h (median 0 [0-1] in both groups; p = 0.566) and QoR-15 scores at any time point (all p > 0.05), which returned to baseline by day 15. In secondary, exploratory analyses, resting NRS at 15 and 30 min in the PACU was significantly lower in the lateral TAP group (p = 0.010 and p = 0.013, respectively); NRS did not differ between groups at any other secondary time point. Cumulative 24-h tramadol consumption did not differ significantly between groups (median 50 mg [30-90] in the TAP group vs 107.5 mg [30-147.5] in the M-TAPA group; p = 0.090). PONV incidence and rescue medication use did not differ. No block-related complications occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: On the prespecified co-primary outcomes, ultrasound-guided lateral TAP and M-TAPA blocks provided comparable postoperative analgesia at 24 h and comparable quality of recovery. In secondary, exploratory analyses, the lateral TAP block produced lower NRS scores during the early PACU period, possibly because its injection site lies closer to the surgical area; this finding should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in adequately powered trials. Both techniques can be considered safe alternatives within a multimodal analgesia regimen.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06753240; retrospectively registered on 22 December 2024, after completion of patient enrollment.

articles.title: Burnout profiles among anesthesiology specialists in Türkiye: a nationwide cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Burnout is a critical occupational issue in anesthesiology, with implications for physician well-being, patient safety, and workforce sustainability. Although burnout among anesthesiology specialists in Türkiye has been reported, national data interpreted through the current MBI-HSS profile-based framework remain scarce. We aimed to characterize burnout profiles among anesthesiology specialists in Türkiye and identify factors associated with an investigator-defined burnout risk profile.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional online survey in June 2025 among anesthesiology specialists reached through the Turkish Society of Anesthesiology and Reanimation mailing list. The anonymous questionnaire collected demographic, occupational, psychosocial, and health-related data and included the 22-item Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey for Medical Personnel (MBI-HSS-MP). Burnout was assessed using the MBI-HSS 4th edition profile approach. The investigator-defined burnout risk profile comprised the Burnout, Overextended, and Disengaged profiles; associated factors were examined using multivariable logistic regression, with two sensitivity analyses using alternative outcome definitions.
RESULTS: A total of 193 anesthesiology specialists completed the survey, yielding a response rate of 21.0%. The mean age was 43.7 ± 8.6 years, and 116 participants (60.1%) were female. Using the MBI-HSS profile-based classification, we found that 47 participants (24.4%) met the Burnout profile, 61 (31.6%) were classified as Overextended, 9 (4.7%) as Disengaged, 54 (28.0%) as Ineffective, and 22 (11.4%) as Engaged. Overall, 117 respondents (60.6%; 95% CI: 53.6-67.2%) belonged to the burnout risk profile. Absence of weekly social activity was associated with higher odds of this risk profile (adjusted OR = 2.15; 95% CI: 1.08-4.29; p = 0.029), whereas greater perceived workplace support was associated with lower odds (adjusted OR = 0.56 per one-point increase; 95% CI: 0.39-0.79; p = 0.001). Results were consistent with Firth penalized estimation; in the strictest sensitivity analysis restricted to the Burnout profile, perceived workplace support remained associated with the outcome, whereas weekly social activity did not.
CONCLUSIONS: Burnout-related profiles were frequent among responding anesthesiology specialists in Türkiye, particularly profiles characterized by elevated emotional exhaustion and/or depersonalization. Lower perceived workplace support was the factor most consistently associated with the burnout risk profile, and absence of weekly social activity was also independently associated with it. Given the cross-sectional design, these associations cannot establish causality; workplace support, work organization, and recovery opportunities warrant further longitudinal and interventional evaluation.

articles.title: Ferroptosis Targeting: A Novel Therapeutic Strategy Against Anesthetic-Induced Neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Anesthetic-induced neurotoxicity (AIN), particularly postoperative cognitive dysfunction and related perioperative neurocognitive disorders, remains a significant clinical challenge. Ferroptosis-an iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-driven regulated cell death-has emerged as a key mechanism in preclinical models of anesthetic neurotoxicity. However, administration contexts (e.g., developmental, aged, spinal, or ototoxic) differ in patient populations, exposure paradigms, and tissue -specific outcomes. Preclinical evidence indicates that anesthetics like propofol, sevoflurane, and isoflurane trigger ferroptosis via iron dysregulation, antioxidant depletion, and lethal lipid peroxidation, contributing to neuronal injury and cognitive decline.Pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis-associated pathways confers neuroprotection in these experimental models, although these findings remain strictly preclinical and do not establish clinical efficacy. This review first outlines core ferroptosis mechanisms, then details the distinct molecular pathways by which various anesthetics induce ferroptosis, and finally summarizes recent advances in ferroptosis-targeted neuroprotection. Crucially, all current evidence is derived exclusively from preclinical studies; clinical translation remains to be established. Moreover, ferroptosis's relative contribution versus other cell death pathways likely varies across developmental stages, tissue types, and exposure conditions. Nonetheless, targeting ferroptosis represents a promising therapeutic strategy that warrants further investigation in well-designed translational studies to assess its potential for mitigating AIN across diverse clinical contexts.

articles.title: Parental knowledge and attitudes toward conscious sedation in pediatric dentistry in Türkiye: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dental treatment in children is often complicated by anxiety, fear, and lack of cooperation, which may hinder the successful completion of procedures. Conscious sedation is widely used as an advanced behavior management technique to facilitate pediatric dental treatment. However, parental knowledge and perceptions of conscious sedation may influence clinical decision-making. This study aimed to evaluate parental knowledge and attitudes toward conscious sedation and their association with demographic factors and previous conscious sedation experience.
METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire study included parents of pediatric patients for whom conscious sedation was planned following clinical evaluation at the Departments of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Pediatric Dentistry of Tokat Gaziosmanpaşa University Faculty of Dentistry. A 17-item questionnaire based on previously published surveys assessed demographic characteristics, knowledge about conscious sedation procedures, previous conscious sedation experience, safety perception, and attitudes toward conscious sedation. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26.0. Descriptive statistics, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons were used (p < 0.05).
RESULTS: A total of 422 questionnaires were analyzed. Limited parental knowledge regarding conscious sedation procedures was observed. Specifically, 40.8% were unsure whether conscious sedation meant the child would be completely asleep, 62.6% reported that they did not know the pre-sedation fasting requirements applied in the clinical protocol, and 51.7% were unsure whether local anesthesia would be required during conscious sedation. Additionally, 56.9% were uncertain about when their child could return to school. Parental education level and previous conscious sedation experience were significantly associated with several knowledge and attitude variables (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Parents demonstrated notable gaps in knowledge regarding key aspects of conscious sedation in pediatric dental care. Educational level and previous conscious sedation experience were significantly associated with parental knowledge and attitudes. These findings highlight the need for improved parental education and communication regarding conscious sedation in pediatric dental practice.

articles.title: Association of placental weight and the umbilical coiling ındex with early neonatal adaptation in term neonates delivered by elective cesarean section under general anesthesia: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: General anesthesia for cesarean delivery may affect early neonatal adaptation, but neonatal condition at birth may also reflect fetoplacental characteristics. This study evaluated associations of placental weight and umbilical coiling index with 1-minute Apgar score and umbilical arterial blood gas parameters in term neonates delivered by elective cesarean delivery under general anesthesia.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study included 60 term singleton mother-neonate pairs undergoing elective cesarean delivery under standardized general anesthesia. Placental weight, umbilical cord measurements, umbilical coiling index, birth weight, 1-minute Apgar score, and umbilical arterial blood gas parameters were recorded. Neonates were compared according to Apgar score ≤ 7 or ≥ 8. Correlations were assessed using Spearman analysis. Associations with Apgar ≤ 7 were examined using Firth logistic regression adjusted for birth weight and induction-to-cord-clamping interval.
RESULTS: Fourteen neonates had a 1-minute Apgar score of 7, 10 had a score of 8, and 36 had a score of 9; no neonate had a score of ≤ 6. For the binary analyses, scores were categorized as ≤ 7 versus ≥ 8. Placental weight was lower in the Apgar ≤ 7 group than in the Apgar ≥ 8 group (528.0 [456.2-567.5] g vs. 602.5 [546.2-675.0] g; p = 0.004) and remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Umbilical coiling index was also lower in the Apgar ≤ 7 group (0.24 [0.22-0.28] vs. 0.29 [0.23-0.35]; p = 0.025), but not after correction. The 1-minute Apgar score correlated positively with placental weight, umbilical coiling index, umbilical arterial pH, base excess, and bicarbonate. In adjusted models, each 100-g increase in placental weight was associated with lower odds of Apgar ≤ 7 (adjusted OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.12-0.85; p = 0.017), as was each 0.10-unit increase in umbilical coiling index (adjusted OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.09-0.82; p = 0.015). Lower Apgar scores were accompanied by lower pH, base excess, and bicarbonate values, without group-level evidence of severe acidemia.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small, single-center cohort of term neonates delivered by elective cesarean delivery under standardized general anesthesia, lower placental weight and lower umbilical coiling index were associated with a 1-minute Apgar score of ≤ 7. Given the limited sample size and the small number of neonates in the Apgar ≤ 7 group, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Their clinical significance remains uncertain because 5-minute Apgar scores and other clinically important neonatal outcomes were not assessed, and external validation is required before any clinical application.

articles.title: Age-related effects of comprehensive in-patient physiotherapy after lung cancer surgery across age groups: an ambispective observational cohort study in middle-aged and older patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery after lung cancer surgery may be influenced by age, comorbidity burden, and perioperative rehabilitation strategies. However, evidence regarding the age-related effects of structured early inpatient physiotherapy programs remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the age-related effects of a comprehensive in patient physiotherapy (CIPT) program on hospital length of stay (LoS), clinical parameters, symptom-related outcomes, and inflammatory biomarkers in patients undergoing lung cancer surgery.
METHODS: This ambispective observational cohort study included patients who underwent lung cancer surgery and received a structured CIPT program during the postoperative inpatient period as part of standard postoperative care. Participants were categorized into middle-aged and older groups. Outcomes included hospital LoS, clinical parameters (blood pressure, resting heart rate, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate), symptom-related outcomes (dyspnea and fatigue with Modified Borg Scale, and incisional pain with Visual analog scale), and inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein (CRP), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and albumin). Pre- and post-program changes within groups and differences between age groups were analyzed.
RESULTS: Median LoS was 7 [5-10] days in the middle-aged group and 7 [6-10] days in the older group, with no significant difference between groups. Significant improvements in resting heart rate, oxygen saturation, and dyspnea were observed in the older group, whereas dyspnea, fatigue, and incisional pain improved significantly in the middle-aged group. No significant differences were detected between age groups in clinical parameters or symptom-related outcomes. CRP and NLR levels decreased significantly in both groups, while albumin showed a non-significant upward trend over time. Despite a higher comorbidity burden in the older group, no adverse events or clinical instability were observed during the rehabilitation program.
CONCLUSION: The CIPT program appears to be safe and feasible for both middle-aged and older patients following lung cancer surgery. Similar outcomes between age groups suggest that age alone may not represent a barrier to participation in structured early inpatient rehabilitation programs. Early physiotherapy integrated into postoperative care pathways may facilitate recovery without increasing hospital length of stay across age groups, which may also help reduce the potential economic burden associated with prolonged hospitalization.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07441863. First submitted on 17 February 2026 and first posted on 02 March 2026 retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Effects and safety of magnetic lidocaine microsphere as novel strategy to targeted long-acting peripheral nerve blocks.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Local anesthetics have been a cornerstone in the field of anesthesia for over a century, yet they face ongoing challenges in providing sustained postoperative analgesia. The ideal duration for such analgesia is 48-72 hours, a benchmark that current formulations often fail to meet. There is a recognized need for long-acting local anesthetics that can maintain their presence at the periphery of target nerves, thereby extending their therapeutic window. Despite advancements, traditional methods for prolonging nerve blockade-such as adjuvant addition, nerve catheter placement, and repetitive blocks-each have their limitations. The specific gap is the development of a targeted, long-acting peripheral nerve block that can prolong the duration of action of local anesthetics without significant toxic side effects.
METHODS: In this study, we developed magnetic lidocaine microspheres using an ultrasonic W1/O/W2 re‑emulsion method, incorporating nano‑iron oxide (Fe₃O₄) and poly(lactic‑co‑glycolic acid) (PLGA). The microspheres were characterized for morphology, magnetic properties, and in vitro drug release. Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics were evaluated in animal models, including electrophysiological and behavioral assessments of peripheral nerve block and analgesia. Blood concentrations were measured by liquid chromatography‑mass spectrometry (LC‑MS), and drug distribution was observed by MRI. Toxicity was assessed via sciatic nerve pathology and cytotoxicity tests on rat Schwann cells.
RESULTS: Under a static magnetic field, the magnetic lidocaine microspheres prolonged peripheral nerve blockade for up to 60 hours, with the compound action potential amplitude suppressed to <20% of baseline for 48 hours. In vitro release reached 97.3 ± 2.1% at 60 hours with an initial burst of 76% at 24 hours. The formulation exhibited concentration‑dependent cytotoxicity on Schwann cells, with significantly higher cell viability compared to free lidocaine at clinically relevant concentrations (≥250 μM, p < 0.01; 500 μM, p < 0.05). Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed that the MLM‑M group had a 21.33‑fold longer Tₘₐₓ and a 15.62‑fold longer t₁/₂ compared to free lidocaine, with AUC₀‑₄₈ reduced to approximately 4.5% of that in the free lidocaine groups (0.341 ± 0.034 vs. 7.566 ± 0.302 μg·h/mL), confirming sustained local delivery with minimal systemic exposure.
CONCLUSION: The magnetic lidocaine microspheres effectively prolonged peripheral nerve blocks under the influence of a static magnetic field, achieving sustained drug release over 60 hours with significantly reduced systemic absorption compared to conventional lidocaine. Notably, this targeted approach demonstrated concentration‑dependent cytotoxicity on Schwann cells and maintained therapeutic concentrations at the nerve site while limiting systemic exposure, as evidenced by pharmacokinetic and MRI analyses. These findings demonstrate that magnetic lidocaine microspheres can achieve prolonged, site-targeted nerve blockade in a preclinical model, with reduced systemic exposure and favorable local tissue compatibility. While these results are encouraging, further studies in postoperative pain models and large-animal studies are needed before clinical translation can be considered. If successfully translated, this technology could potentially offer a new approach to prolonged regional analgesia with reduced reliance on systemic opioids.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is not a randomized controlled trial and therefore was not registered in a public clinical trials registry.

articles.title: Medially based conchal cartilage flap: an addition to cartilage-preserving otoplasty and its cognitive-perceptual outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prominent ear is the most common congenital deformity of the auricle, for which a variety of surgical and nonsurgical methods have been tried to correct it. Thus, this study aimed to reduce the conchal bowl height, while preserving the conchal cartilage and to prevent wrinkling of anterior skin of auricular concha of prominent ear.
METHODS: This prospective case series was conducted on 26 patients (49 prominent ears), from March 2021 to December 2023 at Shar Private Hospital, Erbil, Iraq. Initially, patients' demographic data were collected, followed by their clinical data. Then, they were operated under local anaesthesia, using cartilage-sparing with cartilage-cutting techniques. After that, they were followed up for 1 week, 6 months, 1 year, and one year or more to report postoperative complications and their satisfaction with the outcomes. Additionally, the psychological dimension was integrated as a primary metric for evaluating the surgical outcomes of this technique, as well as to investigate the impact of this novel surgical approach on the patients' internal constructs, specifically focusing on self-image, self-esteem, and their overall outlook on life.
RESULTS: Among operated patients (n = 26), 23 presented with bilateral prominent ears and 3 with unilateral prominent ears. Patients' ages ranged between 6 and 43 years, and all of them had hypertrophic concha, regardless of the antihelical fold definition. The operative time ranged from 60 to 120 min. After one year of follow-up, all patients and/or their guardians were satisfied with the results (100%). Additionally, 8 cases (18.6%) were reported to have postoperative complications.
CONCLUSIONS: The applied technique helps reduce and prevent the recurrence rate of prominent ears. It also preserves the conchal cartilage and prevents wrinkling of the anterior skin of the auricular concha. The patients' psychological status also improved after otoplasty.

articles.title: Effects of opioid-free intraoperative anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative immune function in elderly patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty: a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in elderly patients may involve postoperative immune suppression. This study compares intraoperative opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) and opioid-based anesthesia (OBA) effects on postoperative proportion of immune cells. The core pharmacological difference between groups lies in the intraoperative anesthetic regimen: the OBA group received sufentanil for induction and continuous remifentanil infusion for maintenance, while the OFA group replaced all intraoperative opioids with esketamine. Both groups received opioid-containing patient-controlled intravenous analgesia and rescue analgesia after surgery, and the opioid-free anesthesia protocol was only applied during the intraoperative phase.
METHODS: A single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial of 60 patients (60-80 years) undergoing unilateral TKA. The opioid-free strategy was exclusively implemented during the intraoperative period, and both groups received identical opioid-inclusive postoperative analgesia. Patients were randomized into OFA (n = 30) and OBA (n = 30) groups.
PRIMARY OUTCOME: change in natural killer (NK) cell proportion.
SECONDARY OUTCOMES: T-cell subsets (CD3⁺, CD4⁺, CD8⁺), B cells, dynamic/static visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) demands, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), hemodynamics, and adverse events.
RESULTS: We conducted an intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis in 60 patients (30 in each group). Baseline demographics and preoperative immune indices showed no significant differences between the groups. Compared with the levels one day before the operation, the postoperative reduction in NK cell proportion was significantly smaller in the OFA group than in the OBA group (Δ = -5.51% ± 4.89% vs. Δ = -10.12% ± 5.39%; P < 0.001). The OFA group demonstrated superior early postoperative analgesia, with lower dynamic and static VAS scores at 4-48 h (P < 0.05), reduced PCIA demands at 24 h (5.8 ± 0.9 vs. 7.2 ± 1.1) and 48 h (6.1 ± 1.0 vs. 8.5 ± 1.3; P < 0.05), and better PSQI (7.50 ± 3.34 vs. 10.86 ± 4.01; P < 0.001). The OFA group had significantly lower intraoperative vasoactive agent consumption (atropine, norepinephrine, ephedrine) and 72-hour postoperative opioid consumption (all P < 0.05), and exhibited superior postoperative functional exercise capacity (active knee flexion angle and maximum walking distance) at 48 and 72 h postoperatively (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed between the groups in CD8⁺ T cell, B cell proportions, extubation time, length of hospital stay, rescue analgesia rate or postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) incidence (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In elderly patients undergoing unilateral total knee arthroplasty, intraoperative esketamine-based opioid-free anesthesia was associated with a smaller decline in NK-cell proportion, superior early analgesia, and improved short-term sleep quality compared with opioid-based anesthesia. These findings are limited to the comparison of intraoperative strategies and cannot be extrapolated to full perioperative opioid-free management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese clinical trial registry, ID: ChiCTR2300069836; Date: 27/03/2023.

articles.title: The effect of music medicine with virtual reality glasses on patients' surgical anxiety and comfort during ureteroscopy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a combined music medicine and virtual reality intervention on the surgical anxiety and perianesthesia comfort among patients undergoing elective semi-rigid ureteroscopy under spinal anesthesia.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment was conducted between June and December 2024 at Aydın State Hospital, Türkiye. A total of 60 patients (30 experimental, 30 control) who met the inclusion criteria were randomly assigned to two groups. The experimental group experienced a virtual reality (VR)-based music medicine intervention, while the control group received routine perioperative care. Outcomes were assessed by a researcher blinded to group allocation. Ethical approval was obtained from the Aydın Adnan Menderes University Faculty of Medicine Non-Interventional Clinical Research Ethics Committee (Decision No: 12; Protocol No: 2024/80). The study was reported in accordance with the CONSORT statement.
RESULTS: No significant difference was found between the groups in surgery-specific anxiety scores (p = 0.285). However, the experimental group had significantly higher comfort levels than the control group (2.92 ± 0.28 vs. 2.26 ± 0.52; p < 0.001), with a moderate effect size (r = 0.63). Regression analysis confirmed that the intervention group scored, on average, 0.62 points higher in comfort (B = 0.621, p < 0.001), explaining 39% of the variance (R2 = 0.390).
CONCLUSION: Music medicine combined with VR may serve as a practical, non-pharmacological intervention to enhance perioperative comfort and improve the patient experience during ureteroscopy. The findings support the integration of immersive audiovisual interventions into perioperative care. Further research with larger, multicenter samples and personalized content is recommended to evaluate long-term and physiological outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov id: NCT06914830.

articles.title: Streamlining the Evidence-to-Practice Pathway With Computerised Decision Support in Anaesthesiology and Critical Care: A Qualitative Study of Clinician and System-Level Interest Holder Perspectives Across Five Scandinavian Countries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implementing evidence-based recommendations in anaesthesiology and critical care remains challenging due to guideline, workflow and contextual barriers. Guideline-based computerised clinical decision support systems (CDSS), embedded in structured pathways linking international guidelines to Scandinavian-endorsed recommendations and delivered via electronic health records, may help strengthen the evidence-to-practice pathway. This study aimed to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to their use.
METHODS: This qualitative study interviewed 10 clinicians (anaesthesiologists and intensivists; specialists and non-specialists; < 40 and ≥ 40 years; male and female) and nine system-level stakeholders (hospital and health authority representatives) from Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden. We integrated endorsed international guidelines into a CDSS providing patient-specific reminders linked to recommendations, as well as shared decision-making tools and decision-analytic components. Using a simulation application, participants explored the CDSS in a demo electronic health record. Through a framework analysis based on the GUIDES checklist, we categorised perspectives as barriers, facilitators or suggestions.
RESULTS: Clinicians and system-level interest holders expressed broad interest in this multifunctional CDSS to support evidence-based, patient-centred care and appreciated the collaborative international pathway facilitated by digital tools. Key themes included the challenges hospitals face in translating international guidelines into up-to-date, locally adapted guidance. Artificial intelligence (AI) was perceived as having the potential to both enhance and challenge traditional CDSS. Opportunities were identified to strengthen shared decision-making for major decisions through the proposed system. Finally, participants highlighted the potential value of using a decision-analytic tool to prioritise reminders, although the tool was considered conceptually challenging in its current form and would require clearer presentation before being applied in CDSS.
CONCLUSIONS: This prototype study indicates support for a multifunctional CDSS. Building on the barriers and facilitators identified in this study, interviewees advocated for real-world evaluation with particular attention to sustainable implementation.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This study aimed to describe how ICU clinicians experience interaction in a simulated electronic health record where there were chosen elements of decision support based on international treatment guidelines incorporated into the simulation. Participants were interviewed for their perceptions of what types of decision support might be most helpful to support their clinical work in future patient information and management systems.

articles.title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.
METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.
RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).
CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

articles.title: Epidural in Labour and Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perineal injury during childbirth is common. The most severe injuries involve damage to the anal sphincter (obstetric anal sphincter injuries). Epidural analgesia provides effective labour pain relief but its impact on the risk of obstetric anal sphincter injury is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the association between epidural analgesia and the likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injuries.
SEARCH STRATEGY: Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, PubMed, CINAHL and Web of Science were searched from database inception to October 18, 2025, using key words relating to epidural, perineal trauma and labour.
SELECTION CRITERIA: Randomised trials and observational studies (cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies) were included.
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS: Studies reporting the same outcomes were pooled, and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random effects meta-analysis.
MAIN RESULTS: From 24 977 identified studies, 86 were included (N = 9 826 330 women). Pooled adjusted analyses showed epidural use in labour was associated with a 15% reduced likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injury in the overall population (n = 9 302 188; aOR 0.85 [95% CI 0.80-0.91]). Among nulliparous women, there was a 23% reduced likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injury (n = 1 083 923; aOR 0.77 [95% CI 0.71-0.83]).
CONCLUSION: After pooling effect measures that corrected for important clinical confounders, our meta-analysis suggests that epidural use in labour may reduce the likelihood of obstetric anal sphincter injuries among nulliparous women. While our findings must be interpreted within the limitations of observational data, they provide valuable evidence to guide clinical practice and highlight the need for more high-quality studies to establish causality.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO Registration CRD42023412771, 09 April 2023 https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023412771.

articles.title: Perioperative Management of the Orthopedic Patient Taking Antipsychotics: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Antipsychotic prescribing continues to rise among older adults, the group most likely to present for orthopedic surgery, and orthopedic surgeons now operate regularly on patients taking these agents. Guidance for managing them around an operation sits largely in the psychiatric, anesthesiology and pharmacologic literature rather than the surgical one. This narrative review gathers the orthopedic-specific evidence and organizes it by whether a finding reflects the medication or the psychiatric illness for which it was prescribed.
FINDINGS: Antipsychotic exposure is associated with higher all-cause revision and periprosthetic fracture after total knee arthroplasty, and second-generation exposure raises all-cause and aseptic revision after shoulder arthroplasty independent of psychiatric diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism roughly doubles after primary total knee arthroplasty. Among geriatric hip fracture patients antipsychotics are the only medication class independently linked to in-hospital falls, and preoperative use independently predicts postoperative delirium that prophylaxis does not prevent. Spine, sports medicine and trauma surgery all show worse outcomes in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis, yet none of those literatures disentangles the drug from the disorder. Thromboembolism and the shoulder revision signal are the clearest drug-attributable exceptions. Hyperprolactinemia-mediated hypogonadism, metabolic derangement and impaired fracture healing remain plausible but unproven. Nearly all available evidence is retrospective.
CONCLUSION: Antipsychotic therapy should continue through the perioperative period unless a specific reason exists to stop it. Abrupt discontinuation risks psychiatric relapse, which is harder to manage than the perioperative risks the drugs themselves carry. Low bone mineral density, poor glycemic control and thromboembolic risk are all worth addressing before surgery, drawing on psychiatry and internal medicine. Antipsychotics are not recommended for delirium prophylaxis. Whether altering therapy improves orthopedic outcomes has not been studied prospectively.

articles.title: Evaluation of short term outcomes of tubeless thoracoscopic lobectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The concept of a 'tubeless' technique has gradually attracted the attention of surgeons. The 'tubeless' technique that uses spontaneous ventilation anesthesia (SVA) without tracheal intubation and no or as little as possible drainage, has seldom been attempted. The purpose of the present study was to determine the efficacy of the 'tubeless' technique on the early outcomes of lung lobectomy.
METHODS: All patients who underwent lobectomy for lung tumors between January 2012 and September 2017 were divided into two groups: the mechanical ventilation video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (MV-VATS) group and the spontaneous ventilation video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (SV-VATS) group.
RESULTS: A total of 498 patients were enrolled. Two hundred and eighty patients were included in the mechanical ventilation group and 218 patients were included in the spontaneous ventilation group. After 1:1 propensity score matching. The body mass index (BMI) and use of a muscle relaxant in the SVA group (22.50 vs. 22.06 kg/m2; 24.83 vs. 3.75 mg; P=0.001) were lower. Both operation time (168.62 vs. 152.26 min; P=0.009) and chest tube (4.08 vs. 3.01 days; P=0.001) were shorter in the SV-VATS group. Furthermore, intraoperative bleeding (69.91 vs. 38.74 mL; P=0.002) was decreased in the SV-VATS group, compared with MV-VATS.
CONCLUSIONS: Tubeless thoracoscopic is safe and feasible for lobectomy in thoracic surgery, and can result in good short-term outcomes, reduce the use of muscle relaxants, and accelerate postoperative recovery. In addition, it can shorten the chest tube and operation time.

articles.title: Selective Nerve Block of A- or C-Afferents Confirms Dual Role in Touch Pleasantness but Not Touch-Pain Modulation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Gentle and deep pressure are distinct types of touch that often elicit pleasant sensations and modulate pain. Although touch pleasantness has traditionally been attributed to unmyelinated C-tactile afferents, growing evidence suggests an important contribution of myelinated A-fibers. However, the relative role of A- and C-fibers in touch-evoked pleasantness and pain modulation remains unclear. To test the role of A- and C-fibers in touch pleasantness, healthy adults underwent selective peripheral nerve block of the superficial radial nerve to preferentially impair either A- or C-fiber function. Touch pleasantness of brushing (Study 1; N = 24) or deep pressure (Study 2; N = 24) and touch-induced modulation of heat pain were assessed before and after the nerve block. Both nerve blocks significantly reduced the perceived pleasantness of both gentle brushing and deep pressure, supporting a substantial contribution of myelinated A-fibers and well as unmyelinated C-fibers (presumably C-tactile fibers) to affective touch. In addition, block of A-fibers did not diminish touch-induced modulation of experimental heat pain, suggesting a particular pain-inhibiting role for C-tactile fibers. These findings supply causal evidence in healthy adults that myelinated A-fibers are highly involved in touch pleasantness-alongside C-tactile fibers-but are not involved in touch-induced pain relief.
KEY POINTS: Unmyelinated C-tactile afferents are thought to relay the pleasantness of touch, however growing evidence suggests myelinated A-afferents may also play a role.Preferential nerve block of either A- or C-fibers reduced the perceived pleasantness of gentle brushing and deep pressure.A-fiber nerve block did not alter touch-induced modulation of heat pain.These findings suggest both A- and C-fibers are involved in touch pleasantness, but point to a pain-inhibiting role of C-tactile afferents.

articles.title: Risk factors for positive depression screening at 6 weeks postpartum: a single center retrospective cohort study (2014-2023).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As universal postpartum depression screening is implemented, contemporary risk factors for positive screens in the United States population remain understudied. Our aim was to evaluate demographic, obstetric, neonatal, anesthetic and psychiatric factors associated with positive depression screening scores at 6 weeks postpartum.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at an academic center in the United States (2014-2023). Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores recorded at 6 weeks postpartum were analyzed (positive screen score ≥ 10). We included adults (≥18 years) delivering a live or nonviable fetus from gestational age ≥ 20 weeks by any mode who completed screening at 6 weeks post-delivery; we excluded patients with an incomplete or missing score. The primary outcome was factors independently associated with a positive depression screen at 6 weeks postpartum. Secondary outcomes were to characterize depression scores and explore differences in inpatient pain outcomes based on positive or negative depression screening at 6 weeks postpartum.
RESULTS: Of 8155 deliveries analyzed, 13.6% (n = 1107) screened positive on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. Factors independently associated with higher odds of a positive screen included Hispanic ethnicity, single marital status, delivery of neonate with very low birth weight, worst postpartum pain score up to 48 h following delivery, and psychiatric diagnosis. Positive and negative screen median scores were 12 [IQR 11-16] {Range 10-27} and 3 [IQR 1-5] {Range 0-9}, respectively. The positive depression screening group experienced worse inpatient pain.
CONCLUSION: Future studies should explore inpatient pain as a potential predictor of positive 6-week depression screening.

articles.title: Severe obesity as an independent risk factor for post-operative dislocation following reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: a PearlDiver database analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is a reliable procedure for a broad spectrum of shoulder pathologies, with post-operative dislocation representing a clinically impactful complication. Obesity has been associated with adverse peri-operative outcomes following shoulder arthroplasty; however, it has not been specifically assessed in relation to post-operative dislocation in the setting of rTSA. We hypothesized that severe obesity (body mass index [BMI] >35 kg/m2, corresponding to World Health Organization class II obesity) would be independently associated with an increased risk of dislocation following rTSA.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the PearlDiver Mariner national administrative claims database. Patients aged >17 years who underwent primary rTSA for degenerative shoulder osteoarthritis were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) procedural codes. Patients with shoulder trauma, neoplasm, or infection within 90 days of the index procedure were excluded. Two cohorts were defined: non-obese (BMI <30 kg/m2) and severely obese (BMI >35 kg/m2; patients with BMI 30-35 kg/m2 were excluded), and matched 4:1 by age, sex, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, and smoking status. Post-operative dislocation was identified using ICD-10 diagnostic codes (ICD-10-D-T84028A, ICD-10-D-T84029A). Outcomes were assessed at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years post-operatively. Multivariable logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed.
RESULTS: After 4:1 matching, 12,667 non-obese and 3,210 severely obese patients were included. Severely obese patients demonstrated statistically significantly higher rates of post-operative dislocation at 6 months (2.43% vs. 1.46%; P = .0002), 1 year (2.83% vs. 1.75%; P = .0001), and 2 years (3.30% vs. 2.16%; P = .0002). This corresponds to an absolute risk increase of approximately 1.1% at 2 years. On multivariable logistic regression, severe obesity was independently associated with increased dislocation risk at 2 years (odds ratio 1.54, 95% confidence interval 1.23-1.96; P < .0001), corresponding to a 54% relative increase in odds. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated statistically significantly lower dislocation-free survivorship in the severely obese cohort (log-rank P < .0001). All 3 time-point comparisons remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (adjusted α = 0.017).
CONCLUSION: Severe obesity (BMI >35 kg/m2) was associated with a statistically significant but modest increase in the risk of post-operative dislocation following rTSA at short-term follow-up. The magnitude of the association was moderate and the absolute risk difference small. These findings support obesity-specific pre-operative risk counseling on the risk of post-operative instability after rTSA.

articles.title: Perioperative and early oncologic outcomes of complex segmentectomy via uniportal video-assisted thoracic surgery for primary lung cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uniportal video-assisted thoracic surgery (U-VATS) has been increasingly adopted. However, evidence regarding the safety and oncologic outcomes of U-VATS complex segmentectomy remains limited. We aimed to evaluate the perioperative and early oncologic outcomes of U-VATS complex segmentectomy for primary lung cancer.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent U-VATS complex segmentectomy for primary lung cancer at our institution between December 2021 and November 2025. Patient characteristics, perioperative outcomes, and oncologic outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: Eighty-two patients were enrolled. The median age of the patients was 72 years. The indication for segmentectomy was intentional in 61 patients (74.4%) and compromised in 21 patients (25.6%). The median operative time was 152 min and the median estimated blood loss was 6 mL. Conversion was required in 3 patients (3.7%). All conversions were performed in a controlled manner; no patients required emergency thoracotomy. Postoperative complications occurred in 4 patients (4.9%). There were no 30- or 90-day mortalities or readmissions within 30 days after surgery. R0 resection was achieved in all patients. The median follow-up duration was 10 months. No local recurrence was observed during the follow-up period. Distant recurrence occurred in 4 patients (4.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: U-VATS complex segmentectomy for primary lung cancer was associated with postoperative complication and conversion rates consistent with those reported for other thoracoscopic approaches. These findings support the technical feasibility of U-VATS complex segmentectomy in appropriately selected patients when performed with meticulous preoperative planning and standardized intraoperative strategies.

articles.title: Postoperative outcomes of jaw surgery under general anesthesia using a standardized dexamethasone and local anesthesia protocol: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery after jaw surgery is often compromised by pain, swelling, and trismus. Although corticosteroids are commonly used, there is a need for clinical protocols that reduce the reliance on prolonged systemic analgesics. This study evaluates the efficacy of a multimodal protocol combining intraoperative local anesthesia with a weight-based single dose of IV Dexamethasone.
METHODS: This prospective clinical study included 60 patients (ASA I-II) undergoing cyst enucleation or impacted tooth extraction under general anesthesia. A standardized protocol of a local anesthetic block (Articaine + Epinephrine) and weight-based IV Dexamethasone (0.1 mg/kg) was administered intraoperatively. Outcomes included VAS scores, facial swelling (Daniel Lim's method), and trismus on days 1, 2, and 7. Total analgesic consumption during the first 24 h and the subsequent week was recorded. Data were analyzed using SPSS v20.0. Normality was tested via Kolmogorov-Smirnov. Changes over the follow-up period were evaluated using repeated-measures analysis, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The protocol achieved excellent pain control, with mean VAS scores of 2.3 at 30 minutes and 0.8 at 6 hours. Notably, 95% of patients required no rescue analgesia during post-anesthesia care. While 81.7% of patients required oral analgesics at home within the first 24 hours, no further medication was needed thereafter. Facial swelling and trismus were minimal and resolved rapidly, with 78.3% of patients showing no functional restriction by Day 1.
CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, combining intraoperative local anesthesia with 0.1 mg/kg IV Dexamethasone showed an 'analgesic-sparing' effect. However, the lack of a control group in this single-arm observational study limits definitive conclusions about causality. This protocol not only enhances patient comfort but also notably decreases the need for systemic analgesics during the early postoperative phase.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06787196. Registered December 27, 2024. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Impact of rhomboid intercostal plane block on chronic pain incidence and acute pain scores after oncologic breast surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent chronic pain after oncologic breast surgery remains a major clinical problem, affecting approximately 25-60% of patients and significantly impairing quality of life. Although the rhomboid intercostal plane block (RIB) has been shown to reduce acute postoperative pain, its role in preventing chronic postoperative pain remains inadequately investigated.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial included 254 adult women undergoing oncologic breast surgery with or without lymph node dissection. Patients were randomized to receive either a pre-operative ultrasound-guided single-shot RIB using 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine or no regional block (control group). All patients received standardized multimodal systemic analgesia. The primary outcome was the incidence of chronic pain at 3 months postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included chronic pain at 6 months, Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form scores at 3 and 6 months, neuropathic pain assessed using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 questionnaire, acute postoperative pain scores, and 24-h postoperative opioid consumption.
RESULTS: Of the 254 randomized patients, 247 completed the study. Chronic pain incidence was significantly lower in the RIB group at 3 months (17% vs 31%; p = 0.009) and 6 months (13% vs 30%; p < 0.001), with reduced neuropathic pain at 6 months. The RIB group had lower 24-h opioid consumption than controls (p = 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-operative single-shot RIB significantly reduced chronic postoperative pain and opioid consumption following oncologic breast surgery, and may be considered as part of multimodal analgesia to decrease chronic pain incidence, neuropathic pain and improve acute postoperative pain control.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06019325 registered August 17, 2023).

articles.title: Trial of vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC): external validation of the Polish prediction indices of the VBAC.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC) is a safe option for both mothers and children. Currently available prediction tools have not been validated in the Polish population. Dobrowolska-Redo proposed a model for predicting VBAC success, and the aim of this study was to evaluate its clinical utility.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis of data collected from 462 pregnant women with a history of one previous cesarean section, all qualified for a VBAC attempt. Deliveries occurred between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2023, at the II Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Medical University of Warsaw. Inclusion criteria were: previous low transverse cesarean section, singleton pregnancy, no indication for elective cesarean delivery, and live birth. Ethical approval was granted by the local committee (reference no. AKBE/300/2024). The data were anonymized before analysis.
RESULTS: Among the cohort of 462 women, 271 (58.7%) had successful VBAC, whereas 191 (41.3%) underwent intrapartum cesarean section. The prediction model for preterm births (pTi) showed no clinical utility. The median Ti score differed significantly between the VBAC group and the cesarean group. Removing two parameters (manual labor and place of residence) improved model performance. Higher BMI increased the likelihood of cesarean delivery, both before pregnancy (23.43 vs. 24.54 kg/m²; p = 0.006) and at delivery (27.99 vs. 29.36 kg/m²; p = 0.007). Prior vaginal birth was a strong predictor of successful VBAC (31.5% vs. 11.2%; p = 0.000), as was a history of fetal macrosomia (15.5% vs. 8.7%; p = 0.047). Gestational diabetes was more common in women who ultimately required cesarean delivery (34.2% vs. 23.7%; p = 0.023). Epidural anesthesia use correlated with a lower cesarean rate (26.6%; p = 0.000).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center cohort, the Polish index model for full-term VBAC (Ti) prediction showed moderate accuracy. A refined version demonstrated improved performance compared with the original. Several predictors of successful VBAC were confirmed, including prior vaginal delivery and history of macrosomia, while high BMI and gestational diabetes increased the risk of intrapartum cesarean section.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Same-day versus overnight discharge after total knee arthroplasty: a national propensity-matched analysis of 90-day readmission and hospital charges.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Same-day discharge (SDD) following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has gained traction, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic. However, large-scale post-pandemic evidence on safety and cost outcomes remains limited. This study evaluated 90-day readmissions and economic impact among patients discharged on the day of surgery versus those discharged after an overnight stay.
METHODS: Elective primary TKA admissions were identified in the 2020-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Admissions involving fracture, infection, revision, oncologic diagnoses, bilateral TKA, or COVID-19 were excluded. Only procedures performed on admission day with a length of stay of 0 or 1 day were included. Propensity scores were estimated using demographic characteristics, comorbidities, robotic assistance, and hospital characteristics. Matching was performed on the unweighted discharge-level records using sequential greedy 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching without replacement and an absolute caliper of 0.1 on the propensity-score scale. NRD discharge weights were applied after matching to generate weighted national estimates. Because individual matched records carried different discharge weights, the reported weighted group totals were not numerically identical despite equal-sized underlying matched groups. The primary outcome was 90-day readmission.
RESULTS: The eligible cohort represented 208,103 weighted elective primary TKA admissions, including 10,460 same-day discharge admissions and 197,643 overnight-stay admissions. After 1:1 matching of the underlying unweighted discharge records and subsequent application of NRD discharge weights, the matched cohort represented 10,460 same-day discharge admissions and 10,894 overnight-stay admissions nationally. Ninety-day readmission occurred in 3.4% and 4.0% of admissions, respectively, corresponding to a relative risk of 0.85 (95% CI 0.74-0.98) and an absolute risk difference of - 0.6% points (95% CI - 1.1 to - 0.1; p = 0.02). A coded surgical procedure during readmission occurred in 2.4% versus 1.9%, corresponding to a relative risk of 1.26 (95% CI 1.05-1.52) and an absolute risk difference of 0.5% points (95% CI 0.1-0.9; p = 0.007). Mortality during readmission, readmission length of stay, time to readmission, readmission charges, and index hospitalization charges were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this matched observational analysis, same-day discharge was associated with a small absolute reduction in 90-day readmission and a similarly small absolute increase in coded surgical procedures during readmission. Other measured inpatient outcomes and hospital charges were comparable. These findings do not establish causal equivalence or universal safety and should be applied only to appropriately selected patients within structured perioperative pathways.
LEVELS OF EVIDENCE: Level II.

articles.title: Predicting long-term survival following lung cancer resection based on early perioperative immune-metabolic response patterns.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer resection is usually associated with surgical stress and systemic immune-metabolic shifts. Existing prognostic tools largely depend on static parameters. We aimed to characterize early perioperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) response patterns and construct a predictive nomogram to risk-stratify patients undergoing lung cancer resection.
METHODS: We selected patients with malignant lung neoplasms who underwent resection and had complete perioperative laboratory records from the INSPIRE database (2011-2020). Gaussian finite-mixture modeling within an LCGA framework was applied to classify early SII response patterns from baseline to 24 h postoperatively. Primary and secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, respectively. A perioperative immune-metabolic stress index (PIMSI) nomogram via multivariable logistic regression was established to predict the high-risk Severe Surge response pattern and was internally validated using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: A total of 2,186 patients were included and classified into three early perioperative SII response patterns: Class 1 (Stable; 57.4%), Class 2 (Moderate Increase; 35.8%), and Class 3 (Severe Surge; 6.8%). Compared with the Stable group, patients in the Severe Surge group had longer ICU stays and a higher risk of 5-year mortality (Hazard Ratio [HR] = 2.38, 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.69-3.35, p < 0.001). The PIMSI model, incorporating diabetes history, preoperative C-reactive protein, operative time, prognostic nutritional index, body weight, age, and ASA physical status, showed good discrimination for identifying patients at risk of a Severe Surge response pattern (apparent AUC, 0.828; optimism-corrected AUC, 0.820) and demonstrated clinical net benefit on decision curve analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Early perioperative SII trajectories were associated with ICU dependency and prognosis after lung cancer resection. The PIMSI nomogram may support early risk stratification and perioperative care escalation, but it needs further validation with oncological staging and histological adjustment.

articles.title: Medial calcaneal neuropathic pain clinically diagnosed in a child initially considered to have Sever's disease: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sever's disease is a common cause of pediatric heel pain and usually improves with conservative treatment. However, persistent pain with allodynia and difficulty in heel contact may indicate a neuropathic mechanism.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 9-year-old boy developed persistent right heel pain after treatment for a suspected left calcaneal avulsion fracture. Despite a diagnosis of Sever's disease and conservative therapy, pain, allodynia, and difficulty in heel contact persisted. The pain was localized to the medial and plantar heel, with a Tinel-like sign along the presumed course of the medial calcaneal nerve. Topical lidocaine-prilocaine cream and ultrasound-guided perineural injection of a local anesthetic temporarily relieved the allodynia and enabled heel contact. Ultimately, the symptoms resolved with multimodal treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Medial calcaneal neuropathic pain should be considered in children with persistent heel pain accompanied by sensory abnormalities, localized pain consistent with nerve distribution, and a Tinel-like sign.

articles.title: Right- versus left-sided double-lumen tubes and hypoxemia during anesthesia in patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Right-sided double-lumen endobronchial tubes (DLTs) are often avoided because of technical difficulties and concerns about respiratory complications, although evidence that they increase hypoxemia during anesthesia remains limited and inconsistent. We evaluated the association between DLT side and hypoxemia during anesthesia in patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors between October 2008 and May 2023. The primary outcome was hypoxemia during anesthesia, defined as SpO2 ≤ 90% for at least 3 consecutive min during the anesthetic period. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to adjust for measured differences between patients receiving right-sided and left-sided DLTs. Odds ratios (ORs) and absolute risk differences (RDs) were estimated.
RESULTS: Among 1,280 patients, 842 received right-sided DLTs and 438 received left-sided DLTs. After overlap weighting, measured covariates were well balanced. The incidence of hypoxemia during anesthesia was 20.0% with right-sided DLTs and 18.5% with left-sided DLTs (OR, 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68-1.79; P = 0.70). The RD was 1.51 percentage points (95% CI - 3.86-6.87). No clear between-group differences were observed in exploratory secondary respiratory outcomes.
CONCLUSION: We found no clear evidence that right-sided DLT use was associated with a higher incidence of hypoxemia during anesthesia than left-sided DLT use. However, equivalence between the two devices was not established, and further studies are needed to determine whether clinically important differences in hypoxemia risk exist.

articles.title: Effect of cardiac-index guided intraoperative haemodynamic therapy on postoperative outcome in non-cardiac surgery patients - a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal perioperative haemodynamic management is essential to reduce postoperative complications. While multiple technologies allow for advanced monitoring, clear evidence on the effectiveness of Cardiac Index-guided goal-directed therapy (CI-GDT) compared to standard care in non-cardiac surgery is lacking. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to investigate the impact of CI-GDT on postoperative outcome.
METHODS: A systematic search using PubMed and Web of Science (2010-2025) identified randomised controlled trials (RCT) comparing CI-GDT to standard care in adult non-cardiac surgery. Study selection and data extraction were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251058399). Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and 95% prediction intervals (PI) were calculated using a random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed via the RoB 2 tool. Heterogeneity was quantified with I2, τ2, and Cochran's Q. Reporting bias was evaluated by funnel plots, Egger's test, and trim-and-fill method. Sensitivity was assessed by leave-one-out analysis.
RESULTS: Twenty-one RCTs were included, of which 20 contributed data to the meta-analysis of postoperative complications. CI-GDT significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative complications (OR .59 [.45-.78]; PI .20-1.74; I2 = 62.9%). Mortality did not differ significantly between groups (OR 0.77 [.57-1.05]; I2 = 0%). Funnel plot and Egger's test indicated no significant publication bias (p=.15). Leave-one-out analysis confirmed robustness of findings. Trim-and-fill did not suggest missing studies. Certainty of evidence was graded high.
DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION: CI-GDT was associated with a lower incidence of patients experiencing at least one postoperative complication, whereas mortality did not differ significantly. However, substantial heterogeneity and a prediction interval crossing the null indicate that the benefit may not be consistent across clinical settings. These findings do not establish an independent advantage of CI targeting over other GDT strategies.

articles.title: Anesthetic Care of Children With Epilepsy Receiving Ketogenic Diet Therapy: An Educational Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ketogenic diet therapy (KDT) is a nonpharmacologic treatment for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy that induces ketosis through high-fat, low-carbohydrate intake. These children frequently present for anesthesia, and their baseline metabolic alterations, compounded by fasting and surgical stress, place them at higher risk of perioperative complications than other pediatric patients. This educational review organizes anesthetic considerations into preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases and synthesizes them into best-practice recommendations for perianesthesia clinicians.
DESIGN: Educational review.
METHODS: A research librarian-assisted search of PubMed and Ovid MEDLINE was conducted in June 2025, limited to English-language publications from 2015 forward; of 202 unique records screened, 83 underwent full-text review, and 14 met inclusion criteria, and an unrestricted hand-search of included studies' reference lists added seven more, for 21 included studies (seven case reports, one case series, five retrospective record reviews, two prospective cohorts, two animal studies, three narrative reviews, and one summary of expert opinion).
FINDINGS: Across this literature, the central requirement is maintenance of ketosis throughout all phases of perioperative care, with evaluation of every medication and intravenous fluid for carbohydrate and gluconeogenic potential, metabolic monitoring with prompt recognition and treatment of acidosis and hypoglycemia, anesthetic technique tailored to the patient's comorbidities and the planned procedure, and interdisciplinary coordination with the ketogenic diet team.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence base remains dominated by case reports and retrospective record reviews, with no randomized trials in this population, limiting generalizability; nonetheless, reviews and guidelines published since 2020 provide a workable foundation for safe perioperative care.

articles.title: A nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of postpartum hemorrhage in twin pregnancies with cesarean section.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising prevalence of twin pregnancies and cesarean sections (CS) is a significant risk factor for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), contributing to increased maternal morbidity and mortality globally. Establishing a reliable risk assessment model for PPH could facilitate timely identification and intervention, thereby improving maternal outcomes. This study aimed to develop an effective nomogram for predicting PPH in twin pregnancies undergoing CS.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed data from 1704 women with twin pregnancies who delivered by CS between 2016 and 2022 at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China. To identify risk factors for PPH after CS in twin pregnancies, univariate analysis and LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) regression were employed. A nomogram was subsequently developed based on the results of binary logistic regression analysis and the Akaike information criterion (AIC). Model validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, with performance assessed through discrimination (receiver operating characteristic curve), calibration (calibration plot and Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision cur analysis, DCA).
RESULTS: The nomogram for PPH was created using eight best predictor variables, namely, parity, assisted reproductive technology (ART), preeclampsia (PE), placenta previa, placenta accreta, anemia, the sum of the neonatal birthweight, and general anesthesia, which were all independent risk factors for PPH after CS in twin pregnancies. The nomogram demonstrated strong discrimination and calibration performance, with robust clinical utility as evidenced by area under the curve (AUC) analysis and DCA. Internal verification confirmed the consistency between predicted and actual values.
CONCLUSIONS: Parity, the use of ART, PE, placenta previa, placenta accreta, degree of prenatal anemia, total neonatal birthweight, and the use of general anesthesia are significant risk factors affecting the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage after CS in patients. The prediction model based on the above factors provides an accurate tool for assessing PPH risk, offering potential to guide clinical decision-making and further reduce maternal mortality.

articles.title: Pudendal Neuralgia in a Tertiary Pain Clinic: Presentation, Treatment, and Factors Associated with Neuromodulation in 224 Adults.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pudendal neuralgia is an under-recognized cause of chronic, disabling neuropathic perineal pain affecting both women and men. Real-world data on its presentation, its treatment within a specialty pain service, and the factors that accompany escalation to interventional therapy are scarce. We hypothesized that an iatrogenic (postsurgical) origin and relief after a diagnostic pudendal nerve block would identify the patients who reach neuromodulation.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective manual review of the complete electronic records of all adults with documented pudendal neuralgia, pudendal neuropathy, or pudendal nerve entrapment managed at a single tertiary pain clinic between 2009 and 2026. Demographics, clinical presentation, presumed etiology, treatments, and outcomes were abstracted from the free-text record. Ascertainment was in two stages: variables were first identified by structured text screening of the free-text record, and the two variables most susceptible to false-positive screening, a postsurgical etiology and receipt of neuromodulation, were then verified against the source charts by manual review of every screen-positive record. The chart-verified definitions are used throughout. Associations between binary variables were tested by the chi-squared test, with odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI); factors associated with neuromodulation were assessed by multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 224 patients (138 women [61.6%], 86 men [38.4%]; median age 48.5 years, interquartile range 35-64), pain was worse when sitting in 57.6% and burning in 39.3%, and involvement was bilateral in 21.9%. Text screening identified a possible postsurgical onset in 46.4%, but chart re-adjudication confirmed a named operation preceding the pain in only 31 patients (13.8%), of whom 6 had undergone a clearly non-pelvic procedure; confirmed postsurgical onset was therefore less frequent than documented entrapment features (24.1%) and comparable to childbirth (15.9% of women). Care was heavily interventional: 59.4% received a pudendal nerve block, 28.6% pulsed radiofrequency, and 9.4% underwent surgical decompression. Neuromodulation was documented in the record of 64 patients (28.6%), but an electrode was placed in only 26 (11.6%) and a permanent device implanted in 18 (8.0%): spinal cord stimulation in 14, sacral neuromodulation in 2, dorsal root ganglion stimulation in 1, and pudendal nerve stimulation in 1. Three factors were independently associated with documented neuromodulation: relief after a diagnostic block (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.91-12.46%), a refractory course (2.92, 1.52-5.60%), and chart-confirmed postsurgical onset (2.83, 1.17-6.82%); c-statistic 0.76. In an exploratory model restricted to the 18 implanted patients, a refractory course (7.40, 1.98-27.61%) and postsurgical onset (4.24, 1.29-13.94%) remained associated with the outcome whereas relief after a block did not (5.90, 0.72-48.31%).
CONCLUSIONS: In routine pain-clinic practice, pudendal neuralgia is managed along an interventional pathway, but device implantation is considerably less common than the frequency with which neuromodulation is discussed. A confirmed postsurgical onset is less common than text screening suggests, yet is disproportionately associated with escalation. Being observational, these findings describe how care proceeds rather than establishing cause.

articles.title: A Retrospective Study of the Efficacy of Regional Anesthesia in Reducing Donor Site Harvest Pain in Burn Patients.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in burn care, the pain of burn treatment remains unresolved. The creation of donor harvest sites is often unavoidable, and the subsequent pain is difficult to treat. Regional anesthesia for the donor harvest sites can provide effective analgesia, however, there is limited literature regarding its efficacy. The purpose of this study was to assess the use of regional anesthesia for donor harvest site pain. Patients admitted to the burn center from January 1, 2011, to May 15, 2025, with thigh donor site harvest(s) were reviewed for study inclusion. Data collected included demographics, burn variables, hospital course data, and regional anesthesia procedure details. Descriptive statistics were used to determine differences between the block and non-block groups. Of the 524 patients included, 164 (31.3%) had donor site blocks and 360 (68.7%) did not. There were 77 (47%) with single shot blocks and 87 (53%) had indwelling catheters (groin or epidural). The groups were well-matched in their demographics, burn injury data, and hospital variables. The overall oral morphine equivalents (OME) and pain report levels were similar between the block and control groups in all three post-operative periods. However, causal conclusions are limited by this retrospective, heterogenous study. An appropriately protocolized prospective study is planned.

articles.title: Pain Characterization: Presentation Patterns, and Multidimensional Assessment in Women with Advanced Gynecologic Cancer in a Palliative Care Service.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain in advanced cancer is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon extending beyond intensity to include biological, psychological, and social components. In women with advanced gynecologic malignancies, pain is highly prevalent yet often undercharacterized, particularly in resource-limited settings where disparities in access and delayed integration of palliative care may influence its presentation and management.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize multidimensional pain features and identify distinct descriptive pain patterns in women with advanced gynecologic cancer receiving palliative care.
DESIGN: Observational study.
SETTING/SUBJECTS: Electronic medical records of women aged ≥18 years with advanced gynecologic cancer and documented pain, treated at a tertiary cancer center in Mexico between 2013 and 2023, were reviewed.
MEASUREMENTS: Sociodemographic and clinical variables were collected. Pain assessment included location, intensity, time of onset, and characteristics (somatic, visceral, neuropathic, or mixed). Psychosocial factors, including anxiety and depression, were also evaluated. Descriptive statistics were used to explore multidimensional pain patterns.
RESULTS: A total of 1,015 women were included (median age 56 years; most had≤12 years of education). Cervical and ovarian cancers predominated (43.4% and 32.3%). Pain was mainly pelvic or abdominal (81.0%) and commonly mixed visceral/neuropathic. Median intensity was moderate (4/10), with higher intensity in uterine sarcoma (median 7/10). Nearly half of patients presented anxiety or depression.
CONCLUSIONS: Pain in advanced gynecologic cancer is heterogeneous and multidimensional, with identifiable tumor-type-specific pain patterns that may inform individualized, patient-centered management strategies, particularly in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Systemic Inflammation in Bronchiectasis: Data from the EMBARC-BRIDGE Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neutrophilic inflammation in the airways is associated with exacerbation risk in patients with bronchiectasis. Systemic inflammation and neutrophil function are less characterised. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between systemic inflammation and neutrophil function with severity of disease and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Observational international multi-centre study of adults with bronchiectasis (EMBARC-BRIDGE). Serum inflammatory profiling was performed in 487 patients using Olink® proteomics, and associations with key clinical and patient reported outcomes, including severe exacerbations during follow-up, were analysed. In a sub-study, peripheral blood neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients and controls were analysed for surface activation and functional markers, and functional responses including degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation.
RESULTS: Systemic inflammatory profiling revealed a dominant neutrophil-endothelial signature. Several proteins including PR3, AZU1, MPO, the soluble IL-33 receptor ST2, and the cellular stress marker GDF-15 were associated with increased disease severity using the bronchiectasis severity index, lower lung function, increased symptoms and for many markers, higher rates of severe exacerbations during follow-up. Neutrophils from bronchiectasis patients exhibited reduced surface CD11b and increased CXCR2, with lower CD11b correlating with lower lung function. Basal degranulation was reduced in bronchiectasis, whereas responsiveness to LPS stimulation was preserved.
CONCLUSION: Bronchiectasis is associated with a systemic neutrophil and endothelial inflammatory signature linked to disease severity and risk of severe exacerbations, alongside altered but functionally-responsive circulating neutrophils.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Bibliometric Analysis and Cluster Analysis of Research Trends on Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Patients After Anesthesia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to analyze research on postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia and to identify research hotspots and trends.
DESIGN: A bibliometric analysis.
METHODS: We searched the Web of Science Core Collection for English-language publications on postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia published from 1988 to 2024. The retrieved data were analyzed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R 4.3.3.
FINDINGS: A total of 1,119 articles were included in the analysis. Among countries, China had the highest number of publications. Among institutions, Harvard University ranked first, with 165 publications. Among journals, Anesthesiology had the highest total number of citations, with 3,074 citations and an impact factor of 9.1. Among authors, Xie Zhongcong had the largest number of publications, with 24 articles and 1,045 citations.
