Keyword cluster analysis identified seven major research themes: anesthesia approach, risk, and clinical management; pathophysiological mechanisms and neuroinflammation; cardiovascular surgery and perioperative monitoring; biomarkers and neurodegeneration; anesthetic drugs and assessment tools; outcomes and neurophysiological responses; and recommendations. High-frequency keywords such as "anesthesia," "surgery," and "dysfunction" reflected the main research hotspots and trends in this field.
CONCLUSIONS: This bibliometric study summarizes the research landscape of postoperative cognitive dysfunction in elderly patients after anesthesia and identifies major contributors, research hotspots, and evolving trends. The findings may provide a useful reference for future research in this field.

articles.title: The incidence of postoperative hypotension among non-cardiac surgical specialties: A single-centre retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Postoperative hypotension is associated with increased risk of postoperative complications and mortality. There are limited studies quantifying the incidence of this potentially life-threatening condition among different surgical cohorts. We aimed to describe and compare the incidence of postoperative hypotension in the first 48 h after leaving the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) across different surgical specialties after non-cardiac surgery. We conducted a single-centre retrospective study at the Royal Melbourne Hospital. The primary outcome was postoperative hypotension (systolic blood pressure (SBP) <90 mmHg) within 48 h after surgery and discharge from PACU, noted on routine blood pressure monitoring or a requirement for postoperative vasopressor or inotropic support. We estimated odds ratios (OR) using mixed-effects logistic regression models to account for multiple surgical procedures within the same patient. We identified 11,634 surgeries from 17 specialties, of which 47.3% were emergency operations. The median age was 53 years (interquartile range 35-68), with 42.2% being female and 42.5% of patients on regular antihypertensive medication. The overall incidence of ward hypotension was 4.4%. Trauma had the highest rate of postoperative hypotension (27.3%), followed by thoracic surgery (11.6%). Surgical specialties that had a higher risk of hypotension included trauma surgery (OR 13.0, 95% confidence interval (CI) 3.7-46.0) and thoracic surgery (OR 3.6, 95% CI 2.3-5.5). Specialties with a lower risk of hypotension included breast and endocrine surgery (OR 0.4, 95% CI 0.2-0.7) and plastic surgery (OR 0.4, 95% CI 0.3-0.6). Postoperative hypotension is relatively common with substantial variation in incidence between surgical specialties. These findings highlight the need for heightened vigilance for hypotension in certain patients.

articles.title: Liposomal bupivacaine-containing versus standard bupivacaine interscalene nerve blocks in shoulder surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review compares the effectiveness of liposomal bupivacaine (LB) versus bupivacaine hydrochloride (HCl) for interscalene nerve blocks in shoulder surgery.
METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases were searched from 2010 to 2025 for studies comparing LB versus bupivacaine HCl for interscalene blocks in shoulder surgery. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included in the primary analysis; one retrospective cohort study was included in a secondary analysis. Pain scores at 24 and 72 h were primary outcomes; pain at 0 h and opioid consumption at 24 and 72 h were secondary outcomes. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was performed.
RESULTS: Across four RCTs (n = 181), LB showed statistically lower pain scores at 24 (mean difference -0.6, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.9 to -0.3) and 72 h (-0.4, 95% CI -0.5 to -0.3), both below minimal clinically important difference thresholds. No significant difference in opioid consumption was observed at 24 or 72 h. Heterogeneity was high at 24 h (I 2 = 92.5%) and low at 72 h (I 2 = 0%). Evidence certainty ranged from low to moderate.
DISCUSSION: LB shows statistically lower pain scores but no clinically meaningful improvement after shoulder surgery. Given the limited clinical significance and higher acquisition cost, routine use of LB for interscalene nerve blocks may not be warranted.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: II.

articles.title: The role of central nervous system sensitization in obstetric pain: A focused review.
articles.abstract: Obstetric pain conditions are clinically significant but often underrecognized complications of pregnancy and childbirth. Central nervous system sensitization (central sensitization) refers to the amplification of neural signaling in the central nervous system leading to pain hypersensitivity and offers a mechanistic framework for understanding acute and persistent obstetric pain. Central sensitization does not, however, act in isolation. It is initiated and sustained by ongoing input from sensitized peripheral nociceptors, potentially associated with pain amplification and persistence. This focused review synthesizes the neurophysiological mechanisms which may underlie sensitization in the peripartum period and examines the main obstetric pain conditions in which sensitization has been implicated, including pregnancy-related lumbopelvic pain, labor pain and persistent postpartum pain after vaginal delivery, persistent perineal pain, and chronic postcesarean pain. We also discuss psychological factors including anxiety, depression, pain catastrophizing, and fear of childbirth, as potential active modulators of central pain processing rather than merely coexisting conditions. These factors may represent modifiable targets for prevention, mitigation, and management. Key evidence gaps include the absence of obstetric-specific validation for clinical assessment tools such as the Central Sensitization Inventory, and limited prospective data linking intraprocedural nociception to postprocedural pain sensitization. Addressing these gaps through rigorously designed peripartum studies is essential for developing targeted, mechanism-based strategies to prevent and treat obstetric pain.

articles.title: Internal Medicine-Led Multidisciplinary Co-Management is Associated with Improved Perioperative Outcomes in Elderly Patients with Hip Fracture: A Propensity Score Matched Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fractures in the elderly are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. We compared perioperative outcomes between an internal medicine-led multidisciplinary co-management (IM) model and the traditional orthopedic-led consultation (OC) model in elderly hip fracture patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at Beijing Jishuitan Hospital Guizhou Hospital from March 2023 to June 2025, enrolling 1095 patients aged ≥65 years with hip fractures (IM, n=872; OC, n=223). Propensity score matching (2:1 optimal maximum matching; caliper 0.45 on the logit of the propensity score) balanced 13 covariates, with exact matching for sex, fracture type, and renal insufficiency. Multivariate regression evaluated associations between the care model and perioperative outcomes.
RESULTS: After matching, all 223 OC patients were successfully matched (final cohort 668: 445 IM, 223 OC), with all covariates achieving SMD < 0.1 (maximum 0.078). The IM group showed shorter hospital stay (10.0 vs 14.3 days), shorter time to surgery (42.3 vs 110.1 hours), less blood loss, and lower costs (all p < 0.001). Surgery within 48 hours was more frequent (70.3% vs 8.5%, p < 0.001), and allogeneic transfusion (49.4% vs 68.2%, p < 0.001) and one-year mortality (7.0% vs 12.6%, p = 0.016) were lower in the IM group. Multivariate analysis confirmed an independent association with lower mortality (OR 0.492, 95% CI 0.280-0.863, p = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: Internal medicine-led multidisciplinary co-management may be associated with shorter preoperative waiting time and hospital stay, reduced blood loss, allogeneic transfusion, one-year mortality, and medical costs. This model may serve as a reference strategy for perioperative management of geriatric hip fracture where multidisciplinary internal medicine resources are available; multicenter prospective studies are warranted.

articles.title: Pain Management in Orthopedic Surgery: A Procedure-Specific Orthopedic-Anesthesia Approach to Perioperative Analgesia.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Post-operative pain in orthopedic surgery is clinically important because inadequate analgesia can impair mobilization, sleep, physiotherapy and discharge, while excessive analgesia can cause sedation, motor weakness, drug toxicity and unnecessary opioid exposure. This narrative review uses a structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and targeted review of recent systematic reviews, randomized trials, consensus statements and procedure-specific recommendations, with emphasis on publications available through September 2026. Evidence is synthesized qualitatively according to procedure, analgesic strategy, functional outcomes, and limitations of the underlying evidence. Present evidence supports multimodal analgesia, but does not support a universal regimen or routine addition of every available intervention. Regional techniques can improve early analgesia, although benefits vary by procedure and may be offset by motor block, rebound pain, or limitations in post-operative examination. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide opioid-sparing analgesia, but the relationship between NSAID exposure and fracture healing remains uncertain and appears to depend on drug, dose, duration, fracture type, and patient factors. Opioids remain appropriate as rescue therapy when clinically indicated. Persistent post-surgical pain is influenced by pre-operative and biopsychosocial factors and acute analgesia has not been shown consistently to prevent it. The practical framework proposed here therefore links the operation, patient risk profile, analgesic options, and rehabilitation task, with unexpected severe pain treated as a trigger for clinical reassessment rather than automatic escalation.

articles.title: Optimizing Post-operative Analgesia for Early Rehabilitation after Orthopedic Knee Surgery: A Randomized Comparison of Adductor Canal, Infiltration between the Popliteal Artery and Capsule of the Posterior Knee and Genicular Nerve Blocks.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Orthopedic knee surgery, including anterior cruciate ligament tear repair, patellar fracture fixation, and surgery for knee osteoarthritis, is often followed by moderate to severe pain that delays early mobilization, quadriceps activation, and physiotherapy. Motor-sparing, opioid-sparing analgesia is therefore preferred. Ultrasound-guided adductor canal block (ACB), infiltration between the popliteal artery and capsule of the posterior knee (IPACK) block, and genicular nerve block (GNB) are three such options, but direct comparisons in orthopedic knee surgery are limited.
AIMS: To compare the post-operative analgesic efficacy of ultrasound-guided ACB, IPACK block, and GNB in patients undergoing knee surgeries under subarachnoid block.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, randomized, single-blind comparative study was conducted in the Department of Anaesthesiology, N.S.C.B. Medical College and Hospital, Jabalpur, over 18 months after institutional ethics committee approval (IEC/2023/7335-1). Ninety-nine ASA physical status I-II patients aged 18-60 years scheduled for elective knee surgery were randomized equally into three groups (n = 33 each). Group A received ultrasound-guided ACB, Group I received ultrasound-guided IPACK block, and Group G received ultrasound-guided GNB. Each block was performed with 20 mL of 0.375% ropivacaine, followed by standardized spinal anesthesia. Post-operative pain was assessed using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) over 24 h. Time to rescue intravenous paracetamol, tramadol requirement, and block-related complications were recorded.
RESULTS: Baseline demographic characteristics were comparable among groups. Group G had lower mean VAS scores at most post-operative time points, including 16, 20 and 24 h. The time to first rescue paracetamol was longest in Group G (5.87 ± 0.43 h), followed by Group A (5.62 ± 0.48 h) and Group I (5.42 ± 0.49 h). The second paracetamol dose was also delayed the longest in Group G (11.79 ± 0.83 h). Tramadol was required in 6.06% of patients in Group G, compared with 21.21% in Group A and 30.30% in Group I.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing orthopedic knee surgery, all three ultrasound-guided motor-sparing blocks provided clinically useful post-operative analgesia. GNB was associated with lower pain scores at most intervals, delayed rescue analgesic requirement, and reduced tramadol use compared with ACB and IPACK block, making it a promising option to support early rehabilitation. Larger adequately powered trials with procedure-specific subgroup analysis and functional outcomes, such as quadriceps strength and range of motion, are warranted.

articles.title: Mortality, Morbidity, and Treatment-Related Outcomes Following Pathological Hip Fractures: An 8-Year Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, type of treatment, and factors associated with mortality and morbidity, including the length of hospital stay, among patients with pathological hip fractures in a tertiary center in Saudi Arabia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted, which included all adult patients diagnosed with pathological hip fractures from 2016 to 2024. Demographics, fracture type, type of treatment, complications, and outcomes data were evaluated. A univariate analysis was performed to identify associations between clinical variables and patient outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included, with a mean age of 60.6 ± 17.12 years. Most patients were female (61.7%) and had femoral neck fractures (63.8%). Surgical treatment was performed in 78.7% of cases. The overall mortality rate was 6.4%, and 17.0% of patients experienced complications, including gait disturbances, bleeding, and deep vein thrombosis. Mortality was significantly associated with conservative treatment (P = 0.007). All deaths occurred in the conservatively treated group. Longer hospital stays were linked to pre-operative anticoagulant use (P = 0.011) and osteoporosis (P = 0.03).
CONCLUSION: Surgical management of pathological hip fractures was associated with improved survival and should be prioritized when clinically feasible. Awareness of pre-operative anticoagulant use and osteoporosis is essential for perioperative planning and may help reduce prolonged hospitalization in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Laparoscopic intravesical ureteroneocystostomy for pediatric vesicoureteral reflux: A comparison of Cohen and Politano-Leadbetter techniques.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Laparoscopic intravesical ureteroneocystostomy has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to open surgery for the management of pediatric vesicoureteral reflux (VUR). However, direct comparative data between the Cohen cross-trigonal and Politano-Leadbetter (PL) techniques remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare perioperative and functional outcomes of laparoscopic intravesical ureteroneocystostomy using the Cohen and PL techniques in children with primary VUR.
STUDY DESIGN: We retrospectively reviewed 61 consecutive pediatric patients who underwent laparoscopic intravesical ureteroneocystostomy between 2015 and 2025. Patients were categorized into the Cohen (n = 37) and PL (n = 24) groups. Reflux resolution was assessed per ureter using voiding cystourethrography at 6 months. Multivariable generalized estimating equation logistic regression was used to evaluate complete resolution while accounting for bilateral cases and adjusting for age and preoperative reflux grade. Operative time was analyzed using multivariable linear regression. Given the non-random allocation of surgical technique, propensity score-adjusted analyses were treated as the primary adjusted analyses, with conventional multivariable models also reported for comparison.
RESULTS: A total of 113 ureters were analyzed. Complete resolution was achieved in 95.7% of ureters in the Cohen group and 97.7% in the PL group. Surgical technique was not significantly associated with reflux resolution in either the conventional multivariable GEE model (adjusted OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.03-10.03, p = 0.707) or the propensity score-adjusted GEE analysis (OR 3.13, 95% CI 0.06-166.67, p = 0.568). For operative time, the PL technique was associated with longer duration in the conventional multivariable model (β = 39.8 min, p = 0.007), whereas this association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant in the propensity score-adjusted analysis (β = 19.4 min, p = 0.394). Median follow-up was 7.0 months (IQR 6.0-9.0), and renal function remained stable in both groups without evidence of deterioration.
CONCLUSION: Both laparoscopic intravesical Cohen and PL techniques provide high reflux resolution rates with comparable safety and functional outcomes. Although operative time was longer in the PL group in conventional analyses, this association was attenuated after propensity score adjustment. Technique selection may therefore be individualized according to patient-specific anatomical considerations rather than presumed superiority of either technique.

articles.title: Ethical considerations in the management of complications after lung resection: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Complications following lung resection present complex clinical, ethical and interpersonal challenges that extend beyond technical management. Although substantial literature addresses the prevention and treatment of complications after lung resection, there is limited guidance regarding the ethical principles that should shape clinical decision-making as complications evolve. This review proposes a practical ethical framework for the management of complications following lung resection.
METHODS: Recommendations were developed based on clinical expertise and relevant published sources. A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase, supplemented by targeted searches of relevant clinical resources and reference lists. English-language literature published within the last fifteen years was considered, with more recent evidence prioritized alongside foundational literature. Where lung resection-specific evidence was limited, related thoracic surgery, critical care, perioperative medicine, and surgical ethics literature was incorporated.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: The developed framework is focused on six foundational ethical principles spanning patient-centered and provider-/systems-centered domains. Patient-centered principles include autonomy, shared decision-making and proportionate goal-concordant care, which help define patient values and integrate those values with clinical expertise to align treatment strategies with meaningful outcomes. Provider-/systems-centered principles include beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice, transparency and accountability, all of which guide professional responsibility, equitable care, honest communication and collaboration throughout recovery. The application of these principles is examined across the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative phases of care.
CONCLUSIONS: This framework emphasizes aligning treatment decisions with patient-defined goals, while balancing the potential benefits and burdens of intervention. Overall, these six ethical principles provide a structured and durable framework for navigating complications following lung resection.

articles.title: Clinical and prognostic analysis of unicentric mediastinal Castleman disease: a 10-year retrospective series study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Castleman disease (CD) is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder, and unicentric mediastinal CD (UMCD) represents an uncommon thoracic manifestation for which surgical resection remains the mainstay of treatment.This study aims to: (I) characterize the anatomical distribution of UMCD in a single-center cohort; (II) evaluate the efficacy of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for UMCD resection and identify preoperative predictors of thoracotomy; (III) analyze prognostic outcomes in surgically managed UMCD patients.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 49 consecutive UMCD patients (26 males, 23 females; mean age 37.27±15.27 years) undergoing surgical resection at the department of thoracic surgery (Tangdu Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University) between May 2014 and October 2024. Demographic characteristics, anatomical distributions, and perioperative outcomes were systematically analyzed. Comparative analysis between VATS and thoracotomy groups was performed using independent samples t-tests. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of thoracotomy, with diagnostic performance evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methodology.
RESULTS: The most frequent anatomical involvement occurred in station 3A lymph nodes (12 cases, 24.5%), followed by station 10 (11 cases, 22.3%) and station 4 (8 cases, 16.3%). Mean tumor size was 6.25±3.09 cm (intraoperative measurement). Histopathological subtypes included hyaline vascular variant (43 cases, 87.7%), plasma cell variant (4 cases, 8.2%), and mixed-type (2 cases, 4.1%). Compared to thoracotomy, VATS demonstrated shorter operative duration (P<0.05), reduced intraoperative blood loss (P<0.05), and shorter postoperative chest tube retention (3±2.81 vs. 5.52±3.54 days, P<0.05). Multivariate analysis identified tumor diameter >6.6 cm (P<0.05) and arterial-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) attenuation >102 Hounsfield units (HU) (P<0.05) as independent predictors of thoracotomy. ROC analysis revealed an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875 for the combined diagnostic model. With a median follow-up duration of 52 months, the VATS group maintained 100% recurrence-free survival. In the thoracotomy group, three patients succumbed to disease (two from local recurrence refractory to conservative therapy, one from postoperative pneumonia with respiratory failure following pneumonectomy). The overall survival (OS) rate for the cohort was 91.83%.
CONCLUSIONS: Station 3A lymph nodes represent the predominant anatomical site of UMCD involvement. VATS resection confers significant advantages over thoracotomy, including reduced operative time, blood loss, and postoperative recovery duration. The diameter >6.6 cm and arterial-phase CT attenuation >102 HU of tumors serve as reliable preoperative indicators for thoracotomy. Early surgical intervention correlates with favorable prognosis, while postoperative complications and local recurrence demonstrate significant association with mortality.

articles.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown.
METHODS: We conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients.
RESULTS: ALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearman's rho = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearman's rho = -0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p < 0.001).
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.

articles.title: Preoperative cranial computed tomography in pediatric cochlear implantation: clinical necessity or optional step?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Due to growing evidence regarding the risks of ionizing radiation, especially in children, some centers now perform cochlear implantation (CI) without a preoperative computed tomography (CT) scan, relying solely on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This study evaluates the necessity and safety of omitting CT scans before bilateral CI in children.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 164 children, implanted bilaterally between 2018 and 2024 and aged under 10 years at the time of either simultaneous or second CI, were included. The impact of preoperative imaging on duration of surgery and perioperative complications was analyzed. The surgical procedure was compared between cases with and without a preoperative CT scan and analyzed for surgeons in training and experienced surgeons.
RESULTS: 105 children were implanted with a preoperative CT scan and 59 without a CT scan. The duration of bilateral CI surgery was 122.5 (±41.4) min for procedures [CI without CT: 122.5 (±41.4) min; CI with CT: 116.1 (±33.84) min; (p = 0.4861)] and anesthesia [CI without CT: 237.2 (±47.38) min; CI with CT: 226.3 (±41.50) min; (p = 0.1352)] did not differ significantly between the groups, irrespective of the experience of the surgeons. Seven cases showed relevant malformations visible on MRI, such as large vestibular aqueduct syndrome, which were relevant during the surgery. Minor and major complications occurred rarely in both cohorts but more frequently in patients without CT scan (without CT: 10.2% (6/59); with CT: 4.8% (5/105); p = 0.2052; risk difference [RD], 5.4%; 95% CI, -6.3 to 14.3%). Intraoperative X-ray imaging revealed no cases of electrode tip fold-over, and no patients developed postoperative complete or incomplete facial nerve palsy.
CONCLUSION: In summary, an MRI-based imaging strategy without routine preoperative CT may be safe and sufficient in appropriately selected pediatric CI candidates, with additional CT reserved for patients in whom clinical or MRI findings suggest relevant bony abnormalities, complex inner ear malformations, or syndromic conditions. This approach reduces unnecessary radiation exposure and the use of healthcare resources, while avoiding redundant diagnostic information from both imaging modalities, without compromising surgical safety or outcomes.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes and tissue trauma after uncomplicated total hysterectomy for benign uterine disease: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hysterectomy is the most frequently performed non-obstetric gynecological surgery for benign disease, and the surgical route affects perioperative outcomes and recovery. While minimally invasive approaches reduce surgical morbidity, their relative effect on the systemic inflammatory response remains incompletely characterized, particularly when indication and case complexity are accounted for. We compared tissue trauma, operative data, and early postoperative outcomes after uncomplicated vaginal hysterectomy (VH), laparoscopic hysterectomy (LH), and abdominal hysterectomy (AH).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed women aged 25-80 years who underwent total hysterectomy for benign indications at our institution (2021-2024). Patients with malignant disease, chronic inflammatory conditions, prophylactic drains, or complicated postoperative courses were excluded. Primary endpoints were postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and white blood cell (WBC) and neutrophil (Neu) count trajectories over the first three postoperative days; secondary endpoints were hemoglobin drop, operative time, blood loss, bowel function recovery, and length of stay. Multivariable models adjusted for age, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status, surgical indication, and previous abdominal surgery, with uterine weight assessed in a sensitivity analysis; trajectories were modelled with linear mixed-effects models, and the route effect was examined within a single-indication (fibromatosis) subgroup.
RESULTS: We included 281 patients (84 VH, 86 LH, 111 AH). AH and LH required longer operative times than VH, and AH was additionally associated with higher blood loss, delayed gastrointestinal recovery, and longer hospitalization. In unadjusted analyses AH showed the highest CRP at all three days and higher WBC and neutrophil counts on Days 1 and 2; the haematological differences were attenuated after adjustment, whereas the CRP elevation persisted. Because route, indication, and uterine size were strongly collinear, the route effect was examined within the fibromatosis subgroup, where AH remained independently associated with higher CRP than LH across all postoperative days.
CONCLUSIONS: After uncomplicated hysterectomy for benign disease, surgical route was independently associated with the postoperative systemic inflammatory response. AH carried a greater inflammatory burden and slower functional recovery, whereas VH and LH were broadly comparable; compared with LH, VH showed faster recovery and certain perioperative advantages. Minimally invasive techniques should be prioritized when clinically feasible.

articles.title: Establishment of canine nasal carcinoma organoids for drug sensitivity testing and functional characterization of S100A2.
articles.abstract: Canine nasal carcinoma (NC) is highly malignant and progressive, with metastasis. Radiation therapy is a common treatment; however, it has various drawbacks, including cost and anesthetic risks in elderly patients. Therefore, the development of alternative anti-cancer drug therapies has been required. In this study, we established an NC organoid culture method as an experimental model and explored more effective therapeutic targets. NC organoids were generated from patient-derived tissues from diseased dogs with NC. Electron microscopy of NC organoids revealed goblet cell differentiation with mucus granules and luminal structures. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CK19, E-cadherin, and Ki67, and their expression patterns corresponded to those in the original tissues. Furthermore, NC organoids were tumorigenic in immunodeficient mice. We identified useful supplements for culturing NC organoids and found that each NC organoid line exhibited different sensitivities to anti-cancer drugs. RNA sequencing was performed using samples from healthy dogs and NC organoids. Pathways related to MYC targets, oxidative phosphorylation, and protein secretion were enriched in NC organoids compared with normal nasal cells. Among the differentially expressed genes, S100A2 was selected for further functional investigation based on its increased expression and previously reported involvement in cancer-related processes. S100A2 knockdown reduced cell proliferation and invasiveness, supporting a functional contribution of S100A2 to malignant phenotypes in canine NC. These findings establish canine NC organoids as an experimental platform for investigating canine NC biology and provide a basis for future comparative studies.

articles.title: Comparison of short- to mid-term outcomes between DAA hemiarthroplasty and PFNA internal fixation in elderly patients with trochanteric fractures: a propensity score-matched retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trochanteric fractures (TF) are common in elderly patients. Although Proximal Femoral Nail Antirotation (PFNA) internal fixation is widely used, hemiarthroplasty via the direct anterior approach (DAA) has attracted increasing interest because of concerns regarding prolonged bed rest and associated complications. This study compares early outcomes of DAA hemiarthroplasty vs. PFNA internal fixation in elderly TF patients.
METHODS: Patients aged ≥75 years with TF treated between January 2018 and January 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. After application of the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 54 patients who underwent DAA hemiarthroplasty were identified. To minimize selection bias, 1:1 propensity score matching was performed based on age, sex, body mass index (BMI), fracture type, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade, yielding 54 matched patients who received PFNA. Outcomes included operative duration, blood loss, incision length, bedridden duration, Harris Hip Scores (HHS) at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months, complications, and radiographic findings.
RESULTS: After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. The PFNA group had significantly less blood loss (220.3 vs. 349.6 mL, P < 0.001) and a shorter operative time (40.05 vs. 75.02 min, P < 0.001), but a longer total incision length (11.49 vs. 9.29 cm, P < 0.001). Bedridden duration was markedly shorter in the DAA group (0.99 vs. 52.86 days, P < 0.001). At all follow-up points, HHS was significantly higher in the DAA group (1 month: 78.85 vs. 63.89, P < 0.001; 24 months: 92.03 vs. 82.86, P < 0.001). Complication rates were lower in the DAA group, although the difference did not reach statistical significance. Mean prosthesis subsidence in the DAA group was 2.7 mm.
CONCLUSION: In this propensity score-matched retrospective study, DAA hemiarthroplasty was associated with faster early functional recovery and a shorter bedridden duration than PFNA internal fixation in elderly patients with TF, but also with a longer operative time and greater blood loss. The substantial difference in postoperative rehabilitation protocols between the two groups may have contributed to the observed gap in functional outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: Level of evidence, 3.

articles.title: Chloride load and serum chloride in critically ill adults: a randomization-anchored analysis of the BaSICS trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 0.9% saline solution has a supraphysiological chloride concentration and has been associated observationally with acute kidney injury and mortality. How randomized fluid type changes serum chloride early in critical illness, and what determines this change, remain uncertain. Focusing on the first three days after randomization, we estimated the randomized saline-versus-Plasma-Lyte difference in serum chloride and its variation by renal function, the observational association with study-saline volume, and the sources of variation in serum chloride.
METHODS: This secondary analysis of BaSICS (75 Brazilian ICUs; Plasma-Lyte 148 vs 0.9% saline) included participants with baseline serum chloride and at least one measurement on days 1-3. A Bayesian hierarchical longitudinal model estimated the treatment effect over time and its variation by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Group-level analyses used day 2, which balanced accumulated exposure against attrition of measurements. We normalized randomized between-group differences, estimated an inverse-probability-weighted within-saline volume association, and partitioned modeled variation in serum chloride.
RESULTS: Among 3,482 patients (33% of the trial population), serum chloride rose 2.15 mmol/L (95% confidence interval, 1.76-2.53) more with saline than with Plasma-Lyte by day 2, when saline recipients had received on average 145.7 mmol more study-fluid chloride, corresponding to 1.47 mmol/L per 100 mmol of additional chloride (1.17-1.81). Within saline recipients, the weighted association was +0.31 mmol/L per 100 mmol (0.22 to 0.44). The day-2 between-group difference decreased by 0.29 mmol/L (95% credible interval, 0.12 to 0.46) per 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 higher baseline eGFR (+3.0 mmol/L at 30 vs +1.8 mmol/L at 90 mL/min/1.73 m2). Of modeled variation in serum chloride, the fluid component accounted for 0.7% (0.4-1.0; 1.8% with randomized arm included); measured baseline characteristics, almost entirely baseline serum chloride, for 48.1%; persistent patient-specific differences not explained by measured characteristics for 24.5%; and day-to-day within-patient fluctuation for 26.9%.
CONCLUSIONS: Over the first three ICU days, randomization to saline increased serum chloride relative to Plasma-Lyte, and the between-group difference was larger at lower baseline eGFR. Most modeled variation in serum chloride reflected each patient's baseline chloride and persistent patient-specific differences that measured characteristics did not explain; the fluid component was small.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02875873.

articles.title: Effects of the Sodium Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Empagliflozin on Perioperative Endothelial Function in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: An Exploratory Analysis of MERCURI-1.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether short-term treatment with empagliflozin (EMPA) is associated with attenuation of endothelial dysfunction and cardiac injury in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: An exploratory study using samples from the open-label randomized MERCURI-1 study.
SETTING: Academic university hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients received 10 mg/d EMPA starting 3 days before surgery and continuing until 2 days postoperatively or received standard perioperative care.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Blood samples were collected at baseline (prior to EMPA therapy), on the day of surgery (before the first incision), and 1 day after surgery. Plasma biomarkers for endothelial activation (endothelin-1), vascular leakage (angiopoietin-2), glycocalyx degradation (syndecan-1), cardiac injury (Troponin I and NT-proBNP), and systemic inflammation (IL-6, IL-8, and CRP) were measured. In vitro, human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells were exposed to patient plasma, and endothelial permeability was assessed. Surgery-induced changes in biomarkers of endothelial activation and vascular leakage did not differ significantly between the EMPA and control groups. The adjusted between-group differences were 0.097 pg/mL for endothelin-1 (95% confidence interval [CI] -0.478 to 0.672, p = 0.735), -465 pg/mL for angiopoietin-2 (95% CI -2,355 to 1,426, p = 0.623), and 19,540 pg/mL for syndecan-1 (95% CI -10,016 to 49,095, p = 0.19). No significant differences were found for cardiac injury or inflammatory biomarkers. In vitro, endothelial resistance did not differ between the EMPA and control groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory substudy, no significant differences in endothelial activation, vascular leakage, cardiac injury, or inflammation between were found the EMPA and control groups. Given the limited sample size, smaller treatment effects cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Ultrasonic texture features for assessing abnormal interventricular septum motion following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery alters cardiomyocyte geometry and architecture, leading to changes in the acoustic properties of the myocardium. This study investigated ultrasomics-a novel cardiac ultrasound-based radiomics technique that extracts high-throughput pixel-level information from images-to identify ultrasonic texture and morphological changes associated with abnormal motion of the interventricular septum (IVS) following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A total of 650 patients from two centers were included in the study. The 460 patients from Center A were randomly allocated to the training (n=322) and internal validation (n=138) sets at a 7:3 ratio, while the 190 patients from Center B constituted the independent external validation set. All patients underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at two time points: 10 minutes after anesthesia induction (preoperative) and 10 minutes after chest closure (postoperative). Standard left ventricular long-axis and four-chamber views were acquired to visualize the IVS. The workflow consisted of IVS segmentation, radiomics feature extraction, and feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Three machine learning methods were compared: logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM). Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis.
RESULTS: Twenty-six significant radiomics features, including shape, first-order, and texture features, were identified. The incidence of postoperative abnormal IVS motion was 50.93%, 46.38%, and 40.00% in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively, with no significant intergroup difference (P>0.05). The SVM model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.943 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.925-0.961] in the training set, 0.948 (95% CI: 0.921-0.974) in the internal validation set, and 0.803 (95% CI: 0.772-0.834) in the external validation set. Postoperative analysis revealed significant changes in the core IVS radiomics features. Specifically, increased gray-scale heterogeneity and decreased texture correlation in the IVS were observed in patients with abnormal septal motion after cardiac surgery (all relevant P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the potential of cardiac ultrasomics to differentiate between normal and abnormal IVS motion in patients after cardiac surgery. A highly interpretable SVM ultrasomics model was developed based on texture and morphological features, providing quantitative characterization of microstructural changes in the IVS associated with abnormal motion following cardiac surgery and potentially supporting more precise perioperative clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Evaluating how preoperative symptom predominance is associated with outcomes following uniportal full-endoscopic lateral recess decompression: a comparative cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with lumbar lateral recess stenosis present with varying degrees of radicular leg pain and axial back pain, yet the exact impact of each preoperative symptom on postoperative outcomes following full-endoscopic decompression remains poorly understood. Existing literature does not stratify patients by symptom profile, revealing a gap that could inform patient selection and preoperative counselling. This study aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes between back pain-predominant (BP) and leg pain-predominant (LP) patients following endoscopic unilateral uniportal lateral recess decompression.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed on patients with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed single-level lumbar lateral recess stenosis who underwent isolated unilateral index-level lateral recess decompression using a full-endoscopic uniportal approach. Patients were stratified into BP and LP groups according to preoperative symptom predominance, while patients with equivalent back and leg pain scores were excluded. Baseline characteristics, postoperative patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), changes from baseline, and minimal clinically important difference (MCID) attainment [defined as a ≥2-point improvement in Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores] were compared using independent t-tests and Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: A total of 50 patients were included, comprising 19 BP and 31 LP patients. Median follow-up was 5 months (interquartile range, 2-6 months). Baseline demographic and perioperative characteristics were comparable between groups (all P>0.05). BP patients reported higher preoperative VAS back pain scores (7.16±1.89 vs. 4.35±2.99, P<0.001), whereas LP patients reported higher VAS leg pain scores (7.81±1.83 vs. 3.53±2.99, P<0.001). Preoperative VAS numbness and North American Spine Society (NASS) scores were similar between groups. Postoperative PROMs were comparable across all domains (all P>0.05). However, BP patients demonstrated greater improvement in VAS back pain (5.11±3.35 vs. 2.29±3.33, P=0.006), while LP patients achieved greater improvements in VAS leg pain (6.23±3.43 vs. 2.47±3.15, P<0.001) and NASS neurogenic symptoms (37.77±26.14 vs. 21.58±19.44, P=0.02). MCID attainment for leg pain was higher in the LP group [90.3% vs. 52.6%; OR 8.40, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.89-37.40; P=0.005].
CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant between-group differences were noted in postoperative outcomes following full-endoscopic uniportal lateral recess decompression, suggesting that axial back pain predominance should not preclude surgical candidacy. Recovery patterns differed according to symptom profile, with BP patients experiencing greater back pain relief and LP patients demonstrating greater improvement in leg pain and neurogenic symptoms. These findings support individualized preoperative counselling and expectation management. Prospective studies with larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Sex differences in limitations of life-sustaining treatment in the intensive care unit: A nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous research suggests that limitations of life-sustaining treatment (LST) may be more common in women than men, but few studies have included data on clinical reasoning or limitation type. This study aimed to investigate sex differences in LST-limitations in the ICU and in their documented characteristics.
METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) ICU patients registered in the Swedish Intensive Care Register between 2019 and 2024 were included. A multivariable logistic regression model, adjusted for SAPS3 and age, analysed the association between sex and LST-limitations. Limitation characteristics were compared using Chi-square test (categorical variables) and Wilcoxon rank-sum test (numeric variables).
RESULTS: The cohort included 111,354 patients; 41.7% women. LST-limitations occurred in 24.4% of patients and were more frequent in women than in men (25.3% vs. 23.8%, p < 0.0001). In adjusted analyses women had higher odds of receiving an LST-limitation than men, both in the full cohort (OR 1.21, 95% CI 1.17-1.25) and among 30-day non-survivors (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.32). Women received LST-limitations earlier than men (2.8 h after admission vs 4.5 h, p < 0.0001). Acute disease and therapy failure were more often documented reasons in men than in women (78.8% vs 74.3%, p < 0.0001; 21.2% vs. 18.6%, p = 0.0001), whereas autonomy and chronic disease were more frequent in women (7.8% vs 5.9%, p < 0.0001; 63.2% vs. 60.7%, p = 0.0021). Women were more often involved in decision-making (13.3% vs 11.8%, p = 0.0074).
CONCLUSIONS: Women were more likely to receive LST-limitations and received them earlier. Men who died within 30 days were less likely to have had an LST-limitation than women. Documented reasons for LST-limitations differed by sex, and women had higher rates of documented patient involvement.

articles.title: Complications in anatomical lung resection: a comprehensive surgical perspective in a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The development of new technologies and techniques has reduced the frequency and duration of many complications following pulmonary resection. This article reviews complications following lung resection including contemporary strategies in preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative management.
METHODS: A literature review was performed using PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Searches were conducted using topic-specific keywords related to perioperative management and complications following anatomical lung resection.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Minimally invasive surgery is standard and has reduced cost and rates of many complications; however, rates of air leak remain unchanged. Resection following neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, including minimally invasive surgery, does not appear to increase surgical risk although the available data reflects smaller sample sizes. Significant postoperative complications including bronchopleural fistula and empyema continue to require intensive and thoughtful management. Endoluminal therapies can be effective independently or as adjuncts in management these complications. A high index of suspicion should prompt early intervention to limit negative impact of postoperative complication.
CONCLUSIONS: While many postoperative complications have reduced in frequency, the rate of postoperative air leak has not changed in two decades. Robust surgical clinical data following neoadjuvant treatment is limited and larger studies, which also report robotic surgical outcomes, are needed to reflect cotemporary surgical practice.

articles.title: The Pulmonary Artery to Body Surface Area Ratio in Acute Type A Aortic Dissections: An Innocent Bystander.
Anesthetic Management of Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency in Cardiac Surgery: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Global prevalence of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency approaches 450 million individuals. G6PD deficiency impairs management of oxidative stress and has been associated with premature development of coronary atherosclerosis. Anesthesia, cardiac surgery, and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) may exacerbate oxidative stress. This review article summarizes literature pertaining to perioperative management of individuals with G6PD deficiency undergoing cardiac surgery. Perioperative care for individuals with G6PD deficiency centers on avoidance of oxidative stress and triggering medications. Although many anesthetic medications have been safely used in G6PD-deficient populations, emerging evidence suggests propofol, dexmedetomidine, and remifentanil have pleiotropic antioxidant properties. Cardiac surgery and CPB potentially instigate erythrocyte trauma and promote oxidative stress. Centrifugal pumps avoid mechanical deformation of red cells and generate a significantly lower inflammatory response than roller pumps. While selection of large vascular cannulae promotes laminar flow and imparts less shear stress on erythrocytes, minimized CPB circuitry reduces the nonbiologic contact interface with erythrocytes and is associated with less inflammation than conventional CPB circuitry. Moreover, maintenance of normothermia during CPB may help prevent hemolysis in individuals with G6PD deficiency by preserving red cell deformability. Importantly, transient acidemia during CPB may potentially trigger hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals, and the balance between perfusion supply and demand warrants consideration. Strategies to mitigate intraoperative hemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals are needed to support safe perioperative care. Intraoperative care demands vigilance for signs of hemolysis to support prompt diagnosis and management.

articles.title: The three-tube method for esophageal perforation with mediastinal abscess caused by a foreign body: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Foreign body-induced esophageal perforation can cause mediastinal abscess and life-threatening infection. Treatment is particularly challenging in patients with substantial physiological impairment who may poorly tolerate surgery or repeated endoscopic procedures. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes of fluoroscopy-guided tube-based management for this condition.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 72 patients with foreign body-induced esophageal perforation complicated by mediastinal abscess who underwent fluoroscopy-guided tube-based treatment between June 2015 and December 2025. The treatment framework combined nasojejunal feeding and gastrointestinal decompression with transnasal or percutaneous abscess drainage when indicated. Six patients with small fistulous openings, abscess cavities smaller than 2 cm, and favorable general conditions received a modified two-tube regimen without direct abscess drainage. Technical success, fistula healing, healing time, mortality, persistent fistula, and treatment-related complications were evaluated. Exploratory discrimination of clinical variables for delayed healing was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with 1,000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: The planned tube configuration was successfully placed in all 72 patients. Before intervention, 65 patients (90.3%) had an American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status of III or IV, and 18 required mechanical ventilation. During a median follow-up of 9 months, 58 patients (80.6%) achieved complete fistula healing and resumed oral intake, with a mean healing time of 98.16±43.56 days. Five patients died of severe infection, one died of massive hemorrhage, and eight developed persistent fistulas requiring long-term tube management. Abscess-drainage tube suction failure occurred in 41 patients and required fluoroscopic adjustment or replacement. Referral time (bootstrap-corrected area under the curve, 0.718; cutoff >5.50 days) and fistula size (corrected area under the curve, 0.705; cutoff >1.15 cm) showed exploratory discriminatory ability for delayed healing.
CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopy-guided tube-based management was technically feasible and resulted in complete healing in 80.6% of this selected cohort, including patients requiring mechanical ventilation. However, prolonged healing, frequent catheter dysfunction, six deaths, and eight persistent fistulas demonstrate a substantial treatment burden. This approach may be considered within multidisciplinary care for carefully selected patients, but prospective comparative studies are required to establish its safety and effectiveness relative to surgical and endoscopic treatments.

articles.title: Preoperative Chemotherapy and Its Efficacy in Pediatric Wilms Tumor: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) is the most common malignant renal tumor in children. Preoperative (neoadjuvant) chemotherapy has been widely adopted to reduce tumor size, facilitate surgical resection, and decrease the risk of intraoperative tumor rupture. However, the magnitude of its clinical benefits remains a subject of debate. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of preoperative chemotherapy in children with Wilms tumor in terms of tumor shrinkage, complete tumor resection, and event-free survival (EFS). This systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to 2024 that evaluated preoperative chemotherapy in pediatric patients with Wilms tumor. Eligible studies compared preoperative chemotherapy with upfront surgery, alternative chemotherapy strategies, or different durations of preoperative treatment. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers. Due to the limited number of studies and substantial clinical heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was conducted instead of a meta-analysis. Three RCTs involving 631 pediatric patients were included. Preoperative chemotherapy consistently resulted in significant tumor shrinkage and facilitated surgical management. A reduction in intraoperative complications, particularly tumor rupture, was observed in patients receiving preoperative therapy compared with upfront surgery. Survival outcomes were generally comparable between treatment groups, with no significant improvement in EFS or overall survival (OS) associated with prolonged preoperative treatment. Evidence from one trial demonstrated improved tumor response and reduced perioperative blood loss with trans-arterial chemoembolization combined with surgery. Overall, extending preoperative chemotherapy beyond four weeks did not provide additional clinical benefit. These findings suggest that preoperative chemotherapy in pediatric Wilms tumor improves tumor shrinkage and surgical feasibility while reducing operative complications. Current evidence does not support extending treatment duration beyond standard short-course regimens, as longer courses do not appear to improve survival outcomes and may increase treatment-related toxicity. Further high-quality randomized studies are needed to strengthen the evidence base and clarify long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Suspected Rib Fractures in Blunt Thoracic Trauma: A Proposed Emergency Department Protocol.
articles.abstract: Blunt thoracic trauma accounts for substantial emergency department admissions, with rib fractures representing a predominant injury pattern. Undetected or inadequately characterised rib fractures exacerbate the risks of hypoventilation, atelectasis, secondary pneumonia, and delayed pleuropulmonary complications, particularly in older adults. Conventional initial diagnostic evaluation relies heavily on plain chest radiography, which exhibits recognised diagnostic insensitivity for undisplaced cortical breaches and injuries traversing the costochondral junctions. Although computed tomography provides definitive anatomical resolution, routine acquisition in stable, minor blunt trauma imposes ionising radiation burdens, emergency department delays, and escalating healthcare expenditures. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) offers an accessible, radiation-free imaging adjunct possessing high sensitivity for superficial cortical breaches, chondral disruptions, and adjacent pleural complications. To address persistent diagnostic blind spots and documentation deficits in acute thoracic care, a structured emergency department POCUS workflow is proposed. The operational protocol integrates targeted high-frequency linear interrogation of symptomatic cortical margins, multi-zone transducer exclusion of pleural collections and pneumothorax, standardised sonographic criteria, and a structured clinical escalation algorithm. When integrated with comprehensive clinical assessment, this proposed POCUS protocol is intended to support acute trauma stratification, facilitate targeted regional anaesthesia, optimise clinical documentation, and complement conventional radiography in acute care environments. Prospective implementation studies are required to determine its diagnostic accuracy and impact on patient outcomes.

articles.title: Digital subtraction angiography-guided spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis and microsurgical varicocelectomy in the treatment of varicocele: a comparative study with propensity score matching.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varicocele (VC) adversely affects spermatogenesis and is a recognized contributor to male infertility. This study aimed to compare the safety, efficacy, and clinical value of spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis guided by digital subtraction angiography (DSA) vs. microsurgical varicocelectomy.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 181 patients with VC who were treated from January 2021 to December 2024. After propensity score matching (PSM) at a 1:2 ratio, 38 interventional and 76 surgical patients were included. The interventional group underwent embolization plus sclerosis guided by DSA under local anesthesia; the surgical group received microsurgical subinguinal varicocelectomy under general anesthesia. Postoperative outcomes and semen parameters were compared with a minimum follow-up of 12 months.
RESULTS: The interventional group had a significantly shorter procedure duration (52.11±16.97 vs. 67.89±27.91 min, P=0.0003), earlier ambulation [0.47 (0.32, 0.81) vs. 25.06 (24.48, 25.73) h, P<0.001], and shorter hospital stay [2.00 (2.00, 3.75) vs. 3.00 (2.00, 5.00) days, P=0.0173]. Pain relief rates were similar (94.73% vs. 93.42%, P>0.99). The complication rate was numerically lower in the interventional group but did not differ significantly [13.16% (5/38) vs. 28.95% (22/76), P=0.084], with no Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher complications in either group. At 1-year follow-up, both groups showed significant improvements in all semen parameters (all P<0.001), with no significant between-group differences in the degree of improvement (all P>0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Spermatic vein embolization plus sclerosis guided by DSA may be a safe and effective alternative to microsurgical varicocelectomy, offering faster recovery and comparable semen parameter improvement, particularly for young infertile patients and day-surgery settings, pending further validation.

articles.title: Retrospective comparative study of early postoperative complications and recovery following modified gasless subclavian endoscopic thyroidectomy in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma at different tumor stages.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is the most common malignant tumor of the endocrine system. Modified gasless subclavian endoscopic thyroidectomy has been increasingly used because of its minimally invasive nature and cosmetic advantages. However, postoperative complications may adversely affect patient recovery, and reliable risk prediction tools remain limited. This study aimed to compare early postoperative complications and recovery outcomes among patients with PTC at different tumor stages and to develop a model for predicting postoperative complications.
METHODS: A total of 212 patients with PTC who underwent gasless subclavian endoscopic thyroidectomy were retrospectively enrolled. The primary outcome was the occurrence of overall postoperative complications. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors and establish a predictive model. The discriminatory ability of the model was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration performance was assessed using calibration curves, and clinical utility was evaluated through decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Postoperative complications occurred in 71 patients (33.49%). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that T2-T3 stage [odds ratio (OR) =4.72], total thyroidectomy (OR =4.70), central lymph node dissection (CLND) (OR =4.25), and prolonged operative time (OR =1.05/min) were independent risk factors (all P<0.05). The combined predictive model showed favorable predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8757 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.8272-0.9242], along with good calibration and clinical applicability. Hypocalcemia was the most common postoperative complication, while recurrent laryngeal nerve injury occurred more frequently in patients with advanced-stage disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Tumor stage, surgical extent, and operative complexity are important factors influencing postoperative complications in patients with PTC. The proposed predictive model demonstrated good risk assessment capability and may provide a useful reference for individualized perioperative management.

articles.title: Risk factors and clinical implications of sternal dehiscence following clamshell incision in bilateral lung transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clamshell incisions provide excellent exposure for bilateral lung transplantation (BLT) but carry an inherent risk of sternal dehiscence. This study aimed to identify the risk factors for sternal dehiscence and evaluate its impact on pulmonary function.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 129 adult patients who underwent BLT via clamshell incision between 2007 and 2024. Sternal dehiscence was defined as radiographic nonunion of the sternum confirmed by chest computed tomography scan at least 3 months postoperatively, or any sternal dehiscence requiring surgical correction regardless of the time interval. Risk factors were identified using Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression analysis. Pulmonary function tests were compared between patients with and without dehiscence at 1 year postoperatively and the last follow-up.
RESULTS: Sternal dehiscence occurred in 15 patients (11.6%), of which 11 (8.5%) were classified as major cases. Multivariable analysis identified male sex as an independent risk factor associated with dehiscence [odds ratio (OR) 8.89, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.27-108.74, P=0.02], whereas perioperative tracheostomy was independently associated with a lower incidence (OR =0.12, 95% CI: 0.02-0.53, P=0.004). Surgical closure techniques, including wiring and parasternal fixation, were not significantly associated with dehiscence (P=0.73 and P>0.99, respectively). No significant differences in pulmonary function were observed between groups at 1 year postoperatively and last follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Male sex was independently associated with sternal dehiscence following BLT, whereas perioperative tracheostomy was associated with a lower incidence; these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating given the observational design. Pulmonary function during the follow-up period was not significantly associated with sternal dehiscence in this cohort. Surgeons may consider reinforced closure in male patients, while the protective role of tracheostomy warrants further study.

articles.title: Clinical efficacy of minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery concomitant with radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) and valvular heart disease (VHD) present complex clinical challenges. Standard radiofrequency ablation (RFA) combined with valve surgery via median sternotomy offers robust rhythm correction but causes significant surgical trauma. Minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery with concomitant RFA (MICVS-RFA) is a promising strategy, but clinical data regarding its comprehensive safety, efficacy, and predictive risk factors for AF recurrence remain scarce. Thus, we aimed to evaluate the safety and clinical efficacy of MICVS-RFA and to develop an exploratory prognostic model for risk stratification.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 146 patients with concomitant VHD and AF who underwent MICVS-RFA between April 1, 2020, and August 1, 2025. Surgical cohorts included mitral valve replacement (MVR; n=34), mitral valve repair (MVr; n=19), MVR combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVR + TVr; n=57), and MVr combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVr + TVr; n=36). Pre-operative predictors for post-operative AF recurrence were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and elastic net regularization integrated within a multiple imputation framework to develop an exploratory model. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvements were assessed dynamically.
RESULTS: Procedural success was achieved in all 146 patients, with an overall 30-day freedom from recurrent AF (FFAF) rate of 89.7% and no observed major adverse events (stroke, bleeding, or thromboembolism) within the first post-operative month. Length of stay (LOS) showed no statistical differences among surgical cohorts (P=0.71). Logistic regression modeling identified pre-operative metoprolol usage as associated with lower odds of AF recurrence [odds ratio (OR) =0.17; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.04-0.62], while pre-operative pulmonary hypertension (PH) showed a non-significant association with higher odds of AF recurrence (OR =3.07; 95% CI: 0.67-14.10). The predictive model showed moderate discrimination [bootstrap-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) =0.773] and apparent calibration. Patients with baseline LVEF <55% experienced superior functional recovery compared to those with LVEF ≥55% (ΔLVEF: 13.07%±2.56% vs. 0.18%±0.80%, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: MICVS-RFA was a feasible "dual minimally invasive" strategy that permits concomitant treatment of valvular pathology and AF through a minimally invasive approach, minimizing perioperative trauma. Comparative and long-term effects require further study.

articles.title: Association between age and in-hospital mortality and arch repair strategy in acute type A aortic dissection: a dose-response analysis of a retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced age is a recognized risk factor in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but its dose-response relationship with in-hospital mortality and the optimal extent of arch repair in elderly patients remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. The association between age (as a continuous variable) and in-hospital mortality was assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis. In a subgroup of elderly patients (≥60 years, n=115), perioperative outcomes between no/partial arch replacement and total arch replacement were compared after 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Among 1,042 included patients, overall in-hospital mortality was 3.7% (39/1,042), and median age was 51 (interquartile range, 40-59) years. Age was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.04 per year, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.07, P=0.01), and RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear association without evidence of a threshold effect (P overall =0.02; P for non-linearity =0.31). In the elderly subgroup (n=244), 115 patients met imaging eligibility criteria for PSM, yielding 30 matched pairs. In this small matched cohort, total arch replacement was associated with longer cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, with no statistically significant differences in mortality (6.7% vs. 3.3%) or major complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Age shows a continuous linear association with in-hospital mortality after ATAAD repair, without evidence of a threshold effect. In elderly patients, total arch replacement and limited arch repair showed no statistically significant differences in early outcomes in this small matched cohort, suggesting that operative strategy should be individualized based on anatomical and physiological risk rather than age alone-a finding that warrants validation in larger studies.

articles.title: Real-world implementation of video-assisted thoracic surgery for lung cancer: a decade-long regional propensity score-weighted cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The perioperative advantages of video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) over thoracotomy are established, but the real-world introduction of a minimally invasive program is shaped by patient selection, technical maturation, conversion and secular change in care. We evaluated the decade-long implementation of VATS within a regional thoracic surgery service and estimated its association with early postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study of anatomical lung resections performed over the first decade [2009-2018] of a VATS implementation program at two tertiary hospitals covered by a single thoracic surgery department. The primary exposure was the approach with which the operation was started under an intention-to-treat analysis strategy, and the outcomes were 90-day mortality, a composite of major morbidity and perioperative mortality, and 30-day readmission. Propensity score weighting used preoperative covariates, including calendar year and hospital. Covariate balance before and after weighting was assessed by absolute standardized mean differences. The average treatment effect (ATE), reported as risk difference with 95% confidence interval (CI), was the primary estimand, with average treatment on the treated (ATT) and average treatment effect on the overlap population (ATO) as sensitivity estimands. An exploratory analysis comparing conversion with upfront thoracotomy was carried out under the same prespecification.
RESULTS: A total of 964 out of 1,404 anatomical lung resections met the inclusion criteria. The series included 472 operations begun thoracoscopically, of which 97 were converted (20%), versus 492 upfront thoracotomies. Completed VATS rose from 16.7% of anatomical resections in 2009 to 53.7% in 2018, while conversion annual rates fell from 50.0% to 6.5%. Converted procedures had the highest crude rate of every adverse outcome. Under intention to treat, an intended VATS approach was not significantly associated with 90-day mortality (ATE -1.9 percentage points; 95% CI: -4.7 to +0.9; P=0.17), major morbidity and mortality (ATE -4.6 points; 95% CI: -9.4 to +0.2; P=0.06) or readmission (ATE -2.0 points; 95% CI: -5.9 to +2.0; P=0.33); for the composite outcome, the ATT (P=0.04) and ATO (P=0.047) estimands reached significance. In the as-treated analysis, all three outcomes were significant in favor of completed VATS. No statistically significant differences were detected between conversions and upfront thoracotomies in the exploratory analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Across a decade-long regional implementation trajectory, adoption of VATS rose and conversion fell. When conversions are analyzed in the arm in which the operation was begun, the association between an intended thoracoscopic approach and better perioperative outcomes is attenuated and no longer significant. These findings do not question the perioperative advantages of thoracoscopic lobectomy, but the benefit attributable to adopting a thoracoscopic strategy at service level is smaller and less certain than that observed among the operations it completes.

articles.title: Dose-response association between early postoperative serum magnesium and in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study in MIMIC-IV with external replication in the eICU-CRD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypomagnesemia is common following cardiac surgery and is associated with arrhythmias and adverse outcomes. In postoperative cardiac intensive care unit (ICU) patients, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), hemodilution, perioperative electrolyte administration, and acute changes in renal function may alter early serum magnesium concentrations and their clinical interpretation. However, the dose-response relationship between early postoperative serum magnesium levels and mortality in this setting remains unclear. We investigated this association and sought to characterize its dose-response pattern.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult cardiac surgery patients admitted to the ICU in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV; version 3.1; 2008-2022) who had an ICU stay of at least 24 hours and a serum magnesium measurement within 24 hours of ICU admission. The exposure was the first recorded serum magnesium concentration, modeled continuously for the principal dose-response analysis and secondarily categorized into quartiles. Baseline covariates were obtained from ICD-coded diagnoses and electronic health record data. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, ascertained from hospital discharge records in MIMIC-IV and unit or hospital discharge status in the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and piecewise regression were performed, with the threshold estimated from the data. The same eligibility criteria were applied in the eICU-CRD, and the replication analysis used a harmonized covariate set.
RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV cohort included 7,783 patients {median age 68 years [interquartile range (IQR), 60-75 years]; 27.9% women; 70.8% underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score 7}, with 130 in-hospital deaths (1.7%). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P=0.003) compatible with an L-shaped pattern, although the formal test for nonlinearity was not significant. Piecewise regression with a threshold of 2.5 mg/dL showed that each 1 mg/dL increase below this threshold was associated with lower odds of mortality [odds ratio (OR) =0.35; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.68; P=0.002], whereas no association was observed above the threshold (OR =0.97; P=0.89). In the fully adjusted model, compared with Q2 (2.1-2.3 mg/dL), Q3 (2.4-2.6 mg/dL) was associated with lower odds of mortality (OR =0.50; 95% CI: 0.26-0.95; P=0.03). Sensitivity analyses were broadly consistent, and exploratory subgroup estimates were directionally similar overall.
