The eICU-CRD cohort included 3,929 patients (median age 68 years; 31.1% women; median SOFA score 8), with 67 deaths (1.71%); the Q3 estimate was directionally consistent but imprecise (OR =0.64; 95% CI: 0.29-1.36).
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative serum magnesium was associated with in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery, with a hypothesis-generating inflection near 2.5 mg/dL and an association concentrated in the lower magnesium range. Because this is an observational analysis, the findings do not establish a treatment target or demonstrate that increasing magnesium to a specific concentration improves outcomes. Prospective studies are needed to validate this pattern and assess its relevance to postoperative risk stratification.

articles.title: Vitamin C status and oxidative profile in lung transplantation: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin C (VitC) is a key circulating antioxidant, yet its perioperative kinetics and relationship with oxidative stress in lung transplantation (LuTx) remain undefined. This study aimed to describe perioperative trajectories of VitC and oxidative status markers in LuTx recipients, and to explore whether pre-transplant VitC status is associated with postoperative oxidative stress or early clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Serum was collected at anesthesia induction for LuTx (pre-LuTx), at intensive care unit (ICU) admission, 72 hours after LuTx (72 h post-LuTx), and LuTx on postoperative day 7 (7 d post-LuTx). VitC, total antioxidant capacity, total hydroperoxides (THs), 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), and the Oxidative Stress Index (OSI) were quantified. Patients were classified based on pre-LuTx VitC levels: HypoC: <28 µmol/L and NormC: ≥28 µmol/L.
RESULTS: Twenty-one recipients were enrolled, with 8 (38%) HypoC. VitC declined over time (P<0.001) in the NormC group, while HypoC had persistently low VitC. THs and 8-OHdG increased from ICU admission to postoperative day 7 (both P<0.001), while total antioxidant capacity remained stable and below reference values. No significant differences in oxidative markers, OSI, or clinical outcomes emerged between HypoC and NormC.
CONCLUSIONS: VitC levels fall markedly after LuTx, particularly in patients with initially adequate concentrations, but this decline does not appear to increase oxidative injury or worsen early postoperative outcomes. Larger studies are needed to identify whether specific subgroups may benefit from targeted VitC supplementation.

articles.title: Fluid-intolerance signals as bedside safety limits during early septic shock resuscitation: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluid resuscitation in early septic shock has a narrow therapeutic index. Signals of fluid intolerance are frequently present during early resuscitation, yet current resuscitation strategies do not incorporate them to guide when to limit fluid administration. We evaluated whether integrating fluid-intolerance signals as safety limits could reduce fluid-induced harm without compromising hypoperfusion resolution.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label randomized trial in three Chilean ICUs, mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock, persistent hypoperfusion, fluid responsiveness, and at least one high-risk criterion for fluid-induced harm were randomized 1:1 to a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy or standard care during a 6-hour protocol window. In the intervention arm, before each bolus, fluid-intolerance signals (lung ultrasound score, VExUS, E/lateral e', and central venous pressure) were graded as traffic-light: green received a 500-mL bolus, yellow 250 mL, and red no further fluid. Standard care delivered 500-mL boluses while hypoperfusion and fluid responsiveness persisted. The primary outcome was the change in PaO2:FiO2 from baseline to 6 h (ΔPaO2:FiO2).
RESULTS: Recruitment was discontinued before the planned sample size was reached because continued enrollment was no longer feasible. Among 113 screened patients, 36 of a planned 62 were randomized, and 35 were analyzed (18 standard care, 17 intervention). The intervention group received a lower protocol bolus volume during the 6-hour intervention window than the standard-care group (250 [125-500] vs. 650 [500-1500] mL; between-group difference, - 500 mL [95% CI, - 750 to - 250]). Cumulative fluid exposure from pre-randomization through the end of the protocol window was similar between groups (3375 [2375-3875] vs. 3750 [1875-4851] mL; between-group difference, - 150 mL [95% CI, - 1470 to 1250]). The primary outcome favored the intervention: median ΔPaO2:FiO2 was 40.5 [24.0-58.5] versus - 37.9 [-69.2 to -12.5]; p < 0.001 (between-group median difference + 78.3 points; 95% CI 50.5 to 110.0), and 0-6-hour changes in lactate and capillary refill time did not differ.
CONCLUSION: Because the trial was stopped early, the effect of a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy on oxygenation remains uncertain. A larger trial would be needed to determine whether this strategy improves oxygenation. Such a trial appears feasible.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT06568744, registered August 21, 2024.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of contrast-enhanced transabdominal ultrasound with gastric filling in preoperative T-staging of advanced gastric cancer: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate preoperative assessment of local invasion remains important in gastric cancer, particularly in distinguishing T3/T4 disease that may alter operative planning and perioperative treatment. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of transabdominal contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) with gastric filling for preoperative T staging in surgically treated advanced gastric cancer.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study included consecutive patients who underwent CEUS with gastric filling (CEUS-GF) within 2 weeks before gastrectomy between January 2023 and December 2025 and had postoperative pathologic T2-T4 disease. Two blinded sonographers independently assigned clinical T (cT) stage; discrepant cases were adjudicated for the final imaging classification. Exact agreement, Cohen's κ, stage-specific performance, binary discrimination, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and subgroup accuracy were assessed against postoperative pathology as the reference standard.
RESULTS: In this cohort of 180 patients, exact agreement between final CEUS stage and pathology was 84.4%, with substantial agreement after grouping T4a and T4b as T4 (κ=0.781); initial inter-reader agreement was κ=0.822. For identifying pathologic T4 disease, sensitivity was 95.8%, specificity was 94.4%, positive predictive value was 92.0%, negative predictive value was 97.1%, and accuracy was 95.0%. Stage-specific accuracy was 90.0% for T2, 87.2% for T3, and 95.0% for grouped T4 disease. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.876 for discrimination of pathologic T stage (pT) 3-or-higher disease from pT2 and 0.966 for discrimination of pT4 from non-T4 disease. Exact T4a/T4b subclassification accuracy was 91.7%. In descriptive subgroup analyses, accuracy was numerically highest for gastric body lesions (91.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this surgically treated single-center T2-T4 cohort, CEUS-GF showed good agreement with pathology and high discrimination for pathologic T4 disease. CEUS-GF may be a useful adjunct for assessing suspected serosal or extragastric extension before surgery; prospective multicenter paired-comparison studies are needed to define its incremental value beyond computed tomography (CT)/endoscopic ultrasound (EUS).

articles.title: Structural imbalances in open-access critical care research: a bibliometric analysis of abstracts from ICU database studies, 2018-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Open access intensive care unit (ICU) databases, including MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD), AmsterdamUMCdb, HiRID-high time resolution ICU data set, and the Salzburg Intensive Care Database (SICdb), have fundamentally transformed critical care research over the past decade. Despite their widespread use, no comprehensive bibliometric analysis has systematically mapped the scientific output generated by studies relying on these resources.
METHODS: A structured search was conducted in PubMed and Web of Science covering 2018 to 2025, retrieving original articles citing at least one of six defined open access ICU databases in title or abstract. Database selection followed the methodology of two prior systematic reviews of publicly available adult ICU datasets. Structured fields covering database used, machine learning (ML) methods, study design, clinical outcomes, AUROC values and patient counts were extracted via a semi-automated AI pipeline (DeepSeek API, multi-label JSON schema). The extraction pipeline was validated against a manually coded reference sample of 110 publications. Bibliometric analyses used R (bibliometrix v4.0.1) and Python. Citation counts, open-access status and SCImago journal quartile were retrieved via OpenAlex and SCImago to characterise the visibility and venue quality of the corpus. Four network analyses were performed: database-to-ML-method co-occurrence, country-to-database, international collaboration, and clinical topic co-occurrence networks.
RESULTS: A total of 4,648 publications were included. Annual publication counts increased 45-fold from 42 (2018) to 1,907 (2025), accelerating markedly after 2021 following the release of MIMIC-IV. MIMIC-IV dominated database attributions (54.6%), followed by MIMIC-III (30.0%) and eICU-CRD (13.5%); European databases (AmsterdamUMCdb, HiRID, SICdb) collectively accounted for only 1.9%. China contributed 65.6% of publications (n = 3,048) and the USA 10.6%. Median citations per paper were 5.0 (1.50 per year). 76.4% of publications were open access and 49.3% appeared in a Q1 SCImago-ranked journal. AUROC showed no meaningful correlation with citation impact (p = 0.10). Logistic regression was the most frequent ML method (38.5%), followed by neural networks (15.6%) and gradient boosting (13.8%). Retrospective observational designs dominated (67.9%), with mortality prediction in sepsis as the primary research focus. Median AUROC among 1,263 publications with extractable values was 0.798.
CONCLUSION: Open access database-based critical care research is growing almost exponentially, driven primarily by Chinese groups using MIMIC-IV for retrospective mortality studies. European databases remain underutilized. The field exhibits methodological homogeneity and a heavy bias toward US-American clinical practice patterns, with cross-dataset external validation rarely foregrounded in study abstracts. Greater use of European databases, systematic external validation and topical diversification are key priorities.

articles.title: Perioperative teriparatide use in osteopenic and osteoporotic patients undergoing multi- and long-segment posterior spinal fusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis and osteopenia are common in spine surgical patients and are associated with adverse outcomes. Perioperative Teriparatide use improves bone quality and decreases the risk of adverse events. We hypothesized that teriparatide use before and after long-segment posterior spinal fusion (PSF) would decrease the rate of adverse surgical events, including pseudoarthrosis, secondary fracture, and revision surgery, in osteoporotic and osteopenic patients compared to patients in a non-osteoporotic, non-teriparatide group.
METHODS: Between 2016 and 2020, 58 adult patients who underwent long-segment PSF were included. The cases (n = 17) were patients with osteoporosis or osteopenia who received a minimum of six weeks of pre- and at least six months of post-operative teriparatide treatment. The control group (n = 41) included patients without osteoporosis who did not require teriparatide treatment. Cases and controls were matched based on surgery type, surgical levels, and follow-up length. The minimum follow-up time was 12 months.
RESULTS: The mean age was 69.0 in the cases vs. 65.4 years in the control group. There were no significant differences based on age, body mass index, gender, race, history of diabetes, history of steroid use, or tobacco usage between the 2 groups. The number of fused vertebral levels and interbody cages placed did not significantly differ either, with 7.8 vs. 6.4 fused levels (p-value = 0.06) and 0.7 interbodies vs. 0.3 interbodies (p-value = 0.15) for the cases and controls, respectively. The case group experienced a higher rate of extension into the pelvis (47.1% vs. 17.1%, p-value = 0.03). The rates of pseudarthrosis (29.4% vs. 17.1%, p-value = 0.31) and reoperation rate (23.5% vs. 17.1%, p-value = 0.72) were not statistically different for the case or control groups, respectively. No postoperative fractures were observed.
CONCLUSION: Teriparatide use resulted in similar postoperative outcomes in the case group compared to the control group in patients undergoing long-segment PSF despite a less favorable baseline in the case group, including the presence of osteoporosis and fusion that required extension into the pelvis. Given the retrospective observational design and absence of an untreated osteopenic/osteoporotic comparison group, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are needed to determine whether teriparatide independently influences outcomes after long-segment spinal fusion.

articles.title: Same-day EHR-coded sevoflurane versus propofol exposure and long-term coded dementia in older surgical adults: a propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Whether perioperative EHR records of sevoflurane and propofol identify clinically meaningful differences in long-term dementia risk is uncertain. We compared same-day EHR-coded sevoflurane versus propofol exposure in relation to subsequent coded dementia among older adults undergoing major inpatient surgery.
METHODS: We conducted a multinational propensity-score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX federated EHR network. Adults aged 60 years or older undergoing major inpatient surgery from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2024, were classified by a same-calendar-day record of the index procedure and sevoflurane or propofol. The aggregate export did not consistently provide route, bolus-versus-infusion status, dose, duration, or anesthesia timestamps; therefore, exposure groups were interpreted as EHR-coded patterns rather than validated exclusive maintenance regimens. The primary outcome was incident coded dementia from index + 1 day. Death was treated as censoring for the cause-specific Cox estimand. Sensitivity analyses included 90- and 180-day landmarks, a higher-specificity dementia definition, stricter exposure coding, and a 5-year dementia-or-death composite.
RESULTS: After matching, 35,363 patients were included in each group. Matching retained 99.94% of the sevoflurane-coded cohort but 2.49% of the much larger propofol-coded cohort. Coded dementia occurred in 701 patients (1.98%) in the sevoflurane-coded group and 384 (1.09%) in the propofol-coded group (hazard ratio [HR], 1.84; 95% CI, 1.62-2.08; P < 0.001). The 5-year dementia-or-death composite occurred in 3,024 patients (8.55%) and 2,195 patients (6.21%), respectively (HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.33-1.52). Most measured covariates were balanced after matching, although residual imbalance remained for diastolic blood pressure and C-reactive protein.
CONCLUSIONS: In a selected matched common-support EHR population, same-day sevoflurane-coded exposure was associated with a higher subsequent incidence of coded dementia than same-day propofol-coded exposure. Exposure misclassification, restricted overlap, residual confounding, surveillance differences, and competing mortality preclude causal inference or prescribing recommendations.

articles.title: Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: A Continuum from Pathophysiological Mechanisms to Prevention, Management, and Long-Term Care : Short title: Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) remains a frequent and clinically important complication after coronary artery bypass grafting, valve surgery, and complex aortic procedures. Its development reflects the interaction of pre-existing renal vulnerability with perioperative insults, including renal hypoperfusion, ischemia-reperfusion injury, systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, hemolysis, cardiopulmonary bypass-related injury, and nephrotoxic exposure. Conventional diagnostic markers, particularly serum creatinine and urine output, often identify AKI only after functional decline has occurred, limiting opportunities for early intervention. Novel biomarkers such as NGAL, KIM-1, cystatin C, and TIMP-2/IGFBP7 may improve early risk stratification, although their routine clinical implementation remains limited by cost, availability, and uncertainty regarding biomarker-guided treatment pathways. Current prevention and management strategies therefore rely primarily on early risk assessment, hemodynamic optimization, avoidance of nephrotoxins, careful fluid management, and timely renal support. Importantly, CSA-AKI is increasingly recognized as a continuum extending beyond hospitalization, with increased risks of chronic kidney disease, cardiovascular events, and long-term mortality. This review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms, diagnosis, prevention, management, and follow-up of CSA-AKI, while highlighting areas where stronger clinical evidence is still needed.

articles.title: A Shock to the System: Vasopressors for Sepsis in Africa and Beyond.
Noninvasive Sweat Patch Collection of Neuroinjury Biomarkers in Critically Ill Children: A Feasibility Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Critically ill children experience neurologic injury that is associated with specific biomarkers. Monitoring of these biomarkers in this population is limited by invasive sampling methods and single timepoint measurements. We sought to evaluate the feasibility of using a novel noninvasive sweat patch to collect cumulative concentrations of neuroinjury-associated biomarkers over time in the PICU.
DESIGN: Single-center prospective pilot feasibility study conducted across three sequential enrollment cohorts.
SETTING: A tertiary-care PICU.
PATIENTS: Forty-two children admitted to the PICU 5 weeks to 17 years old.
INTERVENTIONS: Sweat patches were placed and worn for 24-96 hours. Sweat samples were analyzed for four neuroinjury-associated biomarkers: glial fibrillary acidic protein, ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1, tau, and neurofilament light chain using single-molecule array assays.
MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: Biomarkers were reported as total cumulative concentrations and concentrations per hour of patch wear. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, safety, protocol adherence, and assay success. All approached families consented, and no patch-related adverse effects were observed. One patch was removed early due to uncertainty regarding MRI compatibility. Adequate sweat volumes required for assay were obtained from all 41 analyzed patches, and biomarker levels were measured successfully in each, with 97% of samples maintaining coefficient of variation (CV) within an acceptable range (< 20%) and 100% of samples within a borderline CV range (< 25%).
CONCLUSIONS: Sweat patch collection of neurologic injury biomarkers was feasible, safe, and acceptable to families in a PICU setting. This minimally invasive method yielded consistently adequate and analyzable volumes in infants through adolescents and may support future studies designed to evaluate the relationship between elements of critical care and neurologic injury in children admitted to the PICU.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted versus open pancreatoduodenectomy for non-pancreatic periampullary carcinoma: comparison of long-term survival using causal mediation analysis.
articles.abstract: The clinical merits of robotic-assisted pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) relative to open pancreatoduodenectomy (OPD) remain poorly defined among patients with non-pancreatic periampullary cancer (NPPC). This retrospective single-center cohort enrolled 293 NPPC patients (104 RPD, 189 OPD) treated between January 2017 and December 2025 at our institution. Baseline inter‑group imbalances were mitigated via inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Cox regression analyses, both univariate and multivariate, along with causal mediation analyses, were performed to evaluate perioperative metrics and long-term survival. After weighting, RPD was associated with prolonged operative duration (440.0 [390.0, 510.0] min vs. 330.0 [280.0, 385.0] min, p < 0.001) but yielded less intraoperative blood loss (50.0 [45.7, 98.0] ml vs. 200.0 [150.0, 400.0] ml, p < 0.001) and lower intraoperative transfusion rate (0% vs. 5.0%, p = 0.023), alongside marginally lower major complication rates (26.0% vs. 36.5%, p = 0.097), a lower 90-day mortality (0.0% vs. 3.5%, p = 0.030) and a greater percentage of patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy within 3 months postoperatively (55.4% vs. 28.1%, p < 0.001). Multivariate Cox analysis identified RPD as a protective factor for overall survival (HR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.36-0.89, p = 0.014). Mediation analysis further revealed that part of RPD's survival advantage was indirectly driven by increased uptake of early adjuvant chemotherapy. In conclusion, RPD offers equivalent perioperative safety to OPD while minimizing surgical trauma, facilitating timely systemic therapy and conferring partial survival benefits mediated by early postoperative chemotherapy for NPPC patients.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics of fibrinogen in postpartum haemorrhage during Caesarean section: a secondary analysis of the TRACES trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), hypofibrinogenaemia is strongly associated with bleeding severity. To correct fibrinogen depletion, various fixed dosing regimens have been evaluated, but the optimal fibrinogen dosing regimen remains unknown. To date, fibrinogen pharmacokinetics have only been studied outside haemorrhagic settings (healthy or afibrinogenaemic patients) METHODS: This ancillary analysis of the TRACES trial assessed fibrinogen kinetics in 142 women with PPH > 800 ml during caesarean section, among which 31 received fibrinogen replacement. Plasma fibrinogen concentrations (n = 593) were measured using the Clauss method. A population pharmacokinetic model was developed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling. Simulations were performed to estimate loading and maintenance doses required to achieve target fibrinogen concentrations.
RESULTS: A one-compartment logistic model adequately described plasma fibrinogen levels. Bleeding rate was identified as a key covariate to explain fibrinogen loss rate. Based on the estimated model, an optimised dosing regimen was derived to achieve and maintain predefined target fibrinogen levels. To achieve a target increase of 1 g.L-¹ in plasma fibrinogen level, the required fibrinogen loading dose is at least 2.7 g for a body weight of 50 kg. To maintain plasma fibrinogen level at a target of 2 g.L-¹ during a 1000 mL.h-¹ bleeding rate, a fibrinogen infusion rate of 0.9 g.h-¹ would be required.
CONCLUSIONS: This work supports that an individualized target-controlled fibrinogen dosing strategy is probably required to effectively correct fibrinogen levels. Integrating such models as a clinical decision support tool into a multimodal strategy that also utilizes viscoelastic testing could optimize PPH management.

articles.title: Postoperative pain management: a national prospective study including 3879 patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pain management remains a critical issue in peri-operative medicine, but contemporary national data are lacking.
METHODS: AlgoSFAR 2 was a prospective, multicentre and observational study, conducted in randomly selected French surgical centres. Adult patients undergoing elective surgery were included. Pain was assessed at rest and during mobilization over the first three postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included postoperative opioid consumption and multimodal analgesia strategies defined as the use of at least two non-opioid strategies such as analgesics and/or regional anaesthesia.
RESULTS: A total of 3879 patients from 80 centres were analysed. While pre-operative and immediate postoperative pain levels at rest were low, pain peaked on day 1, with high interindividual variability, and 6% of patients reported severe pain. Two thirds (66%) did not need any rescue opioids postoperatively. Overall, 95% received multimodal analgesia.
CONCLUSION: These results highlight a major change in postoperative pain management in France, with broad adoption of multimodal opioid-sparing strategies. Nonetheless, a minority of patients still experience severe pain, highlighting the need for personalized management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06487442.

articles.title: Individualized mean arterial pressure during cardiac surgery The OPTIPAM Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether targeting an individualized mean arterial pressure (MAP) during cardiac surgery improves outcomes remains uncertain. The balance between improved perfusion and vasopressor-driven blood pressure augmentation is unclear.
METHODS: In this single-blind, multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in 10 tertiary centers in France, adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned to either individualized MAP management (target within ±10% of preoperative baseline during surgery and for 24 h postoperatively) or standard management (target MAP ≥65 mm Hg). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute kidney injury, or prespecified neurologic complications within 7 days. Safety outcomes included hemorrhagic complications and transfusion requirements.
RESULTS: A total of 172 patients were enrolled before the trial was stopped early by the data and safety monitoring board because of increased bleeding in the individualized group. Mean intraoperative MAP was higher with individualized management (80.6 vs 75.6 mm Hg; P<0.001), despite limited target adherence (33% of intraoperative time) and greater vasopressor use. The primary outcome occurred in 27 of 85 patients (32%) in the individualized group and 25 of 87 (29%) in the standard group (relative risk, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.7 to 1.8; P=0.76). Hemorrhagic complications occurred more frequently in the individualized group (18% vs 3%; P=0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, it was not possible to determine whether an individualized MAP strategy reduced major postoperative complications. More bleeding complications were observed in the individualized group. Future studies should further investigate this safety signal when evaluating individualized blood pressure targets.

articles.title: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome: what the intensivist needs to know.
articles.abstract: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) is a significant complication of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, a revolutionary treatment for hematologic malignancies. This syndrome, which might affect approximately 30% of CAR-T therapy recipients, presents a wide spectrum of neurological symptoms, ranging from mild confusion to life-threatening cerebral edema. In the intensive care unit (ICU), managing ICANS is critical due to its potential severity. Pathophysiology of ICANS is driven by immune-mediated inflammation disrupting the blood-brain barrier, resulting in cerebral cytokine infiltration and glial cell activation. Its severity is associated with elevated cytokine levels in cerebrospinal fluid and serum, which points to the need for specific biomarkers and predictive tools. Standardized assessments, including the Immune Effector Cell-Associated Encephalopathy (ICE) Score, together with brain imaging and adjunctive diagnostic tests, provide clinicians with essential baseline information for the assessment and monitoring of neurological complications. ICU management focuses on supportive care and pharmacologic strategies. Corticosteroids represent the cornerstone of treatment, effectively targeting neuroinflammation while preserving the antitumor efficacy of CAR-T cell therapy. Anticonvulsants, hyperosmolar agents and advanced neurocritical care measures are also pivotal. Recent advances suggest potential benefits of alternative therapies, such as anti-cytokine agents and innovative immune cell products with reduced neurotoxic risks. Despite advancements, challenges persist, including diagnostic ambiguities, resource allocation, and variability in care protocols. This review highlighted challenges in ICANS management for ICU physicians, intending to underline the importance of early detection, rigorous monitoring, and tailored interventions to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Histology of the parietal peritoneum: a scoping review of microanatomy and potential relevance to preperitoneal analgesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The abdominal preperitoneal plane beneath the posterior rectus sheath has been recently described as a potential target for regional analgesia. Techniques such as ultrasound-guided preperitoneal or deep rectus sheath blocks aim to deposit local anesthetic adjacent to the abdominal parietal peritoneum, a structure traditionally regarded as a serosal membrane. Some anatomical and clinical evidence suggests that the parietal peritoneum may represent a more complex neurovascular interface relevant to pain transmission.
METHODS: A systematic scoping review of the literature was conducted to synthesize available histological evidence on the abdominal parietal peritoneum. Studies investigating its microanatomy, vascularization, and innervation were included. Given the heterogeneity of study designs and outcomes, a descriptive mapping approach was adopted without quantitative synthesis.
RESULTS: The included studies show that the parietal peritoneum is composed of a mesothelial layer supported by a submesothelial connective tissue matrix. The matrix contains collagen fibers, microvasculature, immune cells, and both myelinated and unmyelinated nerve fibers. Neuroanatomical findings indicate sensory afferents originating from the thoracolumbar nerves, as well as mechanoreceptive and nociceptive fibers within the submesothelial layer.
CONCLUSIONS: While conclusive evidence of visceral afferent innervation is still scarce, these experimental observations imply a more complex sensory organization. Overall, these results may support the notion of the parietal peritoneum as a biologically active fascial interface. This perspective may provide a conceptual framework for considering the preperitoneal plane as a potential target in abdominal pain. Further translational and human-based studies are needed to clarify its role in regional analgesia.

articles.title: Nutritional support in immunosuppressed critically ill patients.
articles.abstract: Immunosuppressed patients now make up a growing share of intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, largely as a result of advances in cancer treatment, organ transplantation, and immunomodulatory therapies. While their short-term ICU mortality may be similar to that of immunocompetent patients when illness severity is taken into account, these individuals often face longer ICU stays, more complications, and poorer long-term outcomes. In this context, artificial nutrition plays a central role in ICU management and represents a potentially modifiable intervention. Beyond meeting energy requirements, nutritional support may help sustain immune function, preserve gut integrity, and reduce the risk of infectious complications. Whenever possible, enteral nutrition should be favored, as it supports the intestinal barrier and gut-associated lymphoid tissue, even when delivered at low, trophic doses. Parenteral nutrition remains indispensable in the presence of intestinal failure but should be used cautiously, given its association with complications such as catheter-related bloodstream infections. Critical illness profoundly alters gut-immune interactions, promoting dysbiosis, increased intestinal permeability, and immune dysfunction - processes that may be further amplified by immunosuppressive therapies. This has fueled interest in immunonutrition strategies, including arginine, ω-3 fatty acids, glutamine, and nucleotides. However, evidence in immunosuppressed critically ill patients remains limited and inconsistent, preventing firm recommendations. Looking ahead, the integration of body composition assessment, immune-metabolic phenotyping, multi-omics technologies, and artificial intelligence may enable more personalized nutritional strategies. Future studies should focus on phenotype-specific randomized trials to better define the optimal route, composition, timing, and dosing of nutritional support in this complex population.

articles.title: Sedation success and safety of combination regimens in paediatric MRI: A network meta-analysis of randomised trials.
Critical adverse events during emergency department ketamine-propofol sedation in children.: A secondary analysis of a multicentre study.
Primary repair during the neonatal period for tetralogy of Fallot (RIFAN): a multicentre randomised controlled trial protocol in China.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: For clinically stable infants with tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), complete repair at 3–6 months is commonly recommended but the comparative effects of elective neonatal repair remain uncertain. Observational comparisons are vulnerable to confounding because infants repaired early often have more severe disease. The RIFAN trial will compare planned neonatal and infant repair in a randomised design.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective, multicentre, open-label trial will enrol 160 term neonates aged ≤28 days with isolated TOF at five paediatric cardiac centres in China. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to complete repair at ≤28 days or at 3–6 months. The co-primary outcomes are all-cause death within 30 days after surgery, regardless of discharge status and therapeutic cardiac reintervention within 12 months after surgery, excluding procedures during the index hospitalisation. The respective non-inferiority margins are 7.5 and 10 percentage points. Secondary outcomes include perioperative morbidity, cardiac function, growth, neurodevelopment, healthcare use and longer-term survival. The planned sample of 80 participants per group was calculated to provide 80% power for each co-primary outcome separately under the stated assumptions. A supportive 12-month analysis beginning at randomisation will report death and unplanned therapeutic cardiac intervention. Analyses will follow randomised allocation, with a per-protocol sensitivity analysis.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The protocol was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University, on 1 March 2025 (reference number: Ethical Review 2025(5)). Each participating centre obtained approval from its hospital ethics committee before enrolling its first participant. The findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and presentations at scientific conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06822400 (first submitted 2 January 2025; first posted 12 February 2025).

articles.title: Preoperative SASP burden predicts perioperative vulnerability in older patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Cellular senescence and its associated secretory phenotype (SASP) represent a fundamental mechanism of biological aging. SASP-related inflammation has been implicated in cardiovascular disease. However, its role in perioperative risk in cardiac surgery remains largely unexplored, and established risk scores such as EuroSCORE II and the STS Score do not regard biological aging or senescence. In this prospective single-center cohort study, 131 patients aged ≥ 65 years undergoing elective cardiac surgery were enrolled. A panel of 19 preoperative SASP biomarkers was quantified by a multiplex immunoassay. Of those, 17 markers were evaluated as predictors of a composite adverse outcome, an adapted multimorbidity score with 21.4% event rate, with MACCE (36.6%) as a secondary endpoint. Logistic regression, false discovery rate correction, bootstrap validation, and incremental value analyses (DeLong test, IDI, NRI) were used. Five markers showed nominal univariable significance (IGFBP-1, GDF-15, TNF-RI, TNF-α, and IGFBP-4), though none survived FDR correction. Adjusted for procedure type, IGFBP-1 (OR = 1.675, 95% CI = 1.175-2.389, p = 0.004) and IGFBP-4 (OR = 1.432, 95% CI = 1.044-1.966, p = 0.026) emerged as independent predictors of the composite adverse outcome (Model M3, AUCcorrected = 0.746), numerically comparable to EuroSCORE II (AUC = 0.727). Model M3 improved net reclassification over EuroSCORE II (NRI + 0.528, p = 0.008) and the STS Score (NRI + 0.418, p = 0.040), with consistent estimates under Firth-penalized sensitivity analysis. Preoperative SASP biomarkers, particularly IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-4, independently predict adverse outcomes, namely multimorbidity, after elective cardiac surgery. They improve individual risk stratification beyond standard clinical scores in older patients, suggesting a measurable dimension of perioperative vulnerability that warrants external validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Nuclear receptor NR4A2 is upregulated with cardiac surgery and triggers spontaneous arrhythmias in mice.
articles.abstract: Postoperative arrhythmias (POAs) are a common complication of cardiac surgery and a major cause for in-hospital morbidity and mortality. Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2 (NR4A2) is an immediate-early response gene induced by inflammation and catecholamines, two well-known contributors of POAs. Here we aimed to elucidate the impact that open-heart surgery exerts on cardiac NR4A2 expression, and to determine the consequences for cardiomyocyte physiology and heart rhythm. First, using a novel NR4A2 monoclonal antibody, the comparison of left ventricular tissue samples from donor individuals and cardiac surgery patients confirmed that NR4A2 is induced in the heart during the perioperative period. Next, male and female mice with inducible, cardiomyocyte-specific overexpression of NR4A2 were found to develop arrhythmias within a timeframe consistent with the incidence of POAs. Three days after NR4A2 induction, ventricular myocytes exhibited a transcriptional down-regulation of several proteins critical for dyads formation. This was linked to the deregulation of a large network of non-coding RNAs governing cardiac development, including the down-regulation of the muscle-specific microRNAs (miRNAs) miR-133a and miR-499, and the up-regulation of a supercluster of 36 miRNAs encoded by a paternally imprinted polycistronic transcript located within the Dlk1-Dio3 locus. Short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated knockdown of the polycistronic transcript initiated prior to NR4A2 induction was sufficient to partially restore the expression of critical dyad components and attenuate the occurrence of arrhythmias. In conclusion, our findings expose NR4A2 as a novel proarrhythmogenic substrate and a potential new target for the treatment of POAs in cardiac surgery patients.
articles.journal: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

articles.title: Effects of opioid-free and opioid-sparing anesthesia on postoperative delirium: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common neurocognitive condition linked with increased morbidity, long-term cognitive decline, and death. Perioperative opioid exposure may contribute to delirium through sedation, neuroinflammation, and neurotransmitter dysregulation. Opioid-free anesthesia and opioid-sparing anesthesia using agents such as ketamine, esketamine, and dexmedetomidine have emerged as a potential strategy to reduce POD. This meta-analysis evaluated the effects of opioid-free and opioid-sparing anesthetic regimens on POD in adult surgical patients.
METHODS: Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing ketamine-, esketamine-, or dexmedetomidine-based opioid-free and opioid-sparing strategies with placebo, conventional opioid-based anesthesia, or standard care were included. The primary outcome was POD. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Forty-one randomized controlled trials involving 7852 patients were analyzed. POD occurred in 488 of 4013 patients receiving opioid-free/opioid-sparing interventions and 633 of 3839 controls. Overall, these strategies significantly reduced the risk of delirium (RR = 0.641, 95% CI: 0.525-0.784; I2 = 52.2%). Subgroup analyses showed reductions with esketamine (RR = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.526-1.053) and dexmedetomidine (RR = 0.612, 95% CI: 0.471-0.796), while ketamine demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward benefit (RR = 0.598, 95% CI: 0.251-1.423). No significant publication bias was detected.
CONCLUSIONS: Opioid-free and opioid-sparing anesthetic strategies reduce POD in adult surgical patients, with dexmedetomidine and esketamine showing the most consistent benefits. These findings support multimodal opioid-sparing anesthesia for perioperative neurocognitive protection.

articles.title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor use in third trimester of pregnancy and birth outcomes after vaginal birth - a Swedish retrospective register study 2005-2015.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are prescribed for depression during pregnancy, yet the impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes remains insufficiently studied. The study aimed to describe the prevalence of prescribed SSRIs to pregnant women and its association with birth outcomes after a vaginal birth.
METHODS: A registry study included 405,936 term vaginal births in Sweden. SSRI prescriptions were identified. Crude and adjusted odds ratios with 99% confidence intervals were calculated, with statistical significance set at p < 0.001.
RESULTS: SSRIs were prescribed to 6.374 women (1.6%), with prevalence rising from 0.3% to 2.6% between 2005 and 2015. SSRI was associated with significantly higher rates of labor induction, epidural anesthesia and PPH > 1000 mL. postpartum. Women prescribed SSRIs were more likely to give birth at 37-38 weeks' gestation and have neonates with head circumference < 35 cm and with Apgar score < 7 at 5 min.
CONCLUSIONS: SSRI prescriptions increased significantly between 2005 and 2015 and were associated with higher risks of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Until more conclusive evidence is availble midwives and obstetricians should remain vigilant when supporting pregnant women with depression or anxiety, considering the potential risks of pharmacological treatment alongside non-pharmacological management of maternal mental health conditions.

articles.title: Familial Exudative Vitreoretinopathy Phenotype in a Full-term Infant with Cri-du-Chat Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe a familial exudative vitreoretinopathy (FEVR) phenotype with progressive neovascularization in a full-term infant with genetically confirmed cri-du-chat (CdC) syndrome.
METHODS: Retrospective case report with serial examinations under anesthesia (EUA), fundus photography, and fluorescein angiography (FA).
RESULTS: A 1-year-old female with CdC due to a maternally inherited unbalanced translocation (terminal 5p deletion, terminal 10q duplication) presented with bilateral microphthalmos and a phenotype resembling FEVR. The right eye demonstrated a falciform retinal fold with extensive peripheral nonperfusion. The left eye had temporal dragging, preretinal hemorrhage, and less extensive nonperfusion. After laser photocoagulation to the left eye, the hemorrhage resolved but progressive neovascularization required additional laser treatment. The right eye remained stable.
CONCLUSION: CdC syndrome may be associated with a FEVR-like phenotype including asymmetric peripheral nonperfusion and progressive neovascularization. Genes along the 5p locus may contribute to impaired retinal vascular development. Retinal screening with FA may be considered in CdC patients.

articles.title: Utility of Ophthalmic Exam Under Anaesthesia in Adult Patients With Intellectual Disability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While ophthalmic exam under anaesthesia (EUA) is well-described in the paediatric patient population, it is rarely performed on adult patients. Ophthalmic EUA is often necessary for accurate diagnosis and management in adults with intellectual disability due to inability to tolerate an outpatient eye exam. This paper is a retrospective chart review aiming to explore the diagnostic and therapeutic benefits of ophthalmic EUA in patients with intellectual disability.
METHODS: This study is a retrospective chart review of all adult patients with intellectual disability who underwent an ophthalmic EUA at our rural academic centre from 1 April 2015 to 1 April 2025. Thirty-eight exams on 15 different patients met the inclusion criteria.
RESULTS: 21.1% of exams resulted in a new diagnosis, and 44.7% of exams resulted in a change in eye care management, including procedural intervention during the EUA, subsequent surgical procedures or alterations of the eyedrop regimen. None of our patients experienced postoperative complications following EUA. However, two patients had complicated postoperative courses following subsequent cataract or retina surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: In both our series and the previously published literature, EUA proved instrumental in the proper ophthalmic management of patients who are unable to tolerate an outpatient eye exam. However, the risks and benefits of the procedure should be carefully discussed with patients and their caregivers/medical decision makers before proceeding with anaesthesia, as this patient population is at higher risk of anaesthesia complications than their age-matched peers.

articles.title: Comparing Subglottic Ultrasound and Distal Phalanx Width for Pediatric Endotracheal Tube Sizing in a Predominantly School-Aged Pediatric Cohort: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate endotracheal tube (ETT) sizing is essential in pediatric airway management to optimize ventilation and reduce complications. Traditional methods, including age-based formulas and distal phalanx width (DPW), may lack precision. Subglottic ultrasound (US) has emerged as a promising tool, but its predictive accuracy compared with DPW remains unclear. This study aimed to compare accuracy, agreement, diagnostic performance, and clinical applicability of subglottic US versus DPW for predicting optimal ETT size in children, while recognizing that the enrolled cohort was predominantly school-aged.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, pediatric patients aged 0-12 years undergoing elective or emergency intubation were assessed. Pre-intubation measurements included subglottic transverse airway diameter by ultrasound (ACUSON Juniper, microconvex probe, 5-10 MHz) and DPW by digital calipers. Predicted ETT sizes were compared with the final clinically accepted cuffed ETT inner diameter confirmed by leak testing and cuff pressure optimization. Agreement was evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients, while diagnostic performance was defined a priori as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), likelihood ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Logistic regression identified predictors of good ETT fit.
RESULTS: Among 160 patients, the median age was 8.8 years (IQR 7.0-10.5), indicating predominance of older children. Ultrasound-predicted ETT size showed a stronger correlation with actual size (r = 0.479, p < 0.001) than DPW (r = 0.248, p = 0.002). Ultrasound predictions had narrower Bland-Altman limits of agreement, although ultrasound measurement is operator-dependent. DPW showed poor sensitivity (5.9%) but high specificity (99.3%) for identifying underfit ETTs, with limited overall discrimination (ROC AUC = 0.53). Only subglottic diameter was a significant predictor of good ETT fit.
CONCLUSION: Subglottic ultrasound showed better agreement with clinically accepted ETT size than DPW in this predominantly school-aged pediatric cohort. These findings support the potential role of ultrasound as an adjunct to pediatric airway assessment, but conclusions should be interpreted cautiously in infants and younger children because they were under-represented. Standardized measurement protocols and operator training are needed before broad implementation.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted microdissection testicular sperm extraction improves sperm retrieval efficiency and clinical outcomes in men with non-obstructive azoospermia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study compared the efficacy, safety, and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) outcomes of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted versus conventional microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). To this end, we retrospectively analyzed 1286 consecutive NOA patients undergoing micro-TESE at the two reproductive medicine center of Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital (Chengdu, China) and Sichuan Jinxin Xinan Women's and Children's Hospital (Chengdu, China) from January 2020 to December 2024, including 542 patients receiving AI-assisted procedures and 744 undergoing conventional surgery. The primary outcome was sperm retrieval rate (SRR), while secondary outcomes covered intraoperative parameters, postoperative complications, and ICSI outcomes, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors of SRR and live birth. The results showed that the overall SRR reached 56.2% in the entire cohort, and the AI group had a significantly higher SRR (68.1% vs 47.6%, P < 0.001), with the most prominent improvement observed in patients with Sertoli cell-only syndrome (47.2% vs 22.7%, P < 0.001). The AI group also exhibited shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, fewer biopsy sites, shorter postoperative hospital stay, and lower complication rates (all P < 0.001), as well as superior ICSI outcomes including higher fertilization, high-quality embryo, blastocyst, clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, and live birth rates (all P < 0.01). Further multivariable analysis confirmed that AI-assisted surgery serves as an independent predictor of both successful SRR (odds ratio [OR] = 3.182, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.374-4.265, P < 0.001) and live birth rate (OR = 1.876, 95% CI: 1.325-2.656, P < 0.001). Taken together, AI-assisted micro-TESE improves sperm retrieval efficiency, reduces perioperative morbidity, and enhances ICSI and live birth outcomes in NOA patients as an independent predictor for both SRR and live birth rate, and prospective multicenter randomized trials are warranted for further validation.

articles.title: High Prevalence of Preoperative Malnutrition and Associated Factors in Pediatric Liver Transplant Candidates: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: IntroductionMalnutrition is common among children awaiting liver transplantation and may compromise perioperative outcomes. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of preoperative malnutrition and identify associated factors among pediatric liver transplant candidates.MethodsA cross-sectional study with prospective data collection was conducted among 300 children admitted to the liver transplantation center of a tertiary hospital, from January 2023 to June 2025. Demographic and clinical data were collected. Nutritional status before transplantation was assessed using the standard deviation score method based on Chinese growth standards for children younger than 7 years. Univariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with malnutrition.ResultsThe prevalence of preoperative malnutrition was 63.3%. Moderate and severe malnutrition each accounted for 31.7% of the cohort. Multivariable logistic regression showed that history of Kasai portoenterostomy, history of allergy, lower birth weight, and caregiver unemployment were independently associated with preoperative malnutrition. Children with a history of allergy had the highest odds of malnutrition, with an odds ratio of 13.015 and a 95% confidence interval of 5.364 to 31.580.ConclusionsPreoperative malnutrition was highly prevalent among pediatric liver transplant candidates. Children with a history of Kasai portoenterostomy, allergy, lower birth weight, or an unemployed primary caregiver may require prioritized nutritional screening, risk stratification, and early targeted intervention before transplantation.

articles.title: Postpartum repair of umbilical hernias following conservative management during pregnancy: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of elective umbilical hernia repair following conservative management during pregnancy remains controversial. Physiological postpartum changes, including persistent abdominal wall laxity and elevated intra-abdominal pressure, may influence surgical outcomes and recurrence risk. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes and impact of surgical timing on postpartum umbilical hernia repair.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center between January 2010 and December 2018. Pregnant women diagnosed with umbilical hernia were initially managed conservatively unless emergent intervention was required. Patients subsequently underwent elective open mesh repair during the postpartum period. Primary outcome was hernia recurrence. Secondary outcomes included operative time, length of hospital stay (LOS), postoperative pain assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and perioperative complications. Statistical analysis was performed using ANOVA, Chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: A total of 114 women underwent elective postpartum umbilical hernia repair following conservative management during pregnancy. Mean age was [Formula: see text] years, and mean BMI was 38.8 kg/m², with most patients classified as obese and multiparous. Overall recurrence rate was 3.5% (n = 4). All recurrences occurred either in patients undergoing early repair (< 6 months postpartum) or in those who became pregnant within one year after surgery. Delayed repair was associated with significantly improved perioperative outcomes. Mean operative time decreased from 145 min in the early repair group to 91 min in patients repaired after 24 months postpartum (p < 0.001). Mean LOS decreased from 49 to 30 h (p < 0.001). Patients undergoing delayed repair also demonstrated significantly lower postoperative pain scores (VAS 3.2 vs. 6.8, p < 0.001) and reduced postoperative complication rates. No recurrences were observed in women who delayed subsequent pregnancy for more than two years after repair.
CONCLUSION: Elective postpartum umbilical hernia repair following conservative management during pregnancy is safe and associated with favorable perioperative outcomes. Delayed repair was associated with reduced operative complexity, postoperative pain, and complications. Although recurrence events were observed predominantly after early repair or subsequent early pregnancy, larger prospective studies are required to clarify the relationship between repair timing and recurrence risk.

articles.title: Evolving role of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis for interventional pain management.
articles.abstract: Despite advances in pain management, pain remains a major global health challenge in both oncological and non-oncological patients. Long-term pharmacological treatment is often restricted by insufficient therapeutic benefit and adverse events, highlighting the need for alternative approaches such as image-guided pain therapies. The idea of treating pain with cold has been recognized for centuries, and today cryotherapy has emerged as a valuable minimally invasive option for pain management. Cryoablation refers to the destruction of tissue with extreme cold and has an increasing role, especially in the treatment of benign (e.g., osteoid osteoma), malignant bone (i.e., metastases), and soft tissue tumors, either with a curative or palliative intent. Cryoneurolysis is a related but distinct application, focusing either on peripheral nerve modulation or nerve destruction. Cryoneurolysis may be highly effective for the treatment of acute or chronic pain, including sympathetic neurolysis in cancer and non-cancer-related pain syndromes. The general approach in patients with tumor-related pain depends on whether the lesion itself can be ablated or not. In non-oncologic patients, cryoneurolysis of the responsible nerve is typically performed following a positive response to a diagnostic nerve block. Potential indications for cryotherapy are constantly evolving; however, evidence, especially for cryoneurolysis, is still limited and based mostly on single-center case series and retrospective studies. Standardized ablation protocols are lacking, and for the duration of cycles, most experts rely on imaging visualization and validated protocols. Equally important, successful integration of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis into daily practice requires structured workflows across different patient pathways and interdisciplinary management. KEY POINTS: Question Pain management remains a major global health challenge and an unmet need in oncological and non-oncological patients. Findings Cryotherapy, in terms of cryoablation and cryoneurolysis, is increasingly incorporated in multimodal curative and palliative pain care concepts, for treatment of acute and chronic pain syndromes. Clinical relevance Advancement and validation of standardized treatment protocols are needed to strengthen evidence and further enhance clinical implementation in interventional radiology practice and interdisciplinary patient care.

articles.title: Social determinants of health and outcomes after spinal cord stimulation: a retrospective cohort study.
Pericapsular Nerve Group Block Significantly Reduces Morphine Consumption and Improves Early Recovery Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Double-Blind Sham-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block has emerged as a promising regional analgesic technique for hip surgery. However, evidence regarding its opioid-sparing efficacy following primary total hip arthroplasty remains limited. This study evaluated the effect of ultrasound-guided PENG block on postoperative opioid consumption, pain scores, and recovery outcomes following primary total hip arthroplasty.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 40 patients undergoing elective primary total hip arthroplasty under general anesthesia were randomized to receive either ultrasound-guided PENG block with one mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 30 mL (n = 20) or a sham procedure with 30 mL saline (n = 20). The primary outcome was cumulative morphine consumption during the first 24 postoperative hours. The secondary outcomes included visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, time to first rescue analgesia, patient satisfaction, and opioid-related adverse events. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups.
RESULTS: Cumulative morphine consumption was significantly lower in the PENG group throughout the postoperative period and at 24 hours (6.2 ± 3.3 versus 30.2 ± 5.6 mg, P < 0.001), representing an approximately 79% reduction in opioid requirement. The visual analog scale pain scores were significantly lower at all postoperative assessment points (all P < 0.001). Time to first rescue analgesic requirement was significantly prolonged in the PENG group (16.0 ± 0.0 versus 1.4 ± 0.5 hours, P < 0.001). Patient satisfaction was significantly greater in the PENG group (P < 0.001), while postoperative nausea occurred less frequently (zero versus 25%, P = 0.017). There were no block-related complications observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided PENG block provided effective opioid-sparing analgesia following primary total hip arthroplasty, significantly reducing postoperative morphine consumption and pain scores while improving patient satisfaction and reducing postoperative nausea. These findings support the incorporation of PENG block into multimodal analgesic protocols for total hip arthroplasty.

articles.title: Comparison of Spinal Anesthesia Against General Anesthesia for Surgical Management of Hip Fracture Patients: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hip fracture surgery in older adults is associated with substantial perioperative morbidity and functional decline. Whether spinal anesthesia offers advantages over general anesthesia for key perioperative complications and recovery outcomes remains uncertain. Hence, we conducted this review comparing spinal anesthesia versus general anesthesia for surgical management of hip fracture.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
METHODS: Databases [MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science, and clinical trial registries] were searched till January 2026. Primary outcomes were major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular complications, delirium, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), hypotension, pain score, and functional recovery. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) were performed using risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.
FINDINGS: Nineteen trials were included. Spinal anesthesia showed no significant difference versus general anesthesia for major cardiovascular/cerebrovascular complications (RR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.69 to 1.20), delirium (RR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.81 to 1.21), PONV (RR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.60 to 1.58), and hypotension (RR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.58 to 1.50), with substantial heterogeneity for hypotension. Spinal anesthesia was associated with improved functional recovery (SMD = -0.49, 95% CI: -0.76 to -0.22) and lower pain scores (SMD = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.68 to -0.38), though these outcomes were informed by few trials. Publication bias was suggested for cardiovascular/cerebrovascular complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, no clear superiority was observed between spinal and general anesthesia for hip fracture surgery. Limited evidence suggests potential improvements in short-term pain and functional recovery with spinal anesthesia; however, these findings are based on a small number of studies and require confirmation in future well-designed trials.

articles.title: Early post-discharge pain persistence, not opioid use, is associated with new-onset chronic pain among opioid-naive emergency department patients: a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain may develop after emergency department (ED) visits for acute pain, but early predictors of new-onset chronic pain among opioid-naïve patients are incompletely understood. We conducted a secondary analysis of a prospective observational cohort of opioid-naïve adults presenting to two urban EDs primarily for pain and discharged home with a new opioid prescription. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 48 h, two weeks, and six months. The primary outcome was new-onset chronic pain at six months, defined as pain occurring on >50% of days during the six months after ED discharge. Of 699 participants in the parent cohort, 562 (80.4%) provided six-month outcome data, including 483 participants without chronic pain at baseline. Among these participants, 129 (26.7%) met criteria for new-onset chronic pain at six months. In multivariable models, neck/back pain and longer pain duration before the ED visit were consistently associated with higher odds of new-onset chronic pain. Pain sometimes/usually/always at 48 h versus never/rarely was associated with higher odds of new-onset chronic pain (OR 2.77, 95% CI: 1.40-5.48). When 48-hour and two-week pain frequency were included simultaneously as predictors, two-week pain frequency remained associated with new-onset chronic pain (OR 2.36, 95% CI: 1.39-4.00), whereas the 48-hour estimate attenuated. Moderate/severe pain at two weeks was associated with new-onset chronic pain (OR 2.20, 95% CI: 1.37-3.53). Opioid use at 48 h and two weeks was not associated with new-onset chronic pain. Baseline pain characteristics and early post-discharge pain persistence may help identify patients at elevated risk for new-onset chronic pain. PERSPECTIVE: Persistent pain after an emergency department visit may provide an early signal of risk for subsequent chronic pain. Among opioid-naive patients discharged with a new opioid prescription, pain frequency and intensity during the first two weeks, but not early opioid use, were associated with new-onset chronic pain.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Pre-COPD Score to Predict Incident COPD.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The ability to predict progression from a pre-disease state in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pre-COPD, to overt COPD remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To test the hypothesis that development of COPD can be predicted by characterizing pre-COPD and creating a simple pre-COPD score.
METHODS: We identified individuals without airflow obstruction, defined as pre-bronchodilator (BD) forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC)≥0.70 and ≥lower limit of normal, from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS)(N = 14,506), Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS)(N = 8673), and Genetic Epidemiology for COPD (COPDGene) Study(N = 2982). A pre-COPD score was developed in CGPS by assigning 1 point to each of smoking history≥10 pack-years, active smoking, any respiratory symptom, asthma, and pre-BD FEV1/FVC 0.70-0.75, and 4 points for pre-BD FEV1<80% predicted, indicating presence of Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry (PRISm), with external validation in CCHS and COPDGene. Participants were followed for 5-10 years for incident COPD, defined as pre-BD FEV1/FVC<0.70 and FEV1<80% predicted.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: During follow-up, COPD developed in 669 individuals (4.6%) in CGPS, 685 (7.9%) in CCHS, and 367 (12%) in COPDGene. In CGPS, 10-year incidence was 1.5% in the low-risk, 9.3% in the intermediate-risk, 24% in the high-risk, and 42% in the very high-risk category. Corresponding 5-year incidences were 3.7%, 7.3%, 12%, and 25% in CCHS, and 4.1%, 5.3%, 13%, and 31% in COPDGene, respectively. The pre-COPD score demonstrated good discrimination with areas under curve of 0.88 in CGPS, 0.76 in CCHS, and 0.81 in COPDGene. The pre-COPD score was also associated with exacerbations.
CONCLUSIONS: The pre-COPD score is useful in predicting the onset of COPD with clinically relevant discrimination in three cohorts with different risk profiles.

articles.title: Complications After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The outcomes after total joint arthroplasty (TJA) for patients who have solid organ transplants (SOT) remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate: 1) overall medical and surgical complication rates, 2) survivorship-free rates from periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) and mortality specifically, and 3) risk factors for complications in SOT recipients undergoing TJA.
METHODS: A retrospective study was performed of all SOT recipients undergoing primary TJA at a single academic institution between 2005 and 2024, with a minimum one-year follow-up. Demographics, surgical characteristics, medical comorbidities, transplant type, and immunosuppressive therapy were recorded. We identified 103 TJAs (69 total hip arthroplasties [THA], 34 total knee arthroplasties [TKA]) in 89 SOT recipients who had a mean follow-up of 4.9 years. The overall complication rate was 26.2% (27 of 103). Logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed. An alpha level of 0.05 denoted significance.
RESULTS: The surgical and medical complication rates were 13.0 and 13.0% after THA, and 5.9 and 20.6% after TKA, respectively. After THA, five-year infection-free and mortality-free survivorships were 97.8 and 92.0%, respectively, with no difference by transplant type (P = 0.40 and P = 0.84, respectively). After TKA, five-year infection-free and mortality-free survivorships were 96.4 and 74.8%, respectively, with no difference by transplant type (P = 0.57 and P = 0.29, respectively). When controlling for confounders, body mass index (Odds Ratio [OR] 0.88, P = 0.02) and history of liver transplant (OR 0.21, P = 0.04) were associated with increased complications.
CONCLUSION: While overall complication rates were high, SOT recipients demonstrated low PJI rates following TJA when managed with multidisciplinary perioperative care. Only renal transplant recipients developed PJI, demonstrating potentially higher susceptibility in this subgroup. The mortality rates identified are concordant with literature describing general survivorship of patients after SOT and therefore appear to not be affected by undergoing TJA.

articles.title: A practical framework for using GLP-1 RAs, SGLT2i, and MRAs with contemporary immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) remain central to kidney-transplant (KTX) immunosuppression (IS) but contribute to nephrotoxicity and cardiometabolic (CM) complications which negatively affect patient and graft survival. This review presents a practical framework for adding glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) to established IS regimens. These agents complement individualized optimization of IS, including CNI-sparing strategies when indicated.
RECENT FINDINGS: Evidence in KTX recipients remains limited, but available studies suggest that these agents may improve glycemic control, weight, blood pressure, proteinuria, and cardiorenal risk without routinely requiring changes to IS choice or dose. Whether these changes improve patient and graft survival remains unproven. GLP-1 RA related gastrointestinal effects may alter oral IS absorption, warranting continued CNI trough monitoring, particularly when significant gastrointestinal symptoms occur after initiation or dose escalation. SGLT2i require assessment of volume status, renal-function, and infection risk. MRAs may compound CNIs associated hyperkalemia and early eGFR decline, requiring close potassium and renal-function monitoring.
SUMMARY: These therapies may extend cardiorenal benefits observed in nontransplant chronic kidney disease to selected KTX recipients. Their use should be individualized, introduced sequentially, and supported by monitoring of graft function, electrolytes, volume status, blood pressure, and IS exposure. Temporary withholding should follow drug-specific perioperative and sick-day guidance, particularly for SGLT2i.

articles.title: Utility and Perceived Patient Benefit of In-Office Dilation for Female Urethral Strictures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine utility and patient perception of treatment of female urethral stricture disease utilizing in office urethral dilation with topical anesthesia.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patient perception and course of therapy of outpatient urethral dilation by a single surgeon in women with diagnosed urethral stricture disease using the self-administered PGI-I questionnaire.
RESULTS: Thirty women underwent in-office urethral dilation and returned for the first dilation in a serial protocol. No complications were reported, and all patients received intramuscular aminoglycoside prophylaxis. Median age at original dilation was 62 years (range 29-90), and the median interval from a patient's first lifetime dilation to the original dilation was 746 days. Initial patient-reported improvement (PGI-I) scores were 1 in 60%, 2 in 17%, 3 in 13%, and 4 in 10%. There were no significant differences in age, dilation size, prior number of dilations, or time intervals between patients reporting the best initial score (PGI-I=1) versus ≥2. Sixteen patients provided a second score; those with versus without a second score differed only in the number of prior dilations (median 5 vs 2, p=0.014). Among patients with two scores, 81% reported stable or improved symptoms at the second assessment.
CONCLUSION: Office-based urethral dilation for female urethral stricture disease was rated by patients as a beneficial treatment. While urethral dilation is not be a definitive therapy for female urethral stricture disease compared to formal urethroplasty, repeat urethral dilation is a safe treatment for urethral stricture disease and highly valued by the appropriate patient as a non-operative management method.

articles.title: What's Coming Up Next? The Physiology of Gastroparesis and GLP-1 Agonists.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin to regulate glycemia, activates peripheral and central neural pathways to control appetite, and inhibits upper gut transit to reduce food intake. Peptide and nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), as well as a combined GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), agonist are approved for type 2 diabetes, weight reduction, and other indications. GLP-1RA therapy can be complicated by upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, including nausea and vomiting. Delayed gastric emptying secondary to GLP-1RAs may be influenced by drug pharmacokinetics, associated neuropathy, and development of tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing. A theoretical risk of pulmonary aspiration from retained gastric contents is concerning for patients undergoing anesthesia before endoscopy or surgery. Managing upper GI complications of GLP-1RA therapy includes diet modifications, antiemetic medications, and treatments that stimulate gastric emptying. Newer agents in testing include nonpeptide GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RAs acting in concert with GIP, glucagon, or other receptor-mediated pathways.

articles.title: Same day discharge following bimaxillary osteotomy surgery a single center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe same-day discharge and recorded postoperative complications after bimaxillary osteotomy in a selected retrospective cohort, without establishing comparative safety.
METHODS: The cohort comprised 80 adults classified as American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) I-II who underwent bimaxillary osteotomy, with or without adjunctive procedures, at a day-surgery center in Riyadh between January 2022 and November 2023. Forty were discharged on the same day and 40 were admitted overnight. Discharge planning reflected patient preference and clinical assessment. The primary endpoint was the recorded postoperative-complication indicator in the available clinical dataset. Post Anesthetic Discharge Scoring System (PADSS) readiness was described separately. Complication proportions were compared without adjustment for confounding.
RESULTS: PADSS scores ≥ 9 were recorded in 40/40 same-day and 32/40 overnight patients. Recorded complications affected 2/40 (5.0%) and 9/40 (22.5%), respectively. The unadjusted risk difference was - 17.5% points (95% CI, - 32.9 to - 2.1). Adjunctive procedures differed between groups. A standardized outcome window, detailed event classification and an intention-to-discharge denominator were unavailable, limiting interpretation.
CONCLUSION: Same-day discharge was achieved in 40 selected ASA I-II patients at an experienced center. These observations support feasibility within the analyzed cohort but do not establish comparative safety, noninferiority or the success rate among all patients originally intended for same-day discharge.

articles.title: Risk factors and morbidity characteristics of surgical site infection following ankle fracture ORIF: A comprehensive analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to describe the incidence and microbiological characteristics of surgical site infection (SSI) after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of ankle fractures and identify clinical factors associated with SSI. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 248 patients who underwent ankle fracture ORIF between January and December 2023. SSI occurring within 30 postoperative days was identified from available inpatient and postoperative medical records. Demographic, injury-related, laboratory, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with and without SSI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with SSI. SSI occurred in 32 of 248 patients (12.9%), including 25 superficial and 7 deep infections. Cultured organisms included Escherichia coli (n = 10), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 7), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 6), Enterobacter cloacae (n = 5), and Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 4). In multivariable analysis, open fracture, wound class II-III, and neutrophil percentage > 75% were associated with SSI. Age and body mass index (BMI) also showed positive associations, although the precise unit-specific effect sizes could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived statistical analysis; these comparatively large per-unit estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of SSI events and potential residual confounding. SSI occurred in 12.9% of this single-center ankle fracture cohort. Older age and higher BMI showed associations with SSI, together with open fracture, less-clean operative wounds, and neutrophilia. The magnitude of the age- and BMI-related effects should be interpreted cautiously because their original regression scaling could not be independently reconstructed.
