Obliterative versus Reconstructive Surgery for Advanced Pelvic Organ Prolapse in Older Women: A Systematic Review for Preference-Sensitive Surgical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: The choice between obliterative and reconstructive surgery for older women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse is preference sensitive. This review synthesized comparative evidence across perioperative safety, durability, urinary, bowel/anorectal, and patient-reported outcomes.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 1 May 2026. English-language comparative studies in older advanced-prolapse populations were included. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, assessed risk of bias using Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions, and rated certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Findings were narratively synthesized because of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Of 664 records, 29 reports representing 27 study families were included. Safety outcomes were reported in 23 reports, durability/recurrence in 16, urinary outcomes in 12, bowel/anorectal outcomes in 9, and broad patient-reported outcomes/quality of life in 10. Twelve of the 14 non-overlapping comparisons reported shorter operative time after obliterative surgery; blood loss favored obliteration in 8 of the 12 comparisons and hospital stay in 5 out of 11. Overall complications were not consistently lower. Anatomical/composite durability numerically favored obliteration in 7 out of 10 comparisons, and recurrence-related reoperation was lower in 7 out of 8. Urinary, bowel, and patient-reported outcomes were inconsistent or similar. Certainty was low for operative time and very low for other key outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports a more definitive conclusion about lower procedural burden, particularly shorter operative time, than about global complications, anatomical superiority, or functional outcomes. Findings should inform counseling that integrates frailty, comorbidity, sexual goals, functional symptoms, durability expectations, treatment burden, and patient preference.

articles.title: The Vertebral Nerve as a Selective Target for Upper Limb Sympathetic Blockade: Anatomy, Ultrasound-Guided Technique, and Proof of Concept.
articles.abstract: The vertebral nerve (VN) is a postganglionic sympathetic structure that arises from the cervicothoracic ganglion, ascends alongside the vertebral artery, and provides sympathetic innervation to the upper limb via the brachial plexus. Despite its anatomical relevance, it remains largely unknown to anesthesiologists and pain clinicians. The stellate ganglion block (SGB) is the current standard for upper-limb sympatholysis but produces nonselective effects, including Horner's syndrome and potential cardiac involvement. A more selective approach targeting the VN could achieve equivalent upper-limb sympatholysis while potentially offering a superior safety profile. We conducted a comprehensive anatomical review of the VN, covering its origin, trajectory, branching patterns, and communications with both the cervical spinal nerves and the vertebral plexus. Using this anatomical framework, we describe an ultrasound-guided technique for selective VN blockade at the C7 level, validated with fluoroscopic contrast confirmation. We objectively evaluated clinical efficacy using infrared thermography and laser Doppler flowmetry. The VN is an anatomically consistent and sonographically accessible target for selective upper-limb sympathetic blockade. At this target, effective sympatholysis can be achieved with minimal injectate volumes, thereby avoiding the nonselective effects of conventional SGB. Further studies are needed to compare efficacy, optimal technique parameters, and complication rates with existing approaches.

articles.title: Reconstructing Skull Base Reconstruction: The State of the Art.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skull base reconstruction has continued to evolve in parallel with advances in endoscopic skull base ablation in order to accomplish the goal of restoring larger and more complicated defects between the cranial and nasal cavities while balancing morbidity, cost, and recovery.
METHODS: We reviewed recent literature on advances in skull base reconstruction including graded endoscopic reconstruction, appropriate use of perioperative adjuncts, endoscopic free tissue inset, patient-specific planning, dural substitutes, regenerative scaffolds, and autologous biologics.
RESULTS: Graded reconstruction supports free grafts or local flaps for selected low-flow defects and multilayer vascularized closure for high-flow defects. Lumbar drainage benefits selected high-risk patients, whereas routine packing and prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis are not consistently supported. Endoscopic free flap inset, virtual surgical planning, and patient-specific implants expand options for complex composite and salvage defects. Synthetic dural substitutes can reduce donor-site morbidity in appropriate cases. Leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) has emerging clinical support, while most regenerative scaffolds, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), and cell-based strategies remain preclinical.
CONCLUSIONS: With advancements in skull base reconstruction, the paradigm has shifted toward using the least morbid construct that reliably restores the intracranial-sinonasal barrier while preserving function and quality of life. Standardized, prospective studies with attention to patient- and value-centric outcomes are crucial for improving care. Material science advances will continue to expand reconstructive options.

articles.title: Spinal Anesthesia Can Be Appropriate in B2 Periprosthetic Fracture Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic fractures (PPFx) after total hip arthroplasty, especially Vancouver B2 fractures, are associated with high morbidity and mortality. Anesthesia type may influence early postoperative outcomes, yet limited data exist comparing spinal versus general anesthesia in this population.
METHODS: A retrospective review of 165 PPFx cases from January 1, 2019, to June 30, 2024, at a high-volume orthopaedic specialty hospital identified 95 patients with Vancouver B2 PPFx. Patients were grouped by anesthesia type: spinal (40) or general (55). Demographics, perioperative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were analyzed. Statistical analysis included chi-squared tests, t-tests, and regression modeling.
RESULTS: Patients receiving general anesthesia had significantly higher American Society of Anesthesiologists scores (3.1 vs. 2.8; P = 0.008) and Charlson Comorbidity Index scores (5.4 vs. 4.0; P < 0.001). General anesthesia was associated with longer surgical time (+21 minutes, P = 0.029), longer postoperative acute care unit time (+25 minutes, P = 0.034), longer length of stay (+1.8 days, P = 0.024), and a higher transfusion rate (76.5% vs. 55.0%; P = 0.028). Pain scores, physical therapy performance, and complication rates were similar. One-year mortality was approximately 20% in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Spinal anesthesia is a safe and effective option for appropriately selected patients undergoing surgery for Vancouver B2 periprosthetic femoral fractures. Despite differences in some perioperative metrics (longer surgical time, postoperative acute care unit time, length of stay, and higher transfusion rates with general anesthesia), complication and mortality rates were equivalent between the two groups. This suggests that the choice of anesthesia should be individualized based on the patient's health status and the complexity of the surgery.
articles.journal: J Am Acad Orthop Surg Glob Res Rev

articles.title: Pain Management in Elective Orthopaedic Surgery: A Delphi Consensus of the Academic Orthopaedic Consortium.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain management is a critical component of orthopaedic care, aimed at minimizing discomfort, facilitating recovery, and enhancing functional outcomes. The purpose of this study was to establish consensus statements through the Delphi process on pain management from preoperatively to postoperatively at the time of elective orthopaedic sports medicine and arthroplasty surgery.
METHODS: A consensus process using the Delphi technique was conducted. Thirty-seven orthopaedic surgeons, anaesthesiologist pain management physicians, and musculoskeletal researchers participated in these consensus statements. Consensus was defined as achieving 80 to 89% agreement, strong consensus was defined as 90 to 99% agreement, and unanimous consensus was indicated by 100% agreement with a proposed statement.
RESULTS: Of the 40 total questions and consensus statements in this group, four achieved unanimous consensus, 21 achieved strong consensus, 14 achieved consensus, and one did not reach any consensus.
CONCLUSION: The majority of statements reached some degree of consensus, with most achieving at least strong consensus. The statements that achieved unanimous consensus were on preoperative patient counselling for those with opioid addiction risk factors, including preoperative plans, preoperative education, frank discussions on expectations of pain after surgery, and pain management contracts. In addition, unanimous consensus was achieved that practices should have a standard opioid prescribing protocol to minimize prescribing, based on the procedure performed and with a maximum prescribing amount, and regarding the advantages of e-prescribing for opioids. Finally, unanimous consensus was determined that acetaminophen is always indicated, except when there is a medical contraindication such as liver impairment.

articles.title: Tetracaine hydrochloride gel delays and reduces catheter-related bladder discomfort after transurethral resection: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-related bladder discomfort (CRBD) results from involuntary bladder contractions triggered by both the indwelling urinary catheter and surgical trauma during transurethral resection. Systemic analgesics and anticholinergics are often used but carry risks of side effects. Topical anesthetics like tetracaine hydrochloride gel offer a potential targeted approach, but their efficacy in delaying and reducing CRBD remains unclear.
METHODS: In this randomized, single-blind study, patients undergoing transurethral resection were allocated to the tetracaine gel group (n = 65) or the lubricant control group (n = 65). Before catheter insertion, three g of tetracaine gel or standard lubricant was evenly applied to the catheter surface. The primary outcome was the time to first-reported moderate-to-severe CRBD after tracheal extubation. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of new-onset moderate and severe CRBD at specified intervals, as well as the patient satisfaction, postoperative pain scores, analgesic requirements, and adverse events. The incidence of moderate-to-severe CRBD stratified by age and procedure type was also analyzed.
RESULTS: The time to first-reported moderate-to-severe CRBD was significantly longer in the tetracaine gel group compared to the control group (30 [10.0-61.3] min vs. 5 [4.8-10.0] min, p < 0.001) among patients who developed this event. The incidence of new-onset moderate-to-severe CRBD was significantly lower in the tetracaine gel group within 30 min (15 [23.1%] vs. 43 [66.2%]; RR = 0.153, 95% CI [0.071-0.332]; p < 0.001) and over the total 24 hours assessment period (30 [46.2%] vs. 46 [70.8%]; RR = 0.354, 95% CI [0.172-0.730]; p = 0.004). A transient increase in incidence was noted in the tetracaine group between 30-120 min (11 [16.9%] vs. 2 [3.1%]; RR = 6.417, 95% CI [1.362-30.228]; p = 0.016). The non-significant interaction test indicates that the effect magnitude of tetracaine gel did not differ by age (P for interaction = 0.392) or procedure type (P for interaction = 0.883). Patient satisfaction at 6 hours was higher (6.7 ± 0.5 vs. 6.2 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), and postoperative pain scores were lower at all assessed time points. No significant differences were found in analgesic requirements, postoperative delirium, infections, or hospital stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Topical application of tetracaine gel to the urinary catheter effectively delays the onset and reduces the incidence of moderate-to-severe CRBD in the early postoperative period.

articles.title: Surgical wound infiltration with liposomal bupivacaine admixture as an adjunct to intrathecal morphine for post-caesarean analgesia: a randomised, double-blind controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrathecal morphine is the gold standard for post-caesarean analgesia, but it lasts only 18-24 h. Whether wound infiltration adds benefit in patients receiving intrathecal morphine remains controversial. This study evaluated the opioid-sparing efficacy of wound infiltration with a liposomal bupivacaine-bupivacaine hydrochloride admixture as an adjunct to intrathecal morphine.
METHODS: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 188 patients undergoing elective caesarean delivery with intrathecal morphine (100 μg) received either wound infiltration with liposomal bupivacaine (266 mg) plus bupivacaine hydrochloride (100 mg), or saline placebo. All patients received standardised multimodal analgesia including scheduled non-opioid analgesics and hydromorphone patient-controlled analgesia. The primary outcome was cumulative opioid consumption (oral morphine milligram equivalents) at 48 h.
RESULTS: With treatment, 48-h opioid consumption was significantly lower (12.60 mg [IQR 6.30-15.80] vs. 15.75 mg [IQR 9.45-25.50]; Hodges-Lehmann estimate -3.05 mg, 95% CI -5.9 to -1.4; P = 0.002). Secondary outcomes also favoured treatment: 24-h opioid consumption (6.30 vs. 9.45 mg; P < 0.001), movement-evoked pain at 24 h (40 vs. 50 mm; P < 0.001) and 48 h (30 vs. 40 mm; P < 0.001), time to first analgesic request (14.5 vs. 9.5 h; P < 0.001), and opioid-free status at 48 h (19.1% vs. 2.1%; RR 9.0; 95% CI 2.1-37.8; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In women undergoing scheduled caesarean delivery, wound infiltration with a liposomal bupivacaine-bupivacaine hydrochloride admixture significantly reduced postoperative opioid consumption and improved pain scores. It may be an effective opioid-sparing adjunct to intrathecal morphine.

articles.title: Effects of Concomitant Ovariohysterectomy During Elective Caesarean Section in Bitches: A Prospective Clinical Study.
articles.abstract: The association of ovariohysterectomy with caesarean section in bitches remains controversial due to concerns regarding surgical time, haemorrhage, maternal recovery, lactation, and neonatal care. This prospective study evaluated intraoperative findings, postoperative recovery, and puerperal outcomes in bitches undergoing elective caesarean section with or without concomitant ovariohysterectomy. Twenty-five pregnant bitches undergoing elective caesarean section were prospectively enrolled and classified according to the surgical procedure performed into a Caesarean Group (CG, n = 15) and a Caesarean plus Ovariohysterectomy Group (COHG, n = 10). Group assignment was not randomized and was determined by owner consent and clinical and reproductive management considerations. Clinical, surgical, and postpartum variables were assessed from the preoperative period until 30 days postpartum. No statistically significant differences were detected between groups regarding anaesthetic time, surgical time, total weight of blood-contaminated surgical waste, postoperative recovery, lactation, neonatal viability, or wound healing. Vital parameters remained within physiological limits throughout the puerperal period in both groups, although heart rate differed significantly between groups at 30 days postpartum. One bitch in the COHG group was not available for behavioural and lactation assessments. Maternal rejection was observed in 13.3% (2/15) of bitches in the CG and 55.6% (5/9) in the COHG group, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.061). No major maternal or neonatal complications were observed during the study period. However, the limited sample size, particularly in the COHG group, warrants cautious interpretation of these findings and limits the ability to exclude clinically relevant differences between groups. The possible influence of concomitant ovariohysterectomy on maternal behaviour warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Prevalence of Self-Reported Self-Harm and Suicidal Ideation by Levels of Pain Intensity: An Analysis of the Australian National Survey of Mental Health and Wellbeing, 2020-2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain is common, and may co-occur with suicide attempts, self-harm and suicidal ideation. However, data on the prevalence of these outcomes across pain intensity levels is limited.
METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of the 2020-2022 National Survey of Mental Health and Wellbeing. Australian residents aged 16 to 85 years were recruited over two waves: December 2020 to July 2021 (n = 5554) and December 2021 to October 2022 (n = 10,339). We estimated the prevalence of self-reported self-harm or suicidal ideation in the past year by levels of recent pain intensity (none, mild, moderate, severe) in the past four weeks. Subgroup analyses were stratified by sex assigned at birth, age, presence of mental health conditions, linguistic diversity and geographic location.
RESULTS: Of the 15,880 (weighted) respondents with available data, 35% reported no pain, 41% mild pain, and 23% moderate or severe pain in the past four weeks. Past year self-harm and suicidal ideation were reported by 2% and 3%, respectively. The prevalence of self-harm increased with pain intensity: 0.9% (no pain), 1.9% (mild), 2.7% (moderate) and 3.5% (severe). The prevalence of suicidal ideation also increased with pain intensity: 1.6% (none), 3.0% (mild), 4.7% (moderate), 8.7% (severe). These patterns were largely consistent by sex and age group.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater recent pain intensity is associated with higher prevalence of self-reported self-harm and suicidal ideation. Monitoring mental health among people experiencing pain is important, and integrating routine suicide risk assessment into pain management and physical health care settings could support targeted suicide prevention efforts and inform policy and clinical practice.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: In this nationally representative Australian general population sample, we found a graded association between recent bodily pain and suicidal ideation and self-harm. The consistency of this graded association across major demographic subgroups strengthens the case for pain intensity as a practical, low-burden screening cue in primary care, pain management and physiotherapy settings. Enhanced training for general practitioners and physiotherapists should be a cornerstone of suicide prevention strategies.

articles.title: From Experimental Conditioning to Clinical Pain: Bridging the Learning-Transfer Gap.
Establishing Key Concepts for Pain Science Education for People With Spinal Cord Injury Related Neuropathic Pain: A Delphi Study of Experts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuropathic pain (NP) is a common and debilitating consequence of a spinal cord injury (SCI) with considerable effects on function, quality of life, and social participation. Current treatment approaches have limited effectiveness. Clinical guidelines recommend pain science education (PSE) as a first-line intervention for persistent pain; however, the uniqueness of SCI-related NP warrants its adaptation.
METHODS: A four-round modified e-Delphi was conducted to identify and refine PSE concepts for those with SCI-related NP. An international multidisciplinary panel of expert clinicians and researchers specialising in SCI pain and/or PSE (n = 33) was established. The experts initially reviewed and adapted 58 concepts from general PSE (Round 1), followed by rating and iterative refinement across survey rounds (Rounds 2-4). Acceptance criteria for a concept were: rated as important (≥ 75% of responses ≥ 4 on a 1-6 Likert scale), reached consensus (interquartile range ≤ 2), and demonstrated stability (no significant change on Wilcoxon test).
RESULTS: Across four rounds, experts identified 81 PSE concepts grouped under nine themes, 75 of which were accepted. All 58 established general PSE concepts required modification to align with the SCI-related NP context, and 23 new concepts were added.
CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi study establishes key PSE concepts tailored to a SCI-related NP population. The findings highlight the need to adapt general PSE for this population, including a paradigm shift from a focus on an "overprotective" to an "overactive" pain system, and the explicit inclusion of information on understanding NP, immune modulation, and medication.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This Delphi study is the first expert-derived framework of pain science education concepts tailored specifically for individuals with spinal cord injury-related neuropathic pain. The findings highlight important differences from general chronic musculoskeletal PSE to those with neuropathic pain. These concepts provide a foundation for developing tailored pain science education interventions to improve self-management and pain outcomes for people living with spinal cord injury-related neuropathic pain.

articles.title: The Impact of Outcome Measures for Responder Analyses in Placebo-Controlled Trials of Pharmacological Treatments for Neuropathic Pain.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dichotomous responder outcomes, including ≥ 30% and ≥ 50% pain reduction, patient-reported pain relief, and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), are widely used in trials assessing interventions for neuropathic pain and have been suggested to be comparable, but their differences and influence on estimated treatment effects remain uncertain.
METHODS: The study presents secondary analyses of 222 double-blind RCTs in neuropathic pain. Trials assessing drugs with recommended or inconclusive recommendations reporting at least two different dichotomous outcomes were included. Risk differences, numbers needed to treat (NNT), and relative risks were calculated.
RESULTS: Ninety-one trials were included. Across 76 trials, the risk difference was higher for ≥ 30% than ≥ 50% pain reduction (difference 0.023, 95% CI 0.012-0.034; p < 0.001), corresponding to lower NNTs for ≥ 30% pain reduction (8.8 vs. 11.1). PGIC-based outcomes yielded numerically lower NNTs than ≥ 50% pain reduction and were similar to ≥ 30% pain reduction, although variability was substantial. Within 31 trials reporting all outcomes, ≥ 30% pain reduction and PGIC showed comparable NNTs on average, whereas ≥ 50% pain reduction consistently produced higher NNTs. Comparisons involving pain relief scales were limited by sparse data and heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: Estimated treatment effects in neuropathic pain trials depend on the responder definition used. Outcomes based on ≥ 50% pain reduction yield systematically higher NNTs than ≥ 30% pain reduction and PGIC, indicating lower assay sensitivity. Standardization of outcome measures may improve interpretability and comparability of analgesic efficacy.
SIGNIFICANCE: Indicating the main aspects where this work adds significantly to existing knowledge in the field, and if appropriate to clinical practice. We show that stricter responder thresholds (≥ 50% pain reduction) attenuate detectable treatment effects compared with ≥ 30% pain reduction. This has direct implications for meta-analyses and comparisons of treatment effects as well as for clinical trials, as suboptimal endpoint choice may contribute to underpowered trials and premature discontinuation of potentially effective therapies.

articles.title: Classification of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Patients Using Neuropathic Pain Symptoms-A Secondary, Retrospective Analysis From ncRNAPain.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) is a rare chronic pain disorder characterized by a heterogeneous symptom profile, including severe pain, allodynia and motor dysfunction. In previous work, we demonstrated elevated levels of neuropathic pain symptoms in CRPS, suggesting that refined symptom-based stratification may improve patient classification. This study applied neuropathic pain clusters derived from the Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory (NPSI), which were developed by Bouhassira et al. as a phenotyping method to optimize treatment response for neuropathic pain and assessed its relevance for CRPS subgrouping.
METHODS: Patients (212 CRPS, 34 follow-ups) were evaluated using standardized clinical examinations and questionnaires. They were allocated to one of three NPSI clusters (deep, evoked, pinpointed pain) at baseline and follow up after a mean interval of 2.5 years. Clustered CRPS patients were analysed for treatment differences and associations with established subgrouping methods, for example, CRPS type.
RESULTS: Most CRPS patients were allocated to the deep pain cluster, characterized by low levels of paraesthesia/dysaesthesia and pronounced pressure-like and squeezing pain. Cluster instability was observed at follow-up, particularly among patients initially assigned to the evoked or pinpointed pain clusters. Pinpointed pain-clustered patients received less standard treatment.
CONCLUSION: NPSI-based clusters represent a promising stratification approach for CRPS that may enhance pathophysiological insights and support personalized treatment strategies.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study applies the NPSI and the clusters developed by Bouhassira to classify CRPS patients based on their neuropathic symptoms. These results were compared to the complaints of the same patients after 2.5 years. Most CRPS patients remained in the deep pain cluster, even after more than 2 years. The CRPS pattern did not correlate with common classifications for CRPS.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trial Register registration number: DRKS00008964.

articles.title: Peri-operative surgical care optimisation for patients requiring emergency surgery (PERI-SCOPES): Protocol for a multicentre mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Emergency General Surgery is a common reason for an emergency admission in the UK with over 25,000 emergency laparotomies (EmLap) performed every year.(1) For frail and co-morbid patients an alternative decision is often made that not undergoing surgery is in their best interest (NoLap). For both EmLap and NoLap patients, little is known about survivorship. This study aims to quantify quality of life (QoL) for EmLap and NoLap patients and explore the decision-making process.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PERI-SCOPES is a mixed-methods multicentre study exploring QoL and decision-making in Emergency General Surgery. The study will involve two separate workstreams. WORKSTREAM 1: Up to 30 patients, EmLap or NoLap, will be eligible for inclusion and identified by the local research teams. Patients will be recruited from six sites across Scotland. Patients will be invited to nominate a family member/supporter to participate alongside them. Participants will complete validated QoL questionnaires within 4 weeks of EmLap/NoLap decision then again at 3- and 9-12 months post-decision. Questionnaires will include EuroQol five-dimension five-level, Short Form of the Profile of Mood States, International Trauma Questionnaire and Caregiver Strain Index. Patients and their family member/supporter will also take part in three semi-structured interviews at similar time-points to explore their experience of decision-making. WORKSTREAM 2: UK-based consultant decision-makers (surgeons, anaesthetists and intensivists) will be invited to complete an online survey exploring personality, risk-taking and decision-making in Emergency General Surgery. At least 52 consultants will be recruited to ensure sufficient statistical power. Individual semi-structured interviews will be conducted with up to 20 consultants to allow a deeper exploration of decision-making.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: PERI-SCOPES is sponsored by The University of Glasgow and has received ethical approval from East of Scotland REC (25/ES/0015). This study has Research and Innovation (R&I) approval from NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde, Grampian, Tayside and Lothian (6 hospital sites). We aim to disseminate results via peer-reviewed medical journals and conferences.
TRIALS REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06972017.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes and cost-effectiveness of a modified electrocautery-assisted intracapsular tonsillectomy technique (E-ICT) for the pediatric population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracapsular tonsillectomy (ICT) may reduce postoperative morbidity compared with extracapsular tonsillectomy, but long-term outcomes of electrocautery-assisted ICT (E-ICT) remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated long-term outcomes, safety, tonsillar regrowth, and parental satisfaction associated with E-ICT in children.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 278 children aged 2-18 years who underwent E-ICT at a secondary care hospital in Saudi Arabia between 2015 and 2023. A one-time cross-sectional long-term assessment of the historical cohort was conducted during 2024-2026. Retrospective data included demographic, clinical, perioperative, and early postoperative outcomes. The one-time long-term assessment was obtained for 195 children (70.1%): the same structured parent-reported questionnaire was administered to all 195 children; 62 additionally underwent in-clinic physical examination including fiberoptic nasolaryngoscopy, whereas 133 completed the assessment by telephone/virtual contact. Outcomes included hemorrhage, healthcare utilization, symptom improvement, tonsillar regrowth, revision surgery, and long-term parent-reported satisfaction.
RESULTS: Mean age was 6.48 years, and 78.4% underwent surgery for obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (oSDB). Primary hemorrhage occurred in 0.4% and secondary hemorrhage in 3.2%; 0.7% required operative intervention. Mean long-term follow-up was approximately 6 years. Recurrent tonsillitis improved in 98.5%, recurrent sore throat in 94.4%, and oSDB in 91.3%. Among 62 clinically examined children, tonsillar regrowth occurred in 9.7%, with one revision surgery; the overall revision rate was 0.4%. Long-term parent-reported satisfaction was high, with 94.9% rating the outcome as 4-5/5.
CONCLUSION: E-ICT was associated with durable symptom improvement, low hemorrhage and revision rates, and high long-term parent-reported satisfaction, supporting its practicality in resource-limited healthcare settings.

articles.title: Effect of intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common neurological complication associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Intranasal insulin may improve cognitive function, but its effectiveness and optimal dose for preventing POD remain uncertain. We evaluated the effect of intranasal insulin on POD and explored its dose-response relationship.
REVIEW METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 2025. Randomised controlled trials comparing intranasal insulin with placebo in adult surgical patients were included. Random-effect pairwise and one-stage dose-response meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework.
RESULTS: Eight randomised controlled trials involving 892 patients were included (502 receiving intranasal insulin and 390 receiving placebo). Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD (moderate-certainty evidence) compared with placebo (risk ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.29-0.51). Subgroup analyses found no significant differences according to surgery type or anaesthetic technique. A dose-response analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association, with a rapid reduction in POD risk at lower doses and the greatest modelled benefit at 30 IU (risk ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.29-0.53). The dose-response curve plateaued above 30 IU, with no additional reduction in POD risk at higher doses. Seven trials had a low risk of bias, while one raised some concerns because of bias in measurement of the outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD in adult surgical patients. The dose-response findings suggest that 30 IU may provide the greatest benefit, with no apparent additional reduction at higher doses. Larger multicentre trials are needed to confirm the optimal regimen and comprehensively evaluate safety.

articles.title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm.
DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL).
RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group.
CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

articles.title: Patient preference for intraoperative opioid strategy and early postoperative recovery after noncardiac surgery: a prospective partially randomised patient-preference trial (the PERFECT trial).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient-centred care increasingly encourages patients to participate in decisions regarding their anaesthetic management. However, whether expressing a preference regarding their anaesthetic management is associated with improved postoperative recovery remains unknown. We evaluated the association between preference expression and quality of recovery after noncardiac surgery.
METHODS: In this prospective partially randomised patient-preference study conducted at two academic hospitals, adults undergoing minimally invasive abdominal, urologic, or gynaecologic surgery received standardised information on opioid-based and opioid-free anaesthesia, co-developed with patient partners. Participants expressing a preference received their preferred strategy, whereas those without a preference were randomised 1:1 to either strategy. The primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score on postoperative day (POD) 1.
RESULTS: Among 220 analysed participants, 177 (80.5%) expressed a preference, and 43 (19.5%) underwent random allocation. Mean [standard deviation] QoR-15 scores on POD 1 were higher among participants expressing a preference than among randomised participants (108.8 [18.2] vs 100.8 [23.5]), with an unadjusted mean difference of 7.9 points (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.5-14.4; P=0.017). The adjusted marginal mean difference was 7.1 points (95% CI 0.3-13.9; P=0.042). Scores on the QoR-15 also remained higher on POD 2. Sensitivity analyses showed consistent effect estimates but attenuated statistical significance. Secondary outcomes, including postoperative nausea and vomiting and bradycardia, were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Expression of a preference regarding intraoperative opioid management was associated with better reported early postoperative patient-reported recovery. Given the non-randomised comparison and limited precision, -generating and support further investigation into the role of patient-preference expression in perioperative recovery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The full, long-term study is pre-registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier, NCT06855641; first posted, 3 March 2025; Alexandre Joosten). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06855641.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of trans-fornix conjunctival retrobulbar block in a prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Retrobulbar block is widely used for vitreoretinal surgery, but the conventional transcutaneous technique advances a sharp needle blindly through the lower eyelid. We evaluated a trans-fornix conjunctival approach in which a curved blunt-tip needle is advanced into the muscle cone under the operating microscope. In a two-center randomized trial, 196 patients were stratified by expected surgical duration and allocated to the transcutaneous or the trans-fornix technique, and pain was graded at predefined procedural stages. The trans-fornix approach reduced pain during anesthetic injection in both cohorts and during scleral indentation in longer procedures, and fewer patients required supplemental anesthesia. Ocular akinesia was better with the trans-fornix technique, and periorbital hemorrhage and ecchymosis occurred only in the transcutaneous group. These findings support the trans-fornix block as a practical and reproducible option for regional anesthesia in vitreoretinal surgery.

articles.title: Recognizing sclerosing encapsulating peritonitis before liver transplantation: clinical predictors and surgical implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to identify preoperative predictors of SEP and evaluate its influence on perioperative and long-term outcomes after LT.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 795 consecutive adult LT recipients between 2018 and 2025. Perioperative and long-term outcomes were evaluated in a 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort of patients with and without SEP.
RESULTS: SEP was diagnosed intraoperatively in 24 of 273 patients with pre-transplant ascites (8.8%). Preoperative computed tomography suggested the diagnosis in 39% of cases. Compared with patients without SEP, those with SEP had a distinct pre-transplant phenotype characterized by a greater burden of ascites-related complications despite lower MELD scores. Previous spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (OR 7.24, 95% CI 2.06-25.49; p = 0.002) and pre-transplant renal dysfunction (OR 10.59, 95% CI 2.64-42.59; p = 0.001) were independently associated with SEP. In the matched cohort, SEP was associated with increased transfusion requirements, higher pulmonary and renal postoperative morbidity, and longer hospital stay. Five-year overall and graft survival were comparable between groups, whereas ascites-related event-free survival was significantly reduced in patients with SEP.
CONCLUSION: SEP identifies liver transplant recipients at increased perioperative risk rather than poorer long-term prognosis. Earlier identification of SEP may also contribute to optimizing recipient selection and donor-recipient matching strategies.

articles.title: Association between short-term fine particulate matter exposure and hospital-acquired pneumonia risk in critically ill post-cardiac surgery patients: a 10-year cohort study using distributed lag non-linear models.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambient air pollution (AAP) exposure is a substantial health threat to humans globally. However, whether AAP could promote hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) onset in critically ill patients, a vulnerable population undergoing cardiac surgery in the intensive care unit (ICU), remains elusive. This study evaluated the correlation of HAP onset with fine particulate matter (PM2.5).
METHODS: In total, this study included 6,196 patients who underwent cardiovascular surgery at the ICU of a major hospital in Shandong province, China, over 10 years, from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2023. The daily mean levels of sulfur dioxide (SO2), PM2.5, carbon monoxide (CO), PM10, and ozone (O3) were assessed from publicly available data. The outcome was HAP, defined according to CDC/NHSN pneumonia criteria as pneumonia developing >48 h after hospital admission and not present or incubating at admission; VAP was not analyzed as a separate endpoint. The association between PM2.5 and HAP was estimated via a distributed lag non-linear model, adjusted for pollutants, time trends, and weather conditions.
RESULTS: This study analyzed 1938 (31.278%) HAP cases. The mean levels of PM10, O3, PM2.5, and SO2 were 120, 75, 59, and 25 μg/m3, respectively, and the mean CO level was 0.979 mg/m3. The association between PM2.5 and HAP was statistically significant at lag 1 day within the perioperative exposure window. At a PM2.5 concentration of 30 μg/m3 compared with the reference concentration of 10 μg/m3, 14.2% higher odds of HAP were observed (95% CI: 2.6-27%). The stratified analyses indicated stronger associations among elders aged ≥ 60 years, patients with body mass index (BMI) > 23.9 kg/m2 and patients with diabetes. Additional adjustment for clinical covariates, including duration of mechanical ventilation, confirmed the robustness of the observed exposure-response association.
CONCLUSION: These findings revealed a substantial and robust link between short-term PM2.5 exposure and elevated HAP incidence in the vulnerable population undergoing cardiovascular surgeries.

articles.title: Remimazolam in older surgical patients: postoperative delirium, hemodynamic stability, and mechanistic considerations.
articles.abstract: The growing number of older adults undergoing surgery has increased interest in anesthetic strategies that preserve physiological stability without worsening postoperative neurocognitive outcomes. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that produces hypnosis through positive allosteric modulation of the γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor and is rapidly hydrolyzed to the low-activity metabolite CNS7054. This focused narrative review examines remimazolam in older surgical patients, with particular emphasis on postoperative delirium (POD) and hemodynamic stability. Randomized trials and meta-analyses generally report fewer hypotensive events with remimazolam than with propofol, but neurocognitive findings are heterogeneous. Earlier trials in orthopedic, hip, gastrectomy, and abdominal surgery largely reported similar POD incidence, and one trial in frail patients undergoing hip surgery reported a lower POD incidence with remimazolam. In contrast, a 2026 randomized non-inferiority trial involving 455 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing lung resection found a higher overall incidence of delirium with remimazolam (48% vs. 31%), driven predominantly by emergence delirium in the post-anesthesia care unit (46% vs. 28%), whereas delirium after post-anesthesia care unit discharge through postoperative day 3 was similar (4% vs. 5%). This temporal distinction indicates that outcome definitions and assessment windows materially influence apparent treatment effects. PACU delirium is also associated with subsequent adverse outcomes in observational studies, underscoring the clinical importance of this early phenotype. The relatively consistent hemodynamic advantage of remimazolam should therefore be regarded separately from neurocognitive benefit; reduced hypotension has not yet been shown to translate into delirium prevention. Preclinical anti-inflammatory and organ-protective pathways are biologically plausible but remain unconfirmed at clinically relevant neurocognitive endpoints. Current evidence supports individualized use rather than routine selection of remimazolam for delirium prevention.

articles.title: Adjunctive screw fixation and screw corridors for spiral tibial fractures involving the distal tibial articular surface: a retrospective case series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Building on a CT-based regional evaluation framework developed in our previous morphological study, this study retrospectively summarized the adjunctive screw corridors actually used and their fixation targets in spiral tibial fractures involving the distal tibial articular surface that were treated with intramedullary nailing combined with adjunctive screw fixation, and used representative intraoperative and postoperative images to illustrate the relationship between the adjunctive screws and the intramedullary nail.
METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective case series of patients with spiral tibial fractures involving the distal tibial articular surface who underwent tibial intramedullary nailing combined with adjunctive screw fixation at the Department of Lower Limb Trauma, Honghui Hospital, Xi'an Jiaotong University, between May 2020 and May 2025. During the study period, 110 patients were treated with this combined fixation; 98 patients with a follow-up duration of at least 12 months and complete clinical and imaging records were included in the analysis, and 12 patients were excluded because of insufficient follow-up or incomplete imaging records. Two observers independently assessed the involvement of the posterior malleolar/Volkmann region, the anterior malleolar/Chaput region, and the medial malleolar region on preoperative CT, and Cohen's kappa was calculated from the original independent assessments obtained before consensus discussion. The four types of adjunctive screw corridors actually used were retrospectively summarized from operative records and postoperative imaging. All patients underwent adjunctive screw fixation before reaming and intramedullary nail insertion. Corridor use was summarized using descriptive statistics, and perioperative variables, time to full weight bearing, the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score, the visual analog scale (VAS) pain score, the difference in ankle dorsiflexion angle between the affected and contralateral sides, and related complications were recorded.
RESULTS: A total of 98 patients were included, comprising 62 men and 36 women, with a mean age of 45.67 ± 13.61 years. The posterior malleolar/Volkmann region, the anterior malleolar/Chaput region, and the medial malleolar region were involved in 76 (77.6%), 40 (40.8%), and 23 (23.5%) patients, respectively; single-region, two-region, and three-region involvement was present in 64, 27, and 7 patients. Interobserver agreement for the individual regions and for their combinations ranged from 95.9% to 98.0%, with kappa values of 0.924-0.957. The tibiofibular incisura, anterior cortical, posterior cortical, and medial malleolar corridors were used in 93, 8, 7, and 6 patients, respectively; 87 patients received a single corridor and 11 received multiple corridors. The number of adjunctive screws ranged from 1 to 4, with a mean of 1.23 ± 0.62. Mean operative time was 73.45 ± 7.88 min, mean intraoperative blood loss was 67.56 ± 10.46 mL, and mean follow-up was 16.13 ± 2.20 months. Ninety-seven patients were included in the analyses of time to full weight bearing and final functional outcomes. Mean time to full weight bearing was 64.81 ± 16.91 days; at the final follow-up, the mean AOFAS ankle-hindfoot score was 91.67 ± 3.13, the mean VAS pain score was 1.36 ± 0.50, and the mean difference in ankle dorsiflexion angle between sides was 6.06 ± 3.27 degrees. Two patients developed delayed healing of the anterior ankle incision used for distal locking screws, which healed after dressing changes, and one patient developed an infection at the tibial shaft fracture site and was treated with implant removal and antibiotic-loaded bone cement. Among the 98 patients with complete follow-up, no obvious articular redisplacement or fixation failure was observed on the available follow-up radiographs.
CONCLUSION: This retrospective case series summarized the four types of adjunctive screw corridors actually used when spiral tibial fractures involving the distal tibial articular surface were treated with intramedullary nailing combined with adjunctive screw fixation, and described the fixation target of each corridor. Representative images are used to illustrate, but do not systematically analyze, the relationship between the adjunctive screws and the intramedullary nail. These results provide descriptive information on the adjunctive fixation technique used in this cohort, and their value for guiding preoperative planning and surgical decision-making requires further validation.

articles.title: Association and incremental predictive performance of preoperative nutritional and inflammatory indices for postoperative ICU admission after hepatobiliary and pancreatic tumor surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative nutritional and inflammatory status may influence perioperative outcomes in patients undergoing hepatobiliary and pancreatic tumor surgery. This study aimed to compare the associations and incremental predictive value of six nutrition- and inflammation-related indices for postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,195 patients undergoing hepatobiliary or pancreatic tumor surgery from the INSPIRE database. We evaluated the geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI) and five other nutritional and inflammatory indices using logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. Regression estimates were pooled across 20 imputed datasets using Rubin's rules. Predictive metrics were averaged across imputations, with bootstrap assessment of uncertainty and optimism.
RESULTS: Among 1,195 patients, 141 (11.8%) experienced postoperative ICU admission. Higher transformed GNRI was associated with lower adjusted odds of ICU admission (OR 0.601, 95% CI 0.497-0.728). Adding GNRI increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.766 to 0.800 (95% CI, 0.764-0.835). The incremental AUC was 0.033 before rounding, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.780 (95% CI, 0.744-0.816). Albumin alone yielded a similar apparent AUC of 0.799. Other indices added little discrimination beyond GNRI.
CONCLUSION: GNRI showed the highest observed incremental discrimination among the six indices, although albumin alone performed similarly. These findings support further evaluation of preoperative risk assessment in hepatobiliary and pancreatic tumor surgery.

articles.title: Virtual reality goggles as a strategy to reduce preoperative anxiety.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Preoperative anxiety in pediatric patients is frequent and can be associated with unfavorable outcomes. Virtual reality has been proposed as a non-pharmacological intervention to reduce presurgical anxiety.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A prospective, non-randomized comparative pilot study in patients aged 6 to 12 years undergoing outpatient surgery. Thirty-four children were included: exposed to an immersive virtual reality experience during transport to the surgical area (n= 17) and a control group, not exposed (n= 17). Anxiety was assessed using the modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (m-YPAS) in the holding area. Subsequently, after midazolam administration, cooperation during anesthetic induction was assessed using the Induction Compliance Checklist (ICC).
RESULTS: The m-YPAS score was lower in the virtual reality group compared to the control group, without reaching statistical significance (p= 0.150), with a moderate effect size (d= 0.59). No statistically significant differences were observed in cooperation during anesthetic induction assessed by the ICC scale (p= 0.413). A positive and significant correlation was observed between the m-YPAS and ICC scores (rho= 0.664; p< 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: The use of virtual reality showed a trend toward lower levels of preoperative anxiety in patients undergoing outpatient surgery, with a moderate effect size, although without statistically significant differences. These results support the potential utility of virtual reality as a complementary intervention and justify studies with larger sample sizes and comparative designs with other strategies.

articles.title: Topical timolol in the treatment of pediatric pyogenic granuloma: A 23-case series.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pyogenic granuloma (PG) is a common benign vascular lesion in pediatric patients, characterized by rapid growth and a tendency to bleed. Surgical excision allows immediate resolution and histological confirmation, with low recurrence when including the base of the lesion, although it may require anesthesia and leave a scar. Topical timolol has emerged as a conservative alternative in selected patients.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical timolol 0.5% in the treatment of PG in pediatric patients.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Retrospective case series of 23 pediatric patients (4 months-13 years) diagnosed with PG and treated between 2018 and 2024 with a 0.5% timolol formulation applied topically over the lesion as an off-label use. Demographic and clinical variables, treatment duration, final response, need for surgery, recurrence, and documented adverse events were analyzed.
RESULTS: Ten patients (43.5%) achieved complete or near-complete resolution of the lesion, 6 (26.1%) showed a partial response at the end of treatment or prior to surgery, 5 (21.7%) did not respond or exhibited progression, and 2 (8.7%) were still receiving treatment at data cutoff. Twelve patients completed treatment without surgery; at cutoff, 14 (60.9%) had not undergone surgery, including the 2 cases still under treatment. Nine patients (39.1%) required surgery. No recurrences were documented among patients with complete or near-complete resolution during available follow-up, and no adverse events attributable to treatment were recorded.
CONCLUSIONS: Topical timolol 0.5% can be considered an initial conservative alternative in selected pediatric patients, especially when avoiding or deferring surgery or anesthesia is desired. Surgery remains a definitive option, offering immediate resolution and the possibility of histological confirmation. Prospective comparative studies are needed to define more precisely the role of timolol compared to surgical treatment.

articles.title: Anesthesia Management in Pregnant Women with Cardiac Disease: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: This review addresses the perspective of an obstetric anesthesiologist, focusing on the practical principles of peripartum anesthetic management by integrating current evidence with contemporary guideline recommendations rather than providing a comprehensive overview of cardiovascular disease during pregnancy. It also provides a clinically oriented approach to hemodynamic optimization, delivery planning, neuraxial and general anesthetic management, and the treatment of obstetric cardiac emergencies. Ultimately, this review aims to answer the question every anesthesiologist faces in daily practice: "What should the anaesthesiologist do for cardiac pregnant patient?" Cite this article as: Gunaydin DB, Camgoz Eryilmaz N, Inan G. Anesthesia management in pregnant women with cardiac disease: a narrative review. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1693, doi: 10.5152/eurasianjmed.2026.261693.

articles.title: Anesthetic Management of Pregnant Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: A Practical, Lesion-Based Clinical Review.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality and increasingly complicates pregnancy as more women with congenital and acquired heart disease reach reproductive age. Anesthetic management of these patients requires integrating lesion-specific cardiovascular physiology, pregnancy-related hemodynamic changes, obstetric considerations, and the anticipated effects of labor, anesthesia, delivery, hemorrhage, and the postpartum transition. Despite contemporary cardiovascular and obstetric guidelines, translating lesion-specific physiology into practical anesthetic decisions remains challenging. This narrative review provides a practical framework for the peripartum anesthetic management of pregnant patients with CVD. We discuss contemporary risk assessment using the modified World Health Organization 2.0 classification and the Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy II risk model, followed by principles of Pregnancy Heart Team planning, labor analgesia, cesarean delivery, monitoring, anticoagulation, uterotonic therapy, and postpartum surveillance. Lesion-specific considerations are reviewed for mitral stenosis, aortic stenosis, aortic disease and coarctation, pulmonary hypertension, pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction, peripartum cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation. Particular attention is given to maintaining appropriate preload, ventricular filling, systemic vascular resistance, cardiac rhythm, and oxygenation while avoiding abrupt changes in vascular resistance or cardiac loading conditions. The review emphasizes individualized anesthetic planning rather than universal preferences for a particular anesthetic technique or mode of delivery. Neuraxial anesthesia can be advantageous in selected patients but should be considered in the context of ventricular function, pulmonary pressures, anticoagulation, urgency, and the expected hemodynamic response. General anesthesia remains an important option when neuraxial anesthesia is contraindicated or inadequate, rapid delivery is required, airway or ventilatory control is necessary, or maternal or surgical circumstances dictate. Uterotonic therapy should similarly be individualized according to cardiovascular physiology, with careful attention to dose, route, and hemodynamic effects. Close multidisciplinary planning and coordinated postpartum care are particularly important for women with pulmonary hypertension, ventricular dysfunction, complex congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation.

articles.title: The extent of intervertebral disc removal is associated with the occurrence of Modic change after percutaneous endoscopic transforaminal discectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous endoscopic transforaminal discectomy (PETD) for lumbar disc herniation may increase the incidence of postoperative Modic change (PMC). However, whether variables reflecting the degree of intervertebral disc removal are associated with PMC is not yet investigated.
METHODS: One hundred and sixty-seven patients with lumbar disc herniation who underwent PETD were divided into 2 groups according to the presence (PMC group) or absence (NPMC group) of Modic changes within 1 year postoperative follow-up. Preoperative demographic characteristics and perioperative imaging parameters were recorded and compared between the 2 groups. Further multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed for identifying confounding and independent influencing factors. Finally, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to identify the optimal cutoff value of disc removal for the prediction of PMC.
RESULTS: Fifty-two cases (31.1%) developed PMC. At 6 months postoperatively, the visual analogue scale (VAS) of the PMC group was significantly higher than that of the control group (p < .05). Logistic regression analysis showed that reduced preoperative intervertebral disc height (p = .003), large anterior-posterior diameter of the removed intervertebral disc (p = .018), and the intervertebral disc removed crossing the midline during surgery (p < .001), and the higher Pfirrmann grade (p < .001) were independent risk factors for the occurrence of PMC.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study identified an independent association between the extent of intervertebral disc resection during PETD and the incidence of PMC. A prospective study is warranted to investigate the effect of sufficient decompression without aggressive disc resection on postoperative Modic changes.

articles.title: Complications associated with local anesthesia in dentistry: Review and considerations for a classification proposal.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Commonly occurring and known complications associated with local anesthesia and possible treatment modalities have been discussed. The dentist should recognize the symptoms and know that there may be more serious complications. This study aimed to review the literature on accidents and complications associated with dental local anesthetics and propose a classification based on anatomical depth and clinical presentation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus until June 2025. The keywords were based on MeSH and DeCS terms related to dental anesthesia and its complications. In vivo studies, case reports, and case series in oral surgery were included. After reviewing 364 records, 28 studies met the inclusion criteria. Data on study characteristics, type of anesthesia, complications, and treatment were extracted.
RESULTS: Complications were more frequent with inferior alveolar nerve blocks. Local events included puncture fractures, paresthesia, hematoma, ischemia, infections, and trismus. Systemic complications included syncope, toxicity, vasoconstrictive reactions, and allergies. While many resolved spontaneously, others required surgical or pharmacological intervention. A new classification based on the anatomical planes affected (superficial, deep, neurological, and orbitoocular) and systemic categories is proposed, facilitating recognition and treatment.
CONCLUSION: Local anesthetics, although widely used and generally safe, can cause various complications in oral surgery. The proposed classification systematizes these events and may improve diagnostic clarity, prevention strategies, and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pre-anaesthetic Evaluation and Perioperative Planning: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Preanesthetic evaluation is essential for perioperative safety, yet it remains time-consuming, heavily reliant on documentation, and vulnerable to variability in data collection, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. The increase in surgical cases, patient complexity, and digital health records has created opportunities for artificial intelligence (AI) to assist anesthesiologists in preoperative screening, risk assessment, and perioperative planning. New AI applications in anesthesiology include machine learning models for predicting perioperative risks, natural language processing (NLP) systems for extracting key information from unstructured records, and large language model (LLM)-based tools for documentation support and structured clinical summaries. Studies indicate these systems may enhance workflow efficiency, expand preanesthetic data collection, aid ASA physical status classification, and generate structured recommendations for investigations, optimization, and anesthetic plans, all with clinician oversight. This review explores the current role of AI in preanesthetic evaluation and perioperative planning, focusing on practical uses such as automated history synthesis, investigation choices, risk stratification, preoperative orders, and personalized anesthetic decision support. It also addresses system limitations like hallucination, bias, privacy issues, lack of explainability, and medicolegal concerns. Based on current evidence, AI is best suited as a decision-support tool for clinicians rather than a standalone replacement for anesthesiologists.

articles.title: Pre-operative proton pump inhibitor use is associated with increased post-operative complications following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are frequently prescribed in the perioperative setting for gastrointestinal prophylaxis. However, emerging evidence suggests that pre-operative PPI exposure may influence post-operative outcomes through effects on host immune function, nutritional status, and bone metabolism. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between pre-operative PPI use and post-operative complications following anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients undergoing primary anatomic TSA between 2005 and 2023 were stratified by pre-operative PPI use. Patients with a history of gastrointestinal bleeding were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed for demographic characteristics, modified frailty index variables, additional comorbidities, medications, and body mass index, yielding 7,075 patients per cohort. Ninety-day medical and 1-year and 2-year surgical complications were compared using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Within 90 days, PPI exposure was associated with increased risks of readmission and acute kidney injury. Rates of emergency department utilization were also higher among patients receiving PPIs, whereas differences in pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, post-operative infection, and stroke did not reach statistical significance. At 1 year, perioperative PPI use was associated with significantly higher rates of periprosthetic joint infection (1.7% vs. 1.2%; RR, 1.45; P = .008), dislocation (2.0% vs. 1.5%; RR, 1.33; P = .027), aseptic loosening (0.8% vs. 0.4%; RR, 1.71; P = .016), and mortality (1.2% vs. 0.9%; RR, 1.40; P = .044). At 2 years, PPI use remained associated with increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (2.4% vs. 1.6%; RR, 1.52; P < .001) and mortality (2.5% vs. 1.7%; RR, 1.48; P = .001). No significant differences were observed in revision arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, dislocation, or aseptic loosening at 2 years.
CONCLUSION: Pre-operative PPI use following TSA was associated with increased early medical complications and higher rates of implant-related complications at midterm follow-up. These findings highlight the importance of careful medication review and risk stratification in patients undergoing anatomic TSA.

articles.title: Post-operative results of Bentall surgery at a national reference center in Peru.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the mortality and postoperative complications of patients undergoing Bentall-DeBono surgery at the Cardiovascular Surgery Service of the National Cardiovascular Institute, EsSalud, Lima, Peru, between 2019 and 2024.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a single-center, retrospective, descriptive, case series observational study of patients undergoing composite valve-conduit replacement (Bentall-De Bono procedure) for aortic root pathology between January 2019 and December 2024. The primary objective was to determine all-cause mortality and major complications.
RESULTS: Sixty-three patients underwent Bentall-De Bono surgery. The median age was 58 years (IQR: 40-71), and 19% of patients had Marfan syndrome. The 30-day mortality rate was 7.9% (5 patients). The main complications were: stroke (6.3%), perioperative myocardial infarction (4.8%), permanent pacemaker implantation (11%), and excessive postoperative bleeding (6.3%). The median length of hospital stay was 17 days, and the median length of stay in the ICU was 4 days. In a median follow-up of 745 days (403-1060), the mortality rate was 14%, the stroke rate was 7.9%, the myocardial infarction rate was 4.8%, and the definitive pacemaker implantation rate was 14%.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results for the Bentall-De Bono procedure are acceptable and comparable to those reported in the international literature.

articles.title: Erector spinae plane block within ERAS protocols reduces analgesic requirements in aged, high-risk patients after MIS-TLIF: a propensity score-matched analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Managing postoperative pain in frail spine surgery patients remains a clinical dilemma due to conventional analgesic risks.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the perioperative benefits and 1-year functional outcomes of integrating the erector spinae plane block (ESPB) into an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol for patients undergoing minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (MIS-TLIF) for degenerative lumbar disorders.
RESULTS: Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline differences between the ERAS + ESPB group (n = 100) and the ERAS-alone group (n = 170). After matching, the ESPB group demonstrated significantly lower morphine equivalent doses (mean 30.15 mg vs. 40.09 mg, p < .05), a shorter length of hospital stays (mean 2.58 days vs. 4.01 days, p < .001), and earlier mobilization. Subgroup analysis revealed that these benefits were singularly pronounced in aged (≥70 years) and high-risk (CCI ≥ 3) patients, suggesting a lowered recovery threshold for vulnerable individuals. However, at the 1-year follow-up, both groups exhibited comparable outcomes in Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Physical Component Summary (PCS), and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores, alongside similar rates of achieving the minimal clinically important difference (MCID).
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ESPB into an ERAS protocol significantly optimizes the acute recovery phase by reducing opioid dependency and accelerating hospital discharge, particularly for elderly and high-comorbidity patients. Although these perioperative advantages do not alter the 1-year functional prognosis, ESPB serves as a critical facilitator of perioperative safety and resource efficiency in high-risk surgical candidates.

articles.title: Silver diamine fluoride for the treatment of dental caries: A comprehensive review of the literature.
articles.abstract: Silver diamine fluoride (SDF) is an aqueous solution of silver (Ag+) and fluoride (F-) ions stabilized by ammonia. It is regarded by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a safe, efficacious and cost-effective pharmacological agent for the minimally invasive management of dental caries. The Ag+ ions in SDF mainly exert an antibacterial effect, while the F- ions remineralize dental tissues. Recently, SDF has also been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for desensitization. The main advantages of SDF over other treatment options are its shorter application time, ease of application and no need for anesthesia. Furthermore, it is suitable for individuals with physical or mental disabilities, non-ambulatory patients, and elderly patients, as it can also be applied by dental nurses, hygienists and healthcare workers. Various studies have confirmed the efficacy of SDF in arresting and preventing coronal and root caries, desensitizing teeth, and disinfecting root canals, highlighting its potential to reduce the global healthcare and economic burden associated with untreated dental caries. The aim of this review is to provide an updated overview of SDF properties and its use in the minimally invasive management of dental caries.

articles.title: The Evaluation of Estrogen and Tacrolimus in an Experimental Sciatic Nerve Injury Model Following Bipolar Electrocautery in an Animal Model.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Iatrogenic peripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) cause neurogenic deficits because of the limited regeneration potential of nerves and scar formation. This study evaluates the effects of tacrolimus and estrogen on sciatic nerve healing following its lesion by bipolar electrocautery in rats.
MATERIALS & METHODS: Twenty-five mature female Wistar rats were included in this study. The rats were kept under the same photoperiod 12:12 for one week. The rats were divided into five groups as follows: Sham, DW (distilled water), Tacrolimus (Tac), Estrogen (Est), and Tacrolimus + Estrogen (Tac + Est). All rats were anesthetized, and the left sciatic nerve was cauterized by bipolar electrocautery, except for the rats in the sham group. Treatments were given for 28 days after the injury; on day 28, clinical, electrophysiological, and histopathological evaluations were carried out. The Rota-rod performance test, sciatic functional index (SFI), electromyography (EMG) latency, and toe-out angle (TOA) were carried out for evaluation of functional nerve recovery. Finally, the rats were humanly euthanized and samples of sciatic nerve tissue were submitted for histopathological evaluation on day 28.
RESULTS: There was no statistically significant difference in SFI (P=0.249) among the groups. In the Rota rod tests, the Est group showed significantly greater motor function improvement compared with the DW (distilled water), Tac, and Est + Tac groups (P<0.01). Mean EMG latency in the DW group was significantly longer than in the sham (P<0.001), Tac (P=0.023) and Est + Tac (P=0.012) groups. Axonal swelling and inflammatory cell infiltration were less in the Tac, Est, and Est + Tac groups compared with the DW group (P<0.01). There was no significant difference among the Tac, Est, and Est + Tac groups in EMG latency. Therefore, tacrolimus and estrogen each showed a neuroprotective effect based on histopathological results. Motor function improvement and reduced inflammation were statistically significant in the Est and Tac groups, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The findings of this investigation did not confirm a significant impact of the combination of estrogen plus tacrolimus compared with the estrogen and tacrolimus groups in functional recovery and inflammation.

articles.title: Inter-Individual Variation in LUNG Mechanics Assessed by the Non-Invasive PEEP-Step Method During Laparoscopic and Robotic Surgery Indicates Need for Individualized Ventilatory Settings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During laparoscopic surgery, abdominal carbon dioxide (CO2) insufflation in the supine position and with head-down tilt for robotic surgery increases abdominal pressure and pushes the diaphragm cranially. This causes a decrease in end-expiratory lung volume and in lung and chest wall compliance. These effects can be counteracted by the application of PEEP. Our study aimed to measure lung and chest wall mechanics during laparoscopic surgery using a non-invasive method (PEEP-step method) and to determine the optimal PEEP level for each patient.
METHODS: Thirty-two patients scheduled for abdominal surgery participated in this observational study with pneumoperitoneum. Fourteen patients underwent surgery for pelvic conditions in head-down position and 18 in supine position. Data from the ventilator was collected and analysed with a dedicated software, which calculated lung compliance and transpulmonary pressure from a two-step PEEP increase. Measurements were performed after induction, after pneumoperitoneum in supine/tilt head-down and before emergence.
RESULTS: Lung and chest wall compliance decreased during CO2 insufflation with high individual variation, and we observed a≈90% increase in transpulmonary driving pressure. After CO2-desufflation, lung and chest wall compliance returned to near baseline levels on a group level. However, 19 patients had a remaining reduction in lung compliance, six with 20%-50%. Optimal PEEP level calculated by the software was twice the clinical routine level.
CONCLUSIONS: The study found substantial individual variation in lung compliance during laparoscopic surgery in patients without evident lung disease. This variability does not align well with respiratory system compliance. The findings highlight the need for individualized ventilator settings based on lung- rather than respiratory system mechanics. The PEEP-step method may be a non-invasive, real-time bedside tool to identify patients who would benefit from higher PEEP to preserve lung volume and possibly prevent postoperative complications.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: Laparascopic surgical conditions can affect lung mechanics, though not always predictably. This study examined how a test of higher or lower PEEP directly after anaesthesia induction might inform PEEP optimization in the same cases undergoing laparoscopic surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04484727, 2022-05-01).

articles.title: Risk of red blood cell transfusion in patients with preoperative anemia requiring cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative anemia is common and a strong predictor of perioperative red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in cardiac surgical patients. Both anemia and RBC transfusion are independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes, but their interrelationship is difficult to disentangle because RBC transfusion acts as a mediator rather than a confounder.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the relationship between preoperative anemia, RBC transfusion, and postoperative outcomes in cardiac surgery, with particular emphasis on recent advances in causal inference mediation analysis. We discuss outcome-specific mediation patterns, patient characteristics that may modify anemia and transfusion related risk, and implications for perioperative management.
EXPERT OPINION: Mediation analysis provides a valuable framework for distinguishing the direct effects of anemia from RBC transfusion-mediated effects. Current evidence suggests that RBC transfusion mediates a substantial proportion of anemia-associated mortality, whereas direct anemia effects appear more important for renal complications. Future patient blood management should move beyond uniform transfusion thresholds toward individualized strategies that account for patient's risk profile, physiological reserve, intraoperative factors and the outcome-specific balance between the potential benefits of correcting anemia and the risks of RBC transfusion.

articles.title: Cardiac output monitoring using an automatic arm cuff device in surgical patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulse contour devices estimate cardiac output (CO) from an invasive arterial blood pressure waveform. However, arterial catheters are generally used only in higher-risk patients. By contrast, automatic arm cuff devices are used for noninvasive BP monitoring in almost all hospital patients. Furthermore, these devices measure cuff pressure oscillations, which are directly related to pulsatile blood volume rather than BP. We hypothesised that automatic arm cuff devices can offer an effective means to monitor CO.
METHODS: A custom-built cuff device was used to measure cuff pressure and make a unique measurement of the volume of air pumped into and out of the cuff during linear deflation.
