Cuff device measurements, an invasive BP waveform from a radial artery catheter, and reference CO from pulmonary artery catheter bolus thermodilution were obtained during interventions from 24 liver transplant and 10 cardiac surgery patients (191 measurement sets). A basic analysis was applied to estimate CO in L min-1 as the product of heart rate, the maximum cuff pressure oscillation amplitude, the cuff-arm system compliance (derived from the cuff pressure-volume relationship), and the body-to-arm surface area ratio (derived from anthropometric information).
RESULTS: The arm cuff-based method yielded a correlation of 0.61 (95% confidence interval 0.37-0.79) and a concordance rate of 83% (75%-91%) against the reference CO. For comparison, classic pulse contour analysis of the invasive BP waveform produced a correlation of 0.59 (0.37-0.75) and a concordance rate of 81% (72%-90%).
CONCLUSIONS: These initial findings suggest potential for convenient CO monitoring using an automatic arm cuff device in surgical patients.

articles.title: Dietitian involvement and nutritional care organization in intensive care and perioperative settings in France: a cross-sectional survey of healthcare professionals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutrition is a key component of care for critically ill and surgical patients, but the organization of nutritional care and the involvement of dietitians in ICU and perioperative pathways remain variable. This survey aimed to describe respondent-reported nutritional care organization and dietitian involvement among healthcare professionals working in ICU and perioperative settings in France, with a focus on dietitian availability, clinical involvement, nutritional governance, and selected aspects of perioperative care.
METHODS: We conducted a voluntary cross-sectional survey among physicians and dietitians working in French ICU and perioperative settings. The survey was disseminated during the French Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care Medicine congress, through national professional nutrition and dietetics networks, and via social media. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: Overall, 147 professionals responded, mainly ICU physicians and dietitians, and most worked in university hospitals. Among respondents, dietitian availability was reported in 67% of responses, but dedicated time was frequently limited. Involvement was mainly request-based, and participation in medical meetings or ward rounds was uncommon. A medical nutrition lead was identified in 44% of responses, a written nutrition protocol in 50%, and a task-sharing protocol allowing dietitian prescription in 9%.
CONCLUSION: Reported practices suggest that dietitians are available in many French ICUs and contribute to perioperative care pathways. However, access to dietetic expertise does not necessarily translate into dedicated staffing, routine multidisciplinary participation, or structured nutritional governance. Strengthening local organization through medical leadership, written protocols, and multidisciplinary collaboration may help improve the implementation of nutritional care.

articles.title: Factors associated with the ionized-to-total magnesium ratio in major hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery: a single-center prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify perioperative factors associated with the ionized-to-total magnesium (iMg/tMg) ratio at intensive care unit (ICU) admission and on postoperative day (POD) 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled adults undergoing elective surgery. Paired iMg and tMg measurements were obtained at ICU admission and on POD 1. The primary analyses evaluated perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio at each time point using univariable linear regression and multivariable linear regression with backward elimination. Exploratory analyses assessed temporal changes using paired t tests.
RESULTS: Of 150 enrolled patients, 141 were analyzed. At ICU admission, the ratio was positively associated with iMg immediately after anesthesia induction (P = 0.007) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (P = 0.041), and negatively associated with anesthesia time (P = 0.005) and total cholesterol (P = 0.018). On POD 1, the ratio was positively associated with intraoperative non-Mg-containing fluid volume (P = 0.016), and negatively associated with operation time (P < 0.001), hypertension (P = 0.013), and albumin (P = 0.007). Model R2 values were 0.10 and 0.20 at ICU admission and on POD 1, respectively. In exploratory analyses, the mean ratio increased between postoperative measurements (0.659 to 0.713; P < 0.001). Mean iMg decreased from 0.589 mmol/L after induction to 0.545 at ICU admission, then increased to 0.640 on POD 1 (all P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Perioperative factors associated with the iMg/tMg ratio differed between ICU admission and POD 1 after major open hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. Both models had limited explanatory power. These findings should be interpreted in relation to sampling time and require independent validation before informing clinical management.

articles.title: Video double-lumen tube intubation in a modified lateral position for unilateral video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate and report a protocol for video double-lumen tube (VDLT) intubation in a modified lateral position and evaluate whether it shortens in-room to cut time (IRCT; defined as the time from patient entry to incision) compared with conventional supine intubation in patients undergoing elective unilateral video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre, prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial at a tertiary university hospital in Xi'an, China. We enrolled adults aged 18-75 yr (American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status I-III) scheduled for elective unilateral VATS requiring VDLT intubation; exclusions included body mass index > 30 kg·m-2, mouth opening < 3 cm, Mallampati class 3-4, or anticipated difficult airway. Participants were randomized 1:1 to modified-lateral-position (Group L) or supine-position (Group S) VDLT intubation using a computer-generated sequence with sealed-envelope allocation concealment. Operators were unblinded; nonoperator staff collecting postoperative data and the outcome analyst were blinded to allocation. The primary outcome was IRCT.
RESULTS: Sixty-two patients were randomized (Group L, N = 31; Group S, N = 31), and all were analyzed for the primary outcome. Mean (standard deviation [SD]) IRCT was shorter in Group L (18.1 [2.0] min) than in Group S (31.1 [3.3] min), with a mean difference (L-S) of -13.0 min (95% confidence interval [CI], -14.4 to -11.6; P < 0.001). Intubation time was similar (mean [SD], 103 [15] sec vs 97 [15] sec; P = 0.10). Video double-lumen tube malpositioning occurred in 1/31 (3%) cases in Group L vs 15/31 (48%) cases in Group S (relative risk [RR], 0.067; 95% CI, 0.009 to 0.474; P < 0.001). Sore throat within 48 h occurred in 9/31 (29%) patients in Group L vs 18/31 (58%) patients in Group S (RR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.27 to 0.94; P = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing unilateral VATS, VDLT intubation in a modified lateral position shortened IRCT. In exploratory analyses, several secondary outcomes favoured this approach. Intubation in a modified lateral position may be a feasible alternative to conventional supine position intubation in these patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR.org.cn ( ChiCTR2500112254 ); first posted 21 October 2025.

articles.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.
DESIGN: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: 15 thoracic centres in the UK.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications.
RESULTS: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.
CONCLUSIONS: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03677856.

articles.title: Pharmacological Prevention of Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: Why Trials Failed and a Reimagined Endpoint Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury affects approximately one in four adults and is independently associated with perioperative mortality and progression to chronic kidney disease. Despite more than two decades of randomized pharmacological trials, few have met their primary endpoint.
METHODS: This invited narrative review examined 33 pivotal randomized trials of pharmacological prevention published from 2004 to 2026, grouped by mechanism, and related population, intervention timing, and endpoint selection to trial outcome.
RESULTS: Trials using short-term creatinine-based kidney injury endpoints produced the positive signals, whereas trials using major adverse kidney events at 90 days as the primary endpoint were negative. This divergence reflects both the low power of that composite for detecting injury prevention and unresolved biology, since no agent has shown benefit on both types of endpoint. Positive trials shared a matched mechanism, a defined population, and an aligned endpoint. Recurrent failure modes were endpoint misalignment, mismatch between population and the timing of injury, confounding by postoperative cardiac recovery, and direct drug effects on creatinine or urine output that mimic or mask injury.
CONCLUSIONS: We propose a trial framework with persistent stage 2 or 3 acute kidney disease at 30 days, by Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria, as the primary endpoint; preoperative albuminuria as an enrichment criterion; and attenuation of the postoperative rise in albuminuria at 30 and 90 days as a key secondary endpoint. Platform designs with biomarker-enriched enrollment could convert the next generation of trials into interpretable tests of kidney protection.

articles.title: Chronic postsurgical pain after minimally invasive cardiac surgery via mini-thoracotomy: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mini-thoracotomy cardiac surgery avoids sternotomy but requires intercostal access, and persistent pain after this approach is poorly characterized. We determined the frequency and intensity of chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) 3 months after cardiac surgery via anterolateral mini-thoracotomy and described its sensory features.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02660749), adults undergoing on-pump mitral valve or septal defect surgery through a 5-cm anterolateral mini-thoracotomy received standardized multimodal analgesia. Pain was rated on a 0-10 visual analog scale (VAS). At 3 months, current pain, post-discharge pain descriptors and sensory findings were recorded. CPSP was defined as pain (VAS ≥ 1) at the incision area at 3 months in patients without pre-existing chronic pain; VAS ≥ 4 was considered moderate-to-severe.
RESULTS: Of 80 registered patients, 56 who underwent mini-thoracotomy were analyzed. CPSP was present in 33 patients (58.9%; 95% confidence interval [CI] 45.9-70.8%), but it was mild in all of them: 32 rated their pain as VAS 1 and one as VAS 3, and no patient reported moderate-to-severe pain (0%; 95% CI 0-6.4%). Hypoesthesia (71.4%) and numbness (58.9%) were frequent regardless of CPSP status. Electric shock-like pain was more frequent in patients with CPSP (30.3% vs. 4.3%; p = 0.019) in an unadjusted exploratory comparison. Perioperative and in-hospital pain variables were not associated with CPSP.
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent pain 3 months after mini-thoracotomy cardiac surgery was common but uniformly mild, and moderate-to-severe CPSP was not observed. Sensory disturbances were frequent. CPSP after minimally invasive cardiac surgery should be reported with its intensity, not prevalence alone.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02660749 (https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02660749) registered retrospectively on 18 January 2016.

articles.title: In-Hospital Stroke in Patients with Cardiac Conditions: Do Cardiac Procedures Impact Stroke Outcomes?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: It is unclear if stroke occurring after cardiac procedures is more severe than stroke associated with cardiac conditions without procedures. We compared in-hospital acute ischemic stroke patients admitted with a cardiac diagnosis who did versus did not undergo cardiac procedures.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed adults with in-hospital stroke admitted with a primary cardiac diagnosis in Alberta (2018-2022). Patients were categorized into no prior cardiac procedure, cardiac procedure, or cardiac surgery within 30 days of stroke diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations between exposure groups and outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 499 patients (median age 70 years IQR [62-77], 36.7% women), 116 (23.2%) underwent a cardiac procedure, and 227 (45.5%) underwent cardiac surgery prior to stroke diagnosis. Median time from procedure to stroke diagnosis was 1.75 days (IQR 0.87-3.83). In-hospital mortality was 34.6%, 24.1% and 22.5% in patients with no prior procedure, cardiac procedures and cardiac surgery, respectively. After adjustment for age, sex, facility level and comorbidities, no significant differences were observed in mortality (cardiac procedure vs no procedure: aOR 0.73, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.40-1.33; cardiac surgery vs no procedure: aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.42-1.45). Among procedural patients, strokes recognized ≥2 days post-procedure were associated with higher mortality (2-7 days: OR 2.31, [1.18-4.52]; 8-30 days: OR 3.23, [1.59-6.59]).
CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted mortality did not differ by cardiac procedural status, although residual confounding is possible. Later stroke recognition after cardiac procedures was associated with higher mortality, identifying a high-risk monitoring window.

articles.title: Effect of pneumatic leg compression on post-induction hypotension in adult patients with isolated traumatic brain injury undergoing decompressive craniotomy: a randomised, double-blind, controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-induction hypotension is common after induction of general anaesthesia, and in traumatic brain injury even a brief fall in systemic pressure can compromise cerebral perfusion when autoregulation is already impaired. Pneumatic leg compression augments venous return and has reduced post-induction hypotension in obstetric and urological surgery, but has not been examined in neurotrauma patients undergoing decompressive craniotomy.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomised, double-blind trial, adults aged 18-65 years with isolated traumatic brain injury and radiological features of severity (midline shift ≥5 mm with basal cistern effacement) undergoing decompressive craniotomy were allocated 1:1 to a pneumatic compression device activated before induction (Group PC) or an identical device left inactive (Group NC). The primary outcome was the incidence of post-induction hypotension, defined as any recorded one-minute systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg within 20 minutes of induction. Secondary outcomes included the haemodynamic trend, fluid and vasopressor requirement, arterial blood gas changes, and device-related complications up to 72 hours. Analysis was by modified intention-to-treat.
RESULTS: Of 90 randomised patients, 89 were analysed (Group NC, n=44; Group PC, n=45). Post-induction hypotension occurred in 33.3% of Group PC patients compared with 59.1% of Group NC patients (risk ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.35-0.91; risk difference -25.8 percentage points, 95% CI -45.8 to -5.7; P=0.015). Baseline systolic pressure, recorded after the device had been active for 10 minutes, was higher in Group PC, but adjustment for it did not change the estimate (adjusted risk ratio 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.93). Time-weighted average systolic pressure over the first 20 minutes was higher in Group PC (baseline-adjusted difference 6.0 mmHg, 95% CI 1.8-10.2), although the fall from baseline did not differ between groups. Fewer Group PC patients required mephentermine (15.9% vs 40.9%; risk ratio 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.84) or phenylephrine (8.9% vs 36.4%; risk ratio 0.24, 95% CI 0.09-0.67); noradrenaline was used too rarely (2 vs 1 patients) for comparison. Hypotension after the first 20 minutes (17.8% vs 25.0%; risk ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.32-1.60), arterial pH, base excess and lactate did not differ. No device-related complications were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Activating pneumatic leg compression before induction reduced post-induction hypotension and early vasopressor use in patients undergoing decompressive craniotomy for isolated traumatic brain injury, with no device-related complications observed in this cohort. The effect demonstrated is systemic and haemodynamic; whether it improves cerebral perfusion or neurological outcome requires larger, multicentre trials.

articles.title: Awake Craniotomy for Eloquent and Near-Eloquent Brain Tumors Without MRI or Intraoperative Neuromonitoring During the Gaza War: A Six-Patient Case Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe patient selection, intraoperative neurological assessment, and postoperative observations in six awake brain tumor resections performed without MRI or electrical stimulation mapping during the Gaza war.
METHODS: We reviewed six awake procedures undertaken at two Gaza neurosurgical services between February 2025 and July 2026. CT guided anatomical planning; patients remained awake with scalp block, local infiltration, and anesthesiologist-supervised sedation. The operating surgeon performed motor or language assessment appropriate to the lesion location. Operative records, available CT descriptions, and subsequent clinical clarifications informed the analysis.
RESULTS: Among 125 tumor craniotomies reported by the participating services, six were performed awake; the number eligible for awake surgery was not recorded. All six procedures were completed without conversion to general anesthesia or a reported intraoperative clinical functional change. Five resections were judged complete by the surgeon and one intentionally subtotal, without MRI-based volumetric verification. One patient developed postoperative right hemiplegia with only partial improvement reported about one week later and died three months after surgery. The five other patients had reported follow-up of 1-18 months (median, 9 months). CT lesion dimensions were supplied for all cases, but source imaging was not independently re-reviewed. The surgeon recalled operative durations of approximately two to three hours.
CONCLUSIONS: Awake clinical examination provided limited real-time functional feedback when standard mapping tools were unavailable. These observations do not establish comparative safety, complete resection, or equivalence to stimulation mapping. Their relevance lies in the operative choices, limitations, and postoperative morbidity documented under resource constraints.

articles.title: The impact of robot-assisted frameless brain biopsy on performance differences between junior and senior neurosurgeons.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Frameless stereotactic brain biopsy is a standardized and routinely performed neurosurgical procedure, frequently carried out by residents under supervision in academic centers. Robot-assisted (RA) guidance has been introduced to standardize workflow and reduce operator-dependent variability. This study investigates whether RA frameless biopsy reduces experience-related performance differences between residents and attending neurosurgeons compared with a manually operated frameless system (MFS).
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, non-randomized cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing RA frameless stereotactic brain biopsy for intracranial lesions at a tertiary academic center between 2021 and 2025. Outcomes included perioperative complications, diagnostic yield, and operative time, stratified by surgeon experience level (residents vs. attendings). Results were compared with those of a cohort operated with a MFS.
RESULTS: A total of 98 procedures were analyzed (49 RA, 49 MFS). Across the entire cohort, total operative time was longer with RA than with MFS (115.6 ± 34.1 vs. 97.9 ± 27.2 minutes; p = 0.0036), primarily due to longer setup times. Diagnostic yield and complication rates were comparable between systems. Importantly, subgroup analysis demonstrated that residents using RA achieved operative times, diagnostic yield, and complication rates comparable to attending surgeons. In the MFS cohort, total operative time did not differ significantly between residents and attendings.
CONCLUSIONS: RA-assisted biopsy was associated with comparable diagnostic accuracy and safety relative to MFS. Robotic assistance was associated with smaller observed differences in operative efficiency between residents and attending surgeons, suggesting a potential role in bridging experience-related performance differences during neurosurgical training.

articles.title: CD55-targeted modulation of C3-mediated microglia polarization improves perioperative neurocognitive disorders in male mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are common postoperative complications driven by neuroinflammation and an imbalance in microglial M1/M2 polarization. Complement component 3 (C3) is elevated in PND, while CD55 inhibits C3 activation. Whether CD55 regulates PND via C3 remains unclear.
METHODS: A PND mouse model and an lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced BV2 model were established. Lentivirus-mediated CD55/C3 overexpression was performed. Cognitive function, neuronal injury, inflammation, microglial polarization, and CD55/C3 expression were assessed using behavioral tests, HE staining, ELISA, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR, and WB.
RESULTS: PND mice exhibited cognitive impairment, hippocampal neuronal damage, elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and C3, and reduced CD55 expression. Overexpression of CD55 improved cognitive function, alleviated damage and inflammation, and suppressed C3. It also restored the balance of M1/M2 markers in BV2 cells. Overexpression of C3 reversed the protective effects of CD55 both in vitro and in vivo.
CONCLUSION: CD55 alleviates PND by regulating complement C3, which may be related to promoting the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. We have preliminarily identified a potential regulatory target for PND.

articles.title: Rethinking the timing of congenital ptosis repair: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: The optimal timing of congenital ptosis repair remains uncertain when visual development is not immediately threatened. We review the available evidence to distinguish indications for prompt surgery, earlier elective repair, and active surveillance. Visual-axis obstruction or documented or progressive deprivation amblyopia warrants surgery once the child is medically suitable for anesthesia, with intervention within the first 6 months serving as a reasonable pragmatic target. Without an immediate visual threat, earlier elective repair may be considered for significant superior visual-field restriction, documented binocular dysfunction, compensatory chin elevation, functional limitations, or psychosocial concerns. Refractive abnormalities should be treated directly and monitored rather than used alone to determine surgical timing. Laterality, ocular-surface status, procedure suitability, postoperative monitoring, and anesthetic exposure may modify timing. Observation is appropriate for mild, asymptomatic ptosis with normal visual development and reliable follow-up. Direct age-comparative evidence remains sparse and confounded and does not support routine deferral until school age. Clinicians should individualize timing through shared decision-making and reassess it as the child's visual, functional, psychosocial, and surgical circumstances evolve.

articles.title: Virtual reality as a non-pharmacological intervention for pediatric preoperative anxiety: A quality improvement initiative and retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract: Preoperative anxiety affects a majority of children undergoing surgery and is associated with adverse perioperative and psychological outcomes. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising non-pharmacological option, but real-world implementation data remain limited. We report a nine-month quality-improvement (QI) initiative that implemented a custom VR intervention in a pediatric preoperative holding area, followed by retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data. Using a single-arm, pre-post design without a comparison group, we evaluated within-subject changes in self-reported distress and fear, physiological indicators, and stakeholder experience in 80 children aged 6-15 years. Between the pre-VR and immediately post-VR assessments, distress (0-10 Numerical Rating Scale) decreased by a median of 2.0 points (median 3.0 to 1.0; p < 0.001) and fear (0-4 Children's Fear Scale) by a median of 1.0 point (1.0 to 0.0; p < 0.001). Heart rate fell by a mean of 5.8 beats/min and systolic blood pressure by 4.1 mmHg (both p < 0.001). Acceptance was high: 91% of children were willing to use VR again, 95% of parents would recommend it, and all participating nurses endorsed it, with few, minor adverse effects (3 of 80). In this uncontrolled QI initiative, VR was feasible and safe to implement and was accompanied by clinically meaningful within-subject reductions in anxiety and physiological arousal. Because the design included no comparison group, these changes cannot be attributed to VR alone and may partly reflect natural settling, acclimation, non-specific attention, or regression to the mean. Controlled trials are needed to establish comparative effectiveness before routine adoption.

articles.title: Evolution of surgical management for pediatric hepatic hydatid disease: open versus standardized laparoscopic approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgery remains the mainstay of treatment for hepatic cystic echinococcosis (CE) in children, but the laparoscopic approach is incompletely standardized, particularly for giant, multisegment, and posterior-superior cysts. We report the evolution of surgical management following the establishment of a dedicated hepatopancreatobiliary minimally invasive program and compare a standardized laparoscopic technique with conventional open surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center comparative cohort study included pediatric patients who underwent surgery for hepatic CE between January 2020 and January 2025, grouped by surgical approach (open vs. laparoscopic). Perioperative outcomes, complications (Clavien-Dindo), and recurrence were analyzed. Independent predictors of recurrence were assessed by multivariable Firth logistic regression. Given the differing follow-up duration, recurrence was additionally expressed per 100 patient-years and evaluated with a 12-month landmark analysis and Kaplan-Meier/log-rank testing.
RESULTS: Of 63 children, 39 (61.9%) underwent open and 24 (38.1%) laparoscopic surgery, with comparable age, cyst size, multiplicity, WHO stage, and localization. Laparoscopy was associated with significantly shorter operative time (59.4 ± 8.5 vs. 123.2 ± 35.2 min, P < 0.0001), lower ICU use (4.2% vs. 100%, P < 0.0001), and shorter hospital stay (4.1 ± 1.1 vs. 7.1 ± 1.4 days, P < 0.0001), with no conversions. Complications (8.3% vs. 12.8%, P = 0.699) and recurrence (4.2% vs. 12.8%, P = 0.394) were comparable. After adjustment for follow-up, recurrence rates were similar (4.78 vs. 4.99 per 100 patient-years; incidence rate ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.02-8.56), and the 12-month landmark analysis showed no early excess recurrence after laparoscopy (log-rank P = 0.73). On multivariable analysis, albendazole treatment compliance-not surgical approach-was the dominant independent protective factor against recurrence (OR 0.006, 95% CI 0.00002-0.085, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In children with hepatic CE, recurrence was associated with albendazole treatment compliance rather than surgical approach; a standardized laparoscopic technique achieved shorter operative time, less ICU use, and shorter hospitalization than open surgery, with comparable safety and recurrence.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Supraclavicular Brachiocephalic Vein Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Hematological Disorders: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central venous access is indispensable for clinical management of pediatric patients with hematological disorders, including chemotherapy administration, blood product transfusion, and critical rescue. Repeated venipuncture attempts, procedural failure, postoperative catheter malposition, and cannulation-related complications can substantially disrupt subsequent treatment courses and compromise therapeutic efficacy.
AIMS: This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of ultrasound-guided brachiocephalic vein (BCV) cannulation, with the goal of optimizing central venous catheterization protocols, reducing procedure-related adverse events, and improving the efficiency and safety of treatment via central venous access in pediatric patients.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 580 children (303 subclavian vein [SCV], 277 BCV) who underwent ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization between January 2021 and December 2024. We compared first-attempt success rate, overall success rate, procedural duration, intraoperative adverse events, postoperative complications, and catheter malposition. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to improve comparability between the groups with respect to measured baseline covariates. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors.
RESULTS: After IPTW, the BCV approach was associated with a higher first-attempt success rate (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.05-2.81; risk difference [RD] = 0.119, 95% CI: 0.015-0.222) and a higher overall success rate (RD = 0.091, 95% CI: 0.013-0.168). The mean procedural duration was 6 min shorter in the BCV group (95% CI: -9.5 to -2.5). The BCV approach was independently associated with lower odds of intraoperative malposition (OR = 0.096, 95% CI: 0.037-0.249), postoperative malposition (OR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.16-0.74), and perioperative complications (OR = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.08-0.94). Multivariable regression analysis showed that catheterization approach was independently associated with catheter malposition.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with SCV, ultrasound-guided BCV cannulation is associated with higher success rates, shorter procedural duration, and fewer malpositions and complications. This technique may offer particular benefits for children with hematological disorders.

articles.title: The impact of gestational weight gain on perineal injury in primiparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to determine the association between gestational weight gain (GWG) and the risk of perineal injury in nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study (January 2012-January 2024) at a single tertiary center including nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI (18.5-24.9 kg/m2) who delivered a singleton, live, term infant (≥37 weeks) vaginally, excluding pregestational or gestational diabetes. Participants were stratified by GWG per American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists guidelines (recommended 11.5-16 kg) into below-, within-, and above-recommended GWG groups. The primary outcome was perineal injury (1st-4th degree). Multivariable logistic regression assessed the independent association between GWG and perineal trauma.
RESULTS: Of 26 828 women, a total of 9019 (33.6%) had below-, 11 527 (43.0%) within-, and 6282 (23.4%) above-recommended GWG. Overall perineal injury was more common with above-recommended GWG (86.4% vs. 84.9% vs. 84.2%, P = 0.001), whereas obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) rates were comparable (0.9% vs. 0.7% vs. 0.7%, P = 0.506). The above-recommended group had higher rates of induction and epidural analgesia, longer second-stage duration, and higher birthweight (all P < 0.001). After adjustment, GWG category was not independently associated with overall perineal injury (above-recommended: odds ratio [OR] 1.021; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.930-1.120, P = 0.665) or OASI (above-recommended: OR 1.065; 95% CI 0.743-1.526, P = 0.733). Independent risk factors for perineal injury included vacuum extraction (OR 3.288), epidural analgesia (OR 1.489), occiput-posterior position (OR 1.450), induction (OR 1.285), and higher birthweight (OR 1.957 per kg).
CONCLUSION: Among nulliparous women with normal pre-pregnancy BMI, GWG, whether below, within, or above American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommendations, did not independently affect the risk of perineal tears or OASI. Intrapartum and fetal factors remain the primary determinants of perineal injury.

articles.title: A step toward understanding pediatric occipital neuralgia: Investigating occipital headaches in a pediatric neurology clinic.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occipital neuralgia (ON) is well characterized in adults but remains poorly understood in children. Pediatric ON may present with overlapping headache features and variable treatment responses, creating diagnostic and management challenges.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to (1) characterize pediatric patients presenting to a tertiary outpatient neurology clinic with occipital headache symptoms consistent with ON, (2) describe their overlap with other headache symptom profiles, and (3) summarize documented diagnostic evaluation, treatment patterns, and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected, standardized headache intake questionnaire data from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) headache registry, including pediatric patients evaluated in outpatient neurology from July 2016 through August 2024. Self-reported headache characteristics were used to identify a cohort of patients with symptoms consistent with ON, defined as recurrent, short-duration, stabbing or sharp, severe pain involving the occipital region. We excluded patients who also had frontotemporal or holocephalic pain. However, to avoid missing patients with overlapping headache phenotypes, we did not exclude patients whose headaches also met criteria for other diagnoses such as migraine.
RESULTS: We identified 89 of 14,876 (0.6%) patients within the registry with symptoms consistent with ON, predominantly male (54%) with a median age of 12.7 years (interquartile range, 9.3-15.5). Sixty of the 89 (67%) patients additionally met symptom-based criteria for another headache disorder, mostly migraine. Forty-five of 89 (51%) patients followed up over a median of 1.1 years (interquartile range, 0.6-4.2), with 35 of 45 attempting treatment. At the most recent follow-up of those treated, 26% reported significant improvement (9 of 35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5%-43.3%), 29% some improvement (10 of 35; 95% CI, 14.6%-46.3%), 26% no change (9 of 35; 95% CI, 12.5%-43.3%), and 20% worsened (7 of 35; 95% CI, 8.4%-36.9%).
CONCLUSION: Symptoms consistent with ON are rare, even among children with occipital headaches, and frequently overlap with features of other primary headache disorders. These findings highlight the diagnostic complexity of pediatric occipital headache and the need for improved characterization and standardized evaluation to inform future treatment pathways for children with persistent ON-like symptoms.

articles.title: Annual medical care expenditures and financial toxicity among families of children with pain conditions in the United States: A nationally representative study.
articles.abstract: Pediatric pain conditions are associated with significant economic burden. We quantify U.S. national pediatric pain medical expenditures and examine associations with family financial toxicity. We conducted cross-sectional analysis of the 2017-2023 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), including children <18 years (n=43,813). Pediatric pain conditions were identified by parent report and included participants seeking treatment for headache, musculoskeletal pain, abdominopelvic pain, menstrual pain, and nervous system-related pain. Associations between pediatric pain and total medical expenditures were estimated using multivariable ordinary least squares modeling, controlling for covariates including age, sex, race, insurance, family income, pediatric comorbidity index, and survey year. Associations between pediatric pain conditions and high family financial burden and extreme financial burden (>10% of income) were evaluated with multivariable logistic regression modeling, controlling for the same covariates. In the MEPS sample, the survey-weighted treated prevalence of pediatric pain conditions was 4.7% (95% CI: 4.4-5.0%). The adjusted medical expenditure associated with pain was $1703 per child (95% confidence interval $550-2857, p=0.004). National expenditures associated with pediatric pain were estimated at $6.3 billion dollars annually. Pediatric pain conditions were associated with significantly increased family financial toxicity across both subjective (27.3% with pain vs. 20.5% without pain; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.3; 95% CI, 1.1-1.5;<0.0001) and objective measures (high financial burden: 7.3% vs. 4.2%; aOR, 1.3; 95% CI, 1.0-1.7; p=0.031). Our study highlights the significant economic burden associated with pediatric pain conditions in the U.S. Optimizing pediatric pain management could result in significant savings and reduce financial burden on families. PERSPECTIVE: This nationally representative study quantifies the contemporary economic burden of treated pediatric pain in the United States. Pain conditions were associated with higher medical expenditures and greater subjective and objective family financial toxicity. Optimizing pediatric pain management may reduce societal costs and financial hardship for families.

articles.title: The many faces of primary myofascial orofacial pain: Hypothetical pathophysiology-based phenotypes to inform clinical decisions for management.
articles.abstract: Primary myofascial orofacial pain (PM-OFP) or painful myogenous temporomandibular disorder is a pain condition involving the masticatory muscles without identifiable organic pathology. A biopsychosocial approach has been adopted for the assessment and management of orofacial pain, including PM-OFP, incorporating psychological and social factors for a more comprehensive understanding of pain as both disease and illness. Nevertheless, integration of psychosocial assessment with physical examination is generally underutilized, often resulting in suboptimal patient care. We proposed that phenotyping PM-OFP by incorporating assessments consistent with measuring pathophysiological mechanisms within the biopsychosocial framework will have meaningful implications for clinical decision-making. To evaluate this proposition, clinical presentations of PM-OFP and their associated presumed pathophysiological mechanisms were reviewed. Existing management guidelines were also examined to identify relevant clinical and pathophysiological features of PM-OFP for which specific management options might be recommended. Drawing on our analysis of the literature, we propose a new hypothetical phenotyping framework for PM-OFP characterized by four pathophysiological domains, including pain mechanisms, psychological distress, functional disability (i.e., limited mouth opening), and oral behaviors. Such phenotyping could complement existing classification systems and guide targeted management strategies. Further research combining retrospective data analysis, mechanistic studies, and prospective trials is needed to validate the intended outcomes of the proposed phenotyping framework. PERSPECTIVE: This paper hypothesizes a phenotyping framework for primary myofascial orofacial pain (PM-OFP) based on clinically oriented pathophysiological concepts within the biopsychosocial model. This framework could help researchers gain a clearer understanding of PM-OFP pathophysiological domains and guide clinicians towards more mechanism-driven decisions for management.

articles.title: Mobile health interventions for chronic non-cancer pain: A systematic scoping review of studies assessing opioid use.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic scoping review examined the scope and characteristics of mobile health (mHealth) interventions for adults with chronic non-cancer pain in studies that included opioid use as an outcome.
DESIGN: This study was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute Reviewer's Manual and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analysis extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). This review included studies evaluating mHealth interventions for adults with chronic non-cancer pain which included opioid use as a measured outcome.
DATA EXTRACTION: Information on study characteristics were extracted, including co-design processes, technology used, degree of human contact, theoretical basis, tailoring and engagement strategies, and key findings.
RESULTS: From 4,344 records, 33 records (29 unique studies) comprising 21 published articles and 12 protocols met criteria. Interventions utilised mobile apps (n = 14), text messaging (n = 5), and telephone-based interactive voice response (n = 3). Opioid use was an eligibility criterion in 14 studies, of which seven were specifically designed to support opioid tapering. Published results indicated high acceptability and feasibility, with findings also suggesting potential efficacy.
CONCLUSIONS: Although most studies targeted pain management with opioid use as a secondary outcome, interventions specifically designed to support patients with tapering are emerging. There is early evidence suggesting they are acceptable, feasible, and potentially effective. Future research should evaluate efficacy, as well as examine mediating and moderating factors to better understand how and for whom mHealth interventions are effective.

articles.title: Long-Term Mortality in Sepsis Survivors: A Population-Based Study During 15 Years.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate long-term mortality among sepsis survivors in Catalonia over a 15-year period and to identify factors associated with increased mortality within 2 years after hospital discharge.
DESIGN: Retrospective population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Acute-care hospitals in Catalonia, Spain.
PATIENTS: Adult and pediatric patients hospitalized with sepsis between 2005 and 2019 identified using the International Classification of Diseases, 9th Revision, Clinical Modification and International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification codes for infection and acute organ dysfunction. Patients who died during hospitalization, were transferred to another facility, or represented readmission episodes were excluded.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Data were obtained from the Catalan Minimum Basic Dataset of Acute-Care Hospitals, with longitudinal follow-up through the Central Registry of Insured Persons. Comorbidities were assessed using the Charlson comorbidity index. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify predictors of long-term mortality. Among 296,554 hospital admissions for sepsis, 237,075 patients (79.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Of these, 42% died (99,571) within 2 years. Long-term mortality increased significantly with age, ranging from 5.8% in patients younger than 15 years to 62% in those older than 84 years (p < 0.0001), and with comorbidity burden (21%, 38%, 51%, and 67% for Charlson index 0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥ 5, respectively; p < 0.0001). Neoplasia (hazard ratio [HR], 2.011), liver cirrhosis (HR, 1.562), and dementia (HR, 1.304) were the comorbidities most strongly associated with mortality. Longer hospital stays were also associated with increased mortality. A progressive decline in long-term mortality was observed during 2017-2019.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term mortality among sepsis survivors remains high, with more than 40% dying within 2 years after hospital discharge. These findings support the need for structured post-sepsis care strategies focused on high-risk patients, improved continuity of care, and prevention of long-term sepsis-related complications.

articles.title: Shortening the Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU): Development and Validation of a 12-Item Family Satisfaction Survey for Adult ICUs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a shorter Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU) questionnaire that reduces survey length while preserving content and psychometric performance for quality improvement and benchmarking. The FS-ICU survey assesses family perceptions of care, communication, and decision-making and has been translated into multiple languages with implementation across diverse health care systems internationally. In a province-wide electronic implementation in Ontario, more than 40% of initiated surveys were incomplete, suggesting that survey length may limit practicality for large-scale quality improvement and benchmarking.
DESIGN: Multistage study using provincial FS-ICU survey data and an independent multicenter validation dataset for item reduction, psychometric evaluation, agreement testing, and external validation of a shortened questionnaire.
SETTING: A 12-member expert working group, convened for a Critical Care Services Ontario initiative, used provincial web-based data from adult ICUs across Ontario to develop a shorter version, FS-ICUshort. External validation was applied to FS-ICUshort using a separate multicenter Canadian revised FS-ICU dataset.
PARTICIPANTS: A 12-member expert working group led by Dr. Daren K. Heyland, including administrative staff, ICU clinical staff, patient experience specialists, and quality improvement specialists from Ontario, used provincial FS-ICU rollout data.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Using empirical criteria and expert ratings, the FS-ICU was reduced from 29 to 12 items: seven in the satisfaction-with-care domain (FS-Care) and five in the communication and decision-making domain (FS-DM). FS-ICUshort showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.93 for FS-Care, 0.86 for FS-DM, and 0.94 for total). Confirmatory factor analysis supported a two-factor structure with better fit than a single-factor model. Scores from FS-ICUshort closely matched full FS-ICU, with mean differences less than or equal to 1.1 points on a 0-100 scale and intraclass correlations of 0.97-0.99. External validation replicated these results.
CONCLUSIONS: The 12-item FS-ICUshort maintains the core content and psychometric quality of the original FS-ICU while significantly reducing length, supporting routine use in ICU family experience measurement and benchmarking.

articles.title: Consensus on a core outcome set for ventilation trials in critically ill patients with acute brain injury: results of an international Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Clinical research evaluating mechanical ventilation liberation in patients with acute brain injury (ABI) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity, limiting evidence synthesis. We aimed to develop an internationally endorsed core outcome set (COS) and a hierarchical composite endpoint for ventilation trials in neurocritical care.
METHODS: Following COS-STAD/COS-STAP standards, we conducted a 4-round international Delphi study. Candidate outcomes were identified via a scoping review. A multidisciplinary panel from 31 countries scored outcomes using a 9-point GRADE scale. Inclusion required >70% rating as "critical" (score 7-9) and ≤15% as "not important" (1-3). Two consensus meetings were held to categorize outcomes, select representative measures, and ratify a hierarchical composite endpoint.
RESULTS: 78 stakeholders participated in Round 1; 60 completed all rounds (23.1% attrition). Fifty-four outcomes achieved Delphi consensus. At Consensus Meeting 1, these were organized into 16 categories; the highest-scoring outcome per category was selected. Three outcomes were not ratified due to disease-specificity (NIH Stroke Scale) or lack of universal applicability (brain death, coma-free days). The final COS comprised 13 outcomes across 5 domains: respiratory function, survival, complications, functional status, and quality of life. A 3-level hierarchical composite endpoint was ratified at Consensus Meeting 2: (1) intensive care unit survival, (2) no reintubation within 72 hours, and (3) days alive without mechanical ventilation.
CONCLUSION: This study establishes the first COS for ventilation weaning trials in ABI patients. Widespread adoption of these 13 outcomes and the hierarchical composite endpoint will standardize reporting, enable meaningful evidence synthesis, and facilitate clinical translation in neurocritical care.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) Initiative, registration number 2320.

articles.title: End of the Beginning: The Second Generation of Anti-fibrotic Therapy Grows.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Basiliximab use and early graft dysfunction after liver transplantation: an overlap-weighted multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Basiliximab has been associated with a reduced risk of acute cellular rejection, infection and renal failure in liver transplantation. However, its association with early graft dysfunction (EAD) and EAD-related outcomes remains unclear.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cohort was enrolled. Association of basiliximab use with EAD, and EAD-related outcomes (prolonged ICU stay and peri‑operative mortality) were evaluated. The treatment effects were estimated using overlap weighting method based on outcome-specific propensity score models incorporating recipient, donor and peri‑operative characteristics. Sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding centers with highly imbalanced basiliximab use.
RESULTS: Of 903 eligible recipients, 393 (43.5%) received basiliximab induction. Overlap weighting achieved excellent covariate balance (nearly all absolute standardized mean differences < 0.03). After weighting, EAD incidence was 7.8 percentage points lower with basiliximab (23.3%vs. 31.1%); overlap-weighted logistic regression showed that basiliximab use was associated with significantly lower odds of EAD (OR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.94; p = 0.02). No significant associations were observed with prolonged ICU stay or peri‑operative mortality, and findings remained robust in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Basiliximab induction was associated with lower odds of EAD after liver transplantation; however, as confounding by indication cannot be excluded in this observational design, validation in larger prospective studies is warranted.

articles.title: Advances in assessing donor organ quality and perioperative risk for kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract: Kidney transplantation faces persistent challenges in accurately evaluating donor organ quality and predicting long-term outcomes, with traditional assessment methods demonstrating limited predictive capacity. The increasing utilization of marginal-quality donor organs has intensified the need for sophisticated evaluation strategies. Machine perfusion technology has transformed organ preservation from mere static storage to a dynamic platform potentially enabling real-time monitoring, assessment, and interventions during the preservation period. Molecular profiling technologies such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics could provide refined biomarkers for donor kidney assessment across several phases of kidney transplantation. The first window arises during donor evaluation. Techniques such as high-resolution molecular typing, genetic profiling, epigenomic markers, and artificial intelligence-enhanced imaging provide additional information compared to traditional scoring systems. During organ preservation, a second window emerges, allowing additional, isolated assessment of the organ after procurement but before transplantation. Machine perfusion systems enable sampling of perfusate and tissue for multi-omics analysis to characterize injury or function, although most candidate biomarkers remain at the discovery or early validation stage. After transplantation, donor-derived cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid, urinary chemokines, and advanced imaging modalities offer non-invasive early detection of graft injury. Clinical translation of these new techniques faces substantial challenges: most studies are single-center and have small sample sizes, assay standardization remains incomplete, and evidence linking biomarker-guided decisions to improved long-term graft survival is lacking. Machine learning may enhance risk stratification but remains largely unvalidated in prospective trials. Future progress requires a shift from short-term endpoint prediction to long-term outcome validation through multicenter studies, standardized protocols, and equitable implementation strategies.

articles.title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis.
articles.abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.

articles.title: The (R)evolution of vNOTES in gynecology.
articles.abstract: Transvaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) has emerged as an innovative minimally invasive approach in gynecologic surgery, aiming to combine the benefits of vaginal surgery and conventional laparoscopy while avoiding abdominal incisions. Over the past two decades, its clinical applications have expanded considerably, encompassing an increasingly wide range of gynecologic procedures. The of this study was to provide a comprehensive narrative review of the evolution of vNOTES in gynecology, summarizing current evidence on surgical indications, perioperative outcomes, limitations, and future perspectives. A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from January 2004 to June 2026. Original studies, randomized trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses evaluating vNOTES in gynecologic surgery were included. vNOTES has evolved from an experimental access technique to an established minimally invasive approach for benign hysterectomy and adnexal surgery. Emerging applications include myomectomy, endometriosis surgery, urogynecologic procedures, gynecologic emergencies and selected oncologic indications. While high-quality evidence is available for hysterectomy and adnexal surgery, comparative data remain limited for most other gynecologic procedures, although preliminary results are highly promising. Learning curve, patient selection, and technical constraints remain key determinants of successful implementation. vNOTES represents a significant evolution in minimally invasive gynecologic surgery, with clear benefits in selected benign indications. However, its broader adoption is currently limited by heterogeneous evidence and technical challenges. Future studies should focus on standardization, training, and long-term oncologic and functional outcomes.

articles.title: Epidemiology and outcome of sudden cardiac arrest in elderly Nigerians: a prospective multicentre observational survey.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Limited information is available on sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) care in the elderly population in sub-Saharan Africa, despite the growing incidence of risk factors such as cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to describe the epidemiology and assess the outcomes of out-of-hospital and in-hospital SCA among the elderly population in Nigeria.
DESIGN: Prospective, multicentre observational survey on epidemiology and outcome of SCA arrest in Nigerian adults over a 20-month period.
SETTING: Six purposefully selected teaching hospitals in the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged 65 years and above who experienced either out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) brought to the selected hospital or in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA). Data were analysed using IBM-SPSS V.25.0 (SPSS, Chicago, Illinois, USA). Descriptive statistics were used to summarise the data.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Main outcome measures were return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) from initial arrest, survival to hospital admission and survival to hospital discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 1069 (27.3%) out of the 3909 SCA data collected were elderly (aged ≥65 years). Of this, 91.0% were IHCA and 9.0% were OHCA. The age ranged from 65 years to 105 years, with a median of 75 (IQR 70–81) years for IHCA, and 65 years to 115 years, with a median of 72 (IQR 68–78) years for OHCA. There was a male preponderance in both cohorts, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.971). Arrests were witnessed in 97.2% of IHCA and 94.8% of OHCA events. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) yielded ROSC of 0.3% in IHCA and 3.1% in OHCA, and an overall hospital discharge survival of 0.1% and 2.1%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The overall survival in both IHCA and OHCA was poor in elderly Nigerians, with a very low rate of bystander CPR in both OHCA and IHCA, despite the high rate of witness presence.

articles.title: Outcomes after lung transplantation for connective tissue disease-related interstitial lung disease: single center in South Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary involvement is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in connective tissue diseases (CTDs), particularly in the form of CTD-related interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), and patients with severe CTD-ILD may eventually require lung transplantation (LT). However, post-transplant outcomes specific to CTD-ILD remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult patients who underwent LT for ILD between 2008 and 2025 at a single tertiary center. Patients were classified into CTD-ILD and non-CTD-ILD groups. Clinical and perioperative data were obtained through chart review. Overall survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: A total of 170 patients were included; 39 had CTD-ILD and 131 had non-CTD-ILD. CTD-ILD recipients were more often female (22/39, 56.4% vs. 32/131, 24.4%; P<0.001) and had a numerically higher prevalence of preoperative pulmonary hypertension (7/39, 17.9% vs. 12/131, 9.2%; P=0.094). Overall survival did not differ significantly between the CTD-ILD and non-CTD-ILD groups (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.923; 95% CI, 0.383-2.229; P=0.859; log-rank P=0.334). CTD-ILD recipients had a longer postoperative intensive care unit stay (median [interquartile range], 23.0 days [13.0-35.0] vs. 17.0 days [11.0-28.0]; P=0.026), a longer duration of mechanical ventilation (17.0 days [8.0-32.0] vs. 8.0 days [5.0-18.0]; P=0.009), fewer ventilator-free days (8.0 [0.0-19.0] vs. 11.0 [0.0-22.0]; P=0.002), and a higher incidence of postoperative thromboembolic events (10/39, 25.6% vs. 6/131, 4.6%; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Although survival did not differ significantly in the present study, CTD-ILD recipients had a greater perioperative burden, including higher rates of thromboembolic events and greater use of intensive care resources.

articles.title: Patient-selected music listening and heartrate patterns during paediatric dental hygiene: an exploratory pilot study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore heart-rate changes across predefined procedural phases in paediatric patients undergoing professional dental hygiene with passive patient-selected music listening compared with standard care, and to descriptively examine HR patterns in a small clinically indicated nitrous oxide/oxygen (N2O/O2) conscious sedation reference group.
BACKGROUND: Dental procedures may elicit fear and anxiety in children, potentially affecting cooperation and the overall quality of care. Music lis-tening is a simple, low-cost, non-pharmacological intervention that can be easily integrated into preventive dental procedures. However, physiological measures such as heart rate (HR) are non-specific and should not be inter-preted as direct measures of dental anxiety, fear, or behavioral cooperation.
MATERIALS: This single-center pilot study included 45 children aged 5-14 years undergoing scaling and polishing. Participants were allocated to Group A (standard care; n=19), Group B (passive patient-selected music listening via headphones; n=21), and Group C (clinically indicated N2O/O2 conscious sedation; n=5; non-randomised reference group). Groups A and B were assigned by simple randomization, whereas Group C was not randomised. HR was recorded by fingertip pulse oximetry throughout the appointment and summarised at three predefined procedural phases: before the procedure (T0), during scaling (T1), and at the end of the session (T2).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory pilot sample, passive patient-selected music listening was associated with a different pattern of HR change across the dental hygiene session compared with standard care, with lower mean HR values observed during scaling and at the end of the session. Because HR is a non-specific physiological parameter and no validated psychological or behavioural measure of dental anxiety, fear, or cooperation was collected, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of an anxiolytic effect. Larger controlled studies incorporating standardised procedures, subject-level analyses, and validated psycho-logical and behavioural outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Effect of Intravenous Acetaminophen on Preemptive Multimodal Analgesia for Pediatric Osteotomy Correction Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Children undergoing Osteotomy correction surgery can experience substantial postoperative pain and frequently require opioids. We evaluated whether a single preincision dose of intravenous acetaminophen, added to a standardized multimodal analgesic regimen, reduces postoperative pain and perioperative opioid requirements.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 96 children aged 6-18 years undergoing elective lower-limb osteotomy correction surgery were randomized 1:1 to intravenous acetaminophen 15 mg/kg or volume-matched 0.9% sodium chloride administered 30 minutes before skin incision. The primary outcome was the incidence of moderate-to-severe pain within 72 hours after surgery, defined as a Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) score ≥4 at any scheduled assessment. The primary analysis used the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (n=95; 48 acetaminophen, 47 placebo). Secondary outcomes included perioperative opioid consumption, pain intensity, rescue analgesia, patient-controlled intravenous analgesia use, subjective sleep quality, and adverse events. The trial was prospectively registered (ChiCTR2500095363; January 6, 2025).
RESULTS: Moderate-to-severe pain occurred in 8/48 (16.7%) versus 21/47 (44.7%) children, an absolute risk reduction of 28.0% (RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.2-0.8; P=0.004). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was lower in the acetaminophen group (median, 0.8 vs 1.3 mg; between-group difference, 0.6 mg; 95% CI, 0.3-0.9; P<0.001). Postoperative 72-hour morphine-equivalent consumption was also lower (median, 90.0 vs 105.0 mg; difference, 14.4 mg; 95% CI, 2.7-26.5; P=0.018). Longitudinal ordinal GEE demonstrated significant group-by-time interactions for FLACC scores both at rest (P<0.001) and during movement (P=0.002), with the analgesic benefit concentrated in the early postoperative period. Subjective sleep NRS scores were lower in the acetaminophen group on POD1 (Holm-adjusted P=0.005), although the overall group-by-time interaction was not significant (P=0.411). No increase in perioperative adverse events was observed in the acetaminophen group.
CONCLUSION: Preincision intravenous acetaminophen was associated with a lower incidence of moderate-to-severe postoperative pain and reduced opioid requirements in children undergoing osteotomy correction surgery. Larger multicenter trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Experimental evidence for electroacupuncture in managing pain from chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This study systematically evaluated the evidence from animal experiments on electroacupuncture (EA) for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) pain models. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted using the PICOS framework to assess the behavioral and molecular effects of EA and clarify its underlying mechanisms and translational potential. Thirteen eligible studies involving 235 animals were included. Methodological quality scores ranged from 5 to 8, with a mean of 6.5. Meta-analysis showed that EA significantly increased the paw withdrawal threshold (PWT), thermal pain withdrawal latency (PWL), and nerve conduction velocity (NCV), while reducing cold allodynia. At the molecular level, EA significantly decreased the expression of pro-inflammatory and sensitization markers, including TNF-α, IL-1β, GFAP, TLR4, TRPA1, and TRPV1, and increased the oxidative stress regulator Nrf2. Sensitivity analysis, publication bias assessment, subgroup analysis, and meta-regression were performed for the highly heterogeneous PWT outcome. Significant publication bias was identified and may account for much of the observed heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis for TRPV1 suggested that this result may be disproportionately influenced by individual studies and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Heterogeneity in the remaining outcomes likely reflects differences in animal models, acupoint selection, treatment duration, and intervention protocols. Overall, EA demonstrated analgesic and neuroprotective effects in CIPN models, primarily through modulation of neuroinflammation, attenuation of oxidative stress, and reduction of neuronal sensitization. These findings provide systematic preclinical evidence supporting EA as a promising adjuvant therapy for CIPN pain and highlight the need for high-quality clinical trials to optimize treatment protocols and facilitate clinical translation.

articles.title: Endoscopic Spine Surgery for Adjacent Segment Disease After Lumbar Fusion: Indications, Outcomes, and a Proposed Treatment Algorithm.
articles.abstract: Spinal fusion alters segmental biomechanics and redistributes mechanical load to the levels above and below the arthrodesis, which may accelerate degeneration at those levels. When such degeneration becomes symptomatic, producing new-onset back pain, radiculopathy, or neurological deficit, the condition is termed adjacent segment disease (ASD). ASD is a recognized cause of late postoperative morbidity and revision surgery after lumbar fusion, with cumulative estimates of approximately 16.5% at 5 years and 22-36% at 10 years. Conventional management has centered on neural decompression combined with extension of the existing fusion construct. Although effective, revision fusion carries greater operative complexity, increased blood loss, prolonged recovery, and higher complication rates than the index procedure, and lengthening the construct transfers stress to newly adjacent levels. Endoscopic spine surgery has emerged as a less invasive alternative that permits targeted neural decompression through small working corridors while preserving the paraspinal musculature and posterior stabilizing structures. This narrative review examines the evolving role of endoscopic techniques in ASD after lumbar fusion and compares them with conventional revision fusion in terms of indications, outcomes, and limitations. The transforaminal, interlaminar, and unilateral biportal endoscopic approaches are described, together with the technical challenges imposed by reduced disc height, epidural scarring, and distorted anatomy in previously operated segments. Reported series demonstrate significant improvements in pain and function, favorable perioperative profiles, and low complication rates, with clinical efficacy comparable to open revision surgery in controlled comparisons. A pragmatic treatment algorithm is proposed that stratifies patients by symptom pattern, imaging-defined pathology, and segmental stability. Endoscopic decompression appears most appropriate for stable segments with focal neural compression, after assessing segmental translation and angulation on flexion-extension radiographs; significant instability or deformity remains an indication for fusion-based revision. The available evidence is dominated by retrospective series, and randomized comparative trials are lacking.

articles.title: Efficacy of chlorhexidine vaginal preparation in reducing postoperative infections during emergency cesarean deliveries for women in labor: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative infections are a leading cause of maternal morbidity after emergency cesarean delivery. This trial explores the effectiveness of preoperative vaginal cleansing via the use of chlorhexidine for reducing these complications in women in labor.
METHODS: This single-blinded superiority randomized controlled trial included 840 women in labor equally distributed to either immediate preoperative chlorhexidine gluconate 0.05% vaginal cleansing or no-cleansing; 826 were analyzed under a modified intention-to-treat approach. The co-primary outcomes were postcesarean endometritis and surgical site infection (SSI). Secondary outcomes included composite wound complications, postoperative fever, significant leukocytosis, hospital readmission, length of stay, and adverse drug reactions. Effects are expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals, with adjusted, sensitivity, and subgroup analyses for the co-primary outcomes.
RESULTS: Chlorhexidine significantly reduced both co-primary outcomes; postcesarean endometritis (1.9% vs. 6.3%; RR 0.303, 95% CI 0.139-0.662; P = 0.001) and SSI (1.4% vs. 5.4%; RR 0.269, 95% CI 0.110-0.656; P = 0.002); both remained significant against a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of 0.025. Other outcomes were also reduced, including composite wound complications (3.4% vs. 11.0%; RR 0.307, 95% CI 0.171-0.550; P < 0.001), and readmission for infection (1.4% vs. 6.3%; P < 0.001; RR 0.227, 95% CI 0.095-0.547). The co-primary outcome effects persisted after adjustment and in sensitivity analyses. Treatment effects were in the same direction across premature rupture of membranes (PROM) and obesity subgroups with no significant interaction, although the SSI reduction reached significance overall and in the non-obese stratum but not within the obese stratum.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial, preoperative chlorhexidine vaginal cleansing produced lower rates of postcesarean endometritis and SSI and of related infectious morbidity. As a low-cost intervention that can be integrated into existing perioperative workflows, it is a promising strategy for reducing maternal infection; however, adverse events were not systematically solicited, and neonatal exposure was not assessed. Multicenter confirmation, systematic maternal and neonatal safety data, and cost-effectiveness analysis are required before routine adoption.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04385680 submitted 9 May 2020, first posted 13 May 2020.

articles.title: Dose- and endpoint-dependent effects of perioperative esketamine in children: evidence from a targeted review.
articles.abstract: Esketamine is being evaluated for several paediatric perioperative indications, including analgesia, procedural sedation, attenuation of propofol injection pain, and prevention of emergence delirium (ED) or emergence agitation (EA). This mini review examines whether evidence identified in a targeted search supports a clinically useful therapeutic window and how dose, timing, route, developmental stage, anaesthetic technique, procedure, co-medication, and outcome definition modify treatment effects. Randomised trials and meta-analyses generally report fewer ED or EA events after low intravenous doses, particularly during sevoflurane anaesthesia for adenotonsillectomy. Direct dose-comparison evidence shows increasing benefit up to 0.5 mg·kg-1 intravenously in that setting, without identifying an upper efficacy or safety boundary. An observational association between esketamine exposure and more ED cannot establish a threshold because treatment selection and perioperative context were not controlled. Effective doses are endpoint-specific: propofol injection pain, procedural sedation, analgesia, and emergence outcomes require different exposure profiles. Intranasal regimens cannot be converted into intravenous equivalents from bioavailability alone, and preclinical neurotoxicity findings do not define a ceiling for a single perioperative dose in children. Among the studies identified, 0.2-0.5 mg·kg-1 was the best-studied intravenous range in selected emergence-prevention settings, not a universal recommendation or validated therapeutic window. Future trials should compare dose and timing directly, incorporate paediatric pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic sampling, use endpoint-specific assessment, and extend safety follow-up.

articles.title: Trends, outcomes and patient- and hospital-level factors associated with sepsis following cesarean delivery: a propensity-matched nationwide inpatient analysis (2016-2022).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern and a serious complication of cesarean delivery. However, contemporary nationwide data describing both the temporal trend in post-cesarean sepsis and its downstream clinical and economic burden-particularly in propensity-matched comparisons-remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity-matched analysis of all adult inpatients undergoing cesarean delivery recorded in the U.S. Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2016-2022). Sepsis and cesarean delivery were defined using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. After 1:5 propensity-score matching on demographics, comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics, we compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total hospitalization costs, and the incidence of perioperative complications between septic and non-septic patients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient- and hospital-level factors independently associated with sepsis.
RESULTS: Of 1,619,187 hospitalizations for cesarean delivery, 1,589,186 adults met the inclusion criteria. Annual sepsis prevalence rose from 0.058% in 2016 to 0.136% in 2022.
