In the 1:5 propensity-matched cohort (n = 10,050), septic patients had markedly higher in-hospital mortality (2.4% vs. 0.0%, P < 0.001), longer median LOS (6 vs. 3 days, P < 0.001), and approximately 2.6-fold higher median total hospitalization costs (USD 71,466 vs. USD 27,063, P < 0.001). Non-elective admission, treatment in teaching hospitals, a higher comorbidity burden, Asian/Pacific Islander race, and hospital region were independently associated with sepsis. After propensity matching, septic patients also showed substantially elevated adjusted odds of pulmonary embolism (OR 61.7), postoperative shock (OR 28.7), deep-vein thrombosis (OR 24.6), urinary tract infection (OR 25.5), and chronic respiratory diseases (OR 13.2).
CONCLUSIONS: In this large U.S. study, sepsis after cesarean section was linked to much higher death rates, twice the hospital stay, about 2.6 times higher costs, and more severe problems like blood clots, shock, infections, and heavy bleeding. These results show that post-cesarean section sepsis is a growing concern, remind us to spot at-risk mothers early, and offer a benchmark against which prevention and cost-effective care can be evaluated.

articles.title: The median effective dose of hyperbaric ropivacaine and lateral decubitus time for unilateral spinal anesthesia in lower extremity varicose vein surgery: a dose- and time-finding study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to determine the median effective dose (ED50) of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for motor block in the non-surgical extremity and the median effective lateral decubitus time (ET50) for preventing motor block in the non-surgical extremity during lower extremity varicose vein surgery.
METHODS: Sixty patients undergoing unilateral lower extremity varicose vein surgery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia were enrolled in two sequential phases: a dose-finding phase (n = 30) and a time-finding phase (n = 30). All patients received intrathecal 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine. A modified Dixon up-and-down method was applied sequentially. In the dose-finding phase, the lateral decubitus position was maintained for 20 min. In the subsequent time-finding phase, patients received the ED5 of hyperbaric ropivacaine estimated in the dose-finding phase, corresponding to a 5% probability of motor block in the non-surgical extremity. Successful prevention of motor block was defined as a modified Bromage score <1. For probit analysis, motor block (modified Bromage score ≥1) was coded as the positive response in the dose-finding phase, whereas successful prevention of motor block in the non-surgical extremity was coded as the positive response in the time-finding phase. The ED50 and ET50 were treated as the primary estimates, whereas additional quantile estimates derived from the fitted probit models were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: The ED50 of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for motor block in the non-surgical extremity was 12.683 mg (95% CI: 12.367-12.997 mg). The ET50 of lateral decubitus time for preventing motor block in the non-surgical extremity was 13.887 min (95% CI: 13.390-14.338 min). The exploratory ED5, corresponding to a 5% probability of motor block, was 11.956 mg (95% CI, 10.304-12.303 mg), while the exploratory ET95 was 14.957 min (95% CI, 14.455-17.016 min). Adverse events were infrequent, and intraoperative hemodynamics remained stable.
CONCLUSION: The ED50 of 0.5% hyperbaric ropivacaine for non-surgical extremity was 12.683 mg (95%CI: 12.367-12.997 mg), and the ET50 of lateral decubitus time for preventing motor block was 13.887 min (95% CI: 13.390-14.338 min).
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: [www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=239741], identifier [ChiCTR2400088340].

articles.title: Machine learning model with post-hoc SHAP interpretation based on perioperative clinical and imaging parameters for prediction of 1-year radiographic recurrence after hallux valgus surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Radiographic recurrence after hallux valgus surgery is an important issue affecting long-term imaging outcomes. Previous studies have suggested that preoperative deformity, postoperative residual HVA/IMA, and sesamoid reduction are associated with recurrence, but nonlinear relationships may exist among multiple parameters. The aim of this study was to establish and temporally validate a machine learning prediction model based on conventional perioperative clinical and imaging parameters and to provide post-hoc model interpretation using SHAP.
METHODS: 597 patients undergoing hallux valgus surgery in the Department of Trauma, First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from 2021 to 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Radiographic recurrence was defined as HVA >20° on the fixed 12-month postoperative weight-bearing anteroposterior radiograph. Patients operated from 2021 to 2023 formed the development cohort (n=389), and patients operated from 2024 to 2025 formed the independent temporal-validation cohort (n=208). Eighteen candidate predictors were screened in the development cohort using collinearity assessment, LASSO, RFE, and permutation importance. A unified eight-feature set was then locked and used for comparison of LR, RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVM using 5-fold outer/3-fold inner nested cross-validation conditional on the fixed feature set. Models were evaluated using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Brier score, calibration, and DCA, with post-hoc SHAP-based interpretation of the final SVM.
RESULTS: A total of 109 patients met the 1-year radiographic recurrence criterion (18.3%). Eight variables were retained: age, preoperative HVA, preoperative IMA, preoperative DMAA, 6-week postoperative HVA, 6-week postoperative IMA, 6-week postoperative DMAA, and 6-week postoperative sesamoid grade. The development-cohort ROC-AUCs of LR and SVM were 0.908 and 0.906, respectively, with corresponding PR-AUCs of 0.766 and 0.757. SVM was retained as the final model on the basis of its lower Brier score and overall performance profile, without claiming statistical superiority over LR. In the temporal-validation cohort, SVM ROC-AUC was 0.944 (95% CI 0.908-0.973), PR-AUC 0.805, Brier score 0.071, sensitivity 0.892, and specificity 0.842. SHAP showed the largest model contributions for 6-week IMA, HVA, and sesamoid grade.
CONCLUSION: The SVM model with post-hoc SHAP-based interpretation showed promising performance for prediction of fixed 1-year radiographic recurrence using routine clinical and perioperative imaging parameters. Residual IMA, HVA, and sesamoid grade at 6 weeks were leading predictive signals within the model rather than causal determinants of recurrence. The model may support early risk stratification and enhanced follow-up, but multicenter external validation, reproducibility assessment, and prospective impact studies remain necessary before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Wound healing complications after tooth extraction in dogs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective clinical study aimed to assess incidence of wound healing complications associated with extraction sites following permanent tooth extractions in healthy dogs.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-seven client-owned healthy adult dogs undergoing clinically indicated closed or open dental extractions, comprising 404 extraction sites, were included in the study. No perioperative and immediate postoperative antibiotics or antiseptics were used in any of the dogs. All dogs were discharged on the day of the procedure with pain management as clinically indicated and underwent a routine (non-sedated) follow-up examination 10 days later. Sites with incomplete epithelial healing and wound edge separation were classified as dehisced. Weekly in-person or telemedicine follow-up examinations were performed until complete healing was confirmed.
RESULTS: Dehiscence was the most common postoperative complication, diagnosed in 19.5% (17/87) of the dogs and 4.2% (17/404) of the extraction sites within 10 days after the procedure. Most affected sites involved large, functionally important teeth, and 76.5% (13/17) of cases were mild. None of the dehisced sites required surgical revision, and only 23.5% (4/17) dogs required additional medical management with antibiotics and/or analgesia. All dehisced sites healed by second intention within one month. Increasing body weight was associated with higher odds of dehiscence, with a 13% increase in odds for each additional kilogram of body weight. Removal of at least 50% of the alveolar bone, extraction in the rostral mandibular region, and the use of triangular flaps during open extraction were also significantly associated with increased odds of dehiscence. Traumatic dentoalveolar injury was the only indication for tooth extraction significantly associated with increased odds of dehiscence.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Extraction wound dehiscence was uncommon at the individual-site level, but remained a clinically relevant postoperative complication when assessed per treated dog. Most affected sites healed uneventfully by second intention within one month, without surgical revision or prolonged medical management. This finding supports conservative management of extraction wound dehiscence in uncomplicated cases.

articles.title: Early adequate empiric antifungal therapy and 28-day mortality in ICU patients with candidemia: a pooled patient-level analysis of EUROBACT-1 and EUROBACT-2 cohorts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of empiric antifungal therapy in patients with suspected candidemia remains uncertain. In practice, many antifungal treatments initiated empirically are eventually found to be unnecessary, exposing patients to potential toxicity, selection of non-albicans Candida species, emergence of resistance, and additional costs. The objective of the study was to evaluate whether adequate empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 2 days after blood culture draw was associated with 28-day mortality.
METHODS: We performed a pooled secondary analysis of two prospective worldwide observational cohorts (EUROBACT-1 and EUROBACT-2) including adult patients with Candida bloodstream infection. The exposure was defined as receipt of adequate antifungal therapy within 2 days after blood culture draw. Propensity scores for receiving early adequate antifungal therapy were estimated using prespecified covariates, and inverse probability of treatment weights were applied in a weighted Cox proportional hazards model to assess the association with 28-day mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to study cohort, Candida species, and presence of hypotension at the time of bloodstream infection. As a sensitivity analysis, a frailty Cox proportional hazards model including a random center effect was performed.
RESULTS: The final study population included 272 patients with candidemia from 158 centers, including 81 from EUROBACT-1 and 191 from EUROBACT-2. One hundred and ten patients received early adequate antifungal therapy and 162 did not. Overall, 38.6% of patients (105/272) died within 28 days, including 40.9% (45/110) in the early adequate therapy group and 37.0% (60/162) in the non-early adequate therapy group. In the weighted Cox model, early adequate antifungal therapy was not significantly associated with 28-day mortality (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.82-1.83, p = 0.314). Results were consistent across subgroup analyses according to study cohort, Candida species, the presence of hypotension at the time of bloodstream infection, as well as in the frailty Cox sensitivity analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Early adequate antifungal therapy was not independently associated with improved 28-day survival in ICU patients with candidemia. These findings support a more targeted approach to early empirical antifungal treatment and underscore the need to identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit from immediate therapy.

articles.title: Female Sex and Ventilatory Recovery After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether female sex is associated with postoperative mechanical ventilation duration and prolonged ventilation >24 hours after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study.
SETTING: Four German academic centers, 2017-2023.
PARTICIPANTS: Five hundred seventy-four adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%; 70 (12.2%) were women.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Primary outcomes were postoperative mechanical ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay. The primary models were adjusted for baseline/preoperative covariates without CPB. Female sex corresponded to +30.2% longer ventilation (95% CI -3.6% to +75.8%; p = 0.086), which did not reach conventional statistical significance, and higher odds of ventilation >24 hours (aOR 1.82, 95% CI 1.01-3.26; p = 0.045). Adding CPB strengthened the estimates, whereas extracorporeal life support exclusion and center fixed-effects adjustment attenuated them. In 69 matched pairs, women had longer ventilation (16.0 [8.0-33.2] v 11.0 [5.8-18.0] hours; p = 0.021) and more ventilation >24 hours (30.9% v 13.2%; p = 0.029). No clear association was observed with acute kidney injury or 30-day mortality.
CONCLUSION: Female sex showed a model-dependent association with prolonged postoperative ventilation in this HFrEF CABG cohort. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation with standardized perioperative and extubation protocols.

articles.title: Intravenous Prostacyclins to Permit Heparin Use During Cardiopulmonary Bypass in Patients with Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the efficacy and safety of prostacyclin analogs used to permit heparin anticoagulation during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT).
DESIGN: We conducted a systematic review of PubMed and Scopus. Studies describing iloprost or epoprostenol use to permit heparinization during CPB were included. Efficacy and safety outcomes were analyzed by using descriptive statistics.
SETTING: Published literature.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients with HIT or suspected HIT undergoing CPB with prostacyclin-assisted heparin anticoagulation.
INTERVENTIONS: Iloprost or epoprostenol administration to inhibit platelet function and permit heparin anticoagulation during CPB, followed by protamine reversal.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 172 identified records, 23 studies encompassing 207 patients met inclusion criteria. Iloprost dosing was more variable and more frequently titrated using platelet function testing than epoprostenol dosing. Both agents permitted heparinization and protamine reversal. Norepinephrine, phenylephrine, vasopressin, and epinephrine use to manage prostacyclin-mediated hypotension was reported in 14 of 17 (82.3%), 4 of 18 (22.2%), 3 of 16 (18.8%), and 2 of 16 (12.5%) studies, respectively. Transfusion occurred in 122 of 207 patients (58.9%), thrombotic outcomes in 17 of 207 (8.2%), and mortality in 18 of 207 (8.7%). Only 1 of 207 patients (0.5%) experienced thrombosis during CPB; the remaining thrombotic events occurred after CPB.
CONCLUSION: Prostacyclin-assisted heparin anticoagulation can permit CPB and protamine reversal in patients with HIT requiring urgent surgery. Although prostacyclin-mediated hypotension frequently necessitates vasopressor support, intraoperative thrombotic events appear uncommon.

articles.title: Vasopressors to Treat or Prevent Hypotension During and After Major Surgery: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Perioperative hypotension is common and associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. Vasopressors are central to management, yet the optimal agent and their subsequent impacts on end-organ outcomes remain unclear. This scoping review characterizes the current evidence base and addresses the need for a full systematic review or meta-analysis. A protocol was formulated a priori per the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews. Subsequently, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from January 1, 2000, to July 18, 2025, for studies comparing parenteral vasopressors in adults undergoing major surgery. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies were included. Data on study design, vasopressor strategies, initiation criteria, and postoperative outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Sixteen studies (n = 6,927) were included. Most were small, single-center, and observational, predominantly in cardiothoracic surgery. Vasopressor initiation criteria were highly variable, with studies divided broadly between hypotension-based triggers and vasoplegic syndrome, the latter inconsistently defined. A variety of vasopressors were evaluated, yet no 2 studies compared identical regimens. Postoperative outcome reporting was heterogeneous, and outcome definitions varied and showed minimal alignment with the Standardised Endpoints in Perioperative Medicine-Core Outcome Measures for Perioperative and Anaesthetic Care consensus standards. Eight studies reported significant differences in postoperative clinical outcomes between vasopressor strategies; however, effects were inconsistent, and no vasopressor strategy demonstrated a consistent benefit across studies. Overall, the evidence base for vasopressor therapy in perioperative hypotension is fragmented. Variability in initiation criteria, interventions, and outcome definitions limits comparability and precludes meaningful synthesis. Standardized definitions and adequately powered multicenter trials are required to determine optimal vasopressor strategies and their effects on postoperative organ dysfunction.

articles.title: Morphometric Analysis of the Supraorbital Foramen and Notch in Adult North Indian Dry Skulls: Anatomical Variations With Clinical and Anthropological Implications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The supraorbital foramen (SOF) and supraorbital notch (SON) are important anatomical landmarks transmitting the supraorbital neurovascular bundle. Their morphology and position exhibit considerable population-specific variation, directly influencing the safety and success of supraorbital nerve blocks, craniofacial and orbital surgeries, and reconstructive procedures. Despite their clinical and forensic significance, comprehensive morphometric data for the North Indian population remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the morphology, morphometric characteristics, and anatomical variations of the supraorbital foramen and notch in adult North Indian dry skulls and establish population-specific reference data with clinical and anthropological relevance.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An observational study was conducted on 63 adult dry human skulls (126 supraorbital regions) obtained from the Department of Anatomy, Institute of Medical Sciences, Banaras Hindu University. Morphological variants of the supraorbital opening, presence and location of accessory foramina, foraminal shape, morphometric dimensions, and distances from established anatomical landmarks were recorded using a digital Vernier caliper. Measurements were performed in triplicate. Categorical variables were summarized as frequencies and percentages, and continuous variables as mean ± standard deviation. Independent-samples t-tests were used to compare right- and left-sided measurements of complete supraorbital foramina, whereas paired-samples t-tests were used for bilateral measurements obtained from the same skull. All tests were two-tailed, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Supraorbital notch variants predominated, accounting for 76 (60.3%) of all supraorbital margins, while foramen variants constituted 32 (25.4%), combined notch-foramen variants constituted 14 (11.1%), and supraorbital depressions (SOD) constituted 4 (3.2%). Accessory supraorbital foramina were identified in 20 (15.9%) supraorbital regions, most commonly as a single lateral accessory foramen. Oval foramina represented the predominant shape, occurring in 19 (48.7%) of complete supraorbital foramina. The mean vertical and transverse diameters of complete foramina showed no significant bilateral differences. A statistically significant right-left difference was observed only for the distance from the nasion to the supraorbital opening (p < 0.001), indicating slight lateralization on the right side.
CONCLUSION: The examined North Indian osteological sample demonstrated a predominance of supraorbital notch variants, frequent accessory foramina, and measurable bilateral variation in selected anatomical relationships. These findings provide descriptive morphometric data that may be useful for comparative and clinical anatomical research.

articles.title: Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor Signaling in von Hippel-Lindau Disease: Belzutifan as a Disease-Modifying Therapy.
articles.abstract: von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition syndrome in which central nervous system (CNS) hemangioblastomas are a major cause of neurological morbidity. Management has long relied on serial imaging surveillance and symptom-driven local therapy, with surgery or radiosurgery performed when lesions produce mass effect or progressive deficits. Although this strategy provides effective local control, it does not address the systemic and recurrent nature of VHL and often leads to repeated interventions over a patient's lifetime. At a molecular level, loss of VHL function disrupts oxygen-dependent degradation of hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs), resulting in constitutive pathway activation ("pseudohypoxia"). Sustained HIF signaling promotes angiogenic and permeability programs that shape the hypervascular phenotype of CNS hemangioblastomas and may possibly contributes to cyst formation and perilesional edema. These insights led to a vigorous effort to develop various strategies to target HIF, and the first-in-class selective HIF-2α inhibitor, belzutifan, has been finally approved for clinical use. Clinical studies show that belzutifan produces durable radiographic responses across multiple VHL-associated tumor types including CNS hemangioblastomas with the most consistent activity in solid tumor components. Improvements in edema and reductions in cystic volume have been reported in selected patients as well. Belzutifan is now considered as a disease-modifying systemic treatment option that complements-rather than replaces-neurosurgical management and may help defer or reduce the frequency of local interventions in appropriately selected patients. This review discusses the biological rationale for HIF-2α inhibition in VHL disease, summarizes current clinical evidence for belzutifan, and highlights practical considerations for neurosurgeons regarding patient selection, monitoring, perioperative coordination, and remaining knowledge gaps.

articles.title: Risk factors and predictive value of lung ultrasound aeration score for postoperative pulmonary complications in pediatric patients undergoing abdominal tumor resection: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) constitute a leading source of perioperative morbidity in children undergoing abdominal malignant tumor resection. However, the risk factors of PPCs in this specific pediatric population remains unclear, and effective predictive tools are lacking. This study aimed to identify the risk factors for PPCs and evaluate the predictive value of the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) lung ultrasound aeration score (LUSS).
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary cancer center in China. Pediatric patients aged 1-18 years scheduled for abdominal malignant tumor resection were enrolled between January 2025 and January 2026. Perioperative clinical data and PACU LUSS measurements were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for PPCs. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were adopted to quantify the predictive performance of relevant indicators.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of PPCs was 60.98% (150/246). Multivariate logistic regression analysis confirmed that American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) classification (OR = 3.60, 95% CI = 1.77-7.34, P < 0.001), recent resolved upper respiratory tract infection (URI) (OR = 4.71, 95% CI = 1.84-12.08, P = 0.001), duration of mechanical ventilation (OR = 1.01, 95% CI = 1.01-1.01, P = 0.002), and PACU LUSS (OR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.17-1.42, P < 0.001) were independent risk factors for PPCs. ROC curve analysis revealed that PACU LUSS alone exhibited favorable predictive efficacy for PPCs, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.80. A combined predictive model integrating LUSS and the other three independent risk factors yielded an elevated AUC of 0.88. Calibration curves demonstrated strong consistency between predicted and actual PPCs risks, and DCA verified satisfactory clinical utility and net clinical benefit of the combined model.
CONCLUSIONS: PPCs are highly prevalent in pediatric patients undergoing abdominal malignant tumor resection. Higher ASA classification, recent resolved URI, prolonged duration of mechanical ventilation, and elevated PACU LUSS may be associated with an increased risk of PPCs. As a non-invasive bedside assessment tool, PACU LUSS may provide useful predictive information and could potentially assist with perioperative risk stratification and targeted prevention of PPCs in this vulnerable pediatric population.

articles.title: Treatment and outcomes of difficult-to-treat Stenotrophomonas maltophilia pneumonia in the intensive care unit: a multinational retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR) in Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging concern in ICU-acquired pneumonia, associated with high mortality and limited evidence to guide therapy. This study aimed to evaluate the association between antibiotic regimens and 30-day mortality in DTR S. maltophilia ICU-acquired pneumonia.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, international, retrospective study across 31 centers in eight countries, including all adult patients with DTR S. maltophilia ICU-acquired pneumonia treated with ≥24 hours of an in vitro-active antibiotic. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included clinical cure and a composite of 30-day survival with clinical cure. Each agent was analyzed as a separate exposure using modified Poisson regression with robust variance in a day-3 landmark cohort. Combination therapy and treatment duration were evaluated using overlap weighting.
RESULTS: A total of 119 patients were included. Thirty-day mortality was 37.8%. Tigecycline was associated with higher 30-day mortality (aRR 1.95, 95% CI 1.21-3.13). Aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam showed a favorable but non-significant trend toward lower mortality (aRR 0.38, 95% CI 0.12-1.15), as did colistin (aRR 0.51, 95% CI 0.22-1.20). No agent other than tigecycline was significantly associated with any outcome, and the active agents had wide, overlapping confidence intervals. Neither combination therapy nor a treatment duration longer than 8 days was associated with any outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Tigecycline was associated with excess mortality and should be used with caution. Aztreonam/ceftazidime-avibactam and colistin trended toward lower mortality, whereas the other agents, including cefiderocol, appeared neutral. The study is underpowered to separate the active agents, and these hypothesis-generating findings require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Assessing vascular barrier permeability in critically ill patients: what are we really measuring?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perturbation of vascular barrier permeability is a central mechanism in the pathophysiology of critical illness, contributing to tissue edema, impaired oxygen diffusion, and organ dysfunction. Despite advances in the field, direct bedside assessment of vascular permeability remains unavailable. Current approaches rely on indirect and compartment-specific surrogates, raising important questions about what is actually being measured.
MAIN BODY: This narrative review summarizes the physiological principles underlying vascular barrier function and its disruption in conditions such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and major surgery. Currently available bedside tools used to assess vascular permeability or its consequences are critically appraised, including clinical examination, ultrasonography, transpulmonary thermodilution, bioelectrical impedance analysis, circulating biomarkers of endothelial injury (e.g., glycocalyx degradation products, angiopoietin-2), and albumin kinetics-based methods. While these techniques provide valuable insights, they predominantly reflect downstream consequences such as tissue edema, intravascular volume shifts, or endothelial activation rather than permeability itself. In addition, vascular permeability is a dynamic, context-dependent, and organ-specific process influenced by inflammatory, hemodynamic, and therapeutic factors, further complicating its interpretation. Each method therefore captures only a partial dimension of vascular barrier dysfunction, with important limitations related to specificity, feasibility, validation and standardization.
CONCLUSIONS: No single bedside tool currently provides a comprehensive assessment of vascular permeability in critically ill patients. A multimodal approach integrating clinical evaluation, imaging, hemodynamic monitoring, and biomarkers is required to better characterize vascular barrier dysfunction. Future research should focus on validating composite indices and developing reliable, real-time bedside tools capable of directly assessing vascular permeability, with the ultimate goal of improving risk stratification and guiding personalized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: The relationship between preoperative anxiety, self-efficacy, and positive coping style in lung cancer patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with lung cancer undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) may experience preoperative anxiety arising from cancer-related uncertainty and surgery-related concerns. Although VATS is less invasive than conventional thoracotomy, patients may still worry about malignancy, prognosis, anaesthesia, postoperative recovery, and long-term health. General self-efficacy and positive coping style are potentially modifiable psychological resources associated with preoperative anxiety, but their interrelationships and the potential indirect role of positive coping style remain insufficiently understood.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study recruited patients with lung cancer scheduled for VATS from a large tertiary grade-A general hospital in Hainan Province, China, between April 2023 and October 2024. Preoperative anxiety, general self-efficacy, and positive coping style were assessed using validated questionnaires. A total of 387 valid questionnaires were analysed. Descriptive statistics, group comparisons, Spearman's correlation analysis, structural equation modelling, and Bootstrap mediation analysis were performed using SPSS 26.0 and AMOS.
RESULTS: A total of 387 valid questionnaires were included in the analysis, yielding a valid response rate of 89.38%. The mean scores of preoperative anxiety, general self-efficacy, and positive coping style were 34.88 ± 13.54 out of 64, 22.21 ± 5.95 out of 40, and 19.57 ± 7.30 out of 36, respectively, with corresponding standardized scores of 54.50%, 55.53%, and 54.36%. Spearman's correlation analysis showed that preoperative anxiety was negatively correlated with general self-efficacy (r=-0.384, P < 0.01) and positive coping style (r=-0.415, P < 0.01), while general self-efficacy was positively correlated with positive coping style (r = 0.642, P < 0.01). In the structural equation model, general self-efficacy was positively associated with positive coping style (β = 0.795, P < 0.001), and positive coping style was negatively associated with preoperative anxiety (β=-0.294, P = 0.006). The direct path from general self-efficacy to preoperative anxiety was not statistically significant (β=-0.154, P = 0.131).
CONCLUSION: This cross-sectional study documented preoperative anxiety among patients with lung cancer awaiting VATS, together with relatively low levels of general self-efficacy and positive coping style. The observed indirect-only statistical mediation pattern suggests that general self-efficacy was indirectly associated with lower preoperative anxiety through positive coping style. This pattern extends the understanding of psychological factors associated with preoperative anxiety and may inform combined assessment of anxiety, self-efficacy, and coping responses, as well as targeted preoperative support aimed at strengthening patients' confidence, improving their understanding of perioperative information, and encouraging positive coping.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Effects of ultrasound-guided superior trunk block with different ropivacaine volumes on hemidiaphragmatic paralysis and analgesic efficacy in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a study protocol for a prospective randomized controlled trial {1a}.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective management of acute pain after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR) is pivotal for implementing Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols. The superior trunk block (STB)-a technique targeting the C5-C6 nerve roots that innervate the shoulder joint-is widely used for this purpose. However, the optimal balance between local anesthetic (LA) volume, its volume-related impact on phrenic nerve function, and analgesic efficacy remains poorly defined, underscoring the urgency to identify an evidence-based LA volume. This study aims to systematically evaluate the effects of 5 mL, 10 mL, and 15 mL of 0.4% ropivacaine for STB on hemidiaphragmatic paralysis (HDP) incidence (assessed via diaphragmatic excursion) and postoperative analgesic efficacy in patients undergoing ARCR, with the goal of generating actionable evidence for optimizing clinical block regimens.
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial will enroll 129 patients, who will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive STB with 5 mL, 10 mL, or 15 mL of 0.4% ropivacaine. The primary outcome is the incidence of HDP at 30 min post-block. Secondary outcomes include changes in diaphragmatic excursion, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), sensory and motor block characteristics (onset time, duration, and extent of sensory-motor dissociation), static and dynamic visual analog scale (VAS) scores within the first 24 postoperative hours, intraoperative propofol and remifentanil consumption, and frequency of postoperative rescue analgesia requirements. All blocks will be performed by uniformly trained designated anesthesiologists using a standardized ultrasound-guided technique (high-frequency linear transducer + in-plane needle approach) to minimize technical variability.
DISCUSSION: This protocol is designed to provide high-quality evidence to guide clinical decisions on LA volume selection for STB. By systematically evaluating the trade-off between analgesic efficacy and phrenic nerve involvement across three distinct LA volumes, this study addresses a key clinical dilemma in regional anesthesia for arthroscopic shoulder surgery. We hypothesize that our findings will establish a volume-dependent risk-benefit profile for STB, enabling individualized LA volume selection in clinical practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400088722. Registered on 2024-08-26. www.chictr.org.cn .

articles.title: Awake craniotomy for drug-resistant non-oncological epilepsy: a systematic review of feasibility, reported safety, and seizure outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Complete resection of the epileptogenic zone offers the best chance of seizure control in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. However, surgical management remains challenging when the epileptogenic zone is located within or adjacent to eloquent brain regions. Awake craniotomy (AC), combined with intraoperative functional mapping, has the potential to maximize resection while preserving neurological function. Despite its increasing use, evidence regarding its safety and efficacy in epilepsy surgery remains limited. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the feasibility, reported safety, and reported seizure outcomes of awake craniotomy in patients undergoing surgery for drug-resistant non-oncological epilepsy.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases in accordance with PRISMA guidelines.
RESULTS: Seven retrospective studies comprising 231 patients from six countries were included; 120 patients underwent AC. Four studies (57.1%) included mixed adult and pediatric populations and three (42.9%) included adults only; however, none provided age-stratified seizure or complication outcomes, precluding separate pediatric analysis. Reported seizure duration ranged from 2 to 39 years. The frontal lobe was the most frequently involved region (n = 52; 43.3%), followed by the temporal lobe (n = 27; 22.5%), and cortical dysplasia was the most common underlying pathology (n = 30; 25.0%). Language and sensorimotor functions were the most commonly mapped eloquent areas, each reported in five studies (71.4%). Seizure outcomes were predominantly assessed using the Engel classification. Complete seizure freedom (Engel class I) was reported in 69 of 120 AC patients (57.5%); a random-effects single-arm synthesis estimated an Engel I proportion of 59.3% (95% CI: 46.3-71.2%; I2 = 31.9%). Comparisons with surgery under general anesthesia (GA) were available in only two non-randomized studies and should be interpreted cautiously. No study reported conversion from AC to GA. Postoperative neurological deficits were largely transient, with a low reported incidence of permanent morbidity. Owing to substantial differences in patient selection, surgical indications, and study design, these findings should be considered exploratory and should not be interpreted as demonstrating comparable seizure outcomes or treatment effectiveness.
CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with drug-resistant non-tumor epilepsy involving or adjacent to eloquent cortex, AC with intraoperative functional mapping appears feasible and may help preserve neurological function while enabling tailored resection. The current evidence base remains limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous populations and techniques, inconsistent outcome reporting, and sparse comparative data; therefore, efficacy and equivalence with surgery under general anesthesia should not be inferred.

articles.title: How reliable is percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy during the learning curve? A comparison of outcomes with microsurgical discectomy experiences.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to share our early experience with percutaneous transforaminal endoscopic discectomy (PTED) during the initial phase of the learning curve and to compare its clinical and perioperative outcomes with microsurgical discectomy (MD) in selected patients with symptomatic lumbar disc herniation (LDH).
METHODS: In this retrospective study, patients who underwent PTED or MD for symptomatic LDH since 2019 and completed at least 6 months of postoperative follow-up were analyzed. Patients with acute paresis, cauda equina syndrome, significant concomitant spinal stenosis, calcified disc herniation, high-positioned iliac crest preventing safe transforaminal access, markedly migrated disc fragments, or a need for multilevel surgery were excluded from the comparative cohort. VAS and ODI scores, operative duration, transfusion requirement, length of stay, complications, follow-up, and reoperation rates were evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 185 patients (88 PTED and 97 MD) were included. Postoperative VAS scores and ODI changes were not significantly different between the groups, while both techniques produced significant postoperative pain improvement. Mean operative duration was similar between the groups. PTED was associated with a shorter hospital stay (p < 0.001) and fewer perioperative complications (p = 0.004). No patient in the PTED group required transfusion; however, this variable should be interpreted as transfusion requirement rather than measured blood loss. Reoperation was required in 11 patients (7 PTED and 4 MD), without a statistically significant difference between groups (p = 0.125).
CONCLUSION: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic lumbar disc herniation, PTED provided postoperative pain relief and functional outcomes comparable to MD, even during the early learning curve period. PTED was also associated with shorter hospital stay and fewer postoperative complications, while operative times were similar between groups. However, given the retrospective design and selected patient population, these findings should be confirmed by prospective studies with longer follow-up and quantitative learning curve analysis.

articles.title: Bougie guided versus Endotracheal tube with Stylet guided intubation in critically injured patients with Difficult airway characteristics (BEST trial): randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency airway management in critically injured trauma patients is frequently complicated by distorted anatomy, airway contamination, cervical spine immobilisation, and prior airway manipulation. Although bougie and stylet are commonly used adjuncts for tracheal intubation, evidence comparing their effectiveness in difficult trauma airways remains limited. We aimed to compare first-pass intubation success between bougie-guided and stylet-guided tracheal intubation in critically injured trauma patients with predefined difficult airway characteristics.
METHODS: In this prospective randomised clinical trial, 188 adult critically injured trauma patients requiring emergency tracheal intubation and having at least one predefined difficult airway characteristic were randomised to bougie-guided intubation (Group B, n = 94) or stylet-guided intubation (Group S, n = 94). All first-attempt intubations were performed by trauma anaesthesia senior residents using video laryngoscopy and a standardised drug-assisted delayed sequence intubation protocol. The primary outcome was first-pass intubation success. Secondary outcomes included time to intubation, rescue airway interventions, need for alternate adjunct or front-of-neck access, and peri-intubation complications.
RESULTS: First-pass intubation success was achieved in 67 of 94 patients (71.3%) in Group B and 63 of 94 patients (67.0%) in Group S, corresponding to an absolute difference of 4.3% points (95% CI, - 8.9 to 17.2; p = 0.53). Time to successful first-attempt intubation was similar between groups (39.55 ± 11.72 s in Group B versus 37.97 ± 13.54 s in Group S; mean difference 1.58 s, 95% CI - 2.80 to 5.97; p = 0.48). Emergency front-of-neck access was required in one patient in Group B. Oesophageal intubation occurred in five patients (5.3%) in Group S and in none in Group B; this difference did not reach statistical significance using Fisher's exact test (p = 0.059). On multivariable logistic regression, polytrauma with facial fractures was associated with increased odds of first-pass intubation failure (adjusted OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.10-5.83; p = 0.028).
CONCLUSION: In selected trauma patients with predefined difficult-airway characteristics undergoing protocolised delayed sequence intubation with video laryngoscopy, no statistically significant difference in first-pass success was observed between bougie-guided and stylet-guided intubation. Oesophageal intubation occurred only in the stylet group, an exploratory finding that requires confirmation in larger studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was approved by the Institute Ethics Committee (IEC-INT-2022/MD-543) and registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2022/11/047043).
articles.journal: Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med

articles.title: Eleven questions on Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome management in the ICU.
articles.abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) due to Andes virus (ANDV) is a fulminant yet potentially reversible cause of respiratory and circulatory failure requiring timely critical care. This article addresses eleven practical questions on ICU management, drawing on clinical experience and research from the Chilean healthcare system. The recommendations cover early recognition, diagnostic workup, haemodynamic monitoring, cautious fluid and vasoactive support, respiratory management, VA-ECMO referral, daily ICU care, recovery, common pitfalls, and therapies with limited evidence. Because no antiviral or immunomodulatory therapy has consistently improved outcomes, survival relies on early suspicion, physiology-guided supportive care, and rapid escalation to ECMO-capable centres when severe cardiopulmonary failure develops.

articles.title: Minimally invasive transanal repair (MITAR) for rectovaginal fistulas: a novel technique.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A rectovaginal fistula (RVF) is an abnormal epithelialized connection between the rectum and vagina. Surgical repair is the treatment of choice but is challenging, particularly for fistulas in the middle and lower rectum, where conventional transabdominal or transperineal procedures offer limited access. This study describes a novel minimally invasive transanal repair (MITAR) technique for mid- and lower rectovaginal fistulas.
METHODS: RVF develop following vaginoplasty for a rudimentary vagina, low colorectal anastomosis for rectal carcinoma, and rectocele repair. All had preexisting protective diversion stomas. Patients were operated on under general anesthesia in the prone position. The transanal access port (Gel POINT path platform) was introduced, and the pneumorectum was maintained at 12-14 mmHg. The rectal and vaginal walls were separated at the fistula site and mobilized circumferentially along the rectovaginal septum for at least 1 cm. The mobilized vaginal and rectal walls were closed transversely one after the other through the transanal route. The diversion stoma was subsequently closed.
RESULTS: MITAR was completed successfully in all three patients. The technique provides direct access to the fistula site. A magnified and excellent endoscopic view helped with precise and meticulous dissection. Patient recovery was uneventful. At a mean follow-up of 29 months, there was no recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: MITAR is a safe, feasible, and effective approach for the repair of middle and low rectovaginal fistulas. This minimally invasive technique offers excellent visualization, precision, and tension-free closure of the fistula. This technique can be considered an alternative to existing techniques for RVF repair.

articles.title: Navigating intraoperative hypotension: rethinking traditional management for improved patient outcomes.
articles.abstract: Intraoperative hemodynamic instability and hypotension commonly occur in anesthetized patients and are associated with postoperative morbidity and mortality. A growing body of evidence establishes a strong correlation between intraoperative hypotension (IOH) and adverse events such as acute kidney injury (AKI), myocardial injury, postoperative cognitive dysfunction, and mortality. Recent recommendations for mean arterial pressure (MAP) maintenance above 65 mm Hg and consensus guidelines endorsing a MAP target of 60-70 mm Hg highlight the imperative for meticulous hemodynamic management. However, achieving this goal presents challenges for anesthesia clinicians. This article reviews issues with recent trends in hemodynamic monitoring and management strategies, emphasizing the importance of avoiding unintended patient harm by looking beyond traditional blood pressure management, such as relying solely on vasopressors.

articles.title: Stepwise versus one-step intubation strategy for tracheal injury in thoracic surgery: a multicenter randomized controlled trial protocol based on a combined visual lung isolation tube versus a video double-lumen tube.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracheal injury remains a clinically relevant complication during lung isolation for thoracic surgery. Although video double-lumen tubes (VDLTs) improve visualization during intubation and bronchial positioning, visualization alone may not sufficiently reduce airway trauma if post-glottic rotational manipulation remains necessary. A combined visual lung isolation tube (combined tube) was developed to enable a predefined stepwise insertion strategy while maintaining an external diameter comparable to that of a double-lumen tube. This trial aims to compare a stepwise strategy based on the combined tube with a conventional one-step strategy based on a VDLT.
METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial will enroll 192 adult patients undergoing elective thoracic surgery requiring left-sided one-lung ventilation. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to either the combined-tube group or the VDLT group. The primary outcome is the incidence of moderate-to-severe tracheal injury, defined as moderate or severe mucosal injury at the subglottic region, tracheal shaft, carina, or bronchus. Secondary outcomes include site-specific tracheal injury, vocal cord injury, postoperative sore throat, hoarseness, intubation-related variables, lung isolation quality, hypoxemic events, airway pressure variables, and perioperative adverse events. Bronchoscopic recordings will undergo centralized blinded review by two independent assessors. The primary analysis will be conducted in the full analysis set using mixed-effects regression models to account for center effects.
DISCUSSION: This trial will evaluate whether a predefined stepwise intubation strategy can reduce tracheal injury during lung isolation. By comparing two strategies represented by devices with comparable external diameters, the study may help distinguish the effect of insertion pathway from that of device size and provide mechanistic insight into the role of post-glottic rotational manipulation in airway injury.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR; Registration number: ChiCTR2600125149) on 21 May 2026. Details of the trial are publicly accessible at: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=321664 .

articles.title: Physiological determinants of piperacillin and cefazolin clearance in septic and trauma patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physiological alterations in patients with sepsis and trauma can influence antibiotic clearance, yet reliable predictors remain poorly defined. We aimed to investigate the determinants of piperacillin and cefazolin clearance in these populations to identify bedside indicators of subtherapeutic exposure.
METHODS: Prospective physiological and pharmacokinetic study in patients receiving piperacillin/tazobactam for sepsis or prophylactic cefazolin post-trauma. Patients also received intravenous sinistrin. Intensive pharmacokinetic sampling, cardiac output (CO) monitoring and four urinary creatinine clearance (uCLCR) measurements were performed. Data were analysed with non-compartmental pharmacokinetic methods, and linear and logistic regression.
RESULTS: We enrolled 49 septic and 28 trauma patients. Trauma patients were younger (33.5 vs. 46.5 years) and had higher uCLCR (155.5 vs. 107.5 mL/min). Linear regression identified that lower Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores and an hyperdynamic state with higher CO and 2 and 8-h uCLCR were the strongest predictors of increased piperacillin total clearance; higher 2-h uCLCR and hypoalbuminemia were the main predictors for cefazolin total clearance. Sinistrin CL was a weak predictor. Logistic regression identified augmented renal clearance (8-h uCLCR > 130 mL/min) as the main risk factor for piperacillin subtherapeutic exposure (OR 10.9, p < 0.05), also when defined using the Cockcroft-Gault cut-off of 114.5 mL/min from ROC analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: In sepsis, low sickness severity and a hyperdynamic state with high cardiac output lead to increased uCLCR and high piperacillin clearance. In trauma, high cefazolin clearance occurs in the presence of an elevated uCLCR and hypoalbuminemia. These bedside physiological indicators, along with Cockcroft-Gault CLCR, may serve as early indicators of risk for subtherapeutic exposure.

articles.title: Clinical application of a dual-surface, four-edge 3D-printed pedicle screw guide in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis surgery: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate pedicle screw placement is essential for safety in scoliosis correction surgery. Conventional freehand techniques are operator-dependent, while navigation-assisted techniques may increase intraoperative imaging requirements and workflow complexity. Patient-specific 3D-printed drill guide templates have been proposed to improve accuracy and reduce imaging use.
METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated the clinical efficacy, safety, and accuracy of a novel dual-surface four-edge 3D-printed drill guide template versus computer navigation-assisted and freehand techniques. A total of 64 patients (24 males, 40 females) undergoing posterior pedicle screw fixation at Fuyang People's Hospital from January 2017 to January 2024 were included, with 1204 screws placed. In this retrospective, non-randomized cohort, patients were grouped according to the screw placement technique actually used during surgery: Group A (3D-printed guide, n = 22, 430 screws), Group B (navigation-assisted, n = 18, 357 screws), and Group C (freehand, n = 24, 417 screws). Screw accuracy was assessed using the Gertzbein-Robbins system (A-E). The primary metric was the proportion of Grade A screws; Grade A + B was additionally reported as clinically acceptable placement and Grades C-E as clinically relevant breach, together with screw revisions. Baseline characteristics, deformity-correction outcomes, perioperative indicators, intraoperative C-arm fluoroscopy acquisitions, and complications were compared among groups.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics (age, sex, BMI, preoperative Cobb angle, sagittal vertical axis, coronal balance distance, Lenke classification, number of fused segments) were comparable among groups (P > 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in coronal and sagittal offset correction, number of screws, intraoperative blood loss, or length of hospital stay (P > 0.05). The main curve correction rate was also comparable (P = 0.608). Group A required significantly fewer recorded intraoperative 2D C-arm fluoroscopy acquisitions than Groups B and C (P < 0.001). Grade A + B acceptable placement rates were 99.30, 96.36, and 96.64%, and clinically relevant breach (Grades C-E) occurred in 0.70, 3.64, and 3.36% of screws in Groups A, B, and C, respectively; no screw revision was required in any group. In the primary cluster-adjusted GEE analysis, the 3D-printed guide group showed a higher Grade A placement rate than the freehand group (OR = 3.48, 95% CI: 2.67-4.53, Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.001) and than the navigation-assisted group (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.20-2.10, Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.004). One postoperative incision infection occurred in Group B, and one case of cerebrospinal fluid leakage occurred in Group C; no other surgery-related complications were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, all three techniques were associated with few observed complications and postoperative improvement. The dual-surface, four-edge 3D-printed guide was associated with fewer intraoperative 2D C-arm fluoroscopy acquisitions and high screw-placement accuracy. After accounting for clustering of screws within patients, the comparisons with both freehand and navigation-assisted placement favored the 3D-printed guide; however, these comparative findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective, non-randomized design and potential temporal confounding. These findings support the clinical feasibility of the guide, but further prospective studies with patient-level and cluster-adjusted analyses are needed to confirm its comparative effectiveness.

articles.title: A Survey of Clinician-Reported Management of Hypernatremia in the ICU.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypernatremia is frequent in the intensive care unit (ICU) and is associated with adverse outcomes. Despite its prevalence, robust evidence to guide treatment is lacking, and global practice patterns are largely unknown. We investigated global treatment preferences and clinicians' willingness to enroll patients in a randomized trial to inform its feasibility.
METHODS: This international cross-sectional online survey comprised 20 primarily closed-ended questions, using five-point Likert-scale responses, across four themes: treatment method, threshold, correction rate, and opinion on a proposed trial. Respondents considered a clinical vignette of hypernatremia developing before or during ICU admission, excluding dehydration and chronic causes. It was distributed to ICU physicians worldwide.
RESULTS: The survey was sent to 3053 ICU physicians in 17 countries, with 1051 respondents, yielding a response rate of 34%. Of respondents, 74% were consultants, and 26% were residents. The mean ICU experience was 14 years. Increasing free water intake via enteral route was the most frequently reported treatment strategy (80% reporting "often" or "always"). Moderate hypernatremia (plasma sodium 151-156 mmol/L) was the most frequently reported threshold for initiating correction (533/892, 60%). 45% (396/888) preferred a correction rate of 8-12 mmol/L/day, and 41% (366/888) of < 8 mmol/L/day, with the remainder having no correction rate target or correction rate target of > 12 mmol/L/day. 74% (654/882) reported no barriers to enrolling eligible patients in the proposed trial.
CONCLUSION: Among ICU physicians, correction of hypernatremia is mostly achieved by increasing free water intake using hypotonic fluids, predominantly via the enteral route. Most clinicians initiate treatment once hypernatremia reaches a moderate level, aiming for a correction rate of < 12 mmol/L/day. Most clinicians expressed willingness to enroll eligible patients in the proposed trial.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This survey study aimed to sample physician preferences for treatment of hypernatremia when on their way to or in the ICU. This study sampled respondents in many countries, and based on different phases of treatment and assessment, as well as participant willingness for a future treatment trial.

articles.title: Development, Implementation and Mixed-Methods Evaluation of a Multicomponent Peer-Support Programme in an Anaesthesiology Department.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare professionals working in anaesthesiology are exposed to frequent emotionally challenging situations. Many well-being initiatives focus on individual coping or support after major events, whereas less attention has been given to organisationally embedded support for everyday work-related challenges. We aimed to describe the development, implementation, uptake and staff experience of a department-wide peer-support programme.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre, uncontrolled pre-post mixed-methods implementation and evaluation study in a university hospital anaesthesiology department. Kern's six-step approach guided development and implementation of a multicomponent programme comprising education about well-being and psychological safety, leadership modelling, local change champions, structured collegial conversations and brief team defusing. Evaluation combined pre- and post-intervention surveys, implementation/process data and post-intervention group interviews. Survey outcomes across five dimensions-well-being, coping, teamwork, psychological safety and patient safety culture-were exploratory.
RESULTS: Approximately 80% of staff were trained in structured collegial conversations; 55% of post-intervention respondents reported participating in at least one structured collegial conversation and 35% in at least one defusing. Across the five survey dimensions there was no consistent pattern of change. In exploratory analyses, the proportion of respondents with coping scores in the highest quartile increased from 31.3% to 42.0% (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.08-2.34), while the proportion reporting 'being new' as a source of emotional burden decreased from 14.0% to 6.8% (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.23-0.86). Group interview participants described a shared language for discussing challenging experiences, increased attention to colleagues' support needs and value in the structured listening approach. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the uncontrolled design and multiple exploratory outcomes.
CONCLUSION: A multicomponent peer-support programme was implemented with substantial staff participation in an anaesthesiology department. The study provides evidence about implementation, uptake and staff experience, but does not establish that the programme caused improvements in well-being or organisational culture. Leadership engagement, local champions and integration into existing departmental structures appeared important to implementation.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: The present study describes the implementation of a departmental peer-support programme addressing everyday emotional challenges in anaesthesiology. Substantial participation and positive qualitative accounts suggest that structured conversations can be integrated into clinical practice. However, inconsistent survey findings and the uncontrolled design preclude strong conclusions about effectiveness.

articles.title: Patient-referenced and trajectory features from serial ECGs for haemodynamic monitoring: an in silico study with external feasibility analysis.
articles.abstract: Objective.Physiological measurements are read against population thresholds, although the within-person change that signals deterioration is smaller than the spread between people. We asked, in simulation, whether serial electrocardiograms read against a patient's own earlier recording carry information about haemodynamic state, and whether the trajectory of that change adds to its current value, in acute haemorrhage.Approach.A nine-dimensional circulatory state-space model generated 600 synthetic subjects in whom haemorrhage reached the waveform only through subject-specific couplings. Results were audited against elapsed time and heart rate, repeated under alternative observation models and with an unknown bleeding onset, and examined in an external feasibility analysis of 77 intraoperative recordings.Main results.Under the generative model, a personal reference raised state discrimination from 0.847 to 0.951 but helped event prediction less than the slope and curvature of the change, which raised five-minute decompensation discrimination from 0.876 to 0.953. Elapsed time, patient characteristics and heart rate reached 0.930 without any electrocardiogram; with onset randomised that shortcut disappeared and the waveform still added +0.084. This division of labour held in all 7 observation models and 24 sampled coupling sets. Intraoperatively, patient-referenced features discriminated concurrent hypotension better (0.683) than absolute features or heart rate, but added nothing distinguishable from zero to the recorded anaesthetic and ventilatory state.Significance.Under the stated assumptions, a personal reference estimates where a patient is and its trajectory where they are going. The external cohort provides preliminary evidence for the portability of the patient-referenced representation but is insufficient to establish clinical performance.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes of Bariatric Surgery Across Chronic Kidney Disease Stages: National Inpatient Sample Analysis 2016-2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery is increasingly performed in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but perioperative outcomes across CKD severity remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated stage-specific perioperative outcomes after bariatric surgery in a contemporary national cohort.
METHODS: We analyzed 284,230 adult bariatric surgery hospitalizations from the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), stratified as no CKD, CKD stages 1-2, 3, 4, 5, and dialysis-dependent end-stage renal disease (ESRD). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included acute kidney injury, major bleeding, sepsis, acute respiratory failure, new dialysis, length of stay, and hospital charges. Survey-weighted multivariable regression (the primary models) evaluated associations between CKD stage and outcomes. A separate fully specified mortality model included CKD stage, age group, sex, diabetes, frailty, procedure type, and hospital volume.
RESULTS: CKD was documented in 3.4% of hospitalizations. Crude mortality was 0.3% without CKD, 2.0% in stage 3, 5.9% in stage 4, and 4.9% in dialysis-dependent ESRD. In the primary models, stage 4 CKD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.85, 95% CI 2.58-5.75) and ESRD (aOR 7.34, 95% CI 5.33-10.12) were associated with greater mortality, whereas stages 1-3 were not significantly associated with mortality after adjustment. Advanced CKD was also associated with greater bleeding, sepsis, respiratory failure, and resource utilization. Stage 4 CKD was strongly associated with new dialysis (primary model aOR 16.47, 95% CI 9.19-29.51). Sleeve gastrectomy had lower crude event rates than Roux-en-Y gastric bypass across CKD strata, although the procedure-by-stage interaction for a composite adverse event was modest (P = 0.048).
CONCLUSION: Advanced CKD, particularly stage 4 disease and dialysis-dependent ESRD, was associated with substantially greater in-hospital risk after bariatric surgery. These findings support CKD-stage-specific risk assessment, multidisciplinary perioperative management, and individualized procedural planning. Observed differences between procedures should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for residual confounding.

articles.title: Decision support and automation in goal-directed fluid therapy: current evidence and remaining questions.
articles.abstract: Goal-directed fluid therapy (GDFT) individualizes perioperative fluid administration according to dynamic hemodynamic variables, but its implementation remains inconsistent and its impact on patient-centered outcomes is still debated. Decision-support and automated systems have been developed to improve adherence, identify fluid responsiveness more efficiently, and reduce the workload of protocolized hemodynamic management. This structured narrative review summarizes the evidence across four outcome levels: process, surrogate hemodynamic, intermediate physiological, and patient-centered clinical. The most consistent evidence concerns process improvement: decision support increases protocol adherence and improves the proportion of fluid challenges that achieve a predefined stroke volume response, largely on non-randomized evidence. Improvements in surrogate hemodynamic control have also been reported, and selected randomized trials suggest favorable effects on microcirculatory flow and lactate. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical benefit. Fluid responsiveness does not necessarily indicate a need for fluid administration, and most available studies remain small, single-center, or focused on surrogate outcomes. Evidence that these systems improve postoperative complications, acute kidney injury, length of stay, or mortality is currently lacking. Ongoing multicenter trials should address this gap. Decision support appears to improve how perioperative fluids are administered, but whether it improves what ultimately happens to patients remains unresolved.

articles.title: Effect of age on the association between oxygen exposure and mortality in ARDS: a secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials with independent multicenter evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractions of inspired oxygen up to 60% in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation are commonly perceived by clinicians as safe, implying a non-linear association between oxygen exposure and mortality. Also, although it seems pathophysiologically plausible that the association between oxygen exposure and mortality may depend on age, relevant evidence in adult patients is lacking. We examined whether the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality a) is non-linear and b) depends on age.
METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of individual patient-level data from six acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) Network and PETAL Network randomized controlled trials ("ARDSNet cohort"). We assessed linearity of the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality along with the effect of age after adjusting for covariates, including partial pressure of arterial oxygen. We tested our findings in an independent multicenter cohort.
RESULTS: In the ARDSNet cohort involving 4953 patients with ARDS, we found that the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality was linear and independent of age (p = 0.655 for the interaction between fraction of inspired oxygen and age). In the independent cohort involving 559 patients with ARDS, we confirmed both the linearity of the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality and the lack of effect of age (p = 0.955 for the interaction).
CONCLUSION: Data from the two tested multicenter cohorts suggest that the association between fraction of inspired oxygen and mortality in ARDS may be linear and independent of age.
authors: Greek REsearch on Treatment of Acute illness Collaborators (GRETA)

articles.title: Going the Extra Mile for Stroke Thrombectomy Patients.

Perinatal multidisciplinary management for neonates with prenatally-diagnosed congenital complete heart block undergoing early epicardial pacemaker implantation: a retrospective single-center case series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report our single-center multidisciplinary perinatal experience for neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated congenital complete heart block (CCHB) requiring early epicardial pacemaker implantation.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included four consecutive neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated CCHB (2016-2020). A multidisciplinary team coordinated perinatal planning. Maternal data, fetal echocardiography, delivery-room resuscitation, vasoactive support, and short-term neonatal outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Four neonates (gestation 35 + 6-37 + 6 weeks; birth weight 2270-2500 g) were delivered by cesarean section. Umbilical vein catheterization was achieved rapidly in all. All neonates had a heart rate <50 bpm at birth and received immediate vasoactive resuscitation. All neonates underwent successful epicardial permanent pacemaker implantation within 10 days after birth with improved cardiac function and were discharged home. One infant was readmitted 8 days after discharge due to pocket infection and ultimately died on postnatal day 46.
CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary coordination, early umbilical-vein access, and individualized vasoactive support are critical for managing these high-risk neonates. Our findings provide practical guidance but require validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Pre-operative respiratory optimisation before paediatric neuromuscular scoliosis surgery: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Respiratory complications remain a major cause of perioperative morbidity following paediatric neuromuscular scoliosis (NMS) surgery. Although respiratory optimisation strategies are widely used, their effectiveness remains uncertain. This systematic review evaluated respiratory optimisation strategies and postoperative pulmonary outcomes in children undergoing NMS correction.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to June 2026. Studies evaluating respiratory optimisation in paediatric NMS surgery were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed methodological quality using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Findings were synthesised narratively owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Ten observational studies involving 308 children were included. Interventions comprised non-invasive ventilation (NIV), mechanical insufflation-exsufflation, pulmonary rehabilitation, inspiratory muscle training, protocolised extubation and multidisciplinary perioperative pathways. NIV-based protocols reported successful early extubation and few respiratory complications, including amongst children with severe restrictive lung disease. Pulmonary rehabilitation and inspiratory muscle training were associated with improved pre-operative respiratory function, whilst multidisciplinary pathways reported favourable postoperative outcomes. Four studies had low and six had moderate methodological risk. However, the certainty of evidence was very low across principal respiratory outcomes, reflecting uncontrolled designs, heterogeneous interventions and imprecise comparative estimates.
CONCLUSIONS: Structured respiratory optimisation appears feasible in children undergoing NMS correction, including those with substantial respiratory impairment. NIV and airway clearance are recurring components of reported pathways, but their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to establish effective optimisation strategies and standardise perioperative respiratory care.

articles.title: Distribution of applied forces during face mask ventilation: a preterm neonatal manikin study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resuscitators may apply different forces to optimize the mask seal during neonatal resuscitation. We investigated the distribution of applied forces across the face of a preterm neonatal manikin during positive pressure ventilation.
DESIGN: This sub-study involved 30 neonatologists and pediatric/anesthesiology residents participating in a scenario of a preterm infant requiring face mask ventilation. The outcome was the force applied on the manikin face by the operator using a soft-cushion anatomical mask. Force was recorded by sensors positioned on the nose, right chin, central chin and left chin. Force-related indicators included maximum force, average peak force and standard deviation of applied forces.
RESULTS: The sensors recorded higher median applied forces on the nose than on the right chin (maximum force: median difference [MD] 0.9 N, 99%CI 0.2 to 1.3; average peak force: MD 0.9 N, 99%CI 0.1 to 1.1). The sensors also recorded higher values of top 10th percentile of applied forces (maximum force, average peak force and standard deviation of applied forces) on the nose, central chin and left chin compared to the right chin.
CONCLUSIONS: The participants applied uneven forces across key points of the manikin face during face mask ventilation. Providing trainees with real-time feedback on applied forces may improve the acquisition of PPV skills.
IMPACT: In a preterm neonatal manikin model, health care providers exerted uneven force on different key points of the manikin face during face mask ventilation. The operator may be prone to apply more force on the hand-holding side. Offering real-time feedback on applied forces to trainees may improve the attainment of PPV skills.

articles.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial.
SETTING: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24.
PARTICIPANTS: 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.
RESULTS: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.
CONCLUSION: Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chictr.org.cn ChiCTR2300071399.

articles.title: Perioperative Determinants of Anastomotic Leak after Pediatric Esophageal Replacement: A 27-Year Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal replacement (ER) in children, primarily for caustic stricture or long-gap atresia, remains a high-morbidity procedure. Anastomotic leak is a critical postoperative complication. This study aimed to identify perioperative predictors of anastomotic leak following colonic interposition, thereby guiding risk stratification and management.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort study included 51 pediatric patients (median age: 48 months) who underwent colonic interposition for ER between 1998 and 2025. Cervical anastomotic leak within 30 days was the primary outcome.
