Patients with and without leak were compared using univariate analysis of demographic, preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables, followed by multivariate logistic regression. A secondary analysis was performed in the caustic stenosis subgroup (n = 43).
RESULTS: Anastomotic leak occurred in 12 patients (23.5%). On univariate analysis, patients with leak were younger, more often had a preoperative feeding stoma, less frequently received nasogastric tube placement, and had higher rates of postoperative respiratory complications with longer ventilation duration. In multivariate analysis, older age at ER was independently associated with a decreased risk of anastomotic leak (a OR 0.95 per month; 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.017). Conversely, a preoperative feeding stoma independently increased the odds of leak formation (a OR of 15.00; 95% CI 2.64-85.19; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, younger age at ER and a preoperative feeding stoma were independently associated with anastomotic leak. Among children with caustic stricture, severe initial esophageal injury and a complicated dilatation history were also associated with leak. These findings support individualized preoperative risk assessment and should be validated in larger multicenter studies.

articles.title: Contemporary Management of Vesicouterine Fistula.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Vesicouterine fistula (VUF) is an uncommon complication that predominantly occurs after cesarean delivery. Current evidence regarding its diagnosis and management is limited and largely derived from small retrospective studies.
OBJECTIVE: The objective was to evaluate the etiological factors, clinical characteristics, diagnostic approaches, and surgical outcomes associated with VUF through a systematic review and proportional meta-analysis.
STUDY DESIGN: This systematic review and proportional meta-analysis was carried out following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science databases identified studies published between 2006 and 2026. Studies including at least 8 patients with VUF and reporting clinical or surgical outcomes were eligible. Pooled prevalence estimates with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Eight retrospective studies involving 447 patients were included. Cesarean delivery was the predominant etiological factor (pooled proportion, 95.3%), while a history of repeat cesarean delivery was identified in 78.4% of patients. Cyclic hematuria represented the most characteristic symptom. Cystoscopy was the most frequently used diagnostic modality. Surgical treatment demonstrated a pooled success rate of 97.1%, with low recurrence and postoperative complication rates of 4.3% and 5.6%, respectively. Open abdominal repair remained the most common surgical approach, although minimally invasive surgery was increasingly reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Vesicouterine fistula has evolved into a predominantly cesarean delivery-related iatrogenic condition with diverse clinical manifestations. Surgical repair provides excellent outcomes with low recurrence when appropriate reconstructive principles are followed. Although the pooled surgical success rate of 97.1% is impressive, this estimate is derived entirely from retrospective observational studies, several of which are small case series. Minimally invasive surgery is a feasible option in selected patients, but comparative evidence is insufficient to determine whether it improves perioperative or long-term outcomes relative to open abdominal repair.

articles.title: Fluid dynamics of local anesthetic spread: a hypothesis-generating review.
The Role of Treatment Choice in Open-Label Placebo Analgesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Open-label placebos (OLPs; placebos administered without deception) can reduce pain. However, their effects are sometimes smaller than those of deceptive placebos. The present study (DRKS00038359) investigated whether allowing participants to choose a specific OLP type (capsule vs. spray in four different colors) could enhance its efficacy. A total of 90 healthy females (M = 23.2 years, SD = 2.92) were assigned to one of three groups: two groups receiving an OLP for pain reduction, either with the opportunity to choose the OLP type or with no choice, and a control group receiving no placebo. All participants underwent transcutaneous electrical stimulation twice during the experiment (baseline assessment and after OLP treatment or a waiting period) to assess perceived pain intensity. To identify factors that may influence the OLP effect, several trait measures were included, such as reported pain sensitivity and positive superstition (the belief that certain objects/ rituals can bring positive outcomes). The OLP reduced reported pain intensity regardless of whether participants were given the opportunity to choose the placebo type. Overall, there was no preference for capsules versus sprays or for any particular color in the choice group. Higher levels of positive superstition were associated with greater pain reduction in the OLP groups, whereas the opposite pattern was observed for reported pain sensitivity. PERSPECTIVE: Providing participants with a choice of placebo type did not further enhance analgesic effects. However, trait differences were associated with the responsiveness to OLP treatment and should be considered in future research.

articles.title: Built to last: Online operant conditioning induces nocebo expectancies resistant to modification in patients with chronic pain and pain-free participants.
articles.abstract: Digital environments increasingly shape health beliefs and treatment expectancies, including negative expectancies that may contribute to nocebo effects. This study examined whether nocebo expectancies can be induced online through operant conditioning, reduced through verbal modeling, and whether these processes differ between patients with chronic pain and pain-free participants. Participants were assigned to one of four groups: experimental pain-free, experimental chronic pain, control pain-free, and control chronic pain. They watched videos of a model receiving pain stimuli either with or without a placebo. During the induction phase, participants rated how much pain they expected the model to experience after each stimulus. In the experimental groups, responses indicating higher expected pain in the placebo trial were reinforced by the experimenter, whereas reinforcement was noncontingent in the control groups. During the modification phase, participants observed the model receiving pain stimuli and were shown ratings allegedly provided by other participants, suggesting that others had rated the model's pain in the placebo trial as lower than in the control trial; in the control groups, these ratings were presented randomly. After each phase and again after a 3-day delay, participants rated expected pain in the placebo and control trials. Online operant conditioning effectively induced nocebo expectancies, which were not reduced by online verbal modeling and persisted after a 3-day delay. No significant differences emerged between patients with chronic pain and pain-free participants. These findings suggest that brief expert-delivered online feedback may be sufficient to shape nocebo expectancies that are resistant to subsequent modification. PERSPECTIVE: Online operant conditioning induced nocebo expectancies that were resistant to modification through verbal modeling and persisted after a 3-day delay. These findings highlight the role of online environments in shaping negative treatment expectancies and suggest that such expectancies can develop similarly in both chronic pain and pain-free populations.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Co-prescription and Pain Trajectories in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain management in hospitalized internal medicine patients is challenging due to multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and behavioral symptoms. Antipsychotics are frequently co-prescribed with analgesics in this population alongside other central nervous system-active medications, yet their relationship with acute pain trajectories remains poorly understood. This retrospective cohort study examined whether antipsychotic co-prescription was associated with pain trajectories and rehospitalization among hospitalized medical patients receiving analgesic therapy, including an opioid-treated subgroup.
METHODS: Internal medicine inpatients receiving in-hospital analgesic therapy were included. Pain outcomes comprised mean, maximum, and last visual analog scale (VAS) scores and peak-to-last change in VAS (ΔVAS); all-cause rehospitalization was assessed after discharge. Propensity score matching accounted for demographic and clinical factors. Additional analyses examined timing of antipsychotic exposure and co-treatment with other central nervous system-active medications.
RESULTS: Among 18,387 patients hospitalized for ≥ 48 h, 6166 with at least one VAS assessment within the first 2 days of hospitalization formed the analgesic-treated cohort, including 2388 receiving opioids. After matching, antipsychotic co-prescription was associated with lower mean and maximum VAS scores in the analgesic-treated cohort, particularly among older adults. The association was most evident among patients already receiving antipsychotics at admission, whereas findings among those initiated during hospitalization were limited. No consistent differences in pain outcomes were observed in the opioid subgroup, while associations in the broader analgesic cohort persisted across central nervous system (CNS) co-medication strata. Antipsychotic co-prescription was not associated with sustained increases in rehospitalization risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Antipsychotic co-prescription was associated with lower peak pain intensity in the broader analgesic-treated cohort, particularly among older adults, but not in the opioid subgroup. This context-dependent pattern differed according to analgesic treatment and timing of antipsychotic exposure and may reflect differences in multidimensional pain processing. These findings highlight the importance of considering central nervous system-active co-medications in pain management and warrant prospective investigation.

articles.title: Remimazolam versus propofol for sedation in mechanically ventilated ICU patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Propofol is widely used for sedation in the intensive care unit (ICU), but its use may be limited by cardiovascular depression, hypertriglyceridemia, and propofol infusion syndrome. Remimazolam has emerged as a potential alternative to propofol, with rapid metabolism, predictable recovery, and flumazenil reversibility. However, evidence regarding its use in mechanically ventilated ICU patients remains limited.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrial.gov databases were reviewed for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing remimazolam with propofol in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. The primary outcome was percentage of time within the target sedation range. Secondary outcomes included sedation success rate, 28-day mortality, ICU mortality, length of ICU stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation. Safety outcomes including adverse events leading to dose reduction, hypotension, and delirium were evaluated. Continuous endpoints were reported using mean differences (MDs), and dichotomous outcomes were analyzed using risk ratios (RRs), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Six RCTs including 705 patients were analyzed. No statistically significant difference was detected in the percentage of time within the target sedation range (MD, -0.45%; 95% CI, -2.46 to 1.55; p = 0.56; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were detected in sedation success rate, 28-day mortality, ICU mortality, ICU length of stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation, or safety outcomes, although several estimates were imprecise.
CONCLUSION: Remimazolam probably results in little to no difference in sedation efficacy compared with propofol in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. However, uncertainty remains regarding clinical and safety outcomes. Larger multinational RCTs are warranted to clarify these effects.

articles.title: Impact of the updated SOFA-2 score on organ dysfunction assessment and trial outcomes in Sepsis: A reanalysis of two randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score is the standard tool for quantifying organ dysfunction in sepsis. The updated SOFA-2 score may alter interpretation of prior trials. We reanalyzed two adult sepsis randomized trials, Ascorbic Acid, Corticosteroids, and Thiamine in Sepsis (ACTS) and Thiamine for Renal Protection in Septic Shock (TRPSS), to evaluate the impact of SOFA-2 on organ-specific scoring and trial interpretation.
METHODS: Patient data were rescored using a best available SOFA-2 reconstruction. Subscores were compared between SOFA-1 and SOFA-2 at baseline, 24, 48, and 72 h using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Gwet's AC2. Trial outcomes were reanalyzed using linear mixed-effects models with SOFA-2. A post hoc, exploratory sensitivity analysis incorporated approximated urine output into the renal subscore.
RESULTS: SOFA-2 produced lower total scores than SOFA-1 in both cohorts (ACTS 9 vs. 7; TRPSS 11 vs. 10; both p < 0.001), with lower respiratory and cardiovascular and higher coagulation subscores. For the ACTS primary outcome, SOFA-2 (mean difference [MD] -0.8, 95% CI -1.6 to 0.0, p = 0.06) was similar to SOFA-1 (MD -0.8, 95% CI -1.7 to 0.2, p = 0.12) but became significant in the post hoc, exploratory urine-output analysis (MD -0.84, 95% CI -1.64 to -0.05, p = 0.04). In TRPSS, SOFA-2 did not change overall interpretation but attenuated the treatment effect at all timepoints.
CONCLUSIONS: SOFA-2 changes how organ dysfunction is defined and may influence interpretation of prior trials, particularly when urine output is included. These findings support SOFA-version transparency and prospective SOFA-2 validation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTS: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03389555), registered December 28, 2017; TRPSS: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03550794), registered May 25, 2018.

articles.title: Oxygen consumption as a measure of metabolic demand during early rehabilitation and bedside activity in critically ill adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early rehabilitation and bedside activity can increase oxygen demand during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but the magnitude and variability of this response remain uncertain. To quantify acute changes in oxygen consumption (VO₂) during rehabilitation and bedside activity in adults receiving IMV and compare intervention domains.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 6, 2026. Activity-related percentage changes in VO₂ were pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using revised Joanna Briggs Institute tools.
RESULTS: Twenty studies were included, and 11 contributed 14 estimates to the primary meta-analysis. VO₂ increased by 29.2% from baseline (95% CI, 16.2%-43.6%; I2 = 96.2%; 95% prediction interval, -9.7% to 84.7%). All 14 point estimates were above baseline (+3.1% to +66.3%), although not all were individually statistically significant. Pooled estimates were higher for respiratory physiotherapy (43.3%; 95% CI, 32.3%-55.2%) than for other rehabilitation and bedside interventions (18.4%; 95% CI, -0.2%-40.5%), although this domain comparison was exploratory and confounded by study era and case mix. Mean arterial pressure and cardiac output showed pooled increases; other secondary analyses included few comparable studies.
CONCLUSION: Oxygen consumption was above baseline in all 14 point estimates, with a pooled increase of 29.2% and estimates ranging from 3.1% to 66.3%. Responses did not follow a simple passive-to-active pattern, showing that clinically indicated bedside care and rehabilitation can impose markedly different metabolic loads. When perceived exertion cannot be assessed, VO₂ offers an objective measure of session-specific metabolic demand that can be interpreted alongside the patient's cardiorespiratory reserve.

articles.title: Reduced desaturation-based detection of sleep apnea events in self-identified Black individuals across two cohorts.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing.
OBJECTIVES: To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification.
METHODS: We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68-0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68-0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09-1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02-1.55]; p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Diaphragmatic Neurostimulation: Potentially Beneficial, Possibly Cost-Saving, but Uncertain Cost-Effectiveness.
Predictors of failed outpatient total hip arthroplasty: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outpatient total hip arthroplasty (THA) offers potential cost savings and efficiency benefits in publicly funded health systems; however, the procedure fails for a subset of patients. This study aimed to identify the primary reasons for failed outpatient THA and perioperative factors associated with failure.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients booked for outpatient primary THA based on institutional eligibility criteria at a single tertiary care centre between January 2015 and December 2021. We obtained demographic, clinical, and operative data from institutional databases. We classified patients as having successful or failed outpatient discharge. Between-group comparisons used t tests and χ2 analyses, and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of failed discharge.
RESULTS: Of 768 patients booked for outpatient THA, 87 (11.3%) required inpatient admission. The most common reasons for failure were inability to meet ambulation goals (24.1%) and hypoxemia (24.1%). Patients with failed discharges had higher rates of diabetes (p < 0.001), cardiac disease (p = 0.001), and obstructive sleep apnea (p = 0.01). Failure rates increased with later operative start times (p = 0.01). Surgical approach and anesthetic type did not differ between patients with successful or failed discharges. In multivariable analysis, diabetes (odds ratio [OR] 3.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.56 to 7.13), cardiac disease (OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.27 to 4.51), midday (OR 3.39, 95% CI 1.60 to 7.16), and afternoon start times (OR 4.49, 95% CI 1.65 to 12.21) independently predicted failed discharge.
CONCLUSION: Operative start time, diabetes, and cardiac disease are significant independent risk factors for failed outpatient discharge following primary THA. These findings underscore the importance of comprehensive preoperative risk assessment and optimized perioperative management for high-risk patients to improve the safety and efficiency of outpatient THA programs.

articles.title: Outcome Disparities in Geriatric Hip Fracture: Orthogeriatric Co-Management Versus Internal Medicine Admission.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fracture carries substantial morbidity and mortality in older adults. Orthogeriatric co-management has emerged as the evidence-based standard of care, yet the influence of admitting service on outcomes at institutions where such programs exist remains poorly characterized.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Patients aged 65 or older who underwent operative management of hip fractures at an urban academic safety-net institution between January 2019 and December 2022. After excluding patients admitted to other services or requiring intensive care, the final cohort comprised 443 patients (349 orthogeriatric co-management, 94 internal medicine).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study compared outcomes between patients admitted to an orthogeriatric co-management service versus internal medicine. Internal medicine patients received no formal geriatric involvement. Univariate logistic regression assessed associations between admitting service and binary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression for 1-year mortality adjusted for age, sex, and ASA score. A matched analysis paired patients 1:1 on ASA score, sex, and age within 3 years using McNemar and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, including ASA score, age, comorbidity burden, and fracture type. Internal medicine admission was associated with higher 1-year mortality (OR: 3.01, 95% CI: 1.53-5.83, p = 0.001), greater surgical delay beyond 24 h (OR: 3.16, 95% CI: 1.98-5.12, p < 0.001), longer length of stay (p < 0.001), and reduced follow-up within 3 weeks (OR: 0.32, p < 0.001). In 91 matched pairs, these associations persisted for 1-year mortality (p = 0.035), surgical delay (p < 0.001), follow-up (p = 0.003), and length of stay (p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was consistent with the univariate and matched analyses (OR: 2.66, 95% CI: 1.32-5.25, p = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: Admitting service is associated with hip fracture outcomes, and this association was not explained by measured patient complexity. These findings support implementation of service-agnostic hip fracture protocols ensuring consistent surgical timing and perioperative management regardless of admitting service, particularly when serving high-risk populations.

articles.title: Network Trauma Research series: Modeling Trauma Complexity: Rodent Platforms for Studying Bone Healing and Hemorrhagic Shock.
articles.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions often accompanied by physiological instability, remains a major global health burden with high morbidity and mortality. Among the most clinically relevant two-injury combinations, long-bone fractures and hemorrhagic shock are particularly important, as both critically influence systemic inflammation, remote organ dysfunction such as lung or kidney damage, and tissue regeneration itself. To improve translational understanding of these complex interactions, robust small-animal models, particularly murine systems, have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying fracture healing, hypovolemic shock, and their combined effects. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current rodent models for isolated fracture, hemorrhagic shock, and combination trauma. Key methodological variables, such as fracture induction methods, fixation strategies, hemorrhage protocols, anesthesia and analgesia, and the influence of age, sex, and comorbidities are outlined to support informed model selection. Additionally, this manuscript highlights the challenges and opportunities in designing clinically relevant "double-hit" models that mimic real-world trauma patterns while maintaining high reproducibility and animal welfare standards. Collectively, the summarized evidence underscores the importance of standardized, physiologically meaningful preclinical trauma models to advance mechanistic insights and foster the development of effective therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Global, regional, and national burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages.
METHODS: We used estimates from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to assess the burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Mortality was modelled with the Cause of Death Ensemble model and prevalence with the Disease Modelling Meta-Regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Years of life lost (YLLs) were calculated as the number of deaths for each age-sex-location-year multiplied by the standard life expectancy at each age. Severity-specific prevalence values were multiplied by their respective disability weights (with asymptomatic cases assigned zero disability) to estimate years lived with disability (YLDs). Disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were computed by summing YLDs and YLLs. We report prevalence, mortality, YLDs, YLLs, and DALYs as counts and age-standardised and age-specific rates per 100 000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), stratified by sex, GBD region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI).
FINDINGS: In 1990 and 2023, the global counts for prevalence attributable to gallbladder and biliary diseases were 157·4 million (95% UI 134·0 to 183·3) and 264·4 million (226·0 to 309·9), for deaths were 65 800 (95% UI 53 000 to 78 800) and 146 700 (121 800 to 171 300), and for DALYs were 4·8 million (95% UI 3·5 to 6·2) and 8·2 million (6·3 to 10·6), representing substantial increases. However, age-standardised rates declined over the same period, from 3573·2 (95% UI 3045·5 to 4159·1) per 100 000 population to 2990·1 (2561·5 to 3492·5) per 100 000 population for prevalence, from 1·95 (1·58 to 2·31) per 100 000 population to 1·67 (1·39 to 1·95) per 100 000 population for mortality, and from 111·5 (84·1 to 143·3) per 100 000 population to 92·3 (70·9 to 119·6) per 100 000 population for DALYs. Over the past three decades, females had higher age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates than males, while sex differences in mortality rates were smaller. In 2023, age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates were lowest in south Asia and highest in central and western Europe, central Asia, and many regions in Latin America. By contrast, several regions in sub-Saharan Africa had relatively low prevalence and DALY rates but comparatively high mortality rates. National patterns broadly mirrored these regional profiles. In 2023, prevalence and DALY counts peaked in middle to early-older adulthood (ages 55-69 years), but age-specific rates continued to rise into the oldest age groups, with DALYs dominated by YLDs in midlife and early-older adulthood and by YLLs at older ages (≥80 years). The number of deaths peaked in the ninth decade of life, but age-specific rates also peaked in the oldest age groups. Across GBD regions, the association between SDI and age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates generally followed a reversed U-shaped pattern, with the lowest rates at low SDI, peak rates at intermediate SDI, and declining rates at the highest SDI levels. The association between SDI and mortality rate was less clear.
INTERPRETATION: The global burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases is rising in absolute terms despite declining age-standardised rates, underscoring the importance of population growth and ageing. Health systems, particularly in settings with rapidly ageing populations and intermediate SDI levels, will need to expand diagnostic, elective, and emergency surgical capacity while investing in prevention of obesity and metabolic risk factors. Marked regional and national heterogeneity, as well as differences in risk factors, might reflect variance in health-system capacity and access to care, including timely diagnosis, availability of surgical services, and perioperative care. The predominance of non-fatal disability in midlife and rising mortality in older age groups indicates that integrated strategies spanning risk-factor control, early diagnosis, elective management, and robust acute care for older adults are essential to reduce both YLDs and YLLs.
FUNDING: Gates Foundation.
authors: GBD 2023 Gallbladder and Biliary Disease Collaborators

articles.title: The December Lesson: When Strategy Matters More Than the Drug.
The Wretched Gift of Life.
Assessing simulation facilitation with the VAST FORM part 4 self-assessment tool.
An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials Comparing the Analgesic Efficacy of Intercostal Nerve Block Versus Erector Spinae Plane Block in Thoracic Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ESPB, an ultrasound-guided fascial plane block, gained considerable attention as a regional anaesthetic because of its longer duration of action, favourable safety profile, and multidermatomal analgesic effect. ICNB, however, is associated with a relatively short duration of action, often requiring repeated dosing and adjunctive systemic analgesics.
METHODS: The methodology of this meta-analysis adhered to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and included randomized controlled trials comparing ESPB with ICNB in thoracoscopic surgery. A systematic PubMed, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov search was performed that reviewed the publications available till March 16, 2025. Studies were screened, data were extracted, and two reviewers independently evaluated the risk of bias using the Cochrane ROB 2 tool. Dynamic pain at 48 h was the primary outcome; the secondary outcome was analgesic use. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) or mean differences (MDs), as appropriate, with 95% confidence intervals were computed. Version 5.4 of Review Manager (RevMan) was used to process the statistical analysis, with a random-effects model where necessary.
RESULTS: We identified 444 records, out of which 6 randomized controlled trials were part of this meta-analysis, totalling 353 cases: 176 being part of the ESPB group, while the remaining 177 constituted the ICNB group. For the principal outcome of dynamic pain score at 48 h postoperatively, combined analysis from five studies (n = 295) revealed a statistically significant lowered pain score with ESPB in contrast to ICNB (SMD = -0.34, 95% CI: -0.57 to -0.10, p = 0.004; I 2 = 0%). For postoperative analgesic use, all six studies (n = 353) data showed insignificant group difference (MD = 0.14, 95% CI: -1.04 to 1.32, p = 0.81; I 2 = 57%).
CONCLUSION: This study suggests that ESPB contributed to a reduction in pain scores at 48 h after thoracoscopic surgery compared with ICNB, yet both methods exhibited equivalent postoperative analgesic consumption. These findings show that ESPB can be a preferable option for prolonged postoperative analgesia; however, additional well-designed studies are needed to corroborate the evidence base.

articles.title: High-intensity theatre lists for robot-assisted major thoracic resection: A proof of concept in the era of lung cancer screening.
articles.abstract: Newly published data from the NHS Targeted Lung Health Check (TLHC) programme confirm that over 75% of screen-detected lung cancers are now diagnosed at stage I or II, a shift that has already driven a 20% annual increase in resections, from 6547 in 2023 to 7878 in 2024. With the programme set to perform nearly one million annual scans by 2030, resection demand will continue to rise steeply. Scaling surgical throughput within existing theatre infrastructure, without opening new units, is therefore both an operational and oncological priority. The High-Intensity Theatre (HIT) list model, a structured, back-to-back operating framework that uses parallel anaesthetic pathways, has transformed throughput in urology and general surgery but had not been applied to major anatomical thoracic resection. We describe the first two HIT lists for robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) at a high-volume UK centre. Fifteen patients underwent major anatomical resection across two lists, including lobectomies, bilobectomy, and complex segmentectomies. All 15 resections achieved R0 status. Median console time was 35 minutes. Thirty-day mortality was nil. Five patients (33%) developed complications, consistent with published RATS benchmarks. These early data suggest that the HIT model is feasible for high-complexity thoracic surgery, with an acceptable early safety profile, and that it may offer a replicable, cost-neutral way to help protect curative intent at population scale. As this is a small, single-centre proof-of-concept series with no control group, it establishes feasibility rather than efficacy.

articles.title: Perioperative Liposomal Bupivacaine for Postoperative Pain Control in Cranial Neurosurgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postcraniotomy pain is common and contributes to increased opioid use and delayed recovery. Liposomal bupivacaine (LB) is a long-acting local anaesthetic that provides sustained analgesia for up to 96 h. Its role in cranial neurosurgery remains uncertain.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered prospectively on PROSPERO. MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched. Eligible studies assessed perioperative LB in elective cranial neurosurgical procedures and compared it with conventional local anaesthetic or no local infiltration. Primary outcomes were postoperative pain scores and opioid consumption expressed as morphine milligram equivalents. Secondary outcomes included length of stay, complications, and cost.
RESULTS: Four retrospective single-centre studies involving 184 patients were included. One study examined adult aneurysm craniotomy, and three examined paediatric cranial vault remodelling or Chiari decompression. In the single adult aneurysm-clipping cohort, mean pain scores, opioid consumption, and length of stay were lower with LB, but the between-group differences were not statistically significant; reported total analgesic cost was significantly higher. In paediatric cohorts, some retrospective studies reported associations between LB use and lower opioid consumption, including during the first 24 h in one Chiari cohort and across the first three postoperative days in a cranial vault remodelling cohort. Effects on pain scores and length of stay were variable.
CONCLUSION: Evidence for perioperative LB in cranial neurosurgery is sparse and of low to very low certainty. The single adult aneurysm-clipping cohort found no statistically significant between-group differences in pain scores, opioid consumption, or length of stay and reported higher total analgesic cost. Three small retrospective paediatric cohorts reported some associations with lower early opioid consumption, but findings were inconsistent across procedures and outcomes. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine use. Prospective, adequately powered randomised trials are required.

articles.title: Clinical Features and Outcomes of Glaucoma Surgery-Associated Bullous Keratopathy: A Subanalysis of the Japanese National Survey on Corneal Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to investigate clinical characteristics and 1-year outcomes of glaucoma surgery-associated bullous keratopathy (BK), comparing eyes with prior incisional glaucoma surgery (IGS-BK) and laser iridotomy (LI-BK), using data from the Japanese National Survey on Corneal Transplantation.
METHODS: Among 1941 BK eyes, 404 IGS-BK and 353 LI-BK eyes were analyzed. Clinical parameters and 1-year graft clarity were compared. Within IGS-BK, glaucoma subtypes were examined. Univariate (n = 382) and multivariable (n = 371, excluding cytomegalovirus and pediatric glaucoma) logistic regression identified predictors of graft failure.
RESULTS: IGS-BK patients were younger (72.8 vs. 77.2 years, P <0.001) and predominantly male (64.6% vs. 18.4%). Primary open-angle/normal-tension glaucoma (34.7%) and exfoliation glaucoma (XFG) (30.0%) were most common. Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty was the predominant procedure (81.7% IGS-BK; 78.2% LI-BK). One-year graft clarity was lower in IGS-BK (82.2% vs. 90.5%, P = 0.002), with XFG showing the poorest outcomes (73.0%). Univariate analysis identified male sex [odds ratio (OR) = 1.83, P = 0.046], younger age (OR = 0.75 per 10-year increase, P = 0.008), and XFG (OR = 2.63, P = 0.004) as predictors of graft failure. After multivariable adjustment, XFG remained an independent risk factor (OR = 3.00, 95% confidence interval: 1.50-5.99, P = 0.002), as did younger age (OR = 0.72, P = 0.019). Complication profiles differed between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: XFG independently predicts poor outcomes in IGS-BK, underscoring the importance of glaucoma subtype stratification. Patients with XFG require intensified perioperative management and postoperative monitoring to optimize graft survival.

articles.title: Diagnostic Yield and Longitudinal Performance of a Dedicated Keratoconus Screening Program for Children With Down Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance, diagnostic yield, and longitudinal outcomes of a dedicated tomography-based keratoconus (KC) screening program for children with Down syndrome (DS).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed involving all children with DS referred to a dedicated KC screening program between March 2019 and April 2026. Demographic characteristics, visual acuity, tomographic indices, KC diagnosis status, and corneal cross-linking outcomes were reviewed.
RESULTS: Forty-five children with DS were screened (mean age 13.5 years, 53.3% female). Fifteen children (33.3%) were classified as having KC or suspected KC at their initial screening visit. Clinically useful corneal tomography was obtained in 40 of 45 children (88.9%), demonstrating the feasibility of outpatient screening in this population. During surveillance, 2 children with initially normal examinations developed suspicious tomographic findings and 3 children with either a normal or suspicious initial examination progressed to confirmed KC, increasing the cumulative screen-positive rate to 18 of 45 children (40.0%). Fourteen eyes of 8 children underwent corneal cross-linking under general anesthesia without intraoperative or postoperative complications, with stable tomographic parameters on follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Dedicated tomography-based screening was feasible in most children and identified a high burden of KC, while longitudinal surveillance detected additional children requiring intervention after an initially reassuring assessment. These findings support repeated tomography-based surveillance as part of routine ophthalmic care for children with DS.

articles.title: Perioperative Anesthesia: Botulinum Toxin Injection in a 6-Year-Old Female With "No Burp Disease".
articles.abstract: Retrograde cricopharyngeus dysfunction is a chronic condition involving inability of the cricopharyngeal muscle to relax in a task-specific manner (eructation). Symptoms commonly include bloating, significant discomfort, excessive flatulence, and often self-imposed limitations in oral diet and activity. Here, we report a 6-year-old patient with several years of symptoms who underwent surgical injection of botulinum toxin under general anesthesia. Anesthesia with propofol and sevoflurane provided adequate sedation and analgesia. Nitrous oxide was avoided due to theoretical concern for impaired ability to clear esophageal and abdominal gas which can lead to postoperative nausea, vomiting, and aspiration risk.

articles.title: The Ghana Surgical Dialogue: A Whole-of-Society Innovation for Advancing Safe Surgery, Obstetric, Trauma, and Anesthesia Care in Ghana.
articles.abstract: Ghana continues to face major gaps in access to safe surgery, obstetric, trauma, and anesthesia (SOTA) care, especially at district level, where workforce shortages, infrastructure deficits, weak referral systems, and limited data constrain service delivery. To support implementation of the Ghana National Surgical, Obstetric and Anesthesia Plan (NSOAP) 2025-2029, the Ministry of Health convened the inaugural Ghana Surgical Dialogue in Koforidua in August 2025. The Dialogue brought together government, professional associations, clinicians, nurses, biomedical engineers, laboratory professionals, health managers, financiers, civil society, and international partners to identify practical solutions for strengthening SOTA care. Key innovations included alignment of SOTA priorities with national budgeting, exploration of public-private partnership models such as build-operate-transfer schemes, investment in district-level mentorship and telemedicine, improved surgical safety and audit culture, and development of biomedical equipment management systems. Participants also emphasized workforce retention, career progression for anesthetists and perioperative nurses, ring-fenced funding, interoperable data systems, and stronger referral networks. The Dialogue demonstrated that sustainable progress in surgical care requires a whole-of-society approach that combines policy, financing, workforce development, technology, and accountability. This report highlights implementation lessons from Ghana that may be useful to other countries seeking to translate surgical plans into action.

articles.title: Fast Facts and Concepts #542: Peripheral Nerve Blocks.
Short-term gepant use during active cluster headache bouts: A consecutive case series.
articles.abstract: AimTo evaluate the short-term effectiveness and tolerability of gepants administered during active cluster headache (CH) bouts in routine clinical practice, focusing primarily on reduction in daily attack frequency and additionally on pain intensity, bout duration, and patient-reported outcomes.MethodsWe conducted an observational, uncontrolled, consecutive case series at a reference headache clinic. Patients fulfilling ICHD-3 criteria for episodic or chronic CH who initiated a standardized 28-day course of a gepant during an active bout between October 2024 and July 2025 were included. Baseline data were abstracted from clinical records and diaries. No systemic corticosteroids, greater occipital nerve blocks, preventive dose adjustments, or new preventives were introduced during the 28-day period. The primary endpoint was ≥50% reduction in mean daily attack frequency at the end of treatment compared with baseline. Secondary outcomes included change in pain intensity (Numerical Rating Scale, NRS), change in attack duration, impact on overall bout duration, Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), and adverse events. Analyses were descriptive.ResultsTen patients were included (seven episodic CH [ECH], three chronic CH [CCH]). Median baseline attack frequency was three attacks/day (range 1-6), and median baseline NRS was 8.5. The primary endpoint was achieved in 7/10 patients (70.0%): 5/7 with ECH (71.4%) and 2/3 with CCH (66.7%). Two ECH patients with a low baseline frequency (two attacks/day) did not meet the ≥50% criterion but demonstrated marked reductions in pain intensity and shortened bout duration. Overall, pain intensity improved in 9/10 patients (90.0%), with a median NRS reduction of 7 points (range 0-10). Median intensity reduction was greater in ECH (7 points; range 2-10) than in CCH (2.5 points; range 0-5). Shortening of individual attacks was reported in 4/10 (40.0%), and reduction in overall bout duration in 7/10 (70.0%), predominantly among ECH. Median time to perceived benefit was 96 h. Adverse events were mild (nausea or constipation in 2/10).ConclusionIn this small real-world case series, short-term gepant use during active cluster bouts was associated with multidimensional clinical improvement, particularly in episodic CH. Benefits extended beyond attack frequency to include substantial reductions in pain intensity and apparent modulation of bout duration. Given the uncontrolled design and limited sample size, findings should be interpreted cautiously but support further prospective, phenotype-stratified investigation.

articles.title: Association of Documented Active Warming with Prolonged Postoperative Hospitalization After Endoscopic Spine Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Intraoperative temperature loss may occur during endoscopic spinal surgery because of general anesthesia, operative exposure, and irrigation. This study examined whether documented active warming was associated with intraoperative thermal outcomes and prolonged postoperative hospitalization after endoscopic spinal surgery. This single-center retrospective cohort included adults who underwent elective single-level endoscopic spinal surgery under general anesthesia from 2020 through 2023. All 115 patients in the active warming group (AWG) received documented forced-air warming, whereas none of the 135 patients in the conventional warming group (CWG) received active warming. Warmed intravenous fluids were additionally used in 86 AWG patients. The primary outcome was postoperative length of stay (LOS) >3 days. The primary logistic regression model was adjusted for age, sex, BMI, ASA physical status ≥ III, diabetes mellitus, surgical approach, surgical duration, and calendar year. Expanded-model, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and categorical-calendar-year sensitivity analyses were also performed. The AWG had a higher median nadir temperature (36.4 °C vs. 35.7 °C), a smaller median temperature fluctuation (0.5 °C vs. 1.0 °C), and a lower incidence of intraoperative hypothermia (19/115 [16.5%] vs. 71/135 [52.6%]); all p < 0.001. Postoperative LOS >3 days occurred in 28 of 115 AWG patients (24.3%) and 59 of 135 CWG patients (43.7%). Documented active warming was associated with lower adjusted odds of prolonged postoperative hospitalization (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; p = 0.018), with similar estimates in the expanded model (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.31-0.94; p = 0.029), stabilized-IPTW analysis (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.30-0.84; p = 0.008), and categorical-calendar-year sensitivity analysis (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.92; p = 0.024). Documented active warming was associated with more favorable intraoperative thermal profiles and lower adjusted odds of postoperative LOS >3 days. The retrospective, nonrandomized design precludes causal inference and subgroup-specific treatment conclusions.

articles.title: EXPRESS: Effect of Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Patients Undergoing Abdominal Surgery: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate whether perioperative intravenous dexmedetomidine (DEX) reduces postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in elderly patients undergoing abdominal surgery.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science from database inception to 15 April 2026. Eligible studies included patients aged ≥60 years undergoing abdominal surgery under general anesthesia and compared intraoperative DEX with placebo. The primary outcome was POCD incidence assessed by the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) or Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Secondary outcomes included MMSE scores, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores; interleukin-6 (IL-6) was summarized narratively because only two trials reported it. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 1 tool. Random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals were used irrespective of heterogeneity, and reporting followed the Framework for Approaches and Methods in Evidence Synthesis (FRAMES).
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs comprising 14 comparisons and 1,361 patients were included. DEX significantly reduced POCD on postoperative day 1 (risk ratio [RR]=0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.40-0.59; P<0.001; 95% prediction interval [PI]: 0.35-0.67) and day 3 (RR=0.29, 95% CI: 0.21-0.41; P<0.001; 95% PI: 0.18-0.47). MMSE scores were higher in the DEX group on day 1 (mean difference [MD]=2.75, 95% CI: 0.97-4.53; P=0.009) but not day 3 (MD=2.50, 95% CI: -1.74 to 6.75; P=0.16), with substantial heterogeneity (I2>98%). TNF-α concentrations were significantly lower with DEX (MD=-38.70 pg/mL, 95% CI: -76.44 to -0.96; P=0.047), but the very wide CI warrants caution. VAS scores were lower on days 1 and 2 but not day 3 (P=0.093). Subgroup analyses by cognitive assessment instrument, DEX loading dose, and surgical approach showed no significant effect modification (all P≥0.41). In the only trial reporting one-week data, MMSE scores remained higher with DEX on day 7 (MD=0.95, 95% CI: 0.31-1.59), whereas no trial reported POCD incidence beyond day 3. Exploratory publication-bias assessments showed no clear evidence of asymmetry.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative intravenous DEX significantly reduces early POCD incidence on postoperative days 1 and 3 and attenuates the early postoperative TNF-α response in elderly patients undergoing abdominal surgery.

articles.title: Double-lumen tube insertion and one-lung ventilation in Coffin-Siris syndrome: navigating airway challenges in severe scoliosis surgery.
articles.abstract: Coffin-Siris syndrome is a rare genetic condition associated with craniofacial and skeletal anomalies, hypotonia, airway malacia and intellectual disability, posing significant challenges for airway management and ventilation. We report the case of a 13-year-old patient with Coffin-Siris syndrome undergoing anterior scoliosis surgery requiring insertion of a double-lumen tracheal tube and one-lung ventilation. Pre-operative assessment identified near-complete C2-3 fusion, severe kyphoscoliosis, pulmonary atelectasis and difficult intravenous access. Pre-operative intranasal dexmedetomidine enabled a smooth inhalational induction with sevoflurane. Anaesthesia was maintained with total intravenous anaesthesia. A 28 Fr left-sided double-lumen tracheal tube was inserted on the first attempt using videolaryngoscopy. However, confirming correct tracheal tube position was challenging. Thick secretions and dynamic airway collapse from hypotonia, bronchomalacia, scoliosis-related distortion and atelectasis limited visualisation. Once correct positioning was confirmed, one-lung ventilation commenced. Initial high airway pressures improved with ventilatory adjustments, achieving adequate tidal volumes and oxygenation. Surgery was uneventful and the patient was transferred to a high-dependency unit for observation. We believe this to be the first reported case of successful double-lumen tracheal tube use and one-lung ventilation in a patient with Coffin-Siris syndrome. The case highlights the importance of a structured peri-operative approach to optimise safety in patients with rare syndromes where the evidence base is limited.

articles.title: Perioperative Anaphylaxis and Respiratory Failure During AVF Surgery in an End-Stage Renal Disease Patient.
articles.abstract: Perioperative anaphylaxis can cause sudden, catastrophic respiratory and cardiovascular collapse in high-risk ESRD patients, even during regional anesthesia. Early recognition, prompt epinephrine administration, serum tryptase measurement, vigilant respiratory monitoring, and multidisciplinary preparedness-including ECMO capability-are critical to improving survival and preventing recurrent perioperative events.

articles.title: Pain-Related Outcome Domains and Measures in Randomized Controlled Trials of Treatment for Acute Abdominal Pain: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Acute abdominal pain frequently presents to emergency departments, yet outcome domains in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remain poorly characterized. This review identified pain-related domains and outcome measures used in RCTs on acute abdominal pain.
DATABASES AND DATA TREATMENT: This PRISMA-guided systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025630171). PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for RCTs (January 2000-February 2025). Eligible studies included adult and paediatric patients with acute abdominal pain reporting pain assessment. Outcome domains extracted included pain intensity, rescue analgesia, adverse effects, pain interference, quality of life (QoL), and psychological function. Bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB2.
RESULTS: Of 826 records, 43 RCTs were included; eight included children. In adult trials, pain intensity was assessed using the visual analogue scale (n = 19) or the numeric rating scale (n = 15). Rescue analgesia (44%) and adverse effects (84%) were frequently reported. No study assessed pain interference or psychological function, and QoL was listed as an outcome in one trial. All were conducted in emergency settings, with short-term follow-up within the first hours.
CONCLUSIONS: Pain assessment in acute abdominal pain RCTs is predominantly limited to intensity measures and short-term outcomes. While appropriate for immediate analgesic effects, this approach may be insufficient when broader treatment goals or longer follow-up are relevant. Context-specific outcome selection is needed, aligning domains with clinical purpose and time frame.
SIGNIFICANCE: RCTs on acute abdominal pain assess pain incompletely, focusing predominantly on intensity rather than broader domains such as pain interference and psychological function. None adhered to the INTEGRATE framework for pain assessment. This review provides the first systematic mapping of outcome domains in this area, offering a foundation for context-specific outcome selection aligned with what matters to patients.

articles.title: Remimazolam for Precision Sedation and Anaesthesia in Vulnerable Populations: A Narrative Review of Pharmacological Mechanisms, Stratified Clinical Evidence, and Individualised Perioperative Strategies.
articles.abstract: Sedation and anaesthesia in vulnerable populations are complicated by altered pharmacokinetics, variable pharmacodynamic sensitivity, and limited physiological reserve. The extent of these differences depends on the underlying condition, disease severity, comorbidity, and treatment setting. These issues are common in older adults, patients with obesity or obstructive sleep apnoea, organ dysfunction, cardiovascular vulnerability, critical illness, and neurological or psychiatric comorbidity. Conventional sedatives may be poorly tolerated in these settings. Propofol can cause hypotension and respiratory depression. Midazolam may lead to delayed recovery and accumulation. Dexmedetomidine may be limited by bradycardia and slow onset. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that undergoes rapid carboxylesterase-mediated hydrolysis and can be antagonised with flumazenil. This narrative review examines its pharmacology, clinical evidence, and practical use across nine vulnerable populations. The synthesis prioritised population-specific clinical studies, pharmacokinetic studies, comparative trials, systematic reviews, and major guidelines. For short procedures, the most consistent evidence concerns older adults and haemodynamically vulnerable patients, in whom remimazolam has often been associated with less hypotension than propofol and faster recovery than midazolam. These findings are based mainly on short-term physiological and recovery outcomes. Evidence in mild to moderate hepatic or renal dysfunction is supportive but remains sparse in severe disease. Data for obesity or obstructive sleep apnoea, prolonged ICU sedation, paediatric care, obstetrics, and neurological or psychiatric vulnerability are limited or indirect. Remimazolam should therefore be considered according to the clinical objective, the expected duration and depth of sedation, opioid exposure, airway risk, and organ reserve. Its pharmacological advantages have not yet been shown to improve delirium, cognition, mechanical ventilation, functional recovery, or long-term safety. Further studies should focus on population-specific dosing models and patient-centred outcomes.

articles.title: Opioid usage between unilateral biportal endoscopic, tubular, and open microdiscectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic spine surgery aims to reduce local tissue trauma and shorten recovery times, while maintaining the established benefits of open and tubular microdiscectomy. In the setting of the current opioid crisis, endoscopic spine surgery may minimize the need for short-term narcotic analgesics.
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine differences in opioid and nonopioid pain medication utilization after open, tubular, and unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) lumbar microdiscectomy.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study.
METHODS: Two hundred seventy patients (94 open, 56 tubular, and 120 UBE) were included in a retrospective cohort study. Postoperative pain medication prescription was recorded across the periods of discharge to 2 weeks, 2 to 6 weeks, 6 weeks to 3 months, and 3 to 6 months. Opioid prescription was converted to morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Chi-squared and Analysis of Variance statistical analyses, including Tukey post hoc testing, assessed differences between groups. Significance was set to P < .05.
RESULTS: Baseline demographics (age, sex, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade) were similar across cohorts. Patients who underwent unilateral biportal endoscopic surgery required significantly less opioid medication early postoperatively (UBE: 150.7 ± 60.0 MME; open: 193.0 ± 85.9; tubular: 180.3 ± 83.0), although differences were not sustained beyond 2 weeks. Tukey post hoc testing demonstrated significantly lower opioid requirements in the UBE cohort than in open (-42.24 MME, P < .001) and tubular (-29.57 MME, P = .04) cohorts. Nonopioid analgesic requirements (muscle relaxants, NSAIDs, gabapentin, acetaminophen) were lower in the UBE group and persisted up to 3 months. Unilateral biportal endoscopic procedures had significantly longer operative times (UBE: 133.8 ± 39.1 minutes; open: 78.6 ± 32.8; tubular: 85.8 ± 25.9, P < .001). Hospital stay was significantly shorter for patients who underwent open surgery (open: 0.3 ± 0.2 days; UBE: 0.4 ± 0.5; tubular: 0.4 ± 0.6, P = .006). though clinically insignificant. Intraoperative and postoperative complications were otherwise comparable among groups.
CONCLUSION: Unilateral biportal endoscopic microdiscectomy is associated with decreased requirement of opioid and nonopioid analgesics in the early postoperative period. Opioid requirements tend to converge across techniques after 2 weeks but overall remain low. Moreover, sustained reductions in nonopioid analgesic requirement beyond 2 weeks suggest improved long-term pain control compared with tubular and open microdiscectomy approaches.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3.

articles.title: Incidence and predictors of hospital readmission following paediatric tonsillectomy in a low-resource setting: A multicentre observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-tonsillectomy readmission is an important indicator of paediatric surgical safety, but evidence from resource-limited settings remains limited. This study investigated the rates and clinical predictors of readmission in Libya. These findings establish critical perioperative quality indicators to inform local discharge strategies and improve surgical safety in fragile health systems.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A prospective multicentre observational study was conducted in five Libyan hospitals between 15 August 2025 and 1 August 2026. Children undergoing tonsillectomy, with or without concurrent procedures, were followed for 30 days after discharge through outpatient visits and structured telephone interviews. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, operative, and postoperative data were collected. Associations with readmission were assessed using non-parametric tests, followed by binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 291 children, the median age was 7 years (interquartile range, 5-10), and 169 (58.1%) were female. Twenty-seven patients were readmitted within 30 days, giving a readmission rate of 9.3%. Postoperative haemorrhage was the most common cause of readmission (13 patients, 48.1% of readmitted cases), followed by poor oral intake (11 patients, 40.7% of readmitted cases). Male sex was associated with increased odds of readmission (odds ratio, 3.96; 95% CI, 1.59-9.89; P = 0.003), as was recurrent tonsillitis compared with obstructive sleep disordered breathing (odds ratio, 3.54; 95% CI, 1.37-9.11; P = 0.009). Dual analgesia was associated with lower odds of readmission (odds ratio, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.06-0.84; P = 0.02).
CONCLUSION: The 30-day readmission rate was 9.3%. Haemorrhage and poor oral intake were the leading causes. Male sex and recurrent tonsillitis were associated with increased odds of readmission, whereas dual-agent postoperative analgesia was associated with a reduced readmission risk. Evaluating these clinical patterns may help inform risk stratification and guide post-discharge strategies in similar clinical settings. Larger studies with standardised outcome assessment and centre-adjusted analyses are warranted.

articles.title: Nutritional status, inflammatory burden, and CT-derived muscle phenotypes for predicting chronic postsurgical pain after total hip arthroplasty: an explainable machine learning study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fracture (HF) is a common fragility fracture in older adults and may lead to persistent pain and impaired recovery. Chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) after total hip arthroplasty (THA) negatively affects rehabilitation and quality of life. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model integrating clinical variables, peri-hip muscle characteristics, and nutrition-related inflammatory indicators for CPSP prediction after THA in patients with HF.
METHODS: This single-center cohort study included patients with HF undergoing primary unilateral THA between October 2022 and March 2026. Patients from October 2022 to September 2024 were randomly divided into training and internal validation sets, while those from October 2024 to March 2026 served as an independent temporal test set. CPSP was defined as surgery-related pain persisting for ≥3 months with NRS ≥4. Candidate predictors included clinical, psychological, nutritional, inflammatory, and CT-derived muscle parameters. LASSO and Boruta were used for feature selection, and six machine learning algorithms were compared. SHAP analysis was applied to interpret the optimal model.
RESULTS: Among 881 patients, 137/529 (25.9%) developed CPSP in the development cohort. Seven predictors were selected: GNRI, gluteus medius/minimus muscle density, gluteus medius/minimus cross-sectional area, NLR, age, preoperative anxiety, and PNI. The SVM model showed the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.854 in the temporal test set, with accuracy of 0.770, sensitivity of 0.789, specificity of 0.763, NPV of 0.913, F1-score of 0.637, and Brier score of 0.125. SHAP analysis identified GNRI as the most influential predictor (35.4%), followed by muscle density (13.6%) and NLR (12.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: A machine learning model integrating clinical, CT-derived muscle, and nutrition-related inflammatory features showed good predictive performance for CPSP after THA in patients with HF and may support early risk stratification and individualized perioperative management.

articles.title: Association between preoperative geriatric nutritional risk index and early postoperative cognitive decline after laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early postoperative cognitive decline (ePOCD) is a frequent complication in elderly surgical patients. The association between preoperative nutritional status and early postoperative cognitive decline remains unclear. This study investigated the relationship between preoperative Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and early postoperative cognitive decline in elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between preoperative GNRI and ePOCD in older patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy, and to explore the discriminatory ability of GNRI for ePOCD and its association with postoperative inflammatory markers.
METHODS: This study was a retrospective secondary analysis of a prospectively collected observational cohort. A total of 361 elderly patients who underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy were included. Preoperative nutritional status was assessed using the GNRI. Cognitive function was evaluated before surgery and on postoperative days 1 and 2 using standardized cognitive assessments. Early postoperative cognitive decline was defined as a decrease of ≥3 points from the preoperative baseline in either the MMSE or MoCA score. Patients were categorized according to GNRI nutritional risk groups, and associations between preoperative GNRI and ePOCD were analyzed using logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Among the 361 patients, 24 (6.6%) experienced early postoperative cognitive decline during the early postoperative period. The incidence of cognitive decline was higher on postoperative day 1 than on postoperative day 2. Patients with early postoperative cognitive decline had lower preoperative GNRI values compared with those without cognitive decline. After adjustment for potential confounding factors, lower GNRI remained associated with an increased risk of early postoperative cognitive decline. Older age was also independently associated with increased risk. Exploratory analyses demonstrated differences in perioperative inflammatory and neuronal injury-related biomarkers among GNRI groups; however, these findings require further validation.
CONCLUSION: Lower preoperative GNRI was associated with an increased risk of early postoperative cognitive decline in elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy. GNRI may serve as a simple indicator for identifying elderly patients with increased vulnerability to early postoperative cognitive changes. Further prospective multicenter studies and interventional trials are required to determine whether improving preoperative nutritional status can modify postoperative cognitive outcomes.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided microwave ablation for biopsy-proven breast fibroadenomas ≤3 cm: clinical, imaging, and safety outcomes at 12-month follow-up.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate the imaging, clinical, and safety outcomes of ultrasound (US)-guided microwave ablation (MWA) for biopsy-proven breast fibroadenomas ≤3.0 cm.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 27 patients with 27 core-biopsy-proven fibroadenomas ≤3.0 cm treated between January and July 2025. MWA was performed for clinical treatment purposes according to a predefined institutional protocol and was not undertaken as part of a prospective research study. Institutional ethics committee approval was subsequently obtained for retrospective review of the clinical and imaging data. US-guided MWA was performed under local anaesthesia using a 2450-MHz system at 40 W. Clinical and US follow-up was performed at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. Changes in tumour volume and maximum diameter were evaluated using repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).
RESULTS: The mean MWA duration was 101.3 ± 26.5 s. All 27 procedures were successfully completed. At 12 months, mean maximum tumour diameter decreased from 20.69 ± 6.96 mm to 5.59 ± 1.53 mm, corresponding to a 73.3% reduction. Mean tumour volume decreased from 2.30 ± 1.87 mL to 0.60 ± 0.28 mL, corresponding to a 73.5% reduction (P < .001). Sixteen of 27 lesions achieved >90% volume reduction without residual vascularity on colour Doppler US. No epidermal burns, haematoma, infection, skin depression, or other major adverse events occurred. All patients were satisfied with the cosmetic outcome at 12 months.
CONCLUSION: US-guided MWA provided substantial 12-month reduction in size and volume of biopsy-proven fibroadenomas ≤3 cm with favourable safety and cosmetic outcomes. It may represent a minimally invasive treatment option for appropriately selected symptomatic patients who wish to avoid surgical excision.

articles.title: Unexpected admissions after planned outpatient non-melanoma skin cancer reconstruction: Risk factors and a bedside risk score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) reconstruction is overwhelmingly performed as outpatient surgery, yet a subset of patients scheduled for same-day discharge may require unplanned admission or prolonged observation. No procedure-specific preoperative risk assessment tool currently exists.
OBJECTIVE: To quantify the incidence and risk factors associated with unexpected admission or prolonged observation after planned outpatient NMSC reconstruction and derive a simplified bedside risk score.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was used to identify reconstructions with a postoperative NMSC diagnosis. Pooled multivariable logistic regression identified independent associations. Discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); an extreme gradient boosting model served as non-linear comparator. An integer points-based bedside score was derived using the Sullivan framework.
RESULTS: Among the 5371 patients, 779 (14.5%) required unexpected admission. Independent associations included operative complexity (regional myocutaneous flap: aOR 7.59; free flap, nodal, and salivary or bone resection: aOR 20.76), anesthesia type (local anesthesia and monitored anesthesia care associated with substantially lower odds relative to general anesthesia), higher ASA physical status, chronic corticosteroid use, and dependent functional status. The regression model achieved an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.789 with excellent calibration (corrected slope 0.966). The simplified integer score retained comparable discrimination (AUC 0.778) and stratified observed admission rates increased approximately fortyfold, from 2.0 (score ≤0) to 79.0% (score ≥10).
CONCLUSION: Unexpected admission after planned outpatient NMSC reconstruction affects approximately 1 in 7 patients and is strongly determined by operative complexity, anesthetic modality, and patient-level factors including ASA classification, corticosteroid use, and functional status. A simple integer bedside score incorporating these variables achieves satisfactory discrimination and calibration and may aid preoperative triage and resource planning for this common surgical population.

articles.title: Barriers to Routine Use of Ultrasound-Guided Fascia Iliaca Blocks in High and Low-Resource Emergency Departments.
articles.abstract: Background Ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia, such as fascia iliaca (FI) blocks, represents an alternative pain management strategy with decreased risk of oversedation and respiratory depression for emergency department patients. Methodology This is a two-site, descriptive, 12-month follow-up survey to evaluate FI block uptake and perceived barriers after training resident physicians at two academic training sites: an urban academic tertiary center in the United States and a resource-limited referral hospital in Malawi. Results In total, 34 participants from the US site and seven participants from the Malawi site completed the survey, with response rates of 87% and 28%, respectively. Nearly all participants agreed that FI blocks were useful and improved patient care (median = 4 on a five-point Likert scale), and the majority reported confidence in performing the procedure. Despite this, most participants had not performed an FI block in the preceding 12 months (62% US participants and 57% Malawian participants). Perceived barriers were rated with "time to perform the procedure" ranking the highest among US participants and "time to perform the procedure" and "patient disinterest/refusal" ranking the highest for Malawian participants. Lack of equipment or supervision was commonly noted as a reason Malawian participants had considered but not performed an FI block, but not for US participants. Patient comorbidities (25%) and orthopedic reluctance (20%) were reasons US participants had considered but not performed the procedure, but were not noted by Malawian participants. Conclusions Reported barriers varied according to location, and the findings suggest that barriers are multifactorial and highly context-dependent.

articles.title: Harmonizing the diagnosis of citrate accumulation - a call for standardized criteria.
articles.abstract: Regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) has emerged as the gold-standard strategy for continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), yet its widespread adoption remains hindered by perceived complexity, heterogeneous protocols, unclear contraindications, and inconsistent terminology. A central challenge lies in the recognition and management of citrate accumulation, for which no single, reliable biomarker exists. The total-to-ionized calcium (tCa/iCa) ratio is widely utilized as a sensitive surrogate, but its specificity is limited by multiple confounding factors, including serum albumin concentration, acid-base status, and exogenous calcium administration. Current evidence supports a paradigm shift from reliance on static thresholds toward a dynamic, physiology-based assessment to define citrate accumulation. The kinetics of the tCa/iCa ratio, when interpreted alongside evolving metabolic parameters, particularly lactate trends, systemic ionized calcium, and acid-base status, provide a more robust framework for identifying citrate accumulation. Crucially, an elevated tCa/iCa ratio should not indiscriminately prompt the discontinuation of RCA. Targeted adjustments to the CRRT prescription can often safely mitigate citrate burden while preserving circuit patency. In the absence of a validated and widely available method for the direct measurement of plasma citrate levels, we propose a stepwise approach incorporating routinely measured screening tools and confirmatory parameters. Studies incorporating direct plasma citrate concentration measurements should be conducted to validate these criteria alongside readily available bedside surrogate markers. Refining this framework is essential to enhance the safe implementation of RCA and ultimately improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

articles.title: THIRTY-DAY INCIDENCE OF SURGICAL SITE INFECTION AND PERIOPERATIVE PROCESS COMPLIANCE IN A UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL DAY-SURGERY UNIT: A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY OF 200 PATIENTS.
articles.abstract:
AIM OF STUDY: To estimate 30-day surgical site infection (SSI) incidence after elective day surgery and assess perioperative prevention measures.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 213 adults; 200 with documented day-30 follow-up formed the analytic cohort. Two blinded reviewers applied January 2026 CDC/NHSN criteria. Wilson confidence intervals, follow-up-group comparison and extreme-case sensitivity analyses were used.
RESULTS: Three superficial incisional primary SSIs occurred (1.5%, 95% CI 0.5-4.3); all had purulent drainage and physician diagnosis. Incidence was 1.4% if none of the 13 patients without follow-up had SSI and 7.5% if all had SSI. Among antibiotic recipients, correct timing and guideline-consistent selection were documented in 97.9% and 98.6%. Aqueous 10% povidone-iodine was used in 95.0%; exposure time was unavailable.
CONCLUSIONS: Observed SSI incidence was low but sensitive to missing outcomes. Defined post-discharge follow-up, reproducible adjudication and complete documentation are essential for valid day-surgery surveillance.

articles.title: Development of machine learning models for predicting delirium in elderly patients after thoracic surgeries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent neurological complication following anesthesia and surgery, which is associated with increased comorbidities and mortality. The current study developed and internally validated a machine learning model for predicting POD in elderly patients undergoing thoracic surgeries based on machine learning (ML) algorithms.
METHODS: Elderly patients who underwent elective segmentectomy, lobectomy, or esophagectomy with general anesthesia from January 2015 to December 2022 were electronically retrieved. Clinical features, preoperative laboratory values, and intraoperative parameters were collected. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to screen critical features associated with POD. Nine ML algorithms were used to construct prediction models in the training dataset (80% of participants), and model performances were evaluated in the validation dataset (20% of participants). Prediction performances of the nine ML models were also compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Model calibration was assessed using the Brier scores. Finally, the best model was determined and was interpreted using the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).
RESULTS: Three thousand nine hundred sixty-seven elderly patients were enrolled, and 277 of them developed POD. Preoperative white blood cell (WBC), preoperative fasting plasma glucose (FPG), intraoperative hypotension, arrhythmia, combined nerve block anesthesia, hypertension, intraoperative vasoactive drugs, current smoker, blood transfusion, glucocorticoids usage, ASA classification, and video-assisted thoracoscopy were identified as prediction variables. The XGBoost model exhibited the best predictive performance (AUC: 0.936, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.932-0.941).
