The XGBoost model also presented the lowest Brier scores (0.110) in terms of model calibration. The three predictive variables with the most influence on the model were preoperative WBC, preoperative FPG and intra-operative hypotension.
CONCLUSIONS: The current study developed a ML model for POD prediction for elderly patients undergoing thoracic surgeries. If validated, the model could potentially serve as a complementary tool to aid POD risk stratification.

articles.title: Incidence, risk factors, and outcomes of postanaesthetic complications: a prospective cohort study in the Mulago National Referral Hospital adult postanaesthesia care unit.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postanaesthetic complications in the postanaesthesia care unit (PACU) carry significant implications for patient recovery, contributing to increased morbidity, prolonged PACU stays, and unplanned ICU admissions where bed availability is limited. Standardised postanaesthetic care pathways enhance early identification of patients at risk of deterioration and improve outcomes. This study aimed to determine the incidence, risk factors, and outcomes of postanaesthetic complications at Mulago National Referral Hospital (MNRH).
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted at the MNRH PACU, enrolling 370 adult participants (≥ 18 years) between June and August 2023. Data were collected using REDCap and analysed with Stata 17. A modified Poisson generalised linear model (GLM) with robust standard errors generated crude risk ratios (CRRs) and adjusted risk ratios (ARRs). Associations between complications and outcomes were evaluated using Fisher's exact test (95% CI); p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The cumulative incidence of postanaesthetic complications was 74% (95% CI: 68.8-77.8%), reflecting an inclusive operational definition capturing physiological deviations meeting predetermined thresholds under continuous real-time surveillance, including transient events. Notably, 98.2% of participants had favourable outcomes, indicating that most recorded events were mild and clinically manageable. Hypothermia was the most frequent complication (50.5%), followed by tachycardia (24.1%) and pain (16.8%); 40.8% experienced multiple complications. Intraoperative hypotension (ARR 1.23; 95% CI 1.08-1.41, p = 0.003), significant blood loss (ARR 1.29; 95% CI 1.09-1.52, p = 0.002), and hypoxia (ARR 1.38; 95% CI 1.21-1.56, p < 0.001) were independently associated with postanaesthetic complications, as were intraoperative opioid use (ARR 1.68; 95% CI 1.15-2.46, p = 0.008) and anaesthesia duration of 2-3 h (ARR 1.35; 95% CI 1.12-1.63, p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: A cumulative postanaesthetic complication incidence of 74% was observed, with 98.2% of participants achieving favourable outcomes. The identified risk factors and high incidence of hypothermia support standardising PACU care in line with WHO-WFSA and ASA recommendations, prioritising enhanced intraoperative monitoring, active warming protocols, and judicious opioid stewardship.

articles.title: CT-based three-dimensional virtual reduction with implant templating for tibial plateau fractures involving the posterolateral region: a retrospective cohort study of early postoperative CT reduction quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures involving the posterolateral region remain technically challenging because of their deep location, limited surgical exposure, and surrounding anatomical constraints. This study investigated whether CT-based three-dimensional virtual reduction with implant templating was associated with better early postoperative CT reduction quality than conventional CT-based planning.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 91 patients surgically treated for tibial plateau fractures involving the posterolateral region between July 2021 and March 2025. Thirty-five patients were planned using CT-based three-dimensional virtual reduction with implant templating, whereas 56 were planned using conventional CT-based planning. The primary outcomes were residual posterolateral articular step-off and gap on CT within 7 days after surgery. Exploratory secondary outcomes included documented planning-to-implementation concordance, perioperative outcomes, early complications, reoperation, 3-month pain and knee flexion range of motion, and 12-month Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) subscale scores. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for prespecified covariates was used to assess the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: The three-dimensional planning group had smaller residual step-off (2.80 [interquartile range, 2.40-3.10] vs. 3.55 [3.00-4.10] mm; P < 0.001) and gap (2.97 ± 0.63 vs. 3.63 ± 0.73 mm; P < 0.001) in the posterolateral quadrant than the conventional planning group. These associations remained after adjustment (step-off: β = -0.75 mm, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 1.08 to - 0.41; gap: β = -0.61 mm, 95% CI - 0.92 to - 0.30; both P < 0.001). Exploratory outcomes showed higher documented fixation-strategy concordance, lower 3-month pain scores, and greater knee flexion ROM in the three-dimensional planning group. No clear between-group differences were observed in surgical-approach concordance, perioperative outcomes, early complications, reoperation, or 12-month KOOS subscale scores.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, CT-based three-dimensional virtual reduction with implant templating was associated with modestly smaller residual posterolateral articular step-off and gap on early postoperative CT than conventional CT-based planning. No clear between-group differences were observed in 12-month KOOS subscale scores, and prospective multicenter validation is needed.

articles.title: Elective caesarean section without routine indwelling bladder catheterization - impact on mobilization and patient satisfaction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Global caesarean section rates have continuously increased. Therefore, a remarkable number of women could benefit from Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS®) protocol aiming to reduce perioperative stress and achieve early recovery. In 2019 the ERAS® protocol for caesarean section was initiated in the Helsinki University Women's Hospital and the Espoo Delivery Hospital in Finland. Among other improvements, the routine use of indwelling urinary catheter was discontinued among healthy women with no significant preoperative risk factors.
METHODS: This retrospective case-control study was carried out at the Espoo Hospital in Finland. Data were collected retrospectively from the hospital's electronic patient information system. The study included 208 women undergoing full term elective caesarean section. Group 1 (n = 104) routinely had an indwelling urinary catheter placed: half of them had no pre-specified time for catheter removal (n = 52) and half of them had an indwelling urinary catheter placed for 8 to 12 h (n = 52). Group 2 (n = 104) had a perioperatively placed urinary catheter only if needed. The primary outcome was the time from the end of the operation to patient mobilization, while secondary outcomes were the length of hospital stay and overall patient satisfaction.
RESULTS: Group 2 without a routine indwelling urinary catheter had a significantly shorter median time to mobilization (median = 5.8 h) than group 1 (median = 9.1 h) p < 0.001. In the multivariable analysis, the absence of the urinary catheter was the strongest factor associated with earlier mobilization. There was no difference in length of hospital stay, patient satisfaction or intraoperative blood loss between the groups and no bladder injuries were recorded.
CONCLUSION: Patients without a routine indwelling urinary catheter mobilized significantly faster compared to patients with a routinely placed urinary catheter. We found no difference in length of stay or patient satisfaction between the groups. These results support limiting the routine use of indwelling urinary catheter among healthy women undergoing caesarean section.

articles.title: Relationship between intraoperative hypotension and postoperative venous thromboembolism in elderly patients undergoing hip surgery and construction of a risk prediction model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the dose-response correlation between intraoperative hypotension (IOH) and postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) among elderly patients receiving hip surgery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia. It also sought to develop and validate a VTE risk prediction nomogram tailored to this patient population, providing evidence-based support for targeted perioperative VTE prophylaxis and individualized intraoperative blood pressure management.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort analysis enrolling 680 patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent primary hip procedures (periacetabular fracture internal fixation, total hip arthroplasty) with combined spinal-epidural anesthesia at our institution between January 2020 and December 2025. Minute-by-minute intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) recordings were extracted from the hospital's anesthesia information system. Using MAP < 65 mmHg as the hypotension cutoff, three quantitative IOH metrics were calculated: time-weighted average hypotension amplitude (TWA), hypotension area under the curve (AUC), and cumulative IOH duration. Variance inflation factor (VIF) testing was first performed to quantify multicollinearity across TWA, AUC, and cumulative hypotension duration prior to multivariable regression modeling. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized regression was applied for variable screening to mitigate collinearity and reduce predictor counts, lowering the risk of model overfitting. The primary study endpoint was incident VTE diagnosed within 14 days postoperatively. Electronic medical records were reviewed to collect clinical data including demographic profiles, comorbidities, surgical parameters, and perioperative thromboprophylaxis protocols. Multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was implemented to handle incomplete hemodynamic and clinical datasets; sample size justification was supplemented with detailed calculation logic to meet standard event-per-predictor ratios for regression modeling. Univariate Logistic regression identified candidate VTE risk factors with P < 0.1, which were subsequently entered into multivariable Logistic regression to screen independent risk correlates. A nomogram predicting postoperative VTE risk was built using these independent correlates. The model's discriminative performance, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). One-thousand-fold bootstrap resampling internal validation was conducted to compute optimism-corrected AUC and calibration metrics, minimizing overfitting bias. Risk stratification was performed based on total nomogram scores.
RESULTS: The 14-day postoperative VTE incidence across the full cohort of 680 elderly hip surgery patients was 4.20% (28/680). VIF values for TWA, AUC, and cumulative IOH duration ranged from 2.14 to 3.07, indicating mild multicollinearity. LASSO regression retained all three IOH metrics after penalty adjustment, which suggests each carries independent predictive value for postoperative VTE. The event-to-predictor ratio reached 4.0 (28 VTE events /7 predictors), nearly satisfying the widely accepted threshold of 10 events per 3 predictors required for stable Logistic regression modeling. Bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.792, slightly lower than the uncorrected original AUC of 0.816, implying mild overfitting. Multivariable Logistic regression indicated the following factors were independently associated with elevated postoperative VTE risk in elderly hip surgery patients: TWA (OR=1.125, 95%CI: 1.058-1.196, P<0.001), AUC (OR=1.098, 95%CI: 1.045-1.154, P<0.001), cumulative IOH duration (OR=1.036, 95%CI: 1.012-1.061, P=0.003), age ≥ 75 years (OR=2.895, 95%CI: 1.216-6.887, P=0.016), diabetes history (OR=2.563, 95%CI: 1.082-6.079, P=0.032), operative time ≥ 120 min (OR=3.102, 95%CI: 1.305-7.376, P=0.010), and non-standard postoperative mechanical thromboprophylaxis (OR=4.018, 95%CI: 1.695-9.523, P=0.001). All three quantitative IOH metrics displayed a graded positive correlation with VTE risk (P for trend <0.001), consistent with a dose-response pattern. For the nomogram constructed from the seven independent correlates above, ROC analysis yielded an uncorrected AUC of 0.816 (95%CI: 0.725-0.907), which suggests satisfactory discriminative capacity; bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC = 0.792 (95%CI: 0.701-0.883). Calibration curves revealed strong alignment between model-predicted VTE probabilities and actual observed event rates (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, χ²=6.895, P=0.542; bootstrap-corrected Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.517). DCA demonstrated that the model generated meaningful net clinical benefit within a threshold probability range of 5%-40%. Patients were stratified by nomogram total score into three risk tiers: low-risk (≤ 100 points), moderate-risk (101-150 points), and high-risk (> 150 points). Corresponding VTE incidences were 1.1% (3/325), 7.6% (22/286), and 22.7% (15/69), with statistically significant intergroup differences (χ²=45.865, P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Among elderly hip surgery patients under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia, the severity, cumulative load, and total duration of IOH appear to follow a dose-response pattern with postoperative VTE risk, and IOH metrics are independently correlated with VTE occurrence. The nomogram integrating quantitative IOH indicators and clinical patient characteristics exhibits favorable predictive performance and clinical applicability. It enables precise VTE risk stratification for this elderly surgical population and may serve as a quantitative reference for developing individualized perioperative VTE prophylaxis and refined intraoperative blood pressure management protocols.

articles.title: Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Transplantation: From Concept to Clinical Pathway.
articles.abstract: Modern healthcare increasingly relies on predictive, proactive, participatory, and personalized paradigms. While Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) has transformed standard cardiac procedures, its application to heart transplantation (HT) remains unmapped. HT patients exhibit unique vulnerability across physical, psychocognitive, social, and nutritional dimensions. Integrating ERACS pathways into HT protocols represents a critical opportunity to optimize patient-centered recovery. This manuscript addresses this gap by establishing the conceptual link between these fields and proposing a novel framework for their integration.

articles.title: The Efficacy of Ultrasound-Guided Thoracic Erector Spinae Plane Block for Perioperative Analgesia During Laparoscopic Bariatric Surgery in Super-Obese Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Super-obese patients undergoing laparoscopic bariatric surgery are at an increased risk of opioid-related respiratory compromise, underscoring the need for opioid-sparing analgesia.
OBJECTIVES: To compare bilateral ultrasound-guided thoracic erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and trocar-site local anesthetic infiltration with respect to perioperative opioid consumption and early postoperative pain.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 60 adults aged 18 - 60 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status III and a Body Mass Index (BMI) > 50 kg/m2 who were scheduled for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass were randomized 1:1 to receive bilateral T7 ESPB with 0.25% bupivacaine (30 mL/side) or trocar-site infiltration with 0.5% bupivacaine (5 mL/site). The primary outcome was cumulative perioperative opioid consumption during the first 24 hours, expressed as an intravenous morphine-equivalent dose. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative fentanyl use, Visual Analog Scale pain scores at rest and during coughing, time to first rescue analgesia, time to ambulation, hemodynamics, the 15-item Quality of Recovery (15-item Quality of Recovery questionnaire (QoR-15)) score at 24 hours, and complications.
RESULTS: ESPB reduced intraoperative fentanyl requirements (56.7% vs 100%; total dose, 50 [25 - 75] vs 100 [100 - 212.5] µg; both P < 0.001) and cumulative 24-hour morphine-equivalent consumption (11 [9.75 - 13] vs 24.5 [22 - 33], mg; P < 0.001). Visual analog scale scores were lower with ESPB at rest at 4 and 8 hours and during coughing within the first 8 hours (all P < 0.001). Erector spinae plane block prolonged the time to first rescue analgesia (8 [8 - 12] vs 4 [4 - 8], h) and enabled earlier ambulation (4.07 ± 0.78 vs 4.60 ± 0.67 h; both P < 0.001). The QoR-15 score was higher with ESPB (118.8 ± 5.35 vs 106.6 ± 3.91; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In super-obese patients, thoracic ESPB provided a clinically meaningful opioid-sparing effect, improved early pain control and quality of recovery, and facilitated earlier mobilization following laparoscopic bariatric surgery.

articles.title: Dynamic Cortical Connectivity Underlying Proprioceptive Processing During NMES-Induced Hand Movements: Insights From an Acute Deafferentation Model.
articles.abstract: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is a promising modality for restoring sensory feedback in upper-limb prosthetics. However, the dynamic cortical mechanisms underlying the perception of NMES-evoked muscle contraction, particularly under conditions of sensory loss (e.g., amputation), remain poorly understood. This study investigates the time-varying effective connectivity of the sensorimotor cortex in response to NMES using the ischemic nerve block (INB) technology to model acute deafferentation. 64-channel EEG data were recorded from 11 healthy participants under a ${2}\times {2}$ factorial design involving INB states (before vs. block) and stimulation intensities (above vs. below motor threshold). The adaptive directed transfer function (ADTF) combined with graph theoretical analysis was employed to quantify dynamic causal interactions in the Beta band (15-30 Hz). The NMES-evoked cortical response progressed through three stages with monotonically increasing network segregation and integration ( $\mathbf {p}_{\mathbf {\textit {FDR}}} \le 0.01$ for all stage-wise comparisons). During the ischemic nerve block (INB), the clustering coefficient (CC) and global efficiency (Ge) decreased under above-threshold stimulation (cluster-level $\mathbf {p}_{\mathbf {\textit {FDR}}} =0.019$ and $\mathbf {p}_{\mathbf {\textit {FDR}}} =0.013$ , respectively), whereas below-threshold stimulation elicited a transient CC increase (150-525 ms, $\mathbf {p}_{\mathbf {\textit {FDR}}} =0.019$ ) followed by late Ge reductions. The differentiation of the network response between above and below motor-threshold stimulation was reconfigured rather than abolished during deafferentation. At the regional level, deafferentation attenuated contralateral somatosensory and ipsilateral motor driving, whereas ipsilateral somatosensory outflow was relatively enhanced. NMES-evoked muscle contractions modulate the dynamics of sensorimotor networks by acute deafferentation. Acute deafferentation attenuates network integration and increases the relative contribution of the ipsilateral hemisphere. These electrophysiological markers may inform the design and evaluation of closed-loop sensory feedback for neuroprostheses.
articles.journal: IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng

articles.title: Minimally Invasive Management of Recurrent Craniopharyngioma: Intraoperative Real-Time Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Guided Transnasal Cyst Aspiration-A Case-Based Technical Note.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Craniopharyngiomas are rare benign epithelial tumors typically located in the sellar and suprasellar region. Standard management includes surgery and radiotherapy. However, recurrence in the form of isolated cystic lesions presents a unique challenge. Herein, we report a case of recurrent cystic craniopharyngioma treated using intraoperative real-time magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and neuronavigation-guided transnasal aspiration.
METHODS: The patient was evaluated with MRI, including T1- and T2-weighted sequences with contrast enhancement. A transnasal surgical approach was planned using neuronavigation. Intraoperative real-time MRI was used to guide catheter placement and ensure complete cyst aspiration. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia using standard sterile technique, and histopathological examination of the aspirated material was conducted.
RESULTS: A 77-year-old female previously underwent endoscopic transnasal resection for a cystic craniopharyngioma confirmed to be of the adamantinomatous subtype. During follow-up, a recurrent suprasellar cystic lesion was identified. The cyst was aspirated intraoperatively via an external ventricular drainage catheter placed through the transnasal route. Real-time MRI using fast low-angle shot (FLASH) sequences enabled real-time monitoring and confirmation of cyst reduction.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a minimally invasive, safe, and effective technique for managing recurrent cystic craniopharyngiomas using real-time MRI guidance. It highlights the potential of image-guided aspiration as a first-line approach in select patients, especially where conventional surgical reintervention may pose significant risks.
articles.journal: J Neurol Surg B Skull Base

articles.title: Point of Care (POCUS) Gastric Ultrasound to Predict Gastric Volume in Patients Presenting for Emergency Surgeries.
articles.abstract: Background In emergency surgery, pulmonary aspiration is a significant anesthetic risk. Traditional fasting hours are often unreliable due to physiological stress. This study evaluated the utility of point-of-care gastric ultrasound in assessing gastric volume and content in an emergency Nepalese cohort. Objective To determine the volume, content and cross sectional area of gastric antrum in emergency surgeries and to determine if they are correlated with age, fasting hours, comorbidity, pain score, body mass index and opioid. Method A prospective cross-sectional study of 145 adult patients was conducted. Gastric antral cross-sectional area was measured in the right lateral decubitus position. Gastric volume was calculated using validated formula. Gastric content was noted. These were correlated with variables using univariate and multivariate regression. Result The mean fasting time was 11.05 ± 4.20 hours. However, gastric ultrasound revealed that 42.7% of patients had gastric contents (37.9% clear fluid, 4.8% solids). Furthermore, 21.4% of patients exceeded the high-risk volume threshold of 1.5 mL/ kg. In the multivariate analysis, advanced age (p = 0.003) and higher visual analogue scale score (p =0.03) were independent predictors of gastric volume and gastric cross sectional area. Conclusion Fasting hours are a poor surrogate for gastric emptiness in emergency settings. One in five patients meeting nil per oral criteria remained at high risk for aspiration. We recommend the routine use of preoperative gastric ultrasound, especially in older patients and those with high pain scores, to individualize airway management.

articles.title: Opioid prescribing and pain trajectories after periacetabular osteotomy : epidural versus periarticular injection analgesia.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is performed in young, opioid-naive patients and is associated with postoperative pain. Optimizing perioperative analgesia while limiting opioid exposure remains a priority. This study evaluated postoperative pain trajectories, hospital length of stay (LOS), and opioid-prescribing patterns associated with an institutional transition from epidural-based to periarticular injection (PAI)-based analgesia after PAO. Secondary aims were to assess the influence of preoperative opioid exposure and compare outcomes between ropivacaine-based and bupivacaine PAI formulations.
METHODS: The study included 724 patients who underwent PAO between January 2010 and December 2022 at a single academic institution, with epidural use replaced by PAI in 2016. Patients were stratified by postoperative analgesia strategy: epidural catheter (n = 333) or PAI (n = 391). Outcomes included daily postoperative pain scores, LOS, discharge opioid prescriptions (morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs)), total opioid exposure, and 30-day refill rates. Statistical comparisons were performed using chi-squared, Fisher's exact, and Kruskal-Wallis tests.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Epidural analgesia was associated with lower pain scores during the first 48 hours (last pain postoperative day 0 to 1: mean 2.9 (SD 2.0) vs 4.7 (SD 2.1); p < 0.001), whereas the PAI group had a shorter LOS (mean 2.2 days (SD 1.0) vs 3.4 days (SD 0.9); p < 0.001) and higher pain scores at discharge (mean 4.8 (SD 1.9) vs 4.0 (SD 1.9); p < 0.001). Median discharge opioid prescriptions (313 (IQR 225 to 388) vs 825 (IQR 600 to 1,000) MMEs) and total 30-day opioid exposure (360 (IQR 275 to 575) vs 900 (IQR 638 to 1,100) MMEs) were lower in the PAI group (both p < 0.001), while refill rates were higher (34.0% vs 19.2%; p < 0.001). Within the PAI cohort, ropivacaine-based and bupivacaine injections showed similar pain trajectories and refill rates.
CONCLUSION: Epidural analgesia provided superior early postoperative pain control, whereas PAI-based pathways enabled earlier discharge and lower overall opioid prescribing but with higher refill rates. These findings highlight trade-offs in contemporary perioperative pathways and support individualized analgesic strategies after PAO.

articles.title: Cumulative multi-threshold intraoperative blood pressure exposure patterns and postoperative mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension is commonly defined as MAP <65 mmHg. We evaluated whether cumulative exposure across multiple MAP thresholds provides additional mortality-associated information beyond this single threshold.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults having non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery using perioperative electronic health record data. Pressure-time burden and proportion of operative time were calculated across MAP thresholds from 50 to 150 mmHg. Decision-tree analysis using recursive partitioning sequentially grouped patients according to MAP exposure patterns associated with 30-day mortality. Discrimination of the multi-threshold blood-pressure-only model was compared with that of a model restricted to exposure below MAP 65 mmHg. Medication associations were exploratory.
RESULTS: Among 388,407 patients, 30-day mortality was 1.49%. The multi-threshold model had greater validation discrimination than the MAP 65 mmHg model (AUROC, 0.619 vs. 0.591; ΔAUROC, 0.028; 95% CI, 0.025-0.037; p < 0.001), although the improvement was modest. Terminal exposure groups defined by complete combinations of MAP level and cumulative exposure had different observed mortality rates. Medication associations varied across groups. Observed 30-day mortality was generally higher with deeper hypotension and a greater proportion of operative time spent below MAP thresholds, although the relationship was not uniformly monotonic.
CONCLUSIONS: Multi-threshold MAP exposure captured mortality-associated information not represented by exposure below MAP 65 mmHg alone, complementing this clinical threshold. The multi-threshold analysis identified groups with distinct pressure-time exposure patterns, providing a basis for hemodynamic profiling and investigation of hypotension-related outcomes. External validation is needed to assess the reproducibility and discrimination of these groups in other populations, followed by prospective studies to determine whether management informed by these patterns improves outcomes.

articles.title: Stellate ganglion block in contemporary anesthesia practice: perioperative applications, emerging indications, and risk management.
articles.abstract: Stellate ganglion block (SGB), an interventional technique that modulates sympathetic activity, has been increasingly investigated beyond traditional pain management in cardiology, neuropsychiatry, and perioperative medicine. This narrative review examines the evolving role of SGB in contemporary anesthesia practice, emphasizing that its effects may extend beyond immediate peripheral sympatholysis to longer-lasting central neural modulation. Technically, ultrasound guidance facilitates precise needle placement and low-volume injection, with improved visualization of relevant anatomy and injectate spread. Dose-finding studies have refined local-anesthetic volume and concentration, whereas continuous blockade may extend sympatholysis in selected refractory conditions. Clinically, SGB has been used in selected pain conditions, including complex regional pain syndrome and herpes zoster-related pain, and has been investigated for non-pain indications such as post-traumatic stress disorder, refractory ventricular arrhythmias, and menopausal vasomotor symptoms. In perioperative settings, SGB has been evaluated for postoperative analgesia, modulation of inflammatory responses, and potential neuroprotective effects. Risk mitigation relies on real-time ultrasound visualization of the needle tip, adjacent vascular structures, and injectate spread, together with predefined management protocols for major complications. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized procedural parameters, and individualized treatment pathways to support the safe, precise, and evidence-based use of SGB across clinical settings.

articles.title: Project SPRUCE: Formation of an International Consortium of Pediatric Anesthesia Groups to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Inhaled Anesthetics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inhaled anesthetic use contributes to environmental harm through release of potent greenhouse gases (GHG). Emissions can be reduced with the use of safe practice changes, including avoidance of high impact agents like desflurane and nitrous oxide, use of low fresh gas flows, and adoption of total intravenous and regional anesthesia when clinically appropriate. These evidence-based practices have been recommended for years, but actual practice changes have not been widely adopted.
METHODS: The Project SPRUCE (Saving our Planet by Reducing Carbon Emissions) consortium brought together twelve pediatric anesthesia groups into a partnership working to reduce GHG emissions from pediatric anesthesia care. The consortium implemented quality improvement strategies, including change management methods, to reduce GHG emissions from inhaled anesthetics by at least 50%. Change management and quality improvement strategies were utilized to disseminate strategies, implement emissions reduction techniques, and track emissions in pediatric anesthesia care. Specific interventions included education and socialization, practice constraints, and direct data feedback to clinical teams.
RESULTS: The consortium facilitated adoption of practice changes among anesthesia groups, and sustained emissions reductions though shifts in culture. Greenhouse gas emissions from inhaled anesthesia decreased by 63% (range 43-91%) During the study period, the incidence of nitrous oxide use was reduced by 62.4%, and the average volume of nitrous oxide used per case decreased by 83.5%. Project SPRUCE prevented a total of 14,381 metric tons of excess carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) emissions from inhaled anesthetics.
CONCLUSIONS: Collaborative action within our consortium supported widespread and significant reductions in harmful greenhouse gas emissions from pediatric anesthesia care through education and socialization, practice constraints, and direct data feedback to clinical teams.

articles.title: Sugammadex versus neostigmine for neuromuscular blockade reversal in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reversal of neuromuscular blockade (NMB) is a routine component of general anaesthesia with important implications for recovery quality and peri-operative safety. Recent changes in the cost of sugammadex, together with its efficacy and adverse effect profile relative to neostigmine, may influence its broader clinical use.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of sugammadex compared with neostigmine in adult patients.
DESIGN: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials with meta-analyses and trial sequential analyses. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grades of Recommendation, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. This is an update of a 2017 Cochrane review.
DATA SOURCES: Online databases were searched up to December 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised trials enrolling adults receiving rocuronium or vecuronium for elective procedures and comparing sugammadex with neostigmine were included. The outcomes included NMB recovery time and risk of various adverse events.
RESULTS: We included 165 trials with 19 124 participants. Risk of bias was generally unclear or high. NMB monitoring technique was reported in 113 trials, mostly acceleromyography. Time to reversal of NMB from second twitch to a train-of-four ratio more than 0.9 was shorter with sugammadex 2 mg kg-1 versus neostigmine 0.05 mg kg-1 (mean difference = -10.49 min (95% confidence interval, -11.90 to -9.08), GRADE: moderate). Sugammadex probably reduces the number of patients with at least one adverse event compared with neostigmine (risk ratio = 0.72 (95% confidence interval, 0.61 to 0.84), GRADE: moderate). When looking at specific adverse events, sugammadex probably reduces the risk of residual NMB, inadequate NMB reversal, desaturation, atelectasis, increased upper airway secretion, airway obstruction, bradycardia, dry mouth and urinary retention (GRADE: moderate).
CONCLUSIONS: Sugammadex probably reverses NMB more rapidly and with fewer adverse events than neostigmine. Broader use of sugammadex has the potential to improve peri-operative outcomes.

articles.title: Effect-site concentrations of remifentanil to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Remifentanil infusion titrated to effect-site concentration (Ce) is commonly used to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia; nevertheless, the optimal Ce range remains unclear. We aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the existing evidence on the optimal Ce values of remifentanil for cough suppression during emergence.
SOURCE: We performed a comprehensive literature search using PubMed®, Embase®, Web of Science™, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar on 27 February 2025. We included prospective studies that used the up-and-down method to estimate the effective concentrations of remifentanil in 50% of patients (EC50) and 95% of patients (EC95) for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia with tracheal intubation in adult patients. We excluded studies in children or patients undergoing cardiac surgery, as well as those that only compared predefined Ce targets of remifentanil to determine optimal dosing. We obtained pooled estimates using a random-effects model with inverse-variance method, and heterogeneity was quantified using the I2 statistic. We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies for nonrandomized comparative or single-arm studies. The primary outcome was EC50 estimated using the up-and-down method, with secondary outcomes including model-based EC50 and EC95 estimates.
PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We included 22 prospective studies comprising 857 adult participants, and none were assessed as being at a high risk of bias or of low methodologic quality. Based on 28 groups and 653 participants across 17 studies, the pooled mean EC50 from the up-and-down method was 2.0 ng·mL-1 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8 to 2.3), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 74.5%). Based on 29 groups and 693 participants across 18 studies, the model-based EC50 was 1.9 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 1.6 to 2.1), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 96.1%). Based on 31 groups and 809 participants across 20 studies, the model-based EC95 was 2.7 ng·mL-1 (95% CI, 2.5 to 3.0), with considerable heterogeneity (I2 = 99.5%). Subgroup analyses revealed higher mean EC50 values in male individuals (2.6 ng·mL-1) and the highest mean EC50 in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracic surgery (2.6 ng·mL-1). Using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework, the certainty of evidence was rated as very low for all outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: The identified EC50 and EC95 values of remifentanil for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults were 2.0 and 2.7 ng·mL-1, respectively. Patient sex and surgical type may influence the required Ce. Careful dose adjustment is recommended to avoid delayed awakening and hypoventilation, especially in cases requiring higher concentrations.
STUDY REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ( CRD42024623581 ); first submitted 20 December 2024.

articles.title: Preoperative lipid concentrations and 28-day mortality after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low cholesterol is associated with poor outcomes in acute illness, although low LDL-Cholesterol (LDL-C) is a therapeutic target in cardiovascular disease. We assessed whether preoperative lipid concentrations were associated with 28-day mortality after cardiac surgery with Cardiopulmonary Bypass (CPB).
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed a prospectively maintained single-centre registry of cardiac surgery with CPB (April 2013-December 2023), linked to preoperative lipid measurements and national death records. LDL-C was the primary exposure. Models were adjusted for EuroSCORE 2, statin use, infective endocarditis, urgent surgery, and critical preoperative state. Secondary analyses were corrected for multiplicity (Benjamini-Hochberg).
RESULTS: Of 10,088 patients, 71 were excluded (reoperation within one year or duplicate record) and 1,986 of the remaining 10,017 had a preoperative lipid panel; 64 (3.2%) died within 28-days. In unadjusted analyses, lower Total Cholesterol (TC), HDL-C and LDL-C were associated with mortality. After adjustment, LDL-C was no longer associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio = 0.803, 95% CI 0.595-1.084; p = 0.152). TC retained a borderline association (0.777, 0.607-0.994; p = 0.045), not surviving correction (q = 0.173). Lipid parameters discriminated poorly (areas under the curve 0.57-0.62) and added nothing to EuroSCORE 2.
CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment for illness severity, preoperative LDL-C was not associated with 28-day mortality, and lipids provided no prognostic information beyond EuroSCORE 2. Very low TC may primarily reflect illness severity rather than an independent causal risk factor, and these data provide no basis for modifying perioperative lipid-lowering therapy.

articles.title: Beyond Weight Loss: A Scoping Review and Thematic Analysis of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Across the Neurosurgical Landscape.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used for diabetes and obesity. Literature spans spinal fusion, idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH), and cerebrovascular disease, but has not been systematically mapped. We aimed to map literature on GLP-1RA exposure in neurosurgical landscapes by characterizing study design, drug class, disease-specific outcomes, and safety considerations.
METHODS: This scoping review was conducted per the PRISMA-ScR guideline. Eligible studies reported GLP-1RA exposure in adults with spinal, intracranial, or cerebrovascular disease, recording clinical, perioperative, or imaging outcomes. Two reviewers screened independently with third-reviewer adjudication. Extracted variables included country, design, agent, timing, indication, neurosurgical and metabolic outcomes, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Of 1342, 48 were included, predominantly from the United States (US) (34/48, 71%). Most were retrospective (43/48, 90%); 31/48 (65%) used propensity score matching; 5/48 (10%) were randomized. Three themes dominated: spinal fusion (24/48, 50%), IIH and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics (14/48, 29%), and cerebrovascular and neurointerventional disease (10/48, 21%). In spinal fusion, perioperative GLP-1RA exposure was repeatedly associated with lower pseudarthrosis, although some studies reported increased postoperative complications. In IIH, GLP-1RAs were associated with lower papilledema, fewer CSF leaks, reduced acetazolamide requirement, and lower shunt placement. Cerebrovascular reports described lower intracerebral hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and post-stroke mortality, mostly in observational studies.
CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA neurosurgical literature is dominated by US-based retrospective, propensity-matched analyses. Benefit signals are most consistent in spinal fusion and IIH, but perioperative adverse effects and overlap among database cohorts limit causal interpretation. Adequately powered prospective trials with standardized endpoints are needed to confirm results.

articles.title: Benson relaxation technique for perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients undergoing brain tumor surgery: a clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing craniotomy for brain tumors confront psychophysiological crisis. Managing perioperative distress poses a clinical paradox, as standard pharmacological sedatives are carefully restricted based on neurological status and institutional protocols to avoid masking critical postoperative neurological signs. This study investigated the efficacy of the Benson relaxation technique (BRT), a nonpharmacological mind-body intervention, on perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in this vulnerable population.
METHODS: In this clinical trial, out of 84 patients assessed for eligibility, 74 eligible patients undergoing brain tumor resection were allocated to either the BRT intervention group (n = 37) or the control group (n = 37). The intervention group completed supervised BRT sessions (muscle relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, and word repetition) on the evening of ICU admission, 60 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively. Both groups received routine care, and anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated at identical time points (baseline on the evening of ICU admission prior to the intervention, 30 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively). Data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).
RESULTS: Seventy patients completed the trial (35 per group). At 24 h postoperatively, ANCOVA adjusted for baseline scores showed that the BRT group had significantly lower anxiety scores compared to the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 4.16 points (95% CI, - 5.40 to - 2.93; P < 0.001). Regarding depressive symptoms, baseline scores were below the threshold for clinically significant symptoms (HADS-D < 8) in both cohorts; however, at 24 h postoperatively, the BRT group had significantly lower adjusted depressive symptom scores than the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 2.32 points (95% CI, - 3.51 to - 1.12; P < 0.001), indicating a preventive effect against postoperative reactive depressive symptoms.
CONCLUSION: The Benson relaxation technique is a safe, feasible, and well-tolerated nurse-led mind-body strategy that effectively mitigates perioperative anxiety and reduces postoperative depressive symptoms without adverse events. These findings support integrating structured nonpharmacological modalities into neurosurgical care.

articles.title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, and gel on pain, anxiety, physiological responses, taste acceptability, and treatment compliance in children aged 7-10 years undergoing their first dental treatment. 100 healthy children were randomly allocated into four groups: 10% lidocaine spray, 20% benzocaine gel, cryotherapy with distilled water cooled to +4 °C, and lidocaine spray cooled to +4 °C. Following topical application, buccal infiltration anesthesia was administered. Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter. Taste acceptability and treatment compliance were evaluated using a three-point Hedonic Scale and the FRANKL Scale. Repeated Measures ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were applied. No significant differences were observed among the groups in anxiety, pain, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, or taste acceptability (p > 0.05). Pulse rate increased from the pre-operative to the post-operative period in all groups (p = 0.006), with no significant group × time interaction. FRANKL scores were significantly higher in the cryotherapy-distilled water group compared with the gel and cooled-spray groups (p = 0.001), a finding considered exploratory. Pain and anxiety outcomes following cryotherapy did not differ significantly from those of the topical anesthetic agents, while treatment compliance was higher, suggesting that cryotherapy may be a promising non-pharmacological option, pending confirmation in non-inferiority trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07198022.

articles.title: Neonatal Teeth in Patau Syndrome: A Rare Oral Phenotype and Bedside Surgical Management.
articles.abstract: This report describes the first cytogenetically confirmed case of complete trisomy 13 associated with a highly mobile mandibular neonatal tooth and a contralateral eruption cyst associated with an unerupted tooth, managed by bedside surgery in the neonatal intensive care unit. A late-preterm newborn with trisomy 13, unilateral complete cleft lip and palate, and congenital heart disease presented with a highly mobile mandibular neonatal tooth and a contralateral eruption cyst associated with an unerupted tooth. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, both teeth were extracted at the bedside under local anesthesia and cardiorespiratory monitoring, without complications. This case expands the oral phenotypic spectrum of trisomy 13 and underscores the importance of early recognition, individualized management, and Hospital Dentistry in preventing airway-related complications in medically complex newborns.

articles.title: Bilateral thoracolumbar erector spinae plane blocks for postoperative pain relief in TRAM flap breast reconstruction: A case report.
articles.abstract: Post-mastectomy breast reconstruction is associated with significant postoperative pain due to the involvement of both the thoracic recipient site and the abdominal donor site. Effective analgesic strategies are essential to optimise recovery, reduce opioid exposure, and support enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathways. We report the perioperative analgesic management of a patient undergoing mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction using a pedicled transverse rectus abdominis myocutaneous (TRAM) flap. A multimodal regional anaesthesia strategy based on bilateral multilevel thoracolumbar erector spinae plane blocks (ESPB), supplemented by a serratus anterior plane block, was employed to address wide thoracoabdominal dermatomal pain distribution. The regional analgesic approach was associated with effective postoperative pain control and minimal systemic opioid requirements during the early postoperative period. Pain scores remained low at rest and during movement, and no block-related complications were observed. This case illustrates the feasibility of combining bilateral multilevel ESPB with adjunct interfascial plane blocks as part of a multimodal analgesic strategy for pedicled TRAM flap reconstruction. While no conclusions regarding comparative efficacy or reproducibility can be drawn from a single case, this experience supports further investigation of ESPB-based approaches within ERAS pathways for autologous breast reconstruction.

Inpatient management of migraine in the United Kingdom: Current practice, evidence, and future directions.
articles.abstract: Migraine is a leading neurological cause of emergency attendance and inpatient admission in the UK. Although most attacks respond to community therapy, a minority develop status migrainosus or medication-overuse headache requiring hospital care. This review summarises evidence-based inpatient strategies aligned with NICE and BASH guidance. Management should begin with intravenous hydration where indicated, parenteral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and dopamine-antagonist antiemetics. Triptans remain the first migraine-specific option; valproate and corticosteroids are reserved for refractory attacks. Peripheral nerve blocks and, in tertiary settings, lidocaine or ketamine infusions provide rescue therapy.

articles.title: Evaluating clinical outcomes associated with regional versus general anesthesia approach in blunt geriatric trauma patients undergoing major operative procedures for hip fractures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic approach for operative management of geriatric hip fractures remains debated, particularly among geriatric trauma patients with limited physiologic reserve and high comorbidity burden. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes associated with anesthesia type in geriatric patients undergoing surgery for isolated hip fractures.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted to evaluate geriatric trauma patients (≥ 65 years) with isolated, blunt, moderate to severe (ISS ≥ 9) hip fractures utilizing the ACS-TQIP database from 2017 to 2023. Patients were grouped by anesthetic technique: regional or general anesthesia. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included regional anesthesia failure rate, complication rates, hospital length of stay (LOS), and ventilator-free days (VFDs).
RESULTS: Among geriatric trauma patients with moderate to severe hip fractures undergoing hip fixation, no statistically significant association was detected between regional and general anesthesia regarding in-hospital mortality (aOR: 0.316, 95% CI: 0.076-1.311, p = 0.112) or VFDs (β = 4.548, 95% CI - 2.478-11.573, p = 0.202). Also, no statistically significant association was detected between patients receiving regional compared to those receiving general anesthesia for major complications, including DVT, PE, and stroke. The conversion-to-general-anesthesia rate was 0.96%.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were detected between regional and general anesthesia among patients with moderate-to-severe hip fractures undergoing major operative fixation. Anesthetic selection should remain individualized.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Therapeutic/Care Management.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Corticosteroid Block Versus Alcohol Neurolysis of the Suprascapular Nerve for Chronic Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical effectiveness of corticosteroid block versus alcohol neurolysis of the suprascapular nerve (SSN) in patients with chronic post-stroke hemiplegic shoulder pain (HSP).
DESIGN: This prospective service evaluation, reported per STROBE guidelines, enrolled 26 consecutive patients with chronic post-stroke HSP (>3 mo) receiving ultrasound-guided SSNB with triamcinolone acetonide 40 mg/lidocaine (corticosteroid, n=13) or 70% ethanol/lidocaine (alcohol neurolysis, n=13) as part of routine clinical care. Pain (Numeric Rating Scale, 0-10) and shoulder range of motion (Constant-Murley ROM) were assessed at baseline, weekly for six weeks, and six months.
RESULTS: Both groups showed significant within-group improvements in all pain domains and ROM at one and six weeks. At six months, resting and movement pain remained improved in both groups. Nocturnal pain and ROM improvements persisted in the alcohol neurolysis group (P=0.005; P=0.004) but not the corticosteroid group (P=0.162; P=0.058). No between-group differences were observed (all P>0.05; effect sizes r=0.03-0.31). Both interventions were well tolerated, with transient post-procedural pain exacerbation reported in two alcohol-treated patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Both interventions produced significant improvements in pain and ROM with no between-group differences. The six-month pattern suggests more durable benefit following alcohol neurolysis; however, dequately powered randomized controlled trials are required.

articles.title: Real-world outcomes of continuous infusion of sedative agents in critically ill patients with invasive mechanical ventilation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Current guidelines recommend non-benzodiazepine (non-BZD) sedatives -dexmedetomidine (DEX) and propofol (PPF) - over benzodiazepines (BZD) in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, but real-world evidence from Asian patients remains limited. We evaluated the clinical outcomes of different continuous-infusion sedatives in this population in Taiwan.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from a tertiary medical center in Taiwan. Adults receiving continuous intravenous sedation within 48 h of intubation were included. Patients with preexisting ventilator dependence, status epilepticus, or prior tracheostomy were excluded. Groups were 1:1 propensity score matched. Outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS), time to extubation, mortality, and total hospitalization cost. Prespecified pairwise comparisons evaluated DEX vs. BZD, PPF vs. BZD, and DEX vs. PPF.
RESULTS: Of 2065 eligible patients, 605 matched pairs were analyzed. Compared with BZD, non-BZD sedation was associated with shorter ICU LOS (9.4 vs. 11.9 days, P = 0.032), earlier extubation (4.1 vs. 6.5 days, P = 0.015), and lower hospitalization cost (US$21,559 vs. US$26,258, P < 0.001), without a significant difference in 90-day mortality (36.7% vs. 38.7%, P = 0.489). In pairwise comparisons with BZD, DEX was associated with significantly shorter ICU LOS and time to extubation, whereas the benefit of PPF was primarily a reduction in hospitalization cost.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-BZD sedatives were associated with shorter ICU LOS, earlier extubation, and lower hospitalization costs without a detectable mortality difference. These findings are consistent with guideline recommendations favoring non-BZD sedation, although residual confounding remains possible.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Arterial Pressure Gradient: Implications for Clinical Practice.
As-needed inhaled corticosteroids in asthma: an Official American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing reliever therapy has demonstrated efficacy in improving asthma outcomes when compared to short-acting beta2-agonists (SABA) alone but remains underutilized. The purpose of this guideline is to provide recommendations surrounding the use of combination ICS-formoterol or ICS+SABA (in combination or separate inhalers) as reliever therapy across the asthma severity spectrum in adolescents and adults.
METHODS: The American Thoracic Society clinical practice guideline panel evaluated six research questions in the PICO format addressing the use of ICS-containing reliever therapy across National Asthma Education and Prevention Program (NAEPP) asthma treatment steps 1-5. The methodology team conducted systematic literature reviews and GRADE assessments, which the panel utilized to inform the recommendations for each specific PICO and overall.
RECOMMENDATIONS: In patients at NAEPP steps 1 and 2, the panel made strong recommendations for the use of as-needed-only ICS-SABA or ICS-formoterol over SABA-only therapy, and conditional recommendations over scheduled ICS + as-needed SABA. In patients at NAEPP steps 3-5, the taskforce made a strong recommendation for the use of maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) with ICS-formoterol over scheduled ICS-LABA plus as-needed SABA. In patients at NAEPP steps 3-5 who are using scheduled maintenance ICS-LABA, the panel made a conditional recommendation for use of ICS+SABA reliever over SABA reliever. In considering these recommendations, the panel valued the importance of preventing severe exacerbations and considered the risk of SABA-only treatment, as well as ICS and systemic corticosteroid (SCS) exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: This clinical practice guideline, informed by systematic reviews and GRADE-based appraisals of PICO-framed evidence, makes these evidence-based recommendations for the safe and effective use of ICS-containing reliever therapy in asthma.
