A Synchronized Two-Surgeon Workflow for Two-Level Unilateral Biportal Endoscopic Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion: Technical Note and Preliminary Case Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a standardized four-phase synchronized two-surgeon workflow for selected two-level unilateral biportal endoscopic transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (UBE-TLIF) and report its preliminary outcomes.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective Technical Note included 33 consecutive patients (66 operated levels) treated in 2025 by a fixed pair of experienced surgeons. Each surgeon performed endoscopic decompression and interbody fusion at an assigned level, with coordinated fluoroscopy, guidewire staging, shared-device use, and percutaneous instrumentation. Perioperative outcomes, pain and disability scores, 90-day adverse events, and CT-based fusion assessments obtained at least 12 months postoperatively were reviewed.
RESULTS: All 33 procedures were completed. Mean operative time was 294 ± 59 minutes, estimated blood loss was 299 ± 78 mL, and median spine-surgery ward stay was 7 days (interquartile range, 6-9). Three patients (9.1%) had recorded adverse events: incidental durotomy, wound infection requiring surgical debridement, and anemia requiring transfusion (one each). At a median final clinical follow-up of 427 days, median back- and leg-pain visual analog scale scores decreased from 6 to 1 and from 7 to 0, respectively; median Oswestry Disability Index decreased from 70 to 18 (all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001 versus baseline). CT at ≥12 months was available for 22/25 eligible patients; fusion (Bridwell I/II) was observed in 40/44 evaluable levels (91%) and at both operated levels in 20/22 patients (91%).
CONCLUSIONS: The coordinated workflow was feasible in an experienced fixed surgical pair. Prospective comparative studies are needed to assess efficiency, safety, resource use, and generalizability.

articles.title: A retrospective cohort study of a midodrine protocol for the prevention of post-operative hypotension for lower limb arthroplasty and emergency hip fracture surgery.
articles.abstract: Hypotension is a common post-operative complication that is associated with morbidity and mortality. There has been growing interest in the use of midodrine (oral alpha-1 adrenergic vasopressor agent) to increase systolic and mean arterial blood pressure in a variety of clinical applications. Our institution developed a 48-h midodrine protocol in 2020 for patients undergoing elective lower limb arthroplasty and emergency hip fracture fixation. The aim of this retrospective, single-centre metropolitan tertiary hospital cohort study was to evaluate the efficacy of the protocol in reducing the incidence and severity of perioperative hypotension (SBP <110 mmHg) within the first 24 h following surgery compared to the pre-protocol period (primary outcome). Secondary outcomes included frequency of hypotension 24-48 h post-operatively, bradycardia, incidence of MET calls and unplanned critical care admission. In total, 328 patients were identified for inclusion in the pre-protocol group and 298 in the protocol group. Introduction of the midodrine protocol was not associated with a significant difference in the incidence of the primary outcome. There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of hypotension between groups post-operatively at 24 or 48 h. Of the secondary outcomes, patients receiving midodrine were more likely to be bradycardic in the post-anaesthesia care unit (43.8% vs 55.9%, p = 0.001) and at 24 h post-operatively (40.7% vs 53.8%, p = 0.003).

articles.title: Transcarotid Artery Stenting Using Flow Reversal for Non-Atherosclerotic Carotid Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the use of transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) in non-atherosclerotic carotid disease and compared outcomes with transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS).
METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for all TCAR and TFCAS procedures performed from 2017-2024. Patients with lesion types categorized as atherosclerosis or restenosis were excluded. The study cohort included dissection, trauma, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), and other non-atherosclerotic etiologies. Primary outcomes included major adverse events, including stroke, death, and composite endpoints. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.
RESULTS: A total of 541 TCAR and 2,348 TFCAS patients met inclusion criteria. TCAR was associated with lower contrast usage and fluoroscopy time across all lesion types. In unadjusted analyses, stroke or death rates were higher with TFCAS than TCAR for dissection (7.1% vs 1.9%, p=0.006), other lesions (8.7% vs 2.1%, p<0.001), and symptomatic (8.1% vs 2.2%, p=0.001) and asymptomatic patients (6.4% vs 1.6%, p<0.001). After propensity matching (527 pairs), TCAR was associated with significantly lower rates of stroke (4.4% vs 1.7%, p=0.0118), death (4.4% vs 0.4%, p<0.001), stroke or death (7.6% vs 1.9%, p<0.001), and stroke, death, or MI (8.0% vs 2.7%, p<0.001) compared with TFCAS (TFCAS vs TCAR, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: This study supports consideration of TCAR for non-atherosclerotic carotid pathology when carotid stenting is indicated and suggests that TCAR may offer important advantages over TFCAS, particularly in reducing the risk of perioperative stroke or death.

articles.title: Physiologic, Metabolic, and Protein Redox Effects of Methylene Blue in a Porcine Hemorrhage Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methylene blue (MB) has established benefit in vasodilatory shock, and a potential role in hemorrhagic shock. Some evidence suggests that MB could lower anesthetic requirements. The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of MB on volatile anesthetic requirements (primary), metabolic markers (secondary), and protein redox modifications (tertiary) in a porcine hemorrhage model.
METHODS: This was a randomized 2 x 2 factorial animal study conducted at a tertiary medical center in 2019-2020. Forty swine were randomized to the following experimental interventions: hemorrhage (0 v. 30 mL/kg, at t = 0 min) and MB (0 v. 2 mg/kg, at t = 20 min). End-tidal isoflurane, blood pressure, and arterial blood gas parameters were recorded at prespecified intervals. Skeletal muscle was used for redox analyses. Group differences were investigated with mixed effects and one-way analyses of variance.
RESULTS: There was no effect of MB on volatile requirements or metabolic markers (all P > 0.05). Hemorrhage was associated with 2.4 mg/dL higher lactate (95% CI, 1.4 to 3.4) and 23 mmHg lower mean arterial pressure (95% CI, 11 to 34). Hemorrhage was also associated with increased protein carbonyl levels (P < 0.001) that were non-significantly attenuated by MB (P = 0.130), and increased protein S-nitrosylation (P < 0.001) that was significantly attenuated by MB (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: MB does not have a significant effect on volatile anesthetic requirements or systemic physiologic and metabolic responses during hemorrhagic shock. However, MB significantly attenuates protein S-nitrosylation and partially attenuates protein carbonyl accumulation.

articles.title: When Winter Comes: Seasonal Patterns in Outcomes After Major Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Seasonal strain may affect perioperative care, yet national evidence on seasonal variation in outcomes after major surgery remains limited. We evaluated whether postoperative outcomes varied by season among older adults undergoing major surgical procedures.
METHODS: Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 y or older undergoing abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, coronary artery bypass grafting, colectomy, lung resection, or pancreaticoduodenectomy from 2016 through 2021 were identified using 100% Medicare Standard Analytic Files. Seasons were defined meteorologically, with spring as the reference. Outcomes included 30-d mortality, 90-d mortality, complications, textbook outcome, failure to rescue, surgical site infection, and length of stay. Multivariable regression models adjusted for patient, procedure, and hospital characteristics and were stratified by elective versus emergency admission. Interactions with the nurse-to-bed ratio and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Hospital Star Rating were assessed.
RESULTS: Among 1,165,265 patients, 738,236 underwent elective surgery and 427,029 underwent emergency surgery. Among emergency admissions, winter was associated with higher adjusted odds of 30-d mortality (adjusted odds ratio: 1.10; 95% confidence interval: 1.07-1.13), 90-d mortality (1.10; 1.07-1.13), complications (1.05; 1.03-1.07), and failure to rescue (1.11; 1.07-1.15), as well as lower odds of textbook outcome (0.96; 0.94-0.98) and longer length of stay. Among elective admissions, winter was associated with smaller increases in 30-d and 90-d mortality. No significant interaction was observed by nurse-to-bed ratio or Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Hospital Star Rating.
CONCLUSIONS: Winter was associated with worse outcomes after major surgery, particularly among emergency admissions, supporting targeted seasonal preparedness strategies.

articles.title: Causes of bias in Delphi studies and consensus statements: a methodological review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Delphi methodology is a widely-used tool for achieving expert consensus in healthcare, particularly in areas where empirical evidence is limited or uncertain. Despite its structured design, the Delphi process remains vulnerable to implicit cognitive biases that may influence judgement and group decision-making. Such biases may inadvertently affect the quality of the consensus process, allow louder voices to influence outcomes, restrict inclusivity and undermine the validity, transparency and evidence-based nature of recommendations.
METHODS: We conducted a methodological review synthesising literature from cognitive psychology, behavioural science and methodological research on consensus development and Delphi processes. Using a concept-mapping approach, established cognitive biases were mapped to different stages of the Delphi process, including study design; panel selection; survey development; iterative scoring; and consensus interpretation.
RESULTS: Ten cognitive biases were organised into four domains reflecting different levels of influence within consensus development: steering-group and design-level biases, panel composition and contextual biases, social influence and conformity biases; and individual cognitive heuristic biases. A conceptual framework was developed to systematically identify these biases within Delphi-based consensus studies. Examples illustrating how these biases may arise in healthcare Delphi processes are presented, alongside potential mitigation strategies.
DISCUSSION: Recognition and mitigation of cognitive biases are essential for strengthening the methodological rigour and credibility of Delphi studies. Strategies to reduce bias include diversifying expert panels; using neutral language in survey statements; maintaining anonymity during voting; involving methodological expertise in Delphi design; and ensuring transparent iterative feedback. The framework needs prospective validation before its widespread use and may assist journal editors and peer reviewers in critically appraising Delphi studies and improving reporting standards in consensus research.

articles.title: Rapid sequence induction: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary aspiration of gastric contents remains an important cause of anaesthetic morbidity and mortality, and is important medicolegally. Rapid sequence induction is a multi-element technique designed to mitigate risk in those patients at increased risk of pulmonary aspiration during induction of general anaesthesia.
METHODS: We undertook a narrative review to summarise evidence and evidence gaps focusing on controversial aspects of rapid sequence induction.
RESULTS: Despite widespread use of rapid sequence induction, many elements of the technique lack robust evidence and consensus. Nasogastric tubes can be used to reduce gastric content, but do not empty the stomach reliably. Correctly applied cricoid force obstructs the hypopharynx and has a limited impact on airway management, but incorrect application can cause clinically significant difficulties. Correct location of cricoid force may require ultrasound localisation of the cricoid cartilage. Applying the correct force, which varies with age and sex, is improved by education, practice and feedback. The use of videolaryngoscopy during rapid sequence induction is supported by evidence. The role of gastric ultrasound in determining anaesthetic technique is uncertain. Cardiovascular complications of rapid sequence induction are common, particularly in the patients who are critically ill, and modifications to the technique may reduce their frequency and severity. Effective use of airway rescue techniques may require removal of cricoid force.
DISCUSSION: There is insufficient evidence for many of the elements of rapid sequence induction to determine whether they reduce patient harm or to state confidently that they do not. Controversies and evidence gaps should be acknowledged. Despite this, optimal use of rapid sequence induction requires a thorough knowledge of the subject, including areas of uncertainty to guide individualised risk assessment; clinical decision-making; and practical conduct of the technique.

articles.title: Recurrent Horner's Syndrome and Cranial Nerve Involvement Following Epidural Analgesia During Labor: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of a 33-year-old primigravida developing an extensive cephalad spread of epidural local anesthetic resulting in bilateral Horner's syndrome and cranial nerve involvement during labor and cesarean delivery. Urgent neuroimaging excluded intracranial hemorrhage. Due to persistent focal neurological symptoms during second-stage labor and inability to exclude a life-threatening cerebrovascular pathology, cesarean delivery was performed for maternal indication. Following epidural top-up for surgical anesthesia, symptoms recurred and progressed bilaterally, thereby supporting extensive cephalad spread as the underlying mechanism. Postpartum MRI and MR angiography revealed no cerebrovascular abnormalities. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenge of acute neurological symptoms during labor, where pregnancy-associated stroke risk necessitates exclusion of life-threatening pathology despite time constraints. Recognition of pregnancy-related factors predisposing to extensive epidural spread, combined with interdisciplinary collaboration and appropriate neuroimaging, enabled safe management.

articles.title: Comparison of Efficacy of Epidural Ropivacaine versus Bupivacaine for Postoperative Pain Relief in Patients Undergoing Infraumbilical Surgeries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative pain control is a cornerstone of enhanced recovery after surgery, facilitating early ambulation, reducing complications, and improving patient satisfaction. Epidural analgesia remains a widely used and reliable technique for postoperative pain management following infraumbilical surgeries. Bupivacaine has long been considered a standard agent for epidural infusion; however, concerns regarding cardiotoxicity and motor blockade have prompted interest in ropivacaine, which is associated with a more favorable safety profile. This study was designed to compare the efficacy and safety of epidural bupivacaine 0.125% and ropivacaine 0.2% for postoperative analgesia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective randomized study included 90 patients aged 18-70 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I and II undergoing infraumbilical surgeries under spinal anesthesia. Patients were randomly allocated into two groups of 45 each. Group B received epidural infusion of 0.125% bupivacaine at 6 ml/h, and Group R received epidural infusion of 0.2% ropivacaine at 6 ml/h. Postoperative pain was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Hemodynamic parameters, time to first rescue analgesia, total number of rescue analgesics required, and adverse effects were recorded over a 12-h postoperative period.
RESULTS: VAS scores showed a significant difference at the 3rd and 4th postoperative hours, with higher pain scores observed in the ropivacaine group. The mean time to first rescue analgesia was significantly longer in the bupivacaine group compared with the ropivacaine group. The total number of rescue analgesics required during the observation period was comparable between the two groups. Hemodynamic parameters, including heart rate and blood pressure, were significantly higher in the ropivacaine group during the initial postoperative hours, although these differences were transient. The incidence of adverse effects such as hypotension, nausea, vomiting, and bradycardia was similar in both groups.
CONCLUSION: Epidural bupivacaine provides a longer duration of postoperative analgesia with better early pain control, whereas ropivacaine offers a favorable safety profile with less motor blockade and acceptable hemodynamic stability. Ropivacaine may be considered a suitable alternative to bupivacaine for postoperative epidural analgesia in patients undergoing infraumbilical surgeries.

articles.title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Distribution of Fentanyl-induced Pruritus in Spinal Anaesthesia with Hyperbaric Bupivacaine: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of fentanyl-induced pruritus in spinal anaesthesia with hyperbaric bupivacaine is highly variable, ranging from 30% to 60%.
AIMS: In our study, we analysed the incidence, risk factors and pattern of distribution of pruritus following intrathecal administration of fentanyl with bupivacaine.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital from August 2025 to January 2026. Adult patients (>18 years) receiving standard spinal anaesthesia with bupivacaine and fentanyl were included. The primary outcome was the incidence and anatomical distribution of pruritus, while secondary outcomes assessed the onset time, duration and severity of pruritus using a Numeric Rating Scale.
RESULTS: Of 100 patients (60% of males; mean age: 46.19 ± 18.16 years), the overall mean fentanyl dose was 22.95 ± 2.57 µg. Intraoperative pruritus occurred in 70% of patients and was predominantly facial (78.6%). Patients experiencing pruritus received significantly higher fentanyl doses compared to those who did not (23.43 ± 2.34 µg vs. 21.83 ± 2.78 µg; P = 0.006). Logistic regression indicated a 27% increase in pruritus odds per 1 µg increase in fentanyl. Symptoms were generally mild, with a mean onset of 18.90 ± 9.07 min and a mean duration of 7.07 ± 3.78 min.
CONCLUSION: The majority receiving spinal anaesthesia had mild pruritus, with the face being the most affected area. The frequency of pruritus significantly correlated with the dosage of fentanyl.

articles.title: Lessons learned from a decade of EUS(-FNA) staging in esophageal and GEJ carcinoma: towards a selective staging strategy.
articles.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasonography with fine-needle aspiration (EUS(-FNA)) is recommended by current guidelines as part of the staging for esophageal and gastro-esophageal junction (GEJ) carcinoma, yet its incremental value over modern 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) remains uncertain. This Lessons Learned article reflects on over a decade of EUS(-FNA) and FDG-PET staging in 402 patients with potentially curable esophageal or GEJ carcinoma at a high-volume tertiary referral center. In 91.3% of patients, EUS(-FNA) did not alter the radiation field as would have been defined by FDG-PET. EUS(-FNA) resulted in an expansion of the radiation field in 4.5% and reduction in 4.2% of patients. Squamous cell carcinoma showed more than two-fold greater likelihood of radiation field modification. Among 193 patients classified as FDG-PET non-suspicious for malignant lymph nodes (LNs), EUS-FNA identified malignant LNs in eight patients (4.1%), which influenced the radiation field. In 5 of 402 patients (1.2%) a malignant LN was detected with EUS-FNA in a station that would not have routinely been resected surgically. In patients planned for neoadjuvant or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), LN staging is of direct therapeutic consequence: underestimation of nodal disease may result in geographic miss, while overestimation leads to unnecessary irradiation. In contrast, in patients treated with perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin and docetaxel (FLOT) followed by surgical lymphadenectomy, most involved LN stations are routinely addressed surgically, limiting the added value of EUS(-FNA) for treatment planning. Therefore, we view EUS(-FNA) as a selective staging tool in patients planned for neoadjuvant or definitive CRT, rather than a procedure applied routinely to all patients.

articles.title: Age Does Not Affect Textbook Outcome After Liver Surgery Within an Enhanced Recovery Pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Textbook outcome in liver surgery (TOLS) is a novel comprehensive quality metric reflecting an ideal postoperative course. Data on TOLS in older adult patients remain limited. This study aimed to compare TOLS achievement between older adults and younger patients and to identify TOLS predictors.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study including all consecutive patients undergoing elective liver surgery within an enhanced recovery (ERAS) program (2013-2023) was conducted. Older adult patients were defined as ≥ 70 years. TOLS achievement was based on international consensus criteria. TOLS predictors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: A total of 618 patients were included, of whom 179 (29%) were ≥ 70 years. Overall, 354 patients (57%) achieved TOLS. TOLS rates were similar in older adults and younger patients (56% vs. 58%, p = 0.78). TOLS predictors were higher ERAS compliance (OR 1.1, p < 0.01), minor hepatectomy (OR 2.0, p < 0.01), absence of biliary anastomosis (OR 0.4, p < 0.01), preoperative biliary stenting (OR 0.2, p < 0.01), and absence of intraoperative blood transfusion (OR 0.2, p < 0.01). Age was not associated with TOLS (OR 1.0, p = 0.10).
CONCLUSION: TOLS rates were comparable in older adults and younger patients. Within an ERAS pathway, age alone does not compromise the likelihood of achieving an optimal postoperative course. Surgical complexity and perioperative factors appear to be more critical determinants of TOLS.

articles.title: Implementation of a Novel Multi-Center Pediatric Liver Transplant Collaborative Network.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Initiation or augmentation of pediatric liver transplant programs in the United States faces challenges of limited expertise, small volumes, and regional variation in access to care. PACH launched a prospective plan of pediatric liver program development at two sites (VAUV and FLFH) with the goals of comprehensive multidisciplinary program support, consistent surgical leadership from one team, consensus protocol development, and standardization of perioperative and postoperative care, and comprehensive long-term follow-up care plans. A third center, NCCM, was launched in June 2024.
METHODS: Between January 2016 and December 31, 2024, 140 children received pediatric liver transplants at one of the collaborative sites. A total of 215 PLT were performed at PACH during the same period.
RESULTS: Patient and graft survival were 94.4% and 93.2% respectively, with current follow-up of 1674 ± 1037 days. Overall patient demographics, complications, and patient outcomes were similar among all institutions.
CONCLUSIONS: A paradigm of systematically extending center experience directly to facilitate safe and high-quality pediatric liver program establishment has been demonstrated, with the additional benefit of increased split liver graft utilization benefiting both adults and children. The success of this model has implications for optimizing pediatric liver transplant care in the United States.

articles.title: Walking for Chronic Pain: More Than an Exercise Prescription.
Comparison of Nursing Workload Between Direct Anterior Approach Versus Posterolateral Approach for Hip Arthroplasty in Femoral Neck Fractures: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To compare the perioperative nursing workload between the direct anterior approach and the posterolateral approach for hip arthroplasty in femoral neck fractures.
DESIGN: A single-centre, prospective observational cohort study.
METHODS: The study population consisted of 27 orthopaedic nurses who provided perioperative care for patients who underwent a direct anterior approach or posterolateral approach. Perceived nursing workload was assessed using the NASA Task Load Index, while actual workload was evaluated using the Orthopaedic Nurse Work Responsibilities Scale, which quantified the cumulative time (in minutes) required to complete nursing tasks. The unit of analysis was each nurse-patient interaction, with assessments conducted at five time points: preoperative Day 1, postoperative Days 1-3 and discharge day. Data were analysed using linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts for both nurse and patient to account for repeated measurements and clustering.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven orthopaedic nurses providing perioperative care for 65 patients completed the study. The two patient groups were comparable in baseline characteristics. The actual nursing workload was similar between the two groups. For perceived workload, the main effect of surgical approach was not statistically significant (β = -0.59, 95% CI [-2.042, 0.862], p = 0.421). However, the group-by-time interaction was significant, and the perceived workload was significantly higher for nurses caring for PLA patients on postoperative Day 3 (β = -1.364, 95% CI [-2.267, -0.461], Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.003) and at discharge (β = -1.406, 95% CI [-2.309, -0.503], Bonferroni-corrected p = 0.002). Descriptive analyses suggested that nurses at higher competency levels tended to report lower perceived and actual workload than their less experienced counterparts, though this was not formally tested.
CONCLUSION: Surgical approach was not associated with actual nursing workload but appeared to be associated with higher perceived workload later in the recovery phase, which may reflect institution-specific care pathways rather than the surgical approach alone. Nurse experience was inversely related to both perceived and actual workload. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that surgical approach and nurse experience may merit consideration when planning staffing and training to optimize workload and enhance patient care.
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: The findings suggest that nursing staffing and training programs could consider both the surgical approach and nurse experience levels to optimize workload management, support nurse well-being and enhance the quality of perioperative patient care. Nurse managers could consider providing additional support to patients receiving PLA when they first get out of bed and upon discharge to alleviate the perceived workload of the nurse.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, reporting or dissemination plans of this research. They participated solely as study participants, providing data through workload assessments during their perioperative care. We sincerely thank both the patients and nurses for their participation in this study.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100878).

articles.title: Association of Ultrasound-Guided PECS II Block with Postoperative Pain Scores and Recovery Outcomes in Subpectoral Breast Augmentation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Breast augmentation is one of the most frequently performed aesthetic surgical procedures. This study evaluated whether adding pectoral nerve II (PECS II) block to standard multimodal analgesia, as part of a multidisciplinary perioperative pain-management strategy, was associated with improved early postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing breast augmentation.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed anesthesia records of 48 patients undergoing subpectoral breast augmentation between April 15, 2024, and November 1, 2025. Patients receiving an ultrasound-guided PECS II block in addition to standard multimodal analgesia were compared with patients receiving multimodal analgesia alone. The primary outcome was the highest post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) Visual Analog Scale score (VAS). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative remifentanil consumption, rescue meperidine use, PACU length of stay (PACU LOS), ward rescue analgesia, and block-related complications.
RESULTS: A total of 48 patients were analyzed, including 27 in the PECS II block group and 21 in the control group. PACU VAS scores were lower in the PECS II block group than in controls (median [interquartile range]: 1 [0-2] vs 4 [3-6], p < 0.001). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was lower in the PECS II block group (p = 0.009). VAS score ≥4 requiring protocol-driven rescue meperidine occurred in 71.4% of control patients but in none of the PECS II block patients (p < 0.001). PACU LOS was significantly shorter in the PECS II block group (p < 0.001). These associations persisted after multivariable adjustment. Ward rescue tramadol use did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.186). No block-related complications were documented.
CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-guided PECS II block combined with multimodal analgesia was associated with improved postoperative analgesia, reduced opioid requirements, and shorter PACU LOS. These findings support its potential integration into multidisciplinary perioperative care after subpectoral breast augmentation. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Comparing the safety and efficacy of low-dose versus high-dose tranexamic acid in reducing blood loss in neurosurgical procedures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative bleeding is a major concern in neurosurgery, including spine fusions and cranial tumor resections. Tranexamic acid (TXA) is commonly used to reduce blood loss, but the ideal dosing strategy remains controversial. High-dose TXA regimens may enhance hemostasis but raise safety concerns, whereas low-dose regimens are commonly used with unclear comparative efficacy. This review aimed to compare the safety and efficacy of low-dose versus high-dose TXA in neurosurgical procedures.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through January 2026 identified studies comparing TXA dosing in neurosurgery. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies reporting at least one relevant outcome were included.
RESULTS: Intraoperative blood loss is the primary outcome. Moreover, total blood loss, length of hospital stay, and duration of the surgery were secondary outcomes. The quality of the included studies was assessed using risk of bias 2 for RCTs and Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies for non-randomized studies. Meta-analysis was performed where appropriate. Eleven studies met inclusion criteria, with seven included in quantitative synthesis. Both low- and high-dose TXA significantly reduced perioperative blood loss compared with no TXA. However, no statistically significant differences were observed across the outcomes. No increase in thromboembolic events, seizures, or other major complications was observed with high-dose TXA.
CONCLUSION: Both dosing strategies of TXA reduced blood loss effectively. Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear advantage of high-dose over low-dose TXA. However, given the limited direct comparative evidence, further high-quality randomized trials are needed to define the optimal dosing strategy.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of one-hole split endoscope versus unilateral biportal endoscopy for lumbar degenerative diseases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to compare the clinical efficacy and safety of the novel One-hole Split Endoscope (OSE) technique with the established Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) technique for the treatment of lumbar degenerative diseases (LDD).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted from January 2021 to December 2023, involving 116 patients with LDD. Patients were allocated to either the OSE group (n = 60) or the UBE group (n = 56). Perioperative outcomes (operative time, blood loss, hospital stay, incision length), clinical scores (VAS for back/leg pain, ODI), and complication rates were systematically compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Both groups demonstrated significant clinical improvement postoperatively. The OSE procedure required a longer operative time (135.8 ± 12.6 min vs. 102.4 ± 10.9 min, P < 0.001). However, the OSE group demonstrated advantages in several key perioperative metrics, including a significantly shorter hospital stay (3.9 ± 0.8 days vs. 5.4 ± 1.1 days, P < 0.001) and a smaller incision length (1.5 ± 0.2 cm vs. 2.7 ± 0.3 cm, P < 0.001). Intraoperative blood loss was minimal and comparable between the two groups (P > 0.05). The OSE group also showed earlier and superior functional recovery, evidenced by significantly lower ODI scores at 1-week, 1-month, and final follow-up (P < 0.05), whereas no significant differences were found in postoperative pain VAS scores or in the overall complication rate (P = 0.127).
CONCLUSION: Both OSE and UBE techniques are effective and safe for treating LDD. Despite a longer operative time, the OSE technique offers distinct advantages in minimizing surgical trauma, promoting faster recovery, and achieving better early functional outcomes. OSE represents a valuable and innovative minimally invasive option in the spine surgeon's arsenal.

articles.title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks in the Treatment of Pediatric Headaches.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral nerve blocks (PNBs), while an effective treatment of headache disorders in adults, have been infrequently studied in pediatric patients. This study aimed to assess practice patterns in PNB use in pediatric headache.
METHODS: This was a prospective study conducted between 2020 and 2022 in a headache clinic at a tertiary children's hospital. Preinjection and postinjection survey data were prospectively obtained from 16 patients over 32 visits where PNBs, including greater and lesser occipital, auriculotemporal, supraorbital, and supratrochlear nerve blocks, were administered.
RESULTS: Participants ranged in age from 10 to 19 years old, with a median age of 16.7 years, and the majority was diagnosed with migraine without aura. Among the total cohort, mean pain scores, obtained on a 10-point scale, decreased from 4.4 preinjection to 2.8 postinjection (P = 0.003). When stratified by specific headache diagnosis, only patients with migraine without aura reported significant pain decrease (P = 0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: These preliminary findings support that PNBs may be a promising treatment in pediatric headache, particularly in migraine without aura.

articles.title: Awake craniotomy as a routine pathway for supratentorial tumor surgery: A 500-case awake-craniotomy experience with institutional resource and charge benchmarking.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrated safety, tolerability, and resource data on awake craniotomy in resource-constrained settings are lacking. Improving accessibility has remained central to our program. We report an experience exceeding 500 awake craniotomies with structured comparator synthesis.
METHODS: Three nested cohorts from one Central American institution were analyzed: 218 awake craniotomies (2007-2018, audited safety), 500 procedures spanning neoplastic and non-neoplastic lesions (2007-2026, program tolerability), and 30 awake versus 30 contemporaneous general-anesthesia craniotomies (2024-2026, descriptive benchmarking). The two contemporary groups were restricted to elective supratentorial intraparenchymal tumor resections. The contemporary cohort was derived from billing and administrative records; baseline clinical, radiological, and histopathological data were unavailable; groups were managed by different teams.
RESULTS: Across the 500-case program, completion without conversion was 99.0%; 30-day mortality, ascertainable only for the 282 registry-era procedures, was 3.2%. In the 218-case cohort, seizures occurred in 5.1%, perioperative mortality was 0.5%, and none required ventilation; extent of resection was 73%, 94%, and 100% in eloquent, adjacent to eloquence, and non-eloquent cortex. In the contemporaneous institutional benchmark, the awake pathway showed shorter stay (1.0 vs. 2.0 days), no intensive-care use (0/30 vs. 9/30), shorter incision-to-closure time, and $5,205 lower median billed charges than the general-anesthesia pathway. Outcomes were consistent with 14 comparator studies.
CONCLUSION: In this high-volume, resource-constrained program, to the best of our knowledge, the only protocolized awake-craniotomy program in the region, awake craniotomy served as a routine pathway for eligible supratentorial intraparenchymal lesions, with high completion, favorable safety, short hospitalization, no intensive-care admission, and lower observed billed charges than conventional practice.

articles.title: Scheduled perioperative intravenous acetaminophen reduces opioid usage in the postoperative period for neonates undergoing gastrointestinal surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multimodal analgesia is recommended by Enhanced Recovery After Surgery guidelines for the pediatric population to prevent deleterious effects of opioids. Acetaminophen offers an effective alternative, and intravenous delivery is the most reliable option. Thus, we implemented a perioperative intravenous acetaminophen protocol for neonates undergoing gastrointestinal surgery to reduce postoperative opioid utilization.
METHODS: A matched, observational cohort study design was utilized. The intervention group received intravenous acetaminophen dosed by weight once preoperatively and at regular intervals postoperatively. Propensity score matching compared the intervention group to historical controls of neonatal gastrointestinal surgery cases that received standard postoperative analgesic care. The primary outcome measure was cumulative postoperative opioid use within 48 hours after surgery in total morphine milligram equivalents per kilogram. Other outcomes included pain score via the Neonatal Pain, Agitation, and Sedation Score, postoperative length of hospital stay, postoperative days to extubation, time to first enteral feed, time on parenteral nutrition, and adverse events.
RESULTS: There were 82 cases included, 41 intervention and 41 control. There was a significant reduction in median morphine milligram equivalents per kilogram in the intervention group (0.6; interquartile range, 0.0-2.6 vs 1.8; interquartile range, 0.7-14.4; P = .0187). Median Neonatal Pain, Agitation, and Sedation Score at 48 hours postoperatively was equivalent between groups (2.6; interquartile range, 1.3-3.6 vs 2.3; interquartile range, 1.3-3.3; P = .8239). There were trends toward decreased duration of intubation and time on parenteral nutrition.
CONCLUSION: Intravenous acetaminophen is effective in reducing opioid use while maintaining adequate analgesia in neonates who have undergone gastrointestinal surgery. This intervention may improve overall outcomes for this population.

articles.title: Psychedelics in neurosurgery: Potential utility in prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurosurgical patients carry a high and frequently undertreated burden of psychological suffering, acute and chronic pain, and neurological deficits amenable to recovery. The resurgence of psychedelic research has produced relevant evidence in adjacent fields, but its applicability to neurosurgery has not been systematized. This review synthesizes that evidence across prevention, perioperative care, pain management, and neurorehabilitation, and delineates the safety considerations specific to neurosurgery.
METHODS: Narrative review structured around a population, intervention, comparator, outcome, and time question, covering 2020-2026. The classic serotonergic psychedelics (psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide [LSD], N,N-dimethyltryptamine, ayahuasca, 5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine, and mescaline), the iboga alkaloid ibogaine, the entactogen 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, and the dissociatives ketamine and esketamine were examined. Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and high-quality mechanistic studies were prioritized.
RESULTS: No trial has administered these agents in neurosurgical cohorts, so all evidence is indirect. Psilocybin- assisted therapy produces substantial, durable reductions in cancer-related depression, anxiety, and existential distress. LSD is anxiolytic; parenteral tryptamines act rapidly in depression; ibogaine improved disability, post- traumatic stress, and cognition after traumatic brain injury but carries arrhythmia risk. Perioperative ketamine and esketamine show antidepressant and opioid-sparing effects. Classic psychedelics promote neuroplasticity and are neuroprotective in preclinical models.
CONCLUSION: A biologically plausible basis exists for exploring these agents in neurosurgery, but direct evidence is absent and translation is constrained by the seizure threshold, hemodynamic and cerebrovascular effects, perioperative serotonergic interactions, and the need for structured psychological support. Perioperative esketamine and psilocybin for neuro-oncological distress are the most feasible starting points. Purpose-designed neurosurgical trials are required.

articles.title: Perspective/short review: Critical early diagnosis and emergency treatment for thoracic epidural hematomas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We reviewed published studies describing postoperative spinal hematomas (ESH) across all spinal levels, with an emphasis on thoracic cases. Postoperative epidural spinal hematomas (ESH) most commonly occur in the thoracic spine, followed by the lumbar and cervical regions. They may arise in association with anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy, epidural anesthesia or interventional procedures, trauma, or spinal decompression and/or fusion. Thoracic ESH (TESH) represent the highest risk group, with reported incidences ranging from 0.12% to 4.46%.
METHODS: We assessed the varied etiologies of ESH/TESH, and analyzed the multitude of risk factors, imaging findings, and optimal timing of surgical intervention for addressing these lesions.
RESULTS: Reported incidences of postoperative epidural spinal hematomas (ESH) ranged from 0.1-3%, with pooled studies showing an overall rate of ~0.52-0.69%. Notably, thoracic procedures (TESH) occurred more frequently, with rates ranging from 0.12% to 4.46%. One review of 40 studies found a 0.52% overall incidence of ESH, including 0.84% thoracic, 0.63% lumbar, and 0.32% cervical lesions. Multilevel ESH/TESH hematomas were more common after posterior (0.70%) vs. anterior (0.24%) surgery, and were five-fold more frequent following minimally invasive (1.94%) vs. open procedures (0.42%).
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative epidural spinal hematomas occur in ~0.52-0.69% of spinal procedures, with thoracic lesions showing higher reported rates (0.12%-4.46%). The strongest predictors of neurological recovery included; the rapid recognition of new postoperative neurological deficits, immediate postoperative MR studies, and emergency surgery. We therefore recommend early/STAT diagnosis and surgery for ESH/TESH (i.e. performed as soon as possible rather than simpley within a < 24 h window) to optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Management of aspirin in lumbar fusion: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The perioperative management of acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) in spine surgery remains a daily clinical dilemma. While ASA discontinuation is traditionally recommended to minimize bleeding risk, cessation may expose patients with cardiovascular comorbidities to thromboembolic complications. In the absence of clear evidence-based guidelines, neurosurgeons frequently rely on institutional practices or personal judgment.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched for studies published from January 2000 to September 2025 comparing perioperative ASA use versus no ASA in adult lumbar fusion surgery. Random-effects models calculated mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I.
RESULTS: Four observational studies including 700 patients (316 ASA, 384 controls) were analyzed. ASA continuation or discontinuation did not significantly affect intraoperative blood loss (MD 31.29 mL; 95% CI -2.89 to 65.47; P=0.07), postoperative drainage, operative time, or hospital stay. Subgroup analysis stratified by timing of ASA discontinuation (≤3 days vs. ≥7 days) revealed no significant differences within or between subgroups. Complication rates, morbidity, and mortality were comparable across treatment arms.
CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of low-dose ASA during lumbar fusion does not appear to increase perioperative bleeding, complications, or mortality. Given the potential cardiovascular risks of interruption, discontinuation should be reserved for carefully selected patients following multidisciplinary evaluation and individualized risk assessment. However, the available evidence in this field is limited by retrospective designs and small sample sizes, requiring further high-quality prospective trials to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Critical Care Management of Patients With Acute Fulminant Myocarditis.
articles.abstract: Fulminant myocarditis is a life-threatening inflammatory cardiac syndrome characterized by severe myocardial injury and abrupt deterioration of cardiac function, leading to rapidly progressive cardiogenic shock. Patients often require intravenous vasoactive therapy and/or temporary mechanical circulatory support to maintain systemic perfusion and prevent multiorgan failure. Although frequently preceded by a viral prodrome and affecting young and healthy individuals, fulminant myocarditis encompasses diverse etiologies, including immune-mediated and toxin-related subtypes, with major implications for diagnosis and treatment. Optimal management relies on early recognition, prompt admission to specialized cardiac intensive care units, and rapid access to advanced diagnostics, including endomyocardial biopsy and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, to confirm myocardial inflammation, exclude ischemic disease, and guide etiology-directed therapy. Hemodynamic stabilization requires tailored use of vasopressors and inotropes while minimizing catecholamine-related arrhythmias and myocardial oxygen demand. For refractory shock, early escalation to temporary mechanical circulatory support, most commonly venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, is central to restore perfusion and provide a bridge to recovery or advanced therapy. Because fulminant myocarditis frequently involves malignant arrhythmias and multiorgan dysfunction, integrated critical care management is essential. This review summarizes a practical intensive care approach to fulminant myocarditis, emphasizing early diagnosis, individualized hemodynamic and device-based support, multiorgan management, and phenotype-driven immunomodulatory treatment strategies.

articles.title: The Impact of Lateral Extra-Articular Tenodesis on Knee Range of Motion After Pediatric Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lateral extra-articular tenodesis (LET) is increasingly used to augment anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction (ACLR) in pediatric patients to improve graft survival and rotational stability. However, concerns remain regarding postoperative knee stiffness after augmentation.
PURPOSE: To determine whether LET augmentation is associated with increased risk of restricted knee range of motion (ROM) after pediatric ACLR and to identify patient and surgical factors associated with postoperative stiffness.
STUDY DESIGN: Case-control study; Level of evidence, 3.
METHODS: The authors reviewed 412 pediatric patients who underwent primary ACLR (2013-2025) at a single tertiary referral center. Restricted knee ROM was defined as a loss of flexion ≥15° or extension ≥5° at 3 months postoperatively compared with the contralateral limb. Exposures included LET utilization, demographic factors, socioeconomic measures (Area Deprivation Index and insurance status), graft characteristics, meniscal procedures, time to initiation of physical therapy, and time from injury to surgery. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify independent predictors of restricted knee ROM.
RESULTS: Restricted knee ROM occurred in 12.9% of procedures overall (16.8% with LET vs 10.2% without). LET was independently associated with increased odds of restricted motion (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2 [95% CI, 1.01-3.95]; P = .046). Female sex was associated with increased risk (AOR, 4.23 [95% CI, 2.09-8.55]; P < .001). Age at surgery, time to initiation of physical therapy, graft type, meniscal procedures, socioeconomic deprivation, insurance status, and time from injury to surgery were not independently associated with restricted knee ROM. Seven patients underwent manipulation under anesthesia, and 3 underwent lysis of adhesions. Overall, manipulation under anesthesia or lysis of adhesions was required in 8 patients and was more common after LET.
CONCLUSION: LET augmentation during pediatric ACLR is associated with an increased risk of early restricted knee ROM, although most cases are mild and resolve with nonoperative management. Female sex represented an additional risk factor for postoperative stiffness.

articles.title: Single or Double: Does it Really Make a Difference?
Evolving indications for metabolic and bariatric surgery.
articles.abstract: This chapter addresses patient selection for metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) in the modern obesity care landscape, where anti-obesity medications (AOMs) such as semaglutide and tirzepatide have changed the clinical decision-making framework. We organize the evidence around four questions a clinician actually asks: who qualifies under current guidelines, who benefits most and from which procedure, who is poorly served by surgery, and when pharmacotherapy is the better answer. We review the evolution of indications from the 1991 NIH Consensus Conference through the 2022 ASMBS/IFSO joint guidelines, with attention to the randomized evidence supporting expanded indications at BMI 30-34.9 kg/m² with type 2 diabetes. We then examine outcomes by patient phenotype, including type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, obstructive sleep apnea, heart failure, transplant candidacy, polycystic ovary syndrome, pregnancy planning, and elevated cancer risk. We identify populations for whom surgery carries an unfavorable risk-benefit profile, including patients with advanced perioperative risk, decompensated cirrhosis, untreated psychiatric illness, active substance use, or inability to maintain long-term nutritional follow-up. Finally, we provide a comparative analysis of MBS and modern AOMs across cardiometabolic outcomes, with attention to the methodological limitations of current cohort comparisons and the role of combination and sequential strategies. The chapter concludes that the two modalities are converging on a complementary framework in which patient phenotype, not BMI alone, determines the right intervention.

articles.title: Efficacy of robot-assisted uniportal spinal endoscopy for lumbar spondylodiscitis: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lumbar spondylodiscitis, particularly at the L4/5 and L5/S1 segments, poses significant clinical challenges due to their impact on spinal stability and function. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of robot-assisted uniportal spinal endoscopy in treating this disease.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study include 96 consecutive patients with lumbar spondylodiscitis treated from January 2022 to December 2022. Patients were classified into a robot-assisted group (n = 47) and a traditional surgery group (n = 49) according to the surgical approach received. The primary outcomes included operative time and length of hospital stay. Secondary outcomes included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fluoroscopy time, complications, and family satisfaction. Longitudinal changes in C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), procalcitonin (PCT), white blood cell count (WBC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)), and visual analog scale (VAS) scores were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).
RESULTS: Compared with the traditional surgery group, the robot-assisted group showed reduced operative time, shorter hospital stay, decreased fluoroscopy time, lower intraoperative blood loss, and higher overall family satisfaction rate (all P < 0.05). The total complication rates were comparable between the two groups (P = 0.141). Repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant group × time interactions for CRP, IL-6, PCT, and VAS scores, indicating different postoperative recovery trajectories between groups. WBC and ESR showed significant temporal changes but no significant group × time interactions.
CONCLUSION: Robot-assisted uniportal spinal endoscopy was associated with favorable perioperative and early clinical outcomes for patients with lumbar spondylodiscitis, suggesting its potential role in facilitating early postoperative recovery.

articles.title: The Impact of Ultrasound-guided Quadratus Lumborum Block on Perioperative Analgesia and Recovery Quality in Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Radical Prostatectomy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ultrasound-guided quadratus lumborum block (QLB) is an effective nerve block technique that is well-suited for providing anesthesia and analgesia during abdominal and hip surgeries. This study aims to evaluate the impact of ultrasound-guided QLB on perioperative analgesia and recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic radical prostatectomy through a retrospective cohort analysis.
METHODS: A total of 208 patients who underwent laparoscopic radical prostatectomy at Nantong University Affiliated Hospital between January 2020 and August 2023 were included in this study. The patients were divided into two groups: the QLB group (n=102) and the control group (n=106). Perioperative management was conducted in accordance with Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols. Data regarding pain scores, analgesic consumption, hemodynamic stability, inflammatory markers, and recovery indicators were collected and analyzed.
RESULTS: Postoperative analgesia revealed reduced analgesic consumption (P < 0.001) and delayed analgesic pump usage in the QLB group (P < 0.001). NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing were significantly lower at all evaluated time points in the QLB group (P < 0.05). Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate were more stable in the QLB group after surgery (P < 0.05). The inflammatory index IL-6 and SII of the QLB group were significantly lower (P < 0.05) than the control group. Time to first anal exhalation (P = 0.012) and length of hospital stay (P = 0.024) improved significantly in the QLB group than the control group.
CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-guided QLB can significantly reduce postoperative pain and improve Recovery Quality in patients with laparoscopic radical prostatectomy, reduce the use of opioid drugs, stabilize hemodynamic parameters, etc. This indicates that QLB has significant clinical significance in lower abdominal surgeries such as prostatectomy.

articles.title: Evolution of Management of Postoperative Pain in Spain: A Nationwide Survey of Organizational Structure and Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitals require standardized processes to effectively manage patients with acute postoperative pain. We aim to evaluate the current pain management practices in Spain through a cross-sectional study, updating the findings from a previous audit conducted in 2012.
METHODS: An online questionnaire was mailed to anesthesiologists in Spain. Responses were stratified based on the hospital size (< 200 or ≥ 200 beds). Categorical variables were presented as percentages with a 95% confidence interval, while continuous variables were expressed as median and interquartile range.
RESULTS: The survey received responses from 67.9% (n = 127) of hospitals with ≥ 200 beds. 70.1% of large hospitals had an acute pain service (APS) and a hospital-wide acute pain management program (APMP). Concerning large hospitals, full-time pain physicians were available in 30.3% of large hospitals, and 41.6% had full-time nurses dedicated to pain management; 40.2% of patients received written information about postoperative pain; 89.0% of participants reported that their hospital used a standardized scale for assessing postoperative pain; 79.5% had pain treatment protocols; professional training in postoperative pain was organized in 46.6% of cases; and 51.2% considered that the acute postoperative pain was well managed in their hospital.
CONCLUSION: Twelve years later, our study shows (in hospitals ≥ 200 beds), there has been an increase in the percentage of centers with APS or APMP, the proportion of nurses with full-time dedication, and the assessment and documentation of pain. However, the implementation of protocols, pain management training, and the analysis of pain-related indicators have worsened. Improvements are necessary to implement standardized acute postoperative pain management.

articles.title: Effects of Sarcopenia and Myosteatosis on Postoperative Recovery in Elderly Patients after Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Few studies have assessed sarcopenia and myosteatosis identified by skeletal muscle parameters using thoracic Computed Tomography (CT) before surgery among elderly patients. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of thoracic CT-defined sarcopenia and myosteatosis and evaluate their associations with perioperative outcomes in elderly patients undergoing surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included elderly patients aged ≥65 years who underwent surgery with available preoperative thoracic CT imaging. Skeletal muscle abnormalities were assessed on chest CT at the T12 vertebral level. Patients were classified according to the presence of imagingdefined sarcopenia and myosteatosis. Baseline characteristics, intraoperative variables, and postoperative outcomes were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression and linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of sarcopenia and myosteatosis with perioperative outcomes.
RESULTS: Among the 195 elderly surgical patients, 43 (22.1%) were identified as having sarcopenia and 83 (42.6%) had myosteatosis. Compared with nonsarcopenic patients, those with sarcopenia were older and exhibited lower Body Mass Index (BMI), hemoglobin, albumin, and lipid levels, as well as a higher prevalence of ASA classification ≥ 3, previous stroke, and pneumonia history. Sarcopenic patients also showed increased intraoperative vasoactive drug use, prolonged recovery time, and longer total and postoperative length of hospital stay (LOS). In univariable analyses, sarcopenia was associated with increased risk of postoperative composite complications (OR 2.609, 95% CI 1.012-6.471, P = 0.041), longer total LOS (β 0.427, 95% CI 0.162-0.691, P = 0.002), and longer post LOS (β 0.316, 95% CI 0.066-0.566, P = 0.014); however, these associations were not maintained after multivariable adjustment. Sarcopenia was not an independent association with adverse outcomes after adjusting for variables. Patients with myosteatosis showed distinct baseline characteristics, including higher BMI, lower hemoglobin concentration, lower creatinine levels, and a different sex distribution compared with patients without myosteatosis. However, myosteatosis was not significantly associated with perioperative outcomes in either univariable or multivariable analyses.
DISCUSSION: Thoracic CT-defined sarcopenia may represent a marker of systemic vulnerability rather than an isolated indicator of muscle loss, whereas myosteatosis showed limited independent prognostic relevance. Opportunistic muscle assessment on routine chest CT may facilitate risk stratification in elderly surgical patients, although validation in larger cohorts incorporating functional measures is needed.
CONCLUSION: Thoracic CT-defined sarcopenia is common among elderly surgical patients and is associated with markers of nutritional impairment, comorbidity burden, and delayed postoperative recovery. Although imaging-defined sarcopenia was not an independent predictor of adverse outcomes after adjustment, it may serve as an imaging marker of reduced physiological reserve and perioperative vulnerability. In contrast, myosteatosis alone showed limited prognostic relevance in this cohort. Routine assessment of skeletal muscle abnormalities on preoperative thoracic CT may provide additional information for perioperative risk assessment and patient optimization.

articles.title: Propofol in Exhaled Air and Plasma During Paedfusor Target-Controlled Infusion in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Target-controlled infusion (TCI) algorithms for propofol are widely employed, but inter-individual variability in achieved plasma concentrations highlights the likely potential value of real-time monitoring. This prospective observational study evaluated the Exhaled Drug Monitor (Edmon) for online estimation of exhaled propofol concentrations (CA) as a proxy for plasma propofol concentrations (CP) in children. We also explored the relationships between Paedfusor-estimated concentrations (CE-P) and CP, and between CP and Bispectral Index (BIS).
METHODS: Children undergoing propofol-based anaesthesia with the Paedfusor TCI model had continuous recordings of CA (parts per billion [ppb]) and CE-P, with BIS values available in a subset of patients, as electrode placement was sometimes incompatible with the surgical field. Four arterial blood samples were obtained to determine CP. Linear mixed-model analyses were employed to assess the relationships between variables.
RESULTS: Twenty-six children aged 3-10 years were included. During maintenance of anaesthesia at a TCI target concentration of 3.0 μg mL-1, CA lagged behind CP by 4 min. At this delay, the slope (gain) for estimation of CP from CA was 0.36 μg mL-1 ppb-1 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.08 to 0.64, p = 0.015) and the intercept (offset) 1.16 μg mL-1 (95% CI -0.52 to 2.84, p = 0.16), RSquare 0.63. The pooled median absolute performance error based on samples obtained at 20 and 30 min after induction was 8.8% for the Edmon and 13.5% for the Paedfusor. CP was 19%, 16% and 1% higher than Paedfusor predictions at 20 min, 30 min and end of surgery, respectively. In an exploratory analysis, BIS values decreased by 4.8 for each 1 μg mL-1 increase in CP.
CONCLUSION: This exploratory study demonstrates that online monitoring of exhaled propofol during surgery is feasible in children. The Edmon provided estimates of CP comparable with those of the Paedfusor algorithm during maintenance of anaesthesia, but its use is limited by a complex setup and a 4-min time lag relative to plasma concentrations.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: In this study, propofol infusion in children using a target-controlled infusion was performed, and propofol concentration in exhaled air was sampled intermittently and measured. This assessment demonstrated practical feasibility aspects of this sampling and measurement along with challenges for clinical application.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04150432): URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04150432?term=NCT04150432&rank=1.

articles.title: Stereotactic radiosurgery for bilateral trigeminal neuralgia: A systematic review and proposed framework for staged treatment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Bilateral trigeminal neuralgia (BTN) is uncommon and surgically complex. Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is a minimally invasive option for medically refractory BTN, although evidence remains sparse and heterogeneous. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy, durability, and toxicity of SRS in medically refractory BTN. It also synthesized the evidence into a practical staged-treatment framework.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 11, 2026. Eligible studies reported BTN-specific SRS outcomes in adults, separately from unilateral cohorts. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using adapted Newcastle-Ottawa and MINORS tools. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using a GRADE-informed approach. Owing to clinical heterogeneity and small samples, findings were synthesized narratively rather than by meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Six reports met the inclusion criteria. Five described 88 BTN patients, including 54 SRS-treated patients across four reports. Of 91 nominally treated nerves, 67 were explicitly reported, and 24 were inferred from staged bilateral SRS in 12 patients. The sixth report described one BTN case without a complete subgroup denominator. Study-reported initial pain relief ranged from 71.4% to 100% across heterogeneous outcome definitions and analytical units. Pain recurrence was frequent, with durability varying markedly from 14 months to 1697 days in the sequential-onset series. Multiple sclerosis appeared associated with poorer outcomes and earlier recurrence, based on small subgroups. Repeat SRS achieved adequate pain relief in 10 of 11 retreated nerves (91%) in the largest cohort, with a median durability of 2.8 years. Sensory disturbance was the most common adverse event. One report described disabling bilateral numbness in a patient with prior bilateral ablative treatment. Anesthesia dolorosa incidence remains uncertain.
CONCLUSION: SRS may provide early pain control in selected patients with medically refractory BTN, but bilateral sensory morbidity remains uncertain. Staged treatment was described in several reports, whereas bilateral treatment timing was unreported in one case. Certainty of evidence remains very low. Current evidence supports individualized decision-making focused on etiology, surgical fitness, first-side response, sensory toxicity, and cumulative bilateral trigeminal morbidity.Registration and Protocol: This systematic review was not registered in a prospective registry (e.g., PROSPERO). A protocol was developed a priori and is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/RBVNE.

articles.title: Perioperative Pain Assessment and Medication Safety in Office-Based Dental Anesthesia: A Practical Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: We examined perioperative pain assessment, medication documentation, toxicity preparedness, emergency medications and preparedness, and discharge readiness in office-based dental practices. By bringing these considerations together, the goal is to provide a practice overview of what providers should consider incorporating into their office-based dental and other similar anesthesia practices.
RECENT FINDINGS: Office- based dental anesthesia consistently delivers care to children and patients who cannot tolerate hospital treatment. Effective perioperative pain management is critically important for safe patient care in the dental office. Age-appropriate pain assessment, local-anesthetic safety, emergency preparedness, and recovery and discharge criteria are important components of office-based dental anesthesia practices. Dental offices are an important setting for patients who require sedation or general anesthesia; A practical framework may help clinicians consistently integrate safeguard elements into daily office-based care.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in Pediatric Perioperative Cardiac Arrest Survival.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Perioperative cardiac arrest (POCA) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Disparities in perioperative outcomes have been reported, but whether similar differences exist following pediatric POCA remains unclear. We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in 30-day mortality after pediatric POCA.
METHOD: Within the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program for Pediatrics (NSQIP-P) registry, we identified 2646 children under 18 who underwent inpatient, noncardiac surgery (2012─2024) and experienced POCA. Race and ethnicity were categorized as Hispanic, non-Hispanic Asian, non-Hispanic Black or African American, non-Hispanic white, or other. Crude and adjusted risk ratios for 30-day mortality following POCA were estimated.
RESULTS: Among 2646 children with POCA, 47.9% (n = 1268) were non-Hispanic white, 28.2% (n = 745) non-Hispanic Black, 4.0% (n = 106) non-Hispanic Asian, 16.2% (n = 430) Hispanic and 3.7% (n = 97) Other race. Overall, 30-day mortality was 32.9% (871/2646). Mortality was similar across racial or ethnic groups (P = .72). In adjusted analyses, mortality risk did not differ significantly for non-Hispanic Black (adjusted relative risks [aRR] 1.02, P = .80), Hispanic children (aRR 1.06, P = .43), or children of other race (aRR 1.02, P = .88) compared with non-Hispanic white children. Emergent surgery (aRR 1.62, P < .001) and preoperative inotrope use (aRR 1.41, P < .001) were independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: We found no significant racial or ethnic differences in mortality risk following POCA among children undergoing inpatient surgery. Mortality was associated with clinical and perioperative factors, including emergent surgery and preoperative inotrope use. This suggests that efforts to identify drivers of disparities in pediatric postsurgical mortality must look beyond POCA outcomes alone.

articles.title: The relationship between early warning scores at intensive care unit discharge and risk of intensive care unit readmission in adult and pediatric populations: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Readmission after discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU) occurs globally at a rate of approximately 1-12% and is associated with adverse patient outcomes. Despite these findings, there is no internationally accepted tool to guide or standardize decisions regarding ICU discharge. In this scoping review, we aimed to evaluate the use of early warning scores (EWSs) measured at or around the time of ICU discharge as predictors of subsequent ICU readmission in adult and pediatric populations.
SOURCE: With support from a medical librarian, we searched MEDLINE®, Embase®, and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature from database inception to December 14, 2025. We included quantitative observational and interventional studies that evaluated any EWS (e.g., National EWS [NEWS]/NEWS2, Modified EWS [MEWS], Pediatric EWS [PEWS], Rothman Index, Risk Scoring Index, or related tools) at ICU discharge, immediately prior to transfer, or immediately upon ward admission and reported unplanned ICU readmission following transfer to a hospital ward. Unplanned ICU readmissions were defined as any unplanned return to an ICU after discharge to the ward. We excluded studies in which patients were discharged to locations other than a ward (e.g., home, long-term care) or that focused solely on interfacility transfer. Screening and data extraction were performed in duplicate using a standardized template, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer.
PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: The search identified 7,977 records, of which 4,824 remained after removal of duplicates. Of the articles, 58 underwent full-text review, and 20 studies met inclusion criteria. The studies were conducted across North America, Europe, and Asia and included both adult (n = 14) and pediatric (n = 6) populations. All were observational (retrospective or prospective) or pre-post intervention designs; no randomized controlled trials were identified. A range of tools were evaluated, including NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS, PEWS, the Rothman Index, the Risk Scoring Index, and several machine-learning-based EWS models. Of the 20 studies, 17 reported a significant association between higher EWS values at or near ICU discharge and increased risk of unplanned ICU readmission, while three found no significant association. Across studies, readmission rates and EWS thresholds varied, and there was considerable heterogeneity in populations, settings, and outcome time frames. The risk of bias was generally low to moderate across QUADAS-2 domains, although several studies had high or unclear risk in key areas-most commonly patient selection and index test blinding-limiting causal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: Most available studies report that higher EWS values at ICU discharge are associated with an increased likelihood of ICU readmission. Early warning scores may therefore serve as useful adjuncts to clinical judgement when assessing discharge readiness. Nevertheless, the current evidence base is limited by the absence of randomized or robust interventional trials, and substantial heterogeneity, which limits causal inference and the ability to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve outcomes. Further multicentre prospective studies are needed to determine whether EWS-guided discharge protocols improve patient outcomes, reduce readmissions, and optimize use of ICU resources.
