Contemporary hand injury management increasingly integrates WALANT, robust tendon repair, anti-adhesion adjuncts, early active rehabilitation, modern orthoses, and digital adherence tools. However, heterogeneity and variable risk of bias across studies warrant cautious interpretation and further high-quality comparative research.

articles.title: How Does Place of Residence Influence the Experience and Management of Chronic Non-Malignant Pain? A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Chronic non-malignant pain (CNMP) affects up to half of the UK population and one third of adults globally. Rural populations experience poorer health outcomes across several chronic conditions; however, the influence of place of residence on CNMP management, outcomes and experiences remains unclear. This systematic review examined how place of residence (urban or rural) impacts CNMP management, outcomes and experiences.
METHODS: PubMed, psycINFO, Medline, Embase and CINAHL databases were searched for qualitative and quantitative studies. Dual title/abstract screening and full-text review were undertaken against pre-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria. A narrative synthesis was performed.
RESULTS: Of 2341 titles screened, 16 studies were included (12 observational, three qualitative and one mixed-methods study). Most studies were rated as fair quality, with limitations including unsatisfactory response rates and non-validated outcome measures. Rural residents were more likely to use primary care and opioid-based treatments, whereas urban residents had greater access to specialist pain services. Outcomes were less consistent; several studies reported poorer pain-related outcomes among rural residents, although some identified no significant differences compared with urban populations. Long travel distances, prolonged waiting times and limited specialist and non-pharmacological services were barriers to care.
CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights geographic inequalities in CNMP management and experiences. Findings should be interpreted in light of methodological limitations and study heterogeneity. Targeted approaches are needed to improve equitable access to pain management across settings.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This systematic review synthesises evidence on how geographic location influences the management, outcomes and experiences of people with chronic non-malignant pain. The findings identify consistent rural-urban disparities in access to evidence-based pain care and highlight important gaps in the current literature, including the limited availability of high-quality comparative studies. These findings provide a foundation for future research and inform the development of more equitable pain services.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO number: CRD42024522734.

articles.title: Denervation Techniques for Chronic Low Back Pain due to Lumbar Facet Joint Arthropathy: A Comparison Between Radiofrequency and Endoscopic Neurotomy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Radiofrequency neurotomy (RFN) of the lumbar medial branch is the standard of care for facet joint arthropathy-related chronic low back pain (CLBP). However, endoscopic neurotomy (EN) has also recently been adopted as a feasible treatment option for CLBP. The increasing population of patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) highlights the need for alternative denervation methods to avoid device interference. We propose that both RFN and EN are effective for CLBP, with EN offering a safe option for patients with CIEDs and therapy-resistant aberrant innervation.
METHODS: Patients with facet joint arthropathy-related CLBP who were treated between 01.01.2016 and 31.12.2019 were prospectively included and grouped as RFN or EN based on treatment. Over a 12-month period, the following outcomes were studied: Core Outcome Measures Index for the back (COMI-back), Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), complications, and costs.
RESULTS: Sixty-five patients (35 female) with a median age of 62 years were included. Prior to the intervention, patients had a median COMI-back of 8.6 (IQR: 7.7-9.0) and a median VAS score of 8.0 (IQR: 7.0-9.0). After intervention, the VAS score dropped significantly for both groups. Thereafter, pain scores rose in the EN group, whereas VAS levels in the RFN group remained unaltered. Complication rates were significantly lower after RFN compared with EN patients (p < 0.007). Total costs were significantly lower for the RFN group (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, this prospective study shows that both EN and percutaneous multilevel RFN are safe and effective treatments for facet joint arthropathy-associated CLBP. RFN is preferred as the first treatment option for uncomplicated CLBP due to its lower invasiveness, while EN is suitable as an alternative for patients with CIEDs and those with therapy-resistant aberrant innervation or anatomical variations.

articles.title: Neuropeptide signaling in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: Receptor biology, mechanistic links, and a cautious prevention framework.
articles.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) encompass postoperative delirium, delayed neurocognitive recovery, and postoperative neurocognitive disorder in patients with a vulnerable brain. Neuropeptides provide a receptor-defined signaling layer that can couple tissue injury, nociception, arousal, sleep, vascular regulation, and glial responses. This review integrates clinical and translational evidence for substance P/neurokinin-1, neuropeptide Y/Y receptors, orexin-A/orexin receptors, and vasoactive intestinal peptide/pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide pathways within the broader biology of PND. Current human evidence is strongest for perioperative risk factors, delirium phenotyping, and selected preventive bundles; direct evidence that neuropeptide pathways cause or predict PND remains limited. We therefore distinguish established associations from preclinical mechanisms and hypothesis-generating therapeutic opportunities. The proposed framework links preoperative brain-reserve assessment and medication optimization with intraoperative protection of neurovascular and circuit function and postoperative restoration of sleep, mobility, and orientation. Biomarkers and neuropeptide signatures may enrich future trials, but no validated thresholds or individual-level neuropeptide-guided treatment pathway is currently available. Progress will require receptor-resolved assays, longitudinal human sampling, external validation, and pragmatic trials that test clinical utility rather than mechanistic plausibility alone.

articles.title: Novel bronchoscopic technique using endoscopic scissors for retrieval of a 12-year-old silicone airway stent placed for a post-intubation tracheal stenosis: A case report.
articles.abstract: Silicone tracheal stents are widely used in the management of benign airway stenosis; however, long-term positioned stents may lead to delayed complications. We report a case of a 28-year-old man who underwent silicone tracheal stent placement 12 years back for post-intubation tracheal stenosis at another centre. The patient subsequently was lost to follow-up, and he was referred to our centre for surgical removal of the stent. However, the patient was unwilling for surgery considering its complex nature. Current bronchoscopy revealed a silicone stent in the upper trachea with extensive granulation tissue, resulting in significant airway obstruction. The patient was taken up for bronchoscopic stent removal under general anaesthesia using suspension laryngoscopy. The adherent stent necessitated the use of rigid endoscopic scissors to cut the anterior aspect of the stent in order to dislodge it, following which the stent was removed using rigid forceps. This case demonstrates that even long-standing silicone stents with extensive granulation tissue can be safely removed using a carefully planned multimodal bronchoscopic approach.

articles.title: Ventilation strategies in reconstructive surgery of the tracheal bifurcation and bronchi: a 40-year retrospective institutional experience of 1,345 procedures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes of differentiated intraoperative ventilation strategies tailored to the level and complexity of reconstructive surgery on the tracheal bifurcation and bronchi.
METHODS: A retrospective descriptive institutional study of 1,345 consecutive reconstructive procedures performed between 1986 and 2025 across four specialized thoracic centers by a single surgical team was conducted. Surgeries were categorized into five procedural groups: circumferential carinal resection (n = 142), partial carinal resection (n = 5), bronchial sleeve resection (n = 231), pneumonectomy with stump-less carinal closure (n = 815), and bronchopleural/tracheopleural fistula repair (n = 152). Intraoperative airway management included selective one-lung volume-controlled ventilation (OLV), catheter-based high-frequency jet ventilation (HFJV), and combined/apnoeic techniques.
RESULTS: No intraoperative deaths occurred, and no complications were directly attributable to ventilation failure. Five transient intraoperative anesthetic incidents occurred in patients with severe cardiopulmonary comorbidities: arterial hypotension (n = 1), supraventricular arrhythmias (n = 2), and asystole/cardiac arrest (n = 2), all successfully resolved. Major postoperative complications occurred in 109 patients (8.1%); 18 patients (1.3%) had complications potentially related to airway management (atelectasis, n = 4; pneumonia, n = 6; acute respiratory distress syndrome, n = 8). Overall 30-day mortality was 0.9% (13/1,345). Mortality was 0% in isolated bronchial resections (0/231), 2.1% after circumferential carinal resection (3/142), 1.3% in post-pneumonectomy fistula repairs (2/152), and 0.98% in stump-less carinal closures (8/815).
CONCLUSIONS: A procedure-tailored ventilation strategy provides safe and reliable intraoperative gas exchange. For carinal reconstructions, catheter-based HFJV is technically advantageous by avoiding bulky tubes in the operative field. For isolated bronchial sleeve resections, conventional selective OLV is sufficient. Managing post-pneumonectomy fistulas requires adaptable maneuvers to maintain gas exchange during induction and airway transection.

articles.title: Authors' Reply to "Additional Insights into the Analgesia Management of a High-risk Postoperative Setting".
Additional Insights Into the Analgesia Management of a High-risk Postoperative Setting.
Microscopic Evaluation of Crystallization Dynamics in 0.25% Levobupivacaine Mixed with Common Regional Anaesthesia Adjuvants: An in vitro Compatibility Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the crystallization dynamics of 0.25% levobupivacaine when combined with common regional anaesthesia adjuvants.
METHODS: This in vitro study examined mixtures of 0.25% levobupivacaine with dexamethasone (20:1), 25% magnesium sulfate (20:1.5), dexmedetomidine (20:1), 8.4% sodium bicarbonate (10:1), and adrenaline (1:100,000). The study protocol was an in vitro investigation. Since no human or animal subjects were involved, the study was exempt from formal ethics committee approval. An institutional waiver was obtained from the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Uzbekistan Research Administration of the Republican Scientific Emergency Medical Centre (ref no: 03-05/119, date: 15.01.2026). All mixtures were incubated at 37 °C and examined under light microscopy (40× magnification) immediately, at 15 minutes, and at 1 hour. Crystallization onset, crystal count, and crystal size were quantified. For accurate dimensional analysis, a stage micrometer was used to calibrate the digital imaging software, and a calibrated scale bar was superimposed on each micrograph. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows, version 30.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Overall changes across the three matched assessment times were evaluated using the Friedman test. Significant omnibus results were followed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. All tests were two-sided, and a P value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Solutions containing sodium bicarbonate and dexamethasone demonstrated the earliest onset of crystallization. Sodium bicarbonate (10:1) produced immediate and massive precipitation. Levobupivacaine-dexamethasone mixtures showed progressive crystallization, with particle counts exceeding 100 per field for particles larger than 10 μm within 60 minutes. Adrenaline, magnesium sulfate, and dexmedetomidine showed significantly lower crystal densities than those of alkaline mixtures.
CONCLUSION: Based on the present in vitro findings, adding either 8.4% sodium bicarbonate or dexamethasone to 0.25% levobupivacaine produced rapid, substantial crystallization, suggesting a physicochemical incompatibility under the tested conditions. These findings suggest that direct admixture of these agents with levobupivacaine in the same syringe should be approached with caution pending confirmation in clinical studies.

articles.title: Early Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting in Routine Clinical Practice: A Retrospective Observational Study of Associated Perioperative Factors and Prophylactic Practices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains a common complication in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) and negatively affects patient comfort and satisfaction. In routine clinical practice, identifying perioperative factors associated with early PONV may help optimize preventive strategies and guide anesthetic management. This study primarily aimed to evaluate PONV during the first postoperative hour and associated perioperative factors, and secondarily to describe PONV at later postoperative time points and antiemetic practices.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study evaluated adult patients who underwent elective surgery under general or regional anaesthesia from January to December 2021. After applying eligibility and complete-case criteria, 584 ASA I-III patients were included. Demographic characteristics, anesthetic techniques, surgical features, Apfel risk factors, antiemetic prophylaxis, rescue antiemetic use, and binary PONV data at postoperative hours 1, 6, 12, and 24 were assessed.
RESULTS: PONV occurred in 128 patients (22%) during the first postoperative hour and decreased at later postoperative time points. In univariate analyses, first-hour PONV was associated with general anaesthesia, inhalational anesthetic use, perioperative opioid use, female sex, non-smoking status, and perioperative medication-related variables (P < 0.05). The adjusted analysis suggested that early PONV in routine clinical practice reflects an overlapping, multifactorial pattern rather than the effect of a single dominant perioperative factor.
CONCLUSION: First-hour PONV remained a clinically relevant problem in routine perioperative care despite the common use of prophylactic antiemetics. These findings highlight the importance of careful early postoperative monitoring and individualized risk-based preventive strategies in daily anaesthesia practice.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics of Local Anesthetics in Fascial Plane Blocks: Clinical Implications and Safety Considerations-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) are increasingly used in modern regional anaesthesia and differ from conventional nerve blocks by delivering local anesthetic (LA) into interfascial compartments. This approach results in distinct pharmacokinetics with clinically relevant systemic absorption. Pharmacokinetic behavior in FPBs is determined by interactions among patient-related factors, drug properties, adjuvant use, and fascial plane characteristics. High-volume injections, tissue vascularity, and injection technique influence peak plasma concentration and time to peak concentration. Patient variables, such as advanced age, pregnancy, obesity, malnutrition, and organ dysfunction, further increase variability and the risk of toxicity. Epinephrine may reduce the absorption rate and improve safety, whereas dexamethasone and dexmedetomidine mainly prolong analgesia through pharmacodynamic effects. Because systemic absorption is inherent to FPBs, LA systemic toxicity remains a key concern. Individualized dosing, appropriate drug selection, and close monitoring are essential for safe and effective clinical practice.

articles.title: Lung Allograft Function After Primary Graft Dysfunction in the Lung Transplant Outcomes Group Cohort.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplant is associated with increased mortality. Whether PGD increases mortality via long-term effects on allograft function is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the association of PGD with potential lung function and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD).
METHODS: We included lung transplant recipients enrolled in an 8-center prospective cohort study from 2007-2018. PGD was defined by ISHLT criteria. Linear mixed effects and logistic regression models evaluated the association between PGD and maximum potential forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) and whether Global Lung Function Initiative defined (GLI) predicted FEV1 was attained, respectively. Flexible parametric survival models evaluated the association between PGD and CLAD, accounting for confounding and mortality as a competing risk.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 2419 recipients, 510 had PGD. Recipients with PGD had lower maximum potential FEV1 (-311 ml, 95% CI -245 to -377 ml) and were less likely to achieve GLI-predicted FEV1 (probability difference -12.5%, 95% CI -17 to -8%). 930 recipients developed CLAD (405 obstructive, 525 restrictive) over median (IQR) 5.9 (3.0-8.0 years). The 5-year cumulative incidence of CLAD did not differ by PGD (cumulative difference: -2.2%, 95% CI - 6.4% to 1.9%). This association was not modified by age, sex, BMI, pretransplant diagnosis, or transplant type. PGD was not associated with a difference in cumulative incidence of obstructive or restrictive CLAD (cumulative difference -1.2% and -0.8%, respectively).
CONCLUSION: PGD is associated with reduced lung function and lower likelihood of achieving GLI-predicted maximum potential lung function but not CLAD.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Dupilumab is associated with improved lung functions in patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation: a post hoc analysis of the BOREAS and NOTUS trials.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Type 2 inflammation is present in 20%-40% of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
OBJECTIVE: To perform in-depth analyses of the efficacy of dupilumab on lung function parameters in patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation.
METHODS: In BOREAS (NCT03930732) and NOTUS (NCT04456673), patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation were randomized to dupilumab 300 mg (n = 938) or placebo (n = 936) subcutaneously every 2 weeks for 52 weeks.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Dupilumab versus placebo improved pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1; least squares mean difference: 83 [95% confidence interval (CI): 53-112] mL; P < .0001), post-bronchodilator FEV1 (71 [41-101] mL; P < .0001), pre-bronchodilator forced vital capacity (FVC; 64 [26-102] mL; P = .0009), post-bronchodilator FVC (41 [3-79] mL; P = .0341), post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC (0.016 [0.010-0.022]; P < .0001), and forced expiratory flow 25%-75% of FVC (78 [45-111] mL/s; P < .0001) at week 12 and sustained to week 52. Improvements in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 were observed regardless of smoking status or the presence of co-existing emphysema; greater improvements were observed in patients with higher baseline eosinophil counts or fractional exhaled nitric oxide. Dupilumab versus placebo achieved >100 mL improvements in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at week 12 (42.2% vs 31.1%) and week 52 (36.9% vs 31.2%), with a similar proportion for post-bronchodilator FEV1 at weeks 12 and 52.
CONCLUSIONS: Dupilumab treatment resulted in early and sustained improvements across multiple spirometric lung function parameters in patients with COPD and type 2 inflammation.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Identifying High-Care-Need Phenotypes After Hip Fracture Surgery Using Nursing-Actionable Registry Variables.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery may differ substantially from one another in baseline function, cognitive status, living situation, and perioperative risk. Such differences can complicate patients' needs postoperatively.
PURPOSES: This study aimed to identify clinically-usable postoperative care-need phenotypes among older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the national registry-based UK National Hip Fracture Database to identify 63 108 older adults who underwent hip fracture surgery between 2016 and 2021. Nursing-actionable variables, including age, pre-fracture residence, pre-fracture mobility, cognitive impairment or dementia, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade, were used to identify clinically-interpretable care-need phenotypes: low-care-need, mobility-limited, and cognitive-institutional high-care-need. The primary outcome was failure to return home after hip fracture surgery, which reflects the combined effects of functional recovery, care dependency, rehabilitation need, and discharge planning.
RESULTS: Using data from the 63 108 patients included, phenotypes were categorized: low-care-need (n = 25 842; 41.0%), mobility-limited (n = 22 671; 35.9%), and cognitive-institutional high-care-need (n = 14 595; 23.1%). Failure to return home increased from 18.4% in the low-care-need phenotype to 39.5% in the mobility-limited phenotype and 73.8% in the cognitive-institutional high-care-need phenotype. The mobility-limited and cognitive-institutional high-care-need phenotypes were also associated with higher adjusted odds of prolonged length of stay of over 21 days, discharge to residential or nursing care, and 30 day mortality.
CONCLUSION: This retrospective database analysis found that identified distinct postoperative care-need phenotypes for older adults after hip fracture surgery. These phenotypes were strongly associated with failure to return home, prolonged hospitalization, institutional care, and mortality. Such risk stratification may help nursing teams and multidisciplinary hip fracture services align rehabilitation, discharge planning, and post-acute care coordination with patient-level recovery needs.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic study level III.

articles.title: Analgesic efficacy of regional and local analgesic techniques for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in adults undergoing general anesthesia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute pain after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) can impair early mobility and rehabilitation. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared regional and local analgesic techniques in adults undergoing ACLR under general anesthesia.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 18, 2026, for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed utilizing the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB2), and a Bayesian random-effects NMA was performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-one studies involving 2,470 patients were included. Only six were at low risk of bias. For oral morphine milligram equivalents (OMME) at 24 h postoperatively, femoral nerve block (FNB) [mean difference (MD) = - 30.31, 95% credible interval (CrI) - 58.02, - 6.79] and FNB with sciatic nerve block (SNB) [MD = - 40.42, 95% CrI - 80.42, - 5.79] were associated with lower estimated opioid consumption than control. FNB with SNB ranked highest for lower 24-h OMME [surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) = 87.44%]. FNB with graft donor-site infiltration was associated with lower estimated pain scores in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) than local infiltration analgesia (MD = - 2.46, 95% CrI: -4.67, - 0.21). At 24 h, adductor canal block (ACB) with graft donor-site infiltration had lower estimated pain scores than ACB (MD = - 1.50, 95% CrI: -2.43, - 0.61). At 48 h, the 95% CrIs for all pain comparisons included 0. ACB with infiltration between the popliteal artery and capsule of the posterior knee (iPACK) had a longer estimated time to first analgesic request (TFAR) than ACB (MD = 7.50, 95% CrI: 1.92, 13.01). Regarding postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), the 95% CrIs for all comparisons included 1. In sensitivity analyses excluding high-risk studies, the CrIs for key comparisons regarding OMME and TFAR widened and included 0. Some treatment nodes were missing from certain outcome networks, and the rankings for PONV changed.
CONCLUSION: Potential analgesic benefits varied across outcomes, but key estimates became less precise after high-risk studies were excluded. Functional outcomes were not systematically synthesized, and adverse event assessment was limited to PONV. These findings do not establish the overall clinical superiority of any single strategy.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Conventional approaches to mechanism in named psychological treatments for chronic pain in the era of personalized precision health care: a square peg in a round hole.
Perioperative hemostatic therapy in adult cardiac surgery: a narrative review highlighting human factors.
articles.abstract: Severe bleeding remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in cardiac surgery, and hemostatic blood components, mainly platelet concentrates and fresh frozen plasma, are essential to perioperative hemostatic management. While restrictive strategies for packed red blood cell transfusions are now well established within Patient Blood Management, inappropriate prophylactic transfusions of these hemostatic therapies continue to receive less attention.This narrative review investigates variations in hemostatic therapy among centres for adult cardiac surgery, and examines the factors that might explain these differences. A review of fourteen original studies involving nearly 220,000 patients from over 1,000 centres worldwide revealed significant variations in platelet and fresh-frozen plasma transfusion rates across centres.Differences in patient and procedural characteristics cannot entirely explain these variations. Although viscoelastic hemostatic tests have improved bedside assessment and lowered exposure in some settings, they have not eradicated significant variations in practice. The available evidence indicates that hospital culture, local organization, transfusion thresholds, and human factors all have an impact on transfusion behaviour.Optimizing the use of hemostatic therapies in adult cardiac surgery will therefore not only require better tools and protocols, but also increased focus on the organizational and non-technical factors that influence decision-making.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Perioperative and Post-Acute Care for Older Adults with Hip Fracture and Cognitive Impairment or Dementia: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Hip fracture care becomes more complex when an older adult has cognitive impairment. Pain may be expressed behaviorally, consent and goals of care may require supported decision-making, delirium can be difficult to distinguish from baseline impairment, and rehabilitation must accommodate altered learning and communication. Unlike reviews focused predominantly on individual management domains, this narrative review integrates evidence across the entire care pathway, from emergency assessment and perioperative management to inpatient care, post-acute rehabilitation, and discharge planning, with particular emphasis on how cognitive impairment affects care coordination and continuity. The most consistent priorities are timely surgery after correction of reversible instability, reliable recognition and treatment of pain and delirium, early supported activity, and access to rehabilitation adapted to the person's abilities. Cognitive impairment changes how these elements are delivered; it is not, by itself, a reason to withhold them. Decisions about discharge and longer-term recovery are better anchored in prefracture function, transfer ability, residence, caregiver capacity, and the patient's goals than in a cognitive label alone. In advanced dementia, operative and non-operative management are both active care pathways and require explicit discussion of comfort, transfers, nursing burden, survival, and previously expressed values. Direct evidence is most limited for patients with moderate or severe dementia, who are commonly excluded from trials despite being among those most vulnerable to gaps in care.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of ultrasound-guided intercostal nerve block versus transversus abdominis plane block in laparoscopic cholecystectomy: A propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical efficacy of ultrasound-guided intercostal nerve block (ICNB) and transversus abdominis plane block (TAPB) in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients undergoing elective LC who received either ultrasound-guided ICNB or TAPB between January 2023 and December 2025. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to reduce baseline imbalances. The primary outcome was the rate of rescue analgesia within 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included time to first rescue analgesia, resting and active Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores, postoperative recovery outcomes, and adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 180 patients were included after PSM, comprising 63 in the ICNB group and 117 in the TAPB group. The rescue analgesia rate was significantly lower in the ICNB group than in the TAPB group (42.9% vs. 60.7%, P = 0.022). ICNB was associated with a lower hazard of first rescue analgesia within 24 h (HR = 0.625, 95% CI 0.401-0.974; P = 0.036). The ICNB group demonstrated lower VAS scores at 2 h and 6 h postoperatively, whereas no significant differences were observed at 12 h and 24 h. Patients in the ICNB group experienced an earlier time to first ambulation (13.3 ± 3.2 h vs. 14.4 ± 3.4 h, P = 0.041) and a decreased incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) (27.0% vs. 42.7%, P = 0.037). No serious block-related complications occurred; one puncture-site hematoma was observed in the ICNB group.
CONCLUSION: Compared to the TAPB, ultrasound-guided ICNB is associated with a decreased need for rescue analgesia, a lower risk of requiring first rescue analgesia, and improved pain control in the early postoperative period for patients undergoing LC. Furthermore, ICNB is linked to earlier ambulation and a reduced incidence of PONV, without a significant increase in serious block-related complications. These findings support the use of ICNB as a potentially effective regional analgesic option for LC; however, prospective studies are required to validate these observations.

articles.title: Catch a TIGAR by the Tail: YTHDC1 Links Epitranscriptomic Regulation to Macrophage-Driven Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med

articles.title: Pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block vs. surgical articular infiltration for direct anterior total hip arthroplasty under general anaesthesia: a randomized pilot trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group (PENG) blocks for postoperative analgesia following direct anterior total hip arthroplasty under general anaesthesia remains uncertain. We conducted a prospective randomized trial to determine whether a PENG block would reduce postoperative intravenous morphine consumption compared with surgical local anaesthetic infiltration.
METHODS: Consecutive patients were randomized to receive either an ultrasound-guided PENG block after induction of anaesthesia or surgical local anaesthetic infiltration after femoral neck resection. General anaesthesia and perioperative analgesic management were standardized according to institutional practice, and all procedures were performed by a single surgeon. The primary outcome was total intravenous morphine consumption during the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. The secondary outcome measure was total oral morphine consumption from PACU discharge to postoperative day 1 (POD#1), expressed in oral morphine equivalents (OME).
RESULTS: Of the 60 recruited patients, 56 were analysed using a modified intention-to-treat analysis. Median (interquartile range) PACU morphine consumption did not differ significantly between the control and PENG groups (0 [0-6] mg vs. 0 [0-3] mg; median difference 0 mg, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2 to 4.5; P = 0.235). Total OME consumption through POD#1 was lower in the PENG group compared to the control group (0 [0-10] mg vs. 7 [3-20] mg; P = 0.040).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing direct anterior total hip arthroplasty, PENG block, when implemented as part of a multimodal analgesic pathway, did not reduce PACU intravenous morphine consumption compared with surgical local infiltration.

articles.title: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries: A 13-year retrospective review of injury characteristics, treatment, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric flexor tendon injuries are rare but potentially devastating. Due to low incidence, optimal perioperative management remains poorly defined, and evidence is scarce. This study evaluates the injury characteristics, surgical treatment, age-specific functional outcomes, and challenges in this population.
METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted on 79 pediatric patients (mean age 6.84 ± 4.27 years; 67.1% male) who underwent surgical repair for flexor tendon lacerations between 2010 and 2023. Outcomes were assessed using Total Active Motion (TAM), Strickland score, grip/pinch strength, Semmes-Weinstein monofilament, two-point discrimination, and QuickDASH questionnaire, with a mean follow-up of 59.9 ± 32.8 months.
RESULTS: Zone 2 was the most common injury site (45.6%), with glass being the predominant mechanism (67.1%). Nerve injury was present in 35.4% of cases. Overall, good/excellent results were achieved in 81.9% (TAM) and 89.0% (Strickland) of patients. The 0-5 years age group had significantly lower Strickland scores than the 6-12 years group (74.28% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.05). Zone 5 injuries demonstrated significantly better outcomes than Zone 2 and 3 (p < 0.001). The overall complication rate was low (5.1%), with a rerupture rate of 2.5%.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric flexor tendon repairs yield favorable functional outcomes with low complication rates. Age-related differences in functional outcomes should be interpreted cautiously because of developmental differences in patient cooperation and age-dependent rehabilitation strategies. Concomitant nerve injury was associated with poorer functional outcomes. The modified Kessler technique remains a reliable repair method.

articles.title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown.
METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications.
RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

articles.title: Mechanisms of behavioral activation, cognitive therapy, and mindfulness meditation for chronic pain: a test of specific vs shared mechanism models in a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: This study tested hypotheses regarding the mechanisms of 3 psychological chronic pain treatments: behavioral activation, cognitive therapy, and mindfulness meditation. The aim was to evaluate the degree to which improvement in the primary outcome (pain interference) was accounted for by preceding changes in cognitive content (pain catastrophizing), cognitive process (mindful nonjudgment), and/or behavior (activity level) during treatment (Primary Aim) and after treatment (Secondary Aim). A total of 302 adults with chronic low back pain were enrolled in a 3-arm parallel randomized clinical trial and completed twice daily ecological momentary assessments of outcome and hypothesized mechanism variables. Participants also wore an activity monitor daily during and after treatment. Slopes were calculated for 4 phases (early treatment, late treatment, early post-treatment, late post-treatment), and analyses of variance were conducted. Structural equation modeling evaluated potential cross-lagged effects. The analyses of variance results showed significant improvement in pain interference, pain catastrophizing, and nonjudgment, but not activity level, with no between treatment differences. The structural equation modeling analyses testing the potential mechanism role of pain catastrophizing and nonjudgment during treatment and after treatment mostly found nonsignificant cross-lagged effects, although changes in outcome and mechanism were significantly correlated at nearly all time periods. Taken together, the strongest support was found for a Shared Mechanisms Model to explain how 3 theoretically unique treatments exert change both during and after treatment. The findings are among the first to delineate the potential mechanisms underlying the variability in post-treatment trajectories of maintenance vs relapse after psychological chronic pain treatment.

articles.title: Oral calcium intake during labor in healthy women: a pharmacokinetic study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recent studies suggest that intravenous calcium may reduce postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony. However, intravenous lines may be unavailable in low-resource settings. We thus evaluated the time course of change in serum ionized calcium after pregnant women ingested commonly available oral calcium formulations.
METHODS: Term, laboring patients 18-45 years of age received oral calcium carbonate (1200 mg). Blood samples were obtained to measure ionized calcium before and after ingestion. Following interim analysis demonstrating minimal effect, the protocol was amended to calcium citrate (1250 mg). Enrollment was stopped at 20 of 60 planned participants for futility without a prespecified statistical futility boundary.
RESULTS: We observed minimal to no increase in serum ionized calcium in ten patients who received calcium carbonate and eight patients who received calcium citrate.
CONCLUSION: The package insert-recommended dose of two oral calcium formulations failed to meaningfully increase serum ionized calcium in laboring patients. Future studies should center on intravenous calcium until alternative oral calcium dosing or formulations successfully increase maternal ionized calcium.

articles.title: Postaxial Polydactyly Type B in Infants: A Narrative Review of Outcomes and Family-Centered Care.
articles.abstract: Postaxial polydactyly type B is a rudimentary ulnar-sided digit attached by a soft-tissue pedicle. Although treatment usually preserves hand function, families must weigh differences in timing, anesthesia, residual appearance, symptoms, and the possibility of another procedure. This narrative review examines the evidence for suture or clip ligation and surgical excision, with particular attention to caregiver experience and the limits of psychosocial outcome data. Targeted literature searches and reference-list review were updated in September 2026. Systematic reviews and observational cohorts generally associate excision with fewer composite complications and less residual prominence, while satisfaction is high after several treatment approaches. Early excision under local anesthesia offers immediate removal and direct management of the neurovascular pedicle when appropriate expertise and facilities are available. Ligation remains an option for selected narrow attachments after discussion of delayed separation and possible residual tissue or revision. Caregiver studies support discussing treatment timing, anesthesia concerns, and satisfaction with appearance; they do not establish that excision prevents childhood bullying, anxiety, or depression. A visible remnant, caregiver dissatisfaction, and child distress should therefore be assessed separately. An anatomy illustration and an author-developed treatment decision aid connect these distinctions to clinical assessment, shared decisions, and follow-up. The pathway includes observation or planned excision when immediate treatment is deferred. Better prospective studies should distinguish initial treatment from revision and measure caregiver concerns separately from the child's later experience.

articles.title: Blood Management Strategies in Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
articles.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) presents a major challenge in obstetric care because attempted placental separation may result in rapid and life-threatening hemorrhage. As PAS is often suspected before delivery, there is an opportunity to identify correctable risks and prepare for anticipated blood loss. This narrative review examines blood-management strategies throughout the antenatal, intraoperative, and postoperative periods. A targeted narrative search of PubMed and PubMed Central, supplemented by searches of journal and publisher websites, was conducted for literature available through September 2026. Antenatal management focuses on identifying and treating maternal anemia, referring patients to experienced centers, and developing a multidisciplinary delivery plan. Perioperative preparation includes coordination with the transfusion service, timely access to appropriate blood components, clear criteria for activating a major obstetric hemorrhage protocol, and defined responsibilities for each team member. Blood-product preparation should be individualized according to the severity suggested by prenatal imaging and the anticipated anatomical extent of placental invasion, ranging from suspected accreta to increta or percreta. Key intraoperative blood-conservation measures include intraoperative cell salvage and timely administration of tranexamic acid when clinically indicated, particularly during significant hemorrhage. Viscoelastic hemostatic testing, fibrinogen-directed therapy, and selected interventional radiology procedures may also contribute to individualized management. However, evidence supporting these interventions remains inconsistent and is frequently derived from observational studies, expert consensus, or broader obstetric hemorrhage populations rather than PAS-specific randomized trials. Consequently, blood-management plans should reflect the anticipated severity of PAS, the patient's clinical condition, and the expertise and resources available at the treating institution. A structured and individualized approach linking antenatal optimization, multidisciplinary preparation, timely hemorrhage control, and postoperative surveillance may support safer and more efficient care for patients with PAS.

articles.title: Bilateral Erector Spinae Plane Block With 0.375% Ropivacaine and Postoperative Analgesia After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Prospective, Randomized, Controlled Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative pain after laparoscopic cholecystectomy may delay recovery and increase opioid exposure. The erector spinae plane block has been proposed as a component of multimodal analgesia, but local prospective data remain limited.
METHODS: This prospective, randomized, controlled cohort study included 40 adults undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Of these, 20 participants received an ultrasound-guided bilateral erector spinae plane block at T9 with 0.375% ropivacaine (20 mL per side) plus multimodal analgesia, and the remaining 20 patients received multimodal analgesia without the block. The prespecified primary endpoint was resting Numeric Rating Scale pain at 12 hours. Secondary outcomes included pain at additional time points and recorded rescue tramadol use. Analyses were unadjusted and included repeated-measures models, Holm-adjusted pointwise comparisons, standardized mean differences, and Fisher exact tests.
RESULTS: At 12 hours, mean resting pain was 1.80 ± 0.70 in the block group and 3.40 ± 1.31 in the comparison group (mean difference -1.60; 95% CI -2.28 to -0.92; p<0.001; Hedges' g=-1.49). The difference did not reach the prespecified two-point threshold used for sample size planning. Recorded rescue tramadol use occurred in two (10.0%) participants in the block group versus 14 (70.0%) participants in the comparison group (risk ratio 0.143; 95% CI 0.037-0.549; absolute risk difference -0.60; p=0.00024). The group-by-time interaction was not significant for resting or movement pain. Postoperative nausea and vomiting occurred in one participant per group.
CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral erector spinae plane block was associated with lower unadjusted pain scores and a marked reduction in recorded rescue tramadol use. The most clinically salient signal was the lower frequency of recorded rescue analgesia, although the indication for every administration could not be independently verified. Because the primary pain difference remained below the prespecified two-point threshold, the findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Self-perception of ageing and postoperative functional decline in older adults undergoing colorectal cancer surgery: A prospective observational study.
Statistical power and endpoint definition in the CARDU-FAST trial.
Early Multiorgan Stress and Time-Varying Mortality After Cardiac Surgery With Postoperative Hypoxemia: A 24-Hour Landmark Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess whether a prespecified 3-domain summary of first-day oxygenation impairment, renal stress, and circulatory/metabolic stress characterizes prognostic heterogeneity after cardiac surgery with postoperative hypoxemia and whether its association with mortality changes over time.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study with a prespecified 24-hour landmark.
SETTING: Single US academic center in MIMIC-IV version 3.1.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing major cardiac surgery who received invasive ventilation, had a partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood (PaO₂)/fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO₂) ratio ≤300 mm Hg (≤40 kPa) during the first day in the intensive care unit, and survived to the landmark.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The oxygenation-renal dysfunction-circulatory stress composite (ODCS-3) was calculated as -z(PaO₂/FiO₂) + z[ln(1 + creatinine)] + z[ln(1 + lactate)] and then standardized to SD units. Cox models evaluated mortality through clinical days 28, 90, and 365. Among 6,451 patients, 114, 203, and 352 died by the respective horizons. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) per 1 SD increase in ODCS-3 were 3.10 (95% confidence interval [CI], 2.64-3.65), 2.61 (95% CI, 2.31-2.95), and 2.09 (95% CI, 1.89-2.30), respectively. Piecewise HRs were 2.69 through clinical day 28, 2.09 during days 29 to 90, and 1.58 during days 91 to 365. Optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values at the 3 timepoints were 0.837, 0.793, and 0.734; discrimination did not differ clearly from that achieved with Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA).
CONCLUSIONS: Concurrent renal and circulatory/metabolic stress marked substantial early prognostic heterogeneity within postoperative hypoxemia. ODCS-3 did not clearly outperform SOFA and should be interpreted as a focused physiologic summary rather than a replacement severity score or validated decision tool. Its association weakened over time, and external validation is required.

articles.title: Evaluation of renal resistive index in patients undergoing arthroscopic shoulder surgery with controlled hypotension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Controlled hypotension is a widely adopted anesthetic method in shoulder arthroscopy to improve visual clarity. However, hypotension-related hypoperfusion may lead to postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI). The renal resistive index (RRI) is considered an effective and reliable parameter for identifying prerenal AKI. This study aimed to evaluate perioperative changes in RRI during shoulder arthroscopy with controlled hypotension.
METHODS: Following ethics committee approval, 90 adult patients undergoing elective shoulder arthroscopy were prospectively assessed. Controlled hypotension was achieved by adjusting the intravenous remifentanil infusion (0.01-0.2 µg/kg/min). RRI was measured pre- and postoperatively in pain-free, hemodynamically and respiratory stable patients. AKI was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria.
RESULTS: Data from 65 patients were analyzed. The postoperative RRI values (mean ± SD: 0.683 ± 0.085) were significantly higher than the preoperative values (mean ± SD: 0.648 ± 0.077) (p < 0.001). The mean change in RRI (delta RRI), calculated as (postoperative RRI - preoperative RRI) / preoperative RRI, was 5.6%. Stage I AKI was observed in 3 patients (4.6%). Preoperative RRI showed a positive correlation with both age and Simple Postoperative AKI Risk (SPARK) score, and a negative correlation with baseline glomerular filtration rate. Postoperative RRI showed a positive correlation with age.
CONCLUSIONS: The observed increase in RRI suggests that controlled hypotensive anesthesia during shoulder arthroscopy may affect renal perfusion. Perioperative RRI assessment may therefore serve as a tool to evaluate renal perfusion changes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT05945706, Registration date: 07 May 2023.

articles.title: Erector spinae plane block in bariatric surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials with trial sequence analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of erector spinae plane (ESP) block has been reported to decrease opioid requirements for patients undergoing bariatric and metabolic surgeries (BMS). We aim to systematically review and examine the evidence for the use of ESP block in BMS.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and CENTRAL electronic databases were searched for all studies on ESP block in BMS from database inception through 21st July 2025. Two reviewers independently assessed and selected studies, collected data, assessed the risk of bias and quality of evidence. The primary outcome for this review is opioid consumption in 24 h post-operation. Secondary outcomes include intraoperative opioid consumption, time to first request for analgesia, and postoperative pain scores.
RESULTS: Nine randomised control trials involving 613 patients were found to be eligible. ESP block significantly reduced opioid consumption in the first 24 h after surgery, with a mean oral morphine equivalent daily dose (oMMED) reduction of 36.94 mg (95% CI -60.85 to -13.03, p = 0.009, I2 = 94%). Trial sequential analysis (TSA) suggests a potential benefit of ESP block though this interpretation is limited by marked statistical heterogeneity. Time to first request for analgesia was significantly prolonged with ESP block. Intraoperative opioid requirements, time to first request for analgesia, and postoperative reported pain scores were reduced in the ESP block group.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that the bilateral ultrasound-guided ESP block may be a practical technique to improve perioperative pain control and reduce opioid usage in patients undergoing BMS. However, these findings must be interpreted with caution due to the very low to moderate certainty of evidence and high clinical heterogeneity.

articles.title: Coagulopathy and anticoagulation management in adult ECPR patients.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a lifesaving strategy for refractory cardiac arrest, restoring systemic perfusion when conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation fails. However, ECPR profoundly disrupts haemostasis, driven by the combined effects of whole-body ischaemia-reperfusion injury, systemic inflammation, endothelial activation, platelet dysfunction, and blood contact with extracorporeal surfaces. Together, these processes create a highly dynamic and unstable thromboinflammatory milieu, marked by the simultaneous risk of thrombosis and life-threatening bleeding. Systemic anticoagulation is required to maintain circuit patency and prevent thromboembolic complications, yet optimal strategies remain uncertain. Haemostasis during ECPR is highly dynamic, shaped by the underlying aetiology of cardiac arrest, patient-specific characteristics, and circuit-related factors. This complexity underscores the limitations of fixed anticoagulation targets and the need for individualized, context-sensitive management guided by continuous clinical and laboratory assessment. Despite the increasing global adoption of ECPR, high-quality evidence to guide anticoagulation practices remains scarce. Current strategies are largely extrapolated from other extracorporeal life support populations, contributing to substantial inter-centre variability. This review synthesizes the available evidence on coagulopathy and anticoagulation in adult patients receiving ECPR and discusses emerging approaches to monitoring and anticoagulation management.

articles.title: Distinct transcriptomic signatures discriminate hyperinflammation from immune paralysis in sepsis: a single-cell RNA sequencing study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a highly heterogeneous syndrome characterized by variable immune dysregulation states, including hyperinflammation and immunosuppression. Previous immunotherapy attempts in sepsis have largely failed, likely due to a "one-size-fits-all" approach that ignores each patient's immune status. The recent ImmunoSep randomized clinical trial demonstrated that precision immunotherapy guided by the presence of either macrophage activation-like syndrome (MALS) or immune paralysis can improve early organ dysfunction in sepsis patients. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these immune endotypes remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To identify the immunological signatures that distinguish MALS and immune paralysis.
METHODS: We used single-cell RNA sequencing to profile circulating leukocytes of 6 healthy controls and 16 sepsis patients classified as MALS, immune paralysis or unclassified (when criteria for neither of these two immune endotypes were applicable). Classification was based on surrogate biomarkers ferritin and HLA-DR expression on monocytes. Thereafter, the transcriptional programs of these groups were compared.
RESULTS: Pronounced differences were detected mainly in the transcriptional signature of monocytes from these patients, with a clear distinction between MALS and immune paralysis. Unsupervised clustering analysis revealed the existence of MALS-specific monocyte clusters, as well as one sepsis-specific monocyte cluster that was linked to greater comorbidity burden and may reflect increased clinical vulnerability in sepsis. These findings were validated in two independent cohorts, in which urosepsis was characterized by heterogeneous MALS and immune paralysis monocyte signatures. Moreover, MALS-specific monocyte clusters showed overlapping transcriptional signatures with severe COVID-19.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings shed light on the heterogeneous immune landscape underlying sepsis and provide opportunities for patient stratification for future therapeutic development.

articles.title: Stony Brook University's Scholars for Medicine 8-Year B.S.-M.D. Program: a Thirteen Year Overview of the Program's Effectiveness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The number of medical students taking time off before medical school has greatly increased recently, prolonging the time needed to enter the physician workforce. Stony Brook's Scholars for Medicine B.S.-M.D. program provides a transition from college to medical school, eliminating the need for gap years and enabling direct entry into the medical profession. Given these potential advantages and the increasing duration of medical education, evaluation of the program's effectiveness is warranted.
METHODS: A longitudinal study, including 66 Stony Brook B.S.-M.D. students who entered medical school from 2009-2021, was conducted over the past 13 years and examined time from undergraduate enrollment to medical school graduation.
RESULTS: The mean time to become a physician from the beginning of college to medical school graduation for Stony Brook's B.S.-M.D. students was 8.1 years. 18 students matched into NRMP-determined competitive specialties, including dermatology, orthopedic surgery, plastic surgery, general surgery, physical medicine and rehabilitation, anesthesiology, and obstetrics and gynecology.
CONCLUSION: Stony Brook's B.S.-M.D. program allows students to enter medical school directly from college, shortening the overall time needed to become a physician, which is increasingly interrupted by gap years in the traditional application process. Although the program spans 8 years, it is still more time-efficient than taking gap years. To streamline physician training, more schools should consider adopting or expanding B.S./B.A.-M.D. programs, as they shorten the timeline to residency and permit students to match into all specialties, including competitive ones.

articles.title: Preoperative screening for cognitive dysfunction including dementia among the elderly.
articles.abstract: Background Neurocognitive disorders are common perioperative complications in older patients, leading to a higher incidence of mortality and morbidity. Pre-existing cognitive impairment is the strongest predictor. As patients who do not have documented dementia may have mild cognitive impairment, evaluating their cognitive status before surgery is important for risk stratification and for subsequent prevention and management. We aimed to assess the magnitude of cognitive impairment and dementia among the elderly and to find out any possible correlation between various sociodemographic factors and comorbid conditions. Methods In this hospital-based, observational, crosssectional study, patients 65 years or older were screened for cognitive dysfunction using the Mini-Cog and 4 'A's test during pre-anaesthetic check-ups. Information regarding sociodemographic profiles and clinical conditions was also collected. Data were analysed using standard statistical tests. Results Most study subjects were men aged 65-70. The prevalence of dementia was 40%, possible cognitive impairment was 43.43%, and delirium was 6.29%. As age increased, the prevalence of cognitive dysfunction also increased and was higher among men, and patients belonging to lower education levels and lower socio-economic status. Significant association of cognitive dysfunction was found with age, gender, socioeconomic status, level of education, past cerebrovascular accident (CVA)/transient ischaemic attack (TIA), and myocardial infarction (Ml). Conclusion There is a significant prevalence of cognitive impairment and dementia among the elderly being assessed for surgery in eastern India.

articles.title: The Effect of Perioperative Video Interventions on Postoperative Pain Control: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative pain is a major cause of suffering and is linked to serious complications, including delayed wound healing, increased cardiovascular risk, delayed rehabilitation, and chronic postsurgical pain. Modifiable psychological factors influence pain outcomes, and preliminary evidence suggests video interventions can reduce preoperative anxiety and improve patient satisfaction. We hypothesized that video interventions could improve postoperative pain control. Therefore, the aim of the current systematic review was to summarize all previous research and investigate the effects of perioperative video interventions on pain levels and/or analgesic consumption.
METHODS: The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024596389) and followed the PRISMA Guidelines. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Academic Search, and the Cochrane Central register of controlled trials from inception to October 2025 for randomized controlled trials in adult surgical patients. Trials assessing any perioperative video interventions reporting on postoperative pain intensity and/or analgesic consumption were included. Data was extracted independently by two authors, and data synthesis was qualitative due to significant heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).
RESULTS: Forty-four trials were included. Of the 42 trials assessing pain, 11 (26%) reported significantly lower pain in the intervention group. Of the 19 trials measuring analgesic consumption, eight (42%) reported significantly lower consumption in the intervention group. Only two trials demonstrated a benefit for both co-primary outcomes. Significant improvements in secondary outcomes, including anxiety, physical function, and satisfaction, were reported in 26 trials. Most trials were judged as having a high risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: The current systematic review suggests that perioperative video interventions may improve acute postoperative pain control, although effects are inconsistent across trials. Future research should focus on identifying patient and intervention characteristics that predict efficacy to guide clinical implementation.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This trustworthy systematic review presents an overview of current research findings for application of perioperative video-based treatments as part of managing postoperative pain. While this approach shows promise, more definitive evidence may be needed to justify more widespread implementation.

articles.title: Prognostic value of modified thrombelastometry for thromboembolic risk stratification in neurosurgical patients: protocol for a prospective, multicenter, observational study (TENS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Neurosurgical patients, particularly those with intracranial tumours such as glioma or meningioma, face a markedly elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), with reported rates of deep vein thrombosis between 15% and 70% depending on tumour entity and surgical extent. Current prophylactic strategies rely predominantly on pharmacological and mechanical measures and do not account for the individual complexity of coagulation dynamics. Modified thromboelastometry, employing a low-dose tissue plasminogen activator (TPA) test, enables functional assessment of both fibrinolytic capacity and prothrombotic states at the point of care. We hypothesize that preoperative and perioperative thromboelastometric parameters - in particular lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test - are associated with the occurrence of thromboembolic events in neurosurgical patients.
METHODS: TENS is a prospective, multicenter, observational prognostic factor study targeting 350 evaluable participants (up to 369 enrolled to account for attrition) across four university hospitals in Cologne, Munich (two centres), and Oldenburg. Eligible patients are adults (≥ 18 years) scheduled for neurosurgical procedures involving intracranial tumour resection or with an anticipated operative duration of ≥ 4 h. Thromboelastometric measurements (EXTEM, INTEM, FIBTEM, low-dose TPA test) are performed at three defined time points: before surgery, at the end of surgery, and on postoperative day 1. The primary objective is to assess the prognostic association between lysis time (LT) in the low-dose TPA test and objectively imaging-confirmed venous thromboembolic events occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints comprise further thromboelastometric parameters, standard coagulation laboratory values, and clinical outcomes including length of hospital stay, duration of surgery, ICU stay, and days at home at day 30.
CONCLUSIONS: Modified thromboelastometry has the potential to improve individualised risk stratification for thromboembolism in neurosurgical patients. If lysis time in the low-dose TPA test demonstrates prognostic value for thromboembolic events, this could inform the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic algorithms for high-risk surgical populations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION, DATE: Deutsches Register Klinischer Studien (DRKS), No. DRKS00034388, registered October 8, 2024. Anonymised participant-level data and the statistical analysis code will be made available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author following publication of the primary results, subject to applicable data protection regulations and the terms of the institutional data sharing agreement (see chapter The full study protocol will be publicly accessible via the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS, No. DRKS00034388).
TRIAL STATUS: The study is currently in active recruitment. Recruitment was initiated at the coordinating centre in Cologne on 19 December 2024, with additional centres opening after completion of their local approval and site-initiation processes. As of March 2026, fewer than 50% of the target sample of 350 evaluable participants had been enrolled. Recruitment is expected to be completed by March 2027.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine and transversus abdominis plane block in multimodal general anesthesia for postoperative patient-controlled analgesia after uterine surgery: a propensity-score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multimodal general anesthesia (MGA) combines hypnotic adjuvants and regional analgesia, but their individual contributions to postoperative patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of dexmedetomidine and transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block on PCA-derived analgesic outcomes after uterine surgery.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective propensity-score-matched study included adult women undergoing elective hysterectomy or myomectomy with morphine-based intravenous PCA between 2021 and 2024. Patients were matched 1:1:1 into three groups: MGA with dexmedetomidine plus TAP block, TAP block without dexmedetomidine, and conventional balanced general anesthesia alone. The primary outcome was the 48-h PCA demand/delivery ratio. Secondary outcomes included morphine consumption, pain scores, PCA-related adverse events, and prescription re-adjustment.
RESULTS: After matching, 192 patients were analyzed, with 64 patients in each group. The MGA group had the lowest 48-h demand/delivery ratio compared with the TAP-block and control groups (1.00 [1.00-1.13] vs. 1.06 [1.00-1.35] and 1.09 [1.00-1.40], respectively; p = 0.013). Both TAP-containing groups consumed less morphine than controls, whereas morphine consumption did not differ between MGA and TAP block alone. The MGA group had lower intraoperative fentanyl requirement and postoperative-day-1 dynamic pain than controls; neither differed significantly between MGA and TAP-block groups. PCA-related adverse events and re-adjustment rates were comparable among groups.
CONCLUSION: In women receiving morphine PCA after uterine surgery, TAP block was the component most consistently associated with postoperative morphine sparing, whereas dexmedetomidine-containing MGA was associated with a lower PCA demand/delivery ratio without increased adverse events.

articles.title: Sequential arterial feeder targeting with microscope-based augmented reality and multimodal navigation for brain arteriovenous malformation resection: an integrated operative workflow in 158 cases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early proximal arterial control is an established principle of brain arteriovenous malformation (bAVM) microsurgery but remains difficult to execute when feeding arteries are deep, obscured, or not apparent at the cortical surface. Herein, the authors describe the longitudinal clinical implementation of a workflow using multimodal navigation and microscope-based augmented reality (AR) to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection in bAVM resections.
METHODS: Case-specific multimodal datasets were assembled according to clinical relevance and availability from CTA, high-resolution structural MRI with thin-slice T2-weighted imaging, MRA, and 3D rotational DSA studies and were fused within standard clinical neuronavigation platforms. All angiographically identifiable arterial feeders were segmented along their surgically relevant courses, prioritized as operative targets, and incorporated into exposure and corridor planning. Targets were displayed intraoperatively using the available navigation configuration, including microscope-based AR as the technology evolved. Functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were coregistered selectively to provide cortical and tractographic context. Consecutive navigation-assisted bAVM resections performed by a single neurosurgeon from 2013 to 2025 were analyzed. Outcomes included angiographic obliteration, perioperative morbidity, mortality, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score change relative to baseline.
RESULTS: Of 192 bAVM resections performed during the study period, 158 consecutive navigation-assisted resections comprised the analytical cohort and included Spetzler-Martin (SM) grades I-V. Complete obliteration on initial angiography after microsurgery was observed in 97.5% of cases (154/158). At a median follow-up of 15 months, 93.0% of patients were functionally independent (mRS score 0-2). An increase in the mRS score relative to baseline occurred in 18.4% of patients, most commonly reflecting minor, nondisabling deficits with preserved independence. Loss of independence attributable to surgery occurred in 3.1% of patients, and the mortality rate was 1.3%.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal navigation with microscope-based AR was implemented longitudinally to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection, with selective integration of fMRI and DTI providing cortical and tractographic context for lesions near eloquent anatomy. Across SM grade I-V bAVMs, the workflow was feasible and was associated with high rates of angiographic obliteration and functional independence. By translating preoperative angioarchitecture into a planned sequence of discrete intraoperative arterial targets within their structural and functional context, the featured workflow provides a structured framework for operative planning, execution, and teaching in feeder-directed bAVM microsurgery.

articles.title: Protective Role of miR-432-5p Against Propofol-Induced Neurotoxicity Through Regulation of ITK in SH-SY5Y Cells.
articles.abstract: The widespread use of propofol in pediatric anesthesia raises significant concerns regarding its potential neurodevelopmental toxicity and long-term cognitive impairment in children. To explore the protective role of miR-432-5p against propofol-induced neurotoxicity and clarify its underlying mechanisms mediated by targeting interleukin-2-inducible T-cell kinase (ITK). An in vitro model of propofol-induced damage was constructed using the SH-SY5Y cell line. Cell survival, the percentage of apoptosis, and the secretion of pro-inflammatory factors (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) were subsequently quantified. Finally, the direct interaction between miR-432-5p and its target, ITK, was verified through dual-luciferase reporter assays. miR-432-5p was markedly downregulated following propofol exposure. In vitro, miR-432-5p overexpression improved cell viability, reduced apoptosis, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine release. ITK was validated as a direct downstream target of miR-432-5p. Furthermore, compensatory overexpression of ITK partially reversed the anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory protective phenotypes induced by miR-432-5p. The miR-432-5p/ITK regulatory axis significantly mitigates propofol-induced cellular injury by restraining apoptosis and neuroinflammation. Maintaining miR-432-5p abundance provides a promising theoretical basis and therapeutic target for preventing anesthesia-related cognitive impairment.

articles.title: The Social Gradient of Pain in Europe: Income-Related Inequities and the Modifying Role of Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bodily pain is a frequent, disabling, and socially patterned population health burden. Although socioeconomic inequalities in pain have been described in Europe, it remains unclear whether this gradient changes in the presence of highly prevalent musculoskeletal conditions such as osteoarthritis.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study using anonymized EHIS Wave 3 microdata from 2018 to 2020. The final sample included 278,250 adults from 30 European countries. Bodily pain in the past 4 weeks was analysed as a binary outcome. Household income quintile was the main exposure and self-reported osteoarthritis the effect modifier. Adjusted prevalence ratios were estimated using robust Poisson regression with an income-by-osteoarthritis interaction. Adjusted probabilities, the Relative Index of Inequality, the Slope Index of Inequality, and between-country heterogeneity were also estimated.
RESULTS: The weighted prevalence of pain was 55.04%. The income-by-osteoarthritis interaction was significant, χ2(4) = 135.00; p < 0.001. Among adults without osteoarthritis, higher income was associated with lower pain prevalence (Q5 vs. Q1: aPR = 0.909; 95% CI: 0.893-0.925), whereas osteoarthritis was associated with substantially higher pain prevalence (aPR = 1.392; 95% CI: 1.370-1.413). Without osteoarthritis, the RII was 1.125 and the SII was 4.75 percentage points; with osteoarthritis, the RII was 0.964 and the SII was -2.21 percentage points. Between-country heterogeneity was significant, χ2(29) = 348.99; p < 0.001.
CONCLUSIONS: Bodily pain affects more than half of European adults and follows an income-related pattern. Osteoarthritis modifies this inequality: without osteoarthritis, pain follows a classic socioeconomic gradient, whereas with osteoarthritis, pain remains highly prevalent across income groups and the gradient is attenuated or slightly reversed.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study demonstrates that income-related inequalities in recent bodily pain vary according to self-reported osteoarthritis status across 30 European countries. Its main contribution is to show that a high prevalence of pain in people reporting osteoarthritis may attenuate or obscure conventional socioeconomic gradients when pain is measured as a binary outcome. These findings highlight the limitations of relying exclusively on pain presence to characterize socioeconomic inequalities and support further investigation of pain severity and functional consequences.

articles.title: Intraoperative hypotension in older adults with hip fracture: a comparative analysis of different definitions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with adverse outcomes, but its definition varies widely and most definitions are derived from younger or mixed-age populations. Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery are particularly susceptible due to reduced physiological reserve. This study compared absolute, relative, and duration-based definitions of IOH and evaluated their associations with postoperative adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included all patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent hip fracture surgery at Maastricht University Medical Centre+ between January 2021 and December 2022. IOH was defined using absolute thresholds (MAP < 65 mmHg, SBP < 100 mmHg), relative reductions (≥ 20%), post-induction decreases, and duration below thresholds. Outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI, KDIGO criteria), and 30 day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, ASA classification, medication use, and nursing home residency.
RESULTS: A total of 473 patients were included (mean age 80.9 years, 69.8% female). Postoperative AKI occurred in 9.9% and 30 day mortality in 5.5%. Absolute and relative IOH thresholds were not significantly associated with outcomes. In contrast, longer IOH duration (SBP < 100 mmHg) was associated with 30 day mortality (OR 1.09 per minute, 95%CI 1.02-1.16). After adjustment, higher ASA classification remained associated with AKI, while IOH duration remained significantly associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, the duration of IOH, rather than static thresholds, appeared more strongly associated with adverse outcomes, particularly 30 day mortality. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of hypotension duration and support further prospective research to establish geriatric-specific IOH definitions and optimal perioperative blood pressure management strategies.
