articles.title: Accuracy and clinical outcomes of robot-assisted deep brain stimulation lead placement using a floor-mounted robotic navigation system: a prospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical data to assess the accuracy and safety of a new robot system used for deep brain stimulation (DBS) lead placement.
METHODS: A prospective, multicenter, single-arm study included 60 patients indicated for DBS. Patients aged 18-85 years with Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, or dystonia were enrolled. The primary outcome was electrode accuracy at the tip, 40 mm from the tip, and the entry point compared with the planned trajectory. Secondary outcomes included operative time (OT), length of stay (LOS), and perioperative complications through discharge.
RESULTS: The cohort (mean age 67.1 ± 9.9 years) primarily consisted of patients with Parkinson's disease (n = 46). The mean OT was 159.0 ± 26.7 minutes, and the mean LOS was 1.6 ± 1.5 days. The complication rate and return to the operating room rate were both 0%. The mean tip error was 0.8 ± 0.5 mm, error at 40 mm from the tip was 0.4 ± 0.5 mm, and entry point error was 1.0 ± 0.8 mm.
CONCLUSIONS: DBS electrode implantation using the new robot-assisted system demonstrated high plan-to-place accuracy comparable or superior to historical frame-based and robotic platforms. The safety profile and operative efficiency, reflected by very low complication rates and similar OT and LOS to published literature, support the system as a viable alternative to standard frame-based stereotaxy.

articles.title: Effects of Permissive Hypercapnia Versus Normocapnia on Cerebral Oxygenation and Postoperative Outcomes in Adult Surgical Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence suggests that intraoperative cerebral hypoxia is the main contributor of postoperative neurological complications, particularly postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) and postoperative delirium (POD) in surgical patients. Permissive hypercapnia may improve cerebral oxygenation by increasing cerebral blood flow, but its perioperative benefits remain uncertain.
RESEARCH QUESTION: In adult surgical patients, is permissive hypercapnia associated with improved cerebral oxygenation and perioperative outcomes compared with normocapnia?
METHOD: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to April 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies of adult surgical patients receiving permissive hypercapnia. Primary outcome included was intraoperative regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2). Secondary outcomes were POCD, POD, all-cause mortality, respiratory parameters, arterial blood gas variables, and hemodynamic outcomes.
RESULTS: Seven studies comprising 824 patients were included. Permissive hypercapnia significantly improved intraoperative rSO2 (MD = 6.65%; 95% Cl: [4.93, 8.37]; p < 0.00001), PaCO2 (MD = 10.21 mmHg (95% CI: [8.81, 11.60]; p < 0.00001), and end-tidal CO2 (MD = 10.83 mmHg; 95% CI [7.91, 13.76]; p < 0.00001), and significantly reduced dead space fraction (MD = -6.38%; 95% CI: [-9.26, -3.50], p < 0.00001), and arterial pH (MD = -0.08; 95% CI: [-0.09, -0.07]; p < 0.00001). Hypercapnia had no significant effect on PaO2, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate. Qualitative analysis suggested reduced incidence of POCD with no significant effect on POD.
CONCLUSION: Permissive hypercapnia improves intraoperative cerebral oxygenation while maintaining hemodynamic stability. However, the available evidence for POCD and POD is limited and heterogeneous. Larger RCTs and observational studies are needed to confirm its effects on clinical outcomes before routine implementation.

articles.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events.
RESULTS: For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.

articles.title: Effect of Adding Esketamine to Patient-Controlled Intravenous Analgesia on Rebound Pain After Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rebound pain after peripheral nerve block (PNB) may diminish the analgesic benefits of regional anesthesia. Whether esketamine administered via postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) can prevent rebound pain remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of esketamine-containing PCIA on rebound pain after interscalene brachial plexus block in patients undergoing shoulder arthroscopic surgery.
METHODS: 132 patients scheduled for arthroscopic shoulder surgery under general anesthesia combined with interscalene brachial plexus block were randomized 1:1 to receive postoperative PCIA with esketamine (1.25 mg/kg) plus sufentanil (100 μg) and flurbiprofen axetil (100 mg) (ES group, n=66) or sufentanil plus flurbiprofen axetil alone (Control group, n=66). The primary outcome was rebound pain, defined as an increase from well-controlled pain (NRS ≤ 3) to severe pain (NRS ≥ 7), typically after resolution of the nerve block. Secondary outcomes included time to rebound pain, modified pain score, rebound pain duration, analgesic consumption, numerical rating scale (NRS) at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h postoperatively, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) sleep quality, and adverse events.
RESULTS: The incidence of rebound pain did not differ significantly between groups (25.8% vs 39.4%; OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.39 to 1.09; P=0.095). Among patients who developed rebound pain, the ES group had a lower modified rebound pain score and shorter pain duration. For other secondary outcomes, patients receiving esketamine had lower NRS pain scores at 12, 24, and 48 h, fewer PCIA demands, less rescue analgesic use, and higher QoR-15 and RCSQ scores (all P<0.05). The incidence of the assessed adverse events did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: Adding esketamine to postoperative PCIA did not demonstrate a reduction in rebound pain incidence after interscalene brachial plexus block. Exploratory subgroup findings suggested lower rebound pain intensity and duration, while improvements in postoperative analgesia, sleep, and recovery had uncertain clinical relevance. Further multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate different dosing strategies and routes of administration.

articles.title: Esketamine as a Perineural Adjuvant to Ropivacaine for Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) Block in Elderly Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hip fractures are increasing with global aging. We evaluated esketamine as a perineural ropivacaine adjuvant for PENG block on early recovery quality and analgesia in elderly hip fracture surgery patients.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study (July 2024-May 2025), 252 elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery under general anesthesia were included. Patients were allocated to control or esketamine groups based on adjuvant use. Propensity score matching yielded 86 pairs. The primary outcome was QoR-15 scores at multiple postoperative time points; secondary outcomes included sensory block duration, sleep quality, pain scores, and adverse events.
RESULTS: At 24 and 48 hours, QoR-15 scores were higher with esketamine (median difference, 9 [95% CI, 7-11] and 4 [95% CI, 2-6]). Sensory block was prolonged (16.51 ± 1.30 vs 10.91 ± 1.26 hours; P <0.001). On day 1, sleep quality and VAS pain scores improved (both P <0.001), but neither difference exceeded the population-specific MCID. Time to first ambulation was shorter, and intraoperative propofol and remifentanil use was lower (both P <0.001). Frailty, age, anxiety, and higher aCCI predicted unfavorable recovery trajectories.
CONCLUSION: Among elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, esketamine added to ropivacaine for PENG block improved 24-hour recovery quality (QoR-15, exceeding MCID; 48-hour scores higher but below MCID), prolonged sensory block, shortened time to first ambulation, and reduced intraoperative anesthetic and opioid use. Sleep and analgesia improved only at 24 hours but did not exceed population-specific MCIDs. No difference in adverse events was detected within sample size constraints. In an exploratory latent trajectory analysis of the control group, frailty, age, anxiety, and aCCI predicted poor recovery.

articles.title: Comparison of intraoperative hemodynamic changes and recovery outcomes between non-menopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing total abdominal hysterectomy under general anesthesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopausal status may influence autonomic and hemodynamic responses during surgery because of hormonal changes affecting vascular tone and thermoregulation. However, evidence comparing perioperative physiological responses and post-anesthesia care unit outcomes between non-menopausal and postmenopausal women undergoing total abdominal hysterectomy remains limited. This study compared perioperative hemodynamic changes and early postoperative recovery between these two populations.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 48 women (25 non-menopausal and 23 postmenopausal) undergoing elective total abdominal hysterectomy under standardized general anesthesia were enrolled. Intraoperative and recovery physiologic parameters, postoperative shivering, pain, nausea and vomiting, agitation, and consciousness were assessed and compared between groups using appropriate statistical analyses.
RESULTS: Non-menopausal women demonstrated significantly higher postoperative HR, higher incidence of postoperative shivering, and lower body temperature than postmenopausal women (both P < 0.05). In contrast, MAP was significantly higher in postmenopausal patients throughout the perioperative period (P = 0.001), although no significant time-by-group interaction was observed. HR and temperature showed a significant interaction between time and menopausal status (P = 0.001). No significant between-group differences were found in postoperative pain, nausea and vomiting, agitation, oxygen saturation, level of consciousness, or recovery time (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Menopausal status was associated with differences in postoperative heart rate and thermoregulatory responses during recovery after total abdominal hysterectomy under general anesthesia, while overall early recovery outcomes remained comparable between groups.

articles.title: Median effective infusion rate (ED50) of continuous cisatracurium for preserving interpretable TceMEP signals during intraspinal tumor resection: a prospective up-and-down sequential allocation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM), particularly transcranial electrical stimulation motor evoked potentials (TceMEP), plays a crucial role in preserving motor function during intraspinal tumor resection. However, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) may attenuate TceMEP signals and complicate reliable monitoring. Partial neuromuscular blockade (pNMB) through continuous NMBA infusion may help balance interpretable TceMEP monitoring with acceptable surgical conditions.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the interpretability of TceMEP signals during continuous cisatracurium infusion and thereby estimate the median effective infusion rate (ED50) associated with preservation of interpretable TceMEP signals during intraspinal tumor resection.
METHODS: Twenty-seven patients undergoing elective intraspinal tumor resection with TceMEP monitoring were enrolled in this prospective, single-center, open-label, sequential dose-finding study using Dixon's up-and-down method. After a standard intubation dose of cisatracurium, continuous infusion was started at 1.0 µg/(kg·min). TceMEP signal interpretability was used as the binary response variable for sequential allocation. A neurophysiologist blinded to the infusion rate classified the signals as interpretable or uninterpretable; the anesthesiology team was not blinded because dose adjustment was required by the sequential design. The infusion rate for each subsequent patient was increased or decreased by a factor of 1.2 according to the response in the preceding patient. ED50 and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were estimated using Dixon's method.
RESULTS: The estimated ED50 of continuous cisatracurium infusion associated with preservation of interpretable TceMEP signals was 1.65 µg/(kg·min) (95% CI, 1.52-1.79 µg/(kg·min)). No clinically significant patient movement or serious infusion-related adverse events were observed during the study.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing intraspinal tumor resection with TceMEP monitoring, the median effective infusion rate of continuous cisatracurium associated with preservation of interpretable TceMEP signals was 1.65 µg/(kg·min). This value should be interpreted as an ED50 estimate rather than a recommended maximum acceptable infusion rate.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2200057610. Registered on March 15, 2022, before enrollment of the first participant.

articles.title: Evaluation of chatbot and specialist knowledge on pediatric sedation and general anesthesia: a comparative analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare has increased rapidly, with large language model-based chatbots emerging as potential tools for education and clinical support. However, their performance in complex medical domains such as sedation and general anesthesia remains underexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of AI-supported chatbot models (ChatGPT 4.0 Mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Claude 3 Sonnet) in comparison to human experts (Anesthesiologists, Pediatric Dentists, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) within the context of sedation and general anesthesia.
METHODS: This descriptive and comparative cross-sectional study utilized a 26-item true/false questionnaire based on ASA, AAP, ADA, and AAPD guidelines. The questionnaire was administered to three chatbots and 72 human participants (24 per specialty). For chatbot evaluation, a zero-shot prompting technique with a uniform command ("Is this statement true or false?") was applied in separate sessions after clearing the cache to ensure standardization. Responses were coded as correct/incorrect by two independent pediatric dentists. Human participants completed the same questionnaire via Google Forms. Descriptive statistics were calculated. Normality of data was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Non-parametric data were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Categorical variables were analyzed using the Pearson Chi-square test. Statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS v27.
RESULTS: Significant differences were found among all groups ($p < 0.001$). In terms of text-based guideline retrieval, Claude 3 Sonnet (92.8%) and Gemini 1.5 Pro (91.7%) demonstrated high factual accuracy, while anesthesiologists achieved the highest performance among human clinicians (87.0%). While the chatbot models showed high proficiency in data retrieval for "General Information" and "Postoperative Monitoring," anesthesiologists significantly outperformed the AI models in "Patient Evaluation and Preparation" (91.7%), highlighting a critical gap in AI's clinical reasoning compared to human expertise. Notable knowledge gaps were identified among oral surgeons regarding pharmacological reversal agents.
CONCLUSIONS: Claude and Gemini chatbots exhibit high factual accuracy in retrieving guideline-based pediatric sedation theory, suggesting potential exclusively as supplementary informational resources. However, anesthesiologists' superior performance in pre-operative assessment underscores the irreplaceable role of clinical judgment. AI integration should therefore follow a synergistic model, positioning language models strictly as adjunct tools under mandatory human oversight.

articles.title: Association between epidural analgesia in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural and maternal and neonatal outcomes: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of epidural analgesia use in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural on maternal and neonatal outcomes remains unclear.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted to assess the impact of epidural analgesia use in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural on maternal and neonatal outcomes between July 1, 2016 and December 31, 2023. Demographic information, as well as gestational and delivery characteristics, were obtained from the hospital's electronic health record system. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were employed to assess the association between epidural analgesia use among multiparous women with a prior labor epidural exposure and maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 1827 women were included for analysis. The total duration of labor and the duration of first-second stage of labor were significantly longer in labor epidural analgesia group than in the non-labor epidural analgesia group (342.3 ± 140.9 min vs. 273.9 ± 114.6 min, p < 0.001; 336.2 ± 140.9 min vs. 267.9 ± 114.4 min, p < 0.001, respectively). Neither neonatal asphyxia nor NICU admission occurred in either group. Labor epidural analgesia was independently associated with prolonged the total duration of labor (β 68.01, 95% CI 55.35-80.67, p < 0.001) and the duration of first-second stage of labor (β 67.92, 95% CI 55.26-80.57, p < 0.001). Additionally, labor epidural analgesia was associated with a significantly increased length of stay (β 0.31, 95% CI 0.19-0.43, p < 0.001). Labor epidural analgesia did not significantly increase the risk of assisted delivery (aOR 0.4, 95% CI 0.07-2.28, p = 0.3), postpartum hemorrhage (aOR 0.98, 95% CI 0.52-1.84, p = 0.954) and postpartum complications (aOR 2.63, 95% CI 0.75-9.22, p = 0.131).
CONCLUSION: Epidural analgesia use in the second delivery among women with a prior epidural was associated with increased length of labor and extended hospital length of stay. However, it did not increase the rates of assisted delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, or postpartum complications.

articles.title: NOSES-facilitated transoral en-bloc excision of tongue squamous cell carcinoma via an adapted face-lift method: an initial technical case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is one of the most common malignancies of the oral cavity, and cervical lymph node status is a major determinant of prognosis. Conventional selective neck dissection (SND) requires a transcervical incision that may result in visible cervical scarring and reduced patient satisfaction. Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES) offers a minimally invasive alternative by enabling transoral specimen retrieval while preserving specimen integrity and avoiding an additional cervical incision. This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and preliminary clinical outcomes of NOSES-facilitated transoral en-bloc specimen extraction combined with a modified facelift incision and endoscopic selective neck dissection in patients with clinically node-negative TSCC.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center case series included seven patients with clinically cT1-3N0 TSCC who underwent hemiglossectomy with in-continuity endoscopic selective neck dissection through a modified facelift incision. Transoral en-bloc specimen extraction was performed using the NOSES technique, and indocyanine green (ICG) near-infrared fluorescence imaging was used intraoperatively for lymphatic mapping and assessment of free flap perfusion. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, cosmetic outcomes, and short-term oncologic outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: All procedures were completed successfully without conversion to a conventional transcervical approach or major intraoperative complications. A mean of 15-16 cervical lymph nodes was harvested per patient, and no pathological cervical lymph node metastases were identified. One patient developed partial free flap necrosis, which resolved following appropriate management. During a follow-up period of 23-36 months (replace with the exact mean or median if available), no local recurrence or cervical lymph node metastasis was observed. All patients achieved favorable cosmetic outcomes, with low postoperative neck scar scores.
CONCLUSIONS: This preliminary case series demonstrates that NOSES-facilitated transoral en-bloc specimen extraction combined with a modified facelift incision is technically feasible in carefully selected patients with clinically node-negative TSCC. The technique achieved acceptable short-term perioperative, cosmetic, and preliminary oncologic outcomes. However, larger prospective comparative studies with longer follow-up are required to confirm its long-term safety, reproducibility, and oncologic effectiveness.

articles.title: Accelerating tracheostomy decannulation with intermittent oro-esophageal feeding in neurogenic dysphagia: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurogenic dysphagia frequently constitutes a major barrier to decannulation for tracheostomized patients. Conventional nasogastric tube (NGT) feeding may promote disuse atrophy of swallowing musculature and persistent aspiration risk. Intermittent oro-esophageal tube (IOE) feeding, a physiologically oriented modality mimicking natural swallowing, may accelerate decannulation, yet high-quality evidence is lacking.
METHODS: In this multicenter randomized controlled trial conducted at three tertiary academic centers in China, tracheostomized adults with neurogenic dysphagia were randomly assigned 1:1 to IOE or NGT. All participants received standardized pharmacological treatment, pulmonary rehabilitation, and structured swallowing training, and entered an institutional decannulation protocol with predefined readiness criteria. The primary outcome was time from protocol entry to actual decannulation. Secondary outcomes included the 30-day successful decannulation rate, nutritional indices, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life. Outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to allocation. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
RESULTS: A total of 140 patients were randomized to IOE (n = 70) or NGT (n = 70). Time to decannulation was shorter with IOE (22.16 ± 1.86 vs. 26.33 ± 1.30 days; between-group difference, 4.17 days; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.90-6.44; p < 0.001; log-rank p = 0.005). The 30-day successful decannulation rate was higher with IOE (65.71% vs. 47.14%; absolute difference, 18.57% points; 95% CI, 2.43-34.71; p = 0.028). At 1 month, the IOE group demonstrated greater improvements in body mass index, serum albumin, serum prealbumin, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life (all p < 0.001). Pharyngeal discomfort was less frequent with IOE (14.06% vs. 34.21%; p = 0.006); no Grade Ⅲ or higher adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Intermittent oro-esophageal tube feeding shortens time to decannulation and improves nutritional, swallowing, and quality-of-life outcomes compared with nasogastric tube feeding in tracheostomized patients with neurogenic dysphagia.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06791590, registration date January 19, 2025.

articles.title: Understanding cerebral autoregulation and cerebrovascular reactivity: mechanistic perspectives and clinical insights from TBI.
articles.abstract: Cerebrovascular reactivity and cerebral blood flow autoregulation are critical determinants of brain homeostasis but are often conflated in clinical practice. Although these constructs are closely related and arise from vascular responses to vasoactive stimuli, they reflect distinct physiological responses and measurement approaches: autoregulation is assessed through changes in cerebral blood flow, and pressure reactivity through changes in cerebral blood volume. A fundamental clinical challenge is that the full autoregulatory curve is rarely observable in an individual patient at a single point in time; consequently, isolated measurements from classical assessments or continuous indices such as the pressure reactivity index (PRx), mean flow index (Mx), and arterial mean flow index (Mxa) are each associated with different components of cerebrovascular physiology, providing only partial views of cerebrovascular function and frequently yielding apparently conflicting results. This Review addresses a central clinical question: can multimodal neuromonitoring help determine where a patient is operating on the autoregulatory curve? We synthesise current understanding of the physiological relationships among cerebral perfusion pressure, cerebral blood flow, and cerebral blood volume, and examine the mechanisms underlying divergent autoregulatory index behaviour. By integrating mechanistic physiological schematics and representative clinical cases, we propose an objective educational framework that links classical cerebrovascular physiology with contemporary bedside monitoring. Within this framework, six conceptual physiological zones are delineated. These zones demonstrate how variations in vascular tone, intracranial compliance, and critical closing pressure shape autoregulatory responses generate differing patterns in PRx, Mx, and Mxa. Fully defining a patient's complex cerebrovascular state requires looking beyond any single parameter. Together, PRx, Mx, and Mxa provide complementary information, where discordant findings may represent distinct physiological mechanisms rather than measurement error. Interpreting these indices together within a mechanistic framework may improve identification of a patient's position along the autoregulatory curve, support more consistent bedside interpretation, and ultimately facilitate personalised cerebral perfusion pressure management.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes and appendiceal malignancy in elderly patients with acute appendicitis: a comparative retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Acute appendicitis (AA) is increasingly diagnosed in elderly patients as life expectancy rises. Because elderly patients often present atypically and are prone to complications, we compared perioperative outcomes between patients younger than 65 and those aged 65 years and older.
METHODS: We included 488 patients who underwent appendectomy between January 2023 and January 2025, divided into Group 1 (18-64 years, n = 445) and Group 2 (≥ 65 years, n = 43). Demographics, comorbidities, symptoms, surgical characteristics, postoperative outcomes, and histopathology were compared. A multivariable logistic regression assessed whether age is an independent predictor of complications. Significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Laparoscopic appendectomy (325 patients, 66.6%) was associated with shorter operative times, fewer complications, and shorter stays (all p < 0.05). Elderly patients more often presented with diffuse abdominal pain (25.6% vs. 8.1%, p < 0.001) and had higher complication rates (65.1% vs. 21.6%, p < 0.001), longer stays (p < 0.001), and higher readmission (18.6% vs. 2.2%, p < 0.001). Appendiceal malignancy was more frequent in the elderly (9.3% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.005). On multivariable analysis, advanced age was the strongest independent predictor of complications (adjusted OR 6.40; 95% CI 3.14-13.04; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients with AA frequently present atypically, which may delay surgery and lead to more advanced disease. Advanced age was independently associated with higher perioperative morbidity. Given the significantly higher malignancy rate in the elderly (9.3% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.005), non-operative management may risk leaving life-threatening neoplasms undetected. However, given the small number of neoplasm cases (n = 4), these inferences are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Comparison of the anaesthetic efficacy and safety of different doses of esketamine combined with propofol in hysteroscopic surgery: a randomised, double-blind controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hysteroscopy is increasingly performed under day-surgery total intravenous anaesthesia, but propofol alone provides insufficient analgesia and the routine adjunct of opioids is associated with respiratory depression and emetic complications. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, offers analgesia together with sympathomimetic support and represents a promising opioid-sparing alternative; however, its optimal dose for combination with propofol in this setting has not been firmly established.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomised, double-blind, controlled trial, 160 women aged 18-60 years (ASA I-II) scheduled for elective hysteroscopy were assigned to four groups using computer-generated random numbers: K1 (esketamine 0.15 mg/kg), K2 (esketamine 0.3 mg/kg), K3 (esketamine 0.5 mg/kg) or S (sufentanil 0.1 µg/kg). All patients received an induction dose of propofol 1.5 mg/kg followed by maintenance infusion of 4-6 mg·kg⁻¹·h⁻¹. The primary outcomes were postoperative pain (Numeric Rating Scale, NRS) and total intra-operative propofol consumption; secondary outcomes were perioperative haemodynamics, recovery time and adverse events. After exclusion of three patients with major protocol deviation, 157 patients were analysed (K1 = 40, K2 = 38, K3 = 40, S = 39).
RESULTS: Demographics, surgical and anaesthesia times were comparable between groups. NRS scores at 10 and 30 min post-recovery were significantly lower in groups K2, K3 and S than in group K1 (p < 0.001). Mean arterial pressure at the start of surgery (T2, immediately after the start of surgery) and at the end of surgery (T3) was significantly higher in K1 than in the other three groups (p < 0.001). Total propofol consumption did not differ between groups (p = 0.95). The incidence of intra-operative hypertension was significantly greater in K1 (22.5%) than in K2 (0%), K3 (5.0%) and S (5.1%) (p = 0.002), and the incidence of SpO₂ < 90% was significantly greater in S (20.5%) than in K1 (0%), K2 (5.3%) and K3 (5.0%) (p = 0.004). The incidence of emergence agitation differed among groups, with the highest incidence observed in K3 (10.0%) (p = 0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: Among the regimens tested, esketamine 0.3 mg/kg combined with propofol 1.5 mg/kg was associated with a favourable balance of analgesia, haemodynamic stability and safety. The 0.15 mg/kg dose was associated with higher postoperative pain scores and a higher incidence of intra-operative hypertension, while 0.5 mg/kg was associated with a higher incidence of agitation and a longer recovery time without additional analgesic benefit at 30 min. All three esketamine doses were associated with a lower incidence of hypoxaemia than the sufentanil regimen.
CLINICAL REGISTER NUMBER: The trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092022) with the retrospective registration date 2024/11/07.

articles.title: Comparison of bedside clinical pupillary assessment with automated pupillometry in sedated ICU patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pupillary assessment is central in neurocritical care and although inherently subjective, bedside penlight examination remains standard practice. While automated pupillometry provides objective, standardized measurements, the reliability of manual assessment across professional categories remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: Prospective observational study in a surgical and trauma intensive care unit (Reims, Feb-Dec 2025). Thirty sedated or comatose adults underwent repeated pupillary assessments by nurses, residents, and senior physicians, which were compared with automated pupillometry as the reference standard, yielding 1,692 paired bilateral measurements from 30 patients. Primary outcome was agreement for anisocoria detection (≥ 1 mm) and secondary outcomes were pupil size and reactivity, measured using Brennan-Prediger adjusted kappa and McNemar test.
RESULTS: Agreement for anisocoria was substantial: nurses κ = 0.64 (95% CI 0.57-0.72), residents κ = 0.74 (0.68-0.81), physicians κ = 0.71 (0.64-0.78 ,p < 0.0001). False-positive rates were high (82-86%), while true anisocoria was detected in 55-73% of cases. For pupil size, agreement was substantial: nurses κ = 0.65 (0.60-0.70), residents κ = 0.64 (0.59-0.65), physicians κ = 0.66 (0.60-0.71), but mydriasis was largely missed (6-11% detection; p < 0.0001). Reactivity showed the weakest agreement: nurses κ = 0.40 (0.34-0.47), residents κ = 0.32 (0.26-0.39), physicians κ = 0.41 (0.34-0.47), with systemic underestimation in nurses (p ≤ 0.0001) and a bidirectional error pattern for residents (p = 0.81).
CONCLUSION: In sedated ICU patients, bedside pupillary assessment showed substantial but systematically biased agreement with automated pupillometry, particularly for anisocoria, mydriasis, and pupillary reactivity. These findings highlight the limitations of subjective bedside assessment and support automated pupillometry as an objective complement to routine clinical examination.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06733207, registered 10 December 2024 - Retrospectively registered, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06733207.

articles.title: Parental involvement for pediatric perioperative anxiety: A systematic review and implementation framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative anxiety is common in children and may contribute to difficult separation, poor cooperation during induction of anesthesia, postoperative pain, emergence delirium, maladaptive behavioral changes, and distress among parents. Parental presence during induction of anesthesia has traditionally been evaluated as a discrete anesthesia intervention. However, contemporary pediatric practice increasingly conceptualizes parental involvement as part of family-centered perioperative care, where the relevant question is not simply whether parents are present, but how parental presence is selected, structured, prepared, and integrated into clinical pathways.
AIM: To synthesize randomized evidence on parental presence and related parental-involvement strategies for reducing pediatric perioperative anxiety, and to identify clinical and implementation conditions under which parental involvement appears most likely to benefit children, families, and perioperative teams.
METHODS: We performed a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of randomized and prospective comparative studies. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 1, 2026, with inclusion limited to studies published from 2000 onward. Eligible studies enrolled children undergoing elective procedures under general anesthesia; the included trials ultimately represented children aged 18 months to 12 years. Interventions included physical or virtual parental presence, parental accompaniment, active or coached parental participation, or family-centered preparation in which parents had a defined role. The primary outcome was child anxiety or behavioral distress during separation, transfer to the operating room, mask introduction, or induction. Secondary outcomes included parental anxiety, induction cooperation, emergence delirium, postoperative behavior, pain, satisfaction, sedative requirements, and implementation aspects. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2 framework. Because the studies differed in intervention structure, comparator, timing of assessment, and anxiety scale, we used narrative synthesis rather than meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Twelve randomized or prospective comparative trials involving 1104 child-parent dyads were included. The evidence was dominated by parental presence during induction of anesthesia; broader parental-involvement models were represented by fewer active, coached, multimodal, or virtual interventions. Unstructured parental presence alone produced inconsistent effects on child anxiety and was generally less reliable than sedative premedication. Active participation, coaching, family-centered preparation, selected pharmacological combination, and virtual parental presence showed more favorable signals, but certainty was low because these data came from few heterogeneous trials. Calm and prepared parents may support child coping, whereas high parental anxiety may transmit distress or increase staff workload. Implementation issues identified from the evidence and related clinical literature included parent selection, emotional preparation, role assignment, infection-control constraints, workflow, and safety stop criteria.
CONCLUSION: Parental involvement should be viewed as a potentially useful, context-dependent adjunct rather than a universal substitute for pharmacological anxiolysis. The trial evidence mainly supports a careful approach to structured parental presence during induction in selected elective cases; it does not demonstrate comprehensive family-centered perioperative protocols as proven interventions. Institutions that use parental presence may consider structured, locally adapted processes for selecting and preparing parents, defining their role, protecting operating-room safety, and combining parental involvement with behavioral or pharmacological strategies when indicated.

articles.title: An Evaluation of ICU Follow-Up Clinic Attendance and Subsequent Healthcare Resource Utilization in Wales, United Kingdom: A Retrospective, Population-Level Data-Linkage Study.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Postintensive care syndrome encapsulates the long-term physical, psychologic, and cognitive impairments often seen among ICU survivors. Post-ICU follow-up clinics may support recovery and reduce avoidable healthcare utilization, but population-level evidence remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To identify patient characteristics associated with follow-up clinic attendance and evaluate differences in healthcare resource utilization (HRU) across three groups: invited and attended, invited but did not attend, and not invited.
DESIGN SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: A retrospective cohort study using anonymised, linked administrative data from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage Databank in Wales, United Kingdom. Adults (≥ 18 yr) with ICU admissions between 2016 and 2023 who survived to discharge were included. Follow-up clinic data were obtained from three regional health boards (healthcare organizations responsible for delivering National Health Services in Wales) with follow-up clinic availability.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: HRU outcomes included ICU readmissions, emergency department attendances, hospital admissions (elective and emergency), hospital bed days, outpatient appointments, and general practitioner (GP) events. Multivariable models assessed associations between clinic attendance and HRU.
RESULTS: Of 6491 eligible patients, 761 attended a follow-up clinic, 1473 were invited but did not attend, and 4257 were not invited. Among invited patients, attendance was associated with increasing age, comorbidity, deprivation, and ICU length of stay. Compared with attendees, nonattendees and those not invited had higher adjusted odds of ICU readmission (odds ratio [OR] = 2.81 and 2.22, respectively), elective admissions, and hospital bed days. No significant differences were observed for emergency admissions or GP events. Attendees were more likely to have 4 or more (non-follow-up clinic) outpatient appointments.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Clinic attendance was associated with differences in several HRU domains. Variability in access and engagement suggests potential inequalities in post‑ICU recovery pathways. Standardizing referral practices and expanding clinic availability may improve outcomes for ICU survivors.

articles.title: Social and Environmental Exposures and the Developing Gut of Newborns With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysbiotic gut microbiomes are linked to morbidity, mortality, and poor outcomes, so it is critical to understand their influencing factors.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of nosocomial and socioecological factors on the gut microbiome in newborns with congenital heart disease (CHD).
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort of newborns with CHD matched to healthy newborns by age, sex, and race and ethnicity. Data on feeding type and routes and disease-related factors were collected from electronic medical records. Stool samples were collected at 3 perioperative time points. Gut microbiome diversity and abundance were analyzed using QIIME 2.
RESULTS: Newborns with CHD (n = 41) showed higher alpha diversity (P = .007) and dissimilar beta diversity (P = .001) versus controls (n = 40). Beta diversity was dissimilar between those receiving human milk versus formula (P = .05), between those receiving fortified versus nonfortified human milk (P = .04), and between those receiving naso-orogastric tube feeds versus other routes (P = .02). Newborns with CHD fed only human milk had higher relative abundance of Haemophilus (P = .04), those with longer duration of aortic cross-clamping had lower relative abundance of Streptococcus (P = .10), and those of higher socioeconomic deprivation had higher relative abundance of Enterococcus (P = .03).
CONCLUSIONS: Feeding tubes, formula exposure, aortic cross-clamp, and socioeconomic status were associated with altered gut microbiome diversity. Further study is needed to determine the causal relationships leading to gut microbial dysbiosis in newborns in the cardiac intensive care unit.

articles.title: Implementation of a Preoperative Nursing Consultation in Elective Paediatric Surgery: An Implementation Science Perspective.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To analyse the role of standardized protocols and nurse-led preoperative consultations in elective paediatric surgery and the factors influencing their implementation.
DESIGN: Perspective article guided by the integrated Promoting Action on Research Implementation in Health Services framework.
DATA SOURCES: Structured search of Dialnet, PubMed, SciELO and the Cochrane Library for studies published between 2018 and 2025, conducted between January and March 2025. Of 547 records identified, 40 sources were eligible and 17 inform this article.
CONCLUSION: Available studies suggest that non-pharmacological interventions, family involvement and nurse-led preoperative preparation may reduce anxiety and improve the surgical experience. However, implementation remains inconsistent because of workload, limited training and resources and insufficient institutional support. Nurses are well placed to facilitate the translation of evidence into practice, while organizational culture and leadership determine sustainability.
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: Nurses can operationalize preoperative consultations through structured, developmentally appropriate assessment of child and parental anxiety and of pain; child- and family-centered education; non-pharmacological preparation; escalation of high anxiety or pain through agreed referral pathways; and local adaptation of evidence-based protocols with the multidisciplinary team.
IMPACT: This article addresses the gap between evidence and practice in paediatric preoperative care. It identifies barriers and facilitators related to the innovation, its recipients, the context and facilitation, and proposes nurse-led implementation strategies that require evaluation. It is relevant to perioperative nurses, managers and policymakers in paediatric surgical services.
REPORTING METHOD: No EQUATOR reporting guideline applies to perspective articles; the literature search is reported in the Methods.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: This perspective article is based on a structured literature search and on theoretical implementation frameworks. No primary data were collected, and no patients, caregivers, service users, or members of the public were involved in the design, conduct, analysis, or preparation of this manuscript.

articles.title: Cell salvage volume and hemostatic changes in cardiac surgery: A retrospective cohort study using routine coagulation and viscoelastic assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative cell salvage (CS) reduces allogeneic transfusion in cardiac surgery, but the washing process removes coagulation factors and platelets, raising hemostatic concerns. The dose-response relationship between CS volume and perioperative hemostatic changes remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: In this retrospective study of adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CS use, two cohorts with paired hemostatic measurements were identified: a routine coagulation cohort (primary analysis) and a viscoelastic cohort (exploratory analysis). Both cohorts were restricted to patients without coagulation-affecting blood products between measurements. Multivariable linear regression examined CS volume and absolute changes in each parameter, adjusted for surgical and patient characteristics and baseline values.
RESULTS: In the routine coagulation cohort (N = 677; median CS 0.5 L, range 0.1-1.6 L), CS volume was not significantly associated with absolute changes in any parameter (all p ≥ 0.144). In the viscoelastic cohort (N = 50; median CS 0.8 L, range 0.2-3.7 L), CS volume was significantly associated with decreased functional fibrinogen clot strength (CFF MA: β = -3.31 mm/L; 95% CI: -5.53, -1.08; p = 0.004) and overall clot strength (CK MA: β = -2.93 mm/L; 95% CI: -5.73, -0.13; p = 0.041); after Holm correction for multiple testing, the CFF MA association remained significant (adjusted p = 0.031), whereas the CK MA association did not (adjusted p = 0.244).
CONCLUSIONS: At observed reinfusion volumes, CS was not associated with changes in routine coagulation parameters, but in the exploratory viscoelastic cohort, higher CS volume was associated with lower functional fibrinogen clot strength. These findings highlight the potential value of viscoelastic monitoring when higher volumes are anticipated.

articles.title: Learning curve of da vinci robotic lobectomy: a single-surgeon CUSUM analysis of operative time and perioperative outcomes.
articles.abstract: To characterize the operative-time learning curve for da Vinci robotic-assisted lobectomy in a single surgeon's initial experience, and to examine, using trend analyses of patient comorbidity and surgical-complexity variables and adjusted regression models, whether any apparent change in operative time was influenced by a shift in case complexity. We retrospectively reviewed 47 consecutive patients who underwent da Vinci robotic-assisted lobectomy performed by a single board-certified thoracic surgeon at Kaohsiung Chang Gung Memorial Hospital between September 30, 2024, and July 6, 2026. Patients who underwent wedge resection, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), segmentectomy, or resection with the da Vinci SP system were excluded. Cases were ordered chronologically, and cumulative sum (CUSUM) of operative time was calculated as the cumulative deviation from the group mean. Because CUSUM based on the mean deviation is a descriptive method without formal decision limits, a 10,000-iteration permutation test was used to construct an empirical 95% decision-limit envelope and to test whether the observed CUSUM path exceeded the range expected under random case ordering; leave-one-out and moving-average sensitivity analyses were also performed. Early and late phases, divided at the CUSUM peak, were compared using the Mann-Whitney test for continuous variables and Fisher's exact test for categorical variables; time to chest tube removal was additionally analyzed with the Kaplan-Meier method and log-rank test. The relationship between case sequence and Charlson Comorbidity Index and surgical-complexity variables (tumor size on pathology, malignant histology, pathologic T category, nodal status, stage, operative lobe, concomitant procedures, lymph node yield, pleural adhesions) was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation and Fisher's exact test; operative time was additionally modeled by linear regression with robust standard errors, adjusted successively for malignancy, tumor size, nodal status, lobe, concomitant procedures, and Charlson index. The CUSUM curve for operative time peaked at case 20 (value 265.0), with a nearly equal local peak at case 10 (260.5); leave-one-out and smoothing analyses showed the identified peak was unstable between cases 10 and 20, and the entire observed CUSUM path remained within the 95% permutation-derived decision-limit envelope (global p = 0.73), indicating that this descriptive breakpoint could not be formally distinguished from random case-to-case variation at this sample size. Operative time did not differ significantly between early (n = 20) and late (n = 27) phases (median 315.0 [IQR 283.8-357.2] vs. 284.0 [268.5-338.0] minutes, p = 0.186) and showed no monotonic trend with case sequence overall (Spearman's ρ = 0.01, p = 0.93). Chest tube duration differed significantly between phases on both Mann-Whitney testing (p = 0.041) and Kaplan-Meier/log-rank analysis (χ²=5.43, p = 0.020), although this and other secondary comparisons were not corrected for multiplicity. Charlson Comorbidity Index increased significantly with case sequence (ρ = 0.34, p = 0.02); the other surgical-complexity variables moved in the same direction without reaching significance (malignant histology 65% vs. 89%, p = 0.07; concomitant procedures 5% vs. 19%, p = 0.22), tumor size did not change (median 2.2 vs. 2.1 cm, p = 0.80), lobe distribution did not differ between phases, and no patient had pleural adhesions. Adjustment for malignancy and these variables did not materially change the association between case sequence and operative time (unadjusted - 0.03 min per case, 95% CI - 1.53 to + 1.46; fully adjusted + 0.12, - 1.48 to + 1.72) or the early-late difference (- 23.1 min unadjusted vs. -16.0 min adjusted; all p ≥ 0.27), although confidence intervals were wide. By the time of the CUSUM-identified breakpoint (lobectomy case 20), the surgeon had already accumulated 39 total robotic console cases when segmentectomy, wedge resection, and da Vinci SP cases are included. In this single-surgeon series, the operative-time CUSUM breakpoint at approximately case 10-20 should be interpreted as an exploratory, descriptive signal rather than a formally validated learning-to-proficiency transition, as it was not statistically distinguishable from random variation and the dichotomized early/late operative-time comparison was not significant. Comorbidity burden increased significantly over the study period and surgical-complexity indicators trended in the same direction, and adjustment for them did not alter the operative-time estimates; there was thus no evidence that the surgeon progressively selected easier cases, but the small sample precludes firm conclusions, and adhesion severity could not be studied because no patient had adhesions, so the findings may not apply to patients with adhesions. The surgeon's cumulative robotic experience at the time of the breakpoint substantially exceeded the lobectomy case count alone once other robotic procedures are considered.

articles.title: Regional Anesthesia in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Current Landscape and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Regional anesthesia (RA) is increasingly promoted as a strategy for expanding safe surgical and obstetric anesthesia access in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where general anesthesia (GA) carries disproportionate risk. This review examines current RA utilization patterns, recent advances in training and implementation, persistent barriers, and the evidence linking RA to clinical outcomes in LMICs, in order to identify what is needed for durable, system-wide scale-up.
RECENT FINDINGS: Large observational analyses show lower perioperative and maternal mortality with regional or neuraxial anesthesia compared with GA. Hybrid training models combining online instruction, simulation, and mentored clinical practice have improved provider knowledge and peripheral nerve block competence, and portable ultrasound has expanded point-of-care applications. However, workforce shortages, inconsistent equipment and medication supply, limited capacity to manage local anesthetic systemic toxicity, and fragmented, single-center safety data continue to constrain reliable implementation. RA offers a safe, lower-resource alternative to GA in LMICs, but sustainable expansion depends on addressing underlying workforce, supply, and monitoring deficits rather than isolated procedural training. Embedding RA within National Surgical, Obstetric, and Anesthesia Plans, supported by multicenter outcome registries and economic evaluation, should guide future research and implementation efforts.

articles.title: Family risk and resilience patterns differentiate early childhood vulnerability to intergenerational transmission of abdominal pain.
articles.abstract: Children are at increased risk of developing chronic abdominal pain if a parent has an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction such as irritable bowel syndrome, suggesting family mechanisms of intergenerational pain transmission. However, patterns of family risk and resilience factors that predict children's vulnerability for developing chronic abdominal pain remain unknown. In a sample of parents with an abdominal pain-related disorder of brain-gut interaction and their young child without chronic pain, this cross-sectional study identified subgroups representing different constellations of family risk and resilience factors. It also tested subgroup differences on two vulnerability markers for children's future development of chronic abdominal pain: child emotional functioning and parental protective behavior. Baseline data from 212 parents and their 4-7-year-old child, participating in a randomized controlled trial testing a preventative intervention, were included. Latent mixture modeling indicated a 3-group solution: (1) "High Socioeconomic Status, High Functioning" (55%) characterized by lower anxiety and depression and higher family resilience, (2) "Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" (13%) characterized by higher pain catastrophizing and gastrointestinal symptoms, and (3) "High Socioeconomic Status, High Distress" (32%) characterized by higher parenting stress. Two of the three groups ("Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" and "High Socioeconomic Status, High Distress" groups) showed lower child emotional functioning, and the "Low Socioeconomic Status, High Pain Burden" group also showed higher parental protective behavior, than the "High Socioeconomic Status, High Functioning" group. Results contribute to theoretical models of intergenerational pain transmission and help identify families who could benefit from preventative interventions. PERSPECTIVE: Among families of parents with chronic abdominal pain, low family resilience, low socioeconomic status, high parent pain burden, and high parent psychological distress may make young children more vulnerable to developing chronic abdominal pain in the future. These findings inform targeted interventions to prevent intergenerational transmission of abdominal pain.

articles.title: From Hartert's Thrombelastograph to Pathway-Specific Viscoelastic Testing: A Historical Sketch.
articles.abstract: Viscoelastic haemostatic testing is now widely used in clinical practice, but its adoption unfolded slowly. Introduced by Hellmut Hartert in 1948 as thrombelastography, it offered a dynamic whole-blood recording of clot initiation, propagation, strength, and lysis at a time when most coagulation testing relied on endpoint clotting times in plasma. Hartert and others applied the method clinically from the 1950s, and it reached the first human liver transplant programmes in the 1960s, yet for almost four decades it did not spread beyond individual centres. Its expansion required not only technical modernisation but also a conceptual change. The original thrombelastographic tracing represented coagulation as a broad, monolithic process. Successive generations of instruments and reagents progressively decomposed this single signal into interpretable functional modules through defined activators, platelet inhibitors, fibrinolytic challenge and drug-specific triggers. Mechanical cup-and-pin and probe systems (e.g., Hartert, ROTEM, ClotPro, Sonoclot), resonance with optical detection (e.g., TEG 6s), and ultrasound-based sonorheometry (e.g., Quantra) all follow a broader historical movement from global observation toward pathway-directed analysis of haemostasis. This historical sketch traces that trajectory from Hartert's mechanical instrument to today's viscoelastic assay panels, illustrating the long latency before clinical adoption, the methodological revival through standardised activators and perioperative algorithms, and the more recent development of assays directed at fibrinolysis and direct oral anticoagulants.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes of CO2 insufflation and retractor-assisted endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy: a single-institution retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative data directly comparing CO2 insufflation and retractor-assisted endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy (E-NSM) within the same institution remain limited. Therefore, we evaluated the perioperative outcomes and practical differences between these approaches.
METHODS: This single-institution retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent E-NSM for breast cancer from April 2020 to April 2026. Patients were classified into the CO2 insufflation and the retractor-assisted groups by working-space creation method. The primary outcome was clinically significant postoperative complications within 90 days; secondary outcomes were operative time and blood loss. Bilateral procedures were excluded from operative-time, blood-loss, and reconstruction-stratified analyses.
RESULTS: The study included 65 patients with 69 breasts: 28 patients with 28 breasts in the CO2 insufflation group and 37 patients with 41 breasts in the retractor-assisted group. Clinically significant complications occurred in 4/28 (14.3%) and 5/41 (12.2%) breasts, and total nipple necrosis in 2/28 (7.1%) and 3/41 (7.3%). After excluding bilateral procedures, complication rates were 4/28 (14.3%) and 5/33 (15.2%). Operative time was longer in the CO2 insufflation group, including among patients undergoing immediate reconstruction, whereas blood loss was similar between groups. The approaches differed in terms of working-space creation, reconstruction workflow, instrument manipulation, and device requirements.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, operative time was longer in the CO2insufflation group, whereas no statistically significant differences in short-term complication rates or blood loss were observed. The two approaches also differed in operative workflow and device requirements. These findings may provide practical information for surgeons and institutions considering the introduction of E-NSM.

articles.title: Minimally invasive versus open surgery for the management of thoracolumbar spondylodiscitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Thoracolumbar spondylodiscitis increasingly affects older patients in whom surgical morbidity strongly influences recovery. Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) aims to achieve debridement, microbial diagnosis, and mechanical stabilization while reducing soft-tissue disruption, but its comparative performance relative to open surgery (OS) remains uncertain. This review evaluated the efficacy and safety of MIS versus OS for thoracolumbar spondylodiscitis.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative retrospective cohort studies. MIS approaches included percutaneous pedicle screw fixation, transforaminal interbody fusion, and endoscopic debridement techniques, compared with conventional open surgical approaches. Electronic searches of PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL (24th September 2025) were performed. All ten included studies were retrospective comparative cohorts. Random-effects meta-analysis generated pooled mean differences and risk ratios. Heterogeneity, sensitivity analyses, and risk of bias (ROBINS-I) were assessed. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Ten retrospective cohorts of 855 adults (MIS 383; OS 472) were included. No randomized controlled trials were identified. MIS was associated with fewer post-operative complications, including halved overall complication risk and reduced surgical-site infections. MIS also demonstrated shorter operative time, reduced intraoperative blood loss and transfusion requirement, lower early post-operative pain, and 3.8-day reduction in hospital stay. Measures of infection control, including culture positivity, early post-operative C-reactive protein levels, and recurrence, showed no statistically detectable difference between MIS and OS, although the observational evidence base precludes causal inference. Certainty of evidence was moderate for overall complications, surgical-site infection, operative time, length of stay, and CRP change; low for blood loss, sepsis, and mortality; and very low for transfusion volume, recurrence, and screw misplacement.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that MIS was associated with lower peri-operative morbidity and comparable infection-control outcomes, supporting its use as a tissue-sparing surgical option for surgically indicated cases of thoracolumbar spondylodiscitis. Prospective standardized studies are needed to refine patient selection and clarify the role of emerging full endoscopic techniques.

articles.title: Preop​erative Frailty and Adverse Outcomes after Metab​olic and Bariatric Surgery: a Systematic Review of Prognostic Evidence.
articles.abstract: Preoperative frailty is increasingly recognized as a predictor of adverse outcomes following metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). We systematically reviewed eight retrospective studies with sample sizes ranging from 895 to 693,066 participants, although five analyzed overlapping MBSAQIP registry cohorts hence the number of unique patients cannot be precisely determined. Five frailty instruments were evaluated (mFI-11, bFI, BFS, mBFS and MSK-FI). Frailty was consistently associated with higher 30-day mortality (adjusted ORs 3.23 and 28.5) and major​ complications (categorical adjusted ORs 1.24-1.99; continuous mFI OR 39.7). Frailty was also associated with increased unplanned intensive care admission, prolonged hospital stay, non-home discharge, readmission, reoperation and suboptimal weight-loss outcomes. Among frail patients, reported mortality rates were 0.5-0.6% following SG and 1.0-1.1% following RYGB, although direct comparative estimates were unavailable. Despite generally consistent associations, certainty of evidence ranged from low to high across outcomes. Current evidence supports frailty assessment for perioperative risk stratification, although prospective validation of standardized instruments remains needed.

articles.title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes.
RESULTS: We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%.
CONCLUSIONS: The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Colchicine and Perioperative Acute Kidney Injury: A Substudy of the COP-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Perioperative inflammation may result in organ injury, including acute kidney injury (AKI). Colchicine, an anti-inflammatory drug, may help protect the organs from inflammation. This clinical trial substudy examined whether colchicine reduced the risk of perioperative AKI compared with placebo.
STUDY DESIGN: Prespecified substudy of a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged 55 years or older undergoing major noncardiac thoracic surgery enrolled in the Colchicine for the Prevention of Perioperative Atrial Fibrillation (COP-AF) trial from 45 centers in 11 countries (2018-2023). Patients were excluded for a history of atrial fibrillation, for taking antiarrhythmic medication, or for a preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min per 1.73 m2.
EXPOSURE: Participants were randomized 1:1 to 0.5 mg oral colchicine or placebo, given twice daily for a total of 10 days. Patients, health care providers, data collectors, and outcome adjudicators were masked to the treatment assignment.
OUTCOME: Perioperative AKI, defined as an increase in serum creatinine concentration of either ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours of surgery or ≥50% within 7 days of surgery. Alternative definitions of AKI were examined, as was effect modification by pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD).
RESULTS: Among 3,209 patients enrolled in the main trial, 2,947 were included in this substudy (mean age, 68 years; mean eGFR, 83 mL/min/1.73 m2) and were randomly allocated to receive colchicine (n = 1,476) or placebo (n = 1,471). Perioperative AKI occurred in 67 participants (4.7%) in the colchicine group and in 63 participants (4.4%) in the placebo group (risk ratio [RR], 1.07 [95% CI, 0.76-1.50], P = 0.72; risk difference [RD], 0.3% [95% CI, -1.2% to 1.8%]). The RD of AKI in patients with CKD treated with colchicine versus placebo was -0.9%, and it was 0.5% in those without CKD (interaction P = 0.62).
LIMITATIONS: Limited statistical power to detect small clinically important effects on AKI treated with dialysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing noncardiac thoracic surgery, the risk of perioperative AKI did not differ between patients allocated to receive colchicine versus placebo.
FUNDING: Grants from academic (Department of Medicine, Western University; Division of Cardiology, McMaster University), government (Canadian Institutes of Health Research; General Research Fund, Research Grants Council, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China), and not-for-profit (Accelerating Clinical Trials Consortium; Innovation Fund of the Alternative Funding Plan for the Academic Health Sciences Centres of Ontario; Population Health Research Institute; Hamilton Health Sciences; Hanela Foundation) sources.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov with study number NCT03310125.
PLAIN-LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Inflammation during and after surgery can lead to organ injury, including acute kidney injury (AKI). Colchicine, an anti-inflammatory drug, may help protect the organs from inflammation. This prespecified kidney substudy of the COP-AF trial (a placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial of 3,209 patients aged 55 years and older having major noncardiac thoracic surgery), examined the effect of oral colchicine (0.5 mg tablet, taken twice daily starting within 4 hours before surgery for a total of 10 days) on the risk of perioperative AKI. The study found that the risk of perioperative AKI did not differ between patients assigned to receive colchicine versus placebo. The results were consistent for multiple definitions of AKI and in patients with pre-existing chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: Effects of perioperative dexmedetomidine on postoperative delirium in older surgical patients: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of perioperative intravenous dexmedetomidine in preventing postoperative delirium (POD) in older surgical patients.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was performed across three authoritative databases: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to July 7, 2026, included all available RCTs evaluating the effect of dexmedetomidine on POD in older surgical patients undergoing general anesthesia. The primary outcome was the incidence of POD. Secondary outcomes encompassed adverse events, including PONV, intraoperative and postoperative bradycardia and intraoperative and postoperative hypotension. The study was registered in the PROSPERO database under the identifier CRD420251001512.
RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs, involving 4161 patients, were included in the analysis. The results show that dexmedetomidine significantly reduced the incidence of POD (RR = 0.56, 95% CI: 0.47 to 0.66; P < 0.00001; I2 = 24%) and reduced PONV (RR = 0.79; 95% CI = 0.62 to 0.99; P = 0.04; I2 = 0%). Furthermore, dexmedetomidine was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative and postoperative bradycardia as well as intraoperative hypotension.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that dexmedetomidine reduces POD and PONV incidence in older surgical patients but increases intraoperative and postoperative bradycardia and intraoperative hypotension.

articles.title: Comparing quadratus lumborum and transversus abdominis plane blocks for pain control after open ventral hernia repair: a propensity score-matched analysis of the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks are commonly used to reduce postoperative pain after ventral hernia repair (VHR). However, quadratus lumborum (QL) blocks may provide improved pain control. While TAP blocks have been studied in VHR, no literature directly compares TAP and QL blocks for open VHR.
METHODS: A propensity score-matched analysis of the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative (ACHQC) was performed for patients undergoing elective open VHR between January 2023 and July 2025 who received TAP or QL blocks. Outcomes included length of stay (LOS), post-discharge opioid use, patient-reported pain and quality of life, and 30-day complications and readmissions.
RESULTS: After matching, 445 patients met inclusion criteria: 333 (75%) received TAP blocks and 112 (25%) received QL blocks. Median age was 62 years, and median BMI was 32 kg/m2. Most patients underwent myofascial release with retromuscular mesh placement. Hernia width was similar between groups (11 vs 12 cm, p = 0.6). Median LOS was 4 days in both groups (p = 0.07). At 30 days, 87% of TAP and 90% of QL patients reported no opioid use after discharge (p = 0.5). HerQLes scores were similar, but PROMIS-3a pain scores were higher in QL patients at 30 days (p = 0.006). Complications and readmissions were similar.
CONCLUSION: This is the first study to compare the outcomes of QL and TAP blocks for patients undergoing open VHR. There was no difference in pain control between each group as measured by hospital LOS and post-discharge opioid consumption; however, QL block patients reported higher pain scores at 30 days.

articles.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain and comorbid depression through Gut-Metabolite-Brain axis remodeling to restore mPFC Glu/GABA balance.
articles.abstract: The comorbidity of chronic pain and depression is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving dysregulated microbiota-gut-brain communication. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for both pain and depression, the mechanisms linking peripheral microbial-metabolic remodeling to central neurotransmitter regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach in a spared nerve injury (SNI) rat model to investigate the gut-metabolite-brain mechanisms underlying EA's efficacy. EA significantly alleviated mechanical hypersensitivity and depressive-like behaviors while restoring mPFC Glu/GABA balance, accompanied by normalization of the glutamate transporter EAAT2 and the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67. Metagenomic analysis showed that EA remodeled the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing microbial diversity, suppressing opportunistic pathobionts, including Bacillus cereus, Alistipes onderdonkii, while enriching SCFA-associated genera, including Butyricimonas and Romboutsia. These alterations were accompanied by coordinated remodeling of amino acid and butanoate metabolism. Correlation network analysis identified Pipecolic acid as a central metabolic node linking gut microbial alterations with mPFC GABAergic neurotransmission and behavioral recovery. Although individual bacterial genera did not significantly mediate its restoration, causal mediation analysis demonstrated that the Pipecolic acid-GABA axis significantly mediated improvements in both mechanical allodynia and anhedonia, supporting Pipecolic acid as a functional metabolic hub linking peripheral metabolic remodeling to central GABAergic regulation. Collectively, these findings identify peripheral metabolic remodeling as a key mechanistic interface through which EA coordinates gut microbial ecology and central neurochemical homeostasis, providing a systems-level framework for understanding the therapeutic mechanisms of acupuncture in pain-depression comorbidity.

articles.title: Efficiency of Dual Minor Procedure Rooms in Plastic Surgery: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Minor procedure rooms (MPRs) using local anesthesia are an efficient alternative for selected ambulatory procedures, with reduced resource utilization, shorter procedure-related times, and comparable clinical outcomes with traditional operating rooms. However, strategies to optimize MPR workflows and increase procedural capacity remain poorly studied in outpatient plastic surgery. This pilot study evaluated parallelized MPR workflows.
METHODS: This prospective quasi-experimental pilot study compared 1 versus 2 MPR configurations across 8 outpatient clinic days in New Brunswick, Canada, using the same plastic surgeon. Adult patients undergoing elective plastic surgery procedures under local anesthesia were included. Outcomes included patients treated per day and percentage of the surgeon's clinic time spent providing direct patient care.
RESULTS: The median number of patients treated per clinic day was significantly higher with 2 MPRs than 1 MPR (17.0 vs 9.0 patients/day, P = .02). Two MPRs were associated with less surgeon clinic time outside direct patient care (4.85% vs 32.57%, P = .04) and more time providing direct patient care (95.15% vs 67.43%, P = .04). After adjustment for daily case-mix complexity, 2 MPRs remained independently associated with increased direct patient care time (B = 20.64, 95% CI [10.70, 30.58], P = .003).
CONCLUSION: A dual-MPR workflow increased patient throughput and direct patient care time while reducing non-clinical downtime. When surgeon time is limiting, parallelizing patient flow across 2 MPRs can reduce idle time and increase the number of patients treated by a single surgeon. Larger multi-center studies are needed to assess safety, patient satisfaction, and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Computed tomography-guided splanchnic nerve neurolysis outcomes by tumor site in unresectable pancreatic cancer: A single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-guided neurolytic splanchnic nerve block (NSNB) is used to treat pain in unresectable pancreatic cancers. Whether outcomes differ according to tumor site remains uncertain.
AIM: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of CT-guided NSNB in unresectable pancreatic cancer and explore differences by tumor site.
