METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 22 patients who underwent initial CT-guided NSNB at the Oita Red Cross Hospital between 2007 and 2023. Clinical success comprised recorded pain relief or opioid reduction within 1 week; standardized pain scores were not routinely recorded. Technical success required bilateral retrocrural distribution. Adverse events were graded using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE). Proportions were reported with 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs); comparisons used Fisher's exact and exact permutation Mann-Whitney U tests.
RESULTS: Technical and clinical success occurred in 17/22 (77.3%; 95%CI: 56.6%-89.9%) and 18/22 (81.8%; 95%CI: 61.5%-92.7%), respectively. The recorded duration was available for 13 clinical responders, with a median of 40 days (interquartile range: 19-144 days); four transfers and one death lacked an evaluable duration. The clinical success rates were 6/9 for head tumors and 12/13 for body/tail tumors. The available duration medians were 29.5 days and 117 days, respectively. Adverse events occurred in 6/22 (27.3%; 95%CI: 13.2%-48.2%), with no CTCAE grade ≥ 3 events.
CONCLUSION: CT-guided NSNB is associated with encouraging clinical responses at both tumor sites in this small retrospective cohort. Prospective studies should confirm these findings and clarify potential tumor-site differences.

articles.title: Sequential Lidocaine and Liposomal Bupivacaine for Popliteal Sciatic Nerve Block in Foot and Ankle Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In foot and ankle surgery, prolonged analgesia after popliteal sciatic nerve block (PSNB) may be accompanied by delayed motor recovery. The effects of sequential lidocaine and liposomal bupivacaine (LB), particularly on early motor function, remain uncertain.
METHODS: Eighty adults undergoing foot and ankle surgery were randomized to preoperative 1.5% lidocaine (20 mL) followed by postoperative 0.665% LB (20 mL), or preoperative 0.5% ropivacaine (20 mL). Participants and outcome assessors were blinded; block providers were not. For the coprimary comparisons, resting pain was assessed at 24 hours using a 0-10 visual analog scale and motor function at 3 hours using the modified Bromage score.
RESULTS: In complete-case analyses, 37 lidocaine-LB and 38 ropivacaine recipients were included. Median (IQR) 24-hour resting pain was 0 (0-2) versus 1 (0-3) (difference, -1; 95% CI, -3 to 0; P<0.001); the difference was below the prespecified 1.5-point threshold for clinical importance. The 3-hour motor score was 1 (1-1) versus 0 (0-0) (difference, 1; 95% CI, 1 to 1; P<0.001), meeting the study-defined 1-point threshold. Exploratory comparisons favored lidocaine-LB for later pain, 24-hour rescue analgesia and recovery quality, and postoperative nausea and vomiting. One suspected local anesthetic systemic toxicity event-mild tinnitus 15 minutes after preoperative lidocaine-was recorded; no specific treatment was given.
CONCLUSION: Compared with single-injection ropivacaine, sequential lidocaine-LB was associated with better early motor scores and statistically lower 24-hour resting pain. The pain difference did not meet the prespecified threshold for clinical importance. Functional benefit and comparative safety remain unestablished. Larger multicenter trials should assess mobility and safety, together with the cost and feasibility of the additional block.

articles.title: Best Evidence Summary of Non-Pharmacological Pain Assessment and Management in Elderly Patients During the Perioperative Period.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate and synthesize the best available evidence on non-pharmacological approaches to pain assessment and management in elderly patients aged ≥60 years during the perioperative period, and to provide an evidence-based reference for clinical practice.
DESIGN: This study synthesized the evidence in accordance with the evidence summary report standards of the Evidence-based Nursing Center at Fudan University.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted to identify evidence on non-pharmacological pain assessment and management in elderly patients during the perioperative period. Eligible literature included clinical decision-making documents, guidelines, expert consensus statements, recommended practices, evidence summaries, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, CINAHL, the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang, and VIP. UpToDate, the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN), the Guidelines International Network (GIN), and Yimaitong were searched from database inception to July 2024.
RESULTS: A total of 12 articles were included, comprising 3 guidelines, 3 expert consensus statements, 4 meta-analyses, 1 randomized controlled trial, and 1 systematic review. From these, 23 evidence statements were extracted and synthesized into four domains: team building, pain assessment, pain management, and health education. The non-pharmacological interventions mainly included physical approaches, psychological interventions, music intervention, and education for patients and caregivers.
CONCLUSION: The evidence summarized in this study provides a structured reference for non-pharmacological pain assessment and management in elderly perioperative patients. Clinical application should consider the patient's condition, type of surgery, strength of the evidence, and available healthcare resources.

articles.title: From Gaps in Maternity Care to Maternal Rescue: An Interprofessional Implementation Agenda for Anesthesia and Maternal Critical Care in Somalia.
articles.abstract: Somalia's maternal health system faces a dual challenge: limited access to skilled maternity care and insufficient capacity to rescue women who deteriorate during or after obstetric emergencies. Hemorrhage, hypertensive emergencies including eclampsia, sepsis, obstructed labor, and urgent cesarean delivery require coordinated maternity, anesthesia, nursing, resuscitation, postoperative surveillance, and critical-care functions. This evidence-informed commentary shifts the discussion from documenting gaps to an interprofessional implementation agenda. We propose five linked priorities: a regulated and supported maternity and obstetric-anesthesia workforce; an evidence-based cesarean safety bundle; step-up maternal high-care capacity; early-warning, crisis resource management, escalation, and referral pathways; and routine measurement through maternal and perioperative quality systems. The approach emphasizes actions that referral maternity hospitals can introduce progressively, with named local accountability, team training, minimum resource requirements, and measurable indicators, while avoiding unsupported assumptions about national critical-care capacity. Somalia does not need to wait for a fully developed intensive-care system before improving maternal rescue. The immediate opportunity is to connect five functions that are too often fragmented: competent anesthesia provision, reliable cesarean safety processes, early recognition of deterioration, monitored maternal high care, and accountable review of outcomes. Strengthening these functions as one interprofessional maternal-rescue pathway offers a practical route to reducing preventable severe maternal morbidity and mortality in Somalia.

articles.title: Clinically Actionable Prevention and Management of Major Complications During Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Support: A Contemporary Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) have become an established therapy for selected patients with advanced heart failure as bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy. Despite major progress in continuous-flow pump design and perioperative care, long-term benefit remains constrained by a recurrent burden of right heart failure, aortic regurgitation, pump thrombosis, stroke, bleeding, infection, and end-organ dysfunction. Because these events often arise from the interaction of altered hemodynamics, hemocompatibility-related injury, chronic antithrombotic exposure, and the practical complexity of longitudinal device care, a complication-centered management framework is clinically useful. This contemporary narrative review focuses on actionable prevention, surveillance, and treatment strategies for the major complications encountered during durable LVAD support. Rather than providing a broad device-oriented overview, we emphasize clinically relevant decision points across the perioperative and long-term course, including right ventricular protection, antithrombotic balance, structured monitoring for aortic regurgitation and hemolysis, prevention of driveline infection, and multidisciplinary outpatient follow-up. By organizing current evidence around practical management pathways, this review aims to support earlier recognition of adverse events and more durable long-term support.

articles.title: Components of institution-free days as a composite outcome after critical illness: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the components of institution-free days (IFD) after intensive care unit (ICU) admission and assess the distribution of IFD at 365 d across various admission categories.
DESIGN: Multicentre, retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Adult patients (aged ≥18 y) admitted to 12 ICUs in Queensland from 2017 to 2020.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: IFD is the primary composite outcome defined as the number of days alive and free of healthcare institution exposure. IFD is calculated by subtracting total number of days with healthcare institution exposure from 365. Distribution of IFD and its components were evaluated across four prespecified subgroups-diagnostic category, comorbidity groups, age quartiles, and remoteness of area of residence.
RESULTS: 44 541 ICU admissions were analysed, of which 19 706 (44.2%), 17 488 (39.2%), and 7347 (16.5%) were medical, elective, and nonelective surgical admissions, respectively. The median IFD was higher for elective surgical patients as compared to nonelective surgical and medical admissions (348 d [interquartile range (IQR): 330-355] vs. 330 [IQR: 267-349] d vs. 325 [IQR: 185-349]). Hospital readmission days were the major contributor to IFD, with 60.4% of all survivors experiencing at least one hospital readmission day within 365 d. The mean hospital readmission days were highest for nonelective surgical admissions as compared to elective and medical admissions (18.5 [standard deviation (SD):18.4] vs. 13.9 [SD: 15.9] vs. 16.1 [SD: 19.2] days).
CONCLUSION: Hospital readmission days were the predominant contributor to institution-days and principal driver of lower IFD for ICU survivors. Medical ICU admissions had the least IFD, followed by nonelective surgical and elective surgical patients.

articles.title: Predictors, risk factors and management of intestinal failure in crohn's disease: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Intestinal failure in Crohn's disease is a preventable complication arising from primarily three pathways: progressive inflammatory bowel destruction, cumulative surgical loss, and postoperative septic complications. Crohn's disease is one of the most common benign causes, with a cumulative incidence of approximately 8.5% at 20 years after initial surgery. Postoperative abdominal sepsis accounts for over half the cases, highlighting the importance of perioperative optimization. Several predictors such as young age at diagnosis, penetrating disease behavior, upper gastrointestinal localisation, cumulative inflammatory burden, residual small intestinal length less than 200 cm, and non-use of biologic therapy. Prevention should be the focus of management. Modern treat-to-target interventions aiming for endoscopic and transmural healing, early effective biologic therapy, timely surgical intervention with bowel-sparing techniques including strictureplasty and the Kono-S anastomosis, and structured perioperative optimization with nutritional rehabilitation collectively address each of the three pathways to intestinal failure. Management of established intestinal failure requires multidisciplinary intestinal rehabilitation encompassing parenteral nutrition, pharmacological intestinotrophic therapy with glucagon-like peptide-2 agonists, active Crohn's disease management, autologous gastrointestinal reconstruction and intestinal transplantation in refractory cases. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence through unifying framework that intestinal failure in Crohn's disease is preventable at each step of the disease trajectory and proposes a risk stratification model and management algorithm to guide clinical decision making.

articles.title: Remimazolam versus propofol for elderly patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery: a randomized trial concentrating on delirium and hemodynamic stability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common complication in elderly surgical patients that can impede recovery. While remimazolam offers superior hemodynamic stability compared to propofol, its impact on POD incidence remains unclear. This randomized trial aimed to determine whether two induction doses of remimazolam are more effective than propofol in reducing POD and improving hemodynamic stability in older patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal surgery.
METHODS: In this prospective trial, 186 patients (aged 60-80 years) were randomized to receive anesthesia induction with remimazolam 0.15 mg/kg (R1), remimazolam 0.3 mg/kg (R2), or propofol 1.5 mg/kg (P). The primary endpoint was the incidence of POD within 5 days post-surgery, assessed using the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for Confusion Assessment Method. Secondary endpoints included hemodynamic parameters, recovery times, and adverse events.
RESULTS: The incidence of POD was 12.9% in the R1 group, 11.3% in the R2 group, and 6.5% in the P group (P = 0.467). Both remimazolam groups exhibited significantly higher mean arterial pressure following induction and intubation (both P < 0.05). Furthermore, remimazolam was associated with a lower incidence of treated hypotension (P = 0.010), fewer bradycardia events (P < 0.001), and reduced vasopressor requirements (P < 0.05). However, the time to loss of consciousness (P < 0.001) and extubation time (P < 0.001) were longer with remimazolam.
CONCLUSIONS: Remimazolam at induction doses of 0.15 mg/kg and 0.3 mg/kg did not reduce the incidence of POD compared with propofol. Nevertheless, the study was not adequately powered to exclude a clinically relevant difference in POD incidence given the substantially lower-than-expected event rate, as no statistically significant between-group difference was detected. In addition, remimazolam at these doses was associated with higher post-induction blood pressure, fewer hypotensive events, and lower vasopressor requirements compared with propofol. Therefore, remimazolam at these induction doses may serve as suitable alternatives for this vulnerable patient population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn, Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2400082176.

articles.title: Rebound pain after regional anesthesia in orthopedic surgery: current evidence and clinical implications - a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Regional anesthesia is widely used in orthopedic surgery because it provides effective postoperative analgesia and reduces opioid requirements. However, increasing attention has been directed toward rebound pain, a phenomenon characterized by the abrupt emergence of severe pain following the resolution of a peripheral nerve block. Although frequently reported, rebound pain remains inconsistently defined, and its true incidence and clinical significance are still debated. Current evidence suggests that rebound pain is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced not only by block resolution itself but also by the transition from regional analgesia to systemic pain management. Variability in postoperative analgesic strategies, timing of rescue analgesia, patient expectations, and surgical factors may substantially affect both its occurrence and perceived severity. Differences in definitions and outcome measures across studies further contribute to the wide variation in reported incidence rates. Available data support several potential mechanisms, including the unmasking of ongoing postoperative nociceptive input after block resolution, inflammatory responses related to surgical tissue injury, and, in some cases, central sensitization. Clinical observations also indicate that inadequate multimodal analgesia and failure to anticipate the analgesic transition period may play a major role in the development of severe rebound pain episodes. Current evidence suggests that proactive analgesic planning, scheduled multimodal analgesia initiated before block resolution, intravenous dexamethasone, and prolonged regional anesthesia techniques may reduce the incidence or severity of rebound pain. However, the reported benefits are not consistent across all studies, and some interventions improved early analgesia or prolonged block duration without reducing rebound pain or opioid consumption. Interpretation remains limited by substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Rebound pain appears to represent a complex interaction between physiological nociceptive processes and modifiable perioperative management factors rather than a simple consequence of peripheral nerve block resolution alone. Greater standardization of definitions and outcome measures is needed to better characterize its incidence, mechanisms, and clinical relevance in orthopedic surgery.

articles.title: Use of NSAIDs in orthopedic pain management: a Delphi consensus promoted by the Italian Society of Orthopedics and Traumatology (SIOT).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are a cornerstone of pain management in orthopedics, yet significant variability persists in prescribing practices and adherence to guidelines.
METHODS: A two-round modified Delphi consensus was conducted under the coordination of a methodologist, involving a scientific board of seven members and a broader expert panel of orthopedic surgeons, anesthesiologists, and pharmacologists affiliated with the Italian Society of Orthopedics and Traumatology (SIOT). Twenty statements spanning four domains-NSAID mechanisms of action, perioperative pain management in elective surgery, traumatic pain, and non-oncological/oncological pain-were submitted for evaluation using a six-point Likert scale; consensus was defined as ≥75% of ratings concentrating within a single tertile.
RESULTS: Of the 20 statements, 12 reached consensus in the first round; six revised statements reached consensus in the second round; and two were eliminated because of persistent opinion dispersion. Final recommendations endorse short-cycle NSAID therapy (7-10 days) within multimodal analgesia, support the use of symptomatic slow-acting drugs for osteoarthritis to reduce NSAID consumption in osteoarthritis, recommend NSAIDs perioperatively in frail fracture patients to limit opioid use and delirium, identify ketoprofen lysine salt as having a favorable risk-benefit profile for postdischarge pain, and emphasize individualized NSAID selection based on cardiovascular, renal, and antiplatelet risk factors.
DISCUSSION: This SIOT consensus provides evidence-informed, clinically actionable recommendations for NSAID use across the principal orthopedic pain scenarios, aiming to improve prescribing appropriateness and patient safety in routine practice.

articles.title: A Multidimensional Weight-Time-Frequency Score for Quantifying Intraoperative Hypotensive Burden During Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a multidimensional weight-time-frequency (WTF) score for quantifying cumulative intraoperative hypotensive burden during off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) and to evaluate its association with postoperative outcomes.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: A tertiary cardiac surgery center.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing OPCABG with continuous intraoperative arterial pressure monitoring.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A qualifying hypotensive episode was defined as mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg sustained for at least 1 minute. The WTF score integrated hypotension depth, duration, and frequency, and outcome-specific cohorts were used for 30-day all-cause mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF). Among 2,070 patients undergoing OPCABG, each 10-point increase in WTF was associated with higher adjusted odds of AF (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.155; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.001-1.333), AKI (adjusted OR, 1.216; 95% CI, 1.001-1.478), and 30-day all-cause mortality (adjusted OR, 2.346; 95% CI, 1.332-4.130). Restricted cubic spline analyses showed generally increasing adjusted odds across the WTF range without significant nonlinearity. In test-set analyses, adding WTF yielded significant integrated discrimination improvement for AKI and significant IDI and continuous net reclassification improvement for 30-day mortality, whereas incremental gains for AF were minimal. Mortality findings should be interpreted cautiously because only 31 deaths occurred. WTF met the prespecified noninferiority criterion in 14 of 15 comparisons with conventional MAP-based metrics, including all comparisons for AF and AKI.
CONCLUSION: The WTF score provides an interpretable cumulative measure of intraoperative hypotensive burden during OPCABG, shows adjusted associations with postoperative AF, AKI, and 30-day all-cause mortality and generally preserves discrimination comparable to conventional mean arterial pressure‒based metrics.

articles.title: Intraoperative Alprostadil for Perioperative Management of Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
Rigid Ring versus Flexible Band for Functional Tricuspid Regurgitation? Long-Term Survival and Tricuspid Regurgitation Recurrence Using Reconstructed Individual Patient Data Time-to-Event Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare long-term survival and recurrent tricuspid regurgitation (TR) following tricuspid valve repair (TVr) using flexible bands versus rigid rings for functional TR.
DESIGN: Systematic review and reconstructed individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis with parallel study-level random-effects meta-analysis.
SETTING: Meta-analysis of published studies identified through PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 4,407 adult patients from 11 studies undergoing TVr for functional TR; 59% received flexible bands.
INTERVENTIONS: Comparison of flexible band versus rigid ring annuloplasty. Time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves, and pooled hazard ratios were estimated using Cox frailty models. Propensity-matched subgroup analyses were performed.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Primary outcome was long-term survival; secondary outcome was freedom from recurrent TR. Study-level meta-analysis showed no significant difference in survival between device types (HR 0.86; 95% CI 0.72-1.04; p = 0.110). In contrast, reconstructed IPD analysis demonstrated an association between flexible bands and improved long-term survival compared with rigid rings (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.65-0.89; p < 0.001) and greater freedom from recurrent TR (HR 0.62; 95% CI 0.48-0.80; p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in propensity-matched cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Reconstructed IPD analyses demonstrated associations between flexible bands and improved long-term survival and greater freedom from recurrent TR; however, these associations were not confirmed in study-level or propensity-matched analyses. The available evidence therefore does not establish superiority of either annuloplasty strategy.

articles.title: Predictors of Technical Difficulty in Emergency Department Ultrasound-Guided Nerve Blocks: A Multicenter NURVE Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks (UGNBs) are increasingly used in emergency departments (EDs), but factors associated with technical difficulty remain poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the frequency of technical difficulty during ED UGNBs and explore patient-, provider-, and block-level factors associated with difficult procedures.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of the multicenter National Ultrasound-guided neRVE (NURVE) Registry, including UGNBs performed at 11 U.S. EDs from January 2022 through December 2023. This interval was selected to capture the complete initial two-year period of NURVE Registry data collection. Technical difficulty was defined by operator self-report using a standardized registry question. Mixed-effects logistic regression with institution as a random intercept was used to evaluate factors associated with technical difficulty.
RESULTS: Among 1725 UGNBs included in the analysis, 82 (4.8%) were reported as technically difficult. In unadjusted analyses, technical difficulty was more common among patients with obesity and differed by block group. In mixed-effects regression, body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m² was independently associated with increased odds of technical difficulty compared with BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m² (odds ratio [OR] 2.94, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 1.58-5.47). Compared with fascia iliaca/femoral region blocks, truncal plane blocks (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.05-0.87), distal upper-extremity blocks (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.94), and distal lower-extremity blocks (OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.10-0.99) were associated with lower odds of technical difficulty. Provider role and prior procedural experience were not significantly associated with difficulty in unadjusted analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Technical difficulty during ED UGNBs was uncommon. Obesity was the most consistent predictor of procedural difficulty, while block-group associations were more modest and influenced by site-level factors. These findings may help inform procedural planning and UGNB training initiatives.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Concerns and Factors Associated With Anesthetic Preference: A Cross-Sectional Study on Why Patients Choose General Over Regional Anesthesia.
articles.abstract: Background Regional anesthesia (RA) offers established perioperative benefits, yet many patients choose general anesthesia (GA) even when RA is a clinically appropriate option. Understanding patients' specific concerns and other factors associated with anesthetic preference may help improve patient-centered preoperative communication and shared decision-making. Methods This cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study included 276 adult patients scheduled for elective surgery at a public general hospital in Greece. Before preoperative anesthetic consultation, participants reported their anesthetic preference, previous RA experience, and sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Patients who preferred GA identified their concerns regarding RA from 11 predefined items. Factors independently associated with anesthetic preference were assessed using multivariable binary logistic regression. Results Of 350 eligible patients invited, 276 completed the survey (response rate = 78.9%); 65.9% (n = 182) preferred GA and 34.1% (n = 94) preferred RA. Male sex (odds ratio {OR} = 7.12; 95% confidence interval {CI}: 3.13-16.22; p < 0.001) and previous RA experience (OR = 3.50; 95% CI: 1.70-7.19; p = 0.001) were independently associated with RA preference. Surgical specialty, education, and employment status were also independently associated with anesthetic preference. Among patients preferring GA (n = 182), the most frequently reported concerns were hearing events during surgery (90.1%, n = 164), seeing the procedure (77.5%, n = 141), and experiencing intraoperative pain (73.1%, n = 133). Concerns about permanent paralysis (40.7%, n = 74) and back injury (40.1%, n = 73) were less frequent. Among respondents to the information-related items (n = 202), 31.2% (n = 63) reported having heard that RA could cause complications, most commonly from relatives (66.7%, n = 42), while 95.5% (n = 193) wanted their anesthesiologist to address their questions about RA. Conclusions GA was preferred by approximately two-thirds of elective surgical patients despite RA being a clinically viable option. The leading concerns regarding RA centered on the awareness of the surgical environment and intraoperative pain rather than rare neurological complications. Anesthetic preference was also independently associated with previous RA experience and several patient characteristics. Identifying and directly addressing these concerns during preoperative counseling may support more informed and individualized anesthetic decision-making.

articles.title: Evaluating the Clinical Impact of an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Program: A Quality Improvement and Practice Change Study at Al-hada Armed Forces Hospital.
articles.abstract: Introduction Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) is a proven perioperative framework designed to attenuate surgical stress and accelerate recovery. However, translating global ERAS evidence into localized practice requires bridging significant implementation gaps and modifying entrenched clinical habits. This study evaluates the clinical and operational impact of a multidisciplinary ERAS implementation model for laparoscopic cholecystectomy at a tertiary military hospital. ​Methods This quasi-experimental pre- and post-intervention quality improvement study at Alhada Armed Forces Hospital evaluated an ERAS protocol for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy (aged 18-80 years, ASA I-III), comparing prospective post-intervention (n = 120) and retrospective baseline (n = 88) cohorts. Excluded patients included emergency cases, severe comorbidities, cognitive impairment, or open conversions (30 excluded; 208 analyzed). Interventions spanned three plan-do-study-act (PDSA) cycles featuring opioid-reducing analgesia, standardized perioperative care, point-of-care checklists, and protocol-driven discharge. Clinical, economic, and satisfaction outcomes were extracted from hospital databases and SMS surveys, then analyzed in jamovi via Student's t-tests and Chi-square (χ2 ) tests (p < 0.05). ​Results Among 208 analyzed patients (baseline: n = 88; ERAS: n = 120), ERAS implementation increased checklist compliance to 100.0% (mean: 72.1% ± 38.7%). Ambulatory day-case success increased from 0.0% to 27.5% (33/120; p < 0.0001), while mean length of stay (LOS) dropped from 4.33 ± 0.89 to 2.67 ± 1.15 days (t = 3.96, p = 0.0007). Implementation of the ERAS protocol saved 231 inpatient bed days across 77 patients, achieving total cost savings of Saudi Riyal (SAR) 346,500 [$92,400 United States Dollars (USD)]. Postoperative complications were recorded in only one patient (1/120; 0.83%), with zero surgical site infections (0.0%). Patient satisfaction averaged 89.4% ± 3.3%, with a 30-day readmission rate of 0.83% (1/120). Conclusion Integrating a file-embedded ERAS checklist into routine multidisciplinary care safely reduces LOS and expands same-day discharge for laparoscopic cholecystectomy without sacrificing safety, outcomes, or patient satisfaction. By maximizing existing infrastructure and structured patient education, this low-cost model provides a practical framework for healthcare systems seeking to optimize ambulatory capacity and operational efficiency.

articles.title: Cerebral Embolization During Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation is Linked to Early Right Ventricular Failure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of air introduction into the left ventricular (LV) cavity and right coronary artery (RCA) during durable left ventricular assist device (dLVAD) implantation on the incidence of early right heart failure (RHF) within 7 postoperative days, specifically to investigate whether the quantity of air emboli, as detected by transcranial Doppler (TCD) monitoring, correlates with an increased risk of early RHF.
DESIGN: This single-center retrospective analysis involved intraoperative TCD monitoring of the middle cerebral arteries. Between January 2021 and April 2024, 62 cases of dLVAD implantations (all of them HeartMate3) were performed, 59 of which were eligible for inclusion in the statistical analysis. TCD recorded high-intensity transient signals (HITS), indicative of emboli. Based on the number of intraoperative HITS, 2 categories were created: minimal-mild (<2,500 HITS; group A) and moderate-severe (>2,500 HITS; group B).
SETTING: A single-center retrospective chart review.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients who received dLVAD implantation under TCD surveillance.
INTERVENTIONS: A retrospective chart review of patients receiving standard of care; no study interventions were performed.
MEASUREMENTS & MAIN RESULTS: In group A, 9 out of 40 patients (22.5%) experienced early postoperative RHF. In contrast, 14 out of 19 patients (73.7%) in Group B developed early RHF, indicating a strong statistical significance (P < .001). A statistically significant difference was also demonstrated in postoperative 30-day all-cause mortality; there were no deaths (0% mortality) in group A, whereas in group B, 4 out of 19 patients (21.1%) died within 30 days (p = 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: The presence of >2,500 intraoperative HITS was correlated with a higher incidence of complications in the postoperative period. TCD monitoring during dLVAD implantation may be a potential tool to monitor for RV dysfunction.

articles.title: Revisiting extended-criteria donors in lung transplantation.
articles.abstract: Lung transplantation (LTx) is an established life-saving therapy for patients with end-stage lung disease. Despite continuous improvements in surgical technique, immunosuppressive regimen and perioperative care, organ shortage remains the principal limitation to broader access. Historically, conservative donor criteria have contributed to the underutilization of potentially transplantable lungs. Over time, lungs from donors outside standard criteria - commonly referred to as extended-criteria donors (ECD) - have been increasingly accepted. This narrative review evaluates contemporary evidence on the experience and outcomes of specific ECD lungs in LTx. We focus first on typically defined ECD including older donor age, smoking history and substance abuse, oxygenation status, radiological abnormalities, microbial colonization, donation after circulatory death, and extended ischemic times. Subsequently, we look at specific donor traits tempering them as emerging ECD. Finally, we evaluate the role and potential benefits of novel preservation and assessment techniques such as controlled hypothermic storage and ex vivo lung perfusion. While accumulating data support the safe use of ECD lungs under appropriate conditions, a paradigm shift toward individualized donor assessment rather than rigid thresholds is mandatory to sustainably expand the donor pool and reduce waitlist mortality.

articles.title: Periprocedural management of patients with hereditary angioedema undergoing coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.abstract: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare, potentially life-threatening genetic disorder caused by dysregulation of the kallikrein-kinin pathway and excessive bradykinin generation. Although advances in targeted therapies have substantially improved disease control and prognosis, patients with HAE remain vulnerable to procedure-related attacks triggered by tissue trauma, psychological stress, and airway manipulation. As the HAE population ages and cardiovascular comorbidities become increasingly prevalent, interventional cardiologists are increasingly likely to encounter patients requiring coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The periprocedural management of HAE in the catheterization laboratory presents unique challenges. Invasive vascular procedures may potentially precipitate angioedema attacks, while urgent coronary revascularization must not be delayed because of concerns related to HAE. Current evidence is largely derived from expert consensus, perioperative recommendations, and limited clinical experience rather than dedicated cardiovascular studies. This review summarizes the current understanding of HAE pathophysiology relevant to invasive cardiology, discusses available prophylactic and on-demand treatment strategies, and proposes a practical management algorithm for patients undergoing coronary angiography and PCI. Particular emphasis is placed on risk stratification, short-term prophylaxis, procedural planning, airway management, and multidisciplinary collaboration. Adoption of standardized institutional protocols may improve procedural safety and clinical outcomes in this unique patient population. The review also incorporates the recommendations of the recently published 2025 World Allergy Organization Guidelines, providing an updated framework for individualized periprocedural management in contemporary invasive cardiology practice.

articles.title: Prognostic value of preprocedural neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio for in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced ejection fraction undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) represent a particularly vulnerable subgroup with elevated perioperative and long-term mortality. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), an integrated marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, has not been specifically evaluated as a prognostic marker in this population.
AIM: To examine the prognostic value of preprocedural NPAR for in-hospital and overall (all-cause) mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study enrolled 169 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI between June 2020 and January 2026. Preprocedural NPAR was derived from blood samples obtained within 24 h before the procedure. In-hospital and overall mortality were assessed using logistic and Cox regression models with limited covariate adjustment.
RESULTS: Using an NPAR cut-off of 20.74, patients with elevated NPAR exhibited higher rates of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and both in-hospital and overall mortality, along with higher C-reactive protein and BNP levels and lower haemoglobin, albumin, postprocedural LVEF, and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) values. NPAR remained associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for chronic kidney disease or TAPSE and was also associated with overall mortality in multivariable Cox regression analyses. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly reduced survival among patients with elevated NPAR.
CONCLUSIONS: After limited multivariable adjustment, preprocedural NPAR was associated with both in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI. As a simple marker of inflammatory and nutritional burden, NPAR may provide additional prognostic information and complement preprocedural risk assessment, although its incremental value beyond established risk models and other biomarkers remains uncertain.

articles.title: Sevoflurane pretreatment attenuates hypoxia/reoxygenation injury in cardiomyocytes by regulating the GAS6-AS1/miR-483-3p/IGF1 axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the role and mechanism of the lncRNA GAS6-AS1 in sevoflurane (Sev)-mediated cardio-protection against hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) injury in cardiomyocytes.
METHODS: AC16 cardiomyocytes were subjected to H/R injury (6 h hypoxia/24 h reoxygenation) and pretreated with Sev. RT‑qPCR was used to detect the level of GAS6-AS1, miR-483-3p, and IGF1. CCK‑8 and flow cytometry were applied to measure cell proliferation and apoptosis. ELISA determined myocardial injury markers, inflammatory factors, and oxidative stress levels. The targeting relationships were verified by dual‑luciferase reporter and RIP assays.
RESULTS: GAS6-AS1 and IGF1 were downregulated, while miR-483-3p was upregulated in H/R‑treated cardiomyocytes. Sev pretreatment upregulated GAS6-AS1 and IGF1, downregulated miR-483-3p, promoted proliferation, inhibited apoptosis, and reduced myocardial damage, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Silencing GAS6-AS1 reversed the cardioprotective effects of Sev. GAS6-AS1 directly targeted miR-483-3p, which in turn directly inhibited IGF1. Inhibiting miR-483-3p restored IGF1 expression and reversed the detrimental effects of GAS6-AS1 silencing.
CONCLUSION: Sev pretreatment protects cardiomyocytes against H/R injury by upregulating the GAS6-AS1/miR-483-3p/IGF1 axis, which offers a novel molecular target for perioperative cardio-protection.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Outcomes and organ protection effects of perioperative precision venous access management strategies in patients undergoing complex hepatobiliary, pancreatic, splenic and abdominal great vascular surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: With continuous advances in surgical techniques, complex hepatobiliary pancreatic (HPB) and vascular surgical procedures are increasingly being applied clinically. Whilst such operations can improve patient prognosis, the extensive surgical trauma and severe physiological disruption they entail trigger intense physiological stress responses, significantly heightening the risk of perioperative organ injury. This has become a critical clinical challenge that impedes postoperative recovery and exacerbates the burden on healthcare systems. Current conventional fluid management strategies in clinical practice are primarily guided by static haemodynamic parameters. They lack dynamic adaptability to individual patient physiological reserves and surgical stress levels, readily leading to inadequate or excessive volume resuscitation, thereby exacerbating organ dysfunction. Precision Venous Access Management (PVAM) during the perioperative period represents an innovative therapeutic strategy integrating advanced haemodynamic monitoring, algorithm-guided therapy, and specialised access support. This approach overcomes the limitations of conventional management, offering a new direction for individualised perioperative care. This meta-analysis aims to systematically evaluate the impact of perioperative precision venous access management (PVAM) on organ-specific complication rates and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing complex hepatobiliary, pancreatic, and vascular surgery. It seeks to clarify its organ-protective value and clinical feasibility, providing high-quality evidence-based support for the clinical implementation of this strategy in high-risk surgical patients.
METHODS: Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases, with the search cutoff date set at 15 April 2024. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective cohort studies comparing perioperative precision venous access management (PVAM) (integrating advanced haemodynamic monitoring, goal-directed therapy, and specialised access) with standard treatment in adults undergoing complex hepatobiliary-pancreatic or major vascular surgery were included. Primary outcomes comprised acute kidney injury (AKI) and clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF). Data were synthesised using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies involving 2,158 patients were included. Perioperative precision venous access management (PVAM) significantly reduced the incidence of AKI (RR=0.61, 95% CI 0.49-0.76; P<0.001) and CR-POPF (RR=0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.88; P=0.002), while also reducing the overall complication rate (RR=0.76, 95% CI 0.65-0.89) and shortening hospital stay (MD=-2.4 days, 95% CI -3.8 to -1.0).
CONCLUSIONS: The perioperative precision venous access management (PVAM) strategy demonstrates significant renal and pancreatic protective effects, promoting postoperative recovery in patients undergoing complex hepatobiliary, pancreatic, and vascular surgery, thereby supporting its integration into clinical practice.

articles.title: Assessing women's knowledge on the use of pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods of pain relief during labour at Tema General Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In many low-resource settings like Ghana, labour pain is often endured without adequate relief due to limited access to information and services. Understanding women's knowledge is crucial for improving maternal care and empowering women during childbirth.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 215 postpartum women at Tema General Hospital in Ghana. Using interviewer-administered questionnaires, we assessed knowledge of pain relief methods, identified information sources, and explored perceived benefits. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and univariate logistic regression.
RESULTS: Significant knowledge gaps were identified, with only 55% of women aware of any pain relief methods. Education was the strongest knowledge associated factor; women with tertiary education had nearly three times the odds of adequate knowledge compared to those with primary education. The internet (15.3%) was the most common information source, surpassing healthcare providers (midwives and doctors combined: <16%). While epidural anesthesia was recognized by 48.3%, awareness of low-intervention methods like upright birthing positions was critically low (4.2%). Women viewed pharmacological methods primarily for pain minimization and non-pharmacological approaches for safety, indicating limited understanding of holistic benefits.
CONCLUSIONS: Knowledge of labour pain relief is strongly influenced by education and often sourced outside clinical settings. To address these gaps, we recommend restructuring antenatal education to be more inclusive, training providers in proactive counseling, and leveraging digital tools for credible information. Integrating pain relief as a core component of respectful maternity care is essential for improving childbirth experiences in Ghana and similar contexts.

articles.title: Serious Adverse Events in Adult ICU Patients: A Substudy of the PATIENCE Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. We aimed to provide detailed epidemiological data on predefined serious adverse events (SAEs) in a cohort of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without prokinetic treatment. We hypothesised that all predefined SAEs would occur in both patients treated and those not treated with prokinetic agents, and that a higher number of SAEs would occur among patients treated with prokinetic agents for more than three consecutive days.
METHODS: This substudy of the inception cohort study "Prokinetic agents in adult intensive care unit patients" included acutely admitted adult ICU patients. The prokinetic agents assessed (exposures) were erythromycin, metoclopramide, domperidone, and prucalopride. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least one episode of five pre-specified SAEs during ICU stay (cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, vomiting with aspiration, diarrhoea, extrapyramidal symptoms). Secondary outcomes were (1) proportion of patients experiencing each SAE, (2) the proportion of patients experiencing any of the SAEs after prokinetic treatment stratified by longest consecutive treatment duration, (3) time from index ICU admission to first SAE and (4) time from prokinetic initiation to first SAE. All analyses were descriptive, summarising SAE proportions and timing overall and according to prokinetic exposure.
RESULTS: Among 1440 adult ICU patients, 710 SAEs occurred in 354 patients (24.6%), most commonly cardiac arrhythmias (199/1440, 13.8%). Across the exposure groups, the proportion of patients experiencing one or more SAEs ranged from 23.0% to 42.5%. Among patients treated with prokinetic agents for > 3 consecutive days, 14/59 (23.7%) experienced a SAE, which was similar to the proportion observed among patients not receiving prokinetic agents (291/1.253, 23.2%). Most SAEs occurred on median Day 2 after ICU admission and on median Day 3 after prokinetic initiation.
CONCLUSION: One in four adult ICU patients experienced at least one SAE, with cardiac arrhythmias being the most frequent. Among patients receiving prokinetic agents, the proportion experiencing one or more SAEs ranged from 23.0% to 42.5% across treatment groups. The findings from this study may help inform the design of a future clinical trial.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This analysis presents reported serious adverse event observed in an ICU trial cohort assessing gastrointestinal prokinetic drug effects. Serious adverse events were reported frequently in both the drug treatment groups and the comparison (no prokinetic drug) group. Types of serious adverse events reported are presented.

articles.title: Modulating Perioperative Ventricular Excitability.
articles.abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Ventricular arrhythmogenesis is a dynamic interplay among an arrhythmogenic substrate, myocardial electrophysiologic properties, modifying factors, and triggering factors. Imbalances in the autonomic nervous system can lead to increased myocardial excitability, which is a major contributor to the pathophysiology of ventricular tachyarrhythmias. Myocardial excitability and ventricular arrhythmogenesis are modulated perioperatively through hemodynamic and physiologic management, anesthetic agents, or regional anesthetic and surgical techniques.

articles.title: Ecological Momentary Assessments of Daily Pain Experiences in Bothersome and High-Impact Chronic Pain.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-impact chronic pain (HICP), defined as persistent pain substantially limiting daily activities, affects millions of adults and poses a public health challenge. However, as prior knowledge comes largely from retrospective self-report measures, little is known about how HICP manifests in daily life.
METHODS: This study used the comprehensive Ecological Momentary Assessment of pain (cEMAp) instrument to assess pain-related experiences four times daily over 7 days in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal pain. Using the Graded Chronic Pain Scale-Revised, we compared individuals with HICP (n = 66) with bothersome chronic pain (n = 41), a group with similar pain frequency but less interference with daily activities. Each prompt assessed pain intensity, interference, cognitions, behaviours, coping strategies, and pain characteristics over the preceding 2 h.
RESULTS: Both groups reported similar pain intensity levels, but the HICP group reported more frequent interference with physical, mental, and social activities. No group differences emerged in daily mood or negative pain-related cognitions. Exploratory analyses suggested that many daily experiences were similar across groups, with differences observed in selected pain qualities, coping strategies, and pain behaviours. Analyses of response distributions showed some similarity across groups in many experiences.
CONCLUSIONS: The most consistent distinction between the groups was interference frequency, consistent with the operationalization of HICP as pain that disrupts daily functioning, while several other pain-related experiences were similar across groups. cEMAp data complement traditional retrospective assessment by providing a more detailed view of biopsychosocial aspects of chronic pain in everyday life.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Prior understanding of high-impact chronic pain (HICP) has largely relied on retrospective measures. Using the comprehensive Ecological Momentary Assessment of pain (cEMAp) instrument, we found that HICP was distinguished primarily by more frequent interference with daily activities rather than greater pain intensity. Our findings also reveal similarities and differences across other pain-related experiences, highlighting the value of multidimensional real-world assessment beyond pain intensity alone.

articles.title: Conceptual model of multidisciplinary shared decision-making for high-risk surgical patients: a Delphi study.
articles.abstract: High-risk patients need to carefully consider the risks and benefits of surgery. Shared decision-making is a collaborative process that enables patients and clinicians to share information and weigh up options and preferences. There is limited evidence about how best to organise the participation of the full range of healthcare professionals who can contribute to such decision-making processes. We conducted a Delphi study with a panel of experts to clarify how, and for what purposes, different healthcare professionals can contribute to shared decision-making with high-risk surgical patients. Consensus was reached on a conceptual model of multidisciplinary shared decision-making. The model recommends that interactions between patients, supported by family members and informal carers, and healthcare professionals are organised around five areas: options for management and treatment; patient values, goals, and preferences; comprehensive needs assessment; social context and home environment; and perioperative preparations. Experts agreed that achieving multidisciplinary shared decision-making in practice requires four key facilitators: early identification of patients with complex decision-making needs, availability of specialist expertise and support, sufficient time for discussion and decision-making, and coordination and information sharing between interactions. This model organises multidisciplinary involvement in high-risk surgical shared decision-making into five conceptually distinct and operationally interdependent areas. The model has the potential to inform practice and enhance opportunities for shared decision-making for high-risk surgical patients and their multidisciplinary teams.

articles.title: Hepatic dysfunction and recovery after remimazolam-based general anaesthesia: a prospective cohort study.
Anterior inferior psoas epimysial injection: a cadaveric feasibility study of an anterior pathway to the lumbar plexus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior lumbar plexus block provides reliable anesthesia but is technically challenging and associated with risks related to deep paraspinal needle placement. Existing anterior approaches provide variable lumbar plexus coverage, and the anatomical pathways by which newer iliopsoas-based techniques reach individual plexus branches remain incompletely defined. This feasibility study evaluated whether an anterior inferior, trans-psoas injection targeting the posterior epimysium of the psoas muscle could provide a direct anterior pathway toward the lumbar plexus.
METHODS: A cadaveric dye study was performed on four GreenMBalmed cadaver hips. Under ultrasound guidance in the supine position, 30 mL of 0.1% methylene blue was injected in a caudal-to-cranial trajectory along the posterior epimysium of the psoas. Layered dissections assessed dye spread relative to the psoas, thoracolumbar fascia, and lumbar plexus nerves.
RESULTS: Cranial and anterior fascial spread was observed in all four hips, with dye tracking anterior to the quadratus lumborum and extending toward the 12th rib and perinephric region. Dense staining of the lateral femoral cutaneous and iliohypogastric nerves was seen in all hips. The femoral nerve demonstrated predominantly moderate staining, while obturator nerve involvement was variable. Minimal intramuscular staining of the psoas was observed, suggesting preferential spread along fascial planes.
CONCLUSIONS: Anterior inferior injection along the posterior epimysium of the psoas produced spread toward lumbar plexus regions in all four hips, in this limited cadaveric sample, suggesting this plane warrants further investigation. Clinical studies are needed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of this approach.

articles.title: Processed electroencephalogram-guided anesthesia and its impact on postoperative delirium and perioperative efficiency: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Processed electroencephalography (pEEG) provides quantitative indices for monitoring anesthetic depth and is recommended in international guidelines. Prior meta-analyses have assessed EEG-guided anesthesia but none have evaluated available evidence stratified by pEEG technology.
METHODS: We performed a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in adults undergoing surgical, endoscopic, or dental procedures comparing pEEG-guided with non-pEEG-guided anesthesia. Primary outcomes were anesthetic drug use (TIVA and volatile agents) and postoperative delirium (POD ≤10 days). Secondary outcomes were extubation time, wake-up time, time to orientation, and post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) length of stay. Searches (PubMed Central, MEDLINE) were conducted on 11 April 2025; the protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251067170). Random-effects models produced standardized mean differences (SMD), mean differences (MD), and risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI).
RESULTS: Eighty-seven RCTs (30,611 patients; 13,586 pEEG; 17,025 non-pEEG) were included. pEEG significantly reduced propofol use (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.74 to -0.10; p = 0.01) and volatile anesthetic use (SMD -1.27, 95% CI -1.88 to -0.66; p < 0.01). The risk of POD decreased by 27% (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.84; p < 0.01). Efficiency outcomes favored pEEG: extubation time (MD -2.90 min, 95% CI -3.64 to -2.16; p < 0.01), wake-up time (MD -1.83 min, 95% CI -2.42 to -1.25; p < 0.01), time to orientation (MD -4.11 min, 95% CI -6.99 to -1.23; p < 0.01), and PACU length of stay (MD -2.81 min, 95% CI -4.66 to -0.96; p < 0.01). Subgroup analyses suggested benefits were most consistently observed for BIS; estimates for Entropy and SEDLine were less precise due to fewer studies. Heterogeneity was substantial for several outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Across 87 RCTs, pEEG-guided monitoring utilizing multiple device types improved perioperative efficiency and reduced POD compared with not using pEEG. Evidence is strongest for BIS; further well-reported trials are needed to delineate device-specific effects.

articles.title: Patients as Partners: A New Article Type in Anesthesia & Analgesia Extending Perspectives in Practice and Research.
Pain That Falls Through the Gap: Recognition, Uncertainty, and Voice During Caesarean Delivery.
From failed to failing epidural: an evolution of concepts around the management of labor epidural analgesia for a better maternal comfort and safety.
articles.abstract: Labor epidural analgesia has markedly improved in quality and safety over the past two decades. However, maintaining consistent analgesic efficacy throughout labor remains challenging, and inadequate blocks continue to be encountered in routine practice. In this Experts' opinion, we examine the spectrum of failed and failing epidural analgesia and identify critical periods during labor associated with an increased risk of block inadequacy. We propose pragmatic definitions for onset failure, breakthrough pain, failing epidural, and failed conversion to surgical anesthesia, based on the most recent evidence. We contend that a clear conceptual framework is essential for obstetric anesthesia teams to anticipate, recognize, and manage inadequate epidural analgesia effectively. We therefore outline practical, evidence-informed strategies for prevention and treatment. A structured and anticipatory approach to epidural management may improve maternal comfort and safety, while supporting a more patient-centered model of care.

articles.title: NeuroPOCUS: what every intensivist should know.
articles.abstract: Ultrasound has become a paramount tool in critical care. Nowadays, it is common for intensivists to use ultrasound to evaluate cardiac function, pulmonary alterations, guide vascular access, and monitor systemic venous congestion through ultrasound-based techniques. However, the brain remains often overlooked in the point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) practice. NeuroPOCUS encompasses cerebral hemodynamic assessment, mainly at the level of the middle cerebral artery, as well as evaluation of hydrocephalus, hematoma size, midline shift and intracranial pressure. Most of these are basic or basic-plus skills. In this manuscript, we present a concise guide on what every intensivist should know about NeuroPOCUS, including basic key concepts, technique and several real illustrative figures.

articles.title: Macroscopic dye distribution after classical versus extrafascial interscalene block: an exploratory comparative cadaveric pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extrafascial injection has been proposed as a phrenic nerve-sparing alternative for interscalene brachial plexus block (ISB), but the anatomical basis for the reported reduction in phrenic nerve involvement remains incompletely characterized. We compared macroscopic dye distribution patterns between classical ISB and extrafascial injection in paired cadaveric specimens.
METHODS: In five formalin-fixed cadavers, bilateral ultrasound-guided injections with indigo carmine (20 ml per side) were performed. A classical ISB and extrafascial injection were applied to contralateral sides. Three blinded anatomists independently assessed staining intensity (deep, light, none) in real time during dissection.
RESULTS: Both techniques produced deep staining of C5-6 roots, upper trunk, and suprascapular nerve in 5/5 specimens. The phrenic nerve was stained in all 10 specimens (5/5 in each group); deep staining occurred in 4/5 (80%) classical ISB specimens and 0/5 extrafascial specimens, though all 5 extrafascial specimens showed only light staining. Spread to infraclavicular cords was limited with both techniques.
CONCLUSIONS: Dye reached the C5-6 roots, upper trunk, suprascapular nerve, and phrenic nerve in all 5 specimens of both groups. Phrenic nerve staining intensity was lower with the extrafascial technique than with classical ISB in 4 of 5 paired cadavers, identical in 1 of 5, and never higher. The functional and clinical implications of this intensity difference cannot be determined from the present anatomical model and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046).
CONCLUSIONS: While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

articles.title: Association of epilepsy with utilization and acute outcomes following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Despite increased recognition of cardiovascular morbidity in patients with epilepsy, the influence of epilepsy on outcomes following cardiac operations remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: Adults (≥18 years) undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), valve, or aortic procedures were identified in the 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Epilepsy was identified using validated International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) diagnosis codes (G40.x) present on a prior inpatient admission or as a non-primary diagnosis on the index admission; patients with epilepsy coded as the primary admitting diagnosis were excluded to avoid misclassifying acute presentations as preexisting disease. Entropy balancing across prespecified covariates (age, sex, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, operation type, elective admission status, insurance type) was followed by mixed-effects regression with hospital-level random effects to assess the association of epilepsy with in-hospital mortality, postoperative complications, non-home discharge, and resource utilization including 30-day readmissions.
RESULTS: Of 1,932,935 adult patients undergoing cardiac operations, 27,325 (1.4%) had a preexisting diagnosis of epilepsy. On adjusted analysis, epilepsy was associated with significantly higher odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.35-1.59), blood transfusion (AOR: 1.24; 95% CI: 1.20-1.29), infectious (AOR: 1.34; 95% CI: 1.27-1.40), and respiratory (AOR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.26-1.37) complications. Epilepsy was also linked with prolonged hospitalization (β + 2.32 days; 95% CI: 2.12-2.47), greater costs (β + $9,121; 95% CI: 8,292-9,951), higher odds of non-home discharge (AOR: 2.01; 95% CI: 1.93-2.10), and 30-day non-elective readmission (AOR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.21-1.34).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing cardiac operations, epilepsy was associated with increased risk of mortality, complications, and resource utilization. These findings demonstrate the need for enhanced perioperative strategies tailored to mitigate adverse events in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Shunt outcomes following multidisciplinary ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement with general surgery involvement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS) placement is a common neurosurgical procedure, but the impact of general surgery (GS) participation during distal catheter insertion remains uncertain. The authors evaluated whether same-day abdominal access procedures during VPS placement are associated with improved 90-day shunt-related outcomes.
METHODS: The authors performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX network. Patients with a first recorded VPS procedure were identified using ICD-10 Procedure Coding System codes and stratified by the presence or absence of concurrent abdominal access procedures on the index date. Propensity score matching was used to balance demographics, comorbidities, abdominal conditions, prior CSF diversion, and perioperative factors. Outcomes from 1 to 90 days included VPS reoperation (primary), conversion to alternative CSF diversion, mechanical shunt complications, and other complications, including mortality, infection, epilepsy or seizures, wound disruption, and venous thromboembolism or pulmonary embolism.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 8955 patients were included in each cohort with balanced baseline characteristics. At 90 days, the GS involvement cohort had lower VPS reoperation rates (2.68% vs 4.56%, p < 0.0001) and fewer mechanical shunt complications (8.01% vs 10.85%, p < 0.0001) than the neurosurgery-only cohort. Conversion to alternative CSF diversion was also less frequent in the GS involvement cohort (0.85% vs 1.71%, p < 0.0001). Mortality (5.30% and 5.51%, respectively; p = 0.524), infection (5.25% and 4.85%, respectively; p = 0.185), epilepsy or seizures (14.92% and 15.21%, respectively; p = 0.664), and wound disruption (2.20% and 1.80%, respectively; p = 0.080) were similar between the GS involvement and neurosurgery-only cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: In a multicenter cohort, VPS placement with concurrent abdominal GS procedures was associated with lower 90-day VPS reoperation, conversion to alternative CSF diversion, and mechanical shunt complications, without increases in mortality, infection, or other 90-day complications. These findings support consideration of a multidisciplinary approach to distal catheter placement when GS expertise is available.

articles.title: How to '10-for-10': a qualitative research protocol to determine best practice use of the 10-for-10 principle.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Critical situations in clinical medicine are associated with high cognitive load, time pressure and an increased risk to patient safety. Crisis Resource Management aims to address these challenges through skills such as communication, situational awareness, task management, team performance and decision-making. The ‘10-for-10 principle’, which encourages clinicians to pause briefly to reassess and plan ahead, is widely taught in simulation-based training and applied in clinical practice throughout German-speaking countries. Despite its widespread use, the principle lacks a clear scientific definition and has not been systematically investigated. This study aims to develop an empirically informed conceptual understanding of this principle based on expert perspectives as an early exploration, a foundation for future research and educational model development.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This qualitative study will use 15–20 semistructured expert interviews to explore current applications, variations, structural components and perceived barriers related to the 10-for-10 principle, aiming to provide an early exploration of the principle across German-speaking countries. Participants will be purposively sampled from clinical and simulation-based education contexts. Data collection and analysis will be conducted concurrently using the iterative content-structuring qualitative approach as described by Kuckartz and Rädiker. Deductive codes derived from existing conceptual descriptions will be combined with inductively developed codes informed by expert narratives to identify core categories across interviews. Findings will be synthesised into a taxonomy organised by expert-perceived relevance and frequency of reference.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval has been obtained from the Ethics Committee of Charité—Universitätsmedizin Berlin (EA 1/093/25). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. Data will be pseudonymised and handled in accordance with institutional and data protection regulations. Study findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and conference presentations and are intended to inform future empirical research and the development of simulation-based educational approaches related to the 10-for-10 principle.

articles.title: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve.
DESIGN: Modified Delphi-based global consensus study.
PARTICIPANTS: International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases.
METHODS: A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. Experts responded anonymously to statements assessing consensus and to revised items addressing indications, contraindications, timing, preoperative workup, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative management. Results are reported using item-specific denominators because occasional non-response occurred across the survey items.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement among the experts. Agreement between 60% and 69.9% was considered to be near consensus.
RESULTS: The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.

articles.title: Therapeutic play in pediatric nursing: a bibliometric map of a persistent core and diversifying research fronts.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To map research performance, collaboration structure, intellectual foundations, conceptual themes, research fronts, and recent thematic signals of therapeutic play research in pediatric nursing using Scopus data.
DESIGN AND METHODS: A descriptive bibliometric analysis used a final Scopus search on 27 August 2026. After eligibility screening and removal of one duplicate/versioned record, 145 unique articles and reviews published from 1974 to 2026 were analyzed. Performance indicators and VOSviewer 1.6.21 were used to examine collaboration, cited-reference co-citation, keyword co-occurrence, and document bibliographic coupling. A post-hoc descriptive analysis compared keyword prevalence across three periods.
RESULTS: The corpus comprised 145 publications, including 71 (49.0%) published during 2020-2026; the 2026 count was partial. Institutional and country collaboration showed limited connectivity. Intellectual and conceptual structures remained centered on therapeutic play, pediatric nursing, perioperative preparation, coping, and psychosocial adaptation. Bibliographic coupling identified eight research fronts spanning procedural, family-related, educational, self-management, professional, implementation, and nursing-application domains. Therapeutic play remained a persistent core. Fear and pain showed the clearest recent thematic intensification, whereas anxiety was already established.
CONCLUSION: Therapeutic-play research in pediatric nursing shows continuity alongside diversification around a persistent core.
PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: This map can help pediatric nurses and researchers identify established and developing research areas, prioritize cross-setting and implementation research, and distinguish bibliographic prominence from evidence of clinical effectiveness.

articles.title: Iliohypogastric and Ilioinguinal Nerve Block for Awake ECPella Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Nonpostcardiotomy Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.abstract: In pediatric cardiogenic shock, endotracheal intubation may carry a high risk of cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction. This single-center retrospective case series (2020-2025) evaluated the feasibility, safety, and outcomes of ultrasound (US)-guided ilioinguinal-iliohypogastric (IhIG) nerve blocks (0.05-0.1 ml/kg of 0.25% ropivacaine) under light sedation to facilitate awake venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella (ECPella) surgical cannulation. Five adolescents (median age: 13 years, range: 7-17; median weight: 45 kg, range: 21-58) with nonpostcardiotomy cardiogenic shock underwent successful IhIG block placement in the pediatric intensive care unit by anesthesia-trained intensivists, followed by surgical cannulation in the catheterization laboratory. Intubation and mechanical ventilation were avoided during initial cannulation and throughout ECPella duration. Three patients required a modified chimney Y-graft for cannula placement, and two experienced local surgical bleeding. All five patients survived to hospital discharge, with three achieving direct biventricular recovery. Based on these preliminary data, US-guided IhIG nerve block seems a feasible and safe strategy for awake ECPella cannulation in selected pediatric patients, successfully avoiding high-risk invasive ventilation and general anesthesia.

articles.title: Dysphagia and feeding outcomes in paediatric patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries undergoing pulmonary artery intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major aortopulmonary collateral arteries represent a complex subgroup of CHD with unique cardiopulmonary physiology. While surgical outcomes have been well described, feeding and swallowing outcomes remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterise dysphagia prevalence and functional feeding outcomes in these paediatric patients undergoing pulmonary artery intervention.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of paediatric patients with major aortopulmonary collateral arteries at a tertiary paediatric cardiac centre between January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2025.
