This narrative review evaluates drug selection, safety principles, and emerging pharmacological trends in PSA outside the operating room, with particular attention to the nonanesthesiologist provider model. Midazolam combined with fentanyl or ketamine remains the evidence-based foundation for nonanesthesiologist PSA. Ketamine's dissociative profile preserves airway reflexes, spontaneous ventilation, and hemodynamic stability while providing reliable analgesia. Propofol and dexmedetomidine are unsuitable for nonanesthesiologist use: propofol carries the risk of irreversible transition to general anesthesia without a reversal agent, and dexmedetomidine is associated with significant bradycardia (odds ratio [OR]: 3.60; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.29-5.67) and hypotension (OR: 1.95; 95% CI: 1.25-3.05) without pharmacological reversal. Remimazolam, an ultra-short-acting reversible benzodiazepine with organ-independent metabolism, is the most promising emerging agent. Structured credentialing, capnography monitoring, and defined rescue competencies are essential institutional requirements for safe nonanesthesiologist practice.

articles.title: Association Between Intraoperative Administration of High-Dose Insulin in the Setting of Massive Transfusion and Postoperative Hypoglycemia: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
Association between triglyceride high-density cholesterol-glucose body index and 28-day mortality in critically ill patients: a multicenter observational study in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose body mass index (TyHGB) is a novel composite indicator integrating triglyceride, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, fasting glucose and body mass index and may provide a more comprehensive assessment of systemic metabolic status than current indices. This multicenter landmark cohort study aimed to determine the association between TyHGB measured at the landmark time and 28-day mortality in patients present in the intensive care units (ICUs) at that time and to evaluate its potential utility as a prognostic marker.
METHODS: This multicenter observational cohort study included 1649 patients from 113 ICUs in China. The association between TyHGB and 28-day mortality was evaluated using three sequentially adjusted logistic regression models with restricted cubic splines: Model 1 adjusted for demographics; Model 2 further adjusted for disease severity and organ dysfunction; Model 3 additionally adjusted for therapeutic interventions. Subgroup analyses with interaction tests were conducted. Model performance was assessed by discrimination (AUC), calibration (Brier score and calibration slope) and internal validation via bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a positive association between TyHGB and 28-day mortality across fully adjusted models (P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses identified a statistically significant interaction with diabetes (P for interaction = 0.011). In the overall cohort, adding TyHGB to the base model improved AUC from 0.731 to 0.745 (ΔAUC = +0.014, P = 0.043), with significant improvements in reclassification (NRI = 0.328, P < 0.001; IDI = 0.012, P = 0.009) and model fit (LRT P < 0.001). Among diabetic patients (N = 401), TyHGB significantly improved AUC from 0.673 to 0.723 (ΔAUC = +0.050, P = 0.049; NRI = 0.515, P < 0.001; IDI = 0.041, P = 0.022). In contrast, no significant improvement was observed in non-diabetic patients (ΔAUC = +0.009, P = 0.152).
CONCLUSION: Among patients present in participating ICUs at the landmark time, higher TyHGB was associated with subsequent 28-day mortality. However, adding TyHGB to the baseline risk prediction model led to only small improvements in overall predictive performance. Findings in diabetic patients are exploratory and require further validation.

articles.title: Predictors of Postoperative Neurological Outcome After Surgical Evacuation of Traumatic Acute Subdural Hematoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic acute subdural hematoma (ASDH) is a severe consequence of traumatic brain injury and is associated with substantial mortality and neurological disability among surgically treated patients.
OBJECTIVE: To identify clinical, physiological, radiological, and operative factors associated with unfavorable three-month neurological outcome and to support risk stratification among patients undergoing surgical evacuation of traumatic ASDH.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 120 adults who underwent surgical evacuation of traumatic ASDH at Ghurki Trust Teaching Hospital, Lahore, between March 2025 and March 2026. Demographic, clinical, radiological, and perioperative variables were evaluated. The primary outcome was unfavorable neurological status at three months, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE) score of 1-4. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with unfavorable outcomes. As all participants underwent surgery and no non-operative comparison group was included, the study was designed to evaluate prognostic associations rather than the effect of surgical evacuation itself.
RESULTS: The mean age was 50.8 ± 17.9 years; 75 (62.5%) patients were male, and 45 (37.5%) were female. An unfavorable neurological outcome occurred in 74 (61.7%) patients, and three-month mortality was 21.7% (26/120). Factors independently associated with unfavorable outcome were admission Glasgow Coma Scale ≤8 (aOR 4.86, 95% CI 2.05-11.50), bilateral non-reactive pupils (aOR 4.10, 95% CI 1.13-14.86), age per 10-year increase (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.13-1.79), preoperative hypotension (aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.01-7.71), midline shift >10 mm (aOR 2.53, 95% CI 1.07-5.98), and compressed or absent basal cisterns (aOR 2.71, 95% CI 1.12-6.57). The model showed apparent good discrimination with an in-sample AUC of 0.86.
CONCLUSION: Greater neurological injury severity, bilateral nonreactive pupils, preoperative hypotension, increasing age, and CT markers of intracranial mass effect were independently associated with unfavorable three-month neurological outcome among surgically treated patients with traumatic ASDH. These findings may assist postoperative risk stratification but should not be interpreted as evidence of the effectiveness or appropriateness of surgical evacuation.

articles.title: Sequential surgery after conversion therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: Evidence, controversies, and perspectives.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often has an insidious onset. Therefore, most patients with HCC are diagnosed at intermediate-to-advanced stages, and upfront radical resection cannot be performed. Systemic regimens that combine immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with antiangiogenic targeted drugs (AATDs) have established conversion therapy followed by sequential surgery as an important research direction for initially unresectable HCC. The aim of conversion therapy is not only to achieve radiographic response and technical resectability but also to reduce tumor viability, identify patients with favorable tumor biology, and gain durable oncologic benefit. Current evidence supports the combination of ICIs and AATDs as the backbone of conversion therapy, with locoregional therapies, including transarterial chemoembolization, hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy, and stereotactic body radiotherapy, selectively integrated to address heavy intrahepatic tumor burden, control macrovascular thrombus, or treat residual viable lesions. The decision to proceed with sequential surgery should be made after a successful conversion is confirmed by a multidisciplinary evaluation incorporating tumor necrosis, hepatic functional reserve, future liver remnant volume, overall condition, perioperative drug-related risks, and patient preference. This review focuses on identifying the conversion-specific information required to guide surgical decision-making. Additionally, this study aimed to evaluate conversion rate, R0 resection, pathological response, and postoperative outcomes, explain why high objective response rates may not translate into improved postoperative survival, and provide a practical framework integrating tumor biology, hepatic reserve, perioperative risk, and patient preference.

articles.title: Renal cell carcinoma with venous tumor thrombus in young adults: Distinct clinicopathological features and shorter progression-free survival.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterize the clinicopathological features and survival outcomes of young patients with renal cell carcinoma and venous tumor thrombus (RCC-VTT).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 468 patients with RCC-VTT who underwent radical nephrectomy and thrombectomy at a high-volume center. Patients were classified as young (≤40 years, n = 43) or older (>40 years, n = 425). Propensity score matching and overlap weighting were used to improve intergroup comparability. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression were used to evaluate survival outcomes and prognostic associations.
RESULTS: Compared with older patients, young patients had larger tumors, more frequent enlarged lymph nodes, more advanced T stages, and greater perioperative transfusion requirements. They also exhibited distinct histological profiles, with higher proportions of papillary RCC and molecularly defined subtypes. Young age was associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS) in the unadjusted analysis (hazard ratio, 1.79; 95% confidence interval, 1.19-2.70) and remained associated with shorter PFS after accounting for measured clinicopathological characteristics. Across multivariable modeling approaches, young age was consistently retained in the PFS models, together with established prognostic factors, including distant metastasis and nuclear grade.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with RCC-VTT undergoing surgical treatment, young patients exhibited distinct clinicopathological characteristics and shorter PFS. These findings suggest that age-related prognostic differences may not be fully explained by conventional clinicopathological characteristics and warrant further biological investigation.

articles.title: Classical popliteal sciatic block versus Crosswise Approach to Popliteal Sciatic (CAPS) block for below-knee surgery: a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided popliteal sciatic nerve block is frequently used for below-knee surgery. The classical approach often requires lateral decubitus or prone positioning, which may be uncomfortable for patients with lower limb injuries. The Crosswise Approach to Popliteal Sciatic (CAPS) block allows the procedure to be performed with the patient supine. This randomised trial compared the classical approach with CAPS in terms of patient comfort, block performance, and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Eighty American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status I-III patients undergoing unilateral below-knee surgery were randomised to receive either a classical popliteal sciatic block in the lateral position (Group A) or a CAPS block in the supine position (Group B). All procedures were ultrasound-guided with 20 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine after lignocaine skin infiltration. All patients also received a femoral nerve block. Pain scores (verbal numerical rating scale [VNRS]) during positioning and block performance, fentanyl requirements, block performance time, sensory onset time, block success, adverse effects, and patient satisfaction were assessed.
RESULTS: All blocks were successful. Median highest pain scores were low in both groups (1.5 [classical] vs. 3.0 [CAPS] VNRS; p = 0.050). The proportion of patients reporting no pain (VNRS = 0) did not differ significantly between groups (30.0% [classical] vs. 15.0% [CAPS]; p = 0.180). Fentanyl supplementation (any dose) was required in 45% of Group A and 60% of Group B (p = 0.365). Block performance time was shorter with CAPS (10.5 min) than the classical approach (12.0 min; p = 0.002). Sensory onset time was similar (~ 20 min; p = 0.919). No major complications occurred. Transient sensory symptoms lasting more than 24 h occurred in two patients (5.0%) in Group A and one (2.5%) in Group B. Patient satisfaction remained high in both groups, with 75.0% of Group A and 67.5% of Group B rating satisfaction as 4 or 5 on a 5-point Likert scale (p = 0.120).
CONCLUSION: Both techniques provide effective and safe anaesthesia for below-knee surgery with comparable clinical outcomes. CAPS provides a logistical advantage by allowing the procedure to be performed in the supine position, which may be of value in patients unable to tolerate lateral decubitus positioning, as well as a modest reduction in procedural time (approximately 1.5 min). Either technique may be selected based on patient factors and operator preference.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07134608), registered 21 March 2025. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Combined regional anesthesia versus general anesthesia for elective shoulder arthroscopy: a prospective randomized trial of postoperative pain, with an exploratory cost analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shoulder arthroscopy causes substantial postoperative pain and operating room resource use. Randomized trials integrating postoperative pain trajectory with sensitivity-tested cost analysis are limited. We compared combined three-block regional anesthesia with standard general anesthesia in elective shoulder arthroscopy.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, parallel-group, single-center trial, 50 adults undergoing elective shoulder arthroscopy in the beach-chair position were allocated 1:1 to ultrasound-guided combined interscalene, supraclavicular, and superficial cervical plexus blocks with dexmedetomidine sedation or standard general anesthesia. The primary outcome was the resting Numeric Rating Scale (NRS, 0-10) pain score at 4 h. Pre-specified secondary outcomes included pain scores at the remaining timepoints, movement-evoked pain, patient and surgeon satisfaction, surgical duration, and intraoperative opioid consumption. Exploratory post-hoc outcomes included cumulative pain burden (area under the NRS-time curve), total perioperative cost, hemodynamic parameters, perioperative time components, rescue analgesia, postoperative nausea and vomiting, and complications.
RESULTS: Resting NRS at 4 h was lower with regional anesthesia than with general anesthesia (median 0 [IQR 0-0] vs. 4 [IQR 3-5]; Hodges-Lehmann median difference 4 points, 95% CI 3 to 4; p < 0.001) and remained lower through the 4-hour timepoint. Movement NRS increased at 12 and 24 h after block regression. Among the pre-specified secondary outcomes, patient and surgeon satisfaction was higher with regional anesthesia, while surgical duration was similar. In exploratory post-hoc analyses, the 24-hour cumulative pain burden was lower with regional anesthesia, total perioperative cost was approximately 38% lower with regional anesthesia across all sensitivity scenarios, total operating room time was shorter, and complication types differed qualitatively between groups with no significant difference in incidence detected.
CONCLUSIONS: Combined regional anesthesia provided superior early analgesia and greater patient and surgeon satisfaction than general anesthesia. Exploratory post-hoc analyses suggested lower 24-hour cumulative pain burden, lower total perioperative cost and shorter operating room utilization. These economic and operational findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials Registration No: NCT06674954, Date: October 16, 2024.

articles.title: Mechanical stability of endotracheal tube fixation: a performance comparison between two tube holders and a conventional method.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accidental extubation remains a significant clinical concern in airway management, particularly in emergency and anesthetic settings. While commercial tube holders have shown improved fixation stability over adhesive tape, cost and availability limit their use in many healthcare systems. This study introduces a newly developed Iranian endotracheal tube (ETT) holder, Persifix, and evaluates its mechanical performance relative to a commercial Locktite model and the conventional adhesive tape method.
METHODS: A total of 170 controlled tests were conducted using a human airway manikin. Three fixation methods-adhesive tape, Persifix, and Locktite tube holders-were assessed under lateral and frontal force vectors using weights of 750 g and 1000 g. Displacement was measured in both depth and lateral dimensions under dynamic (tug) and static (non-tug) conditions. Statistical analysis was performed using Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests, with Bonferroni's post hoc comparisons (α = 0.05).
RESULTS: The adhesive tape method demonstrated significantly greater displacement in depth across most test conditions (e.g., left side, 1000 g, no tug: 2.54 ± 3.63 mm vs. Persifix: 1.76 ± 1.78 mm, p = 0.032; Locktite: 0.53 ± 0.44 mm, p < 0.001). In frontal force tests with 1000 g and tug, the Persifix showed reduced displacement (0.41 ± 0.16 mm) compared to both adhesive tape (2.62 ± 4.25 mm, p = 0.001) and Locktite (0.52 ± 1.33 mm, p = 0.032). Lateral displacement in width was also significantly lower with both tube holders (e.g., 750 g with tug: Persifix 3.34 ± 5.20 mm vs. adhesive tape 3.16 ± 15.00 mm, p = 0.005). No statistically significant differences were observed between the Persifix and Locktite tube holders in most conditions (p > 0.05), indicating comparable fixation stability.
CONCLUSION: The Iranian tube holder, Persifix, demonstrated statistically significant reductions in ETT displacement compared to adhesive tape across multiple force vectors and weight conditions. Its mechanical performance was comparable to the commercial Locktite model, suggesting its potential utility as a cost-effective and clinically reliable alternative for airway stabilization in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: B‑lines on lung ultrasound: a non‑invasive marker for short‑term outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications increase morbidity and mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Lung ultrasound detection of B-lines is an established method to quantify pulmonary congestion, and while B-lines have been studied as predictive markers in heart failure and general critical care settings, their role in predicting outcomes specifically for post-CABG patients remains inadequately defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between B-lines detected on postoperative lung ultrasound and 30-day mortality and hospital length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted in a single-center intensive care unit between 2023 and 2024. A total of 148 adult patients scheduled for elective CABG were enrolled. Lung ultrasound was performed on postoperative days 1 (POD1) and 3 (POD3) using a standardized 8-zone protocol to quantify B-lines. The primary outcomes were all-cause 30-day mortality, assessed via hospital records and telephone follow-up, and total hospital length of stay. Univariate and multivariate logistic and linear regression analyses were used to identify predictors.
RESULTS: The mean patient age was 60.15 ± 9.8 years, and 57% were male. Within 30 days, 22 patients (15%) died. In the multivariate logistic regression, the number of B-lines on POD1 was an independent predictor of 30-day mortality (Adjusted Odds Ratio: 1.090, 95% CI: 1.018-1.167, p = 0.013), indicating a 9% increase in the odds of death for each additional B-line. In contrast, the B-line count on POD3 was not significantly associated with mortality. B-line counts on both days were also not associated with hospital length of stay. Instead, higher body mass index (β = 0.22, p = 0.022) and a history of smoking (β = 2.20, p = 0.020) were independently associated with longer hospitalization.
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative pulmonary congestion, as quantified by B-lines on POD1 lung ultrasound, is an independent predictor of 30-day mortality after CABG. Routine bedside lung ultrasound on the first day after surgery can serve as a non-invasive tool to stratify high-risk patients, potentially allowing for earlier intervention to optimize fluid status and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Preoperative empagliflozin and ventricular remodeling after coronary artery bypass grafting in type 2 diabetes: a prespecified analysis of the POST-CABGDM randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and coronary artery disease (CAD) are associated with adverse ventricular remodeling. Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) may further contribute to myocardial injury through inflammatory and ischemia-reperfusion mechanisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardioprotective effects, including reduction in left ventricular mass, but their impact in the perioperative setting of cardiac surgery remains unclear.
METHODS: This study is a prespecified secondary analysis of the open-label randomized POST-CABGDM trial (NCT04523064). Patients with T2DM and multivessel CAD undergoing CABG with CPB were randomized to receive empagliflozin 25 mg once daily or standard antidiabetic therapy. SGLT2i were discontinued 3 days before surgery and were not protocol-mandated postoperatively. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively and at 1-6 months postoperatively. The primary endpoint was the change in left ventricular mass index (ΔLVMI). Secondary endpoints included changes in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF) and ventricular dimensions.
RESULTS: A total of 118 patients were included (53 in the intervention group and 65 in the control group). Baseline characteristics were well balanced. No significant difference was observed in ΔLVMI between groups (- 1.39 ± 18.7 vs. -4.55 ± 16.8 g/m²; p = 0.337), and this finding remained unchanged after adjustment for baseline LVMI. Similarly, no differences were found in ΔLVEF or ventricular dimensions. Surgical characteristics and postoperative complications were comparable. In a separate exploratory, non-randomized multivariable analysis, continued use of SGLT2i during follow-up was associated with a higher likelihood of LVMI reduction (OR 4.69; 95% CI 1.20-18.40; p = 0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative empagliflozin use was not associated with significant short-term changes in LVMI, LVEF, or ventricular dimensions after CABG with CPB. Exploratory, non-randomized analyses suggested an association between continued SGLT2i use during follow-up and LVMI reduction, but these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies designed to evaluate sustained perioperative and postoperative therapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04523064.

articles.title: Single-center clinical analysis of anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) in children: a multimodal imaging approach to risk stratification.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA), explore the application of multimodal imaging in risk stratification, and establish individualized diagnosis and treatment protocols for this population.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was performed on children diagnosed with AAOCA at Wuhan Children's Hospital between January 2015 and April 2026. Clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging findings, therapeutic strategies, and long-term outcomes were comprehensively analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 58 AAOCA patients confirmed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled. Initial transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) yielded false-negative results in 24 patients (41.4%). Twenty-seven patients underwent single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI, MPS), among whom 6 had normal perfusion and 21 showed perfusion defects. Seven patients with positive MPS findings received surgical correction, including 2 patients with L-AAOCA( 1 coronary angioplasty and 1 coronary unroofing) and 5 patients with R-AAOCA; all treated with coronary unroofing. No patients with negative MPS results underwent surgery, indicating that negative MPS findings perhaps provide limited valuable evidence to avoid unnecessary coronary revascularization. Two patients developed massive postoperative pericardial effusion and recovered after pericardiotomy and drainage; the remaining 5 surgical patients experienced no perioperative complications. All surgical patients were discharged after full recovery and received 3 months of aspirin antiplatelet therapy. Non-surgical patients were instructed to restrict strenuous physical activity and followed up for 3 months to 3 years. Follow-up CCTA or TTE revealed normal coronary ostia without stenosis in all patients.
CONCLUSION: Clinical manifestations of pediatric AAOCA vary widely across age groups, ranging from asymptomatic presentation to sudden cardiac arrest (SCA), leading to marked discrepancies in risk evaluation and therapeutic decision-making. Multimodal imaging including TTE, CCTA and SPECT-MPI facilitates risk stratification and guides personalized clinical management of children with AAOCA.

articles.title: WSES-PSOGI-SICO evidence-infomed guidelines on surgical emergencies in patients with peritoneal surface malignancies: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and structured expert consensus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peritoneal surface malignancies (PSM) are primary or secondary neoplastic deposits involving the peritoneum and are commonly associated with colorectal, gastric, appendiceal, gynecological, pancreaticobiliary, and other intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal cancers. Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is one of the most frequent and clinically consequential emergency presentations in this population, yet diagnostic and therapeutic pathways remain heterogeneous. We aimed to develop evidence-informed recommendations for emergency management of MBO in patients with PSM by integrating a systematic review, meta-analysis and a structured international expert consensus process.
METHODS: This systematic review, meta-analysis, and Delphi consensus followed PRISMA, Cochrane, and relevant MOOSE reporting principles. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 2025 (English language). Five predefined PICO/PIRT questions addressed: (1) the diagnostic role of CT, plain abdominal X-ray, or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; (2) nonoperative medical management versus surgical or endoscopic therapy; (3) surgical versus endoscopic treatment after failure of nonoperative management; (4) bowel resection versus stoma or bypass in surgical candidates; and (5) endoscopic stenting versus endoscopic ultrasound-guided bypass with lumen-apposing metal stents in endoscopic candidates. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and MINORS for non-comparative studies; certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses (REML) produced odds ratios (OR), mean differences (MD), pooled means, or pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was summarized using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Evidence profiles informed statements voted on by the WSES-PSOGI-SICO expert panel during the 2025 WSES Congress.
RESULTS: No comparative diagnostic study evaluated abdominal X-ray or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; two small retrospective CT-based series supported contrast-enhanced CT for mapping obstruction and excluding urgent complications, but no diagnostic meta-analysis was possible. For medical versus procedural treatment, medical management was associated with lower morbidity (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.07-0.39) and shorter length of stay (MD - 9.48 days, 95% CI - 12.65 to -6.32), while success, mortality, and overall survival remained inconclusive. For surgery versus endoscopy, surgery showed higher clinical success (OR 2.57, 95% CI 1.47-4.50), whereas endoscopy shortened hospital stay (MD 3.35 days, 95% CI 1.46-5.23); mortality did not differ (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.70-1.49). Among surgical options, resection showed a signal toward higher perioperative mortality than bypass or ostomy (OR 3.55, 95% CI 1.45-8.68). Endoscopic stenting showed a pooled clinical success rate of 0.71 (95% CI 0.62-0.79), whereas evidence on LAMS was limited to one retrospective study. All guideline statements reached 100% agreement among voting participants.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the low certainty of available evidence, integration of systematic review findings with expert consensus provides a structured international framework to support decision-making in emergency presentations of PSM-related MBO. These consensus-based recommendations are intended to assist clinicians in harmonizing care across peripheral and referral hospitals, while emphasizing individualized multidisciplinary judgement and the need for future higher-quality evidence.

articles.title: Evolving practices in pretransplant cardiovascular screening: moving toward personalized assessments.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular (CV) disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease, including those evaluated for kidney transplantation. Pretransplant CV screening has traditionally focused on detecting occult coronary artery disease and guiding revascularization to reduce perioperative risk. However, emerging evidence, most notably from the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial, has challenged this paradigm, demonstrating no clear benefit of routine invasive strategies or prophylactic revascularization in stable, asymptomatic patients over optimal medical therapy. Risk assessment in kidney transplant candidates should rely on an integrated clinical evaluation that incorporates symptoms, functional capacity, baseline electrocardiography and echocardiographic findings, and the presence of major CV risk factors. When further evaluation is indicated, stress echocardiography is generally preferred as the noninvasive modality. Invasive coronary angiography should be reserved for patients with cardiac symptoms or findings suggestive of significant ischemia, including reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, regional wall motion abnormalities, or moderate-to-large ischemia on stress testing. Pre-emptive revascularization should be limited to established guideline-based indications, such as left main disease, multivessel disease with reduced ejection fraction, or refractory angina despite optimal medical therapy. Noncoronary CV disorders, including heart failure, valvular disease, and pulmonary hypertension, require systematic assessment and cardiology referral. In conclusion, pretransplant CV assessment is shifting from protocol-driven screening toward individualized, clinical suspicion-based evaluation, prioritizing optimal medical therapy, avoidance of unnecessary testing, and timely access to transplantation.

articles.title: A Novel Resource-Adapted Neurocritical Care Education Program in Tanzania: Implementation, Outcomes, and a Framework for Sustainable Training.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE/OBJECTIVE: Neurologic emergencies contribute disproportionately to morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, yet structured neurocritical care training remains limited. Emergency Neurologic Life Support (ENLS) standardizes early management of neurologic emergencies, but implementation in resource-limited settings requires contextual adaptation. Limited access to neuroimaging and monitoring compounds diagnostic uncertainty. Portable neuroultrasound (NeuroUS) offers a feasible bedside adjunct. We developed, implemented, and evaluated Tanzania's first resource-adapted neurocritical care educational program, including hands-on NeuroUS training in a low- and middle-income country (LMIC) setting.
DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: We conducted a prospective observational study during a 2-day in-person training program (October 2025). Multidisciplinary healthcare professionals caring for neurocritical care patients completed pre- and postcourse assessments evaluating medical knowledge, self-reported knowledge, and confidence across ENLS and NeuroUS domains (5-point Likert scale). Ordinal Likert outcomes were summarized using median and interquartile range (IQR) and compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Correct-response proportions were compared using Fisher exact tests. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment was applied within each outcome family.
RESULTS: Twenty-two participants completed precourse assessments; 17 completed postcourse assessments. Self-reported medical knowledge improved across 15 of 16 domains. The largest effects were observed for NeuroUS knowledge, which increased from a median of 1.5 (IQR, 1-2) to 4 (IQR, 4-5; rank-biserial, r = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.64-1.00; q < 0.001); Broad-Reaching Acute Interventions in Neurocritical Care, from 3 (IQR, 2-3) to 4 (IQR, 4-5; r = 0.73; 95% CI, 0.48-0.93; q < 0.001); and intracranial hypertension and herniation, from 3 (IQR, 3-4) to 5 (IQR, 4-5; r = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.45-0.89; q < 0.001). Confidence scores were higher in eight of 16 domains after adjustment. Both NeuroUS diagnostic-application items demonstrated large postcourse differences (q < 0.001). Correct-response proportions increased across all six exploratory knowledge items, but none remained statistically significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Ninety-four percent found the program relevant to their practice.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Implementation of resource-limited ENLS integrated with structured neuroultrasound is feasible and significantly improved knowledge and confidence. This hybrid approach represents a scalable education model for LMICs.

articles.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) in Patients With Persistent Pain Are Associated With Low Health-Related Quality of Life and Distress-Perceived Injustice Mediates the Association Between ACEs and Pain Interference.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with poor health in adulthood and may predispose individuals to anxiety-related problems and somatic morbidity. However, their role in persistent pain is not fully understood. This study assessed several factors that may link ACEs with persistent pain and offer possible treatment targets.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included two cohorts of patients attending tertiary pain care (total n = 644). We examined associations between ACEs, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), comorbid conditions, pain-related measures and psychological factors, including perceived injustice related to pain.
RESULTS: Increases in the number of ACEs from two to three and from five to six were associated with lower HRQoL and more comorbid conditions. Medium ACE burden (3-5 ACEs) associated with more depression and other psychiatric comorbidities than low ACE burden (0-2 ACEs) (34.5% vs. 22.9%, p < 0.05; 12.2% vs. 3.3%, p < 0.05, respectively). High ACE burden (≥ 6 ACEs) associated also with more asthma (29.3% vs. 13.7%, p < 0.05). ACEs were associated with all anxiety- and distress-related factors, correlations being relevant with depression (r = 0.26), trait anxiety (r = 0.25) and worry (r = 0.24). Among the pain-related outcomes, only pain interference was significantly associated with ACEs (r = 0.13), and this association was statistically fully mediated by injustice perceptions.
CONCLUSIONS: ACE burden was associated with reduced HRQoL, psychological distress and pain interference. Perceived injustice mediated the association between ACEs and pain interference, possibly representing a treatment target for patients with pain and high ACE burden.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study shows that patients treated in tertiary pain care report a high number of ACEs, stress- and anxiety-related processes and perceptions of injustice, which may contribute to pain persistence and may offer potential targets for treatment.

articles.title: The Effect of Bupropion in Peripheral Neuropathic Pain A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoamine reuptake inhibitors are evidenced first-line treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. The aim was to investigate if bupropion, a drug that specifically inhibits neuronal noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake, relieves neuropathic pain and if a potential effect depends on status of conditioned pain modulation (CPM) and sensory phenotype (irritable vs. non-irritable nociceptor).
METHOD: Study design was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and cross-over. Patients with peripheral neuropathic pain were treated with bupropion and placebo in a random order, with treatment periods lasting 6 weeks preceded by a 1-week baseline. Change in daily average pain was the primary outcome. Other outcomes included pain relief and 30% and 50% pain reduction.
RESULTS: 67 patients were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean daily average pain changed from NRS 6.4 to 5.5 after bupropion treatment with an average effect as compared with placebo of -0.5 (95% CI -0.8 to -0.1, p = 0.005). No relation was found between response to treatment and efficiency of CPM or sensory phenotype. There was no significant effect on the pain relief scale. A 30% and 50% pain reduction was found in 10 and 6 patients respectively with a NNT for 50% pain reduction of 15. Bupropion was well tolerated.
CONCLUSION: Bupropion had a pain-relieving effect independent of CPM efficiency and sensory phenotype. NNT for 50% pain reduction was higher than reported for first-line treatments, but bupropion treatment may still be an option in patients with insufficient response or intolerable side effects on such treatments.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study finds a modest pain-relieving effect of bupropion on peripheral neuropathic pain independent of function of conditioned pain modulation. Bupropion could be an alternative treatment for patients with a lack of effect or intolerable side effects to first-choice treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. Further, larger studies are needed to determine optimal dosage.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered with the EU clinical trials Register (EudraCT 2019-000243-27) on March 15th 2019. The study is approved by the Ethical Committee of the Region of Southern Denmark (also included approval for Regions of Central Denmark; no. S-20190010) and the Danish Medicine Agency (no. 2019012986) and is registered with the Danish Data Protection Agency (via the Region of Southern Denmark's internal notification; no. 19/17111).

articles.title: Investigating Interoceptive Beliefs in Individuals With Endometriosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research has indicated that individuals experiencing chronic pain differ in their ability to sense and interpret signals arising from inside the body, termed interoception. It is unclear whether differences in interoception exist for those with endometriosis, a common condition where pain is a major symptom.
METHODS: This study aimed to investigate whether interoceptive beliefs are altered in individuals with a diagnosis of endometriosis compared to those without, and whether pain experienced by those with endometriosis predicted interoceptive beliefs. Interoceptive beliefs were assessed in 247 participants with endometriosis and 98 participants without the condition. Those with endometriosis also reported their experience of dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, dyschezia, and chronic pelvic pain.
RESULTS: Individuals with endometriosis reported that they noticed more internal signals but had reduced trust in these signals and were more worried by them. They also reported that they try to distract themselves from internal sensations more than those without endometriosis. Increased pain intensity predicted higher scores in one facet of interoceptive beliefs, such that higher levels of pain were associated with higher awareness of internal sensations in individuals with endometriosis.
CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that those with endometriosis differ in their interoceptive beliefs and that these differences may be influenced by their pain experience. Given these findings largely align with changes observed in other conditions marked by pain, it is possible that interoceptive changes may represent a transdiagnostic characteristic across individuals experiencing pain.
SIGNIFICANCE: This study addresses previously conflicted findings in the literature, providing a clearer picture of the changes in interoceptive beliefs present in people with endometriosis. Developing a stronger understanding of interoceptive functioning in this unique population may lead to opportunities to develop stronger interventions targeting bodily sensations in pain management in those with the condition.

articles.title: Aortic valve replacement and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting: technical considerations in the era of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coexistence of severe aortic stenosis (AS) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently encountered in contemporary practice, particularly amongst elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combined with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an alternative strategy, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the reference treatment for these patient groups. The introduction of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves (RDAV) has considerably expanded the surgical armamentarium by facilitating implantation and reducing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp times. Appropriate application of these technologies requires specific technical considerations that ultimately influence operative planning and execution.
AREAS COVERED: This review summarizes contemporary evidence associated with the use of sutureless and RDAVs in combined CABG and SAVR procedures. To ensure relevant literature is included, a literature search across PubMed and ScienceDirect has been carried out, spanning the last 20 years, utilizing relevant medical subject headings (MeSH) terms and keywords.
EXPERT OPINION: As evidence on sutureless and RDAVs technologies continues to accumulate, with associated advancements in perioperative planning, these valves are expected to become valuable adjuncts in combined procedures, by minimizing operative burden while also allowing for robust, aortic valve pathology correction.

articles.title: Comparison of 3 guideline lipid emulsion regimens for local anesthetic systemic toxicity: an in silico study of bolus duration, total dose, and treatment delay in intravenous bupivacaine overdose.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Lipid emulsion is the only specific antidote for local anesthetic systemic toxicity, but no dose-finding study has been conducted. We compared 3 published regimens and alternative schedules that deliver the same dose in different ways using a human model of intravenous bupivacaine overdose.
METHODS: A 14-compartment human bupivacaine model was independently reimplemented without fitted parameters, replacing first-order lipid elimination with a saturable term. Toxicity was modeled as 112.5 mg administered intravenously over 3 minutes. Benefit was defined as the predicted maximum decrease in myocardial bupivacaine within 30 minutes, and harm as the predicted relative lipid load, indexed by peak plasma triglyceride concentration. Neither measure is a validated surrogate.
RESULTS: The 3 guidelines specify the same doses but different bolus durations: 1 minute versus 2-3 minutes. At a matched dose of 12 mL/kg, myocardial bupivacaine decreased by 30.5% with the 1-minute bolus and 24.9% with the 2.5-minute bolus, with the same lipid load. The completed American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine regimen (7.64 mL/kg) achieved a 24.6% decrease versus 24.9% with 12 mL/kg; thus, complete regimens differ in schedule as well as dose. Repeating the 1-minute bolus twice, for a total of 4.5 mL/kg, achieved a 31.9% decrease with 62% less emulsion. Start time had the greatest effect: the best regimen achieved a 41.8% decrease when started at the end of the injection, but only 9.6% when started at 10 minutes.
CONCLUSION: In this bupivacaine model, bolus duration distinguished the regimens more than dose did, and delay had a greater effect than either, eliminating most of the benefit without changing the lipid load. Treatment should begin at the first signs of toxicity, and 20% lipid emulsion should be immediately available wherever local anesthetics are used.

articles.title: Effect of remimazolam versus propofol anaesthesia on postoperative delirium in neurovascular surgery: a randomised noninferiority trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Propofol-based total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) is commonly used in neurovascular surgery, in which intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring limits inhalation anaesthetic use. However, propofol causes hypotension, and prolonged infusions can delay emergence. Remimazolam, a benzodiazepine whose effects are reversible with flumazenil, has been associated with less intraoperative hypotension than propofol, but its use raises concerns about postoperative delirium (POD). We tested whether remimazolam-based TIVA is noninferior to propofol-based TIVA for POD.
METHODS: In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised noninferiority trial, adults undergoing elective intracranial aneurysm clipping, arteriovenous malformation resection, microvascular decompression, or superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass received remimazolam-based TIVA with flumazenil reversal at emergence, or propofol-based TIVA, both with remifentanil. The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of POD within 5 days, assessed twice daily with the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined delirium (3D-CAM). The prespecified noninferiority margin was 10 percentage points.
RESULTS: Among 686 patients in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, POD occurred in 44 of 344 (12.8%) with remimazolam and 37 of 342 (10.8%) with propofol (risk difference, 1.97 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.85 to 6.80; one-sided P<0.001 for noninferiority); per-protocol results were consistent. Hypotensive burden below a mean arterial pressure threshold of 65 mm Hg was lower in the remimazolam group (median, 0 vs 7.5 mm Hg min; P<0.001), and tracheal extubation in the operating room was more frequent (85.2% vs 67.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: Remimazolam-based TIVA met the prespecified criterion for noninferiority to propofol-based TIVA with respect to postoperative delirium after elective neurovascular surgery. Interpretation should take into account that the observed incidence of postoperative delirium was lower than anticipated when the noninferiority margin was defined.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06115031 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

articles.title: Ultrasound assessment of fluid tolerance in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery: epidemiology of pulmonary and systemic congestion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluid accumulation in surgical patients is associated with worse outcomes. Lung ultrasound (LUS) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading can assess congestion and thereby fluid tolerance. However, evidence regarding epidemiology, feasibility, and associations of reduced fluid tolerance with outcomes in surgical patients is lacking.
METHODS: This was a prospective single-centre observational cohort study in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery. LUS and VExUS were performed before surgery and daily for up to 5 days after surgery. Reduced fluid tolerance was defined as pulmonary congestion (B profile on LUS), systemic congestion (VExUS ≥2), or both. The primary outcome was the prevalence of reduced fluid tolerance. Secondary outcomes were feasibility of ultrasound assessments, Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 complications, and length of stay (LOS).
RESULTS: Of the 200 participants included, 73 (37%) exhibited signs of reduced fluid tolerance, most commonly on postoperative day 4 (n=28; 14%). Reduced fluid tolerance was primarily driven by pulmonary congestion (n=69; 95%), whereas systemic congestion was rare. In most affected patients (47 of 73; 64%), reduced fluid tolerance was limited to 1 day. Of 1200 planned assessments, 146 (12%) were missing: 123 because participants declined, mostly owing to the burden of repeated assessments, and 23 (2%) because of incomplete views. Reduced fluid tolerance was associated with LOS of >7 days (odds ratio 3.29; 95% CI 1.03-10.70), but not with major postoperative complications (hazard ratio 1.18; 95% CI 0.49-2.86).
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced fluid tolerance detected by ultrasound is common after major gastrointestinal surgery and associated with increased LOS. Ultrasound assessments were technically feasible, but repeated assessments were perceived as a burden by a substantial proportion of patients.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06166719 (principal investigator: A.P.J. Vlaar; first registered: 04-12-2023).

articles.title: Dysnatremia in critically ill burn patients: incidence, timing and association with kidney outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia (<135 mmol/L) or hypernatremia (>145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity.
RESULTS: Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes).
CONCLUSION: Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

articles.title: Peripheral nerve block injection pressure monitoring: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection.
DESIGN: Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis.
SETTING: Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection.
INTERVENTIONS: Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations.
MEASUREMENTS: CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate.
MAIN RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations.
CONCLUSIONS: Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.

articles.title: Short-term peripheral nerve stimulation for pain relief in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-term peripheral nerve stimulation serves as a neuromodulation therapy that modulates neural activity to provide therapeutic benefit, particularly pain relief. This study investigated the effectiveness of short-term peripheral nerve stimulation as a minimally invasive approach for achieving pain relief.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from database inception till September 10, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults comparing short-term peripheral nerve stimulation with sham stimulation or usual care. The primary outcome was the change in average pain intensity during the implantation period.
RESULTS: Eight RCTs (543 participants) were included. Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in average pain intensity during the implantation period at 1-4 weeks (SMD = -0.48, 95% CI = -0.71 to -0.26, P < 0.0001) and 5-8 weeks (SMD = -0.96, 95% CI = -1.22 to -0.70, P < 0.0001), but no significant result after electrode removal. For worst pain intensity, the intervention group showed a greater reduction than the control group at all time periods except 1-4 weeks after EOT. Improvements in pain interference were delayed, becoming significant at 5-8 weeks during the implantation period (MD = -1.34, 95% CI = -1.86 to -0.82, P < 0.00001) and ≥8 weeks after the end of treatment (MD = -1.09, 95%CI = -1.69 to -0.50, P = 0.0003). Subgroup analyses showed improvements in postoperative pain. The usual care-controlled subgroup showed more pronounced and sustained benefits than the sham-controlled subgroup, and the chronic pain subgroup also showed more pronounced and sustained benefits compared to the acute/subacute pain subgroup.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis provided preliminary evidence that short-term peripheral nerve stimulation may relieve pain during the implantation period, but not all outcomes suggest sustained improvements after electrode removal.
REGISTRATION PROSPERO: CRD420251243978.

Perioperative Calls for Help and Associated Management Changes: A Prospective Observational Study.
The latest guidelines for the perioperative management of the thoracic noncardiac patient: a critical appraisal of the literature.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The management of patients before, during, and after surgical procedures on the thorax is influenced by a rapidly expanding set of guidelines that are only partially overlapping. The review is intended for clinicians who are interested in understanding how publication date influences their recommendations, and the points of agreement and divergence between sources.
RECENT FINDINGS: Across the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases, the reviewed documents converge strongly on core process measures. These measures encompass multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, a single chest drain, early ambulation, and the avoidance of reflex ICU admission. However, there is less consistency in the numerical thresholds, including exercise-testing cut-offs, transfusion triggers, and drain-removal volumes. The most recent documents demonstrate a shift toward more permissive values and an increasing emphasis on frailty, sarcopenia, and patient-reported outcomes.
SUMMARY: The core enhanced recovery after surgery process measures have been demonstrated to be reliable. However, it is imperative for clinicians to ascertain the underlying guideline generation for any numerical threshold before its implementation. A significant number of intraoperative decisions are still made based on expert opinion rather than guideline-grade evidence, underscoring the necessity for future trials and consensus on patient-centered outcome measurement.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine versus propofol for the prevention of postoperative delirium in older adults undergoing regional anaesthesia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common complication in older adults undergoing surgery and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. The choice of intraoperative sedative may influence its occurrence, particularly in the setting of regional anesthesia. A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing dexmedetomidine versus propofol in patients aged ≥60 years was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, with protocol registration in PROSPERO. The primary outcome was the incidence of POD assessed using validated instruments (CAM or CAM-ICU). Five randomized controlled trials involving a total of 1613 patients were included. The incidence of POD was 7.7% in the dexmedetomidine groups and 16.7% in the propofol groups. The meta-analysis showed a significant reduction in POD with dexmedetomidine (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.36-0.64; P < .001), with low heterogeneity (I2 = 13.4%). Egger's test did not show significant evidence of publication bias, and trial sequential analysis suggested that the available evidence is sufficient. The certainty of evidence was rated as moderate according to the GRADE approach. In older adults undergoing surgery under regional anesthesia, intraoperative sedation with dexmedetomidine is associated with a lower incidence of POD compared with propofol.

articles.title: Perioperative Continuation Versus Withholding of Angiotensin Receptor Blockers and Postoperative Delirium in Elderly Patients: A Randomized Exploratory Trial.
articles.abstract: ObjectivePostoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent complication after surgery in older adults and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged recovery. The impact of perioperative management of angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on POD remains uncertain. This randomized exploratory trial investigated the association between perioperative ARB continuation or withholding and POD outcomes in elderly patients undergoing elective surgery.MethodsElderly patients (≥65 years) receiving chronic ARB therapy and undergoing elective surgery were randomly assigned to either perioperative ARB continuation or temporary ARB withholding. The allocated ARB management strategy was applied during the perioperative period, and POD was assessed daily for 5 postoperative days using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM). Delirium severity was evaluated using the Delirium Rating Scale-Revised-98 (DRS-R-98). Plasma levels of neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-8 (IL-8), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were evaluated as exploratory biomarkers.ResultsAmong 44 randomized participants, 42 were included in the final analysis (21 per group). POD occurred in 4/21 participants (19.1%) in the ARB continuation group and 12/21 participants (57.1%) in the ARB withholding group, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of -38.1 percentage points (95% confidence interval, -59.7 to -8.7; P = 0.025). Surgical category was markedly imbalanced between groups, with orthopedic procedures accounting for 57.1% of the ARB continuation group and 95.2% of the ARB withholding group (P = 0.009). Lower DRS-R-98 scores were observed in the ARB continuation group compared with the ARB withholding group: median (interquartile range, IQR), 0 (0-7) vs 18 (5-26), P = 0.025, accompanied by shorter delirium duration (median (IQR), 0 (0-40) vs 40 (12-100) hours, P = 0.030). Exploratory biomarker analyses showed smaller postoperative relative increases in NfL, GFAP, and IL-8 in the ARB continuation group, whereas IL-6 and CRP did not differ significantly between groups after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. These biomarker findings are exploratory and should not be interpreted as evidence of causal or mechanistic effects.ConclusionsIn this small randomized exploratory trial, perioperative ARB continuation was associated with lower observed POD incidence and severity compared with temporary ARB withholding. However, the marked imbalance in surgical category and the limited sample size preclude independent attribution of these differences to ARB management. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered randomized studies with better balance of surgical procedures.

articles.title: Contralateral acute subdural hematoma following moyamoya bypass surgery: a rare complication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterized by compensatory development of collateral vessels in response to internal carotid artery occlusion. Superficial temporal artery to middle cerebral artery (STA-MCA) bypass combined with encephalomyosynangiosis is a standard surgical intervention, hemorrhagic complications following such procedures are rare, especially in pediatric patients. We present a rare case of contralateral acute subdural hematoma (ASDH) occurring immediately after revascularization surgery in a child with MMD.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 7-year-old girl with a history of left cerebral infarction due to MMD underwent left STA-MCA bypass with encephalomyosynangiosis. Although the bypass was technically successful and the patient showed no new neurological deficits postoperatively, routine computed tomography revealed a contralateral ASDH. The hematoma was promptly evacuated. Intraoperative findings included oozing from the dura near the sphenoid ridge, but no active bleeding source was identified. She recovered well without neurological deterioration. Notably, follow-up digital subtraction angiography at five months postoperatively revealed the formation of a spontaneous transdural anastomosis from the right middle meningeal artery, eliminating the need for further bypass surgery on the contralateral side.
CONCLUSION: Cerebral atrophy, intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid drainage, and perioperative aspirin use may have contributed to the development of contralateral ASDH. Surgeons should be aware of this possibility. Prompt recognition and evacuation are essential.

articles.title: Fidget and Sensory Toys for Anxiety and Emotional Regulation in Children: A Scoping Review With Implications for Pediatric Perioperative Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-pharmacological interventions are essential to reduce procedural anxiety in pediatric care. Fidget and sensory toys are widely used for distraction and self-regulation, yet evidence on their effectiveness remains fragmented. This scoping review mapped the evidence on fidget and sensory toys across general pediatric settings, with a focus on perioperative outcomes-such as anxiety, distress, and pain-to highlight relevant gaps in care.
METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL, complemented by trial registries, gray literature, citation tracking, and reference screening. Studies involving children (0-18 years) evaluating fidget or sensory toys in any setting were eligible. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction.
FINDINGS: Fifteen studies published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria. Fidget spinners were the most frequently investigated device (n = 9), followed by stress balls (n = 3). Studies were conducted in educational (n = 8) and healthcare settings (n = 7). Educational studies generally reported limited or no benefits for attention, engagement, behavior, or academic performance. In contrast, healthcare studies generally suggested reductions in anxiety, pain, fear, and procedural distress, although findings were heterogeneous, and outcome measures varied substantially.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not support the routine use of fidget toys to improve attention or academic performance in educational settings. Evidence from healthcare and procedural settings suggests that fidget and sensory toys may be feasible distraction tools for selected pediatric patients, but evidence is insufficient to support routine perioperative use. Further high-quality randomized controlled trials are needed to establish standardized intervention protocols and identify the pediatric populations and clinical settings most likely to benefit.

articles.title: Surgical Care of Birth Defects in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Bangladesh Perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Birth defects are a major cause of childhood morbidity and mortality, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Many are surgically treatable, yet access to surgical care remains limited in LMICs by inadequate infrastructure, shortages of specialized healthcare professionals, delayed diagnosis and referral, financial barriers, and sociocultural challenges.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize evidence on surgical care for birth defects in LMICs, with a focus on Bangladesh, and provide a child surgeon's perspective on challenges, context-appropriate innovations, and opportunities to strengthen surgical services.
METHODS: A narrative review of published literature was conducted, focusing on the burden of birth defects, pediatric surgical management, and context-appropriate innovations in LMICs, with particular emphasis on Bangladesh. The literature was complemented by clinical observations illustrating challenges and outcomes in resource-limited settings.
RESULTS: Studies from Bangladesh demonstrated a substantial burden of birth defects, with distributions varying by setting and discipline. Pediatric surgical studies predominantly reported gastrointestinal and genitourinary anomalies, while other studies identified cardiac, central nervous system, and orofacial defects. Context-appropriate innovations improved feasibility, affordability, and access, while staged surgery, follow-up, and family support were associated with favorable functional and quality-of-life outcomes, including school participation.
CONCLUSION: Timely, accessible, and affordable pediatric surgical care can improve outcomes for children with surgically treatable birth defects in LMICs. Strengthening pediatric surgical capacity, neonatal and perioperative care, surveillance systems, and context-appropriate innovations should be prioritized to reduce preventable mortality and disability and advance universal health coverage.

articles.title: Application of protein metabolism and nutritional intervention combined with lower segment circular suture in the treatment of placental caesarean section.
articles.abstract: Background: Perioperative protein metabolism disorder is the core pathophysiological change in patients with postpartum haemorrhage after caesarean section with placenta previa. Purpose: Protein metabolism nutrition intervention, as a core nutritional support strategy during the perioperative period of obstetrics, can provide systemic metabolic support for surgical hemostasis and postoperative recovery by regulating protein metabolism. Results: The results showed that protein metabolism and nutritional intervention established a stable metabolic foundation for both groups of patients. The observation group had significantly lower intraoperative bleeding volume, hemostasis time, hospitalisation costs, and hospitalisation time compared to the control group. The hemostasis effective rate (95.5%) was significantly higher than that of the control group (70.6%); Conclusion: The combination of the new surgical hemostasis scheme has a definite haemostatic effect, can reduce bleeding volume and transfusion requirements, shorten hospitalisation time, reduce medical costs, and has good safety. It is worthy of clinical promotion and application.

articles.title: Pregnancy considerations in women with uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, accounting for approximately 7-10% of all congenital cardiac malformations. Although early surgical repair has transformed its natural history in high-income settings, with contemporary long-term survival exceeding 90%, uncorrected TOF continues to be encountered in pregnancy, particularly in women from resource-limited regions or those with previously undiagnosed disease. The physiological adaptations of pregnancy, including reduction in systemic vascular resistance, plasma volume expansion, and a 30-50% rise in cardiac output, are poorly tolerated in the presence of a non-restrictive ventricular septal defect and fixed right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, leading to progressive cyanosis, right ventricular strain, and uteroplacental hypoperfusion. Current European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidance classifies unrepaired cyanotic heart disease without Eisenmenger syndrome as mWHO 2.0 class III, while Eisenmenger syndrome is classified as mWHO 2.0 class IV. Contemporary data from the ESC EORP Registry of Pregnancy and Cardiac Disease (ROPAC) report maternal mortality of 0.7% and heart failure in 8.7% of pregnancies with uncorrected congenital heart disease, with markedly worse outcomes in cyanotic subsets. This narrative review synthesizes the pathophysiology, risk stratification, obstetric management, intrapartum anesthetic considerations, comparative outcomes of uncorrected versus corrected disease, and key evidence gaps that continue to constrain care for this population, providing a physiology-driven framework for the pregnancy heart team.

articles.title: More Than a Needle: Building Comprehensive Pain Pathways for Major Amputations.
Achieving opioid-free anaesthesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioids have been central to anaesthetic practice for over a century, but they risk adverse effects including postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), ileus, respiratory depression, and opioid-induced hyperalgesia. These complicate recovery and contribute to the wider burden of opioid misuse, a growing concern in Irish healthcare. Opioid-free anaesthesia (OFA) supports Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) principles by removing opioid-related barriers to early mobilisation and functional recovery.
AIMS: To review the rationale for OFA, how it is delivered, its limitations, and to assess how it fits into current perioperative practice in Ireland.
RESULTS: OFA relies on combining agents that target multiple nociceptive pathways, such as N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists (ketamine, magnesium), alpha-2 adrenergic agonists (especially dexmedetomidine), non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), paracetamol, intravenous lidocaine, and gabapentinoids. Where applicable, ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve blocks can reduce intraoperative analgesic requirements and extending postoperative analgesia. Evidence supports OFA across a range of surgical contexts. Benefits are most consistent in laparoscopic and major abdominal surgery, where faster return of bowel function, reduced length of stay, and lower rates of PONV are reported. Evidence on postoperative analgesia is less clear. Opioid consumption in the immediate post-anaesthetic period tends to be lower but is often comparable to a well-executed opioid-inclusive multimodal regimen thereafter.
CONCLUSIONS: Rigid opioid avoidance risks undertreating acute pain, so OFA is best applied selectively, guided by procedure type, patient comorbidities, and institutional resources. This review evaluates the rationale, implementation, and limitations of OFA, providing clinicians with a balanced appraisal of its role in modern perioperative care.

articles.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID).
RESULTS: SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles.
CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

articles.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI.
MAIN TEXT: Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent.
CONCLUSIONS: This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes.
HIGHLIGHTS: VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.
