This meta-analysis evaluated the outcomes of MILR compared to open liver resection (OLR) in older adults (≥ 65 years) with HCC.
METHODS: A search was conducted in Medline, Embase, CINAHL, and The Cochrane Library from their inception until November 20, 2025. The review adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251239665).
RESULTS: Fourteen retrospective studies comprising 3,092 older adults were included (1,367 MILR, 1,725 OLR). MILR was associated with lower overall (odds ratio [OR] = 0.47; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38-0.58; I² = 0%) and major complications (OR = 0.61; 95% CI 0.45-0.83; I² = 15%). However, no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality (OR = 0.75; 95% CI 0.41-1.38; I² = 0%), disease-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.83; 95% CI 0.60-1.15; I² = 72%), or overall survival (HR = 0.80; 95% CI 0.56-1.16; I² = 80%).
CONCLUSIONS: In selected older adults with HCC, MILR was associated with fewer perioperative complications than OLR, while no statistically significant difference was detected in 90-day mortality or long-term survival. Residual confounding, predominance of minor resections, absence of validated frailty assessment, and limited octogenarian data preclude causal inference or confirmation that the association persists with advancing age.

articles.title: Effects of perioperative esketamine infusion on chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic postsurgical pain after thoracoscopic surgery remains common. We investigated whether perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion would reduce chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection.
METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised controlled trial, 914 adults were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine or normal saline. Esketamine was administered as a 0.1 mg kg-1 bolus at induction, followed by continuous intraoperative infusion (0.1 mg kg-1 h-1) and postoperative infusion (0.015 mg kg-1 h-1) for 48 h. The primary outcome was chronic pain at 3 months, defined as persistent pain with a numeric rating scale score ≥1 during coughing in the surgical region. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, supplemental analgesics use, recovery of bowel function, in-hospital adverse events, and esketamine-related side-effects.
RESULTS: We analysed 873 patients (median age, 55 yr; 63% female). The incidence of 3 month chronic pain was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (14.7% vs 21.2%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.62; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-0.90; P=0.013). A reduction was also observed when using a post hoc outcome definition of a numeric rating scale pain score ≥3 during coughing at 3 months (adjusted odds ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.19-0.84; P=0.015). Esketamine also reduced overall pain scores at rest and during coughing within the first 48 h, and decreased supplemental analgesic requirements within 48 h and 3 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion significantly reduced 3 month chronic pain after thoracoscopic lung resection without increasing adverse effects.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2000040012.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Identifier: ChiCTR2000040012; principal investigator: Fu-hai Ji; dated November 18, 2020; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=62319).

articles.title: Effect of a Tailored Educational Programme on Adequacy of Anaesthesia and Major Postoperative Complications: A Before-After Quality-Improvement Study in Intermediate- and High-Risk Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: State Entropy (SE) and Surgical Pleth Index (SPI) parameters aim to optimise anaesthetic depth and intraoperative opioid administration, but their impact on postoperative complications remains unclear. Insufficient training and limited decision support may contribute to inconsistent findings. Thus, we evaluated whether tailored training to improve SE and SPI compliance reduced major postoperative complications.
METHODS: Adult inpatients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk noncardiac surgery were included in this prospective single-centre before-after study in France. The educational intervention and outcomes were based on the Kirkpatrick framework. All anaesthesia providers were invited to participate voluntarily in lectures and bedside training on SE and SPI monitoring. Training impact was assessed using a composite of major postoperative complications within 28 days as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included changes in monitoring practices.
RESULTS: Among 1,623 eligible patients, 1,025 were included over a 13-month period (517 before and 508 after training). Of 202 eligible providers, 91 participated in the one-month training programme (45%). After training, simultaneous SE and SPI sensor use increased from 26% to 42% (P < 0.001), and combined SE-SPI compliance increased from 23% to 39% (P < 0.001). Major postoperative complications occurred in 66/517 patients (13%) before and 71/508 patients (14%) after training (P = 0.6). Multivariable and propensity score analyses showed no significant association between the intervention and the primary outcome.
CONCLUSION: This training did not reduce the incidence of major postoperative complications, despite improvements in intraoperative monitoring practices. Future educational strategies should strengthen provider engagement and reinforcement to translate improved monitoring practices into clinical benefit.
REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06111248.

articles.title: Procedure-specific bleeding risk assessment: a multidisciplinary expert consensus companion to the 2026 periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.
METHODS: A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel.
RESULTS: Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied.
CONCLUSION: This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

articles.title: Infraorbital versus sphenopalatine ganglion block for patient-reported recovery after septorhinoplasty: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block with transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block on recovery quality 24 h after septorhinoplasty.
DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial.
SETTING: Tertiary training hospital; operating room and postoperative ward.
PATIENTS: Ninety adults aged 18 to 65 years, ASA physical status I or II, undergoing elective septorhinoplasty; 89 were analyzed.
INTERVENTIONS: After induction of general anesthesia, patients received bilateral transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block (SPG group) or bilateral ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block (IO group), 2 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine per side. Surgical infiltration and multimodal analgesia were identical in both groups.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was the total Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 h. Secondary outcomes were QoR-15 domains, visual analog scale pain scores, rescue morphine, nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption, emergence agitation, edema, ecchymosis and recovery room stay.
MAIN RESULTS: Total QoR-15 at 24 h was higher in the IO group (129.1 ± 9.4 versus 116.6 ± 11.7; mean difference 12.5 points, 95% CI 8.01 to 17.01; P = 0.001), above the prespecified minimal clinically important difference of 8. More IO patients crossed the acceptable symptom state threshold of 118 (86.4% versus 35.6%; P < 0.001). Pain scores were lower at every time point and fewer IO patients needed rescue analgesia (11.4% versus 53.3%; P = 0.001). Nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption and recovery room stay did not differ.
CONCLUSIONS: Infraorbital nerve block gave better 24 h patient-reported recovery than sphenopalatine ganglion block after septorhinoplasty. Secondary findings are hypothesis-generating.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.govNCT06929429.

articles.title: Practice Patterns and Staffing Models for Nonoperating Room Anesthesia in the Intensive Care Unit: An Exploratory Survey of the Membership of the American Society of Anesthesiologists Committee on Critical Care Medicine.
Optimal Gas Flow in Total Intravenous Anesthesia: Comment.
EEG monitoring in the neonate as part of a multimodal brain protection system in paediatric anaesthesia.
articles.abstract: Neurological monitoring is well established in anesthesia. Applied for assessment and control it also provides indirect information on hemodynamic status, ventilation, oxygenation and perfusion. In pediatric anesthesia, the potential toxicity of anesthetics is a concern. In neonates and young infants, the brain is immature and still developing, making electroencephalogram monitoring complex. To determine the current state of neurological function monitoring in neonates during anesthesia as a brain protection tool, a narrative review was conducted. The search prioritized the last ten years in PubMed, Cochrane, other electronic sources, and snowball sampling using the keywords: Neurotoxicity, Brain Monitoring, Newborn, Anesthesia, Neuroprotective Strategies, combinations thereof, and expert publications. The review concludes that brain protection is necessary, however further knowledge and validated technological support are required.

articles.title: Undescended Testes in Medically Complex Children: Evaluating A Common Urologic Condition Through a Multidisciplinary Lens.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Undescended testis (UDT) is a common genitourinary anomaly in boys. Orchiopexy before 18 months of age is recommended to preserve fertility and reduce testicular cancer risk. However, these recommendations are based on results of outcome studies for otherwise healthy boys and may not be readily applicable for those with developmental and/or genetic disorders for whom anesthetic and surgical risks may be increased and intervention may offer limited benefit. UDT management in boys with complex medical conditions warrants unique considerations, and data-driven guidelines are lacking. In this review, we explore this challenging clinical dilemma through a multidisciplinary lens.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative literature review was performed by specialists in pediatric anesthesia, endocrinology, genetics, oncology, urology, and development-behavioral pediatrics. Iteratively refined structured literature searches of the MEDLINE database, GeneReviews, and online books were performed through PubMed. Anesthetic and surgical risks, fertility potential, testicular cancer risk, and ability to perform self-testicular examinations as dictated by the patient's expected cognitive development were evaluated for healthy boys and boys with Down syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, cerebral palsy, Fragile X syndrome, neurofibromatosis type 1, Williams syndrome, 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, Rett syndrome, Angelman syndrome, tuberous sclerosis, and Smith-Magenis syndrome. The results were then evaluated by a bioethicist.
RESULTS: For children with complex medical conditions, potential harms of intervention are not theoretical. Surgery may expose the child to substantial anesthetic and surgical risks for which their underlying conditions make them especially vulnerable. The ethical threshold for intervention may therefore be higher especially if certain benefits such as fertility remain uncertain.
CONCLUSIONS: Management of UDT for medically complex boys is nuanced and warrants a multidisciplinary approach to thoroughly assess the risks and benefits of proceeding with, deferring, or declining orchiopexy. Multidisciplinary input will best facilitate individualized care that focuses on the specific needs of each child and appropriately respects parental discretion in determining management that is most in line with the child's long-term quality of life.

articles.title: Accuracy, Safety, and Workflow of Frameless Neuronavigation-Guided Stereoelectroencephalography in Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is central to invasive presurgical evaluation in drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). We evaluated the accuracy, safety, and workflow efficiency of frameless neuronavigation-guided SEEG in routine clinical practice.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included consecutive adult and pediatric patients with DRE who underwent SEEG between July 2016 and August 2025. Entry-point and target-point deviations were measured on postoperative computed tomography fused to the preoperative planning data set. Safety end points were perioperative complications. Operative duration and time per electrode were recorded. Comparative analyses between AdTech and Dixi systems were restricted to the primary-surgery cohort to maintain independent samples. A subgroup analysis examined procedures performed by experienced surgeons, defined as more than 250 implanted electrodes.
RESULTS: Seventy-seven patients underwent 82 SEEG procedures. Across all procedures, 984 electrodes were implanted. The median number of electrodes per surgery was 13. The median entry-point and target-point deviations were 2.1 and 1.8 mm, respectively. Entry-point deviation did not differ between AdTech and Dixi electrodes in the primary-surgery cohort (2.1 vs 2.1 mm; P = .579), whereas target-point deviation was slightly lower with Dixi (1.6 vs 1.9 mm; P = .030). The duration of Dixi procedures was shorter than AdTech procedures (102 vs 186 minutes P < .001) and had lower time per electrode (10 vs 14 minutes; P < .001). Four minor hemorrhagic complications occurred (4.9%/procedure; 0.4%/electrode); no permanent neurological deficits, reoperations, hardware-related complications, or procedure-related deaths occurred. A seizure-onset zone was localized in 48 patients (62%), enabling subsequent resective or disconnective surgery.
CONCLUSION: Frameless neuronavigation-guided SEEG achieved reproducible millimetric accuracy, low morbidity, and efficient workflow in a consecutive real-world cohort. These findings support frameless neuronavigation as a safe and scalable option for invasive presurgical evaluation in DRE.

articles.title: Perioperative Care, Challenges, and Innovations in Pediatric Anesthesia Beyond the Operating Room.
Effect of photobiomodulation on recovery from oral soft tissue local anaesthesia in paediatric patients: a preliminary split-mouth randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Paediatric dental patients are particularly vulnerable to inadvertent soft-tissue injury following local anaesthesia (LA) This preliminary study evaluated. the clinical efficacy of 810-nm diode laser photobiomodulation (PBM) in reversing oral soft-tissue anaesthesia in paediatric patients. Thirty-four children aged 8-12 years requiring bilateral primary toothextractions under infiltration LA were enrolled in by consideration of ethical codes. Local anaesthesia was administered using 2% lidocaine with 1:80,000 epinephrine, as per the local infiltration anesthesia protocol. Participants were randomly allocated to receive both PBM and sham Laser with 7-10 days washout period between the two interventions. PBM was delivered using an 810-nm diode laser in continuous mode at 200 mW for 12 s per point at six predefined intraoral and extraoral sites. An independent examiner assessed soft-tissue sensation at 5-minute intervals by standardized bilateral palpation, using the non-anaesthetized side as the reference. The primary outcome was time to first assessment at which sensation on the anaesthetized side was judged normal. Data were analysed using a paired-samples t-test. Mean reflection time was significantly shorter in the PBM group (60.7 ± 27.3 min; p < 0.001) compared with the Sham lasergroup (78.2 ± 17.0 min). Subgroup analysis demonstrated significant reductions in reflection time in both maxillary and mandibular arches. Photobiomodulation using an 810-nm diode laser demonstrated a reduction in subjective soft tissue anaesthesia recovery time following infiltration LA in paediatric dental patients under the conditions tested.

articles.title: Weight and Risk Adjusted Perioperative (WRAP) Bundle for Prevention of Cesarean Delivery Surgical Site Infection: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Many individual interventions to reduce surgical site infection (SSI) risk after Cesarean delivery (CD) have been identified; however, their collective impact when used as a bundle is not well defined. This quality improvement initiative compared SSI rates before and after the implementation of a weight- and risk-adjusted perioperative (WRAP) bundle, developed to improve CD outcomes.
METHODS: The WRAP bundle was designed to standardize care by tailoring evidence-based interventions according to each patient's individual SSI risk category. Risk stratification was based on pre-gravid body mass index (BMI) and the presence of comorbidities associated with increased SSI risk. This quality improvement initiative adopted a before-and-after quasi-experimental design over two years. Post-CD telephone calls by clinical reviewers were made 30-42 days postpartum to identify CD-SSI incidence.
RESULTS: A total of 4014 CDs were performed between July 1, 2022, and March 1, 2024, with 1275 before WRAP bundle implementation and 2739 after. Maternal characteristics were comparable between pre- and post-WRAP bundle groups, except for hypertension in pregnancy, which was more prevalent in the post-implementation period (22.1% vs. 17.1%, P = 0.001). Across all BMI categories, a statistically significant reduction in overall CD-SSI incidence from 8.9% to 5.8% (P = 0.007) was observed. In the high-BMI group, the CD-SSI rate decreased from 13.9% to 6.9% (P = 0.03).
CONCLUSION: Tailored bundled interventions, such as the WRAP bundle may be effective in reducing the incidence of CD-SSI, particularly among high-risk individuals. Continuous monitoring of post-CD SSI is vital for quality improvement efforts aimed at optimizing postpartum outcomes.

articles.title: Extending Sustainable Value Stream Mapping to Hospital Environments: An Empirical Study of Surgical Process Improvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Lean production techniques have been widely adopted in manufacturing to reduce waste, optimize processes, and improve efficiency. With the rising focus on sustainability across economic, environmental, and social dimensions, attention has turned to healthcare settings. However, the application of Sustainable Value Stream Mapping (Sus-VSM) in hospitals remains relatively unexplored.
METHODS: This study addresses that gap by implementing a Sus-VSM approach in the preoperative and postoperative phases of 3 surgery types: general surgery, urology, and obstetrics at a major hospital. We collected 6 months of operational data, identifying key inefficiencies. A current-state VSM was created, followed by Lean-based interventions including 5S, visualization, and forecasting.
RESULTS: Results revealed an 11.5% reduction in anesthesia paperwork time and improved bed-management planning. Additionally, we evaluated the hospital's economic, social, and environmental performance using adapted metrics. Findings indicate particularly high social sustainability (97.85%), moderate environmental performance (77.6%), and an 80.2% economic rating.
CONCLUSION: By integrating triple-bottom-line principles with Lean thinking, this study presents a structured methodology for advancing both operational efficiency and institutional sustainability in healthcare. These findings support the broader adoption of Sus-VSM and point to the need for life-cycle assessments and longitudinal research to validate long-term impacts on healthcare delivery.

articles.title: History of anesthesia: examining 19th century religious objections to obstetric anesthesia and James Young Simpson's rebuttal.
articles.abstract: James Young Simpson's 1847 introduction of chloroform to obstetric practice is popularly remembered as a battle between science and religion, with Simpson portrayed as valiantly confronting a hostile clergy over the "curse of Eve." A closer examination of contemporaneous sources reveals limited clerical opposition, with the most explicit theological objections coming from physicians rather than the pulpit, and prominent religious leaders of the day either in agreement with Simpson or remaining silent on the matter. Not until nearly 50 years later, with Andrew Dickson White's popular polemic, did the science-versus-religion narrative become dominant. A closer reading of Simpson's own 1847 pamphlet, meanwhile, reveals the sophistication of his theological arguments, which draw on extensive biblical exegesis and Hebrew philology to demonstrate that obstetric anesthesia did not violate divine command. Recovering the true history of this episode restores Simpson's identity as a genuine polymath of his age and cautions against the temptation to let convenient myths stand in for the historical record.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation.
METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB, n=72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n=91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis.
RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P<0.001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, while a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P<0.001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P<0.001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs. 35%, P=0.002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.

articles.title: Longitudinal associations among psychophysical factors, biobehavioral vulnerabilities and pain-related outcomes following acute musculoskeletal injury in adolescents.
articles.abstract: Up to 30% of adolescents with acute musculoskeletal (MSK) injuries develop chronic pain. Research has increasingly focused on identification of risk factors associated with outcomes following acute injury; however, prospective longitudinal studies examining both psychophysical and biobehavioral factors beyond short-term follow-up are limited in adolescents. The current study used mixed effects models (MEM) to test longitudinal associations among biobehavioral factors (e.g., sleep disturbances, anxiety and depressive symptoms, pain-related cognitions and behaviors), psychophysical responses (e.g., conditioned pain modulation, temporal summation) and pain-related outcomes (pain intensity, pain-related disability and quality of life; QOL) over one year following acute MSK injury. Participants were 226 adolescents 11-17 years (and one parent) participating in a prospective longitudinal study with data collected via self-report, actigraphy and quantitative sensory testing (QST) at three timepoints (< 30 days, 3 months, 12 months post-injury). Results of MEM revealed within and between-person associations among psychological factors and pain-related disability and QOL. Sleep duration (within-person effect) and pain-related cognitions and behaviors (between-person effect) were associated with pain intensity. Pain-related cognitions and behaviors were also associated with pain-related disability (between-person effect) and QOL (within and between-person effects). Temporal summation (TS) was the only psychophysical factor associated with pain outcomes (between-person effect) with higher average TS associated with higher pain intensity. Findings point to the relatively stronger influence of biobehavioral (versus psychophysical) factors as responsive indicators of adolescents' recovery trajectories and suggest targeted interventions may be directed at general anxiety and depressive symptoms, pain-specific cognitions and behaviors, and sleep to improve outcomes. PERSPECTIVE: This article presents results of a longitudinal multi-method study examining pain-related outcomes in adolescents following musculoskeletal injury. Findings point to the influence of biobehavioral factors in the longer-term recovery period and suggest potential importance of interventions targeting general anxiety and depressive symptoms, pain-specific cognitions and behaviors, and sleep in adolescents post musculoskeletal injury.

articles.title: Heterogeneity In The Effects of Weight Reduction on Pain And Physical Function In Knee Osteoarthritis: A causal forest analysis of the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite the emphasis on weight control, heterogeneity in response to weight loss among individuals with or at high risk for knee osteoarthritis (OA) remains unclear. This study examined heterogeneity in the associations of weight reduction with pain among overweight and obese individuals using a machine learning approach.
METHODS: We analyzed longitudinal data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, comprising community-dwelling adults aged 45-79 years with a body mass index ≥25 who completed baseline assessments between 2008 and 2010, with a 24-month follow-up (n=3,644). The exposure was a ≥5% reduction in body weight from baseline to 24 months. The primary outcome of this study was the pain subscale of the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities (WOMAC) Osteoarthritis Index.
RESULTS: The average treatment effect (ATE) was estimated using a doubly robust estimator, and treatment effect heterogeneity was assessed by estimating conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) using a causal forest approach. A reduction of ≥5% in body weight was not significantly associated with a lower WOMAC pain score (ATE=-0.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.51 to 0.01). The causal forest analysis demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with CATE estimates of -0.77 (95% CI, -1.24 to -0.30) for the high-benefit subgroup (top 20% of estimated CATEs) and 0.41 (95% CI, -0.35 to 1.17) for the low-benefit subgroup (bottom 20%).
DISCUSSION: Our findings highlight the potential value of individualized weight-loss strategies and suggest that patient characteristics may help identify those most likely to benefit from weight reduction.

articles.title: Cell and Gene Therapy in Lung Transplantation: From Experimental Promise towards Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Lung transplantation (LTx) remains the only definitive therapy for selected patients with end-stage lung disease, yet outcomes are limited by early ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and primary graft dysfunction (PGD), and by chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) as the leading cause of late graft failure. These entities share overlapping injury and repair pathways, including alveolocapillary barrier disruption, microvascular dysfunction, innate immune activation, and maladaptive remodeling, which remain incompletely controlled by current perioperative management and systemic immunosuppression. This review summarizes cell and gene therapy approaches in LTx and frames these strategies around the IRI/PGD-to-CLAD continuum. Stromal cell therapies, regulatory immune cell approaches, and cell-free or cell-derived products such as extracellular vesicles and mitochondrial transfer are discussed, with emphasis on route, dose, persistence, and the graft microenvironment as determinants of biological activity. Gene modulation strategies and delivery platforms relevant to the lung, including viral vectors, lipid nanoparticles, and virus-like particles, are outlined, together with preclinical gene therapy strategies targeting IRI and allograft rejection. Ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) is highlighted as a practical window for organ-confined delivery and early mechanistic assessment prior to implantation. Key translational considerations are outlined, including product characterization and potency, clinically interpretable dosing, and the need for harmonized endpoints and pharmacodynamic readouts to improve comparability across studies.

articles.title: Association of Graft Laterality With Outcomes After Single Lung Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate whether graft side (right versus left) is associated with outcomes after single lung transplantation (SLT) and to contextualize this association with lung function and perioperative complications.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of adults transplanted from January 2018 to July 2025 with interstitial lung disease (ILD) or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Survival was evaluated with Kaplan-Meier and Cox models adjusted for clinical covariates. Postoperative respiratory infection was modeled with logistic regression. Longitudinal forced expiratory volume in 1 s was summarized.
RESULTS: Of 530 transplants, 319 met criteria (ILD n = 224; COPD n = 95). Survival differed by procedure (log-rank P = 0.0013). Compared with double lung transplantation, right SLT had higher mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 2.92, 95% CI 1.82-4.67, P < 0.0001), while left SLT did not (HR 1.07, 0.60-1.91, P = 0.82). The excess hazard with right SLT persisted within interstitial lung disease (HR 2.27, 1.28-4.05, P = 0.005) and COPD (HR 2.87, 1.33-6.19, P = 0.007). Primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (HR 2.39, 1.39-4.11, P = 0.002) and acute kidney injury (HR 2.12, 1.33-3.38, P = 0.002) were independently associated with mortality. Respiratory infections were frequent (∼40%-53%) without a clear difference by side; longer operative time correlated with infection (odds ratio 1.16 per h, 1.02-1.32, P = 0.02). Forced expiratory volume in 1 s peaked at 12-18 mo and declined thereafter, with no separation by side.
CONCLUSIONS: Right-but not left-SLT was associated with inferior long-term survival versus double lung transplantation. The lack of side-specific differences in spirometry and infection suggests that other factors may be relevant to the observed association between laterality and survival. Multicenter studies with time-varying covariates and physiologic imaging are warranted.

articles.title: Full-Visualization Endoscopic Paravertebral (Extraforaminal) Decompression Under Local Anesthesia for Far-Out Syndrome: A Consecutive Case Series of 27 Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of full-visualization spinal endoscopic decompression technique performed under local anesthesia for Far-out syndrome (FOS) and to describe its technical nuances.
METHODS: Between March 2023 and March 2025, 27 consecutive FOS patients underwent full-visualization spinal endoscopic decompression via a single-portal paravertebral approach under local anesthesia. This approach allows medial extension of decompression into the intraforaminal zone when necessary to achieve adequate release of the L5 exiting nerve root. Clinical outcomes were assessed using VAS, ODI, and modified MacNab criteria preoperatively and at 3 days, 1, 3, and 12 months postoperatively. Key procedural steps were detailed, and outcomes compared with literature.
RESULTS: Mean age was 69 ± 12 years; mean operative time 102 ± 28 min.
PATHOLOGY: 33% pure bony stenosis, 67% combined with disc herniation. VAS improved from 7.5 ± 0.9 preoperatively to 1.5 ± 1.1 at 12 months (P < 0.0001). ODI decreased from 71 ± 5% to 16 ± 7% (P < 0.0001). MacNab criteria: 89% excellent/good, 7.4% fair, 3.7% poor. Suboptimal outcomes: one preoperative level misidentification, one residual radicular symptom, and one epineurial tear (no deficit). Comparative analysis confirmed favorable outcomes versus other techniques.
CONCLUSION: Full-visualization spinal endoscopic decompression under local anesthesia is effective and safe for FOS, offering real-time patient feedback, avoidance of general anesthesia, and minimal tissue trauma, making it suitable for the often-elderly FOS population.

articles.title: Long-term pancreatic function, reconstruction durability, and disease control after pancreas-preserving total duodenectomy: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreas-preserving total duodenectomy (PPTD) enables complete duodenal resection while preserving the pancreatic head in selected benign or premalignant diseases. Long-term pancreatic function, reconstruction durability, and disease control after PPTD remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: We performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyzes-compliant systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through June 29, 2026. Institutional reports were grouped into cohort families to avoid patient duplication. Pooled proportions were estimated using inverse-variance logit models or generalized linear mixed models for prespecified outcomes with zero events. The risk of bias and the certainty of evidence were assessed using Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Nine independent retrospective cohorts comprising 199 patients were included; 86.4% had familial adenomatous polyposis, and the follow-up ranged from 20 to 125 months. The overall postoperative morbidity was 64.7% (95% CI, 51.5-76.0), major morbidity 40.3% (28.5-53.3), biliopancreatic anastomotic leakage 32.1% (23.5-42.1), and clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula 27.5% (17.5-40.5). One early postoperative death was reported. New-onset diabetes and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency were each reported in 1.8%, and subsequent pancreatic resection occurred in 3.6%. Late pancreatitis occurred in 18.3%, recurrent pancreatitis in 12.4%, biliopancreatic stenosis in 5.0%, cholangitis in 3.3%, and late reoperation in 9.5%. Endoscopic surveillance was documented in 83.3%; jejunal adenomas occurred in 25.8%, additional jejunal resection in 4.8%, jejunal cancer in 2.5%, and gastric cancer in 4.6%. The certainty of evidence was very low across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: PPTD is associated with substantial perioperative morbidity but low early mortality, with infrequently reported long-term endocrine and exocrine impairment, although no study has applied functional testing. Late pancreatitis and metachronous jejunal disease remain clinically relevant and support lifelong endoscopic surveillance. Evidence remains limited to small retrospective series and does not establish comparative superiority over other surgical strategies.

articles.title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test the efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid versus sham injection for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
DESIGN: Single centred, participant and assessor masked, three arm randomised controlled trial (Inject trial).
SETTING: Community.
PARTICIPANTS: From 5 December 2019 and 24 July 2022, 192 adults (18 years or older) diagnosed with midportion Achilles tendinopathy were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63), or high volume injection with corticosteroid (n=65).
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were allocated to sham injection (2-3 mL 0.5% bupivacaine hydrochloride), high volume injection with corticosteroid (50 mL saline and 0.5% bupivacaine with 25 mg hydrocortisone in the first 10 mL), or high volume injection with no corticosteroid (same solution but without hydrocortisone). They received the same exercise programme, education, and activity modification advice.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was pain and disability using the validated VISA-A and the primary endpoint was at 52 weeks. The economic outcome was cost per quality-adjusted life-years from a societal perspective.
RESULTS: VISA-A data were obtained from 181 (94%) of 192 participants at 12 months. No clear differences were noted between sham and high volume injection either with (-3.5 (98.33% confidence interval -12.0 to 5.0)) or without corticosteroid (4.0 (-4.2 to 12.3)), and between the two injections (-7.5 (-15.3 to 0.3)), at 12 months. The point estimate was closest to the target difference for the comparison between injections and favoured the arm without steroid. The only differences observed on VISA-A at intermediate time points were a benefit for high volume with corticosteroid versus sham at six weeks (9.2 (1.5 to 16.9)) but worse outcomes for high volume injection with corticosteroid versus high volume injection with no corticosteroid at 26 weeks (-8.6 (-16.4 to -0.7)). The health economic analysis found high volume injection with corticosteroid to be less costly than the sham with similar effectiveness based on quality-adjusted life-years (>0.90 probability of being cost effective at $AUD50 000 and $100 000 willingness-to-pay thresholds). No serious trial related adverse events were recorded.
CONCLUSION: High volume injections with or without corticosteroids did not improve pain or disability compared with sham at 12 months. Although high volume injections with corticosteroid showed short term clinical benefit and potential reduction in healthcare costs over a year, they were associated with worse longer term clinical outcomes. The clinical data do not support routine use for high volume injections with corticosteroid for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12619001455156.

articles.title: Robotic navigation strategies for PFNA fixation: impact on one-time guide pin success rate and anteversion angle accuracy - a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of three navigation strategies (full robotic navigation, robotic navigation for the main nail only with freehand anteversion, and conventional freehand technique) in PFNA fixation for intertrochanteric fractures, analyzed factors affecting anteversion angle accuracy, and quantified the learning curve of robot-assisted surgery. A retrospective review was conducted on 121 intertrochanteric fracture cases managed with PFNA. We categorized patients into three groups by navigation strategy: G1 (double navigation, n = 41), G2 (single navigation, n = 40), and G3 (non-navigation, n = 40). Perioperative parameters (fluoroscopy time span, total fluoroscopy times, number of attempts, visible intraoperative blood loss, etc.) were compared among groups. The main metric assessed was the attempt frequency for anteversion determination (reflecting one-time success rate). Within G1, Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression explored the associations between anteversion error and medullary canal diameter, as well as fluoroscopy times for main nail insertion. Curve estimation was used to evaluate learning curves for fluoroscopy time span and main nail insertion time. Baseline characteristics were similar across the three groups, with no significant differences (P > 0.05). The number of attempts to determine anteversion in G1 (1.22 ± 0.48) was significantly lower than in G2 (4.30 ± 2.49) and G3 (3.98 ± 1.93) (both P < 0.001). Regarding overall surgical efficiency, fluoroscopy time span in G1 (65.95 ± 8.71 min) was 12.0 min shorter (15.4% reduction, P < 0.05) than in G3 (77.93 ± 29.98 min), total fluoroscopy times (40.63 ± 7.89) were 16.3 fewer (28.6% reduction, P < 0.001); visible intraoperative blood loss (99.8 ± 91.2 mL) was 119.5 mL less (54.5% reduction, P < 0.001), and blood transfusion volume (0.73 ± 1.45 units) was significantly lower than in G3 (2.14 ± 1.72 units, P = 0.002). Compared with G2, G1 also showed significantly reduced fluoroscopy time span, total fluoroscopy times, and visible intraoperative blood loss (all P < 0.05). Main nail insertion time in G2 (43.78 ± 6.94 min) was significantly longer than in G3 (34.65 ± 17.59 min, P = 0.002), whereas G1 (37.80 ± 6.43 min) was not significantly different from G3. Within G1, anteversion error showed a strong negative correlation with medullary canal diameter (r = - 0.807, P < 0.001). Multiple regression identified medullary canal diameter as the only independent predictor of anteversion error (β = - 0.781, P < 0.001). Learning curve analysis demonstrated a marked reduction in fluoroscopy time span with robotic case order (R² = 0.644, P < 0.001), with the quadratic model providing the best fit. Full robotic navigation (double navigation) significantly improves anteversion-angle positioning efficiency (fewer attempts), reduces fluoroscopy time span and exposure frequency (suggesting lower radiation exposure), and decreases visible intraoperative blood loss. However, anteversion accuracy still depends on patient anatomy, particularly medullary canal diameter, necessitating consideration during preoperative planning. Moreover, the learning curve showed rapid early improvement, followed by a gradual plateau.

articles.title: Lactate-to-albumin ratio and 28-day mortality in older postoperative ICU patients: A prospective cohort study with MIMIC-IV replication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older postoperative intensive care patients have heterogeneous mortality risk related to acute illness severity, frailty, and reduced physiological reserve. The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) integrates routinely available markers of perioperative physiological stress, but its prognostic value remains uncertain.
METHODS: Patients aged ≥65 years admitted to a postoperative intensive care unit were prospectively enrolled. LAR was measured at ICU admission, whereas APACHE II used the worst values during the first 24 h. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality. LAR was compared with lactate, albumin, blood urea nitrogen-to-albumin ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, Prognostic Nutritional Index, and Hemoglobin-Albumin-Lymphocyte-Platelet index. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, APACHE II score, Clinical Frailty Scale score, surgical urgency, and comorbidity burden. A harmonized replication analysis was conducted in the MIMIC-IV surgical ICU cohort. Internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples provided optimism-corrected estimates of discrimination, calibration, and overall model performance.
RESULTS: Among 647 patients, 79 (12.2%) died within 28 days. LAR showed the highest discrimination (AUC, 0.803; 95% CI, 0.753-0.851) and was independently associated with mortality (adjusted OR per SD, 3.40; 95% CI, 2.33-4.96). LAR slightly outperformed lactate as a single marker (ΔAUC, 0.029; p = 0.002). Clinical models with LAR or lactate showed similar discrimination (optimism-corrected AUC, 0.885 vs 0.883; ΔAUC, 0.0014; 95% CI, -0.0071 to 0.0099; p = 0.750). In MIMIC-IV, LAR remained independently associated with 28-day mortality (OR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.28-1.94; AUC, 0.704).
CONCLUSIONS: LAR was independently associated with 28-day mortality and performed similarly to lactate when added to the 24-h clinical model, supporting its role as a complementary biomarker. The association was reproduced in MIMIC-IV with attenuation.

articles.title: Environmental scan of Indigenous resources and culturally specific tools across intensive care units in Alberta, Canada.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Indigenous Peoples in Canada are disproportionately burdened with a spectrum of health issues and consistently report lower satisfaction with their health care; nevertheless, little is known about their experiences with critical care and the support received during critical illness. We aimed to describe the current scope of critical-care-specific resources available to Indigenous patients and their families across Alberta to identify gaps and opportunities to implement actionable change to realize more equitable and culturally safe care.
SOURCE: We conducted a two-phase environmental scan. Phase 1 entailed searching websites for information to support Indigenous patients, their families, and health care workers. Phase 2 facilitated 21 interviews with intensive care unit (ICU) stakeholders from across Alberta to further describe site-specific resources, services, tools, or initiatives to support Indigenous Peoples. Indigenous partners were engaged through all aspects of the project.
PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Our environmental scan identified a paucity of ICU-specific resources, programs, or policies to support Indigenous patients and families' navigation with critical care. We identified two national resources aimed at clinicians, rather than patients or families. Interviews with ICU stakeholders confirmed the paucity of Indigenous-specific resources. Stakeholders cited numerous barriers, including inadequate culture training, staff time constraints and burnout, physical space limits, and insufficient personnel, such as Indigenous liaisons and social workers.
CONCLUSIONS: Multiple gaps exist in the availability of critical-care-focused resources and supports for Indigenous Peoples experiencing critical illness in Alberta, Canada. Addressing these care gaps may improve health equity, access, and the experience for Indigenous patients and families during critical illness and further build trust and strengthen relationships with health care workers.

articles.title: Expert consensus on neuro-musculoskeletal functional reconstruction for post-stroke spastic hemiplegia.
articles.abstract: Persistent motor dysfunction in post-stroke spastic hemiplegia may result from impaired voluntary motor control, abnormal muscle overactivity, fixed structural restriction, muscle force imbalance, or their combination. Advances in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), peripheral nerve surgery, and tendon and soft-tissue reconstruction have expanded therapeutic options, yet optimal indications and sequencing remain unclear. A multidisciplinary expert panel reviewed current evidence, addressed key clinical questions, and developed consensus recommendations for noninvasive BCI, diagnostic motor nerve block (DNB), selective or hyperselective peripheral nerve surgery, and reconstructive procedures. The consensus emphasizes evaluation of four major components: central voluntary motor impairment, dynamic abnormal muscle overactivity, fixed structural limitations, and muscle force imbalance. Treatment should be guided by the patient's functional goals and the primary factor restricting performance. Task-oriented motor training remains fundamental when voluntary motor control is impaired, with BCI-based closed-loop training as a potential adjunct in selected patients. Focal, functionally significant muscle overactivity caused by abnormal neural drive may be considered for selective or hyperselective peripheral nerve surgery, with DNB assisting patient selection. Fixed structural restrictions may require tendon or soft-tissue procedures, while muscle force imbalance may benefit from tendon transfer or other dynamic reconstruction. When multiple impairments coexist, combined reconstruction followed by targeted motor retraining and comprehensive reassessment may be appropriate. Overall, neuro-musculoskeletal functional reconstruction should follow an individualized pathway linking functional goals, dominant pathophysiology, treatment targets, and outcomes. Given the variable evidence quality, no universal treatment sequence or combination strategy is currently supported.
authors: “Zunyi Brain‐Computer Interface Medical Center” Working Group

articles.title: From Framework to Toolkit: Practical Guidance for Using the PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PrOcess Evaluation of Trials In Critical care (POETIC) framework was developed to support systematic evaluation of Context, Fidelity, Dose, Reach, and an integrative assessment of Quality of Delivery (QoD). Its practical use, however, requires explicit guidance on selecting measures, constructing QoD, assessing changing context, and governing prospective use.
METHODS: We undertook a retrospective comparative synthesis of process evaluations embedded in four randomized U.K. critical care trials: Biomarker-guided antibiotic stewardship in suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAPrapid-2), Provision of Psychological Support to People in Intensive Care (POPPI), Sedation AND Weaning In CHildren (SANDWICH), and Alpha-2 agonists for sedation to produce Better outcomes from critical illness (A2B). We selected them because they informed POETIC's development or application and provided sufficiently detailed quantitative and qualitative evidence. We mapped the reports, protocols, and process evaluation findings to the five dimensions; compared recurring and contradictory patterns, quantitative-qualitative agreement, measurement and interpretation problems, and mechanism-specific limitations; and translated our learning into guidance for applying the framework.
RESULTS: The relevance and measurement of POETIC dimensions varied according to how each intervention was expected to work. Contextual influences changed over time and differed between sites. Combined assessments of QoD required explicit decisions about component selection, weighting, thresholds, aggregation, and missing data. VAPrapid-2 showed why a separate Dose measure and a QoD composite were not meaningful for a one-off diagnostic recommendation; POPPI used a weighted site composite; SANDWICH summarized delivery of four intervention components, staff training, and patient Reach; and A2B combined four equally weighted indicators in a 0-12 site score. This cross-trial learning informed practical guidance on selecting measures, assessing context over time, integrating quantitative and qualitative findings, constructing QoD, and governing prospective use.
CONCLUSIONS: POETIC is best used as a mechanism-aligned, mixed-method scaffold rather than a requirement to measure every dimension or calculate a universal composite. Prospective use is feasible when outputs, recipients, review times, permitted actions, and safeguards are prespecified. The framework and accompanying toolkit support reproducible assessment while protecting trial integrity.

articles.title: Early Perioperative Recovery Patterns Across Diverse Minimally Invasive Orthopedic Procedures: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Minimally invasive orthopedic surgery (MIOS) has been increasingly adopted to reduce surgical trauma and facilitate postoperative recovery. However, few datasets describe real-world early recovery across diverse minimally invasive procedures. This prospective observational cohort study enrolled 200 adult patients who underwent minimally invasive orthopedic surgery at a tertiary academic center between 15 December 2022 and 31 December 2024. Procedures included minimally invasive spine surgery, minimally invasive total knee arthroplasty (TKA), minimally invasive total hip arthroplasty (THA), percutaneous sacroiliac joint fusion (SI arthrodesis), and arthroscopic or percutaneous fixation procedures. Primary outcomes were hospital stay, time to independent ambulation, VAS pain score, and patient-reported functional outcome. Secondary outcomes included operative time, blood loss in the operating room, complications, readmission, and reoperation. The median hospital stay was 2.1 days (interquartile range [IQR] 1.4-2.9), and the median time to independent ambulation was 1.6 days (IQR 1.1-2.1). Mean operative time was 91.1 ± 24.0 minutes, and mean estimated blood loss was 136.6 ± 47.7 mL. Preoperatively, patients had a mean VAS pain score of 7.2 ± 1.1, which decreased to 3.1 ± 0.8 at hospital discharge. There was a significant improvement in functional outcome for all procedure categories (p < 0.001). The overall incidence of complications was 7.5% (95% CI 3.8-11.2%). The 30-day readmission rate was 2.0% (n = 4), and the 90-day reoperation rate was 1.0% (n = 2). These findings characterize early perioperative recovery trajectories across five categories of minimally invasive orthopedic procedures, providing benchmark recovery timelines to support preoperative patient counseling and inform future comparative studies.

articles.title: Emergency Surgery and Preoperative Frailty with Postoperative Pulmonary Complications in Elderly Patients Undergoing Major Abdominal Surgery.
articles.abstract: This single-center retrospective study investigated associations of emergency surgery and preoperative frailty with postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) in elderly major abdominal surgery patients. Of 350 initially recruited patients at The First Hospital of Jiaxing (Mar 2024-Mar 2025), 294 were eligible after screening and stratified into PPCs (n = 53) and non-PPCs (n = 241) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified PPC predictors; interaction analysis evaluated their joint effect. Receiver operating characteristic curves evaluated the predictive performance of individual indicators and the combined model. Between-group disparities were identified in age, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, smoking, diabetes, emergency surgery, preoperative frailty, assess respiratory risk in surgical patients in Catalonia (ARISCAT) score, infusion volume, and postoperative day 1 visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score (all P < 0.05). The PPCs group had higher rates of emergency surgery (P = 0.002) and preoperative frailty (P < 0.001). Patients with both emergency surgery and preoperative frailty had a 35.7% PPCs rate (P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified age, ARISCAT score, postoperative day 1 VAS pain score, emergency surgery, and preoperative frailty as independent factors associated with PPCs (all P < 0.05). Emergency surgery and preoperative frailty were both independent risk factors for PPCs, and their combination showed a significant multiplicative interaction [interaction odds ratio (OR) = 1.363, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.010-1.832, P = 0.044], yielding a joint OR notably higher than either factor alone. A combined model including age, emergency surgery, preoperative frailty, ARISCAT score, and postoperative day 1 VAS score achieved an area under the curve of 0.894 (95% CI: 0.833-0.956), which was higher than any single indicator (all P < 0.05). Preoperative frailty was associated with PPCs more strongly than emergency surgery in this cohort, and the two factors showed a joint association; assessment and intensified care are recommended.

articles.title: Orthopedic trauma in patients with opioid use disorder: Current concepts in perioperative management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is an important challenge in orthopedic trauma, where acute injury intersects with preexisting opioid exposure, tolerance, complex pain, and barriers to continuity of addiction treatment. OUD has been associated with higher rates of complications, readmission, and treatment disruption, yet OUD-specific perioperative management remains inconsistently incorporated into orthopedic trauma practice. This review synthesizes the epidemiology, outcomes, and perioperative management evidence for this population.
METHODS: A clinically oriented current concepts review synthesized peer-reviewed literature, prioritizing studies published from 2013 onward. PubMed and Embase were searched, supplemented by Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, and manual review of reference lists from relevant articles. Studies examining perioperative outcomes, multimodal analgesia, and management of medications for OUD (MOUD) relevant to orthopedic trauma were included; studies limited to pediatric, elderly, or prenatal populations were excluded.
RESULTS: Preinjury opioid exposure is common among orthopedic trauma patients, whereas formally diagnosed OUD is less prevalent, affecting approximately 1% of operative trauma patients and up to 2.3% of patients with open lower-extremity fractures. OUD and opioid-related disorders are associated with higher rates of infection, nonunion, revision, prolonged hospitalization, and readmission. Consensus guidance and observational evidence support continuation of evidence-based MOUD, individualized opioid supplementation, multimodal nonopioid analgesia, regional anesthesia when appropriate, and early coordination with addiction and acute pain services. Guideline-based approaches to postoperative opioid prescribing, tapering, and patient education are also summarized.
CONCLUSIONS: Orthopedic trauma patients with OUD require individualized, multidisciplinary perioperative care. The strongest available evidence supports preservation of OUD treatment, multimodal analgesia, early addiction and pain consultation, and coordinated discharge planning rather than either opioid avoidance or opioid-only treatment. The review concludes with the authors' recommendations for the operating surgeon, including in-hospital and outpatient tapering plans, management of requests for additional opioids, and patient education.

articles.title: Evaluating the usefulness and reporting quality of randomized clinical trials for pediatric tonsillectomy pharmacologic interventions: A systematic assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) underpin evidence-based perioperative and pharmacologic care in pediatric tonsillectomy, yet their real-world usefulness depends on clinically meaningful design and transparent reporting. We applied the van 't Hooft usefulness framework, an eight-criterion, 13-item instrument derived from the features of useful clinical research described by Ioannidis, to appraise the usefulness and reporting quality of contemporary pediatric tonsillectomy pharmacology RCTs.
METHODS: We systematically identified RCTs of pharmacologic interventions in children undergoing tonsillectomy or adenotonsillectomy, published in English between 2019 and 2025. Records were screened in duplicate (Rayyan) with third-reviewer adjudication. Each trial was scored on 13 items across two domains (core clinical utility and transparency) on a 0-2 scale (0 = not fulfilled, 1 = partial, 2 = full; maximum composite score 26). The problem-base item was adjudicated by an otolaryngology resident physician. We summarized item- and domain-level fulfillment, examined temporal trends, and assessed the correlation between the utility and transparency domains.
RESULTS: Sixty-two RCTs met inclusion criteria. The median composite usefulness score was 11 of 26 (IQR 10-15; mean 11.8 ± 3.8), and only 1 trial (1.6%) exceeded 75% of the maximum. Most trials were conducted in Asia (41; 66%) and published in general medicine (21; 34%) or otolaryngology (19; 31%) journals; the median journal impact factor was 2.00 (IQR 1.30-2.90). Pragmatic design was nearly absent (0 trials fully pragmatic; 60/62 [96.8%] non-pragmatic), no trial included a value-for-money assessment (62/62 [100%] absent), and only 7 trials (11.3%) made raw data available. Utility and transparency domain scores were weakly positively correlated (r = 0.30, p = 0.016). Composite usefulness increased modestly over the study period (+0.75 points/year, p = 0.018), driven by the utility domain; journal impact factor was the only independent predictor of usefulness in multivariable analysis (β = 0.57, p = 0.049).
CONCLUSION: Contemporary pediatric tonsillectomy pharmacology RCTs show consistent deficits in pragmatism, patient-centered design, economic evaluation, and data transparency. Systematic adoption of the van 't Hooft usefulness criteria and established reporting standards (SPIRIT, CONSORT) at the design stage could help improve the clinical value of future trials in this high-volume surgical population.

articles.title: Perioperative Blood Management in General Surgery: Recent Advances, Current Limitations, and the Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Patient blood management (PBM) is a patient-centered approach to blood use that aligns with modern medical practice. It is based on multidisciplinary collaboration and evidence-based medicine. Its aim is to improve clinical outcomes by correcting preoperative anemia, reducing perioperative blood loss, standardizing transfusion practices, and optimizing the management of coagulation function. Patients undergoing general surgery, particularly complex liver surgery or gastrointestinal cancer surgery, often face preoperative anemia, intraoperative bleeding, increased transfusion requirements, and postoperative coagulation abnormalities. These factors make perioperative blood management more complex. This narrative review searched PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) for relevant studies published over the past 10 years. It summarizes recent advances, current limitations, and challenges in the clinical translation of perioperative blood management in general surgery. This review focuses on the assessment and management of preoperative anemia, bleeding control and hemostatic strategies, transfusion management, coagulation monitoring, and thrombotic risk management. It also discusses recent advances and current limitations in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for risk prediction, clinical decision support, and individualized management. Current evidence suggests that PBM may help optimize perioperative care in general surgery. AI/ML may also support clinical decision-making by predicting bleeding risk, estimating transfusion requirements, and stratifying thrombotic risk. However, studies specifically focusing on general surgery patients remain limited. Most available evidence comes from cardiac surgery, orthopedics, or other surgical populations. In addition, current prediction models still have several limitations, including insufficient external validation, a lack of prospective evaluation, and limited interpretability. Therefore, these models should currently be used only as tools to support clinical judgment. Therefore, future studies should include more multicenter prospective research in general surgery populations. AI/ML-assisted decision support should also be further explored within standardized PBM pathways to improve the precision and standardization of perioperative blood management in general surgery.

articles.title: Low-Dose Epidural Hydromorphone as an Adjunct to Ropivacaine for Intraoperative Visceral Traction Pain During Elective Cesarean Delivery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Visceral traction during cesarean delivery may cause pain, nausea, and autonomic activation despite an adequate neuraxial block. We evaluated whether adding 0.3 mg epidural hydromorphone to ropivacaine altered patient-reported pain and clinically relevant traction responses across predefined perioperative phases.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 96 women undergoing elective cesarean delivery were randomized 1:1 to epidural hydromorphone or saline. The registered primary outcome domains were visual analog scale (VAS) pain score and heart rate variability (HRV) across five time points. Other prespecified clinical measures included clinician-rated traction response, maternal adverse events, and neonatal outcomes. The protocol-specified repeated-measures analysis was used for longitudinal pain; abdominal exploration (T2) was selected after registration as the focal phase for detailed reporting.
RESULTS: All 96 women completed the trial. The longitudinal pain analysis showed a group-by-time interaction (Greenhouse-Geisser corrected p=0.008; participant-level randomization-based permutation p=0.009). At the post-registration focal comparison during abdominal exploration, median (IQR) VAS was 1.65 (0.70-2.60) with hydromorphone and 1.90 (0.78-3.92) with saline (nominal Mann-Whitney p=0.039). Clinician-rated traction grade favored hydromorphone (trend p=0.003). Nausea or vomiting occurred in 3/48 (6.2%) versus 12/48 (25.0%) women (risk ratio 0.25, 95% CI 0.08-0.83; p=0.022). For the registered HRV domain, the interaction for ln(LF/HF), selected after registration as the principal reported metric, was not significant (p=0.442). No maternal respiratory depression occurred, and neonatal outcomes showed no material between-group differences.
CONCLUSION: Low-dose epidural hydromorphone added to ropivacaine was associated with a different longitudinal pain profile and fewer episodes of intraoperative nausea or vomiting during elective cesarean delivery. Post hoc pain-distribution and exploratory physiological findings require prospective confirmation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400094749; registered December 26, 2024, before enrollment.

articles.title: Perioperative immunogenomics and clinical outcomes under ERAS-based nursing care in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical trauma is associated with perioperative immune perturbation in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) combines multidisciplinary perioperative management with structured nursing care, but its immunogenomic associations remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: This retrospective historical-control cohort included 126 MIBC patients undergoing radical cystectomy with Bricker ileal conduit (ERAS-based care, n = 63; conventional care, n = 63). Serial peripheral immune profiling was performed at T0 (preoperative), T1 (24 h postoperative), and T2 (POD7/discharge). Tumor analyses included multiplex immunofluorescence, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and NanoString immune-gene profiling; spatial transcriptomics was performed in 24 specimens (12/group). Clinical outcomes included 30-day infectious complications and survival, while biomarker and immunogenomic analyses were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: ERAS-based care was associated with a less pronounced postoperative CD8+ T-cell decline (22.8% vs. 41.6%, P < 0.001) and lower T1 serum IL-6 (43.2 vs. 87.4 pg/mL, P < 0.001). An exploratory four-marker T1 immune index (CD8+ count, IL-6, sPD-L1, and NK activity) showed predictive performance for 30-day infectious complications (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI 0.76-0.92). In resection specimens, the ERAS cohort had a higher proportion of the immune-inflamed tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) phenotype (52.4% vs. 28.6%, P = 0.012). Exploratory survival analyses also identified associations with an eight-gene immune signature and TMB status; these findings require validation.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, ERAS-based perioperative nursing and multidisciplinary care were associated with differences in systemic immune recovery, postoperative outcomes, and cross-sectional tumor immune features. The proposed immune-marker and gene-signature findings are exploratory and require independent validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Development and multicenter validation of a machine learning model for predicting in-hospital postoperative cardiac arrest in elderly surgical patients: the critical role of intraoperative hemodynamic disturbances and blood transfusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is a rare but life-threatening complication in elderly surgical patients. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model for predicting IHCA and to identify key perioperative risk factors.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients aged ≥65 years who underwent non-cardiac surgery at six tertiary hospitals between January 2020 and January 2025. Clinical, laboratory, and perioperative variables were collected. Five machine learning algorithms, including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), were developed and compared. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, cross-validation, and external validation. SHAP analysis was applied to interpret the optimal model.
RESULTS: Among the five models, XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.967 and 0.960 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. It also achieved the lowest Brier score and the highest clinical net benefit. External validation confirmed excellent discrimination (AUC=0.971) and calibration. SHAP analysis identified advanced age, intraoperative tachycardia, intraoperative hypotension, intraoperative blood transfusion, intraoperative hypoxemia, elevated postoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, B-type natriuretic peptide, lactate, and D-dimer levels as the most important predictors of IHCA.
CONCLUSION: An interpretable XGBoost-based model demonstrated excellent performance for predicting postoperative cardiac arrest in elderly patients. The identified risk factors reflected perioperative vulnerability, intraoperative hemodynamic instability, and postoperative physiological deterioration.

articles.title: Effect of adding preoperative serratus anterior plane block to intercostal nerve block with liposomal bupivacaine on postoperative pain in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection: study protocol for a prospective randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative pain management is fundamental to enhanced recovery after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Previous studies have demonstrated that both serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) and intercostal nerve block (ICNB) effectively alleviate postoperative pain. However, data on the combination of these two techniques using liposomal bupivacaine, a sustained-release local anesthetic formulation, remain limited. Accordingly, this randomized controlled trial aims to compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of combined preoperative SAPB and intraoperative ICNB vs. sham SAPB plus active ICNB in patients undergoing VATS lung resection, with liposomal bupivacaine administered for both blocks.
METHODS: This single-center randomized controlled trial will enroll 98 patients scheduled for video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection to compare the postoperative analgesic efficacy of combined preoperative SAPB and intraoperative ICNB vs. sham SAPB plus intraoperative ICNB, with liposomal bupivacaine administered for both nerve blocks. The primary outcome is the VAS (0-10) pain score with movement at 24 h postoperatively; secondary outcomes include cumulative sufentanil consumption within 48 h and the number of patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) demands.
DISCUSSION: This trial will provide the first head-to-head evidence comparing the analgesic efficacy of combined SAPB and ICNB vs. sham SAPB plus ICNB using liposomal bupivacaine in VATS lung resection. If the combination strategy demonstrates superior analgesic efficacy, it may establish a more effective multimodal analgesic regimen for postoperative pain management in thoracic surgery. These findings are expected to inform clinical practice and guide the development of future perioperative analgesic protocols.Clinical Trial Registration: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=295245, identifier ChiCTR2500112224.

articles.title: Research trends and hotspots of liposomal bupivacaine: a bibliometric analysis from 2000 to 2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pain remains a persistent challenge in perioperative care, frequently contributing to delayed patient mobilization, hindered functional recovery, and increased opioid consumption. Liposomal bupivacaine was developed to extend the release duration of local anesthetics following a single-dose administration; however, its clinical utility exhibits considerable variability across surgical procedures, block techniques, and comparator regimens. From a bibliometric perspective, this study aims to systematically investigate the overall developmental trajectory, intellectual structure, and emerging research frontiers of liposomal bupivacaine.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was performed in the Web of Science and Scopus databases for studies on liposomal bupivacaine published between 2000 and 2025. After deduplicating and merging records from both databases using a custom script, the consolidated dataset was analyzed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the Bibliometrix R package.
RESULTS: A total of 3,552 publications were included in this study. The annual publication volume increased markedly between 2020 and 2025, reaching its peak in 2025. In terms of geographical and institutional distribution, the United States dominated the field, ranking first with 2,075 publications and 63,218 total citations; China ranked second with 565 publications, though its international co-authorship rate was only 13.23%. Major contributions were made by leading institutions such as the Mayo Clinic. At the author level, De Paula demonstrated the highest publication output and network betweenness centrality, Urman recorded the highest average citations per paper, and Onel accumulated the highest total citations; collectively, these three scholars constituted the intellectual core of the field with the most prominent contributions. Regarding journal distribution, The Journal of Arthroplasty ranked first in productivity, whereas Advanced Drug Delivery Reviews garnered the highest cumulative citations, reflecting distinct emphases on clinical translation and basic pharmaceutical dissemination, respectively. Co-citation clustering identified five major thematic domains: arthroplasty, liposomal bupivacaine, fascial plane blocks, breast reconstruction, and local anesthetic delivery. "Extended-release bupivacaine" emerged as a core keyword characterized by high occurrence and high centrality. Concurrently, "erector spinae plane block" and "autologous breast reconstruction" have surged rapidly in recent years, demonstrating an ongoing thematic shift toward procedure-specific applications.
CONCLUSION: This study represents the first quantitative bibliometric analysis of liposomal bupivacaine, revealing an evolutionary shift in research focus from early investigations centered on pharmacokinetics and formulation to diversified, procedure-specific clinical applications. Future studies should prioritize expanding international collaborative networks and further exploring emerging techniques, such as fascial plane blocks, across understudied surgical populations. This research roadmap provides directional guidance for investigators, clinicians, and funding agencies alike.

articles.title: Cadaveric study of the ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block over the dorsolateral edge of the transverse process of the ninth thoracic vertebra in dogs: transverse vs. longitudinal approach.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Studies of the ultrasound-guided thoracic erector spinae plane (ESP) blocks in dogs are limited. This study aimed to describe a transverse (TV) ultrasound-guided ESP approach at the dorsolateral edge of the transverse process (DLETP) of T9, compare its distribution with a longitudinal (LNG) approach, and analyze the thoracic transverse process anatomy.
METHODS: Twenty-three canine cadavers were used in this double-blinded experimental study. An ESP injection using 0.6 mL/kg of dye/contrast was performed on each lateral of 21 cadavers with a TV or LNG approach at T9, followed by computed tomography and dissection.
RESULTS: Five cadavers were excluded from dissection analysis. All TV injections were placed over the DLETP, whereas 18.75% of LNG injections were misplaced laterally. Both approaches produced craniocaudal spread within the ESP, with median (range) spreads of 8 (5-14) and 8.5 (4-13) vertebrae for the TV and LNG groups, respectively. Cranial spread exceeded caudal in the TV group, with 4.5 (2-6) vs. 3.5 (0-7) vertebrae (p = 0.027), and LNG, with 5 (3-7) vs. 3 (0-6) (p = 0.004).
