Staining of the medial branches of the dorsal rami (MBDR) of the spinal nerves showed median (range) values of 5 (4-8) and 5 (0-6) in TV and LNG. Cranial MBDR staining predominated in TV, with 4.5 (1-6) over caudal with 1 (0-3) (p = 0.003), and LNG, with 4 (0-6) vs. 0 (0-3) (p < 0.001). Lateral branches (LBDR) staining showed 4 (1-9) and 4 (2-12) in TV and LNG. Cranial LBDR staining exceeded caudal in TV, with 3 (0-6) vs. 1 (0-3) (p = 0.019), and LNG, with 3 (1-8) vs. 1 (0-5) (p = 0.034). Ventral branches staining occurred in 10/16 TV injections (62.5%) and 11/16 (68.75%) LNG. Both approaches showed epidural and sympathetic trunk spread while one intravascular injection occurred in LNG. No significant differences were found between approaches. The DLETP was predominantly absent caudal to T10 and smaller than the transverse process (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The TV and LNG approaches produced comparable nerve staining and ESP spread at T9 in dogs, with preferential cranial distribution. The TV approach reduced injectate misplacement. The DLETP was smaller than the transverse process and consistently identified cranial to T11.

articles.title: A novel endoscopy-guided airway management strategy for lateral decubitus endoscopic procedures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigates the feasibility and safety of gastrointestinal endoscopy-guided endotracheal intubation in patients undergoing elective gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery under general anesthesia requiring airway management in the lateral decubitus position.
METHODS: Forty patients undergoing elective gastrointestinal endoscopy in the left lateral decubitus position were enrolled. Standardized anesthesia induction included midazolam, etomidate, sufentanil, and atracurium. Under endoscopic visualization, endotracheal intubation was performed using a stiff stylet-assisted tube inserted through a bite block's right lateral port. Primary outcomes were first-attempt success rate and intubation time. Secondary outcomes included hemodynamic stability, adverse events, and procedural complications.
RESULTS: The first-attempt intubation success rate was 100%. The mean intubation time was 30.95 ± 6.58 s. Hemodynamic parameters showed a transient hypotensive response following induction in 15 out of 40 patients (37.5%); MAP had returned to ≥65 mmHg by the post-intubation measurement, and no vasopressor agents were administered. Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed a statistically significant main effect of time on both MAP [F (3.048, 118.888) = 23.05, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.372] and HR [F (4, 156) = 3.258, p = 0.013, partial η 2 = 0.077], with a transient stress response observed post-intubation (maximal increase: MAP +4.5%, HR +6.1% vs. baseline). No severe complications (e.g., esophageal intubation, dental injury, hypoxia) occurred (0/40; 95% CI: 0%-8.8%). Mild sore throat was observed in 22.5% of cases, resolving spontaneously within 24 h.
CONCLUSION: In this feasibility cohort, gastrointestinal endoscopy-guided endotracheal intubation demonstrated a 100% first-attempt success rate with a mean intubation time of 30.95 ± 6.58 s and no severe complications. These preliminary findings suggest that the technique appears to be a feasible and safe option for airway management in patients undergoing lateral-position gastrointestinal endoscopy. However, these findings are from an uncontrolled, single-center study with a limited sample size. Larger comparative studies are warranted to confirm these results.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT06990490.

articles.title: Irrigation fluid absorption induces metabolic and oxidative stress dysregulation activating NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways to drive hippocampal inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Irrigation fluid absorption during endoscopic procedures can lead to serious complications, but its effects on hippocampal function remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the impact of irrigation fluid absorption on hippocampal metabolic homeostasis and inflammatory responses.
METHODS: Adult female Sprague-Dawley rats received intravenous 0.9% saline (control, 40 mL/kg, or 80 mL/kg) to simulate irrigation fluid absorption. Saline was infused over 30 min, and the animals were euthanized 15 min after cessation of anesthesia, corresponding to 45 min after initiation of the infusion. We assessed emergence time from anesthesia, hippocampal energy metabolism through targeted metabolomics, mitochondrial ultrastructure via transmission electron microscopy (TEM), oxidative stress markers, and NLRP3- and NF-κB-related inflammatory markers.
RESULTS: The 80 mL/kg group showed significantly prolonged anesthesia emergence time compared to controls (59.0 ± 13.5 vs. 31.7 ± 4.5 s; p < 0.01). Metabolomics revealed dose-dependent perturbations in the TCA cycle, glycolysis, and oxidative phosphorylation (p < 0.05). TEM analysis demonstrated severe mitochondrial ultrastructural damage in hippocampal neurons, including dose-dependent swelling, internal membrane disruption, and matrix dissolution. Both absorption groups showed altered glutathione redox status, characterized by increased GSSG levels and decreased GSH/GSSG ratios (p < 0.01), whereas SOD, CAT, MDA, NADPH, and GSH exhibited heterogeneous and non-linear changes across doses. At this early endpoint, increased NLRP3, P50/P65, IL-6, IL-18, and IL-33 immunoreactivity, together with decreased IκB immunoreactivity, indicated early changes in NLRP3- and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling.
CONCLUSION: Excessive irrigation fluid absorption induces hippocampal neuroinflammation through metabolic disturbance and redox dysregulation, which activates NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways. These findings suggest potential therapeutic targets for preventing neurological complications during endoscopic procedures.

articles.title: Palatal microcirculation in minimal-incision cleft palate repair: Impact of lateral releasing incisions - A controlled intraoperative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tissue perfusion is critical for wound healing after cleft palate repair. Many palatoplasty techniques incorporate lateral releasing incisions for tissue mobilization, yet their impact on palatal microcirculation remains unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, children aged 7-15 months underwent primary cleft palate repair using medial-only or medial-and-lateral incision palatoplasty; children who underwent cleft lip repair alone served as controls. Tissue oxygen saturation (StO₂%) was measured noninvasively at the premaxilla, hard and soft palate before and after surgery using visible light spectroscopy. The primary outcome was change in StO₂% (ΔStO₂%). Secondary outcomes included perioperative complications, fistulas, and associations with cleft severity assessed using the palatal index.
RESULTS: Seventy patients were included. Medial-only palatoplasty was associated with better preservation of palatal tissue oxygenation than lateral incision palatoplasty. In complete cleft palate, ∆StO2% at the hard and soft palate differed between the incision designs, with medial-only incisions showing values closer to controls. In unilateral cleft lip and palate, lateral incisions reduced ∆StO2% at most sites compared with the controls, with the greatest reduction in the non-cleft hard palate, whereas medial-only incisions were comparable to the controls. No consistent association was identified between palatal index and ΔStO₂%. Perioperative complications were rare, and fistula rates were similar between the incision designs.
CONCLUSION: Palatal tissue oxygenation varied with cleft type and incision design. Medial-only palatoplasty was associated with better preservation of palatal tissue oxygenation. This suggest, that incision design may represent a modifiable surgical factor associated with early postoperative tissue perfusion during cleft palate repair.

articles.title: Impact of obesity on reduction quality and operative outcomes of proximal femoral nail for intertrochanteric femoral fractures in the lateral decubitus position.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study is to compare the clinical and radiological outcomes of proximal femoral nailing performed in the lateral decubitus position between obese and non-obese patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study, approved by the institutional ethics committee, included patients with acute AO/OTA classification types 31A1, 31A2, and 31A3 intertrochanteric femoral fractures treated with closed reduction and osteosynthesis using a short proximal femoral nail between 2022 and 2024. Obesity was defined as a body mass index of ≥ 30 kg/m2. Patients were divided into obese and non-obese groups, and clinical, radiological, and complication outcomes were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: A total of 533 patients were included, comprising 95 obese and 438 non-obese individuals. Obese patients were significantly younger and had higher Charlson Comorbidity Index scores (p < 0.001). Operative time and intensive care unit admission rates were significantly higher in the obese group (p < 0.001), and anesthesia type distribution differed between groups (p < 0.001). Length of hospital stay and Harris Hip Scores were comparable (p > 0.05). Radiologically, the distribution of tip-apex distance according to the 25-mm threshold did not differ between groups (p = 0.244). However, optimal screw placement according to the Cleveland index was significantly less frequent in obese patients (p < 0.001), and malposition in the lateral view was more common (p < 0.001). Varus alignment and differences in reduction quality were also significantly associated with obesity status (p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that obesity remained an independent predictor of postoperative varus malalignment (OR 2.80, 95% CI 1.58-4.96; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Obesity negatively affects reduction quality and operative parameters during proximal femoral nailing for intertrochanteric femoral fractures performed in the lateral decubitus position, although acceptable reductions can generally still be achieved. Furthermore, obesity remained an independent predictor of postoperative varus malalignment after adjustment for potential confounding factors. Surgeons should be aware of these technical challenges when treating obese patients and consider them during preoperative planning and intraoperative reduction maneuvers.

articles.title: Immersive virtual reality (HypnoVR) for pain and anxiety reduction during wound care procedures.
Individualized intraoperative BIS targeting based on preoperative BIS values in the awake state: a review and strategy prospect for preventing postoperative delirium in older patients.
articles.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication in older surgical patients and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Bispectral Index (BIS) monitoring is widely used to guide intraoperative depth of anesthesia. However, the conventional strategy of maintaining a uniform BIS target range may not adequately account for interindividual differences in preoperative brain function, particularly in older adults with reduced neural reserve. This narrative review integrates evidence from three complementary domains: 1) clinical studies evaluating the association between preoperative resting BIS values in the awake state and the risk of POD; 2) mechanistic and clinical evidence linking excessive anesthetic depth, particularly electroencephalographic burst suppression, to POD; 3) interventional trials assessing the effect of intraoperative BIS-guided anesthesia management on delirium outcomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that a lower preoperative resting BIS value in the awake state is potentially independently associated with an increased risk of POD in older patients. Intraoperative BIS-guided anesthesia has been shown to reduce exposure to deep anesthesia and EEG burst suppression, which are consistently linked to higher delirium incidence. These findings suggest that patients with preoperatively identified brain vulnerability may benefit from higher individualized intraoperative BIS targets, rather than a fixed universal range. Integrating preoperative resting BIS assessment into perioperative anesthesia management may enable risk stratification and support individualized regulation of anesthetic depth in older adults. When incorporated into a multimodal delirium prevention framework, this individualized approach may offer a rational pathway toward improved delirium prevention and perioperative neuroprotection in older adults, warranting validation in future prospective randomized studies.

articles.title: Perioperative Lactate, Survival, and Complications Following Lung Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine perioperative lactate and its association with survival and postoperative complications following lung transplantation (LTx).
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Academic tertiary-care transplant center.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing LTx between February 2018 and January 2023.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Serum lactate was measured at 6-hour intervals from the start of surgery, and the maximum value within the first 0 to 6 hours was recorded. Patients were categorized into the high-lactate group (upper quartile, ≥4.2 mmol/L) and low-lactate group (lower 3 quartiles). Primary outcomes were 1-year and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included renal failure, venous thromboembolism (VTE), primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3), mechanical ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and post-transplant length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Among 225 recipients (median age, 62.3 years; 34.2% female), high lactate was not associated with 1-year or overall survival. However, recipients with high lactate had higher rates of PGD3 at 72 hours (42.1% v 13.1%, p < 0.001), longer mechanical ventilation duration (3 days v 2 days, p = 0.003), longer ICU stay (11.6 days v 7 days, p = 0.013), and higher in-hospital mortality rate (7% v 0.6%, p = 0.019). No significant differences were observed in renal failure, VTE, or post-transplant length of stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated perioperative serum lactate was associated with PGD3 at 72 hours, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU stay, and in-hospital mortality but not 1-year or overall survival following LTx. These findings suggest that perioperative lactate may aid in identifying high-risk patients early in their postoperative course despite its lack of association with long-term survival.

articles.title: Efficiency of Blood Utilization in Elective Neurosurgery Patients and Development of a Maximum Surgical Blood Order Schedule.
articles.abstract: Objectives Primary Objective To evaluate the efficiency of perioperative blood utilization in elective neurosurgical procedures using the crossmatch-to-transfusion (C/T) ratio, transfusion probability (TP), and transfusion index (TI). Secondary Objective To develop procedure-specific maximum surgical blood ordering schedules (MSBOS) using Mead's criteria, categorizing procedures according to the need for no routine preoperative blood preparation, type-and-screen (T&S) only, or preoperative crossmatching, and to determine the recommended number of packed cell volume (PCV) units for procedures requiring crossmatching. Materials and methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted over six months at a tertiary care hospital. A total of 142 patients (100%) undergoing elective neurosurgical procedures were included. Details of blood grouping, cross-matching, and blood transfusion were recorded for each patient. Blood utilization was assessed using the C/T ratio, TP, and TI, and the MSBOS was formulated according to Mead's criteria. Statistical analysis The C/T ratio, TP, and TI were calculated using standard formulae. The MSBOS was derived using the formula MSBOS = 1.5 × TI to recommend the appropriate number of preoperative blood units for elective neurosurgical procedures. Results Blood grouping and cross-matching were performed in 136 (95.7%) and 135 (95.4%) patients, respectively. Blood transfusion was required in 29 patients (20.4%), with 44 units transfused. The overall C/T ratio was 9.1, while the TP and TI were 22.3% and 0.33, respectively, indicating inefficient blood utilization. Relatively efficient blood utilization was observed in spinal tumour surgery, aneurysm clipping, and meningioma resection. Based on the calculated MSBOS, one unit of packed red blood cells (PRBCs) was recommended for laminectomy, spine fixation, spinal tumour surgery, aneurysm clipping, and posterior fossa surgery, whereas two units were recommended for meningioma resection. Conclusions Blood utilization in elective neurosurgical procedures was inefficient. Implementation of a procedure-specific MSBOS may reduce unnecessary cross-matching, optimize blood resource utilization, and improve transfusion practices in neurosurgical patients.

articles.title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks for Postoperative Pain Management in Cardiothoracic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness, comparative effectiveness, and safety of peripheral nerve blocks for postoperative pain management after cardiothoracic surgery.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, with strength of evidence rated using the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality methodology (PROSPERO CRD42024549561).
SETTING: Perioperative care settings in studies published between 2013 and 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing open or minimally invasive cardiothoracic surgery.
INTERVENTIONS: Peripheral nerve blocks, including chest wall blocks and erector spinae plane blocks, compared with sham, no block, local infiltration, or neuraxial techniques.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 104 randomized controlled trials were included. Chest wall blocks reduced 24-hour pain scores and opioid consumption compared with sham or no block in both open cardiac and minimally invasive thoracic surgery. Erector spinae plane blocks demonstrated similar effects, with no clinically meaningful differences compared with chest wall blocks. Peripheral nerve blocks provided analgesia comparable to neuraxial techniques across several outcomes. Reported adverse events were rare and inconsistently defined.
CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral nerve blocks provide some reductions in postoperative pain and opioid use after cardiothoracic surgery and appear to have a favorable safety profile. Chest wall blocks and erector spinae plane blocks were found not to differ in effectiveness, and both offer analgesia comparable to neuraxial techniques.

articles.title: In Celebration of the Life and Contributions of J. Earl Wynands, MD, OC (Order of Canada).
articles.abstract: On November 14, 2025, Dr. John Earl Wynands died at the age of 94, leaving behind a legacy defined by clinical innovation, mentorship, and a lifelong commitment to advancing patient care and medical education. He was one of the pioneers in the development of anesthesiology for cardiac disease, an early member and later a board member and president of the Society of Cardiovascular Anesthesiologists and one of the founders and first associate editor of the Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia. In this memorial, the authors review his career and his many contributions and notable publications.

articles.title: A Comparison of Pediatric Patient Populations and Clinical Treatment at a Hospital Dental Clinic and School-Based Dental Clinic.
articles.abstract: Purpose: To compare pediatric patient populations and clinical treatment data at a children's hospital dental clinic (HDC) and a school based dental clinic (SBC). Methods: Retrospective data for patients treated over 17 months at both clinics were abstracted from electronic health records. Patients with caries from each clinic were matched based on age, sex, insurance status, and diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and treatment visit data were compared. Results: Included were 31,547 unique patients treated in a HDC versus 1,348 in an SBC. The SBC served a higher proportion of nonWhite patients (P<0.001), patients with lower child opportunity index (COI) scores (P<0.001), and patients with Medicaid (P=0.043) or no insurance (P=0.015). The HDC treated a higher proportion of Latino/Hispanic patients (P<0.001), households with a home language other than English (P<0.001), and patients with ASD. Treatment data comparing the 556 matched pairs revealed that SBC patients had a higher mean number of visits (P<0.001), more treatment plans completed (P<0.001), and a higher average number of procedures completed (P<0.001). SBC patients had better cooperation (P<0.001) without access to nitrous oxide and with fewer referrals for general anesthesia (P<0.001). Conclusions: Comparable to the hospital dental clinic, school-based dentistry provided comprehensive and, in some ways, superior dental treatment for children of all ages and access for uniquely vulnerable populations such as nonWhite children, Medicaid or uninsured children, and children from low COI zip codes.

articles.title: Acceptability, Feasibility, and Satisfaction of Buzzy®and VibradentTM for Pain and Anxiety Management in Children During Local Anesthesia Administration.
articles.abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the efficacy of 2 vibrotactile devices, Buzzy® and VibradentTM, in reducing pain and anxiety during local anesthesia (LA) administration for dental extractions in children. Methods: The study included 126 children aged 7 to 10 years, divided into 3 groups (N=42 each): Group 1 (conventional syringe), Group 2 (Vibradent TM), and Group 3 (Buzzy®). Pain was assessed using the Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale (WBFPS), Face-Legs-Activity-Cry-Consolability scale (FLACC), and Sound-Eye-Motor scale (SEM) at baseline (T0), needle insertion (Tn), and end of local anesthesia administration (Te). Anxiety was measured through the Facial-Image-Scale (FIS) and heart rate. Salivary cortisol was evaluated at T0 and T20 (20 minutes after needle insertion) to assess physiological stress. Parent and child satisfaction were also recorded. Results: Both Buzzy® and VibradentTM significantly reduced pain, anxiety, and salivary cortisol compared to the control group (P<0.001). Buzzy® showed more favorable outcomes in WBFPS, FLACC, SEM, heart rate, and FIS scores (P<0.05) and the highest satisfaction ratings. Both devices showed significantly lower salivary cortisol levels (P<0.05), with no significant difference between them. Conclusions: Buzzy® and Vibradent TM are effective, non-invasive techniques for reducing pain, anxiety, and physiological stress. Buzzy® demonstrated superior overall efficacy.

articles.title: Anesthetic Considerations for Delivery of Patients with Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.abstract: Pregnant patients with cardiovascular disease benefit from early evaluation by a pregnancy heart team and formal risk stratification to guide delivery planning and determine the need for care at a tertiary center. Carefully titrated neuraxial anesthesia is preferred to reduce maternal catecholamines, decrease cardiac workload, and enable controlled hemodynamic management. From a cardiovascular standpoint, vaginal delivery is generally favored over cesarean delivery due to its more gradual hemodynamic changes and lower physiologic stress. Intrapartum management should be guided by lesion-specific physiology, with contingencies in place for obstetric and cardiac emergencies.

articles.title: Washout characteristics of sevoflurane and desflurane in surgical patients: a prospective observational study using gas chromatography - ion mobility spectrometry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sevoflurane and desflurane are routinely used volatile anaesthetics in balanced general anaesthesia, but their elimination time from the human body may be underestimated.
METHODS: Levels of sevoflurane and desflurane in end-tidal exhaled breath and ambient room air were measured pre- and post-operatively using calibrated Gas Chromatography-Ion Mobility Spectrometry (GC-IMS). Exponential regressions were applied to determine half-lives and to estimate the time required for exhaled breath concentrations to return to baseline (preoperative) levels.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine surgical patients (aged 18-87 years) were enrolled. A total of 526 exhaled breath and 263 ambient room air samples were analysed. In ASA II patients, the median elimination half-life was 6.5 h (IQR: 5.4-10.1) for sevoflurane and 12.8 h (IQR: 7.4-18.7) for desflurane. The estimated time for exhaled breath concentrations to return to preoperative values ranged from 66 to 737 h for sevoflurane and 135 to 593 h for desflurane.
CONCLUSION: GC-IMS detected trace concentrations of exhaled sevoflurane and desflurane well beyond the immediate postoperative period. These findings suggest prolonged low-level elimination, although the clinical relevance of this extended washout remains unclear.

articles.title: Cardiovascular adaptation to spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension during scheduled cesarean section: the paradigm of ionized calcium and nitric oxide in a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal arterial hypotension occurs in 55-90% of cesarean sections performed under spinal anesthesia. While sympatholysis and aortocaval compression are conventional explanations, refractory cases suggest possible biochemical contributors beyond sympatholysis. We hypothesized that an acute deficit in ionized calcium coupled with endothelial mediator overproduction may constitute a "double lock" mechanism that contributes to hemodynamic decompensation. This prospective observational study examined these associations.
METHODS: A prospective, single-center analytical study was conducted from June 2025 to February 2026 at the Centre Hospitalier d'Essos, Yaoundé, enrolling 80 ASA I-II parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Hemodynamic parameters (SBP, DBP, MAP, HR, SpO₂), plasma electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻, iCa²⁺), and vasoactive mediators (nitric oxide [NO], prostaglandin I₂ [PGI₂]) were measured at baseline (T0) and 10 min post-induction (T1).
RESULTS: Hypotension was confirmed in 78% of participants. MAP fell by 23% (92.4 ± 8.1 to 71.2 ± 9.5 mmHg; p < 0.001). Ionized calcium dropped significantly below the critical threshold (1.18 ± 0.06 to 0.98 ± 0.04 mmol/L; p < 0.01), correlating strongly with SBP decline (r = 0.72; p < 0.01). NOₓ increased by 37.9% and PGI₂ by 25.3% (both p < 0.01). Na⁺, K⁺, and Cl⁻ remained stable.
CONCLUSION: Spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension in parturients was associated with concurrent acute ionized calcium reduction and elevated vasoactive mediators (NOₓ and PGI₂), consistent with a "double lock" hypothesis. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. They support prospective interventional investigation of ionized calcium and vasoactive mediators as contributors to hemodynamic decompensation during spinal anesthesia for cesarean section.

articles.title: Effects of intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium in older patients with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus: a secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study analyzed the data from a previous randomized clinical trial to investigate the effects of intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium (POD) in older patients with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 128 older surgical patients, stratified into diabetes mellitus (DM, n = 50) and non-diabetes (Non-DM, n = 78) cohorts. Patients received either perioperative intranasal insulin or saline. The primary outcome was POD incidence; secondary outcomes included the perioperative changes Mini-Mental Status Examination (MMSE) scores and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Basic (MoCA-B) scores. Logistic and linear regression models were used to evaluate the association between intranasal insulin and outcomes within each subgroup. Additionally, sensitivity analyses adjusting for different covariates were performed to evaluate the consistency.
RESULTS: The incidences of POD in Group DM-S (DM + saline, n = 22), Group DM-I (DM + insulin, n = 28), Group Non-DM-S (non-DM + saline, n = 42), Group Non-DM-I (non-DM + insulin, n = 36) were 36.4%, 10.7%, 19% and 11.1%, respectively. Intranasal insulin was associated with reduced POD risk in T2DM patients (adjusted OR = 0.195, 95% CI: 0.036-0.826, P = 0.035), but not significant in non-T2DM patients. Additionally, insulin positively correlated with perioperative changes of MMSE and MoCA-B scores in both T2DM (MMSE: β = 1.042, 95% CI: 0.230-1.854, P = 0.013; MoCA-B: β = 1.093, 95% CI: 0.013-2.173, P = 0.047) and non-T2DM cohorts (MMSE: β = 0.748, 95% CI: 0.124-1.373, P = 0.019; MoCA-B: β = 0.887, 95% CI: 0.116-1.658, P = 0.025). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent trends.
CONCLUSION: Intranasal insulin was associated with reduced POD incidence in older patients with T2DM and exhibited a potential protective effect on postoperative cognition.

articles.title: Short-term clinical and radiographic outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopic decompressive laminectomy for lumbar spinal stenosis with mild-to-moderate vertebral rotation: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Unilateral biportal endoscopic spinal surgery (UBE) has demonstrated good decompressive outcomes in patients with conventional lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). However, its efficacy in patients with LSS accompanied by significant vertebral rotation remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the surgical techniques and clinical outcomes of unilateral biportal endoscopic decompressive laminectomy for severe LSS combined with vertebral rotation.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 110 patients with single-level severe LSS who underwent UBE decompressive laminectomy between September 2022 and September 2024. Based on preoperative imaging (vertebral rotation angle > 5°), patients were divided into two groups: the LSS group (n = 81, without vertebral rotation) and the Rotation group (n = 29, with vertebral rotation). Demographic data, perioperative indicators (operative time, complications), clinical outcomes [Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score, Macnab criteria], and radiographic results (dural sac cross-sectional area preoperatively and at 3 months postoperatively) were collected and compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences between the two groups in terms of age, gender, BMI, surgical level, or preoperative stenosis grade (Schizas grade C/D) (P > 0.05). The mean operative time in the Rotation group (86.27 ± 10.65 min) was significantly longer than that in the LSS group (67.52 ± 6.37 min) (P < 0.05). The incidence of intraoperative dural tear was 2.5% (2/81) in the LSS group and 3.4% (1/29) in the Rotation group, with no statistically significant difference between the two groups. The incidence of postoperative symptomatic epidural hematoma was 11.1% (9/81) in the LSS group and 13.8% (4/29) in the Rotation group. At 3 months postoperatively, both groups showed significant improvement in low back pain VAS, leg pain VAS,ODI and dural sac cross-sectional area compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05), but the magnitude of improvement was not statistically different between the groups (P > 0.05). According to the modified Macnab criteria, the excellent/good rate was 93.8% (76/81) in the LSS group and 93.1% (27/29) in the Rotation group, with no statistically significant difference between the groups.
CONCLUSION: UBE decompressive laminectomy achieves satisfactory short-term (3-month) clinical outcomes for LSS with mild-to-moderate vertebral rotation, comparable to those without rotation, though operative time is longer. However, long-term spinal stability and deformity progression risk remain to be determined, and extended follow-up is warranted.

articles.title: Arthroscopic versus open reduction and internal fixation for tibial plateau fractures: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically compare the efficacy and safety of arthroscopy-assisted reduction and percutaneous internal fixation (ARIF) versus open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) for Schatzker type I-III tibial plateau fractures.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI up to November 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ARIF with ORIF were included. Data on functional outcomes and complication rates were extracted and pooled using random-effects models. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and GRADE approach were used for quality assessment.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs involving 1, 346 patients were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated that ARIF was associated with significantly superior excellent-good functional outcomes (OR = 3.14, 95%CI: 2.02-4.88, p < 0.001) and substantially reduced perioperative complication rates (OR = 0.27, 95%CI: 0.18-0.40, p < 0.001) compared to ORIF.
CONCLUSION: For Schatzker type I-III tibial plateau fractures, ARIF provides superior functional recovery and significantly lower complication rates compared to ORIF. As a result, ARIF represents a favorable treatment option for these fracture patterns.

articles.title: Weekend versus weekday cardiac surgery: A comprehensive meta-analysis of more than 500,000 cases with meta-regression.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The "weekend effect" describes worse outcomes with weekend hospital care, but its impact on cardiac surgery remains unclear. We performed a comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression to assess whether weekend cardiac surgery is associated with poorer perioperative outcomes than weekday procedures.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing weekend versus weekday cardiac surgery outcomes. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by procedure type (emergent, coronary artery bypass grafting, acute type A aortic dissection) and geographic region. Meta-regressions explored effects of mean age, percentage of female patients, proportion of emergent cases, and publication year. A day-by-day mortality heat map was constructed to assess daily trends.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies comprising 527,195 patients were included; 7.4% underwent surgery on weekends. Weekend surgery was associated with significantly greater mortality (OR, 1.5; 95% CI, 1.2-1.8; P = .001) and longer stay in the intensive care unit (mean difference, 0.4 days; 95% CI, 0.1-0.7; P = .01). No significant differences were found for acute kidney injury, stroke, aortic crossclamp time, reoperation for bleeding, or total hospital stay. The incidence of transient ischemic attack was slightly lower on weekends (OR, 0.8; 95% CI, 0.6-1.0; P = .02). Subgroup analyses showed consistently elevated mortality in weekend cases across emergent, coronary artery bypass grafting, and acute type A aortic dissection subgroups, and in studies from Asia and the United States but not Europe. Meta-regression showed no significant effect of age, sex, emergent case proportion, or publication year on mortality differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Weekend cardiac surgery is associated with greater mortality and longer stay in the intensive care unit, independent of case mix. The absence of patient-level effect modification suggests that systemic or institutional factors, rather than patient acuity, underlie the weekend effect, supporting the need for policies ensuring consistent care across all days.

articles.title: Variable retinal presentations after retrobulbar needle perforation: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retrobulbar anesthesia is widely used in ophthalmic surgery due to its rapid onset and effective akinesia. However, although uncommon, globe perforation remains one of its most severe complications and may lead to a wide spectrum of posterior segment damage. While incidence and risk factors have been extensively described, less attention has been given to the management of the resulting retinal and choroidal injuries.
MAIN BODY: We report a retrospective case series of four patients with retinal or choroidal complications following retrobulbar needle perforation. Clinical presentations were heterogeneous, including proliferative vitreoretinopathy, subretinal hemorrhage, choroidal neovascularization, and submacular hemorrhage. Management was individualized according to the predominant retinal pathology and included pars plana vitrectomy-based approaches, subretinal recombinant tissue plasminogen activator, and intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy. Anatomical stabilization was achieved in all cases, with visual outcomes appearing to be influenced by macular involvement and timing of intervention.
CONCLUSION: Retrobulbar needle perforation can result in diverse retinal pathologies despite a common mechanism of injury. This small case series illustrates the importance of early recognition, multimodal imaging, and individualized management in selected complex cases.

articles.title: The impact of prior asymptomatic COVID-19 infection on outcomes following coronary bypass surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing and expected postoperative course of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) after asymptomatic coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain uncertain. Evidence guiding cardiac surgical practice has largely been extrapolated from mixed surgical cohorts or broader cardiac surgery series rather than from isolated CABG populations.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults who underwent isolated CABG during 2021-2022. Patients with documented asymptomatic preoperative SARS-CoV-2 infection were compared with patients without documented prior COVID-19. Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables were extracted from institutional records. Outcomes included early clinical recovery, respiratory support, transfusion exposure, laboratory trajectories, and mortality. A timing subgroup analysis (< 4 weeks vs >= 4 weeks from infection to surgery) was prespecified as exploratory.
RESULTS: Seventy-six patients met eligibility criteria: 37 with prior asymptomatic COVID-19 and 39 without documented prior COVID-19. The cohort was predominantly male (81.6%), low risk by EuroSCORE II, and largely elective. Baseline demographics, major comorbidities, ventricular function, operative priority, number of grafted vessels, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, extubation time, intensive care unit stay, hospital stay, oxygen requirement, and transfusion exposure were similar between groups. Postoperative complications were more frequent in the prior-COVID group (16.2% vs 0.0%; risk difference 16.2%, 95% CI 3.8-31.1%; P = 0.011), whereas mortality remained rare and not significantly different (2.7% vs 0.0%; P = 0.487). Longitudinal laboratory analyses showed expected perioperative inflammatory and hematologic changes within both groups, without consistent between-group separation. In the exploratory timing subgroup, no statistically significant differences were detected between earlier and later surgery, but this analysis was markedly underpowered.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center exploratory cohort of predominantly elective, low-risk CABG patients, prior asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection was not associated with a generalized worsening of early postoperative recovery, although postoperative complications were more frequent in the exposed group. These data are insufficient to inform CABG timing recommendations after asymptomatic infection and should not be extrapolated to unstable or higher-risk patients. Larger multicenter studies with better exposure characterization, vaccination data, and longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Neurocognitive dysfunction among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery-A prospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neurocognitive dysfunction (NCD) remains a common complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, the trajectory of cognitive recovery and associated risk factors remain incompletely understood. This study evaluated the prevalence, early postoperative course, and predictors of NCD among patients undergoing elective CABG.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 110 consecutive patients undergoing elective CABG between January 2025 and August 2025 at a tertiary care center were enrolled. Neurocognitive function was assessed using Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III preoperatively, at hospital discharge, and at postoperative day 10 follow-up. Changes in cognitive performance were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Transitions in categorical cognitive status were evaluated using the McNemar-Bowker test. Associations between patient characteristics and NCD were examined using multivariable analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 110 patients undergoing CABG were included in the study, with a mean age of 57.5 ± 8.5 years; 79.1% were male, and 85.5% underwent off-pump CABG. Mean Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III scores declined significantly from baseline (77.0 ± 9.1) to discharge (73.8 ± 9.9), followed by recovery at follow-up (77.1 ± 10.0) (P < .001). Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons demonstrated a significant decline from baseline to discharge (mean difference -3.2; 95% CI, -4.8 to -1.6; P = .001) and a significant improvement from discharge to follow-up (mean difference +3.3; 95% CI, 1.7-4.9; P = .001), whereas baseline and follow-up scores did not differ significantly (mean difference +0.1; 95% CI, -1.5 to 1.7; P = .865). NCD was present in 68.2% of patients preoperatively, increased to 80.0% at discharge, and decreased to 64.5% at follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified increasing age as independently associated with NCD at follow-up (adjusted odds ratio, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.14; P = .007).
CONCLUSIONS: In this group of patients undergoing CABG, cognitive impairment was often seen before surgery. There was a temporary decline right after the operation, followed by partial recovery by the early follow-up. The link between older age and early postoperative cognitive issues indicates that older patients may benefit from cognitive screening around the time of surgery. More research is needed to look at long-term cognitive changes and the effectiveness of specific interventions.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy in geriatric patients with non-small cell lung cancer: A real-world analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has been shown to significantly improve survival in patients with stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer. However, it is unknown whether geriatric patients experience similar benefits. Using a large national cohort, we studied outcomes of neoadjuvant immunotherapy in geriatric patients with stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer.
METHODS: Patients with stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer treated over 24 months (2022-2023) were identified in the National Cancer Database. Geriatric patients were defined as being older than 75 years. Geriatric patients and younger patients aged 75 years or less were compared in terms of treatment intensity, perioperative outcomes, and survival. Kaplan-Meier curves, log-rank tests, and Cox proportional hazards models were used for statistical analysis of survival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to analyze perioperative outcomes.
RESULTS: 21,070 patients aged more than 75 years with clinical stage IB-IIIB non-small cell lung cancer were included in this analysis. Among them, 4467 (21.2%) received surgery and 447 (10.0%) received neoadjuvant immunotherapy, compared with 35.3% and 17.9% of younger patients, respectively (P < .001). Both surgery (adjusted HR 0.34 [0.27-0.43], P < .001) and neoadjuvant immunotherapy (0.39 [0.25-0.63], P < .001) were associated with improved survival in geriatric patients. Geriatric patients who received neoadjuvant immunotherapy also demonstrated acceptable perioperative outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In a large national cohort, we show that although geriatric patients have lower treatment intensity than younger patients, both surgery and neoadjuvant immunotherapy render a survival benefit while retaining acceptable perioperative outcomes. Whenever possible, standard of care treatment should be pursued in geriatric patients, and age in isolation should not exclude patients from optimal treatments.

articles.title: Association between Early Postoperative Sodium Change and Postoperative Delirium after General Anesthesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent neuropsychiatric complication after surgery under general anesthesia and is associated with adverse outcomes. Although perioperative dysnatremia has been linked to POD, most studies relied on static sodium measurements and failed to capture early postoperative dynamics. We investigated whether early postoperative sodium change is associated with late-onset POD.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults undergoing surgery under general anesthesia between July 2021 and December 2025. A Day-3 landmark design ensured temporal precedence between exposure and outcome. Perioperative sodium change (ΔNa) was defined as the difference between preoperative baseline sodium and the most recent sodium value within 48 hours after surgery and was categorized as decrease (≤-3 mmol/L), stable (-3 to +3 mmol/L), or increase (≥+3 mmol/L). Late-onset POD occurring on postoperative days 3 through 7 was identified using the Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist and antipsychotic prescriptions. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models were applied.
RESULTS: Among 18,424 patients, both perioperative sodium increase and decrease were independently associated with higher odds of late-onset POD, as compared with stable sodium levels. Baseline preoperative sodium was not associated with POD. Spline analyses showed a U-shaped association between ΔNa and POD, with the lowest risk was near ΔNa = 0 mmol/L. Findings were consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative sodium fluctuations were associated with increased risk of late-onset POD. Monitoring of perioperative sodium trajectories may aid in stratifying early postoperative risk.

articles.title: Attitudes Towards Clinical Research in Acute Illness-A Population-Based Survey in Sweden.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the attitudes of the Swedish population towards participation in research and preferences regarding legally authorized representative when a participant is unable to give informed consent.
METHODS: A national survey conducted by a Swedish analysis and research company on a representative sample of the Swedish population on two occasions (2020 and 2023). The questions were based on the prerequisite that the respondents could not provide informed consent on their own. The questionnaire included two scenarios: one allowing time to consult a legal representative (non-emergency) and one where research had to start immediately, before consulting a legal representative (emergency).
RESULTS: In total, 2086 respondents were included in the analysis. A majority were positive to participate in both non-emergency (81% [1690/2086]) and emergency research (82% [1714/2086]) in situations where they would be unable to provide informed consent. Next of kin was preferred as a surrogate decision maker in 81% (1686/2086) of respondents and less than 1% (11/2086) preferred an unrelated legal representative such as an attorney.
CONCLUSION: This study shows that in a representative sample of the Swedish population there is a positive attitude towards research in the acute setting and in critical illness, even in situations when a potential participant cannot receive information and provide informed consent and that a next of kin is the preferred legally authorized representative.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This article reports results of a national survey from Sweden, where it shows that, among Swedish citizens, there appears to be broad acceptance of allowing family members to act as surrogate decision-makers in informed consent decisions for study participation among acutely critically ill patients who cannot perform consent themselves. At this point in time, Swedish law does not allow this.

articles.title: Discussing Future Treatment and Care in the ICU: Perspectives From Patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) is usually predicated on curative treatment, but continuing all available treatment options may not always be beneficial for the patient or in line with their wishes. However, patients admitted to the ICU are often assessed as incapable of making decisions regarding their care; hence conversations about wishes for treatment are postponed. This study aimed to investigate the experiences of patients who participated in a conversation concerning treatment and care following ICU discharge based on the Danish version of the Recommended Summary Plan for Emergency Care and Treatment (ReSPECT) form.
METHOD: Semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with patients who had a conversation about future treatment and care with an intensivist using the ReSPECT form during an ICU admission between November 2024 and July 2025. Relatives who participated in the conversation and were present during the interviews were asked to elaborate on their experiences of the conversation's timing and how they felt about participating in the conversation. Data was analysed using content analysis.
RESULTS: Nineteen patients were included in the study, of whom 15 patients (83%) participated in a telephone interview. Two themes were identified: Timing of the conversation and Clarifying goals of care and options. Based on these, four sub-themes were identified, two for each theme: Too soon, but not much later; Wishes in accordance; Hard, but necessary and Communicating in an understandable manner. Most patients were satisfied with having had a conversation about future treatment and care. Patients found the conversation relevant and necessary. The intensivists were praised for their communication skills and their ability to know and explain recommendations for future treatment and care. However, most patients believed that the conversation was conducted too soon after recovering from intensive care. They would have preferred to have had the conversation later during their admission.
CONCLUSIONS: Most participating ICU patients found a conversation about future treatment and care relevant but preferred it to be held after ICU discharge. Future research should investigate the benefits of incorporating intensivists in these conversations in general wards.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: In this prospective study, former ICU patients were interviewed and asked about their experiences and opinions regarding a structured ReSPECT discussion that had been conducted in the end of their ICU stay. The goal of that interview was advance care planning, involving the patients and their family members. This study reports a qualitative analysis of interviews conducted at least 4 weeks later. Two main themes and four subthemes were identified. Almost all patients remembered having had the discussion, but the content was less clearly remembered. ICU physicians' communication skills were appreciated. The study assesses a function of our daily work from patient and family perspective, and discusses important issues such as optimal timing of the advance care planning.

articles.title: Evolution of medical thoracoscopy - 100 years on.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: More than a century after Jacobaeus, medical thoracoscopy is being reshaped by demands for precise pleural diagnosis, adequate tissue for molecular characterisation, combined local treatment and efficient care. This review uses its historical evolution to examine current indications, instruments, biopsy strategies, anaesthetic design and service models, with emphasis on recent evidence.
RECENT FINDINGS: Rigid and semirigid thoracoscopy achieve similarly high diagnostic yield but differ in access, force transmission, tissue size, pain and sedative requirements. Recent studies favour needs-led sampling: standard forceps for most visible lesions, with cryobiopsy or advanced tools when depth, invasion, fibrosis or molecular profiling is limiting. Trials support selective rather than routine use of pleurodesis, indwelling catheters, regional blocks, high-flow oxygen or first-line thoracoscopy for pleural infection. Image enhancement, artificial intelligence, hybrid instruments and single-use platforms remain promising but incompletely validated.
SUMMARY: Medical thoracoscopy should remain a targeted pleural procedure that preserves spontaneous ventilation while integrating diagnosis, adequate tissue acquisition, selected therapy and pathway efficiency. Technology and anaesthetic intensity should be matched to clinical need and adopted only when they improve measurable patient or system outcomes.

articles.title: Feasibility of Enucleation in Standing Sedated Horses With Retrobulbar Anesthesia and Auriculopalpebral Nerve Block: Impact of Ultrasound Guidance in a Case Series.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Examining the feasibility of enucleation in standing sedated horses with dorsal retrobulbar anesthesia (RBA) and auriculopalpebral (AP) nerve block and the impact of ultrasound (US) guidance on RBA success.
ANIMALS STUDIED: Thirty horses.
PROCEDURES: In a prospective clinical case series, horses (n = 15/group) received standardized sedation, dorsal RBA (12 mL mepivacaine) and AP nerve block (4 mL lidocaine). Group 1 received US-assisted RBA (10 MHz linear probe), Group 2 underwent blind RBA subsequently. Needle positioning time was recorded. Eyelid sensitivity was measured before (t0) and 20 min after injection (t20). RBA success was defined as surgical tolerance at t20. US image quality (excellent/good/poor) was assessed and compared with RBA success. If RBA failed, additional local anesthetic was injected.
RESULTS: RBA success was 63.4% (19/30) with 73.3% (11/15) in Group 1 and 53.3% (8/15) in Group 2 (p = 0.179). 3/19 successful cases required additional retrobulbar anesthetic top ups intraoperatively (t60-t80). A significant association was found between the number of successfully anesthetized lid areas per horse and RBA success (p < 0.001). Mean time for US-assisted RBA was 5.2 min (±1.7 min). US image quality was rated as "excellent" in 3/15, "good" in 7/15, and "poor" in 5/15 cases, with corresponding success rates of 100% (3/3), 85.7% (6/7), and 40% (2/5), respectively. Improved US image quality showed a non-significant trend toward higher success (p = 0.053).
CONCLUSION: RBA combined with AP nerve block provides adequate anesthesia for standing equine enucleation. US image quality and eyelid sensitivity are suitable block success predictors.

articles.title: Postoperative Pain Treatment After Pancreatic Surgery: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analyses and Trial Sequential Analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major pancreatic surgery is associated with significant postoperative pain that impairs early mobilisation and recovery. ERAS guidelines for pancreaticoduodenectomy recommend multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, with a strong recommendation for epidural analgesia and continuous wound infiltration as an alternative. Other techniques may be beneficial, but their efficacy and safety remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy and adverse events of different postoperative analgesic modalities for patients undergoing total pancreatectomy, pancreaticoduodenectomy and distal pancreatectomy.
DATABASES AND DATA TREATMENT: This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (ID CRD420251085003) reported in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. A search for randomised controlled trials was conducted in Medline, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and Embase. Meta-analyses were performed in Review Manger, risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, trial sequential analyses were performed, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs comprising 1468 patients were included, and 10 meta-analyses were performed. Meta-analyses demonstrated reduced pain scores at rest on postoperative day (POD) two with COX-inhibitors compared with placebo/no intervention. Pain scores were similar when comparing epidural analgesia with less invasive strategies (paravertebral block and wound infiltration) on POD1-POD2, but lower with the less invasive techniques on POD3. Meta-analyses were small, and GRADE recommendations ranged from very low to low.
CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence was insufficient to establish the superiority of any single analgesic strategy after major pancreatic surgery. Several analgesic strategies, including COX inhibitors, paravertebral block and continuous wound infiltration, showed promising results. Larger RCTs are needed to provide stronger evidence-based recommendations.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Epidural analgesia has long been considered the gold standard for treatment of postoperative pain after major pancreatic surgery. The present review adds to the field by demonstrating that less invasive strategies as continuous wound infiltration and paravertebral block provide comparable pain scores in the first postoperative days, with a significantly lower score on postoperative day three. This supports positioning less invasive strategies as viable alternatives to epidural analgesia.

articles.title: Feasibility and Short-term Outcomes of Robotic Surgery for Transverse Colon Cancer: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Patients with transverse colon cancer have been excluded from randomized controlled trials due to its anatomical complexity and high technical difficulty. Few studies have compared robotic surgery with laparoscopic or open surgery for transverse colon cancer. We conducted a comparative analysis of the safety and efficacy of robotic surgery for transverse colon cancer.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 635 patients treated for transverse colon cancer between 2016 and 2025. Patients were categorized according to the surgical approach: robotic surgery (Robot group, n=38), laparoscopic surgery (Lap group, n=530), and open surgery (Open group, n=67). Clinicopathological and surgical features were compared between groups.
RESULTS: Operative time was longer (Robot vs. Lap vs. Open; 233 vs. 226 vs. 181 min, p<0.001), blood loss was lower (15 vs. 20 vs. 120 ml, p<0.001), more lymph nodes were retrieved (19 vs. 16 vs. 10, p=0.002), and hospital stay was shorter (9 vs. 12 vs. 22 days, p<0.001) in the Robot group. The postoperative complication rate tended to be lower in the Robot group (7.9% vs. 23.2% vs. 25.4%, p=0.077). In multivariate analysis, male sex (OR=1.559, 95% CI=1.056-2.301, p=0.025) and ASA-PS 3 (OR=2.486, 95% CI=1.460-4.232, p<0.001) were identified as independent risk factors for postoperative complications.
CONCLUSION: Although favorable short-term outcomes were observed in this small, highly selected robotic cohort, these descriptive findings do not establish the clinical superiority or equivalence of robotic surgery over laparoscopic or open surgery. Larger prospective studies are needed to define its oncological and surgical value.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Preoperative Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio in Advanced Gastric Cancer After Curative Resection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Even after curative (R0) resection, a subset of patients with advanced gastric cancer (AGC) experiences poor clinical outcomes. Identifying simple and reliable preoperative prognostic indicators is essential for risk stratification. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of preoperative immuno-nutritional indices, particularly the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), as prognostic factors after statistically controlling for confounding factors associated with the patients' general physical status using the American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS) classification.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 169 patients with stage II or higher AGC who underwent R0 resection between 2012 and 2022. The impacts of various preoperative immuno-nutritional indices on overall (OS) and recurrence-free (RFS) survival were evaluated using ASA-PS-stratified log-rank tests and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analysis.
RESULTS: In the ASA-PS-stratified log-rank analysis, a high preoperative PLR was significantly associated with shortened OS (p=0.035) and RFS (p=0.042). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that after adjusting for general physical status, a high PLR remained an independent adverse prognostic factor for both OS (hazard ratio=1.917, 95% confidence interval=1.001-3.677; p=0.0495) and RFS (hazard ratio=1.801, 95% confidence interval=1.007-3.218; p=0.0472).
CONCLUSION: The preoperative PLR is a simple, cost-effective, and independent prognostic indicator in patients with resectable AGC, functioning independently of the patient's baseline physical status. This biomarker may contribute to the optimization of perioperative individualized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Increased Trends of Spinal Injections in South Korea : A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate nationwide trends in spinal injections in South Korea and to analyze the demographic, providerrelated, and sociocultural subgroups that may explain the continuous rise observed in clinical practice.
METHODS: Using the National Health Insurance Sharing Service (NHISS) dataset, all spinal injection procedures were identified using Fee-for-Service codes. Annual utilization was expressed as total procedures and population-normalized rates per 100000 persons. Demographic characteristics, provider specialty distribution, and regional injection patterns were analyzed.
RESULTS: The annual number of patients receiving spinal injections increased from 432795 in 2008 to 3743410 in 2022. Population-adjusted rates rose from 882.23 to 7244.77 per 100000 persons, reflecting an 8.21-fold increase. The mean patient age increased from 56.9 to 58.7 years, with the ≥70-year population accounting for the largest growth. All specialties demonstrated higher procedural volumes, particularly neurosurgery and other departments. After 2020, the Seoul capital area exceeded non-capital regions in procedure numbers.
CONCLUSION: The present nationwide study suggests that the number of patients and procedures regarding spinal injections increased significantly between 2008 and 2022 in Korea.

articles.title: Emerging mechanisms underlying neuropathic pain.
Fatigue links sociodemographic risk to pain intensity and spread in 2 surgical cohorts.
articles.abstract: Why some surgical patients develop pain that extends beyond the original site of injury while others do not remains poorly understood. The recently proposed Risk of Pain Spread (ROPS) framework integrates multiple psychosocial risk factors associated with widespread pain, but its generalizability to surgical populations has not been established. Using 2 large presurgical cohorts of participants undergoing total knee arthroplasty or thoracic surgery, we evaluated the generalizability of the ROPS framework and examined relationships among psychosocial and sociodemographic factors, surgical-site pain, nonsurgical-site pain, and widespread pain using complementary latent-variable, regression, Bayesian network, and mediation analyses. Across cohorts and analytical approaches, fatigue emerged as the most consistent correlate of pain outcomes, independent of other measured risk factors. Fatigue also occupied a central position within the conditional dependency structure of psychosocial and pain variables and accounted for substantial shared variance linking sleep disturbance, depressive symptoms, neuroticism, adverse childhood experiences, and socioeconomic disadvantage with pain intensity. Nonsurgical-site pain consistently occupied a position linking pain intensity with widespread pain across complementary analyses. Together, these findings externally validate the ROPS framework in clinically relevant surgical populations and identify fatigue as a central correlate linking biopsychosocial vulnerability with pain burden.

articles.title: Safety in electroconvulsive therapy: a narrative review of cardiopulmonary complications.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is an effective and widely practiced treatment. As stigma surrounding the technique continues to diminish, it has become a therapeutic option for a broad range of psychiatric disorders, including in older and frail patients. With ECT increasingly delivered in ambulatory or remote settings, anesthesiologists and psychiatrists must remain aware of the potential cardiopulmonary complications that may arise during the procedure.
RECENT FINDINGS: Although high-quality evidence is still limited, recent studies, often using heterogeneous methodologies, consistently underline the cardiopulmonary complications inherent to ECT and their rare but tragic result. However, no consensus has yet emerged regarding optimal anesthetic management or prevention strategies.
SUMMARY: ECT is a safe and efficient therapeutic option, even for patients with significant comorbidities, and should be performed by well-trained multidisciplinary teams. Serious cardiopulmonary complications remain a rare event, but clinicians should be prepared to anticipate and manage them promptly to minimize morbidity and mortality.

articles.title: Ambulatory anesthesia in transition: growing caseloads, a changing patient population, and the need for a sharpened focus on perioperative complications.
Regional analgesic techniques for postoperative pain after kidney transplantation: a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pain after kidney transplantation is often severe, and graft function constrains the use of systemic analgesia. Previous syntheses of regional techniques pooled them as a class, combined donors with recipients, and did not use a minimal clinically important difference (MCID).
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through 5 September 2026 for randomised trials of regional analgesia in adult kidney transplant recipients (PROSPERO CRD420261478933); a trial-registry search and network meta-analysis were added post hoc. Bayesian random-effects models with MCID-scaled priors yielded posterior probabilities of benefit and of exceeding the MCID, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Fourteen trials (903 participants) were included. Only quadratus lumborum (QL) and transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks could be pooled against control. Both yielded lower pain at every pooled time point, but no pairwise pain comparison reached 80% probability of exceeding the 1.0 point MCID. Opioid consumption at 24 h was lower with the QL block (-15.5 morphine milligram equivalents; 95% credible interval -23.6 to -6.7) and the TAP block (-10.5; -14.4 to -5.5), with each reduction exceeding the 5 mg MCID with a probability >97%. In the network meta-analysis, no difference between QL and TAP blocks in pain or opioid consumption reached 80% probability of exceeding the MCID. Graft function and safety data were too sparse to pool. Twelve eligible registered trials were unpublished; certainty of evidence was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Quadrtus lumborum and transversus abdominus plane blocks reduce pain and opioid consumption at 24 h, but only the reduction in opioid consumption has a high probability of being clinically important. Certainty of evidence is very low; no technique is preferred, and effects on graft function are unknown.

articles.title: Anticholinergic Drug Burden and Postoperative Delirium: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative delirium (POD) is an important postoperative neurocognitive complication, and cumulative anticholinergic drug burden (ADB) may increase its risk by impairing central cholinergic neurotransmission. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to clarify the overall association between ADB scores and POD risk in adult surgical patients.
METHODS: We searched major databases and trial registries through February 2026 for studies that assessed ADB using validated scales and reported POD outcomes in adult surgical patients. Random-effects models pooled SMDs and ORs. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses explored heterogeneity and robustness. Risk of bias was assessed using NOS, and evidence certainty was rated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Ten reports from nine independent cohorts comprising 10,457 participants were included. Patients with POD had higher ADB scores than those without POD (SMD = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.20-0.43). Each one-point increase in continuous ADB was associated with 22% higher odds of POD (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.09-1.37). Both low-to-moderate and high burden were associated with increased POD risk. In scale-specific analyses, the association was significant for ACB. The association was attenuated in studies that excluded patients with cognitive impairment. Methodological quality ranged from moderate to high, and certainty of evidence was low.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher ADB is significantly associated with higher odds of POD, with a graded increase in risk across burden levels. Baseline cognitive impairment appears to amplify this association. These findings support preoperative ADB assessment and medication optimization in vulnerable surgical patients, while highlighting the need for prospective head-to-head comparisons of anticholinergic burden scales.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD420261294941).

articles.title: Which spontaneous breathing trial should be used to reproduce post-extubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related ARDS? A multicenter randomized crossover study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous breathing trials (SBT) guide extubation decisions in intensive care unit (ICU), predicting the respiratory effort required by the patient after extubation. Different SBTs exist and should be adapted to critical illness. Viral pneumonias such as COVID-19 combine lung injury, sepsis-induced systemic inflammation, and encephalopathy, making classification challenging. The objective was to assess which SBT could be used to reproduce postextubation respiratory effort in COVID-19-related acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) patients.
METHODS: In this multicenter randomized crossover study, COVID-19-related ARDS patients mechanically ventilated at least 24 hours and ready for extubation underwent 3 different 15-minute SBT at random order: pressure support ventilation of 7-cmH2O with positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 0-cmH2O (PSV7PEEP0), PSV 0-cmH2O with PEEP 0-cmH2O (PSV0PEEP0) and T-piece trial. At baseline, end of each SBT, and 20 minutes after extubation, surrogates of respiratory effort were measured: esophageal pressure-time-product (PTPes), PTPes per minute (PTPes.min), swing esophageal pressure (SwingPes), and SwingPes per minute (SwingPes.min).
RESULTS: Sixty measurements of respiratory effort from 12 patients were analyzed. Median PTPes.min increased from 193.8 [170.8-227.2] cmH2O.s/min at baseline to 236.6 [192.1-313.6] after extubation, with no significant differences between SBTs and postextubation. SwingPes and SwingPes.min were lower during PSV7-PEEP0 than after extubation, with median paired differences of 4.7 (95% CI 0.6-9.8) and 115.3 (95% CI 4.8-297.8), but these differences did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons.
CONCLUSION: No SBT modality differed significantly from post-extubation respiratory effort, suggesting that none could be excluded in COVID-19-related ARDS patients.

articles.title: Impact of additional tailored Information and music to reduce preoperative anxiety in surgical outpatients: a prospective before-after study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-pharmacological techniques have recently been developed to decrease preoperative anxiety, and music or video may be combined, as in children. This study aims to compare two additional preoperative strategies in adult outpatients.
PATIENTS AND METHOD: This before-after trial was approved by the ethics committee and included adults undergoing ambulatory procedures under general anaesthesia. It compared usual care before surgery and another period with a video of the expected local journey combined with a relaxing music session. After consent, the level of anxiety was measured via the APAIS score, a repeated visual analogue scale for anxiety, and investigators collected preoperative fears. The main objective was to reduce the number of patients with significant preoperative anxiety. Secondary outcomes compared anxiety during the journey, pain, and quality of recovery after surgery. A P-value < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: 99 patients were included in each period, and 194 completed the study. The intervention group showed a significant reduction in the rate of patients with significant anxiety at admission in the operating room: 23/95 (24.2%, 95%CI [16.7-33.7]) vs. 43/99 (43.4%, 95%CI [34.1-53.3]) with P = 0.005. Secondary outcomes showed no difference in anxiety after surgery, neither in length of stay nor incidence of PONV. The postoperative level of pain was also statistically reduced (P = 0.033).
CONCLUSION: The study suggests that a combined video and music strategy decreases the rate of significant anxiety in patients undergoing outpatient procedures. This low-cost strategy showed a high level of satisfaction and should be encouraged in adults.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT06461052.

articles.title: Observational study for perioperative intensive care unit (OPICU): Planned and unplanned ICU admissions, follow-up, discharge, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Due to limited resources, identifying high-risk surgical patients who derive clinical benefit from Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission is essential. Our primary aim was to characterize resource allocation and evaluate the true clinical benefit of ICU admissions using modified Wang criteria. Secondary aim is to identify independent risk factors for ICU admission; validate clinical scoring systems; and compare inter-group outcomes, including Clavien-Dindo complication rates, lengths of stay, and mortality.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study was conducted across 75 ICUs. Adult inpatient surgery cases were categorized into four groups: planned admission (PAG), unplanned admission (UPAG), planned but not admitted (PBNAG), and emergent admission (EAG). Data included preoperative/intraoperative/postoperative(ICU) variables, modified Wang criteria, and mortality rates (ICU, hospital, 30/90-day).
RESULTS: Of 55,963 preoperatively evaluated patients, 2764 (4.9%) were planned for ICU admission; 804/2764 patients could not be admitted because of limited ICU beds, remaining of 1960 patients with a planned ICU admission, 411/1960 did not require postoperative ICU care forming the PBNAG (14.8% of 2764). Overall, 1980 patients (3.09% of all cases) were admitted to the ICU (78.2% PAG, 12.5% EAG, 9.1% UPAG). POSSUM scores effectively differentiated PBNAG (lower) and EAG (higher) from PAG. ICU benefit indicators (e.g., vasopressor need, prolonged ventilation >12 h, arrest events) were significantly higher in UPAG and EAG versus PAG (p < 0.001). Emergency surgery (OR 12.4), intraoperative complications (OR 3.1), and ASA >2 (OR 2.7) independently increased UPAG risk, whereas minimally invasive surgery and regional anesthesia reduced ICU admissions. Overall ICU and 90-day mortality rates were 5.9% and 7.5%, respectively, peaking in the EAG group (18.1% and 18.9%).
CONCLUSION: Integrating modified Wang criteria, POSSUM scores, intraoperative complications, emergency status, and ASA class >2 is effective in predicting the necessity of ICU admission.

articles.title: What the Probe Cannot Show.
Left Anterior Descending Artery Also Lives at the Apex: A Cardiac Point-of-Care Ultrasound Blind Spot and the Risk of False Reassurance.
Inadvertent Intrathecal Thoracic Epidural Catheter Placement.
Nociception during General Anesthesia: Reply.
The Ties Connecting Us to the Past.
Unexpected Difficult Intubation Caused by Asymptomatic Complete Tracheal Rings.
Nociception during General Anesthesia: Comment.
Occupational Radiation Exposure During Robotic-Assisted Navigational Bronchoscopy: A Prospective Real-Time Dosimetry Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) uses fluoroscopy and cone-beam CT (CBCT), which can expose procedural staff to ionizing radiation. Real-time, role-specific occupational dosimetry data from live RAB procedures remain limited.
METHODS: We prospectively collected continuous personal dosimetry from attending physicians, anesthesia providers, and scrub nurses during 51 consecutive RAB procedures at a single academic center using a standardized low-dose imaging protocol and shielding. Collar-badge readings were converted to estimated effective dose using a conservative upper-bound conversion factor. Role-specific dose distributions were compared, and scenario-based annual estimates were generated by bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Median per-procedure estimated dose was 1.27 µSv for attending physicians, 0.58 µSv for anesthesia providers, and 0.55 µSv for scrub nurses. Exposure differed by role, with the primary operator receiving the highest dose. CBCT cases were associated with higher staff and patient radiation measures but also involved smaller lesions and longer fluoroscopy times, indicating confounding by procedural complexity. Patient BMI was independently associated with physician exposure. Projected annual exposures remained well below the ICRP 20 mSv occupational limit across all roles.
CONCLUSION: Occupational radiation exposure during RAB was low across all staff roles under an optimized imaging workflow. Role-specific dosimetry captures exposure differences across the procedural team and supports standardized low-dose imaging and shielding as core safety practices.

articles.title: Preoperative Predictors of Outcome for Adults Undergoing Congenital Cardiac Surgery: Multicenter Model Validation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) undergoing cardiac surgery represent a growing population in whom conventional surgical risk models perform suboptimally. We externally validated a previously described ACHD-specific preoperative risk model and evaluated whether performance could be improved through recalibration/model updating.
