METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study of patients ≥16 years undergoing congenital cardiac surgery at four centers (March 2020-April 2023). The primary composite adverse outcome (CAO) comprised in-hospital death, prolonged ventilation >7 days, or new-onset dialysis. We evaluated discrimination and calibration of the original preoperative model (including MELD-XI, cognitive impairment, body-mass index [BMI], prior chest wall incisions, and complex anatomy) and then performed bootstrap-based model updating (200 resamples) to derive refined models with and without the Adult Congenital Heart Surgery (ACHS) procedural mortality score.
RESULTS: Among 538 patients, CAO occurred in 4.3% (n=23). In external validation (n=383 complete cases), the original model preserved discrimination (AUC=0.729, 95% confidence interval: 0.602-0.855) but systematically overestimated risk, indicating need for recalibration. The refined model retained BMI, prior chest incisions, cognitive impairment, age, serum albumin level, and ventricular systolic dysfunction. Discrimination was good without procedural complexity (AUC=0.799; 0.697-0.900) and improved with inclusion of the ACHS score (AUC=0.857; 0.779-0.935).
CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective multicenter external validation, an ACHD-specific preoperative risk model maintained discrimination but required recalibration. Incorporating procedural complexity enhanced discrimination, supporting a hybrid patient- and procedure-based approach to guide perioperative planning.

articles.title: Erector spinae plane block added to intercostal nerve block versus intercostal nerve block alone for postoperative analgesia in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to investigate whether the addition of an erector spinae plane block (ESPB) to surgical intercostal nerve block (INB) provides additional postoperative analgesic benefits in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).
METHODS: This prospective, randomized controlled trial included 60 adult patients undergoing elective three-port VATS. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either combined ESPB plus INB (EI) or INB alone. Patients, surgeons, ward nurses, postoperative outcome assessors, and data analysts were blinded to group assignment, whereas the anesthesiologists performing the intervention were unblinded. The primary outcome was pain intensity at 1 hour postoperatively, assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Prespecified secondary outcomes included repeated postoperative NRS pain assessments through 48 hours and cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours.
RESULTS: The NRS pain score at 1 hour postoperatively was 5.83 ± 2.86 in the EI group and 5.52 ± 3.10 in the INB group (mean difference 0.31, 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.25 to 1.87, p = 0.691). In a post hoc exploratory longitudinal analysis, a linear mixed-effects model demonstrated no significant group-by-time interaction in postoperative NRS pain scores (F[7, 401.2] = 0.81, p = 0.581). Cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours, expressed as intravenous morphine equivalents, was 41.0 mg (interquartile range [IQR], 31.0-58.5) in the EI group and 40.0 mg (IQR, 29.1-48.3) in the INB group (between-group difference, 3.0 mg; 95% CI, -6.2 to 12.0; p = 0.501).
CONCLUSIONS: Adding single-injection ESPB to surgical INB did not significantly reduce 1-hour postoperative pain scores or 24-hour opioid consumption following VATS. Larger adequately powered studies are required to determine whether smaller clinically relevant incremental benefits exist.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03949790.

articles.title: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: feasibility, practical benefits, and surgical pitfalls from a single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe surgical outcomes, technical considerations, and feasibility of redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery using initial cases as a reference cohort.
METHODS: A single-center, retrospective review of minimally invasive mitral valve surgery performed between January 2014 and January 2024 was conducted. Perioperative data, mid-term survival, and cardiac-related events were assessed in both initial and redo groups.
RESULTS: A total of 647 patients were included: 30 in the redo group and 617 in the initial group. The redo group had higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II scores (p < 0.001). In the redo group, 26 (86.7%) had undergone previous cardiac surgery via sternotomy, and 18 (60.0%) had previous mitral valve surgery. The operative time was longer in the redo group (p = 0.041), while the cross-clamping time was longer in the initial group (p = 0.019), and cardiopulmonary bypass time was comparable between groups (p = 0.95). Intubation time (p = 0.049), intensive care unit stay (p = 0.020), and in-hospital stay (p = 0.003) were longer in the redo group. However, there were no significant differences in postoperative chest tube output for 24 h (p = 0.32) or blood transfusion requirements (p = 0.087). The overall survival rates at 5 years were 70.7% (95% CI: 41.0%-87.0%) vs. 92.0% (95% CI: 88.0%-94.0%) for the redo and initial groups, respectively. Freedom from cardiac-related events did not significantly differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Redo minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was feasible despite higher surgical risk and longer operative times. Early and mid-term cardiac-related outcomes appeared acceptable, although overall survival was lower in redo cases.

articles.title: Intraoperative neuromonitoring findings after erector spinae plane block during posterior thoracolumbar fusion surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the potential adverse influence of erector spinae plane block (ESPB) on intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) during posterior spinal fusion for thoracolumbar fractures.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of patients who underwent posterior spinal fusion for thoracolumbar fractures between January 2018 and December 2022. Patients were categorized into ESPB and non-ESPB groups based on whether ESPB was administered. The primary endpoint was the change in transcranial motor evoked potential (Tc-MEP) and posterior tibial nerve somatosensory evoked potential (PTN-SEP) waveform derivation rates. Secondary outcomes included Tc-MEP and PTN-SEP alarm occurrence and postoperative neurological deterioration.
RESULTS: Overall, 154 patients were included in the final analysis (89 males, 65 females; mean age: 68.6 years; mean BMI: 22.1). There were 52 patients in the ESPB group and 102 in the non-ESPB group. No significant differences were observed in preoperative neurological findings between the two groups. ESPB did not significantly affect Tc-MEP or PTN-SEP waveform derivation rates. Tc-MEP alarms occurred in the quadriceps femoris muscle (QC) in 2 patients in the ESPB group, but not in the non-ESPB group. Both alarms occurred during T11-level procedures, and waveform recovery was obtained after surgical interruption. No postoperative motor deficits were noted in these patients.
CONCLUSIONS: ESPB did not significantly affect Tc-MEP or PTN-SEP rates. Two unexplained QC Tc-MEP alarms occurred only in the ESPB group. These findings do not establish a clinically actionable association between ESPB and IONM changes, but unexpected isolated QC Tc-MEP changes during surgery with ESPB should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Videolaryngoscopy versus direct laryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures (NasoVISI): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasotracheal intubation is a common procedure for infants undergoing surgery, and successful intubation at first attempt reduces the risk of complications. First-attempt success is improved with videolaryngoscopy compared with direct laryngoscopy in infants requiring orotracheal intubation, but the value of videolaryngoscopy in infants requiring nasotracheal intubation is unknown. We aimed to compare first-attempt success of nasotracheal intubation by videolaryngoscopy and direct laryngoscopy in infants undergoing cardiac procedures.
METHODS: In this multicentre, parallel group, randomised controlled trial across eight paediatric cardiac centres in the USA, we enrolled infants aged 365 days or younger without anticipated difficult airways requiring nasotracheal intubation for elective cardiothoracic surgery or cardiac catheterisation. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy using permuted block randomisation stratified by site. The primary outcome was first-attempt intubation success rate. Analysis was by modified intention to treat using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering within intubating clinicians. Complications associated with first attempt and across all attempts were compared between groups with the same marginal models as the primary outcome analysis. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05433155) and is closed to new participants.
FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024, 684 infants were randomly assigned, of whom 673 were included in the primary outcome analysis: 340 in the videolaryngoscopy group and 333 in the direct laryngoscopy group. 311 (46%) participants were female, 362 (54%) were male, and 457 (68%) were White. The median age was 14·04 weeks (IQR 1·48-22·89) and the mean weight was 4·77 kg (SD 1·74). First-attempt success was higher in the videolaryngoscopy group than in the direct laryngoscopy group (281 [83%] vs 249 [75%]; adjusted risk difference 8·2% [95% CI 2·0-14·3], p=0·0093). First-attempt complications occurred in 85 (13%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (45 [13%] vs 40 [12%]; 0·4% [-3·5 to 4·3], p=0·83). Considering all attempts cumulatively, any complication occurred in 94 (14%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (46 [14%] vs 48 [14%]; -1·9% [-6·0 to 2·3], p=0·38). No cases of cardiac arrest or death occurred in either group.
INTERPRETATION: Improved first-attempt success rates with videolaryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures add to growing evidence favouring videolaryngoscopy as the first-line technique for tracheal intubation in infants. Key remaining questions for ongoing research include whether this benefit extends to infants with difficult airways and at non-specialist centres or urgent settings, and how clinician training should evolve as videolaryngoscopy becomes standard practice.
FUNDING: Anesthesia Patient Safety Foundation and The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

articles.title: Airway management and anaesthetic interventions for children with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with cleft lip and/or palate may present unique challenges during perioperative airway management because of altered upper-airway and craniofacial anatomy. These children frequently undergo surgical procedures requiring general anaesthesia and airway instrumentation. Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis will include randomised controlled trials involving children < 18 years with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia. Eligible studies will compare alternative techniques or devices for airway management or other anaesthetic strategies between two groups of cleft lip/palate patients. The primary outcome will be difficulty in tracheal intubation. Where definitions vary substantially, outcomes will be analysed separately or synthesised narratively. Secondary outcomes will include difficult mask ventilation, oxygen desaturation, airway obstruction, difficult laryngoscopy, first-attempt intubation success, number of intubation attempts, time to successful intubation or airway establishment, failed intubation and other perioperative airway or respiratory adverse events. Two reviewers will independently select RCTs, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis will be performed where clinically appropriate. Risk ratios will be used for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence for important outcomes will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
REGISTRATION AND REVIEW STATUS: The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO on 10 March 2026 (CRD420261326076). Full-text screening and data extraction are ongoing and not yet complete. Protocol amendments are documented transparently in PROSPERO.

articles.title: Paediatric Fentanyl Population Pharmacokinetics: A Scoping Review of Published Models.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE AND PURPOSE: Fentanyl is a highly lipophilic opioid widely used within paediatric peri-operative and intensive-care settings, yet dosing is commonly titrated empirically because of substantial pharmacokinetic variability across developmental stages and clinical contexts. Population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) models provide a quantitative framework to characterise variability, but these have not been systematically synthesised. This scoping review aimed to identify and summarise published paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl, to compare model structures and covariate effects.
METHODS: We searched Embase and MEDLINE databases from database inception to 17 February 2026 for paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl. Two reviewers independently screened papers and extracted data in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines.
RESULTS: Fourteen paediatric PopPK models of fentanyl were identified. Infants (64%, 9/14) and patient populations spanning multiple age groups (e.g., inclusion of infants and children) (64%, 9/14) were most frequently studied. Intravenous fentanyl was modelled in all studies. Two-compartment structures predominated (79%, 11/14). Body weight was the most consistently retained covariate (79%, 11/14), while maturation functions based on postnatal or postmenstrual age were frequently required in neonatal and infant cohorts (50%, 5/10). Other covariates (e.g., obesity, concomitant CYP3A modulators, and genetic factors) were variably explored and inconsistently retained.
CONCLUSION: Within the existing fentanyl literature, important evidence gaps remain, particularly beyond intravenous administration. Existing models highlight body weight and developmental maturation as principal determinants of clearance and distribution. Evidence remains limited to intravenous administration, with no model data of non-intravenous routes and under-representation of dynamic covariates and external validation. Addressing these gaps will support robust model-informed precision dosing of fentanyl in children.

articles.title: Astrocyte Orai1 signaling promotes spinal excitatory synaptic potentiation and neuropathic pain after nerve injury in male mice.
articles.abstract: Neuropathic pain after peripheral nerve injury is a multifactorial condition mediated partly by inflammation in the spinal cord that results in potentiation of excitatory synaptic transmission in nociceptive circuits. Glial cells including astrocytes are key mediators of the underlying inflammation, but the signaling checkpoints that regulate astrocyte-driven spinal cord inflammation and sensitization of nociceptive circuits are not well understood. Here, we identify Orai1-mediated store-operated Ca 2+ entry (SOCE) as an important regulator of spinal astrocyte cytokine production, metabolic reprogramming, and pain hypersensitivity in mice. Conditional deletion of Orai1 in astrocytes attenuated mechanical allodynia after nerve injury in male but not female mice, despite comparable SOCE suppression in both sexes. Orai1 deficiency also attenuated production of proinflammatory cytokines after SOCE activation, including TNFα, IL-6, and IL-33, both in vivo and in vitro. Electrophysiological recordings revealed that astrocyte Orai1 deletion prevented injury-induced enhancement of glutamatergic synaptic transmission in dorsal horn neurons, linking astrocytic Ca 2+ signaling to central sensitization. Metabolomic profiling showed that Orai1 loss disrupted glycolysis and TCA cycle intermediates while promoting accumulation of immunomodulatory metabolites such as itaconate, consistent with a less inflammatory astrocyte metabolic state. These findings identify Orai1 channels as integrators of astrocyte Ca 2+ signaling, immunometabolism, and excitatory synaptic potentiation after nerve injury, and identify a sexually dimorphic astrocyte mechanism governing neuropathic pain pathogenesis. Targeting astrocyte Orai1 channels may provide a selective therapeutic strategy for male-predominant chronic pain.

articles.title: Thermal pain tolerance depends on stimulus duration and thermode type.
articles.abstract: Quantitative Sensory Testing (QST) measures how acute pain and sensation vary within and across individuals. It remains unclear how specific stimulus features, such as thermode type and stimulation duration, affect QST outcomes. We measured acute thermal pain in 93 healthy volunteers using three thermode types and two durations to assess potential impacts on QST outcomes. Across three experiments, participants completed two QST tasks, in which heat was applied to 8 sites on the left forearm. Thermode type (ATS, CHEPS, T03) and stimulus duration (3 s, 8 s) varied across tasks. We used linear regression to identify pain threshold, tolerance, and temperature-pain correlation (r²). Briefer stimuli were associated with higher pain tolerance (t(45) = 5.84, p < 0.001). Thermode type also influenced pain tolerance, such that tolerance was lower with higher surface area (t(45) = 4.79, p < 0.001). There was a weak effect of duration on pain threshold, such that pain threshold was higher in 3 s duration than in 8 s duration (t(45) = 2.25, p = 0.03). Neither duration nor thermode type affected temperature-pain correlation, and these effects did not differ by controlling for biological sex or task order (all p values > 0.05). These results demonstrate that QST outcomes are differentially sensitive to stimulus features, highlighting the importance of methodological standardization and the careful selection of suprathreshold stimuli in pain experiments. PERSPECTIVE: This study demonstrates the importance of considering stimulus features in "big data" approaches, as pain tolerance is significantly affected by stimulus duration and thermode type, whereas pain thresholds and temperature-pain correlations remain relatively stable.

articles.title: Reimagining Postoperative Recovery: Evaluating an Accelerated Discharge Pathway Following Robotic Radical Prostatectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate postoperative outcomes of patients who underwent same-day discharge to a hybrid Care Hotel recovery model following robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP).
METHODS: The Care Hotel is an outpatient postoperative recovery unit that provides virtual and in-person care as an alternative to overnight hospital admission. The primary outcome was 30-day hospital readmission and secondary outcomes were Clavien-Dindo complication rates, 48-hour emergency department (ED) visits, and 30-day ED visits. Demographic characteristics, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class, operation duration, and Care Hotel call frequency and duration were analyzed for associations with outcomes.
RESULTS: Between August 2021 and August 2023, 174 patients underwent RARP with same-day discharge to the Care Hotel. Almost three-quarters of patients (74.2%) traveled >50 miles for surgery. The 30-day hospital admission rate was 2.3%. The overall Clavien-Dindo complication rate was 9.2%, with all complications classified as Grade 1 (81%) or Grade 2 (19%). 48-hour and 30-day ED visit rates were 2.3% and 8.0%, respectively. Nearly half of patients (48.9%) initiated at least 1 Care Hotel call, with a median duration of 1.6 minutes. No statistically significant associations were identified between postoperative outcomes and demographic variables, ASA class, or operation duration.
CONCLUSION: Same-day discharge to the Care Hotel following RARP was associated with low readmission, ED utilization, and complication rates. These findings support the Care Hotel as a safe alternative to inpatient admission that may optimize postoperative care and resource utilization.

articles.title: Factors associated with 120-day mortality, functional decline, and residential status following fragility hip fractures: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVE: To identify predictors of 120-day mortality and to describe changes in walking capacity, residential status, and secondary fracture prevention following fragility hip fracture in older adults.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Prospective longitudinal observational study. From 340 consecutive patients ≥75 years with fragility hip fractures, an analytical cohort of 324 surgically treated patients was defined. Cumulative 120-day mortality and its predictors (age, American Society of Anesthesiologists [ASA] physical status III-IV, surgical delay>48h, and preoperative moderate/severe malnutrition according to Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition [GLIM] criteria) were evaluated using unadjusted and multivariable binary logistic regression models (primary complete-case analysis, n=321). Changes in walking capacity, residential destination, and pharmacotherapy at 120 days were evaluated over the respective baseline populations at risk.
RESULTS: Of 340 patients, 324 underwent surgery (mean age 88.2 years, 74.1% women; ASA III-IV 82.7%). In 209 (64.5%), surgery was delayed>48h. At 120 days (0% loss to follow-up), 47 patients died (14.5% overall: 10.4% [12/115] in surgery ≤48h vs. 16.7% [35/209] in surgery>48h; unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.73, 95% CI 0.86-3.48; p=0.126). In the multivariable logistic regression model (n=321), preoperative moderate/severe malnutrition was independently associated with higher 120-day mortality (adjusted OR 4.80, 95% CI 2.14-10.78; p<0.001). After adjusting for age, ASA physical status III-IV, and preoperative malnutrition, surgical delay>48h was not statistically associated with mortality (adjusted OR 1.80, 95% CI 0.87-3.75; p=0.113), although the wide confidence interval does not exclude a clinically relevant risk. At 120 days, among pre-fracture independent walkers (n=303), 13.9% (42/303) transitioned to severe dependence/immobility, 72.3% (219/303) maintained independent walking, and 13.9% (42/303) had died. Among patients previously living at home (n=205), 38.0% (78/205) required de novo institutionalization, 48.3% (99/205) remained at home, and 13.7% (28/205) had died. Antiresorptive prescription increased from 2.8% at baseline to 5.8% among survivors.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative moderate/severe malnutrition was independently associated with increased 120-day mortality after adjusting for age, ASA physical status, and surgical delay. Surgical delay>48h was not statistically associated with 120-day mortality in unadjusted or adjusted analyses, although estimates were imprecise and residual confounding cannot be excluded. Loss of independent walking capacity and de novo institutionalization affected a substantial proportion of at-risk patients at 120 days, while antiresorptive prescription remained low.

articles.title: Can risk factors predict the development of subdural haematoma after shunt surgery?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Subdural haematoma is a well-recognized complication following ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery. However, limited data exist regarding which clinical and surgical factors may predict its development. This study aims to identify specific risk factors associated with subdural haematoma formation following ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 499 patients who underwent ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement between June 2010 and June 2020. Patients with a history of trauma were excluded. Demographic characteristics, surgical details, and radiological data were recorded. The primary outcome was the incidence of postoperative subdural haematoma. Statistical analyses were performed to identify significant predictors.
RESULTS: Of the 499 patients included in the study, 79 (15%) developed subdural haematoma during follow-up. Univariate and multivariate analyses revealed that older age, male gender, preoperative Evans index >48%, acetylsalicylic acid use, and placement of the ventricular catheter through Kocher's point were significantly associated with increased risk of subdural haematoma development (p < 0.05). No significant association was found with other surgical variables.
CONCLUSION: Subdural haematoma occurred in 15% of patients following ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery. The presence of certain preoperative and perioperative factors (particularly age, sex, ventricular size, acetylsalicylic acid use, and catheter trajectory) may help identify high-risk patients. Risk-based follow-up and tailored surgical planning could potentially reduce the incidence of subdural haematoma after shunting procedures.

articles.title: Endoscopic management of buried bumper syndrome in children using a dedicated endoscopic resection device (Flamingo): A single-centre retrospective case series.
articles.abstract: Buried bumper syndrome (BBS) is a serious complication of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) tubes. Management of completely buried bumpers is challenging, as surgical approaches carry significant morbidity and endoscopic techniques can be technically demanding. A dedicated endoscopic resection device (Flamingo) is a tool designed to facilitate controlled incision and exposure of the buried bumper, but its use in paediatric patients has not previously been reported. We performed a single-centre retrospective review of paediatric patients with BBS treated using this device. Nine patients aged 2-16 years with a median American Society of Anesthesiologists Grade 3 were identified. Successful bumper removal was achieved in all cases, with a mean procedure time of 46.1 min. One recurrence was successfully retreated, and one readmission occurred due to jejunostomy tube displacement. No procedure-related complications were observed. These findings suggest the device is a safe and effective minimally invasive treatment for paediatric BBS.

articles.title: Mineralocorticoid receptor signaling reduces somatostatin expression in developing sensory neurons and drives neonatal pain after early-life stress.
articles.abstract: Early-life stress (ELS) causes pain hypersensitivity in neonatal mice and alters the transcriptional profile of the immature dorsal root ganglia (DRG), highlighted by a marked reduction in the expression of a neuropeptide, somatostatin (Sst), which is known to constitutively suppress peripheral nociceptive transmission during adulthood. However, the mechanisms that drive plasticity in gene expression within the developing DRG and neonatal pain after ELS remain unclear. Here, we investigated the degree to which ELS-induced neonatal pain was mediated by corticosterone signaling onto sensory neurons and potential changes in peripheral Sst transmission. The conditional knockout of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), but not the glucocorticoid receptor, from immature DRG neurons prevented ELS-evoked neonatal pain. In contrast, the systemic administration of the selective MR antagonist eplerenone failed to acutely influence pain after ELS, thus suggesting that MR activation enhances pain during the neonatal period via canonical effects on gene transcription. Meanwhile, hind paw injection of the Sst receptor antagonist cyclo-somatostatin increased spontaneous nocifensive behaviors in control pups, but not in pups previously subjected to ELS, raising the possibility that a disruption in tonic antinociception mediated by peripheral Sst contributes to neonatal pain after ELS. Furthermore, administration of the peripherally restricted Sst analog octreotide reversed noxious cold and pressure hypersensitivity in neonatal mice after ELS. Finally, the selective deletion of MR from sensory neurons prevented the ELS-induced decrease in Sst expression. Collectively, these results provide novel mechanistic insight into the effects of chronic early-life adversity on nociceptive processing in the developing nervous system.

articles.title: Challenges in obese liver transplant recipients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The global obesity epidemic has significantly altered the epidemiology of chronic liver disease and liver transplantation, with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis emerging as a rapidly increasing indication for liver transplantation worldwide. Obesity in liver transplantation candidates is frequently accompanied by sarcopenia, frailty, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic comorbidities, creating complex perioperative and long-term management challenges. This review summarizes contemporary evidence regarding assessment, pretransplant preparation, perioperative management, and long-term outcomes of obese liver transplant recipients, while highlighting evolving therapeutic strategies and unresolved clinical questions.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent literature emphasizes that BMI alone inadequately characterizes obesity in cirrhosis, with body composition, sarcopenic obesity, visceral adiposity, and frailty emerging as important prognostic factors. Structured prehabilitation, lifestyle modification, incretin-based pharmacotherapy, and selective metabolic bariatric surgery have shown promising results in carefully selected patients. Although obesity increases perioperative complexity and postoperative complications, carefully selected obese recipients can achieve graft and patient survival comparable to nonobese recipients.
SUMMARY: Obesity should not be considered a contraindication to liver transplantation. Individualized recipient assessment, coordinated perioperative optimization, and long-term metabolic surveillance are essential to improve outcomes. Future research should refine obesity assessment beyond BMI and clarify the optimal integration of pharmacologic and surgical weight-loss strategies in liver transplantation candidates before and after transplantation.

articles.title: Modified Frailty Index and Postoperative Outcomes of Zygomaticomaxillary Complex Fracture Repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The modified 5-item frailty index (mFI-5) is a comorbidity-based risk stratification tool previously validated in patients undergoing facial plastic and reconstructive surgery. This retrospective US hospital database study investigates the association between mFI-5 score and postoperative complications following zygomaticomaxillary complex (ZMC) fracture repair.
METHODS: The National Surgical Quality Improvement Program was queried for patients undergoing ZMC fracture repair between 2005 and 2020. The mFI-5 score was calculated by assigning one point for each of the following comorbidities: diabetes mellitus, hypertension, congestive heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and dependent functional status. Patients were stratified by mFI-5 score. Univariate and multivariable analyses were performed to assess associations between frailty and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: A total of 2260 patients were included and stratified by mFI-5 scores of 0 (n = 1890), 1 (n = 285), and 2 or greater (n = 85). Higher mFI-5 scores were associated with male sex, older age, higher American Society of Anesthesiologists classification, inpatient status, obesity, weight loss, bleeding disorders, and dependent functional status. Higher mFI-5 was associated with increased rates of surgical complications, urinary tract infections, prolonged ventilation over 48 h, pneumonia, cumulative morbidity, and cumulative medical complications. On multivariable analysis, mFI-5 scores of 1 (p = 0.027) and 2 or greater (p = 0.049) were independently associated with cumulative morbidity, and a score of 1 was associated with surgical complications (p = 0.022).
CONCLUSION: The mFI-5 is associated with cumulative morbidity and surgical complications following ZMC fracture repair. Assessment of frailty may improve perioperative risk stratification in this population.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4.

articles.title: Oral Irrigation and Microbiome Remodeling after Oral Cancer Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Patients with oral cancer undergoing free flap reconstruction face significant surgical trauma, making the prevention of postoperative wound infection and the maintenance of oral microecological balance critical. This study systematically evaluated oral microbiome changes before and after surgery and assessed the effectiveness of postoperative oral irrigation using 2 different regimens. In an exploratory randomized controlled trial, 60 patients were assigned to receive oral irrigation with either bipolar water or a combination of hydrogen peroxide and sodium bicarbonate solution. Saliva and irrigation samples were collected at 7 time points, preoperatively and before and 5 minutes after oral irrigation on postoperative days 1, 4, and 7, and analyzed using specialized sequencing techniques to determine microbial abundance and diversity. Clinical outcomes, including wound infection rates and patient comfort, were also recorded. The results indicated that surgical treatment reduced the diversity of the oral microbiota and altered its composition. Before surgery, the oral cavity was dominated by potentially pathogenic taxa, which shifted toward oral resident microorganisms postoperatively. Continued oral irrigation promoted a transition from an unstable, anaerobic-enriched state toward a relatively stable community structure dominated by facultative anaerobes. While no differences were observed between the 2 groups regarding wound infection rates or microbial composition, the bipolar water group reported higher patient comfort and required shorter irrigation times. Furthermore, the bipolar water group maintained more stable microbial diversity, whereas the hydrogen peroxide group exhibited more pronounced fluctuations and higher fungal detection rates. In conclusion, surgery induces early microbial imbalance, but staged oral irrigation facilitates the stabilization of the oral microecosystem. Bipolar water is an effective alternative for perioperative care, helping to maintain microbial stability while improving the patient experience.

articles.title: Predictive Performance of POSPOM and EuroSCORE-II for Perioperative Mortality in Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Simpler generalized scores such as POSPOM (PreOperative Score to Predict Post-Operative Mortality) may appear attractive because they can be derived from routinely available variables and applied across surgical specialties, although their reliability in cardiac surgery remains uncertain.
AIM: To compare the performance of POSPOM and EuroSCORE-II scores for predicting in-hospital mortality among patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary university cardiac surgery center. A total of 320 adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, valve surgery, or combined procedures between 2021 and 2024 were included. Discrimination was assessed using ROC and precision-recall curves with DeLong's test. Calibration was evaluated using calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, Hosmer-Lemeshow testing, and GiViTI calibration belts. Agreement was analyzed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC), Bland- Altman plots, and Passing-Bablok and Deming regression.
RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 7.5% (24/320). POSPOM showed poorer discrimination than EuroSCORE-II (AUC 0.611 vs. 0.745; P = 0.012) and lower PR-AUC (0.115 vs. 0.287). Both models showed imperfect calibration, and agreement between scores was weak (ICC 0.283), with systematic differences observed between predicted mortality estimates. Exploratory segmented regression suggested that inter-model divergence increased with age, with an estimated breakpoint near 59 years. POSPOM did not improve reclassification (continuous NRI -0.31), and decision curve analysis favored EuroSCORE-II.
CONCLUSION: POSPOM showed poorer predictive performance than EuroSCORE-II for in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously in light of the limited number of mortality events, retrospective reconstruction of POSPOM, and the need for external validation.

articles.title: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay.
METHODS: Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis.
RESULTS: Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of ultrasound-guided transforaminal cervical nerve root block for cervical spondylotic radiculopathy: A retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Cervical spondylotic radiculopathy causes neck and upper-extremity pain, sensory disturbances, and functional impairment. Evidence on short-term outcomes after ultrasound-guided transforaminal cervical nerve root block (TF-CNRB) remains limited. This study examined changes in pain, neck-related disability, patient-reported improvement, analgesic use, and documented adverse events after TF-CNRB. This single-center retrospective observational study included 42 patients with cervical spondylotic radiculopathy who underwent ultrasound-guided TF-CNRB between January 2024 and December 2025. Eligible patients had a baseline Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) score ≥4 and persistent symptoms despite at least 4 weeks of conservative treatment. Patients received a single TF-CNRB and were assessed at baseline and at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure. The primary outcome was pain intensity measured using the NRS. Secondary outcomes included the Neck Disability Index (NDI), Patient Global Impression of Change, analgesic use, and adverse events. Changes in NRS and NDI scores were evaluated using repeated-measures analyses. All 42 patients completed the 3-month follow-up. The mean NRS score decreased from 6.07 ± 0.95 at baseline to 3.17 ± 1.38 at 1 week, 3.40 ± 1.13 at 1 month, and 3.52 ± 1.13 at 3 months (overall P < .001). The mean NDI decreased from 19.3 ± 4.4% to 9.0 ± 4.2%, 9.2 ± 4.1%, and 9.7 ± 3.9%, respectively (all P < .001). The prespecified NDI minimal clinically important difference (≥5.42 percentage points) was achieved by 88.1%, 85.7%, and 83.3% of patients, respectively. At the same follow-up points, 73.8%, 73.8%, and 71.4% of patients reported being "markedly improved" or "improved" on the Patient Global Impression of Change. Analgesic use was reported by 14.3%, 11.9%, and 19.0% of patients, respectively. No serious procedure-related adverse events were documented in the available clinical records. Pain and neck-related disability were lower during the 3 months after ultrasound-guided TF-CNRB. Most patients achieved a clinically meaningful NDI reduction, and more than 70% reported favorable global improvement. No serious adverse events were documented, but the sample size and retrospective ascertainment limit conclusions about safety. The uncontrolled design precludes causal inference regarding treatment effectiveness. Larger prospective controlled studies are warranted.

articles.title: Retrospective evaluation of predictors and clinical impact of postoperative delirium in liver transplant recipients.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the epidemiology, predictors, and clinical outcomes of postoperative delirium (POD) in liver transplant (LT) recipients. Clinical data from 427 LT recipients from the Third Xiangya Hospital were retrospectively reviewed. The epidemiology (incidence, onset, and duration), predictors, and associated clinical outcomes of POD were analyzed using standardized delirium assessment tools and multivariate regression. POD occurred in 19.0% of recipients, with a median onset at 26.0 hours posttransplant. Multivariate analysis identified 4 independent pre and postoperative predictors, including a higher model for end-stage liver disease score and hepatic encephalopathy within 24 hours before LT, infection within 2 months prior to LT, and abnormal sodium within 1 hour after LT (all P < .05). In a sensitivity analysis treating early death or persistent coma as a composite outcome with POD (n = 436), the same 4 independent predictors were identified, with consistent effect estimates. Regarding clinical outcomes, POD was significantly associated with prolonged intensive care unit stays, extended mechanical ventilation requirements, and increased use of renal replacement therapy (all P < .01). Although recipients with POD showed higher 1- and 6-month all-cause mortality in unadjusted analyses, POD was not an independent predictor of mortality after adjustment for confounding factors. POD occurs frequently and early after LT, with identifiable pre and postoperative risk factors. While POD markedly increases perioperative morbidity and resource utilization, it does not independently predict short-term all-cause mortality in this cohort.

articles.title: Comparative perioperative and follow-up outcomes of three laparoscopic reconstructive procedures for pediatric duplex kidney: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to describe and compare perioperative characteristics, postoperative recovery, complications, and observed follow-up outcomes among children undergoing 3 laparoscopic renal-preserving reconstructive procedures selected according to anatomical and functional characteristics. This retrospective cohort study included children with duplex kidney who underwent laparoscopic renal-preserving reconstructive surgery between January 2016 and December 2025. Patients were divided into 3 groups according to the surgical procedure performed. Baseline characteristics, preoperative anatomical findings, surgical indications, operative outcomes, postoperative recovery, complications, and follow-up outcomes were compared among the groups. Additional pairwise comparison was performed between pelvic-level end-to-side ureteroureterostomy (UU) and upper-pole ureteral bladder reimplantation. A total of 91 children were included: 29 who underwent renal pelvic-level upper-pole ureter to lower-pole renal pelvis anastomosis, 36 who underwent pelvic-level end-to-side UU, and 26 who underwent upper-pole ureteral bladder reimplantation. Baseline demographic characteristics were comparable among the 3 groups. Significant differences were observed in anatomical features and surgical indications. Markedly dilated or obstructed upper-pole ureters were more frequent in the renal pelvic-level ureteropyelostomy and pelvic-level end-to-side UU groups, whereas distal upper-pole ureteral abnormality and reflux-related indications were more common in the upper-pole ureteral bladder reimplantation group. Operative time differed significantly among the 3 groups, with the shortest time observed in the pelvic-level end-to-side UU group. Estimated blood loss was also lowest in this group. Pairwise comparison showed that pelvic-level end-to-side UU was associated with significantly shorter operative time and lower estimated blood loss than upper-pole ureteral bladder reimplantation. Laparoscopic renal pelvic-level upper-pole ureter to lower-pole renal pelvis anastomosis, pelvic-level end-to-side UU, and upper-pole ureteral bladder reimplantation appear to be feasible and effective renal-preserving reconstructive procedures for pediatric duplex kidney when selected according to anatomical and functional characteristics. Pelvic-level end-to-side UU was associated with shorter operative time and lower estimated blood loss than upper-pole ureteral bladder reimplantation when a suitable ipsilateral recipient ureter was available. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in postoperative recovery, complications, or the measured follow-up outcomes. These findings should be interpreted in the context of anatomy-based procedure selection rather than as evidence of equivalent effectiveness.

articles.title: Determination of the ED50 and ED95 of intrathecal ropivacaine for labor analgesia in multiparous women: A prospective, sequential allocation study.
articles.abstract: With the implementation of China's two-child policy,the number of multiparous women has increased significantly. However, most studies on labor analgesia have focused on nulliparous women, and research on analgesia for multiparous women remains relatively limited. This study aimed to determine the median effective dose (ED50) and 95% effective dose (ED95) of intrathecal ropivacaine for labor analgesia in multiparous women. Thirty multiparous parturients were enrolled. The initial dose of intrathecal ropivacaine was set at 3.0 mg. For each subsequent participant, the dose was adjusted by 0.3 mg increments or decrements based on the analgesic response of the previous subject. Effective analgesia was defined as a numerical rating scale (NRS) score ≤ 3 achieved within 10 minutes after intrathecal administration. If analgesia was effective, the ropivacaine dose for the subsequent patient in that group was decreased by 0.3 mg. Conversely, if analgesia was ineffective, the dose for the next patient in that group was increased by 0.3mg. For women with ineffective analgesia 10 minutes after intrathecal study drug administration,10 mL of 0.08% ropivacaine combined with 0.4 μg/mL sufentanil was administered epidurally as rescue analgesia. The ED50 and ED95 of intrathecal ropivacaine determined by Probit regression were 2.16 mg (95% CI: 1.83-2.39 mg) and 2.76 mg (95% CI: 2.49-3.02 mg), respectively. The incidence of adverse events during effective spinal analgesia was low. No cases of bradycardia, respiratory depression, hypotension, or motor block were observed. The ED50 and ED95 of intrathecal ropivacaine for labor analgesia in multiparous women during spontaneous latent phase labor were 2.16 mg and 2.76 mg, respectively. (www.chictr.org.cn, registration number: ChiCTR2100054379).

articles.title: Association of preoperative systemic immune-inflammation index and geriatric nutritional risk index with prolonged postoperative length of stay in older patients with hip fracture: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the associations of the preoperative systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI), and their joint exposure with prolonged postoperative length of stay (LOS) in older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. This retrospective cohort study included older patients who underwent surgery for hip fracture. SII was calculated from preoperative platelet, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts, and GNRI from albumin and body weight. High SII was defined as above the cohort-specific 75th percentile, GNRI ≤98 as nutritional risk, and prolonged postoperative LOS as above the cohort-specific 75th percentile. Logistic regression was used to assess associations of SII, GNRI, and their joint exposure with prolonged postoperative LOS, adjusting for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, fracture type, and preoperative waiting time. Interaction, discrimination, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were also performed. Among 653 patients, higher log(SII) was associated with greater odds of prolonged postoperative LOS (OR = 2.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.68-2.94), as was each 10-point decrease in GNRI (OR = 1.84, 95% CI 1.26-2.68). Compared with patients with non-high SII and no nutritional risk, those with both high SII and GNRI-defined nutritional risk had substantially higher odds of prolonged postoperative LOS (OR = 10.16, 95% CI 5.52-18.67). Each 1-point increase in the SII-GNRI risk burden score was associated with higher odds (OR = 3.30, 95% CI 2.42-4.51; P for trend <.001). Multiplicative interaction was not significant (P = .138), whereas exploratory OR-based additive interaction measures were positive. The clinical model area under the receiver operating characteristic curve increased from 0.697 to 0.774 after adding SII-GNRI joint exposure. Findings were generally consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Coexisting high SII and GNRI-defined nutritional risk may identify older patients with higher odds of prolonged postoperative LOS after hip fracture surgery. Joint assessment of inflammatory and nutritional status may provide additional information for perioperative risk stratification. Given the single-center retrospective design, cohort-derived thresholds, and lack of validation, these findings are preliminary and require confirmation in independent populations.

articles.title: Postoperative complications and care requirements following Achilles tendon repair: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Achilles tendon rupture is a common injury in orthopedic and sports medicine practice. Although surgical repair is widely performed, postoperative complications remain clinically relevant and may increase postoperative care burden. This study aimed to investigate postoperative complications and care requirements following Achilles tendon repair and to identify factors associated with postoperative complications. This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent surgical repair for acute Achilles tendon rupture between January 2021 and December 2024. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, perioperative variables, postoperative complications, and postoperative care indicators were collected from electronic medical records. The primary outcome was the occurrence of any postoperative complication within 3 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, number of dressing changes, outpatient follow-up visits, unplanned readmission, reoperation, and outpatient secondary wound procedures. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative complications. A total of 86 patients were included, and postoperative complications occurred in 16 patients (18.6%). Wound-related complications were the most common adverse events, including delayed wound healing in 6 patients (7.0%), superficial surgical site infection in 4 (4.7%), deep infection requiring operative debridement in 1 (1.2%), and chronic wound problems requiring prolonged outpatient care in 2 (2.3%). Compared with patients without complications, those with complications had significantly higher body mass index, a higher prevalence of smoking history, and a longer interval from injury to surgery. They also had significantly longer hospital stay, more dressing changes, more outpatient visits, and higher rates of readmission and reoperation. In multivariable analysis, smoking history (odds ratio 3.21, 95% confidence interval 1.07-9.61, P = .037) and interval from injury to surgery (odds ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.08-1.71, P = .010) remained independently associated with postoperative complications. Postoperative complications following Achilles tendon repair were relatively common and were predominantly wound-related. Patients who developed complications required substantially greater postoperative care. Smoking history and a longer interval from injury to surgery were independently associated with postoperative complications.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and recovery impact of implementing enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathway in elderly patients with gynecological malignant tumors.
articles.abstract: Perioperative management is critical for optimizing recovery outcomes in elderly patients with gynecological malignant tumors, a demographic often facing significant health challenges. The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway has been proposed as a multifaceted approach designed to enhance recovery and minimize complications during the perioperative phase, particularly in vulnerable populations such as the elderly. Patients who underwent traditional perioperative management at the affiliated hospital of Chengde Medical University between January 2011 and December 2018 were selected as the conventional group. Patients who underwent ERAS perioperative management between January 2019 and July 2025 were selected as the ERAS group. Postoperative recovery and complications were then compared between the groups. The ERAS and control groups involved 149 and 90 patients, respectively. Patient characteristics were not significantly different between the 2 groups (P > .05). However, the ERAS group showed a lower volume of intraoperative fluid rehydration and a shorter time to first postoperative flatus, time to first defecation, duration of postoperative hospitalization, and interval time between surgery and the first postoperative chemotherapy session. The Visual Analogue Scale score at 24 hours postoperatively was also significantly lower in the ERAS group (P < .05). Meanwhile, there was no significant between-group difference in the incidence of postoperative complications and the 30-day readmission rate (all P > .05). Use of the ERAS pathway during the perioperative period does not increase the occurrence of postoperative complications and can accelerate recovery, shorten the postoperative hospitalization duration, and help with earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy in elderly patients with gynecological malignant tumors.

articles.title: Early versus late duodenal atresia repair in preterm and low birth weight neonates.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Duodenal atresia (DA) is a common cause of neonatal intestinal obstruction requiring surgical correction. The timing of repair in very low birth weight (VLBW, <1.5 kg) and extremely preterm (<32 weeks gestation) neonates remains debated. Early repair may reduce total parenteral nutrition (TPN)-associated morbidity, whereas delayed repair may mitigate anaesthetic and technical risks in fragile neonates.
METHODS: A retrospective 20-year review (2004-2024) was conducted at a tertiary paediatric surgical centre. Infants <1.5 kg and/or <32 weeks were classified as early repair (≤14 days) or delayed repair (>14 days). Outcomes included postoperative complications, time to full enteral feeding, hospital stay, and mortality.
RESULTS: Sixteen infants met inclusion criteria. Of these, 7 (43.8%) underwent early repair and 9 (56.2%) underwent delayed repair. There were no significant differences in comorbidities or overall complication rates between groups. Time to full feeds was shorter in the early repair group (median 11 vs 40 days, p = 0.013). No surgery-related deaths occurred (0 [0%] in both groups).
DISCUSSION: Early repair of DA in stable preterm or VLBW infants is feasible and safe when undertaken by experienced teams. Surgical timing should be guided by physiological stability rather than arbitrary gestational or weight thresholds. Further studies are needed to refine evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Impact of Chronic Heart Failure on Vascular Responsiveness: A Prospective Observational In Vivo and Ex Vivo Study in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract: Background: Patients with chronic heart failure (HF) are at increased risk of vasoplegia after cardiac surgery, potentially because neurohormonal activation in the context of HF alters vascular regulation. Methods: We compared perioperative vasoresponsiveness in patients with and without HF undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Patients were prospectively enrolled, and changes in systemic vascular resistance (ΔSVR) after phenylephrine and nitroglycerin were measured perioperatively (in vivo). Ex vivo vasoreactivity to phenylephrine and vasopressin was tested in 40 biopsies. Results: In vivo and ex vivo analyses included 36 and 13 patients (10 controls and 3 HF patients), respectively. At baseline, phenylephrine increased SVR by 26% in HF patients (estimated marginal mean, 95% CI 16-35%) versus 51% in controls (95% CI 38-64%; p = 0.002). This attenuated response persisted during CPB, and ex vivo observations suggested a similar pattern. Responsiveness to nitroglycerin was unchanged. Lower post-CPB ΔSVR was associated with greater norepinephrine use during the first postoperative day (β = -346.6, 95% CI -541.2 to -151.9; R2 = 0.291). Conversely, HF patients showed greater ex vivo responsiveness to vasopressin. Conclusions: HF is associated with marked impairment of α1-adrenergic vasoresponsiveness, indicating impaired α1-adrenergic signaling. Preserved vasopressin responsiveness may support its earlier use for postoperative hypotension in these patients.

articles.title: Genetic and Molecular Mechanisms of Synaptic Plasticity in Perioperative Delirium: From Neuroinflammation to Circuit Dysfunction and Recovery.
articles.abstract: Perioperative delirium is an acute disturbance of attention and awareness that arises when surgical stress interacts with limited brain reserve. Synaptic dysfunction provides a plausible connection between genetic susceptibility, neuroimmune responses and fluctuating network activity, but the strength of evidence differs substantially across these levels. This narrative review examines human genetic and molecular studies alongside experimental investigations of synaptic plasticity, with emphasis on recent primary research. Large association studies now support an association between APOE ε4 and delirium susceptibility, whereas blood transcriptomics and brain tissue profiling implicate complement regulation, immune responses and glial cell states. Experimental studies identify mechanisms involving complement-dependent synaptic engulfment, astrocytic cholesterol and glucose support, glutamate handling, mitochondrial stress and epigenetic regulation of BDNF-ARC signaling. These findings suggest that reversible changes in synaptic efficacy and slower structural remodeling can coexist, without requiring synapse loss to explain every delirium episode. Human neurogranin, neurofilament and electrophysiological studies also reveal important negative or context-dependent findings. Translation therefore requires separation of preoperative vulnerability from acute disease activity, direct assessment of attention and arousal, and evidence that a molecular intervention improves clinically meaningful outcomes. The phase 2 trial of the APOE mimetic CN-105 illustrates the distinction between mechanistic plausibility and clinical efficacy, as its benefit for delirium prevention remains unproven. A cell-specific, temporally resolved approach is needed to determine which synaptic mechanisms are causal, reversible and therapeutically accessible in human perioperative delirium.

articles.title: Ten-Year Outcomes in Liver Transplantation for HBV/HDV Coinfection: A Romanian Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV)/hepatitis D virus (HDV) coinfection is a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and remains a disproportionately frequent indication for liver transplantation (LT) in Romania, one of the highest-HDV-prevalence countries in Europe, yet patient-level outcome data from this high-burden Eastern European setting are lacking. We report the ten-year outcomes of LT for HBV/HDV-related cirrhosis in a large single-centre Romanian cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analysed 236 adults transplanted for HBV/HDV-related cirrhosis at a single tertiary centre. Survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method and predictors were assessed by Cox regression. HBV, HDV and HCC recurrence, and anti-HBs kinetics under combined hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG)/nucleos(t)ide-analogue prophylaxis, were analysed. Results: Over a median follow-up of 8.1 years (maximum 14.4), overall survival was 89.8%, 82.8% and 79.5% at 1, 5 and 10 years; among 90-day survivors, conditional survival reached 86.9% at 10 years. Under an "on-demand" low-dose HBIG protocol combined with nucleos(t)ide analogues, HBV recurrence (HBsAg reappearance) occurred in 4.7% and HDV recurrence in 1.7% of patients, without graft dysfunction or death attributable to viral recurrence; anti-HBs titres stabilised at 120-140 IU/L beyond the first year, with approximately 60% of patients maintaining levels above 100 IU/L long-term. HBsAg reappearance occurred exclusively in HCC recipients (11/87 vs. 0/149, p < 0.001) and clustered in patients with tumour recurrence (9/17 vs. 2/70, p < 0.001), preceding the radiological diagnosis of recurrence in six of the nine patients concerned. Mortality was concentrated in the perioperative period (90-day mortality 8.5%), driven mainly by sepsis and surgical complications, and recurrent HCC was the most common recorded cause of late death. Neither the severity of liver disease at listing (MELD, ALBI) nor any viral variable was associated with survival; HCC as indication was associated with survival in univariable analysis and beyond-Milan tumour burden independently (HR 2.74, 95% CI 1.36-5.54). Conclusions: LT for HBV/HDV-related cirrhosis achieves excellent long-term survival and very low viral recurrence under combined prophylaxis, even in this HDV-hyperendemic setting; beyond the perioperative period, viral factors were not associated with survival, whereas beyond-Milan tumour burden was associated with worse survival in one of the sensitivity analyses. In this HBV/HDV cohort, HBsAg reappearance after transplantation for HCC was associated with tumour recurrence and may be regarded as a warning sign prompting oncological reassessment; whether it represents a true early marker requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Axillary Dacron Graft Versus Direct Femoral Arterial Cannulation for Peripheral VA-ECMO After Heart Transplantation: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) remains a major cause of early morbidity and mortality after heart transplantation, and peripheral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) represents an established rescue therapy for severe cases. Although direct femoral arterial cannulation is commonly used because of its rapid deployment, axillary artery cannulation through a Dacron graft provides antegrade arterial perfusion and may represent an alternative approach. This study compared early clinical outcomes and cannulation-related complications between these two arterial cannulation strategies. Methods: In this retrospective single-center observational study, 42 consecutive adult heart transplant recipients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for PGD were included. Patients were divided according to arterial cannulation strategy into direct femoral cannulation (DFC, n = 25) and axillary Dacron graft cannulation (ADG, n = 17). Baseline recipient and donor characteristics, perioperative variables, postoperative outcomes, vascular complications, successful VA-ECMO weaning, and survival to hospital discharge were compared. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for major clinical outcomes and cannulation-related complications. Results: The primary composite endpoint of cannulation-related complications occurred in 0/17 patients (0%) in the ADG group and 3/25 patients (12.0%) in the DFC group (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.01-3.80; p = 0.260). Successful VA-ECMO weaning was achieved in 94.1% versus 92.0% (p = 1.000), and survival to hospital discharge was 76.5% versus 64.0% (OR 1.83, 95% CI 0.46-7.32; p = 0.505). Stroke occurred in 5.9% versus 16.0% (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.03-3.23; p = 0.632), while renal replacement therapy was required in 35.3% versus 52.0% (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.14-1.79; p = 0.353). No statistically significant differences were detected between groups. Conclusions: No statistically significant differences in successful VA-ECMO weaning or survival to hospital discharge were observed between axillary Dacron graft and direct femoral arterial cannulation. No statistically significant differences in neurological, vascular, or other major postoperative outcomes were detected. Although several complications occurred numerically less frequently with axillary cannulation, the limited sample size and wide confidence intervals preclude conclusions regarding comparative superiority. Axillary Dacron graft cannulation may therefore represent a feasible alternative in selected heart transplant recipients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for PGD. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted.

articles.title: Papillary Morphology, Periampullary Diverticulum, and Comorbidity Burden in Relation to Cannulation Outcomes and Procedural Difficulty in ERCP.
articles.abstract: Background: Although it has been suggested that papillary morphology and periampullary diverticulum (PAD) may affect the outcomes of endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), the independent effects of these factors have not been clearly established. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the association of papillary morphology and PAD with ERCP success, procedural difficulty, and post-ERCP complications. Methods: Records of 1046 ERCP procedures performed at a single center were retrospectively reviewed. The primary analysis included 693 patients with native papillae and no prior sphincterotomy. Papilla morphology was available for 381 patients and periampullary diverticulum (PAD) status for 633. Outcomes included cannulation success, difficult cannulation, cannulation time, number of cannulation attempts, post-ERCP complications, and length of hospital stay. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression was used to evaluate independent associations with difficult cannulation, overall complications, cannulation failure, and post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP), adjusting for papilla morphology, PAD status, age, sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status class, and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Results: Regular papilla morphology, compared with the pooled group of atypical papilla morphologies (Small, Bulging, Ridged), was associated with significantly higher cannulation success (97.4% vs. 91.2%; p = 0.012), shorter cannulation time (median 3.0 vs. 4.0 min; p = 0.009), fewer cannulation attempts (p = 0.007), and shorter hospital stay (median 5.0 vs. 6.0 days; p = 0.013). The presence of a PAD was not significantly associated with any procedural outcome or complication (all p > 0.05). CCI was independently associated with cannulation failure (adjusted OR 1.40 per one-point increase; 95% CI 1.03-1.91; p = 0.031) and was the only factor reaching statistical significance across the four multivariable models. The multivariable model showed modest discrimination for difficult cannulation (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.596; 95% CI 0.515-0.675). Conclusions: Atypical papillary morphology was associated with lower cannulation success, longer cannulation time, and more cannulation attempts in univariable analyses; however, neither papillary morphology nor periampullary diverticulum was independently associated with ERCP outcomes. Among the variables evaluated, higher CCI was the only factor independently associated with cannulation failure; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of failure events.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Hip Fractures in Centenarians Compared to Non-Centenarians.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: The number of hip fractures among centenarians is rising, yet their outcomes and the factors influencing mortality remain inadequately characterized. This study compared postoperative outcomes between centenarians and non-centenarians and examined perioperative factors associated with mortality. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 31 centenarians (≥100 years) who underwent hip fracture surgery between October 2022 and March 2024 and 176 consecutive non-centenarians (65-99 years) admitted between October 2022 and April 2023. Associations between centenarian status, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score, comorbidity-only Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), surgical procedure, and time to surgery with 30-day and 12-month mortality were analyzed using logistic regression with clinically pre-selected covariates (Firth's method for 30-day mortality). Results: Centenarians exhibited higher ASA scores, while CCI values did not differ between groups. Centenarians experienced longer intensive care unit and hospital stays. The complication rate was numerically higher among centenarians (35.5% vs. 30.1%), although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.55). Thirty-day mortality was 29.0% for centenarians compared to 6.2% for non-centenarians, and 12-month mortality was 80.6% versus 30.1% (both p < 0.001). Centenarian status (30-day odds ratio [OR] 4.87, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.73-13.60; 12-month OR 8.19, 95% CI 3.16-24.22) and higher ASA scores were associated with increased mortality, whereas CCI was not. Longer time to surgery was associated with higher 12-month mortality (OR 1.23 per 24 h, 95% CI 1.01-1.51). Conclusions: Centenarians demonstrated substantially higher short- and long-term mortality following hip fracture surgery compared to younger older adults. Extreme age and elevated ASA scores were associated with increased mortality, although unmeasured factors such as frailty may contribute to these associations. Hip fracture in centenarians should be considered a major life-limiting event that necessitates early goals-of-care discussions.

articles.title: Transition from open surgery to ultrasound-guided minimally invasive surgery for insertional Achilles tendinopathy: similar patient-reported outcomes and substantially lower treatment costs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy is commonly treated surgically when conservative management fails. Traditionally, open central-splitting surgery (OCS) has been the standard approach, but minimally invasive ultrasound-guided techniques have recently been introduced. This study compared patient-reported outcomes and treatment costs following a transition in surgical practice from open central-splitting surgery to ultrasound- and colour Doppler-guided minimally invasive wide-awake local anaesthesia no tourniquet (WALANT) surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective historical cohort study included fifty-two consecutive patients with insertional Achilles tendinopathy. Twenty patients underwent OCS surgery during 2017-2019, followed by thirty-two patients who underwent US-/CD-guided WALANT surgery during 2020-2022. The primary clinical outcome was the SEFAS score at 12 months. Between-group differences in the 12-month SEFAS scores were analysed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for baseline SEFAS score, age, sex, and BMI. Direct medical costs were estimated from the resource use observed across the two treatment pathways.
RESULTS: The mean SEFAS score improved from 18 at baseline to 40 at 12 months in the US-/CD group and from 23 to 41 in the OCS group. In the adjusted analysis, the mean difference in the 12-month SEFAS was 0.62 points in favour of US-/CD (95% CI, - 3.50 to 4.73). Estimated direct medical costs were $1,432 per patient for US-/CD and $3,343 for OCS, corresponding to an absolute reduction of $1,911 per patient and approximately 50% lower costs with the US-/CD treatment pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: Following a transition in surgical practice, US-/CD-guided surgery was associated with similar 12-month patient-reported outcomes and approximately 50% lower direct medical costs compared with OCS surgery. These findings suggest that minimally invasive US-/CD-guided surgery under local anaesthesia may offer a less resource-intensive alternative for the surgical treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Development and Prospective Internal-Validation Protocol of the SpinePROTECT Score: A Digital Biopsychosocial Risk Stratification Framework for Spine Surgery.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Postoperative recovery after spine surgery remains heterogeneous, and conventional perioperative risk assessment insufficiently represents psychosocial determinants. We developed the preliminary SpinePROTECT Score within a digital biopsychosocial framework intended to support structured preoperative risk stratification. Materials and Methods: Framework development integrated a structured narrative evidence review, evidence from three complementary institutional research programs, predefined candidate-predictor criteria, expert-informed preliminary weighting, and translation into a modular digital platform. The protocol defines a prospective model-development and internal-validation cohort of 300 adults undergoing elective primary or revision surgery for spinal disorders, with follow-up at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months. The study was prospectively registered in the German Clinical Trials Register on 8 September 2026 (DRKS00041544) following ethics approval on 28 August 2026 (protocol code 151/26). At prospective registration, recruitment was scheduled to begin on 10 September 2026; the present protocol article reports no prospective outcome data. Results: The development process yielded three complementary domains: psychological vulnerability, clinical burden, and procedural invasiveness. The preliminary framework includes Type-D personality, depression, anxiety, pain catastrophizing, fear-avoidance beliefs, baseline disability, symptom duration, opioid use, revision status, and surgical trauma. Digital implementation enables electronic questionnaire acquisition, automated calculation of the preliminary SpinePROTECT Score, standardized reports, longitudinal follow-up, and structured research-data capture. Predictive performance is not reported in this protocol article. Conclusions: The SpinePROTECT framework provides a transparent methodological and digital foundation for biopsychosocial risk stratification in spine surgery. The planned prospective study will estimate model coefficients and determine discrimination, calibration, internal validity, and clinical utility before the SpinePROTECT Score is considered for outcome prediction or treatment guidance.

articles.title: Intraoperative Dysglycemia in Neonates and Infants Undergoing Major Surgery: Frequency, Associated Factors and Perioperative Nutritional Management. A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Introduction: Neonates and young infants undergoing major surgery are highly vulnerable to perioperative dysglycemia due to limited metabolic reserves and high metabolic demands, yet standardized management guidelines are lacking. This study aimed to describe the proportion of patients with detected intraoperative dysglycemia and identify associated clinical factors. Methods: This retrospective observational study analysed infants aged 0 to 90 days undergoing major surgery at a single third-level centre. Dysglycemia was defined as hypoglycemia (<46 mg/dL) or hyperglycemia (>180 mg/dL). Clinical, surgical, and nutritional variables were analysed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression. Results: Among 318 infants, intraoperative dysglycemia detected under routine clinical practice occurred in 25.5% (81/318): hypoglycemia in 18.9% and hyperglycemia in 7.2%. In multivariable analysis, longer procedure duration (aOR 1.33 per additional hour; p = 0.001) and preoperative parenteral nutrition (PN; aOR 2.17; p = 0.014) were independently associated with overall dysglycemia, whereas prematurity was not. In separate models, hypoglycemia was independently associated with longer procedure duration (aOR 1.40 per hour; p < 0.001) and with the absence of preoperative enteral nutrition (aOR 0.45; p = 0.038), whereas the association with preoperative PN was attenuated and lost statistical significance after adjustment for procedure duration and preoperative enteral nutrition (aOR 1.87; p = 0.068). Hyperglycemia was independently associated only with intraoperative inotrope/vasopressor use (aOR 5.59; p = 0.008), likely reflecting illness severity.
