Among 127 infants on preoperative PN, no hypoglycemia occurred when PN was continued intraoperatively (n = 21), compared with 31.1% when it was discontinued (n = 106; p = 0.002; exploratory analysis). Conclusions: Intraoperative dysglycemia (particularly hypoglycemia) is frequent in young infants undergoing major surgery. The high observed frequency and variability in management support the need for standardized, protocol-driven perioperative glucose stewardship and the need for prospective, protocolized studies on perioperative glucose management in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Bedside Lung Ultrasound for Early Postoperative Risk Stratification for Prolonged Mechanical Ventilation After Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Objectives: Pulmonary complications remain a major determinant of postoperative morbidity following liver transplantation and frequently lead to prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). This study aimed to evaluate the value of lung ultrasound (LUS) for early postoperative risk stratification of PMV and to develop a multivariable model integrating LUS with conventional clinical variables. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 116 adults undergoing primary liver transplantation were enrolled. A standardized 12-zone LUS examination was performed within 1-3 h of ICU admission. PMV was defined as the need for mechanical ventilation for ≥24 h. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was constructed by sequentially incorporating perioperative variables and postoperative PaO2/FiO2, followed by LUS. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. Results: PMV occurred in 39.7% (n = 46) of the patients. Those requiring PMV had significantly higher early postoperative LUS scores than patients extubated within 24 h (median: 18.0 vs. 12.0, p < 0.001). LUS scores were inversely correlated with oxygenation (SpO2/FiO2 ratio, ⍴ = -0.615, p < 0.001). LUS remained independently associated with PMV (OR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.27-1.83). LUS alone demonstrated good discrimination (AUC: 0.830). After postoperative PaO2/FiO2 was included in the clinical model, incorporation of LUS significantly improved model discrimination (AUC: 0.935, 95% CI: 0.894-0.976) compared with the model without LUS (AUC: 0.862, DeLong p = 0.011). Decision curve analysis showed greater net benefit of the LUS-integrated model across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Conclusions: Early postoperative LUS is independently associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation after liver transplantation. Integration of LUS into a multivariable framework provides incremental prognostic information beyond conventional postoperative respiratory assessment and may improve early postoperative risk stratification. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Effects of Remifentanil and Dexmedetomidine on Renal Functions in a Rat Model of Crush Injury.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Crush injury frequently leads to acute kidney injury (AKI) through rhabdomyolysis, and the choice of anesthetic agent may influence renal outcomes in patients requiring surgery after such injury. This study aimed to compare the effects of remifentanil and dexmedetomidine on renal injury following crush injury using biochemical markers and histopathological examination. Materials and Methods: In this experimental study, 28 male Wistar-Albino rats were allocated to four groups (n = 7 each): Control, Sham (crush injury and surgery without drug), Dexmedetomidine, and Remifentanil. Bilateral gastrocnemius compression for two hours induced crush injury, followed by a one-hour intravenous drug infusion and simulated laparotomy. Blood samples were collected at 0, 2, and 6 h; animals were sacrificed at 6 h and kidney tissue was harvested. Serum urea, creatinine, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1), (TIMP-2) × (IGFBP7), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), and total oxidative status (TOS) were measured, and renal histopathology was evaluated. One Sham-group animal died during the experiment; the final analysis included 27 animals. Results: When all time points were evaluated together, serum creatinine and NGAL levels were significantly higher in the Remifentanil group than in the Dexmedetomidine group (although creatinine was already higher in the Remifentanil group at 2 h, before drug administration), whereas KIM-1 and (TIMP-2) × (IGFBP7) did not differ significantly between groups. The correlation between TAC and TOS was weakly positive early after injury and became weakly negative by 6 h. Histopathological analysis showed more pronounced necrosis, brush-border loss, and congestion in the Remifentanil group, whereas renal tissue preservation was more evident in the Dexmedetomidine group; these mixed biochemical results do not uniformly support a renoprotective conclusion. Conclusions: In this experimental crush injury model, dexmedetomidine was associated with more favorable early renal biochemical and histopathological findings than remifentanil, suggesting a potential renoprotective association. However, the mixed biomarker findings, small sample size, and short observation period preclude a definitive conclusion regarding direct renal protection.

articles.title: Clinical Risk Factors and Inflammatory Markers as Predictors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients Undergoing Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery.
articles.abstract: Background: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious neurological complication following acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the critical role of systemic inflammation in POD pathogenesis, this study aimed to evaluate perioperative inflammatory profiles in patients undergoing ATAAD repair and to develop a predictive nomogram for early POD risk stratification. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 355 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD. Serial inflammatory markers were assessed across multiple perioperative time points. A two-stage variable selection process, incorporating variance inflation factor (VIF) and the Boruta algorithm, was utilized to identify robust predictors. A predictive nomogram was constructed via multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results: POD occurred in 29.86% of the cohort. Patients who developed POD had higher inflammatory marker levels at several individual postoperative time points compared to the non-delirium group. The final predictive model integrated 11 key variables: age, EuroSCORE I, CPB time, SIRI_6h, PLR_6h, IL-10_6h, IL-8_6h, IL-8_pre, IL-6_6h, IL-6_pre, and PCT_6h. The nomogram demonstrated acceptable internal discrimination with an AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.794-0.876) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. Notably, IL-6_6h and PCT_6h emerged as strong independent risk factors, while SIRI_6h demonstrated an inverse association with POD. Calibration and DCA analyses confirmed the model's acceptable performance and potential clinical utility, though independent external validation remains essential prior to any clinical translation. An exploratory, web-based risk calculator was developed to facilitate bedside implementation. Conclusions: This study develops and internally validates an exploratory biomarker-based prediction model for POD in ATAAD patients. By integrating early inflammatory profiles with established clinical variables, this preliminary model provides a preliminary foundation for early risk stratification, though rigorous prospective multicenter external validation is required before real-world clinical implementation can be considered.

articles.title: 5-Aminolevulinic Acid-Guided Glioma Resection During Awake Craniotomy: Systematic Review of Functional Safety and Surgical Benefit.
articles.abstract: Background: Maximal safe resection remains the cornerstone of glioma surgery, particularly in eloquent regions where oncologic gain must be balanced against functional preservation. While 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) fluorescence-guided surgery improves extent of resection in high-grade gliomas under general anesthesia, its role during awake craniotomy (AC) remains underdeveloped. We aimed to evaluate the oncologic and functional outcomes of 5-ALA-guided tumor resection during AC. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to February 2026 for studies reporting original data on AC using 5-ALA following PRISMA guidelines. Results: Across ten studies comprising 108 patients, fluorescence positivity was 79.2% in high-grade gliomas (Grade III-IV) and 24.1% in low-grade gliomas (Grade II), among the 83 patients with both grade and fluorescence data available (grade was not reported for 19 patients in one case series, and 6 patients in one cohort study did not receive 5-ALA and were excluded from grade- and fluorescence-stratified analyses). Gross total resection was achieved in 62.2% of patients with evaluable extent-of-resection data (56.5% of the full cohort), reaching 66.7% in the largest comparative cohort. Transient aphasia occurred in 32.6% of evaluable patients, while permanent aphasia and persistent hemiparesis were observed in 14.6% and 16.9%, respectively. In multiple studies, resection was intentionally halted despite persistent fluorescence when functional mapping identified an eloquent cortex, underscoring that mapping remained the decisive determinant of surgical boundaries. No study reported conversion to general anesthesia. Conclusions: 5-ALA-guided resection during AC appears feasible and clinically useful, particularly for high-grade gliomas in eloquent regions. Permanent neurological morbidity was observed in a minority of patients, within a range broadly consistent with awake glioma surgery generally, but the absence of a non-5-ALA comparator group means that functional safety relative to awake mapping alone cannot yet be established with confidence. Across the available literature, 5-ALA consistently enhances intraoperative tumor visualization, supports identification of residual fluorescent disease, and integrates well with cortical and subcortical mapping without clear evidence of increased permanent neurological morbidity. Although functional mapping remains the decisive determinant of the final resection boundary, the available evidence supports 5-ALA as a valuable complementary adjunct in onco-functional glioma surgery.

articles.title: Nonintubated thoracic anesthesia and postoperative cough after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: A propensity score-adjusted cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the association of nonintubated thoracic anesthesia with postoperative in-hospital antitussive medication use and postoperative complications after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 223 patients who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery between January and December 2025. The exposure was nonintubated thoracic anesthesia (NITS) versus double-lumen tube intubation. The primary outcome was postoperative in-hospital antitussive medication use. Secondary outcomes included chronic cough, sore throat, hoarseness, overall postoperative complications, postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs), and antibiotic use beyond 48 h. Propensity score-based stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied.
RESULTS: After weighting, NITS was associated with lower odds of postoperative antitussive medication use (odds ratio [OR]: 0.46; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.85; P = 0.013), chronic cough (OR: 0.36; 95% CI: 0.16-0.84; P = 0.019), and hoarseness (OR: 0.27; 95% CI: 0.08-0.87; P = 0.029). NITS was also associated with lower odds of overall postoperative complications (OR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.27-0.94; P = 0.031). No significant association was observed for PPCs (OR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.49-2.19; P = 0.929).
CONCLUSION: In this propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study, NITS was associated with lower odds of postoperative in-hospital antitussive medication use, chronic cough, hoarseness, and overall postoperative complications after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery but not with PPCs. Prospective randomized studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Disentangling the Effects of Craniotomy and Traumatic Brain Injury in Experimental Models: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Many widely used open-head models of traumatic brain injury (TBI) require craniotomy before injury, while sham-operated animals undergo surgery without impact and serve as controls. However, sham surgery itself may alter physiological, molecular, and behavioral parameters, complicating interpretation of TBI-specific effects. This narrative review, based on a structured PubMed search, synthesizes studies employing a three-group design to distinguish injury-related changes from those associated with craniotomy and other perioperative procedures. Evidence indicates that sham surgery produces outcome-, region-, and time-dependent effects that are generally milder, more localized, and more transient than TBI. These include neuroinflammatory responses, localized neuronal alterations, temporary sensorimotor and cognitive deficits, nociceptive changes, and shifts in gut microbiota. In contrast, TBI causes more severe abnormalities, including extensive neuronal damage, sustained astrogliosis, microglial activation, neutrophilic infiltration, mitochondrial dysfunction, and long-term dysbiosis. Most electrophysiological parameters are relatively unaffected by sham surgery, although selected changes have been reported. Importantly, differences between naïve and sham animals cannot be attributed exclusively to craniotomy, as anesthesia, analgesia, and surgical technique may contribute. Thus, sham surgery should not be considered a biologically neutral control. Inclusion of both naïve and sham groups is particularly important when distinguishing surgery-associated from injury-specific effects in preclinical studies.

articles.title: Neurosurgical Management of Refractory Trigeminal Neuralgia in Older Adults: A Structured Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) disproportionately affects older adults, in whom medication intolerance, drug interactions, comorbidities, and limited physiological reserve may complicate management. This structured narrative review examines the evidence concerning the selection, effectiveness, durability, and complications of neurosurgical treatments for medication-refractory TN in older adults.
METHODS: PubMed was searched from database inception through 1 July 2026 using terms related to TN, older age, and neurosurgical treatment. Eligible publications evaluated microvascular decompression (MVD), radiofrequency lesioning, percutaneous balloon compression (PBC), glycerol rhizotomy, or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). Titles and abstracts were screened using predefined eligibility criteria, followed by further assessment of potentially eligible publications and standardized data extraction. Studies reporting separately extractable outcomes for defined older populations were classified as direct evidence; mixed-age studies without age-stratified outcomes were treated as indirect evidence and used primarily for procedural and comparative context.
RESULTS: The principal search identified 1324 unique records, and 22 publications were included: six provided direct older-adult evidence and 16 provided indirect contextual evidence. Direct evidence was largely limited to MVD and PBC. In selected older adults, MVD was associated with favorable and potentially durable pain outcomes, whereas PBC generally provided rapid initial pain relief. However, differences in outcome definitions, assessment times, follow-up, and patient selection precluded direct comparison. No included study provided separately extractable outcomes for adults aged ≥65 years undergoing radiofrequency lesioning, glycerol rhizotomy, or SRS. GRADE certainty was low or very low for most procedure-specific and comparative conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: Favorable observational outcomes in selected older patients suggest that chronological age alone should not automatically exclude an otherwise appropriate patient from consideration for MVD. Treatment should be individualized according to TN subtype, physiological reserve, comorbidity and anesthetic risk, imaging findings, pain urgency, previous interventions, baseline facial sensation, and patient preferences.

articles.title: Impact of Hepatic Artery Diameter on Immediate Postoperative Graft Function and Hemodynamic Profiles in Living-Donor Liver Transplantation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Reconstruction of small-caliber hepatic arteries (HAs) in living-donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is technically challenging. We evaluated clinical and hemodynamic outcomes according to intraoperative HA diameter in a retrospective single-center cohort of 49 patients who underwent LDLT between 2017 and 2026. Materials and Methods: Patients were stratified into Group 1 (≤2.0 mm, n = 28), Group 2 (2.5 mm, n = 6), and Group 3 (≥3.0 mm, n = 15). Perioperative variables, laboratory markers of graft function for 14 days, and Doppler hemodynamic parameters for 7 days were analyzed using linear mixed models; HA diameter was also analyzed as a continuous variable, with adjustment for graft-to-recipient weight ratio and MELD-Na score. Results: Baseline and surgical variables did not differ significantly, and neither group nor group × time effects were significant for any outcome. Per 1-mm increase in diameter, AST and ALT ratios were 1.01 (95% CI 0.83-1.23) and 1.06 (0.79-1.42). Early allograft dysfunction occurred in 5 patients (indeterminate in 3). No hepatic artery thrombosis, arterial re-intervention, retransplantation or 90-day death was documented; 14 patients (28.6%) required biliary intervention. Conclusions: In this small cohort, a smaller donor HA diameter was not associated with worse early biochemical or Doppler trajectories, but the estimates were imprecise and cannot establish equivalence or vascular safety.

articles.title: From virtual reality to artificial intelligence-driven digital humans in perioperative lung cancer care: An updated scoping review and translational framework for pulmonary rehabilitation.
articles.abstract: Digital pulmonary rehabilitation may improve access and continuity around lung cancer surgery, but virtual reality, scripted avatars, connected applications, and artificial intelligence (ai)-driven digital humans are frequently conflated. we conducted an updated scoping synthesis using a two-stage architecture: an inherited systematic review corpus searched through January 1, 2024, and a targeted PubMed/citation update from January 2, 2024, to August 31, 2026. Direct clinical studies were classified by operational Level 1-3 criteria. Risk of bias (RoB) was appraised with RoB 2 or ROBINS-I where feasible; implementation findings were mapped to Nonadoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread, and Sustainability while separating reported barriers from framework-derived concerns. The direct map contained 19 completed reports and one protocol: 5 Level 1 fixed-display/immersive interventions, 14 Level 2 deterministic connected systems, no completed Level 3 digital human trials, and one Level 2/3 protocol candidate. In the inherited meta-analysis, digital rehabilitation was associated with fewer postoperative pulmonary complications (risk ratio: 0.45, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.30-0.66) and shorter chest tube duration (-1.53 days), whereas postoperative length of stay was not significantly reduced (-1.42 days, 95% CI: -3.45 to 0.62). Updated studies reported heterogeneous functional and workflow benefits, but no direct evidence validated Level 3 outcome superiority. Current evidence supports digitally delivered rehabilitation, not AI-driven digital humans. The proposed taxonomy converts this evidence gap into testable design requirements. Future trials should prioritize head-to-head comparisons, standardized outcomes, AI safety and external validation, geriatric accessibility, interoperability, health economics, and sustained real-world implementation.

articles.title: Peripheral nerve blocks reduce opioid requirements in the first 24 h following surgical fixation of acute tibial shaft fractures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of peripheral nerve blocks (PNB) on postoperative opioid use, length of stay (LOS), and incidence of acute compartment syndrome (ACS) in patients presenting with acute tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nail (IMN) fixation.
METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study Setting: Level 1 Academic Trauma Center from 2018 to 2022. Patient Selection Criteria: Patients aged 18-79 years with acute AO/OTA 42A-C tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN within 7 days of injury Outcome Measures and Comparisons: The primary outcome was postoperative opioid use, measured in morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during hospital stay, up to a maximum of 72 h after surgery. Patients who received a preoperative PNB were compared to those who did not receive a block. Secondary outcomes included postoperative LOS and incidence of ACS.
RESULTS: 246 patients were eligible for analysis of which 78 (32%) received a PNB (PNB=yes) and 168 (68%) did not (PNB=no). Mean MME were significantly lower in the PNB=yes group compared to the PNB=no group at 24 h (73 vs. 138, p < 0.001). Controlling for age, Injury Severity Score (ISS), and time to surgery, a multivariable regression model demonstrated a 36% reduction in MME per hour for patients that received PNBs. There were 3 cases of ACS in PNB=No and 1 in PNB=Yes. All 3 patients without a PNB were diagnosed within 2 days of surgery and underwent uncomplicated fasciotomies. One patient with a PNB re-presented to the hospital 5 days postoperatively, underwent fasciotomies, and was found to have anterior and lateral compartment necrosis.
CONCLUSION: PNBs for select acute tibial shaft fractures treated with IMN were associated with decreased opioid requirements in the first 24 h after surgery. No effect was noted beyond 24 h after surgery. Extreme vigilance is essential in patients with tibia fractures to monitor for ACS, especially when PNB is utilized.

articles.title: Association Between Chronic Tamsulosin Therapy and Intraoperative Hemodynamics During Spinal Anesthesia: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background: This prospective observational study investigated the association between chronic tamsulosin therapy and intraoperative hemodynamic changes in patients undergoing elective transurethral resection of the prostate (TUR-P) under spinal anesthesia. Methods: Adult patients scheduled for elective TUR-P under spinal anesthesia were prospectively enrolled. Patients receiving long-term tamsulosin therapy comprised the tamsulosin group, whereas those with no history of α1-adrenergic blocker use served as the control group. Hemodynamic variables, including mean arterial pressure (MAP) and heart rate, were recorded before spinal anesthesia and at predefined time points during the first 60 min after spinal anesthesia. Results: A total of 115 patients were analyzed (tamsulosin, n = 56; control, n = 59). Baseline MAP was comparable between groups. The adjusted linear mixed-effects model demonstrated a significant group × time interaction for MAP (F(5, 565.10) = 8.34, p < 0.001). Adjusted between-group MAP differences were -4.9 mmHg (95% CI, -8.8 to -1.0; p = 0.015) at 5 min, -17.0 mmHg (95% CI, -20.2 to -13.8; p < 0.001) at 30 min, and -16.4 mmHg (95% CI, -19.5 to -13.3; p < 0.001) at 60 min. Criteria-defined hypotension occurred in 21/56 (37.5%) patients in the tamsulosin group and 17/59 (28.8%) in the control group (p = 0.32). Conclusions: Chronic tamsulosin therapy was associated with lower intraoperative MAP values during spinal anesthesia, without a statistically significant increase in the incidence of clinically defined hypotension. These findings suggest that chronic tamsulosin use may be associated with a different intraoperative blood pressure response following spinal anesthesia.

articles.title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygenation Is Associated with Improved Respiratory Stability During Moderate Multimodal Analgosedation for Pars Plana Vitrectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: High-flow nasal oxygenation (HFNO) may improve respiratory stability during procedural sedation, but treatment-associated differences across patient risk categories remain uncertain. We compared HFNO with low-flow nasal oxygenation (LFNO) during moderate multimodal analgosedation (MMAS) for pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in patients with ASA physical status I-III. Methods: In this prospective, single-center randomized trial, 164 adults undergoing elective PPV under regional eye anesthesia with MMAS were randomized to HFNO (40 L·min-1, set FiO2 0.40) or LFNO (5 L·min-1, intended to approximate a nominal FiO2 of 0.40). Sedation depth was monitored using the Patient State Index and evaluated using the Ramsay Sedation Scale. The primary outcome was maintenance of target oxygenation (SpO2 94-98%) without hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%), assessed by peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) at three predefined time points (T0, T1, and T2). Secondary outcomes included breathing frequency (BF), measured end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2), and clinically significant bradypnea (CSB), defined as ≥1 bradypnea episode (BF < 12 breaths·min-1 persisting ≥1 min) accompanied by SpO2 90-93%, EtCO2 > 45 mmHg, or both. Results: The primary outcome showed no between-group difference. No hypoxemia (SpO2 < 90%) occurred. Oxygenation below the target range (SpO2 90-93%) was less frequent with HFNO peri-procedurally (adjusted RR, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.03-0.56; p = 0.006) and post-procedurally (adjusted RR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.04-0.64; p = 0.010). Significant treatment × ASA interactions were observed for BF and measured EtCO2 peri-procedurally. In exploratory ASA-stratified analyses, ASA III patients receiving HFNO had higher BF, fewer CSB episodes, and lower measured EtCO2 than those receiving LFNO. Conclusions: HFNO was associated with improved respiratory stability compared with LFNO, with treatment-associated differences varying across ASA strata.

articles.title: Postoperative Delirium After OLIF-PPSF Versus TLIF: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis over 16 Years.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Postoperative delirium is a clinically important complication after lumbar fusion surgery, yet whether the choice of fusion technique influences its occurrence remains unclear. We compared the incidence of postoperative delirium between oblique lateral interbody fusion with percutaneous pedicle screw fixation (OLIF-PPSF) and transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF). Methods: The medical records of 850 patients (335 OLIF-PPSF, 515 TLIF) treated between 2008 and 2023 were retrospectively reviewed; 487 patients were eligible, and propensity score matching yielded 141 matched pairs. Delirium was identified through symptom-triggered psychiatric consultation rather than routine screening. Analyses were stratified by treatment era and repeated within the period in which both procedures were performed. Results: Delirium occurred in no OLIF-PPSF patient and in 9 TLIF patients (6.4%; risk difference 6.4%, 95% CI 2.4-11.7%; McNemar exact p = 0.004; adjusted odds ratio 19.82, 95% CI 1.20-326.53). However, OLIF-PPSF was performed only from 2017 onward, whereas 118 of the 141 matched TLIF operations (83.7%) preceded 2017, and all events occurred during 2008-2014. Within 2017-2023 no delirium occurred after either procedure (0/168 versus 0/34). Conclusions: Although delirium was less frequent after OLIF-PPSF, every event preceded its introduction, and none occurred after either procedure once both were performed contemporaneously. The difference cannot be attributed to the surgical approach and more likely reflects changes in perioperative care over time. These findings are exploratory.

articles.title: Routine Pringle Maneuver During Recipient Hepatectomy Is Associated with Improved Perioperative and Early Graft Outcomes After Adult Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Background: Recipient hepatectomy during orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) is frequently complicated by severe bleeding due to portal hypertension and collateral circulation. The Pringle maneuver's benefit in this setting remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed data from 141 adults who underwent primary deceased-donor OLT at a single center between January 2020 and June 2026. A routine intermittent Pringle maneuver was introduced in 2023; 79 subsequent recipients comprised the Pringle group, while 62 earlier recipients served as historical controls. Multivariable regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to address confounding, and temporal trends within each period were examined. Results: Indication for transplantation, markers of hepatic decompensation, and extended-criteria donor status did not differ between groups. Compared with controls, the Pringle group required fewer packed red blood cell units (median 2 {IQR 0-4} vs. 3 {1-5}; p = 0.046), fresh frozen plasma units (4 {0-6} vs. 4 {3-8}; mean 4.1 vs. 6.9; no plasma transfused in 30.8% vs. 13.6%; p = 0.005), and total blood products (5 {0-9} vs. 8 {4-14}; p = 0.009). Recipient hepatectomy was shorter (129 {105-165} vs. 177 {146-208} minutes; p < 0.001), and postoperative bleeding (2.5% vs. 22.6%; p < 0.001), biliary leak (2.5% vs. 11.3%; p = 0.043), and early allograft dysfunction (EAD; 6.3% vs. 29.0%; p < 0.001) were less frequent. After adjustment, the Pringle maneuver remained associated with shorter hepatectomy (time ratio 0.76; 95% CI 0.67-0.87), reduced fresh frozen plasma (IRR 0.60; 0.40-0.91) and total blood product use (IRR 0.61; 0.40-0.92), and lower odds of postoperative bleeding (OR 0.04; 0.01-0.25), biliary leak (OR 0.13; 0.02-0.63), and EAD (OR 0.14; 0.04-0.58). Packed red blood cell transfusion was nonsignificant after adjustment (IRR 0.70; 0.43-1.12). IPTW yielded consistent findings. Overall survival did not differ (p = 0.885). Conclusions: In this historical-control study, routine intermittent Pringle maneuver was associated with improved operative efficiency, lower transfusion requirements, and fewer early complications without affecting survival; given the retrospective design and the modest absolute differences in transfusion, these findings require prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Pre-Transplant Laboratory Parameters and Early Outcomes in HBV-Related Deceased Donor Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Background: Early postoperative outcomes after deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) are influenced by recipient, donor, and perioperative factors. Routinely available pre-transplant laboratory tests may provide complementary information for risk assessment. This study aimed to explore associations between routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters and early postoperative outcomes after DDLT. Methods: This retrospective single-center descriptive pilot study included 32 adult recipients who underwent DDLT for hepatitis B virus-related liver disease between 2004 and 2019. Pre-transplant biochemical and hematologic parameters were evaluated in relation to in-hospital mortality, biliary complications, infectious complications, bleeding, and hospital stay. Descriptive group comparisons and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: In-hospital mortality occurred in 6/32 recipients (18.8%), biliary complications in 5/32 (15.6%), infectious complications in 9/32 (28.1%), and postoperative bleeding in 2/32 (6.2%). Routine laboratory parameters did not significantly discriminate mortality. Among 28 recipients with available potassium measurements, four developed biliary complications. Potassium showed exploratory discrimination for biliary complications (AUC = 0.818, p = 0.048), based on only four biliary events. Bilirubin and GGT did not significantly discriminate mortality. Conclusions: Routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters showed no consistent association with in-hospital mortality after DDLT. The potassium association is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

articles.title: Predictive Models of Morbidity and Mortality in Gynaecological Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gynaecological-oncological surgery involves substantial perioperative morbidity and mortality risks. Reliable preoperative risk stratification could inform consent, shared decision-making and perioperative optimisation. Several prediction models exist, but their performance and methodological quality in this population remain uncertain. We aimed to provide a comprehensive synthesis of existing evidence to guide the selection and development of prediction tools in this population. Methods: We searched MEDLINE and EMBASE using a prospective protocol (PROSPERO CRD420251179495) and included studies developing or validating multivariable prediction models or risk scores for graded postoperative morbidity/mortality after gynaecological-oncological surgery. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) at the study (publication) level. Findings were synthesised narratively. Results: Twenty-eight studies (75,999 patient records, including overlapping cohorts) were included (23 retrospective, five prospective; sample sizes 100-21,359). Models were multifactorial (n = 17), including generic and gynaecological-oncological-specific tools, frailty-based (n = 8) models or biomarker and index-based (n = 3) models. A numerical c-statistic was reported in 20 studies (binary c-statistics 0.50-0.92 across heterogeneous outcome definitions), calibration was reported in nine studies, and internal validation was reported in thirteen. No frailty-based model reported calibration or validation. One model specific to ovarian cytoreductive surgery was independently externally validated, retaining discrimination (c-index 0.715) with reduced calibration. Generic tools performed poorly, (c-statistics ranged from 0.529-0.644). Twenty studies were at high risk of bias, predominantly within the analysis domain. Conclusions: Existing models show, at best, moderate discrimination, limited calibration and infrequent external validation within the gynaecological-oncological surgical population. No model can currently be recommended for routine clinical practice. Further independent external validation of specialty-specific models in local settings, with full calibration reporting, is needed to support preoperative counselling.

articles.title: Rapidly Reversible Monitored Anesthesia Care with Remimazolam and Flumazenil Reversal for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) is increasingly used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), where rapid recovery of consciousness may facilitate early postoperative neurological assessment. Remimazolam provides sedation that can be pharmacologically reversed with flumazenil. We compared emergence from sedation between a remimazolam-flumazenil-based MAC strategy and a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy in patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR. Methods: In this single-center randomized controlled trial, 84 patients undergoing transfemoral TAVR were randomized 1:1 to remimazolam-remifentanil (R group) or dexmedetomidine-propofol-remifentanil (D group) MAC. Flumazenil was administered at the initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt in the R group. The primary outcome was arousal time, assessed using two prespecified measures: time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal and time from initiation of the postoperative awakening attempt to arousal. Arousal was defined as a Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation score of 5. Results: Eighty-three patients were included in the analysis (R group, n = 42; D group, n = 41). The time from discontinuation of all anesthetic infusions to arousal was shorter in the R group than in the D group (19.05 [15.77-23.59] vs. 24.09 [19.25-34.78] min; p = 0.0045). The time from initiation of the awakening attempt to arousal was also shorter (0.60 [0.33-1.00] vs. 1.00 [0-4.72] min; p = 0.0117). No patient in the R group required rescue propofol. No significant between-group differences were observed in major procedural or postoperative outcomes. Conclusions: A remimazolam-based MAC strategy with flumazenil reversal provided faster and more reliable emergence from sedation than a conventional dexmedetomidine-based strategy during transfemoral TAVR. These findings suggest that a reversible sedation strategy may facilitate rapid recovery of consciousness when early postoperative assessment is desired, although its impact on neurological or other clinical outcomes remains to be established.

articles.title: A Facet-Associated Cyst with Aneurysmal Bone Cyst Morphology Causing T10-T11 Compressive Myelopathy Mimicking Cauda Equina Syndrome in an Octogenarian.
articles.abstract: Aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs) are benign, locally aggressive osseous lesions that predominantly affect children and young adults; ABC morphology in a facet-associated cystic lesion in an octogenarian is highly unusual and may overlap radiologically with a degenerative facet or synovial cyst. An 81-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of progressive bilateral lower-limb weakness, sensory disturbance, and gait deterioration, followed by acute saddle anaesthesia and bowel dysfunction, prompting concern for cauda equina syndrome. Examination showed bilateral MRC 3/5 weakness, mildly increased lower-limb tone, brisk reflexes, and bilateral Hoffmann signs. Lumbar MRI did not demonstrate cauda equina compression. Dedicated thoracic MRI revealed severe multifactorial T10-T11 canal stenosis with marked cord compression, together with a small right posterolateral extradural lesion adjacent to the facet/posterior elements. Posterior T10-T11 decompression, including laminectomy and flavectomy, with excision of the cystic lesion resulted in neurological improvement. Histopathology demonstrated blood-filled cystic spaces separated by fibrovascular septa containing osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and reactive bone, without malignant features, consistent with ABC morphology. This case emphasizes careful neurological localization when cauda equina-like symptoms coexist with upper motor neuron signs and highlights an unusual facet-associated cystic lesion with ABC morphology contributing to multifactorial thoracic spinal stenosis in an elderly patient.

articles.title: Viscoelastic Testing for Hemostatic Assessment in Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: End-stage liver disease leads to a unique coagulation profile. This rebalanced coagulation status is characterized by the propensity to bleed easily and form clots in blood vessels. Managing these patients requires close monitoring and an understanding of the underlying pathophysiology. Decreased production of coagulation factors by the liver and splenic sequestration of platelets lead to conditions favoring a hypocoagulable picture. Increased levels of factor VIII and von Willebrand factor along with decreased production of anticlotting factors lead to an environment favoring thrombosis. Viscoelastic testing allows clinicians to navigate this challenging coagulation scenario and preserve the delicate balance. Methods: We review recent technological advancements in coagulation monitoring during liver transplantation. Viscoelastic testing has been used and validated in liver transplantation initially using mechanical methods for assessing clot formation and strength, but newer viscoelastic testing platforms are transitioning toward resonance-based technologies and cartridge-based point-of-care devices that allow for faster assessment of coagulopathies. Development of faster point-of-care devices is beneficial for liver transplantation given acute coagulopathies that can occur throughout phases of the case. Results/Conclusions: This paper will discuss briefly transfusion thresholds; how the SEER-based Quantra, resonance-based TEG 6s, and automated cartridge-based ROTEM SIGMA work; gaps using conventional coagulation testing; and the integration of these systems into perioperative decision making to support goal-directed transfusion strategies.

articles.title: Rethinking Postoperative Pain in the Era of Robotic Thoracic Surgery: A Surgeon's Perspective on Functional Recovery and Potential Oncologic Implications.
articles.abstract: Persistent postoperative pain remains an incompletely resolved problem after minimally invasive thoracic surgery, despite expectations that robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS) would meaningfully outperform video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) in analgesia. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from randomized trials, cohort studies, and meta-analyses comparing acute and chronic pain outcomes between VATS and RATS, examines mechanisms and surgically modifiable risk factors underlying intercostal nerve injury and pain chronification, and evaluates the emerging concept of Return to Intended Oncologic Treatment (RIOT) as a perioperative endpoint linking pain control to oncologic recovery. Across randomized and propensity-matched comparisons, RATS has generally failed to demonstrate superior pain outcomes relative to VATS, and several studies suggest multiport robotic platforms may produce greater early pain than uniportal thoracoscopic approaches. Port number, operative time, and drainage duration emerge as modifiable surgical predictors of chronic pain, while inadequately controlled acute pain compromises functional recovery and is associated with delayed RIOT; direct evidence that pain independently influences RIOT or long-term survival remains limited, and this link should currently be regarded as a plausible, testable hypothesis rather than an established causal pathway. We conclude that, on the comparative evidence available to date, robotic instrumentation has not shown a consistent, clinically meaningful reduction in pain burden relative to VATS, and that pain management should be reframed as a shared surgical-anesthetic target relevant to oncologic recovery rather than a comfort-oriented endpoint alone. Emerging robotic platforms warrant evaluation against this expanded outcome set.

articles.title: Independent correlates of vancomycin steady-state trough concentration among patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery: observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) combined with valve surgery represent a high-risk surgical population with substantial perioperative hemodynamic disturbances and highly variable organ function, leading to high variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetics. Conventional vancomycin dosing solely on renal function frequently fails to achieve target trough concentrations in this complex subgroup. This study aimed to identify independent correlates c of vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations (Css-min), and to report observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, to inform individualized therapeutic drug monitoring.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery from January 2018 to October 2024. Clinical data and vancomycin TDM records were extracted from electronic medical records. Vancomycin Css-min was detected by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay technique. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) accounting for within-patient repeated TDM measurements were used to identify clinical correlates of Css-min. IABP support was pre-specified and force-entered into the multivariable model based on clinical observations and pathophysiological reasoning, independent of univariate screening results. We performed a sensitivity analysis for patients with at least one TDM within postoperative day 7, prespecified interaction tests for effect modification, and binary logistic-GEE for the supratherapeutic endpoint (Css-min > 20 mg/L). A two-tailed P < 0.05 was set as statistical significance.
RESULTS: A total of 283 eligible patients with 473 valid Css-min measurements were included. Multivariate GEE demonstrated that categorical vancomycin dosing regimen, age, ventilator dependence ≥96 h, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), IABP support, serum creatinine (Scr), and serum urea nitrogen (SUN) were positively associated with higher geometric-mean Css-min. Associations remained largely consistent in the sensitivity-analysis subgroup of patients with at least one early-phase TDM within postoperative day 7. A significant CRRT-by-postoperative-time interaction was detected, indicating that the influence of CRRT on vancomycin exposure varied across different postoperative phases. Of note, the association signal linking IABP to supratherapeutic trough concentrations (Css-min>20 mg/L) was modest and requires cautious interpretation.
CONCLUSION: Multiple clinical factors jointly affect vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations in patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery, including dosing regimen, age, renal biomarkers, and critical-care supportive interventions such as IABP, CRRT and prolonged mechanical ventilation. IABP support represents an intriguing observational signal; this finding remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation before it can guide formal dose-adjustment strategies. Individualized vancomycin management for this population should comprehensively integrate hemodynamic support measures and laboratory indices rather than depend merely on renal-function markers. This study focuses on clinically accessible trough concentration monitoring rather than constructing complex pharmacokinetic models, which is more in line with real-world clinical practice.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559).
CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

articles.title: Immunometabolic crosstalk between dysfunctional adipose tissue and the brain: implications for postoperative cognitive dysfunction in obesity.
articles.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is an important complication after surgery, particularly in patients with pre-existing metabolic and inflammatory vulnerability. Obesity may increase susceptibility to postoperative cognitive decline, but its independent association with POCD and the underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. This review critically examines a proposed adipose-immune-brain pathway linking obesity-associated adipose dysfunction to perioperative neurocognitive outcomes. In obesity, adipocyte hypertrophy, hypoxia, fibrosis, macrophage accumulation, T-cell imbalance, and activation of inflammasome and innate immune signaling pathways promote chronic low-grade inflammation and altered endocrine function. The resulting changes in cytokines, adipokines, free fatty acids, lipid mediators, insulin sensitivity, and glucose and lipid metabolism may establish a systemically primed immunometabolic state. Surgical trauma may then act as a second inflammatory hit, amplifying peripheral immune activation and promoting blood-brain barrier dysfunction, glial activation, oxidative stress, and impaired neuronal function. However, direct clinical evidence linking adipose tissue inflammation to POCD remains limited; current support is derived largely from preclinical studies, indirect biomarker associations, and heterogeneous clinical studies that sometimes combine postoperative delirium with longer-term cognitive outcomes. Accordingly, the adipose-immune-brain axis should be regarded as a biologically plausible framework rather than an established causal pathway. Better phenotyping of visceral adiposity and metabolic dysfunction, standardized neurocognitive outcomes, and integrated assessment of adipose, circulating, and blood-brain barrier biomarkers are needed. Potential interventions include weight and metabolic optimization, incretin-based therapies, modulation of inflammatory and pro-resolving pathways, and perioperative physiological management, although their efficacy for preventing POCD remains to be established.

articles.title: Procedural interventions for chronic migraine: an umbrella review intervention-specific evidence map.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize and map intervention-specific evidence on the efficacy, clinical relevance, and safety of procedural interventions for chronic migraine (CM).
METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered umbrella review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and methodological guidance for umbrella reviews. Eligible systematic reviews evaluated onabotulinumtoxinA, greater occipital nerve block (GONB), other peripheral nerve blocks and percutaneous procedures, acupuncture, implanted occipital nerve stimulation (ONS), or surgical interventions. Evidence concerning the addition of CGRP-targeted monoclonal antibody therapy to ongoing onabotulinumtoxinA treatment was retained separately as contextual evidence on adjunctive pharmacotherapy and was not classified as a procedural intervention. Methodological quality was assessed using A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and primary-study overlap using the corrected covered area (CCA). Evidence was synthesized separately by intervention, outcome, comparator, and follow-up period. Pooled estimates from different systematic reviews were not statistically combined, and clinically heterogeneous evidence was summarized narratively.
RESULTS: Seventeen reviews were included, of which 12 contained at least one meta-analysis. The strength and maturity of evidence varied substantially across interventions. OnabotulinumtoxinA had the most established evidence base and the clearest role in CM prevention. For GONB, low-certainty evidence from clinically comparable randomized trials suggested a possible short-term reduction in headache day and headache severity, although sustained benefit remains uncertain. Evidence for combined onabotulinumtoxinA-CGRP monoclonal antibody therapy was derived predominantly from uncontrolled observational cohorts and should therefore be considered preliminary. Implanted ONS showed possible benefit in selected patients with refractory CM, but evidence was limited by small study numbers, imprecision, heterogeneous outcomes, and device- or procedure-related risks. Evidence for acupuncture, other peripheral nerve blocks, percutaneous procedures, and surgical interventions was limited by clinical heterogeneity, indirectness, uncontrolled study designs, or uncertain applicability specifically to CM. TRAEs profiles differed substantially among intervention categories and were therefore not pooled across procedures. Most intervention-outcome evidence was rated as low or very low certainty.
CONCLUSIONS: Procedural interventions for CM should not be interpreted as a homogeneous therapeutic class. OnabotulinumtoxinA is supported by the most mature evidence and established clinical positioning, whereas GONB may provide a short-term, protocol-specific benefit with low certainty. Evidence for other procedures remains preliminary, heterogeneous, or restricted to selected patient populations. Clinical interpretation and treatment selection should therefore be intervention-specific and patient-specific. Future research should prioritize standardized diagnostic criteria, treatment protocols, comparators, clinically meaningful outcomes, TRAEs reporting, and longer-term follow-up. Systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261415558, identifier: CRD420261415558.

articles.title: Predicting spinal hypotension during cesarean delivery: what is being predicted, and when.
articles.abstract: Spinal hypotension during cesarean delivery has generated a large prediction literature, but the term "prediction" is applied to signals obtained at very different points in the peri-spinal course. Most reviews group predictors by physiology or device. Here we organize them by when the signal becomes available and which clinical decision remains open. This changes how reported performance should be interpreted. A preoperative low-frequency/high-frequency heart rate variability threshold of 2.5, for example, showed only 35% sensitivity and discrimination around 0.60 in an independent cohort, whereas small development studies of other preoperative tools have reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve approaching 0.9. Pre-spinal provocation may improve discrimination while preserving time to adjust prophylaxis. Measurements obtained after intrathecal injection, and real-time algorithms operating minutes before hypotension, answer a different question because sympathetic blockade is already evolving and the decision window is narrower. Variation in hypotension definitions, treatment background, case mix, and small development samples further limits direct comparison. Routine vasopressor prophylaxis also changes what a useful predictor should do: rather than decide who receives prevention, it should help identify who needs earlier, stronger, or differently titrated treatment. Two randomized cesarean trials now support Hypotension Prediction Index-guided management, while treatment-impact evidence for true preoperative prediction remains limited.

articles.title: Prophylactic Carbetocin Versus Oxytocin and Blood Loss After Vaginal Delivery: Agent Selection and Confounding by Indication in a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Carbetocin is increasingly used for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) prophylaxis, but its selection in routine practice may bias comparisons with oxytocin. This observational study examined the association between the agent received and blood loss after vaginal delivery. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cohort included 559 women delivering vaginally in 2022-2023 who received carbetocin 100 μg intravenously (n = 474) or oxytocin 10 IU by infusion (n = 85). Gravimetric blood loss was analyzed using linear (primary), robust and median (co-primary) regression, and propensity score methods. Results: Carbetocin recipients more often underwent induction (63.3% vs. 43.5%), vacuum extraction (26.8% vs. 15.3%), and epidural analgesia (76.2% vs. 29.4%). Blood loss was higher with carbetocin before adjustment (223.7 vs. 180.0 mL, p = 0.003) but not after adjustment (β 12.72 mL, 95% CI -50.19 to 75.64, p = 0.691; robust p = 0.479; median p = 0.354). Propensity score results conflicted: inverse probability weighting showed higher blood loss with carbetocin (47.84 mL, p = 0.002), whereas matching and trimmed weighting did not. PPH occurred in 2.7% vs. 0% (p = 0.234). Conclusions: Carbetocin was preferentially used in higher-risk labors, indicating confounding by indication. Adjusted blood loss did not differ significantly, although a modest increase could not be excluded. The study was severely underpowered for PPH.

articles.title: Effects of isobaric spinal anesthesia combined with different nerve block techniques on postoperative pain and complications in elderly patients undergoing proximal femoral nail antirotation: a retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the impacts of isobaric spinal anesthesia combined with different nerve blocks on postoperative pain, complications, satisfaction and perioperative comfort in elderly patients undergoing proximal femoral nail antirotation(PFNA).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on elderly PFNA patients enrolled from 2019 to 2021 in the Department of Traumatic Orthopedics at the People's Hospital of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Patients were divided into four groups: group S(simple isobaric spinal anesthesia), group S + FNB(spinal anesthesia plus femoral nerve block), group S + LFCN(spinal anesthesia plus lateral femoral cutaneous nerve block), group S + FICB(spinal anesthesia plus fascia iliaca compartment block). Primary outcomes were dynamic VAS scores at different postoperative time points, while secondary outcomes comprised postoperative complications and pain management indicators. All data were collected and statistically compared.
RESULTS: A total of 191 elderly patients who underwent PFNA met the inclusion criteria. In group S, VAS scores on postoperative days 2 and 3 were lower than those at 1 day preoperatively, whereas in groups S + FNB, S + LFCN, and S + FICB, VAS scores on postoperative days 1, 2, and 3 were lower than preoperative values. In all four groups, VAS scores on postoperative days 2 and 3 were lower than those on postoperative day 1 (P < 0.05). On postoperative day 1, VAS scores in groups S + FNB and S + LFCN were lower than those in group S, while VAS scores in group S + FICB were significantly lower than those in groups S + FNB, S + LFCN, and S on postoperative days 1, 2, and 3 (P < 0.05). The incidence of postoperative nausea, vomiting, and pruritus was lower in group S + FICB than in group S (P < 0.05). The dose of sufentanil required for rescue analgesia was lower in groups S + LFCN and S + FICB than in group S, and lower in group S + FICB than in groups S + FNB and S + LFCN (P < 0.05). The number of patients requiring postoperative rescue analgesia was lower in group S + FICB than in groups S + FNB, S + LFCN, and S (P < 0.05). Postoperative satisfaction was higher in group S + FICB than in group S (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative isobaric spinal anesthesia combined with fascia iliaca compartment block was associated with better postoperative pain relief, reduced adverse reactions, and improved perioperative comfort in elderly patients, and was more effective than other anesthesia strategies.

articles.title: Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy with Intracorporeal Urinary Diversion: Perioperative Management and Operative Technique.
articles.abstract: Radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy and urinary diversion remains the standard of care for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and selected high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease. The procedure carries substantial morbidity, in part because the typical patient is elderly and burdened by cardiorespiratory comorbidity. Robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC) was developed to attenuate this morbidity, and RARC with intracorporeal urinary diversion (iRARC) avoids the laparotomy that earlier randomized trials required for extracorporeal reconstruction. In this technical narrative review, we present a single-institution operative approach to iRARC, distinguishing institutional practice from evidence-based recommendations. We describe patient selection, preoperative optimization and enhanced recovery, and provide a step-by-step account of our operative technique for male and female radical cystectomy, pelvic lymph node dissection template, and totally intracorporeal ileal conduit and orthotopic neobladder reconstruction. We also summarize the perioperative, oncological, and functional outcomes of iRARC, which support its role as a safe option with specific perioperative advantages in experienced, high-volume centers.

articles.title: D-Dimer as a Novel Factor for Recurrent Chronic Subdural Hematoma: Development and Assessment of a New Predictive Nomogram.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is the most common bleeding disorder in the nervous system and has a high recurrence rate, posing a serious threat to the lives of elderly individuals. Early identification and adjustment of the treatment regimen in the perioperative period is crucial. The aim of this study was to create a perioperative predictive nomogram for the early prediction of recurrent CSDH (R-CSDH).
METHODS: A predictive model was developed including 632 patients with CSDH hospitalized between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2025 from Wuhan University People's Hospital. The 206 patients from the First People's Hospital of Xiantao City who were hospitalized between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2025 formed an external validation cohort. Minimum absolute shrinkage was used to optimize feature selection, and logistic regression analysis was applied to further select features and construct a risk prediction model for recurrent CSDH. The calibration, discrimination, and clinical utility of the predictive models were assessed using calibration plots, the C-index, the area under the curve (AUC), and decision curve analysis. External validation was performed by an external validation cohort.
FINDINGS: Age, CT hematoma size, hematoma location, atrophy, density, surgical procedure and D-dimer were the predictors for constructing the predictive nomogram, and the results showed that a logistic regression model based on the above seven factors had good calibration and discriminative ability (C-index: 0.925; 95% confidence interval: 0.893-0.957). The AUC of this predictive model was 0.92487. The calibration curve of the nomogram was close to the ideal diagonal. In addition, the decision curve analysis showed that the net benefit of the model was significantly better. External validation demonstrated the reliability of the predictive nomogram.
INTERPRETATION: D-dimer was found to be a novel factor for recurrent chronic subdural hematoma. Our study provides clinicians with an accurate tool for identification and early intervention and therapy to reduce the incidence of R-CSDH.

articles.title: P2Y12 inhibition, adenosine signaling, and bone remodeling: differential skeletal pharmacology of antiplatelet agents.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, and fragility fractures frequently coexist in older adults, creating an important overlap between antiplatelet therapy and orthopedic care. This narrative review examines mechanistic, preclinical, observational, and perioperative evidence concerning the skeletal effects of aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors, and other clinically relevant antiplatelet agents. Purinergic signaling provides biological plausibility for interactions between platelet inhibition and bone remodeling because P2Y12, P2Y1, P2X7, adenosine receptors, and equilibrative nucleoside transporter 1 (ENT1) regulate osteoblast differentiation, osteoclast activity, inflammatory responses, and tissue repair. Aspirin shows dose- and context-dependent skeletal effects, whereas clopidogrel has been associated with impaired osteoblast mineralization in preclinical studies and conflicting fracture-risk estimates in observational cohorts. Direct skeletal evidence for prasugrel and other agents remains limited. Selected preclinical studies suggest that ticagrelor-associated ENT1 inhibition can enhance adenosine-dependent osteogenic signaling; however, clinical evidence is limited to one retrospective cohort in which ticagrelor-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was associated with lower fracture risk than clopidogrel-based DAPT, while prospective skeletal outcome data are lacking. Perioperative antiplatelet management in orthopedic surgery should remain guided by cardiovascular indications, thrombotic risk, and bleeding risk. A conceptual framework may help define priorities for evaluating skeletal outcomes during antiplatelet therapy. However, current evidence is insufficient to support antiplatelet selection or switching on the basis of presumed skeletal effects.

articles.title: Camk2d upregulation is associated with postoperative cognitive dysfunction in aged rats: pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII attenuates hippocampal neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a common complication in elderly patients after major surgery. It delays postoperative recovery and increases the risk of neurodegenerative disorders. CaMKIIδ is a key calcium-signaling regulator of neuronal survival and neuroinflammation, yet its functional role in POCD remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify injury-inducible calcium-signaling genes and to characterize the association of Camk2d, the gene encoding CaMKIIδ, with POCD progression in aged rats.
METHODS: A POCD model was established in aged rats by sevoflurane anesthesia combined with splenectomy. Cognitive function was evaluated with the Morris water maze (MWM) and Y-maze tests. Hippocampal transcriptome profiling was performed using RNA sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Key molecular and pathological alterations were validated by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, ELISA, and histological staining, and the pan-CaMKII inhibitor KN-93 was administered for functional validation. Serum inflammatory cytokines were measured in parallel to characterize peripheral-to-central inflammatory coupling.
RESULTS: Cognitive performance was worst on postoperative day 3, which was therefore identified as the critical injury window of POCD. Hippocampal CaMKIIδ, phosphorylated NF-κB (p-NF-κB), pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), and pro-apoptotic Bax were markedly upregulated, whereas anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 reached its lowest level and neuronal apoptosis peaked on day 3. KN-93 treatment downregulated CaMKIIδ expression, suppressed neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, and effectively rescued cognitive impairment in POCD rats.
CONCLUSION: Camk2d upregulation is closely associated with POCD pathogenesis, paralleling hippocampal neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of CaMKII by KN-93 alleviates POCD, supporting CaMKII signaling as a potential therapeutic target for perioperative cognitive protection.

articles.title: Transesophageal Echocardiographic Appearance of a Cavitary Septic Pulmonary Embolic Lesion in Tricuspid Valve Infective Endocarditis.
Treatment-Requiring Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting in Ambulatory Oncology Surgery: Four-Year Trends in Antiemetic Utilization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) remains an important complication after ambulatory cancer surgery. This study evaluated four-year trends in treatment-requiring post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) PONV, prophylactic aprepitant utilization, and rescue amisulpride administration.
METHODS: A retrospective descriptive analysis of monthly perioperative quality-improvement data was conducted from January 2022 through December 2025. The primary outcome was postoperative nausea and/or vomiting requiring antiemetic treatment in the PACU. Because the source data were aggregated, nausea and vomiting could not be analyzed separately, and patient-level risk adjustment was not possible.
RESULTS: A total of 15,467 ambulatory cancer surgeries were analyzed. Treatment-requiring PACU PONV occurred in 2041 cases (13.2%) overall and was 20.3% in 2022, 13.3% in 2023, 9.1% in 2024, and 9.9% in 2025. Aprepitant was administered in 6927 cases (44.8%); among aprepitant recipients, 1331 (19.2%) required PACU treatment for PONV. Among 8540 cases without aprepitant, 710 (8.3%) required PACU treatment for PONV. This unadjusted difference should not be interpreted as an estimate of aprepitant effectiveness because treatment allocation was influenced by baseline risk. Rescue amisulpride was administered in 748 cases (4.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: Treatment-requiring PACU PONV declined over the four-year observation period. Concurrent changes in antiemetic utilization are descriptive and cannot establish that any specific medication or practice change caused the observed decline.

articles.title: Clinical, Hematologic, and Inflammatory Factors Associated with Early Mortality and Postoperative ICU Admission After Geriatric Hip Fracture Surgery.
articles.abstract: Background: This study evaluated whether routinely available admission hematologic and inflammatory markers remained associated with postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission and 1-month mortality when considered alongside established clinical and perioperative factors. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 598 patients aged 65 years or older who underwent proximal femoral nailing (PFN) or hemiarthroplasty for hip fracture between October 2021 and October 2025. Admission laboratory values were obtained from the first blood tests at presentation. The primary outcome was 1-month mortality, and the secondary outcome was postoperative ICU admission. Group comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U and chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression was used for adjusted analyses. Given the limited number of deaths, the mortality analysis was considered exploratory. Results: Among 594 patients in the clinical ICU comparison, 228 (38.4%) were admitted to the ICU. One-month mortality occurred in 41 of 596 patients (6.9%). ICU admission was associated with age (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), ASA score (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.45-2.87), and number of packed red blood cell (PRBC) units transfused (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.36-1.88). Mortality was associated with age (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02-1.12), male sex (OR 3.30, 95% CI 1.66-6.56), the fracture-treatment pathway represented by hemiarthroplasty versus PFN (OR 3.69, 95% CI 1.78-7.64), CRP per 10 mg/L (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.10), and greater PRBC exposure (OR 1.37 per unit, 95% CI 1.11-1.70). RDW-CV was not associated with either outcome after adjustment. Conclusions: The observed associations with procedure and transfusion should not be interpreted as causal effects. Early outcomes were associated with multiple baseline, inflammatory, and perioperative factors, and the mortality findings remain exploratory and require confirmation in prospectively characterized cohorts.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Placement Following Posterior Fossa Tumor Resection in Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Posterior fossa tumors (PFTs) are common pediatric brain tumors and frequently present with obstructive hydrocephalus. Although tumor resection restores cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation in many patients, a subset subsequently requires ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS) placement. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify factors associated with postoperative VP shunt placement following PFT resection in children. Materials and Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261455396). A comprehensive search of major electronic databases was conducted from inception to April 2025. Observational studies evaluating factors associated with postoperative VP Shunt placement in children undergoing PFT resection were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the modified Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework for prognostic factor research. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Results: Nine retrospective cohort studies comprising 922 children were included. Higher odds of postoperative VP shunt placement were observed with preoperative hydrocephalus (OR = 7.62, 95% CI 2.19-26.47), midline tumor location (OR = 4.75, 95% CI 1.21-18.69), ependymoma (OR = 2.56, 95% CI 1.38-4.76), subtotal resection (OR = 3.04, 95% CI 1.92-4.79), postoperative intraventricular hemorrhage (OR = 4.36, 95% CI 1.16-16.44), postoperative infection (OR = 4.96, 95% CI 1.77-13.91), and pseudomeningocele (OR = 6.17, 95% CI 3.12-12.19). Astrocytoma was associated with lower odds of VP shunt placement (OR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.27-0.85), whereas sex, medulloblastoma, and postoperative CSF leakage were not significantly associated. EVD exposure was associated with higher odds of subsequent VP shunt placement (OR = 4.79, 95% CI 2.11-10.87), although this association is susceptible to confounding by indication. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to low, with most pooled estimates derived from unadjusted data. Conclusions: Several clinical and perioperative characteristics may help identify children requiring closer surveillance for persistent hydrocephalus after posterior fossa tumor resection. The observed relationship with EVD likely reflects underlying hydrocephalus severity rather than an independent prognostic effect. Given the limited certainty and predominantly unadjusted evidence, these findings should support risk-informed surveillance rather than decisions for permanent CSF diversion. Future prospective studies with standardized definitions and multivariable adjustment are needed to develop reliable prediction models.

articles.title: Information needs and engagement profiles of adults undergoing ambulatory surgery: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambulatory surgery compresses preparation, treatment and discharge into a short period, followed by recovery at home. Information support must address emotional concerns, information preferences and ways of engaging with care. Although unmet information needs have been described, less is known about how these needs form recognisable engagement profiles.
OBJECTIVE: To explore adult patients' information needs across the ambulatory surgery pathway and develop empirically informed engagement profiles to guide future personalised information support, this qualitative descriptive study recruited thirty-three adult patients through purposive maximum-variation sampling at an ambulatory surgery centre at a tertiary hospital in Eastern China from October to December 2025; nine caregivers of children interviewed in the original study were excluded from this analysis.
METHODS: Individual semi-structured interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Thematic analysis identified information domains, followed by cross-case synthesis to construct exploratory engagement profiles from adult patient accounts.
RESULTS: Six domains concerned disease and diagnosis, surgical procedures, anaesthesia, post-discharge care and follow-up, psychosocial and practical support, and information delivery preferences. Four non-exclusive profiles were constructed: Anxious Proceduralist, Guidance-Seeking User, Collaborative Learner and Pragmatic Self-Manager. These profiles describe differing preferences for procedural detail, clear guidance, dialogue and practical recovery support.
CONCLUSIONS: Similar information needs may be organised through different ways of engaging with care. The profiles offer preliminary, hypothesis-generating design tools for personalised information support. Refinement, item development, co-design and feasibility testing are required before clinical use. The findings concern adult patients and cannot be transferred directly to caregivers of children.
REGISTRATION: Not registered.

articles.title: Dental Treatment Needs and Management in Medically Compromised Children at a Tertiary Pediatric Dental Center-A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Medically compromised pediatric patients often present with extensive dental treatment needs and may require treatment under general anesthesia due to behavioral limitations or systemic health conditions. The aim of this study was to evaluate dental treatment needs, clinical status, and indications for general anesthesia among medically compromised children referred for dental consultation from a tertiary children's hospital. Methods: This retrospective study included 215 medically compromised children referred from a tertiary children's hospital to the Department of Pediatric Dentistry between 2020 and 2024. Data extracted included age, sex, type of dentition, systemic diagnosis, dmft/DMFT and pufa/PUFA (the clinical consequences of untreated dental caries, including pulpal involvement, ulceration, fistula, and abscess formation), treatment type, and reasons for the use of general anesthesia. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and the chi-square or Fisher's exact test for categorical variables. Results: A total of 62 patients (28.8%) required treatment under general anaesthesia, whereas 153 patients (71.2%) were treated in the outpatient setting. Children treated under general anaesthesia were significantly younger (6.13 vs. 10.60 years; p < 0.001) and generally presented with a greater burden of untreated dental disease, with the most pronounced differences observed in primary and mixed dentition. They underwent more extractions and restorative procedures than outpatients. The most common reasons for general anaesthesia were lack of cooperation and extensive dental treatment needs, often co-occurring with systemic comorbidities.
