Compared with controls and not considering the stimulated region, migraine was associated with lower pressure pain thresholds (p < 0.001) and higher mechanical pain sensitivity (p = 0.001), alongside elevated central sensitization and catastrophizing scores (p < 0.001). Across migraine phases, pain sensitivity measures were largely stable; however, trigeminal mechanical pain sensitivity was selectively higher during the peri-ictal phase (p = 0.017).
CONCLUSIONS: CPM appears preserved in migraine across phases and anatomical territories, whereas sensory alterations may be modality- and region-specific, supporting a pain sensitivity amplification phenotype rather than a generalized deficit in endogenous inhibition.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Patients with migraine could inhibit pain similarly to controls, but they present in general lower pressure and mechanical pain thresholds in contrast to controls and increased mechanical sensitivity on the forehead during the peri-ictal phase. This suggests that migraine involves specific changes in pain processing rather than a general disruption of the descending inhibitory system.

articles.title: Vascular Anatomic Variations in Living Donor Kidney Transplantation: A Single Centre Experience.
articles.abstract: The implication of individual renal vascular anatomical variations remains an important consideration in terms of donor safety and successful graft outcomes in living kidney transplantation, and therefore requires careful preoperative assessment and accurate, personalized surgical planning. This study aimed to characterize these variations, describe their surgical management, and explore their associations with donor postoperative complications and recipient graft outcomes. We retrospectively reviewed 466 hand-assisted laparoscopic donor nephrectomies performed at Semmelweis University between March 2008 and December 2023. Vascular anatomical variations, surgical management, donor postoperative complications, and recipient outcomes were assessed. Vascular anatomical variations were identified in 149 cases (32%), while 317 donors (68%) had standard vascular anatomy. Two renal arteries were present in 86 grafts (18.5%); no grafts with 3 or more renal arteries were transplanted. Venous variations occurred in approximately 17% of cases. Postoperative complications occurred in 8 of 149 donors (5.4%) with variant anatomy and 22 of 317 donors (6.9%) with standard anatomy, without a statistically significant difference (Fisher's exact test, P = .686). Two recipients of kidneys with 2 renal arteries lost their grafts due to vascular complications in the perioperative period, whereas no perioperative graft losses occurred among recipients of single-artery kidneys. In our single-center experience, donor postoperative complication rates did not differ significantly between standard and variant vascular anatomy. Hand-assisted laparoscopic donor nephrectomy was feasible in selected donors with vascular variations. Three-dimensional vascular reconstruction may aid surgical planning, although its impact on outcomes requires further evaluation.

articles.title: Intraoperative hypotension and postoperative acute kidney injury: Evidence and controversies.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) remains one of the most common serious complications after noncardiac surgery, and intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is consistently identified as a modifiable risk factor. Observational studies show a consistent, roughly dose-response association between IOH, particularly at mean arterial pressures below 60-65 mmHg, and postoperative AKI, with stronger associations in patients with limited renal reserve. Definitions of IOH vary widely, which complicates the comparison of studies and the translation of thresholds into clinical targets. Randomized trials of individualized or higher blood pressure targets have generally not confirmed a kidney-protective benefit, and pooled analyses with trial sequential analysis have not demonstrated that higher targets reduce AKI. This narrative review examines how IOH definitions evolved, summarizes the conflicting intervention evidence, and assesses the controversies that shape current practice. The review concludes that avoiding severe and sustained hypotension remains reasonable, whereas current randomized trial evidence does not support a general kidney-protective benefit of higher or individualized blood pressure targets. This conclusion is provisional and is tempered by the methodologic and causal uncertainties.

articles.title: Influence of Preoperative Virtual Reality on Preoperative State Anxiety in the Ambulatory Setting: The AMBLUMEEN Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative anxiety affects 30% to 80 % of ambulatory surgery patients and is associated with increased anesthetic requirements, postoperative pain, and delayed recovery. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising nonpharmacological anxiolytic, but evidence remains limited in the ambulatory setting.
METHODS: The AMBLUMEEN (AMBulatory LUMEEN) trial is a single-center, randomized, open-label, superiority trial conducted in an adult ambulatory surgery unit. Patients with moderate-to-severe preoperative anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y-A [STAI-YA] > 45) were randomized 1:1 to standard care alone (control) or standard care and a single 20-minute preoperative VR session (immersive 360° natural contemplative scenes). The primary end point was the change in STAI-YA score from arrival in the ambulatory unit (baseline) to immediately before operating room transfer (presurgery), analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle with a linear mixed model. Secondary end points included preoperative benzodiazepine use, postoperative morphine requirement, unplanned overnight admission, patient satisfaction, and device acceptability.
RESULTS: Of 106 randomized patients (53 per group) with a median [interquartile range] baseline STAI-YA of 49 [46-55] and 49 [46-58] respectively in the control and VR group, the VR group experienced a markedly greater reduction in state anxiety than controls. Adjusted mean between-group difference in STAI-YA change from baseline to presurgery was -18.7 95% confidence interval (CI) [-21.4 to -16.1] points in favor of VR. Although benzodiazepine requirement, postoperative pain, and unplanned overnight admission were comparable between groups, the morphine requirement in postanesthesia care unit was lower in the VR group (6/53 [11.3% 95% CI, 11.3 {4.3-23.0}] vs 0/53 [0.0%, 95% CI, {0.0-6.7}]; P = .027). Global perioperative satisfaction was high in both groups (median 8 [8-9] on 10).
CONCLUSIONS: A single 20-minute session of medical-grade VR significantly reduced preoperative anxiety in ambulatory surgery patients, with high acceptability and an excellent safety profile.

articles.title: The Association Between Perioperative Enhanced Care Unit Characteristics and Surgical Cancelation: A Nationwide Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients referred for postoperative care within enhanced care units in the United Kingdom are less likely to have their surgery canceled than those referred to critical care. Presently, it is unclear whether this association remains when examined at an individual hospital level, and whether specific structure and process features of enhanced care services influence cancelation rates within a facility.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, observational study documenting clinical and organizational features of enhanced and critical care facilities in the United Kingdom. Features of interest included resource protections, staffing, and clinical scope. Sites with availability of both enhanced and critical care facilities, with >10 referrals to enhanced care during the study period, were selected for analysis. Cancelation rates of elective surgery within these facilities were quantified over a 3-month period between September 1, 2023, and November 30, 2023. Rates were defined as the number of elective cases canceled divided by the number of elective referrals to each facility. Multilevel regression was used to explore relationships between structure and process features of enhanced care units and surgical cancelation, using a two-level model with cases nested within hospitals to account for institutional confounding.
RESULTS: Complete data were available for 65 sites, of which 28 had an enhanced care facility with sufficient activity for analysis, representing 4112 patients referred to enhanced or critical care. In most institutions, surgical cancelation rates were lower within their enhanced care facility than in critical care. Enhanced care units with beds reserved exclusively for elective cases (odds ratio [OR], 0.54 [0.39-0.76]; P < .001) and clinical care involving multiple specialities (OR, 0.48 [0.33-0.69]; P < .001) were associated with reduced odds of cancelation. On the other hand, enhanced care units that permitted admission of emergency cases (OR, 1.61 [1.06-2.43]; P = .024) were associated with a greater odds of cancelation.
CONCLUSIONS: Structure and process features of enhanced care pathways are associated with cancelation rates among high-risk surgical patients in the United Kingdom. These findings may explain why cancelation rates in enhanced care are typically lower than within critical care and may have important policy implications.
authors: Pan-London Perioperative Audit and Research Network Committee, The REPACC Study Investigators

articles.title: Comparison of upper limb muscle activity and workload during intubation with the Macintosh direct laryngoscope versus C-MAC® and King Vision® videolaryngoscopes in simulated difficult airway scenarios: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Tracheal intubation is a physically and mentally demanding for anesthesiologists because it requires fine motor control, technical precision, rapid decision-making, situational awareness, and error avoidance. While videolaryngoscopes reduce muscle strain in normal airways, their ergonomic impact during difficult airway management remains poorly established. We aimed to compare upper limb muscle activity using dynamic surface electromyography during intubation via direct laryngoscopy (DL) vs videolaryngoscopy (VL) in simulated difficult airway scenarios.
METHODS: We conducted a randomized crossover trial involving 35 experienced anesthesiologists who performed tracheal intubation on a high-fidelity manikin with a normal airway, locked jaw, and rigid neck, respectively, using a Macintosh direct laryngoscope, a C-MAC® videolaryngoscope (C blade), and a King Vision® channeled videolaryngoscope. The primary outcome was upper limb muscle activity, measured by surface electromyography. Secondary outcomes included intubation time, force on upper incisors, first-attempt success rate, and perceived workload (National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index [NASA-TLX] score).
RESULTS: Direct laryngoscopy produced significantly higher brachioradialis muscle activity than C-MAC VL in the simulated normal airway (16 vs 13 µV; median difference [MD], 3 µV; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0 to 5; P = 0.04), locked jaw (18 vs 12 µV; MD, 6 µV; 95% CI, 1 to 11; P = 0.02), and rigid neck (16 vs 13 µV; MD, 4 µV; 95% CI, 0 to 9; P = 0.03) scenarios. Direct laryngoscopy was the fastest method but exerted the highest force on the incisors (P < 0.001). King Vision VL was associated with the highest NASA-TLX workload score (P < 0.001 compared with DL), whereas C-MAC VL was least demanding.
CONCLUSION: In simulated difficult airways, VL reduced upper limb muscle activity compared with DL. Nevertheless, perceived workload was higher with King Vision VL than with DL, whereas it was lower with C-MAC VL. Among the devices tested, C-MAC VL provided the most favorable ergonomic balance, combining reduced muscle strain, lower perceived workload, and highest first-attempt success rate across all airway scenarios.
STUDY REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2021/11/038305); first submitted on 26 November 2021.

articles.title: Early outcomes after complete atrioventricular septal defect repair beyond one year of age: a single-centre comparative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete atrioventricular septal defect is usually repaired during early infancy, but delayed referral remains common where access to specialised congenital cardiac surgery is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare early outcomes after repair in patients aged 12 months or younger and those older than 12 months.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included 81 patients who underwent repair between 2020 and 2024. All patients evaluated for repair underwent cardiac catheterisation, and those with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance underwent vasoreactivity testing with 100% oxygen and inhaled nitric oxide. In-hospital mortality, major complications, pulmonary artery pressure, atrioventricular valve regurgitation, and perioperative outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Thirty-five patients were aged 12 months or younger and 46 were older than 12 months. Median ages were 8 and 14 months, respectively. In-hospital mortality occurred in 3 of 35 and 4 of 46 patients, respectively. Major complications occurred in 6 of 35 and 11 of 46 patients. No statistically significant differences were detected in mortality, major complications, ventilation duration, ICU stay, pulmonary artery pressure, or early atrioventricular valve regurgitation. Confidence intervals around mortality and major-complication estimates were wide.
CONCLUSION: Repair beyond 12 months was feasible in selected patients considered operable after invasive assessment, but in-hospital mortality remained substantial and estimates were imprecise. These findings do not establish equivalence and should not support intentional delay of repair.

articles.title: Developing Consensus on the Diagnosis and Management of Cauda Equina Syndrome: A Modified Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cauda equina syndrome (CES) necessitates urgent intervention to prevent permanent neurological damage. Current literature calls for decompression within 48 hours of symptom onset. Great heterogeneity exists in criteria informing surgical decision-making. Unified consensus statements may provide clarity in these topics.
METHODS: We performed a modified Delphi study to investigate CES diagnosis and management. A 30-question survey was distributed to 18 spine surgeons, addressing diagnosis, sensorimotor/bladder/bowel findings, and surgical decision-making. Consensus was ≥80% agreement (agree/strongly agree) or ≤ 20% agreement (consensus to opposite statement) on a 4-point Likert scale. Teleconferences and final survey followed to clarify contentious statements.
RESULTS: Eighteen responses were received (15 neurosurgeons, 3 orthopedic surgeons). Seventeen statements achieved final consensus, pertaining to diagnosis (4), sensorimotor findings (4), bowel/bladder function (1), and surgical management (8). In our practice, 100% consensus was achieved for sensorimotor findings in CES comprising a constellation of symptoms, including pain and/or paresthesia and/or lower extremity motor weakness, and for time to decompression to be informed by duration and severity of symptoms. Ninety-four percent consensus was achieved on one of the following symptoms required to diagnose CES: lower extremity motor dysfunction, bowel/bladder dysfunction, or saddle anesthesia, in addition to confirmatory magnetic resonance imaging.
CONCLUSIONS: We present institutional consensus on key factors in CES symptom identification and operative management. Our local findings highlight the importance of recognizing the heterogeneous presentation of CES and the utility of combining symptom acuity with clinical context for operative planning. We hope they spur further discussion in CES management on a national scale.

articles.title: Endoscope-Assisted Evacuation of Acute Subdural Hematoma Through a Mini-Craniotomy in Selected Elderly, Medically Fragile Patients: Operative Technique and Illustrative Cases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE/BACKGROUND: Standard craniotomy for acute subdural hematoma (ASDH) evacuation carries substantial operative burden, particularly in elderly patients with comorbidities. Combining smaller craniotomies with endoscope-assisted evacuation offers a less invasive alternative. However, detailed technical descriptions remain limited. This technical note describes a reproducible operative technique for endoscope-assisted ASDH evacuation through a mini-craniotomy and illustrates its feasibility in selected patients.
METHODS: Endoscope-assisted evacuation was performed through a 3-cm osteoplastic mini-craniotomy under general anesthesia. A handheld rigid 0° neuroendoscope served as the primary visualization tool for stepwise clot mobilization, systematic inspection of the entire subdural compartment up to the skull base, and targeted hemostasis.
RESULTS: The technique was applied in 3 selected patients treated between late 2025 and early 2026. In all 3 cases, the planned approach was completed without conversion to standard craniotomy, with a median operative time of 52 minutes, with satisfactory postoperative imaging results and favorable early neurological outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Endoscope-assisted ASDH evacuation through a mini-craniotomy is a feasible and less invasive alternative in selected patients. The endoscopic approach provides systematic access to the entire subdural compartment, detailed visualization, and minimal surgical trauma. Direct endoscopic visualization permits targeted hemostasis through a limited opening. This report provides a step-by-step technical description of this approach intended to support further evaluation in prospective comparative studies.

articles.title: Postoperative Paramedian Thalamic Infarction after Sellar and Deep Midline Tumor Surgery: Incidence, Imaging Findings, and Operative Context.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the incidence of postoperative paramedian thalamic infarction after microsurgical resection of sellar and deep midline lesions and characterize its clinical, imaging, and operative features.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort, we screened 330 eligible microsurgical resections performed between 2020 and 2025. Patients with newly developed postoperative paramedian thalamic infarction confirmed by diffusion-weighted imaging and apparent diffusion coefficient were identified. Perioperative clinical data, lesion distribution, rostral midbrain involvement, the "V sign," and early postoperative computed tomography findings were reviewed. Incidence was estimated with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Postoperative paramedian thalamic infarction occurred after 6/330 resections (1.8%; 95% CI, 0.84%-3.91%). Impaired consciousness was recorded in all 6 patients, with delayed emergence in 3. The observed magnetic resonance imaging distributions were unilateral paramedian thalamic involvement (3/6), bilateral paramedian thalamic involvement without rostral midbrain extension (2/6), and bilateral paramedian thalamic involvement with rostral midbrain extension (1/6). Recorded operative corridors in affected cases were interhemispheric, transcallosal-interforniceal, or Poppen. The highest descriptive subgroup incidence was in sellar/suprasellar lesions (5/117, 4.3%; 95% CI, 1.84%-9.62%). Extensive basal cisternal blood on early postoperative computed tomography was observed in the patient with bilateral thalamic infarction and rostral midbrain extension.
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative paramedian thalamic infarction after sellar and deep midline lesion surgery is an uncommon but clinically important complication. The observed infarct distributions are consistent with the involvement of the thalamoperforating arterial territory. Early diffusion-weighted imaging/apparent diffusion coefficient should be prioritized when delayed emergence or impaired consciousness occurs after surgery.

articles.title: Associations Between Anthropometric Growth Patterns and Feeding Complexity with Readmission Following Primary Palatoplasty.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate whether preoperative anthropometric measures and feeding-related variables are associated with readmission following primary palatoplasty.DesignRetrospective cohort studySettingTertiary pediatric craniofacial center.ParticipantsInfants undergoing primary palatoplasty between 2015 and 2022 with documented weight-for-age (WAZ) and height-for-age (HAZ) z scores.Main Outcome MeasuresReadmission within 30 days of primary palatoplasty. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations with anthropometric, demographic, and feeding-related covariates.ResultsAmong 282 patients, 43 (15.2%) experienced 30-day readmission. Higher WAZ was associated with increased odds of readmission (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.23-2.84; p = .003), whereas higher HAZ was associated with decreased odds (OR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.49-0.90; p = .009). Concentrated formula use was also associated with increased odds (OR: 2.92; 95% CI: 1.18-7.19; p = .020). These associations persisted among patients without a syndromic diagnosis. Nutrition- or feeding-related concerns accounted for 19 of 43 readmissions (44.2%) and higher WAZ and lower HAZ remained associated with this outcome.ConclusionsHigher WAZ, lower HAZ, and concentrated formula use were associated with readmission following primary palatoplasty with similar anthropometric associations observed among patients without a syndromic diagnosis and for nutrition- or feeding-related readmissions. Anthropometric variables should be interpreted alongside the feeding and nutritional support required during surgical preparation and may help identify patients requiring closer perioperative feeding surveillance.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Perioperative Management and Follow-Up After Mandibular Distraction Osteogenesis in a Neonate With Severe Pierre Robin Sequence: A Report.
articles.abstract: This case describes the multidisciplinary perioperative management and 7-month follow-up of a neonate with severe Pierre Robin sequence (PRS) who underwent mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO), with a particular focus on difficult-airway management, distraction-device care, nutritional support, and recovery of oral feeding. The clinical course, multidisciplinary perioperative management, and postdischarge follow-up of this neonate were retrospectively reviewed, and the case was prepared in accordance with the CARE case-report guideline. After surgery, mandibular advancement was achieved and upper-airway patency improved. The infant was successfully extubated on postoperative day 10, remained clinically stable on spontaneous breathing, and maintained an SpO₂ above 95%. No wound infection, pressure injury, or other major postoperative complication was documented during hospitalization. Follow-up at 1, 3, 6, and 7 months after discharge showed continued somatic growth and stable airway status; however, recovery of oral feeding was slower, and nasogastric tube feeding remained necessary for an extended period. This case suggests that perioperative care after MDO in severe PRS should address the difficult airway, distraction-device management, nutritional support, and functional rehabilitation in parallel. Improvement in airway anatomy and recovery of oral feeding may follow different time courses; therefore, airway recovery should not be used as the sole predictor of oral-feeding recovery. In infants with complex airway and feeding problems, multidisciplinary collaboration can provide a practical framework for integrating specialist assessment and longitudinal care.

articles.title: Giant Bilateral Submandibular Dermoid Cysts.
articles.abstract: Dermoid cysts are benign developmental lesions arising from ectodermal remnants formed during embryogenesis, predominantly observed in children and young adults. These cysts most frequently occur in the floor of the mouth and submental region, typically located deep within the mucosa or subcutaneous tissue, or between the muscles of the floor of the mouth. Herein, we present a case of a 39-year-old male with a 30-year history of bilateral submandibular masses. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a sublingual cystic lesion extending into the bilateral submandibular spaces, with well-demarcated borders. After exclusion of contraindications for general anesthesia, complete resection of the lesion was performed. Postoperative histopathologic examination confirmed an epidermoid cyst. The patient achieved a favorable postoperative outcome without signs of recurrence.

articles.title: Sedation Versus General Anesthesia During Pediatric Electrophysiology Studies: A Paired Comparison.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthetic strategy may influence tachycardia inducibility during pediatric electrophysiology studies, but direct paired comparisons between sedation and general anesthesia remain limited.
METHODS: This prospective paired-comparison study included 51 pediatric patients aged 5-21 years with supraventricular tachycardia undergoing electrophysiology study under both procedural sedation and general anesthesia during the same session. Procedural sedation consisted of midazolam, fentanyl, and supplemental propofol boluses as needed. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and fentanyl and maintained with sevoflurane. Tachycardia inducibility and electrophysiological parameters were compared between anesthetic conditions using paired analyses.
RESULTS: Overall tachycardia inducibility was higher during sedation than during general anesthesia (40/51 [78.4%] vs. 29/51 [56.9%], p = 0.007). No significant differences were observed in atrial effective refractory period, ventricular effective refractory period, atrioventricular nodal Wenckebach point, jump, echo interval, or ventriculoatrial block duration. In patients with atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, inducibility decreased from 84.0% during sedation to 60.0% during general anesthesia (p = 0.109). In the Wolff-Parkinson-White/atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia subgroup, inducibility decreased from 73.1% to 53.8% (p = 0.063), and the accessory pathway effective refractory period, measured by extrastimulus pacing, was prolonged under general anesthesia (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: Procedural sedation was associated with greater overall tachycardia inducibility than general anesthesia during pediatric electrophysiology studies. The AVNRT and WPW/AVRT subgroups showed numerically lower inducibility under general anesthesia in the same direction as the overall finding, although these subgroup differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings support individualized anesthetic planning that considers the arrhythmia substrate, the need to preserve inducibility for mapping and post-ablation validation, and patient-specific requirements for procedural stability.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Risk Assessment Outcomes Are Associated With 30-Day in Hospital Complications Following Pediatric Scoliosis Surgery: Evaluation of a Three-Tiered Traffic-Light Triage System at Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scoliosis surgery is complex and associated with significant morbidity. Accurate risk assessment is essential for appropriate resource allocation and improved care. Risk factors for developing complications have been identified; however, structured frameworks to support preoperative assessment are limited. Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) uses a three-tier multidisciplinary team (MDT) traffic-light system to triage patients based on well-defined risk factors and expert clinical judgment.
AIM: We aimed to describe complications following scoliosis surgery at GOSH and evaluate the relationship between preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment and outcomes such as complication rates, operative times, and length of stay.
METHOD: A retrospective hospital file review was conducted for all patients presenting to GOSH for primary scoliosis surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Institutional approval was obtained, and the need for ethical approval was waived. Preoperative risk is quantified by the MDT using a three-tier traffic-light system categorizing patients as low (green), intermediate (amber), and high-risk (red). Outcomes including 30-day in-hospital complications, operative time, and length of stay were analyzed in relation to preoperative MDT traffic-light score.
RESULTS: Of 350 eligible patients, 337 had a documented preoperative MDT traffic-light assessment. Low-risk patients comprised 43.6% (n = 147/337), intermediate-risk 49.3% (n = 166/337), and high-risk 7.1% (n = 24/337). Major complications occurred in 2% (n = 3/147) of low-risk patients compared with 50% (n = 12/24) of high-risk patients, corresponding to an adjusted odds ratio of 11.4 ([95% CI 1.98-65.4], p = 0.006). High-risk patients also had significantly longer operative times (381 min vs. 320 min, p < 0.001) and length of stay (12 days vs. 5 days, p < 0.001) when compared to low-risk patients.
CONCLUSION: Patients classified as high-risk by the MDT demonstrated an increased odds of developing major complications, longer operative time, and extended length of stay when compared to low-risk patients. Similar structured tools, with local adaptations, may be valuable in other centers to support preoperative assessment, shared decision making, and guide resource allocation.

articles.title: Regional Anesthesia for Pediatric Penile Surgery in Contemporary Practice: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
Robot-assisted laparoscopic resection of paediatric retroperitoneal neurogenic tumours: a retrospective single-centre study of 117 patients.
articles.abstract: Although robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery (RALS) is increasingly used in paediatric surgery, evidence regarding its safety and feasibility in retroperitoneal neurogenic tumours (RNTs) remains limited. This study aims to evaluate perioperative and short-term oncological outcomes of RALS in children with RNTs. This single-centre retrospective study included all consecutive paediatric patients who underwent RALS for RNTs between May 2020 and May 2025. Patient demographics, tumour characteristics, perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, and follow-up data were analysed. A total of 117 patients were included; 29 (24.8%) had a single IDRF (image-defined risk factors), and none had multiple IDRFs. Robotic resection was completed in 116 of 117 patients (99.1%). Subgroup completion rates were 100.0% (29/29) among IDRF-positive patients, 92.9% (13/14) among children younger than 5 months, 95.7% (22/23) among those weighing less than 10 kg, and 100.0% (16/16) among those with tumours > 6 cm. One infant required conversion following major haemorrhage during dissection of a tumour invading the inferior vena cava. Complete macroscopic excision was achieved in all patients. Median blood loss was 5.0 mL and median postoperative stay was 3.0 days. Grade IIIb and IVb complications occurred in one patient each, with no 30-day deaths. During a median follow-up of 741 days, one local recurrence and two deaths from systemic tumour progression occurred. RALS was feasible in carefully selected children with RNTs, with a high completion rate and infrequent serious complications. A selected single IDRF, low body weight, young age, or large tumour size should not alone be considered an absolute contraindication to RALS. Multicentre prospective comparative studies are needed to refine selection criteria and assess long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Be aware of the tuft of hair: traumatic lumbar intradural hematoma following spinal anesthesia in a case of occult spinal dysraphism. Illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal intradural hematoma is a rare but potentially devastating complication of spinal anesthesia. Known risk factors include anticoagulation, coagulopathies, spinal trauma, tumors, infections, and congenital spinal anomalies.
OBSERVATIONS: The authors report the case of a 27-year-old postpartum female who developed acute bilateral lower limb weakness 3 days post-cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. On examination, she had a tuft of hair in the midline of the low back. MRI of the whole spine revealed a lumbosacral intradural hematoma with incidental findings of spinal dysraphism-diastematomyelia and tethering of the spinal cord. Emergency surgical evacuation was performed, but the patient was left with persistent neurological deficits.
LESSONS: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion and performing a thorough preanesthetic spinal evaluation when cutaneous stigmata suggestive of occult spinal dysraphism are present. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26343.

articles.title: Early clinical experience with the OB balloon for prophylactic intrauterine tamponade during cesarean section for placenta previa: a prospective multicenter phase II study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Placenta previa is a major cause of severe postpartum hemorrhage, and effective intraoperative strategies to prevent bleeding during cesarean section remain an important clinical challenge. Intrauterine balloon tamponade has been reported as an effective strategy for hemorrhage control. We developed a novel double-balloon device, the OB balloon, intended for intrauterine tamponade during cesarean section in patients with placenta previa. This study evaluated the safety, feasibility, and clinical effectiveness of the OB balloon.
METHODS: In this prospective multicenter phase II study, 55 patients with placenta previa, including low-lying placenta, underwent cesarean section with prophylactic placement of the OB balloon. Perioperative outcomes, including blood loss, need for additional hemostatic interventions, and device-related complications, were analyzed.
RESULTS: Mean blood loss before balloon placement was 1306 g, whereas median blood loss after placement was 70 g. No patient required cesarean hysterectomy or additional surgical or interventional hemostatic procedures after balloon placement. The device was inserted directly through the uterine incision, and both balloons were inflated intraoperatively by the operating surgeon under sterile conditions. Median inflation volumes were 80 mL for the uterine balloon and 50 mL for the vaginal balloon. The balloon was maintained for 12-24 hours and removed without complication. Balloon prolapse occurred in 3.6% of cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic use of the OB balloon during cesarean section for placenta previa was safe, feasible, and associated with reduced blood loss in this cohort. The dual-balloon design provided stable tamponade with a low rate of prolapse and eliminated the need for additional hemostatic interventions.

articles.title: Post-market device experience reports of dorsal root ganglion stimulation: a 10-year retrospective analysis of the FDA MAUDE database.
Spinal Cord Stimulation Attenuates Cognitive Deficits in Chronic Pain in Association with Modulation of the Microglial lnc-PCM1/PCM1/PKC/IFN-γ Signaling Network.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation plays a pivotal role in chronic pain with cognitive dysfunction (CPCD), a debilitating condition where effective treatments are limited. While spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is an established analgesic therapy, its potential to ameliorate cognitive deficits via central immunomodulation remains largely unexplored. A rat model of CPCD was generated by spared nerve injury (SNI). RNA sequencing was used to identify SCS-regulated long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the prefrontal cortex (PFC). The functional involvement of the candidate microglial transcript NONRATT012007.2 (hereafter termed lnc-PCM1) was examined using adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated manipulation, behavioral testing, molecular assays, and primary-cell conditioned-medium experiments. SCS improved cognitive performance in CPCD rats. lnc-PCM1 was predominantly expressed in microglia and was reduced after SCS. Lower lnc-PCM1 expression was accompanied by increased pericentriolar material 1 (PCM1), reduced protein kinase C (PKC) phosphorylation and IFN-γ abundance, less M1-polarized microglial activation, and lower pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Conditioned medium from manipulated microglia produced corresponding changes in neuronal oxidative stress, mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis-related proteins, and synaptic markers. In vivo overexpression of lnc-PCM1 or knockdown of PCM1 partially attenuated the cognitive and neuroinflammatory effects associated with SCS. The findings support an association between the cognitive effects of SCS and modulation of a microglial lnc-PCM1/PCM1/PKC/IFN-γ signaling network in the PFC. Because formal epistasis and IFN-γ neutralization or receptor-blockade experiments were not performed, the directionality and IFN-γ dependence of this network remain to be established.

articles.title: Acetaminophen and chronic post-surgical neuropathic pain: a randomized double blind cross-over study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite not being recommended in treatment algorithms, people often take acetaminophen for pain relief in neuropathic pain. As there is no randomized clinical trial on oral acetaminophen in neuropathic pain, this study aims to evaluate the efficacy of oral therapeutic-dose acetaminophen compared to placebo in patients with peripheral neuropathic pain.
DESIGN: This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover, double-blind clinical study. The protocol and informed consent form were approved by the French Research Ethics Committee and National Drug Agency (trial number: NCT03559985).
SETTING: It took place in University Hospital, Clermont-Fd, France.
SUBJECTS: Thirty patients with chronic post-surgery neuropathic pain were randomised.
METHODS: Acetaminophen or placebo was taken for 7 days with a wash-out period of 7 days and treatments were compared. Outcomes were 7-day mean pain intensity (numerical rating scale) after treatment, Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory (NPSI), Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HAD), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and adverse events.
RESULTS: Acetaminophen presents no statistical difference with the placebo for pain report (effect-size [95%CI]: -0.09 [-0.45; 0.26], P = 0.607) and for all secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates no clinically meaningful analgesic benefit of short-term, 3g/day oral acetaminophen as add-on therapy in chronic post-surgical peripheral neuropathic pain, and no adverse events. Although findings should not be generalized, patients with neuropathic pain using self-medicated acetaminophen should always be informed about the risks of long-term use of acetaminophen to avoid unnecessary intake and potential long term adverse events.

articles.title: Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ): Development and Initial Validation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Nociplastic pain is implicated in many chronic pain conditions, yet it has been defined primarily by the absence of structural causes-a diagnosis by exclusion. No validated nociplastic pain questionnaire exists. This study examined hypothesized pain-specific features of nociplastic pain and developed a brief self-report instrument, the Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ).
METHODS: We generated items based on literature review and input from experts and individuals with lived experience. We administered the items and measures of other pain-related constructs (pain intensity/interference, catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, and perceived stress) to 888 participants with diverse chronic pain conditions.
RESULTS: Factor analyses supported four dimensions captured by internally consistent 4-item subscales (αs ≥0.74): 1) location variability, 2) exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, 3) widespreadness, and 4) allodynia. The NociQ total score adequately discriminated presumed nociplastic and non-nociplastic conditions (AUCs 0.73-0.75). Participants who had widespread pain or reported more presumed nociplastic conditions scored higher on all scales (ps <.001, ds=0.35-1.37). NociQ scales demonstrated small-to-moderate correlations with measures of theoretically distinct constructs (rs=0.10-0.44), supporting discriminant validity, and explained additional variance in pain intensity beyond those measures (ΔR²s=.02-.07; ps <.05), supporting incremental validity.
DISCUSSION: Results indicate four nociplastic pain characteristics, including two, location variability and exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, psychometrically validated here for the first time. The 16-item NociQ demonstrates promising reliability and validity as a brief questionnaire of nociplastic pain. Future research should examine its clinical utility, such as in matching patients to pain mechanism-targeted treatments.

articles.title: Therapeutic Targeting of the Macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB Axis Mitigates Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Immune dysregulation is a pivotal driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) pathogenesis, yet therapeutic targeting of inflammation has yielded limited clinical success. Although cytosolic RNA-binding proteins are known to regulate immune responses in PH, the specific role of the nuclear m⁶A reader YTHDC1 remains undefined.
OBJECTIVES: To elucidate the function of macrophage YTHDC1 in orchestrating inflammatory vascular remodeling during PH.
METHODS: Expression profiles of YTHDC1 and TP53-induced glycolysis and apoptosis regulator (TIGAR) were evaluated in human and rodent PH specimens. The mechanistic and therapeutic roles of this axis were assessed using myeloid-specific knockout mice and pharmacological inhibitors (YL-5092, 5Z-7-oxozeaenol) across hypoxia-, SU5416/hypoxia-, and monocrotaline-induced PH models.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In patients with idiopathic or connective tissue disease-associated PAH, YTHDC1 and TIGAR expression levels were elevated in pulmonary and circulating macrophages, correlating with disease severity. In murine models, myeloid-specific deletion of Ythdc1 or Tigar conferred profound protection against hypoxia- and SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH. Mechanistically, hypoxia upregulated Ythdc1, which directly bound and stabilized Tigar mRNA. The subsequent accumulation of Tigar protein operated non-enzymatically via a specific domain (residues 152-161) to interact with Tak1, thereby activating the NF-κB cascade, augmenting pro-inflammatory cytokine release, and driving pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell proliferation. Pharmacological inhibition of YTHDC1 (YL-5092) or disruption of the TIGAR-TAK1 interaction (5Z-7-oxozeaenol) effectively attenuated vascular inflammation and mitigated PH progression in diverse rodent models.
CONCLUSIONS: The macrophage YTHDC1/TIGAR/NF-κB signaling axis acts as a critical determinant of inflammation and vascular remodeling in PH, representing a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for this disease.

articles.title: Mitral annular plane systolic excursion as a prognostic marker in critical illness: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac dysfunction is common in critical illness, yet conventional indices such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) may fail to detect early impairment. Mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE), a marker of longitudinal function, may provide prognostic information, but its role in critical illness remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies evaluating MAPSE in critically ill adults. Studies were included if MAPSE could be dichotomized using prespecified cutoffs (10 or 12 mm). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included 28-30-day mortality and exploratory measures of cardiac function and organ support. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS and certainty of evidence with GRADE.
RESULTS: Ten observational studies including 1313 patients were analyzed; 414 (31.5%) had reduced MAPSE. Most patients had sepsis or septic shock. Reduced MAPSE was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (37.7% vs 11.7%; RR 4.81; 95% CI 1.28-18.04; p = 0.02; I2 = 70.6%), with consistent effects across both cutoffs (p = 0.111) and adequate information size on trial sequential analysis. Reduced MAPSE was also associated with lower LVEF (MD -13.0%; 95% CI -20.6 to -5.4; p < 0.01; I2 = 94.6%), but not with 28-30-day mortality or exploratory outcomes. Certainty of evidence was low for in-hospital mortality and very low for secondary and exploratory outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Reduced MAPSE was associated with higher in-hospital mortality and may be a bedside marker of myocardial dysfunction. Given the limitations of the available evidence, MAPSE remains a hypothesis-generating marker requiring prospective validation.

articles.title: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: A human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit (ICU) aims to integrate person-centred care, communication, emotional support, equity, and collaboration into ICU environments. The European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) developed a consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU following a systematic, multi-phase, evidence-informed methodology incorporating the views of ICU professionals, academics, and patient and family representatives. This international multidisciplinary panel of 46 members conducted rapid reviews addressing 20 Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes (PICO) questions across six domains: person-centred care; communication and transparency; emotional well-being; equity, diversity, and inclusion; ICU environment; technology and innovation. Based on the evidence synthesis, 53 draft statements were developed and evaluated through a two-round eDelphi study. The final set of statements was discussed and ratified at an expert consensus meeting with the initial panel of experts and with patients and family representatives. A total of 201 international stakeholders participated in round 1 and 149 in round 2. Members of the expert consensus meeting ultimately endorsed 43 consensus statements. Key recommendations supported flexible family visitation, structured interdisciplinary communication, empathy-based staff training, psychological support for patients and ICU professionals, culturally responsive care, environmental interventions to improve sleep and reduce delirium, and the integration of digital supported technologies. The consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians with evidence-informed directions to deliver high-quality practice across diverse ICU settings. By prioritising person-centred care, communication, inclusivity, and well-being alongside responsible technological innovation, the experiences and outcomes of patients, families, and ICU professionals may improve.

articles.title: A randomized controlled trial of normothermic versus dual-hypothermic oxygenated ex situ perfusion in DCD liver transplantation.
articles.abstract: DCD (donation after circulatory death) liver transplantation has expanded worldwide but remains associated with an increased risk of complications. Sequential use of normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) followed by ex situ machine perfusion (MP) is increasingly adopted, but the choice of MP technique remains controversial. This randomized controlled trial compares outcomes of dual-hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (D-HOPE) versus normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) following NRP in DCD liver transplantation. After NRP, 50 grafts (44 controlled and 6 uncontrolled DCD) were randomized 1:1 to D-HOPE or NMP using concealed allocation with sequentially numbered sealed envelopes. Ex situ perfusion was not performed for additional assessment. The primary endpoint was 1-year incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs), including graft or patient loss and biliary or vascular complications. Secondary endpoints included other perioperative outcomes. We have also performed an exploratory analysis to identify predictive factors of graft loss and SAEs. No case of primary nonfunction or vascular complication occurred. One-year graft and patient survival were both 88% in the D-HOPE group and 100% in the NMP group ( p =0.07). One-year SAE rate was similar (16% vs. 20%, p =0.31). Biliary leakage and postoperative dialysis rate were comparable between the 2 groups (16% vs. 0%, p =0.12). Blood pH variation, lactate and IL-6 levels during NRP, perfusate lactate trend, portal flow, IL-6, IL-10 and TNF levels during D-HOPE, and perfusate pH variations and IL-10 levels during NMP were related to graft loss. When applied after NRP, D-HOPE and NMP provide comparable mid-term clinical outcomes in DCD liver transplantation. Differences in specific complications may require individualized selection of ex situ MP. The limited sample size and number of events preclude definitive conclusions regarding differences in individual complications or the relative efficacy of either ex situ perfusion strategy. The observed differences in specific complications and exploratory associations with perfusion parameters warrant evaluation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort.
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).
RESULTS: All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, -4.20; 95% CI, -4.53 to -3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period.
CONCLUSIONS: The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up.

articles.title: The DayCOR clinical quality registry: Recording patient-reported measures in day care anaesthesia.
articles.abstract: Day case surgery is changing, with older and sicker patients presenting, new procedures occurring and many previously inpatient procedures converted to day-stay. The impact of these changes and additions, especially the management of elderly patients, was assessed using a digital survey of patient-reported measures commencing in March 2018. Running initially in two hospitals, spreading to include a large group of Private Hospitals in Melbourne, the survey was offered to all patients attending the facilities, following an introduction of the survey process in patient admission papers with consent obtained on the day of surgery. A 15-question digital questionnaire was sent to each consenting patient by text and email 24 h post-discharge. The patient could opt out at that stage by not opening the message; 242,025 adult patients responded (response rate of 84%), with 4.5% opting out and 9% failing to complete the survey. An 'Alert,' generated digitally for any problem identified in the response, was emailed to the treating anaesthetist and to an oversight group comprised of an anaesthetist, a nurse and an administrator to facilitate appropriate action and early resolution. This digital survey saves the staff costs associated with initiating individual patient contact and fully satisfied the requirements for patient-reported outcome measures and experience measures. As well as early indication of the patient's postoperative course, confirmation of the ability to manage the elderly patient and the reliability of transferring inpatient procedures to day case management were indicated.

articles.title: Ophthalmologists' Perspectives on Cataract Surgery Sedation: A National Survey Study.
articles.abstract: In this national survey assessing US cataract surgery sedation practices, among 659 of 3,406 (19.3%) respondents, 578 (87.7%) routinely performed cataract surgery with anesthesia care. For sedation, 534 (81.0%) routinely used light-to-moderate IV sedation; 69 (10.5%) routinely used oral or no additional sedation. Forty-two (6.4%) performed cataract surgery in office-based surgery (OBS) suites. For future consideration of OBS, 76.0% (n=501), 76.0% (n=501) and 77.2% (n=509) indicated it was "moderately" or "very important" for Medicare to establish physician payment policies for OBS; to maintain access to ambulatory surgery center or hospital outpatient department privileges for complex cases; and for Medicare to continue allowing anesthesia services in the office when needed, respectively. Ophthalmologists nationwide rely heavily on anesthesia care for cataract surgery sedation. With appropriate training and favorable Medicare policies to make OBS financially viable and safe, ophthalmologists may be willing to assume additional, selected sedation roles traditionally performed by anesthesia teams.

articles.title: Needle-free jet injection in translation: a narrative review of the state of the art, key trends, and research gaps.
articles.abstract: Needle-free jet injectors (NFJIs) deliver drugs through high-velocity liquid microjets that penetrate skin without needles, offering potential advantages in patient acceptability, sharps waste reduction, and intradermal targeting. We reviewed recent translational evidence for NFJIs with emphasis on commercially accessible spring- and gas-powered systems. A PubMed search yielded 12,364 records; 351 articles were assessed for eligibility and 143 studies (2010- February 2025) were included for analysis, with figures summarizing investigation frequency and publication count. Across studies, spring-powered devices were evaluated more evenly across in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo stages, whereas gas-powered systems were more frequently studied in clinical trials, with comparatively limited ex vivo assessment. Commonly-investigated parameters were nozzle diameters of 150-200 μm and intradermal injection volumes of 50-100 μL. Jet performance and safety were strongly influenced by pressure/velocity, stand-off distance, formulation viscosity, and skin mechanics; velocities of ~100 m/s are frequently cited as a threshold for reliable penetration, while excessive pressure can increase splash-back and tissue trauma. Despite expanding applications e.g., vaccination, anesthesia, dermatologic intralesional therapies, translation is hindered by inconsistent reporting of jet parameters and limited standardized, quantitative endpoints. We propose that harmonized reporting and assessment methods should integrate model selection, parameter documentation, and clinically meaningful endpoints. With these key improvements reproducibility and acceleration of NFJI adoption can be achieved.

articles.title: Preoperative Intranasal Oxytocin and Probable Acute Stress Disorder After Traumatic Fracture Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Acute stress disorder (ASD) is a common and debilitating psychological sequela following traumatic fracture surgery, adversely affecting recovery and predicting chronic posttraumatic stress disorder. Effective pharmacological prevention strategies are currently lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a single preoperative dose of intranasal oxytocin for the prevention of screening-positive probable ASD in patients undergoing traumatic fracture surgery.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted at the General Hospital of Western Theater Command in China. From April 2024 to April 2025, adult patients scheduled for traumatic fracture surgery were enrolled and randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either receive intranasal oxytocin, 40 IU, or an equivalent volume of intranasal saline placebo 10 minutes before the induction of anesthesia.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of a first screening-positive probable ASD within 3 days postoperatively, defined by a Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SAS-RQ) score of 40 or higher. Key secondary outcomes included the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and salivary malondialdehyde, cortisol, and superoxide dismutase levels.
RESULTS: A total of 328 patients were randomized (164 to the saline group and 164 to the oxytocin group) and included in the intention-to-treat analysis. The median (IQR) age of all participants was 50 (34-57) years; 210 participants (64.0%) were male, and 118 participants (36.0%) were female. The 3-day cumulative incidence of screening-positive probable ASD was 26 of 164 (15.9%) in the oxytocin group vs 50 of 164 (30.5%) in the saline group (risk difference, -14.6 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI, -23.5 to -5.5 pp; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.34-0.79). In the prespecified Cox model, preoperative oxytocin was associated with a lower hazard of a positive screening result during follow-up (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.27-0.75). Exploratory analyses suggested improved psychological outcomes and directionally consistent alterations in stress biomarker trajectories. No serious adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, preoperative intranasal oxytocin is associated with a lower cumulative incidence of probable ASD after traumatic fracture surgery. These findings suggest that intranasal oxytocin may represent a feasible perioperative preventive strategy; however, these exploratory mechanistic insights and long-term safety profile warrant further investigation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry Identifier: ChiCTR2400082612.

articles.title: Risk Factors of Inferior Alveolar Nerve Block Failure: A Dental Student-Centred Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The inferior alveolar nerve block (IANB) is the most widely used mandibular anaesthesia technique; however, it remains prone to failure due to both anatomical and operator-related factors. Understanding these factors is essential to enhancing student training and patient comfort. This study aimed to identify risk factors associated with IANB failure among dental students.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted at Selcuk University Faculty of Dentistry (February 2023-July 2024). Fourth- and fifth-year right-handed dental students administered IANBs to 340 patients using the Halstead technique with 4% articaine and epinephrine. Anaesthesia success was evaluated after 10 min through both clinical testing and patient feedback by a blinded assessor. Logistic regression analyses identified significant predictors of failure, while receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves assessed discriminative performance.
RESULTS: Out of 340 procedures, 301 were successful, yielding an overall success rate of 88.5%. Failures were associated with limited interincisal opening, higher body mass index (BMI) and lower student experience level. Multiple logistic regression confirmed these three as independent predictors (p < 0.05). Among these, BMI showed the strongest predictive performance (AUC = 0.72), followed by interincisal distance (AUC = 0.68) and student grade (AUC = 0.66).
CONCLUSION: IANB success depends on both operator experience and patient morphology. Incorporating structured psychomotor and simulation-based anaesthesia training early in dental education may reduce failure rates and improve clinical proficiency.

articles.title: Clinical Phenotypes, Neuroimaging, and Outcomes in Prolonged and Persistent Non-Motor Migraine Aura: A Systematic Review and Episode-Level Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Prolonged and persistent migraine aura may mimic cerebral ischemia, but its clinical course and neuroimaging features are poorly characterized. We synthesized episode-level evidence on non-motor aura lasting more than 60 min without reported established infarction.
METHODS: This systematic review (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews [PROSPERO] CRD420261461238) followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to August 2026 and the searches were rerun with an extended strategy on 5 October 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching. Eligible reports provided individual-episode clinical data and temporally related neuroimaging. Owing to publication selection, heterogeneous reporting, and clustering, the synthesis was descriptive.
RESULTS: Forty-eight studies described 80 episodes in 79 individuals (49 prolonged; 31 persistent). Visual aura occurred in 63/80 episodes. Although magnetic resonance imaging was performed in 77/80 episodes, patient-level informative diffusion imaging was available in only 28/80 and imaging-based perfusion data in 28/80. Five of the 28 episodes with informative diffusion imaging were diffusion-positive (17.9%); the acute apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) was reduced in 3, non-restricted in 1, and unreported in 1, and all diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) abnormalities resolved on follow-up. Unusual imaging findings are more likely to be published; this proportion is therefore hypothesis-generating rather than a frequency estimate. In the longer-follow-up stratum, aura improvement was reported in 36/36 prolonged and 18/22 persistent episodes, with complete resolution in 35/35 and 15/22, respectively; a nerve-block series with a fixed 24-h assessment (14 episodes) was analyzed separately.
CONCLUSIONS: Published cases show heterogeneous phenotypes and cannot support estimates of prognosis or treatment effectiveness. Standardized prospective data collection should incorporate symptom-level duration, imaging timing, DWI/ADC reporting, treatment timing, and protocol-defined follow-up.

articles.title: Life's Essential 8 and Life's Crucial 9 as Prognostic Indicators for Hip Fracture Outcomes: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic utility of LE8 and LC9 for mortality and functional recovery following hip fracture surgery.
METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort study enrolled 1796 patients aged 50 years or older who underwent surgical treatment for hip fracture at two tertiary medical institutions in China between January 2017 and December 2022. Patients were followed for 1 year post-surgery. LE8 and LC9 were calculated on the first day after admission. Discriminative performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis; independent prognostic value was determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models.
RESULTS: Among 1796 participants, 311 deaths (17.3%) occurred during 1-year follow-up. LC9 demonstrated superior predictive accuracy compared with LE8 for 1-year mortality and free walking ability. Patients with low LE8 and LC9 experienced dramatically elevated 1-year mortality rates and markedly reduced functional recovery. In multivariable analyses, increase in both LE8 and LC9 related to significant mortality risk reduction and improved functional recovery, independent of age, comorbidity burden, and surgical factors.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter prospective cohort study, LC9 was independently associated with mortality and functional recovery and demonstrated greater discriminative performance than LE8, with psychological health assessment providing critical incremental value. Integration of LC9 into clinical practice may enhance risk stratification and inform targeted perioperative interventions for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Quadratus lumborum block with or without subfascial wound catheter and post-caesarean delivery pain outcomes: a single-center retrospective cohort study (2026).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated whether adding a subfascial wound catheter to a posterior quadratus lumborum block-based multimodal analgesic pathway improves pain and recovery after caesarean delivery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 361 women undergoing scheduled or urgent caesarean delivery from January to June 2026. All received bilateral posterior quadratus lumborum block and non-opioid multimodal analgesia; wound catheter use was optional. Ropivacaine infusion was continued for 48 h. Pain scores were recorded at 6, 24, and 48 h. Mobilisation, rescue analgesia, satisfaction, breastfeeding-related concern, breastfeeding outcomes, and repeat quadratus lumborum block were assessed. Catheter effects on pain were analysed using generalized estimating equations adjusted for anaesthetic technique, operative duration, repeat caesarean delivery, adhesions, age, and blood loss.
RESULTS: Catheter use was associated with lower pain scores at 6 h (adjusted difference - 0.209, 95% confidence interval - 0.369 to -0.049; P = 0.011) and 24 h (-0.174, -0.309 to -0.039; P = 0.012), but not at 48 h (-0.016, -0.139 to 0.108; P = 0.805). These differences were too small to be clinically meaningful. Mobilisation, rescue analgesia, satisfaction, and breastfeeding outcomes were similar between groups. Breastfeeding-related concern was greater with catheter use. Repeat quadratus lumborum block was infrequently required and did not delay return to normal activity.
DISCUSSION: Subfascial wound catheter use was not associated with clinically meaningful additional pain or recovery benefit. Patient counselling may help address breastfeeding-related concerns.

articles.title: Beyond Mallampati: From Universal Bedside Tests to Precision Airway Risk Stratification.
articles.abstract: Airway management remains one of the few domains of anaesthetic practice still governed by universal, dichotomous screening thresholds applied to profoundly heterogeneous populations. Conventional bedside tests-the modified Mallampati test, thyromental distance and the upper lip bite test-retain modest and inconsistent diagnostic accuracy, leaving the majority of difficult intubations unanticipated while generating false alarms that drive resource-intensive contingency plans. This narrative review reframes preoperative airway evaluation as a problem of individualised risk stratification rather than population screening. We first summarise the performance limits of classical bedside predictors and the reasons for their ceiling effect, including low target prevalence, inter-observer variability, spectrum bias and heterogeneous outcome definitions. We then examine the data streams reshaping the field: point-of-care upper airway ultrasound, whose parameters provide operator-accessible and objective anatomical information; cross-sectional and craniofacial imaging; and machine-learning models based on clinical variables, facial images and voice analysis. For each we discuss accuracy, reproducibility, validation status and barriers to adoption. We then propose a phenotype-oriented framework in which assessment intensity is matched to pre-test probability, with dedicated pathways for obesity and obstructive sleep apnoea, obstetric, head-and-neck oncological and post-radiotherapy, critically ill and emergency, and paediatric populations. We map this framework onto the 2025 European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care and Difficult Airway Society recommendations and outline the validation, calibration and equity requirements-including algorithmic bias across skin tone, sex and ethnicity-that must be met before precision airway assessment can enter routine practice.

articles.title: Effects of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Combined With Perioperative Refined Nursing on Postoperative Sleep Disturbances, Anxiety, and Depression in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess whether integrating mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) into refined perioperative nursing is associated with improvements in postoperative sleep disturbances, anxiety, and depression in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 146 CABG patients treated at Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, from July 2023 to August 2025. To reduce selection bias, 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on baseline characteristics, yielding 73 matched pairs for analysis. Based on the nursing protocol documented in the medical records, patients were classified into two groups: a standard care group had received standard refined perioperative nursing, while an MBSR group had received the same care supplemented with MBSR. Outcome measures included Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) scores assessed preoperatively and on postoperative day 7, objective sleep architecture indices obtained via actigraphy on the day of surgery and on postoperative day 7, length of hospital stay, time to first postoperative ambulation, incidence of sleep disturbances on postoperative day 7, and serum levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6), cortisol, orexin, and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) measured preoperatively and at 24 and 72 hours postoperatively. Statistical analyses included t-tests, repeated measures analysis of variance, and chi‑square tests.
RESULTS: After PSM, 73 patients were included in each group, with all standardized mean differences <0.1. Baseline preoperative HADS scores did not differ between groups (p > 0.05). On postoperative day 7, bothgroups showed reductions in (HADS-Anxiety) HADS-A and HADS-Depression (HADS-D), with the MBSR group exhibiting significantly lower scores on all HADS subscales than the standard care group (p < 0.05). PSQI scores on the day of surgery were similar (p > 0.05); On postoperative day 7, both groups improved in total PSQI and across its seven domains versus the surgical day. The MBSR group had significantly better scores than the standard care group for all PSQI domains and total score except subjective sleep quality and hypnotic use(p < 0.05). Time to first postoperative ambulation was shorter and the rate of sleep disturbance on postoperative day 7 was lower in the MBSR group (p < 0.05); mean hospital stay did not differ (p > 0.05). Objective sleep parameters on the day of surgery were comparable (p > 0.05); on postoperative day 7 both groups showed increased total sleep time and sleep efficiency, with greater gains in the MBSR group (p < 0.05). Nighttime awakenings decreased in both groups, with the MBSR group showing a larger reduction (p < 0.05). Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed significant effects of time, group, and time-by-group interaction for cortisol, orexin, IL-6, and TNF-α (p < 0.05). Within-group analyses showed postoperative increases in cortisol, IL-6, and TNF-α at 24 and 72 hours and declines in orexin versus baseline (p < 0.05). Between-group comparisons at 24 and 72 hours postoperatively demonstrated lower cortisol, IL-6, and TNF-α and higher orexin in the MBSR group compared with the standard care group (p < 0.05), and the temporal patterns differed significantly between groups (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Refined perioperative nursing incorporating MBSR was associated with alleviation of negative emotions in patients undergoing CABG, a lower incidence of sleep disturbances on the 7th postoperative day, and shorter time to first postoperative ambulation.

articles.title: Inflammatory and Metabolic Biomarkers Associated with Chronic Subdural Hematoma Recurrence: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) recurs in 5-20% of patients despite surgical treatment, and readily accessible biomarkers associated with recurrence remain limited. This study evaluated perioperative hematological, biochemical, and metabolic biomarkers associated with CSDH recurrence, focusing on preoperative lactate and the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR). Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 163 adults who underwent burr-hole evacuation for CSDH between January 2021 and December 2025. All patients underwent saline irrigation without placement of a postoperative subdural drain, in accordance with the institutional surgical protocol. Clinical, radiological, laboratory, and perioperative arterial blood gas data were analyzed. Recurrence was defined as symptomatic re-expansion requiring repeat surgery within six months. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multivariable logistic regression were used to assess discrimination and associations with recurrence. Results: Postoperative recurrence occurred in 22 patients (13.5%). Recurrence was associated with higher preoperative lactate, LAR, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and systemic immune-inflammation index, as well as lower serum albumin. LAR showed moderate discrimination (AUC 0.758, 95% CI 0.652-0.864), while lactate had an AUC of 0.744. Increased LAR (OR 1.42 per 0.1-unit increase, 95% CI 1.15-1.76; p = 0.001), bilateral hematoma (OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.08-7.84; p = 0.035), and mixed-density hematoma (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.01-6.89; p = 0.047) were independently associated with recurrence in the fitted model. The age × lactate interaction did not reach conventional statistical significance (p = 0.058) and was considered exploratory. Conclusions: Higher preoperative LAR was associated with CSDH recurrence and showed moderate discriminative performance in this cohort. These findings are exploratory and require independent validation before LAR or the combined model can be considered for clinical risk prediction.

articles.title: Male Sex, Early Postoperative C-Reactive Protein and Prolonged Hospital Stay After Lung Resection in Older Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Older patients make up a growing share of the lung-resection workload, and C-reactive protein measured in the first days after operation is used to judge recovery. Whether the same concentration means the same thing in older men and older women is not established.
METHODS: We analysed 724 lung resections in 716 patients from VitalDB, an open perioperative dataset from a Korean tertiary hospital; 313 (43.2%) were aged 65 years or older. The primary outcome was a postoperative stay of 7 days or longer. Older general surgical patients from the same institution served as an age-matched negative control.
RESULTS: Among patients aged 65 or older, prolonged stay occurred in 55 of 192 men (28.6%) and 10 of 121 women (8.3%), adjusted odds ratio 3.031 (95% CI 1.425-6.446, p = 0.0040). Median day 1 C-reactive protein was 51.9 mg/L in older men and 27.4 mg/L in older women, adjusted ratio of geometric means 1.825 (1.593-2.090, p = 1.8 × 10-16). C-reactive protein predicted prolonged stay unadjusted (1.594 per doubling, 1.292-1.967) but not once sex entered the model (0.865, 0.691-1.084, p = 0.208), an interval that remains compatible with a modest association in either direction. In 1635 older general surgical patients, neither effect was present (0.863, p = 0.302; 1.238, p = 0.163). The sex-by-age interaction was not significant (p = 0.519).
CONCLUSIONS: In older patients undergoing lung resection, men mount a larger early inflammatory response than women to comparable operations and are three times as likely to stay a week or longer, an association absent from older general surgical patients at the same institution. In this dataset and with the measured covariates, C-reactive protein on the first postoperative day was not independently associated with prolonged hospital stay after adjustment for sex and the other available factors; with 113 events, this does not establish absence of prognostic value. These data do not derive, validate, or justify sex-specific C-reactive protein thresholds, and none is proposed.

articles.title: Feasibility of the Pleural Sliding Test for Detection and Management of Lung Adhesions During Robotic Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract: Pleural adhesions can complicate access in robotic cardiac surgery, risking lung injury or conversion to sternotomy. The sliding test using thoracic ultrasound can predict thoracic adhesions and guide the surgeon during robotic set-up. We evaluated the utility of the sliding test in robotic cardiac surgery. The pleural sliding test was performed in 300 consecutive robotic cardiac surgery patients between August 2022 and September 2025. The test was performed by the surgeon using a linear probe at six intercostal sites after intubation. Intraoperative findings were used to validate the test.
