Tailored port placement and minithoracotomy strategies were used when adhesions were suspected. The mean age was 60.3 ± 13.7 years and 91 (30.3%) of the patients were female. Adhesions were encountered in 20 (6.7%) patients. Prior cardiothoracic surgery was associated with thoracic adhesions (p < 0.001). The pleural sliding test had a sensitivity of 95.0%, specificity of 97.9%, positive predictive value of 76.0%, negative predictive value of 99.6%. No pulmonary injuries occurred and no conversions to sternotomy were necessary in the cohort. Patients with adhesions had higher 24 h chest tube output (p = 0.006) but had similar mechanical ventilation times and intensive care unit stay durations. Pleural adhesions are not rare in patients undergoing robotic cardiac surgery, and their optimal management enhances the safety and efficiency of robotic cardiac procedures. The pleural sliding test offers high accuracy for preoperative detection, enabling tailored access strategies that enhance safety and maintain benefits of the robotic approach.

articles.title: Systems Toxicology Indicates AKT1/PTGS2-Centered Neuroinflammatory-Mitochondrial Crosstalk in Lidocaine Associated Neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lidocaine-containing teething gels are commonly used for pediatric oral analgesia, yet excessive exposure may induce severe neurotoxic effects, including seizure-related events. The molecular mechanisms underlying lidocaine-associated neurotoxicity remain poorly defined.
METHODS: We employed an integrative systems toxicology approach combining network toxicology, transcriptomic analysis (GSE143272), weighted gene co-expression network analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation using Kamistad Gel extract at defined lidocaine-equivalent concentration to characterize the molecular basis of lidocaine-induced neurotoxicity.
RESULTS: Sixteen shared targets were identified through the integration of lidocaine-related targets, epilepsy-associated genes, and transcriptomic signatures. AKT1 and PTGS2 emerged as key hub genes. Functional analyses consistently suggested neuroinflammatory signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and synaptic dysregulation as major pathogenic mechanisms. Molecular docking and 10-ns molecular dynamics simulations indicated stable interactions between lidocaine and AKT1/PTGS2. ROC analysis indicated moderate predictive performance of these genes in epilepsy datasets. In SH-SY5Y cells, Kamistad Gel extract significantly increased AKT1 and PTGS2 expression, supporting activation of inflammation-related neurotoxic pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: Lidocaine-associated neurotoxicity may involve an AKT1/PTGS2-centered neuroinflammatory-mitochondrial crosstalk network accompanied by synaptic dysfunction. This study provides a systems-level mechanistic insight into lidocaine neurotoxicity and identifies potential targets for improving the safety of pediatric lidocaine-containing formulations.

articles.title: Surgical Antimicrobial Prophylaxis: Clinical and Economic Impacts on Surgical Site Infection Prevention and Healthcare System Sustainability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis (SAP) is a cornerstone of surgical site infection (SSI) prevention and represents one of the most cost-effective interventions in perioperative care. However, inappropriate antimicrobial selection, timing, dosing, and duration remain common, compromising clinical outcomes and increasing healthcare costs. This narrative review summarizes the clinical and economic impacts of SAP and its role in antimicrobial stewardship, value-based healthcare, and healthcare sustainability.
METHODS: A narrative review was conducted to synthesize current evidence on the clinical and economic impacts of SAP. The literature addressing the burden of SSIs, the clinical and economic impacts of prophylactic strategies, antimicrobial selection and duration, stewardship interventions, and future perspectives for optimizing perioperative infection prevention was reviewed.
RESULTS: Available evidence indicates that appropriate SAP reduces SSI-related morbidity and healthcare resource utilization, whereas inappropriate prophylaxis and prolonged antimicrobial exposure increase costs without improving outcomes. In a Brazilian microcosting study, deep sternal wound infection increased hospitalization costs by 152%, and mediastinitis by 188%, compared with uninfected patients. In orthopedic surgery, actual prophylaxis costs were approximately 11-fold higher than guideline-based regimens when inappropriate prescribing predominated. In neurosurgery, prolonged prophylaxis increased antimicrobial costs from US$3.35 to US$20.41 per patient, despite similar SSI rates (3.5% vs. 3.6%). Stewardship interventions have also demonstrated substantial economic benefits; one arthroplasty program improved optimal prophylactic antimicrobial selection from 64.9% to 95.4% and generated estimated savings of US$197,050 per 1000 procedures.
CONCLUSIONS: Appropriate SAP is a high-value intervention that improves patient outcomes while reducing healthcare costs. Optimizing antimicrobial selection, timing, dosing, and duration through stewardship initiatives is essential to maximize clinical effectiveness, minimize unnecessary antimicrobial exposure, and promote sustainable healthcare systems. Future studies should incorporate standardized pharmacoeconomic methodologies to strengthen evidence-based decision-making and value-based surgical care.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Liver Transplantation: Clinical Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Liver transplantation remains a technically demanding procedure despite continued surgical advances. Successful outcomes depend on balancing donor selection with perioperative complexity, where each decision shapes graft and patient survival. Conventional scoring systems such as Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD)-based prioritisation only partially explain differences in patient outcomes across transplant centres worldwide. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-including longitudinal modelling of electronic health records, deep learning for imaging, and multimodal data integration-offer new opportunities to individualise risk stratification for graft selection, predict allograft dysfunction and rejection, and improve long-term survival. Clinically developed AI models may strengthen organ matching decisions and acceptance, while identifying candidates who require intensified immunosuppressant monitoring or targeted diagnostic testing in the postoperative period, without increasing rejection risk. However, introducing AI/ML systems requires thorough validation, careful calibration, and ongoing clinical audit to reduce bias, detect technical errors, and ensure reproducible performance. This review summarises current and emerging clinical applications of AI in liver transplantation and explores near-future directions. These include AI-driven graft evaluation during organ retrieval and normothermic machine perfusion, along with emerging evidence for the safety, reliability, and clinical utility of AI in transplantation practice.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients with Pure Native Aortic Regurgitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic valve regurgitation is a common valvular heart disease. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are the principal therapeutic modalities, while the comparative efficacy of these two approaches remains controversial.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420261411339). We systematically searched Web of Science, PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library databases for relevant studies from their inception to 26 July 2026. RevMan 5.4 software was used to conduct this analysis. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were used to evaluate the outcomes.
RESULTS: We assessed in-hospital outcomes and post-discharge 30-day outcomes. The primary outcomes were length of hospital stay, perioperative complications, and valve condition. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF), and new permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). Nine articles involving 28,811 patients were included. Compared with SAVR, TAVR reduced length of hospital stay [mean difference (MD) = -4.49, 95% confidence interval (CI): -4.98, -4.01, p < 0.00001, I2 = 80%], perioperative complications [Odds ratios (OR): 0.55, 95% CI: 0.50 to 0.60, p < 0.00001, I2 = 62%) and new-AF(OR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.43 to 0.59, p < 0.00001 I2 = 30%). However, there was a significant increase in perivalvular leakage (OR: 17.13, 95% CI: 4.13 to 71.13, p < 0.0001 I2 = 29%) and new PPI (OR: 2.63, 95% CI: 2.13 to 3.25, p < 0.00001 I2 = 80%). There was no significant difference observed in all-cause mortality (OR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.69-1.20, p = 0.49, I2 = 69%).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with SAVR, TAVR reduced length of hospital stay, perioperative complications, and new AF. However, it was associated with an increase in perivalvular leakage and new PPI. These findings suggest that TAVR may represent a better strategy for patients with pure native aortic regurgitation.

articles.title: Non-Cardiac Surgery After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation: Perioperative Management and Outcomes from a Single Center.
articles.abstract: As survival after left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation improves, an increasing number of patients require non-cardiac surgery (NCS) during follow-up. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics and perioperative management of LVAD recipients undergoing NCS and to compare outcomes between elective and emergent procedures. Among 434 adults who underwent LVAD implantation between 2014 and 2026, 42 subsequently underwent NCS and were classified into elective (n = 26) and emergent (n = 16) groups. Overall, 9.68% of LVAD recipients required NCS, of which 61.9% were elective. Preoperative urea, creatinine, and international normalized ratio (INR) levels were significantly higher in the emergent group. Thirty-day mortality (31.2% vs. 3.8%; p = 0.023) and 1-year mortality (68.8% vs. 30.8%; p = 0.026) were significantly higher after emergent surgery. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly lower survival in the emergent group (log-rank p = 0.018). On univariable Cox regression analysis, emergent surgery was associated with a 2.87-fold higher mortality risk (HR, 2.87; 95% CI, 1.15-7.15; p = 0.024). NCS after LVAD implantation can be performed safely with appropriate patient selection, anticoagulation management, and multidisciplinary care; however, emergent surgery is associated with a less favorable preoperative clinical profile, limited opportunity for anticoagulation optimization, and substantially higher mortality.

articles.title: Buccal Articaine Infiltration as a Minimally Invasive Technique for Mandibular Primary Molars: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Effective pain control is essential for successful dental treatment in children. Although the inferior alveolar nerve block remains the standard technique for achieving mandibular anesthesia, it is associated with injection discomfort, prolonged soft tissue numbness, and an increased risk of postoperative self-inflicted soft tissue injury. Buccal infiltration with 4% articaine has emerged as a promising minimally invasive alternative because of its favorable diffusion properties. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of buccal infiltration with 4% articaine for local anesthesia of primary mandibular molars in pediatric patients. Methods: This systematic review was conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases were searched to identify randomized controlled clinical trials evaluating buccal infiltration with 4% articaine in primary mandibular molars. Owing to methodological heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized qualitatively. Results: Five randomized controlled trials met the eligibility criteria. Buccal infiltration with 4% articaine demonstrated high anesthetic success and was generally associated with comparable pain scores, favorable patient comfort, and favorable postoperative outcomes compared with conventional anesthetic techniques. However, heterogeneity was observed in clinical procedures, comparator interventions, and outcome assessment methods. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that buccal infiltration with 4% articaine is an effective and clinically comparable, minimally invasive anesthetic technique for selected procedures involving primary mandibular molars in children.

articles.title: Perioperative Safety Considerations and Surgical Outcomes Associated With GLP-1-Based Therapies: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly prescribed for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. Their effects on gastric emptying have raised concerns in the perioperative setting, where standard fasting protocols are used to reduce aspiration risk. However, the clinical significance of altered gastric physiology and its implications for perioperative management remain uncertain. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. The protocol was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (registration number: CRD420261289189). A comprehensive literature search identified studies evaluating perioperative gastric physiology and procedural safety outcomes associated with GLP-1 RA use in adults undergoing procedures requiring sedation or general anesthesia. Outcomes included delayed gastric emptying, residual gastric contents, aspiration or regurgitation events, and perioperative management adaptations. Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising seven observational studies and nine case reports or case series. Observational evidence demonstrated an association between GLP-1 RA use, particularly semaglutide, and increased residual gastric contents or delayed gastric emptying despite adherence to standard fasting protocols. These findings were identified primarily through gastric ultrasound and endoscopic assessment. In contrast, clinically apparent aspiration or regurgitation events were uncommon and were reported predominantly in case-based literature. Larger observational studies did not demonstrate a clear increase in aspiration or broader perioperative complications. Identification of retained gastric contents also influenced clinical management in several reports, resulting in changes to anesthetic planning, additional gastric assessment, or postponement of elective procedures. GLP-1 RA therapy is associated with alterations in gastric physiology that may challenge the assumptions underlying standard preoperative fasting protocols. Although increased residual gastric contents are consistently reported, current evidence does not establish a corresponding increase in clinically significant aspiration events. Individualized preoperative risk assessment, including consideration of medication exposure and selective use of gastric ultrasound, may assist perioperative decision-making. Further prospective studies are needed to quantify aspiration risk and establish evidence-based perioperative management strategies.

articles.title: What to Do When You Can't Transfuse: Update on Optimizing Outcomes for Jehovah's Witness Patients.
articles.abstract: Patients who decline allogeneic blood transfusion for religious reasons, most commonly Jehovah's Witnesses, represent a growing population requiring specialized perioperative and inpatient care. Over the past decade, comprehensive "bloodless medicine" programs have emerged to safely manage these patients using principles of patient blood management, including preoperative anemia diagnosis and treatment with oral or intravenous iron and erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, intraoperative blood conservation techniques such as cell salvage, acute normovolemic hemodilution, antifibrinolytics, controlled hypotension, and meticulous surgical technique, and postoperative strategies to minimize iatrogenic blood loss from phlebotomy. This review synthesizes evidence from a large single-institution experience, encompassing propensity-matched cohort studies of adult, pediatric, and surgical/medical subgroups, alongside novel tools such as a preoperative hemoglobin target algorithm and comparative data on intravenous iron versus red cell transfusion. We also discuss a March 2026 update to Jehovah's Witness doctrine permitting preoperative autologous blood donation as a matter of personal conscience, and its practical implications for clinical teams. Across these studies, patients receiving bloodless care demonstrated morbidity, mortality, and length of stay comparable to or better than those receiving standard transfusion-inclusive care, with some analyses showing reduced hospital-acquired infection rates and consistently lower hospital costs and charges. A 10-year financial analysis further demonstrated that a comprehensive blood management program generated a greater than sevenfold return on investment while maintaining equivalent clinical outcomes. Collectively, these findings support bloodless medicine as a safe, cost-effective, and increasingly generalizable model of high-value perioperative care.

articles.title: Complications Associated with the Management of Infected Pancreatic Necrosis.
articles.abstract: Contemporary management of infected pancreatic necrosis utilizes the "step-up approach," which emphasizes delayed, staged intervention. This strategy contrasts with historical early open surgery and begins with antibiotics and minimally invasive drainage (percutaneous or endoscopic) after necrosis has matured, typically 4 weeks or later after onset. The staged approach minimizes operative trauma, reduces complications and improves outcomes and mortality compared to open necrosectomy. However, these patients are still at risk for significant complications in the perioperative period.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of impact of 'Vascular Geriatrics' interventions on short-term outcomes for vascular surgery inpatients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vascular surgeons are treating more older, frail and multimorbid patients. Integrated care models including both surgeons and geriatricians have improved peri-operative outcomes in orthopaedics. This meta-analysis investigated the impact of 'Vascular Geriatrics' services on short-term outcomes for vascular surgery inpatients.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Embase and recent conference abstracts were searched for studies of all methodologies comparing outcomes before and after the introduction of 'Vascular Geriatrics' service. Risk of bias was assessed using Methodological Index for Non-Randomised Studies criteria for non-randomised studies and Risk of Bias Tool (Version Two) tool for randomised. Certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations analysis. Meta-analyses compared the relative risks of inpatient mortality, complications, discharge to home and 30-day readmission using a random-effects model. Length of stay (LOS) in days was compared using mean difference.
RESULTS: Eight studies with 2441 patients were included. Models included outpatient pre-operative comprehensive geriatric assessment, inpatient geriatric liaison service and geriatrician-surgeon co-management. 'Vascular Geriatrics' was associated with a lower risk of inpatient mortality (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.46-0.9, P = .010), cardiac complications (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.19-0.62, P < .001) and infective complications (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38-0.63, P < .001). Delirium risk was reduced but not significantly (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.25-1.34, P = .20). There was no association in LOS (P = .37), discharge to home (P = .55) or 30-day readmission risk (P = .64).
CONCLUSIONS: Though study quality was poor, formalised geriatric involvement was associated with a decreased risk of adverse peri-operative outcomes in vascular patients compared to traditional care models. Further studies are needed to investigate the most effective design of geriatrician-surgeon partnership.

articles.title: Preoperative ultrasound assessment of gastric volume in diabetic patients scheduled for elective surgery: a prospective, observational, comparative cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic gastroparesis is a chronic complication that increases the risk of perioperative aspiration. Despite adherence to current fasting guidelines, gastric emptying remains difficult to predict in patients with diabetes. However, comparative data on ultrasound-defined gastric contents and residual gastric volume in fasting patients with and without diabetes scheduled for elective surgery remain limited. This knowledge gap provides the rationale for the present study. Therefore, this study aimed to assess gastric contents and volume using gastric ultrasonography in patients with diabetes scheduled for elective surgery and to investigate clinical variables associated with a full stomach, indicative of an increased risk of aspiration.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 39 patients with diabetes and 39 control participants, all of whom had fasted for at least 8 h, were enrolled. Preoperative gastric ultrasonography was performed to assess the Perlas grade, antral cross-sectional area (CSA, cm²), and estimated gastric volume (mL). High aspiration risk was defined using ultrasound-based surrogate markers, rather than clinically observed aspiration events, and was identified by the presence of solid or thick fluid contents (Perlas grade 3) or an estimated clear fluid volume exceeding 1.5 mL/kg. Gastric aspirate volume (mL) and pH were subsequently recorded. Among patients with diabetes, the associations of glycemic control (HbA1c), disease duration, and diabetes-related complications (ascertained from pre-existing medical records) on gastric parameters were evaluated. Statistical analyses included the independent-samples t-test or Mann-Whitney U test for group comparisons, chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate for categorical variables, Spearman correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
RESULTS: In the diabetes group, antral CSA was significantly greater than that in the control group (10.91 ± 9.49 cm² vs. 5.11 ± 2.01 cm²; p < 0.001), as were estimated gastric volume (94.21 ± 110.65 mL vs. 41.04 ± 29.78 mL; p = 0.008), aspirated gastric fluid volume (19.67 ± 14.49 mL vs. 8.69 ± 5.68 mL; p < 0.001), Perlas score (median 0 [range 0-3] vs. 0 [range 0-0]; p < 0.001), and gastric pH (2.56 ± 0.54 vs. 2.14 ± 0.85; p = 0.011). A full stomach was identified in 17.94% of patients in the diabetes group (7/39) and in none of the control participants (0/39). Among participants classified as having high aspiration risk, the prevalence of diabetes-related neuropathy and the volume of aspirated gastric fluid were significantly higher. An internal exploratory ROC analysis indicated that a CSA threshold of ≥ 10 cm² may have descriptive value within this cohort (AUC: 0.862; 95% CI: 0.728-0.995, estimated using the DeLong method); however, as the outcome was partly derived from CSA, this threshold is descriptive and should not be interpreted as an independently validated diagnostic cutoff. No significant correlation was observed between HbA1c levels and gastric volume or gastric fluid pH, and no significant association was found between diabetes duration and gastric parameters.
CONCLUSION: Despite adherence to standard fasting protocols, patients with diabetes exhibited higher residual gastric volumes and a greater prevalence of a full stomach than control participants. Among patients with diabetes, neuropathy was more prevalent in those classified as having ultrasound-defined high aspiration risk than in those with low aspiration risk (57.1% vs. 9.4%; p = 0.012). No significant correlation was identified between HbA1c levels and gastric volume, and no statistically significant association was found between glycemic control and ultrasound-defined aspiration risk. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory rather than conclusive. Preoperative bedside gastric ultrasonography may provide additional information for aspiration risk assessment in selected patients with diabetes, but these findings require confirmation in larger studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06195488 first posted January 8, 2024). As participant enrollment commenced on November 1, 2022, prior to the registration date, this trial was retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Consensus recommendations for patient selection and clinical implementation of polymyxin B hemoadsorption in endotoxic septic shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite long-standing clinical use and emerging evidence, no structured framework exists guiding clinicians in identifying septic shock patients for endotoxemia assessment, interpretation of the Endotoxin Activity Assay (EAA), or practical implementation of polymyxin B hemoadsorption (PMX-HA) therapy.
METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus process was conducted with ten critical care and nephrology experts, compromising a pre-meeting survey, a one-day in-person consensus conference, and iterative voting on draft statements. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement.
RESULTS: Consensus was achieved on 20 statements across three domains: (1) operational criteria to prompt endotoxemia assessment in suspected or presumed septic shock, (2) role and interpretation of the EAA, and (3) logistics and clinical implementation of PMX-HA. Key recommendations included standardized criteria to identify eligible patients, EAA thresholds of ≥ 0.60 and < 0.90 to support PMX‑HA consideration, initiation of therapy as early as possible once eligibility is confirmed, with ≤ 36 h from septic shock onset proposed as a pragmatic implementation benchmark, and standardized treatment protocols consisting of two sessions, 24 h apart, targeting 120 min each. A multidisciplinary team model was endorsed for implementation. Identified research priorities were in treatment effect heterogeneity, EAA kinetics, clinical implementation, and healthcare system integration.
CONCLUSIONS: These consensus recommendations provide a structured, implementation-focused framework for PMX-HA use in suspected endotoxic shock. The framework emphasizes stepwise operational criteria, biomarker-guided decision-making, multidisciplinary team-based implementation, and standardized protocols. It is intended to support institutions currently using PMX-HA and to assist U.S. clinicians and health systems in preparing for potential adoption pending regulatory approval.

articles.title: Application of a nursing care bundle combined with a clinical nursing pathway in liver transplantation and its impact on patient self-management: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the effects of a nursing care bundle combined with a clinical nursing pathway on self-management ability, postoperative biochemical markers, medication adherence, psychological status, and quality of life among liver transplant recipients.
METHODS: This study was a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial. A total of 103 patients who underwent liver transplantation were initially screened. Three individuals were excluded due to severe postoperative complications (n = 1), incomplete medical records (n = 1), or inability to adhere to follow-up procedures (n = 1). The remaining 100 patients completed follow-up and were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the control group (n = 50) or the intervention group (n = 50) using a random number table. The control group received routine perioperative nursing care and standard follow-up after discharge. The intervention group received a structured nursing care bundle integrated with a clinical nursing pathway under the enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) framework. Primary outcome included self-management ability [assessed using the Chinese version of the Exercise of Self-Care Agency Scale (ESCA)]. Secondary outcomes included postoperative biochemical indicators at 1 and 6 months after discharge [including fasting blood glucose (FBG), 2-hour postprandial blood glucose (2 h-PBG), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), serum creatinine (SCr), total bilirubin (TBil), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and therapeutic drug concentrations], medication adherence [assessed by the Basel Assessment of Adherence to Immunosuppressive Medications Scale (BAASIS)], psychological status [measured by the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) and Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS)], and quality of life (evaluated using the GQOLI-74 questionnaire).
RESULTS: At both 1 and 6 months following discharge, patients in the intervention group demonstrated better biochemical outcomes, including lower FBG, 2 h-PBG, ALT, SCr, TBil, and BUN levels, as well as more stable drug concentrations compared with the control group (P < 0.05). Furthermore, ESCA scores, BAASIS scores, and GQOLI-74 scores were all higher in the intervention group than in the control group (P < 0.05). SDS and SAS scores were reduced in the intervention group relative to the control group (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The integration of a nursing care bundle with a clinical nursing pathway has a positive effect on improving self-management ability and medication adherence, optimizing postoperative biochemical indicators, alleviating negative emotions, and enhancing quality of life in liver transplant patients.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of subtalar arthrodesis for calcaneal fracture malunion and their association with preoperative anxiety and depression: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with foot and ankle disorders often experience preoperative anxiety / depression, which can adversely affect surgical outcomes. This study aimed to explore the factors influencing preoperative mental health status in patients with malunited calcaneal fractures and to evaluate the potential impact of preoperative mental health on prognosis following subtalar arthrodesis (STA).
METHODS: This study retrospectively enrolled 45 patients with malunited calcaneal fractures who underwent subtalar arthrodesis from January 2015 to May 2023. Demographic data were collected, and assessments using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score, and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) were performed. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare preoperative and final follow-up VAS and AOFAS scores. Spearman correlation was used to analyze the associations between preoperative HADS scores and preoperative VAS/AOFAS scores, and the associations between preoperative HADS scores and final follow-up VAS/AOFAS scores. A HADS-A or HADS-D score ≥ 8 was defined as indicating anxiety/depressive symptoms.
RESULTS: A total of 39 patients (32 male, 7 female) completed follow-up. Sixteen patients (41.03%) had preoperative HADS-A or HADS-D scores ≥ 8, indicating anxiety/depressive symptoms. Significant improvements in VAS and AOFAS scores were observed at final follow-up compared to preoperative assessments (P < 0.001). Preoperative VAS scores showed significant positive correlations with both anxiety and depressive symptoms (P < 0.05), while preoperative AOFAS scores showed a significant negative correlation with anxiety (P < 0.05) but not with depression (P > 0.05). No significant correlations were found between preoperative anxiety/depressive symptoms and baseline characteristics (gender, age, BMI, disease duration; all P > 0.05). Notably, preoperative HADS scores were not significantly correlated with final follow-up VAS or AOFAS scores (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: STA effectively treats malunited calcaneal fractures, significantly improving clinical outcomes. Preoperative pain levels correlated with both anxiety and depressive symptoms, whereas functional status correlated only with anxiety. No statistically significant association was identified between preoperative anxiety/depressive symptoms and final follow-up pain relief or functional recovery in this cohort. Given the modest sample size, these null findings should be interpreted cautiously. Clinicians should prioritize preoperative pain management to alleviate psychological distress and optimize perioperative care.

articles.title: Early neurological deterioration after endovascular treatment in acute ischemic stroke with large vessel occlusion.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore the occurrence, identify independent predictors, and assess the clinical implications of END following EVT in individuals with acute LVO.
METHODS: Participants were enrolled from the ANGEL-ACT registry. END was characterized by a rise of ≥ 4 points in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score from baseline to 24 h post-EVT. We conducted logistic regression analyses to pinpoint independent predictors of END.
RESULTS: Among the 1557 patients included in the study, the occurrence of END stood at 9.8%. Factors independently associated with END included an admission NIHSS (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 4.067, 95% CI 2.513 to 6.582, p < 0.0001), an admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) exceeding 5 (aOR = 1.811, 95% CI 1.246 to 2.632, p = 0.0018), the use of general anesthesia (GA) (aOR = 0.474, 95% CI 0.330 to 0.682, p < 0.0001), longer procedure duration (aOR = 5.500, 95% CI 1.45 to 20.871, p = 0.0122), and more than three retrieval attempts (aOR = 1.294, 95% CI 1.177 to 1.422, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: END manifested in 9.8% of patients undergoing endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute large vessel occlusion (LVO). This investigation highlights various independent predictors of END, providing valuable insights for daily clinical practice aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of intravascular thrombectomy.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.
CLINICALTRIALS: gov ; Unique identifier: NCT03370939; registration date: 11th November 2017.

articles.title: Novel surgical approach to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction: an acute volume overload rat model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction frequently complicates cardiac surgery, primarily driven by perioperative acute volume overload (AVO). This study aimed to establish a novel surgical rat model that recapitulates AVO-mediated left ventricular diastolic dysfunction for translational research.
METHODS: Twenty male Sprague Dawley rats (6-8 weeks old) were equally and randomly divided into AVO group (intraventricular saline infusion at 3 ml/h) and Sham group (no fluid infusion). A 22-gauge cannula was inserted into left ventricle chamber to record pressure and inject fluid after left thoracotomy. Hemodynamic and echocardiographic statistics were obtained at baseline, 10 min, 20 min, 30 min and 40 min. Two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was applied to compare longitudinal cardiac parameters, with Mauchly's sphericity test and Greenhouse-Geisser correction for sphericity violation; Bonferroni post-hoc tests corrected for multiple pairwise comparisons.
RESULTS: RM-ANOVA detected statistically significant main effects of group, time, and group×time interaction for LV systolic pressure (LVSP), LV diastolic pressure (LVDP), and LV end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) (all P < 0.001). In the AVO group, LVEDP increased progressively over time, rising by 102.7% relative to baseline at the 40 min time point. Post-hoc testing confirmed substantially higher LVEDP in AVO rats versus sham animals at 40 min (15.2 ± 0.79 mmHg vs. 7.5 ± 0.71 mmHg, adjusted P < 0.001). A prominent group×time interaction was also observed for the mitral E/A ratio (P < 0.001): this ratio declined to 0.54 in the AVO group at 40 min, which differed significantly from sham controls (0.54 ± 0.01 vs. 1.73 ± 0.01, adjusted P < 0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) exhibited a significant group×time interaction as well, falling to 62.82% at 40 min in AVO rats compared with 76.34% ± 0.36 in sham animals (adjusted P < 0.001). All hemodynamic and echocardiographic readouts remained stable across all time points in the sham group, with no statistically significant temporal changes observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute volume overload induced heart diastolic dysfunction in rats is a cost-effective and time-efficient experimental animal model.

articles.title: Need for a definitive trial of local versus general anaesthesia in chronic subdural haematoma; survey and literature review of ongoing trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural haematoma (cSDH) is a common neurosurgical condition, many patients have significant comorbidity or are living with frailty. Surgery is effective and can be performed under local anaesthesia (with or without sedation) (LAS) or general anaesthesia (GA). Optimal technique for both GA and LAS is poorly defined but similar questions have been explored in other surgical settings. We sought to clarify the breadth of evidence for anaesthetic technique in cSDH surgery, while drawing on relevant literature from other disciplines to understand how a definitive trial of this question could be performed.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used a combination of review of trial registries, the Cochrane database, and a survey of anaesthetic and neurosurgical practitioners.
RESULTS: We identified a paucity of high-quality studies, especially randomised trials, exploring this question. The literature, and survey of anaesthetists and surgeons suggest that LAS may achieve equivalent outcomes, but significant confounding exists in current studies. Registered trials are single centre, and Cochrane reviews in other fields present issues of equipoise, study design, and outcome choice as key challenges in designing a definitive trial.
CONCLUSIONS: There is significant interest in this topic as evidenced by published and emerging literature and views of anaesthetists and surgeons. No registered trial is multi-centre or draws on challenges identified in similar trials from other disciplines.
authors: Improving Care In Elderly Neurosurgery Initiative (ICENI) Working Group

articles.title: Acute Profound Hypotension Following Intraoperative Plasma Transfusion-A Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood transfusions can be lifesaving but carry risks of serious adverse reactions, including the less recognized hypotensive transfusion reaction, characterized by hypotension that may be difficult to distinguish from other transfusion reactions or haemorrhage-related shock. At the Karolinska University Hospital, an increased incidence of perioperative hypotensive transfusion reactions without typical allergic features has been observed during recent years. The aim of this study was to identify and describe common clinical characteristics among patients who experienced perioperative transfusion reactions.
METHODS: This case series utilized data from a local quality registry at the Karolinska University Hospital, Sweden, covering the period from June 2024 to June 2025. Data collected included patient demographics, relevant clinical parameters and summaries of each reaction. Descriptive statistics were applied to identify potential common traits.
RESULTS: Seventeen patients with perioperative transfusion reactions were included. All but one developed hypotension and in 11 cases hypotension was the sole manifestation. None of these 11 showed elevated serum tryptase levels. All patients except one received plasma via a Belmont Rapid Infuser RI-2 and seven patients also received packed red blood cells. In 11 cases, the blood pressure drop occurred immediately after plasma infusion. During this period, the Belmont Rapid Infuser was withdrawn after 7 months. No reactions were reported in the 4 months following withdrawal. However, reactions recurred following subsequent device use.
CONCLUSION: Most transfusion reactions were characterized by profound and immediate hypotension following plasma transfusion, often presenting as isolated hypotension without biochemical or clinical evidence consistent with IgE-mediated anaphylaxis. A temporal association with the use of the Belmont Rapid Infuser RI-2 was observed. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating, warranting further prospective mechanistic and safety studies.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: Hypotensive transfusion reactions are uncommon but clinically important, and may be mistaken for bleeding or anaphylaxis. This case series describes 17 perioperative cases, mainly presenting as abrupt isolated hypotension after plasma administration. The absence of device-use denominators, signs of anaphylaxis in most patients and the incomplete, delayed calcium measurements mean that other mechanisms cannot be separated from a device-related effect. The main message for practice is therefore active vigilance when using a rapid plasma infusion device.

articles.title: Swedish Consensus Recommendation for Follow-Up After ICU Stay.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors experience long-term physical, psychological and cognitive impairments after critical illness. However, methods for identifying patients in need of post-ICU support vary widely. As a result, many patients are left without access to established rehabilitation pathways. This consensus recommendation provides a framework for the organisation and content of follow-up for adult ICU survivors in Sweden, informed by available evidence, stakeholder perspectives and expert consensus.
METHODS: The National System for Knowledge-Driven Healthcare Management (NPO) in Sweden commissioned the development of a practice recommendation for the follow-up of critically ill adults. Multidisciplinary experts in ICU survivorship formed a task force group. A systematic literature search in four databases was conducted in 2024 to identify pre-existing systematic reviews on the topic. The literature was reviewed, assessed for quality and recommendations were developed based on the literature evidence. The draft was discussed among multiprofessional groups involved in follow-up, in workshops with critical care nurses (n = 30) and professionals responsible for follow-up clinics (n = 74) and among patient representatives (n = 4). The final draft underwent external peer review by representatives from relevant professional organisations, the national registry for intensive care and governmental agencies in Sweden.
RESULTS: The consensus recommendation suggests that all adult patients with an ICU length of stay ≥ 48 h are recommended for follow-up, with an initial contact within 1 week of ICU discharge to assess clinical status, identify early problems and ensure continuity of care. Patients and their families are recommended to be offered an outpatient follow-up visit at 2-3 months after discharge, led by ICU clinicians and, when possible, delivered by a multidisciplinary team. Validated screening tools and objective tests are recommended to assess relevant outcomes, including post-traumatic stress, anxiety, depression, cognitive impairment, physical function and Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) as appropriate. Patients with identified problems should be referred to appropriate healthcare providers or specialist services for further management.
CONCLUSION: This consensus recommendation provides a framework for patient selection, timing and assessment to support a more structured and equitable management of post-intensive care syndrome.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: Systematic follow up of ICU survivors after hospital discharge is needed in order to assess long-term patient-centred outcomes. This is a consensus set of recommendations and not a GRADE-based clinical practice guideline for doing this, which can be considered by relevant ICUs.

articles.title: Preoperative cognitive training for preventing perioperative neurocognitive disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis and meta-regression of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Although nonpharmacological interventions are recommended for preventing perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), cognitive training has not been explicitly advocated. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and meta-regression tested the hypothesis that preoperative cognitive training, compared with usual care, reduces the incidence of PND.
METHODS: Eight databases and two clinical trial registries were searched for RCTs comparing preoperative cognitive training with usual care. Primary outcomes were postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder.
RESULTS: Thirteen RCTs with 1446 patients were identified. Preoperative cognitive training was associated with a lower risk of POD (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.77; P = 0.001; low certainty). Subgroup analysis (P for interaction = 0.01) and meta-regression (β1 1.072, 95% CI 0.006-2.138, P = 0.049) suggested an association between training format and treatment effect on POD, with a potentially greater benefit for traditional training. For DNR, the incidence was lower in the training group than in the usual care group (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.46-0.96; P = 0.03; very low certainty), but this finding was not supported by several sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were detected between subgroups for training format, total duration, or surgery type (P for interaction = 0.06, 0.37, and 0.34, respectively), and meta-regression suggested that overall risk of bias was a potential moderator for DNR (P = 0.045). TSA suggested a potential for false-positive findings, as the cumulative Z-curves did not cross the TSA boundaries, and the required information sizes were not reached for either outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative cognitive training may reduce the incidence of POD, with traditional training showing a potentially greater benefit than digital training. For DNR, the current evidence is insufficient to support a preventive effect of preoperative cognitive training, although a trend toward benefit was observed. These findings are limited by high risk of bias in several included trials and failure to reach the required information sizes in TSA, particularly for DNR, which need to be confirmed in future large-scale RCTs.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW PROTOCOL: PROSPERO (CRD420261293607).

articles.title: The use of patient-specific implants: a promising strategy to reduce rigid external distractor-associated complications in syndromic craniosynostosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Midface distraction osteogenesis (DO) with rigid external distraction (RED) is an established technique for treating severe midfacial hypoplasia in patients with syndromic craniosynostosis. However, halo-type distractors are associated with substantial device-related complications, particularly at the cranial pin fixation and midfacial anchorage sites. Patient-specific implants (PSIs) for the retention of the halo frame and the maxillary anchorage may reduce fixation-related complications while maintaining reliable force transmission and distraction vectors.
METHODS: This monocentric retrospective study included a cohort of consecutively treated patients with Apert, Crouzon, or Pfeiffer syndrome who underwent Le Fort III or Wassmund III midface advancement using DO with PSI bases for the RED fixation combined with either conventional or patient-specific maxillary anchorage between January 2022 and July 2024. Demographics, perioperative parameters, achievement of the planned distraction goal, and complications classified by Clavien-Dindo were analyzed, with particular focus on distractor- and fixation-related events.
RESULTS: Eight children (six boys, two girls; five Crouzon, two Pfeiffer, one Apert) were included. Mean age at surgery was 14.1 years (±0.4 years), and mean time to distractor removal was 3.3 months (±0.29 months). No intraoperative complications occurred. One patient developed a transient cerebrospinal fluid leak that resolved spontaneously (Clavien-Dindo grade I). Cranial RED fixation using PSIs was not associated with infections, loosening, migration, or transcranial penetration. One device-related complication occurred during retention (crossbar ball-joint screw loosening), managed by retightening (grade II). Three patients underwent conventional midfacial fixation using Leipzig retention plates, with one case of intraoral wound dehiscence requiring secondary suturing and antibiotics (grade II) and subjectively reduced oral hygiene/food intake. Five patients received PSI-based midfacial fixation with two transcutaneous wires; no fixation-related complications, dental injuries, or wound problems were observed. All patients achieved the planned advancement with correction of exorbitism and Angle Class III malocclusion. At mean follow-up of 25.7 months (±8.8 months), all patients had Whitaker Class I outcomes, with predominantly excellent aesthetic results.
CONCLUSIONS: PSI-based fixation of rigid external distractors (RED) to the cranium and midface appeared to be a feasible and safe approach in this preliminary cohort. While no fixation-related complications were observed, the retrospective design, small sample size, and absence of a comparative control group preclude conclusions regarding a reduction in complication rates. Larger comparative studies are required.

articles.title: Longitudinal assessment of pulmonary morphological patterns using structured serial chest radiography in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portable chest radiography is routinely available in mechanically ventilated ICU patients, yet serial findings are rarely standardized. We evaluated whether a structured morphological classification of serial chest radiographs could describe early radiographic evolution during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) and explored associations with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Single-centre retrospective cohort of 57 adults receiving IMV ≥48 h in the ICU of Hospital General IESS Babahoyo, Ecuador (2018-2019). Radiographs from Days 1-5 of IMV were classified into 13 predefined predominant morphological categories; radiological change was defined as any modification of the predominant pattern relative to baseline. IMV duration, ICU length of stay, and mortality were analysed using an exploratory logistic regression model.
RESULTS: Radiographs were available for 57 patients on Days 1-2, 46 on Day 3, 39 on Day 4, and 34 on Day 5. Normal predominant patterns decreased from 52.6% at baseline to 14.7% on Day 5, while alveolar patterns increased from 10.5% to 35.3%. Thirty-two patients (56.1%) had documented radiological pattern change, first identified at a median of Day 2. Patients with documented change had longer IMV duration (5.5 vs. 3 days; p < 0.001) and ICU stay (8 vs. 3 days; p < 0.001). In the exploratory adjusted model, IMV duration was associated with documented change (adjusted OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.0-1.6; p = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: Structured serial chest radiography converted routine ICU images into comparable longitudinal morphological variables. Documented radiological change was common and frequently early; its association with longer IMV duration should be interpreted as concurrent and exploratory. Prospective multicentre studies are needed.

articles.title: Association between perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy and reoperation following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: A TriNetX database study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia (HLD) impairs tendon healing and is associated with increased revision risk following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR). While statins may partially mitigate this effect, residual dyslipidemia may impair healing. Ezetimibe, through inhibition of intestinal cholesterol absorption, has demonstrated favorable effects on tendon healing in preclinical studies.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy is associated with improved postoperative outcomes following ARCR compared with statin monotherapy and patients without HLD.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult patients undergoing ARCR were stratified into three cohorts based on HLD status and perioperative (± 6 months) lipid-lowering therapy: (1) documented HLD treated with statin-ezetimibe prescriptions, (2) patients without documented HLD or lipid-lowering therapy prescriptions, and (3) documented HLD treated with statin monotherapy prescriptions. Primary comparisons were predefined between cohort 1 and cohorts 2 and 3. Propensity score matching (1:1) adjusted for demographics and comorbidities. Tear size and presence of fatty atrophy and fatty infiltration were not adjusted for. Outcomes occurring within 5 years included revision rotator cuff repair (RCR), conversion to shoulder arthroplasty, and secondary shoulder arthroscopy.
RESULTS: After matching, 1,066 patients were included in cohorts 1 and 2 and 1,114 patients in cohorts 1 and 3. Compared with patients without HLD, statin-ezetimibe therapy demonstrated similar rates of revision RCR (5.4% vs. 6.4%; RR 0.853; p = 0.358), conversion to shoulder arthroplasty (RR 1.227; p = 0.470), and secondary arthroscopy (RR 0.846; p = 0.260). Compared with statin monotherapy, statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower rates of revision RCR (5.6% vs. 8.0%; RR 0.697; p = 0.023) and secondary shoulder arthroscopy (7.3% vs. 9.6%; RR 0.757; p = 0.048), while arthroplasty rates remained similar (RR 1.261; p = 0.400).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with HLD undergoing ARCR, perioperative statin-ezetimibe therapy was associated with lower reoperation rates compared with statin monotherapy and postoperative outcomes comparable to patients without HLD. These findings support further investigation of intensified lipid-lowering therapy, while accounting for tear size and fatty infiltration.

articles.title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement.
METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression.
RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

articles.title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018).
CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

articles.title: Continuous thoracic epidural analgesia as a bridge to delivery for refractory pregnancy-associated anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome.
articles.abstract: Anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome (ACNES) is an underrecognized cause of abdominal wall pain. Pregnancy-associated ACNES is uncommon, and its optimal management remains uncertain. A 38-year-old woman in her first pregnancy at 37 weeks and 2 days of gestation presented with severe localized abdominal pain and a positive Carnett's sign. Repeated local anesthetic injections provided insufficient relief. Continuous thoracic epidural analgesia at the T8-T9 level achieved sustained pain control and served as a bridge to cesarean delivery. No recurrence was observed during the first postpartum week. This case suggests that continuous thoracic epidural analgesia may be considered for refractory pregnancy-associated ACNES when less invasive treatments are ineffective.

articles.title: Enhanced recovery after orthopaedic surgery: global research trends, collaboration, and emerging themes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathways are increasingly used in arthroplasty and spine surgery, but the structure of the orthopaedic literature remains incompletely characterized. This study mapped publication growth, contributors, collaboration, citation influence, and research themes.
METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection records were retrieved with a title-based search and exported on June 15, 2026. Reproducibility screening of 655 exported records excluded 347 stemming-related false positives in which "ERAS" matched the word "era" and 13 enhanced-recovery records that were trauma-related but not orthopaedic, leaving 295 eligible publications. Publication patterns, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and reference co-citation were analyzed.
RESULTS: The 295 publications spanned 2012-2026; 242 (82.0%) were published from 2020 onward, and annual output peaked at 53 in 2025. China contributed to 129 records (43.7%), the United States to 59 (20.0%), and England to 16 (5.4%). Sichuan University was the leading standardized organization (12 publications). Major themes centered on total knee and hip arthroplasty, length of stay, complications, perioperative care, pain, and spine surgery.
CONCLUSION: Orthopaedic ERAS research has grown rapidly and continued to increase through 2025, but output remains geographically concentrated. The literature is mature around clinical efficacy and perioperative outcomes; implementation, dissemination, and broader international representation are important priorities.

articles.title: Tranexamic Acid in Femoral and Tibial Fracture Surgery A Narrative Review of Administration Routes and Effects on Blood Loss Safety and Fracture Healing.
articles.abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is used to reduce perioperative bleeding in fracture surgery, but the preferred administration route and its effects on fracture healing remain uncertain. This narrative review examines intravenous, topical, and combined TXA in adult femoral and tibial fracture surgery, emphasizing direct route comparisons and the distinction between blood conservation and patient-centered outcomes. Publications identified in an initial Elicit-assisted evidence report were selectively checked against primary sources, supplemented by targeted source searches. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was performed. Randomized trials generally support reductions in calculated blood loss with intravenous TXA, although transfusion benefits are not uniform. Topical TXA improves selected blood-conservation outcomes, while direct comparisons with intravenous administration yield procedure-dependent results. Adding local TXA to intravenous treatment reduced calculated blood loss in a tibial nailing trial, but observational hip-fracture studies do not establish a consistent advantage for combined administration. Studies generally did not detect increased thromboembolic events; limited sample sizes and selected populations preclude firm conclusions about uncommon harms or comparative safety. Fracture-union evidence is sparse and does not establish that TXA accelerates healing or that one route is preferable for this purpose. TXA is a useful blood-conservation adjunct in selected femoral and tibial fracture procedures, but current evidence does not support a universal ranking of administration routes. Procedure-specific randomized comparisons with standardized transfusion criteria and longer-term union and functional outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Impact of direct transfer to critical care on mortality for patients who undergo emergency colorectal cancer resection: a national population-based cohort study in England.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is recommended that patients receiving emergency surgery and with 'high-risk' of morbidity and mortality should be transferred directly from theatre to critical care. Using a national, population-based cohort study, we estimated the effect of direct transfer to critical care on 90-day mortality after emergency colorectal cancer resection, and the variation amongst English NHS hospitals.
METHODS: Patients who underwent emergency colorectal cancer resection between December 2016 and November 2019 according to Hospital Episodes Statistics, National Bowel Cancer Audit or National Emergency Laparotomy Audit were included. Patients were identified as having a direct transfer to critical care through linkage with the Intensive Care National Audit and Research Centre Case Mix Programme. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score methods were used to measure the effect of direct transfer to critical care on 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: In total, 10,441 patients underwent an emergency colorectal cancer resection. Unadjusted 90-day mortality was higher in the direct transfer to critical care cohort (10.9%) than in patients without direct transfer to critical care (3.7%) (odds ratio [OR]: 3.16, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.65-3.77). There was no evidence of an association after risk adjustment (adjusted OR: 1.16, 95% CI: 0.94-1.43) or after propensity score analysis (weighted OR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.69-1.27). For patients at high risk with a predicted mortality ≥5%, the proportion of patients with a direct transfer to critical care varied widely amongst hospitals (interquartile range 68%-92%; median 83%).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that apparent higher postoperative mortality in patients having direct transfer to critical care can be mostly explained by characteristics of patients, tumours, physiology and surgery. However, the extent to which direct transfer to critical care is used varies widely amongst hospitals. Further work to understand this variation has the potential to improve patient outcomes after emergency colorectal cancer resection.

articles.title: Outcomes of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis admitted to the ICU for acute respiratory failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for acute respiratory failure are scarce, and early prognostic markers are lacking.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with ALS admitted for acute respiratory failure to two ICUs of a tertiary referral center between 2016 and 2022. The primary outcome was 3-month mortality. Factors associated with 3-month mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Survival and functional outcomes were evaluated up to 12 months.
RESULTS: Among 139 patients [median age 66 (IQR 57-73) years, 61.2% being men], 109 (78.4%) patients presented with hypercapnia and 82 (59.0%) with hypoxemia (defined as PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio < 300) at ICU admission, with frequent overlap between both conditions. Non-invasive ventilation was used in 79.9% of patients, while 13.7% were intubated, and 2.2% underwent tracheostomy. Three-month mortality was 48.2%, increasing to 61.2% and 74.1% at 6 and 12 months respectively. In multivariable analysis, hypoxemia at ICU admission was independently associated with increased 3-month mortality (HR = 2.27, 95% CI: 1.28-4.01; P = 0.005), along with older age (HR=1.03 per year, 95% CI: 1.00-1.06; P = 0.035). Among patients alive at 3 months, a majority (79.2%) were living at home.
CONCLUSION: ICU admission for acute respiratory failure in ALS is associated with substantial short-term mortality, consistent with the poor prognosis inherent to the natural history of the disease. Hypoxemia at admission identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk of death and may help inform early prognostic assessment and shared decision-making. However, patients who survive the acute ICU phase frequently achieve favorable short-term outcomes, with most living at home at 3 months.

articles.title: Synergistic psychosocial pathways linking resilience to self-efficacy in lung cancer following video-assisted thoracic surgery: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recovery after video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) can involve pain, fatigue, distress, and reduced confidence in rehabilitation activities.
OBJECTIVES: Guided by conservation of resources theory, this study examined associations between resilience and cancer-related self-care self-efficacy measured during early postoperative recovery, the indirect roles of social support and negative emotion, and whether social support moderated the resilience-self-efficacy association.
DESIGN: A cross-sectional study.
SETTINGS: One tertiary Grade A cancer hospital in South China.
PARTICIPANTS: A convenience sample of 225 adults with primary lung cancer who underwent elective VATS was assessed on postoperative days 3 to 5 before discharge.
METHODS: Participants completed a sociodemographic/clinical questionnaire and validated Chinese versions of the social support, cancer self-care self-efficacy, resilience, and negative emotion scales. Observed-variable serial mediation paths were estimated with 5000 bootstrap resamples; moderation was examined with a resilience by social support interaction.
RESULTS: Resilience was positively associated with self-efficacy (B = 2.080, 95% CI 1.826 to 2.334). The indirect associations through social support (B = 0.118, 95% CI 0.024 to 0.212), negative emotion (B = 0.084, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.164), and both variables sequentially (B = 0.018, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.032) were statistically significant. The resilience by social support interaction was also significant (beta = 0.083, p = 0.010).
CONCLUSIONS: In this early postoperative sample, resilience, social support, negative emotion, and self-efficacy showed patterns consistent with the proposed resource-based model. Nursing strategies that assess and support these resources should be tested in longitudinal and interventional studies.

articles.title: Non-Technical Skills for Surgery in African Perioperative Curricula: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-technical skills (NTS) such as situation-awareness, decision-making, communication, and leadership among surgical healthcare providers are vital to safe surgical care. Studies have associated poor NTS with errors in the operating room. The extent to which African training curricula address NTS is unclear. We mapped the presence and absence of NTS content in surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, anesthesia, and nursing/midwifery training curricula across Africa.
METHODS: Using the Arksey and O'Malley methodological framework, we conducted a scoping review on PubMed, AJOL, and Google Scholar databases, followed by a grey literature search to identify published perioperative training curricula from African institutions. Data on NTS were abstracted and were categorized as explicitly teaching, explicitly mentioning, implicitly mentioning, or making no mention of NTS.
RESULTS: From 55 screened documents, 31 specialty curricula from 18 institutions across 11 countries met inclusion criteria. West Africa was represented at 45.2%, followed by East Africa at 29.0%, and North and South Africa at 6.5% each. Curricula from the College of Surgeons of East, Central and Southern Africa, the College of Anesthesiologists of East, Central and Southern Africa, the East, Central and Southern African College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, and the WHO Africa Prototype Competency-Based Curriculum accounted for 12.9%. No single-country NTS curriculum was identified from Central Africa. NTS were mentioned implicitly (38.7%), explicitly (48.4%), both implicitly and explicitly (6.5%), or not at all (6.5%). Most curricula (93.5%) mentioned at least one NTS. Among NTS domains, leadership was most frequently mentioned (67.7%), followed by teamwork (61.3%), communication (45.2%), professionalism (35.5%), decision-making (32.3%), and problem-solving (29.0%). Critical thinking and situation awareness (6.5%) were the least represented domains.
CONCLUSION: While several African perioperative curricula mention NTS, gaps exist in the incorporation of formalized NTS training in existing courses and assessments, especially in Central Africa. Targeted curriculum reform is needed to transition NTS from implicit expectations to explicitly taught and assessed competencies in African perioperative training. Structured coursework, such as the Non-Technical Skills for Surgeons in Variable Resource Contexts (NOTSS-VRC) may help fill these gaps.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes after thoracic aortic surgery in Johannesburg: a retrospective observational cohort study, 1995-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thoracic aortic diseases require complex surgery, and outcomes data from African populations are scarce. We described the patient characteristic profile, documented risk factors, and perioperative outcomes of patients undergoing thoracic aortic surgery at a quaternary hospital in South Africa.
METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study reported per the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines, we included patients aged 18 yr or older who underwent open thoracic aortic surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital between 1995 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. We assessed correlates using modified Poisson regression with robust variance (risk ratios [RRs]).
RESULTS: Of 366 patients (median age 48 yr [inter-quartile range 37-59]; 219 [59.8%] male), diagnoses were dissection in 157 (42.9%), aneurysm in 157 (42.9%), traumatic rupture in 26 (7.1%), and other in 26 (7.1%). In-hospital mortality was 21.9% (80 of 366; 95% confidence interval [CI] 17.7-26.4) and did not differ significantly across diagnosis groups (P=0.693), being identical after dissection and aneurysm (22.9% in each). Prolonged operative duration (>600 min) was the only variable independently associated with mortality (adjusted RR 7.2; 95% CI 1.5-34.9), an imprecise, sparse-data estimate. Mortality was numerically higher in female than male patients (26.2% vs 19.2%) but this difference was not significant after adjustment (adjusted RR 1.30; 95% CI 0.89-1.89); age and diagnosis were not independently associated.
CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality after thoracic aortic surgery was 21.9%. Prolonged operative duration was associated with in-hospital mortality, although the estimate was imprecise, and operative duration is likely to be a marker of procedural complexity and adverse intraoperative course rather than an independently modifiable risk factor. The findings support intensive postoperative care.

articles.title: Assessment of Variations of Pressure Sensitivity Within and Between Chronic Painful Jaw Muscles-A Case-Control Clinical Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orofacial myofascial pain shows variable muscle sensitivity, referred pain, and complex spatiotemporal pressure processing profiles.
METHODS: This participant-, examiner- and data analyst-blinded case-control study compared masticatory muscle sensitivity and entropy patterns between 28 chronic myofascial TMD pain patients and 28 age- and sex-matched controls, introducing a comprehensive approach for 'topoalgesia' assessment. Mechanical pain sensitivity (MPS) was assessed at nine sites on the masseter and temporalis muscles bilaterally using a palpometer with 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 kgf for 2 s. Participants rated MPS on a 0-50-100 numeric rating scale after each palpation and reported referred sensations. Entropy and center of gravity (COG) were analysed.
RESULTS: Chronic myofascial TMD pain patients reported significantly greater MPS scores than controls across all force levels and muscles (p < 0.05). Both groups showed increased MPS with higher applied forces. TMD patients exhibited significantly greater entropy in the masseter muscle at 0.5 and 1.0 kgf, and in the temporalis muscle at 2.0 kgf (p < 0.001). TMD patients also reported more referred sensations than controls across all force levels (p < 0.001). COG analysis showed myofascial TMD patients presented more centrally located COG within the masseter muscle than controls particularly at lower forces.
CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that chronic myofascial TMD patients present greater muscle sensitivity, differing entropy profiles across muscles and force levels, and distinct spatiotemporal patterns compared to controls, associated with more frequent referred sensations. These findings contribute to understanding chronic muscle pain manifestations, and topoalgesia may help better track disease progression or remission over time.
SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Quantification of spatial variation in pressure sensitivity (topoalgesia) showed that chronic myofascial TMD patients diverge from healthy controls at 0.5 kg and 2.0 kg palpation forces, but not at 1.0 kg, identifying force-specific parameters that could sharpen diagnostic sensitivity for orofacial pain.

articles.title: Unravelling Sleep-Pain Interactions: Methodological Advantages and Inflammation.
Specificity and Equivalence in Chronic Pain Psychological Therapy: We Need to Look Beyond Average Package Comparison.
Limitations in the Assessment of Pain Reporting Reliability-Validation of the Focused Analgesia Selection Test.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unreliable pain reporting predicts placebo responses in clinical trials and has been documented in chronic pain populations. The thermal Focused Analgesia Selection Test (FAST) quantifies Pain Reporting Reliability (PRR) by assessing consistency when rating repeated thermal stimuli of varying intensities presented in pseudo-randomized order. However, FAST's validity as a pure measure of reporting reliability remains unclear.
METHODS: We investigated whether PRR derived from the thermal FAST is confounded by individual differences in pain sensitivity (pain and tolerance thresholds), stimuli extending beyond individual pain ranges, and temporal trends. Fifty-five healthy participants (32 women) completed the thermal FAST protocol comprising 49 stimuli across seven temperatures (43°C-50°C).
RESULTS: Higher pain thresholds predicted lower PRR (b = -4.66, 95% HDI [-9.18, -0.07]). Exploratory analysis suggests that rating variability was reduced when stimulation fell outside individual pain ranges (below-range: b = -8.04, 95% HDI [-11.44, -4.72]; above-range: b = -4.45, 95% HDI [-7.98, -0.90]). Greater coverage of FAST temperatures by individual pain ranges correlated with higher PRR (ρ = 0.33). Thermode repositioning to prevent habituation at the stimulation site may have induced acute sensitization at the repositioned site as pain ratings increased by +33 and +19 VAS points at the first two stimuli following repositioning. Excluding these trials improved median PRR by 16% (from R2 = 0.65 to 0.81).
