CONCLUSIONS: PRR derived from the current thermal FAST implementation likely conflates reporting consistency with pain sensitivity, psychophysical range effects, and procedural artifacts and may therefore risk misclassifying pain phenotypes as reporting inconsistencies. We propose methodological refinements, particularly individualized stimulus calibration and optimized repositioning protocols, which should be evaluated in confirmatory studies and chronic pain populations.

articles.title: Long-Term Response of Occipital Nerve Stimulation on Central Sensitization in Patients With Chronic Primary Refractory Daily Headache: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central sensitization and impaired conditioned pain modulation (CPM) response have been associated with chronic migraine. Consequently, migraine patients can present with allodynia. Occipital nerve stimulation (ONS) is a neuromodulation procedure used in patients with refractory chronic primary headache disorders such as cluster headaches and migraines. We report on long-term outcome data on the effects of ONS on central sensitization. Efficacy outcomes for ONS typically employ standardized headache questionnaire measures. However, more objective tests of endogenous pain mechanisms, such as Quantitative Sensory Testing (QST), have not been utilized to measure whether reported outcomes are paralleled by QST changes following the long-term implementation of ONS. Our group has published one-year outcomes in central sensitization following ONS.
OBJECTIVE: This prospective study aimed to evaluate whether QST detects a change in central sensitisation in patients with refractory chronic primary headache and provides more long-term outcome data for patients receiving ONS.
METHODS: Six patients, three new persistent daily headaches, two chronic migraines, and one chronic cluster headache were implanted between 2013 and 2015 with percutaneous leads placed bilaterally parallel to the greater occipital nerve; IPG was a Genesis/Prodigy St Jude Medical, Plano, TX, USA now Abbott systems. Baseline QST and questionnaires were completed and monitored for up to 12 months and then annual review for 10 years.
RESULTS: Patients showed substantial reductions in headache-related disability and quality of life measures. Patients demonstrated impaired/reduced CPM in all but one patient at baseline, and this reverted to an increased CPM at 12 months. Then, this was maintained at the 10-year visit.
CONCLUSION: This is a long-term prospective follow-up investigating the effect on central sensitization following ONS implantation. Responders showed substantial reductions in headache-related disability and improved conditioned pain modulation over a 10-year period.

articles.title: State-dependent roles of inflammation across pain conditions: insights from human transcriptomics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation is widely viewed as a driver of pain, yet clinical and transcriptomic studies report conflicting associations. A clearer understanding of how inflammatory processes relate to pain across clinical contexts is essential for improving diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of chronic pain.
METHODS: We analysed whole-blood RNA sequencing from seven human cohorts spanning four pain conditions, including acute, postoperative, chronic localised, and chronic widespread pain in almost 500 blood samples with corresponding pain intensity scores. Using gene-level meta-analyses, pathway enrichment, and immune cell-specific gene ontologies, we tested how inflammatory responses relate to current pain, future pain trajectories, and within-person changes over time.
RESULTS: Inflammation emerged as one of the strongest biological correlates of pain across all cohorts, yet its association direction depended on the pain state. In acute musculoskeletal and postoperative pain, higher inflammatory activation, which correlated with enhanced neutrophil and macrophage function, was associated with greater pain intensity but also correlated with better subsequent recovery, consistent with an adaptive inflammatory response. In chronic localised pain, this relationship was disrupted and inverted: higher inflammatory activity was linked to lower pain intensity and associated with worse long-term outcomes. In chronic widespread pain, macrophage-related inflammatory activity remained positively associated with both pain severity and persistence, suggesting progression toward a maladaptive immune state.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that inflammation is not uniformly detrimental in pain but plays distinct roles depending on disease stage and context. Inflammation might support resolution during acute injury yet become dysregulated in chronic and nociplastic pain. Recognising these context-dependent roles could help explain conflicting findings in the literature and guide more precise use of anti-inflammatory therapies.

articles.title: One Year Survival of Patients With High Risk Undergoing Coronary Revascularization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients considered high risk requiring coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), we sought to evaluate the differential impact of comorbid and cardiovascular risk factors on perioperative vs 1 year survival with the hypothesis that different phenotypes of perioperative risk may portend different longitudinal outcomes and that not all high-risk features are equivalent.
METHODS: The Society Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database was used to assess all patients (n = 75,385) ≥65 years of age undergoing isolated CABG with a predicted risk of mortality greater than 4% (2012-2022). The database was linked with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services claims data to evaluate 1-year mortality. Changes in risk-adjusted odds ratios for 30-day and 1-year mortality were assessed using landmark analysis to identify variables associated with early vs late mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 67,376 (89.4%) patients survived 30 days. Among them, 8998 (13.4%) died between 30 days and 1 year. Liver disease and home oxygen therapy were associated with increased mortality at both 30 days and 1 year. However, unresponsive state, prior CABG, percutaneous coronary intervention within 6 hours, cardiogenic shock, and temporary mechanical support were associated with early mortality but exhibited no significant effects at 1 year. Finally, cancer, Medicaid coverage, and dialysis were initially neutral for 30-day mortality but emerged as independent risk factors for 1-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk CABG, prognostic determinants evolve over time. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating temporal risk dynamics into clinical decisions.

articles.title: Minimally invasive anaortic quadruple and quintuple coronary artery bypass grafting: Feasibility and early outcomes of automated titanium suture fastener - a case series.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo describe the feasibility and early outcomes of automated terminal suture fastening and conventional hand tying during complex anaortic total-arterial minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG).MethodsThis retrospective, descriptive, single-center surgical case series included 12 patients who underwent elective anaortic off-pump MICS-CABG between January 2024 and May 2025. The first seven patients underwent conventional hand-tied terminal suture securing, whereas the subsequent five underwent automated terminal suture fastening, reflecting the chronological introduction of the device later in the surgeon's experience. Nine patients underwent quadruple and three underwent quintuple bypass grafting. Clinical follow-up was performed at 30 days and six months after surgery, with CT coronary angiography performed at six months.ResultsAll patients were male, with a mean age of 69.4 ± 7.5 years. Mean operating-room time was 373.0 ± 60.1 minutes overall, 384.3 ± 50.0 minutes in the hand-tied group, and 358.0 ± 75.6 minutes in the automated fastener group. No device-related technical failures, incomplete deployments, or device-related anastomotic revisions occurred. No deaths, perioperative myocardial infarctions, strokes, conversions to sternotomy or cardiopulmonary bypass, or repeat revascularizations occurred. Two patients developed pleural effusion, one developed atrial fibrillation, and one patient with pleural effusion required rehospitalization. At six-month CT angiography, all 30 arterial grafts were evaluable; 28 were classified as FitzGibbon grade A, one as grade B, and one as grade O. Both non-grade-A findings occurred in the hand-tied group, whereas all 13 grafts in the automated fastener group were grade A.ConclusionsIn this selected 12-patient, single-surgeon case series, automated terminal suture fastening using COR-KNOT® MICRO was technically achievable during complex anaortic total-arterial MICS-CABG without observed device-related failure. The small sample, chronological device introduction, operator learning curve, and short follow-up preclude conclusions regarding comparative operating-room time, safety, or graft outcomes. Larger prospective studies with anastomosis-specific timing and graft-level follow-up are required.

articles.title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks for Headaches.
articles.abstract: Patients have numerous options for headache management at home, yet when those fail, use of peripheral nerve blocks (PNBs) in the outpatient clinical or emergency department setting can be useful. Peripheral nerve blocks (PNBs) targeting the occipital and trigeminal scalp nerves are increasingly used by primary care and emergency medicine providers for acute headache relief and prophylaxis. The purpose of this article is to provide context, with an overview of epidemiology, diagnostic considerations, and trial evidence, along with procedural guidance for use of PNBs to treat headache disorders in the primary care setting. Despite methodological and outcome heterogeneities amongst randomized controlled trials (RCTs), evidence supports the use of PNBs, particularly greater occipital nerve block (GONB), for both acute headache relief and prophylaxis. It is within the scope of the primary care clinician to provide the option of PNB for appropriate patients. Further RCTs are warranted to define optimal nerve block combinations and procedural standards.

articles.title: Noninvasive Diagnostic Ultrasound-Guided Focused Ultrasound-Induced Peripheral Nerve Blockade Attenuates Pain Behaviors in a Model of Chronic Inflammatory Pain.
Reduction in fear of movement predicts long-term decreases in functional disability among adolescents with juvenile fibromyalgia.
articles.abstract: Fear of movement and pain catastrophizing are associated with higher pain intensity and disability in adolescents with juvenile fibromyalgia (JFM), but it is unknown whether treatment-related reductions in these areas predict long-term outcomes. This study reports results of secondary data analyses from a multi-center randomized clinical trial (Fibromyalgia Integrative Training; FIT Teens) in which adolescents with JFM (N=317) received either cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), graded aerobic exercise, or CBT combined with neuromuscular exercise training. In the parent trial, functional disability of youth in all three treatments improved significantly at post-treatment and was maintained over one year. The objective of this study was to assess whether reductions in fear of movement and pain catastrophizing through 3-month follow-up predicted functional disability at 3- and 12-months. A novel latent curve modeling approach was employed to estimate distal outcomes across treatment groups. Results indicated that reductions in pain catastrophizing and fear of movement through 3-month follow-up both significantly predicted functional disability at the 3-month follow-up (p's<.05). However, only a reduction in fear of movement predicted functional disability at 12-months. Results support prioritizing strategies to reduce fear of movement in non-pharmacologic interventions for JFM which are associated with long-term improvements in function. PERSPECTIVE: Results of this study highlight the importance of assessing and addressing fear of movement among youth with widespread musculoskeletal pain. Treatments that include effective ways to improve movement confidence in adolescents with JFM may help optimize their long-term functional outcomes.

articles.title: Comparison of locomotor depression and spontaneous pain-related behaviors induced by colon and bladder visceral pain models in mice.
articles.abstract: Visceral pain is a prevalent class of pain states that can depress normal behavior and reduce quality of life. Behavioral recovery is a goal of treatment, but pharmacotherapy is challenging, and refinement of preclinical visceral-pain endpoints could facilitate evaluation of novel candidate analgesics. Accordingly, the goal of the present study was to evaluate expression and treatment of pain-related locomotor depression in mouse models of visceral pain. Intracolonic 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS) and intraperitoneal cyclophosphamide (CYP) modeled colon and bladder pain, respectively, and these organ-targeted models were compared to intraperitoneal lactic acid (IP acid) as another more extensively evaluated visceral-pain model. Locomotion by male and female ICR mice was assessed in chambers with two compartments separated by a wire-mesh barrier that could be surmounted to cross between compartments. Primary dependent measures were vertical locomotion between compartments (Crosses) and horizontal locomotion represented by the sum of photobeam breaks within each compartment (Movement). Hunched posture and facial grimace were assessed as supplemental pain behaviors, and sensitivity of pain-related behaviors to the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug ketoprofen and opioid agonist morphine were also examined. IP acid, TNBS, and CYP all produced depression of Crosses and Movement along with stimulation of hunched posture and grimace, although CYP effects were weaker than those of IP acid and TNBS. We have shown previously that IP acid effects can be blocked by ketoprofen and morphine, but both drugs were less effective against TNBS and CYP. The procedure described here could aid future efforts to discover improved pharmacotherapies for visceral pain. PERSPECTIVE: Visceral pain can depress normal behavior, and behavioral recovery is a treatment goal. This article compared locomotor depression produced by three visceral pain models in mice. All models depressed locomotion, but colon- and bladder-pain models were resistant to conventional analgesics. This procedure could aid development of improved visceral-pain pharmacotherapies.

articles.title: Monitoring the incidence of hypotension and hypoxemia as systemic secondary insults in patients with catastrophic brain injury evolving to brain death. A prospective observational pilot study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Maintenance of systemic homeostasis and prevention of secondary injury are a cornerstone of treatment in neurocritical care to prevent organ dysfunction and adverse clinical outcome. This is a pilot descriptive and hypothesis generating study aiming to measure and characterize the incidence of systemic hypotension and hypoxemia occurring during the intensive care unit (ICU) stay in patients with catastrophic brain injury potentially evolving to brain death.
METHODS: Adult patients admitted to ICU with catastrophic brain injury and Glasgow coma scale ≤5 have been enrolled. Arterial blood pressure and SpO2 were collected minute by minute from a central station connected to patients' bedside monitors.
RESULTS: We report on 24 patients recruited prospectively from the University Hospital of Messina, Italy as a part of a larger ongoing multi-centre study. Patient monitoring data ranged from 8-3000 hours (0.3-125 days). Admission diagnoses were intracerebral haemorrhage (N= 13), TBI (N=4), SAH (N=3), ischaemic stroke (N=3) and hypoxic encephalopathy (N=1). The proportion of valid monitoring time spent with secondary insults and the pressure time index (PTI) are presented and discussed. Day 3 and 4 demonstrated the largest number of secondary insults which were mainly hypotension. Patients who progressed to brain death (n = 9) or who died in ICU from cardiac complications (n = 7) exhibited a more severe and sustained hypotensive burden compared with patients alive at discharge (n = 8). This descriptive study proved useful for identifying an optimal window for tracking insults as well as piloting several key summary measures and visualisations which will be utilized in a larger multi-centre study.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with catastrophic brain injury, the incidence of hypotension remains the highest among systemic secondary insults in patients progressing to brain death and cardiac death.

articles.title: Predictors of Perioperative Patient Communications in Endoscopic Sinus Surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence and reasons for patient-initiated communications (PIC) in the perioperative period for outpatient endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) and identify patient or surgical factors associated with increased PIC.
METHODS: Retrospective chart review at a single tertiary care center performing outpatient endoscopic sinus surgery between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2023. Patient demographics, surgical characteristics, frequency of PIC, and reasons for perioperative PIC were recorded. The average number of communications, as well as the likelihood of engaging in PIC, were compared between patient, and surgical characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 167 patient charts were reviewed, among which 98 patients (59%) generated 149 PICs. Patients were 51% male, 33% had a smoking history, and 30% had a history of anxiety/depression. Most (84%) underwent primary surgery. Gender (OR 1.22; 95% CI 0.53-2.8) and smoking history (OR 1.80; 95% CI 0.71-4.7) were not associated with higher PIC frequency. PICs were more likely among patients with anxiety/depression (OR 11.9; 95% CI 4.0-35) and those who received nasal septal splints (OR 2.59; 95% CI 1.08-6.23). Preoperative PICs most commonly involved scheduling and recovery questions, while postoperative PICs were primarily related to nasal obstruction and epistaxis.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative PIC is frequent among ESS patients, particularly those with anxiety/depression or nasal splints. Understanding the most common communication triggers may guide quality improvement initiatives to pre-emptively address these concerns.

articles.title: Prehabilitation before thoracic surgery: do we need it, and does it make a difference?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Prehabilitation is increasingly used before thoracic surgery to increase physiological reserve, but whether improved functional capacity translates into better postoperative outcomes remains uncertain. This review examines the physiological rationale, recent evidence, and appropriate role of prehabilitation in noncardiac thoracic surgery.
RECENT FINDINGS: Preoperative exercise and multimodal programs consistently improve functional capacity, including 6-min walk distance and cardiopulmonary fitness. Thoracic-specific meta-analyses suggest reductions in postoperative pulmonary complications and hospital stay; however, individual randomized trials remain heterogeneous, and a recent fragility analysis of prehabilitation trials in cancer surgery showed that statistically positive complication outcomes typically hinged on a single event. Functional improvement does not necessarily mediate reductions in complex postoperative morbidity, and similar medium-term recovery may be achievable with postoperative rehabilitation. Optimal patient selection remains uncertain.
SUMMARY: Prehabilitation can increase physiological reserve, but it cannot neutralize the multidimensional stress of major noncardiac thoracic surgery. A risk-adapted approach is preferable to universal implementation. Prehabilitation should exploit an existing oncologically acceptable waiting period, avoid delaying definitive surgery, and be integrated with early postoperative rehabilitation.

articles.title: Protamine-to-heparin Ratio and Postoperative Bleeding in Complex Cardiac Surgery: A Post Hoc Analysis of the FARES-II Trial.
Liberal vs. conventional pre-operative clear fluid fasting policies in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised and non-randomised studies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pre-operative clear fluid fasting in children aims to reduce the risk of pulmonary aspiration. Recent studies have shown the safety of shorter clear fluid fasting durations. However, because pulmonary aspiration is rare, it remains uncertain whether the incidence differs between the liberal (< 2 h) and conventional (≥ 2 h) clear fluid fasting policies.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, performing comprehensive searches across five databases. We included studies with patients aged < 18 y who underwent general anaesthesia or sedation for surgery or procedures. Primary outcome was pulmonary aspiration and secondary outcome was vomiting without pulmonary aspiration. We performed meta-analyses to estimate pooled incidences according to fasting policy (< 2 h vs. ≥ 2 h).
RESULTS: We included 33 studies involving 580,197 patients. Twenty-nine studies (579,737 patients) reported pulmonary aspiration. The pooled incidence of pulmonary aspiration was 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with conventional fasting policies and 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with liberal policies. Risk ratios were available from 14 studies (475,399 patients) and showed no difference in pulmonary aspiration between policies (risk ratio 0.77, 95%CI 0.40-1.47). Seventeen studies (344,653 patients) reported vomiting; the pooled incidence was 0.99% (95%CI 0.27-3.51%) with conventional policies and 0.76% (95%CI 0.18-3.14%) with liberal policies. The certainty of evidence was very low for both outcomes.
DISCUSSION: Pulmonary aspiration is rare in children, and similar incidences of aspiration and vomiting were observed under liberal and conventional clear fluid fasting policies. The results should be interpreted cautiously due to the very low certainty of evidence.

articles.title: Advantages and Limitations of the Use of Robots in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Results From a Matched Direct Comparison.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the surgical outcomes of nonrobotic and robotic minimally invasive mitral valve repair.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair from January 2014 to March 2024. After excluding the learning curve cases, early and midterm outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 422 patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair (nonrobotic, n = 103; robotic, n = 319) were enrolled. The robotic group had a higher EuroSCORE II (P < 0.001). After propensity matching, the final cohort included 84 and 168 patients in each group. In the robotic group after matching, concomitant procedures remained significantly more frequent (P = 0.030). However, operative time (P = 0.782) and cross-clamping time (P = 0.452) were comparable, whereas cardiopulmonary bypass time was significantly longer in the robotic group (P = 0.031). Postoperative blood transfusion (P < 0.001), chest tube output within 24 h (P < 0.001), and intensive care unit stay (P = 0.042) remained higher in the robotic group after matching. Postoperative mitral regurgitation was no greater than mild in both groups (P = 0.146). At 4 years, overall survival was 94.4% versus 98.4% (P = 0.215), and freedom from recurrence of moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5% versus 97.9% (P = 0.230) after matching. These results are consistent with those observed before matching.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic mitral valve repair demonstrated comparable perioperative and midterm outcomes despite greater transfusion requirements and a higher frequency of concomitant procedures. The higher rate of concomitant procedures should be interpreted with caution because it may partly reflect differences in surgical era and patient selection.

articles.title: Differences between Japan and France in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the TOTO-TAVI study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The number of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures is increasing worldwide. However, studies comparing regional differences remain scarce.
AIMS: This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes after TAVI between Japan and France using a database compiled from two large hospitals.
METHODS: The TOTO-TAVI study included patients who underwent TAVI in Japan and France. The primary endpoint was in-hospital death. Periprocedural safety outcomes and 3-year all-cause mortality were also evaluated. A subgroup analysis was performed to assess the independent TAVI risk for each country.
RESULTS: Among 6,967 patients who underwent TAVI between 2016 and 2024, 1,422 in Japan and 4,771 in France were included. Although patients in Japan showed a significantly smaller body size, a smaller aortic valve, and a higher operative risk than those in France, the in-hospital death rate was comparable between the two groups (0.6% vs 1.3%; p=0.068). The new pacemaker implantation rate was lower in Japan than in France. There was no significant difference in 3-year all-cause mortality between Japan and France (22.5% vs 23.5%, hazard ratio 0.678, 95% confidence interval: 0.114-4.033; p=0.583). For the subgroup analysis, there were no statistically significant independent risk factors for composite outcomes, including in-hospital death, stroke, and bleeding, in Japan; however, in France, female sex, higher body mass index, lower haemoglobin levels, previous coronary artery bypass grafting and cerebrovascular disease, bicuspid annulus, and general anaesthesia were independent risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite differences in patient backgrounds, in-hospital and 3-year mortality were comparable between Japan and France, suggesting that procedural safety and medium-term prognosis after TAVI were established regardless of procedural risks.

articles.title: Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy-Guided Bronchial Blocker Placement in Lateral Versus Supine Positions in Video-Assisted Thoracic Surgery: A Comparative Study.
articles.abstract: Bronchial blockers (BBs) are widely used for one-lung ventilation during video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), but malposition remains a common cause of repeated fiberoptic bronchoscopy (FOB) examinations and procedural inefficiency. Whether BB placement performed directly in the lateral decubitus position improves device stability and perioperative outcomes remains unclear. Clinical data from adult patients undergoing elective unilateral VATS with BB-assisted one-lung ventilation were analyzed to compare lateral-position BB placement with the conventional supine approach followed by repositioning. Patients were categorized according to the position used during BB deployment. BB malposition occurred less frequently in the lateral group than in the supine group (12.5% vs 30.8%; relative risk [RR] 0.41, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.23-0.72; p = 0.001). Lateral placement was associated with shorter BB placement time (3.8 ± 0.9 vs 5.6 ± 1.2 min; p < 0.001), fewer FOB examinations (1.3 ± 0.3 vs 2.1 ± 0.5; p < 0.001), and a shorter anesthesia-to-incision interval (18.4 ± 3.5 vs 24.7 ± 4.2 min; p < 0.001). Intraoperative oxygenation was improved (arterial partial pressure of oxygen [PaO2]: 186.5 ± 22.4 vs 158.3 ± 25.1 mmHg; p < 0.001), accompanied by lower peak airway pressures (23.4 ± 3.1 vs 26.8 ± 3.6 cmH2O; p < 0.001) and fewer hypoxemic events. Postoperative sore throat, hoarseness, hypoxemia, and airway mucosal injury occurred less frequently in the lateral group (all p < 0.05). In conclusion, BB placement in the lateral decubitus position was associated with greater device stability, improved procedural efficiency, and fewer airway-related complications. Aligning BB deployment with the final surgical position may provide a practical strategy to optimize lung isolation during minimally invasive thoracic surgery.

articles.title: Establishment and Optimization of a Mouse Model of Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) severely impairs cardiac prognosis after revascularization for acute myocardial infarction. Standardized mouse left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) ligation models are widely used for MIRI research, yet conventional protocols rely on indwelling support tubes and secondary thoracotomy to restore reperfusion. Such procedures feature complicated operations, high risks of pneumothorax, severe thoracic trauma, and low batch modeling efficiency. To address these drawbacks, we established an optimized MIRI mouse model with a single thoracotomy and carbon-synthesis fishing line pull-out for reperfusion. Male C57BL/6 mice aged 6-8 weeks were divided into normal control (NC), traditional model (TM), and optimized model (OM) groups. Echocardiography, triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) and hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, as well as serum inflammatory cytokines, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), c-reactive protein (CRP), and myocardial injury marker cardiac troponin I (cTnI) levels were detected to compare modeling efficacy. Identical cardiac function, serum inflammatory cytokines, myocardial injury marker, infarct size, and myocardial pathological morphology changes were observed between TM and OM groups. The OM group displayed more homogeneous infarct regions and higher serum myocardial injury markers and cardiac function injury, indicating milder non-surgical trauma. Compared with the traditional method, this optimized procedure shortens surgical and anesthesia time, avoids fatal intraoperative pneumothorax, accelerates post-operative recovery, and improves animal survival. In conclusion, the optimized model produces equivalent MIRI lesions with higher safety, efficiency, and reproducibility. It serves as an ideal alternative to classic modeling approaches.

articles.title: Perioperative Cerebral Metabolism in Patients Under General Anaesthesia With Sevoflurane or Propofol: Evaluation of the Arterial and Jugular Bulb Metabolome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Arterial serum was generally used to uncover shifts in the metabolic profile induced by surgery and anaesthesia. The specific perioperative metabolic alterations in the brain remain largely unknown. We aimed to detect perioperative changes in cerebral metabolism by arteriovenous gradients of circulating metabolites across the brain using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis.
METHODS: The prospective study was conducted at Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital, China. Twenty patients with unilateral pulmonary lesion were recruited. Patients undergoing thoracic surgery were randomised to receive general anaesthesia with sevoflurane or propofol. Blood samples from radial artery and jugular bulb were collected before and after first anaesthetic administration, at the end of 60 min of maintenance of anaesthesia and 60 min after patients regained consciousness. LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics strategies were used to determine the difference in abundance of circulating metabolites between artery and jugular bulb.
RESULTS: A total of 3900 metabolites were detected. Potential critical alterations of metabolites including phosphatidylcholine (PC), phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), choline, isocitrate and lactate and pathways were identified. Brain took up PC and PE in group sevoflurane but secreted these compounds in group propofol. Additionally, propofol was associated with the release of choline and isocitrate from brain. In both groups, lactic acid entered brain intraoperatively.
CONCLUSION: This work may offer a comprehensive mapping of perioperative alterations of cerebral metabolism in patients under general anaesthesia and a new direction for further studies in pharmacology of general anaesthetics and pathogenesis of perioperative brain dysfunction. Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2500111204.

articles.title: Vaginal Septum Resection Technique for Optimizing Fertility in Mice.
articles.abstract: A vaginal septum is a congenital anomaly in which a fibrous tissue band divides the vaginal canal longitudinally. Humans diagnosed with vaginal septum may suffer negative effects on fertility and childbirth. Similarly, mice with a vaginal septum may exhibit poor fertility, prolonged breeding times, and labor dystocia. High rates of vaginal septum in some mouse colonies, with reports as high as 38%, can delay breeding programs and increase animal housing costs. To address this problem, we developed a surgical approach to remove the septum and restore reproductive function in affected mice. Female mice from our colony were screened at 6-8 weeks of age and assigned to three groups: septum resection, septum without resection, and nonseptate controls. Septal tissue was excised under general anesthesia using microscissors and a dissection microscope. Compared with septate mice that did not undergo surgery, mice that underwent resection had higher copulatory plug rates (82% vs. 46%, p < 0.05), higher pregnancy rates after 30 days of breeding (95% vs. 36%, p < 0.0001), higher pregnancy rates after 75 days of breeding (100% vs. 72%, p < 0.01), and a shorter time to pregnancy (p < 0.01). Mice that underwent septum resection showed normalization of reproductive outcomes, including copulatory plug rates and pregnancy rates, to levels comparable to the nonseptate control mice. This suggests that resection of a longitudinal vaginal septum can restore reproductive performance in affected mice while reducing breeding delays, resource use, and animal waste in laboratory colonies.

articles.title: Continuous-Flow Left Ventricular Assist Devices in Biventricular Configuration: A Systematic Review and Comparative Meta-Analysis of HeartMate 3 and HeartWare Biventricular Assist Devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced biventricular heart failure may require durable biventricular assist device (BiVAD) support when heart transplantation is not immediately feasible or patients are ineligible for heart transplantation. We aimed to compare baseline characteristics, perioperative features, and clinical outcomes between patients supported with HeartMate 3-BiVAD (HM3-BiVAD) and HeartWare-BiVAD (HW-BiVAD).
METHODS: A systematic search was performed in October 2025 across MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and CINAHL. We identified studies of adult patients supported with dual HeartMate 3 LVAD and HeartWare HVAD continuous-flow pumps in a BiVAD configuration. Study-level data were pooled to compare patients supported with HM3-BiVAD and those with HW-BiVAD.
RESULTS: The proportion of females was significantly lower among HM3-BiVAD patients [HM3: 4.8% (95% CI: 1.2, 17.1) vs. HW: 22.5% (16.8, 29.4), p = 0.02], whereas patient age was comparable between groups [HM3: 47 (43, 52) years vs. HW: 48 (45, 50) years, p = 0.9]. Chronic kidney disease [HM3: 57.1% (23, 85.6) vs. HW: 10.9% (4.6, 23.6), p = 0.01] was more common among HM3-BiVAD patients. Concomitant right ventricular assist device (RVAD) placement was the predominant approach across both groups [HM3: 66.2% (35.5, 87.4) vs. HW: 78.5% (70.1, 85), p = 0.36]. Right atrium was used more frequently as RVAD implantation site in the HM3-BiVAD group [HM3: 96.7% (63.4, 99.8) vs. HW: 33.9% (19, 52.9), p = 0.01], whereas the right ventricle predominated in the HW-BiVAD group [HM3: 3.2% (0.2, 36.6) vs. HW: 64.5% (45.2, 80.1), p = 0.01]. Overall survival was significantly higher among HM3-BiVAD patients [78.1% (49.3, 92.9)] compared to HW-BiVAD patients [48% (40.6, 55.4); p = 0.05]. The mean follow-up was 274 (200, 349) days in patients with HM3-BiVAD and 210 (143, 277) days in HW-BiVAD patients (p = 0.21).
CONCLUSION: Patients with HW-BiVAD were characterized by a higher proportion of females and more frequent use of the RV as the RVAD implantation site, likely both due to the smaller device profile. HM3-BiVAD patients demonstrated higher post-implant survival despite a more severe preimplant clinical profile, suggesting a possible device-related advantage.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Added to Hyperventilation Improves Surgical Field Visibility Without Compromising Cerebral Oxygenation During Endoscopic Sinus Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal surgical field visibility is essential during endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), yet strategies that reduce bleeding may raise concern about impaired cerebral oxygenation. We evaluated whether adding dexmedetomidine to hyperventilation improves surgical field visibility during ESS without compromising cerebral oxygenation.
METHODS: In this double-blinded randomized controlled trial, 74 patients with chronic rhinosinusitis undergoing ESS were randomly assigned to receive dexmedetomidine plus hyperventilation or hyperventilation alone. The primary endpoint was the Boezaart surgical field score assessed 30 min after the start of surgery. Secondary endpoints were intraoperative cerebral oxygen saturation (ScO2), bleeding rate, hemodynamic variables, anesthetic consumption, and postoperative recovery outcomes.
RESULTS: Compared with hyperventilation alone, dexmedetomidine plus hyperventilation improved surgical field visibility, with a lower Boezaart score at 30 min after surgery onset (2.0 (1.0-2.0) vs. 3.0 (2.0-3.0), p = 0.003). Longitudinal analysis further demonstrated that dexmedetomidine plus hyperventilation was associated with lower odds of poorer surgical field scores over time (OR = 0.180, 95% CI, 0.062-0.524; p = 0.002). The bleeding rate was lower with dexmedetomidine plus hyperventilation, whereas intraoperative ScO2 was comparable between groups and no cerebral desaturation events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing ESS, adding dexmedetomidine to hyperventilation improved surgical field visibility without compromising intraoperative cerebral oxygenation. This combined strategy may help optimize operative conditions in ESS.

articles.title: A Surgical Protocol for Infraorbital Nerve Chronic Constriction Injury in Mice.
articles.abstract: Trigeminal neuropathic pain arises from injury to sensory pathways of the trigeminal system and is associated with persistent changes in neuronal excitability, gene expression, and pain-related behaviors. Infraorbital nerve chronic constriction injury (IoN-CCI) is a widely used model for investigating the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying chronic orofacial neuropathic pain. This video demonstrates a surgical approach for IoN-CCI in adult mice by placing a single controlled constrictive ligature around the infraorbital nerve while preserving the gross anatomical continuity of the nerve. The protocol includes preoperative preparation, anesthesia and analgesia, extraoral exposure of the infraorbital nerve, placement and tightening of the ligature, wound closure, perioperative care, and postoperative monitoring. The ligature is tightened under magnification until a mild indentation is visible without complete nerve occlusion, transection, or discoloration. Key procedural considerations include accurate nerve identification, consistent ligature placement and tension, and standardized postoperative care. Related IoN-CCI paradigms have been associated with long-lasting mechanical hypersensitivity and molecular changes within trigeminal ganglion neurons. This protocol provides a detailed method for studying mechanisms associated with trigeminal nerve injury and chronic orofacial neuropathic pain.

articles.title: Salvage Use of Sotatercept for Potts Shunt in Refractory Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract: The reverse Potts shunt (RPS) is a promising palliative intervention for pediatric patients with drug-refractory severe pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet it carries substantial risks of perioperative mortality and hemodynamic instability. We report two high-risk pediatric female patients who developed acute hemodynamic instability and recurrent pulmonary hypertensive crises following successful percutaneous RPS creation. Despite maximal targeted triple therapy and vasoactive support, no sustained improvement was observed. Following multidisciplinary consensus, a single salvage dose of sotatercept (0.3 mg/kg) was administered. Both patients demonstrated rapid, hemodynamic stabilization within 48 h, enabling the swift withdrawal of vasoactive support and inhaled nitric oxide within 1 week. Follow-up echocardiography revealed significant recovery of right ventricular function, and both patients were successfully weaned off treprostinil. These findings suggest that short-term perioperative sotatercept can serve as an effective acute rescue therapy to safeguard high-risk surgical interventions in critical pediatric PAH.

articles.title: Timing, dose, and Behavioral engagement in perioperative Behavioral activation: a secondary analysis of predictors of improvement in a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression and anxiety are associated with poor outcomes in older adults undergoing surgery. Perioperative psychological interventions may improve symptoms, but the optimal dose, timing, and therapeutic processes remain unclear.
METHODS: This secondary analysis examined the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial. Participants were aged ≥60, scheduled for cardiac, oncologic, or orthopedic surgeries, and had clinically meaningful depression and/or anxiety symptoms on the Patient Health Questionnaire-Anxiety Depression Scale (PHQ-ADS). Analyses included participants who completed baseline and 3-month assessments. Associations between intervention components and changes in PHQ-ADS, PHQ-9 depression and GAD-7 anxiety scores were evaluated across four a priori domains: intervention dose and perioperative timing, behavioral engagement through activity plan enactment, implementation quality and target engagement through measures of activation, compassion, and surgical preparedness scores.
RESULTS: Among 138 intervention participants, greater intervention dose was associated with larger reductions in anxiety at 3 months. Pre-operative initiation was consistently associated with symptom improvement. Participants completing ≥3 pre-operative sessions had a 6.05-point greater reduction in PHQ-ADS than those completing none (p = .003). Greater mean activity-plan completion was associated with larger reductions in PHQ-ADS (b = -2.42, SE = 1.00, p = .02), PHQ-9 (b = -1.35, SE = 0.65, p = .04), and GAD-7 scores (b = -1.07, SE = 0.53, p = .05).
CONCLUSIONS: More sessions, earlier initiation, and greater behavioral engagement of patients were associated with greater reductions in depression and anxiety. Initiating behavioral activation before surgery and supporting activity-plan enactment may improve postoperative depression and anxiety symptoms for older surgical patients. Limitations include lack of random assignment to the variables studied and single-site population.

articles.title: Role of Mitochondrial Impairment in Sepsis-Induced Platelet Activation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sepsis-induced mitochondrial impairment has been described in different organs, in both animal models and humans. Excessive radical oxygen species (ROS) could be involved in this phenomenon. As a result, antioxidants have been proposed as a potential therapeutic strategy, although results remain controversial. Platelet hyperactivation is considered a central pathogenic mechanism in the development of sepsis-induced organ damage. In this study, we aimed to determine whether mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to platelet hyperactivation during sepsis. We also evaluated the effect of ROS scavenging using the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO.
DESIGN: Laboratory investigation.
SETTING: University Hospital.
PATIENTS AND SUBJECTS: Patients with sepsis/septic shock (n = 3/7), nonseptic burn patients (n = 10), and healthy control subjects (n = 10).
INTERVENTIONS: Platelet mitochondria and isolated platelets from healthy donors were treated in vitro with plasma from patients with sepsis/septic shock and healthy subjects, before and after preincubation with MitoTEMPO.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We measured platelet oxygen consumption rates in isolated human platelets using the Seahorse Extracellular Flux Analyzer. Platelet mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity was measured in mitochondria-enriched fractions by spectrophotometry. Platelet aggregation in platelet-rich plasma was analyzed using light-transmission aggregometry, and leukocyte-platelet adhesion in whole blood by flow cytometry.We found that incubating platelets with septic plasma significantly reduced basal, maximal, and adenosine triphosphate-linked oxygen consumption rate. Incubation of platelet mitochondria with septic plasma also reduced platelet Complex I activity, compared with healthy plasma or plasma from nonseptic burn patients. This decrease was associated with an increase in Epinephrine-induced platelet activation. Preincubating platelets with the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO significantly reversed these effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results show that the mitochondria-selective ROS scavenger MitoTEMPO prevents mitochondrial dysfunction and enhances platelet activation induced by septic plasma in human platelets in vitro. This may help in designing new therapeutic approaches to prevent sepsis-induced organ damage mediated by mitochondrial dysfunction and platelet hyperactivation.

articles.title: Effectiveness and safety of adjunct interventions for external cephalic version in breech presentation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunct and implementation-related strategies associated with external cephalic version (ECV) in pregnant women with breech presentation.
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials comparing adjunct or protocol-based strategies related to ECV (including pharmacological tocolysis, neuraxial anesthesia or analgesia, systemic analgesia, or timing/procedural approaches) with standard care, placebo, or expectant management were included.
SEARCH STRATEGY: MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and LILACS were searched from inception to February 2026.
DATA SELECTION AND EXTRACTION: Data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled using risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) under random-effects models.
RESULTS: Ten randomized controlled trials comprising 2,745 randomized women were included; 2,722 contributed complete outcome data to the primary meta-analysis. Adjunct and implementation-related strategies were associated with higher ECV success rates (RR 1.53; 95% CI 1.15-2.04; I² = 87%). Pharmacological tocolysis demonstrated the largest effect (RR 2.39; 95% CI 1.39-4.11), followed by neuraxial anesthesia (RR 1.75; 95% CI 1.07-2.85) and systemic analgesia (RR 1.39; 95% CI 1.15-1.69). Protocol-based strategies did not significantly improve success rates. No statistically significant reduction in cesarean delivery was observed (RR 0.88; 95% CI 0.76-1.02). Serious maternal and neonatal complications were uncommon.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjunct and implementation-related strategies, particularly pharmacological tocolysis and neuraxial anesthesia, increase the likelihood of successful ECV. Although the effect on cesarean delivery remains inconclusive, ECV appears safe when performed in appropriate clinical settings.

articles.title: Autophagy and Inflammation in Cardiothoracic Surgery: The Mechanisms of Perioperative Lung Injury and Therapeutic Opportunities.
articles.abstract: Autophagy is a lysosome-dependent stress-response pathway that maintains cellular homeostasis through the degradation and recycling of damaged proteins, dysfunctional organelles, and other cytoplasmic components. In the lung, autophagy is closely linked to inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial quality control, oxidative stress, epithelial barrier integrity, and immune-cell activation. These processes are highly relevant to respiratory diseases and perioperative pulmonary injury because hypoxia, mechanical stretch, ischemia-reperfusion, hyperoxia, infection-related stress, and systemic inflammation may alter autophagic flux. Context-dependent autophagic responses may protect lung tissue by limiting mitochondrial damage and excessive inflammatory activation, whereas impaired pathway completion may promote persistent reactive oxygen species production, endothelial and epithelial injury, fibroblast activation, and maladaptive tissue remodeling. In cardiothoracic surgery, lung resection, one-lung ventilation, cardiopulmonary bypass, and transplantation are clinically relevant settings in which autophagy-inflammation crosstalk may affect postoperative pulmonary complications and organ recovery. Here, we present a perioperative, flux-centered framework that distinguishes stress-induced initiation from autophagosome-lysosome fusion and lysosomal degradation. The framework integrates AMPK-mTORC1-ULK1 signaling with TFEB-dependent lysosomal biogenesis, FOXO transcriptional control, selective mitophagy, and downstream NLRP3, NF-κB, and cytokine responses. Human studies demonstrate biological heterogeneity but rarely measure dynamic flux; LC3-II, p62/SQSTM1, Beclin-1, or ATG abundance alone cannot establish pathway completion. Translational studies should use serial, compartment-aware autophagy-lysosome, mitochondrial-injury, and inflammatory readouts linked to standardized pulmonary outcomes. Major priorities include cell-resolved perioperative phenotyping, harmonized reporting of flux uncertainty, prospective one-lung-ventilation and cardiopulmonary-bypass cohorts, and short, mechanism-matched intervention studies with explicit safety endpoints.

articles.title: Radical versus simple trachelectomy for fertility preservation in early-stage cervical cancer: a retrospective cohort study based on propensity score inverse probability of treatment weighting.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare oncologic, perioperative, and reproductive outcomes between simple trachelectomy (ST) and radical trachelectomy (RT) in patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) 2018 stage IB1-IB2 cervical cancer.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study including FIGO 2018 stage IB1-IB2 cervical cancer patients with negative lymph nodes and margins who underwent RT or ST between January 2010 and December 2023. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Primary outcome was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary outcomes included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative hospitalization, antibiotic-therapy days, and postoperative laboratory changes, and pregnancy/obstetric outcomes among patients who intended to conceive.
RESULTS: Among 45 patients (RT, n=23; ST, n=22), measured covariate balance was substantially improved after weighting. Median follow-up was 47 months, with two recurrences in the ST group. No statistically significant difference in PFS was detected between groups after weighting (p=0.148). ST was associated with shorter operative time (p<0.001), less intraoperative blood loss (p<0.001), fewer antibiotic-therapy days (p<0.001), smaller increases in white blood cell count (p=0.036) and C-reactive protein (p<0.001), and less albumin decline (p=0.018). Among 15 patients with pregnancy intention, successful pregnancies were observed in 1/6 (16.7%) in the RT group and 3/9 (33.3%) in the ST group.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in PFS was detected between ST and RT in this limited cohort. ST was associated with lower perioperative burden, while reproductive findings were descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective or multicenter studies with standardized selection criteria and fertility follow-up are needed, particularly for IB2 disease.

articles.title: Mortality after ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus and its clinical predictors.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) often have comorbid conditions that may adversely impact survival, but long-term mortality risk in this population remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Patients who underwent VPS placement for iNPH at a single tertiary care center between 2017 and 2025 were identified. Comorbidities, demographic characteristics, and perioperative complications were evaluated using univariable Cox regression analyses to identify factors associated with mortality at the last follow-up. Comorbidities were quantified with the modified Frailty Index-5 (mFI-5) and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).
RESULTS: 452 patients were included (median age, 75.3 years; 61.9% male). Forty-four (9.7%) died during follow-up (median 39.1 months), with a median postoperative survival of 19.8 months and a median age at death of 78.4 years. Median mFI-5 was 1.0 and median CCI was 2.0. Baseline comorbidities in total cohort included prior myocardial infarction (MI) in 5.8% of patients, congestive heart failure (CHF) in 6.9%, cerebrovascular accident (CVA) in 14.4%, dementia in 27.1%, and functional dependence in 54.9%. At presentation, 96.0% had gait impairment, 84.5% had cognitive deficits, and 81.6% had urinary incontinence. Regarding perioperative outcomes, 57 patients (12.6%) were hospitalized more than one day and 30 (6.7%) required non-home discharge. Postoperative subdural fluid collections occurred in 13.6% of patients, while 6.9% underwent shunt revision. On multivariable Cox regression analysis, higher CCI (HR 1.27, p = 0.005) and hospitalization >1 day (HR 3.20, p = 0.001) were independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: Nontrivial rates of mortality are seen following VPS in iNPH - approximately estimated at 10% over four years in the present study. Increased mortality appears correlated with more extensive comorbidities and poorer functional status, highlighting the importance of careful patient selection in this frail population. Notably, this mortality rate closely approximates the mortality expected on an actuarial basis for an age- and sex-matched general population and is substantially lower than mortality previously reported for patients with mild cognitive impairment, suggesting that VPS may mitigate the excess mortality otherwise anticipated in this population.

articles.title: General anesthesia is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anesthetic management of hip fracture fixation has two primary modalities: general anesthesia (GA) and spinal anesthesia (SA). Choice of anesthesia often depends on institutional protocols and the individual anesthesiologist, due to a lack of consensus guidelines. Most studies have conflicting evidence and focus primarily on elderly age as a risk factor, without accounting for frailty. This study investigates whether frailty influences the relationship between anesthetic modality and postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective study queried the ACS-NSQIP from 2015 to 2020 for patients who underwent hip fracture fixation with open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws or intramedullary implant insertion. Patients were separated based on whether they received GA or SA. Frailty was evaluated using the 5-Item Modified Frailty Index (mFI-5). Patients classified as frail or severely frail were included. Multivariable regression adjusting for age, sex, ASA classification, smoking, and the comorbidities significant on univariate regression was performed. The outcomes examined were mortality, unplanned readmission, and overall complications within 30 days postoperatively.
RESULTS: This study included 24,401 patients under GA and 6193 patients under SA. On multivariable regression analysis, GA was independently associated with increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications among frail patients. Severely frail patients under GA had increased odds of unplanned readmission and all complications. When looking at both frail and severely frail patients together, GA remained a significant predictor of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications.
DISCUSSION: After controlling for ASA classification, our study found that frail and severely frail patients undergoing GA for hip fracture fixation had significantly increased odds of mortality, unplanned readmission, and all complications. Our findings suggest that SA may be safer compared to GA in frail patients undergoing hip fracture fixation. Frail patients that undergo GA may benefit from increased postoperative monitoring to help mitigate complications.

articles.title: Comparison of feasibility, inter-instrument agreement, and prognostic value of four frailty assessment instruments in geriatric colorectal cancer patients: a 3-year multicenter prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although multiple instruments exist to assess frailty, it remains unclear whether the association between frailty and clinical outcomes in older colorectal cancer (CRC) patients varies by the assessment tool used. Accordingly, the aim of this study was to compare the feasibility and clinical utility of four common frailty scales in this patient population.
METHODS: We conducted a 3-year prospective cohort study involving geriatric patients (≥65 years) with CRC. Preoperative frailty was assessed using four established scales: the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), the Frailty Phenotype (FP), the Geriatric-8 (G-8) scale, and the 32-item Frailty Index (FI). The differences in the perioperative outcomes and postoperative one-year all-cause mortality rate were compared across the four scoring systems.
RESULTS: A total of 1,096 patients were included in the primary analysis. The effective response rates and median completion times for the four frailty scales were as follows: CFS (91.1%; 6 min), FP (65.7%; 10 min), G-8 (71.6%; 8 min), and 32-item FI (58.3%; 18 min). The final analysis included 615 patients who completed all assessments. Frailty prevalence was estimated at 27.0% (CFS), 23.6% (FP), 33.0% (G-8), and 36.9% (FI). The four frailty scales demonstrated good predictive efficacy for postoperative clinically relevant complications, postoperative recovery, 30-day readmission, and one-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that the G-8 scale (OR = 2.412, 95%CI: 1.300-4.474, P = 0.008) and 32-item FI (OR = 3.035, 95%CI: 1.359-6.779, P = 0.017) served as independent risk factors for postoperative clinically relevant complications. Only the 32-item FI emerged as an independent predictor of 1-year all-cause mortality (HR = 2.777, 95%CI: 1.247-6.218, P = 0.020).
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, all four frailty scales demonstrated robust discriminatory capacity for clinical outcomes in older CRC patients. Although the 32-item FI exhibited a stronger independent correlation with adverse outcomes following multivariate adjustment, its clinical utility must be weighed against a longer administration time. This study provides crucial evidence to guide the selection of an appropriate frailty assessment tool based on specific clinical contexts.

articles.title: Healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding perioperative ischemic stroke in elderly patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to perioperative ischemic stroke in elderly patients.
METHODS: A single-center, cross-sectional survey was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Ningxia, China, between 1 March 2025 and 1 June 2025. Healthcare professionals were recruited by convenience sampling and completed a structured questionnaire covering demographic information and their KAP regarding perioperative ischemic stroke.
RESULTS: A total of 273 valid responses were included in the final analysis. The majority of respondents were physicians (75.46%), with most affiliated with anesthesiology departments (86.08%). The scores for knowledge, attitude, and practice were 14.41 ± 4.22 (possible range: 0-20), 36.77 ± 3.57 (possible range: 8-40), and 30.07 ± 6.51 (possible range: 8-40), respectively. Structural equation modeling showed that knowledge, attitude, and practice were positively interrelated, whereas training related to perioperative ischemic stroke and specialization in elderly patient care showed negative associations with knowledge or practice (β range: -0.287 to 0.352; all P < 0.05). Knowledge was also indirectly associated with practice through attitude, whereas training and specialization in elderly care showed negative indirect associations with attitude and practice.
CONCLUSION: Healthcare professionals exhibited inadequate perceived knowledge, positive attitudes, and suboptimal practices regarding perioperative ischemic stroke in elderly patients. These findings underscore the necessity for targeted, evidence-based educational interventions to strengthen knowledge awareness and practice-related competencies, thereby addressing the observed gaps between perceived knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices.

articles.title: Combined aromatherapy and music or sound for emotional distress: a systematic review of controlled studies published between 2019 and 2026.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emotional distress is common around clinical procedures, cancer supportive care, and health-professions training. Aromatherapy and music are easy to deliver, yet it remains unclear when combining them is worthwhile and whether the combination offers more than either component alone.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize experimental studies of aromatherapy combined with music or sound published from January 2019 through September 7, 2026; identify the populations and settings in which benefits were most consistent; and separate benefit over inactive care from incremental benefit over a single sensory intervention.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, APA PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, CENTRAL, CNKI, and Dentistry & Oral Sciences Source from January 1, 2019, to September 7, 2026. Randomized trials and controlled nonrandomized or quasi-experimental studies were eligible when they included an identifiable arm combining aromatherapy with music or sound and reported emotional-distress or related physiological outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesized narratively using SWiM guidance.
RESULTS: Twenty-four studies involving 2,530 participants from 12 countries or regions were included. Of these, 21 were randomized studies and three were controlled nonrandomized or quasi-experimental studies. The evidence covered procedural and perioperative care, dentistry, nursing education and occupational stress, and cancer or palliative care. Results were most consistent in pediatric dentistry, magnetic resonance imaging, nursing examinations or skills testing, and some repeated cancer-support programs. Two lithotripsy trials and the adult endodontic study did not show a clear benefit. Although combined treatment often outperformed inactive care, it frequently failed to outperform aromatherapy or music alone. Adverse events, acceptability, and economic outcomes were poorly reported.
CONCLUSION: Combined aromatherapy and music or sound showed the most consistent reductions in anxiety or distress in pediatric dentistry, MRI examinations, nursing examinations or skills training, and some perioperative and cancer-support settings. Clear benefit was not demonstrated in lithotripsy or endodontic care; in general surgery, pregnancy non-stress testing, coronary angiography, palliative care, and outpatient oncology, the combination generally did not outperform a single modality. Future adequately powered factorial trials should standardize the interventions and use prespecified between-group comparisons, longer follow-up, and systematic reporting of adverse events and costs.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024570691, CRD42024570691.

articles.title: The correlation between surgical, anaesthetic and obstetric workforce and surgical volume: a modelling study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Lancet Commission on Global Surgery has stated that two-thirds of the world's population does not have adequate access to surgical and anaesthesia care. Surgical, Obstetric and Anaesthetic (SAO) workforce and surgical volume (SV) are two of the six indicators recommended for monitoring and planning. This study aims to examine the correlation between SAO density and SV at the national level.
METHODOLOGY: A cross-sectional ecological regression study was conducted with SAO workforce per 100,000 population and SV per 100,000 population, extracted from the World Bank Database. Countries that reported both indicators were included. If SAO was not available for the corresponding SV year, it was adjusted according to the population growth. A logarithmic regression model was used to describe the nonlinear association between SAO workforce density and surgical volume with SPSS. Model fit (R2) analysis, diagnostics, and a model implied marginal slope analysis were conducted.
RESULT: A total of 57 countries were included, with 37 (64.9%) requiring adjustment. The fitted logarithmic regression model (y = 884 ln(x) + 685) had an R2 of 0.524. At an SAO density of 10 per 100,000 population, the fitted model predicted approximately 2720 procedures per 100,000 population. At 20 and 40 SAO, 3333.7 (95% CI for fitted mean: 2917.2-3750.2) and 3946.5 (95% CI for fitted mean: 3470.7-4,422.3) procedures are expected, respectively. The marginal slope analysis of our model was progressively smaller at higher SAO densities.
CONCLUSION: This study provides empirical insights into the nonlinear relationship between SAO workforce density and surgical volume. The findings highlight the need to balance workforce expansion with wider health-system capacity and may contribute to the future development of more informative surgical planning and performance indicators.

articles.title: A Puzzling Left-to-Right Flow After Transcatheter Atrial Septal Defect Closure in a Child.
Development and internal validation of explainable machine learning models for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Early ambulation is a notable component of postoperative recovery after cesarean delivery, but some women fail to complete first ambulation within the early postoperative period because of pain, dizziness, orthostatic discomfort, residual lower limb numbness, nausea or vomiting, hypotension or poor activity tolerance. Early identification of women at high risk of ambulation failure may support timely and individualized nursing interventions. The present study aimed to develop and internally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery using routinely collected obstetric perioperative nursing assessment data. The present single-center retrospective cohort study included relatively stable women who underwent cesarean delivery between January 2022 and December 2025 and were considered clinically eligible for early mobilization. The primary outcome was failure of first ambulation within 12 h after surgery, defined as no documented successful ambulation within 12 h or discontinuation of an ambulation attempt because of nursing-documented intolerance. Candidate predictors included demographic, obstetric, pregnancy-related, laboratory, anesthetic, surgical and early postoperative nursing assessment variables. Postoperative symptoms and vital signs were assessed within predefined early postoperative intervals, whereas first turning time was treated as a dynamically updated indicator that became available when the first spontaneous or assisted turning event was documented. The model was therefore interpreted as a dynamic early postoperative risk-assessment approach rather than a prediction model applied exclusively at a fixed 4-h time point. The final analytic dataset contained no item-level missing values; therefore, no imputation was performed. The cohort was randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts at a ratio of 7:3. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and LightGBM models were developed and compared. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, classification metrics, calibration, Brier score and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the final model. A total of 1,486 women were included, and 326 women experienced failure of first ambulation within 12 h, with an incidence of 21.9%. The training and validation cohorts included 1,040 and 446 women, respectively. In the validation cohort, LightGBM achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.809 and a Brier score of 0.132, whereas XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.805 and a Brier score of 0.134. The paired DeLong test showed no statistically significant difference between the validation AUCs of the two models (P=0.647). XGBoost achieved higher sensitivity, negative predictive value and F1 score than LightGBM (0.714 vs. 0.653, 0.906 vs. 0.892 and 0.567 vs. 0.561, respectively). Because these metrics were particularly relevant to identifying high-risk women and minimizing missed high-risk cases, XGBoost was selected as the final model. Calibration curves showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks, and decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit across relevant threshold probabilities. The 10 highest-ranked predictors according to mean absolute SHAP value were postoperative pain NRS score at 2 h, emergency cesarean delivery, time to first documented turning, lower limb numbness within 0-4 h, systolic blood pressure at 2 h, body mass index, preoperative hemoglobin, age, intraoperative fluid volume and dizziness or orthostatic discomfort within 0-4 h. In conclusion, in the present single-center retrospective cohort of relatively stable women considered clinically eligible for early mobilization, the explainable XGBoost model showed promising internal performance for predicting failure of first ambulation within 12 h after cesarean delivery. The model should not be extrapolated to women transferred to intensive care, women with severe postpartum hemorrhage, women with explicit medical restrictions on ambulation or women with severe postoperative complications. These findings support further evaluation but do not establish clinical utility, transportability or readiness for implementation. Temporal and external validation, followed by prospective assessment of workflow feasibility and clinical impact, is required before clinical use can be considered.

articles.title: Closed Versus Open Vent Port Techniques and the Disconnection Technique for Optimizing Lung Collapse With Bronchial Blockers in Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for lung cancer or other pulmonary lesions, effective one-lung ventilation (OLV) is essential to provide surgical exposure. Bronchial blockers (BBs) are increasingly used for OLV, but the optimal management of their vent port to accelerate lung collapse remains unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, controlled trial, 75 patients were allocated to three groups (n = 25 each): Group 1-BB with vent port closed; Group 2 (control)-BB with vent port open; Group 3-BB with the disconnection technique. Primary outcome was the time to complete lung collapse, which was scored according to the video clips obtained during the operation. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hypoxemia, blood gas analysis, blocker malposition, perioperative complications, and surgeon satisfaction.
RESULTS: A total of 72 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, with 24 patients in each group. Median time to complete lung collapse was 15 min (95% CI: 10-15) in Groups 1 and 3 but was not reached in Group 2 (15/24, 62.5% had not achieved complete collapse by 30 min). In an exploratory 30-min restricted mean survival time (RMST), complete collapse occurred on average 14.17 min earlier in Group 1 (95% CI: 11.10-17.23) and 12.50 min earlier in Group 3 (95% CI: 9.62-15.38) than in Group 2, with no difference between Groups 1 and 3 (1.67 min, 95% CI: -1.85 to 5.19); time-averaged hazard ratios were consistent (Group 1 vs. 2, 9.80 [4.22-22.73]; Group 3 vs. 2, 7.63 [3.36-17.31]; Group 1 vs. 3, 1.20 [0.67-2.16]). No significant differences were detected in hypoxemia, blocker malposition, or complications across groups; however, the trial was not powered for safety outcomes.
CONCLUSION: In patients aged 18-65 years with ASA I-II and normal pulmonary function undergoing thoracic surgery, the closure of the BB vent port results in a more rapid lung collapse compared to maintaining the vent port open. However, there was no statistically significant difference observed between the vent port closure technique and the disconnection technique regarding the time required for complete lung collapse.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR identifier: ChiCTR2000039896.

articles.title: Outcomes and Risk Factors of Pediatric Liver Transplantation in A Resource-Limited Setting: A 15-Year Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation is the definitive treatment for end-stage liver disease in children. Despite improved survival, mortality and acute rejection remain significant. Evidence from developing countries is limited; therefore, this study aimed to evaluate one-year mortality, acute rejection, and associated risk factors in pediatric liver transplant recipients at a national referral center in Indonesia.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among pediatric liver transplant recipients aged < 18 years at Cipto Mangunkusumo Hospital (2010-2025). Survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox proportional hazards regression and logistic regression were applied to identify factors associated with one-year mortality and acute rejection, respectively. Variables with p < 0.25 in univariate analysis and clinically relevant factors were included in multivariable models.
RESULTS: A total of 87 patients were included. The one-year mortality rate was 18.4% (overall survival 81.6%), with most deaths occurring within the first 5 months, particularly the first month. Operation duration > 12 h was independently associated with increased mortality (HR 4.13, 95% CI 1.16-14.64; p = 0.028). Acute rejection occurred in 27.6% of patients. No independent factor was significantly associated with acute rejection in multivariable analysis, although vascular complications showed a borderline association (OR 3.83, 95% CI 0.95-15.43; p = 0.059).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates favorable one-year outcomes. Prolonged operative duration was independently associated with increased mortality, while no independent predictor was significantly associated with acute rejection. These findings highlight the importance of perioperative optimization and continued evaluation of factors influencing graft-related outcomes.

articles.title: Eye Protection Chamber for Preventing Corneal Injury in Surgical Patients: Protocol for a Randomised Pilot and Feasibility Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess the feasibility of conducting a definitive randomised trial comparing an eye protection chamber with standard microporous adhesive tape in adults undergoing general anaesthesia for surgery expected to last more than 120 min, and to obtain preliminary estimates of perioperative corneal-injury event rates and device-related outcomes.
METHODS: This single-centre, parallel-group, assessor-blinded, randomised pilot and feasibility trial will allocate participants using simple randomisation with a 1:1 allocation probability to either the control group (adhesive tape and lubricating eye drops) or the intervention group (lubricating eye drops and an eye protection chamber). Primary feasibility outcomes will include recruitment, retention and completeness of the planned corneal assessments, intervention adherence, device displacement/reapplication and safety. Corneal examinations using fluorescein staining and slit-lamp assessment will be performed before induction of general anaesthesia (T0), during the immediate postoperative period after completion of surgery and removal of the eye-protection device (T1), and 24 h after surgery (T2). The incidence of any new corneal epithelial injury detected at T1 and/or T2 that was absent at T0 will be estimated as an exploratory clinical outcome. A pragmatic total sample of 120 participants will be retained to estimate feasibility parameters and preliminary event rates; the trial is not powered for confirmatory superiority testing.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public involvement occurred in the development of this protocol. Nursing relevance: The trial is intended to inform the design of a definitive study and may support the development of evidence-based perioperative eye-protection protocols.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (Registro Brasileiro de Ensaios Clínicos [ReBEC]) under UTN number U1111-1285-5334.

articles.title: Origin and composition of the brachial plexus in the alpaca (Vicugna pacos ).
articles.abstract: Alpacas (Vicugna pacos), members of the family Camelidae, are gaining popularity in Europe and worldwide. This study describes the origin and composition of the brachial plexus in alpacas and compares them with those of selected mammals. Six alpacas, aged one day to 16 years, were examined. In five animals, the plexus was formed by the ventral branches of C7, C8, and T1; in one specimen, T2 also contributed. After passing through the scalenus muscles - with C7 traversing separately from the caudal roots (C8, T1) - the roots continued as trunks toward the forelimb. Fibre exchange resulted in the formation of two cords. Nerves to the shoulder girdle muscles, except for the caudal pectoral nerve, contained only C8 fibre bundles. The suprascapular, subscapular, and axillary nerves arose from the cranial cord (C7, C8), which continued distally as the radial nerve (C8, T1). The caudal cord first gave rise to the cranial pectoral nerve (C8), followed by the caudal pectoral nerve (C8, T1) and the ulnar nerve (C8, T1), and then continued as the median nerve.
