The musculocutaneous nerve (C7, C8) originated at the trunk level, coursed caudally, and joined the median nerve in the ansa axillaris, resulting in the median nerve containing fibre bundles from all three spinal nerves. The reduced number of contributing spinal nerves and the distinctive arrangement of the plexus may be related to the elongated cervical vertebrae of alpacas. These findings support clinical applications, particularly in forelimb surgery and nerve block techniques, and provide comparative insights into morphological adaptation of the brachial plexus among mammals.

articles.title: Successful vaginal birth after two or more cesareans versus failed trial of labor: A systematic review and meta-analysis of maternal and fetal outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess maternal and neonatal outcomes associated with a failed versus successful (VBAC-2).
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search across Pubmed, Embase and Cochrane was conducted up to October 2025, supplemented by backward snowballing.
STUDY SELECTION: Studies with pregnant women with a two or more previous cesarean deliveries undergoing a trial of labor were included. No restrictions were applied.
DATA COLLECTION: Data on maternal and neonatal outcomes and risk and protective factors were extracted. The DerSimonian and Laird random effects model was applied, reporting Odds Ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was evaluated using I2 statistics and the Cochran Q test. Methodological quality was appraised using the Cochrane Risk-of-bias tool for non-randomized trials (ROBINS-I).
DATA SYNTHESIS: Out of 4065 studies screened, 12 studies (n= 3429) were included. We observed higher odds of postpartum hemorrhage (OR 1.98), maternal transfusion (OR 3.29), uterine rupture (OR 6.47), and neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR 6.44) in the VBAC-2 failure group. Epidural anesthesia (OR 0.56) and a history of previous vaginal birth (OR 0.27) were identified as protective factors, while a higher Body Mass Index was a risk factor for VBAC- 2 failure.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the critical need for comprehensive patient counseling, risk assessment, and heightened clinical vigilance to optimize care strategies in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Improving surgical antibiotic prophylaxis in obstetric and gynaecological surgery: a prospective two-cycle quality-improvement clinical audit in a North African tertiary hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inappropriate surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (SAP), particularly continuation beyond the recommended prophylactic period, increases avoidable antimicrobial exposure and is a key target for infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship.
METHODS: A prospective two-cycle targeted clinical audit evaluated 60 eligible procedures included consecutively during active audit observation periods (30 baseline and 30 postintervention) in an obstetric and gynaecological operating theatre of a North African tertiary hospital. Criteria were based on French Haute Autorité de Santé audit tools and Société Française d'Anesthésie et de Réanimation/ Société de Pathologie Infectieuse de Langue Française recommendations. The primary outcome was SAP duration compliant with procedure-specific guidance. The multi-faceted intervention comprised protocol revision and validation, point-of-care access, multi-disciplinary training, visual reminders, role clarification, and surveillance tools.
RESULTS: Protocol-governance compliance rose from 30% to 100%; allergy documentation from 67% to 100%; documentation of administration modalities from 3% to 37%; and appropriate antibiotic choice from 57% to 90%. Appropriate SAP duration improved from 10% to 53% (P < 0.001), while SAP continuation beyond 48 h decreased from 83% to 47% (P = 0.006). Documented administration within 60 min before incision decreased from 70% to 47%; this documentation-sensitive indicator was interpreted cautiously because non-compliance could reflect either missing timing information or administration outside the recommended window.
CONCLUSION: A pragmatic multi-disciplinary intervention improved several SAP process indicators and reduced unnecessary continuation beyond the recommended prophylactic period. Further audit cycles should prioritise reliable timing documentation, sustained reduction of prolonged SAP, and feedback of local surveillance data.

articles.title: Combined Pectoral Nerve Block and Intravenous Dexmedetomidine in Contemporary Multimodal Breast Cancer Analgesia: A Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background Ultrasound-guided pectoral nerve (PECS) block and intravenous dexmedetomidine are established opioid-sparing strategies for breast cancer surgery, but in contemporary multimodal analgesic pathways, postoperative pain scores are frequently low across treatment groups, potentially limiting their ability to discriminate between analgesic approaches. This study evaluated whether complementary outcome measures provide additional insight into perioperative analgesic efficacy when combining PECS block and dexmedetomidine. Methods This retrospective, real-world, single-center cohort study included 292 adult females undergoing oncologic breast surgery between January 2020 and December 2024, receiving one of four routinely applied analgesic strategies: combined PECS block plus dexmedetomidine (n = 169), dexmedetomidine alone (n = 53), PECS block alone (n = 52), or neither (n = 18). The primary outcome was time to first postoperative rescue opioid administration; secondary outcomes included pain intensity, perioperative opioid consumption, heart-rate response to surgical stimulation, and safety. Results Postoperative pain scores remained uniformly low across all groups (median numeric rating scale score of 0 throughout the first 24 hours), and the primary outcome did not differ significantly between the combined strategy and the remaining cohort (HR: 0.83, 95% CI: 0.198-3.47; p = 0.798). Combined PECS block and dexmedetomidine was associated with lower unadjusted intraoperative opioid consumption (17.7 vs. 50.7 morphine milligram equivalents; p < 0.001). However, this difference tracked almost entirely with intraoperative remifentanil use rather than with analgesic strategy, and largely disappeared once remifentanil-exposed cases were excluded. Heart-rate attenuation between induction and incision tracked with receipt of a PECS block rather than with dexmedetomidine. Rescue opioid use, pain scores, and clinically relevant bradycardia were comparable between groups throughout. Conclusions Postoperative pain scores and opioid requirements were uniformly low regardless of analgesic strategy, and the primary time-to-rescue-opioid outcome was inconclusive. Both apparent secondary "positive" findings, the opioid-sparing effect and the heart-rate attenuation, were attributable to confounding by anesthetic maintenance technique and PECS block status, respectively, rather than to the combined strategy itself. These findings illustrate a floor effect in postoperative pain scores under contemporary multimodal pathways, and highlight anesthetic-technique confounding, calendar-time drift, and single-clinician decision-making as underappreciated sources of bias in retrospective analgesia research more broadly.

articles.title: Update on the Management of Acute Sigmoid Volvulus: Endoscopic Decompression and Definitive Surgical Treatment.
articles.abstract: Sigmoid volvulus (SV) is a form of mechanical bowel obstruction with a likely multifactorial etiology. It occurs far more frequently in the so-called "volvulus belt" countries than in Western nations. In Western countries, its relatively low incidence has led to a lack of management experience. Establishing a diagnosis can be difficult and challenging, while the timing of presentation is a crucial determinant of prognosis. Delayed admission may result in bowel ischemia and gangrene. These complications are associated with increased morbidity and high mortality. Many aspects of SV management remain debatable, and proposed treatment algorithms are not universally accepted. In most cases of acute, uncomplicated SV, endoscopic decompression is the first-line treatment. However, this approach is commonly associated with SV recurrence if it is not followed by surgery. For complicated SV cases, emergent resection surgery can provide an effective and definitive treatment. Elderly patients and those with severe comorbidities may require careful preoperative assessment and optimization. Definitive surgery under general anesthesia is often postponed in this high-risk population. This review aims to examine the diagnostic challenges associated with acute SV and to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of currently available therapies. Further clinical research is needed to clarify the most appropriate treatment strategies for SV.

articles.title: Frailty in anaesthesia and intensive care.
Effectiveness of Kirschner wire versus clavicular hook plate fixation in the treatment of distal clavicle fractures in children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the treatment results of Kirschner wire (K-wire) fixation and clavicular hook plate (CHP) fixation for pediatric distal clavicle fractures, and to investigate the influence of age and fracture type on treatment selection.
METHOD: This retrospective study analyzed data from 136 children with distal clavicular fractures treated between January 2020 and December 2023, divided into a K-wire group (n = 68) and a CHP group (n = 68) based on the surgical method. Perioperative indicators, radiographic healing quality, shoulder function, quality of life and complications were all observed. Subgroup analyses were performed based on age (≤ 6 years vs. 7-14 years) and fracture type (Neer II vs. Neer IV/V).
RESULTS: The K-wire group demonstrated a minimally invasive profile, with significantly shorter operative times and less intraoperative blood loss. At 6 months post-injury, the CHP group showed a larger callus volume, a smaller fracture gap (P < 0.001), and a 0.5-month shorter healing time for Neer IV/V fractures (P = 0.007). The CHP group had significantly higher Constant-Murley scores, greater range of motion in forward flexion/abduction, and lower QuickDASH scores. The CHP group showed superior short-term physical health outcomes. Subgroup analysis showed that K-wires were better for controlling surgical trauma in children aged 6 and below (P < 0.05), and that the CHP group had faster healing and better functional recovery for children aged 7-14 years and Neer IV/V fractures (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: K-wire fixation is more suitable for younger children and simple fractures due to its minimally invasive nature; CHP fixation is highly effective in promoting fracture healing and functional recovery of complex fractures in older children, and both techniques demonstrated acceptable safety profiles.

articles.title: Measures of physical fitness and postoperative mortality in patients with colorectal cancer: national cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Measures of physical fitness are essential for case mix adjustment when comparing surgical outcomes between patient groups, surgical approaches, and healthcare providers. Commonly used measures include clinician-reported American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, as well as the Secondary Care Administrative Records Frailty (SCARF) index, derived from routinely collected administrative hospital data. This study compared how these measures of physical fitness, perform for case mix adjustment of postoperative colorectal cancer mortality.
METHODS: All patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer (CRC) between April 2017 and March 2022 in the English and Welsh National Health Service who underwent surgery were included. The primary outcome was 90-day postoperative mortality. Using an established risk-adjustment model, different combinations of ASA grade, performance status, and the SCARF index were added to create eight models for 90-day mortality risk adjustment. Model performance was compared with a full model including all three measures of physical fitness. The basic model included no measures of physical fitness. The scaled Brier score (SBS) measured overall model performance and the C-statistic measured discriminatory ability.
RESULTS: Among 91 957 patients, 90-day mortality was 2.8%. A model including both ASA grade and performance status achieved equivalent performance (SBS 0.092; C-statistic 0.833 (95% confidence interval (c.i.) 0.825 to 0.841)) to the full model (SBS 0.092; C-statistic 0.834 (95% c.i. 0.827 to 0.842)). The basic model with only performance status was slightly inferior (SBS 0.076; C-statistic 0.822 (95% c.i. 0.814 to 0.830)) to the basic model with only ASA grade (SBS 0.084; C-statistic 0.827 (95% c.i. 0.819 to 0.835)).
CONCLUSION: Performance status and ASA grade together accurately adjust for physical fitness when risk adjusting postoperative mortality in patients with CRC. When only one measure is available, performance status or ASA grade alone is suitable to support risk-adjusted hospital benchmarking.

articles.title: The physiology of labour.
Amniotic fluid embolism Number 11 - 2026.
articles.abstract: •Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare condition with high maternal mortality. It typically occurs during labor or delivery, and the pathogenesis has not yet been fully elucidated. •Survival of parturients with amniotic fluid embolism requires early recognition, rapid initiation of treatment, and access to skilled care based on the management of critically ill obstetric patients. •The classic clinical presentation of amniotic fluid embolism involves sudden hypoxia and hypotension or cardiopulmonary arrest, accompanied or immediately followed by non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and hemorrhage secondary to disseminated intravascular coagulation. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism occurring during labor, bleeding typically originates at invasive interventions sites (intravascular lines and urinary catheterization). Following vaginal or cesarean delivery, bleeding arises primarily from the uterus, birth canal lacerations, and incision sites (abdominal wall and episiotomies). •Key laboratory abnormalities observed in amniotic fluid embolism include decreased fibrinogen levels, thrombocytopenia, and elevated D-dimer levels. The latter has limited diagnostic value, as levels are typically elevated during pregnancy and the postpartum period. •Arterial blood gas analysis in amniotic fluid embolism indicates the presence of hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis. Although chest radiography is initially unremarkable, if pulmonary edema and respiratory distress syndrome are present, dense bilateral pulmonary infiltrates may be observed. •The identification of amniotic fluid debris in pulmonary artery catheters or histopathological samples of lung tissue should not be considered diagnostic of amniotic fluid embolism. •The primary goals in managing amniotic fluid embolism are cardiopulmonary resuscitation, hemorrhage control, reversal of coagulopathy, and when indicated, fetal delivery. •In cases of amniotic fluid embolism accompanied by coagulopathy, massive transfusion is a necessary measure for effective, definitive treatment. The infusion of uterotonics, non-surgical invasive interventions (intrauterine balloons and intrauterine suction systems), and surgical procedures (vascular ligation, uterine compression sutures, and hysterectomy) may be used as adjuncts to control hemorrhage but are not considered definitive treatments. •The main differential diagnoses for amniotic fluid embolism include complications of neuraxial anesthesia; hemorrhage due to uterine atony, retained products of conception, and/or birth canal trauma; placental abruption; pulmonary thromboembolism; air embolism; acute myocardial infarction; and anaphylactic, cardiogenic, or septic shock.

articles.title: Combined laparoscopic and endoscopic technique for safe percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy in a patient with challenging abdominal anatomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: PEG is the standard method for long-term enteral access but may fail when anatomical distortion or visceral interposition prevents safe placement. Laparoscopic-assisted PEG combines laparoscopic exposure with endoscopic guidance, providing a minimally invasive rescue technique in such cases.
METHOODS: We report a 69-year-old man with advanced mixed salivary gland carcinoma (T4N3bM0) previously treated with bilateral neck dissection and radiotherapy. He developed severe dysphagia secondary to a postradiation esophageal stricture and bilateral vocal cord paralysis, leading to significant malnutrition with weight decline from 72 to 58 kg over 1 year. Long-term enteral feeding was indicated. Two conventional PEG attempts failed because of absent transillumination, and a radiologic gastrostomy attempt was aborted because the transverse colon was interposed between the abdominal wall and the stomach. With the patient under general anesthesia via tracheostomy, laparoscopic-assisted PEG was performed. Laparoscopy identified a superiorly displaced transverse colon overlying the stomach, which was mobilized to create a safe window. A 14F pull-type PEG tube was successfully inserted under combined laparoscopic and endoscopic visualization, confirming intragastric positioning.
RESULTS: Enteral feeding began the same day, and recovery was uneventful. Laparoscopic-assisted PEG enabled safe gastrostomy placement after multiple failed approaches.
CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic-assisted PEG is a minimally invasive alternative that avoids the morbidity of formal surgical gastrostomy when PEG or radiologic interventional gastrostomy are not feasible.

articles.title: Novel use of an endoscopic suturing device for rectal foreign body retrieval.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic removal of gastrointestinal tract foreign bodies could be difficult when the foreign body significantly exceeds the size of the available endoscopic extraction devices (snares, nets, etc). We present successful use of an endoscopic suturing device for retrieval of a large rectal foreign body not amenable to retrieval by traditional endoscopic extraction devices.
METHODS: The patient was a 45-year-old biological male transitioning to female who presented to the emergency department with a self-reported 8-inch rectal foreign body. Extraction with the patient under anesthesia was unsuccessful, and to avoid surgery, a flexible sigmoidoscopy was attempted.
RESULTS: Attempts to remove the rectal foreign body using traditional retrieval devices were unsuccessful because of a large diameter and very slippery surface of the silicone sex toy. After 11 minutes of unsuccessful attempts, we inserted the OverStitch endoscopic suturing device (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, Mass, USA) into the rectum. We pierced the suturing arm of the device through the foreign body and were able to retrieve it from the rectum in 5 minutes.
CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates unexpected value of an endoscopic suturing device for endoscopic removal of a large foreign body not amenable to extraction with traditional dedicated endoscopic devices. Use of an endoscopic suturing device enabled successful removal of the difficult foreign body and eliminated the need for urgent surgery.

articles.title: Learning Curve in Thoracoscopic Mediastinal Mass Excision: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study Using Cumulative Sum and Multivariable Regression Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) mediastinal mass excision has become the standard approach for anterior mediastinal lesions. Understanding its learning curve is essential for surgical training and quality assurance. The primary objective was to quantify the association between cumulative case experience (case sequence number) and operative time, the primary outcome, using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis and multivariable regression modelling. We tested the null hypothesis that operative time does not change with increasing case sequence after adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Secondary objectives were to estimate the number of cases required to achieve proficiency and to compare perioperative outcomes across learning phases and between participating countries.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at five academic and tertiary-care centers in Egypt and Saudi Arabia between January 2023 and December 2025. Seventy-seven consecutive patients undergoing VATS excision of mediastinal masses were categorized into three phases: Early (first 20 cases), Intermediate (next 20 cases), and Late (last 37 cases). Cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis was performed. Operative outcomes, including operative time, blood loss, conversion rate, and postoperative complications, were compared across phases and between countries (Egypt vs. Saudi Arabia). Multivariable linear regression and a linear mixed-effects model with participating centre as a random intercept were used to identify factors independently associated with operative time.
RESULTS: Mean operative time significantly decreased across phases (189.5 ± 21.9 vs. 156.5 ± 26.4 vs. 139.7 ± 30.5 minutes; p < 0.001). CUSUM analysis demonstrated a learning curve inflection point between cases 20 and 26. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, myasthenia gravis, presence of a discrete mass, thymic neoplasm and country, case sequence number remained independently associated with shorter operative time (β = -1.14 min per case; 95% CI -1.47 to -0.80; p < 0.001; R² = 0.48, adjusted R² = 0.42), with consistent estimates using robust standard errors and a mixed-effects model with centre as a random intercept (β = -1.37; 95% CI -1.80 to -0.95). Patients treated in Saudi Arabia (n = 7) were older and more often had discrete neoplastic masses, but operative time did not differ significantly between countries before (p = 0.128) or after adjustment (p = 0.548). Conversion to open surgery occurred in 3.9% (n = 3), all in the Intermediate and Late phases. Overall mortality was 2.6% (n = 2), both in the Late phase and associated with complex cases. No significant differences were observed regarding ICU stay, hospital stay, or postoperative complications.
CONCLUSION: VATS mediastinal mass excision is safe and feasible, with surgical proficiency achieved after approximately 20-26 cases. Operative time was the most reliable indicator of learning progression, and the learning effect persisted after multivariable adjustment for patient-, tumour- and country-related factors. Structured mentorship and careful case selection are recommended during the early learning phase.

articles.title: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery versus Thoracotomy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis and Exploratory Predictive Modelling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component.
METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded.
RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology.
CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Perioperative Transcranial Electrical Stimulation for Postoperative Pain and Related Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential and Subgroup Analyses.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) is a neuromodulation technique that can serve as an adjuvant tool during the perioperative period. With emerging randomized controlled trials (RCTs) supporting its efficacy across various surgical procedures, synthesis of current evidence and evaluation of its potential for postoperative analgesia in elective-surgery patients and related outcomes are urgently needed.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We initially searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, and Embase for RCTs investigating perioperative tES in patients undergoing elective surgery. The search period covered from the inception of each database to September 2025, and an updated search for newly published studies was conducted in September 2026. We analyzed the outcomes, including postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, quality of recovery, incidence of postoperative delirium, and adverse events. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool was used to evaluate the risk of bias in included studies. Sensitivity and publication bias analyses were performed. Exploratory subgroup analysis and meta-regression were performed to identify sources of heterogeneity. We also analyzed outlier studies. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was further performed to evaluate the robustness of evidence. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system was used to assess the certainty of the evidence.
RESULTS: A total of 21 RCTs with 2186 participants were included in this meta-analysis. Compared with the control group, the tES group showed lower pain scores on postoperative day 1 (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -0.57, 95% CI: -0.84 to -0.30, p < 0.01), reduced total opioid consumption (SMD = -0.47, 95% CI: -0.74 to -0.20, p < 0.01), a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (risk ratio [RR] = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.25 to 0.79, p < 0.01), and a lower incidence of postoperative nausea or vomiting (RR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.75 to 0.95, p < 0.01). No significant differences were observed between the two groups in postoperative day 1 quality of recovery (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI: -0.18 to 1.05, p = 0.16) and dizziness or headache (RR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.70 to 1.47, p = 0.94). In addition, tES might increase the risk of mild and transient stimulation site discomfort (RR = 3.10, 95% CI: 1.96 to 4.90, p < 0.01). The initial timing and number of stimulation sessions were potential sources of heterogeneity for postoperative day 1 pain scores, while initial stimulation timing, stimulation modality, and target sites were associated with heterogeneity in total opioid consumption. TSA results indicated that the current sample size was sufficient to confirm the beneficial effects of tES on postoperative day 1 pain, total opioid consumption, and postoperative delirium. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that tES, as an adjuvant perioperative intervention, may alleviate postoperative pain, reduce opioid consumption, and decrease the incidence of postoperative delirium. However, the effect of tES on postoperative quality of recovery remains unclear. Considering the limited overall quality of current evidence, whether tES can serve as a universal adjuvant analgesic method for patients undergoing elective surgery still needs further clarification.

articles.title: Comparison of Sevoflurane and Propofol-Fentanyl for Laryngeal Mask Airway Insertion in Pediatric cases.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) is a commonly used minimally invasive supraglottic airway device used in pediatric anesthesia. Intravenous propofol is the commonly preferred anesthetic drug due to its favorable insertion conditions for LMA while inhalational sevoflurane offers a non-invasive induction with better hemodynamic stability. The addition of fentanyl to propofol may further optimize insertion conditions by enhancing analgesia and attenuating airway reflexes. Existing literature predominantly compares sevoflurane with propofol alone for LMA insertion whereas direct comparisons between sevoflurane and propofol-fentanyl combination are limited, hence the present study was undertaken.
METHODS: A prospective, single blinded randomized study was conducted in 60 pediatric patients aged 4-12 years with ASA physical status I and II undergoing elective surgical procedures. Using shuffle method, patients were randomly allocated to two groups Group P- Propofol with fentanyl group and Group S- Sevoflurane group. Group P received intravenous propofol (2 mg/kg) with fentanyl (2 µg/kg bolus) along with mask ventilation using a nitrous oxide-oxygen mixture (2:1), while Group S underwent inhalational induction with sevoflurane (7%) using nitrous oxide-oxygen mixture (2:1). Time to induction, jaw relaxation, and LMA insertion were recorded. Hemodynamic parameters and procedure-related complications were also monitored.
RESULTS: The time to jaw relaxation was significantly longer in the sevoflurane group compared to the propofol-fentanyl group (108.41 ± 6.90 vs 53.35 ± 4.12 seconds; p < 0.05). Similarly, the time to LMA insertion was significantly prolonged in the sevoflurane group (118.96 ± 6.65 vs 63.19 ± 4.31 seconds; p < 0.05), with sevoflurane demonstrating better hemodynamic stability.
CONCLUSION: Propofol-fentanyl provides faster induction and LMA insertion, whereas sevoflurane offers superior hemodynamic stability with comparable safety profiles in pediatric patients.

articles.title: Outcomes of a Multidisciplinary Endovascular Aortic Program at the Vietnam National Heart Institute: A Single-Center Observational Study of TEVAR, EVAR, and Registry Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary aortic programs integrate advanced imaging, standardized clinical pathways, procedural expertise, and longitudinal surveillance. We evaluated the evolution and outcomes of endovascular aortic care at Vietnam National Heart Institute (VNHI), Bach Mai Hospital, using institutional TEVAR and EVAR cohorts and the prospective VNHI Aortic Registry through June 2026.
METHODS: Single-center observational report drawing on two historical institutional endovascular cohorts (TEVAR from January 2014 to December 2020, n=102; EVAR from January 2019 to August 2025, n=235) and a prospectively maintained registry (January-June 2026, n=96) in the VNHI Aortic Registry, Bach Mai hospital. Cohorts were summarized separately because enrollment periods, disease profiles, and follow-up differed. Outcomes were analyzed within each source cohort. Prespecified outcomes included technical success, perioperative mortality, major procedure-related complications, aortic remodeling, secondary reintervention, and mid-term survival.
RESULTS: Technical success was 100/102 (98.0%) TEVAR and 235/235 (100%) EVAR cases. In-hospital mortality was 3/102 (2.9%) in the dedicated TEVAR cohort; 30-day mortality was 2/235 (0.9%) in the EVAR cohort. Spinal cord ischemia occurred after TEVAR in 5/102 (4.9%) patients; all affected patients recovered before discharge following a standardized rescue protocol. Thoracic aortic coverage ≥ 270 mm was independently associated with spinal cord ischemia (odds ratio, 10.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.41-72.55; P=0.021). In the historical TEVAR source, complete false-lumen thrombosis in the covered thoracic segment was reported in 87.1% at 12 months; the imaging denominator remains to be confirmed. Estimates of long-term survival and regression-derived associations are withheld from this abstract pending verification of follow-up dates, numbers at risk, and model specifications. The 2026 registry contains 96 recorded entries but is not treated as an additional independent patient cohort until overlap is assessed. Four-year cumulative survival was 87.9% TEVAR and 84.6% EVAR; secondary reintervention occurred in 3.9% and 4.3%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: A structured multidisciplinary endovascular aortic program at VNHI was associated with high technical success and favorable mid-term outcomes in selected patients undergoing TEVAR or EVAR. These findings support the feasibility of organized aortic care in an emerging healthcare system; however, prospective risk-adjusted evaluation is required to determine the independent effect of the program on clinical outcomes. Complete patient-level reconciliation and standardized longitudinal surveillance are necessary for robust benchmarking.

articles.title: Microbial Etiology of Postoperative Spinal Fusion Infections and Factors Associated with Gram-Negative Infections, United States, 2021-2022.
articles.abstract: Accurate knowledge of microbial etiology is essential for optimizing spinal fusion surgical site infection (SSI) management, yet contemporary national data in the United States, particularly prevalence and factors associated with gram-negative infections, remain poorly understood. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of US data reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Healthcare Safety Network (2021-2022) to characterize the microbiology of spinal fusion SSI and identify factors associated with gram-negative infection. Among 7,187 cases, gram-negative organisms caused 31.5% (n = 2,265) of SSIs. Older age, female sex, higher body mass index, longer operative times, higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class, lumbar involvement, inpatient surgery, and emergent and trauma surgeries were independently associated with gram-negative infections relative to monomicrobial Staphylococcus aureus infections. Our findings might inform future studies focusing on high-risk cohorts as targets for expanded gram-negative prophylactic regimens. Clinicians can use risk profiles to guide empiric gram-negative antibiotic coverage in treating SSIs.

articles.title: Uniportal versus multiportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery for anatomical pulmonary resection: a systematic review and meta-analysis of perioperative recovery and surgical quality.
articles.abstract: Uniportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (uRATS) seeks to combine the dexterity of robotic platforms with reduced access trauma, yet its comparative value over multiportal RATS (mRATS) remains uncertain. We systematically evaluated perioperative recovery and surgical quality after anatomical pulmonary resection. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 2026. Comparative studies of uniportal/single-port versus multiportal robotic anatomical lung resection were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I V2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Nine non-randomised studies involving 813 patients were included, with seven studies rated at critical risk of bias. Postoperative complications occurred in 16.0% of uniportal and 30.2% of multiportal patients, with no statistically significant pooled difference (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22-1.06; p = 0.069; I²=66%). No significant differences were identified in major complications, conversion, mortality, operative time, blood loss, chest-tube duration, length of stay, or lymph-node yield, or R0 resection. Uniportal surgery was associated with shorter console time (MD - 23.5 min, 95% CI - 35.6 to - 11.4) and lower postoperative day-1 pain (MD - 0.6 points, 95% CI - 0.9 to - 0.3). The 0.5- point pain difference was below commonly used thresholds for clinical importance and lost statistical significance when digitised values were excluded (p = 0.092). Available observational evidence does not demonstrate a clear difference in perioperative safety or surgical quality between uniportal/single-port and multiportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differences in length of stay and operative time by comparator port count, potentially reflecting confounding by operative era and experience. A possible reduction in console time and early postoperative pain was observed, but these findings were based on very-low-certainty evidence and were sensitive to individual studies.

articles.title: Postoperative esophageal achalasia after robotic left lower lobectomy for lung cancer: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative esophageal achalasia after lung surgery is extremely rare. Vagal nerve injury has been proposed as a possible mechanism of postsurgical esophageal dysmotility. We report a rare case of esophageal achalasia following robot-assisted lung cancer surgery.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old woman with lung adenocarcinoma (cT1cN0M0, stage IA3) underwent robot-assisted left lower lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection. On postoperative day 2, she developed vomiting and difficulty eating. Computed tomography revealed esophageal dilatation with retained food, and esophagography demonstrated absent esophageal peristalsis, narrowing at the esophagogastric junction, and contrast retention. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed no mechanical obstruction. High-resolution manometry confirmed esophageal achalasia. Pneumatic dilation was performed on postoperative day 15, resulting in improvement of esophagogastric junction relaxation. She was discharged on postoperative day 24 and remained well without recurrence of achalasia 6 years after surgery.
CONCLUSION: Postoperative achalasia is a rare complication of lung surgery. Although the causal mechanism in this case could not be established, perioperative vagal nerve or esophageal plexus injury was considered a possible mechanism. Careful handling of the vagus nerve and cautious use of energy devices near the esophagus may help prevent this complication, and achalasia should be considered in patients with persistent dysphagia after lung surgery.

articles.title: Learning curve and clinical outcomes of robotic-assisted heart bypass surgery: Real-world evidence from India.
articles.abstract: BackgroundRobotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) using bilateral internal mammary arteries (BIMA) provides a minimally invasive option for advanced coronary artery disease (CAD), but evidence on its learning curve and outcomes in the Indian population remains limited.ObjectivesTo evaluate the learning curve associated with robotic CABG using BIMA and to compare perioperative and clinical outcomes between the early and late phases of surgical experience in a real-world setting.DesignRetrospective, single-center, observational chart review conducted at a high-volume quaternary cardiac care center in India.MethodsThis retrospective chart review was performed for 341 patients who underwent robotic-assisted BIMA CABG between 2020 and 2025. The learning curve was assessed using risk-adjusted cumulative summation (CUSUM), while complication trends were examined through sequential probability CUSUM failure analysis.ResultsThe cohort comprised 295 (86.51%) males with a mean age of 59.56 ± 9.93 years and a body mass index (BMI) of 25.98 ± 3.74 kg/m2. Mean console time was 101.66 ± 29.99 minutes, ICU stay 2.85 ± 0.98 days, and hospital stay 6.01 ± 2.38 days; conversion to open surgery occurred in 2.93% of cases, with in-hospital mortality of 3.52%. CUSUM analysis identified case 125 as the proficiency inflection point, after which console time significantly decreased (94.95 ± 24.32 vs. 113.38 ± 35.04 minutes; p<0.001), while ventilator duration, ICU and hospital stay, complications, and mortality remained comparable between phases. Readmission and re-exploration rates were low (2.05% each), with no deaths at 6-month follow-up. CUSUM failure analysis confirmed complication rates remained within acceptable thresholds throughout the study.ConclusionsRobotic-assisted BIMA CABG demonstrated acceptable outcomes, with operative efficiency improving after approximately 125 cases. These findings support its feasibility in experienced, high-volume centers and warrant further multicentre evaluation.

articles.title: Acute Pain Management in the Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes current approaches to pain assessment and pharmacologic therapy in the intensive care unit (ICU) and evaluates the expanding role of regional anesthesia (RA).
RECENT FINDINGS: Contemporary ICU analgesia emphasizes systematic pain assessment and multimodal therapy while avoiding unnecessary deep sedation. RA provides targeted, opioid-sparing analgesia for localized pain but is limited by coagulopathy, infection, altered anatomy, and practical considerations. Fascial-plane blocks may provide useful alternatives in selected patients. Thoracic epidural and paravertebral techniques remain options for selected patients but may cause hypotension and clinically significant bleeding. Ultrasound-guided techniques, including erector spinae, serratus anterior, parasternal, rectus sheath, and transversus abdominis plane blocks, expand analgesic options. Continuous catheter techniques may extend analgesia when prolonged pain is anticipated. However, evidence in heterogeneous ICU populations remains limited, and much of the current evidence is derived from perioperative or trauma populations rather than general medical ICU cohorts. Further ICU-specific comparative trials are needed to define patient selection and clinically meaningful outcomes.

articles.title: Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor Inhibitor ISO-1 Attenuates Anesthesia/Surgery-Induced Cognitive Impairment in Aged Mice: Association with NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibition.
articles.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a serious clinical complication and lacks effective therapeutic approaches. Recent studies demonstrate that targeting macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) offers a novel strategy to cognitive impairment disorders. Here, we aim to investigate whether MIF inhibitor ISO-1 mitigates anesthesia/surgery-evoked cognitive defects via regulating NLRP3 inflammasome. C57BL/6 mice (18-month-old) were selected to establish a POCD model via unilateral nephrectomy under sevoflurane anesthesia. Cognitive and behavioral capabilities were evaluated by fear conditioning, Morris water maze and open field tests. On day 3 postsurgery, MIF levels in the serum and hippocampus were measured through ELISA, immunofluorescence and western blotting. Furthermore, to clarify whether elevated hippocampal MIF following nephrectomy contribute to cognitive decline, ISO-1 (30 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally 30 min before and after surgery to reduce hippocampal MIF expression. ELISA and immunofluorescence were used to gauge the levels of hippocampal MIF, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β and microglial activation. HE and TUNEL staining were used to assess the morphological alterations and apoptosis in hippocampal neurons. Western blotting was applied to determine the expression of hippocampal MIF, caspase-1, IL-1β, ASC, NLRP3, Bcl-2, Bax and Iba1. We found that surgery-treated mice exhibited pronounced cognitive impairment, accompanied by increased levels of MIF, neuronal apoptosis and neuroinflammation in the hippocampus, as well as the activation of microglia and NLRP3 inflammasome. Inhibition of MIF with ISO-1 can effectively reverse these detrimental changes. Our results reveal that ISO-1 exerts a neuroprotective effect against POCD, which may be associated with the inhibition of NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

articles.title: Developing and implementing a remote patient management program at a large academic children's hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) can improve access, engagement, and clinical outcomes, yet evidence describing how health systems develop, scale, and sustain enterprise-wide RPM programs remains limited, particularly in pediatrics. We describe the development of a centralized RPM program at a large academic children's hospital and lessons learned from implementing 16 programs across diverse clinical settings.
METHODS: Beginning with a single cardiology pilot in 2021, we iteratively developed an enterprise RPM model spanning complex transitions from hospital to home, perioperative care, and specialty care. A centralized Digital Health team provided program intake and prioritization, implementation support, technology and electronic health record (EHR) integration, analytics, and ongoing optimization, while clinical divisions retained responsibility for clinical workflows and patient management.
RESULTS: The portfolio expanded to 16 RPM programs. Experience across implementations demonstrated the importance of clearly defining the clinical or operational problem and measures of success before launch, identifying strong clinical champions, integrating RPM into existing workflows, selecting technology aligned with organizational and patient needs, and establishing sustainable operational and financial models. Centralized infrastructure enabled shared expertise, standardized measurement, and ongoing optimization while preserving specialty-specific clinical ownership.
CONCLUSIONS: A centralized operational model with decentralized clinical ownership can support scalable pediatric RPM across diverse populations and workflows. Our experience demonstrates that successful enterprise RPM requires more than technology deployment; sustained growth depends on standardized implementation processes, clinical engagement, governance, measurement, equity considerations, and early planning for long-term sustainability.
articles.journal: Curr Probl Pediatr Adolesc Health Care

articles.title: Analyzing the Economic and Logistical Impact of Lung Procurement on Transplant Centers in the Era of Continuous Distribution.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The recent transition to the Composite Allocation Score (CAS) has increased travel distances for lung transplants, but an associated cost analysis has not been performed. We assessed travel costs and short-term outcomes of lung transplantation before and after transitioning to CAS.
METHODS: The United Network for Organ Sharing database was queried for all lung transplants from 1/2020 to 12/2024. Redo and pediatric lung and multiorgan transplants were excluded. Patients were stratified between pre- and post-CAS, which began on 3/9/2023. Outcomes were distance of donor-to-recipient in nautical miles (nm), inflation-adjusted travel costs, and perioperative outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 7,835 (58.6%) pre-CAS and 5,538 (41.4%) post-CAS patients were included. Post-CAS patients were more likely female (41.7% vs. 38.5%, p<0.001), less likely White race (69.1% vs. 72.7%, p<0.001), and had shorter waitlist durations (28 vs. 33 days, p<0.001) compared to pre-CAS patients. Donor lungs were procured from greater distances in the CAS era (411 vs. 185 nm, p<0.001). Post-CAS, more procurements required flights (80.8% vs. 68.6%, p<0.001), and very long-distance procurements (>1000 nm) increased (10.7% vs. 2.0%, p<0.001). Travel costs increased, with median inflation-adjusted costs rising from $13,967 to $16,818; p<0.001. Ischemic times were longer post-CAS (7.1 vs. 5.7 hours, p<0.001). Importantly, one-year survival was similar pre- and post-CAS (88.9% vs. 90.1%, p=0.069).
CONCLUSIONS: CAS has reduced waitlist duration with preserved one-year survival for lung transplant patients, but introduces greater logistical complexity and cost, which requires continued reevaluation to ensure economic viability and long-term sustainability of transplant programs.

articles.title: Intravenous regional limb perfusion techniques in the anesthetized foal.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To provide a video tutorial on how to perform IV regional limb perfusion (IVRLP) using the cephalic or saphenous vein in anesthetized foals.
ANIMALS: Foals from neonatal to weaning age not amenable to standing, sedated procedures.
METHODS: A pneumatic or wide-rubber tourniquet is applied around the proximal antebrachium or gaskin. The IVRLP dose of desired antimicrobial is diluted with physiologic saline to 30 mL of total volume. A 23-gauge winged infusion set or 22-gauge, 1-inch IV catheter is inserted into either the cephalic or saphenous vein distal to the tourniquet, and the entire perfusate volume is administered slowly by hand or with a syringe pump. The needle or catheter is removed, a pressure bandage applied over the venipuncture site, and the tourniquet left in place for a minimum of 20 minutes and up to 30 minutes. When IVRLP is administered in conjunction with systemic antimicrobial administration, the dose administered via IVRLP should be subtracted from the total systemic dose to avoid systemic toxicity.
RESULTS: When combined with systemic administration, cephalic or saphenous IVRLP in the anesthetized foal is considered an effective technique for achieving adequate systemic antimicrobial concentrations and supraphysiologic antimicrobial concentrations in the tissues and synovial compartments of the limbs.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: While IVRLP in foals is commonly performed in equine practice, appropriate technique is essential to maximize the clinical effect. This tutorial video is intended to provide practitioners with basic instruction for proper technique of IVRLP using the cephalic or saphenous vein in the anesthetized foal.

articles.title: Liposomal bupivacaine utilization in the pain management of postoperative selective dorsal rhizotomy patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Selective dorsal rhizotomy (SDR) is a procedure commonly utilized to treat spasticity in children with cerebral palsy. Limited studies have evaluated postoperative pain management with the objective of opiate dosage reduction. This retrospective cohort study examined the role of liposomal bupivacaine (LB) in postoperative pain management and the outcomes of SDR patients.
METHODS: This retrospective study used the Pediatric Movement Disorders Center's prospective database to query electronic medical records for demographic, surgical, and postoperative data for all patients who underwent SDR from 2023 through 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: those treated with 0.25% bupivacaine HCl (comparison group) or a mixture of LB and bupivacaine HCl (LB group). Both modalities were administered via local infusion during closure of the SDR incision. All patients also received our previously developed protocol that includes infusion of dexmedetomidine during SDR surgery combined with perioperative gabapentin and scheduled acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs postoperatively, henceforth referred to as the dexmedetomidine infusion (INF) protocol.
RESULTS: Operative duration, postoperative opioid and nonopioid medication administration, and therapy notes were collected for 41 patients. Patients who underwent SDR between May 2023 and July 2024 received our INF postoperative pain management protocol and bupivacaine HCl (comparison group [n = 20]). Patients who underwent SDR between October 2024 and July 2025 received INF along with a mixture of bupivacaine HCl and LB (LB group [n = 21]). Differences in demographic characteristics, preoperative Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) scores, operative duration, hospital length of stay (LOS), and postoperative opiate/nonopiate medication administration were recorded. When converted to morphine milligram equivalent, there were no significant differences in opioid dosage or total opioid use between groups. There was a trend toward significance, in that the comparison group participated in physical therapy for a longer duration than the LB group on postoperative day 2. This was attributed to differences in discharge dates between the two groups: the LB group was more likely to be discharged on postoperative day 2 than the comparison group due to changes in our center's rehabilitation pathway during this study.
CONCLUSIONS: Local infiltration of LB mixed with standard bupivacaine, given at the conclusion of SDR surgery in conjunction with our established postoperative pain management protocol, was not associated with decreased use of postoperative pain medications when compared to the infusion of standard bupivacaine.

articles.title: Aorto-Pulmonary Shunt Creation in Congenital Heart Disease: Different Indications, Various Modifications, but Common Technical Challenges.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous creation of an aorto-pulmonary (AP) shunt has been explored in preclinical models for over 15 years, yet its clinical application remains limited. Surgical AP shunts are widely used to augment pulmonary blood flow in cyanotic congenital heart disease, but repeated thoracic operations and general anesthesia carry substantial risks in critically ill or surgically complex patients. A less invasive transcatheter alternative could therefore represent a transformative option. We report a case series of two pediatric patients in whom a percutaneous connection between the aorta and pulmonary artery was successfully established. Indications were severe cyanosis due to compromised pulmonary blood flow in one child and suprasystemic pulmonary arterial hypertension requiring decompression in the other. The procedures were technically feasible and resulted in the intended immediate hemodynamic effects, either by enhancing pulmonary perfusion or by enabling right-to-left shunting for right heart decompression. Conceptually, percutaneous AP shunt creation parallels the transcatheter Potts shunt, which is increasingly recognized as a therapeutic option in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Both approaches establish controlled communication between the aorta and pulmonary artery, adapted to distinct physiological settings. Our report represents, to our knowledge, the first description of percutaneous AP shunt creation to improve pulmonary blood flow and oxygenation in congenital heart disease, as well as the first percutaneous connection between the ascending aorta and the pulmonary artery. These cases illustrate the technical feasibility of catheter-based AP shunt creation in selected pediatric patients and support further evaluation of this approach.

articles.title: Effect of auricular acupressure on labour analgesia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Labour pain significantly influences maternal childbirth experiences and outcomes. Auricular acupressure has shown potential as a non-pharmacological method for labour analgesia. However, comprehensive evidence regarding its efficacy across distinct stages of Labour-specifically the latent and active phases remain unclear, and optimal practice protocols require further clarification.
METHODS: Computerized searches of Chinese and English databases were conducted to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining auricular acupressure for labour analgesia. Meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4 software. Primary analyses were stratified by labour stage (latent vs. active phase), supplemented with subgroup analyses based on acupoint number, practitioner training, and the timing of outcome measurement.
RESULTS: Auricular acupressure significantly reduced pain during both the latent phase (SMD = -2.89, 95% CI: -4.03 to -1.75; P < 0.001) and the active phase (SMD = -1.62, 95% CI: -2.37 to -0.87; P < 0.001). During the latent phase, stimulation of six or more auricular points produced a greater analgesic effect (SMD = -4.13) than stimulation of fewer than six points (SMD = -2.38). During the active phase, fewer than six points showed a numerically greater effect (SMD = -1.83) than six or more points (SMD = -1.60), but this finding was unstable in sensitivity analyses. Studies reporting trained providers showed greater pain reduction (SMD = -1.97 vs. -1.30), although the between-subgroup difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.38), and only one latent-phase study reported formal practitioner training.
CONCLUSION: Auricular acupressure may reduce labour pain and may be useful as a non-pharmacological adjunct to routine care. However, the certainty of these findings is limited by predictable allocation in two studies, incomplete reporting of blinding, and substantial heterogeneity. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of effectiveness.

articles.title: Abdominal circumference and its relationship with the incidence of hypotension during elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypotension is a common complication in pregnant mothers during cesarean section after spinal anesthesia. Identifying the association between abdominal circumference and the likelihood of developing hypotension following a cesarean delivery while under spinal anesthesia can facilitate preventing hypotension.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to assess the relationship between the abdominal circumference of pregnant women and the occurrence of hypotension during cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024.
METHOD: A prospective observational study through a simple systematic random sampling technique was conducted on 360 pregnant mothers who underwent elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia from January 7, 2024, to March 30, 2024. Data was collected using a data collection questionnaire and checklist. The data was entered using Epi Info 7.2 and exported into SPSS 26. The Patients were categorized by their median abdominal circumference, < 102 cm (small abdominal circumference (SAC)) and ≥102 cm (large abdominal circumference (LAC)). The chi-square test was used to compare the numerical and percentage representations of the categorical variables. Descriptive analyses, bivariate logistic regression, and multivariate regression were carried out. In multivariate variables, p ≤ 0.05 was used as statistical significance, and an odds ratio was used for the strength of association.
RESULT: Among 360 study subjects, the incidence of post-spinal hypotension was 76.67% with 95%CI [71.9-80.9]. The Large abdominal circumference (LAC) group showed a greater maximal decrease in MAP from baseline compared to the SAC group (LAC 85.6% and SAC 63.3%, p < 0.001). The identified associated factors with the incidence of hypotension were LAC (AOR = 2.98, 95% CI [1.57, 5.65] p = 0.01); BMI > 25 kg/m2 (AOR = 2.3, 95%CI [1.16-4.6], P = 0.018); baby weight> 4 kg (AOR = 11.41 95%CI [2.0-64.86] P = 0.006); sensory block of above T6 level (AOR = 2.22, 95%CI [1.12, 4.42]) p = 0.023) and greater than 500 ml preload given (AOR = 0.42 [95%CI 0.2-0.89] p = 0.023.
CONCLUSIONS: The study found that there was a high incidence of hypotension during elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia and a significant difference between the SAC and LAC groups. Also, the study found that the independent factors significantly associated with the incidence of hypotension were LAC, higher BMI, higher baby weight, and higher sensory block level, while greater preload volume was protective.

articles.title: Comparison of oral and intravenous methadone for postoperative analgesia after cardiac surgery: a pilot randomized clinical trial.
Neighborhood and individual socioeconomic predictors of 5-year pain trajectories after burn injury.
articles.abstract: This study identified 5-year pain trajectories in adult burn survivors and examined whether neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage was associated with adverse trajectory membership. Using the Burn Model System National Database (2015-2025), Growth Mixture Modeling identified pain intensity trajectory classes in 1354 adults assessed at 6, 12, 24, and 60 months. In the geocoded subsample (n=909), multinomial regression with multiple imputation (m=100) estimated associations between the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) and trajectory membership, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and site characteristics and then additionally for individual socioeconomic characteristics. Three trajectories emerged: Low Pain (56%), Moderate Pain (30%), and High Pain (14%). Each 1-SD increase in ADI was associated with estimated relative risk ratios of 1.19 for Moderate Pain (95% CI 0.996-1.43, p=0.056) and 1.27 for High Pain (95% CI 0.99-1.63, p=0.058) versus Low Pain; both intervals included the null. Using Neighborhood Atlas ADI, disadvantage was associated with Moderate Pain (RRR 1.27, 95% CI 1.03-1.55) but not High Pain membership. Estimates were attenuated after additional socioeconomic adjustment. After correction for multiple comparisons, pre-injury unemployment and other public insurance (vs. private) were associated with higher High Pain risk, and household income of $50,000-$99,999 (vs. <$50,000) with lower Moderate Pain risk. Evidence was most consistent for persistent Moderate Pain, though estimates varied in precision across ADI measures. Individual socioeconomic characteristics were also associated with trajectory membership. PERSPECTIVE: Neighborhood disadvantage was associated with long-term pain after burn injury, with evidence most consistent for persistent moderate pain. Individual socioeconomic characteristics, including unemployment, income, and insurance, were also associated with trajectory membership. Neighborhood and individual socioeconomic information may guide sustained, multilevel support for burn survivors.

articles.title: Association of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Radiographic Findings Identified by Machine Learning and Outcomes of Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Single academic medical center.
INTERVENTION: None.
PATIENTS: Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation.
METHODS AND MAIN RESULTS: We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation.
CONCLUSIONS: A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents.
DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, observational study.
SETTING: Thirteen ICUs in Poland.
PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in 2015-2023: A Report From the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children Multicenter Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the contemporary incidence of tracheal intubation-associated cardiac arrest (TI-CA) in critically ill children and identify potentially modifiable factors to prevent TI-CA in PICUs and pediatric cardiac ICUs (PCICUs).
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Seventy international PICUs and PCICUs.
PATIENTS: Critically ill children requiring tracheal intubation in PICUs and PCICUs.
INTERVENTIONS: Tracheal intubation data were prospectively collected for all initial intubations in 68 PICUs and PCICUs from January 2015 to December 2023 using the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children registry.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: TI-CA was defined as CA occurrence or receipt of chest compressions for at least 1 minute within 20 minutes of endotracheal tube placement. TI during ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation was not considered TI-CA. A total of 27,773 TIs were evaluated, with TI-CA reported in 1.2% (n = 331). Pre-TI oxygenation failure and shock were associated with higher odds of TI-CA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.29; 95% CI, 1.81-2.89 and aOR, 4.67; 95% CI, 3.68-5.92, respectively). Each additional TI attempt required was associated with increased odds of TI-CA (aOR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.56-1.85, for each attempt). Use of ketamine (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.82), propofol (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72), neuromuscular blockade (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.49-0.91), and video laryngoscopy (aOR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.6-0.97) were associated with lower odds of TI-CA. Mediation analysis indicated that 13% of video laryngoscopy's protective effect was due to a reduction in TI attempt counts. The protective effects of ketamine, propofol, and neuromuscular blockade were minimally mediated by reduced TI attempt counts (5%, 4%, and 7%).
CONCLUSIONS: TI-CA occurred in 1.2% of TIs performed in the PICUs. Odds of TI-CA increased incrementally with successive TI attempts. Video laryngoscopy was protective against TI-CA. Mediation analysis revealed that reduced TI attempts accounted for 13% of the protective benefit associated with video laryngoscopy.
authors: National Emergency Airway Registry for Children (NEAR4KIDS) investigators as a subgroup of Pediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators (PALISI)

articles.title: Anatomical and Functional Outcomes of Allogeneic Internal Limiting Membrane Transplantation for Refractory Full-Thickness Macular Holes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the anatomical, functional, and outer retinal structural outcomes of allogeneic internal limiting membrane (ILM) transplantation for the treatment of refractory full-thickness macular holes (MH) in eyes where autologous ILM is unavailable due to prior surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included 13 eyes of 13 patients. All surgeries were performed using a standard pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) under retrobulbar anesthesia. Allogeneic ILM grafts harvested from donor eyes were stored in Eusol-C at 4-8°C and transplanted under perfluorocarbon liquid using a bimanual forceps-assisted technique. When required, additional ILM tissue was inserted for complete defect filling, and the graft was stabilized with a dispersive viscoelastic agent under air. No postoperative head positioning was prescribed. Pre- and postoperative MH size, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), closure rate, and closure morphology were analyzed.
RESULTS: Anatomical closure was achieved in all eyes (100%), with primary closure in 12 eyes (92.3%) and successful closure after reoperation in one eye (7.7%). W-type closure was most frequent (61.5%), followed by V-type (30.8%) and U-type (7.7%). BCVA improved significantly from 20/200 (logMAR 1.00) to 20/66 (logMAR 0.52) at final follow-up, corresponding to a median gain of approximately 5 ETDRS lines (p<0.001), whereas intraocular pressure showed no significant change (p=0.118). Despite complete anatomical closure, ellipsoid zone defects persisted in all eyes (100%), and external limiting membrane defects were present in 76.9%, indicating limited outer retinal restoration.
CONCLUSION: In this 13-case retrospective series, allogeneic ILM transplantation provided consistent anatomical closure and meaningful visual improvement in refractory macular holes lacking autologous ILM, although restoration of outer retinal microstructure remained limited.

articles.title: Comparative outcomes of uni-portal non-coaxial spinal endoscopic surgery and unilateral biportal spinal endoscopy for far-lateral lumbar disc herniation involving the foraminal region: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety and efficacy of unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (UBE) and uniportal non-coaxial spinal endoscopic surgery (UNSES) in patients with far-lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH) involving the foraminal region.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 102 patients with foraminal-region FLLDH who were treated between January 2022 and October 2024. Among them, 43 patients underwent UNSES and 59 underwent UBE. Perioperative variables were recorded. Back and leg pain visual analog scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) scores, Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) scores, and modified Macnab outcomes were compared between groups preoperatively and at each postoperative follow-up. Preoperative and postoperative day 1 computed tomography images were analyzed to assess changes in foraminal area.
RESULTS: All procedures were completed successfully. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups. Operative time was significantly shorter in the UNSES group than in the UBE group (P < 0.001). In both groups, VAS scores for back and leg pain and ODI scores improved significantly from baseline at all postoperative follow-up time points (all P < 0.05). However, these outcomes did not differ significantly between the groups at any postoperative follow-up time point.On postoperative day 3, the JOA score was significantly higher in the UNSES group than in the UBE group (P = 0.031). JOA scores did not differ significantly between the groups at 3, 6, or 12 months after surgery. Imaging analysis showed that the foraminal area increased postoperatively in both groups. On postoperative day 1, the foraminal area was significantly greater in the UNSES group than in the UBE group (P = 0.017). Surgical-site infection occurred in one patient in the UBE group and two patients in the UNSES group. Neurologic symptoms or signs were observed in four patients in the UBE group and three patients in the UNSES group. These manifestations gradually resolved during follow-up after symptomatic treatment. Recurrence was observed in one patient in the UBE group and two patients in the UNSES group. At the final follow-up, clinical outcomes assessed using the modified Macnab criteria did not differ significantly between the groups.
CONCLUSION: Both UNSES and UBE resulted in significant pain relief and functional improvement in patients with foraminal-region FLLDH. Compared with UBE, UNSES was associated with shorter operative time and greater foraminal enlargement. However, long-term clinical outcomes were comparable between the two techniques.

articles.title: UTILITY OF INDOCYANINE GREEN FLUORESCENCE IMAGING IN BURN MANAGEMENT: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW.
articles.abstract: The implementation of near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging using indocyanine green (ICG) has seen a rising implementation in burn care in recent years, with expanding clinical indications and increasing evidence supporting its use. A systematic review was carried out following PRISMA guidelines, employing PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, and EMBASE databases to locate studies on the perioperative use of ICG in burn patients. Two independent reviewers assessed all articles for eligibility based on predefined inclusion criteria. Extracted data included study characteristics, patient demographics, clinical indications, ICG dosing regimens, administration timing, and reported perioperative outcomes. A total of 12 studies enrolling 204 burn patients, published between 1995 and 2025, were included for qualitative synthesis. Of these, 7 (58.3%) were prospective, single-center experimental studies; 3 (25%) were prospective, multicenter, blinded trials; 1 (8.3%) was a retrospective study; and 1 (8.3%) was a case series. The primary clinical uses of ICG in burn management included: assessment of burn depth reported in 6 studies, intraoperative delineation of necrotic tissue requiring excision in 3 studies, utility of ICG in liver function measurement in 2 studies and another research analyzed the estimation of plasma volume in burn patients. ICG fluorescence imaging is a promising adjunctive tool for burn assessment, particularly in identifying non-perfused tissue. It enhances the ability to accurately assess burn depth and helps to determine surgical margins during burn excision. Furthermore, ICG pharmacokinetics may provide insight into liver involvement and prognostic outlook in severe burn cases. However, its current role remains complementary to clinical evaluation. Further standardized and high-quality studies are required to define its diagnostic accuracy and clinical impact.

articles.title: Repeated intra-operative heparin dosing for cardiopulmonary bypass and the PRODOSE algorithm.
Salmon calcitonin prescribing for acute phantom limb pain after amputation.
The impact of dexmedetomidine on postoperative delirium and early postoperative cognitive impairment in elderly patients undergoing general surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Anesthetic management in general surgery poses substantial risks in elderly patients because age-related physiologic decline and preexisting comorbidities increase vulnerability to peri-operative complications. Older adults have reduced physiological reserve, impaired organ function, and slower recovery from surgical and anesthetic stress, placing them at increased risk for postoperative delirium and early postoperative cognitive impairment. Dexmedetomidine, a selective α2-adrenergic receptor agonist, has sedative, anti-inflammatory, and opioid-sparing properties that may influence early postoperative cognitive outcomes without significant respiratory depression. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between dexmedetomidine and 24-h postoperative delirium/early postoperative cognitive impairment in elderly patients undergoing general surgery. Four studies involving 479 patients met the inclusion criteria. Across the included studies, dexmedetomidine was generally administered as a 1 µg/kg loading dose followed by continuous intraoperative maintenance infusion of 0.2-0.7 µg/kg/h. Pooled analysis showed that dexmedetomidine was associated with significantly lower odds of 24-h postoperative delirium/early postoperative cognitive impairment compared with control treatment (pooled OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.24-0.61; p < 0.001). These findings suggest that dexmedetomidine is associated with lower odds of early postoperative cognitive outcomes in elderly surgical patients compared with control treatment. Larger, long-term studies are needed to confirm these findings and establish standardized dosing protocols.

articles.title: Clinical Factors Associated with Intraoperative Increase in Cardiac Troponin and Its Prognostic Value During Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative elevations of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) are common during liver transplantation (LT); however, the clinical significance of new-onset intraoperative elevations remains unclear. We evaluated the frequency, magnitude, associated factors, and prognostic implications of intraoperative hs-cTnI elevations, distinguishing new-onset from pre-existing elevations.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 4151 consecutive LT recipients (2008-2021). The primary endpoint was 90-day mortality. Elevated hs-cTnI was defined as > 40 pg/mL (1× upper reference limit [URL]). The relative importance of 19 variables for new-onset intraoperative hs-cTnI > 400 pg/mL (10× URL) was ranked using an exploratory shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis.
