RESULTS: Intraoperative hs-cTnI > 1× URL occurred in 66.1% (2745/4151) of patients, including new-onset elevation in 62.5% (2304/3685) of patients with normal baselines (~90% had an increase of > 20%). In pre-existing elevation, an exploratory threshold > 22× URL was associated with mortality (adjusted HR 5.91, 95% CI 3.11-11.22; P < 0.001), whereas new-onset elevation was not (P = 0.74). Per doubling of intraoperative hs-cTnI, 90-day mortality increased overall (adjusted HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.11-1.32) and in pre-existing elevation (adjusted HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.13-1.46; both P < 0.001). Low intraoperative hematocrit, anemia, factor VIII, von Willebrand factor, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio showed the highest SHAP importance for new-onset >10× URL.
CONCLUSIONS: New-onset intraoperative hs-cTnI elevations were common during LT and linked to anemia, hypercoagulability, and inflammation. However, they did not predict 90-day mortality in patients with normal baselines; risk increased only in pre-existing elevations. Intraoperative hs-cTnI elevations should be interpreted in the context of preoperative levels.

articles.title: Association of Altered Anteriorization of Electroencephalographic Alpha Oscillation During Transition to Unconsciousness With Postoperative Delirium: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During sevoflurane-induced anesthesia, electroencephalography analysis demonstrates alpha oscillations shifting from the occipital to the frontal regions, with further characteristic changes during maintenance and emergence. We aimed to exploratorily investigate whether alterations in alpha anteriorization and functional network efficiency are associated with postoperative delirium.
METHODS: This prospective, exploratory observational study enrolled 100 patients from a single tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into nondelirium (n = 81) and delirium (n = 19) groups based on delirium assessments. After excluding 17 patients due to artifacts on electroencephalography, 19-channel electroencephalography data were collected from 83 elderly patients under sevoflurane-induced anesthesia. Artifact-free epochs were extracted during the induction, maintenance, emergence, and postanesthesia care unit phases. Spectral, topographical, and network analyses were conducted. Postoperative delirium was assessed using confusion assessment method for intensive care unit and a chart review.
RESULTS: Significant group differences emerged just before the loss of responsiveness, with the nondelirium group exhibiting robust alpha power amplification across all brain regions (median [interquartile range {IQR}] in dB; frontal: 4.24 [1.86-6.57] vs -0.88 [-1.59-3.38], P = .007; parietal: 3.71 [0.51-5.55] vs -0.95 [-2.33-1.11], P = .046; occipital: 2.81 [0.49-5.71] vs -0.04 [-2.06-1.27], P = .048), whereas the delirium group showed minimal changes. During the maintenance phase, spectral analysis revealed higher alpha power in the nondelirium group across all 19 channels (frontal: 5.42 [2.90-8.16] vs 2.89 [-0.03-5.09], P = .007; 18 of 19 channels significant by false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected permutation test). Network analysis demonstrated longer averaged characteristic path lengths in the delirium group (mean ± standard deviation [SD], 4.49 ± 0.62 vs 3.57 ± 0.16, P = .026, FDR-corrected), consistently in the frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, suggesting reduced network efficiency.
CONCLUSIONS: Delirium was associated with early disruption of alpha anteriorization during induction and globally reduced functional network efficiency during maintenance. Perioperative electroencephalogram (EEG) transition features may serve as early markers of delirium susceptibility.

Pain management after total shoulder arthroplasty: a systematic review and procedure-specific postoperative pain management (PROSPECT) recommendations.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Total shoulder arthroplasty is associated with moderate-to-severe postoperative pain. The aim of this systematic review was to assess the available literature and provide PROSPECT (PROcedure SPECific Postoperative Pain ManagemenT) recommendations for optimal pain management after total shoulder arthroplasty.
METHODS: A systematic review utilising PROSPECT methodology was performed. Randomised controlled trials and systematic reviews published in the English language that assessed postoperative pain using analgesic, anaesthetic and surgical interventions were identified from databases.
RESULTS: Of the 1809 articles identified, 30 randomised controlled trials and seven systematic reviews/meta-analyses met our inclusion criteria. Interventions that improved postoperative pain relief included: paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; dexamethasone; interscalene brachial plexus block and, as an alternative, local infiltration analgesia. Conflicting evidence was found for continuous interscalene brachial plexus block (catheter) or liposomal bupivacaine for interscalene block or local infiltration analgesia. No evidence was found for a specific surgical technique.
DISCUSSION: In the absence of contraindication, the analgesic regimen should include: paracetamol; a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug administered peri-operatively and continued postoperatively; intravenous dexamethasone (8-10 mg); and postoperative opioids for rescue analgesia. As a regional technique, an interscalene brachial plexus block with a single-bolus injection of long-acting local anaesthetic (bupivacaine or ropivacaine), but not liposomal bupivacaine, should be provided. In case of contraindications or absence of expertise, local infiltration analgesia is a reasonable alternative. Further studies are required to investigate the analgesic benefit of a continuous infusion for the interscalene brachial plexus block.
authors: PROSPECT Working Group of the European Society of Regional Anaesthesia and Pain Therapy (ESRA)

articles.title: Pneumothorax rates following cardiac surgery with versus without continuous serratus anterior plane catheters: a secondary analysis of trial data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Moderate to severe pain is common after cardiac surgery, especially in the first two postoperative days. Inadequate pain control may prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay, may increase cost, and contributes to chronic pain. Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols prioritize multimodal analgesia, including regional anesthesia techniques. In a recent randomized trial with continuous serratus anterior plane (SAP) catheters, we found unexpectedly high pneumothorax rates. To address this, we aimed to design a propensity-score-matched comparison using patients from the same institution to control for institutional practice patterns, surgical techniques, and patient demographics that could confound comparisons with published literature rates from other centres.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of RCT data with propensity score matching to a historic cohort. We compared the pneumothorax rates in patients receiving continuous SAP catheters in our previous Cardiac-Serratus Anterior Plane (Cardiac-SAP) trial with those in a retrospective institutional database cohort of patients receiving standard care undergoing cardiac surgery via sternotomy. The two groups were propensity score matched in a 1:20 ratio based on age, sex, smoking status, surgery type, and pre-existing respiratory disease. We analyzed univariate comparisons using Fisher's exact test or the percentile bootstrapping method.
RESULTS: We matched 50 patients from the Cardiac-SAP trial to 989 retrospective cohort patients. After matching, the SAP catheter group was associated with a significantly higher risk of pneumothorax (12% vs 3%; odds ratio, 5.3; 95% confidence interval, 2.1 to 13.6; P < 0.001). There were no significant differences for other outcomes, including ICU readmissions, length of ventilation, and length of ICU or hospital stay. Patients who developed a pneumothorax had longer ventilation time and longer hospital stays.
CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggest that SAP catheter use as a part of a randomized trial for cardiac surgery was associated with a higher rate of pneumothorax in trial participants than in a historic cohort of a similar population, though causality is unclear. Differences in monitoring within the trial and the inherent risks in this population may have contributed.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
articles.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.
authors: American Heart Association Council on Cardiovascular Surgery and Anesthesia, Education and Publication Committee; Council on Clinical Cardiology; Council on Cardiovascular Surgery and Anesthesia; Council on Peripheral Vascular Disease; Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young; and Council on Cardiovascular Radiology and Intervention

articles.title: Management of Antiplatelet Regimen During Surgical Procedures: A Report From the MARS Registry.
articles.abstract: Optimal perioperative management of patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial, with substantial variability in current clinical practice. The MARS registry is a prospective multicenter observational study evaluating perioperative outcomes in post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing surgery within 2 years of PCI. We assessed the incidence of Net Adverse Cardiovascular Events (NACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization, or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type ≥3 bleeding. A total of 132 consecutive patients undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery were followed from 14 days preoperatively to 30 days postoperatively. Of the 132 patients, 79 underwent noncardiac surgery (NCS) and 53 underwent cardiac surgery (CS). The mean age was 66 years, and 68% were male. Diabetes mellitus was present in 48%, chronic kidney disease in 29%, and 42% had undergone PCI for an acute coronary syndrome. Mean time from PCI to surgery was 269 ± 217 days. Previous bleeding and stent thrombosis were reported in 11% and 5% of patients, respectively. Aspirin was continued in 60% and P2Y12 inhibitors in 36%, with mean discontinuation 4 and 6 days preoperatively, respectively. Intravenous antiplatelet bridging with cangrelor was used in 12 patients (9.1%) and unfractionated heparin as anticoagulant therapy in 15 patients (11%). NACE occurred more frequently after CS compared with NCS (18.9% vs 10.1%, p = 0.17). Major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium ≥3) occurred in 5.3% with no difference between CS and NCS. There were no cardiovascular deaths and no difference in all-cause mortality. Compared with no bridging, cangrelor bridging was associated with numerically higher NACE (25% vs 12.5%, p = 0.22), without differences in bleeding. On multivariable logistic regression, cangrelor bridging was not independently associated with NACE (adjusted odds ratio 2.18, 95% confidence interval 0.43 to 8.71, p = 0.34). In conclusion, among post-PCI patients on DAPT undergoing moderate- to high-risk surgery, aspirin was continued in 60%, cangrelor bridging was used in 9.1%, and although NACE rates were numerically higher after CS and with bridging, these differences were not significant after multivariable adjustment, consistent with confounding by indication.

articles.title: Impact of hypothermia level on neurological and renal outcomes in emergency aortic surgery: a single-centre experience.
articles.abstract: BackgroundTemperature management during emergency surgery for acute aortic syndrome is critical for neurological, renal, and systemic protection. Recent European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines recommend moderate hypothermia with antegrade cerebral perfusion for hemiarch procedures. Nevertheless, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA) remains common. This study evaluates neurological and other postoperative outcomes across different intraoperative temperature ranges.MethodsA single-centre retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing surgery for acute aortic syndrome between 2018-2023. Demographic, intraoperative, and postoperative data on mortality, hospitalization, neurological, renal outcomes, and blood product usage were collected. Patients were stratified by intraoperative temperature: deep (≤20°C), low-moderate (20.1-24°C), high-moderate (24.1-28°C), and mild (>28°C) hypothermia. Logistic regression identified predictors of binary adverse outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was conducted using 24.0°C as the threshold in hemiarch surgery patients.ResultsA total of 175 patients (median age 64 years; 37% female) were included; of whom 89% underwent hemiarch replacement. Cardiopulmonary bypass duration decreased progressively with warmer intraoperative temperatures, ranging from 270.5 minutes in deep hypothermia to 164 minutes in mild hypothermia. The 30-day mortality was 18.9% (n = 33/175), and the overall stroke rate was 19.4% (n = 34/175). Among patients undergoing hemiarch repair, warmer temperatures were associated with lower stroke incidence (mild hypothermia 11%) compared with high-moderate (8.8%), low-moderate (26%), and deep hypothermia (27%) (p = 0.049), and with shorter intensive care admission (p = 0.036). However, multivariate regression showed that the four-category comparison did not reach significance for the assessed outcomes once adjusted for confounding variables. A sensitivity analysis at 24.0°C showed an independent association with reduced stroke risk (OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.64, p = 0.005).DiscussionOur findings support current EACTS recommendations favouring moderate-to-mild hypothermia for hemiarch replacement, with potential protective effects. Further studies should determine the optimal temperature strategy for patients undergoing total arch replacement.

articles.title: Cinchona Alkaloids-Derived Ammonium Salts for Long-Acting and Sensory-Selective Nerve Blockades.
articles.abstract: Local anesthetics (LAs), a type of substance with the ability of blocking nerve fiber conduction, are indispensable in clinical practice for pain relief. However, the duration of action and sensory-motor nerve selectivity of conventional LAs require further optimization. Herein, we wish to report the discovery of novel ammonium salts derived from natural cinchona alkaloids for long-acting and sensory-selective nerve blockades. The bicyclic quincoridine skeleton exhibited superior nerve blockade efficacy compared to acyclic and monocyclic analogs. Compound CLA-1-3 produced prolonged nerve blockade (over 50 h) in the rat sciatic nerve block model, possessing an IC50 value of approximately 0.39 μmol/L for voltage-gated sodium channel inhibition. On the other hand, at a concentration range of 0.30% to 0.60%, compound CLA-3-5 achieved sensory-selective nerve blockade lasting up to 3 h. The candidate molecules and underlying mechanistic insights will be valuable assets for drug development and therapeutic innovation.

articles.title: Potential sphenopalatine ganglion block efficacy as an alternative to epidural bloodpatch for post-dural puncture headache: a monocentric french study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-dural puncture headache (PDPH) is a common complication of lumbar puncture caused by cerebrospinal fluid leakage and intracranial hypotension. Epidural blood patch (EBP) is considered the gold standard treatment but remains invasive. Sphenopalatine ganglion block (SPGB), a non-invasive technique, has shown promising results in recent studies, but it was not evaluated as an alternative of EBP. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of SPGB in PDPH by determining whether it could reduce the need for EBP in clinical practice.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective monocentric cohort study including patients meeting ICHD-3 criteria for PDPH with significant pain or functional impairment. SPGB was performed using lidocaine 5% administered via an atomization device (MADgic™). Pain intensity was measured using a visual analog scale (VAS) at predefined intervals up to 24 h. In cases of SPGB failure, EBP was performed. Demographic and procedural variables were recorded. SPGB was considered clinically relevant if it prevented at least 50% of EBPs; 14 patients were required to achieve 90% power with alpha risk of 5%.
RESULTS: Fourteen patients (mean age 31.9 years; 78% women) were analyzed. SPGB was performed a median of 3 days after PDPH onset. Five patients (36%) required subsequent EBP, meaning 64% were successfully managed with SPGB alone, exceeding the predefined efficacy threshold. VAS scores showed significant pain reduction from 45 min post-procedure, sustained at 24 h. A trend toward association between traumatic needle use and SPGB failure was observed (80% vs. 22%, p = 0.091). Throat numbness was more frequent in responders (p = 0.014). No serious adverse events occurred; tolerability was rated good to moderate.
CONCLUSION: SPGB appears safe, well tolerated, and effective in a substantial proportion of PDPH cases, potentially reducing the need for EBP. Based on these findings, we proposed an algorithm for PDPH management. Larger comparative studies are needed to establish definitive treatment recommendations.

articles.title: Neonatal brain network integration trajectories predict neurodevelopment in congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infants with critical congenital heart disease (CHD) are at high risk for abnormal brain development and later neurodevelopmental impairment. We hypothesized that the trajectory of perioperative whole-brain network development would predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood.
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal cohort of neonates with critical CHD (n = 97) underwent preoperative and/or postoperative brain MRI with diffusion imaging. Whole-brain network measures were derived from structural connectomes from 80 infants, and 50 had neurodevelopment assessed at 1-4 years using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development.
RESULTS: White matter injury was associated with a slower perioperative increase in global efficiency (p = 0.013), a measure of network integration, whereas cardiac physiology was not associated with network development. Infants with greater perioperative increases in global efficiency had higher cognitive (p = 0.001), language (p < 0.001), and motor (p = 0.008) scores. For each 1-standard deviation increase in the trajectory of global efficiency, cognitive scores increased by 8.2 points (95% CI: 3.64-12.78), independent of brain injury and socioeconomic factors.
CONCLUSION: In infants with critical CHD, longitudinal whole-brain network development was associated with neurodevelopment across multiple domains. Early network development may serve as a biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience in this population.
IMPACT: In infants with critical congenital heart disease, perioperative increase in whole-brain network integration was associated with cognitive, language, and motor outcomes in early childhood. White matter injury was associated with a slower increase in network integration, whereas cardiac physiology subtype was not associated with network development. This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

Greater and Lesser Occipital Nerve Blocks for Frequent and Severe Headaches in Children and Adolescents: A Protocolized Repetitive Intervention Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Headache management in children and adolescents remains challenging, particularly in patients with high headache-related disability, medication overuse, and comorbid conditions, for whom evidence-based preventive treatment options are limited and often ineffective. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes and safety of a protocolized, repetitive bilateral greater and lesser occipital nerve block (GONB/LONB) strategy in pediatric patients with frequent and severe headaches.
METHODS: This retrospective study included adolescents aged 11-18 years who underwent bilateral GONB and LONB for headache between 2018 and 2025. At each treatment session, 1 mL of 2% lidocaine was administered at each of four injection sites (bilateral GON and LON), corresponding to a total volume of 4 mL (80 mg) per session. Blocks were administered weekly for 4 weeks, followed by additional applications at 1 and 3 months. Headache severity and disability were evaluated using the visual analog scale (VAS) and the Pediatric Migraine Disability Assessment (PedMIDAS) before and after completion of the block protocol.
RESULTS: Forty-five patients (91.1% female) received a total of 258 bilateral GONB/LONB procedures. The mean number of headache days per month was 20.8 ± 7.9, and the mean headache duration was 11.6 ± 10.7 months. Significant reductions were observed in both VAS and PedMIDAS disability grades following treatment (p < 0.001). At the patient level, 41 of 45 patients (91.1%) met the predefined criteria for clinical response. No serious adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Protocolized repetitive bilateral GONB/LONB was well tolerated and was associated with reductions in headache severity and headache-related disability in this predominantly adolescent cohort. However, the uncontrolled retrospective design precludes attribution of these improvements specifically to the intervention. Prospective sham-controlled studies are needed to establish treatment-specific efficacy.

articles.title: Comparison of oral 5-aminolevulinic acid-induced hypotension between general and spinal anesthesia during photodynamic diagnosis-assisted transurethral resection of bladder tumor for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) using photodynamic diagnosis (PDD) with oral 5-aminolevulinic acid hydrochloride (5-ALA) with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) frequently results in hypotension being reported as a common serious side effect. Previous papers have reported that oral 5-ALA-induced hypotension is associated with both general and spinal anesthesia However, no study has analyzed oral 5-ALA-induced hypotension by separately evaluating each anesthesia type.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared the systolic blood pressure (SBP) values with the frequency of vasopressor uses between general anesthesia group of 295 patients and spinal anesthesia group of 139 patients. Multivariable logistic regression analysis between general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups was performed for hypotensive patients with SBP less than 80 mmHg using vasopressors.
RESULTS: A total of 434 patients who underwent PDD‑TURBT were included in the final analysis. The incidence of hypotension and the incidence of severe hypotension (among cases of hypotension) were determined for the general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups. The mean intraoperative lowest SBP was 73.1 mmHg in the general anesthesia group and 95.2 mmHg in the spinal anesthesia group (p < 0.001). In general anesthesia, older age, shorter 5‑ALA exposure, and lower initial SBP at the beginning of anesthesia predicted hypotension, whereas in spinal anesthesia, male sex and lower initial SBP at the beginning of anesthesia were significant predictors by multivariate analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: The risk factors for oral 5‑ALA‑induced hypotension differ between the general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups, which is highlighting the importance of managing blood pressure while considering the specific risks associated with each type of anesthesia.

articles.title: Effects of cannabidiol (CBD) oral solution in patients undergoing bilateral total knee arthroplasty: A randomized, controlled, parallel, triple blind, pilot study.
articles.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid with limited clinical evidence of its analgesic and opioid sparing effects. In the United States, the oral cannabidiol solution, Epidiolex®, is FDA-approved for intractable seizures. We conducted an off-label pilot randomized trial to evaluate its perioperative effects in patients undergoing bilateral total knee arthroplasty (BTKA). After IRB-approval and trial registration (NCT04749628), 36 patients were randomized to receive four perioperative doses of placebo (n=12), 400 mg (n=12) or 800 mg (n=12) oral CBD with standardized anesthesia and multimodal analgesia. The primary outcome was cumulative 72-hour opioid consumption (MME). Secondary outcomes included pain scores, adjunct analgesic use, inflammatory markers (IL-6), sleep, mood (HADS), safety, and pharmacokinetics. Dunnett's test showed no significant differences in 72-hour opioid consumption versus placebo (400 mg: 144 vs 209 MME, p=0.10; 800 mg: 203.2 vs 209 MME, p=0.98), although post hoc testing demonstrated lower opioid use with 400 mg CBD compared with placebo (p=0.04). The 400 mg group also had lower pain scores and fewer rescue analgesic requirements, but greater NSAID use. The 800 mg group showed no opioid-sparing effect and had greater adverse event burden. CBD groups reported improved subjective sleep domains, while anxiety and depression scores were higher, particularly at 800 mg. IL-6 levels were higher in CBD groups. Pharmacokinetic analyses confirmed measurable, dose-dependent exposure with substantial interindividual variability. These pilot data suggest a potential therapeutic signal at moderate dosing but not at higher doses. Larger trials are needed to confirm efficacy and define optimal dosing. PERSPECTIVE: Among BTKA patients, 400 mg cannabidiol reduced opioid use and pain while remaining tolerable, whereas higher dosing increased side effects, supporting further evaluation of CBD analgesia.

articles.title: Principles of drug dosing for obese patients in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The increasing prevalence of severe obesity in intensive care unit (ICU) patients has led to several challenges with medication dosing. Doses listed in product labels or tertiary references typically do not account for the pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic variability encountered with obesity, leading to the potential for treatment failure or an adverse effect. The purpose of this review is to provide guidance for ICU clinicians when crafting pharmacotherapy regimens in critically ill patients with extreme obesity.
METHODS: A literature search was performed to identify relevant articles pertaining to the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of medications in obese patients. Articles describing both general treatment principles and medication specific assessments were retrieved. Bibliographies were searched for additional publications.
RESULTS: Evidence guiding medication use in critically ill obese patients is limited by the small number of patients with more extreme forms of obesity, the lack of clinical outcome measurements, and the few studies that are specific to the ICU. Obesity-related alterations in pharmacokinetic parameters, such as apparent volume of distribution and drug clearance, may hinder attainment of pharmacodynamic targets. Individualized dosing strategies are essential to optimize therapeutic outcomes. This review provides dosing recommendations for selected ICU medications and proposes a practical framework to guide medication dosing decisions in this patient population.
CONCLUSION: Drug dosing in critically ill obese patients should be individualized by assessing pharmacokinetic variability and whether pharmacodynamic goals can be achieved. Selecting the correct weight for weight-based calculations or dose for fixed regimens is paramount for achieving these goals. Consultation with a clinical pharmacist may be beneficial.

articles.title: Differences in donation after circulatory determination of death (DCD) liver donor management-An international survey initiated by the International Liver Transplantation Society (ILTS), Society for the Advancement of Transplant Anesthesia (SATA), and Liver Intensive Care Group of Europe (LICAGE).
articles.abstract: We conducted a survey to evaluate variability in determination of death and management of donation after circulatory determination of death (DCD) liver donors across different countries. In all, 153 centers from 17 countries were included (48.4% US, 51.6% non-US). Most reported using onset of hemodynamic instability, rather than withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy (WLST), as the beginning of the waiting time for decision-making related to organ acceptance (76.1% US vs. 47.1% non-US). Actual and maximum acceptable waiting times were comparable between groups (43.7 vs. 50.2 and 50.8 vs. 60.3 min, respectively), frequently exceeding limits defined by national policies. Onset of hemodynamic instability was most commonly defined using systolic blood pressure (SBP) alone (51.4% US vs. 31.6% non-US) or a combination of SBP and oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) (41.6% US vs. 56.6% non-US). Less commonly, centers used SpO 2 (4.2% vs. 3.9%) or arrythymia alone (1.4% US vs. 0.0% non-US). Thresholds for SBP and SpO2 were similar between US and non-US centers (SBP 80 mm Hg; and 80% for both). Sedation and analgesia for donor comfort were used less frequently in US centers compared with non-US centers (27.8% vs. 48.1%, p =0.02). Decision-making regarding waiting time was more commonly performed by a multidisciplinary team outside the US (26.1% vs. 52.0%). Over half of US and non-US centers reported using machine perfusion in over 50% of DCD grafts (64.9% vs. 51.9%). When used, normothermic regional perfusion cannulation was more commonly initiated after declaration of death (71.6% US vs. 62.0% non-US). These findings demonstrate substantial variability in DCD donor management. Standardization of definitions and practices, particularly with regard to exclusion of hemodynamic stability period from warm ischemic time (WIT), may improve consistency in decision-making related to organ acceptance.

articles.title: Multimodal Antiemetic Prophylaxis in Patients Undergoing Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty: A Single-Center Retrospective Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) is associated with a high incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) due to gastric volume reduction, preservation of vagal innervation, and inherent patient-related risk factors. Standard antiemetic prophylactic regimens are frequently insufficient in this population. This case series describes the clinical experience and postoperative outcomes associated with a multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis regimen.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective case series, data from 20 adult patients who underwent ESG under general anesthesia were analyzed. Anesthesia maintenance was standardized using manually controlled intravenous infusions of propofol and remifentanil (TIVA), without volatile anesthetics. Multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis consisted of intravenous granisetron (3 mg), dexamethasone (8 mg), haloperidol (1 mg at induction + 1 mg before emergence), and fosaprepitant (150 mg). Postoperative analgesia was managed primarily with paracetamol and ibuprofen. The primary outcome was clinically documented PONV during the early postoperative period, including the PACU stay and the first 12 postoperative hours. Emergency department presentations for severe PONV within 5 postoperative days were assessed as a secondary outcome using institutional electronic health records.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 20 patients (70% female, mean age 41.05 ± 11.22 years, mean BMI 38.33 ± 4.94 kg/m2). Comorbidities were present in 55% of patients, and 80% were non-smokers. During the early postoperative period, no clinically documented episodes of PONV requiring rescue antiemetic treatment were identified.
CONCLUSION: In this small retrospective case series, multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis combined with TIVA was associated with no institutionally documented early postoperative PONV presentations and emergency department presentations for severe PONV within 5 days after ESG. Prospective studies with standardized postoperative PONV assessment are needed to determine the efficacy of this approach. Given the limitations of a retrospective case series, prospective controlled trials incorporating systematic PONV severity scoring are warranted to establish optimized guidelines.
articles.journal: J Laparoendosc Adv Surg Tech A

articles.title: Recent Advances in Research on Risk Prediction of Complications Following Transnasal Endoscopic Surgery for Pituitary Tumors.
articles.abstract: Transnasal endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery has become the primary treatment modality for pituitary tumors, offering advantages such as minimal invasiveness, clear visualization, and rapid recovery. However, postoperative complications remain relatively common, and severe cases can affect patient prognosis or even be life-threatening. Research on risk factors and risk prediction for postoperative complications after endoscopic endonasal pituitary surgery has gradually increased. These studies cover various aspects, including patient demographic characteristics, underlying medical diseases, tumor features, surgical techniques, and perioperative management, and attempt to quantitatively assess the risk of complications using statistical models and visualization tools. While existing studies have made some progress in identifying certain high-risk factors, challenges remain, including limited sample sizes, inconsistent definitions of outcome measures, insufficient external validation of predictive models, and limited clinical applicability. A systematic review of progress in risk prediction research for complications after endoscopic endonasal pituitary surgery will help clarify current research priorities and gaps, providing a theoretical basis for developing stable, reliable, and clinically useful risk prediction models.

articles.title: Clinical safety, tolerability, and efficacy of fospropofol disodium for sedation: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fospropofol disodium (fospropofol) is a water-soluble prodrug of propofol with a distinct pharmacological and tolerability profile. However, evidence regarding the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of fospropofol across broader sedation contexts and different comparators remains insufficiently synthesized. This systematic review summarized current research findings on fospropofol to clarify its clinical role and guide future research.
METHODS: This systematic review was registered prior to initiation (PROSPERO CRD42023477740). Comprehensive searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via Ovid, Embase via Ovid, ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to 26 August 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating fospropofol for sedation and reporting extractable efficacy or safety outcomes were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated according to the GRADE approach. Meta-analysis was performed for clinically comparable evidence groups, with other findings synthesized according to SWiM principles.
RESULTS: This systematic review included 10 original studies, comprising six procedural-sedation trials and four trials for ICU sedation. Quantitative synthesis was conducted for two comparable evidence groups, whereas the remaining outcomes were synthesized narratively. In three endoscopic procedural-sedation trials, fospropofol 6.5 mg/kg achieved a higher sedation success than 2 mg/kg (RR 3.27, 95% CI 2.62-4.08). In mechanically ventilated ICU patients, hypotension risk did not clearly differ between fospropofol and propofol (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.67-1.28). Procedural studies showed a dose-dependent pattern in sedation efficacy, whereas ICU studies generally reported comparable target-sedation attainment between fospropofol and comparator sedatives. Paresthesia/pruritus was commonly reported, while rates of cardiorespiratory adverse events varied across settings and doses and showed no consistent comparative advantage for fospropofol. Evidence for injection pain and satisfaction was limited. Certainty of evidence ranged from high to very low, mainly because of risk of bias and imprecision.
CONCLUSIONS: Fospropofol can provide effective sedation across procedural and ICU settings, but its efficacy and safety profiles vary according to dose, comparator, and clinical setting. Higher doses may improve procedural-sedation efficacy but may also increase adverse effects in some settings. Current evidence does not establish a consistent cardiorespiratory safety advantage for fospropofol over other sedatives, and further adequately powered randomized trials are needed to clarify its comparative safety and optimal clinical role.

articles.title: Age-stratified mortality following operative management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT/OBJECTIVE: Postoperative mortality following traumatic subaxial cervical spinal cord injury (cSCI) remains substantial, yet the combined influence of neurologic completeness and age on survival is poorly characterized in operatively treated patients. This study evaluated age-stratified mortality after surgical management of complete versus incomplete traumatic subaxial cSCI.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using risk ratio analysis, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards.
SETTING: Global federated electronic health record database (TriNetX).
PARTICIPANTS: Adults who underwent surgery for traumatic subaxial cSCI, identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes, with injury classified as complete or incomplete (n = 5,477).
INTERVENTIONS: Operative management of traumatic subaxial cSCI.
OUTCOME MEASURES: All-cause mortality at 3, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively. Independent predictors of mortality were identified via Cox regression.
RESULTS: Complete cSCI was associated with significantly higher mortality at 3 months (10.73% vs. 7.7%; RR 1.39), 6 months (12.5% vs. 9.2%; RR 1.36), and 1 year (14.7% vs. 11.2%; RR 1.31) (all P < 0.001). Mortality differences were most pronounced in patients aged 61-80 years, with approximately twofold higher risk in complete injuries. Increasing age, male sex, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease independently predicted mortality.
CONCLUSION: Complete traumatic cSCI carries significantly higher postoperative mortality than incomplete injury, particularly among patients aged 61-80 years. These findings underscore the combined prognostic impact of neurologic severity and age, and may guide perioperative counseling and risk stratification, but should not be interpreted as demonstrating formal age-dependent effect modification.

articles.title: Perioperative Neurocognitive Disorders in Older Adults: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Evidence-Informed Management.
articles.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PNDs) encompass cognitive change identified before or after surgery. Postoperative delirium (POD) is an acute, fluctuating disorder of attention and awareness, whereas delayed neurocognitive recovery and postoperative mild or major neurocognitive disorder describe objectively assessed decline over longer intervals. This narrative review focuses on older adults undergoing noncardiac and cardiac surgery and examines neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, neurotransmitter imbalance, oxidative stress, synaptic dysfunction, candidate fluid biomarkers, and electroencephalography (EEG) features, and evidence-informed management. Multicomponent prevention, medication review, mobilization, sleep support, and individualized anesthetic care remain the most defensible clinical strategies. EEG-guided anesthetic titration can reduce anesthetic exposure but has not consistently reduced POD. Blood biomarkers, machine-learning models, trial-by-trial neural variability, and noninvasive brain stimulation are promising research tools, but none currently replaces standardized clinical assessment or justifies routine mechanism-specific treatment.

articles.title: Environmental and systems-based safety in the obstetric operating room: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Cesarean delivery requires an operating room (OR) that supports maternal surgery and anesthesia while preparing for fetal-to-newborn transition and, when needed, concurrent maternal and neonatal resuscitation. This narrative review applies a human factors framework to noise, information displays, medication and equipment organization, layout, communication, ergonomics, and emergency preparedness. These factors are examined in relation to hearing the awake patient's concerns, recognizing maternal or fetal deterioration, accessing hemorrhage treatment, and coordinating newborn assessment without interrupting maternal care. Standardized layouts, structured communication, cognitive aids, and simulation may improve care processes, but evidence for their effects on maternal and neonatal morbidity varies, and some findings are extrapolated from non-obstetric surgery. Environmental safety initiatives should therefore assess both the reliability of cesarean care and patient outcomes, including maternal morbidity, newborn thermal status, and the maternal birth experience.

articles.title: Anesthesia Considerations for Transfemoral Osseointegration in a Patient With CRPS, Propofol, and Ketamine Allergies: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A 20-year-old female with asthma, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, mast cell activation syndrome, and complex regional pain syndrome Type 1 (CRPS1) presented for left transfemoral amputation with osseointegration and nerve reconstruction. To limit CRPS1 exacerbation, neuraxial anesthesia with femoral and sciatic blocks was administered for analgesia. Given the reported history of convulsions following ketamine and propofol, sedation with midazolam, dexmedetomidine, and fentanyl was used. On POD 1, fascia iliaca and sciatic blocks were repeated to mitigate postoperative pain. There were no intraoperative or postoperative complications. With limited literature on anesthesia for osseointegration, this novel case highlights individualized planning, in the setting of adverse responses to anesthetic medications and challenging pain management.

articles.title: A three-month physiology score correlates with CLAD after lung transplant.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Long-term survival after lung transplant is limited by chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD). Oscillometry is a novel pulmonary function technique that complements spirometry. We hypothesise that oscillometry and spirometry at 3 months post-transplant are associated with CLAD.
METHODS: Double lung transplant recipients (n=280) were enrolled from 2017 to 2020 for oscillometry at the first post-transplant spirometry. We excluded re-transplantation and patients missing 3-month oscillometry-spirometry data. Patients who died within 3 years where a CLAD diagnosis was ascertained were included. We used Mann-Whitney U and Pearson’s χ2 tests for group comparisons, logistic regression to assess the associations of spirometry and oscillometry with CLAD, and receiver operating characteristic curves to identify the threshold values for CLAD.
RESULTS: At 3 years post-transplant, 129 were alive and CLAD-free while 75 patients had CLAD. Preoperative and perioperative characteristics were similar except for higher body mass index in the CLAD group. At 3 months, CLAD patients had lower forced expiratory volume in 1 s (%FEV1) and FEV1/FVC (forced vital capacity), and worst lung mechanics with high R5 (resistance at 5 Hz), low X5 (reactance at 5 Hz) and high AX (area of reactance). %FEV1, FEV1/FVC, R5 and R5−19 (difference in resistance from 5 to 19 Hz), X5, X5 z-score and AX were independently associated with CLAD. A composite metric of %FEV1, FEV1/FVC, R5 z-score, R5−19 and AX provided the strongest association with CLAD.
CONCLUSIONS: The 3-month composite spirometry-oscillometry score post-transplant provides risk stratification of CLAD. Patients at risk can be monitored closely, to enable earlier interventions and minimise progression to CLAD.

articles.title: Organ damage after hemorrhagic shock: roles of anesthesia, shock duration, and assessment time.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic shock (HS) is a condition associated with organ failure. Animal models are widely used to study pathophysiology and potential therapies. Our aim was to clarify how anesthetic choice, shock duration, decompensation phase length, and time post-reperfusion influence plasma damage markers in HS. For this, male rats were anesthetized with either thiopental or ketamine/xylazine and subjected to HS. Blood pressure was reduced to 40 mmHg for 60 or 90 minutes, followed by reperfusion with shed blood. Blood samples were collected 4 or 24 hours after reperfusion. Liver and renal damage were observed in animals that underwent a 90-minute shock, but not a 60-minute shock. Animals anesthetized with ketamine/xylazine exhibited higher hepatic aminotransferases levels than those anesthetized with thiopental, suggesting more severe liver injury in the former group. AST levels were higher 4 hours after reperfusion. The duration of decompensation phase was positively correlated with liver injury but not with kidney dysfunction. Cardiovascular parameters and other organ damage markers were similar among the groups. Therefore, HS protocols in rats require a minimum of 90 minutes of the ischemic phase to induce consistent organ dysfunction detectable through plasma markers. The duration of the decompensation phase directly influences the outcome.

articles.title: Routine MRI in Pediatric Scoliosis: A Narrative Review of Risk-Stratified and Abbreviated Protocols.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the reference standard for detecting neural axis abnormalities (NAA) in children with presumed idiopathic scoliosis, but whether MRI should be used routinely or selectively remains debated. This SANRA-guided narrative review used structured searches of MEDLINE/PubMed, last run on July 19, 2026, to examine NAA prevalence, the performance of clinical and radiographic predictors, risk-stratified imaging, abbreviated MRI, and the consequences of imaging. Large series and pooled analyses report NAA in approximately 8-10% of presumed idiopathic cases, with higher prevalence in early-onset, congenital, and neurologically abnormal presentations. No single predictor, including left thoracic curvature or abnormal abdominal reflexes, reliably excludes intraspinal pathology. We propose a two-axis strategy that reframes the question from whether to image to when, for whom, and in what form. Axis 1 is PACE (Presentation age, Anatomic etiology, Curve characteristics, Examination), a literature-derived, rule-based, unvalidated framework in which the highest-risk finding determines a high-, intermediate-, or low-risk tier; some thresholds are expert assumptions. Axis 2 is protocol intensity: early full whole-spine MRI, abbreviated first-line MRI, or surveillance with predefined escalation. Evidence for abbreviated MRI is limited to one small retrospective single-center early-onset scoliosis cohort (n = 50), in which limited sagittal sequences identified all 10 NAA detected on full MRI with an estimated 68% shorter acquisition; diagnostic accuracy, anesthesia savings, and cost effects remain unproven. PACE is not a clinical prediction rule or guideline. The conceptual contribution of this review is to separate two decisions that are usually conflated, who should be imaged (risk stratification) and in what form (protocol intensity); both axes, and artificial-intelligence triage, require prospective multicenter and external validation.

articles.title: Economic Value and Caregiver Burden of Continuous Fascia iliaca Compartment Block in Elderly Patients with Intertrochanteric or Subtrochanteric Fracture: A Cost-Consequence Analysis Based on a Propensity Score-Matched Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fracture imposes substantial clinical and economic burden on older adults in China. Continuous fascia iliaca compartment block (CFICB) may improve perioperative recovery in elderly patients with intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric fracture, but its economic consequences remain uncertain. We compared direct medical costs, caregiver-related indirect costs, and clinical outcomes of CFICB with routine systemic analgesia (RA; a non-block regimen, distinct from regional anaesthesia, of which CFICB is itself a technique).
METHODS: We performed a cost-consequence analysis alongside a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study at Beijing Friendship Hospital. Patients aged ≥65 years treated January 2020-December 2023 were included after 1:1 matching (CFICB n = 40; RA n = 40). Healthcare-system and societal perspectives were adopted over a pre-specified one-month postoperative horizon. Direct costs came from itemised billing; caregiver time costs were valued by the replacement-cost approach and productivity losses by the human capital approach. Mean cost differences and 95% CIs used bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Total hospitalisation costs did not differ significantly between groups (CFICB ¥51,346 ± 10,924 vs RA ¥52,481 ± 12,267; difference -¥1,135; 95% CI -¥6,287 to +¥4,017; P = 0.523). CFICB was associated with lower scheduled-analgesic (-¥177), opioid-rescue (-¥142), cognitive-change-management (-¥2,473), rehabilitation (-¥631), and ward-overhead costs from a 2.4-day shorter stay (-¥1,440; 12.3 vs 14.7 days; P = 0.001). Informal caregiver time costs (-¥3,249) and productivity losses (-¥2,536) were lower with CFICB, yielding caregiver-related indirect savings of ¥5,785 per patient; this reflects caregiverborne costs only, not total societal cost.
CONCLUSION: In this single-centre matched cohort, total hospitalisation cost did not differ significantly between groups (difference -¥1,135; P = 0.523), while pre-specified downstream and caregiver-related costs were lower with CFICB. Given the small, single-centre, retrospective design, these hypothesisgenerating findings warrant cautious interpretation and support prospective, multicentre evaluation of CFICB in elderly proximal femoral fracture patients.

articles.title: Post-cesarean analgesia: transversalis fascia plane block versus wound infiltration in a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to compare ultrasound-guided transversalis fascia plane block with local wound infiltration using equivalent local anesthetic doses within a standardized multimodal analgesia protocol.
METHODS: This prospective, single-blind randomized trial was conducted between May and June 2024 at a tertiary care hospital. Women with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II-III undergoing cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia received either bilateral ultrasound-guided transversalis fascia plane block or local wound infiltration with the same total dose and volume of bupivacaine. All patients were managed with standardized multimodal analgesia. Patients with contraindications to the study interventions or inability to use patient-controlled analgesia were excluded. The primary outcome was 24-h opioid consumption. Secondary outcomes included pain scores, rescue analgesia use, opioid-related adverse events, and complications.
RESULTS: Forty-two patients (n=21/group) were analyzed. Twenty-four-hour opioid consumption was similar between transversalis fascia plane block and local wound infiltration groups (median 100 [65-152] mg vs. 85 [65-135] mg; p=0.554). Pain scores remained low and comparable throughout 48 h. Rescue analgesia was rarely required, and no postoperative nausea, opioid-related adverse events, or procedure-related complications were observed.
CONCLUSION: In a standardized multimodal analgesia setting after cesarean delivery, transversalis fascia plane block did not reduce opioid consumption or improve postoperative pain scores compared with local wound infiltration.

articles.title: Application of image analysis in the evaluation of blood feeding by Lutzomyia longipalpis using an artificial feeding system with synthetic membranes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood feeding is essential for the maintenance of laboratory colonies and for experimental studies involving sand fly-parasite interactions. However, artificial feeding systems for Lutzomyia longipalpis, the principal vector of Leishmania infantum, the etiological agent of visceral leishmaniasis in the Americas, remain limited by low engorgement rates and methodological constraints in blood meal quantification.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the feeding performance of Lu. longipalpis on different membranes in an artificial feeder and applied an image-based approach to quantify blood meal size.
METHODS: Females were fed either on anaesthetised hamsters (in vivo control) or using a Hemotek® artificial feeder equipped with chick skin (CHK), hydrated collagen membrane treated with plasma gel (COL+PG), or untreated hydrated collagen membrane (COL). Blood meal size was estimated through digital image analysis in Fiji/ImageJ using two regions of interest: whole abdomen area (AbdA) and red-coloured blood area (BldA).
FINDINGS: Feeding rates were highest on live hosts (88.75%), followed by CHK (72.34%) and COL+PG (72.08%), whereas COL yielded significantly lower engorgement (54.67%). Although abdominal area was greater in females fed on hamsters, no significant differences in red-coloured area were detected among artificial membrane treatments. A strong positive correlation was observed between AbdA and BldA measurements (R² = 0.85), validating the image-based method. The use of plasma-treated collagen membranes achieved feeding rates comparable to CHK and was fully compatible with semi-automated image analysis.
MAIN CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that hydrated collagen membranes treated with plasma gel constitute a viable and ethically preferable alternative to bird-derived membranes for the artificial feeding of Lu. longipalpis, while image analysis provides a precise, reproducible, and practical method for blood meal quantification. Collectively, this approach refines laboratory experiments Lu. longipalpis and enhances methodological reliability in studies of sand fly biology and vector-parasite interactions.

articles.title: Clinical prediction models in cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a frequent postoperative complication associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Clinical prediction models (CPM) may identify high-risk patients enabling targeted preventive interventions and improved outcomes. The objective of the study was to identify available CPMs for the risk of developing CSA-AKI and summarize their performance.
METHODS: A systematic search of studies published in Pubmed, Scopus, the Chocrane Library and Web of Science was conducted, including studies that developed or validated CPMs for CSA-AKI in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Data were extracted by two independent reviewers. Summary measures of diagnostic performance were calculated when feasible using random-effects models. Calibration and sensitivity analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: The pooled incidence of CSA-AKI was 26.3% (95% CI, 26.0-26.4), whereas CSA-AKI requiring renal replacement therapy (CSA-AKI RRT) occurred in 2.2% of patients (95% CI, 2.1-2.2). Among validated CPMs, Thakar 2005 demonstrated the best predictive performance for CSA-AKI RRT: pooled AUC 0.80 (95% CI, 0.77-0.82), sensitivity of 0.87, and a specificity of 0.49 at a threshold of ≥ 3 points. Calibration analyses indicated underestimation of risk. The Mehta 2006 and Wijeysundera 2007 models also demonstrated good discrimination. Discrimination for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI was poorer, but newer models such as the Demirjian 2022 model showed promising performance.
CONCLUSION: Accurate and well-validated CPMs can facilitate risk stratification for CSA-AKI which can influence clinical practice and research. Thakar 2005 demonstrated very good discrimination for predicting CSA-AKI RRT, whereas more validation studies for the prediction of milder stages of CSA-AKI are warranted.

articles.title: The impact of socioeconomic deprivation on outcomes following open upper-limb fractures.
articles.abstract: Socioeconomic deprivation is associated with increased trauma burden and poorer outcomes following open fractures. However, its impact on open upper-limb fractures remains unclear. This study examined whether socioeconomic deprivation influenced physiological status at presentation, Injury Severity Score and Gustilo-Anderson grade, time to surgical debridement, and early postoperative outcomes in patients treated within a regional major trauma network. We performed a retrospective cohort study using a prospectively maintained regional trauma registry at a Level I Major Trauma Centre. Consecutive patients presenting between 1 April 2014 and 1 April 2023 with open fractures of the humerus, radius, ulna, scapula, or clavicle were identified. Deprivation was determined using the postcode-linked 2019 Index of Multiple Deprivation. Patients without valid English IMD linkage were excluded. Outcomes were time to debridement, length of stay, 30- and 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, and postoperative infection. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, Injury Severity Score category, and Gustilo-Anderson grade. Of 297 identified patients, 291 were included. Patients from more deprived areas had poorer baseline physiological status, with ASA 3-4 status in 31.8% of the most deprived quintile compared with 10.0% of the least deprived quintile (p = 0.030). Gustilo-Anderson grade distribution differed across deprivation quintiles (p = 0.016), whereas Injury Severity Score category did not (p = 0.637). Time to debridement differed across IMD quintiles in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.017), but there was no linear association with continuous IMD decile after adjustment. IMD decile was not independently associated with length of stay, 90-day readmission, reoperation within 1 year, or postoperative infection. There was no statistically significant association with 30-day readmission (odds ratio 1.196, 95% CI 0.979-1.480; p = 0.080), although the estimate was imprecise. Patients from more deprived areas presented with poorer physiological status, and the distribution of Gustilo-Anderson grades differed across deprivation quintiles. However, after adjustment for measured clinical covariates, there was no clear evidence that deprivation was independently associated with delay to surgery or worse early postoperative outcomes. Standardised trauma care may help mitigate socioeconomic differences in early outcomes after upper-limb fractures.

articles.title: Outcomes following Pancreatoduodenectomy in Patients ≥80 Years: An Analysis of the Prospective Pancreas Registry of the German Society for General and Visceral Surgery (DGAV|Registry Pancreas).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: With rising life expectancy, the number of elderly patients undergoing pancreatoduodenectomy is steadily increasing. This study aimed to assess peri- and postoperative outcomes in patients aged ≥ 80 years undergoing pancreatoduodenectomy, using data from the DGAV|registry pancreas.
METHODS: All pancreatoduodenectomies performed between September 2013 and April 2024 and recorded in the DGAV|registry pancreas were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups: <80 and ≥80 years. Demographic, perioperative, and postoperative data were compared. A multivariate analysis was conducted to identify independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Out of 12,305 pancreatoduodenectomies, 1,566 (12.7%) were performed in patients aged ≥ 80 years. The proportion of very elderly patients more than doubled from 6.9% in 2014 to a peak of 17.3% in 2021. Malignant diseases, particularly pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, were more common in this group. While overall complication rates were slightly higher in the elderly (64.0% vs. 60.7%, p = 0.013), there was no significant difference in severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grades 3 and 4). However, 30-day mortality (7.2% vs. 3.6%) and in-hospital mortality (8.2% vs. 4.4%) were significantly higher in patients aged ≥ 80 years. Cardiopulmonary complications were also more frequent. Multivariate analysis identified age ≥ 80, male sex, ASA class 3 or 4, obesity, COPD, anticoagulant therapy, the need for intraoperative blood transfusions, and extended resections as independent predictors of in-hospital mortality.
CONCLUSION: Chronological age ≥ 80 years is associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality after pancreatoduodenectomy. However, age alone should not be considered an exclusion criterion. Careful patient selection, taking biological age, comorbidities, and functional status into account, is essential. Integrating geriatric expertise and prehabilitation strategies may improve outcomes in this growing patient population.

articles.title: Postoperative platelet dynamic trajectories in patients with type A aortic dissection and development of a predictive model for thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia is common after cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, platelet counts are typically assessed at single time points, and longitudinal platelet trajectories after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) surgery remain poorly characterized. This study used trajectory analysis to identify perioperative platelet count trajectories in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery.
METHODS: We retrospectively included 773 patients who underwent surgery for Stanford type A aortic dissection in this study. Platelet count data were collected over time within the first seven days after surgery. Trajectory patterns of platelet counts were determined using growth mixture modeling (GMM). The Kaplan-Meier method and log-rank test were applied to compare intergroup survival differences, and Cox regression analysis was performed to estimate mortality risks and stratify patient phenotypes. With trajectory phenotype as the outcome, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection, followed by the construction of a logistic regression predictive model.
RESULTS: GMM identified three distinct nonlinear postoperative platelet trajectories, designated as TrajeA, TrajeB, and TrajeC. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated significant differences in both early (postoperative days 7-30) and long-term survival among trajectory groups (log-rank P < 0.001). TrajeC was associated with the highest mortality risk. Five clinical variables, namely age, preoperative creatinine, total transfusion volume, end-stage renal disease, and operative duration, were ultimately incorporated into the final logistic regression model. The model achieved an AUC of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.69-0.78) in the training cohort and 0.69 (95% CI: 0.61-0.76) in the validation cohort, demonstrating moderate, stable discriminative performance and no apparent overfitting.
CONCLUSIONS: A persistently low postoperative platelet trajectory is associated with elevated short- and long-term mortality in patients undergoing acute type A aortic dissection surgery.

articles.title: Beyond complication rates: Nationwide neurosurgical compensation claims in a No-fault system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Medico-legal claims are often used as proxies for malpractice burden and health care quality. However, they reflect not only underlying clinical events but also the structure of the compensation system through which they are adjudicated. This is particularly relevant in neurosurgery, where high baseline risk and uncertainty in outcome attribution may influence both the propensity to file claims and their subsequent resolution. The objective of this study was to characterize compensation outcomes, clinical domains, decision grounds, and failure-process patterns in a nationwide no-fault neurosurgical dataset.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 620 neurosurgery-related compensation decisions issued in Norway between 2015 and 2024, examining clinical domains, decision grounds, and failure-process patterns.
RESULTS: Compensation was granted in 93 of 620 decisions (15.0%). Nontraumatic spinal disorders represented the largest domain (225/620, 36.3%) but had a low grant rate (23/225, 10.2%), whereas grant rates were higher in cerebrospinal fluid and shunt disorders (17/43, 39.5%) and trauma (9/29, 31.0%). Within nontraumatic spinal disorders, cervical degenerative disease showed particularly low compensability (8/149, 5.4%). Among granted decisions, the leading failure-process domains were preoperative or diagnostic (35/93, 37.6%), intraoperative or procedural (22/93, 23.7%), and perioperative or postoperative management (13/93, 14.0%).
CONCLUSION: In this nationwide neurosurgical series from a no-fault compensation system, compensation was granted in 15.0% of decisions and primarily reflected avoidable failures along the care pathway rather than adverse outcomes alone. Compensation decision data should therefore not be interpreted as complication rates, but as system-filtered signals of compensable and avoidable harm shaped by adjudicatory framework and system design.

articles.title: Use of intraoperative right ventricular strain as a predictor of outcomes in adult heart transplant patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricle (RV) evaluation in the perioperative period is challenging for anesthesiologists, given the limited objective assessment methods available for transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Speckle-tracking strain imaging may offer a more objective evaluation of RV function. This study evaluated the predictive value of intraoperative RV free wall strain (RVFWS) for early outcomes following orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT).
METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of 147 adults who underwent isolated OHT between January 2025 and December 2025. Patients with multiorgan transplant, congenital cases, and those without measurable intraoperative RVFWS were excluded. Post-bypass RVFWS was measured using TEE at a single time point with speckle-tracking analysis. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included severe primary graft dysfunction, 30-day mortality, need for postoperative venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), vasoactive-inotropic score, and cardiac index at 24 and 72 h, and intensive care unit length of stay. Multivariable Firth-penalized logistic and median quantile regressions were used, adjusted for a priori pre-transplant weighted risk score.
RESULTS: The median post-bypass RVFWS was -13.9% IQR (interquartile range) -19.3 to -9.6. Fourteen recipients (9.5%) died within 90 days of transplantation. After adjusting for the pre-transplant risk score, RVFWS was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality [odds ratio (OR) 2.84 per 5% decrease in magnitude, 95% confidence interval 1.65-5.58; p < 0.001]. Among the secondary outcomes, the associations with severe primary graft dysfunction (OR 2.70; raw p = 0.001), CRRT (OR 1.58; raw p = 0.001), and 30-day mortality (OR 2.94; raw p = 0.002) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni adjustment for eleven secondary comparisons (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.011, and 0.022, respectively). RVFWS demonstrated higher discrimination for 90-day mortality [area under the curve (AUC) 0.83] than qualitative intraoperative RV grading (AUC 0.68), although this difference in AUC did not reach statistical significance. RVFWS retained independent prognostic value in a combined model.
CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative post-bypass RVFWS is a feasible and objective intraoperative measure that is independently associated with early adverse outcomes after adult OHT. RVFWS shows promise as a signal of early allograft dysfunction that is not fully explained by pre-transplant risk factors.

articles.title: Flexible expansive tubular endoscopic (Flextube) spine surgery for lumbar disc herniation: a case series of 35 patients with 6-month follow-up.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the safety, efficacy, and clinical outcomes of Flexible Expansive Tubular Endoscopic (Flextube) spine surgery-a novel, non-rigid, air-medium endoscopic technique-for the treatment of single-level lumbar disc herniation (LDH).
METHODS: A retrospective case series was conducted on 35 consecutive patients with single-level LDH treated with Flextube surgery between January 2025 and June 2025. All procedures were performed using a flexible, atraumatic, expandable working tube. Clinical outcomes were evaluated preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) for back and leg pain, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and modified MacNab criteria. Perioperative parameters including operative time, blood loss, length of hospital stay, and complications were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 35 consecutive patients (mean age 47.2 ± 12.3 years) with single-level lumbar disc herniation underwent Flextube surgery. All patients completed the 6-month follow-up. The mean operative time was 49.3 ± 11.7 min, and mean intraoperative blood loss was 14.8 ± 6.5 mL. The mean hospital stay was 1.7 ± 0.6 days. Clinical outcomes improved significantly at each postoperative follow-up compared with baseline. VAS back, VAS leg, and ODI scores improved significantly at each follow-up time point (P < 0.05). At 6-month follow-up, the excellent-good rate was 94.3% (33/35). No major complications such as dural tear, nerve root injury, or surgical site infection occurred.
CONCLUSION: Flextube spine surgery is a safe and feasible minimally invasive procedure for single-level LDH, with satisfactory short-term clinical outcomes and a favorable safety profile. Further studies are needed to confirm its long-term efficacy and comparative advantages.

articles.title: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Decreases Intraoperative Allogeneic Transfusion in Cyanotic Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effect of autologous platelet-rich plasma (aPRP) on perioperative allogeneic blood product transfusion requirement in patients undergoing cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) surgery and patients' prognosis.
DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: A tertiary university hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 95 patients with CCHD who underwent cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) between January 2020 and August 2025 were included, of whom 81 (85.3%) underwent redo operation.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were divided into the aPRP group and the control group according to whether aPRP apheresis was employed. In the aPRP group, aPRP was harvested after anesthesia and transfused back to the patient after protamine neutralization, whereas the concurrently collected concentrated red blood cells (cRBCs) were reinfused during CPB or chest closure (from weaning from CPB to skin closure).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: In the original cohort, the aPRP group had significantly lower packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion rates, as well as PRBC and fresh-frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion volume, than the control group. After propensity score matching, the intraoperative PRBC transfusion rate no longer differed significantly between groups (aPRP v control: 17.4% v 43.5%, p = 0.180). However, the PRBC transfusion volume remained significantly lower in the aPRP group, both as total volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 400] mL; p = 0.037) and as weight-adjusted volume (0 [0, 0] v 0 [0, 15.7] mL/kg; p = 0.045). The matched intraoperative FFP transfusion requirements were also significantly reduced in the aPRP group (200 [0, 600] v 600 [400, 1,000] mL, p < 0.05). Viscoelastic testing indicated significantly improved coagulation and platelet function following aPRP administration in the treatment group. No difference in intraoperative blood loss, postoperative allogeneic blood products, 24-hour chest tube drainage, use of coagulation agents, postoperative ventilation time, or intensive care unit stay was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In a predominantly redo cohort of patients with CCHD undergoing cardiac surgery, the use of aPRP was associated with reduced intraoperative allogeneic blood and plasma transfusion requirements, and it also effectively preserved hemostatic function in these patients. However, the reduction in allogeneic product use may not be primarily due to the preserved hemostatic function conferred by aPRP but rather to autologous substitution of allogeneic products.

articles.title: Association of Enteral Chloral Hydrate with Benzodiazepine Exposure and Delirium After Pediatric Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Before-and-After Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol and benzodiazepine exposure, sedation quality, withdrawal, delirium, and short-term clinical outcomes in children undergoing congenital heart surgery.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective before-and-after cohort study.
SETTING: Pediatric cardiac intensive care unit of a tertiary referral center.
PARTICIPANTS: Eighty-six children who underwent congenital heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, required postoperative mechanical ventilation for more than 24 hours, and received sedation for at least 24 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were treated according to the institutional postoperative sedation protocol before (July 2021-June 2023) and after (August 2023-July 2025) implementation of enteral chloral hydrate as an adjunctive sedative.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary endpoint was cumulative midazolam exposure during the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit stay. Secondary endpoints included sedative and analgesic requirements, sedation and pain scores, withdrawal, delirium, and clinical outcomes. Compared with the preprotocol group, the chloral hydrate group had significantly lower cumulative midazolam exposure (10.2 v 13.2 mg/kg, p = 0.010) and peak midazolam infusion rates (0.15 v 0.20 mg/kg/h, p < 0.001), and a lower observed frequency of delirium (14.6% v 37.8%, p = 0.015). No significant between-group differences were observed in sedation quality, pain scores, withdrawal, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the pediatric cardiac intensive care unit or hospital, or mortality.
CONCLUSION: Addition of enteral chloral hydrate to a postoperative sedation protocol was associated with reduced benzodiazepine exposure and a lower observed frequency of delirium without statistically significant differences in sedation quality or short-term clinical outcomes. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Integrated Proteomic Profiling of Inner Ear and Systemic Fluids Following Noise-Induced Hearing Loss in Rats.
articles.abstract: Noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) arises from acute or prolonged exposure to loud sounds, yet early diagnosis remains difficult as some individuals show minimal changes in standard audiometry. This study presents the first comparative mass spectrometry-based proteomic analysis of perilymph, cochlear-derived cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), whole blood, and plasma in Sprague-Dawley rats following acute noise exposure, to identify molecular signatures of NIHL. Rats were exposed to 110 dB noise for 1 h under anesthesia, inducing an approximately 40 dB threshold shift measured by cochlear nerve Compound Action Potential (CAP). Nano LC-MS/MS in data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode followed by peptide- and protein-level filtering, identified 310 proteins in perilymph, 396 in CSF, 1688 in blood, and 281 in plasma. Differential expression analysis revealed 50, 79, 281, and 49 significantly changed proteins, respectively. A shared inflammatory response was observed, highlighted by consistent upregulation of IGHM across all fluids. Cochlear samples showed enrichment of metabolic and injury-related proteins, including PGAM2 and ALDOA, while systemic samples exhibited changes in fibrinogen chains, IGFBP5, and apolipoproteins. KEGG pathway analysis indicated involvement of metabolic, immune, and lipid-regulatory pathways. Targeted PRM validation confirmed selected protein changes. These findings demonstrate coordinated local and systemic responses to noise trauma, supporting the potential of peripheral biomarkers for early NIHL detection.

articles.title: Advances in Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy. XI: Sotatercept in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Sotatercept is a groundbreaking new treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The disease-modifying drug is a recombinant fusion protein that consists of the extracellular domain of the activin receptor 2A linked to the Fc fragment of human immunoglobulin G1. Sotatercept potently traps activins and growth differentiation factors to inhibit transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling through its activin receptor 2A/2B pathway, thereby restoring the neutral balance between pro-proliferative and antiproliferative signaling in PAH and causing a striking reversal of the disease's pathologic consequences.
