This article had the following objectives: (1) describe the parallel TGF-β signaling pathways and their opposing effects on pulmonary artery endothelial and smooth muscle cell quiescence and proliferation; (2) discuss the mechanisms by which sotatercept differentially affects TGF-β signaling to inhibit and reverse aberrant vascular proliferation and facilitate cellular quiescence; (3) review the preclinical evidence indicating that sotatercept has favorable actions in experimental models of PAH; (4) examine the findings of major clinical trials and their substudies demonstrating that sotatercept exerts temporally durable benefits on pulmonary and right ventricular hemodynamics, clinical symptoms, exercise tolerance, quality of life, and mortality in patients with long-standing, high-risk, and newly identified PAH; (5) assess recent findings indicating that sotatercept produces salutary actions in patients with precapillary and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension resulting from heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; and lastly, (6) comment on the adverse effects of sotatercept and its potential anesthetic implications.

articles.title: Supine versus prone percutaneous nephrolithotomy: A narrative and analytical review of technique.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) remains the gold standard for large and complex renal calculi. Although the prone position has traditionally been used since the introduction of PCNL in 1976, supine PCNL and its modifications have gained increasing acceptance with growing evidence supporting their efficacy and safety. This narrative review aims to compare supine and prone PCNL across various domains.
METHODS: Databases, PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were included. Priority was given to randomized-controlled trials, meta-analyses, and large prospective studies (>100 patients). Evidence was synthesized across operative, anesthetic, safety and technological domains.
RESULTS: Supine PCNL demonstrated stone-free rates comparable to prone PCNL. Multiple meta-analyses showed significantly shorter operative times (by 13-25 min), improved anesthetic safety, reduced radiation exposure, shorter learning curve, lower infectious complications, and superior ergonomics with the supine approach. Supine PCNL facilitates Endoscopic Combined Intrarenal Surgery and is particularly advantageous in obese, pediatric, elderly, and cardiovascular high-risk patients. Miniaturized PCNL techniques further enhance these benefits. Ultrasound-guided access contributes to improved procedural safety, whereas gravity-assisted drainage helps maintain low intrarenal pressure and facilitates gravity-assisted fragment evacuation. Emerging technologies such as vacuum-assisted systems and robotic-assisted PCNL appear inherently more compatible with the supine position.
CONCLUSION: Supine PCNL offers significant operative, anesthetic, and technological advantages while maintaining equivalent stone-free outcomes. It can be considered an equally useful approach in most clinical scenarios, whereas prone PCNL has definite advantages in selected anatomical situations.

articles.title: Robot-assisted kidney transplantation for right versus left living donor kidneys: A single-center outcome and learning curve analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Robot-assisted kidney transplantation (RAKT) is the standard of care in experienced hands. Transplantation of right kidney (RK) from a living donor (LD) is challenging because the right renal vein is shorter and thinner, which can lead to underutilization of RKs from LD. Data for RK-RAKT are scarce. We aim to compare the surgical, peri-operative, and long-term outcomes after RAKT from RK donors versus left kidney (LK) donors and the learning curve (LC) for the entire RAKT cohort.
METHODS: After ethical committee approval, we retrospectively analyzed 409 adult RAKTs from LDs performed by a single surgeon between 2013 and 2021. We compared donor/recipient demographics, intra-operative data, immediate and late graft function, and graft/patient survival.
RESULTS: Overall, 18.5% were RK-RAKT. Donor/recipient demographics were similar between the groups. Total vascular (32.9 ± 8.9 vs. 29.6 ± 5.8 min, P = 0.003) and venous anastomosis times (14.4 ± 6.1 vs. 11.4 ± 2.5 min, P < 0.0001) were significantly longer in the RK group. No significant differences were observed in the serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate levels at day 1 and 7; 1 month; 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 years. 10-year Death-censored graft survival (77.4% for left vs. 79.17% for right, P = 0.917) and patient survival (83.9% for left vs. 75% for right, P = 0.10) were comparable. LC was shorter for critical vascular steps and graft functional outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: RK-RAKT achieves equivalent functional and survival outcomes to LK-RAKT. Concerns regarding vascular thrombosis are not supported by our findings. These results advocate for broader use of RK, potentially decreasing the wait times and improving the access to transplantation.

articles.title: Evaluation of opioid consumption using the quadratus lumborum block or intraperitoneal instillation with bupivacaine in dogs undergoing ovariohysterectomy in a teaching institution.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative opioid consumption between ultrasound-guided quadratus lumborum block (QLB) with bupivacaine and intraperitoneal bupivacaine instillation.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, single-blinded, cross-sectional, clinical study.
ANIMALS: A total of 74 owned female dogs undergoing elective ovariohysterectomy.
METHODS: Dogs were premedicated with dexmedetomidine (5 μg kg-1) and methadone (0.3 mg kg-1) intramuscularly. Anesthesia was induced with intravenous propofol and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen. Carprofen (4 mg kg-1) was given subcutaneously after orotracheal intubation. Dogs underwent either a QLB with 0.3 mL kg-1 (1.5 mg kg-1) per side of 0.5% bupivacaine (group QLB) or intraoperative intraperitoneal instillation (group IP) of 0.5% bupivacaine (3 mg kg-1) as part of a multimodal analgesic protocol. Ovariohysterectomies were performed by undergraduate students under instructor supervision. Postoperative pain was assessed at 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 hours after extubation, using the short form of the Glasgow Composite Measure Pain Scale, and methadone (0.2 mg kg-1) was given as rescue analgesia if the pain score was ≥ 6/24. Opioid consumption was quantified by the number of rescue boluses required, using Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: Methadone boluses were given at least once to 9/37 dogs (24%) in group QLB and 15/37 dogs (41%) in group IP. Dogs in group QLB were given 0-2 (range) methadone boluses, whereas those in group IP were given 0-3 boluses, with a total of 11 and 21 boluses, respectively. Methadone consumption was significantly reduced in group QLB versus group IP with a rate ratio of 0.42 (95% confidence interval = 0.19-0.92, p = 0.023).
CONCLUSIONS: As part of a multimodal analgesic protocol, the QLB reduced postoperative opioid consumption compared with intraperitoneal instillation of bupivacaine in dogs undergoing ovariohysterectomy performed by veterinary students.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The QLB can be an alternative to the IP instillation of bupivacaine in dogs undergoing OVH, particularly in teaching settings where surgical procedures may be longer and more stimulating.

articles.title: Post-Operative Complications in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people experience significant perioperative health inequity following cardiac surgery. While post-operative outcomes have been summarized in those undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), perioperative cardiac surgical outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have not.
METHODS: A literature review was conducted using MEDLINE, Scopus and Embase databases to identify published data comparing post-operative complications in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and non-Indigenous Australian adults undergoing cardiac surgery. Selected search terms were used to identify abstracts from eligible studies, which were then screened to identify relevant articles.
RESULTS: We identified 15 observational studies examining post-operative complications in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people undergoing cardiac surgery. Seven focused on isolated CABG, two on isolated valve surgery, and the remainder examined a combination of both. These studies revealed higher post-operative complication rates including myocardial infarction, kidney failure, and long-term mortality among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people compared to their (frequently >10 year) older non-Indigenous Australian counterparts. Post-CABG, this was largely driven by greater preoperative comorbidity (including higher rates of diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease). No studies evaluated pre-operative socioeconomic status, frailty or malnutrition, post-operative self-discharge rates or sepsis, or adjusted analyses of post-operative outcomes following valve surgery. No interventional studies were identified.
CONCLUSION: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people experience greater post-operative morbidity and mortality following cardiac surgery than non-Indigenous Australians. However, further research is warranted to explore several clinically relevant pre-operative variables and post-operative complications, and potential interventions to reduce perioperative inequity in this setting.

articles.title: Inhaled nitric oxide: Expanding indications beyond traditional boundaries.
articles.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that improves ventilation-perfusion matching with minimal effect on systemic blood pressure. Although the FDA approval is restricted to neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure associated with pulmonary hypertension, many clinicians now use iNO in adults with conditions where elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular dysfunction threaten stability and hypoxic respiratory failure. This review examines both the mechanistic rationale and the available evidence for such off-label use. Examples range from acute RV failure in the ICU to perioperative support in cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, including COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). In these settings, iNO offers rapid afterload reduction and short-term improvement in oxygenation, but randomized trials are lacking and limited studies to date have failed to consistently show outcome benefits. Adverse effects such as methemoglobinemia, nitrogen dioxide toxicity, rebound pulmonary hypertension, and a potential increase in acute kidney injury risk in certain non-cardiac surgical populations. Additionally, cost considerations and other practical limitations must be weighed carefully. Overall, current evidence supports the use of iNO as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected critically ill patients.

articles.title: A Prospective Evaluation of Right Ventricular Function in High- and Low-Flow Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
The Impact of Postoperative Mechanical Ventilation Duration on Visual and Auditory Hallucinations After Cardiac Surgery: Insights from the VAACS Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether postoperative mechanical ventilation duration is associated with the risk and timing of visual and auditory hallucinations after adult cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Prospective multicenter cohort study.
SETTING: Ten major cardiac surgery centers in the West Bank, Palestine.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1,332 adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting or valve surgery, stratified by postoperative ventilation duration: ≤6 hours or >6 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: No experimental intervention was performed; patients were grouped by early versus delayed postoperative extubation.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Visual and auditory hallucinations were assessed during the first 7 postoperative days using the Questionnaire for Psychotic Experiences. Cox regression and restricted mean survival time analyses evaluated associations between ventilation duration and hallucination outcomes. Delayed extubation (>6 hours) was associated with lower overall adjusted risk of visual hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.62-0.80; p < .001) and auditory hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% confidence interval, 0.31-0.77; p = .002). However, time-varying analysis showed increased immediate postoperative hazard in the delayed-extubation group, with risk declining rapidly over time. Restricted mean survival time analysis showed that auditory hallucination-free time was approximately 0.24 days shorter in patients with delayed extubation (p < .001). Preoperative white blood cell count was the most consistent predictor.
CONCLUSION: Delayed postoperative extubation was associated with lower overall 7-day hallucination risk but higher immediate postoperative vulnerability, suggesting that the early postextubation period may represent a critical window for targeted monitoring and preventive neuropsychiatric care after cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Trajectories of postoperative fatigue and their association with physical and mental health among patients with peritoneal metastases from colorectal and appendiceal cancer after cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy: a 1-year longitudinal study.
articles.abstract: Postoperative fatigue (POF) is a common complication following major or medium-sized surgeries. It is influenced by surgical trauma, pain, sleep quality, nutrition, and mental state, and can significantly hinder postoperative recovery. As enhanced recovery protocols become more widely adopted in perioperative care, attention to the prevention and management of POF has increased. This 1-year longitudinal study enrolled patients with peritoneal metastases from colorectal and appendiceal cancer following cytoreductive surgery and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC) at two tertiary hospitals. Participants completed self-administered questionnaires at discharge, and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months after surgery. POF was assessed using the 10-item Identity-Consequence Fatigue Scale (ICFS-10). Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was utilized to identify distinct POF trajectories, and multivariable models were fitted to examine their associations with sleep quality, pain, and physical and mental conditions over time. The reporting of this study adhered to the Guidelines for Reporting on Latent Trajectory Studies (GRoLTS) checklist. Among 182 participants who experienced POF during follow-up, three distinct fatigue trajectories were identified: high-increasing (29.67%), moderate-increasing (37.36%), and low-increasing (31.87%). Poor sleep quality, inadequate pain management, and compromised physical and mental conditions were linked to trajectory groups with more severe fatigue symptoms. After adjusting for covariates, the high-increasing trajectory group demonstrated significantly lower scores in mental dimensions at 12 months post-discharge. This study presents the cumulative incidence and longitudinal trajectories of POF over a 1-year postoperative period, analyzing the relationship between physical and mental conditions in peritoneal metastatic cancer survivors. Our findings underscore the importance of early identification and targeted treatment of high-risk patients to prevent the chronic progression of POF. These trajectory patterns provide potential clinical avenues for the early detection and management of persistent fatigue based on a patient's evolving symptom profile.

articles.title: Perioperative and oncological outcomes of single-port versus two-port thoracoscopic lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer: a propensity score-matched retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Although single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy is increasingly adopted for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evidence comparing its long-term oncological efficacy with that of the two-port approach remains scarce. This propensity score-matched study evaluated perioperative outcomes, postoperative recovery, and 3-year survival following single-port versus two-port thoracoscopic lobectomy in patients with NSCLC. We retrospectively analyzed 167 consecutive patients (single-port, n = 82; two-port, n = 85); propensity score matching (1:1, caliper = 0.2) yielded 72 matched pairs. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative pain (VAS), inflammatory markers (CRP, PCT, IL-1β), pulmonary function, 30-day complications, 3-year overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and multivariable Cox regression were compared. Following matching, the single-port group demonstrated significantly longer operative time (187.3 ± 56.4 vs. 142.2 ± 49.4 minutes; P<0.001) but reduced blood loss (96.5 ± 42.0 vs. 121.7 ± 48.1 mL; P<0.001) 24-hour chest drainage volume (632.3 ± 447.3 vs. 945.5 ± 501.3 mL; P<0.001), and incision length (3.57 ± 1.37 vs. 4.94 ± 1.52 cm; P<0.001). Lymph node yield did not differ significantly (17.3 ± 4.1 vs. 16.1 ± 3.6; P = 0.058). Postoperative VAS scores were significantly lower in the single-port group on days 3, 5, and 7 (all P<0.001), with attenuated inflammatory responses (lower CRP, PCT, and IL-1β; all P<0.001) and better pulmonary function recovery (higher PaO2, SpO2, FVC, and FEV1; all P<0.05). Thirty-day complication rates did not differ significantly (6.9% vs. 9.7%; P = 0.763). Over a median follow-up of 38 months, 3-year OS (86.5% vs. 84.4%; P = 0.572) and 3-year DFS (79.2% vs. 77.1%; P = 0.684) were comparable. Multivariable analysis identified pathological stage II (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.35-4.43; P = 0.003) and lymphovascular invasion (HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.18-3.72; P = 0.012) as independent predictors of poorer DFS, whereas surgical approach was not associated with DFS or OS. In conclusion, single-port thoracoscopic lobectomy was associated with reduced surgical trauma, decreased postoperative pain and inflammation, and improved pulmonary function recovery, without compromising lymph node dissection, short-term safety, or 3-year oncological outcomes. These findings support the continued use and wider adoption of single-port VATS in appropriately selected patients with NSCLC, while acknowledging that Stage I disease predominance limits generalizability to more advanced stages.

articles.title: Outcomes and Challenges of Redo Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Propensity-Matched Comparative Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aims to compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of reoperative coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with primary CABG in a propensity score-matched patient cohort.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,021 patients who underwent CABG between January 2003 and January 2024. Among them, 35 (1.7%) patients underwent redo CABG. Using 1:1 propensity score matching based on age, ejection fraction, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, 36 patients who underwent primary CABG were selected for comparison. Patients with incomplete records or combined cardiac procedures were excluded. Perioperative variables, in-hospital mortality, and long-term survival were analyzed.
RESULTS: The redo CABG group had significantly longer intensive care unit stays (2.15 ± 2.37 vs. 1.39 ± 1.36 days, P = 0.006), hospital stays (12.11 ± 17.40 vs. 7.36 ± 2.21 days, P = 0.009), and postoperative bleeding (899.12 ± 445.17 vs. 576.39 ± 323.92 ml, P = 0.001). Hospital mortality occurred in two patients (5.7%) in the redo group and one patient (2.8%) in the primary group (P = 0.614). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed higher long-term survival in the redo CABG group (77.1%) compared to the primary CABG group (58.3%), though not statistically significant (P = 0.168).
CONCLUSION: Despite the increased perioperative complexity, redo CABG is associated with low in-hospital mortality and promising long-term outcomes when appropriate patient selection and meticulous surgical technique are employed. These findings are especially relevant in guiding revascularization strategies for patients with prior CABG, where redo surgery is often underutilized despite its clinical viability.

articles.title: Perimenstrual repetitive greater occipital nerve blockade for menstrual migraine: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The main purpose of this study is to demonstrate the decrease in headache severity, pain duration and the number of painful days in a month after repetitive GON blockade applied with local anesthetic in menstrual migraine patients compared to the placebo group.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study included 48 menstrual migraine patients. 24 patients received medication (0.5% bupivacaine) and 24 received placebo (saline) GON blockade twice a month for three months. Baseline data (month 0) relied on retrospective recall, whereas post-treatment data (months 3 and 6) were collected prospectively using a paper-based headache diary. The primary outcome was the change in headache severity (VAS score). Secondary outcomes included attack frequency, duration, number of headache days, analgesic use, and MIDAS scores.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. At month 3, the active group showed a significantly greater reduction in the primary outcome, VAS scores, compared to the placebo group (decreasing from 8.75 ± 0.67 to 3.80 ± 3.18 vs. 8.71 ± 1.04 to 7.16 ± 1.31; p < 0.001). Significant reductions were also observed in secondary outcomes including monthly attack frequency (p = 0.002), mean attack duration (p < 0.001), number of headache days (p = 0.002), MIDAS scores (p = 0.003), and analgesic use (p = 0.009). Mild, transient injection-site tenderness was the only reported side effect. The clinical improvements were maintained at the 6th month, suggesting a potential sustained benefit, though natural history or late placebo responses cannot be fully excluded.
CONCLUSION: Repetitive perimenstrual GON blockade may be an effective short-term prophylaxis for MM. However, the observed effects on the subjective primary endpoint (VAS) may be partially attributable to imperfect blinding, and all secondary outcomes are exploratory. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and exclude natural history or placebo responses.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07576309. Registered on 08 May 2026. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients: a 9-year multicenter cohort study of clinical features, management, and 90-day outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mucormycosis is a rare but life-threatening invasive fungal infection that primarily affects immunocompromised patients. Data on its presentation, management, and prognosis in the intensive care unit setting remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate 90-day mortality and to explore clinical, microbiological, therapeutic, and immunological factors associated with outcome in critically ill patients with mucormycosis.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included patients diagnosed with mucormycosis and admitted to the ICUs of the Hospices Civils de Lyon between January 2014 and July 2023. Patients were identified through mycological records and hospital discharge codes. Univariable analysis and multivariable Cox model were performed to identify factors associated with 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: Among 43 patients included, hematological malignancy and trauma were the most common underlying conditions (26% each), followed by solid organ transplantation (21%), and burns (16%). Cutaneous forms (49%) predominated, especially among trauma and burn patients, while pulmonary and rhinocerebral forms were mostly observed in previously immunocompromised individuals. The number of mucormycosis diagnoses increased nearly threefold over the study period, paralleling the implementation of Mucorales-specific polymerase chain reaction. Antifungal therapy was initiated in 39 patients (91%); first-line treatment was liposomal amphotericin B in 32 (74%), at a median maximum dose of 7.5 [3.5-9.4] mg/kg/day, and 12 (28%) received a combination therapy. The 90-day mortality was 47%. In the multivariable Cox model, older age, hematological malignancy, and a higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score at diagnosis were independently associated with mortality, while lower liposomal amphotericin B dosing was associated with mortality in univariable analysis. In eight patients without previous immunosuppression and uncontrolled disease, immune monitoring was performed and revealed decreased monocyte HLA-DR expression at 4556 [4194-6936] Ab/c, in favor of injury-induced immunosuppression. Among them, six patients received interferon-gamma as immunotherapy; four responded immunologically and survived.
CONCLUSIONS: Mucormycosis in critically ill patients is associated with high mortality, particularly in those with hematological malignancies. Polymerase chain reaction-based diagnostics may allow earlier detection, and immune monitoring could help identify high-risk patients, particularly in trauma and burn settings.

articles.title: Unilateral biportal endoscopic thoracic costotransversectomy approach: a minimally invasive technique for thoracic disc herniation-a technical feasibility report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) surgery has advanced minimally invasive spine surgery, but existing techniques for thoracic disc herniation (TDH) face challenges when addressing calcified/sequestered discs and spinal stability. UBE with thoracic costotransversectomy (UBE-TCT) is a novel approach designed to preserve posterior bony architecture while allowing precise ventral decompression.
OBJECTIVE: The primary aim of this study was to describe the detailed standardized surgical technique of UBE-TCT, and to preliminarily verify its anatomical feasibility, surgical safety, and short-term clinical outcomes in the treatment of TDH, as a technical feasibility report.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 6 patients with TDH who underwent UBE-TCT between March 2023 and September 2024. Three-dimensional computed tomography (3D-CT) was obtained to measure the Lateral Skin Entry Distance (LSED), thereby evaluating the anatomical feasibility of the UBE-TCT approach. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were examined to measure the cross-sectional area of the thoracic spinal canal (CSA-TSC) and to assess the extent of decompression at the herniated disc site. Clinical outcomes were assessed using Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) scores for back and leg pain, and the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) for thoracic-related disability.
RESULTS: A total of 6 patients (mean age 59.67 ± 8.78 years) involving 7 herniated thoracic disc levels were included in this study. The mean follow-up period was 17.83 ± 5.71 months. No conversion to open surgery or perioperative complications occurred. The average operative time was 120.83 ± 29.94 min, and the average postoperative hospital stay was 4.50 ± 1.38 days. The preoperative LSED, measured across all treated levels, was 36.07 ± 3.66 mm. Postoperatively, the CSA-TSC increased significantly from 135.48 ± 57.47 mm2 to 174.93 ± 48.82 mm2 (P < 0.05). Regarding clinical outcomes, significant alleviation of pain and functional improvement were observed immediately after surgery and maintained throughout the follow-up period (P < 0.01). Back VAS scores decreased rapidly from 7.50 ± 0.84 preoperatively to 3.17 ± 0.75 at 48 h postoperatively, further to 1.50 ± 0.84 at the last follow-up. Similarly, Leg VAS scores dropped from 6.17 ± 0.98 to 2.83 ± 0.75 at 48 h, and finally to 1.33 ± 0.52. The ODI also showed a progressive decline, improving from a preoperative baseline of 59.67 ± 9.07% to 44.00 ± 8.20% at 48 h, and reaching 15.33 ± 3.72% at the final assessment. According to the modified MacNab criteria, the excellent/good rate was 100% (5 excellent, 1 good).
CONCLUSION: This preliminary technical feasibility report suggests that UBE-TCT, as a minimally invasive endoscopic technique, is a preliminarily safe and anatomically feasible strategy for the treatment of ventral thoracic spinal canal stenosis caused by TDH.

articles.title: Randomized pilot trial of intraoperative hemoadsorption in clopidogrel treated patients undergoing urgent coronary artery bypass grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving clopidogrel who undergo urgent CABG before the recommended 5-day washout period are at increased risk of perioperative bleeding. This study evaluated whether intraoperative hemoadsorption can reduce bleeding in such patients.
METHODS: Patients undergoing CABG within 24 h of clopidogrel discontinuation were randomized 1:1 to intraoperative hemoadsorption (Group 1) or control (Group 2). In the intervention group, the device was incorporated into the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuit. Efficacy was assessed by 24-hour chest tube drainage (CTD), blood product transfusions and surgical revisions for bleeding control.
RESULTS: A total of 50 patients were randomized (mean age 64 ± 8.6 years, 82% male). There were no differences in baseline characteristics between groups. Group 1 showed significantly reduced median 24-hr CTD of 300mL [250-400] vs. 500mL [400-700], p = 0.0003, transfusions of packed red blood cells 0 [0-1] vs. 1 [0-2] units, p = 0.047), fresh frozen plasma 0 [0-0] vs. 2 [2-3] units, p < 0.0001) and platelets 0 [0-0] vs. 2 [1-3] units, p < 0.0001 compared with Group 2. One revision for bleeding control occurred in Group 2 (4.0%). No device-related serious adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of clopidogrel-treated patients undergoing CABG within 24 h of discontinuation, intraoperative hemoadsorption was associated with lower postoperative bleeding and transfusion requirements.

articles.title: Humanization of care: a geospatial analysis of key indicators of quality and safety of health care and service in the Centre region, Cameroon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrating the principles of humanized care into healthcare systems is critical to promoting optimal well-being. In a context of limited resources, improving quality of care means identifying priority sites to optimize cost-effectiveness. The objective was to measure key indicators of quality and safety in health facilities and map priority health districts (HDs) for effective implementation of high-impact interventions in the Centre Region.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional analysis of retrospective data from 32 HDs in the Centre Region for the period 2018-2022. Data were extracted from the national District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2) database in April 2023 and checked for completeness. The health indicators assessed were those defined in the Cameroon Health Sector Strategy for 2020-2030. Data were analyzed using R statistics version 4.2.3.
RESULTS: The density of the qualified healthcare workers was 13.7 per 10 000 inhabitants in 2022. Over the five-year study period, the density of doctors in rural areas declined by almost 20% by 2020, whereas urban areas experienced a concurrent increase. The Odza HD had the highest inpatient mortality rate over the five-year study period (49%). In rural areas, the Esse HD had the highest mortality rate (32.4%). Esse (18.8%) and Odza (6.7%) HDs had the highest perioperative mortality rates in rural and urban areas, respectively. Most of the urban HDs (5/8 = 62.5%) had a neonatal mortality rate higher than the regional median (RM = 3.1). Half of the rural HDs had a maternal mortality ratio higher than the RM = 118 per 1000 live births and the Mbandjock (357/1,000) and Mvog-Ada (285/1,000) HDs carried the highest burden in rural and urban areas respectively. More than two thirds of urban HDs recorded a proportion of free malaria treatment cases below the RM (14%).
CONCLUSIONS: Efforts to humanize healthcare in the Centre Region are hindered by persistent disparities in care quality and inconsistent policy implementation. Addressing these challenges requires timely implementation of a National Strategic Plan to Improve the Quality of Healthcare and Service Delivery, emphasizing on capacity building through training and supervision.

articles.title: The Analgesic Efficacy of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Ropivacaine in Preoperative Interscalene Block for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative pain management is essential after arthroscopic shoulder surgery. Ultrasound-guided interscalene block (ISB) is widely used for perioperative analgesia; however, the benefits of adding dexmedetomidine to local anesthetics remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the analgesic efficacy and hemodynamic effects of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to ropivacaine for ultrasound-guided ISB in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.
METHODS: This double-blind randomized clinical trial included patients aged ≥ 18 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-III who were scheduled for elective arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. Forty-two patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio using a random-number table to receive ultrasound-guided ISB with either 20 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine plus 2 mL of normal saline (R group) or 20 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine plus dexmedetomidine (1.5 μg/kg), diluted to a total volume of 2 mL (ropivacaine-dexmedetomidine (RD) group). Randomization and preparation of the study solutions were performed by an independent investigator. The anesthesiologist performing the block, the patients, and the postoperative outcome assessor remained blinded to the treatment allocation. Pain intensity was assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) in the recovery room and at 2, 6, 18, and 24 hours postoperatively. Intraoperative remifentanil consumption, time to the first patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) request, number of PCIA requests, pethidine requirements, and hemodynamic variables were recorded. Data were analyzed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, independent-samples t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate.
RESULTS: Forty patients completed the study and were included in the per-protocol analysis (20 patients in each group). Compared with the R group, the RD group had significantly lower intraoperative remifentanil consumption (0.11 ± 0.02 vs 0.24 ± 0.04 μg/kg/min, P < 0.001), a longer time to the first PCIA request (17.57 ± 0.93 vs 13.37 ± 1.25 hours after ISB, P < 0.001), fewer PCIA requests (4.50 ± 1.19 vs 9.95 ± 1.50, P < 0.001), a longer time to the first pethidine administration (19.20 ± 0.83 vs 16.33 ± 1.52 hours after ISB, P < 0.001), and fewer pethidine administrations (0.35 ± 0.67 vs 3.45 ± 1.05, P < 0.001). NRS pain scores at 18 and 24 hours were also significantly lower in the RD group. No significant between-group differences were observed in systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and heart rate.
CONCLUSIONS: The addition of dexmedetomidine to ropivacaine for an ultrasound-guided interscalene block significantly prolonged postoperative analgesia, reduced intraoperative remifentanil consumption, decreased postoperative analgesic requirements, and improved postoperative pain control, without significant adverse effects on hemodynamic parameters, in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.

articles.title: Effect of Sub-antagonist Doses of Naloxone as an Adjuvant to Ropivacaine on the Onset and Quality of Axillary Brachial Plexus Block in Patients Undergoing Forearm and Hand Surgery: A Randomized Double-Blind Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Axillary brachial plexus block (ABPB) is the preferred regional anesthetic technique for forearm and hand surgery. Naloxone at sub-antagonist doses may paradoxically enhance local anesthetic effects through selective opioid receptor modulation; however, the optimal dose and its clinical benefit in ABPB with ropivacaine remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the effects of ultra-low-dose naloxone (0.4 µg), low-dose naloxone (4 µg), and placebo added to 0.5% ropivacaine on block onset, intensity, and postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing elective forearm and hand surgery. To our knowledge, this is the first trial to directly compare two sub-antagonist doses of naloxone as adjuvants to ropivacaine for axillary block.
METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind clinical trial, 120 patients with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I or II were allocated equally to three groups: Group 1 (control; ropivacaine plus saline), Group 2 (ropivacaine plus low-dose naloxone, 4 µg), and Group 3 (ropivacaine plus ultra-low-dose naloxone, 0.4 µg). All blocks were performed using combined ultrasound and nerve stimulator guidance. The co-primary outcomes were sensory and motor block onset times. Secondary outcomes included block intensity, visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores during recovery, and the proportion of patients requiring pethidine within 24 hours.
RESULTS: All 120 blocks (100%) were clinically successful, with no intraoperative rescue analgesia or conversion to general anesthesia in any group. Motor block onset was significantly faster in Groups 2 and 3 than in Group 1 (P < 0.001); no patient in the naloxone groups required 9 minutes to achieve motor block, compared with 30% in Group 1. Sensory block onset did not differ significantly among groups (P = 0.163). At 30 minutes, VAS scores were lower in both naloxone groups than in Group 1; the overall analysis of variance (ANOVA) result was P < 0.001, and the reported comparison between Group 3 and Group 1 was significant (P < 0.001). The 15-minute difference was not significant after Bonferroni correction. The proportion requiring pethidine within 24 hours was significantly lower in Group 3 than in Group 1, with a risk ratio of 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33 - 0.82] (27.5% vs. 52.5%; P = 0.005). Group 2 had a numerically higher pethidine requirement than Group 1 (62.5% vs. 52.5%), suggesting possible dose-dependent partial receptor antagonism that requires confirmation in future studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultra-low-dose naloxone (0.4 µg) significantly accelerates motor block onset and reduces postoperative pethidine requirements in patients with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I or II undergoing elective hand and forearm surgery with ABPB, without adverse effects. Although the 4 µg dose was associated with lower VAS scores at 30 minutes, it did not reduce pethidine requirements and was associated with a nonsignificant increase in the proportion of patients requiring pethidine, consistent with a biphasic dose-response model. These findings highlight the narrow therapeutic margin of perineural naloxone and suggest caution with doses above the ultra-low-dose range, as higher sub-antagonist doses may paradoxically antagonize endogenous analgesic mechanisms.

articles.title: Frailty patterns in European surgical patients: The FRAGILE multicentre prospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional decline in physiological reserve that increases vulnerability to surgical stress. Its peri-operative dynamics and association with outcomes across diverse surgical populations remain insufficiently characterised.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the prevalence of frailty before and after surgery and to evaluate its association with postoperative complications, mortality, and hospital length of stay.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicentre European cohort study including adults undergoing elective or emergency surgery under general or regional anaesthesia across 64 participating centres in 10 countries. Each centre contributed data from one to three predefined recruitment days between April 2021 and December 2022. Frailty was assessed preoperatively and at 30 days using the Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), the FRAIL questionnaire, and the Barthel Index. The primary outcome was the association between preoperative frailty and 30-day postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ II); secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, postoperative cognitive impairment, and new-onset frailty.
RESULTS: Among 1472 patients (mean age 60.9 years; 52.9% male), preoperative frailty prevalence was 14.6% (FRAIL), 10.4% (CFS), and 10.4% (Barthel). Within 30 days, 11.9% of nonfrail patients became frail, increasing overall frailty prevalence to 21.2%. Postoperative complications occurred in 19.2% and mortality in 1.7%. Preoperative frailty was independently associated with complications: adjusted odds ratio (OR) 2.35 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.53 to 3.60], P < 0.001); 30-day mortality OR 10.9 (95% CI 1.28 to 93.0), P = 0.029). Frailty was also associated with postoperative cognitive impairment: OR 3.47 (95% CI 1.98 to 6.08), P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is common among surgical patients, increases after surgery, and independently predicts postoperative complications and mortality. These findings highlight frailty as a dynamic and potentially modifiable marker of surgical vulnerability that should be routinely assessed and integrated into peri-operative care.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04140370.

articles.title: DTI-Associated Blood Biomarkers in a Human Perioperative Brain Perturbation Model.
articles.abstract: Circulating biomarkers of brain perturbation are rarely evaluated against anatomically localized in vivo imaging measures, limiting biological interpretation. We tested whether perioperative changes in candidate biomarkers were associated with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI)-defined microstructural changes in a controlled human perioperative model. In a paired cohort of 75 patients undergoing left-sided encephaloduroarteriosynangiosis, we obtained matched pre- and postoperative DTI and blood samples. Six biomarkers (ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase-L1 [UCH-L1], glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP], S100 calcium-binding protein B [S100B], neurofilament light chain, neuron-specific enolase, and protein tau) were quantified. Analyses included paired comparisons, region-of-interest-based cross-modal correlations, sparse canonical correlation analysis (sCCA) with bootstrap stability assessment, and patient-grouped regularized logistic regression for state discrimination. DTI showed perioperative changes in bilateral temporal-limbic regions and connected white matter, with the largest effects in left hippocampal and amygdalar territories on the operated side. UCH-L1, GFAP, and S100B showed the clearest paired increases and dominated internal perioperative-state discrimination. Blood-DTI associations were heterogeneous across biomarkers and states, and paired-change associations were not confined to these three markers. An observed three-biomarker panel discriminated perioperative state with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.914 in the test set. Several circulating biomarkers covaried with regional DTI measures in this exploratory perioperative cohort. UCH-L1, GFAP, and S100B were the most perioperatively responsive and state-discriminative markers, but the DTI-association pattern was not specific to this trio. The findings support a structure-associated framework for evaluating blood biomarkers against regional imaging changes; they do not validate these biomarkers for traumatic brain injury, and relevance to traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: National Patterns of Botulinum Toxin A Use in Children With Cerebral Palsy in Aotearoa New Zealand: A Register Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To analyse botulinum toxin A (BTX-A) use in children with cerebral palsy (CP) in a high-resource country and explore practice variations.
METHODS: Demographic data for 1149 children/young adults enrolled in the New Zealand Cerebral Palsy Register (born 2002-2018) were linked with hospital procedural records (2002-2023) and analysed using multivariable regression models.
RESULTS: Seven hundred and twenty-five of 1149 children (63%) had ≥ 1 BTX-A episode by age 15 years (n = 3734 episodes), with 101 (8.8%) having ≥ 10 episodes. From 2009 to 2023, between 15% and 25% of children < 15 years old had one or more BTX-A injections per year. Three thousand and four hundred episodes (91%) were under general anaesthesia, 3290 (88%) were linked to the orthopaedic surgical service and only 55 (1.5%) were linked to otorhinolaryngology service. Children classified as gross motor classification system (GMFCS) Levels II and III were more likely to have BTX-A compared to GMFCS Level I (odds ratio (OR) 2.21 (95% CI 1.56, 3.11) and 3.11 (1.85, 5.22). Repeat injections were more common at GMFCS Levels III or IV hazard ratio 1.48 (1.25, 1.74) and 1.33 (1.13, 1.56). Those children living within a health district with a tertiary hospital (628; 55%), had twice the odds of ever receiving BTX-A [OR 1.97 (1.49, 2.62)] and were younger at first episode.
CONCLUSIONS: BTX-A is widely used in childhood CP in New Zealand, particularly for those with moderate functional limitations. Total level of BTX-A use remained similar from 2009 to 2023 but appears to be influenced by both individual clinical features and availability of local tertiary hospital services.

articles.title: Oncologic Outcomes and Treatment Feasibility of Transoral Carbon Dioxide Laser Microsurgery for Hypopharyngeal Tumors in Older Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated outcomes and complications of transoral CO2 laser microsurgery (TLM) for hypopharyngeal tumors and its feasibility in ≥ 75-year-old patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 116 patients (without metastases) treated from February 2012 to October 2024 at our hospital. Oncologic outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves (110 patients; median follow-up: 5.3 years).
RESULTS: Five-year local control, disease-specific survival, and overall survival rates were 87.8%, 94.6%, and 85.6%, respectively. Postoperative dysphagia, aspiration pneumonia, pharyngolaryngeal edema, and vocal fold paralysis occurred in 9%, 4%, 3%, and 3% of patients, respectively; none required tracheostomy or surgical hemostasis under general anesthesia. The group with a history of head and neck irradiation had higher rates of dysphagia (p = 0.010) and aspiration pneumonia (p = 0.031) than those without. Differences between age groups were nonsignificant.
CONCLUSIONS: TLM appears safe and effective for older patients with appropriately selected hypopharyngeal tumors.
